stories.title: Iran allows Chinese ships to pass Hormuz since Wednesday
stories.summary: Iranian media reported that Tehran allowed Chinese commercial vessels to transit the Strait of Hormuz under special protocols. The passage was permitted while the strait remains otherwise restricted.

stories.title: Israel to sue NY Times over opinion alleging widespread rape of Palestinian prisoners
stories.summary: Israel announced plans to sue The New York Times over a Nicholas Kristof opinion piece alleging widespread rape of Palestinian prisoners. Prime Minister Netanyahu and Foreign Minister Sa'ar called the article one of the 'most hideous and distorted lies' published against Israel.

stories.title: Fatah gathers for first election in decade, as PA’s Abbas pledges to continue reforms
stories.summary: The Fatah movement convened its first internal election in a decade during a three-day conference. Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas pledged to continue reforms and criticized Israel's withholding of PA funds. Delegates voted for an 18-member committee expected to shape the post-Abbas era.

stories.title: No Exit From El Fasher
stories.summary: An investigation by Fault Lines and Lighthouse documents the siege of el-Fasher in Sudan, where civilians were trapped, starved, and killed amid ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Warning of record global temperatures
stories.summary: Global meteorological agencies issued warnings about potential record global temperatures as the probability of a very strong El Niño event increased.

stories.title: Syria: Prosecuting Assad-era security officials
stories.summary: Syria's new administration has begun prosecuting officials from the former regime of Bashar al-Assad for widespread torture and killings. A trial of Assad and his brother Maher is underway in Damascus, though both are being tried in absentia as neither is in the country.

stories.title: Russia is building 168,000-strong drone force by year-end through stealing Kyiv UAV model, says Ukraine’s drone commander Madiar
stories.summary: Ukraine's drone commander Madiar reported that Russia is building a 168,000-strong drone force by year-end, partly by copying a Ukrainian UAV model. He said an average Ukrainian brigade now intercepts up to 60 Russian "Molniya" strike drones daily due to Russia's centralized production efforts.

stories.title: Michael Wegier: British Jews aren’t living in fear, but they’re certainly anxious
stories.summary: Michael Wegier, CEO of the Board of Deputies of British Jews, described the British Jewish community as anxious but resilient. He cited hostility toward Israel, violent antisemitism, and shifting national politics as sources of concern.

stories.title: Lithuania signs full Drone Deal, Latvia receives Ukrainian air defense experts
stories.summary: Lithuania signed a comprehensive drone deal with Ukraine covering joint production of long-range strike, naval, interceptor, and bomber drones, including technology transfer between Ukrainian and Lithuanian companies. Separately, Latvia is hosting Ukrainian air defense specialists under a proposed cooperation agreement.

stories.title: Switzerland to join agreement on Special Tribunal
stories.summary: Switzerland has notified the Council of Europe of its intention to join the Enlarged Partial Agreement enabling the Special Tribunal for the crime of aggression against Ukraine. The move adds another country to the international effort to establish accountability for the conflict.

stories.title: Israel to take legal action against 'New York Times' over claims of 'dog rape' of Palestinians
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar directed officials to prepare a defamation lawsuit against The New York Times over its reporting on allegations of abuse of Palestinian detainees, calling the claims deeply distorted.

stories.title: Ben-Gvir declares ownership of Temple Mount as activists clash in Jerusalem ahead of flag march
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir declared ownership over the Temple Mount in Jerusalem. Earlier on Thursday, Israeli activists from across the political spectrum clashed in the Old City ahead of the annual flag march.

stories.title: Why should the US-China meetings matter for the Middle East? Here are five reasons - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis examines five reasons why ongoing U.S.-China diplomatic meetings carry significant implications for the Middle East. Beijing has reportedly been cautious about involvement in regional conflicts while maintaining its interests in the area.

stories.title: ‘The world is sounding an alarm’: Why big tech is the new colonist
stories.summary: The article examines how major technology companies exert global power through finance, data control, and information infrastructure, drawing comparisons to historical colonialism rather than traditional military force.

stories.title: Ukraine UGV ‘Simba’ rolls out of the shadows in NATO Baltic exercise
stories.summary: Ukraine's unmanned ground vehicle known as Simba was demonstrated during a NATO exercise in the Baltic region. Video footage showed the UGV completing night missions despite losing a wheel and being struck by a first-person-view drone.

stories.title: Canadian officer accused of spying for China acquitted of charges
stories.summary: William Majcher, a retired Royal Canadian Mounted Police officer, was acquitted of national security charges in Canada. He had been accused in 2023 of breaching the Security of Information Act by allegedly helping Chinese police coerce a Vancouver-area real estate investor to return to China.

stories.title: Nobel winner Mukwege warns of predatory US deal for DR Congo
stories.summary: Nobel Peace Prize-winning Congolese doctor Denis Mukwege warned that a US-brokered peace deal for the Democratic Republic of Congo prioritizes resource extraction over security for the Congolese people.

stories.title: Prominent Australian academic denies links to powerful Iranian politician
stories.summary: Professor Abbas Rajabifard of the University of Melbourne denied collaborating on research with Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, the speaker of Iran's parliament and Tehran's lead negotiator in recent peace talks with the United States. Rajabifard said he was listed as a co-author on a journal article without his knowledge.

stories.title: Is China set to benefit from new US Fed chair Kevin Warsh’s policy vision?
stories.summary: The US Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh as the 17th Federal Reserve chair in a 54-45 vote, succeeding Jerome Powell. Analysts are debating whether potential policy compromises with the Trump administration could affect US financial credibility and benefit Chinese assets.

stories.title: Indian pharma fuels Africa's 'zombie drug' and opioid crisis despite crackdown
stories.summary: An AFP investigation found that Indian pharmaceutical firms are flooding West Africa with cheap, high-strength tapentadol tablets not approved by any regulatory authority. The pills are fueling an opioid crisis in the region and are reportedly being added to the street drug known as kush.

stories.title: Mandatory evacuation of children announced in two villages in Kherson region
stories.summary: Authorities in Ukraine's Kherson region announced a mandatory evacuation of children and their parents from the villages of Naddniprianske and Molodizhne. The decision followed a deteriorating security situation and an increase in Russian drone attacks.

stories.title: Tira resident accused of spying for Iran, refusing payment, urging missiles on hometown
stories.summary: Israeli prosecutors charged Ahmad Da'as, a resident of Tira, with spying for Iran. He allegedly provided an Iranian agent with information on a military base, Ashdod port, and a power station, reportedly acting out of ideological motivation without accepting payment.

stories.title: NYT defends op-ed on Palestinian abuse as Israel’s military readies new F-35 upgrade
stories.summary: The Jerusalem Post's daily news roundup covered the New York Times' defense of an op-ed on Palestinian abuse allegations and Israel's military preparing a new upgrade for its F-35 fighter jets.

stories.title: Ship anchored off east coast of UAE seized, heading toward Iranian waters
stories.summary: The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre reported that a ship anchored off the eastern coast of the UAE was seized by unauthorized personnel near the Strait of Hormuz and was heading toward Iranian waters.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia budget deficit doubles amid US-Israeli war on Iran
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's budget deficit doubled amid disruptions caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran. The widening deficit reflects increased war spending, export disruptions, and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz straining the kingdom's finances.

stories.title: Synthetic drugs from India fuelling West Africa's opioid epidemic
stories.summary: Indian pharmaceutical manufacturers are increasingly exporting synthetic opioids to West Africa, fueling a growing opioid epidemic in the region. The push into African markets comes as opioids face heavy regulation in wealthier countries.

stories.title: Zelensky’s former top aide remanded in corruption probe
stories.summary: A Ukrainian anti-corruption court ordered the arrest of Andriy Yermak, President Zelenskyy's former chief of staff, on money-laundering charges. Yermak, who served as Zelenskyy's top aide during most of Russia's invasion, was placed in pre-trial detention for 60 days. He had resigned from his position in November.

stories.title: Israel to sue New York Times for article describing its rape of Palestinians
stories.summary: Israel announced plans to file a defamation lawsuit against The New York Times over an article describing allegations of rape of Palestinians in Israeli detention. The newspaper had previously stood by its report featuring Palestinian testimonies.

stories.title: Syria foils attempted bombing of Orthodox cathedral in Aleppo
stories.summary: Syrian authorities foiled an attempted bombing at the St. Ephrem Orthodox Cathedral in Aleppo after discovering a suspected explosive device concealed inside a funeral truck entering the site.

stories.title: Netanyahu's boast of secret visit to UAE sparks awkward denial from Abu Dhabi
stories.summary: Israel and the UAE issued conflicting statements about a reported secret meeting between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed al-Nahyan. Iran's foreign minister subsequently accused the UAE of being directly involved in the war against Iran.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz calls for efforts to turn Pakistan into an 'economic power'
stories.summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif addressed Pakistan's federal cabinet in Islamabad, calling for efforts to transform the country into an economic power. He referenced Pakistan's May 28, 1998 nuclear tests, describing the nuclear capability as a defensive asset.

stories.title: Israel and Lebanon begin talks in Washington, say diplomats
stories.summary: Israeli and Lebanese envoys opened a new round of peace talks at the U.S. State Department in Washington on Thursday, as the latest ceasefire between the two countries was approaching its expiration date.

stories.title: At least 20 people missing in capital following Russian attack, says State Emergency Service
stories.summary: Ukraine's State Emergency Service reported that at least 20 people remain missing in Kyiv following a massive Russian attack on May 14. Search and rescue operations are ongoing in the capital.

stories.title: Tallal Chaudhry says Pakistan's ties with UAE 'absolutely fine'
stories.summary: Pakistan's Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry told the National Assembly that Pakistan's relationship with the UAE remains stable, responding to concerns about reported deportations of Pakistani workers from the Gulf state. The Interior Ministry has denied claims of large-scale expulsions.

stories.title: ISW: Russia’s grand territorial ambitions are divorced from battlefield reality
stories.summary: The Institute for the Study of War reported that Russian forces first entered Kostiantynivka in October 2025 but have achieved no significant tactical gains in six months. Kremlin spokesman Peskov reiterated Moscow's demand that Ukraine withdraw from four oblasts.

stories.title: If this were real life, they would already be dead: Ukrainian drone pilots force NATO drills on Gotland to stop three times
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone pilots participating in NATO exercises on Sweden's Gotland island forced drills to halt three times by demonstrating capabilities that would have been lethal in real combat. The pauses gave opposing forces time to reassess their tactics against drone threats.

stories.title: How stray Ukrainian drones pushed Latvia's prime minister to resign
stories.summary: Latvian Prime Minister Evika Silina resigned after a coalition partner withdrew support over her dismissal of Defense Minister Andris Spruds. Silina had blamed Spruds for inadequate deployment of anti-drone systems after Ukrainian drones repeatedly strayed into Latvian territory.

stories.title: Finland hosts large Israeli defense delegation for two-day seminar
stories.summary: Finland hosted a large Israeli defense delegation for a two-day seminar. The event follows similar defense seminars held recently in India, Miami, and other locations across Asia and Europe.

stories.title: Defense Business Brief: Tulsa’s space draw; Cadenazzi’s wish; Anduril’s $5B round
stories.summary: The article briefly notes developments including Tulsa's growing appeal for space industry investment, remarks from Cadenazzi, and Anduril Industries closing a $5 billion funding round. No further details were provided in the source text.

stories.title: Italian Visa Centers Ban Third-Party Submissions, Russian Tour Lobby Says
stories.summary: Italian visa centers have banned third-party submissions for visa applications from Russian applicants. The change reportedly followed the arrest of Italy's former ambassador in Uzbekistan over an alleged scheme involving illicit Schengen visa approvals.

stories.title: "Conflict" possible: Xi Jinping issues Taiwan warning during Donald Trump's visit
stories.summary: During President Donald Trump's visit to Beijing—the first by a U.S. leader in nearly a decade—Chinese President Xi Jinping warned that disagreements over Taiwan's future could lead to conflict. The two leaders also exchanged cordial greetings and emphasized bilateral ties alongside discussions on trade.

stories.title: How has Eurovision voting changed this year?
stories.summary: Eurovision Song Contest organizers announced changes to voting procedures and said they are closely monitoring voting patterns. The move follows concerns raised about Israel's potential influence on results at last year's contest.

stories.title: ‘It’s like stealing’: Palestinian family’s seized property listed on Booking.com
stories.summary: A Palestinian family's seized property in the hills south of Bethlehem in the occupied West Bank has been listed as a rental on Booking.com, described as ideal for outdoor gatherings. The listing is among 41 rental properties advertised in illegal Israeli settlements on the platform.

stories.title: Former Bryansk Region governor becomes a State Duma deputy — the day after resigning as governor.
stories.summary: Russia's Central Election Commission assigned former Bryansk Region Governor Alexander Bogomaz a vacant State Duma seat one day after his resignation as governor. The commission registered him as a deputy at its May 14 session.

stories.title: Israeli minister blasts Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal for Palestinian flag wave
stories.summary: An Israeli minister criticized FC Barcelona's Lamine Yamal, the Spanish international footballer, for waving a Palestinian flag during a bus parade celebrating Barcelona's La Liga title victory.

stories.title: Who is Mario Draghi, this year's Charlemagne Prize winner?
stories.summary: Former European Central Bank president and Italian ex-prime minister Mario Draghi was named the 2025 winner of the Charlemagne Prize, which honors contributions to European unity. Draghi is recognized as a key architect of European stability during economic crises.

stories.title: Mali's army carries out overnight strikes on rebel-held city of Kidal
stories.summary: Mali's military carried out overnight airstrikes on the rebel-held city of Kidal. An army officer said the strikes targeted specific objectives and warned that operations would intensify in the coming days.

stories.title: Attack on Indian-flagged ship off Oman coast ‘unacceptable’, says MEA; crew members safe
stories.summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs condemned an attack on an Indian-flagged ship off the coast of Oman as "unacceptable" and confirmed that all crew members are safe. The ministry did not identify who carried out the attack.

stories.title: Why did Saudi Arabia and the UAE allegedly carry out secret bombing raids on Iran?
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal and Reuters reported that Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates secretly carried out airstrikes against Iran in April during the broader U.S.-Israeli conflict with Tehran. Analysts described the alleged raids as clandestine retaliation for Iranian drone and missile strikes on Gulf state infrastructure. Neither country has confirmed the operations.

stories.title: China’s view on Elon Musk? Visionary, occasional villain
stories.summary: Tesla's self-driving technology continues to be regarded as the industry standard in China, where Elon Musk is viewed as both a visionary innovator and an occasional controversial figure.

stories.title: Inside the rising wave of anti-Christian violence in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Palestinian church leaders in Jerusalem are warning about escalating Israeli violence against Christian communities in the city. The incidents are raising concerns about the future of one of the world's oldest Christian populations.

stories.title: Russian strike on Kyiv: About 40 people injured, death toll climbs to five, including child
stories.summary: A massive Russian strike on Kyiv killed at least five people, including a child, and injured approximately 40 others. More than 10 people were reported missing following the attack.

stories.title: Saudi investment fund seals FIFA deal as official World Cup 2026 supporter
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund signed a deal with FIFA to become an official supporter of the 2026 World Cup, co-hosted by the United States, Canada, and Mexico. Saudi Arabia is also set to host the 2034 World Cup.

stories.title: Israeli settlers storm Al-Aqsa compound ahead of 'Flag Day'
stories.summary: Israeli settlers, accompanied by a Knesset member and protected by police, stormed the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound in Jerusalem as part of annual Flag Day celebrations.

stories.title: Ship said seized, diverted to Iran, another sunk, in latest Strait of Hormuz actions
stories.summary: A vessel anchored off the UAE coast was reportedly seized and diverted to Iran, according to a British navy monitor. Separately, a cargo ship carrying livestock was sunk off Oman, with 114 crew members rescued. India condemned the sinking.

stories.title: The toast, the tastes and the tech selfie that crowned the US-China summit
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted US President Donald Trump for a state banquet at Beijing's Great Hall of the People, capping a summit Trump described as "fantastic." It was Trump's first presidential visit to Beijing in nearly nine years.

stories.title: UAE defense giant EDGE to acquire ‘controlling’ stake in Italian engine maker
stories.summary: UAE defense conglomerate EDGE Group announced plans to acquire a controlling stake in Italian engine manufacturer CMD. EDGE CEO Hamad Al Marar said the acquisition would help build a European propulsion hub to complement the company's global industrial footprint.

stories.title: South Africa: Ramaphosa Fires Disgraced Social Development Minister Sisisi Tolashe
stories.summary: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa fired Social Development Minister Sisisi Tolashe and appointed Sindisiwe Chikunga, Minister for Women, Youth and Persons with Disabilities, as acting minister pending a permanent replacement.

stories.title: Ethiopia: New Tensions in Tigray Region of Ethiopia
stories.summary: Tigray regional president and TPLF leader Debretsion Gebremichael addressed a deteriorating security situation in Ethiopia's Tigray region, stating that protecting the security and safety of the population is the administration's top priority.

stories.title: What is Euro-Med, the Hamas-linked organization relied upon for sexual abuse claims in NYT column?
stories.summary: A New York Times column cited allegations of sexual abuse of Palestinian prisoners by Israeli security forces, relying in part on information from Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor. Questions have been raised about the organization's alleged links to Hamas.

stories.title: Xi warns Trump about ‘extremely dangerous’ risks if Taiwan issue mishandled
stories.summary: During the Beijing summit, Chinese President Xi Jinping warned US President Donald Trump that mishandling the Taiwan issue could lead to conflict and an "extremely dangerous situation." Analysts noted Xi's tone on Taiwan was tougher than during their 2017 summit.

stories.title: The dark side of Nigeria's crypto craze: Hope, scam and money laundering
stories.summary: Cryptocurrency has become widely adopted in Nigeria amid high inflation and the collapse of the naira, with many Nigerians using it to save, trade, and transfer money outside traditional banks. However, the growing crypto economy has also fueled scams, fraud, market manipulation, and money laundering, prompting authorities to take action.

stories.title: Resigned Russian regional governor posts video address. He thanked Putin and wished everyone ‘the most important thing — Victory’
stories.summary: Former Belgorod Region Governor Vyacheslav Gladkov posted a video address on Telegram on May 14 following his resignation. In the message, he thanked President Putin and wished everyone victory.

stories.title: Netanyahu's boast of secret visit to UAE sparks awkward denial from Abu Dhabi
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office disclosed he made a secret visit to the UAE and met with President Mohammed bin Zayed. Abu Dhabi issued an awkward denial, though the revelation suggests deepening ties amid the conflict with Iran.

stories.title: China's view on Elon Musk? Visionary, occasional villain
stories.summary: In China, Tesla CEO Elon Musk is viewed as both a visionary entrepreneur and a controversial figure. Chinese regulators and the public have criticized Tesla's handling of customer complaints, while the People's Liberation Army has expressed concern over SpaceX's Starlink satellite dominance. Musk accompanied President Trump to Beijing for the summit with Xi Jinping.

stories.title: Fast & Furious marks 25th anniversary with emotional premiere in Cannes
stories.summary: The Fast & Furious franchise celebrated its 25th anniversary with a special midnight screening at the Cannes Film Festival. Star Vin Diesel and cast members attended the premiere marking the original film's release in 2000.

stories.title: Africa forward summit: Africa’s space race takes off {Business Africa}
stories.summary: At the Africa Forward Summit, SkyConnect presented plans to convert idle ground stations across Africa into a shared satellite data network to reduce costs. Separately, Mauritius showcased its strategy to attract African talent and counter brain drain.

stories.title: Steadicopter unveils Golden Eagle 'mothership' for complex missions
stories.summary: Israeli company Steadicopter unveiled the Golden Eagle unmanned aerial system designed to serve as a 'mothership' platform. The system is intended for complex missions in environments with heavy air defenses and electronic-warfare activity.

stories.title: Hezbollah drone threat is serious, but blown out of proportion, IDF tells ToI in Lebanon
stories.summary: IDF Givati Brigade officers in Khiam, southern Lebanon, described the Hezbollah drone threat as serious but overstated. They showed journalists a Hezbollah tunnel discovered deep beneath a children's clothing charity in the area.

stories.title: Substation and high-voltage power line damaged in the capital due to Russian attack
stories.summary: A substation and a high-voltage power line in Kyiv were damaged during a massive Russian attack. The strike targeted the Ukrainian capital's power infrastructure.

stories.title: Heavy Russian strikes on Kyiv kill one, wound 31; Ukraine ties attack to Trump-Xi summit
stories.summary: Russia launched over 670 attack drones and 56 missiles targeting Kyiv, killing at least one person and wounding 31. President Zelenskyy linked the timing of the attack to the ongoing Trump-Xi summit in Beijing.

stories.title: Iraq sought financial assistance from IMF as result of Iran war, says report
stories.summary: Iraqi officials approached the International Monetary Fund for financial assistance due to the economic impact of the Iran war. Initial discussions took place during the IMF and World Bank spring meetings in Washington, with negotiations ongoing over the size and structure of potential funding.

stories.title: Israel to extend F-35I range amid war with Iran
stories.summary: Israeli defense firm Elbit Systems received a development contract worth approximately $34 million to extend the range of Israel's F-35I fighter jets. The effort comes amid Israel's ongoing military conflict with Iran.

stories.title: BRICS meeting overshadowed by war on Iran
stories.summary: A BRICS gathering was overshadowed by the ongoing conflict involving Iran, though specific details of the meeting's agenda and participants were not elaborated in the report.

stories.title: 2,000-year-old coin with earliest menorah image returned to Israel after US seizure
stories.summary: A 2,000-year-old coin bearing the earliest known menorah image was returned to Israel following a US seizure operation. A rare 2,500-year-old silver coin was also recovered, with officials emphasizing international cooperation against antiquities looting.

stories.title: Vessel seized off UAE and heading toward Iranian waters: UKMTO
stories.summary: The UK Maritime Trade Operations office reported that a vessel near the UAE port of Fujairah was boarded by unauthorized personnel and redirected toward Iranian waters.

stories.title: Ukraine: Volodymyr Zelensy's former top aide arrested as corruption probe widens
stories.summary: Former Ukrainian presidential chief of staff Andriy Yermak was arrested on charges of laundering nearly 9 million euros. A Kyiv judge ordered pre-trial detention on Thursday as part of a widening corruption probe that has deepened political tensions during the ongoing war.

stories.title: Iran still waiting for US visas less than a month before World Cup
stories.summary: Iran's national football team held a farewell ceremony in Tehran ahead of the World Cup, but U.S. visas for the squad had still not been issued with less than a month before the tournament begins.

stories.title: 3 civilians hurt in Hezbollah attack on north as Israel, Lebanon set for 3rd round of talks
stories.summary: Three Israeli civilians were injured in a Hezbollah drone attack on northern Israel, with two seriously wounded. The IDF struck several towns in Lebanon after issuing warnings. Israel and Lebanon are preparing for a third round of talks on disarmament and long-term relations.

stories.title: 'Floating armoury' ship reportedly seized by Iran
stories.summary: Iranian military personnel seized a vessel described as a 'floating armoury' in the Gulf of Oman, according to reports. The ship's exact origin and cargo details have not been fully confirmed.

stories.title: Anatomy of a speech: how does a Republican leader say no to Trump?
stories.summary: South Carolina's Republican state senate majority leader publicly opposed President Trump's congressional redistricting demands. The speech offered a case study in how Republican officials navigate disagreement with the president while avoiding political backlash.

stories.title: Xi-Trump diplomacy: Beijing envisions 4 pillars of 'stability', warns US over Taiwan 'interference'
stories.summary: During President Trump's state visit to Beijing, China outlined four pillars of "stability" for U.S.-China relations while warning against American "interference" in Taiwan. Trump is the first U.S. president to visit Beijing in nearly a decade.

stories.title: Russian drone attack hits Kyiv apartment block during ceasefire
stories.summary: A Russian drone strike hit and collapsed a residential apartment building in Kyiv during what was supposed to be a ceasefire period in the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: BRICS Foreign Ministers meet in India as Iran war, oil prices, internal divisions test bloc’s unity
stories.summary: BRICS foreign ministers convened in India for discussions amid tensions over the Iran war, fluctuating oil prices, and internal disagreements. The meeting included diplomats from founding members Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa, as well as newer member states.

stories.title: Voloshyn: Enemies deploy new forces and employ wave-based assault tactics in Huliaipole sector
stories.summary: Ukrainian military spokesperson Voloshyn reported that Russian troops are rotating units and deploying new formations using wave-based assault tactics in the Huliaipole sector of the Zaporizhzhia front. Ukrainian forces have been holding back the enemy advance despite the reinforced Russian assaults.

stories.title: Lebanese split over diplomatic normalisation amid Washington talks
stories.summary: Lebanese opinion remains deeply divided over diplomatic normalization with Israel as unprecedented U.S.-mediated negotiations began in Washington. While many Lebanese see the talks as an opportunity for stability, Hezbollah and its supporters firmly reject any normalization with Israel.

stories.title: Cuba says oil reserves have 'run out' as blackouts, fuel shortages spark protests
stories.summary: Cuba's energy minister said Russian oil reserves sent to the island have "run out" amid a tightened U.S. fuel embargo, worsening power blackouts across the country. Dozens of Cubans protested outside Havana on Wednesday night over the crippling blackouts and fuel shortages.

stories.title: Mysterious ancient tunnel, possibly thousands of years old, discovered in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Archaeologists in Jerusalem discovered a mysterious ancient tunnel that may be thousands of years old. The structure's exact date and purpose remain unclear, though researchers say its construction would have required significant resources.

stories.title: On Nakba Day, Israel to approve army museum on ruins of UNRWA HQ
stories.summary: The Israeli government is expected to approve plans for an army museum on the site of the former UNRWA headquarters on May 17, a date marked by Israelis as Jerusalem Day and by Palestinians as Nakba Day.

stories.title: Medical blunder probe opened over death linked to improperly sealed catheter
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Hospital Authority opened an investigation into a suspected medical error involving an improperly sealed catheter used during heart surgery on a 75-year-old man who subsequently died at Tuen Mun Hospital.

stories.title: Israel closes Al-Aqsa for Muslims amid mass settler raids and ‘Flag March’
stories.summary: Israeli forces blocked Palestinian Muslims from entering Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem on Thursday, while facilitating large-scale incursions by ultranationalist settlers ahead of the annual Flag March through the Old City. The occupied East Jerusalem area was placed under near-total lockdown.

stories.title: Paediatrician in Germany charged with 130 counts of sexual abuse
stories.summary: German prosecutors in Brandenburg state charged a 46-year-old paediatrician with 130 counts of sexual abuse, including child rape, allegedly committed between 2013 and 2025. The doctor, who worked in clinics near Berlin, has been in custody since November after a mother reported suspected assault of her child.

stories.title: Iran war tests India's multi-alignment diplomacy
stories.summary: India's multi-alignment diplomatic strategy, which balances ties with rival Middle Eastern nations, is being tested by the Iran conflict. Analysts suggest New Delhi's carefully maintained neutrality may be reaching a breaking point.

stories.title: Peace activists rally to protect Palestinians during Jerusalem flag march
stories.summary: Israeli peace activists gathered in Jerusalem on Thursday to support Palestinian residents ahead of the annual Jerusalem Day flag march, an event frequently accompanied by nationalist tensions and heavy security presence.

stories.title: What is on the table during Lebanon-Israel direct negotiations?
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon are scheduled to meet for a third round of negotiations this year, with discussions expected to focus on a ceasefire agreement and the disarmament of Hezbollah.

stories.title: Second Japan-linked oil tanker sails via Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: A second Japan-linked oil tanker transited the Strait of Hormuz after Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi held direct talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian to negotiate safe passage through the waterway.

stories.title: Greek-Israeli relations are 'flourishing,' Israel's deputy foreign minister tells 'Post'
stories.summary: Israel's Deputy Foreign Minister Sharren Haskel described Greek-Israeli relations as flourishing during remarks to The Jerusalem Post. Haskel spoke at the Maritime Med conference and the East Med Energy Transition Summit.

stories.title: Latvian prime minister resigns amid row over drone incursions
stories.summary: Latvian Prime Minister Evika Siliņa resigned after her coalition collapsed over the handling of Ukrainian drones that strayed into Latvian territory from Russia. The crisis was triggered by her firing of Defence Minister Andris Sprūds, which led the Progressives party to withdraw from the coalition ahead of October elections.

stories.title: Iran says ships entering strait of Hormuz must cooperate after vessel seized
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that ships entering the Strait of Hormuz must cooperate with the Iranian navy. The declaration came as a vessel was reportedly seized by unauthorized personnel near the UAE port of Fujairah and directed toward Iranian waters.

stories.title: How did the US and China tell 2 different stories about the summit?
stories.summary: Post-summit statements from the U.S. and China revealed divergent priorities following talks between Presidents Trump and Xi Jinping in Beijing. Washington emphasized trade, fentanyl, and Iran, while Beijing highlighted Taiwan, stabilizing bilateral ties, and Trump's compliments about Xi. The visit marked the first U.S. presidential trip to China in nine years.

stories.title: Latvian prime minister resigns after drone incident
stories.summary: Latvian Prime Minister Evika Silina resigned following a series of incidents involving stray drones over Latvian territory that were suspected to have originated from Ukraine.

stories.title: Canada weighs buying Turkish drones it sanctioned in 2019
stories.summary: Canada is considering purchasing Turkish-made Baykar drones despite having sanctioned Turkish defense exports in 2019. The shift reflects broader defense procurement changes as Canadian Prime Minister Carney prepares for an October visit to Turkey.

stories.title: Russia Is Building ‘Pragmatic’ Partnership With Taliban Government, Shoigu Says
stories.summary: Russian Security Council Secretary Nikolai Shoigu stated that Russia is building a 'pragmatic' partnership with the Taliban government in Afghanistan. Russia was the first country to recognize the Taliban-led Islamic Emirate last July after removing the group from its terrorist list.

stories.title: Russians intensify assaults in Orikhiv sector, says Voloshyn
stories.summary: Ukrainian military spokesperson Voloshyn reported that Russian troops have intensified assault operations in the Orikhiv sector and are attempting to advance toward the city of Zaporizhzhia.

stories.title: 'Every time I'm in the forest, I'm like a little kid': Photographer Thomas Nicolon
stories.summary: Photographer Thomas Nicolon published "Kongo," a book of photographs spanning six countries in the Congo Basin and its nearly 4-million-square-kilometre tropical rainforest. The former FRANCE 24 Kinshasa correspondent described his deep personal connection to the region's forests.

stories.title: Flattery and fanfare as Trump welcomed to China - but thorny issues remain
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump was welcomed to Beijing with ceremony and public displays of cordiality from Chinese leaders. Despite the warm reception, significant unresolved issues remain between the two superpowers.

stories.title: Duststorms and lightning kill at least 96 people in northern India
stories.summary: Dust storms and lightning strikes killed at least 96 people across northern India. Such storms are common in the region from March to June, preceding the annual monsoon season.

stories.title: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire nears end: Will fresh talks lead to new truce?
stories.summary: Israel's ruling Likud party submitted a proposal to dissolve parliament, potentially leading to early elections as soon as August amid coalition instability. Separately, as the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire nears expiration, fresh negotiations are taking place in Washington.

stories.title: Russia strikes Kramatorsk daily. The city is putting its monuments out of harm’s way
stories.summary: The city of Kramatorsk in Ukraine's Donetsk Oblast has been subjected to daily Russian strikes. Authorities dismantled monuments to prominent Ukrainians and sculptures, shipping them outside the region for safekeeping.

stories.title: UK health minister quits, calls for leadership contest to oust PM Starmer
stories.summary: UK Health Minister Wes Streeting resigned and called for a leadership contest to oust Prime Minister Keir Starmer following Labour's disastrous results in local elections. The crisis emerged less than two years after Starmer won a large parliamentary majority on promises of political stability.

stories.title: Kenya: Explainer - What the 2026 PBO Regulations Mean for NGOs and Civil Society in Kenya
stories.summary: Kenya has rolled out new Public Benefit Organizations Regulations under the PBO Act of 2013, marking a significant legal shift for NGOs and civil society. The regulations establish a new operational framework for the country's nonprofit sector.

stories.title: Beirut accuses Tehran of violating Vienna Convention in complaint to UN
stories.summary: Beirut accused Tehran of violating the Vienna Convention in a complaint filed with the United Nations. Analysts warned that the UN's enforcement capability is limited and that Iran's allies may become involved.

stories.title: 'What happened to me is proof that Hong Kong is no longer Hong Kong': Antoine Védeilhé
stories.summary: Award-winning documentary filmmaker Antoine Védeilhé was detained and expelled by Hong Kong authorities upon arrival at the airport. Védeilhé, who had been covering Hong Kong for years, was attempting to make a documentary about life under Chinese rule and said his expulsion proves the city has fundamentally changed.

stories.title: Let Them Genocide: How we all paid for Israel’s impunity
stories.summary: An opinion piece by Elrayes and Alaqad argues that the international community has allowed Israel to act with impunity since the 1948 Nakba, enabling it to reshape the Middle East through military force.

stories.title: Klymenko: 10 people missing following Russia's strike on Kyiv
stories.summary: Ukrainian officials reported that more than 10 people remain missing in Kyiv following a massive Russian attack on May 14.

stories.title: Israeli attack injures three people in Lebanon’s Kfer Melki
stories.summary: An Israeli strike on the southern Lebanese town of Kfer Melki injured at least three people, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Separate Israeli attacks also targeted the villages of Sinai in Nabatieh and al-Qusaibah.

stories.title: India condemns attack on ship off Oman, vessel reported sunk
stories.summary: An Indian-flagged vessel reportedly sank off the coast of Oman following a suspected drone or missile strike. India's government condemned the attack and called for an end to continued threats against commercial shipping in the region.

stories.title: China’s Xi warns Trump about Taiwan at Beijing summit
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping warned U.S. President Donald Trump during a summit in Beijing that disagreements over Taiwan could push bilateral relations down a dangerous path.

stories.title: From poachers to refuge: The world's only bonobo orphanage is hidden in DR Congo
stories.summary: A sanctuary on the outskirts of Kinshasa in the Democratic Republic of Congo serves as the world's only orphanage for bonobos. The facility rescues baby bonobos from poachers or from locals who keep them captive, providing care in a forested refuge.

stories.title: How Sudanese children are going back to school in a refugee camp after years of war
stories.summary: In the southern Libyan city of Kufra, authorities in eastern Libya have established schooling programs for Sudanese refugee children who fled the war that erupted in 2023. The city hosts between 40,000 and 60,000 Sudanese refugees, many of them children who had their education interrupted by the conflict.

stories.title: Israeli MP calls for Al-Aqsa’s destruction to build Jewish temple during mass raid
stories.summary: An Israeli lawmaker, Yitzhak Kroizer, called for the destruction of Al-Aqsa Mosque to build a Jewish temple during a large settler incursion into the Jerusalem holy site. Ministers including Itamar Ben Gvir led the raid ahead of the provocative Flag March, while Israeli forces restricted Palestinian access.

stories.title: Salmon farm faces new cruelty claims as Trump seeks to supersize fish farming
stories.summary: New undercover video allegedly shows cruel treatment of salmon at a Cooke hatchery in the United States. The footage emerged as the Trump administration pushes to expand industrial-scale fish farming to boost U.S. seafood production.

stories.title: Chinese foundries SMIC, Hua Hong forecast second-quarter growth amid AI boom
stories.summary: Chinese semiconductor foundries SMIC and Hua Hong projected second-quarter revenue growth driven by surging AI demand and a memory supply crunch. SMIC forecast Q2 revenue between $2.86 billion and $2.91 billion, up from $2.51 billion. Hua Hong expressed hope that the Xi-Trump meetings could help ease U.S. export controls.

stories.title: Salute to China? Protocol-perfect Trump delights social media as he arrives to meet Xi
stories.summary: Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping projected a close personal rapport during their meeting at Beijing's Great Hall of the People. Observers focused on both the substance of the high-stakes talks and the personal dynamics between the leaders of the world's two largest economies.

stories.title: First Thing: Xi warns Trump of ‘clashes and even conflicts’ with US over Taiwan
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping warned President Trump of potential "clashes and even conflicts" between the U.S. and China over Taiwan during their two-hour meeting at Beijing's Great Hall of the People. The leaders also discussed the Middle East conflict, the Ukraine war, and Korean peninsula issues.

stories.title: Somalia: How the Iran War Could Derail Somalia's Fragile Recovery
stories.summary: An analysis by the Institute for Security Studies warns that the Iran war could derail Somalia's fragile recovery. The report argues that Somalia faces risks beyond spillover effects, with broader shocks pushing the country's long-term recovery further out of reach.

stories.title: Israel increasing use of solitary confinement for Palestinians, including for minors
stories.summary: Data published by Physicians for Human Rights shows a significant increase in Israeli use of solitary confinement for Palestinian prisoners, including minors, since the Gaza conflict began. The number of minors placed in solitary confinement rose from one in 2022 to 50 in 2023.

stories.title: Invaders hit Zaporizhzhia, damaging industrial infrastructure
stories.summary: Russian forces struck Zaporizhzhia, causing damage to industrial infrastructure in the city.

stories.title: BRICS foreign ministers meet in India amid differences over Iran war
stories.summary: BRICS foreign ministers convened in India amid internal disagreements over the Iran conflict. Iran's foreign minister called on member states to condemn what he described as unlawful aggression by the United States and Israel against Tehran.

stories.title: South Africa: Western Cape Storm Death Toll Rises to 10
stories.summary: The death toll from severe storms in South Africa's Western Cape province has risen to 10. The provincial government says emergency response and recovery operations remain at a critical stage despite improved weather conditions.

stories.title: US court suspends sanctions on UN expert on Palestinians
stories.summary: A U.S. court suspended sanctions imposed on a United Nations expert on Palestinian affairs. The expert had been sanctioned in July 2025 after publicly criticizing Washington's policy on Gaza.

stories.title: M23 rebels withdraw from several positions under US diplomatic pressure
stories.summary: In eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, AFC/M23 rebels, who are backed by Rwanda, have withdrawn from several positions following US diplomatic pressure. The Congolese army has moved to reassert control over the vacated areas, marking the most significant ground-level shift in months.

stories.title: HRCP 'deeply alarmed' at continued captivity of seafarers onboard tanker seized by Somali pirates
stories.summary: The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan expressed alarm over the continued captivity of Pakistani crew members aboard the MT Honour 25, a Palau-flagged tanker seized by Somali pirates on April 21 off Somalia's Puntland region. Ten of the 17 crew members are Pakistani.

stories.title: Philippine senator wanted by ICC flees from Senate
stories.summary: Philippine Senator Ronald dela Rosa, wanted by the International Criminal Court for alleged crimes against humanity, escaped from the Senate where he had taken refuge. His departure followed an exchange of gunfire between Senate security and a government agent on Wednesday night that caused chaos in the building.

stories.title: Nakba to Gaza: Why Palestinians still carry keys to lost homes
stories.summary: Palestinians in Gaza continue to carry keys from homes destroyed during the ongoing conflict with Israel, connecting current displacement to the historical legacy of the 1948 Nakba.

stories.title: Ghana evacuates 300 citizens caught in xenophobic acts in South Africa
stories.summary: Ghana has begun evacuating approximately 300 of its citizens from South Africa after a wave of xenophobic attacks targeting migrants from sub-Saharan African countries. The evacuations were reported by FRANCE 24's correspondent in Accra.

stories.title: Rights group says M23, Rwandan army committed killings, rapes in Congo’s Uvira
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch or a similar rights organization reported that the M23 rebel group and Rwandan army forces committed killings and rapes in the city of Uvira in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

stories.title: Pakistan has a supreme court. Then it built a supremacist one.
stories.summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court, led by Chief Justice Yahya Afridi, issued a ruling declaring that it and the newly created Federal Constitutional Court are coordinate apex courts with no hierarchy between them. The dispute stems from the 27th Constitutional Amendment, which established the Federal Constitutional Court.

stories.title: Namibia: MPs Urge End to Dry Rural Taps
stories.summary: Members of Namibia's National Council criticized the government's water supply budget, saying many rural communities continue to face severe shortages. MPs called for an end to dry taps in rural areas despite repeated promises and funding allocations.

stories.title: Trump and Xi hail ‘most important’ relationship
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump characterized the U.S.-China relationship as one of the most consequential during discussions with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

stories.title: Israel increasing use of solitary confinement for Palestinians, including for minors
stories.summary: Data from Israel's Prison Service shows a marked increase in the use of solitary confinement for Palestinian detainees, including minors and women. The detainees are being held in facilities such as Kziot prison in Israel's Negev desert.

stories.title: Under shadow of Gaza war, Fatah kicks off eighth conference
stories.summary: The Palestinian political movement Fatah opened its eighth general conference, expected to continue through Sunday. Approximately 2,500 members, senior Palestinian officials, and foreign diplomats are attending.

stories.title: Republicans’ plan for zero state income tax could be ‘devastating’, experts warn
stories.summary: Missouri Republicans are proposing to eliminate the state's income tax, but experts warn the plan could be devastating to public services. Critics point to the failed "Kansas Experiment" of the 2010s, when similar tax cuts led to a $900 million budget shortfall and school closures.

stories.title: Xi-Trump summit: Ford-CATL battery plant shows how global carmakers need China’s prowess
stories.summary: A Ford Motor EV battery plant in Michigan, built with technology from China's CATL at a cost of $3 billion, has highlighted global automakers' reliance on Chinese battery expertise. The facility, capable of producing batteries for over 400,000 EVs annually, drew attention during the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing.

stories.title: Trump’s visit to China: Xi may get the better of Trump, fear Americans
stories.summary: American observers expressed concern that Chinese President Xi Jinping may gain the upper hand in summit negotiations with U.S. President Trump in Beijing. Trump's approach to China has frequently put him at odds with members of his own administration.

stories.title: FC Barcelona distances itself from star’s Palestinian flag-waving, amid Israeli anger
stories.summary: FC Barcelona distanced itself from forward Lamine Yamal's display of a Palestinian flag, calling the act spontaneous and not sanctioned by the club. Israel's defense minister accused the player of inciting against Israel.

stories.title: Ship seized off UAE's Fujairah being pulled toward Iranian waters
stories.summary: A ship was seized off the UAE's Fujairah and is being directed toward Iranian waters. Separately, India confirmed that an Indian-flagged ship was attacked off Oman's coast on Wednesday with all crew safe.

stories.title: Vyacheslav Gladkov resigns as governor of Russia’s Belgorod region
stories.summary: The Kremlin announced that Vyacheslav Gladkov resigned as governor of Russia's Belgorod region, with President Putin accepting the resignation. Putin appointed Alexander Shuvaev, a 45-year-old deputy governor of Irkutsk region and veteran of Russia's war in Ukraine, as acting regional head.

stories.title: China’s economic strengths now rival that of the U.S.
stories.summary: Beijing's economic influence continues to grow, with China now rivaling the United States in economic strength and emerging as a significant diplomatic power on the global stage.

stories.title: In Kyiv, death toll from Russia's massive attack climbs to three, with 40 injured
stories.summary: The death toll from Russia's large-scale attack on Kyiv on May 14 rose to three, with 40 people reported injured, according to Ukrainian officials.

stories.title: Iran says UAE 'directly involved' in war
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi accused the United Arab Emirates of direct involvement in military operations against Iran during a BRICS meeting in New Delhi. He stated the UAE failed to even condemn the attacks when they began.

stories.title: Explosive drone hits Rosh Hanikra, leaving two seriously injured
stories.summary: An explosive drone struck Rosh Hanikra near the Israel-Lebanon border, seriously injuring two people who were evacuated to Galilee Medical Center in Nahariya for treatment.

stories.title: Free live webinar: Be a part of Jerusalem’s future for only 15% down - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A real estate project called The Duet is being marketed to prospective buyers in Jerusalem, with a webinar offering details on purchasing, financing, and the development's vision for a new Modern Orthodox community.

stories.title: PM tells court he’s at ‘top of health scale,’ says now-treated cancer diagnosed late 2025
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu testified in court that he is in the top 10th percentile for health and disclosed that his prostate cancer was diagnosed in late 2025 and has since been treated. The testimony came during a defamation lawsuit against journalists who claimed he had pancreatic cancer.

stories.title: Five Pakistani soldiers killed during operation against terrorists in Balochistan
stories.summary: Five Pakistani soldiers, including a field officer, were killed during a military operation against militants in Balochistan. The Inter-Services Public Relations reported that seven militants were also eliminated during the engagement.

stories.title: BBC at the scene of Russian strikes in Kyiv
stories.summary: Russia launched one of its largest air strikes on Kyiv since the start of the full-scale war. Several apartment blocks in the Ukrainian capital were hit, with BBC journalists reporting from the scene.

stories.title: China, U.S. should be ‘partners not rivals’, says Xi Jinping after meeting Donald Trump
stories.summary: At the Beijing summit, Chinese President Xi Jinping told U.S. President Donald Trump that the two countries should be "partners not rivals." Trump reciprocated warmly, calling it an honor to be Xi's friend and predicting improved bilateral relations.

stories.title: Former Nigerian minister sentenced to 75 years in rare corruption verdict
stories.summary: A Nigerian court sentenced former Power Minister Saleh Mamman to 75 years in prison in a rare corruption conviction. However, authorities have stated they do not know his current whereabouts.

stories.title: US Army says body of second soldier recovered in Morocco
stories.summary: The U.S. Army announced the recovery of the body of a second American service member who went missing during a training exercise near a cliff at Cap Draa, Morocco.

stories.title: All guns blazing: The UK sets up $1.35 billion RCH 155 artillery order
stories.summary: The United Kingdom is moving forward with an order for RCH 155 artillery systems valued at $1.35 billion. The procurement had been delayed pending the release of the Defence Investment Plan, which will outline British military equipment priorities for the next decade.

stories.title: Hungary Summons Russian Ambassador After Drone Attacks on Western Ukraine
stories.summary: Hungary summoned the Russian ambassador following drone attacks on western Ukraine's Zakarpattia region. Ukrainian authorities described the strikes as the most intense Russian aerial assault on the area since the 2022 invasion.

stories.title: Former Indian army chief backs RSS leader's call for engaging in dialogue with Pakistan
stories.summary: Former Indian Army Chief Gen. Manoj Naravane expressed support for RSS Secretary General Dattatreya Hosabale's call to maintain a dialogue window between India and Pakistan. Hosabale emphasized the importance of people-to-people contacts in breaking the diplomatic deadlock between New Delhi and Islamabad.

stories.title: Ukrenergo: Power outages in Kyiv and 11 regions due to massive attack
stories.summary: A sustained Russian attack beginning May 13 caused power outages affecting residents in Kyiv and eleven other Ukrainian regions, according to national grid operator Ukrenergo.

stories.title: India bars sugar exports until September
stories.summary: India banned sugar exports effective immediately through September 30 to ensure adequate domestic supplies and control prices. Limited exceptions were made for shipments already in transit and government-to-government food security agreements.

stories.title: Record complaints filed over UK press smear of anti-genocide artist Misan Harriman
stories.summary: A record number of complaints were filed with UK press regulators over media coverage of artist Misan Harriman, the Southbank Centre chair. Reports allegedly misrepresented his remarks related to the Golders Green attack.

stories.title: US House discharge petition reaches 218 signatures, forcing vote on Ukraine aid, bypassing Speaker Johnson
stories.summary: A discharge petition in the U.S. House of Representatives reached the required 218 signatures, forcing a floor vote on a Ukraine aid bill and bypassing Speaker Mike Johnson. The legislation authorizes $1.3 billion in military assistance and up to $8 billion in direct loans.

stories.title: What we know about Netanyahu's 'secret trip' to the UAE
stories.summary: Israel and the UAE have issued conflicting accounts regarding an alleged secret visit by Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu to the Gulf state. The circumstances and details of the purported trip remain disputed.

stories.title: Japan fires first-ever missiles from Philippine soil
stories.summary: Japan conducted its first-ever missile launch from Philippine territory, firing a Type 88 anti-ship missile. The missile struck a decommissioned WWII-era minesweeper approximately 47 miles away after a six-minute flight.

stories.title: Eurovision: The song contest that broke the continent
stories.summary: Protests took place in Vienna over Israel's continued participation in the Eurovision Song Contest while Russia remains banned. Organisers have not provided a clear explanation for the differing treatment of the two countries.

stories.title: Two killed as Israel ramps up southern Lebanon attacks ahead of US talks
stories.summary: Two people were killed as Israel intensified military strikes in southern Lebanon ahead of expected ceasefire extension talks with Lebanon in Washington.

stories.title: Israeli military, defense firms race to find solution to FPV drone threats
stories.summary: Israeli military and defense companies are developing technologies to counter first-person-view drone threats on the battlefield. Smaller Israeli firms are proposing solutions including smart rifles and counter-drone drones to address the growing tactical challenge.

stories.title: K2, firm tied to US-Israel, is overseeing Arab central banks
stories.summary: K2 Integrity, a firm with reported ties to the U.S. Treasury and Israeli intelligence, is expanding operations across the Middle East and North Africa. The company is overseeing aspects of central banking systems in Iraq, Lebanon, and Libya.

stories.title: Lebanon to press Israel for ceasefire at Washington talks, Lebanese official says
stories.summary: A senior Lebanese official said Lebanon would demand a ceasefire with Israel during face-to-face talks in Washington on Thursday. The meeting marked the third round of discussions since hostilities between Hezbollah and Israel resumed on March 2, with Hezbollah opposing Beirut's attendance.

stories.title: US Army says body of second missing soldier recovered in Morocco
stories.summary: The U.S. Army announced the recovery of the remains of a second soldier who went missing in Morocco. The remains of both soldiers were loaded onto a U.S. Air Force C-130 aircraft for repatriation to the United States.

stories.title: Zimbabweans lured into Russia’s war as families plead for their return
stories.summary: Zimbabwean nationals have been recruited to fight for Russia on the front lines in Ukraine. Their families are appealing to both the Zimbabwean and Russian governments to secure their return.

stories.title: Italy’s visa centers in Russia stop accepting applications through third parties — following a case involving illegal Schengen visa issuance to Russians in Tashkent
stories.summary: Italy's visa centers in Russia, operated by VMS and AlmavivA, stopped accepting visa applications submitted through third parties as of May 12. The change followed a case involving illegal Schengen visa issuance to Russian nationals in Tashkent.

stories.title: Mamdani urges New York state to block Western Union deal
stories.summary: A political figure named Mamdani has urged New York state authorities to block a deal involving Western Union. The effort comes as remittance flows across the U.S. have been increasing, with immigrants sending money home ahead of potential deportation.

stories.title: Cuba has run out of diesel and fuel oil amid U.S. oil blockade
stories.summary: Cuba has completely exhausted its diesel and fuel oil supplies amid a U.S. oil blockade. The country's top energy official stated that negotiations to import fuel were continuing despite the restrictions.

stories.title: Prince Harry: UK antisemitism ‘deeply troubling,’ Mideast violence cannot justify it
stories.summary: Prince Harry described rising antisemitism in the United Kingdom as deeply troubling, saying British Jews feel unsafe in their homes. He implied criticism of Israeli actions but stressed that violence in the Middle East cannot justify hostility toward an entire people or faith.

stories.title: Daily Briefing May 14 – What are ToI’s guiding principles in covering ‘blood libels’?
stories.summary: Times of Israel editor David Horovitz discussed the outlet's editorial approach to covering contested allegations, the complexities of upcoming Israeli elections, and conflicting narratives about a reported Netanyahu visit to the UAE.

stories.title: Japanese crude tanker emerges outside Hormuz in rare, undercover transit
stories.summary: A Japanese-owned crude oil supertanker completed a rare, covert transit through the Strait of Hormuz. It is only the second Japanese-owned supertanker to cross the strategic chokepoint since the Iran war began.

stories.title: NYT column alleging Israeli abuse of Palestinian prisoners sparks debate among Jews
stories.summary: A New York Times opinion column by Nicholas Kristof containing graphic allegations of Israeli abuse of Palestinian prisoners has sparked debate. Some Israel critics argue the piece's most extreme claims risk undermining more substantiated allegations.

stories.title: Xi warns Trump Taiwan issue could lead to 'conflict' as US-China summit starts
stories.summary: At a summit in Beijing, Chinese President Xi Jinping warned U.S. President Donald Trump that mishandling the Taiwan issue could lead to conflict between their nations. Trump struck a positive tone, calling Xi a "great leader" and predicting a "fantastic future" for bilateral relations.

stories.title: Saudi warplanes reportedly struck militias in Iraq during war
stories.summary: Reuters reported that Saudi fighter jets struck Iran-backed militias in Iraq during the broader Iran war. Retaliatory attacks were also reportedly launched from Kuwait.

stories.title: Ukraine arrests Zelensky’s ex-top aide as corruption probe widens
stories.summary: Ukrainian authorities arrested Andriy Yermak, President Zelensky's former chief of staff, on money-laundering charges. Investigators had named Yermak a suspect in a multi-episode corruption case involving nearly 9 million euros. A Kyiv judge ordered his pre-trial detention on Thursday.

stories.title: Russian forces launch drone strikes on Kharkiv this morning, injuring 20 people
stories.summary: Russian forces launched drone strikes on the Shevchenkivskyi and Saltivskyi districts of Kharkiv on Thursday morning, injuring 20 people.

stories.title: U.S.-China summit: Taiwan issue could lead to ‘conflict’, Xi warns Trump
stories.summary: During the U.S.-China summit in Beijing, President Xi Jinping warned President Trump that the Taiwan issue could lead to conflict, while also stating the two sides should be partners rather than rivals. Beijing claims self-ruled democratic Taiwan as its territory.

stories.title: Who are the US CEOs in China with Trump, and what’s in it for them?
stories.summary: Top U.S. corporate executives accompanied President Trump to China, seeking to expand their business operations there as the president looks for economic wins ahead of midterm elections.

stories.title: One dead and two fighting for their lives after bus rolled off road in Whitsundays region
stories.summary: One person died and at least two were critically injured after a Flix coach rolled off the Bruce Highway near Gumlu in Queensland's Whitsundays region. One passenger was trapped beneath the vehicle, and eleven ambulances and two helicopters responded to the scene.

stories.title: Israel’s Smotrich leads settler raid into Joseph’s Tomb in the occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich led hundreds of settlers into Joseph's Tomb in Nablus in the occupied West Bank under heavy military escort. Smotrich vowed to make the Israeli presence at the site permanent.

stories.title: UAE 'denies reports' of secret Netanyahu visit
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates reportedly denied claims that Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu made a secret visit to the country. The denial followed reports that Israel had deployed its Iron Dome air defense systems and personnel to the UAE during the ongoing war with Iran.

stories.title: Palestinian Fatah party to elect leaders for first time in decade
stories.summary: The Palestinian Fatah movement is set to elect a new central committee for the first time in a decade during a three-day general conference, amid existential challenges following Israel's war on Gaza and criticism over corruption.

stories.title: The October 7 report and the media circus that followed
stories.summary: A new report details atrocities committed by Hamas against women and children during the October 7 attack. Media coverage of the report has drawn debate over journalistic priorities, with attention shifting to focus on Israeli forces' actions.

stories.title: Constable injured in attack on checkpost succumbs to wounds in Charsadda
stories.summary: A police constable named Sajjad Khan died from injuries sustained in a militant attack on the Azizabad checkpost in Charsadda, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. Unidentified militants had targeted the post with explosives on April 22, and Khan succumbed to his wounds weeks later.

stories.title: Whatever happens at the Eurovision final, Israelis feel that Noam Bettan has already won
stories.summary: Israeli contestant Noam Bettan advanced to the Eurovision Song Contest final in Vienna, spending the days between the semifinal and Saturday's final rehearsing and enjoying the city with his backup dancers.

stories.title: Israeli attacks Lebanon’s Seddiqine, Tuffahta
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes targeted the towns of Seddiqine and Tuffahta in southern Lebanon, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Earlier strikes also hit Kafra, Majdal Selem, and Souaneh.

stories.title: Latvian PM resigns after row over stray Ukrainian drones
stories.summary: Latvian Prime Minister Evika Siliņa resigned following a political dispute over stray Ukrainian drones that crashed in Latvia while bound for Russia. The incidents last week triggered a significant political fallout in the Baltic nation.

stories.title: Russia pummels Ukraine, hitting regions far from the front lines
stories.summary: Russia has escalated daytime aerial attacks across Ukraine, striking regions far from the front lines. President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that Moscow launched at least 800 drones on Wednesday. The strikes continued into Thursday morning, killing at least six people and wounding dozens more.

stories.title: Air raid alert lasts in Kyiv for more than 8 hours: One person killed and injury toll climbs to 33 following Russian strike
stories.summary: An air raid alert lasted more than eight hours in Kyiv during the May 14 Russian attack. One person was killed and 33 were injured, including a two-month-old infant.

stories.title: A Vienna cafe offers refuge for Israel supporters as tensions brew at Eurovision
stories.summary: A Vienna café called MQ Kantine opened its doors to Israeli Eurovision fans after Israel was excluded from the official Eurofan Cafe listings. The venue offered falafel, kosher wine, and security for attendees.

stories.title: Israel set for first-ever F-35 external fuel tank upgrade in force buildup push
stories.summary: Israel is set to become the first country to receive an external fuel tank upgrade for its F-35 stealth fighters, a modification intended to reduce reliance on aerial refueling and extend long-range mission capabilities.

stories.title: From Rutgers speaker to Kristof column, implausible anti-Israel dog rape claim goes mainstream
stories.summary: Israeli officials rejected allegations that dogs were trained to sexually abuse Palestinian prisoners, a claim that appeared in a Rutgers University speech and a New York Times column. Jewish organizations called the allegation a modern-day blood libel.

stories.title: First real crash test for Ukraine’s anti-corruption institutions
stories.summary: Ukraine's anti-corruption institutions face a major test as investigators pursue cases against high-ranking political figures. The central question is whether the system can credibly investigate individuals at the top of the country's political power structure.

stories.title: First real crash test for Ukraine’s anti-corruption institutions
stories.summary: Ukraine's anti-corruption institutions face a major test of their ability to investigate senior political figures. The key question is whether the system can credibly pursue cases involving individuals at the highest levels of power.

stories.title: In pictures: US president gets red carpet welcome upon arrival for talks with China's Xi in Beijing
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump arrived in Beijing for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, receiving a red carpet welcome at the Great Hall of the People with a military band and gun salute. The two leaders are expected to discuss trade, Iran, and Taiwan.

stories.title: Russia strikes Kyiv with drones and missiles, partially collapsing a residential building. Two people killed, 40 injured.
stories.summary: Russian forces struck Kyiv overnight on May 14 with a combined drone and missile attack that partially collapsed a residential building. At least two people were killed and 40 injured.

stories.title: Watch: What to expect from the Trump-Xi summit
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump arrived in Beijing for a three-day summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The leaders are expected to discuss trade, the war in Iran, the technology race, and other bilateral issues.

stories.title: South Africa: Girls in South Africa Get Free HPV Jabs. Boys Don't. Find Out Why They Should
stories.summary: South Africa currently provides free HPV vaccinations to girls but excludes boys from the program. Health advocates argue boys face serious risks from the virus, including throat and anal cancers and reduced fertility, and should also be vaccinated.

stories.title: Trump-Xi meeting 'like watching a boxer fight a Kung Fu master'
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump visited China, with the trip dominating French front pages. British newspapers focused on Labour Party leadership turmoil as Prime Minister Keir Starmer refused to resign. The Guardian also reported on a secret UN mission in Gaza.

stories.title: Mass cattle slaughter underway in Russia. Authorities say it’s lumpy skin disease. Farmers say it’s foot-and-mouth.
stories.summary: Authorities in Russia's Kemerovo region are conducting mass cattle culling and setting up checkpoints around farms. Officials cite lumpy skin disease, but farmers and unofficial sources suggest the cause may be foot-and-mouth disease, with 2,000 to 4,000 cows reportedly killed in one Kuzbass village in a week. Similar cases have been reported in the Novosibirsk region.

stories.title: Boeing nears ‘large’ China orders as Trump and Xi forge new trade board: Bessent
stories.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said large Boeing orders are expected as part of President Trump's state visit to Beijing. Bessent also announced that the U.S. and China would discuss establishing a joint "board of trade" to manage commercial ties between the two countries.

stories.title: Brazil’s Atlantic forest records lowest deforestation in 40 years
stories.summary: Brazil's Atlantic Forest recorded its lowest deforestation level in 40 years of monitoring, with 8,658 hectares cleared in 2025 — the first time the figure has fallen below 10,000 hectares since 1985. Environmentalists warned that weakened environmental laws could reverse the gains.

stories.title: Lebanon, Israel begin talks on 'disputed issues' in Washington
stories.summary: Lebanon and Israel began negotiations on disputed issues in Washington. Israeli strikes in Lebanon have killed hundreds since the ceasefire agreement, and Israeli forces continue to occupy parts of southern Lebanon.

stories.title: China or the US: Who has the largest army?
stories.summary: A comparison by France 2 examines the military capabilities of the United States and China, the world's two largest armed forces. The analysis covers personnel, weaponry, equipment, naval strength, and their respective defense budgets.

stories.title: Zelensky on Russian night attack: Kyiv main target of strike; damage reported at 20 locations
stories.summary: President Zelensky reported that Russia launched over 670 attack drones and 56 missiles at Ukraine overnight, with Kyiv as the primary target. In total, more than 1,560 drones were deployed against Ukrainian cities and communities over a 24-hour period, causing damage at 20 locations in the capital.

stories.title: Israel’s Smotrich leads settler raid into Joseph’s Tomb in the occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich led a group of settlers into Joseph's Tomb in the occupied West Bank city of Nablus. The far-right minister vowed to establish a permanent Israeli presence at the site.

stories.title: Russia launches hundreds more drones at Ukraine, killing three people
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported that Russia launched more than 1,560 drones at Ukraine since Wednesday, with the latest wave of attacks killing at least three people.

stories.title: What did Trump and Xi discuss at high-profile Beijing summit?
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump held talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping at a summit in Beijing. Major American business leaders, including Elon Musk, Tim Cook, and Jensen Huang, joined the discussions. The agenda covered trade, the war in Iran, and Taiwan.

stories.title: Trump, Xi agree on need for Hormuz to stay open, White House says
stories.summary: During President Trump's state visit to Beijing, he and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed that the Strait of Hormuz must remain open for the free flow of energy, according to the White House.

stories.title: Iran urges BRICS to condemn US, Israel for war, bloc divisions
stories.summary: Iran urged BRICS member nations to condemn what Tehran described as US and Israeli violations of international law during a summit overshadowed by the ongoing war in Iran.

stories.title: Hezbollah drone falls near Israel-Lebanon border, Israeli military says
stories.summary: Israel's military reported that a Hezbollah explosive drone landed in Israeli territory near the Lebanese border, injuring several Israelis who were evacuated and hospitalized.

stories.title: Ukraine just placed one of its highest-ranking corruption suspects under court-ordered custody
stories.summary: A Ukrainian anti-corruption court placed former presidential chief of staff Andriy Yermak under 60-day custody. He is accused of helping launder $11 million through an elite housing project, marking one of the highest-profile corruption cases in Ukraine.

stories.title: The World in Front of Me: Soviet Union - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Photographer Bill Aron's work documenting Soviet Jewish life behind the Iron Curtain is being featured in a series. His photographs captured refuseniks and the resilience of Jewish faith under Soviet repression.

stories.title: Iran Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrives in India, to attend BRICS FM meet
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in India to attend the BRICS Foreign Ministers' meeting in New Delhi. He is expected to encounter UAE Minister of State for Foreign Affairs at the summit on Thursday.

stories.title: Tunisia tourism feels pressure as regional war drives up travel costs
stories.summary: Tunisia's tourism industry is experiencing pressure as the regional conflict drives up oil prices and travel costs. Industry officials on the island of Djerba report that the economic fallout is being felt even thousands of miles from the conflict zone.

stories.title: Indian pharma fuels Africa’s ‘zombie drug’ and opioid crisis
stories.summary: Indian pharmaceutical manufacturers are reportedly producing high-strength tapentadol pills that lack regulatory approval from any authority worldwide. The drugs are being linked to a growing opioid crisis in Africa.

stories.title: In Ivano-Frankivsk, injury toll from Russian attack climbs to ten
stories.summary: In Ivano-Frankivsk, western Ukraine, the casualty toll from a Russian drone strike on a high-rise residential building rose to ten injured, including two teenagers.

stories.title: Zelensky's former top aide Andriy Yermak remanded in Ukraine corruption probe
stories.summary: A Ukrainian anti-corruption court ordered the pretrial detention of Andriy Yermak, President Zelenskyy's former chief of staff, for 60 days on money-laundering charges. Yermak served as Zelenskyy's right-hand man during most of Russia's full-scale invasion until resigning in November.

stories.title: Alibaba, Tencent signal AI spending surge despite earnings pressure as China chips ramp up
stories.summary: Chinese tech giants Alibaba and Tencent announced plans to significantly increase spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure despite weaker-than-expected quarterly revenues. Both companies are betting on domestically produced chips from Huawei and Alibaba's in-house labs to overcome supply bottlenecks caused by export restrictions.

stories.title: New weather study warns of potentially dangerous conditions at 2026 World Cup
stories.summary: A new World Weather Attribution study warns that dozens of matches at the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States, Canada, and Mexico could be played in temperatures exceeding recommended safety thresholds.
