stories.title: Navy to run into financial constraints this summer due to current operations, CNO says
stories.summary: U.S. Chief of Naval Operations reported that the Navy expects to face financial constraints this summer due to the pace of current operations. The aircraft carrier USS Gerald R. Ford is anticipated to require increased maintenance following its extended deployment.

stories.title: Role of Indo-Pacific air defenders has evolved dramatically, US Army commander says
stories.summary: Brig. Gen. William Parker, commander of the U.S. Army's 94th Army Air and Missile Defense Command, described how the role of air defenders in the Indo-Pacific has evolved significantly. He contrasted the current high-demand mission with a past era when an air defense building bore a sign reading "Will work for food."

stories.title: Russia places UK ex-Defence Minister Ben Wallace on wanted list
stories.summary: Russia has placed former UK Defence Minister Ben Wallace on its wanted list after he recommended helping Ukraine strike the bridge connecting Russia to annexed Crimea.

stories.title: Global Faultlines podcast | Why Lebanon remains in perpetual crisis
stories.summary: A podcast episode examines Lebanon's persistent crises, tracing the country's trajectory from post-war recovery through economic collapse, political paralysis, and renewed conflict, spanning the 2006 Israel-Hezbollah war to the 2019 protests and recent upheaval.

stories.title: Rights groups urge Poland to halt support for US deportation flights to Ukraine
stories.summary: Amnesty International and Human Rights First urged Poland on Wednesday to stop cooperating with US deportation flights transferring Ukrainian nationals through Polish territory. The rights organizations argued that the practice may violate international law.

stories.title: France probing if shadowy Israeli firm BlackCore meddled in municipal elections: sources
stories.summary: French intelligence agencies are investigating whether Israeli firm BlackCore interfered in French municipal elections. The probe focuses on deceptive websites and social media accounts allegedly used to smear three candidates from the hard-left Unbowed party.

stories.title: At 10.15pm, do you know where Donald Trump is?
stories.summary: The article discusses U.S. President Donald Trump's late-night social media activity on Truth Social amid multiple pressing issues, including tensions in the Strait of Hormuz related to the Iran conflict, an upcoming meeting with China's president, and the resignation of the FDA director.

stories.title: Chinese supertanker breaks through US-Iran war blockade in Hormuz
stories.summary: The Chinese supertanker Yuan Hua Hu transited the Strait of Hormuz after months of delays caused by U.S.-Iran tensions in the Gulf. The vessel was carrying nearly two million barrels of Iraqi crude oil.

stories.title: EU imports of Russian gas highest since Ukraine invasion: Report
stories.summary: European Union imports of Russian natural gas have reached their highest levels since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The increase comes as nations worldwide scramble for energy supplies after the Iran war disrupted global deliveries.

stories.title: ‘One of the longest’ Russian attacks kills at least six people in Ukraine
stories.summary: At least six people were killed in what has been described as one of the longest Russian aerial attacks on Ukraine. Moscow claimed it intercepted and destroyed 286 Ukrainian drones overnight.

stories.title: Israel: Netanyahu coalition faces collapse as Haredi rift widens
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's coalition faces possible collapse after ultra-Orthodox parties threatened to dissolve the Knesset over a dispute regarding a military conscription exemption law.

stories.title: Rwanda's former first lady to appeal decision to reopen genocide probe against her
stories.summary: Rwanda's former first lady Agathe Habyarimana plans to appeal a French court ruling that reopened an investigation into her alleged role in the 1994 Rwandan genocide. The ruling overturned a 2025 decision that had dismissed the probe.

stories.title: IDF testing counter-drone technologies ahead of security meeting on rising drone threat
stories.summary: The Israeli military is testing counter-drone technologies ahead of a high-level security meeting on the growing drone threat, with defense sources indicating round-the-clock development efforts to present solutions to Defense Minister Israel Katz.

stories.title: Flydubai suspends flights to Islamabad, Lahore, Peshawar till Oct due to 'operational issues'
stories.summary: UAE-based low-cost carrier Flydubai suspended flights to and from Islamabad, Lahore, and Peshawar until October 26 due to operational reasons, while maintaining service to Karachi.

stories.title: Why Congress Can’t Stop Trump’s Iran War
stories.summary: The article examines how decades of political developments have eroded Congress's constitutional authority to declare war, making it difficult for lawmakers to check President Trump's military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Who is the real Wes Streeting? His record on Israel and foreign policy examined
stories.summary: UK Health Secretary Wes Streeting is reportedly poised to resign from the cabinet and launch a leadership challenge to become Prime Minister. His record on Israel and foreign policy is under scrutiny.

stories.title: No, two French soldiers have not been killed in a Russian attack in Ukraine
stories.summary: Pro-Russian social media accounts falsely claimed that two French soldiers, Sergeant Bin Chen and Corporal Axel Delplanque, were killed in a Russian attack in Odesa, Ukraine. While both service members did recently die, their deaths were unrelated to any Russian military action.

stories.title: What Don Bacon has sizzling before he leaves office
stories.summary: Departing U.S. Representative Don Bacon, a former Air Force officer, outlined remaining legislative priorities before the end of the 119th Congress. The article details his to-do list as he prepares to leave office.

stories.title: Gaitanistas – Gulf Clan
stories.summary: A profile examines Colombia's Autodefensas Gaitanistas de Colombia, also known as the Gulf Clan, which emerged from the remnants of the country's paramilitary movement to become a dominant but fragmented criminal organization.

stories.title: Twenty-four cases investigated in Dnipropetrovsk region over business cooperation with Russia despite sanctions
stories.summary: Authorities in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region are investigating 24 criminal cases involving companies accused of cooperating with Russia in violation of wartime sanctions.

stories.title: Israel concerned potential Trump-Iran deal may come with unwanted concessions - CNN
stories.summary: Israeli officials expressed concern that a potential Trump-Iran deal could include unwanted concessions, with sources telling CNN that Israel fears Trump may grow impatient with talks and accept any agreement with last-minute compromises.

stories.title: Streeting to fire starting gun in Starmer leadership battle – The Latest
stories.summary: UK Health Secretary Wes Streeting is expected to launch a leadership challenge against Prime Minister Keir Starmer as soon as Thursday. The news emerged during the king's speech, disrupting Starmer's planned political reset.

stories.title: Nigeria military says no evidence of civilian casualties from Zamfara market airstrike
stories.summary: Nigeria's military stated on Wednesday that it found no evidence of civilian casualties from an airstrike targeting militants in northwestern Zamfara state earlier this month. The military dismissed reports of large death tolls as unverified and misleading.

stories.title: US-Iran talks stalled after Tehran tried skirting up-front nuke concessions — officials
stories.summary: U.S.-Iran negotiations have stalled over disagreements on nuclear concessions. Washington sought a temporary ceasefire including Iranian compromises on its nuclear program, while Tehran demanded a permanent truce followed by separate enrichment talks.

stories.title: About 80 percent of war-damaged areas repaired in Tehran, Iranian official says
stories.summary: An Iranian official said about 80% of war-damaged sites in Tehran have been repaired. Over 60,000 residential and commercial units in Tehran province were hit during the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran that began on February 28.

stories.title: Gaza-bound aid convoy regroups in Libya for renewed push
stories.summary: An aid convoy bound for Gaza is regrouping in Libya for a renewed attempt to reach Rafah. Hundreds of activists and medical teams are joining the effort to deliver vital supplies.

stories.title: Why is the UK’s Prime Minister Keir Starmer so unpopular?
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces severe political pressure as over 80 members of his own Labour Party have called on him to resign. Recent polls show him to be Britain's most unpopular leader on record, just two years after winning a landslide election victory.

stories.title: Trump-Xi Summit: China wants to 'displace' the US in world order
stories.summary: Analyst Philippe Le Corre stated on France 24 that China seeks to displace the United States in the global order by diminishing American relevance rather than directly replacing it. The comments came amid the Trump-Xi summit discussions.

stories.title: Global parliamentarians commit to recognizing Jerusalem's sovereignty during Knesset conference
stories.summary: Parliamentarians from multiple countries pledged to recognize Jerusalem's sovereignty during a conference at the Israeli Knesset, framing the commitment as a moral stance.

stories.title: Three injured in Russian drone attack in Smila in Cherkasy region
stories.summary: Three residents of Smila in Ukraine's Cherkasy region were injured in a Russian drone attack on the city.

stories.title: High Court annuls Karhi’s decision to fire key public broadcaster official
stories.summary: Israel's High Court annulled Communication Minister Shlomo Karhi's decision to fire the head of public broadcaster Kan's search panel. The judge criticized the dismissal, which followed the official's adoption of Attorney General legal guidance.

stories.title: UAE designates 21 Lebanese individuals, organisations as terrorists over alleged Hezbollah links
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates designated 21 Lebanese individuals and organisations as terrorists over alleged links to Hezbollah. The list includes 16 Lebanese nationals and five Lebanon-based organisations, as published by an official Emirati news agency.

stories.title: ‘Enough of the hatred’: Herzog, Gal Gadot call for dialogue at Jerusalem conference
stories.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog and actress Gal Gadot called for dialogue and an end to hatred at a Jerusalem conference. The forum aimed to promote mutual respect within Israeli society.

stories.title: Russia is abandoning its push on Stepnohirsk where average mobilized Russian soldier survived 12 minutes
stories.summary: Russia is reportedly abandoning its offensive push on Stepnohirsk in Ukraine, where newly mobilized Russian soldiers survived an average of only 12 minutes in combat. Elite units had been deployed in the assault.

stories.title: Is the Pentagon’s UFO dump a political distraction?
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense released files related to unidentified flying objects, prompting widespread online scrutiny over the authenticity and significance of the documents.

stories.title: Pentagon launches new framework agreements to acquire 10,000 low-cost cruise missiles
stories.summary: The Pentagon launched the new Low Cost Containerization Munitions Program, signing framework agreements with Anduril, CoAspire, Leidos, and Zone 5 to acquire 10,000 low-cost cruise missiles. The program aims to rapidly scale affordable munitions production.

stories.title: Mossad chief 'visited UAE twice' during US-Israel war on Iran
stories.summary: Mossad chief David Barnea secretly visited the UAE twice during the U.S.-Israel war on Iran, according to the Wall Street Journal. The visits reflect deepening security coordination between Abu Dhabi and Israel.

stories.title: India’s salt workers brave brutal heat on Gujarat’s desert plains
stories.summary: Gujarat's desert plains account for 75% of India's salt production, with tens of thousands of workers laboring under extreme heat conditions.

stories.title: Is It Really a ‘Cease-Fire’ if Both Sides Are Still Shooting?
stories.summary: A mediation expert discusses the fragility of the U.S.-Iran cease-fire, questioning whether it qualifies as a genuine cease-fire given that both sides continue military operations. The analysis highlights the vulnerabilities undermining the agreement.

stories.title: Zelensky proposes bilateral drone deals with European countries
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky proposed bilateral drone production and supply deals with individual European countries, arguing such agreements would strengthen continental security.

stories.title: Wary mood to mark Xi-Trump summit with irritants aplenty on both sides: analysts
stories.summary: Analysts say the upcoming summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping carries a wary mood, with both Washington and Beijing accumulating diplomatic irritants as potential bargaining leverage. Neither side wants to appear responsible for derailing negotiations.

stories.title: Turkey and Armenia to restart direct trade: Ankara
stories.summary: Turkey and Armenia announced they will resume direct trade after a 33-year halt. The move advances normalization of ties long strained by conflict-related tensions.

stories.title: Lebanon denies UN complaint against Iran over interference
stories.summary: Lebanon denied filing a formal complaint against Iran at the United Nations, stating that leaked documents were responses to previous Iranian letters sent to the Security Council.

stories.title: Lebanon files unprecedented UN complaint against Iran
stories.summary: Lebanon filed a formal complaint with the United Nations accusing Iran of violating diplomatic conventions and dragging the country into a devastating war. The complaint is described as unprecedented.

stories.title: Palestinian handed 30-month sentence for trying to sell illegally obtained lion cub
stories.summary: A Palestinian man received a 30-month prison sentence after pleading guilty in a plea deal to attempting to sell an illegally obtained lion cub, other exotic animals, and possessing an illegal M-16 rifle.

stories.title: Trump arrives in Beijing for first US presidential visit in nearly a decade
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump arrived in Beijing for the first American presidential visit to China in nearly a decade, with trade negotiations at the top of the agenda as Washington seeks to resolve business disputes and strengthen bilateral ties.

stories.title: Ukraine's Zelensky warns of incoming Russian drone attacks during daylight
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned on Wednesday of possible waves of Russian drone attacks throughout the day, noting more than a hundred drones were in Ukrainian airspace. He said Moscow has shifted tactics to strike increasingly during daylight hours.

stories.title: US sends military personnel to “Silicon Valley of warfare” to study drones
stories.summary: The United States is sending military personnel to Ukraine to study drone warfare tactics on the front lines. Officials have described Ukraine as the world's most important battlefield laboratory for modern combat technology.

stories.title: Africa Forward Summit: Africa must "build off the basis of what it already owns"
stories.summary: At the Africa Forward Summit, philosopher Achille Mbembe argued that Africa should build on its existing assets and wealth rather than focusing on what it lacks. He urged the continent to reconcile its global knowledge with its own values and resources.

stories.title: Israeli drone strikes kill 8 near Beirut ahead of talks
stories.summary: Israeli drone strikes hit multiple vehicles along a main highway south of Beirut, killing eight people including a woman and her two children, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry. The attack was one of the deadliest escalations since the ceasefire took effect.

stories.title: Beware these pitfalls as Syria begins trying Assad-era figures
stories.summary: Syria has begun prosecuting figures from the Assad era, raising hopes for accountability. Observers warn that without legal reform and inclusive mechanisms, justice efforts could fall short.

stories.title: Khawaja Asif says KP now on 'same page' as Centre in fight against terrorism
stories.summary: Pakistan's Defence Minister Khawaja Asif stated in the National Assembly that the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provincial government is now cooperating with the federal government in combating terrorism. His remarks came in response to criticism from JUI-F lawmaker Noor Alam Khan over rising terrorism in the province.

stories.title: Israeli singer Noa speaks to FRANCE 24 as Israel's participation sparks Eurovision backlash
stories.summary: Ten countries, including Finland and Israel, secured places in the Eurovision Song Contest final. Five nations — Spain, Ireland, the Netherlands, Slovenia, and Iceland — boycotted the 70th anniversary edition in protest against Israel's war in Gaza, which has killed at least 75,000 Palestinians since the October 7 Hamas attack.

stories.title: Zelensky hopes EUR 90B European support package will launch in early June
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed hope that a EUR 90 billion European support package would become operational by early June, with the first tranche directed toward drone production.

stories.title: Watermelons and Handala: Germany outlines symbols of 'secular pro-Palestinian extremism'
stories.summary: Germany's Federal Office for the Protection of the Constitution published a guide identifying watermelons, the Handala figure, and other symbols as indicators of what it calls secular pro-Palestinian extremism.

stories.title: Iran releases prize-winning rights lawyer Nasrin Sotoudeh
stories.summary: Iranian authorities released prize-winning human rights lawyer Nasrin Sotoudeh, who was arrested in April. Activists say her detention was part of a broader crackdown on civil society in Iran.

stories.title: Two Estonians who crossed into Russia seeking asylum reportedly sent to psychiatric hospitals for evaluation
stories.summary: Two Estonian citizens who crossed into Russia last winter seeking asylum have reportedly been placed in psychiatric hospitals for evaluation, according to a letter one of them sent to the independent Russian outlet Mediazona.

stories.title: Magnus the wandering walrus leaves Scotland for Norway
stories.summary: A young male walrus nicknamed Magnus, first spotted at Stronsay pier in Orkney, Scotland, on April 16, has been sighted in Norway after swimming approximately 400 miles across the North Sea.

stories.title: Nigeria: Study Flags Cement As Construction Industry's Biggest Carbon Problem, Offers Greener Solutions
stories.summary: A study by Nigerian researcher Ololade Temitope Oduneye identified cement as the largest source of carbon emissions in the construction industry and proposed greener alternatives to reduce the sector's environmental footprint.

stories.title: Ukraine hits Russia's energy targets after US-brokered ceasefire ends
stories.summary: Ukraine resumed drone attacks on Russian oil refineries and ports on Wednesday, two days after a three-day ceasefire proposed by US President Donald Trump expired. The strikes marked a return to hostilities targeting Russia's energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Kenya: 'Taking Ballot Photos Could Cost You Ksh1 Million,' IEBC Warns
stories.summary: Kenya's Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission warned voters ahead of a Thursday by-election that photographing or recording inside polling booths could result in a fine of up to Ksh1 million, up to three years in prison, or both.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: DRC Journalist Detained Since January, Another in Hiding After Mining Impact Report
stories.summary: The Committee to Protect Journalists called on Democratic Republic of the Congo authorities to release journalist Stéphane Shisso, detained since January after reporting on erosion caused by mining in Kinshasa. His colleague Guelord Shamba is reportedly in hiding over the same report.

stories.title: 27 Syrian civil orgs unveil roadmap for transitional justice
stories.summary: Twenty-seven Syrian civil society organizations released a roadmap for transitional justice. The document proposes special courts, truth-seeking commissions, reparations, and accountability mechanisms.

stories.title: Trump arrives in China for historic trip
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump arrived in Beijing for talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping, marking the first visit by a U.S. leader to China since 2017. The two leaders are expected to discuss the Iran conflict, trade relations, and U.S. arms sales to Taiwan.

stories.title: UAE bank federation chief says no concerns of capital flight
stories.summary: The head of the UAE banking federation said the war on Iran has not triggered capital flight or dollar shortages in the country. The UAE is pursuing a currency swap deal with the United States.

stories.title: Africa Forward Summit: Navigating the nuances of data governance in Africa
stories.summary: At the Africa Forward Summit, data scientist Peter Addo highlighted the data governance challenges facing African nations as artificial intelligence infrastructure expands across the continent. He emphasized the importance of data responsibility in managing these developments.

stories.title: Trump-backed envoy says Gaza ceasefire 'far from perfect' but working
stories.summary: Nickolay Mladenov, the high representative for Trump's Peace Council in Gaza, said the Gaza ceasefire is holding but is "far from perfect," acknowledging daily violations. More than 800 people have been killed since the ceasefire began.

stories.title: One of few Western officials to witness war firsthand: What did  Germany’s defense minister see on Ukraine’s front line?
stories.summary: German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius visited Ukraine's front lines to witness the fighting firsthand, then participated in an EU defense ministers meeting from a headquarters located near the combat zone.

stories.title: UK PM Starmer clings on as leadership talk overshadows king's speech
stories.summary: King Charles III delivered a speech to Britain's parliament on Wednesday, but the event was overshadowed by speculation that Health Secretary Wes Streeting is preparing to resign and launch a leadership challenge against Prime Minister Keir Starmer.

stories.title: Israeli scientists’ microbial research delves into bowels of cow belch prevention
stories.summary: Scientists at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev found that microbial communities in cattle adapt how they use resources. The discovery could help develop methods to reduce methane emissions from cows.

stories.title: Two killed, four injured in Russian strike on Rivne region
stories.summary: A Russian strike on a residential building in Ukraine's Rivne region killed two people and injured four others.

stories.title: Microsoft Israel head ousted reportedly over IDF’s controversial use of cloud tech
stories.summary: Microsoft Israel head Alon Haimovich was reportedly ousted following a review into the IDF's alleged unethical use of Microsoft's cloud platform for surveillance of Palestinians.

stories.title: Board of Peace mulls advancing Trump Gaza plan without Hamas
stories.summary: The Board of Peace for Gaza is reportedly weighing whether to move forward with elements of Donald Trump's Gaza plan without Hamas's participation, should the group reject demands for disarmament.

stories.title: U.K. police pull bodies of three women from sea at Brighton
stories.summary: UK emergency services recovered the bodies of three women from the sea near Brighton on the eastern seafront of the southern English city. Multiple emergency vehicles, lifeboats, and a helicopter responded to the scene.

stories.title: Trump arrives in Beijing for summit with China’s Xi on trade, US arms sales to Taiwan
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump arrived in Beijing for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping covering trade and U.S. arms sales to Taiwan. The Iran war and a nuclear warheads treaty with Russia are also expected to be on the agenda.

stories.title: Air Force greenlights requirements for MQ-9A Reaper drone replacement
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force has approved requirements for a successor to the MQ-9A Reaper drone. Air Force Lt. Gen. Luke Cropsey noted growing interest across the defense industrial base in developing the next-generation unmanned aerial system.

stories.title: Khawaja Asif says KP on 'same page' as Centre in fight against terrorism
stories.summary: Pakistani Defence Minister Khawaja Asif told the National Assembly that the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provincial government is now cooperating with the federal government in the fight against terrorism, a shift from previous tensions between the two.

stories.title: Gunshots fired in standoff at Philippine Senate over ICC suspect
stories.summary: Gunshots were fired at the Philippine Senate on Wednesday during a standoff involving Senator Ronald dela Rosa, a former police chief wanted by the International Criminal Court for his role in ex-President Rodrigo Duterte's drug war. Dela Rosa had urged supporters to mobilize to prevent his arrest and handover to the ICC.

stories.title: US intel contradicts claims Iran arsenal weakened, The New York Times report
stories.summary: The New York Times reported that classified U.S. intelligence assessments indicate Iran retains substantial missile capabilities, with roughly 70 percent of its mobile launchers and pre-war missile stockpile still operational. Iran has also reportedly restored access to 30 of 33 missile sites along the Strait of Hormuz, while U.S. munitions stocks have been depleted.

stories.title: Taiwan new key player as Ukraine shifts drone supply chain away from China
stories.summary: Ukraine has been shifting its drone supply chain away from China amid concerns that Beijing is providing military goods to Russia. Kyiv, along with European nations and the United States, has increasingly turned to Taiwan as an alternative supplier of drone components.

stories.title: Trump arrives in China for two-day summit with Xi
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump landed in Beijing for a two-day summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

stories.title: Britain to legislate to tackle threats from state proxies
stories.summary: The United Kingdom plans to introduce legislation targeting threats from state-backed proxy groups. Several British lawmakers have called for proscribing Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps following a series of attacks against the Jewish community.

stories.title: Possessing weapons is only one of three essentials in modern war, Zelenskyy tells NATO’s eastern flank at B9 summit
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky addressed NATO's eastern-flank Bucharest Nine summit, stating that possessing weapons is only one of three essentials in modern warfare. Russia simultaneously launched strikes on previously untargeted regions during the summit.

stories.title: Working ‘outside the lines’ to scale production isn’t working: Cadenazzi
stories.summary: The Defense Innovation Unit continues to vet drone technology but acknowledges that wartime production scaling requires internal reform rather than ad hoc workarounds. DIU Director Cadenazzi said working "outside the lines" to scale production is not sustainable.

stories.title: President Zardari approves Sitara-i-Shujaat for citizen who sacrified his life while averting suicide attack
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari approved the Sitara-i-Shujaat award for a citizen named Liaqat, a shepherd who sacrificed his life foiling a suicide attack near a security post in Jand tehsil, Attock, on the Punjab–Khyber Pakhtunkhwa border.

stories.title: Alex Murdaugh’s murder convictions overturned by South Carolina supreme court
stories.summary: The South Carolina Supreme Court overturned Alex Murdaugh's murder convictions for the 2021 killings of his wife and son, citing improper external influences on the jury by a court clerk. The justices ordered a new trial, ruling that jury interference compromised Murdaugh's right to a fair trial.

stories.title: Trump arrives in China with tech titans and top aides for high-stakes Xi summit
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump arrived at Beijing Capital International Airport on Wednesday, accompanied by top aides and tech leaders including Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Elon Musk, and Tim Cook. Chinese Vice-President Han Zheng received the delegation.

stories.title: Pentagon reaches agreements with defense firms on containerized missiles
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced framework agreements with defense firms Anduril, CoAspire, Leidos, and Zone 5 to acquire over 10,000 containerized missiles. The deals are part of efforts to bolster low-cost munitions capabilities.

stories.title: Has Labor’s tax reform killed ‘rent-vesting’ for young Australians seeking a foothold in the housing market?
stories.summary: Australia's Labor government introduced tax changes affecting capital gains and negative gearing on investment properties. Experts warn the reforms could undermine the "rent-vesting" strategy used by young Australians who rent in preferred areas while purchasing cheaper properties elsewhere.

stories.title: Palestinian peak body refused leave to appear at royal commission on antisemitism and social cohesion
stories.summary: Australia's Palestine Advocacy Network said it was refused leave to appear before the royal commission on antisemitism and social cohesion, despite having submitted detailed written evidence. The group argued Palestinian voices are being excluded from the debate.

stories.title: Man dies in Sydney prison unit that watchdog wanted shut down because it ‘cannot provide a safe environment’
stories.summary: A 19-year-old remand inmate died by suicide at Long Bay correctional centre's Metropolitan Special Programs Centre in Sydney. An independent watchdog had previously recommended the unit be closed due to ligature points and an inability to provide a safe environment.

stories.title: Perm oil refinery shuts down after drone attack — Reuters
stories.summary: The Perm oil refinery in Russia completely shut down following a May 7 Ukrainian drone attack that caused a fire and damaged equipment, according to Reuters.

stories.title: 12 killed by a series of Israeli strikes on cars in Lebanon
stories.summary: A series of Israeli strikes on vehicles across Lebanon killed at least 12 people, including a woman and her two children.

stories.title: US President Trump arrives in Beijing for two-day summit with Xi Jinping
stories.summary: Air Force One landed in Beijing on Wednesday carrying U.S. President Donald Trump for a two-day summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

stories.title: Chinese court awards compensation to sacked worker replaced by AI
stories.summary: A court in Hangzhou, China, ruled in favor of a quality assurance supervisor who was fired after his employer replaced him with artificial intelligence. The worker, surnamed Zhou, was awarded more than £28,000 in compensation.

stories.title: Latvia moves to ban all bus service to Russia and Belarus, citing recruitment risks
stories.summary: Latvia is moving to ban all bus services to Russia and Belarus, citing concerns about recruitment risks posed by such routes.

stories.title: What Trump and Xi want from China visit
stories.summary: Trade, technology, Taiwan, and the war on Iran are expected to dominate high-stakes talks between U.S. President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping during Trump's China visit.

stories.title: Renewed Tigray tensions raise fears of Ethiopia-Eritrea war
stories.summary: The Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) is reasserting control in Ethiopia's Tigray region after electing Debretsion Gebremichael as its leader. Rising tensions between the TPLF and Ethiopia's federal government are fueling fears of a broader conflict involving Eritrea in the Horn of Africa.

stories.title: Tigray tensions raise fears of Ethiopia-Eritrea war
stories.summary: The Tigray People's Liberation Front is reasserting control in Ethiopia's Tigray region after electing Debretsion Gebremichael as leader. Rising tensions between the TPLF and Ethiopia's federal government are fueling fears of a renewed conflict potentially involving Eritrea.

stories.title: Trump mega-donors pause Wisconsin development project, citing economic uncertainty
stories.summary: Uline, a shipping supplies company owned by billionaire Republican donors Richard and Elizabeth Uihlein, has paused construction of a new distribution facility in Kenosha, Wisconsin, citing economic uncertainty. The Uihleins are prominent Trump supporters, and the halt comes in a key battleground state.

stories.title: Trump urged to rule out ‘unlawful’ Cuba takeover and stop using Guantánamo Bay for migrant detention
stories.summary: More than 30 Democratic members of Congress urged the Trump administration to stop using Guantánamo Bay for immigrant detention and to rule out military action against Cuba. The letter warned that such operations would worsen mass suffering on the island.

stories.title: Macron arrives in Ethiopia ahead of high‑level AU talks
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron arrived in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, where he was received by Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed. He then joined a trilateral meeting at African Union headquarters with UN Secretary-General António Guterres and AU Commission Chairman Mahmoud Ali Youssouf.

stories.title: Hondurasgate: The alleged US-Israeli plot shaking Latin America
stories.summary: Leaked audio recordings have allegedly revealed a plot involving U.S.- and Israeli-linked actors to secure a pardon for Honduras's former president and destabilize progressive governments across Latin America.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone attack sparks fire at gas plant in Russia's Astrakhan region, governor says
stories.summary: Debris from a Ukrainian drone attack caused a fire at a gas processing plant in Russia's southern Astrakhan region on Wednesday, according to the local governor. The strike targeted energy infrastructure in the region.

stories.title: Drone strike on minibus in Kherson: Injury toll climbs to nine
stories.summary: The number of people injured in a Russian drone strike on a minibus in the city of Kherson rose to nine.

stories.title: Karachi police get 3-day physical remand of alleged cocaine queenpin Anmol alias Pinky
stories.summary: A Karachi court granted police a three-day physical remand of Anmol alias Pinky, a woman arrested for allegedly running a cocaine and narcotics distribution network. She was apprehended in a joint raid on her Garden apartment by police and a civilian intelligence agency.

stories.title: Indian arrogance shot down alongside planes during last year's military conflict, Tarar says
stories.summary: Pakistani Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said Indian aircraft shot down during the May 2025 military conflict symbolized the defeat of Indian arrogance. He spoke at a ceremony marking "Marka-i-Haq" at Islamabad's Institute of Strategic Studies.

stories.title: Modi cuts motorcade size to save fuel amid mounting economic pressure
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi significantly reduced the size of his motorcade to save fuel amid rising energy prices linked to the Iran war. The move follows Modi's public appeal for citizens to adopt austerity measures including limiting foreign travel and reducing gold purchases.

stories.title: Owners push back as Wang Fuk Court administrator seeks to delay crucial meeting
stories.summary: Owners of Hong Kong's fire-damaged Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po are pushing back against a government-appointed administrator's attempt to delay an extraordinary general meeting. Over 240 owners petitioned in late April to hold the meeting before a decision on whether to sell their flats.

stories.title: UN food agency halves Syria food aid, halts bread subsidy
stories.summary: The UN World Food Programme halved its food assistance in Syria and halted bread subsidies after the Trump administration slashed U.S. foreign aid funding, affecting millions of Syrians.

stories.title: Russia is hitting Ukraine’s Zakarpattia Oblast, bordering Hungary with drones, for first time. Expert says this is linked to end of Orbán’s era
stories.summary: Russia struck Ukraine's Zakarpattia Oblast, which borders Hungary, with drones for the first time. Analysts suggest the timing of the May 13 attack—potentially record-breaking in scale—may be linked to shifts in Hungarian political dynamics.

stories.title: Russia's Lavrov says 'nothing is happening' with US-Russia relations
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov stated on Wednesday that despite positive rhetoric about US-Russia relations, "nothing is happening" in practice to advance bilateral ties between Moscow and Washington.

stories.title: Can South Africa's President Ramaphosa avoid impeachment again?
stories.summary: South Africa's Constitutional Court revived impeachment proceedings against President Cyril Ramaphosa, who previously avoided an inquiry in 2022 when his ANC-majority parliament blocked it. He now faces a coalition parliament with former political adversaries.

stories.title: Nearly 600 killed in Lebanon since so-called ceasefire began, says NRC
stories.summary: The Norwegian Refugee Council reported that nearly 600 people have been killed in Lebanon since a ceasefire agreement was announced last month, while over one million remain displaced. The NRC described ongoing daily attacks on villages as hallmarks of a repeatedly violated ceasefire.

stories.title: Somalia: Somalia Election Talks Stall in Mogadishu As Dispute Deepens
stories.summary: High-level election talks in Mogadishu between Somali opposition leaders and President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud ended without agreement on Wednesday. Negotiators failed to resolve disputes over the country's electoral framework.

stories.title: US special operations leaders frustrated by inability to modify their own equipment
stories.summary: U.S. special operations leaders expressed frustration with their inability to independently modify or upgrade their own equipment. They said reliance on manufacturers for fixes and upgrades leaves them with outdated capabilities as technology rapidly evolves.

stories.title: Bring it on? Why the ultra-Orthodox, the opposition, and maybe Netanyahu think earlier elections will work for them
stories.summary: Ultra-Orthodox parties in Israel are threatening to dissolve the Knesset over military conscription exemptions, potentially forcing early elections. The opposition, Haredi leaders, and possibly Prime Minister Netanyahu each see strategic advantages in an earlier vote.

stories.title: ‘Short of blue-collar workers’: Ukraine’s battle for labour
stories.summary: Ukraine is facing a significant shortage of blue-collar workers as the ongoing war has drawn men to the front lines. Women have been entering the workforce in record numbers to fill labor gaps across key sectors.

stories.title: Soros’s philanthropic foundation commits $30M to fighting antisemitism, anti-Muslim hate
stories.summary: George Soros's Open Society Foundations pledged $30 million to combat antisemitism and anti-Muslim hatred. The commitment comes amid rising levels of hate against Jews and Muslims linked to the Gaza and Iran wars.

stories.title: France: Cruise ship locked down over likely stomach flu outbreak
stories.summary: The cruise ship Ambition was locked down upon arrival in Bordeaux, France, after a suspected stomach flu outbreak on board. One passenger died and approximately 50 others showed symptoms. French authorities said the outbreak is unrelated to the hantavirus.

stories.title: Record high number of British Jews attend aliyah fair as antisemitism roils country
stories.summary: A record 1,200 British Jews attended an aliyah fair in the UK offering advice on emigrating to Israel. The turnout reflects rising antisemitism in Britain, though data does not yet indicate a mass exodus.

stories.title: Reports: Mossad, Shin Bet chiefs secretly visited UAE during Iran war
stories.summary: The heads of Israel's Mossad and Shin Bet intelligence agencies secretly visited the UAE during the Iran war in March and April. The visits were aimed at coordinating defensive and offensive efforts against Tehran between Jerusalem and Abu Dhabi.

stories.title: ‘Most powerful’: What’s the Sarmat missile Russia has test-launched?
stories.summary: Russia test-launched its RS-28 Sarmat intercontinental ballistic missile. President Vladimir Putin claimed the missile's range exceeds Western estimates.

stories.title: Explosions heard in Lutsk center
stories.summary: Explosions were reported in downtown Lutsk during an air-raid alert prompted by a large-scale Russian drone attack on Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran executes man accused of spying for Israel, allegedly trained by Mossad
stories.summary: Iran executed Ehsan Afrashteh, a man convicted of espionage for Israel. Authorities said he had been trained by the Israeli intelligence agency Mossad before his arrest and trial.

stories.title: Mali Plays Russian Roulette
stories.summary: The article examines recent violence in Mali that has exposed weaknesses in Russia's Kremlin-backed mercenary security model in the country. The incidents raise questions about the effectiveness of Russian private military forces in stabilizing the Sahel region.

stories.title: Six key takeaways about Iran’s missiles, two months into the war
stories.summary: An analysis examines six key takeaways about Iran's missile capabilities after more than ten weeks of conflict, including the importance of air defense systems and the risks posed by dwindling munitions stockpiles on both sides.

stories.title: In Sudan, both sides 'have taken the country to the dogs': Kenya's Ruto
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto, speaking at the conclusion of the Africa Forward Summit in Nairobi, discussed the war in Sudan and rejected claims he sides with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces. Ruto said both the Sudanese Armed Forces and the RSF bear responsibility for the country's devastation.

stories.title: Russia’s Oil Export Revenue Saw Continued Growth in April, IEA Says
stories.summary: Russia's oil export revenue rose to $19.18 billion in April, up $180 million from March, according to the International Energy Agency.

stories.title: UN may put Cyprus peace plan forward this year, Cypriot president says
stories.summary: Cypriot President Nikos Christodoulides said the United Nations is likely to launch a new push to resolve the decades-old division of Cyprus before Secretary-General António Guterres's term expires at the end of 2025.

stories.title: Netanyahu denies role in alleged 2009 efforts to broker Yediot-Israel Hayom understandings
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu denied involvement in alleged 2009 efforts by intermediaries to broker an arrangement between the newspapers Yediot Ahronot and Israel Hayom, which reportedly would have limited Israel Hayom's weekend edition in exchange for favorable coverage of Netanyahu and his family.

stories.title: Amid US-Israel war on Iran, Arizona awaits Iranian team before World Cup
stories.summary: A sports facility and football fans in Tucson, Arizona, are preparing to welcome Iran's national football team ahead of the World Cup, amid the ongoing U.S.-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: Four ejected from Eurovision for pro-Palestine activism during Israeli number
stories.summary: Four audience members were ejected from the Eurovision Song Contest after engaging in pro-Palestine protests during the Israeli entry's performance. The European Broadcasting Union confirmed the individuals were removed by security for disrupting the live broadcast.

stories.title: Speed, AI, and the platform that makes it operational
stories.summary: A sponsored piece discusses the causes of delays in cognitive operations staffing and promotes a platform integrating speed and artificial intelligence to address operational challenges.

stories.title: Pete Hegseth to headline DC faith rally with far-right and Christian nationalist speakers
stories.summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth will headline Rededicate 250, a faith rally on Washington DC's National Mall organized in partnership with the White House. The event's lineup includes speakers characterised by experts as Christian nationalist or extremist, including a pastor who called the Democratic platform "demonic."

stories.title: From Wagner to Eurovision: The debate over Jews in music - opinion
stories.summary: Several European countries have objected to Israel's participation in the 2026 Eurovision Song Contest, reigniting debate over the intersection of politics and cultural events.

stories.title: Philippine Senate in lockdown after gunshots fired
stories.summary: Police commandos entered the Philippine Senate building where a senator wanted by the International Criminal Court had taken refuge, prompting a lockdown after gunshots were fired inside the compound.

stories.title: Taiwan is a ‘model ally,’ not trade bait
stories.summary: A commentary argues that Taiwan should be treated as a valuable strategic ally rather than as a bargaining chip in U.S.-China negotiations. The piece contends that trading Taiwan's security for rhetorical concessions from Beijing would constitute a major strategic error.

stories.title: Nicolas Tenzer: stop talking about peace, the question is victory
stories.summary: French geopolitical expert Nicolas Tenzer discussed his book "Our War," arguing against peace negotiations with what he describes as Putin's nihilist regime and calling for European strategic autonomy independent of Washington.

stories.title: Israeli strikes on cars in southern Lebanon kill 12, health ministry says
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes hit seven cars on a highway south of Beirut in southern Lebanon, killing at least 12 people, including two children, according to Lebanon's health ministry.

stories.title: Wait, Sophie the Giraffe isn't French?
stories.summary: French investigative outlet Mediapart revealed that Sophie the Giraffe, long marketed as a French-made teething toy, has actually been manufactured in China for decades. The toy's producer, Vulli, is now under a fraud investigation over the misrepresentation of the product's origin.

stories.title: DIU: Russia launches combined attack on critical infrastructure
stories.summary: On May 13, Russia launched a combined air strike targeting critical infrastructure across Ukraine, which Ukrainian military intelligence said could be prolonged in nature.

stories.title: Africa should 'let the past be' and welcome all foreign investment, says mogul Elumelu
stories.summary: Nigerian businessman Tony Elumelu, speaking at the Africa Forward summit co-hosted by France and Kenya, urged African nations to welcome all foreign investment and private global capital.

stories.title: Romanians fearful as Danube Delta targeted by Russian attacks
stories.summary: Several heads of state, including Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, gathered in Bucharest for the B9 summit of NATO's eastern flank countries. Romania faces growing security concerns as Russian attacks on Ukrainian Danube ports have intensified near the Romanian border in recent months.

stories.title: Putin hails Russia's test launch of new Sarmat nuclear missile, calls it 'most powerful'
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin announced the successful test launch of the Sarmat intercontinental ballistic missile, calling it the world's most powerful. Putin said Russia plans to deploy the nuclear-capable missile for combat duty by the end of 2025.

stories.title: Call for ‘independent’ inquiry removed from coalition bill establishing Oct. 7 probe
stories.summary: A clause calling for an independent inquiry was removed from an Israeli coalition bill establishing a probe into the October 7 attack. MK Kallner described the removal as a clerical error, while an updated draft would bar former senior military and intelligence officials from the panel.

stories.title: Iran says naval officers 'accidentally' entered Kuwaiti waters
stories.summary: Iran rejected Kuwait's detention of four Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps officers, stating they entered Kuwaiti waters accidentally. Kuwait had accused the officers of attempting to infiltrate the country.

stories.title: Mossad chief, Shin Bet head visited UAE to coordinate during Operation Roaring Lion - report
stories.summary: Mossad chief and Shin Bet head reportedly visited the UAE to coordinate during Operation Roaring Lion, following Wall Street Journal reports that the UAE was behind recent strikes on Iranian assets, including attacks on Lavan Island's refinery in early April.

stories.title: 'Nothing is happening' in U.S.-Russia relations: Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov stated that "nothing is happening" in US-Russia relations. His remarks came despite President Trump's earlier re-establishment of dialogue with President Putin and repeated promises to end the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Xi-Trump summit: The humble soybean at the heart of a trade dispute between the US and China
stories.summary: Soybeans have become a key element in the US-China trade dispute. China halted purchases of US soybeans after Washington launched tariffs, but resumed buying following a truce between Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump last October. The durability of renewed soybean trade remains uncertain.

stories.title: Inside the world’s only Bonobo rescue sanctuary in DRC
stories.summary: A rescue sanctuary on the outskirts of Kinshasa in the Democratic Republic of Congo cares for orphaned bonobos, the world's most endangered great ape, found only in the DRC.

stories.title: King Charles III lays out UK government agenda as Starmer's job hangs in the balance
stories.summary: King Charles III delivered the ceremonial speech outlining the UK government's legislative agenda, focusing on energy policy, defense, and national security. Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces mounting pressure from within his own Labour Party amid calls for his resignation.

stories.title: Russians attack minibus with drone in central Kherson: Injury toll climbs to seven
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a minibus with a drone in central Kherson, injuring at least seven people.

stories.title: Bahamas re-elects Progressive Liberal party’s Philip Davis as prime minister
stories.summary: Bahamas Prime Minister Philip Davis and his Progressive Liberal Party won re-election, making him the country's first leader to serve a second consecutive term in nearly 30 years. Davis pledged to expand opportunity and strengthen security across the islands.

stories.title: Fabled Argentine city Ushuaia tries to shrug off hantavirus suspicions
stories.summary: The Argentine city of Ushuaia, a major departure point for Antarctic expeditions, is under scrutiny as a possible source of a hantavirus outbreak that killed three passengers aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius, which departed the Patagonian port on April 1.

stories.title: REPLAY: King Charles lays out Starmer's agenda as PM fights for survival
stories.summary: King Charles III presented Prime Minister Keir Starmer's legislative program during a ceremonial Parliament opening on Wednesday. Starmer faces calls to resign from within the Labour Party following poor results in local elections, casting uncertainty over his political future.

stories.title: What does Pentagon chief Hegseth’s presence in China say about Trump’s military agenda?
stories.summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's inclusion in President Trump's delegation to Beijing signals both sides' willingness to strengthen military communications. Analysts suggest the visit indicates US arms sales to Taiwan will feature in discussions, with China's Defence Minister Dong Jun expected to participate in talks.

stories.title: Iraq downplays reports of ‘secret’ Israeli base, while sending troops to find it - analysis
stories.summary: Iraq's government downplayed reports of a secret Israeli military base on its territory while deploying troops to search for it. Iraq's military was instructed to defend the country so it would not serve as a launchpad for aggression against neighboring states.

stories.title: Beijing’s Quest for Uniformity May Be Its Achilles’ Heel
stories.summary: The article argues that Beijing's policies of forced cultural and ethnic assimilation are proving counterproductive for China. The analysis suggests that the drive for uniformity may represent a significant strategic vulnerability.

stories.title: Beijing’s Quest for Uniformity May Be Its Achilles’ Heel
stories.summary: An analysis argues that China's policies of forced assimilation of ethnic and cultural minorities may undermine the country's long-term interests. The piece suggests Beijing's pursuit of uniformity could prove to be a strategic vulnerability.

stories.title: Hezbollah launches biggest drone swarm attack yet on Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah launched its largest coordinated drone swarm attack to date against a target in northern Israel, raising concerns about the group's increasingly sophisticated unmanned aerial vehicle capabilities.

stories.title: ‘Going to do whatever is necessary’: Trump on Russian oil waiver; forecasts inflation drop after Iran war
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump discussed potential waivers on Russian oil and predicted that inflationary pressures would ease sharply after the Iran war concludes. He described the US economy as heading toward what he called a "Golden Age."

stories.title: EU won’t ban LGBTQ ‘conversion therapy’ but will push states to act
stories.summary: The European Union announced it will not impose a bloc-wide ban on so-called LGBTQ conversion therapy but will encourage member states to act against such practices. The decision falls short of demands from a petition signed by over one million people calling for a prohibition across the 27-member bloc.

stories.title: Negev desert wins recognition as unique international wine region
stories.summary: Israel's Negev desert region, stretching from Kiryat Gat to Eilat and home to about 60 winemakers, received international recognition as a distinct wine terroir appellation after demonstrating an identifiable wine profile.

stories.title: Pentagon says U.S. cost of Iran war nearing $29 billion
stories.summary: The Pentagon estimated the US cost of the Iran war at nearly $29 billion. Pentagon finance chief Jules Hurst III said teams are continuously updating the figure as expenditures mount.

stories.title: Gunfire erupts in Philippine Senate amid ICC arrest bid for senator
stories.summary: Gunfire erupted inside the Philippine Senate as authorities attempted to arrest Senator Ronald dela Rosa, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court on charges of crimes against humanity related to former President Rodrigo Duterte's anti-drug campaign. The cause of the shooting and any casualties were not immediately confirmed.

stories.title: Baltic nations ponder biggest bang for their bucks in $14 billion arms spending spree
stories.summary: Baltic nations are evaluating how to allocate approximately $14 billion in planned arms spending. Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda emphasized that defense manufacturing and frontline military needs are now closely interconnected.

stories.title: War, Pandemics, and the Struggle for Healthcare Security
stories.summary: An analysis highlights the need for countries to prepare for the combined threats of pandemics and supply chain disruptions. The piece emphasizes the intersection of armed conflict and public health security challenges.

stories.title: OPT fraud: 10,000 foreign students, including Indians, under U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement scanner
stories.summary: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement is investigating approximately 10,000 foreign students, including Indian nationals, suspected of fraud in the Optional Practical Training program. ICE acting director Todd Lyons warned against security threats from the foreign student programme.

stories.title: Trump needs Xi much more than Xi needs Trump
stories.summary: Ahead of a summit between U.S. President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, analysts suggest Beijing holds greater leverage over Washington as the ongoing Iran conflict reshapes global power dynamics.

stories.title: Israel tech firms can locate and identify Starlink users
stories.summary: Israeli technology firms have developed capabilities to locate and identify users of SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet service, which has been used by Ukrainians during the war, Iranian protesters, and aid workers in Gaza.

stories.title: Russia’s noisy central-bank drama hides a quiet trap underneath
stories.summary: Russia's central bank is facing internal institutional tensions, though analysts suggest the underlying economic vulnerabilities persist regardless of leadership changes at the bank.

stories.title: Russia targets Ukraine with more than 200 drones in daytime assault
stories.summary: Russia launched more than 200 drones against Ukraine in a large-scale daytime assault on Wednesday, following an earlier barrage that killed at least eight civilians. The attacks came as Moscow and Kyiv traded long-range strikes after a brief ceasefire.

stories.title: Nigerian actor Alexx Ekubo dies at 40, industry mourns
stories.summary: Nigerian actor Alexx Ekubo died at the age of 40, with colleagues and close associates confirming the news.

stories.title: Naqvi says land-grabbing mafia, illegal constructions to be completely eradicated from Islamabad
stories.summary: Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi pledged to completely eradicate illegal constructions and land-grabbing operations in Islamabad. He said the ongoing "Operation Clean-up" would continue without pressure until its objectives are achieved.

stories.title: Why loyal wingman drones may be the future of global airpower
stories.summary: Breaking Defense launched a video series examining manned-unmanned teaming and the role of autonomous loyal wingman drones in the future of military aviation worldwide.

stories.title: Commuter train derails in Russia after 2 meters of track go missing; governor walks back initial suggestion of explosion
stories.summary: A commuter train on the Razumnoye–Tomarovka route derailed in the Yakovlevsky district of Russia's Belgorod region after approximately two meters of track went missing. Governor Vyacheslav Gladkov initially suggested an explosion may have been involved but later walked back that claim.

stories.title: Why Trump decided to back Iraq’s prime minister-designate, Ali al-Zaidi
stories.summary: The Trump administration has signaled support for Iraq's prime minister-designate Ali al-Zaidi, with U.S. backing contingent on demonstrable progress in curtailing pro-Iran militia operations inside Iraq.

stories.title: East Africa: Truck Drivers' Protest Cripples Trade Flow At Uganda-Kenya Border
stories.summary: A one-day truck drivers' strike at the Malaba border crossing between Uganda and Kenya disrupted cross-border trade, with authorities estimating revenue losses of up to 35 billion Ugandan shillings.

stories.title: Another minor injured in Sumy region due to enemy attacks
stories.summary: A 17-year-old boy was injured in a Russian drone attack in the Bilopillia community of Ukraine's Sumy region and was hospitalized overnight. The incident is the latest in a series of enemy attacks causing civilian casualties in the area.

stories.title: Indians growing anxious as Modi asks them to cut on fuel
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has urged citizens to voluntarily reduce fuel consumption amid rising energy prices linked to the war in Iran. Residents say they are already struggling with the economic strain.

stories.title: Russia’s Central Bank records highest-ever cash demand during May holidays amid internet outages
stories.summary: Russia's central bank recorded its highest-ever demand for cash during the May 2026 holiday period, according to Russian outlet RBC. The surge coincided with widespread internet outages across the country.

stories.title: Israeli strikes on highway south of Beirut kill 8, including 2 children, Lebanon says
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on a highway south of Beirut killed at least eight people, including two children, according to Lebanese authorities. The IDF said it was targeting Hezbollah in the area after issuing evacuation warnings for seven villages in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: West Pointers can be trained to better evaluate, appreciate AI, study finds
stories.summary: New research conducted at West Point suggests that cadets can be trained to better evaluate and appreciate artificial intelligence. The findings may inform efforts to harness AI's potential for both military battlefield applications and broader societal use.

stories.title: France locks down 1,700 on cruise ship after 90-year-old dies
stories.summary: French authorities confined more than 1,700 passengers and crew aboard the British cruise ship Ambition docked in Bordeaux after a 90-year-old passenger died. Dozens also reported stomach illness. Health officials said there was no connection to the recent hantavirus scare.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones strike port in southern Russia, injuring 2 and sparking fire
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the port of Taman in Krasnodar Krai, southern Russia, overnight on May 13, injuring at least one person and igniting a fire at a facility in the village of Volna in the Temryuk district.

stories.title: Gunshots ring out at Philippine Senate where lawmaker is holed up
stories.summary: Gunshots were reported at the Philippine Senate, where former national police chief and Senator Ronald dela Rosa, who served under ex-President Rodrigo Duterte, is holed up while facing an International Criminal Court arrest warrant.

stories.title: Activist confronts Iran’s former crown prince over war on Iran
stories.summary: An activist publicly confronted Reza Pahlavi, Iran's former crown prince, over his stance on the ongoing war against Iran.

stories.title: Russian Police Issue Arrest Warrant for Ex-Deputy Minister Who Reportedly Fled Country
stories.summary: Russian police issued an arrest warrant for Denis Butsayev, who resigned as deputy minister at the Natural Resources and Environment Ministry in late April. Reports suggest he may have fled to the United States amid a fraud investigation involving people close to him.

stories.title: What is Jerusalem Day and the March of Flags?
stories.summary: Jerusalem Day is an annual Israeli commemoration that features the March of Flags through Jerusalem's Old City. The event has increasingly become a focal point for settlers and ultra-nationalist Israelis, accompanied by rising attacks on Palestinians.

stories.title: UAE-owned tanker leaks some fuel off Oman following Iran strike
stories.summary: A UAE-owned tanker leaked fuel off the coast of Oman after being struck by Iranian drones the previous week, according to the vessel's operating company.

stories.title: Israeli attacks on Gaza increased by 35% since Iran ceasefire: Report
stories.summary: The conflict monitoring group ACLED reported that Israeli attacks on Gaza rose by 35% in April, noting the increase followed the ceasefire between the U.S.-led coalition and Iran.

stories.title: Netanyahu's Iran expectations are 'far from reality,' former PM Ehud Barak says
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Barak criticized Benjamin Netanyahu's expectations regarding Iran, saying they are far from reality and expressing concern over Netanyahu's handling of national security and military strategy.

stories.title: Iran has regained access to most missile and underground sites, US intelligence finds
stories.summary: U.S. intelligence assessments indicate that Iran has regained access to most of its missile and underground military sites. The findings, reported by The New York Times, suggest Tehran's military capabilities are stronger than Trump administration officials have publicly stated.

stories.title: Human rights commissioner reports record number of civilian war casualties in 2025
stories.summary: Ukraine's human rights commissioner reported a record number of civilian war casualties in 2025, with Russia killing 2,514 people and wounding more than 12,000. Since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion, more than 15,000 Ukrainian civilians have been killed.

stories.title: World Emunah: The women who are holding Israel together
stories.summary: The article profiles World Emunah and the role of Israeli women in sustaining communities through daily resilience work, describing contributions that often go unrecognized.

stories.title: Who holds the cards at the Trump-Xi summit in Beijing?
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump arrived in Beijing on Wednesday for his first visit to China since 2017. Analysts suggest the two-day summit with President Xi Jinping could mark a turning point in US-China relations, potentially favoring Beijing.

stories.title: South Asia must make water a top priority
stories.summary: Scientists warn that South Asia faces an early and severe summer, with above-average April temperatures and a potential "super El Niño" threatening heatwaves and below-average monsoon rainfall. Parts of Pakistan, India, and Nepal are expected to be particularly affected, straining water resources, agriculture, and public health.

stories.title: Scepticism and tight security as Beijing braces for Trump visit
stories.summary: Beijing prepared with tight security and public scepticism ahead of President Trump's arrival for a state visit. Chinese nationalism has grown amid perceptions of US decline, and Trump has reportedly lost the novelty value he held during his 2017 visit.

stories.title: Irish TV to air Father Ted episode instead of Eurovision final
stories.summary: Ireland's national broadcaster RTÉ announced it would air a classic Father Ted Eurovision parody episode instead of broadcasting the Eurovision 2026 final, in protest over Israel's participation in the contest.

stories.title: Coalition to link immigration limits to new builds as Taylor says ‘migration has run miles ahead of housing’
stories.summary: Australian opposition leader Angus Taylor plans to announce a policy directly linking temporary immigration intake to the number of new homes built nationally. The Coalition proposal would use housing completion figures as a hard ceiling for overseas arrivals, to be outlined in his budget reply speech on Thursday.

stories.title: Nigeria: Court Jails Ex-Minister Mamman for 75 Years Over Power Project Fraud
stories.summary: A Nigerian court sentenced former minister Mamman to 75 years in prison over power project fraud, ordering that sentences on all 12 counts run consecutively rather than concurrently.

stories.title: Lukashenka announces war preparations—Ukrainian official calls it Russian “information agenda”
stories.summary: Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko announced war-readiness preparations, which a Ukrainian official characterized as part of Russia's information agenda. Analysts note Belarus could maintain such a readiness regime indefinitely without launching an invasion.

stories.title: Israel and favorite Finland advance to the Eurovision final
stories.summary: Finland and Israel were among ten countries that advanced to the Eurovision Song Contest final after the first semifinal round. Five countries — Spain, Ireland, the Netherlands, Slovenia, and Iceland — are boycotting the contest's 70th anniversary edition to protest Israel's participation.

stories.title: Trump lands in Beijing for first summit with Xi in China since 2017
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump landed in Beijing on Wednesday for a three-day state visit, his first trip to the Chinese capital in nearly nine years. The summit with President Xi Jinping will address the trade truce from Busan, the US-Israeli war on Iran, technological rivalry, and other disputes.

stories.title: US pressures mount on Iraq's incoming Ali Al-Zaidi government
stories.summary: The incoming Iraqi government of Prime Minister-designate Ali al-Zaidi faces mounting U.S. pressure, described as unprecedented since the 2003 U.S. invasion and the overthrow of Saddam Hussein's regime.

stories.title: Ahead of Trump-Xi summit, China warns on US arms sales to Taiwan
stories.summary: China reiterated its opposition to US arms sales to Taiwan ahead of President Donald Trump's arrival in Beijing for a summit with President Xi Jinping. Beijing views democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory and considers US weapons sales to Taipei a key point of contention.

stories.title: Iran hangs man on Israel spy charges, sixth since war started
stories.summary: Iran executed a 32-year-old man convicted of spying for Israel, the sixth such execution since the start of the war. Human rights groups allege the conviction was based on a forced confession.

stories.title: Gunshots fired in Philippines senate in standoff with senator Ronald dela Rosa
stories.summary: Gunshots were fired at the Philippine Senate as Senator Ronald dela Rosa, wanted by the International Criminal Court for alleged crimes against humanity related to former President Duterte's drug war, remained barricaded inside the building for a second day. It remains unclear who fired the shots or why military troops were present.

stories.title: Trump vows to push Xi to 'open up' China at superpower summit
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said he would urge Chinese President Xi Jinping to "open up" China to American businesses during a high-stakes summit in Beijing. Trump also indicated the Iran war would be discussed during the meetings.

stories.title: Gunshots fired as chaos erupts at Philippine Senate
stories.summary: Gunshots were fired at the Philippine Senate on Wednesday as tensions escalated over the anticipated arrest of Senator Ronald dela Rosa, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court. Military personnel carrying assault rifles were seen arriving at the building. It was unclear who fired the shots.

stories.title: Trump heads to China, says no need for Xi's help on Iran war
stories.summary: President Donald Trump departed for Beijing for a summit with President Xi Jinping, stating he does not expect to need China's help to end the war with Iran. The conflict has continued to block maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries one-fifth of the world's oil supply.

stories.title: Africa Forward Summit concludes with key France-Kenya agreement
stories.summary: The Africa Forward summit concluded in Nairobi with French President Emmanuel Macron and Kenyan President William Ruto signing the Nairobi Declaration. They plan to bring the agreement to the G7 summit, which France will host in Evian in June.

stories.title: Rwanda: Where Rwanda's Rwf7.8tn Budget Will Go in 2026/27
stories.summary: Rwanda's government proposed a budget of 7.8 trillion Rwandan francs for the 2026/27 fiscal year, an increase of 844.2 billion francs over the revised 2025/26 budget.

stories.title: Ukraine imposes sanctions on companies involved in production of Russian missiles, says Vlasiuk
stories.summary: Ukraine imposed a new package of sanctions targeting companies and intermediaries involved in manufacturing Russian missiles and supplying critical components to Russia's defence industry. Kyiv said it would share information on the sanctioned entities with international partners.

stories.title: Why Israel bombs Iranian universities and silences American ones
stories.summary: Israeli strikes hit Sharif University of Technology in Tehran in April 2026, part of what scholars have described as a broader campaign against Iranian academic institutions. The article draws a parallel with restrictions on academic expression at American universities.

stories.title: US-based internet suicide forum implicated in 160 UK deaths fined £950,000
stories.summary: UK regulator Ofcom fined a US-based internet suicide forum £950,000 under the Online Safety Act after linking it to over 160 UK deaths. The site remained accessible in the UK despite more than a year of warnings, with campaigners criticising the regulator's slow response.

stories.title: Mozambique: Mobs Lynch Dozens After Accusations of Witchcraft
stories.summary: At least 60 people have been lynched across Mozambique over the past month after being accused of using witchcraft to steal or shrink penises. The panic began in Cabo Delgado province on April 18 and has since spread to all provinces.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigeria's Kidnappers Exploit Online Public Empathy to Extract Higher Ransoms
stories.summary: Kidnappers in Nigeria are reportedly exploiting online crowdfunding campaigns organized to rescue hostages, using the public visibility of such campaigns to set higher ransom demands.

stories.title: Don’t bury Gaza while its people live
stories.summary: Analyst Alex Foley argues that pro-Palestinian messaging risks reinforcing despair by focusing solely on Gaza's physical destruction, rather than highlighting the resilience and resistance of its people.

stories.title: Bolivian prosecutors confirm they will seek 20 years in prison for Evo Morales on trafficking charges
stories.summary: Bolivian prosecutors confirmed they will seek a 20-year prison sentence against former President Evo Morales on aggravated human trafficking charges. Prosecutors allege Morales had a relationship with a 15-year-old girl during his second term. The case proceeds despite Morales's absence and a fresh arrest warrant.

stories.title: Iran war pushes Asia’s Gulf migrants to use stablecoins for remittances
stories.summary: Asian migrant workers in Gulf states are turning to stablecoins as an alternative remittance channel amid fears that the Iran war and potential US sanctions could disrupt traditional money transfers. Remittances from Gulf-based workers account for 3–5% of GDP in several emerging markets and up to 10% in Nepal.

stories.title: Netherlands protests US proposal to further bar chip giant ASML from China market
stories.summary: The Dutch government has formally objected to a proposed US law that would further restrict semiconductor equipment maker ASML from selling to and servicing customers in China. ASML, the global leader in lithographic chipmaking technology, has already seen its China market access significantly curtailed by existing US sanctions.

stories.title: Iran war to cast a shadow on BRICS FM meeting in Delhi
stories.summary: The ongoing Iran conflict is expected to dominate the BRICS foreign ministers' meeting in Delhi, with Iran urging India to use the gathering to build consensus condemning U.S. and Israeli military strikes.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drone Attack Sparks Fire at Gas Plant in Astrakhan Region
stories.summary: Authorities in Russia's Astrakhan region reported that drone debris caused a fire at the Astrakhan Gas Processing Plant, a major facility in the Caspian Sea region. The incident was attributed to a Ukrainian drone attack.

stories.title: Nissan ponders building cars for Chinese rivals at Sunderland plant
stories.summary: Nissan CEO Ivan Espinosa confirmed the company is considering manufacturing cars for other automakers at its Sunderland plant in the UK, amid talks with China's Chery. The Japanese carmaker reported steep losses for the year to March, putting its 6,000 Sunderland workers' future in focus.

stories.title: Celebrities sign petition defending Southbank Centre head over Golders Green comments
stories.summary: More than 250 celebrities signed a letter defending Southbank Centre chair Misan Harriman after he faced criticism in British media for comments about a Muslim victim of the April 29 attack in Golders Green, London, and about Reform UK's local election victories.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Students Demand Return of Free Education As Fees Crisis Deepens
stories.summary: The Zimbabwe National Students Union called on the government to reinstate free education, warning that rising school fees and deteriorating learning conditions are forcing thousands of children out of school.

stories.title: Border Police seize over 10,000 cannabis plants located in 18 greenhouses in southern Israel
stories.summary: Israeli Border Police seized more than 10,000 cannabis plants found in 18 greenhouses in southern Israel. The seizure was part of a broader operation to locate and destroy illegal drug cultivation sites across the region.

stories.title: Hong Kong Airport Authority takes over 11 Skies retail from New World: sources
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Airport Authority has taken over retail operations of the 2.66 million square foot 11 Skies complex from New World Development ahead of Terminal 2's opening. The authority assumed control of about 70% of the project's retail and dining space.

stories.title: Gaza sisters win prize for turning rubble into reusable bricks
stories.summary: Two displaced Palestinian teenage sisters, Farah and Tala, won a prize for developing a method to convert rubble in Gaza into reusable bricks.

stories.title: Pennsylvania judge leaves Democrats over party’s ‘coddling’ of antisemitism
stories.summary: Pennsylvania Supreme Court Justice David Wecht left the Democratic Party, citing what he called the party's failure to confront antisemitism, which he said had moved from the fringes to its mainstream.

stories.title: Trump faces slew of ‘bad options’ on Iran as diplomacy falters
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump faces limited options on Iran as diplomatic efforts have stalled, with growing domestic discontent and rising geopolitical stakes complicating the administration's strategy.

stories.title: East Africa: EAC Launches Ushirikiano Imara 2026 Security Exercise in Nairobi
stories.summary: Military, police, and civilian personnel from East African Community member states gathered in Nairobi for the launch of the 14th EAC Armed Forces Command Post Exercise, Ushirikiano Imara 2026, focused on regional peace and security cooperation.

stories.title: UN urges independent probes into deadly Nigeria, Chad air attacks
stories.summary: The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights called for independent investigations into airstrikes by Nigerian and Chadian forces that reportedly killed over 100 civilians.

stories.title: Russian forces hit Hlukhiv this morning, destroying educational institution
