stories.summary: North Korea's arms industry has reportedly expanded to approximately 300 defense factories employing 500,000 workers, driven by Russia's demand for artillery shells for its war in Ukraine. North Korean officials claim current shell production has quadrupled compared to normal levels.

stories.title: UK sending warship to Hormuz, says defence ministry
stories.summary: The United Kingdom announced it will deploy the destroyer HMS Dragon to the Strait of Hormuz as part of a multinational coalition jointly led by the UK and France to secure the strategic waterway when conditions allow.

stories.title: Israeli forces bomb Gaza home after evacuation orders
stories.summary: Israeli forces issued evacuation orders and then bombed a home in Gaza, marking the first time since the October ceasefire that Israel has used such orders before conducting strikes in the territory.

stories.title: Traffic advisory issued ahead of Marka-i-Haq event in Islamabad
stories.summary: Islamabad authorities issued a traffic advisory for May 10 ahead of a Marka-i-Haq anniversary ceremony at the National Monument at Zero Point. Top civilian and military leadership were expected to attend the event celebrating Pakistani forces' victory against India the previous May.

stories.title: Settlers dig up Palestinian grave near Sha-Nur, forcing family to relocate burial
stories.summary: Near the Sha-Nur settlement in the occupied West Bank, Israeli settlers reportedly exhumed a Palestinian grave. Palestinian sources allege IDF soldiers assisted the settlers, while the IDF denies involvement and says the family relocated the body voluntarily.

stories.title: 9 May parade Russia held without single tank featured one thing Moscow has never shown before
stories.summary: Russia's May 9 Victory Day parade in Moscow's Red Square was held without a single tank for the first time, featuring instead a display the Kremlin had not previously shown publicly. The scaled-down event reflected shifts in Russia's military posture.

stories.title: 100 Hong Kong-linked ships ‘stranded in Strait of Hormuz’ amid Middle East war
stories.summary: Approximately 100 Hong Kong-linked ships and an estimated 2,300 seafarers are stranded in the Strait of Hormuz due to the risk of attack amid the US-Israel war against Iran. Hong Kong Shipowners Association chairman Richard Hext said sailing through the strait remains very dangerous despite a recent temporary US-Iran ceasefire.

stories.title: Shortest military parade in modern Russian history held in Moscow
stories.summary: Russia's Victory Day parade on Red Square on May 9 lasted approximately 45 minutes, making it one of the shortest military parades in modern Russian history.

stories.title: Iran says will play World Cup, demands hosts accept conditions
stories.summary: Iran announced it will participate in the upcoming FIFA World Cup, scheduled from June 11 to July 19, but demanded that host organizers accept its conditions. Iran's participation had been uncertain leading up to the tournament.

stories.title: Iran says will play in World Cup, but demands soccer officials linked to IRGC be allowed
stories.summary: Iran said it will participate in the 2026 World Cup but demanded that soccer officials linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps be permitted entry. Both the US and Canada have indicated they will bar individuals connected to the IRGC, which is designated a terrorist organization.

stories.title: 'Atmosphere closer to wartime': Moscow’s muted Victory Day reflects growing security fears
stories.summary: Russia's scaled-down Victory Day celebrations on May 9 reflected heightened security concerns amid the ongoing war in Ukraine. Chatham House analyst Grégoire Roos told FRANCE 24 that internet shutdowns, tighter security, and fears of Ukrainian drone strikes created an atmosphere closer to wartime than national celebration.

stories.title: ‘A year of resistance’: Cuba’s private sector faces Trump’s oil blockade
stories.summary: The US oil blockade on Cuba is severely impacting the country's private sector, particularly small family-run businesses. Firms are struggling with chronic power outages and fuel shortages caused by the restrictions.

stories.title: Nigeria: National Security Adviser Ribadu Holds Talks With VP Vance and Secretary Rubio in Washington DC
stories.summary: Nigeria's National Security Adviser Ribadu held talks with US Vice President Vance and Secretary of State Rubio in Washington, DC. The discussions focused on deepening cooperation in security, counterterrorism, regional stability, and strategic partnership.

stories.title: Five reported killed, including girl, in Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon reportedly killed five people, including a girl. The IDF issued evacuation warnings to nine villages and said it struck 85 Hezbollah targets in southern Lebanon and an underground weapons site in the Beqaa Valley over the past day.

stories.title: Trump’s feuds, tensions with allies likely to outlast Iran war
stories.summary: Analysts suggest that diplomatic tensions between President Trump and traditional U.S. allies, intensified during the Iran war, are likely to persist beyond the conflict. Trump's actions have revived concerns among partners about American reliability in future crises.

stories.title: Ukraine's defense minister shows AI turret used in combat to intercept drones on battlefield
stories.summary: Ukraine's defense minister showcased an AI-powered turret designed to intercept enemy drones on the battlefield. The system was developed through the Brave1 defense technology cluster and is already in active combat use.

stories.title: At UN, Pakistan raises alarm at Israel's systematic annexation of occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Pakistan's UN Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad raised concerns at an Arria-formula meeting about Israel's systematic annexation of the occupied West Bank, expansion of illegal settlements, and forced displacement of Palestinians. He called for international community intervention.

stories.title: ‘Watching us is like watching a cousin’: the online creators reshaping Africa’s news ecosphere
stories.summary: African online creators are reshaping how current affairs are consumed across the continent. South African TikTok creator Amahle-Imvelo Jaxa gained 100,000 followers in three days after posting a viral video about South African peacekeepers in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and tensions between the South African and Rwandan presidents.

stories.title: Trump airport branding deal opens new route to profit for family
stories.summary: A licensing and merchandising agreement at a renamed Florida airport grants President Donald Trump's family a new revenue stream. The deal emerged as Spirit Airlines ceased operations, citing high fuel prices linked to the U.S.-Iran conflict.

stories.title: Beijing urges France to respect one-China principle during high-level talks
stories.summary: Chinese top diplomat Wang Yi held talks in Beijing with French presidential adviser Emmanuel Bonne, urging France to respect the one-China principle. Wang called for strengthening the China-France strategic partnership free from external interference.

stories.title: US-Iran war no closer to ending as Gulf clashes flare
stories.summary: The United States and Iran traded fire in the Strait of Hormuz despite a month-old ceasefire, with the UAE coming under renewed attack. A US intelligence assessment concluded that Iran could withstand a naval blockade for months.

stories.title: Israel allocates $345m for bypass roads in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Israel's National Bureau for Defending Land and Resisting Settlements reported that Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich and Transportation Minister Miri Regev approved 1 billion shekels ($345 million) for bypass road construction on Palestinian lands in the occupied West Bank, adding to $2.4 billion previously allocated.

stories.title: Moscow marks Victory Day with a scaled down Red Square parade under tight security
stories.summary: Russia held its annual Victory Day parade on May 9 in Moscow's Red Square under heightened security and in a scaled-down format, with no tanks, missiles, or heavy equipment. President Vladimir Putin vowed to achieve victory in Ukraine. North Korean troops participated in the parade.

stories.title: May 5 strike on Kramatorsk: Deputy head of district administration dies in hospital
stories.summary: Roman Simashov, deputy head of the Kramatorsk District State Administration, died in hospital from injuries sustained in a Russian strike on Kramatorsk on May 5.

stories.title: Indonesian rescuers retrieve body from Mount Dukono as search continues
stories.summary: Rescuers recovered the body of an Indonesian woman killed during a volcanic eruption on Mount Dukono on Halmahera island, while search operations continued for two missing Singaporeans. The 20 hikers had climbed the volcano despite safety restrictions before the eruption on Friday.

stories.title: Iran says it will play at 2026 World Cup if hosts address ‘concerns’
stories.summary: Iran stated it is willing to participate in the 2026 FIFA World Cup, provided host nations address its concerns. Iran's participation has been uncertain since the US and Israel launched military operations against the country.

stories.title: Conflict inflames tensions at Venice Biennale of Art
stories.summary: Russia returned to the Venice Biennale of Art after being absent since its February 2022 invasion of Ukraine, sparking international outcry and inflaming tensions among participating nations over the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Bahrain arrests 41 individuals linked with Iran's IRGC terrorist activities in the Kingdom
stories.summary: Bahrain arrested 41 individuals accused of forming the core of an IRGC-linked network in the kingdom. Authorities charged them with espionage for foreign entities and sympathy with what Bahrain described as Iranian aggression.

stories.title: Indian sailor killed in dhow fire near Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: An Indian sailor was killed in a fire aboard a dhow near the Strait of Hormuz. The remaining crew members were rescued by a passing vessel in the area.

stories.title: Guardian reporter and colleagues detained and beaten by Somali police
stories.summary: Guardian journalist Mohamed Bulbul and two colleagues, Abdihafid Nor Barre and Abdishakur Mohamed Mohamud, were detained and beaten by Somalia's US-trained counter-terrorism police in Mogadishu after Bulbul reported on a woman allegedly tortured in prison.

stories.title: UK Jews’ fears grow as Green, Reform surge elects candidates accused of antisemitism
stories.summary: In UK local elections, the Green Party and Reform UK saw gains, electing candidates who have been accused of espousing antisemitic views and anti-Israel conspiracy theories, raising concerns among British Jewish communities.

stories.title: Moscow begins scaled-back Victory Day parade as 3-day Ukraine truce kicks in
stories.summary: Russia held its annual Victory Day parade on Moscow's Red Square on Saturday with scaled-back events amid security concerns. A three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine took effect for the occasion, following an appeal from US President Donald Trump.

stories.title: Russian drone attack in Zaporizhzhia region damages house, evacuation vehicle, injures two
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack in the Zaporizhzhia region injured two people after one UAV struck a residential house and another hit an evacuation vehicle.

stories.title: Israel set to release two Gaza flotilla activists, representatives say
stories.summary: Two Gaza flotilla activists — a Spanish national and a Brazilian national — are set to be released from Israeli detention after being captured in international waters aboard a humanitarian aid vessel bound for Gaza. A rights group representing them reported they suffered abuse in Israeli prison.

stories.title: Why U.S. Project Freedom couldn’t secure free navigation in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The US initiative known as Project Freedom failed to secure free navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. President Donald Trump cited progress in negotiations with Iran as the reason for calling off the operation.

stories.title: Rosenberg: Scaled-back Victory Parade in Moscow's Red Square
stories.summary: The BBC's Russia editor reported from Moscow that the annual Victory Day military parade on Red Square was quieter and more scaled back than in previous years.

stories.title: Putin attends WW2 victory parade, worries deepen over Ukraine
stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin attended Russia's annual World War II Victory Day parade in Moscow, where soldiers and sailors — some of whom served in Ukraine — marched before Putin and Russian veterans.

stories.title: Officer who cracked serial rapist Worboys case says justice system ‘close to exploding’
stories.summary: Former senior investigating officer Tim Grattan-Kane, who led the arrest of London black-cab rapist John Worboys in 2008, has warned that similar drug-facilitated sexual assaults may still be occurring. He cited the rise of drink spiking and an overstretched criminal justice system that he described as being "close to exploding."

stories.title: Meet China’s moon porter for Chang’e-8 mission: a 4-wheeled robot with 2 arms
stories.summary: China's Hong Kong University of Science and Technology developed a four-wheeled, dual-armed robot rover to serve as an AI-powered porter for the Chang'e-8 lunar mission, scheduled for 2029. The 100-kilogram robot will transport and deploy instruments on the moon's surface.

stories.title: Ukraine-Russia talks at impasse, but US ready to mediate if opportunity arises – Rubio
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that peace talks between Ukraine and Russia are at a standstill. He said the United States remains ready to mediate if an opportunity to resume negotiations arises.

stories.title: Iran's 'fake opposition': The controversial campaign to legitimize the MEK
stories.summary: The People's Mojahedin Organization of Iran (MEK) has evolved from a student-led Marxist movement into an exiled group advocating regime change in Tehran. The organization remains highly controversial, with critics questioning a campaign to legitimize its standing.

stories.title: 'Disposable spies': Poland records unprecedented number of Russian espionage cases
stories.summary: Poland's internal security service, the ABW, reported an unprecedented number of Russian espionage and hybrid attack cases on Polish territory since 2024. Researchers noted that Russian intelligence services have employed amateur "single-use agents" to lay the groundwork for more complex operations against Poland.

stories.title: Pakistan, Bangladesh sign agreement to combat drug trafficking
stories.summary: Pakistan and Bangladesh signed a memorandum of understanding to strengthen cooperation against drug trafficking and narcotics abuse during Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi's visit to Dhaka. Both countries also agreed to establish a secretary-level joint working group.

stories.title: Israeli strikes pound southern Lebanon, hit targets elsewhere
stories.summary: Israeli forces continued striking southern Lebanon, issuing near-daily evacuation orders despite an existing truce. The strikes have killed scores of people across the region.

stories.title: Israel orders nine south Lebanon villages evacuated amid strikes
stories.summary: Israel issued evacuation orders for nine villages in southern Lebanon amid ongoing airstrikes that have killed scores of people. Such orders have become a near-daily occurrence despite a truce being in place.

stories.title: British PM Starmer vows to fight on after local polls drubbing
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer vowed to continue governing after his Labour Party suffered significant losses in local elections. Starmer declared he was "not going to walk away" despite the electoral setback.

stories.title: 'No Other Land' filmmaker warns UN of Israeli settler violence
stories.summary: Basel Adra, Oscar-winning co-director of the documentary 'No Other Land,' addressed the UN Security Council about increasing Israeli settler violence. He urged the body to take action against the escalating attacks.

stories.title: Palestinian Christian body warns EU they are under existential threat
stories.summary: A delegation from the Higher Presidential Committee for Church Affairs in Palestine met EU officials in Brussels to warn that Israeli policies threaten the survival of the Palestinian Christian community. Reverend Dr Mitri Raheb highlighted the dramatic decline in the Palestinian Christian population during the meeting.

stories.title: Canvas cyberattack: Disruptions aplenty as universities cancel or postpone exams, assignments
stories.summary: The Canvas learning management platform, operated by Instructure, suffered a cyberattack after staff detected unauthorized activity on April 29. The disruption forced multiple universities to cancel or postpone exams and assignments.

stories.title: Israel kills five in Gaza in past day, raising death toll to 72,736
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed at least five Palestinians and wounded 15 in Gaza over the past day, according to medical sources. The cumulative death toll since October 2023 has reached 72,736, with 172,535 wounded. Rescue teams report that many victims remain trapped under rubble.

stories.title: Russia holds scaled-back WW2 victory parade as worries over war in Ukraine deepen
stories.summary: Russia held a scaled-back Victory Day parade on Red Square on May 9 to mark the Soviet Union's defeat of Nazi Germany. The event honors the 27 million Soviet citizens who died in World War II, though concerns over the war in Ukraine prompted reduced celebrations.

stories.title: SBU detains Russian agent in Odesa who plotted killing of senior Ukrainian Navy officer ahead of 'Victory Day'
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) detained a Russian agent in Odesa who was planning to assassinate a senior Ukrainian Navy officer ahead of Russia's Victory Day celebrations.

stories.title: Displaced Lebanese children keep learning amid displacement
stories.summary: A school in Sidon, southern Lebanon, is serving as a shelter for displaced families while continuing to hold classes for children uprooted by the conflict.

stories.title: Met Gala 2026 | When India showed up — with steel, saris and mangoes
stories.summary: Several Indian designers and celebrities attended the 2026 Met Gala in New York, incorporating traditional elements such as saris and cultural motifs into their outfits amid broader debate over billionaire patronage of the event.

stories.title: While Russia held its 9 May parade, Warsaw activists placed crosses and photos of killed Ukrainian children outside Russian Embassy
stories.summary: On May 9, activists from Euromaidan-Warsaw placed crosses and photos of killed Ukrainian children outside the Russian Embassy in Warsaw during Russia's Victory Day parade, calling Russia a terrorist state waging a genocidal war in Ukraine.

stories.title: UK local elections: "Starmer must address voters' frustration over change"
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces mounting pressure after the Labour Party suffered significant losses in local elections across England, Wales, and Scotland. Reform UK made notable gains in the contests. The results have prompted questions about Starmer's leadership less than a year after Labour returned to government.

stories.title: Russian forces launch eight attacks on Donetsk region over past day, one wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled Ukraine's Donetsk region eight times on May 8, injuring one person. The attacks damaged residential buildings and a gas pipeline in the area.

stories.title: Hong Kong home market maintains upwards momentum as eager buyers snap up new flats
stories.summary: Hong Kong's residential property market continued its upward trend as all 154 units at Sun Hung Kai Properties' Lime Spark project sold out, and 93% of Henderson Land's Highwood Phase 2 flats found buyers, with home prices rising nearly 8% in 2026.

stories.title: India, IOM discuss expanding, diversifying regular migration pathways
stories.summary: India's Minister of State for External Affairs Kirti Vardhan Singh held discussions with the International Organization for Migration on expanding and diversifying regular migration pathways. The talks also covered India's implementation of the Global Compact for Migration and IOM activities within the country.

stories.title: How Israel's creation mirrors Greek independence - and why it's overlooked - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece draws parallels between Israel's founding and Greece's independence, arguing both involved diaspora nationalism and population displacement. It contends that Israel faces disproportionate scrutiny compared to Greece.

stories.title: U.S. authorities cancel cruise ship worker visas as part of child sexual abuse images case
stories.summary: U.S. Customs and Border Protection reported that authorities boarded eight cruise ships in late April and identified 27 crew members, mostly from the Philippines, involved in child sexual abuse imagery offenses. The individuals' visas were cancelled. Charges relate to the receipt, possession, transportation, distribution, or viewing of such material.

stories.title: Israel police accused of assaulting Palestinian govt prosecutor
stories.summary: A Palestinian citizen of Israel employed as a government prosecutor was allegedly assaulted and arrested by Israeli police following a neighbour's complaint.

stories.title: Army exercises in Morocco focus on countering Sahel threats
stories.summary: The annual African Lion military exercise, held in Morocco for over two decades, brought together multiple foreign contingents for land, air, and naval drills focused on countering security threats emanating from the Sahel region.

stories.title: Russian Uragan MLRS can wipe out city block in 8.8 seconds. Ukraine just destroyed one of its loaders 40 km behind front
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces destroyed a loader for Russia's Uragan multiple-launch rocket system approximately 40 kilometers behind the front line using drones, after Russia had repositioned heavy equipment further from the front to avoid losses.

stories.title: Heroism and grief: 6 residents’ stories from Wang Fuk Court fire hearings
stories.summary: Residents of the fire-ravaged Wang Fuk Court estate in Hong Kong testified at public hearings, recounting acts of heroism, grief, and ignored safety warnings before the blaze — the city's deadliest in decades.

stories.title: ‘Largely slop’: Trump’s new counterterrorism strategy is scant on substance but heavy on enemies
stories.summary: The Trump administration released a 16-page counterterrorism strategy document authored by counter-terrorism adviser Sebastian Gorka. Critics have characterized the memo as light on substantive policy while heavily targeting political opponents, the Biden administration, and other groups. Gorka reportedly used vulgar language to dismiss critics of the administration's military engagement in Iran.

stories.title: ‘We’re going backwards’: Five civil rights activists slam the supreme court’s gutting of Voting Rights Act
stories.summary: Civil rights activists, including veterans of the 1965 Selma marches, have criticized the U.S. Supreme Court's recent decision to weaken the Voting Rights Act. Sheyann Webb-Christburg, who marched in Selma at age eight, called the ruling a means to silence voters. Organizers described it as part of a long history of Black voter disenfranchisement.

stories.title: ‘The worst kind of predator’: Louisiana pastor found guilty for third time of molesting teen boys
stories.summary: Terry Reed, a 66-year-old pastor from suburban New Orleans, Louisiana, has been convicted of sexually molesting two minors. This is the third time Reed has been found guilty of abusing teenage boys. Prosecutors said he used biblical verses to manipulate and justify his behavior, and he faces up to 40 years in prison.

stories.title: ‘Not decoupling’: what US-China trade data signals ahead of Xi-Trump summit
stories.summary: China's merchandise exports to the United States fell 10.2% year-on-year in early 2026 as President Trump prepares to visit Beijing for a summit with President Xi Jinping that could shape future economic relations between the two nations.

stories.title: Tehran could withstand blockade for four months, CIA report shows, as fighting flares
stories.summary: Fighting around the Strait of Hormuz escalated in early May 2026, marking the largest flare-ups since a ceasefire began a month earlier. The UAE came under renewed attack on May 8, 2026. A CIA report indicates Tehran could withstand a naval blockade for approximately four months.

stories.title: Ukraine marks Europe Day as integral part of European family – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky marked Europe Day by affirming Ukraine's place as an integral part of the European family, describing the celebration as reflecting a genuine commitment rather than a formality.

stories.title: Russia’s “Great Victory” cult wasn’t built in 1945 — it was constructed in 1965
stories.summary: An analysis argues that Russia's May 9 Victory Day commemoration is not an unbroken tradition from 1945 but was largely constructed as a national narrative beginning in 1965 under Soviet leadership.

stories.title: Israel doubts US optimism in Iran talks as critical issues on nuclear concessions remain unsolved
stories.summary: US officials have expressed optimism about a potential deal with Iran, but Israel remains skeptical. Israeli officials stress that significant unresolved differences persist between Washington and Tehran, particularly on nuclear concessions.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill at the least three in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes killed at least three people in the Tyre district of southern Lebanon on Saturday, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The strikes hit a car traveling near the Martyr Mohammed Saad High School between Burj Rahhal and al-Abbassieh.

stories.title: Starmer gives Brown and Harman new roles as pressure grows over election mauling – UK politics live
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer appointed former Prime Minister Gordon Brown as a special envoy on global finance and gave Harriet Harman a new role. The moves came as Starmer faces growing internal pressure over Labour's heavy election losses, with several frontbenchers reportedly suggesting his time in office should not extend beyond year's end.

stories.title: Bahrain arrests 41 over alleged links to Iran’s IRGC
stories.summary: Bahrain's interior minister announced the arrest of 41 individuals over alleged connections to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, according to the state news agency.

stories.title: Al-Qard Al-Hasan, Hezbollah main funding source, resumes activities despite IDF strikes during war
stories.summary: Al-Qard Al-Hasan, described as Hezbollah's main funding source, has resumed operations despite Israeli military strikes that targeted around 30 of its branches. The Saudi-owned Al-Arabiya network reported that a branch in Beirut's Haret Khreik neighborhood is again operational.

stories.title: US military kills two people in new eastern Pacific Ocean attack
stories.summary: The US military carried out a strike in the eastern Pacific Ocean that killed two people. It was the third such US attack in the region during May alone.

stories.title: Trump's feuds, tensions with allies likely to outlast Iran war
stories.summary: President Donald Trump's decisions to withdraw some U.S. troops from Germany and threaten force reductions elsewhere in Europe are straining alliances beyond the immediate Iran conflict. Traditional partners from Europe, the Middle East, and the Indo-Pacific have expressed growing concern about U.S. reliability in future crises. Some allied nations are reportedly beginning to pursue independent security arrangements.

stories.title: Russian shelling hits 20 settlements in Kherson region, three civilians injured
stories.summary: Russian attacks struck 20 settlements in Ukraine's Kherson region over the past day, injuring three civilians.

stories.title: Russian occupation troops fighting  in Ukraine are inspired by WWII “generation of victors,” says Putin at 9 May parade at Red Square
stories.summary: President Putin told troops at the May 9 Red Square parade that Russian forces in Ukraine are inspired by the World War II 'generation of victors.' This year's parade featured no heavy military equipment columns; since 2022, Russia has reportedly lost thousands of tanks, armored vehicles, and artillery systems in Ukraine.

stories.title: Jordan sees collapse in tourism since Iran war
stories.summary: Jordan has experienced a sharp decline in tourism since a war involving Iran erupted in the Middle East in late February. The ancient city of Petra, normally a major tourist destination, has seen visitor numbers plummet as the regional conflict continues.

stories.title: Cricket gives special dimension to India-Trinidad and Tobago ties: Jaishankar
stories.summary: Indian External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar arrived in Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago, on May 8, 2026, concluding a three-nation Caribbean tour that included Jamaica and Suriname. Jaishankar highlighted cricket as a unique element strengthening bilateral ties between India and Trinidad and Tobago.

stories.title: Opinion: Germany's 'constructive dialogue' is a sham, a cloak used to shield its support of a genocidal regime
stories.summary: On April 21, Germany and Italy blocked a motion by Spain, Ireland, and Slovenia to suspend the EU-Israel trade agreement over human rights concerns. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul described the move as inappropriate, advocating instead for continued dialogue with Israel.

stories.title: Israel pushes US to Iran war return, targeting energy sector
stories.summary: Israeli officials are reportedly urging the United States to target Iran's energy infrastructure and resume military operations against Tehran. The push aims to draw Washington into a broader confrontation with Iran.

stories.title: 'Integrity costs something': Eurovision winners want Israel out of the contest
stories.summary: Several former Eurovision winners have called for Israel's exclusion from the contest, citing the humanitarian situation in Gaza. They argue that the competition cannot be separated from political reality.

stories.title: Gaza at the Venice Biennale: Where language falls short, threads take over
stories.summary: A tapestry titled the Gaza Genocide Tapestry has been co-commissioned for display at the Venice Biennale. The artwork was created to address the ongoing conflict in Gaza through textile art.

stories.title: Artists strike to protest Israeli participation ahead of Venice Biennale
stories.summary: Around 12 national pavilions at the Venice Biennale closed or partially shuttered in protest against Israeli participation, with some flying Palestinian flags. Police clashed with demonstrators who attempted to reach the Israeli installation.

stories.title: In Victory Day Speech, Putin Says Russia Fighting 'Aggressive' NATO-Backed Force in Ukraine
stories.summary: In his Victory Day speech marking the 81st anniversary of the Soviet World War II victory, Russian President Vladimir Putin stated that Russia is fighting an aggressive NATO-backed force in Ukraine, declaring the cause just.

stories.title: British leader Keir Starmer under pressure after heavy election losses
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces mounting pressure to set a departure timeline after Labour lost more than 1,400 English council seats in local elections. The party also suffered significant defeats in Welsh and Scottish parliament votes held on Thursday.

stories.title: Russian drone hits civilian car in Zaporizhzhia region, leaving one dead, two injured
stories.summary: A Russian FPV drone struck a civilian vehicle in the Polohy district of Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, killing one man and injuring two others.

stories.title: Wanted ‘Hong Kong Parliament’ member could be deported from Thailand
stories.summary: Zhang Xinyan, a member of the overseas opposition group "Hong Kong Parliament," was arrested in Thailand for overstaying her visa and reportedly faces deportation to mainland China. The group said Zhang had been sworn in as a member last year. The type of visa she held was not immediately clear.

stories.title: Germany's 'constructive dialogue' is a sham, a cloak used to shield its support of a genocidal regime
stories.summary: Germany and Italy blocked an EU motion by Spain, Ireland, and Slovenia to suspend the EU-Israel trade agreement. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul rejected the initiative and advocated for continued engagement with Israel.

stories.title: One Nation wins Farrer byelection as Coalition vote collapses
stories.summary: One Nation's David Farley won the Farrer byelection in New South Wales, Australia, marking the party's first-ever lower house seat. He defeated independent candidate Michelle Milthorpe in the race for the seat vacated by former Liberal leader Sussan Ley. The result reflected a significant collapse in the Coalition vote.

stories.title: Iran mulls US peace plan as Hormuz strikes threaten ceasefire
stories.summary: Iran is considering a US peace proposal amid ongoing strikes near the Strait of Hormuz that threaten ceasefire efforts. President Trump has threatened further escalation if Iran does not respond positively to the plan.

stories.title: Iran keeps US waiting for response on ceasefire plan
stories.summary: Iran questioned the seriousness of U.S. diplomacy while delaying its response to Washington's latest negotiating position following renewed naval clashes in the Gulf. A parallel ceasefire on the Lebanon front is also under strain amid daily exchanges of fire between Israel and Iran-backed Hezbollah.

stories.title: China unveils Hanyuan-2, the world’s first dual-core quantum computer
stories.summary: China unveiled Hanyuan-2, described as the world's first dual-core quantum computer, according to state media outlet Science and Technology Daily. The system reportedly uses neutral atoms, reducing energy consumption compared to conventional quantum computers. Officials said the development marks a new stage in Chinese quantum computing technology.

stories.title: Scaled-back Victory Day parade held in Moscow
stories.summary: Russia held a scaled-back Victory Day parade on Red Square in Moscow. President Vladimir Putin used the occasion to pledge victory in what he termed the 'special military operation' in Ukraine.

stories.title: UN says 40,000 Palestinians displaced in West Bank since start of 2025
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that approximately 40,000 Palestinians have been internally displaced in the occupied West Bank since the beginning of 2025 due to Israeli military operations and settler violence. At least 42 people, including 12 children, were displaced by home demolitions in the first week of May alone.

stories.title: IMF's Executive Board approves $1.3bn financing for Pakistan's reform programme, flags heightened risks from Middle East war
stories.summary: The IMF Executive Board approved the latest review of Pakistan's reform programme, releasing $1.32 billion in financing under existing arrangements. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb confirmed the decision in Islamabad, citing continued progress on economic reforms. The Board flagged heightened risks stemming from the ongoing Middle East war.

stories.title: IMF board clears Pakistan to access $1.32 billion
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund's executive board approved Pakistan's access to $1.32 billion under its $7 billion IMF program, following a staff-level agreement reached in March.

stories.title: Overnight Russian attacks on Dnipropetrovsk region leave two dead, two injured
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region more than 20 times overnight using drones and artillery, killing two civilians and injuring two others.

stories.title: Russia will always be victorious, says Putin at scaled-back Victory Day parade
stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin presided over a scaled-back Victory Day parade on Moscow's Red Square, declaring that Russia will always be victorious. The event featured heavy security amid fears of Ukrainian attacks. Putin invoked World War II sacrifices to rally support for the ongoing war in Ukraine, despite a recently announced three-day ceasefire.

stories.title: Gig economy terrorism: Ashab al-Yamin's rise brings new terror threat to Europe
stories.summary: A group called Ashab al-Yamin is identified as a rising terrorism threat in Europe. Emerging evidence suggests the organization may serve as a front for elements operating on behalf of the Iranian regime.

stories.title: Israel, Hezbollah clash in south Lebanon as strikes kill 19
stories.summary: Israeli forces and Hezbollah clashed in southern Lebanon on Saturday, with Israeli strikes killing 19 people. Separately, diplomatic proposals continue to be exchanged between the US and Iran amid ongoing tensions around the blockaded Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Iran to respond to US proposal, Israel continues Lebanon strikes
stories.summary: The US and Iran have exchanged proposals amid ongoing nuclear and conflict negotiations, while sporadic clashes continue around the blockaded Strait of Hormuz. Israel has simultaneously continued conducting air strikes in Lebanon.

stories.title: Russian drone hits agricultural enterprise in Chernihiv region, killing father and son
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck an agricultural enterprise in the Novhorod-Siverskyi district of Ukraine's Chernihiv region, killing a 70-year-old man and his 49-year-old son.

stories.title: DR Congo's Fayulu says Tshisekedi wants to cling to power 'at any cost'
stories.summary: Opposition leader Martin Fayulu accused Democratic Republic of Congo President Felix Tshisekedi of attempting to remain in power beyond the constitutional two-term limit. Fayulu made the accusation on Friday.

stories.title: Israeli air strikes hit southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes targeted the outskirts of Nabatieh and the towns of Aroun and Kfar Tibnit in southern Lebanon. Israeli drones also struck al-Mansouri, Burj Rahhal, and Nabatieh al-Fawqa, according to Al Jazeera Arabic.

stories.title: Hong Kong Golf & Tennis Academy members reject Central service takeover by Carlyle & Co
stories.summary: Members of the Hong Kong Golf & Tennis Academy objected to a takeover of their Central clubhouse operations by private members' club Carlyle & Co. Some members cited concerns about unfair access and incompatible client profiles. The HKGTA board has reportedly decided to proceed with the change despite the opposition.

stories.title: Anti-Israel Greens win 2 mayoralties, 4 councils in UK local elections; hard-right Reform is big winner
stories.summary: In UK local elections, the Green Party won two mayoralties and control of four councils, including in London's Hackney. Nigel Farage's Reform party was projected to become the largest party in Parliament, marking a significant hard-right advance.

stories.title: Two killed as U.S. military strikes on alleged drug boat in eastern Pacific
stories.summary: The U.S. military struck a vessel in the eastern Pacific Ocean, killing two people and leaving one survivor. U.S. Southern Command released video appearing to show the boat being hit by a missile. More than 190 people have been killed in similar strikes on alleged drug trafficking vessels in the Caribbean and Pacific since September.

stories.title: War update: 245 clashes on frontline over past day, heaviest fighting in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 245 combat engagements with Russian troops along the frontline on May 8. The heaviest fighting took place in the Pokrovsk sector.

stories.title: The war on Iran will likely end in American retreat
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the United States cannot sustain a war against Iran due to prohibitive financial, military, and political costs, predicting an eventual American retreat.

stories.title: Hongkongers pack major supermarkets amid ‘price war’ on eve of Mother’s Day
stories.summary: Hong Kong residents crowded supermarkets on the eve of Mother's Day as major chains ParknShop and Wellcome each offered 12 percent storewide discounts, with online platform HKTVmall also joining the competitive price-cutting.

stories.title: US military says it killed 2 in strike on alleged drug-trafficking boat
stories.summary: The US military struck a vessel in the Eastern Pacific on Friday, killing two people and leaving one survivor. The military said the boat was suspected of transporting narcotics as part of ongoing counter-drug-trafficking operations.

stories.title: Xi-Trump summit: why the Iran war could become fresh point of friction
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump is set to visit Beijing for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping after a six-week delay caused by the U.S.-Iran war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The two sides diverge on how to resolve the crisis, risking new friction.

stories.title: ‘Everyone has a breaking point’: the immigration judges at the sharp end of Trump’s deportation drive
stories.summary: Former U.S. immigration judge David Koelsch visited the Minneapolis scene where federal agent Alex Pretti fatally shot someone during an enforcement operation. Current and former immigration judges report that colleagues have been fired or taken buyouts under President Trump's deportation drive, with remaining judges saying they feel compelled to follow the administration's line.

stories.title: Region could witness new political alignment after US-Iran war: Moghadam
stories.summary: Iran's Ambassador to Pakistan, Dr. Reza Amiri Moghadam, said at a roundtable in Islamabad hosted by the Centre for International Strategic Studies that the region could see new political alignments once the US-Israel-Iran conflict ends. Diplomats and academics discussed the evolving regional situation under a fragile ceasefire.

stories.title: Capital Development Authority launches inquiry into ‘illegal sale’ of amenity spaces in Al-Mustafa Tower
stories.summary: Islamabad's Capital Development Authority launched an inquiry into the alleged illegal sale of amenity spaces, including a gym and open areas, in Al-Mustafa Tower in Sector F-10. The investigation aims to determine whether CDA officials played a role in the reported violations.

stories.title: Ukrainian air defenses down 34 out of 43 drones launched by Russia overnight
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 34 of 43 drones launched by Russian forces in overnight attacks beginning on the evening of Friday, May 8. The strikes were part of ongoing Russian aerial assaults on Ukrainian territory.

stories.title: US religious freedom commission calls for designating India as ‘country of particular concern’
stories.summary: The US Commission on International Religious Freedom again urged the State Department to designate India a "country of particular concern" based on its 2026 assessment. A Washington hearing examined conditions faced by religious minorities including Christians, Muslims, Sikhs, and Dalits in India.

stories.title: PAF jets light up skies in twin cities ahead of Marka-i-Haq anniversary
stories.summary: Pakistan Air Force fighter jets conducted a rehearsal aerial display over Rawalpindi and Islamabad ahead of a ceremony marking the first anniversary of Marka-i-Haq. The official ceremony at the National Monument is expected to be attended by top civilian and military leaders celebrating Pakistan's military victory over India.

stories.title: Russia marks Victory Day with parade in Moscow under tight security
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin oversaw a Victory Day military parade on Moscow's Red Square commemorating the defeat of Nazi Germany. Security was heightened, though a U.S.-brokered three-day ceasefire with Ukraine eased concerns about possible disruptions to the event.

stories.title: US awaits Iran's response to latest proposal amid technical ceasefire
stories.summary: The U.S. and Iran remained far from a resolution to their conflict as both sides exchanged fire in the Persian Gulf despite a technical ceasefire. Washington is awaiting Tehran's response to its latest diplomatic proposal.

stories.title: Farewell to Dubai
stories.summary: Reports emerged that Pakistani nationals were being detained and deported from the United Arab Emirates, prompting official denials. Pakistan's interior ministry rejected claims of country- or sect-specific expulsions, calling the reports speculative. The Foreign Office also addressed the allegations as Pakistan-UAE relations showed signs of strain.

stories.title: Ukraine celebrating Europe Day today
stories.summary: Ukraine celebrated Europe Day on Saturday, May 9, in solidarity with European Union member states. The observance underscored Ukraine's alignment with European institutions.

stories.title: Three-day Russia-Ukraine ceasefire begins as Moscow holds Victory Day parade – Europe live
stories.summary: A three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine took effect as Moscow held its Victory Day parade on Red Square. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy emphasized prisoner exchanges over the parade, while in Hungary, Péter Magyar was sworn in as leader, ending Viktor Orbán's 16-year rule.

stories.title: Russia marks Victory Day with scaled-back parade
stories.summary: Russia held a scaled-back Victory Day parade on Red Square, with President Putin expressing confidence in eventual victory in Ukraine. For the first time in nearly two decades, the parade excluded tanks and heavy weapons over fears of a Ukrainian attack, though combat jets flew overhead.

stories.title: Taxation with equity
stories.summary: A significant number of multinational companies have exited Pakistan over the past two years across sectors including telecoms, mobility, and oil and gas. The article argues that policymakers and the IMF have not adequately addressed the underlying domestic factors driving these departures. The trend raises concerns about Pakistan's taxation policies and broader business environment.

stories.title: How Japan’s new economic model could inspire others to ‘look east’
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is steering Japan toward a more state-directed economic model, echoing the development strategies that inspired former Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's "Look East" policy in the 1980s. Analysts suggest the approach could attract renewed interest from Southeast Asian nations.

stories.title: Putin denounces Nato at scaled back Victory Day parade
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin used his Victory Day speech on the 81st anniversary of the Soviet World War II victory to denounce NATO. He characterized Russia's military operation in Ukraine as a fight against an aggressive NATO-backed force.

stories.title: IDF strikes over 85 Hezbollah sites in 24 hours, following rocket fire in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces struck over 85 Hezbollah sites in southern Lebanon within 24 hours, targeting weapon storage facilities and production sites. The strikes were carried out in response to rocket fire directed at IDF soldiers in the area.

stories.title: Chinese military study suggests omega-3 supplements could hurt the brain
stories.summary: Researchers at China's Army Medical University found that oral fish oil intake may not protect against cognitive decline and could accelerate it in Alzheimer's patients. The study analyzed over 800 older adults in North America, roughly half of whom carried the dementia-risk gene APOEε4.

stories.title: DR Congo: Anger after rebel massacre in Ituri
stories.summary: Islamic State-linked rebels killed at least 36 people over two days of attacks in the Ituri province of northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo, according to local and security sources.

stories.title: Russian 90th Tank Division spotted in Pokrovsk
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Assault Forces reported the presence of Russia's 90th Tank Division in the Pokrovsk area. The sighting indicates continued Russian military buildup in the contested eastern Ukrainian region.

stories.title: A year ago today: Risk of ‘unpredictable escalation’ looms over Subcontinent
stories.summary: The article marks the first anniversary of the May 2025 five-day military conflict between Pakistan and India, triggered by the April 22 Pahalgam attack in Indian-occupied Kashmir. India launched air strikes on targets in Punjab and Azad Kashmir on May 7, and Pakistan retaliated by downing Indian aircraft. Both sides struck each other's airbases before the conflict subsided.

stories.title: Russia holds downsized Victory Day parade
stories.summary: Russia held a scaled-back Victory Day parade on Moscow's Red Square on May 9. President Vladimir Putin delivered a speech at the World War II commemoration, with the event reduced in scope due to security concerns.

stories.title: Beijing pushes AI data centres to adopt green energy under action plan
stories.summary: Four Chinese government bodies, including the National Energy Administration and the National Development and Reform Commission, released an action plan requiring new data center projects to prioritize green electricity usage, aligning AI infrastructure expansion with national carbon reduction goals.

stories.title: Surfers in war-torn Gaza find rare moments of relief taking to the waves
stories.summary: A small number of surfers in Gaza continue to ride waves despite the ongoing conflict, facing shortages of equipment, Israeli military restrictions, and limited surfing conditions.

stories.title: Chinese woman accuses tea shop of adding mercury to drink discovers boyfriend is culprit
stories.summary: A woman surnamed Zhang in China's Anhui province accused the tea chain Chagee of placing mercury in her drink, but police later determined her boyfriend was responsible for the poisoning after he had purchased the beverage for her on April 27.

stories.title: Russia’s war casualty toll in Ukraine up by 1,080 over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's military reported that Russia's total combat losses since the full-scale invasion began on February 24, 2022, reached approximately 1,340,270 personnel as of May 8, 2026. Russian casualties over the past day included 1,080 killed or wounded.

stories.title: Israel issues evacuation warnings for nine villages in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military issued evacuation warnings for nine villages in southern Lebanon, including Tayr Debba, Aabbasiyyeh, Burj Rahal, and others, ahead of planned airstrikes. Residents were instructed to move at least one kilometre from targeted areas, which Israel said were Hezbollah positions violating the ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Iran says response to US proposal coming at 'appropriate time'
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Tehran is still reviewing the latest US proposal on ending the conflict and will respond at the "appropriate time." Baghaei dismissed US-imposed deadlines, saying they hold no weight for Iran.

stories.title: Artificial nighttime lighting may be more dangerous than previously thought, study warns
stories.summary: A study found that artificial nighttime lighting may pose greater ecological risks than previously understood, potentially harming ecosystems by disrupting the biological clocks of various organisms.

stories.title: Afghan Taliban leaders reach out to Fazl, express condolences over cleric’s killing in Charsadda
stories.summary: Senior Afghan Taliban leaders, including Defence Minister Mullah Yaqoob, Interior Minister Sirajuddin Haqqani, and Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi, contacted JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman to express condolences over the killing of cleric Sheikh Idris in Charsadda, Pakistan.

stories.title: Taking too many medications may harm older adults, study warns
stories.summary: A study warns that older adults may be harmed by taking too many medications simultaneously. Researchers note that doctors are sometimes unaware of prescriptions from other providers or fail to reassess whether patients still need certain drugs.

stories.title: Draft evasion scheme exposed in Ternopil region
stories.summary: Ukrainian law enforcement in the Ternopil region uncovered a draft evasion scheme involving the illegal smuggling of men across the state border. The operation allegedly involved a doctor and two accomplices facilitating the evasion of military conscription.

stories.title: Tehran could withstand blockade for four months, CIA report shows, as fighting flares
stories.summary: A CIA report indicates that Tehran could withstand a US-imposed blockade for approximately four months, highlighting the limits of American economic leverage. The assessment comes as both sides seek a diplomatic resolution to the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Trump says expecting Iran response to latest proposal soon
stories.summary: A US fighter jet disabled two Iranian-flagged tankers to enforce a port blockade, according to reports. Iranian officials accused the United States of violating the ceasefire with the tanker strikes and hampering diplomatic efforts to end the conflict. President Trump said he expected Iran's response to a US proposal soon.

stories.title: Eurovision 2026: Politics collide with a blockbuster show
stories.summary: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest in Vienna faces controversy over Israel's participation, with boycotts reportedly unprecedented in scale already affecting preparations before the event begins.

stories.title: Rubio perplexed  by allies’ lack of support on Iran
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio criticized allied nations, including Italy, for insufficient support of Washington's efforts to confront Iran and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. After meeting Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni in Rome, Rubio demanded concrete action beyond diplomatic statements. Saudi Arabia has kept U.S. bases open but prohibited their use for Hormuz operations.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: Tensions persist around the Strait of Hormuz, with reports of sporadic clashes between Iranian and US naval forces as Washington awaits Tehran's response to a proposed peace deal. Fighting in Lebanon and rising oil and food prices continue to fuel regional uncertainty.

stories.title: Musk uses slurs to mock French prosecutors investigating X
stories.summary: Elon Musk used slurs to attack French judicial authorities investigating his social media platform X. France opened an inquiry in January 2025 into alleged political interference on X, later expanding it to cover Holocaust denial, sexual deepfakes, and possible distribution of child sexual abuse imagery.

stories.title: Israeli settlers set fire to homes and cars in violent West Bank raids
stories.summary: Dozens of Israeli settlers carried out raids across multiple areas of the occupied West Bank, setting homes and cars on fire and attacking Palestinian residents.

stories.title: Mideast war taking a toll on Pakistan’s ‘wedding economy’
stories.summary: Pakistan's wedding industry is facing disruptions from the Middle East war's economic ripple effects, including surging fuel prices and inflation. Marriage halls in Karachi and elsewhere have raised rates or avoided long-term pricing commitments, while government austerity measures enforce stricter wedding regulations.

stories.title: China aluminium exports surge amid Iran war supply disruptions
stories.summary: China's aluminium exports rose 15 percent year-on-year in April, reaching 598,000 metric tonnes, as the conflict involving Iran and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz tightened global supplies. Year-to-date shipments totalled 2.05 million tonnes.

stories.title: US sanctions 9 mainland China and Hong Kong entities over alleged Iran military links
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury and State departments sanctioned nine mainland Chinese and Hong Kong entities accused of supporting Iran's military, including procuring materials for Iran's Shahed-series drones. The move could complicate President Trump's upcoming visit to China.

stories.title: Financial struggles burden Yemen’s army as soldiers wait for wages
stories.summary: Yemeni government soldiers receive monthly wages ranging from $38 to $116, but ongoing currency instability has significantly reduced the purchasing power of their salaries, placing financial strain on military personnel.

stories.title: Trump says 3-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine agreed at his request
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated that Russia and Ukraine agreed to a three-day ceasefire and prisoner swap at his request. The announcement came amid ongoing US-brokered efforts to de-escalate the conflict between Moscow and Kyiv.

stories.title: Russia urges withdrawal of UN Hormuz resolution targeting Iran
stories.summary: Russia's Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Alimov urged the United States and Bahrain to withdraw a draft UN Security Council resolution calling on Iran to end its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Moscow stated it "cannot support" the proposal, which is also backed by several Gulf states.

stories.title: China’s Huaqiangbei bets on AI innovations to revive global appeal
stories.summary: Shenzhen's Huaqiangbei electronics marketplace is repositioning itself as a global AI showroom, attracting foreign traders and tourists seeking the latest AI-powered gadgets. The district, home to the world's largest electronics market, is leveraging artificial intelligence innovations to revive its international appeal.

stories.title: Barrister says ‘dead woman was put on trial’ after husband cleared of manslaughter
stories.summary: Barrister Charlotte Proudman criticized the trial of Christopher Trybus in the UK, saying a "dead woman was put on trial" after he was acquitted of manslaughter, coercive control, and two counts of rape in the death of his wife Tarryn Baird. A jury of eight women and four men deliberated over 40 hours.

stories.title: The SNP may have won again but Scottish politics has been upended
stories.summary: The Scottish National Party secured a muted victory in Scottish elections, while Labour tied with Reform UK for second place and the Greens claimed significant gains. Labour figures attributed their poor showing to the party's performance under UK leadership in Downing Street.

stories.title: Minister of Culture of Ukraine, Dutch Royals discuss protecting Ukraine’s cultural heritage
stories.summary: Ukraine's Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Culture Tetiana Berezhna met with King Willem-Alexander and Queen Máxima of the Netherlands, along with Dutch Education Minister Rianne Letschert, during the 61st Venice Biennale. Discussions focused on protecting Ukraine's cultural heritage amid the ongoing war.

stories.title: Tenerife braces for race-against-time operation to evacuate 140 from MV Hondius
stories.summary: Spain is preparing a complex emergency operation in Tenerife to evacuate more than 140 passengers and crew from the Dutch-flagged cruise ship MV Hondius, which has been struck by a hantavirus outbreak. Three people have died and five laboratory-confirmed cases have been identified by the WHO. The vessel is scheduled to anchor off Granadilla port early Sunday.

stories.title: Iranian politician calls Trump tactics psychological warfare against Tehran
stories.summary: Hassan Rasouli, a member of Iran's Reformists' Supreme Council for Policymaking, characterized US President Donald Trump's efforts to create divisions among Iranian officials as "psychological warfare." He told the Islamic Republic News Agency that US and Israeli strategies aim to sow discord among Tehran's leadership.

stories.title: Israeli officers fatally shoot man following chase in Rahat
stories.summary: Israeli Border Police officers shot and killed a man in the southern Bedouin city of Rahat after a vehicle chase and foot pursuit. Police said the suspect refused to stop for investigation, fled on foot, and allegedly resisted arrest, prompting officers to open fire after issuing warning shots.

stories.title: Border Guard, detectives arrest suspect moments after shooting during Nazareth operations
stories.summary: Israeli Border Guard officers and detectives arrested a suspect shortly after a shooting incident during security operations in Nazareth. An indictment was subsequently filed in the Nazareth District Court by the Northern District Attorney's Office following an intensive police investigation.

stories.title: In Berlin, people honor memory of Ukrainian victims of World War II
stories.summary: A performative march titled "Ukraine in Memory" took place in central Berlin on Friday, May 8, to honor Ukrainians who died during World War II. Participants called on German authorities to create a dedicated memorial space for Ukrainian victims of the conflict.

stories.title: Who wore it better: Bradley Cooper or Maestro Leonard Bernstein?
stories.summary: A comparison of Bradley Cooper's portrayal of Leonard Bernstein in the Hollywood biopic "Maestro" and the documentary "Bernstein's Wall" was discussed by Times of Israel editors.

stories.title: Vietnam adds over 2 square km of land in South China Sea, US report says
stories.summary: Vietnam has added approximately 2.16 square kilometers of reclaimed land in the Spratly Islands over the past year, according to the Washington-based Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative. This brings Vietnam's total reclaimed area in the South China Sea to roughly 11.2 square kilometers. The expansion reflects an ongoing race between Hanoi and Beijing to reinforce competing territorial claims.

stories.title: Trump hopes for extension to three-day ceasefire agreed by Russia and Ukraine
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump expressed hope for an extension to a three-day ceasefire agreed between Russia and Ukraine. The ceasefire is set to run from May 9 to May 11.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine agree on three-day US-mediated ceasefire
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a US-mediated three-day ceasefire running from May 9 to May 11, coinciding with broader negotiations over a prisoner exchange.

stories.title: US imposes sanctions on 10 individuals, companies for aiding Iran's weapons sector
stories.summary: The US Treasury announced sanctions on 10 individuals and companies, including entities in China and Hong Kong, for aiding Iran's military in acquiring weapons and raw materials used to build Shahed drones.

stories.title: ‘We are talking about energy security for Europe’: Norway doubles down on oil and gas production
stories.summary: Norway's Energy Minister Terje Aasland announced plans to reopen three gas fields off the country's southern coast by the end of 2028, citing a responsibility to address energy shortfalls caused by the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East. Environmental campaigners expressed alarm at the expansion.

stories.title: ‘They have screwed each other pretty badly’: tensions emerge in Netanyahu-Trump alliance
stories.summary: Tensions have emerged between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and U.S. President Donald Trump over the Iran conflict. Despite Netanyahu's claims of "full coordination," Israeli media report that Washington has stopped consulting Israel on the conflict and Pakistani-brokered peace talks.

stories.title: Palestinian agency details new settler attacks across West Bank
stories.summary: The Palestinian news agency Wafa reported overnight Israeli raids and settler attacks across the occupied West Bank. In Khirbet Shuweika near Hebron, settlers reportedly attacked a man and his child with sharp objects, causing head injuries. Israeli forces also detained four Palestinians in the town of Battir near Bethlehem.

stories.title: Quetta on high alert amid rising security threats
stories.summary: Quetta's Deputy Inspector General of Police Imran Shoukat announced the city received approximately 150 threat alerts during April, prompting heightened security across the provincial capital. Additional security personnel were deployed throughout Quetta. Shoukat noted that terrorists have been changing tactics, requiring police and other institutions to revise their counter-strategies.

stories.title: Live: Oil spill detected off Kharg Island in the Persian Gulf
stories.summary: Satellite imagery revealed a large oil spill spreading near Iran's Kharg Island, a major oil export terminal in the Persian Gulf. The spill has raised concerns about damage to Iranian oil infrastructure under strain from a U.S. naval blockade.

stories.title: Bernie Sanders criticises Iran war over soaring fuel costs
stories.summary: US Senator Bernie Sanders called for an immediate end to the war with Iran, citing rising fuel prices burdening American households. Sanders stated that gasoline prices had jumped from $2.98 to $4.55 per gallon since President Trump launched military action against Iran.

stories.title: US fire on Iran tankers sparks reprisals as deal hangs in balance
stories.summary: A US fighter jet disabled two Iranian-flagged oil tankers as part of enforcement of a port blockade, triggering Iranian reprisals amid fragile negotiations over a potential deal.

stories.title: Israeli raids, settler attacks escalate across occupied West Bank
stories.summary: The Palestinian news agency Wafa reported a wave of Israeli military raids, arrests, and settler attacks across the occupied West Bank overnight Friday. Settlers reportedly set fire to a house in al-Lubban Asharqiya south of Nablus. In Jenin, Israeli troops allegedly forced residents of al-Asa'asa village to exhume and relocate a recently buried Palestinian man.

stories.title: CIA estimates Iran can withstand blockade for four months
stories.summary: A CIA assessment reported by Reuters concluded that Iran could withstand the current US naval blockade for approximately four more months before facing sufficient economic pressure to force major concessions. The analysis suggests Washington's pressure campaign has had only limited economic impact so far.

stories.title: Mojtaba Khamenei playing critical role in Iran's war strategy, US intelligence assesses - report
stories.summary: According to a CNN report citing US intelligence assessments, Mojtaba Khamenei, son of Iran's Supreme Leader, is playing a critical role in directing Iran's war strategy. He is reportedly doing so while remaining in hiding.

stories.title: Son of abducted Kherson Mayor: “He is holding on and waiting for exchange”
stories.summary: Kherson Mayor Ihor Kolykhaiev, held captive by Russian forces since June 28, 2022, turned 55 on May 8. His son reported that despite serious health problems, the mayor continues to endure captivity and awaits a prisoner exchange.

stories.title: Moscow set to hold Victory Day parade in Red Square parade amid tight security
stories.summary: Moscow held its annual Victory Day parade in Red Square under heightened security as President Vladimir Putin prepared to address the nation. Authorities scaled back the traditional military display amid concerns about potential Ukrainian attacks, despite a fragile U.S.-backed ceasefire intended to protect the commemorations.

stories.title: Palestinian man and young son reportedly attacked by settlers in southern West Bank
stories.summary: Palestinian media reported that settlers wielding sharp instruments attacked a Palestinian man and his young son in the southern West Bank. Both were wounded and taken to a hospital for treatment.

stories.title: South Korea draws Gulf oil storage interest as Hormuz stays closed
stories.summary: South Korea's petroleum reserve bases, the world's sixth largest, are attracting growing interest from Middle Eastern oil producers seeking crude storage amid the prolonged Strait of Hormuz closure. The blockade, stemming from the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, has disrupted both importing and exporting nations. Oil-producing countries' domestic storage tanks are reportedly filling up.

stories.title: Russia holds scaled-back WW2 victory parade as worries over war in Ukraine deepen
stories.summary: Russia held its most scaled-back Victory Day military parade in years on May 9 in Moscow, citing the threat of Ukrainian attacks. The conflict in Ukraine, now over four years old, remains Europe's deadliest since World War II.

stories.title: Worried Britons ‘prepping’ for major disruption with stash of tins and cash, survey shows
stories.summary: A survey by Link found that millions of Britons are stockpiling cash, tinned goods, and emergency supplies in preparation for potential major disruptions. Fears of natural disasters, cyberattacks, and infrastructure failures are driving the trend. Ongoing conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine have contributed to a sense of heightened global instability.

stories.title: What is ‘authentic’ Filipino identity? New Miss Universe Philippines’ win reignites debate
stories.summary: The Philippines crowned Bea Millan-Windorski as its new Miss Universe Philippines candidate, reigniting debate over Filipino identity. The 23-year-old grew up in Wisconsin and graduated from the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Her selection has prompted public discussion about what constitutes authentic Filipino identity.

stories.title: Rare earth strategy provides ‘opportunities for Africa’ as US attempts to counter China
stories.summary: The United States is shifting its critical minerals strategy in Africa, moving to fund local processing and mining infrastructure to counter China's dominance. Tom Haslett of the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation acknowledged that the U.S. and Europe lack the processing and manufacturing capacity China currently holds. The approach aims to create opportunities for African nations.

stories.title: Massive $7bn oil bets before Trump's Iran announcements raise questions
stories.summary: Reuters reported that investors placed roughly $7 billion in bets on falling oil prices during March and April, shortly before major announcements by President Trump on Iran policy. The trades involved crude oil, diesel, and gasoline futures on the Intercontinental Exchange and Chicago Mercantile Exchange, raising questions about potential advance knowledge.

stories.title: Oil prices rise amid Hormuz tensions, hopes for agreement
stories.summary: Brent crude futures rose to $101.29 per barrel, up 1.23%, amid escalating US-Iran tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, though gains eased on expectations of a possible diplomatic breakthrough. US West Texas Intermediate futures settled at $95.42 per barrel, up 0.64%.

stories.title: U.S. fire on Iran tankers sparks reprisals as deal hangs in balance
stories.summary: Iranian officials accused the United States of violating a ceasefire by striking Iranian-flagged tankers, saying the attacks hampered diplomatic efforts to end the conflict. The incident heightened tensions as both sides sought to maintain negotiations over a potential deal.

stories.title: Colombia suspends arrest and extradition warrants for 29 Clan del Golfo leaders
stories.summary: Colombia's government suspended arrest and extradition warrants for 29 leaders of the Clan del Golfo, the country's largest illegal armed group, as part of ongoing peace negotiations in Bogotá.

stories.title: Pop-up stop for soldiers on Gaza border draws volunteers from across the globe
stories.summary: Shuva Achim, a volunteer-run rest stop for soldiers near the Gaza border, has grown from a small initiative launched on October 7, 2023, into a major support hub. The organization now draws volunteers from around the world to assist Israeli soldiers stationed in the south.

stories.title: U.S. imposes sanctions on 10 individuals, companies for aiding Iran’s weapons sector
stories.summary: The US Treasury imposed sanctions on 10 individuals and companies for supporting Iran's weapons sector. The department stated it remains prepared to take economic action against Iran's military industrial base to prevent Tehran from reconstituting its production capacity and projecting power abroad.

stories.title: Car bombing in Dnipro: Terrorist suspects detained, one caught attempting to flee abroad
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service and National Police detained two suspects in connection with a May 7 car bombing in the city of Dnipro. One suspect was apprehended while attempting to flee the country.

stories.title: The quiet frontier? With minefields cleared, Golan Heights readies for construction boom
stories.summary: Israel's Golan Heights is preparing for a construction boom following the clearance of minefields in the area. A recently approved five-year plan allocates NIS 1 billion for development of the region by 2030, with residents expecting accelerated growth and bolstered infrastructure.

stories.title: US revises UN resolution on Iran but China, Russia still expected to veto
stories.summary: Washington revised its proposed UN Security Council resolution demanding Iran halt attacks and mining operations in the Strait of Hormuz. Diplomats said the changes are unlikely to prevent expected vetoes from China and Russia.

stories.title: Trump says US will start 'Project Freedom Plus' if Iran talks fail
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated the US would initiate "Project Freedom Plus" if ongoing talks with Iran fail. When asked whether Iran was deliberately stalling negotiations, Trump responded that the situation would become clear soon.

stories.title: 2 bike-sharing apps vie for Hong Kong riders amid industry’s roller coaster development
stories.summary: Two dockless bike-sharing operators, Locobike and Helloride, are competing for riders in Hong Kong. Users report different experiences with each service, with Locobike offering more local trip support including maps and recommendations. The industry's development in Hong Kong has seen significant ups and downs.

stories.title: Balikatan 2026: US, Japan, Philippines flex military muscle amid China tensions
stories.summary: The 2026 Balikatan joint military exercises concluded with U.S., Japanese, and Filipino forces conducting live missile firings from northern Philippines. Japan's Type 88 missile struck a decommissioned Philippine warship 75 kilometers off Ilocos Norte, while a U.S. Tomahawk hit a target approximately 630 kilometers away. Analysts described the exercises as a pointed display of resolve amid ongoing tensions with China.

stories.title: US judge rules DOGE’s cuts to Jewish humanities grants were unconstitutional
stories.summary: A US judge ruled that cuts to Jewish humanities grants made by the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) were unconstitutional. The ruling accused the government of terminating a grant because it sought to amplify the voices of Jewish women who were victims of Nazi persecution.

stories.title: Hezbollah claims 26 attacks amid deadly Israeli strikes in Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah claimed 26 attacks against Israeli forces in southern Lebanon since Thursday afternoon, including missile strikes and shelling near the towns of Deir Siryan, Haddatha, and Labbouneh. Lebanese media reported that intensified Israeli strikes across the region killed more than 30 people.

stories.title: Rubio says sanctions target Chinese entities providing Iran with satellite imagery
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced sanctions on Chinese entities accused of providing Iran with satellite imagery used to support attacks against US forces in the Middle East. The sanctions also targeted Iran's overseas arms procurement networks and international companies allegedly supplying materials for Tehran's missile and drone programs.

stories.title: Russian special services draw 260 Ukrainian children into criminal activities – Lohachov
stories.summary: Ukrainian official Lohachov reported that Russian special services have drawn 260 Ukrainian children into criminal activities. The recruitment of minors represents an ongoing concern amid Russia's operations in Ukraine.

stories.title: Israel condemns European criticism over West Bank settler violence
stories.summary: Israel's UN Ambassador Danny Danon criticized Britain and France after both countries called on Israel to halt settler attacks and land seizures in the occupied West Bank. Danon accused European governments of applying a "double standard" toward Israel.

stories.title: 2 Singaporeans, 1 Indonesian still missing after Mount Dukono eruption
stories.summary: Indonesian authorities resumed searching for three hikers—two Singaporeans and one Indonesian—missing after Mount Dukono erupted on Halmahera island. At least 100 rescuers, military and police personnel, and two thermal drones were deployed. Survivors told police that three people, including the two Singaporeans, died in Friday's eruption.

stories.title: China defies Hormuz crisis with record monthly export value in April
stories.summary: China's exports reached a monthly record of $359.44 billion in April 2026, rising 14.1 percent year-on-year despite the ongoing Strait of Hormuz crisis and elevated energy and shipping costs. The strong performance demonstrated resilience in China's export sector amid the U.S.-Israeli war in Iran.

stories.title: Europe-based social networks launch bid to challenge tech giants
stories.summary: Several Europe-based social networking platforms have launched efforts to compete with dominant American and Asian technology companies. The founders cite growing user disillusionment and distrust of major platforms, fueled partly by transatlantic tensions during Donald Trump's second presidency.

stories.title: Vyhivskyi: 165 people killed in Russian drone attacks on railway infrastructure
stories.summary: Ukrainian official Vyhivskyi stated that 165 people have been killed in Russian drone attacks on railway infrastructure since the beginning of the full-scale invasion. The strikes have targeted rail facilities critical to Ukraine's transportation network.

stories.title: Oil spill spotted near Iran export terminal on Kharg Island, AP reports
stories.summary: Satellite imagery reviewed by the Associated Press revealed an oil spill near Iran's Kharg Island, the country's main oil export terminal. The slick was first detected on Tuesday before the latest round of US strikes on Iranian vessels and coastal targets. The US Department of War declined to comment on reports of a possible strike near the island.

stories.title: David Pocock applauds $387m in extra funding for CSIRO after tens of thousands sign petition
stories.summary: The Australian government announced $387.4 million in additional funding for the national science agency CSIRO, following advocacy by independent senator David Pocock and a petition signed by tens of thousands.
