The boost responds to months of concern over job cuts and cost-cutting after CSIRO's funding fell to its lowest level since 1978.

stories.title: Iran mocks Trump nuclear threat with Dr Strangelove reference
stories.summary: Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei mocked US President Donald Trump's recent comments threatening a possible nuclear strike on Iran. Baghaei posted a clip from Stanley Kubrick's Cold War satire Dr. Strangelove on X, calling the contradiction between seeking peace and threatening nuclear attack a "grotesque absurdity."

stories.title: Why Japan’s Mogami-class warship is winning over New Zealand
stories.summary: Japan's Mogami-class destroyer is emerging as the frontrunner to replace New Zealand's aging ANZAC-class frigates under Wellington's 2025 Defence Capability Plan. The potential deal would be a significant milestone for Japan's defence industry, coming weeks after Tokyo lifted its longstanding ban on weapons exports.

stories.title: Michael Jackson biopic revives legend of Jewish music mogul who battled MTV’s ‘color barrier’
stories.summary: A new Michael Jackson biopic has renewed attention on Walter Yetnikoff, the Jewish music executive who led CBS Records. Yetnikoff is credited with challenging MTV's reluctance to air videos by Black artists and managed careers of artists including Billy Joel, Bruce Springsteen, and Gloria Estefan.

stories.title: DOGE’s cuts to Jewish humanities grants were unconstitutional, judge rules
stories.summary: A US District Judge ruled that cuts to Jewish humanities grants by the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) were unconstitutional. In her 143-page ruling, Judge Colleen McMahon specifically cited the agency's targeting of Jewish projects, including Holocaust research.

stories.title: Iran warns US Gulf actions threaten international peace, security
stories.summary: Iran's UN ambassador Amir Saeid Iravani condemned recent US military operations in the Gulf and Strait of Hormuz as unlawful in letters to the UN Security Council and Secretary-General Antonio Guterres. Iravani warned the actions constitute a dangerous escalation that threatens international peace and security.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to 3-day ceasefire, prisoner swap brokered by US
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a three-day ceasefire and prisoner swap brokered by the United States. President Trump expressed hope the truce could be the "beginning of the end," while Ukrainian President Zelensky emphasized the value of Ukrainian prisoners' lives ahead of Russia's WWII Victory Day parade in Moscow.

stories.title: Trump says Russia, Ukraine agree to his request for three-day ceasefire, prisoner swap
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced that both Russia and Ukraine agreed to a three-day ceasefire from May 9 to 11, along with a prisoner exchange, following his mediation efforts.

stories.title: US military strike on vessel in eastern Pacific kills two people, leaving one survivor
stories.summary: The U.S. military struck a vessel in the eastern Pacific on Friday, killing two people and leaving one survivor in an ongoing campaign against suspected drug trafficking boats. The total death toll from such strikes in the Caribbean and Pacific has surpassed 190 since September. U.S. Southern Command released video showing the vessel being hit by what appears to be a missile.

stories.title: US imposes sanctions on 10 individuals, companies for aiding Iran's weapons sector
stories.summary: The US Treasury imposed sanctions on 10 individuals and companies for supporting Iran's weapons sector. The department said it is also prepared to impose secondary sanctions on foreign financial institutions that facilitate illicit Iranian commerce.

stories.title: Qatar and US discuss ending Iran war during Washington meeting
stories.summary: Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani met US Vice President JD Vance in Washington to discuss ending the war involving Iran and achieving Middle East stability. The talks also addressed Pakistan's ongoing mediation efforts between the parties involved in the conflict.

stories.title: UN: Iran war pushes global food prices to three-year high
stories.summary: Global food prices rose to their highest level since 2023 in April, partly driven by the Middle East conflict, according to the UN Food and Agriculture Organisation. The FAO's food price index increased 2 percent year-on-year as higher crude oil prices boosted demand for seed oils used in biofuels.

stories.title: Palestinian journalist recounts Israeli food rations after losing 130 pounds in jail
stories.summary: Palestinian journalist Ali Samoudi was released without charge after a year of administrative detention in Israeli custody. Samoudi reported severe food rationing during his imprisonment, during which he lost approximately 130 pounds. He said he was never questioned about Israeli allegations of ties to Islamic Jihad.

stories.title: Has China just ended the end of history?
stories.summary: An essay argues that the quality of American public intellectuals has declined, contrasting past thinkers like Walter Lippmann and Hannah Arendt with contemporary figures such as Francis Fukuyama and Sam Harris. The piece questions whether China's rise challenges the Western liberal democratic narrative.

stories.title: Cambodians struggle with displaced lives amid tense ceasefire with Thailand
stories.summary: Cambodian families displaced by border clashes with Thailand remain fearful of renewed fighting despite a tense ceasefire. Residents report that education has been among the areas most severely affected by the conflict.

stories.title: US-Iran negotiations key to regional stability, Lavrov tells UAE, urges support
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov urged support for ongoing US-Iran negotiations during a phone call with UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan. Moscow emphasized the importance of backing the talks and avoiding actions that could jeopardize prospects for regional stabilization.

stories.title: Boy arrested for throwing brick at school security guard during argument, injuring girl
stories.summary: Police in Jaffa, Israel, arrested a 15-year-old boy for throwing a brick at a school security guard during an argument at a school entrance gate. A girl was also injured in the incident.

stories.title: Investors have worries about Trump’s pick for Fed chair. Should they?
stories.summary: Central bank leaders from around the world issued a joint statement in January declaring solidarity with the US Federal Reserve and its chair Jerome Powell. The statement defended central bank independence amid concerns over President Trump's choice for the next Fed chair and its potential impact on investor confidence.

stories.title: China boy, 4, survives 11-floor fall after climbing onto window to see if parents were coming home
stories.summary: A four-year-old boy in Dalian, Liaoning province, China, survived a fall from an 11th-floor window on April 11. The child reportedly climbed onto the window while home alone because he missed his parents and wanted to see if they were returning. The story went viral on Chinese social media.

stories.title: US-Iran talks could resume in Pakistan next week, WSJ report says
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that US-Iran talks could resume as early as next week in Islamabad, Pakistan. Both sides are reportedly working on a 14-point memorandum of understanding to frame a month of negotiations covering Iran's nuclear program and tensions in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: OIC urges immediate action to end Israeli occupation of Palestine
stories.summary: The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation called for immediate international action to end Israel's occupation of Palestinian territory during a meeting at UN headquarters. Turkey's UN ambassador Ahmet Yildiz, speaking for the bloc, said the Palestinian issue had reached a "breaking point" amid continuing violence.

stories.title: At least 31 killed in Israeli attacks across Lebanon, local media says
stories.summary: At least 31 people, including a rescue worker, were killed in widespread Israeli attacks across southern Lebanon on Friday, according to Lebanon's state-run National News Agency. The agency described it as one of the deadliest days since fighting between Israeli forces and Hezbollah resumed on March 2. Rescue teams were searching for a missing girl under rubble in the town of Toura.

stories.title: Ahead of May 9, Russia dropping fake banknotes with propaganda QR codes over Ukrainian border regions
stories.summary: Ahead of Russia's May 9 Victory Day, Russian forces dropped fake banknotes embedded with propaganda QR codes from drones over Ukrainian border regions. The materials reportedly aimed to discredit Ukraine's military and political leadership and distort World War II history.

stories.title: Inside the jails where Russia breaks Ukraine prisoners ‘like dogs’
stories.summary: At least 143 Ukrainians, including six civilians, have died in Russian detention facilities over the past four years, according to reports. The article details conditions in Russian jails where Ukrainian prisoners of war are held.

stories.title: Francesca Albanese receives prestigious award from Spanish Prime Minister
stories.summary: UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese received a prestigious award from the Spanish Prime Minister. Albanese, a prominent critic of Israel, has been campaigning within the European Union against the imposition of American sanctions on her and senior International Criminal Court officials.

stories.title: Chile to return ambassador to Israel, Kast tells Herzog
stories.summary: Chilean President José Antonio Kast informed Israeli President Isaac Herzog that Chile will return its ambassador to Israel. The two leaders also discussed expanding bilateral cooperation in health, artificial intelligence, and technology.

stories.title: Trump releases previously classified UFO files
stories.summary: President Donald Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth released dozens of previously classified government files on Friday related to reported UFO sightings and alleged extraterrestrial life. Officials described the move as providing unprecedented transparency to the American public.

stories.title: US court convicts four men in Haitian president's assassination, media reports say
stories.summary: A US federal court in South Florida convicted four men on Friday for plotting the 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse. The defendants were found guilty of hiring mercenaries to kill Moïse at his home in Port-au-Prince.

stories.title: Singapore shines as stable investment oasis amid global storms: ‘very appetising’
stories.summary: Singapore has emerged as a preferred destination for high-net-worth investors amid global geopolitical uncertainty and energy market disruptions from the Middle East conflict. Wealth consultants report increasing interest from Middle Eastern and South Korean clients drawn to Singapore's regulatory stability.

stories.title: Iran war live: US expects Tehran’s reply to peace deal; ‘clashes’ in Hormuz
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed at least 31 people in southern Lebanon on Friday, including a rescue worker, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Separately, the US awaits Tehran's response to a proposed peace deal amid reports of clashes in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Security forces kill five terrorists in Tank, DI Khan in IBOs: ISPR
stories.summary: Pakistani security forces killed five militants in two intelligence-based operations in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Tank and Dera Ismail Khan districts, according to the Inter-Services Public Relations. The military described the fighters as belonging to the group it calls Fitna al-Khawarij.

stories.title: Israeli strike hits home in Shati refugee camp in Gaza, six wounded including children
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes bombed a residential building in the Shati refugee camp west of Gaza City after issuing a forced evacuation warning. Six Palestinians, including two children, were wounded in the strike, which destroyed the targeted house and damaged nearby homes.

stories.title: Trump says expecting Iranian response to latest US proposal ‘tonight’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said he expected Iran's response to Washington's latest proposal imminently. Separately, the US Treasury sanctioned 10 individuals and firms for aiding Iran's production of Shahed drones, and Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov urged UAE to support US-Iran negotiations.

stories.title: Ukraine restores 711 MW of generation in April repair campaign – Shmyhal
stories.summary: Ukraine restored 711 megawatts of electricity generation capacity during April as part of an ongoing infrastructure repair campaign, according to Prime Minister Denys Shmyhal.

stories.title: General Motors to pay $12.75m settlement for selling drivers’ location and data
stories.summary: General Motors agreed to pay $12.75 million to settle claims brought by California Attorney General Rob Bonta that the automaker illegally sold location and driving data of hundreds of thousands of California drivers to two data brokers. Bonta said GM had previously reassured drivers it would not share their data.

stories.title: US arranging repatriation flight for Americans on hantavirus-hit cruise ship
stories.summary: The US State Department announced on Friday it is arranging a repatriation flight for American passengers aboard a Dutch cruise ship affected by a deadly hantavirus outbreak. The flight will return the passengers to the United States.

stories.title: Cultural boycott surge: Israeli artists cut off from global stage after October 7
stories.summary: Israeli artists have faced a growing international cultural boycott since October 7, increasingly being excluded from global stages and events. The trend has raised concerns about one-sided discourse and the broader impact on cultural exchange worldwide.

stories.title: Quadcopter attack in KP's Bannu injures 8, including women
stories.summary: A quadcopter drone reportedly crashed and exploded near a residential area in Bannu district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, injuring eight people including women on Friday night. Police said the drone arrived from an unknown location, and security agencies launched an investigation.

stories.title: US sanctions target firms tied to Iran drone supply network
stories.summary: The US Treasury Department sanctioned 10 individuals and companies, several based in China and Hong Kong, for allegedly helping Iran's military obtain weapons and materials used to produce Shahed drones. The sanctions come amid stalled diplomatic efforts and ahead of President Trump's planned visit to China.

stories.title: Poll: 42% of Likud voters weighing or have decided to back different party in fall
stories.summary: A poll found that 42 percent of voters who supported Israel's Likud party are considering or have decided to back a different party in upcoming fall elections. The most cited reason among those shifting away was the failure to prevent the October 7 attack, followed by efforts to exempt ultra-Orthodox men from military service.

stories.title: War update: 200 clashes on front lines, Pokrovsk sector hottest
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reported 200 combat clashes along front lines over the past day, with the Pokrovsk sector seeing the heaviest fighting. Ukrainian troops repelled 30 enemy attacks on the Pokrovsk axis.

stories.title: US religious freedom commission calls for India to be listed as ‘country of particular concern’
stories.summary: The US Commission on International Religious Freedom held a hearing in Washington and again recommended that the State Department designate India a "country of particular concern" over what it described as systematic violations of religious freedom affecting Christians, Muslims, Sikhs, and Dalits.

stories.title: 'Ideology, family and history': The UAE-Saudi Arabia feud explained
stories.summary: The longstanding rivalry between the UAE and Saudi Arabia traces back to disputes including the 1950s Buraimi oasis conflict, in which Saudi Arabia attempted to bribe a member of the UAE's al-Nahyan family and later launched a failed invasion of the territory also claimed by Oman and the Trucial States.

stories.title: US court torpedoes Democrats’ redistricting win, in struggle for control of Congress
stories.summary: A US court ruling overturned a redistricting outcome that had favoured Democrats, dealing a significant blow to their efforts to reshape congressional district maps. The decision affects the broader struggle for control of Congress.

stories.title: Zelensky signs decree excluding Red Square from Ukrainian strike plans during parade
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky signed a decree ordering that Moscow's Red Square be excluded from Ukrainian weapons targeting plans during Russia's May 9 Victory Day parade.

stories.title: How a China-backed highway may turn landlocked Laos into a trade gateway
stories.summary: China is helping Laos plan its longest highway, linking the capital Vientiane to the northeastern border with Vietnam. The project is part of Beijing's broader strategy to expand transport connectivity in Southeast Asia and develop alternative trade routes amid tensions with the United States.

stories.title: 'Ideology, family and history': The UAE-Saudi Arabia feud explained
stories.summary: An analysis examines the rivalry between the UAE and Saudi Arabia, rooted in competing visions of regional leadership. Saudi Arabia views itself as the leader of the Arab and Muslim world, while the UAE positions itself as a global power seeking to move beyond traditional Gulf alliances.

stories.title: Denmark's coalition talks break down in setback for prime minister Frederiksen
stories.summary: Coalition talks in Denmark broke down on Friday after a key partner withdrew, undermining Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen's effort to form a new government. The setback jeopardises her bid for a third consecutive term following the March election.

stories.title: Palestinian American developer asks US judge to dismiss lawsuit alleging he aided Hamas
stories.summary: A prominent Palestinian American developer asked a U.S. judge to dismiss a lawsuit alleging he supported Hamas through construction projects in Gaza. The defendant argued the suit improperly equates participation in Gaza's economy with support for terrorism.

stories.title: Iran adviser likens Strait of Hormuz control to ‘atomic bomb’ power
stories.summary: Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Iran's supreme leader, compared Iran's control over the Strait of Hormuz to possessing a nuclear weapon, emphasizing the waterway's leverage over the global economy. His remarks come amid heightened tensions in the strategic shipping lane.

stories.title: Zelensky says Ukraine has received Russia's consent for 1,000-for-1,000 prisoner exchange
stories.summary: Ukraine confirmed it received Russia's agreement to conduct a prisoner-of-war exchange in a "1,000 for 1,000" format, as announced by President Zelensky.

stories.title: Trump releases previously classified UFO files
stories.summary: The US Defense Department released previously classified documents and photographs related to "unidentified anomalous phenomena," commonly known as UFOs. President Trump authorized the disclosure, and officials said additional materials will be declassified and released in the future.

stories.title: Doge slashing of humanities grants in 2025 ruled biased and unconstitutional
stories.summary: A US federal judge ruled that the Trump administration's termination of over 1,400 humanities grants worth more than $100 million through the Department of Government Efficiency was unconstitutional, citing blatant discrimination against scholars, writers, and research institutions.

stories.title: Pentagon releases video of strikes on Iranian oil tankers
stories.summary: The Pentagon released footage showing US military strikes on two Iranian oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical global shipping route.

stories.title: Trump announces three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced a three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, effective May 9 through 11, coinciding with Russia's Victory Day celebrations.

stories.title: Russian-declared 'truce' not being felt, no change in combat dynamics – military spox
stories.summary: A Ukrainian military spokesperson said that despite Russia's declared truce, no change in combat dynamics was observed on the ground. Russian forces resumed attempts to infiltrate Kupiansk and attack the Ukrainian bridgehead on the Oskil River's left bank, though all efforts were repelled.

stories.title: Global stocks diverge, oil rises after fresh US-Iran clashes
stories.summary: Global stock markets showed mixed performance as oil prices rose on Friday following renewed military clashes between the United States and Iran in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Greece investigating Ukrainian-made naval drone found in island cave
stories.summary: Greek authorities are investigating a Ukrainian-made MAGURA V3 naval drone discovered in a cave on a Greek island. The unmanned sea drone was found fitted with three detonators.

stories.title: Israeli strike in Lebanon kills one, wounds four including woman
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on the town of Mefdoun in Lebanon's Nabatieh district killed one person and wounded four others, including a woman, according to the Lebanese Ministry of Public Health. Attacks continue across southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Rubio says US ties with Church can withstand Trump's criticism of Pope Leo
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Friday that American relations with the Catholic Church can remain productive despite President Donald Trump's repeated public criticisms of Pope Leo.

stories.title: Latest US-China rivalry combines undersea dominance with a race to riches
stories.summary: President Trump's visit to China coincides with the Iran war's disruption of global energy supplies, adding strain to US-China relations. A new report examines undersea competition between the two powers as a key dimension of their strategic and economic rivalry.

stories.title: IMF's Executive Board approves $1.2 billion financing for Pakistan's reform programme
stories.summary: The IMF Executive Board in Washington approved the latest review of Pakistan's economic reform programme on Friday, unlocking $1.2 billion in financing. Pakistan's Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb confirmed the decision from Islamabad, citing continued progress on economic reforms.

stories.title: Russia's internet crackdown hobbles small businesses
stories.summary: Russia's ongoing internet restrictions are causing unpredictable outages that are disrupting small businesses across the country, putting billions of dollars in digital sales at risk.

stories.title: 6 killed, 13 injured as mortar shell hits civilian area in northwest Pakistan
stories.summary: Six people were killed and 13 injured when mortar shells struck a civilian area in Durrani Banda, Hangu district, in northwest Pakistan on Thursday. Police said the shells were fired by terrorists during a security operation in the area.

stories.title: Nigel Farage hails ‘historic shift in politics’ after Reform UK election gains
stories.summary: Nigel Farage declared a "historic shift in British politics" after Reform UK made significant gains in English local elections, winning control of Essex county council and Havering in London, at the expense of both Labour and the Conservatives.

stories.title: Zelensky visits wounded soldiers at hospital in Dnipro
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky visited wounded service members at a hospital in the city of Dnipro. During the visit, he presented awards to medical personnel for their work treating injured soldiers.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine Agree to U.S.-Brokered Ceasefire This Weekend
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine agreed to a US-brokered ceasefire running from May 9 through May 11, timed to coincide with Russia's Victory Day celebrations. President Trump first announced the deal on Truth Social. The agreement includes a pause in fighting across the front lines.

stories.title: US, Iranian naval forces clash as Washington awaits Tehran’s response to latest proposal
stories.summary: US and Iranian naval forces clashed as CENTCOM struck Iranian tankers and Iran seized a Chinese-owned vessel carrying crude oil, while also firing missiles and drones at the UAE. Separately, Vice President Vance met with Qatar's prime minister in Washington to discuss Iran negotiations.

stories.title: Israeli raid kills two in Lebanon as strikes continue despite truce
stories.summary: An Israeli strike on the town of Aanqoun in southern Lebanon killed at least two people and wounded another, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The attack is part of ongoing Israeli operations in southern Lebanon despite a US-brokered truce.

stories.title: Ukraine ramps up ground robot production to spare soldiers, haul ammo — and rescue grandma
stories.summary: Ukraine is rapidly scaling up production of unmanned ground robots originally designed for military logistics and casualty evacuation, now also using them to extract civilians from contested areas.

stories.title: US revises UN resolution on Iran as China, Russia set to veto
stories.summary: The United States revised a draft UN Security Council resolution aimed at pressuring Iran but retained key provisions. China and Russia are still expected to veto the measure amid rising tensions in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Four south Florida men convicted in Haitian president’s assassination
stories.summary: A Miami federal court convicted four south Florida men for plotting the 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse. Prosecutors said the men hired two dozen former Colombian soldiers and supplied them with money, weapons, and tactical equipment to carry out the killing at his Port-au-Prince residence.

stories.title: North Korea to deploy new artillery guns targeting Seoul
stories.summary: North Korea is preparing to deploy new artillery systems capable of targeting Seoul. The country's artillery capabilities have received less international scrutiny than its ballistic missile programme, which is banned under UN Security Council resolutions.

stories.title: Thanks to Trump, the gloves are off. There may be no new global order
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the post-World War II international order has collapsed under President Trump's foreign policy shifts, leaving uncertainty about what global framework, if any, will replace it.

stories.title: Pro-Iran coverage exposes the illusion of neutrality in Qatar’s media empire - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece alleges that Qatar's media operations, including Al Jazeera, show pro-Iran bias, citing internal evidence from co-author Suzan Quitaz about coordination mechanisms operating behind the scenes.

stories.title: The 'New York Times' wins a Pulitzer Prize for propaganda - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece criticizes The New York Times for its coverage involving contributor Saher Alghorra, alleging the reporting amplified a particular narrative. The article questions editorial standards at the publication.

stories.title: Ukraine says it is running short of air defence missiles
stories.summary: Ukraine's air force announced on Friday that its air defence missile stocks are running low after Russia's extensive winter bombardment campaign. The warning comes as Ukraine prepares for additional Russian strikes.

stories.title: Watch: Vijay meets Governor Arlekar for third time after CPI, CPI(M) support | Above the Fold | 08.05.2026
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu politician Vijay met Governor Arlekar for a third time amid government formation talks, following expressions of support from CPI and CPI(M). Separately, China issued fresh remarks on Operation Sindoor, and West Bengal received its first BJP Chief Minister.

stories.title: Israel-Lebanon talks to resume May 14-15 with US mediation
stories.summary: Israel-Lebanon peace talks are scheduled to resume on May 14–15 with US mediation. The US State Department stated that a comprehensive peace agreement depends on full restoration of Lebanese state authority and the complete disarmament of Hezbollah.

stories.title: Kazakh, Uzbek presidents to attend military parade in Moscow – media
stories.summary: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev are set to travel to Moscow for the May 9 Victory Day military parade, according to media reports. Their attendance signals the continuation of Central Asian diplomatic engagement with Russia.

stories.title: Russia says radiation levels are normal after fires near Chernobyl
stories.summary: Fires broke out near the Chernobyl nuclear plant exclusion zone in Ukraine, with firefighters working to extinguish them. Russia stated that radiation levels in the area remain normal.

stories.title: Israel’s resilience is the country’s strongest message to the world - opinion
stories.summary: The opinion piece argues that Israel's resilience across security and innovation sectors has become a model for addressing modern global threats. It frames the country's endurance as its most powerful message to the international community.

stories.title: A time for healing: Can Israel mend its deep internal rift? - opinion
stories.summary: The opinion article discusses whether Israel can heal its deep internal divisions. It draws on themes from Ecclesiastes about cycles of conflict and reconciliation, reflecting on Israeli society's current state.

stories.title: Israeli strike in Lebanon kills at least four
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike hit a vehicle near Houmin Tahta in southern Lebanon, killing three occupants. A motorcyclist was also killed and his wife wounded in the same strike, Lebanon's National News Agency reported.

stories.title: Court fight with Pentagon raises Senator Mark Kelly’s White House profile
stories.summary: A federal appeals court hearing in Washington saw judges question Pentagon efforts to penalize Democratic Senator Mark Kelly, a retired astronaut and Navy officer, for urging troops to refuse illegal orders. The legal clash with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has elevated Kelly's profile as a potential 2028 presidential challenger.

stories.title: Costa Rica’s Laura Fernandez vows ‘war’ on crime ahead of inauguration
stories.summary: Laura Fernandez is set to be inaugurated as Costa Rica's president on Friday. The right-wing politician has pledged to wage an aggressive campaign against crime in the Central American nation, which has traditionally been known for peace and stability.

stories.title: South Africa’s highest court revives impeachment proceedings against the president Cyril Ramaphosa
stories.summary: South Africa's Constitutional Court has revived impeachment proceedings against President Cyril Ramaphosa by lifting an earlier ruling that blocked them. The case stems from the "Farmgate" scandal involving the disappearance of over $500,000 from Ramaphosa's luxury farmhouse during a 2020 break-in. Ramaphosa denies any wrongdoing.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1535: Ukraine and Russia agree to 9-11 May ceasefire and 1,000-for-1,000 POW swap
stories.summary: On day 1,535 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, a US-mediated agreement established a ceasefire from May 9 to 11 tied to a 1,000-for-1,000 prisoner exchange. Russia's earlier unilateral Victory Day ceasefire was contradicted by over 140 battlefield attacks. Ukrainian drones struck targets in Moscow, Yaroslavl, and Rostov-on-Don, igniting a fire at a major Russian oil refinery.

stories.title: ‘Almost zero’ chance Dutch man got hantavirus in Argentina’s Ushuaia, official says
stories.summary: A Tierra del Fuego health official said there is "almost zero" chance a Dutch man linked to a hantavirus outbreak on the cruise ship MV Hondius contracted the disease in the Argentine port of Ushuaia, citing the virus's incubation period. The man and his wife both died from the virus.

stories.title: Taiwan's Parliament approves $25 billion defence spending bill
stories.summary: Taiwan's parliament approved a $25 billion defence spending bill aimed at strengthening the island's military capabilities against a potential Chinese attack. Lawmakers had been deeply divided over the size of the defence budget. China claims Taiwan as its territory and has threatened forcible reunification.

stories.title: Can artificial intelligence help Nollywood tell African stories differently without losing its soul?
stories.summary: In Nigeria, filmmakers and digital artists are incorporating artificial intelligence tools into Nollywood productions and cultural preservation efforts. Obinna Okere-keocha, founder of the Naija Artificial Intelligence Film Festival, and filmmaker Malik Afegbua are using AI to create digital archives of disappearing oral traditions across Africa.

stories.title: Over 3,000 attacks on Ukraine healthcare since start of war: WHO
stories.summary: The World Health Organisation reported that Ukraine's healthcare system has suffered over 3,000 attacks during 1,534 days of war since Russia's full-scale invasion began.

stories.title: US attacks in Gulf violation of ceasefire, more than a ‘light slap,’ Iranian officials say
stories.summary: Iranian officials characterized recent US attacks in the Persian Gulf as a violation of ceasefire terms and more than a minor provocation. An Iranian military source warned that any US attempt to re-enter the Persian Gulf would be met with a decisive response.

stories.title: General Staff confirms strikes on Russian arsenal, two plants producing explosives and FAB bombs
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed strikes on key Russian military-industrial targets, including the Bryansk Chemical Plant, the Ya.M. Sverdlov Plant in Dzerzhinsk, and the Kedrovka arsenal in Russia's Sverdlovsk region. The facilities are involved in the production of explosives and FAB bombs.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine trade attacks ahead of Kremlin's WWII celebrations
stories.summary: Russia and Ukraine exchanged attacks ahead of Moscow's World War II Victory Day celebrations. Ukraine rejected Russia's call for a temporary halt in strikes, accusing President Vladimir Putin of seeking a pause only to stage a military parade on Red Square in Moscow on Saturday.

stories.title: Man arrested for firing replica weapon in 2 drive-by attacks on Toronto Jews
stories.summary: An 18-year-old man was arrested in Toronto by counter-terrorism police for allegedly firing a replica weapon in two drive-by attacks targeting Jewish people, including one incident outside a synagogue.

stories.title: Palestinian mountaineer is raising $10m for Gaza by climbing Mount Everest
stories.summary: British-Jordanian-Palestinian mountaineer Mostafa Salameh is attempting to climb Mount Everest to raise $10 million for Gaza. Salameh, who has summited Everest three times before, describes this climb as carrying particular personal significance.

stories.title: Poland signs first loan deal as part of EU defence spending push
stories.summary: Poland signed a loan agreement under an EU defence financing programme, securing 43.7 billion euros to strengthen its military. The deal is part of the European Union's broader push to boost defence spending amid heightened geopolitical risks.

stories.title: Russia, Ukraine to enter temporary ceasefire with prisoner exchange, Trump says
stories.summary: President Trump announced that Russia and Ukraine would observe a three-day ceasefire beginning Saturday, May 9, accompanied by a prisoner exchange between the two countries.

stories.title: Report: Netanyahu confidant called Herzog a ‘coward’ over stance on pardon for PM
stories.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog was reportedly called a "coward" by Netanyahu confidant Jacob Bardugo at a secret meeting over Herzog's stance on a potential pardon for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Herzog reportedly told Bardugo that Netanyahu had not submitted a proper pardon request.

stories.title: Hezbollah claims drone attack on Israeli air base in north
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced it launched a drone attack on an Israeli air base near Nahariya in northern Israel, calling it retaliation for recent Israeli operations. The group said it had previously struck the same facility. Israeli authorities did not immediately comment.

stories.title: Russian drones attack Nikopol district in Dnipropetrovsk region, damage reported
stories.summary: Russian forces conducted multiple FPV drone attacks on the Nikopol district in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region. The strikes damaged civilian buildings in the area.

stories.title: The myth of Gulf exceptionalism and US protection is over
stories.summary: An opinion piece reflects on the long-standing US military presence in Qatar during the 1990s and 2000s, arguing that the era of assumed Gulf security under American protection has ended.

stories.title: Senators alarmed by ‘surge’ in violence against women; 5pc conviction rate termed ‘systemic failure’
stories.summary: Senators in Islamabad expressed alarm over rising violence against women in Pakistan, highlighting a conviction rate of just five percent. The debate was prompted by the reported honour killing of Rubina Chandio in Sindh's Tando Masti. PPP Vice President Sherry Rehman, presiding over the session, called the low conviction rate a systemic failure.

stories.title: Explainer-Could UK PM Starmer be forced out after local election losses?
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer vowed to continue as leader after the Labour Party suffered significant losses in local elections. The results have deepened doubts about his ability to govern effectively.

stories.title: Trump announces 3-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine
stories.summary: President Trump announced a three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine for May 9–11, coinciding with Russia's Victory Day. Trump said both sides also agreed to a prisoner exchange, and that negotiations toward ending the war were continuing.

stories.title: Southeast Asian Leaders Tackle Iran War Vulnerabilities
stories.summary: Southeast Asian leaders are addressing economic vulnerabilities stemming from the Iran war, with global market disruptions prompting calls for a regional power grid and emergency fuel stockpile.

stories.title: What in the World?
stories.summary: A news quiz covers the week of May 2, including a US military drawdown announcement in Germany, a foreign visit by Taiwan's president, and Sudan's accusations against Ethiopia.

stories.title: Oil refinery, depots, and more: General Staff reports strikes on key Russian targets
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces struck an oil refinery and a drone storage warehouse inside Russia overnight on May 8. Ukrainian forces also targeted the Luhanska oil depot and air defense facilities in Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory.

stories.title: Ukraine weighs sending security experts to Baltic states amid drone incidents
stories.summary: Ukraine is considering sending air security experts to the Baltic states after two Ukrainian drones reportedly entered Latvia from Russian airspace and crashed. Foreign Minister made the announcement as part of potential cooperation to strengthen Baltic air defences.

stories.title: Russian drones swarm smaller Ukrainian power stations, data shows
stories.summary: Research data from a London-based group shows Russia has increasingly targeted small Ukrainian power substations with drone attacks. Expanded Russian drone capacity allowed greater disruption of Ukraine's electrical grid over the past winter than in previous periods.

stories.title: Being Pedro Sanchez: Is Spain's anti-Israel prime minister on the wrong side of history?
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez faces ongoing accusations of corruption, with his wife also facing charges of corruption and influence peddling. His public appearances are frequently met with calls for his resignation. The article examines his stance on Israel within the broader context of European affairs.

stories.title: Gaza genocide death toll rises to 72,628
stories.summary: The Palestinian Health Ministry reported that the death toll in Gaza has reached 72,628, with 172,520 wounded since October 7, 2023. Officials said nine bodies and 39 wounded were received by hospitals in the past 24 hours. At least 846 people have been killed since the October 11 ceasefire.

stories.title: New York City garden that had barred Zionist members drops the requirement
stories.summary: Sunset Community Garden in Queens, New York City, agreed to settle a lawsuit and drop a requirement that had barred members who identified as Zionist, ending a years-long dispute with the city's parks department.

stories.title: Antisemitic assaults surged 56% in Brooklyn last year — ADL report
stories.summary: The Anti-Defamation League reported that antisemitic physical assaults in Brooklyn, New York, rose 56% in the past year, increasing from 32 to 50 incidents. Most attacks targeted visibly identifiable Orthodox Jewish community members.

stories.title: Labour loses control of Birmingham city council after 14 years of leadership
stories.summary: Labour lost control of Birmingham city council after 14 years, as Reform UK, the Green Party, and pro-Gaza independent candidates made significant gains in UK local elections. No party secured an overall majority on the council.

stories.title: Russian army intensifies operations across entire front – Syrskyi
stories.summary: Ukraine's Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi reported that Russia has intensified military operations across virtually the entire front line and is regrouping forces. Approximately 106,000 Russian troops have been concentrated in the Pokrovsk direction.

stories.title: Somalia faces severe malnutrition crisis as WFP warns of aid halt
stories.summary: The World Food Programme warned that approximately six million people in Somalia — nearly one in three — face acute hunger. The agency cautioned that a potential halt in aid could worsen the severe malnutrition crisis.

stories.title: Pentagon releases previously secret files on UFOs
stories.summary: The U.S. Pentagon released more than 160 previously classified files documenting reported UFO sightings, some dating back to the 1940s. War Secretary Pete Hegseth said the long-classified documents were being made publicly available on the War Department's website.

stories.title: Qatar premier meets with JD Vance in White House talks on Iran
stories.summary: Qatar's Prime Minister met with US Vice President JD Vance at the White House for talks covering Iran war diplomacy, liquefied natural gas trade, and Gulf security.

stories.title: Qatar premier in meeting with Vance in White House talks on Iran
stories.summary: Qatar's premier met with US Vice President JD Vance at the White House for discussions on Iran war diplomacy, LNG trade, and Gulf security. The meeting took place amid ongoing diplomatic efforts related to the conflict involving Iran.

stories.title: Iran’s president rejects ‘colonialism’, calls for respectful ties
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that Tehran will pursue friendly relations with other nations based on mutual respect and shared interests. He rejected what he characterized as colonialism and exploitation, calling such practices incompatible with the future global order.

stories.title: IAEA completes another mission to Ukraine's high-voltage substations
stories.summary: IAEA experts completed another inspection of high-voltage substations in Ukraine that are critical to nuclear safety. The mission is part of the agency's ongoing monitoring of infrastructure supporting Ukraine's nuclear power plants.

stories.title: Militant attack on Nigeria army base kills at least two soldiers
stories.summary: Suspected Islamic State West Africa Province fighters attacked a Nigerian army base in the northeastern town of Magumeri in Borno State, killing at least two soldiers and wounding the commanding officer.

stories.title: Australia sanctions BLA, three senior leaders for 'engagement in and support of terrorist attacks'
stories.summary: Australia imposed counter-terrorism financing sanctions on the Balochistan Liberation Army and three of its senior leaders. Foreign Minister Penny Wong's office said the sanctions target the group's engagement in and support of terrorist attacks across Pakistan targeting civilians and critical infrastructure.

stories.title: Iran warns of renewed clashes if US returns to Hormuz
stories.summary: An unnamed Iranian military source told Tasnim News Agency that the Strait of Hormuz is currently calm but warned that tensions could escalate if US forces return. The source said any US interference with Iranian vessels could trigger further confrontation. Fars News Agency had earlier reported sporadic clashes between Iranian and US naval forces.

stories.title: Ukraine and Russia agree to three-day Victory Day ceasefire tied to large-scale POW exchange
stories.summary: Ukraine announced that Russia agreed to a 1,000-for-1,000 prisoner exchange and a temporary ceasefire from May 9 to 11, following US-mediated negotiations between the two countries.

stories.title: Could Labour and Conservative party dominance in UK politics be ending?
stories.summary: British Prime Minister faces pressure to resign following significant losses in local elections, raising questions about the long-term dominance of the Labour and Conservative parties in UK politics.

stories.title: Al Jazeera reporter witnesses Israeli strikes on Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel has intensified air strikes across southern Lebanon. Al Jazeera correspondent Obaida Hitto reported on the attacks from the city of Tyre.

stories.title: Russia says it regrets decision of Israeli company to refrain from purchasing Russian grain
stories.summary: Russia expressed regret over an Israeli company's decision to stop purchasing Russian grain. Moscow accused Israel of yielding to Ukrainian pressure after a Russian grain shipment was turned away the previous month.

stories.title: Lithuania lodges protest with Russia over threats against diplomatic missions in Kyiv
stories.summary: Lithuania's Ministry of Foreign Affairs summoned a Russian Embassy representative on Friday, May 8, to protest threats made against Lithuanian and other countries' diplomatic missions in Kyiv.

stories.title: Hegseth aims to cut through the bureaucracy with ‘Deal Team Six’
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth assembled a group of private-sector businessmen, dubbed "Deal Team Six," to overhaul how the Pentagon negotiates contracts with defense companies.

stories.title: High-profile terrorist killed in Bannu was Afghan special forces member: security sources
stories.summary: Security forces killed a high-profile terrorist named Fatehullah, alias Mudassir, during an operation in Bannu district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. Security sources identified him as a member of the Afghan Taliban regime's Yarmook 60 Special Forces Battalion, operating under the Taliban's Ministry of Interior Affairs.

stories.title: British PM Starmer says he won't quit after local elections drubbing
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer declared he would not resign after his Labour Party suffered significant losses in local elections, with hard-right Reform UK making notable gains. The elections were widely viewed as an unofficial referendum on Starmer's leadership.

stories.title: Chad sentences eight opposition leaders to prison and bans coalition
stories.summary: A court in Chad sentenced eight opposition leaders to eight years in prison, while the Supreme Court dissolved an anti-Déby coalition, further restricting political opposition in the country.

stories.title: UK's Princess Kate to visit pioneering Italian schools funded by WW2 scrap metal
stories.summary: Britain's Princess of Wales will visit northern Italy next week to tour pioneering early-years education schools. The schools were originally funded by communities that repurposed abandoned World War Two military equipment, including a tank, and have since become a globally influential educational model.

stories.title: Fire in Chornobyl exclusion zone currently poses no radiation threat
stories.summary: A wildfire broke out in the Chornobyl exclusion zone in Ukraine, but authorities said it currently poses no radiation threat. Ukraine's State Nuclear Regulatory Inspectorate is modeling the fire's potential impact on radiation levels.

stories.title: IOC backs Belarus’s return to international sport but withholds recommendation for Russia’s return over doping concerns, sources say
stories.summary: The International Olympic Committee supported Belarus's return to international sport but withheld a recommendation for Russia's full reinstatement. Sources told The Guardian the decision was based on doping concerns rather than Russia's ongoing war with Ukraine.

stories.title: Trump trade chief says US wants balanced trade, not change to China’s system
stories.summary: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Washington seeks to rebalance trade with Beijing rather than reshape China's economic system. The remarks came days before President Donald Trump's planned trip to China, amid ongoing tensions over the bilateral trade imbalance.

stories.title: Poland becomes first nation to sign EU SAFE loans, expects billions for defense
stories.summary: Poland became the first nation to sign up for the European Union's SAFE loan program for defense spending. The country expects to receive over $51 billion in EU loans to bolster its military capabilities after resolving domestic political obstacles.

stories.title: Iran turns bombed Karaj Bridge into a symbol of resistance
stories.summary: Iran is transforming the bombed Karaj Bridge into a symbol of resistance following Israeli strikes. The B1 corridor connecting Tehran with northwestern regions, including areas with large Azeri populations such as Tabriz, passes through the site.

stories.title: Trump announces Russia-Ukraine three-day ceasefire from 9 May
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social a three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine from May 9 to 11. The agreement is set to include a suspension of all military operations and a prisoner swap of 1,000 prisoners from each side.

stories.title: Plaid Cymru wins Welsh Senedd elections, ending 100 years of Labour control
stories.summary: Plaid Cymru won the Welsh Senedd elections, ending roughly a century of Labour dominance in Wales. Party leader Rhun ap Iorwerth declared readiness to become first minister and form a government, displacing Welsh Labour, which had governed since devolution began in 1997.

stories.title: Syria says arrested Assad-era general over chemical attack
stories.summary: Syria's current authorities announced the arrest of a general from the Assad era in connection with a chemical weapons attack. The ousted Assad regime was accused of using chemical weapons against rebel-held areas in 2013, killing more than 1,400 people.

stories.title: Libya’s largest oil refinery halts operations during fighting
stories.summary: Libya's Zawiya refinery, the country's largest, halted operations as a precautionary measure after explosions and gunfire were reported nearby, prompting an emergency declaration in the area.

stories.title: Chile to return ambassador to Israel after more than two years
stories.summary: Chilean right-wing President José Antonio Kast informed Israeli President Herzog of his intention to return Chile's ambassador to Israel after an absence of more than two years. The move aims to restore bilateral ties and expand cooperation following a sharp diplomatic deterioration under Chile's previous leftist government.

stories.title: Russia’s T-72AM is a very old tank with a fresh coat of paint. Expect it to stay parked like other tanks.
stories.summary: Russia has begun fielding refurbished T-72AM tanks, which are upgraded versions of aging T-72A models pulled from long-term storage. These are among the last reserve tanks Russian industry has prepared for deployment to Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran seizes oil tanker Ocean Koi in Gulf of Oman, state media says
stories.summary: Iran seized the oil tanker Ocean Koi in the Gulf of Oman, according to Iranian state media. The vessel was escorted to Iran's southern coast and handed over to judicial authorities.

stories.title: Interior ministry denies reports of 'country or sect-specific' deportation of Pakistanis from UAE
stories.summary: Pakistan's interior ministry denied reports of targeted deportation of Pakistani nationals from the United Arab Emirates. The ministry stated no country- or sect-specific expulsions were taking place, contradicting social media claims and media reports, including coverage by The New York Times.

stories.title: Cracks showing for Labour close to back yards of Starmer’s top team
stories.summary: The Labour Party faced significant local election losses across England, with Reform UK making gains in traditional Labour working-class areas and the Greens eroding its progressive base. The results are increasing pressure on Prime Minister Keir Starmer's leadership.

stories.title: Putin is ready to talk with EU but won’t make the first move, Kremlin says
stories.summary: The Kremlin said on Friday that President Vladimir Putin is prepared to negotiate with European Union leaders but will not initiate contact. The statement followed a Financial Times report that EU leaders were preparing for potential talks with Russia.

stories.title: War update: 52 clashes since morning, Pokrovsk direction remains most active
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked Ukrainian defense positions 52 times since the start of the day, with the Pokrovsk direction remaining the most active sector of fighting along the front line.

stories.title: Washington shooting suspect seeks to bar DoJ officials from prosecution role
stories.summary: Cole Tomas Allen, charged with attacking the White House Correspondents' Association dinner on April 25 at the Washington Hilton, has filed a motion to disqualify acting Attorney General Todd Blanche and US Attorney Jeanine Pirro from the prosecution. His lawyers argue both officials were present at the event and could be considered victims or witnesses.

stories.title: Mali government refuses dialogue with 'terrorist' groups
stories.summary: Mali's foreign minister rejected dialogue with al-Qaeda-linked fighters and Tuareg separatists, labeling them terrorist groups. The refusal follows attacks on the Malian government carried out in April by those armed groups.

stories.title: US to host new Israel-Lebanon talks as Trump team presses for Hezbollah disarmament
stories.summary: The US State Department announced it will host two days of talks between Israeli and Lebanese delegations on May 14–15, building on earlier negotiations held in April. The discussions aim to advance a broader peace and security arrangement, with Washington pressing for Hezbollah's disarmament.

stories.title: US presses allies to act as Rome balances ties with domestic pressure
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio questioned why allied nations, including Italy, have not more strongly backed Washington's war on Iran. Speaking in Rome after meeting Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, Rubio called for actions beyond strongly worded statements. The US and Israel first attacked Iran on February 28.

stories.title: After Rubio meeting, Pope Leo gives speech asking God to inspire leaders to calm tensions
stories.summary: Following a meeting with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Pope Leo delivered a speech calling on God to inspire world leaders to ease tensions. The pontiff warned that peace is endangered by international conflicts and an arms-trade-driven economy. He also praised initiatives to welcome Gazan refugees.

stories.title: Meloni meets Rubio as Iran war strains Italy-US ties
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni met U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Rome on Friday amid unusual strain between Italy and the Trump administration. The tensions are largely driven by disagreements over the ongoing war with Iran.

stories.title: Four convicted in US related to killing of Haitian President Jovenel Moise
stories.summary: Four individuals were convicted in the United States for their roles in the 2021 assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse. Prosecutors identified Florida as the central planning hub for the operation. The killing triggered a prolonged political crisis in Haiti that continues to this day.

stories.title: One Page Peace Plan for Iran? Starmer’s Sinking Ship, Musk V Altman
stories.summary: Renewed peace efforts regarding the Iran conflict have produced a fourteen-point, one-page memorandum of understanding drafted by Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. The document has been sent to Pakistani mediators and is under review by Iran, amid a stalemate and continued skirmishes over the Strait of Hormuz blockade.

stories.title: USF strikes two air defense systems, oil depot, Russian communication hubs
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces struck Russian Tor-M2 and Tunguska air defense systems, an oil depot, and communication hubs. The targets were located in Russia's Bryansk region and Russian-occupied areas of Donetsk, Luhansk, and Zaporizhzhia regions.

stories.title: Labour suffers losses across the UK as Reform surges: “Starmer’s survival depends on improvement”
stories.summary: Labour lost hundreds of council seats across England, fell behind Plaid Cymru in Wales, and continued to trail the SNP in Scotland during local elections. Reform UK made significant gains across all three nations, intensifying questions about Prime Minister Keir Starmer's leadership and Labour's strategic direction.

stories.title: Somalia faces malnutrition crisis as WFP warns of aid halt
stories.summary: The World Food Programme warned that approximately six million people in Somalia face acute hunger. The agency raised concerns about a potential halt to aid operations, which would worsen the country's malnutrition crisis.

stories.title: Trump announces three-day ceasefire in Russia-Ukraine war
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced a three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine. The truce will include an exchange of 1,000 prisoners of war from each side. The pause in fighting is set to coincide with Russia's Victory Day celebrations, running from May 9 through May 11.

stories.title: Ukraine’s new AI-powered laser “Tryzub” can burn holes in Shaheds from 5 km away
stories.summary: Ukraine is in final testing of a new AI-powered laser system called "Tryzub," designed to engage Iranian-made Shahed drones. The system can reportedly burn through drone airframes from a distance of five kilometers.

stories.title: China confirms its support to Pakistan during last year’s war with India
stories.summary: China's South China Morning Post reported that a Chinese aviation engineer provided technical support to Pakistan during the four-day war between Pakistan and India in May of the previous year. Beijing has confirmed its backing of Islamabad during the conflict.

stories.title: Israeli army chief recommends commander who destroyed Gaza university for senior role
stories.summary: Israeli army chief of staff Eyal Zamir recommended commander Barak Hiram for the post of military secretary to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Hiram was responsible for destructive operations in Gaza, including the demolition of a university, and for ordering tank fire on an Israeli home during the October 7 attacks. Israeli outlet Ynet reported he is one of two candidates for the role.

stories.title: Trump announces three-day ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced a three-day ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine beginning May 9, including a pause in all fighting and a prisoner swap of 1,000 prisoners from each side.

stories.title: ASEAN leaders adopt measures to ease economic pain caused by Iran war
stories.summary: ASEAN leaders adopted measures aimed at mitigating the economic impact of the ongoing war involving Iran. The bloc relies on the Middle East for more than half of its crude oil imports, making it particularly vulnerable to disruptions in the region.

stories.title: Suspected oil spill seen on satellite images near Iran's Kharg Island export hub
stories.summary: Satellite imagery revealed a suspected oil spill near Iran's Kharg Island, a major crude oil export hub. The spill appears to cover waters west of the approximately 8-kilometer-long island. The cause of the spill remains unknown.

stories.title: Libya launches 'large-scale' crackdown on crime in Zawiya
stories.summary: Authorities in the Libyan city of Zawiya launched what they described as a large-scale security operation targeting criminal groups. The crackdown followed clashes that disrupted the major oil-producing city.

stories.title: Over 300 Christian leaders urge Congress to stop funding Israel
stories.summary: Over 300 Christian leaders in the United States urged Congress to stop funding Israel. The appeal came as Israeli forces continued military operations in Gaza and conducted raids in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Missiles must be Ukraine’s top priority weapon, defense expert says
stories.summary: A defense expert argued that missiles should be Ukraine's top priority weapon due to their ability to destroy enemy infrastructure and military-industrial capacity. The expert called for joint Ukrainian-European development of missile systems.

stories.title: Yemeni man killed fighting alongside Russian forces in Ukraine
stories.summary: A Yemeni man named Hamza Mahmoud Al-Habashi was killed while fighting alongside Russian forces in Ukraine. He is reportedly the latest Yemeni national to die after being misled into joining Russia's military.

stories.title: JUI-F holds second round of protests over killing of Maulana Idrees
stories.summary: The Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) held a second round of protest rallies across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Friday against the killing of prominent cleric Maulana Muhammad Idrees. Party chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman had called for demonstrations on Wednesday and Friday.

stories.title: Greece examines mystery naval drone found in Ionian Sea
stories.summary: Greek authorities are examining an unidentified naval drone discovered in the Ionian Sea. Greek media reported the device was equipped with explosives and may be linked to the Russia-Ukraine war, with possible Ukrainian origins.

stories.title: Lebanon seeks to ‘solidify’ ceasefire ahead of Israel talks
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said Beirut will prioritize reinforcing the ceasefire with Israel in upcoming negotiations. Speaking to Al Jazeera, Salam warned that continued Israeli strikes would force Lebanon to focus first on solidifying the truce before addressing other agenda items.

stories.title: GitHub access deteriorates in Russia as internet regulator denies blocking
stories.summary: Access to GitHub has deteriorated across Russia, according to data from the internet censorship monitoring service OONI. Russia's internet regulator denied blocking the platform, though independent outlet Verstka reported widespread connectivity issues.

stories.title: Zelensky on ceasefire: “What tomorrow brings depends on what we hear today”
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukraine would "strictly mirror" Russian actions regarding any potential ceasefire. He noted that Russian forces had begun the day with frontline shelling and continued assault activity.

stories.title: Cyber-attack on system widely used in US education disrupts final exams
stories.summary: A cyber-attack took down Canvas, a learning management system widely used by US schools and universities, on Thursday during final exam season. The outage left students unable to access course materials, causing widespread disruption to end-of-year academic schedules.

stories.title: Lebanese president meets delegation chief ahead of direct Israel talks
stories.summary: Lebanese President met with the head of a diplomatic delegation on Friday ahead of planned direct talks with Israel. The delegation is scheduled to travel to Washington next week for the negotiations.

stories.title: Pakistan, Afghanistan: Why is the ‘Durand Line’ on fire?
stories.summary: Tensions along the Durand Line between Pakistan and Afghanistan have escalated. While Pakistan has been mediating between the U.S., Iran, and Israel, it has not pursued dialogue with neighboring Afghanistan over the border dispute.

stories.title: ABC lawyers accuse Trump’s FCC of punishing network for political reasons
stories.summary: Lawyers for ABC-owned KTRK-TV in Houston filed a legal motion accusing the FCC of politically motivated punishment over its investigation into the talkshow The View. The filing alleges the Trump-era FCC is using its regulatory authority to target the network for its editorial content.

stories.title: Frustrated by Iran, Trump at last seizes enriched uranium – but from Venezuela
stories.summary: The US Department of Energy announced the removal of 13.5 kilograms of highly enriched uranium from a legacy research reactor in Caracas, Venezuela. The amount is a small fraction of the 408 kilograms of enriched uranium held by Iran, which remains a separate diplomatic challenge for the Trump administration.

stories.title: World food prices rise to more than three-year high in April, FAO says
stories.summary: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization reported that world food prices rose to a more than three-year high in April. Vegetable oil prices were particularly elevated due to disruptions caused by the Iran war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Iran warns US over ‘adventurism’ after strikes on vessels
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei condemned recent U.S. military strikes on Iranian vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. Baghaei warned Washington against what he called "adventurism and roguish behaviour" and appeared to respond to remarks by U.S. President Donald Trump.

stories.title: Turkish MP says negotiation with Russia on freeing Crimean Tatar prisoners “not possible”
stories.summary: A Turkish member of parliament said that negotiating with Russia on the release of Crimean Tatar political prisoners is practically impossible due to Moscow's position. Turkey continues to monitor the situation of Crimean Tatars in Russian-occupied Crimea.

stories.title: ‘Stop bankrolling genocide’: Palestine activists target Barclays
stories.summary: Pro-Palestine protesters repeatedly interrupted a Barclays shareholder meeting in London, accusing the bank of financially supporting what they called genocide in Gaza. Activists demanded the bank stop its alleged involvement in funding related to the conflict.

stories.title: Return of Palestine Marathon attracts thousands of runners
stories.summary: Thousands of runners participated in the Palestine Marathon in Bethlehem, which returned after a two-year hiatus caused by the Gaza war. The event drew international and local participants.

stories.title: Kyiv prepares massive defence spending increase in 2026 budget as EU funds drive weapons production and military pay
stories.summary: Ukraine's government is preparing a significant increase in defense spending for its 2026 budget. The planned shift focuses on domestic weapons production, military salaries, and resilience infrastructure, supported in part by European Union funding.

stories.title: WHO says hantavirus risk low after flight attendant tests negative
stories.summary: The World Health Organisation said the overall public risk from hantavirus remains low after a flight attendant tested negative. Three passengers aboard the Dutch-flagged MV Hondius have died from the Andes virus strain, which can transmit between humans, prompting international concern and repatriation planning.

stories.title: First batch of UFO files is released as Trump urges public to draw its own conclusions
stories.summary: The US government released its first batch of declassified UFO files, which include military videos showing unidentified objects over Iraq, Syria, and the UAE. President Trump encouraged the public to review the materials and draw its own conclusions.

stories.title: EU ministers to adopt sanctions related to Russia's deportations of Ukrainian children
stories.summary: EU foreign ministers are expected to adopt new sanctions on Monday targeting individuals and entities involved in the deportation of Ukrainian children to Russia. The decision was confirmed by two EU sources in Brussels.

stories.title: More than a dozen reported killed in Israeli attacks on south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli air raids on southern Lebanon killed more than a dozen people, according to reports. The escalation comes ahead of a new round of US-mediated negotiations expected to take place in Washington, DC, the following week.

stories.title: David Attenborough, the excited but hushed voice of nature programs, turns 100
stories.summary: British naturalist and broadcaster David Attenborough celebrated his 100th birthday. The BBC marked the occasion with tributes and events honoring his decades-long career in wildlife programming. Attenborough's family sheltered two German-Jewish refugee girls during World War II.

stories.title: Denmark records third straight year of historically high antisemitism
stories.summary: Denmark recorded a third consecutive year of historically high antisemitism, with the Jewish community of approximately 6,000 people reporting 199 antisemitic incidents. Prior to October 7, the annual average was around seven incidents. Twenty-four incidents targeted Jewish children and teenagers, three of which were violent.

stories.title: A government critic dies in custody in Rwanda, drawing calls for an independent probe
stories.summary: A government critic died in custody in Rwanda, prompting calls for an independent investigation. Many critics accuse Rwandan President Paul Kagame of suppressing dissent and running an authoritarian regime.

stories.title: Drones attack area near one of Russia’s largest military bases in Grozny – media
stories.summary: Drones struck the Khankala area in Grozny, Chechnya, near one of Russia's largest military bases. Strikes also targeted an area near the railway station close to the regional FSB office building.

stories.title: Iran foreign minister says ‘Iranians never bow to pressure’
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi pushed back against U.S. actions, posting on X that "Iranians never bow to pressure." He questioned whether recent U.S. moves were deliberate pressure tactics and accused Washington of choosing military adventure over diplomacy.

stories.title: How did US weapons intended for Iranian Kurds disappear?
stories.summary: Iraqi Kurdish factions traded blame over the disappearance of an alleged U.S. weapons shipment intended for Iranian Kurdish opposition groups. The fate of the arms remains unclear amid mutual accusations among the Kurdish parties.

stories.title: EU climate monitor says sea temperatures could reach record high in May
stories.summary: The EU's climate monitoring service warned that global sea surface temperatures could reach record highs in May. Scientists expressed concern that warming oceans may signal the development of a potentially severe "super El Niño" later in the year.

stories.title: Rubio questions allies' support on Iran following Italy talks
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio questioned why allied nations, including Italy, were not supporting Washington's efforts to confront Iran and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Rubio raised the concerns during talks in Italy.

stories.title: New suspected hantavirus cases found in Spain and remote Tristan da Cunha
stories.summary: Two new suspected hantavirus cases were reported on Friday, one in Spain and one on the remote South Atlantic island of Tristan da Cunha. The cases are linked to an outbreak that began on a luxury cruise ship and has been associated with three deaths. The WHO has said the risk to the wider public remains low.

stories.title: EU wants to move fast on Moldova accession talks, Kallas says
stories.summary: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas stated in Chișinău on Friday that the European Union intends to move quickly on Moldova's accession talks, though no formal date has been set for opening negotiations.

stories.title: South Africa's top court backs case seeking to revive impeachment process against president
stories.summary: South Africa's Constitutional Court on Friday sided with an opposition party seeking to revive impeachment proceedings against President Cyril Ramaphosa over the "Farmgate" scandal involving allegations of misconduct related to his private farm.

stories.title: Zelensky visits command post of 67th Brigade, meets troops and presents awards
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky visited the command post of Ukraine's 67th Separate Mechanized Brigade, where he discussed unit needs with servicemen. He also presented state awards to Ukrainian defenders during the visit.

stories.title: Nintendo to hike Switch 2 price, warns on profits
stories.summary: Nintendo announced that the Switch 2 console's price in Japan will increase by 20 percent effective May 25. The company also issued a warning about its profit outlook.

stories.title: Reform UK gains at Labour’s expense in local elections – podcast
stories.summary: Reform UK made substantial gains in UK local elections at Labour's expense, while the Green Party also achieved notable wins including in London. Prime Minister Keir Starmer faced calls to announce a departure timeline but insisted he would not step down.

stories.title: Israeli army chief recommends commander who destroyed Gaza university for senior role
stories.summary: Israeli army chief of staff recommended Brigadier-General Barak Hiram for the post of military secretary. Hiram commanded forces that destroyed a Gaza university and ordered tank fire at a home during the October 7 attacks.

stories.title: Gaza flotilla heads to Turkey after Israeli Navy's interception, detention of two members
stories.summary: A Gaza-bound flotilla diverted to Marmaris, Turkey, after the Israeli Navy intercepted the mission and detained two of its members. Organizers are meeting in Turkey to develop an updated legal strategy and revised operational plans.

stories.title: Five killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon, including child
stories.summary: At least five people were killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon, including a child. Four victims died in a strike on the town of Ad-Doueir, and one person was killed in a separate attack targeting a motorcycle in Jebchit. The strikes occurred despite an existing ceasefire.

stories.title: Reform and Greens surge in local elections: what next for Labour? – The Latest
stories.summary: Labour suffered heavy losses in UK local elections as Reform UK and the Green Party made significant gains. Prime Minister Keir Starmer vowed to continue leading despite the results, which have prompted questions about whether Britain's traditional two-party political system is ending.

stories.title: Hondurasgate: Leaked recordings allege US-Israeli destabilisation plot in Latin America
stories.summary: Leaked voice recordings published by investigative site Hondurasgate and Spanish platform Canal Red allege U.S. and Israeli efforts to advance interests in Honduras and destabilize left-leaning Latin American governments. The investigation includes 37 authenticated voice notes from WhatsApp, Signal, and Telegram.

stories.title: US waiting on a response from Iran over proposals for ceasefire deal, says Rubio
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington is awaiting Iran's response to proposals for an interim ceasefire deal in the Middle East. The diplomatic effort continues amid escalating clashes around the Strait of Hormuz, where recent fighting has been the most intense since an informal truce began.

stories.title: Ukraine, EU should consider joint development of nuclear weapons – Horbulin
stories.summary: Volodymyr Horbulin, First Vice President of Ukraine's National Academy of Sciences, proposed that Ukraine and Europe begin considering joint development of nuclear weapons. The suggestion reflects growing security concerns amid the ongoing war with Russia.

stories.title: Palestine and the UK elections: What early wins, losses suggest
stories.summary: Pro-Palestine candidates influenced results in UK local elections, contributing to losses for Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour Party. Early results suggest the Palestine issue played a notable role in shaping voter decisions.

stories.title: South Africa: Zulu Royal Wives Face Diana and Camilla Style Social Media War
stories.summary: A social media feud involving Zulu King Misuzulu's third wife in South Africa has drawn comparisons to the public rivalry between fans of Princess Diana and Queen Camilla in Britain.

stories.title: Turkish air force contracts its first batch of indigenous KAAN jets
stories.summary: Turkish Aerospace signed a contract with the Turkish air force for an initial batch of 20 Block 10 KAAN fighter jets, the country's first indigenous fifth-generation combat aircraft. CEO Mehmet Demiroglu said orders are expected to increase over time.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: High Court Blocks Immediate Return of Disputed Bindura Mine Sites
stories.summary: A Zimbabwean High Court dismissed an application by Ouro Tanque Private Limited to take immediate control of disputed mining sites in Bindura. The ruling allows Freda Rebecca Gold Mine Limited to continue its appeal.

stories.title: Nigeria: Court Rejects Sowore's No-Case Submission, Orders Activist to Open Defence
stories.summary: A Nigerian Federal High Court in Abuja rejected activist Omoyele Sowore's no-case submission in a cyberbullying case brought by the Department of State Services. Justice Mohammed Garba Umar ordered Sowore to open his defense over alleged derogatory remarks about President Bola Tinubu.

stories.title: Saudi banned US use of bases, airspace for Hormuz operation: sources
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia refused to allow the United States to use Saudi airspace or military bases for operations related to Washington's brief effort to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, according to sources.

stories.title: Rwanda: Rwandan Youtuber Dies of Alleged Overdose On Day of Release From Prison
stories.summary: Rwandan YouTube commentator Aimable Karasira Uzaramba died of an alleged overdose on the day he was scheduled to be released from prison after completing a five-year sentence. The Committee to Protect Journalists called for an independent investigation into his death.

stories.title: Nigeria: 2027 - Massive Mobilisation for Obi, Kwakwanso Ticket Begins in S/E.
