stories.summary: Russian forces launched a drone strike on the Novobavarskyi district of Kharkiv, Ukraine, igniting a fire and causing casualties. The attack targeted a populated area of Ukraine's second-largest city.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Iran denies ship attack as Trump warns of renewed bombing, eyes deal
stories.summary: Iran denied responsibility for a blast aboard the Panama-flagged vessel HMM Namu, with Tehran's embassy in Seoul categorically rejecting allegations its armed forces were involved. Meanwhile, President Trump warned of renewed bombing against Iran while simultaneously pursuing a diplomatic deal.

stories.title: Irish footballers and celebrities urge boycott of Israel matches
stories.summary: An Irish campaign group and prominent footballers and celebrities are urging a boycott of Israel's matches in the UEFA Nations League, citing Israel's conduct in the war on Gaza.

stories.title: Iran's president says he recently met with the supreme leader
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said he recently met with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who had suffered severe wounds at the start of the US-Israeli war on Iran. Pezeshkian described the meeting as humble and deeply cordial.

stories.title: Turkiye unveils its first intercontinental ballistic missile: What we know
stories.summary: Turkey unveiled its first intercontinental ballistic missile, the Yildirimhan, which has a reported range of 6,000 km, a maximum speed of Mach 25, and a payload capacity of 3,000 kg.

stories.title: 'Time to say goodbye': Judge releases Epstein's alleged 'suicide note'
stories.summary: A US judge has released a purported suicide letter written by Jeffrey Epstein, dated weeks before he was found dead in his prison cell. Separately, Swiss health authorities are working to trace contacts of a Swiss man being treated for a human-to-human strain of hantavirus after he traveled freely while infected.

stories.title: More than 50,000 pupils expected to strike over German rearmament policy
stories.summary: Organisers of a nationwide school strike in Germany expect more than 50,000 pupils to boycott classes on Friday to protest the government's rearmament policy. Students aim to oppose what they describe as policies that could turn young Germans into "cannon fodder," despite threats of penalties from education authorities.

stories.title: France's far-right Le Pen and Bardella court Israel, Germany envoys ahead of presidential vote
stories.summary: France's far-right National Rally leaders Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella have met with the ambassadors of Germany and Israel in recent months. The outreach is part of the party's effort to build diplomatic credibility ahead of next year's French presidential elections.

stories.title: Can Asian economies cope with the fallout from the Iran war?
stories.summary: Asian economies are facing rising fuel costs, inflation, and debt pressures linked to the fallout from the war on Iran, raising questions about their ability to cope with the economic disruption.

stories.title: AI ‘blueprint’ coming soon to NGA to help ‘operationalize’ GEOINT
stories.summary: Lt. Gen. Michelle Bredenkamp, the new director of the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, announced that an AI "blueprint" will soon be released to help operationalize geospatial intelligence. In her first major speech leading NGA, she also revealed the agency has established a new Rapid Capabilities Office to accelerate integration of commercial technology.

stories.title: Africa sees winners and losers as Iran war pushes up oil prices
stories.summary: Several African countries have sought financial assistance amid economic uncertainty driven by rising oil prices caused by the war on Iran. The conflict is creating both winners and losers across the continent.

stories.title: South Africa: Nelson Mandela Bay Issues Flood Warning Amid Hazardous Conditions
stories.summary: The Nelson Mandela Bay Municipality in South Africa issued a flood warning as heavy rainfall caused widespread flooding and hazardous conditions across the metro. The Disaster Management Centre urged residents, motorists, and pedestrians to exercise extreme caution.

stories.title: Motorbike gunmen kill BJP political aide in India's West Bengal
stories.summary: Gunmen on motorbikes shot and killed Chandranath Rath, 41, a close aide of West Bengal BJP chief Suvendu Adhikari, near his home in Kolkata on Wednesday night. The killing came days after the BJP won its first-ever state election victory in West Bengal, securing 207 of 294 assembly seats.

stories.title: Uganda: Uganda's Sickle Cell Patients At Risk As Asthma Goes Undetected
stories.summary: A 16-year-old sickle cell patient in Uganda was treated for two weeks for a suspected chest infection that did not respond to antibiotics. Diagnostic tests, including a chest X-ray and blood work, found no abnormalities, raising concerns that undetected asthma may be putting sickle cell patients at risk.

stories.title: Breathe Pakistan: Envoy notes melting glaciers ‘shared vulnerability’ for countries like Nepal, Pakistan
stories.summary: At the Breathe Pakistan International Climate Change Conference in Islamabad, diplomats highlighted the shared vulnerability of countries like Nepal and Pakistan to melting glaciers. Despite contributing minimally to global emissions, Pakistan remains among the world's most climate-vulnerable nations.

stories.title: Nigeria: Court Convicts Former Minister of Fraud
stories.summary: A Federal High Court in Abuja, Nigeria, convicted former Power Minister Saleh Mamman on 12 counts of fraud and money laundering. The charges were brought by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC).

stories.title: Missile strike on Merefa in Kharkiv region: Death toll climbs to eight
stories.summary: The death toll from a May 4 missile strike on Merefa in Ukraine's Kharkiv region has risen to eight after a seriously wounded man died in hospital. The town is located south of Kharkiv city.

stories.title: Appeals court overturns murder conviction of man who killed girlfriend, orders retrial
stories.summary: A Hong Kong appellate court overturned the murder conviction of Law Wai-man, who was found guilty of killing his girlfriend Lau Lee-chi in 2019. The Court of Appeal ruled that the trial judge failed to properly direct the jury to consider the defendant's violent personality traits and ordered a retrial.

stories.title: Trump’s Europe pullback could open new doors for Israel - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion analysis suggests that the Trump administration's pullback from Europe could create new strategic opportunities for Israel. The shift is reportedly based on a broad U.S. assessment of future challenges and risks.

stories.title: A growing number of US Muslims run for political office in 2026
stories.summary: A growing number of Muslim Americans are running for political office in the 2026 US midterm elections at federal, state, and local levels. This represents a significant increase compared to a decade ago, when Muslim candidacies were far less common.

stories.title: Did Saudi Arabia force Trump to pause Hormuz 'Project Freedom'?
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia reportedly threatened to ban US military aircraft from its airspace and deny access to its bases if the US proceeded with 'Project Freedom' to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The threat reportedly forced President Trump to pause the operation.

stories.title: Did Saudi Arabia force Trump to pause Hormuz 'Freedom' project?
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia reportedly threatened to bar the U.S. military from its airspace and bases, forcing President Trump to pause his "Project Freedom" plan to escort vessels through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: How China Is Winning the Global AI Race
stories.summary: An analysis argues that advanced U.S. artificial intelligence models are too costly for much of the world, giving China a competitive advantage in the global AI race. The high price of cutting-edge American AI technology is limiting its adoption in many countries.

stories.title: Marka-i-Haq: ISPR says any hostile design against Pakistan will be countered with greater strength, resolve
stories.summary: Pakistan's military media wing, ISPR, warned that any hostile design against the country would be met with 'even greater strength, precision and resolve.' The statement marked the anniversary of last year's military conflict with India, which Pakistan has dubbed 'Marka-i-Haq' (Battle of Truth).

stories.title: Russia’s economy slows as war costs mount, budget deficit widens, and rate cuts near their limit
stories.summary: Russia's economy is showing signs of strain after five years of full-scale war in Ukraine, with a widening budget deficit, limited room for further interest rate cuts, and accumulating systemic problems. While some indicators such as low unemployment and a strong ruble appear positive, analysts note they conceal underlying vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Rwanda: Kagame Congratulates PSG On Reaching Champions League Final
stories.summary: Rwandan President Paul Kagame congratulated Paris Saint-Germain after the French football club secured a place in the UEFA Champions League final. Rwanda has a longstanding sponsorship partnership with PSG.

stories.title: Why is Israel concerned over a possible US-Iran deal?
stories.summary: Israeli media coverage reveals growing concern that a potential U.S.-Iran agreement could strengthen Tehran's position and impose restrictions on Israel's military operations. The worry reflects broader Israeli anxieties about being sidelined in the negotiations.

stories.title: Local elections across UK test Starmer as Reform UK eyes major gains
stories.summary: UK voters cast ballots on Thursday, May 7, in local and devolved elections across the country. The polls are seen as a major test for Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour government, with the Reform UK party expected to make significant gains.

stories.title: Rubio to meet Pope Leo as Trump keeps up attacks on pontiff
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Pope Leo at the Vatican on Thursday amid tensions, as President Trump has continued disparaging attacks on the pontiff over the Iran war. The encounter was described as potentially fraught given the ongoing public disagreements.

stories.title: KP PDMA directs deputy commissioners to take precuationary measures ahead of heatwave
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Provincial Disaster Management Authority directed all deputy commissioners to take precautionary measures ahead of a heatwave expected from May 8 to 10. Temperatures may reach 43–47°C in districts including Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, and Bannu.

stories.title: Israeli soldier pictured desecrating Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli soldier was photographed placing a cigarette in the mouth of a Virgin Mary statue in the Christian village of Debel in southern Lebanon. The Israeli military said it would discipline the soldier involved.

stories.title: Israeli military investigates soldier's act against Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military is investigating a soldier who was photographed placing a cigarette in the mouth of a Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon. This marks the second incident targeting a Christian religious figure in the country within weeks.

stories.title: Russia Tells Foreign Embassies in Kyiv to Evacuate as It Warns of ‘Retaliatory’ Strikes
stories.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry warned foreign embassies in Kyiv to evacuate, citing planned retaliatory strikes on the Ukrainian capital. Moscow said it would target Kyiv if Ukrainian attacks disrupted annual Victory Day celebrations on May 9.

stories.title: Russia Tells Foreign Embassies to Evacuate Kyiv as It Warns of ‘Retaliatory’ Strikes
stories.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry warned foreign embassies to evacuate Kyiv, stating that Russia would target the Ukrainian capital with retaliatory strikes if Ukrainian attacks on Saturday disrupted annual Victory Day celebrations in Russia.

stories.title: Russian attacks cause new power outages in frontline regions, says Ukrenergo
stories.summary: Ukraine's national grid operator Ukrenergo reported that Russian attacks as of the morning of May 7 have caused power outages affecting consumers in the Donetsk, Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhzhia, Kharkiv, and Sumy regions.

stories.title: Novelist JM Coetzee declines to attend Jerusalem writers festival over ‘genocidal campaign in Gaza’
stories.summary: Nobel laureate and South African novelist J.M. Coetzee declined an invitation to the Jerusalem International Writers Festival, citing Israel's military campaign in Gaza. He communicated his decision in a letter to the festival's artistic director.

stories.title: Hong Kong restaurants can apply from May 18 to become dog-friendly venues
stories.summary: Hong Kong restaurants can apply from May 18 to June 8 for licences to admit dogs under a new scheme, with the first designated venues expected to welcome pets from July. The Food and Environmental Hygiene Department will cap applications at 1,000 restaurants in the first phase.

stories.title: Dubai hotel occupancy projected to fall to 10 percent due to Iran war, report says
stories.summary: Hotel occupancy in Dubai is projected to plummet to 10 percent in the second quarter of 2026, down from 80 percent before the Iran war began in late February. Moody's Analytics described the decline as an effective shutdown of large parts of the hospitality sector, according to the Wall Street Journal.

stories.title: Somalia: Racing to Reverse the Hunger Tide
stories.summary: The World Food Programme warned that Somalia faces another potential hunger catastrophe as humanitarian needs surge and funding declines. Four years after a major donor mobilization averted famine, drought and resource shortfalls are again threatening the Horn of Africa nation.

stories.title: Palestine Coalition files complaint against London police chief
stories.summary: The Palestine Coalition filed a formal complaint against Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mark Rowley in London. The group is demanding he retract certain accusations and issue a full public apology.

stories.title: Inspector failed to spot illegal alterations, Hong Kong fire probe hears
stories.summary: A Hong Kong public inquiry into a deadly housing estate fire heard that a building inspector failed to conduct a site visit and mistook illegal alterations to emergency staircases for protective measures. Senior maintenance surveyor Nick Yung Siu-lun admitted basing his assessment solely on documents.

stories.title: Junta leader Assimi Goita target of April attacks, Malian army says
stories.summary: Mali's military confirmed that last month's coordinated attacks in the country targeted junta leader Assimi Goita. Separately, allied Burkina Faso banned French television channel TV5 Monde over allegations of disinformation.

stories.title: What are US proposals to end war, and will Iran agree to them?
stories.summary: Iran says it is reviewing a US proposal to end the US-Israeli war against it, a conflict that has triggered a global crisis. The outcome of Tehran's deliberations remains uncertain.

stories.title: Kumanjayi Little Baby: Advocates say five-year-old’s death ‘should not be politicised’ as hundreds gather at vigils
stories.summary: Hundreds gathered at vigils across Australia to mourn five-year-old Warlpiri girl Kumanjayi Little Baby, whose body was found in Alice Springs. Advocates and the national body representing First Nations children called for an end to the politicisation of her alleged murder.

stories.title: New Zealand expands sanctions against Russia
stories.summary: On May 7, New Zealand's government imposed new sanctions on 20 Russian individuals and entities for their support of Russia's war against Ukraine. The move expands New Zealand's existing sanctions regime targeting those involved in the conflict.

stories.title: WHO warns of more hantavirus cases in 'limited' outbreak
stories.summary: The World Health Organization warned on May 7 that additional hantavirus cases may emerge but expects the outbreak to remain limited if precautions are taken. The alert followed the deaths of three cruise ship passengers from the disease.

stories.title: Israeli army disables Hezbollah rocket tracking system in north
stories.summary: Israel's military disabled a key Hezbollah rocket tracking system used by northern local authorities during attacks. The system was cut off over concerns that data could be leaked to Iran.

stories.title: Reopening strait of Hormuz would have limited impact on cargo flows, says Maersk
stories.summary: Maersk CEO Vincent Clerc said reopening the Strait of Hormuz would have a "limited impact" on cargo flows, as the shipping industry contends with sharply higher energy costs from the conflict. Maersk's fuel bill has nearly doubled, adding up to $500 million in monthly costs, which the company has passed on to customers through higher freight rates.

stories.title: Liberia: Boakai Sends War Crimes, Anti-Corruption Court Bills to Legislature
stories.summary: Liberian President Joseph Boakai formally submitted draft legislation to establish a Special War Crimes Court and a National Anti-Corruption Court. Both bills have been forwarded to the National Legislature for consideration.

stories.title: Trump takes another U-turn on Iran
stories.summary: The article references President Trump reversing his position on Iran policy, though specific details of the latest shift were not provided in the available text.

stories.title: Israeli strikes on Lebanon's Nabatieh kill one person
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes and drones struck Nabatieh in southern Lebanon on Wednesday, killing one person and injuring several others. The strikes destroyed two residential buildings near the Evangelical School and cut the main road to Nabatieh al-Fawqa.

stories.title: India loses information war to country that wasn't technically allowed online
stories.summary: During the May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict, Pakistan waged an effective information warfare campaign on social media despite limited internet infrastructure. The article examines how both sides used platforms like X to amplify favorable narratives and suppress damaging ones during the hostilities.

stories.title: Kimi developer Moonshot AI valued at US$20b as it navigates China’s new IPO rules
stories.summary: Chinese AI start-up Moonshot AI, developer of the Kimi chatbot, raised about $2 billion in a new funding round led by Long-Z Investments and Meituan's venture arm, boosting its valuation to over $20 billion. The Beijing-based company has raised a total of $3.9 billion over the past six months.

stories.title: As new Holocaust memorial stone laid in Berlin, relative says plaque serves as substitute for grave
stories.summary: A new Holocaust memorial 'stumbling block' stone was laid in Berlin for Nazi victim Johanna Berger by project initiator Gunter Demnig. Berger's great-nephew said the plaque serves as a substitute for a grave and brings the family's history to a certain conclusion.

stories.title: Vladimir Putin Is Much Weaker Than You Think
stories.summary: An analysis assesses that Russian President Vladimir Putin's strategic position is weaker than widely perceived. The piece argues that Putin, long known for outmaneuvering adversaries, is facing diminishing room for maneuver.

stories.title: Over half of Israeli adults are overweight or obese, Knesset Health Committee told
stories.summary: The Knesset Health Committee was told that over half of Israeli adults are overweight or obese, with 31.4% of seventh graders also overweight. Officials attributed the problem to high medication costs, inadequate health services in low-income areas, and insufficient educational materials in Arab and Ethiopian communities.

stories.title: DRC leader Tshisekedi hints at possible rule beyond second term amid eastern war
stories.summary: DRC President Felix Tshisekedi suggested he may seek a third term and hinted at potentially delaying the presidential election scheduled for 2028 due to ongoing conflict in the country's eastern regions. Tshisekedi, in power since 2019, is constitutionally limited to two five-year terms under current DRC law.

stories.title: France resumes genocide probe against Rwanda ex-president's widow
stories.summary: A French court on Wednesday ordered the resumption of an investigation into Agathe Habyarimana, widow of former Rwandan president Juvenal Habyarimana, over alleged complicity in the 1994 genocide. Investigating magistrates had dismissed the case last year citing insufficient evidence. The probe, which began in France in 2007, will now continue.

stories.title: Burkina Faso junta secretly detained journalist and others, advocacy group says
stories.summary: Reporters Without Borders reported that Burkina Faso's military authorities secretly detained and abused investigative journalist Atiana Serge Oulon and dozens of others at a makeshift facility in the capital. Oulon, editor of the newspaper L'Événement, was taken from his home by armed men in civilian clothes in June 2024.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Iran reviewing peace proposal as Trump says a deal ‘very possible’
stories.summary: The US and Iran have offered conflicting messages over the likelihood of a deal being reached imminentlyHere are the latest pictures from the Dahiyeh neighbourhood of southern Beirut, where rescue wor

stories.title: Rubio set to meet Pope Leo in bid to ease tensions after Trump’s criticism of the pontiff - Europe live
stories.summary: Relations between the Vatican and Washington are increasingly fraught after the US president lashed out at the pope over his criticism of the war in IranEarlier today, Pope Leo welcomed Poland’s prime

stories.title: 2 former Chinese defence ministers handed suspended death sentences
stories.summary: Two former Chinese defence ministers, Wei Fenghe and Li Shangfu, received suspended death sentences after being found guilty of corruption by a military court. Wei was convicted of accepting bribes, while Li was convicted of both accepting and offering bribes. Both were previously expelled from the Communist Party in 2024.

stories.title: DR Congo president hints at extending his term and delaying polls
stories.summary: Democratic Republic of Congo President Félix Tshisekedi indicated he would accept a third presidential term if the public supports it, despite being constitutionally due to step down in 2028. His comments have raised concerns about a potential delay to scheduled elections.

stories.title: China seeks improved US ties and ‘harmony’, FM Wang Yi tells visiting American senators
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told visiting US Senator Steve Daines that Beijing hoped to “truly stabilise and improve” Sino-American ties, a week before a highly anticipated summit between Xi Jinp

stories.title: Islamic State-linked women arrive home in Australia from Syria
stories.summary: A group of nine women and children has landed in Melbourne while another woman and her child arrived in Sydney.

stories.title: Powerful US utilities secretly fund ‘grassroots’ groups to sway cities away from switch to public power
stories.summary: As communities push for publicly owned electricity, private utilities may be deploying dark money and local front groups to stop themThe utility industry is quietly dispatching a network of front grou

stories.title: China woman fired due to husband’s rival firm job receives US$101,000 for unjust dismissal
stories.summary:
A Shanghai company has been ordered to pay a woman employee 690,000 yuan (US$101,000) for illegally firing her because her husband works for a rival firm.
Xuhui District People’s Court made the ruling

stories.title: Air Defense Forces shoot down 92 of 102 Russian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Defense Forces intercepted 92 of 102 Russian drones launched against the country between the evening of May 6 and the following day. Ten drones were not successfully shot down during the barrage.

stories.title: Hamas official confirms killing of leader’s son in Gaza City
stories.summary: Hamas official Basim Naim confirmed that Azzam al-Hayya, son of Hamas political bureau chief Khalil al-Hayya, was killed in an Israeli airstrike on Gaza City. He is the fourth of al-Hayya's sons to be killed by Israeli attacks, including one killed in a strike in Doha, Qatar.

stories.title: US reinstates deportation proceedings against Palestinian green-card holder student
stories.summary: The United States has reinstated deportation proceedings against Mohsen Mahdawi, a Palestinian green-card holder and Columbia University student. Mahdawi, a pro-Palestine activist who led anti-war protests at Columbia, was previously detained for two weeks during his citizenship interview.

stories.title: Taiwan warns of China 'maneuvering' ahead of Trump-Xi summit
stories.summary: Taiwan warned that China may be maneuvering diplomatically ahead of an upcoming summit between President Trump and President Xi Jinping in Beijing. Taipei said it is closely monitoring for any shifts in U.S. policy regarding Taiwan.

stories.title: What is China’s anti-sanctions law and how does it work?
stories.summary: China invoked its 2021 anti-sanctions law for the first time, ordering the blocking of U.S. sanctions targeting five Chinese oil refineries. The law was designed to counter foreign sanctions that Beijing considers unjustified.

stories.title: Israeli soldier mocks Virgin Mary statue in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: An image of an Israeli soldier placing a cigarette in a Virgin Mary statue's mouth in southern Lebanon went viral. The incident followed a previous episode weeks earlier in which a statue of Jesus was bludgeoned in the same region.

stories.title: Latvian police debunk fake claim that Ukrainian drone hit passenger train
stories.summary: Latvia's State Police debunked online claims that a Ukrainian drone struck a passenger train on the Rīga–Daugavpils line on May 5. Authorities said the fire was likely caused by engine damage, not a drone strike.

stories.title: South Africa: Floods Smash Gqeberha As 2,000 Flee to Shelters
stories.summary: Severe flooding struck the city of Gqeberha in South Africa's Eastern Cape, forcing approximately 2,000 residents into 25 emergency shelters. The provincial health department closed a local clinic after storm water flooded the facility, and humanitarian organization Gift of the Givers issued urgent appeals for food and blankets.

stories.title: Rubio faces challenge in Pope Leo meeting after Trump's criticism over Iran
stories.summary: America's top diplomat, Marco Rubio, will meet the first US pope, Leo XIV, on Thursday, seeking to ease Washington-Vatican tensions while also promoting President Donald Trump's agenda. The US secreta

stories.title: US Rubio seeks to ease tensions with US pope after Trump's attacks
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is heading to the Vatican and Italy on a fence-mending visit after President Donald Trump’s broadsides against Pope Leo XIV and the U.S.-Israeli war in Iran have alie

stories.title: Trump sees swift end to war as Iran reviews US peace proposal
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump predicted a swift end to the war with Iran as Tehran considered a US peace proposal that sources said would formally end the conflict while leaving unresolved key US demands

stories.title: UK voters cast ballots in elections expected to deal blow to Starmer
stories.summary: Millions of British voters cast their ballots on Thursday in local and regional elections that are expected to ​deal a huge blow to Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour Party and renew questions over

stories.title: War update: 157 clashes on front lines, most battles reported in Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces recorded 157 combat clashes with Russian forces along the front lines on May 6. The heaviest fighting was reported in the Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors.

stories.title: What to know about hantavirus, the illness linked to a cruise ship outbreak
stories.summary: A hantavirus outbreak aboard a cruise ship has killed three passengers and sickened others. The rodent-borne virus typically spreads through inhalation of contaminated rodent droppings rather than person-to-person transmission. Global health officials say the risk to the general public remains low.

stories.title: Argentina probes link to deadly hantavirus outbreak on Atlantic cruise
stories.summary: Argentine officials are investigating whether their country is the source of the hantavirus outbreak on an Atlantic cruise that departed from Argentina for Antarctica. Argentina is experiencing a surge in hantavirus cases, which local researchers link to climate change. The WHO consistently ranks Argentina as having Latin America's highest incidence of the disease.

stories.title: Indonesia posts fastest first-quarter growth in 3 years, but headwinds loom
stories.summary: Indonesia’s economy grew 5.6 per cent during the first quarter of 2026, its fastest pace in more than three years, but analysts warn that the coming months will pose significant tests for Southeast As

stories.title: Iran’s stance on US war negotiations explained
stories.summary: Iran has outlined its position on ongoing war negotiations with the United States. Tehran's approach to the diplomatic process reflects its broader strategic considerations amid the conflict.

stories.title: Iran accuses US of ceasefire breach after ships, Hormuz struck
stories.summary: Iran accused the United States of violating their ceasefire agreement after strikes were reported in several areas in and around the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Trump ramps up pressure as Iran reviews US peace proposal
stories.summary: Iran is reviewing a new US proposal aimed at ending the conflict, with discussions focusing on reopening the Strait of Hormuz and addressing Tehran's nuclear program. President Trump has ramped up pressure on Iran to accept terms.

stories.title: Trump ramps up pressure on Tehran amid ongoing talks
stories.summary: Tehran is reviewing a new American proposal aimed at ending the conflict, while President Trump pressures Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and limit its nuclear program. Diplomatic talks between the US and Iran are ongoing.

stories.title: Trump says Iran deal 'very possible' as Israel bombs Beirut
stories.summary: President Trump suggested an Iran deal is "very possible" as diplomatic efforts continue. Meanwhile, an Israeli airstrike on Beirut killed a commander of Hezbollah's elite Radwan Force.

stories.title: Cruise ship with hantavirus outbreak heads to Spain's Canary Islands after 3 are evacuated
stories.summary: Two hantavirus patients and one suspected case were evacuated Wednesday from the cruise ship at the center of the deadly outbreak. The vessel then departed Cape Verde for Spain's Canary Islands with nearly 150 people on board, all isolated in their cabins.

stories.title: Antisemitism has become ‘almost fashionable’ among Australians, Jillian Segal tells royal commission
stories.summary: On its fourth day of public hearings, royal commission into antisemitism also hears Jewish Australians have been pressured to resign and verbally abusedGet our breaking news email, free app or daily n

stories.title: Britons set to punish Starmer's Labour in local polls
stories.summary: Polling stations opened Thursday across the United Kingdom for local elections expected to deliver significant losses for Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour Party. Opinion polls predict poor results for Labour, potentially intensifying calls for Starmer to resign or face a party leadership challenge amid rising support for hard-right and left-wing populist movements.

stories.title: Stitching lives back together for Central African Republic's child soldiers
stories.summary: In Bria, in eastern Central African Republic, former child soldiers aged 14 to 17 are learning to sew as part of reintegration efforts after being recruited by armed groups. The diamond-rich eastern region of the CAR has been devastated by years of armed conflict involving multiple militias.

stories.title: Rwanda, Botswana sign six cooperation deals
stories.summary: Rwanda and Botswana signed six cooperation agreements covering aviation, tourism, education, transport, and agriculture during a visit by Rwandan President Paul Kagame. The visit was among the first state visits hosted by Botswana's President Boko since taking office.

stories.title: South Sudan: MSF Forced to Close Lankien Hospital After 31 Years
stories.summary: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) has permanently closed its hospital in Lankien, Jonglei State, South Sudan, after the facility was bombarded on February 3. The closure ends 31 years of continuous medical support to the community. MSF called for an independent investigation into the attack.

stories.title: Planes carrying IS-linked family members land in Australia, with police expected to make arrests
stories.summary: Group of 13 women and children left Syria for Australia on Wednesday, with authorities saying some adults may be chargedGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastThirteen women and ch

stories.title: Australia to tour Pakistan for 3-match ODI series beginning on May 30
stories.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board announced that Australia's men's cricket team will tour Pakistan for a three-match ODI series. The first match is scheduled for May 30 at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium, with the remaining two matches in Lahore on June 2 and 4.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones target Russia’s main army logistics hub—days before Putin’s Victory parade
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones targeted the 200-hectare Nara complex in Russia, the Defense Ministry's primary logistics hub for distributing military cargo to armed forces. The strikes came just days before President Putin's Victory Day parade.

stories.title: Israel says it coordinated delivery of rat pesticides to Gaza to counter infestation
stories.summary: Israel coordinated the delivery of hundreds of cartons of specialized poisons and 20 tons of pesticide to Gaza through the U.S.-led Coordination Center. The effort targets a rodent infestation worsened by warm weather and sewage conditions in tent cities.

stories.title: Britons on hantavirus-hit ship to be asked to isolate back in UK for 45 days
stories.summary: Two British nationals who left MV Hondius before outbreak was detected are already self-isolating at home, say officialsWhat is hantavirus?British passengers onboard a cruise ship hit with a deadly ou

stories.title: Rubio arrives at Vatican to meet Pope Leo amid Trump attacks
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio traveled to the Vatican to meet Pope Leo. Vatican Secretary of State Cardinal Pietro Parolin confirmed the meeting was requested by the American side, amid tensions between the Trump administration and the papacy.

stories.title: Russian army kills three residents of Donetsk region and injures six others
stories.summary: The Russian army killed three civilians and wounded six others in the Donetsk region of Ukraine over a 24-hour period on May 6, according to local authorities.

stories.title: Iran releases video said to show US drone shot down over Hormuz
stories.summary: Iranian state media released video footage purportedly showing the wreckage of a U.S. drone that Iran claims it shot down over the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Dueling Victory Day ceasefires for war in Ukraine collapse almost immediately
stories.summary: Both Russia and Ukraine proclaimed ceasefires around Victory Day, which marks the Soviet Union's role in defeating Nazi Germany. However, the dueling ceasefires collapsed almost immediately, with fighting resuming shortly after they were announced.

stories.title: Gun salutes to mark third anniversary of King’s coronation
stories.summary: Regular soldiers and members of the Army Reserve have paid their respects to King Charles and Queen Camilla by firing a number of royal gun salutes on the third anniversary of their coronation.

stories.title: Man charged for shooting at two Toronto-area synagogues in March
stories.summary: A man has been charged in connection with shootings at two synagogues in the Toronto area in March. The accused, who was a minor at the time, allegedly fired shots at the separate synagogues 30 minutes apart during Shabbat and faces illegal weapons and property damage charges.

stories.title: JD Sports says Iran war could hit consumer spending and raise prices
stories.summary: Retail group with 4,800 stores worldwide expects drop in profits this year amid ‘muted market’Business live – latest updatesThe sports fashion retailer JD has warned that profits will fall this year a

stories.title: Why the War Powers Resolution deadline doesn’t actually constrain presidents
stories.summary: An analysis of the War Powers Resolution explores why its 60-day deadline for unauthorized military action has historically failed to constrain U.S. presidents. The resolution's enforcement mechanisms have a complex and contested legal history.

stories.title: Woman jailed in Somalia for peaceful protest ‘stripped, kicked and beaten’

stories.summary:
US President Donald Trump said conflict in the Middle East would be “over quickly”, as Iran considered a peace proposal that could lead to the reopening of the vital Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Hong Kong recalls Zwilling electric kettle over handle defect and scalding risk
stories.summary:
Hong Kong authorities have urged the public to stop using a certain model of Zwilling electric kettle over concerns that the handle may detach, posing a risk of scalding.
The Electrical and Mechanical

stories.title: Russians attack Kharkiv, 15 other settlements in Kharkiv region, leaving eight injured
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked Kharkiv and 15 other settlements across the Kharkiv region over the past day, injuring eight people. The strikes targeted multiple areas throughout the northeastern Ukrainian oblast.

stories.title: Police investigate alleged indecent assault of boy, 4, at international school
stories.summary: Hong Kong police are investigating an allegation that a four-year-old boy was indecently assaulted at an international school in Stanley, with the institution saying its security footage showed “no ev

stories.title: Qatari PM to The New Arab: 'Positive progress' between US, Iran
stories.summary: Qatari Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani told The New Arab's Arabic edition that there has been "positive progress" in talks between the United States and Iran.

stories.title: French judiciary resumes genocide probe against Rwanda's former first lady
stories.summary: The Paris Court of Appeals ruled that a French judicial investigation should resume against Agathe Habyarimana, Rwanda's former first lady, for alleged complicity in the 1994 Rwandan genocide. The probe had previously been suspended.

stories.title: Why won’t most Ukrainian women refugees come back? The war is no longer the main reason
stories.summary: Ahead of the EAUW leadership forum at the European Parliament, analysts highlighted that war is no longer the primary reason most of the 5.9 million Ukrainian women refugees have not returned home. Other factors including economic opportunities and integration abroad now play a larger role.

stories.title: Hamas leader's son dies of wounds sustained in Israeli strike on Gaza, report says
stories.summary: Azzam al-Hayya, son of Hamas political bureau chief Khalil al-Hayya, died from wounds sustained in an Israeli strike on Gaza. Al-Shifa Hospital confirmed his death after he was initially reported as seriously wounded by his father on Al Jazeera.

stories.title: Ukraine’s diaspora question lands at the European Parliament on Monday
stories.summary: A forum titled "Power. Voice. Legacy" is scheduled for May 11–12 at the European Parliament in Brussels, bringing together around 100 participants. The event will address the future of the Ukrainian diaspora as EU temporary protection for Ukrainian refugees nears its end.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz's daughter, son-in-law acquitted in graft case
stories.summary: An anti-corruption court in Lahore acquitted Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's daughter Rabia Imran and her husband Ali Imran Yousaf in a case involving alleged irregularities in the Punjab Saaf Pani Company. Judge Javed Iqbal Warraich found no evidence linking the two to the alleged offence.

stories.title: Meron rabbi arrested after cult watchdog warned of sex abuse in strictly run group
stories.summary: Rabbi Yosef Shoveli, 54, was arrested in Meron, Israel, after a cult watchdog warned of sexual abuse within his tightly controlled group. Accusers allege he disguised sexual abuse as spiritual acts, while group members had personal decisions controlled and performed unpaid labor.

stories.title: Russian attacks on Sumy region leave four killed, 11 injured over past day
stories.summary: Four people were killed and eleven injured in the Sumy region of Ukraine as a result of Russian strikes over the past 24 hours. An additional man was killed after stepping on a Russian-laid mine in the area.

stories.title: French warship moves towards Hormuz for possible defensive mission
stories.summary: A French warship has been deployed toward the Strait of Hormuz for a possible defensive mission. Meanwhile, Iran announced it is reviewing a U.S. proposal that President Trump claims could bring the war to an end.

stories.title: Irish athletes, celebrities urge boycott of upcoming soccer games against Israel
stories.summary: Irish athletes and celebrities signed a letter titled "Stop the Game" urging the Irish government to boycott upcoming UEFA Nations League soccer matches against Israel. The signatories called on the government to respect public sentiment and cancel the games planned for the fall.

stories.title: From Kabul to Tehran: How US diplomacy turned transactional
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump has criticized NATO allies for not supporting the U.S.-Israeli attack on Iran launched on 28 February, which led to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Trump threatened allies including Spain, warning the U.S. could use Spanish military bases unilaterally.

stories.title: TikTok makes record US$25b investment to expand digital infrastructure in Thailand
stories.summary: TikTok is investing US$25 billion in data infrastructure projects in Thailand, the company’s biggest investment announced to date in Southeast Asia, as China’s technology giants continue expanding the

stories.title: Australia’s interest rate rise signals growing hawkish stance in Asia
stories.summary: For an indication of how much the energy crisis is shaping the path of monetary policy, look no further than Australia. On May 5, the country’s central bank raised interest rates for the third consecu

stories.title: Saudi Arabia, Kuwait cut US base, airspace access, forcing pause of Trump's 'Project Freedom'
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia suspended U.S. access to Prince Sultan Airbase and Saudi airspace, forcing President Trump to pause his "Project Freedom" plan to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz. Kuwait also cut U.S. base and airspace access after being caught off guard by Trump's public announcement.

stories.title: The myth of Gulf exceptionalism and US protection is over
stories.summary: The Iran war has exposed the limits of Gulf states' security alliances with the United States, reducing nations in the region to collateral damage. The conflict has undermined long-held assumptions about U.S. protection for Gulf countries.

stories.title: Russia loses 890 troops, two air defense systems in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's military estimated that Russian forces lost approximately 890 personnel in the past 24 hours, bringing total estimated Russian combat losses since February 24, 2022, to about 1,338,060 as of May 7, 2026. Two Russian air defense systems were also reported destroyed.

stories.title: Plan for water sports at Simly Dam raises environmental concerns
stories.summary: Islamabad's Capital Development Authority is considering developing water sports and recreational facilities near Simly Dam, located 30 kilometres east of the capital. Critics have raised environmental concerns, noting the dam is a primary source of clean drinking water and that nearby Rawal Dam is already heavily polluted.

stories.title: A lopsided equation
stories.summary: An opinion piece highlights how the United States' withdrawal from international climate frameworks, combined with wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, has diverted fiscal resources from climate finance. It notes 2024 was the first year to exceed the 1.5°C pre-industrial threshold, with Pakistan among the most affected nations.

stories.title: The Gaza journalist killed on the day his daughter was born
stories.summary: Palestinian journalist Yahya was killed in an Israeli attack on Gaza just hours after his daughter Sana was born. Sana's first birthday is now marked by the loss of her father.

stories.title: Layers of climate resilience
stories.summary: An opinion article draws parallels between Iran's resilience under decades of sanctions and bombardment and lessons for Pakistan's climate resilience strategy. It argues Iran's national endurance stems from deep investment in human capital and STEM education rather than conventional economic metrics.

stories.title: Venice and Biennale 'shaken': 'The turmoil on the international scene has entered the exhibition'
stories.summary: Russia has returned to the 2026 Venice Biennale for the first time since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The participation has sparked protests from activists, artists, and political dissidents who argue that culture is being used as an extension of state power and warfare.

stories.title: Taiwan firm with mainland branches fires nephew of Taipei minister invoking ire in Beijing
stories.summary:

stories.title: Around 1,600 vessels still stranded near Hormuz Strait
stories.summary: Approximately 1,600 vessels remain stranded near the Strait of Hormuz since the war began in late February. At least 32 ships have been struck by missiles, killing at least 10 people and injuring a dozen more.

stories.title: Top BJP leader's aide shot dead in violence after Indian state election
stories.summary: Chandranath Rath was personal assistant to Suvendu Adhikari, front runner to become West Bengal's new chief minister.

stories.title: DRC President Félix Tshisekedi hints at third term, 2028 poll delay
stories.summary: DRC President Félix Tshisekedi suggested he may seek a third term and warned that the ongoing conflict in eastern Congo could force a postponement of the 2028 presidential elections. Fighting between Congolese forces and Rwanda-backed M23 rebels has intensified in North and South Kivu provinces.

stories.title: The passing spectacle
stories.summary: An opinion column reflects on Pakistan's military victory against India one year ago and its role in brokering a potential US-Iran peace deal. It argues these geopolitical successes should be measured against whether they translate into improved lives and livelihoods for ordinary Pakistanis.

stories.title: The Weeknd to return to Hong Kong after 8 years with Kai Tak show in October
stories.summary: Canadian singer-songwriter The Weeknd will perform in Hong Kong for the first time in eight years as part of the final leg of his “After Hours Til Dawn” Tour, with sources telling the South China Morn

stories.title: Iran war day 69: Tehran ‘reviewing’ US proposals; Israel bombs Beirut
stories.summary: On day 69 of the Iran war, Tehran announced it is reviewing U.S. proposals delivered through Pakistan. President Trump said talks are progressing, while Israel simultaneously conducted airstrikes on Beirut.

stories.title: Myanmar’s military rulers hire Trump ally for US$50,000 a month to lobby Washington
stories.summary: Myanmar’s appointment of a close confidant of US President Donald Trump to rebuild ties with Washington could offer the regime a sliver of hope to rebrand itself, even as a breakthrough on major issue

stories.title: The Pentagon Needs a Playbook for Munitions Surge Production
stories.summary: The U.S. military's use of Tomahawk missiles during Operation Epic Fury highlights ongoing challenges in munitions surge production, as these weapons take months to contract and years to manufacture. The Russo-Ukrainian War has further exposed difficulties in quickly replenishing stockpiles. Defense officials continue seeking ways to compress production timelines.

stories.title: Russians attack five districts of Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 30 times since evening, leaving four injured
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked five districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 30 times using artillery and drones, injuring four people. The strikes targeted multiple areas across the region.

stories.title: A breakthrough?
stories.summary: An editorial examines the potential for a long-term US-Iran ceasefire agreement despite confrontational rhetoric from both sides. After a brief confrontation over the Strait of Hormuz and alleged Iranian attacks on the UAE, President Trump wound down the US escort operation within 24 hours, signaling de-escalation.

stories.title: Pakistan Bar Council seeks end to lawyers promising ‘guaranteed results’
stories.summary: The Pakistan Bar Council's disciplinary committee, headed by Supreme Court Justice Muhammad Ali Mazhar, called for eliminating the practice of lawyers promising guaranteed results or "done basis" outcomes in exchange for fees. The committee urged all bar councils to enact rules and regulations to address the issue.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Zaporizhzhia region 797 times over past day, leaving two dead, 12 injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out 797 attacks on 50 settlements in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region over the past 24 hours, killing two people and injuring 12 others. The casualties occurred in Zaporizhzhia city and the Zaporizhzhia and Polohy districts.

stories.title: US war on Iran: 'A game of high risk, high reward' for both Trump and the Islamic Republic
stories.summary: Analyst Behnam Ben Taleblu of the Foundation for Defense of Democracies described the escalating confrontation between the United States and Iran as a high-stakes contest. He argues Tehran is probing the limits of the Trump administration's tolerance for escalation. The conflict spans military, economic, and psychological dimensions.

stories.title: Marco Rubio to meet pope at the Vatican after Trump attacks on pontiff
stories.summary: US secretary of state will hold talks with Italian government, also berated by Trump for not supporting Iran warThe US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, is to meet Pope Leo at the Vatican on Thursday i

stories.title: Attack on French cargo ship highlights continued risks in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The International Maritime Organization reported that 32 ships have been attacked in the Strait of Hormuz since the war began. A recent attack on a French cargo ship underscored the continued risks to commercial shipping in the waterway.

stories.title: Israeli court rejects flotilla activists’ plea challenging detention
stories.summary: An Israeli court in Beersheva rejected an appeal challenging the detention of Spanish national Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian Thiago Avila, two activists seized from a Gaza-bound flotilla in international waters off Greece. The UN, Brazil, and Spain have demanded their release, and the Israeli rights group representing them called the ruling unlawful.

stories.title: Trump reportedly paused Hormuz operation after Saudi Arabia denied use of its airspace
stories.summary: President Trump reportedly paused his "Project Freedom" Strait of Hormuz operation after Saudi Arabia denied the U.S. military use of its airspace and bases. Gulf states were reportedly surprised by the announcement, while Iran is expected to respond to a U.S. diplomatic proposal.

stories.title: A year ago today: Islamabad turns the tables on New Delhi as de-escalation efforts reach fever pitch
stories.summary: The article marks the first anniversary of the May 2025 military conflict between Pakistan and India, triggered by the April 22 Pahalgam attack in India-occupied Kashmir. Pakistan retaliated against Indian air strikes in Punjab and Azad Kashmir by downing multiple Indian aircraft, before both sides pursued de-escalation.

stories.title: What 300 Emails Say About Americans and the Army’s Direct Commission Program
stories.summary: Over nine months in 2024–2025, a U.S. Army Reserve official reviewed more than 300 inquiries from mid-career professionals seeking direct commissions. Applicants included data scientists, logistics engineers, cyber specialists, and strategic communicators. The effort aimed to connect candidates with decentralized branch pipelines controlling direct commission slots.

stories.title: Drone-and-mine siege: Ukraine takes Oleshky crisis to UN as 2,000 civilians starve in occupied city
stories.summary: Ukraine has raised the humanitarian crisis in Oleshky, a Russian-occupied city in Kherson region, at the United Nations, reporting that approximately 2,000 civilians are starving under a siege involving drones and mines. Russia has rejected proposals for a humanitarian corridor, while Ukraine's Ombudsman is pursuing an alternative, longer evacuation route.

stories.title: Aid cuts, drought and conflict leave Somalis desperate
stories.summary: Severe drought, ongoing conflict, and cuts to international aid have pushed Somalis into acute hunger. Internally displaced persons camps in Kismayo are struggling to cope with the mounting humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: Ukraine's Special Operations Forces show work of their troops on front line
stories.summary: Ukraine's Special Operations Forces released footage showing their troops destroying a Russian position on an unspecified sector of the front line. The operation was carried out by soldiers of the Armed Forces of Ukraine.

stories.title: South Korea rejects Trump’s claim that ship was hit because it ‘decided to go it alone’
stories.summary: South Korea’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Thursday rebutted US President Donald Trump’s assertion that a South Korean-operated vessel was attacked as it was acting on its own without US protection

stories.title: Police search for thieves who allegedly stole $150,000 worth of beehives from rural NSW property
stories.summary: Local beekeeper Mitch McLennan says hive thefts have become ‘quite commonplace’ due to rise of parasitic varroa mitesFollow our Australia news live blog for latest updatesGet our breaking news email,

stories.title: UK votes in key local and regional elections
stories.summary: The United Kingdom held local and regional elections, with Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour Party expected to suffer significant losses. The Reform party, Greens, Plaid Cymru, and SNP were all anticipated to make gains in the vote.

stories.title: The Army Needs to Build Better Command Posts
stories.summary: An analysis of U.S. Army command post design argues that sprawling tactical operations centers, nicknamed "TOC Mahals," are poorly suited for modern warfare. These large complexes of connected tents, vehicles, and generators are common at training center rotations but would be vulnerable in conflicts like the Russo-Ukrainian War.

stories.title: UK holds local elections as left- and right-wing populist parties expected to surge
stories.summary: The United Kingdom held local elections amid expectations that populist parties on both the left and right would gain ground. Polls indicated Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour Party losing support, benefiting the Green Party and Nigel Farage's Reform UK.

stories.title: Nigeria: One Million More Midwives - the Smartest Investment for Safer Births in a Shrinking Aid Landscape
stories.summary: On International Day of the Midwife 2026, under the theme "One Million More Midwives," health advocates in Nigeria are calling on governments and donors to invest in midwifery to improve maternal and newborn survival rates amid declining global aid.

stories.title: Burkina Faso: Burkina Faso's Junta Escalates Attack On Information
stories.summary: Burkina Faso's military junta has banned the French-language broadcaster TV5Monde, in what Human Rights Watch describes as part of a broader offensive against independent media and access to information in the country.

stories.title: Pakistan has fiscal space to fight climate crisis: Aurangzeb
stories.summary: Pakistan's Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb stated at the Breathe Pakistan Climate Conference in Islamabad that the country has sufficient domestic fiscal capacity to address climate change impacts. He urged effective use of local resources before seeking international support, calling macroeconomic stability essential for unlocking climate financing.

stories.title: Somalia: Somali Police Arrest Two SMN Journalists in Mogadishu, Media Outlet Condemns Move
stories.summary: Police in Mogadishu, Somalia, detained two journalists from Shabelle Media Network while they were covering reports on civilian displacement in the capital. The media outlet condemned the arrests.

stories.title: LHC expands scope of property courts  for overseas Pakistanis
stories.summary: The Lahore High Court ruled that special courts established under the Punjab Establishment of Special Courts (Overseas Pakistanis Property) Act, 2025, can hear a broad range of property disputes. Justice Anwaar Hussain's judgement expanded their jurisdiction beyond ownership and possession to include inheritance, partition, and contract matters.

stories.title: Chad: Terrorists Attack Military Base, Killing Dozens
stories.summary: Terrorists attacked a military base in Chad on May 4, killing dozens. Chadian military authorities confirmed the assault and reported that several of the attackers were also killed in the fighting.

stories.title: Nigeria: New Power Minister Vows to Fix Grid Collapse
stories.summary: Nigeria's newly appointed power minister has pledged to address the country's recurring national grid collapses. The minister outlined a 100-day plan focusing first on stabilizing the grid, followed by expanded metering to reduce estimated billing for consumers.

stories.title: Summer-like temperatures of up to +30°C forecast in Ukraine today, rain and thunderstorms expected in western regions
stories.summary: Forecasters predicted summer-like temperatures reaching up to 30°C across Ukraine on Thursday, May 7, with generally dry conditions. Short-term rain and isolated thunderstorms were expected in the western regions during the day.

stories.title: South Africa: City of Joburg's Financial Turmoil Imperils National Economy, Warns Finance Minister
stories.summary: South Africa's Finance Minister warned that the City of Johannesburg's financial turmoil poses a risk to the national economy. DA mayoral candidate Helen Zille is pushing for the city to be placed under National Treasury financial administration, while the ANC seeks to protect a R10.3 billion staff wage deal.

stories.title: ‘Exhaustion and sadness’ in Beirut’s southern suburbs
stories.summary: Residents of Beirut's southern suburbs described feelings of exhaustion and sadness after Israel called for evacuations at the start of the war and carried out strikes in the area.

stories.title: Under rubble and rain, Gaza women try to save rare books in centuries-old library
stories.summary: Palestinian women volunteers in Gaza City are working to salvage rare books and manuscripts from the destroyed Great Omari Mosque library, which was left in ruins after Israeli bombardment. The centuries-old collection is at risk from continued exposure to rubble and rain.

stories.title: France issued 23% more visas to Russians as EU rules tightened
stories.summary: European Union governments issued approximately 620,000 Schengen visas in 2025, a 10% increase over 2024, despite Brussels pledging tighter restrictions over espionage and sabotage concerns. France notably increased visa issuance to Russian nationals by 23% during the same period.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: Congolese Opposition Politicians Condemn US Sanctions On Kabila
stories.summary: Opposition politicians in the Democratic Republic of Congo have called on the United States to lift sanctions imposed on former President Joseph Kabila. The sanctions are related to Kabila's activities during and after his presidency.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: Reports indicate the US and Iran are nearing agreement on a one-page memorandum to end the regional conflict. Meanwhile, intensifying Israeli attacks across south and east Lebanon killed at least 16 people on Wednesday, raising fears the existing ceasefire could collapse.

stories.title: Kenya: Waiguru Backs Ruto, Launches Fierce Attack On Opposition Leaders
stories.summary: Kirinyaga Governor Anne Waiguru publicly voiced support for Kenyan President William Ruto's Kenya Kwanza administration, urging residents to align with the government. She criticized opposition leaders and dissenting voices within the Mt Kenya region.

stories.title: Rwanda: Rwanda's Naming Traditions Explained
stories.summary: Rwandan baby naming traditions are deeply symbolic, often reflecting the circumstances of birth, spiritual beliefs, and family heritage. Naming ceremonies are typically held shortly before or after a child's birth.

stories.title: Uganda: 'We Are Going to Die' - the Frontline Costs of Uganda's New US Health Agreement
stories.summary: A new agreement between Uganda and the United States on health funding is drawing concern from frontline health workers in Kampala. Workers fear the deal's conditions, reportedly linked to political and cultural disputes, will negatively impact healthcare delivery in the country.

stories.title: Russian drone attack on Dnipro leaves two injured, including pregnant woman
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro wounded two people, including a pregnant woman. The strike caused a fire in a five-story apartment building and damaged several vehicles.

stories.title: Sudan: 'Flights From Khartoum Airport Suspended for the Third Day Following Drone Attack'
stories.summary: Flights at Khartoum International Airport in Sudan remained suspended for a third consecutive day following a drone attack on the airport on Monday. Sudan's Prime Minister Kamil Idris inspected the airport, and the UN confirmed the continued disruption.

stories.title: Israeli attack on Gaza kills son of Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on Gaza City killed Azzam Khalil al-Hayya, the son of Hamas political bureau chief Khalil al-Hayya. Senior Hamas official Basem Naim confirmed the death on social media.

stories.title: Sudan: WFP - Sudan Aid Ops Not Impacted By Khartoum Airport Drone Strike
stories.summary: The World Food Programme confirmed that its operations in Sudan have not been affected by the drone strike near Khartoum airport on Monday, which led to the suspension of many flights. WFP stated that all of its staff in the area are accounted for.

stories.title: China-EU investment deal should stay in ‘deep freezer’, outgoing trade chief warns
stories.summary: The EU’s outgoing top trade official used her departing appearance at the European Parliament to pour cold water on the prospect of an investment deal with China, hinting instead that new weapons for

stories.title: Outrage after Ben Gvir posts video glorifying executing Palestinian detainees
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir posted a TikTok video using the 'voices in my head' trend featuring AI-generated images of nooses, declaring he 'dreams' about executions. The video drew backlash, coming weeks after Israel passed a death penalty law targeting Palestinian detainees.

stories.title: Death of elderly pair in Sau Mau Ping flat a case of murder-suicide, police say
stories.summary: Hong Kong police identified the deaths of an elderly couple at a Po Tat Estate flat in Sau Mau Ping as a murder-suicide. A 77-year-old man allegedly killed his 71-year-old ex-wife before hanging himself, reportedly feeling hopeless after their separation, which followed years of marital conflict and their son's suicide.

stories.title: At Beirut shoreline camp, volunteer barber brings dignity with free haircuts
stories.summary: At a shoreline camp in Beirut, Lebanon, a volunteer barber is offering free haircuts to displaced families seeking relief after weeks of conflict. The initiative aims to restore a sense of dignity to those sheltering in the camp.

stories.title: Senior Hezbollah commander killed by Israel in Beirut suburbs: Source
stories.summary: Israel struck Beirut's southern suburbs, killing a senior Hezbollah Radwan force commander and at least 11 other people. Additional Israeli strikes hit targets across southern and eastern Lebanon, according to reports.

stories.title: Alaska 2025 tsunami was second-highest ever, taller than Empire State Building
stories.summary: Researchers determined that a landslide-triggered tsunami at Tracy Arm Fjord in southeastern Alaska on August 10, 2025, was the second-highest ever recorded. The wave reached 481 metres — taller than New York City's Empire State Building — within the Tongass National Forest's narrow sea inlet.

stories.title: One IDF soldier severely injured, three lightly injured by explosive drone in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: One IDF soldier was severely injured and three others sustained light injuries from an explosive drone strike in southern Lebanon. All four soldiers were evacuated to a hospital for treatment, and their families were notified.

stories.title: Israel strikes Beirut for the first time since the ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel carried out airstrikes on Beirut's southern suburbs for the first time since the ceasefire, targeting a commander of Hezbollah's elite Radwan force. The strikes mark a significant resumption of Israeli military operations in the Lebanese capital.

stories.title: Two drones fall on Latvian territory
stories.summary: Latvia's Air Force detected two foreign unmanned aerial vehicles entering Latvian airspace from the direction of Russia. The drones fell on Latvian territory, marking an incursion into the NATO member state's sovereign airspace.

stories.title: Israeli airstrike kills 4 and injures 33 in southern Lebanon despite fragile ceasefire
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike hit a house in the village of Saksakieh in southern Lebanon, killing four people and injuring 33, despite an existing fragile ceasefire. The strike has raised concerns about renewed escalation in the region.

stories.title: New gasfield approved near Twelve Apostles puts climate and ‘pristine’ ocean in jeopardy, environmentalists warn
stories.summary: The Australian federal and Victorian governments approved Amplitude Energy's Annie gasfield project in the Otway basin near the Twelve Apostles. Environmental groups warned the drilling project threatens a pristine ocean environment and makes achieving climate targets harder.

stories.title: Anger over handling of Hezbollah fight could put Netanyahu’s northern support at risk
stories.summary: Residents along Israel's northern border with Lebanon, traditionally a Likud stronghold, may shift their political support away from Prime Minister Netanyahu's party. Dissatisfaction stems from the handling of the Hezbollah conflict and an unpopular ceasefire that locals feel has failed to deliver real security.

stories.title: Major test for Labour as polls open in English, Scottish and Welsh elections
stories.summary: Polls opened across England, Scotland, and Wales on Thursday in local, mayoral, and parliamentary elections representing the biggest test for Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour government since the 2024 general election. Reform UK, the Greens, and the Liberal Democrats are expected to make significant gains.

stories.title: Europe’s AI translation industry told it risks reputation by partnering with US firms
stories.summary: European AI translation industry figures raised concerns after leading startup DeepL partnered with Amazon's cloud computing division. Critics warned European companies risk losing their global lead in machine translation by increasing dependence on US-based Silicon Valley digital infrastructure.

stories.title: Chinese ex-waiter turned top food influencer Bai Bing fined US$2.6 million for tax evasion
stories.summary: Chinese food influencer Bai Bing, who has over 40 million followers, was fined 18.91 million yuan (US$2.6 million) by China's State Tax Administration for evading approximately 9.11 million yuan in personal income taxes between 2021 and 2024. The former waiter's case drew significant social media attention.

stories.title: The Mamdani effect: Jewish resilience in face of NY antisemitism - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial argued that antisemitic incidents in New York, home to one of the world's largest Jewish populations, serve to strengthen Jewish solidarity and ties to Israel rather than weaken them.

stories.title: MSF says Israel has 'manufactured malnutrition crisis' in Gaza
stories.summary: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) accused Israel of deliberately restricting food and aid deliveries to Gaza, creating what it called a 'manufactured malnutrition crisis.' The report highlighted devastating impacts on infants and pregnant and breastfeeding women, and criticized a US- and Israeli-backed private organization that largely replaced UN aid distribution.

stories.title: BJP aide shot dead in India’s West Bengal days after historic election win
stories.summary: Chandranath Rath, a 41-year-old close aide of West Bengal BJP chief Suvendu Adhikari, was shot dead by gunmen on motorbikes in India's West Bengal. The killing came days after the BJP won its first-ever state victory there, taking 207 of 294 assembly seats in elections.

stories.title: Vigils to be held across Australia for 5-year-old girl allegedly murdered in Outback
stories.summary: Vigils are planned across Australia for Kumanjayi Little Baby, a five-year-old girl found dead after going missing from an Aboriginal town camp in Alice Springs in the Northern Territory. An investigation into her alleged murder is underway.

stories.title: Bondi Beach terrorist to face 19 extra charges over Hanukkah massacre
stories.summary: Australian authorities announced that Naveed Akram, charged in connection with the Bondi Beach Hanukkah attack, will face 19 additional charges including intent to murder and resisting arrest. A court hearing was also held regarding a gag order on some names of victims and survivors.

stories.title: Israel targets pickup truck in south Lebanon, kills two
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes struck a pickup truck in Nabatieh, south Lebanon, killing two people, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The NNA also reported additional shelling and strikes targeting southern Lebanon in recent hours.

stories.title: JM Coetzee declines to attend Jerusalem writers festival over Israel’s ‘genocidal campaign in Gaza’
stories.summary: Nobel laureate JM Coetzee declined an invitation to the Jerusalem International Writers Festival, citing Israel's "genocidal campaign" in Gaza. The 86-year-old South African-born, Australia-based author wrote that he previously considered himself a supporter of Israel but that events in Gaza changed his position.

stories.title: Moore Park golf course to be cut by a third instead of 50% under compromise to create new parklands
stories.summary: The New South Wales government announced a compromise plan to reduce Sydney's Moore Park golf course from 18 holes to 12, rather than the originally proposed 9 holes. The revised plan follows public backlash and aims to balance creating new public parklands with preserving golfing facilities.

stories.title: US Jewish group calls for ‘zero tolerance’ as antisemitism surges in school district
stories.summary: A Jewish community group in Maryland reported a surge in antisemitic incidents at local schools, including antisemitic graffiti, physical threats, harassment, and 'Heil Hitler' gestures at events. The group called for a 'zero tolerance' policy in the affected school district.

stories.title: ‘Raid’ regiment drones hit three Russian air defense systems in six days of May
stories.summary: Ukraine's 413th Separate Unmanned Systems Regiment 'Raid' reported destroying three Russian air defense systems in the first six days of May. The targets included two Pantsir-S1 systems and one Tunguska missile-gun system, all struck at considerable distances from the front line.

stories.title: Senior Hezbollah commander killed by Israel in Beirut: Report
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on Beirut's southern suburbs killed Malek Ballout, an operations commander in Hezbollah's elite Radwan Force, according to a source close to the group. A Lebanese security source said the strike hit an apartment during a meeting of the force's leaders. It was the first such strike on Beirut since a truce took effect in April.

stories.title: Russia warns diplomats in Ukraine capital to evacuate in case of ‘retaliatory strike’
stories.summary: Russia warned foreign diplomats in Kyiv to evacuate, threatening retaliatory strikes if Ukraine disrupted World War II commemorations in Moscow. Both sides continued exchanging strikes on Thursday, wounding 13 people in Bryansk, Russia, and one person in Dnipro, Ukraine.

stories.title: Ukraine is a global surrogacy hub - but that could be about to end
stories.summary: Ukraine, currently a major global hub for international surrogacy, is considering legislation that would effectively ban foreigners from accessing surrogacy services in the country.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia denied US access to airspace, pressured Trump to pause Project Freedom - report
stories.summary: Reports indicate Saudi Arabia denied the US access to its airspace and pressured President Trump to pause a military operation. However, during the earlier US Operation Epic Fury against Iran, Saudi Arabia had permitted US aircraft to fly from Prince Sultan Air Base.

stories.title: Photo shows Israeli soldier desecrating Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel's military launched an investigation after a photograph surfaced showing an Israeli soldier placing a cigarette in the mouth of a Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon.

stories.title: Iran denies involvement in attack on South Korean vessel in Hormuz Strait
stories.summary: Iran formally denied any involvement in an explosion that struck the Panama-flagged South Korean cargo ship HMM Namu in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. The blast caused a fire onboard the vessel, which was carrying 24 crew members at the time.

stories.title: Ukrenergo forecasts no power outages for Thursday, May 7
stories.summary: Ukraine's national energy company Ukrenergo announced it does not forecast any power outages across the country for Thursday, May 7.

stories.title: Lutnick testifies he can't recall why his family lunched on Epstein's island
stories.summary: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick testified before a congressional committee that he could not recall why he and his family had lunch on Jeffrey Epstein's private island. The testimony was given in a private session, with details shared by committee members.

stories.title: Israeli soldier places cigarette near Virgin Mary statue's mouth in Lebanon
stories.summary: A viral image showing an Israeli soldier placing a cigarette near the mouth of a Virgin Mary statue in the predominantly Christian town of Debel in southern Lebanon has sparked widespread outrage. The Israeli army said the soldier's behavior 'completely deviates from the values expected of its fighters.'

stories.title: Contentious proposals punctuate planned legislative blitz as Knesset gets back to work
stories.summary: As the Israeli Knesset resumed work, the ruling coalition prepared to advance stalled legislation on Haredi military draft exemptions, an October 7 probe, media reform, and changes to the attorney general's powers. The legislative push comes with elections on the horizon.

stories.title: Iran considering US proposal as Trump says war will be 'over quickly'
stories.summary: Pakistan, acting as mediator between the US and Iran, said it is working to convert the current ceasefire into a permanent end to hostilities. President Trump stated that any war would be 'over quickly,' while Iran is reportedly considering a US proposal.

stories.title: US aims for Fourth of July to deploy Qatar-gifted jet as latest Air Force One
stories.summary: The White House aims to deploy a luxury jet gifted by Qatar in 2025 as the latest Air Force One by the Fourth of July.

stories.title: Passengers on hantavirus-stricken ship sway between fear, boredom
stories.summary: Passengers aboard a cruise ship affected by a hantavirus outbreak are coping with fear and boredom as the vessel remains under health restrictions. The outbreak has killed three people, with eight additional confirmed or suspected cases linked to the ship.

stories.title: U.S. fires on Iranian oil tanker as Trump pressures Tehran for deal to end war
stories.summary: A U.S. fighter jet disabled an Iranian oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman by shooting out its rudder as it attempted to breach the American naval blockade of Iran's ports, according to U.S. Central Command.

stories.title: War Handed Public Space Back to Iran’s Regime
stories.summary: The article examines how Iran's Islamic Republic has reclaimed public urban spaces during wartime. After years of gradual encroachment by ordinary citizens on public areas, the regime has reasserted control over the urban landscape under the cover of the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: UAE’s ruling royal family benefits from more than €71m in EU farming subsidies
stories.summary: A cross-border investigation by DeSmog and the Guardian found that subsidiaries controlled by the UAE's ruling Al Nahyan royal family collected more than €71 million in EU farming subsidies over six years. The payments were for farmland the family controls in Romania, Italy, and Spain, with crops reportedly destined for the Gulf.

stories.title: Cut UK speed limits to reduce Iran war impact on consumers, thinktank urges
stories.summary: The UK thinktank IPPR urged Britain to lower speed limits to 20mph in towns and 60mph on motorways to reduce fuel demand amid rising oil prices caused by the Iran war. The measures are part of a broader proposed package to shield consumers from the conflict's economic impact.

stories.title: New Hungarian PM’s voters want action on climate and LGBTQ+ rights, poll finds
stories.summary: A poll found that over three-quarters of Hungarians who voted for Péter Magyar's Tisza party want stronger action on climate change, and more than 70% support LGBTQ+ rights protections. Magyar's party won a supermajority, ending Viktor Orbán's 16-year rule, and the new prime minister is set to be sworn in on Saturday.

stories.title: French professor accused of ‘gigantic hoax’ after inventing Nobel-style prize
