stories.summary: French authorities are investigating literature professor Florent Montaclair for allegedly fabricating the Gold Medal of Philology, a Nobel-style prize he awarded to himself and others including Noam Chomsky. The 2016 ceremony was held at the French National Assembly and attended by Nobel laureates and former government ministers.

stories.title: Malaysian king’s visit to Russia expected to smooth path for oil deal
stories.summary: Malaysian King Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar arrived in Moscow for a visit aimed at securing alternative oil sources amid fuel shortages linked to the Iran war. He was received at Vnukovo-2 airport by Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Andrey Rudenko and is attending Russia's May 9 Victory Day commemorations.

stories.title: Georgetown Law graduation speaker backs out after students protest his ‘Zionist opinions’
stories.summary: Georgetown Law's planned commencement speaker, Morton Schapiro, withdrew after students protested what they called his 'Zionist opinions.' The university replaced him with a speaker who had previously compared congressional hearings on campus antisemitism to 'McCarthyism.'

stories.title: Russia warns diplomatic missions to evacuate Kyiv staff if Moscow launches mass strike
stories.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry warned diplomatic missions in Kyiv to evacuate staff promptly in the event Moscow launches a mass strike. The warning was linked to potential Ukrainian attempts to disrupt Russia's May 9 Victory Day commemorations.

stories.title: SSU detains Russian agent who organized arson attacks on military vehicles in Kyiv
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service detained an FSB agent in Kyiv who had been organizing arson attacks targeting vehicles belonging to the Ukrainian Defense Forces in the capital.

stories.title: Iran will control Strait of Hormuz 'forever', former senior US official says
stories.summary: Former senior US official Amos Hochstein, who served as energy and Middle East adviser to President Biden, told Bloomberg that Iran will control the Strait of Hormuz 'forever,' regardless of any peace deal. He suggested Gulf states will need to build new pipelines to bypass Iran's strategic chokehold.

stories.title: Tai Po probe: missed checks at Wang Fuk Court due to late notice of new guidelines – as it happened
stories.summary: A witness from Hong Kong's Housing Bureau Independent Checking Unit testified at a hearing into the deadly Wang Fung Court fire in Tai Po. The government-appointed committee questioned ICU members about missed safety checks attributed to late notice of new inspection guidelines.

stories.title: Rutgers disinvites commencement speaker for claiming Israelis 'train dogs to assault prisoners'
stories.summary: Rutgers University rescinded a commencement speaker invitation after social media posts surfaced in which the speaker accused Israel of genocide and claimed Israelis 'train dogs to assault prisoners.' The university cited the inflammatory nature of the posts.

stories.title: Evacuees from hantavirus-hit cruise ship land in Europe
stories.summary: Three people have died in a hantavirus outbreak aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius. Evacuees from the vessel have arrived in Europe.

stories.title: Israeli soldier caught desecrating statue of Virgin Mary in Lebanon
stories.summary: A photograph of an Israeli soldier inserting a cigarette into the mouth of a Virgin Mary statue in Lebanon has drawn widespread outrage. The image has circulated widely on social media.

stories.title: Gas companies will be forced to set aside local supply under major Labor shakeup
stories.summary: Australia's federal Albanese government announced a gas reservation policy requiring east coast producers to set aside 20% of export volumes for domestic use. The scheme aims to shore up local gas supplies and reduce prices for households and businesses.

stories.title: Cuba blasts 'dangerous' US threats of military action against island
stories.summary: Cuban officials condemned escalating U.S. statements and threats of military action against the island, calling them dangerous and an international crime. The criticism came alongside an ongoing U.S. oil blockade that has severely restricted fuel shipments to Cuba amid a deepening energy crisis.

stories.title: Israel struck Lebanese capital in the first attack since April ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel bombed Beirut's southern suburbs, striking the Ghobeiry area in its first direct attack on the Lebanese capital since the April ceasefire. The strike caused major destruction in densely populated neighborhoods, raising fears of wider regional escalation.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Trump says Iran war will be 'over quickly'
stories.summary: President Trump said he believed the war in Iran would be "over quickly" but threatened to resume bombing if negotiations collapsed. The US military reported shooting at an Iranian oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman that attempted to breach the American blockade of Iranian ports.

stories.title: Major fire in Zakarpattia region: Firefighting efforts continue, prosecutor’s office launches investigation
stories.summary: A major fire broke out on the Borzhava Ridge in Ukraine's Zakarpattia region. Firefighting efforts are ongoing, and the Zakarpattia Prosecutor's Office has opened a criminal investigation into the cause.

stories.title: Rubio to visit India for bilateral talks; Quad Foreign Ministers’ meeting May-end
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio is scheduled to visit India for bilateral talks with External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and National Security Adviser Ajit Doval, and will also meet Prime Minister Modi. A Quad Foreign Ministers' meeting is planned for late May, as the two nations seek to stabilize ties after tensions over tariffs and sanctions.

stories.title: Macron says he discussed Hormuz situation with Iran's president
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron said Wednesday he held further talks with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. During the discussions, Macron reaffirmed the importance of ensuring freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Mexico's Sheinbaum battles party split over US cartel charges
stories.summary: A U.S. indictment accusing several Mexican politicians, including the governor of Sinaloa, of drug cartel ties is causing a rift within Mexico's ruling Morena party. Factions within the party are divided over how to respond, posing a significant challenge for President Claudia Sheinbaum.

stories.title: US judge releases note that cellmate says he found after Epstein first attempted suicide
stories.summary: A US judge released a note that a cellmate said he found after Jeffrey Epstein's first suicide attempt in jail. The note, purportedly written by Epstein, contained informal remarks and ended with the phrases 'NO FUN' and 'NOT WORTH IT.'

stories.title: US says Hezbollah is ‘trying to derail talks’ with Israel
stories.summary: A US State Department spokesperson accused Hezbollah of attempting to derail ongoing negotiations between Israel and the group, without providing further details on the status of the talks.

stories.title: Australian director Phillip Noyce shoots feature film for Saudi Arabia celebrating ‘heroism of security men in combating drugs’
stories.summary: Australian director Phillip Noyce is being paid by the Saudi regime to make a feature film called The Watchful Eyes, portraying Saudi narcotics officers as heroes. Rights groups have accused Saudi Arabia, which executed 243 people for drug offences last year, of using entertainment investments to whitewash its human rights record.

stories.title: Motorcyclist, 58, killed in Eastern Harbour Crossing crash, police investigate
stories.summary: A 58-year-old motorcyclist was killed in Hong Kong's Eastern Harbour Crossing in Kwun Tong shortly after midnight on Thursday. Police said the motorcycle struck the left-side kerb before skidding and overturning while traveling toward Hong Kong Island; an investigation is underway.

stories.title: Trump’s last Japanese diehard fans lose faith as Iran war chaos spreads
stories.summary: Former conservative supporters of Donald Trump in Japan have grown disillusioned roughly 18 months into his second term, citing the U.S.-initiated conflict in Iran and deteriorating bilateral relations as key factors eroding their faith.

stories.title: ByteDance’s AI subscription gamble: chatbot faces reality check in China
stories.summary: ByteDance's AI chatbot Doubao faces skepticism among Chinese users over its proposed subscription pricing. Consumers in cities like Shenzhen say they find the tool useful but not worth the cost compared to alternatives.

stories.title: LA mayoral candidate Spencer Pratt reposts scathing AI-generated ad
stories.summary: Los Angeles mayoral candidate and former TV star Spencer Pratt reposted an AI-generated campaign ad depicting the city as a dystopian hellscape under current leadership. The viral video, created by filmmaker Charlie Curran, targeted Mayor Karen Bass and other California political figures ahead of a mayoral debate.

stories.title: New Zealand eyes Japanese Mogami-class warships as possible replacements for ageing fleet
stories.summary: New Zealand is considering purchasing Japanese Mogami-class frigates or British Type 31 frigates to replace its aging naval fleet. Defence discussions are underway with Australia and the United Kingdom on procurement and service arrangements.

stories.title: Argentina races to find origins of cruise ship hantavirus outbreak, amid reports some passengers have returned to US
stories.summary: Argentine officials are investigating whether their country is the source of a hantavirus outbreak aboard the Antarctic-bound cruise ship MV Hondius. Argentina, where the cruise departed, has the highest incidence of the rodent-borne disease in Latin America according to the WHO, and some passengers have reportedly returned to the US.

stories.title: Australia news live: Thredbo snow as cold snap arrives; Queensland education department hit by international cybersecurity breach
stories.summary: Queensland's education department confirmed a cybersecurity breach after a hack of a third-party provider managing the state's online learning platform, QLearn, exposed user data. Separately, Nationals senator Bridget McKenzie criticized the Albanese government's decision to abandon an inland rail project linking New South Wales and Queensland.

stories.title: Trump sees ‘very good chance’ of Iran deal, but threatens strikes if not
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated there is a "very good chance" of reaching a deal with Iran but threatened military strikes if diplomacy fails. Iran has not yet responded to the latest American proposal.

stories.title: Keir Starmer's leadership set to be tested as polls open in UK local elections
stories.summary: Polls opened Thursday across the UK in local elections seen as a major test of Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour government. Nigel Farage's Reform UK party and the Green Party are expected to gain as Starmer's popularity has dropped, prompting internal calls for a leadership change.

stories.title: Day of mourning in Kramatorsk for victims of Russian attack
stories.summary: The city of Kramatorsk in Ukraine's Donetsk region declared a day of mourning for victims killed in a Russian bombing attack on May 5.

stories.title: Has ‘the Beast’ arrived in Beijing? Trump’s motorcade SUVs spotted before visit
stories.summary: Ahead of President Trump's planned May 14 visit to Beijing for a China-U.S. summit, armored U.S. Secret Service vehicles were spotted on Beijing highways, signaling a major security buildup for the diplomatic event.

stories.title: Trump reportedly paused Hormuz naval escorts after Saudi Arabia denied use of its airspace
stories.summary: The U.S. reportedly paused naval escort operations in the Strait of Hormuz after Saudi Arabia denied the use of its airspace. Iran's top negotiator mocked the halt, while President Trump predicted the war would end quickly.

stories.title: North Korea says nuclear status ‘will not change’ despite external pressure
stories.summary: North Korea's UN envoy reiterated that Pyongyang is not bound by the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, from which it formally withdrew in 2003. The country has conducted six nuclear tests and is believed to possess dozens of warheads.

stories.title: Rising Fuel costs overshadowing agenda for ASEAN summit in the Philippines
stories.summary: ASEAN leaders convened a summit in the Philippines, where rising fuel costs and living expenses have emerged as a primary concern among local residents, overshadowing other agenda items.

stories.title: Israeli air strike kills one Palestinian, severely wounds Hamas leader's son
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike on the al-Daraj neighborhood in Gaza City killed one Palestinian, identified as Hamza al-Sharbasi, and seriously wounded Azzam al-Hayya, the son of Hamas leader Khalil al-Hayya. Several others also sustained severe injuries.

stories.title: US FAA head to face questions from lawmakers after agency cited in fatal air collision
stories.summary: The head of the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration is scheduled to testify before lawmakers on Capitol Hill on May 19. A report found that systemic FAA failures contributed to a mid-air collision that killed 67 people the previous year.

stories.title: Trump says Iran wants to make a deal
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated at a White House event that Iran wants to negotiate a deal. No further details about the nature or terms of potential negotiations were provided.

stories.title: Trump says war on Iran will be 'over quickly'
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated during a tele-rally for a Georgia Republican candidate that the war on Iran would be "over quickly," emphasizing that preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon was the primary objective.

stories.title: Israeli assault across Lebanon kills 16 people, wounds over a dozen more
stories.summary: Israeli drone and air strikes across southern and eastern Lebanon killed 16 people and wounded at least 21 others, including paramedics. Targets included a school, residential areas, and civilian infrastructure.

stories.title: Falling sales to widen profit gap between China’s EV makers and battery suppliers
stories.summary: Analysts predict a widening profit gap between Chinese electric vehicle assemblers and battery producers like CATL, as flat car prices and declining vehicle sales contrast with strong demand for energy-storage systems.

stories.title: In China, number of clothing buttons holds meaning; specific counts assigned for the dead
stories.summary: The growing popularity of hanfu and neo-Chinese style clothing in China has drawn attention to traditional folk beliefs about button counts on garments, with certain numbers considered unlucky or associated with the dead in some regions.

stories.title: Fighting for attention, podcasters are stoking outrage against Israel and Jews
stories.summary: Large-audience podcasters, including Tucker Carlson and Hasan Piker, are drawing scrutiny for content that critics say stokes outrage against Israel and Jewish communities, with limited external checks on their growing influence.

stories.title: Russia’s Foreign Ministry urges countries to evacuate diplomats from Kyiv ahead of May 9, warns of ‘retaliatory strike’
stories.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry, through spokeswoman Maria Zakharova, circulated a note urging all accredited diplomatic missions and international organizations to evacuate their staff from Kyiv. The warning came ahead of Russia's May 9 Victory Day celebrations, with Moscow threatening retaliatory strikes against Ukraine.

stories.title: US says migration has made Europe an ‘incubator’ for terrorism in new counter-terrorism strategy
stories.summary: The Trump administration released a 16-page counter-terrorism strategy, led by adviser Sebastian Gorka, that labels Europe an "incubator" for terrorism driven by mass migration. The document also targets drug cartels in the Americas and expands domestic focus to include "violent left-wing extremists" and "radically pro-transgender" groups.

stories.title: North Korea says it is not bound by any treaty on nuclear non-proliferation
stories.summary: North Korea declared it is not bound by the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, asserting that its status as a nuclear-armed state will not change in response to external pressure or rhetoric.

stories.title: Hamas calls on US, mediators to stop the escalating Israeli attacks in Gaza
stories.summary: Hamas issued a statement condemning recent Israeli strikes on Gaza as a "blatant violation" of the October ceasefire agreement and called on the United States and guarantor states of the Sharm El-Sheikh agreement to take immediate action to halt the attacks.

stories.title: New Trump counterterrorism strategy brands Europe an 'incubator' for terrorism
stories.summary: The Trump administration unveiled a new counterterrorism strategy on Wednesday that accuses European nations of fostering terrorism through mass migration. The strategy also broadens the domestic threat focus to include groups the administration describes as "violent left-wing extremists" and "radically pro-transgender" organizations.

stories.title: Lubinets urges recognition of militarization of Ukrainian children in occupied territories as crime against humanity
stories.summary: Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights Dmytro Lubinets called on the international community to classify the militarization of Ukrainian children in Russian-occupied territories as a crime against humanity. Lubinets urged formal recognition of the practice, highlighting Russia's use of children in occupied areas of Ukraine.

stories.title: Federal authorities arrest 18 people in Los Angeles raid amid drug crackdown
stories.summary: Federal authorities arrested 18 people in a drug crackdown at MacArthur Park near downtown Los Angeles, the Department of Justice announced. The operation targeted what officials described as an open-air drug market in the park, which has long struggled with fentanyl use, overdoses, and homelessness.

stories.title: Israeli forces carry out incursion in southern Syria
stories.summary: Israeli forces conducted a raid in the western countryside of Daraa province in southern Syria, deploying eight military vehicles near a bridge in Wadi al-Raqad in the Yarmouk Basin, according to Syrian state news agency SANA.

stories.title: France moves aircraft carrier to Red Sea with eye on Strait of Hormuz mission
stories.summary: France is repositioning its aircraft carrier to the Red Sea in preparation for a potential mission near the Strait of Hormuz. The move comes amid a struggle between the United States and Iran for control of the strategic waterway vital to global energy trade.

stories.title: Police arrest protester after five-days atop Washington bridge
stories.summary: Police in Washington, D.C., arrested an anti-war protester who had staged a five-day sit-in atop the Frederick Douglass Bridge before voluntarily ending the demonstration.

stories.title: Top Vatican cardinal calls Trump's attacks on Pope Leo 'strange'
stories.summary: A senior Vatican cardinal described U.S. President Donald Trump's public attacks on Pope Leo regarding the Iran war as "strange." The remarks came one day before the U.S. Secretary of State was due to hold talks with the pope in Rome.

stories.title: Brussels cathedral installs plaques apologizing for medieval pogrom depicted in stained glass
stories.summary: The Brussels cathedral installed explanatory plaques apologizing for a medieval pogrom depicted in its stained glass windows. The Archbishop asked forgiveness from the Jewish people for suffering caused by a 14th-century antisemitic accusation.

stories.title: Israel strikes Beirut for the first time since ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel struck Beirut's southern suburbs on Wednesday for the first time since a ceasefire with Hezbollah took effect, claiming to target a commander of the group's elite Radwan Force. Prime Minister Netanyahu and Defence Minister Katz confirmed the operation, though Hezbollah did not immediately confirm any casualties. The Lebanon ceasefire had underpinned a broader US-Iran truce framework.

stories.title: Is North Korea’s constitutional shift a move towards ‘peaceful coexistence’ with South?
stories.summary: North Korea removed references to "national reunification" from its constitution and formally defined its territory as bordering South Korea. Analysts interpret this as a shift toward recognizing a state-to-state relationship rather than pursuing unification.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump says deal with Tehran ‘possible’; Israel bombs Beirut
stories.summary: The United Nations called on Israel to release two members of a Gaza-bound aid flotilla who were seized in international waters and held without charge. Separately, Israel carried out strikes on Beirut, and diplomatic signals between the U.S. and Iran continued.

stories.title: Ukrainian General Staff strengthens officer training, implements NATO standards
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff is undertaking systematic reforms to improve officer training and digitize military education. The efforts include integrating foreign instructors and implementing NATO standards across the armed forces' educational institutions.

stories.title: Note linked to Epstein’s first suspected suicide bid released by US judge
stories.summary: A note linked to Jeffrey Epstein's first suspected suicide attempt in jail was unsealed by U.S. District Judge Kenneth Karas in New York after being locked in a courthouse vault for nearly five years. The New York Times had petitioned to release the document.

stories.title: Israeli court rejects flotilla activists’ appeal challenging detention
stories.summary: An Israeli court rejected an appeal by detained flotilla activists challenging their detention, which had been extended to May 10 to allow police additional time for interrogation.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it carried out 17 attacks on Israeli forces in Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced that its fighters carried out 17 attacks on Israeli forces operating inside Lebanese territory, targeting soldiers and military vehicles in locations including Qantara, Naqoura, and Aita al-Shaab using drones and rockets.

stories.title: Trump seeks to halt payment to E. Jean Carroll in hope of eventual Supreme Court win
stories.summary: President Trump's lawyer asked a federal appeals court in New York to temporarily block writer E. Jean Carroll from collecting an $83 million defamation award while Trump seeks to appeal the case to the Supreme Court.

stories.title: Kyiv hails Hungary returning seized cash, eyes mending ties
stories.summary: Hungary returned cash and gold belonging to Ukraine's Oschadbank that had been seized by Budapest's security service in March. Ukrainian President Zelensky announced the move, which Kyiv views as a step toward normalizing strained bilateral relations.

stories.title: What are China’s surprise gains in the war on Iran?
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi traveled to Beijing to seek Chinese support as Tehran pursues a potential deal with the United States amid ongoing tensions.

stories.title: US trial opens over alleged Chinese ‘secret police station’ in New York
stories.summary: The trial of Lu Jianwang, a 64-year-old U.S. citizen of Chinese descent, opened in New York's Eastern District Court. He faces charges of operating an unauthorized Chinese police station in Manhattan and acting as a covert foreign agent.

stories.title: Speaker Stefanchuk discusses defense cooperation, Ukraine’s EU integration with Portuguese PM
stories.summary: Verkhovna Rada Chairman Ruslan Stefanchuk met with Portuguese Prime Minister Luís Montenegro to discuss defense cooperation and Ukraine's European Union integration efforts.

stories.title: Israeli court rejects Gaza flotilla activists' appeal challenging detention
stories.summary: An Israeli court rejected an appeal by Gaza flotilla activists challenging their detention. The two activists had been seized by Israeli forces and brought to Israel for questioning, while other participants were taken to the Greek island of Crete and released.

stories.title: Dollar weakens as investors bet on end to Iran war
stories.summary: The US dollar fell against major currencies on Wednesday, with the dollar index dropping 0.4 percent to 97.941, its lowest level since late February. Investors reacted to signs that the US-Israeli war on Iran could be moving toward a resolution, boosting the euro and British pound.

stories.title: Israeli air strike kills colonel in Hamas-led Gaza police force, medics say
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike in Gaza killed a colonel in the Hamas-led police force and wounded at least 17 other people, according to medics.

stories.title: Cuba says Rubio lying about oil blockade
stories.summary: Cuba's government accused US Secretary of State Marco Rubio of lying about an oil blockade on the island. Rubio, while guest-hosting the White House press briefing, stated that there is no oil blockade on Cuba 'per se.'

stories.title: Key bridge linking North Korea and Russia almost finished, satellite images show
stories.summary: Satellite images reveal that a key road bridge connecting North Korea and Russia is nearing completion. The infrastructure project reflects the deepening relationship between Pyongyang and Moscow.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill five Palestinians across Gaza in one day
stories.summary: Five Palestinians were killed in a single day across the Gaza Strip in separate Israeli air strikes, according to reports from the territory.

stories.title: Police officer receives promotion after Ben Gvir drops opposition
stories.summary: Israeli police officer Ruti Hauslich received a promotion to the rank of commander after far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir dropped his opposition to her advancement.

stories.title: Lebanese PM says premature to talk of any high-level meeting with Israel
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said it is premature to discuss any high-level meeting with Israel, emphasizing that strengthening the existing ceasefire must come before any new negotiations.

stories.title: War update: 120 clashes on front line, heaviest fighting in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces reported 120 combat engagements along the front line, with the heaviest fighting concentrated in the Pokrovsk sector. Ukrainian troops repelled 25 Russian attacks in that sector alone.

stories.title: Gulf economies face long-term hit from Iran conflict
stories.summary: Commentators warn that Gulf economies face long-term damage from the ongoing Iran conflict, with recovery potentially taking years or even decades to achieve.

stories.title: Israeli forces bulldoze farmland near Jenin amid settlement fears
stories.summary: Israeli military forces bulldozed agricultural land in Arrabeh, south of Jenin in the occupied West Bank, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa. Authorities also issued notices for additional land clearing for unspecified expansion projects, raising fears of settlement construction among local Palestinian residents.

stories.title: Al-Hayya's son seriously injured in Gaza, military says 'no interest in targeting him' - report
stories.summary: Azzam al-Hayya, the son of senior Hamas official Khalil al-Hayya, was seriously injured in Gaza. An Israeli military source told the Israeli outlet Maariv that the military had 'no interest' in targeting him and suggested he was harmed because he was in a location he should not have been.

stories.title: Arrest of Pakistani journalist spurs dispute over Al-Qaida allegations
stories.summary: Pakistani journalist and researcher Muhammad Saad bin Riaz was arrested on allegations of links to Al-Qaida, sparking a dispute over the charges. Supporters contend that the accusations are inconsistent with his professional work, which focused on regional conflicts and information warfare.

stories.title: French senate adopts proposed law aimed at combating Islamist infiltration
stories.summary: The French Senate adopted a bill introduced by former interior minister Bruno Retailleau aimed at countering Islamist infiltration. The legislation seeks to establish a new criminal offense for actions that undermine the fundamental principles of the French Republic.

stories.title: India, Algeria hold first joint defence commission meet
stories.summary: India and Algeria convened their first joint defence commission meeting, during which both sides signed Rules of Procedure to guide the implementation of bilateral defence cooperation and streamline future collaboration between the two countries.

stories.title: Zelensky says Hungary returned assets seized from Ukraine bank workers
stories.summary: Hungary returned assets seized from Ukrainian state bank Oschadbank workers, according to President Zelensky. The move follows a thaw in Hungarian-Ukrainian relations after former Kremlin-friendly leader Viktor Orbán was voted out in April.

stories.title: Iran says ports ready to support shipping in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Ports and Maritime Organisation declared the country's ports fully ready to provide maritime services, technical assistance, and medical support to commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The announcement followed US President Donald Trump's decision to pause the military's "Project Freedom" operation in the strait, citing progress in negotiations with Tehran.

stories.title: Ireland’s lower house ratifies Convention Establishing International Claims Commission for Ukraine
stories.summary: The Dáil Éireann, Ireland's lower house of parliament, ratified the Convention Establishing an International Claims Commission for Ukraine. The convention provides a legal framework for processing claims related to damages from the conflict.

stories.title: Russia warns foreign diplomats to leave Kyiv in case of strike
stories.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry warned foreign diplomats in Kyiv to evacuate ahead of Moscow's May 9 Victory Day celebrations. The warning included a threat of retaliatory strikes against Ukraine if commemorations linked to the Red Square military parade are disrupted.

stories.title: Spanish film, 'My Friend Eva' - an unromantic comedy, defined by covert cynicism
stories.summary: The Spanish film "My Friend Eva" follows a female protagonist who abruptly leaves her apartment and begins dating, subverting the typical male midlife-crisis narrative. The film is described as an unromantic comedy marked by covert cynicism.

stories.title: Man charged in DC shooting was walking near JD Vance’s motorcade, agent says
stories.summary: Michael Marx, 45, of Midland, Texas, was charged after allegedly firing at law enforcement officers near the Washington Monument on Monday. According to court filings, Marx had been walking near Vice President JD Vance's motorcade before the confrontation, during which he was shot multiple times by authorities.

stories.title: Oil prices fall as markets react to possible Hormuz agreement
stories.summary: Global oil prices dropped sharply on Wednesday, with Brent crude falling 5.8 percent to $103.54 per barrel, amid hopes of a US-Iran agreement to normalize shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The decline followed President Trump's suggestion that the strait could be opened to all traffic if Iran agrees to a reported deal.

stories.title: Zelensky: Russia ignores ceasefire proposal, Ukraine will respond in kind
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia has not responded to Ukraine's proposal for a full ceasefire and continues to shell Ukrainian regions. Zelensky stated that Ukraine would respond in kind to Russia's continued attacks.

stories.title: Argentina investigates link to deadly hantavirus outbreak on cruise ship
stories.summary: Argentine authorities are investigating a hantavirus outbreak linked to a cruise ship currently anchored off the coast of Cape Verde. Three deaths connected to the South America-related virus have been reported, with the vessel remaining offshore as the investigation continues.

stories.title: Protests as Venice Biennale opens in turmoil over Russia’s presence
stories.summary: Activists protested at the opening of the Venice Biennale over the return of Russia to the art festival and the participation of Israel.

stories.title: Iran’s aging tankers used for oil reserves as blockade strains storage capacity
stories.summary: Iran is reportedly commissioning aging tankers for use as floating oil storage as the US Navy blockade of the Strait of Hormuz continues to prevent Iranian oil exports from leaving the Gulf. The situation suggests Iran's energy sector and storage capacity are under significant strain.

stories.title: In rare push, US lawmakers demand transparency on Israel nuclear capability
stories.summary: A group of US lawmakers has called for greater transparency regarding Israel's nuclear capabilities, challenging Washington's longstanding policy of strategic ambiguity. The legislators argue that the current approach increases risks in the context of the ongoing US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Will warming Arctic trigger further chill in US-China relations or bring them closer?
stories.summary: As US President Donald Trump prepares for a landmark visit to China, the article examines the Arctic as a growing arena for US-China competition. Accelerating Arctic warming and disrupted global energy supplies from the Iran war are adding new dimensions to Washington-Beijing tensions.

stories.title: May 7 declared day of mourning in Sumy community
stories.summary: Authorities in the Sumy community in northeastern Ukraine declared May 7 a day of mourning for civilians killed in Russian attacks on May 6.

stories.title: JUI-F holds protest rallies across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa over killing of Maulana Idrees
stories.summary: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) held protest rallies across all districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, following the killing of former provincial lawmaker Maulana Muhammad Idrees. Party chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman called for nationwide protests and demanded the immediate arrest of those responsible.

stories.title: Iran will control Strait of Hormuz 'forever', former senior US official says
stories.summary: Former senior US official Amos Hochstein stated in a Bloomberg interview that Iran will maintain control over the Strait of Hormuz indefinitely. He warned that oil shortages currently affecting poorer nations could spread to Western countries.

stories.title: US Navy strikes Iranian-flagged ship trying to break Strait of Hormuz blockade from Gulf of Oman
stories.summary: The US Navy struck an Iranian-flagged oil tanker attempting to pass through the Strait of Hormuz blockade from the Gulf of Oman. US Central Command said the vessel was hit with 20mm cannon fire from a Navy jet.

stories.title: US aims to deploy Qatar-gifted luxury jet as Air Force One for Fourth of July
stories.summary: The US Air Force is working to prepare a Boeing 747 gifted by Qatar for service as an Air Force One aircraft by July 4, coinciding with the nation's 250th anniversary. L3Harris has been contracted to rapidly upgrade the luxury jet to presidential standards for President Trump's use.

stories.title: Ukraine urges global help as occupied Kherson region faces severe humanitarian crisis
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs called on the international community to address a severe humanitarian crisis in Russian-occupied parts of the Kherson region. The ministry accused Russian forces of crimes that violate international humanitarian law.

stories.title: Watch: Congress backs Vijay’s TVK; DMK terms it a ‘backstab’ | Above the Fold | 06.05.2026
stories.summary: India's Congress party announced its backing of actor Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) after splitting from the DMK alliance, which called the move a betrayal. The episode also covers post-poll violence in West Bengal and Iran–U.S. tensions.

stories.title: Keir Starmer makes late pitch to voters turning to Greens and Reform
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer urged voters to reject the Green Party and Reform UK ahead of Thursday's local elections in England, calling their leaders unfit to handle global instability. Labour is bracing for potentially record-breaking losses in the elections, which could be decisive for Starmer's political future.

stories.title: Fertiliser shortages will have ‘dramatic’ effect on global food prices, warns farming boss
stories.summary: The Grosvenor Group, a major British property and farming company, warned that fertilizer shortages caused by the Iran war have increased costs for UK farmers by up to 70 percent. Executive trustee Mark Preston cautioned that the disruption will have a dramatic impact on global food prices by next year.

stories.title: Russia tells diplomats to leave Kyiv in case Moscow launches mass strikes
stories.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry warned diplomatic missions and international organizations in Kyiv to evacuate personnel, citing possible retaliatory strikes. Moscow threatened military action if Ukraine targets Russian territory during Victory Day commemorations scheduled for May 9.

stories.title: US allies in Asia are looking to build middle-power coalitions
stories.summary: Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi signaled a significant shift in Tokyo's defense posture, announcing plans to relax longstanding restrictions on military equipment transfers. The move reflects a broader trend among US allies in Asia to build middle-power coalitions in response to an increasingly challenging security environment.

stories.title: Israeli strikes on Lebanon kill 4 despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli strikes hit the Lebanese town of Zellaya, killing four people despite an existing ceasefire. The attack reportedly occurred shortly before the Israeli army issued an evacuation warning for the area.

stories.title: Israeli raids continue across occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli forces conducted military operations across the occupied West Bank, including raids on Qalandiya refugee camp north of Jerusalem and the town of Shuqba east of Ramallah. Troops detained multiple Palestinians, including a young man in Tubas and several individuals in Shuqba, where a house was also demolished.

stories.title: 'Enjoy the show. Ignore the war': Venice Biennale faces backlash after including Russia
stories.summary: The Venice Biennale arts fair faced protests after including Russia for the first time since Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Demonstrators objected to Russia's participation at the prestigious event.

stories.title: Suspect arrested in Oklahoma party shooting that left one dead, 22 injured
stories.summary: Police in Edmond, Oklahoma, arrested an 18-year-old man in connection with a mass shooting at a party near Arcadia Lake that killed one woman and injured 22 others. The shooting on Sunday night reportedly erupted following an argument at the lake gathering, which had been promoted on social media.

stories.title: Executed Iranian prisoners detail abuse, torture ahead of their killing to 'Post' -exclusive
stories.summary: Three Iranian prisoners—Yaghoub Karimpour, 43, Nasser Bakerzadeh, 26, and Mehrab Abdollahzadeh, 28—were executed at Orumiyeh Central Prison over the weekend. Before their deaths, the prisoners detailed accounts of abuse and torture they endured while in custody.

stories.title: U.S. Might Be Close to a Deal With Iran
stories.summary: A reported memorandum between the United States and Iran could end the ongoing war, reopen the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping, and establish a framework for future nuclear negotiations. The potential deal signals a significant diplomatic breakthrough between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Russia–Ukraine Victory Day truce collapses as Moscow and Kyiv trade accusations of violations
stories.summary: A proposed Victory Day truce between Russia and Ukraine collapsed as both sides accused each other of violations. Russia declared a temporary halt from May 8–9, while President Zelensky announced Ukraine's own truce starting May 6, but fighting continued and Ukraine signaled it would not observe a ceasefire on May 9.

stories.title: Civilian killed as Russians attack Zaporizhzhia region
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Zaporizhzhia district in southeastern Ukraine with guided aerial bombs and drones, killing one civilian and wounding two others.

stories.title: Trump says had ‘very good talks’ with Iran as Tehran reviews US proposal
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that he held productive talks with Iran, as Tehran reviews a US proposal. The discussions signal potential momentum toward a diplomatic resolution that could end the ongoing conflict between the US-Israel coalition and Iran.

stories.title: Explainer-What is the hantavirus that killed three cruise ship passengers?
stories.summary: Three passengers have died in a hantavirus outbreak aboard a luxury cruise ship, the MV Hondius, with five additional confirmed or suspected cases. Health authorities are investigating the source of the outbreak.

stories.title: Trump-Xi summit hides simmering trade tensions under the surface, industry experts say
stories.summary: Ahead of a scheduled summit between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, trade experts warn that significant commercial tensions persist beneath diplomatic pleasantries. Analysts note that China has quietly strengthened its position and is less willing than in the past to accept US tariffs and export restrictions.

stories.title: Iran is now a superpower; ties with India are flourishing: Iran Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baqaei
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baqaei stated that Iran is now a superpower and that ties with India are flourishing. He added that Tehran is reviewing America's response to its peace proposal.

stories.title: Trump says ‘very good talks’ held with Iran in past 24 hours
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced that Washington held 'very good talks' with Iran over the preceding 24 hours regarding a proposal to end the US-Israeli war on Iran. Speaking from the Oval Office, Trump said a deal was 'very possible.'

stories.title: Israel bombs Beirut’s southern suburbs
stories.summary: Israel carried out airstrikes on Beirut's southern suburbs, marking the first such attack since a ceasefire agreement took effect on April 17. The strikes represent a significant escalation in renewed hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon.

stories.title: Passengers on hantavirus-stricken ship sway between fear and boredom
stories.summary: The Dutch-flagged expedition ship MV Hondius remains stranded off Cabo Verde due to a hantavirus outbreak that has killed three people and sickened at least eight others. Passengers are confined to their cabins while the ship's operator seeks a safe port for docking.

stories.title: The BJP Scores Big in West Bengal
stories.summary: India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party achieved significant electoral gains in four state elections, including in West Bengal where it unseated a longtime political rival. The results represent a major boost for the BJP's national standing.

stories.title: Russian forces launch missile strike on Popivka community, Sumy region
stories.summary: Russian forces launched a missile strike on the Popivka community in Ukraine's Sumy region, injuring a woman and damaging residential buildings.

stories.title: Venice Biennale previews marred by protests over Israeli, Russian presence
stories.summary: Protesters disrupted preview events at the Venice Biennale art festival, targeting both Russian and Israeli participation. Bare-breasted activists demonstrated against Russia's return to the event for the first time since its invasion of Ukraine, while pro-Palestinian protesters displayed banners reading "No artwashing genocide" outside the Israel pavilion.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1533: Russia preached peace and bombed kindergartens—Switzerland’s report and a Cheboksary crater told the truer story
stories.summary: On day 1,533 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, Russia conducted approximately 1,820 strikes despite declaring a May 9 ceasefire, killing a woman in a kindergarten in Kharkiv. Switzerland's annual intelligence assessment confirmed Russia's escalation of its conflict against the West. Ukraine struck a Russian plant producing Shahed drone antennas with a Flamingo missile, and the US authorized JDAM-ER kits for Kyiv.

stories.title: G7 trade ministers seek common ground on minerals
stories.summary: G7 trade ministers met to seek common ground on securing supply chains for critical minerals amid geopolitical tensions, with an implicit focus on reducing dependence on China. Separately, France's finance minister assured that airlines have sufficient jet fuel supplies through May and June.

stories.title: IDF targets Hezbollah Radwan commander in Beirut in first attack on capital in weeks
stories.summary: The Israeli military targeted a Hezbollah Radwan Force commander in Beirut, marking the first Israeli strike on the Lebanese capital in weeks. A source told The Jerusalem Post that the United States had advance knowledge of the operation but that Israel did not request a formal green light.

stories.title: Paigham-i-Islam Conference awards title of ‘Greatest Victorious General of the Century’ to CDF Asim Munir
stories.summary: At the Sixth International Paigham-i-Islam Conference in Islamabad, Pakistan's Chief of Defence Forces Asim Munir was awarded the titles "Leader of Peace" and "Greatest Victorious General of the Century." The conference also condemned attacks on Iran by the United States and Israel.

stories.title: Bahrain says suspects linked to IRGC arrested
stories.summary: Bahrain's interior ministry announced the arrest of an unspecified number of individuals alleged to have close links to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, with some facing espionage-related charges. The arrests follow Bahrain's late-April decision to revoke the citizenship of 69 people accused of supporting Iranian attacks against the country.

stories.title: Ex-spy Jonathan Pollard joins politics, calls to annex Gaza Strip
stories.summary: Jonathan Pollard, who served 30 years in a US prison for spying on behalf of Israel, announced his entry into Israeli politics and called for the annexation of the Gaza Strip. Pollard has become a vocal critic of Prime Minister Netanyahu.

stories.title: Russian forces attack five districts of Dnipropetrovsk region, injuring a 10-year-old child
stories.summary: Russian troops carried out nearly 80 attacks using drones and artillery across five districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region. A 10-year-old child was among those injured in the strikes.

stories.title: Ben‑Gvir ‘dreams’ of nooses in TikTok video glorifying death penalty for Palestinians
stories.summary: Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir posted a TikTok video featuring an AI-generated montage of nooses, referencing the death penalty for Palestinians. The far-right minister faced significant online backlash for the post, which followed a viral social media trend.

stories.title: Moscow court bans entertainment website ‘YaPlakal’ over alleged racist jokes
stories.summary: A Moscow district court banned the distribution of content from the Russian entertainment website YaPlakal, citing alleged racist jokes. The ruling, issued in late April, was reported by independent Russian outlet Verstka.

stories.title: Russia cuts mobile internet in Moscow citing drone security concerns
stories.summary: Russian authorities have implemented rolling mobile internet shutdowns in Moscow and other cities, citing security concerns related to drone activity.

stories.title: China Tests a Rare Tool in Its Sanctions Arsenal
stories.summary: Ahead of a summit between President Trump and President Xi Jinping, China deployed a rarely used sanctions tool to push back against Washington. The move signals Beijing's willingness to escalate economic countermeasures amid ongoing bilateral tensions.

stories.title: Trump shows control over Republican base with primary wins
stories.summary: Trump-backed candidates won key Republican primary races, including in Ohio, demonstrating the former president's continued control over the party's base. Ohio is expected to play a pivotal role in the battle for Senate control.

stories.title: Indonesia’s new(ish) aircraft carrier: defence boost or expensive gamble?
stories.summary: Indonesia is set to acquire the Italian aircraft carrier Giuseppe Garibaldi as its first aircraft carrier. The Indonesian Naval Chief said the vessel will be used for non-war military operations to enhance maritime capabilities.

stories.title: Defense Business Brief: Pitching America first; Visa deal?; Skunk Works exec moves up; plus a little more
stories.summary: A defense industry briefing covered several developments including advocacy for "America first" procurement policies, a potential visa-related agreement, and a leadership promotion at Lockheed Martin's Skunk Works advanced development division.

stories.title: Tshisekedi hints at possible rule beyond second term
stories.summary: Democratic Republic of Congo President Félix Tshisekedi suggested he would accept a third term if supported by the public through a constitutional referendum. Separately, a French court ordered the reopening of an investigation into the widow of former Rwandan President Habyarimana's alleged involvement in the 1994 genocide. New allegations of secret detentions have also emerged from Burkina Faso.

stories.title: Pioneering CNN founder Ted Turner dead at 87
stories.summary: Ted Turner, the American entrepreneur who founded CNN in 1980, died at age 87 after suffering from Lewy Body Dementia. Turner transformed television news with 24-hour coverage, and CNN gained global recognition during the 1990–91 Gulf War. His business empire also included sports teams and major philanthropic efforts.

stories.title: Israeli strike in Gaza kills senior Palestinian police officer
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike near the al-Mawasi area west of Khan Younis in Gaza killed Colonel Naseem al-Kalazani, a senior officer in Gaza's police force and the Palestinian interior ministry. At least 17 other people were wounded when his vehicle was targeted.

stories.title: Mamdani slams Israeli real estate event in NYC as 'effort to displace Palestinians'
stories.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani criticized an Israeli real estate event held at Park East Synagogue in New York City, calling it an effort to displace Palestinians. A similar event at the same synagogue in November had also drawn protests.

stories.title: Zelensky discusses development of bilateral relations with President of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev discussed bilateral relations and the implementation of agreements reached during Zelensky's recent visit to Azerbaijan.

stories.title: Israel competition watchdog declares top banks an oligopoly, targets deposits
stories.summary: Israel's competition authority declared the country's five largest banks—Hapoalim, Leumi, Mizrahi Tefahot, Discount, and First International—an oligopoly. The watchdog noted the banks control 98% of the banking sector's assets, with Hapoalim and Leumi together holding half. The regulator plans to target deposit market concentration.

stories.title: Canadian Jewish groups call for designating Palestine Action a terrorist entity
stories.summary: Several Canadian Jewish organizations called on the Canadian government to designate Palestine Action as a terrorist entity. The groups cited the activist network's published guide on building 'cells' and 'destroying' targets as incitement to violence.

stories.title: Rare shelter for displaced LGBT people in Lebanon offers safety in war
stories.summary: A rare shelter in Beirut is providing safety for displaced LGBT people fleeing conflict in Lebanon. Among them is Mohammed, a gay man from southern Lebanon who fled after Israeli strikes hit his hometown in March.

stories.title: Zelensky thanks Norway for its support of PURL program
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky thanked Norway for its support of the PURL program, noting that Norway's total contribution has exceeded $1.2 billion, making it the largest contributor among all participating countries.

stories.title: 'Insider trading': Oil and stocks jolt on news of US-Iran deal as some cry 'manipulation'
stories.summary: Minutes before reports emerged of a potential US-Iran deal, approximately $920 million was wagered on oil prices dropping. The sudden market movements in oil and stocks prompted accusations of insider trading and market manipulation from observers.

stories.title: Israel strikes Beirut for first time since Hezbollah ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel carried out an airstrike in Beirut targeting a senior Hezbollah figure, marking the first such strike on the Lebanese capital since a ceasefire took effect in mid-April.

stories.title: Israeli strike on Lebanese town kills two people
stories.summary: An Israeli strike hit a house in the southern Lebanese town of Khirbet Selm, killing at least two people and wounding another.

stories.title: US strikes Iranian tanker amid reports Washington and Tehran near deal
stories.summary: US forces struck an Iranian oil tanker in the Gulf of Oman by targeting its rudder as it attempted to breach an American naval blockade of Iranian ports. The strike occurred even as Washington and Tehran appeared to be nearing a tentative agreement to end their two-month war. President Trump warned that renewed bombing could begin if Iran rejects the proposed deal.

stories.title: Armenia: EU 'isn't poking the bear' enforcing ties with Russian-allied Yerevan
stories.summary: Analyst Thorniké Gordadze argued that the European Union's deepening ties with Armenia are not intended to provoke Russia but are a response to Moscow's threats in the South Caucasus region. The EU maintains that its engagement with Yerevan, a traditional Russian ally, is reactive rather than confrontational.

stories.title: Washington Is Still Chasing the Perfect War
stories.summary: The article argues that the US war against Iran reveals persistent strategic delusions similar to those that led to the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan.

stories.title: Netanyahu 'not surprised' by US-Iran negotiations development, says there is 'full coordination'
stories.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he was 'not surprised' by developments in US-Iran negotiations, asserting there is 'full coordination' between Israel and the United States. Netanyahu stated he speaks with President Trump on an almost daily basis.

stories.title: The Iran War Is Eroding Israel’s Nuclear Ambiguity
stories.summary: The ongoing conflict between the US-Israel coalition and Iran is reportedly eroding Israel's longstanding policy of nuclear ambiguity. Washington is increasingly breaking the taboo by publicly discussing Israel's nuclear capabilities.

stories.title: Could Iran use ‘kamikaze dolphins’ against the US in the Strait of Hormuz?
stories.summary: During a Pentagon briefing, a journalist asked US officials whether Iran could deploy 'kamikaze dolphins' against American warships in the Strait of Hormuz. Multiple countries have historically used marine mammals for military purposes, making the concept less far-fetched than it initially appears.

stories.title: Al-Qaeda-linked fighters storm Mali prison, block food supplies to Bamako
stories.summary: Al-Qaeda-linked fighters attacked a high-security prison in Mali, sometimes referred to as 'Africa's Alcatraz,' which holds high-value detainees. The fighters also disrupted food supply routes to the capital, Bamako.

stories.title: Artists paint dinner plates for lone soldier charity
stories.summary: A Tel Aviv exhibit titled 'A Plate of Hope and Color' features dinner plates painted by well-known Israeli artisans. Proceeds from the exhibit benefit a charity supporting lone soldiers serving in the Israel Defense Forces.

stories.title: IDF soldier seen placing cigarette Virgin Mary statue’s mouth in Lebanese village
stories.summary: An IDF soldier was photographed placing a cigarette in the mouth of a Virgin Mary statue in a Lebanese village. The incident occurred in the same village where another soldier previously smashed a Jesus statue. The Israeli military said the soldier would face disciplinary action.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones strike Russian pilot training center in occupied Luhansk region
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces carried out drone strikes on a Russian training center for artillery spotters and drone operators in Khrustalnyi, a town in the temporarily occupied Luhansk region.

stories.title: Israeli soldier wounded by drone as attacks continue in south Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli soldier was wounded by an explosive drone strike in southern Lebanon. Israeli forces continued extensive air strikes and artillery attacks across the region, including a strike on the town of al-Saksakieh that killed at least five people and wounded 15 others, according to Lebanon's National News Agency.

stories.title: What does the BJP’s victory in West Bengal mean for India’s democracy?
stories.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) secured a victory in West Bengal state elections in India. Analysts suggest the outcome could have significant implications for national politics and the country's approximately 200 million Muslim citizens.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills colonel in Gaza police force, say Palestinian medics
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike in western Khan Younis, Gaza, killed Colonel Naseem al-Kalazani of the Gaza police force, according to Palestinian medics. At least 17 other people were wounded in the targeted strike on his vehicle.

stories.title: Iran urges UN states to reject US-backed Hormuz resolution
stories.summary: Iran's permanent mission to the United Nations urged member states to reject a US-backed draft resolution pressuring Tehran to guarantee safe shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. The mission called the proposal 'flawed' and 'politically motivated,' insisting that ending the war and lifting the maritime blockade are the only viable solutions.

stories.title: Breathe Pakistan: Business leaders, experts stress need to tackle climate change's impact on agri-economy
stories.summary: The second Breathe Pakistan International Climate Change Conference opened in Islamabad, where business leaders and experts discussed climate change's impact on Pakistan's agriculture and the need for stronger policy implementation and climate finance.

stories.title: Rutgers University withdraws invite to graduation speaker over criticism of Israel
stories.summary: Rutgers University withdrew an invitation to graduation speaker Rami Elghandour, an engineering alumnus, after students raised concerns. Elghandour had posted social media content accusing Israel of war crimes, including genocide and ethnic cleansing.

stories.title: India says Pakistani players can visit for multilateral events but bilateral competitions ​remain off table
stories.summary: India's sports ministry announced that Pakistani athletes may participate in multilateral sporting events hosted in India, but bilateral competitions between the two countries remain suspended. Visa procedures for sports officials will also be simplified.

stories.title: Casualty toll after attack on kindergarten in Sumy rises to two, seven others injured
stories.summary: The casualty toll from a Russian drone strike on a kindergarten in the Ukrainian city of Sumy on May 6 rose to two after rescuers recovered another body from the rubble. Seven other people were injured in the attack.

stories.title: British Jews gather for annual celebration in shadow of recent attacks
stories.summary: Thousands of British Jews gathered in north London on Tuesday to celebrate the Lag B'Omer festival amid heightened tensions following a string of recent antisemitic attacks across the country.

stories.title: Sudanese asylum seekers challenge Home Office rule changes for refugees
stories.summary: Two Sudanese asylum seekers are legally challenging UK Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood's plan to cut refugees' leave to remain from five years to 30 months. Under the new rules, refugees would have to wait 20 years before becoming eligible for permanent settlement, a change that has drawn concern from the UN's refugee agency.

stories.title: Israeli airstrike reportedly kills colonel in Hamas-led Gaza police force - report
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike reportedly killed Naseem al-Kalazani, a colonel in the Hamas-run police force in Gaza, by targeting his vehicle near the al-Mawasi area in western Khan Younis in the southern part of the enclave.

stories.title: Netanyahu says he ordered Beirut strike targeting Hezbollah commander
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced that he and Defence Minister Israel Katz ordered a strike targeting a commander in Hezbollah's Radwan Force in Beirut. The attack hit Beirut's southern suburbs for the second time on Wednesday, causing a large explosion and extensive damage. Hezbollah had not yet commented.

stories.title: Third round of Israel-Lebanon talks to take place in US next week - report
stories.summary: A third round of Israel-Lebanon negotiations is reportedly scheduled to take place in the United States next week. Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam stated that Lebanon was pursuing peace with Israel, not normalization.

stories.title: Uncertainty looms as last oil tanker from Middle East arrives in California
stories.summary: The oil tanker New Corolla, the last planned shipment from the Middle East through the Strait of Hormuz, arrived in Long Beach, California, carrying approximately two million barrels of Iraqi crude oil. The delivery comes as California's average gas price already exceeds $6 per gallon, with further supply uncertainty ahead.

stories.title: Fresh forensic leads revive Italy's infamous Garlasco murder mystery
stories.summary: Italian authorities have reopened the nearly two-decade-old murder case of Chiara Poggi, a 26-year-old found dead in her home in the northern town of Garlasco. Fresh forensic leads have revived doubts about the original investigation.

stories.title: Zelensky: Air defense systems concentrated around Moscow for parade open opportunities for our long-range sanctions
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky noted that Russia had relocated additional air defense systems to Moscow from other regions to protect Victory Day parade preparations, creating new vulnerabilities that Ukraine could exploit with long-range strikes.

stories.title: Italy’s Meloni denounces deepfake photo as a political attack
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has denounced a deepfake photo targeting her, calling it a political attack. Meloni warned that deepfake technology is dangerous because it can deceive and manipulate anyone.

stories.title: German woman on hantavirus-hit ship to be tested at German hospital
stories.summary: A German national who was aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship during a deadly hantavirus outbreak will be brought to a hospital in Düsseldorf for testing. A hospital spokesperson said the person is currently showing no symptoms.

stories.title: Israel strikes Beirut for the first time since Lebanon ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel carried out an airstrike in Beirut's southern suburbs on Wednesday, marking its first strike on the city since a ceasefire with Hezbollah was agreed last month. The Israeli government said the strike targeted a commander of Hezbollah's elite Radwan force. Israeli media reported the commander was killed, but neither the military nor Hezbollah confirmed this.

stories.title: Capital Market Development Fund established to strengthen Pakistan’s capital markets
stories.summary: Key Pakistani capital market institutions, including the Pakistan Stock Exchange and Central Depository Company, established the Capital Market Development Fund to promote financial literacy, expand inclusion, and increase retail investor participation.

stories.title: The zen of the siren: Richard Priestman and the architecture of Israeli archery stillness
stories.summary: Richard Priestman, a 71-year-old archery coach, completed a tenure leading Israel's archery program into global competitiveness despite the country's limited background in the sport.

stories.title: Any deal with Israel must include guarantees, Lebanon’s parliament speaker says
stories.summary: Lebanese parliament speaker Nabih Berri said any agreement with Israel must include guarantees, accusing Israel of violating the cessation of hostilities while Hezbollah adhered to it. Berri said Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi assured Lebanese officials that Lebanon would be included in any US-brokered agreement to end the conflict.

stories.title: Belgium indicts 3 Jewish mohels, sparking diplomatic spat with Israel and US
stories.summary: Belgium indicted three Jewish mohels, practitioners of ritual circumcision, prompting a diplomatic dispute with Israel and the United States. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar accused Antwerp of antisemitism, while his Belgian counterpart said the probe was initiated by representatives of the local Jewish community in a country where only doctors may perform medical procedures.

stories.title: Ukraine views return of Oschadbank funds as sign of Hungary's readiness to develop relations – FM Sybiha
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha welcomed Hungary's return of funds and valuables belonging to Ukraine's state-owned Oschadbank, viewing the move as a positive signal of Hungary's willingness to improve bilateral relations.

stories.title: Influencer Clavicular faces charges in Florida tied to alligator shooting video
stories.summary: Social media influencer Braden Eric Peters, known online as Clavicular, faces charges in Florida for unlawfully discharging a firearm in a public place. The charges stem from a live-streamed video showing him shooting an apparently already dead alligator in the Everglades.

stories.title: China says will play 'greater role' in ending Middle East conflict
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said Beijing would play a "greater role" in ending Middle East hostilities during talks with his Iranian counterpart. The discussions come a week before a planned meeting between Presidents Trump and Xi Jinping, with China being a major buyer of Iranian oil.

stories.title: US student groups fundraise to supplement PA funds to 'mothers of martyrs'
stories.summary: Student groups at City College of New York, John Jay College, and the City University of New York organized a bake sale to raise funds intended to supplement Palestinian Authority payments to families of individuals killed in the conflict.

stories.title: 2 Estonians who crossed into Russia seeking asylum are jailed on border violation charges
stories.summary: Two Estonian citizens who independently crossed into Russia on foot over a frozen lake in winter 2026 seeking asylum were detained and jailed on criminal charges of illegally crossing the border.

stories.title: Indiana, Ohio primaries draw midterm battle lines, reinforce Trump’s pull
stories.summary: Primary elections in Indiana and Ohio have set the stage for key midterm Senate races. The results reinforced former President Donald Trump's continued influence over the Republican Party and its candidate selection process.

stories.title: Heatwave conditions expected across Pakistan from May 7-11: PMD
stories.summary: Pakistan's Meteorological Department forecast heatwave conditions across the country from May 7 to 11, with daytime temperatures potentially reaching 46–50°C in parts of Sindh and Balochistan, including Jacobabad, Sukkur, Turbat, and other cities.

stories.title: Iran says no formal response yet to latest US proposal
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei stated that Tehran has not yet formally responded to the latest US proposal but that diplomatic exchanges continue through Pakistani mediation, with ongoing reviews of exchanged texts.

stories.title: Why are Pentagon officials talking about Iran’s ‘deadly dolphins’?
stories.summary: Analyst Soraya Lennie addressed and debunked false claims circulating about Iran allegedly using dolphins or other marine life as weapons in warfare. Pentagon officials had referenced the unverified assertions about Iran's purported 'deadly dolphins' program.

stories.title: IDF soldier 'smokes' with Virgin Mary statue in latest act of disregard towards Lebanese Christians
stories.summary: A photograph surfaced showing an IDF soldier posing with a Virgin Mary statue in the Lebanese village of Debel. The image, reported by Kan News, was uploaded to social media by Israeli soldiers.

stories.title: Trump threatens Iran with ‘higher level’ bombing if it doesn't reopen Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened Iran with escalated bombing if it does not reopen the Strait of Hormuz. He acknowledged it was "perhaps a big assumption" that Iran would accept the terms Washington has offered.

stories.title: Shoot Palestinians, not settlers: Israeli general exposes double standard
stories.summary: Leaked statements from the head of the Israeli army in the occupied West Bank revealed differing rules of engagement for Palestinians and Israeli settlers. The leaks indicated a two-tier firing policy, exposing systemic disparities in how the military treats the two populations.

stories.title: Level of training in Air Assault Forces is high, but some issues still remain – Syrskyi
stories.summary: Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces of Ukraine Oleksandr Syrskyi stated that the level of training in the Air Assault Forces is high, but there are still problematic issues.

stories.title: Russian Customs Seize British Children’s Books as ‘Extremist Literature’
stories.summary: Russian customs officials seized British children's books, including "The Dinosaurs Who Met Santa Claus" and "Baby's Very First Big Play Book," classifying them as extremist literature.

stories.title: US forces fire at, disable Iran-flagged tanker trying to evade blockade
stories.summary: U.S. naval forces fired at and disabled an Iran-flagged tanker that attempted to evade the ongoing American blockade of Iranian ports. The incident occurred despite President Trump's announcement that Project Freedom had been paused, as the Navy continues to enforce restrictions on vessels entering and exiting Iranian ports.

stories.title: Turkey rolls out intercontinental missile with purported 6,000km range
stories.summary: Turkey has unveiled an intercontinental ballistic missile with a reported range of 6,000 kilometers. A defense analyst said the ICBM would add a crucial layer of deterrence to Turkey's military arsenal.

stories.title: Starmer's last stand? The UK local elections
stories.summary: Local elections in the United Kingdom carry unusually high stakes for Prime Minister Keir Starmer's Labour government. The growing popularity of Reform and the Green Party is challenging Britain's traditional two-party political system.

stories.title: US attempts to strong arm Iran will fail, parliament speaker says
stories.summary: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf accused the United States of using economic and media pressure to force Iran into surrender, asserting that the strategy would fail and warning that such decisions would cause widespread harm.

stories.title: Former Russian insider says fear pushed elites to embrace Putin war
stories.summary: A former Russian insider has stated that the start of the war in Ukraine shocked Russia's elite, with attempts made to persuade President Putin to halt hostilities. The source said fear ultimately pushed elites to embrace Putin's war.

stories.title: France moves aircraft carrier to Red Sea with eye on Hormuz mission
stories.summary: France deployed its carrier strike group to the Red Sea on Wednesday as part of planning for a potential mission to secure the Strait of Hormuz. The move signals Paris's readiness to participate in ensuring freedom of navigation in the strategically vital waterway.

stories.title: Iran conflict may have motivated Trump dinner shooting suspect, US intelligence report finds
stories.summary: A U.S. intelligence report found that suspect Cole Allen, linked to a shooting at a Trump dinner, may have been motivated by the Iran conflict. The assessment noted Allen had "multiple social and political grievances."

stories.title: Iran conflict may have motivated Trump dinner shooting suspect, US intelligence report finds
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security identified the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran as a potential motive for the suspect accused of attempting to assassinate President Donald Trump and senior administration members at a White House reporters' gala. The intelligence report was distributed to state, local, and federal law enforcement agencies.

stories.title: Dar says Pakistan's focus is now on making US-Iran ceasefire permanent
stories.summary: Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said Pakistan is working to make the U.S.-Iran ceasefire permanent. President Trump had indefinitely extended the initially two-week ceasefire, which was brokered partly through Pakistani mediation.

stories.title: FBI reportedly probing leaks behind article on bureau chief Kash Patel’s drinking
stories.summary: The FBI has opened a criminal leak investigation related to a journalist who authored a critical article about FBI Director Kash Patel, according to MS Now. Patel filed a $250 million defamation lawsuit last month against The Atlantic magazine and reporter Sarah Fitzpatrick over the piece, which alleged he frequently drank to excess.

stories.title: EU urged to ‘act now’ on West Bank settlement project
stories.summary: Signatories of an appeal urged the European Union to act against West Bank settlement expansion, calling for targeted sanctions including visa bans and business restrictions against those involved in the project.

stories.title: Iran economy deteriorating amid sanctions, continuing blockade
stories.summary: Iran's economy is deteriorating under sanctions and a continuing blockade, with inflation surpassing 73%. The sharp rise has driven up everyday food prices as the value of the Iranian rial continues to fall dramatically.

stories.title: China's 'key priorities': Open Hormuz, get oil flowing, avoid 'getting dragged into conflicts'
stories.summary: Professor Astrid Nordin of King's College London described China's strategy in the Middle East as focused on keeping the Strait of Hormuz open and oil flowing while avoiding direct military entanglement. Beijing seeks diplomatic influence and energy security without assuming the burdens of American-style global policing.

stories.title: Ukraine's Defense Intelligence shows how it struck Russian railway logistics in Crimea
stories.summary: The Main Intelligence Directorate of the Ministry of Defense of Ukraine released video footage of a special operation carried out in April in temporarily occupied Crimea, during which Russian freight

stories.title: Trump issues ultimatum for Iran to accept deal or face bombing
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump issued an ultimatum to Iran, stating that if Tehran fails to agree to a deal to end the war, bombing would resume at a much higher level and intensity than before.

stories.title: US, Iran said closing in on framework for permanent deal, as Trump renews bomb threats
stories.summary: The United States and Iran are reportedly nearing a framework for a permanent deal, based on a one-page memorandum of understanding. The proposed framework includes halting Iranian uranium enrichment, lifting US sanctions, reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a Lebanon ceasefire, and launching monthlong detailed negotiations. President Trump simultaneously renewed threats of military action.

stories.title: B-52 engine replacement clears critical design review, first modifications to begin this year
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force announced on May 4 that the program to replace the B-52H Stratofortress's 1960s-era engines has cleared its critical design review. The first aircraft modifications are expected to begin later this year.

stories.title: Iran ‘has attained an elevated international standing’ says FM
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister stated that Iran has achieved an elevated international standing during the ongoing war. The remarks reflected Tehran's assessment of its diplomatic position amid the broader regional conflict.

stories.title: Lockheed opposes Northrop bid to remove firewall on solid rocket motor business
stories.summary: Lockheed Martin is opposing a bid by Northrop Grumman to remove a firewall on its solid rocket motor business. Northrop argues that a 2018 consent order is hindering its ability to increase production of solid rocket motors needed for critical munitions programs.

stories.title: Eight killed in Iran shopping centre fire as probe targets builder
stories.summary: A major fire engulfed a shopping center near Tehran, Iran, killing eight people and injuring 36 others. Authorities launched a criminal investigation targeting the building's developer.

stories.title: Two bodies recovered after Israeli strike in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Civil defence teams in the southern Lebanese city of Tyre recovered two bodies after an Israeli airstrike targeted a car near Al-Siraj High School. A separate Israeli air raid struck a house in the town of Khirbet Selm near its municipal building.

stories.title: Breathe Pakistan: Law minister decries ‘lack of will’ in tackling climate crisis
stories.summary: The second Breathe Pakistan International Climate Change Conference, organized by DawnMedia, opened in Islamabad. Pakistan's law minister criticized the lack of political will to address the climate crisis, noting Pakistan remains among the most climate-vulnerable nations despite contributing minimally to global emissions.

stories.title: Meet the Green Party candidate taking on Labour in Brixton
stories.summary: Green Party candidate Zvikomborero 'Zviko' Chihoro is running against Labour in the Brixton local election in the UK. He discussed how solidarity with Palestine shapes his political platform in an interview with The New Arab.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Flamingo flew 1,500 km to Russia’s drone-navigation plant. It hit the parking lot.
stories.summary: Ukraine launched its long-range Flamingo drone on a roughly 1,500-kilometer mission targeting a Russian drone-navigation plant.
