However, the strike hit the facility's parking lot rather than the main building, missing the intended target. Only two of 23 Flamingo launches have achieved confirmed direct hits.

stories.title: The Rwanda model: What is Syria's strategy for economic revival?
stories.summary: Syria is pursuing a strategy modeled on Rwanda's economic approach, focusing on privatisation and foreign investment to rebuild its war-ravaged economy. Questions remain about whether the plan can succeed without sufficient transparency and expertise.

stories.title: War update: 63 combat clashes since morning, Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors remain most active
stories.summary: Since the beginning of the day, there have been 63 combat clashes on the front line, with the Pokrovsk and Huliaipole directions being the hottest.

stories.title: Syria ‘to dissolve’ controversial Political Affairs Secretariat
stories.summary: Syria has reportedly decided to dissolve the General Secretariat for Political Affairs, a body originally established to manage assets belonging to the former ruling Baath Party.

stories.title: Israel bombs Beirut’s southern suburb as it targets Hezbollah commander
stories.summary: Israel bombed Beirut's southern Dahiyeh suburb, targeting a Hezbollah commander. It was the first Israeli strike on Beirut's southern suburbs since a truce in the Israel-Hezbollah war took effect on April 17.

stories.title: CISA's sharp reductions in election-security assistance could leave midterms vulnerable, senator says
stories.summary: A U.S. senator warned that sharp reductions in election-security assistance from the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) could leave upcoming midterm elections vulnerable. Senator Warner said state and local officials are reporting decreased access to training, intelligence, and cybersecurity support.

stories.title: Russia snubs Ukraine's unilateral ceasefire, firing dozens of drones
stories.summary: Russia rejected Ukraine's unilateral ceasefire declaration and launched dozens of drone strikes, killing 27 civilians. The attacks underscore the failure of recent peace efforts as the conflict continues.

stories.title: Trump's hopes for an Iran peace deal come with caveats
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump has signaled cautious optimism about reaching a peace deal with Iran, though he has tempered expectations with caveats. Fresh momentum toward ending the conflict has emerged, but significant uncertainties remain.

stories.title: UAE denies involvement in Sudan airport attack
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates denied involvement in an attack on a Sudanese airport. Sudan has long accused the UAE of providing support to the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces operating in the country.

stories.title: Israeli court rejects appeal to free detained Gaza flotilla activists
stories.summary: An Israeli court in Beersheba denied an appeal by legal rights group Adalah to release detained Gaza flotilla activists Thiago Avila and Saif Abu Keshek, extending their detention until Sunday. Both activists are reportedly on hunger strike.

stories.title: How Much Longer Can Russia Last in the War?
stories.summary: Analysts Collin Meisel and Mathew Burrows revisited their 2025 assessment that Russia could sustain its war effort in Ukraine due to advantages in population, economic capacity, and munitions production. After another year of combat, they re-evaluated Russia's ability to continue absorbing losses.

stories.title: How India's pharmaceutical pipeline is fuelling West Africa's opioid crisis
stories.summary: An investigation highlights how pharmaceutical products manufactured in India are being exported in large quantities to West Africa, fueling an opioid crisis in countries including Sierra Leone, Togo, Ghana, and Nigeria that is devastating communities across the region.

stories.title: UK voters need to hear battle over bills and climate crisis are linked, green experts say
stories.summary: Ahead of local elections in the United Kingdom, green energy advocates urged political leaders to communicate the link between rising living costs and dependence on fossil fuels. The Reform party has pledged to block solar and wind farm development, while energy leaders argue renewables offer greater long-term security.

stories.title: Is the Iran War Pushing Southeast Asia into China’s Arms?
stories.summary: A report examines how the U.S.-Iran conflict is generating economic shocks in Southeast Asia, particularly affecting Indonesia, the Philippines, and Vietnam. The analysis suggests that U.S. security guarantees have not insulated these nations from the fallout, potentially pushing the region closer to China.

stories.title: What is everyone misunderstanding about US intelligence report on Iran nuclear threat? - analysis
stories.summary: A US intelligence report on Iran's nuclear threat is being widely discussed, with analysis suggesting that while the US may question whether the 2025 and 2026 wars were worth the cost, Israel views both conflicts as clearly justified.

stories.title: Thiago Avila mourns mother's death as Israel extends detention
stories.summary: Brazilian flotilla activist Thiago Avila is mourning the death of his mother while remaining in Israeli detention after a court upheld his imprisonment following the seizure of a Gaza-bound aid flotilla.

stories.title: Hungary returns gold and cash seized from Ukrainian state bank Oschadbank
stories.summary: Hungary returned gold and cash belonging to Ukraine's state bank Oschadbank that had been seized in March, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

stories.title: Hungary returns funds and valuables belonging to Oschadbank to Ukraine – Zelensky
stories.summary: Hungary returned to Ukraine money and valuables of Oschadbank that had been seized by Hungarian special services in March of this year.

stories.title: How the US-led war in the region created an Arab poverty crisis
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the US-Israel war on Iran could significantly increase poverty across the Middle East and North Africa region, as populations face double-digit price hikes on essential goods.

stories.title: Iran war 'may have motivated' Trump dinner shooting suspect
stories.summary: A US intelligence review of shooting suspect Cole Allen's social media posts found that the ongoing war in Iran may have been among the factors motivating the attack on a dinner event associated with President Trump.

stories.title: US media report points to memorandum to end war after Trump pauses mission to open strait
stories.summary: The United States is reportedly expecting Iranian responses on several key points within 48 hours, as reports point to a memorandum aimed at ending the conflict after President Trump paused the mission to open the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Israel unaware of possible US-Iran agreement: Reuters
stories.summary: Israeli officials were reportedly unaware that US President Donald Trump could be nearing an agreement with Tehran, according to Reuters. Israel had instead been preparing for a possible escalation in the conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Liberman calls for ‘decisive outcome,’ vows not to sit in government with Netanyahu
stories.summary: Launching the campaign at a press conference in Tel Aviv, Yisrael Beytenu leader MK Avigdor Liberman vowed not to sit in a government with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

stories.title: Cyberattacks are now part of US counterterrorism strategy
stories.summary: The White House's updated counterterrorism strategy now formally incorporates offensive and defensive cyberattacks as tools for combating terrorism. The administration stated the approach aims to deter foreign hackers targeting U.S. interests.

stories.title: Russians attack Kharkiv with drones, injuring two people
stories.summary: Two men were injured in a Russian drone strike on the Saltivskyi district of Kharkiv, Ukraine.

stories.title: Malaysia looks for ‘further clarifications’ from Norway after Naval Strike Missile order falters
stories.summary: Malaysia is seeking further clarifications from Norway after its order for Kongsberg Naval Strike Missiles encountered difficulties. The two countries signed a deal in 2018 to supply NSM weapons for six new Malaysian Littoral Combat Ships.

stories.title: Ultraconservative Vitaly Milonov Wants Your Kids to Jam Out to Whitney Houston
stories.summary: Russian State Duma lawmaker Vitaly Milonov, known for his anti-LGBTQ+ and anti-Western positions, has proposed that Russian children listen to music by Whitney Houston.

stories.title: 800 mobile shelters installed to expand Ukraine’s rail protection system amid sustained attacks
stories.summary: Ukraine's national rail operator Ukrzaliznytsia is deploying more than 800 modular mobile shelters across the country to protect rail passengers and staff amid sustained Russian attacks on infrastructure.

stories.title: Indigenous actor sues James Cameron for ‘stealing’ her facial features for Avatar character
stories.summary: Actor Q'orianka Kilcher filed a lawsuit against director James Cameron and the Walt Disney Company, alleging Cameron based the Avatar character Neytiri on her facial features without permission after seeing her in a 2005 advertisement for the film The New World.

stories.title: Indiana shows Republicans have two choices: align with Trump or get ousted
stories.summary: Primary voters in Indiana ousted five of seven Republican state senators who had defied President Trump's demands to redraw congressional district maps. The results underscore Trump's continuing influence within the Republican Party despite his declining broader popularity.

stories.title: Iran war possibly motivated Trump dinner shooting suspect, US intel report finds
stories.summary: A US intelligence report found that shooting suspect Cole Allen's social media posts indicated multiple grievances, including opposition to the war in Iran, Trump's immigration policies, Elon Musk, and Russia's invasion of Ukraine, which may have motivated the attack on a Trump dinner.

stories.title: Armenian Quarter residents descend from genocide survivors, bishop says ahead of exclusive tours
stories.summary: A bishop in Jerusalem's Armenian Quarter noted that residents descend from Armenian Genocide survivors, ahead of exclusive tours highlighting the community's nearly two-millennia-long presence in the Old City.

stories.title: Ukraine brings back six more children from temporarily occupied part of Kherson region
stories.summary: Ukrainian authorities repatriated six children from the temporarily occupied part of the Kherson region.

stories.title: El Salvador puts 486 MS-13 leaders on trial for 29,000 killings in process Bukele compares to Nuremberg
stories.summary: El Salvador began the largest trial in its history, prosecuting 486 alleged MS-13 leaders accused of ordering more than 29,000 killings between 2012 and 2022. President Nayib Bukele compared the proceedings to the Nuremberg trials; the case marks the first global application of command-responsibility doctrine to a gang structure.

stories.title: Why Ukraine’s EU membership is stuck—and it’s not just Zelenskyy
stories.summary: Ukraine's path to EU membership faces multiple obstacles, including internal EU disagreements on what to offer Kyiv, Ukraine's difficulty passing required legislative reforms, and outdated EU accession rules not designed for current geopolitical realities.

stories.title: Pussy Riot protest at Venice Biennale forces Russian pavilion to briefly close
stories.summary: Activist group Pussy Riot staged a protest at the Venice Biennale, forcing the temporary closure of the Russian pavilion. Demonstrators wearing pink balaclavas lit flares and chanted slogans opposing Russia's inclusion in the international arts festival.

stories.title: UN demands Israel ‘immediately’ release Gaza flotilla activists
stories.summary: The United Nations demanded that Israel immediately release Gaza flotilla activists. Spanish national Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian Thiago Avila are being held in a prison in Ashkelon, Israel.

stories.title: Lebanon: Israeli strikes kill four in Bekaa despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Those killed by Israel's strikes on the eastern Bekaa valley include two women and an elderly man, as Israeli forces continue to breach the ceasefire.

stories.title: Could Spain’s tough line on Israel be contagious across Europe?
stories.summary: Under Pedro Sánchez, Spain has moved beyond rhetoric on Israel’s crimes, but can it push the rest of Europe to follow suit? writes Luciano Zaccara.

stories.title: Prosecutors indict Bat Yam daycare workers over alleged assault of 14 toddlers
stories.summary: The defendants allegedly grabbed the children forcefully, dragged them by one arm, threw them onto mattresses, chairs, changing tables, or cribs; slapped them; pinched them; hit them.

stories.title: NATO must spend 5% of GDP on defence by 2030, Poland says
stories.summary: Poland's defence minister urged all NATO member countries to reach the alliance's target of spending 5 percent of GDP on defence by 2030, five years ahead of the official deadline. Speaking in Warsaw, he warned of the risks of delayed rearmament.

stories.title: Canadian Jewish groups urge terror designation for Palestine Action, warn about radical ideology
stories.summary: B'nai Brith Canada warned law enforcement and officials in a press statement that Palestine Action was "inciting its followers to commit criminal acts in furtherance of its radical ideology."

stories.title: Israel military issues evacuation warning for dozen villages in south Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military issued evacuation warnings for a dozen villages in southern Lebanon. Despite an existing ceasefire agreement, Israeli forces and Hezbollah have continued to exchange fire on a daily basis.

stories.title: Lebanese newspaper files complaint in France over remarks on killed journalist
stories.summary:

stories.title: French professor investigated for awarding himself fake prize
stories.summary: A French professor is under investigation for allegedly creating a fictitious academic prize and then awarding it to himself. He has been suspended from his university pending the inquiry.

stories.title: Summer-like temperatures of up to +30°C forecast for Thursday, with rain and thunderstorms in western regions of Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian forecasters predicted summer-like temperatures reaching 30°C across much of Ukraine on Thursday, May 7, with short-term rain and thunderstorms expected only in western regions.

stories.title: France moves carrier into Red Sea ahead of potential Hormuz mission
stories.summary: France is deploying its aircraft carrier to the Red Sea as a precursor to a potential mission to secure the Strait of Hormuz. President Emmanuel Macron stated that any multinational effort to protect the strait would only proceed once the most intense phase of the regional conflict subsides.

stories.title: Kash Patel says FBI used AI to stop US school shootings, claims it stopped attack in North Carolina
stories.summary: Speaking to American conservative television presenter Sean Hannity on his podcast, Patel said that AI had never been used by the bureau before.

stories.title: Trainline says Middle East tensions hitting European rail bookings
stories.summary: UK-based rail ticketing company Trainline reported profits of £122 million but warned that geopolitical tensions between the U.S. and Iran in the Middle East are reducing inbound air traffic to Europe, negatively affecting European rail bookings from foreign visitors.

stories.title: Ugandan lawmakers pass scaled-back sovereignty law after central bank warning
stories.summary: Uganda's parliament passed a scaled-back sovereignty law aimed at curbing alleged foreign influence, after reducing proposed restrictions on foreign funding. The central bank governor had warned that the original version of the legislation risked causing "economic disaster."

stories.title: 'Significant threat to local ecosystem: Israel's war on Lebanon generated 16 million tons of rubble'
stories.summary: An analysis by Antoine Kallab of the American University of Beirut estimates that Israel's military operations in Lebanon generated approximately 16 million tons of rubble containing heavy metals and toxic materials. The debris poses a significant long-term threat to local ecosystems and public health.

stories.title: Take off in formation, fly low, navigate by terrain—Ukraine’s F-16 trainees finished a UK course Russia helped design
stories.summary: Ukrainian F-16 trainees completed a training course in the United Kingdom where RAF instructors incorporated lessons from electronic jamming conditions on the front line. Instructors noted the trainees demonstrated strong aircraft handling from their first sorties.

stories.title: Syrian forces detain Uzbek fighters in security sweep
stories.summary: Syrian security forces detained Uzbek fighters during a security sweep in northwestern Syria after a dispute involving one of the fighters led to protests outside a government security facility.

stories.title: UN demands Israel immediately releases flotilla activists
stories.summary: The United Nations called on Israel to immediately release two activists detained after their flotilla, bound for Gaza, was seized by Israeli forces.

stories.title: It’s not cricket: Pakistan athletes allowed in India for multilateral sport
stories.summary: India's government announced it will permit Pakistani athletes to enter the country for multilateral sporting events while maintaining its existing ban on bilateral competitions, including cricket.

stories.title: Russia is waging a long war against the West. Switzerland’s spies say it is escalating.
stories.summary: Switzerland's annual intelligence report identified Russia as the biggest threat to Europe, aligning with assessments from the Netherlands, Germany, Denmark, and Estonia regarding Moscow's preparations for a possible conflict with NATO.

stories.title: Far-right agitator arrested for allegedly spitting on ex-PM Olmert
stories.summary: Far-right activist Eliran Simantov was arrested in Israel for allegedly spitting on former Prime Minister Ehud Olmert. A judge released him, acknowledging the crime likely occurred but ruling it was not severe enough to warrant continued detention.

stories.title: Israel army chief sees ‘historic opportunity’ to reshape region
stories.summary: Israeli army chief of staff Eyal Zamir visited southern Lebanon and stated that operations against Hezbollah were continuing. He claimed more than 2,000 Hezbollah members had been killed since operations began in early March, describing the situation as a historic opportunity to reshape the region.

stories.title: PM said to ask Haredim to again shelve draft exemption bill — this time until after election
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has reportedly asked ultra-Orthodox political leaders to again delay a bill that would exempt yeshiva students from IDF military service, this time until after the next election. Senior Haredi officials gave conflicting accounts of the request.

stories.title: UK's hard-right Reform eyes huge new gains in local elections
stories.summary: The right-wing populist Reform UK party is set to make gains in the UK's local elections this week, with a campaign focused on migration.

stories.title: Exclusive: Qatar PM says chances 'high' on US-Iran breakthrough
stories.summary: In exclusive comments to The New Arab, Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani said there was "positive progress" in US-Iran contacts

stories.title: Closing the autism diagnosis gap in Israel’s ultra-Orthodox, Arab communities - opinion
stories.summary: Early diagnosis of autism ensures that every child, in every community in Israel, has an equal start to life.

stories.title: Zelensky awards title of Hero of Ukraine to seven servicemen, three of them posthumously
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky awarded the title of Hero of Ukraine to seven members of the armed forces, three of whom received the honor posthumously.

stories.title: 100+ foreigners, $56,000 in cash, 10 raids — Kyiv police bust foreigner-legalization racket
stories.summary: Kyiv police have charged two men with legalizing over 100 foreigners — including two Russian citizens — through fictitious companies and a fake charitable fund, with fees up to $6,000.

stories.title: Amputee football grows in Rwanda, fostering unity and resilience
stories.summary: Amputee football is expanding in Rwanda, helping survivors of conflict and disability overcome social stigma and build community trust and a sense of belonging.

stories.title: China asks Ukraine to treat Chinese POWs well, but doesn’t say if it wants them back
stories.summary: Chinese MFA spokesman invoked international law on the two Chinese citizens captured fighting for Russia, while sidestepping the question of whether China is acting to repatriate them.

stories.title: US approves potential sale of JDAM-ER joint direct attack munitions to Ukraine
stories.summary: The US State Department has approved a potential $373.6 mn sale of 1,532 JDAM-ER kits to Ukraine. Boeing will serve as the principal contractor for the deal.

stories.title: Somalia: Somali PM Replaces Information Minister
stories.summary: Somalia's Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre dismissed Information Minister Daud Aweis and appointed lawmaker Abdifatah Qasim Mahmoud as his replacement.

stories.title: Another day, another pivot as Trump flails in an Iran trap of his own making
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump's shifting approach to Iran has included escalating military rhetoric followed by a humanitarian initiative called "Project Freedom" aimed at freeing trapped ships in the Gulf. Tehran derided the latest U.S. proposal as a "wishlist," while an estimated 5,000 people have died in the conflict.

stories.title: Regional leader of Spain's Canary Islands rejects hantavirus-hit cruise docking there
stories.summary: The regional leader of Spain's Canary Islands, Fernando Clavijo, said his government opposes allowing the hantavirus-stricken luxury cruise ship to dock on the archipelago. The vessel has been affected by a deadly hantavirus outbreak.

stories.title: CMA CGM container ship hit in Strait of Hormuz, injuring crew
stories.summary: The CMA CGM container ship San Antonio was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, resulting in crew injuries. No further details on the attackers or the extent of damage were immediately provided.

stories.title: Somalia: Somalia PM, WFP Discuss Lasting Solutions to Food Insecurity
stories.summary: Somali Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre met with senior World Food Programme officials in Mogadishu to discuss long-term solutions to food insecurity, drought, and recurrent climate shocks affecting the country.

stories.title: Somalia: Somali Forces Kill 13 Al-Shabaab Fighters in Central Operation
stories.summary: Somali National Army forces and local militia fighters killed at least 13 Al-Shabaab members, including senior commanders, during an operation in the Boorey area near Bahdo in the central Mudug region.

stories.title: Leonardo reports 31% surge in new orders in Q1 as former CEO departs
stories.summary: The defense boss highlighted that revenues reached €4.5 billion in the first three months of the year — a 7 percent increase over 2025 —  with a total backlog reaching €57 billion.

stories.title: Two IDF soldiers moderately, lightly wounded, military evacuates several southern Lebanese villages
stories.summary: Two Israeli soldiers were wounded in southern Lebanon after explosive drones detonated near their position. The IDF subsequently evacuated several southern Lebanese villages in response to the attack.

stories.title: Nigeria: EFCC Arraigns Firm for Illegal Rebroadcast of Multichoice's Contents
stories.summary: Nigeria's Economic and Financial Crimes Commission arraigned a firm for the illegal rebroadcast of Multichoice's content. The arraignment is the latest development in a case that had been under investigation for some time.

stories.title: Germany raids suspected members of far-right youth groups
stories.summary: German authorities conducted raids targeting suspected members of far-right youth groups, deploying over 600 federal and state police officers. No arrests were made during the operation.

stories.title: Trump tells Iran to accept deal to end the war or face new wave of US bombing
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump issued an ultimatum to Iran, threatening a new wave of intensified bombing if Tehran does not accept a deal to end the Middle East conflict. The statement came despite US claims of progress in stalled negotiations with Iran.

stories.title: American strategic bases in Europe ‘not yet’ in danger: German president

stories.title: State payments to oil exporters consume nearly half of Russia’s windfall from high prices, data show
stories.summary: Russia's Finance Ministry released April oil and gas revenue data reflecting taxes paid by exporters for March, the first full month during the U.S.-Israeli conflict with Iran, when oil prices spiked. The data showed state payments to oil exporters consumed nearly half the windfall revenue.

stories.title: Zelensky awards another 484 servicemen, 138 of them posthumously
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky bestowed state awards on 484 Ukrainian service members, 138 of whom were honored posthumously for their service in defense of Ukraine.

stories.title: Egypt and Lebanon move to revive Arab Gas Pipeline project
stories.summary: Egypt and Lebanon signed an agreement to rehabilitate Lebanon's gas infrastructure and revive a regional pipeline project to ease the electricity crisis.

stories.title: Rwanda: Experts Warn Decline in Hand Hygiene May Increase Infection Risks
stories.summary: Public health experts in Rwanda warned that a decline in hand hygiene practices may increase infection risks. Dr. Eric Niyongira, a public health practitioner, noted that people exchange microorganisms through routine interactions without realizing it.

stories.title: Rwanda: African Attorneys-General Meet in Kigali Over Policies, Partnerships
stories.summary: Rwanda hosted the second Attorneys-General Public-Private Accelerating Collaboration and Transformation (AG PACT) Forum in Kigali. The event brought together senior legal and policy leaders from across Africa to discuss how public-private partnerships can drive sustainable development.

stories.title: Leningrad Region’s Kirishi Oil Refinery Halts Operations After Drone Strike – Reuters
stories.summary: The Kirishi Oil Refinery in Russia's Leningrad Region halted operations after a drone strike damaged three of its four crude distillation units and several secondary processing units, according to industry sources cited by Reuters.

stories.title: India 'funds organisations behind terror activities in Pakistan': Bilawal Bhutto Zardari
stories.summary: In an interview with FRANCE 24, Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, head of the Pakistan People's Party, discussed the ongoing tensions between India and Pakistan. One year ago, after a five-day war between the t

stories.title: Eastern Poland forest fire kills pilot, scorches over 200ha
stories.summary: A firefighting plane crashed while battling a major forest fire in eastern Poland's protected Solska Forest, killing the pilot. The blaze scorched over 200 hectares of the protected area.

stories.title: Flamboyant US entrepreneur and CNN founder Ted Turner dead at 87
stories.summary: Ted Turner, the flamboyant US entrepreneur who transformed television news with the creation of CNN in 1980, has died at the age of 87, the network said Wednesday.

stories.title: Syrian forces detain Uzbek fighters in Idlib security sweep
stories.summary: The detention of several Uzbek fighters in Idlib came after a dispute involving one of the fighters escalated into protests outside a government facility.

stories.title: Biogas company in DRC aims to cut bills, deforestation and pollution
stories.summary: A biogas company in the Democratic Republic of Congo is promoting biogas as an alternative household energy source. Promoters say the initiative helps reduce charcoal costs, address frequent power outages, and limit indoor air pollution from traditional fuels.

stories.title: Norwegian government attacked over decision to reopen North Sea gasfields
stories.summary: The Norwegian government approved the reopening of three North Sea gasfields closed nearly three decades ago and authorized exploration in 70 new areas across the North Sea, Barents Sea, and Norwegian Sea. The decision, driven by energy shortages linked to the Middle East conflict, drew sharp criticism from fossil fuel opponents.

stories.summary: Chief Justice of Pakistan Yahya Afridi ruled that following the 27th Constitutional Amendment, the Supreme Court and the Federal Constitutional Court operate as coordinate courts with clearly demarcated jurisdictions. The ruling was issued in a 13-page order on petitions stemming from a February 2020 Peshawar High Court judgment.

stories.summary: Three patients with suspected hantavirus infections were being evacuated from a cruise ship to the Netherlands on Wednesday, the U.N. health agency said, as the vessel at the center of a deadly outbre

stories.summary: The Army said the AMPV 30 is not a replacement option for the XM30 program, but an executive said the vehicle “fits a different envelope.”

stories.title: Double murder brings total of Israeli Arabs killed since beginning of year to over 100
stories.summary: Two murders brought the number of Israeli Arabs killed by violent crime since the start of the year to over 100. President Isaac Herzog called the high murder rate an "ugly stain" on Israeli society.

stories.title: European Congress of Ukrainians calls on EU to strengthen support for Ukraine's European future
stories.summary: The European Congress of Ukrainians, along with Ukrainian diaspora communities, issued an appeal to European leaders and EU institutions urging stronger support for Ukraine's path toward European integration.

stories.summary: A French appeals court has ordered the reopening of an investigation into Agathe Habyarimana, Rwanda's former first lady, for alleged complicity in the 1994 Rwandan genocide.

stories.summary: Sheikh Muhammad Idris was assassinated on Tuesday, 5 May, near his home in the town of Charsadda, close to Peshawar, in northwest Pakistan.

stories.title: US and Iran closing in on agreement to end war, sources say
stories.summary: U.S. and Iranian officials are reportedly closing in on an agreement to end the ongoing war, according to sources. President Trump stated the conflict could end if "Iran agrees to give what has been agreed to."

stories.title: Breathe Pakistan: Minister Musadik Malik calls for investing in youth-led climate projects
stories.summary: Pakistan's Minister Musadik Malik called for investment in youth-led climate projects at the second Breathe Pakistan International Climate Change Conference in Islamabad. Despite minimal global emissions, Pakistan remains among the world's most climate-vulnerable nations.

stories.title: Who is Narges Mohammadi, Iranian Nobel laureate at risk of dying in custody?
stories.summary: Jailed Iranian Nobel Peace Prize winner Narges Mohammadi could die in prison unless she is urgently given proper health care after suffering two suspected heart attacks in recent weeks.

stories.title: Four killed in post-election violence in India’s West Bengal
stories.summary: Unrest grips the key eastern state after Modi's Hindu nationalist BJP wins the state election for the first time.

stories.title: ‘Your craft is obsolete’: WiseTech staff in limbo as AI touted as better than humans
stories.summary: Australian logistics software company WiseTech, which announced 7,000 job cuts in February including 2,000 due to AI advances, has left staff waiting nearly three months for confirmation of which roles will be eliminated. The company's founder claimed an AI agent could learn a human's job in 15 minutes.

stories.title: Coalition considers plan to slash net overseas immigration by nearly half its current rate, leaked documents reveal
stories.summary: Australia's Coalition opposition is considering plans to reduce annual net overseas immigration to 150,000–200,000, according to leaked internal documents. The policy roadmap is part of a broader election platform being prepared under opposition leader Angus Taylor.

stories.title: Norway provides Ukraine with over $250 million through PURL program
stories.summary: Norway announced on May 6 that it would provide Ukraine with approximately $259 million (2.8 billion Norwegian krone) through the NATO Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List (PURL) program for the procurement of U.S. weapons.

stories.title: Gaza ceasefire in Cairo talks stall as Israel eyes return to war
stories.summary: Deadlock over Hamas disarmament and shifting ceasefire terms fuels warnings that Israel may resume full-scale military operations in the besieged territory.

stories.title: RBC reports Russia’s Digital Development Ministry plans to cut 15% of staff, with 2 deputy ministers possibly leaving
stories.summary: Russia's Digital Development Ministry plans to cut approximately 15% of its staff as part of an internal reorganization, with two deputy ministers potentially departing, according to a report by the Russian outlet RBC on May 6.

stories.title: ADL says antisemitic incidents dropped by a third in 2025, but assaults reached record levels
stories.summary: The Anti-Defamation League reported that antisemitic incidents in the United States dropped by one-third in 2025, but physical assaults against Jewish individuals reached record levels during the same period.

stories.title: TPLF move to restore leadership raises tensions in Ethiopia’s Tigray
stories.summary: In Ethiopia's Tigray region, political parties and analysts are challenging the legality of the Tigray People's Liberation Front leader serving as head of the local parliament, raising political tensions.

stories.title: Going green with solar
stories.summary: Pakistan is experiencing a rapid, largely grassroots solar energy transition, with households, farmers, and factories installing rooftop panels and solar-powered tubewells across the country. The shift is driven by catastrophic climate events, record heatwaves, and an electricity tariff crisis, positioning solar power as both an economic escape and a contributor to Pakistan's climate goals.

stories.title: Exclusive: Iran-US talks not yet at stage for agreement
stories.summary: Iranian sources say ongoing talks with Washington mediated by Pakistan have made progress but remain far from a final agreement.

stories.title: Army wants to field all 11 divisions NGC2 capabilities in five-year window
stories.summary: I Corps, headquartered in the Pacific, will be the next focus for NGC2 next year.

stories.title: Ukraine says Russia violated ceasefire initiated by Kyiv
stories.summary: Ukraine accused Russia of violating a unilateral ceasefire initiated by President Volodymyr Zelenskiy at midnight on Tuesday. Ukrainian officials reported one person killed and three wounded in the country's northern and eastern regions.

stories.title: Zelensky says Russia is violating Ukraine’s unilateral ceasefire and warns Kyiv may respond in kind during Moscow parade
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of violating Kyiv's unilateral ceasefire and warned that Ukraine might respond with strikes during Moscow's Victory Day parade.

stories.title: Israeli army attacks West Bank Christians marking St George Day
stories.summary: Israeli forces attacked Palestinian Christians celebrating the Feast of St. George in the town of Al-Khader, south of Bethlehem, in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Syria’s crackdown on Hezbollah shows Damascus's commitment to security - analysis
stories.summary: Syrian authorities are cracking down on Hezbollah's presence in the country, signaling Damascus's commitment to security. Hezbollah entered Syria in large numbers around 2012–2013 via Qusayr, but its role has diminished since the fall of the Assad regime.

stories.title: Report: Next round of Israel-Lebanon talks set for next week
stories.summary: A third round of direct Lebanon-Israel talks is scheduled for next week at the U.S. State Department in Washington, according to an official Lebanese source cited by Anadolu Agency. Israeli attacks continue across southern Lebanon despite a U.S.-brokered truce extension in late April.

stories.summary:

stories.title: Nigerian Afrobeats star Tiwa Savage nurtures Africa's musical talent
stories.summary: Nigerian Afrobeats artist Tiwa Savage hosted workshops for over 100 aspiring musicians in collaboration with the Berklee College of Music in the United States.

stories.title: Russian court sentences former cadet school dishwasher to 19 years for recruiting student into ‘Freedom of Russia Legion’
stories.summary: A Russian military court sentenced Alexandra Zhitenko, a former dishwasher at an Investigative Committee cadet school, to 19 years in prison and an 800,000-ruble fine for allegedly recruiting students into the Freedom of Russia Legion, which Moscow has designated a terrorist organization.

stories.title: Hong Kong college’s finance director arrested over HK$770,000 embezzlement
stories.summary: The finance director of Hong Kong's Chu Hai College was arrested on suspicion of embezzling approximately HK$770,000. The college president reported the case after the Bank of China flagged three unusual transactions to the suspect's personal account.

stories.title: Satellite imagery reveals Flamingo missile damage at Russian plant making Shahed navigation antennas

stories.title: Iranian foreign ministry reviewing US proposal, says it will convey views to Pakistan
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry said it is reviewing a U.S. proposal to end the regional war and will communicate its position to Pakistan, which is mediating discussions between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Myanmar: What's behind Suu Kyi's transfer to house arrest?
stories.summary: Myanmar's military transferred ousted leader Aung San Suu Kyi from prison to house arrest. The move has been cautiously welcomed internationally, but analysts suggest the junta may be seeking to bolster its legitimacy amid an ongoing civil war.

stories.title: CNN founder Ted Turner dead at 87
stories.summary: No cause of death disclosed for media mogul who revolutionised news broadcasting.

stories.title: Zoria Publishing House premises in Dnipro damaged by Russian attack
stories.summary: The production facilities of the Zoria Publishing House in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro were damaged by a blast wave from a Russian strike carried out on May 5.

stories.title: Hong Kong teen lured 4 victims for gang to rob and blackmail, court hears
stories.summary: A 23-year-old woman, Hau Yan-ki, is on trial at Hong Kong's High Court for allegedly luring four victims to a remote area in November 2020, where her gang robbed them, beat them, and took nude photos to extort payments.

stories.title: Vietnam President To Lam accorded ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan on his maiden visit to India
stories.summary: Vietnamese President To Lam received a ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi during his first official visit to India. The trip coincides with the 10th anniversary of the comprehensive strategic partnership between India and Vietnam.

stories.title: Over 400 officials urge EU to act over E1 settlement project
stories.summary: Over 400 officials signed an open letter urging the European Union to impose sanctions, including visa bans, against individuals involved in Israel's E1 settlement project between Jerusalem and the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: US wants ‘concrete actions’ on Iran from next Iraqi PM
stories.summary: The United States told Iraq that its next prime minister must take concrete actions to address Iranian influence, specifically the overlap between pro-Iran armed groups and the Iraqi state.

stories.title: Israel uproots thousands of grapevines in Hebron to expand settler road
stories.summary: Israeli forces bulldozed thousands of grapevines in Hebron in the occupied West Bank to expand a road serving settlers. Palestinians say the destruction targets farmland central to local livelihoods in an effort to displace farmers.

stories.title: Historic Lebanon-Israel talks: A no-win situation?
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon recently held talks, but experts and residents of southern Lebanon express little optimism for a meaningful resolution to the conflict.

stories.title: French aircraft carrier group prepares for mission in Hormuz Strait
stories.summary: The French Charles de Gaulle aircraft carrier group crossed the Suez Canal and is heading into the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, preparing for a joint French-British mission to navigate vessels through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Iraq’s Continuing Struggle for Sovereignty
stories.summary: Amid a regional war, political drama and drone strikes are testing Baghdad’s power.

stories.title: Tanzania: Met Gala 2026 Showcases Rare Tanzanite Necklace Worth U.S.$15m
stories.summary: At the 2026 Met Gala in New York, Indian billionaire Sudha Reddy wore a rare tanzanite necklace valued at over $15 million, drawing global attention to Tanzania's gemstone industry.

stories.title: Africa: Africa Forward Summit, Signalling a New Era of Africa-France Partnership
stories.summary: Kenya and France will co-host the inaugural Africa Forward Summit in Nairobi on May 11–12, 2026, nearly a decade after French President Emmanuel Macron's Ouagadougou speech that sought to reset France-Africa relations.

stories.title: Pro-Palestine group protests outside Israeli real estate event in New York
stories.summary: Demonstration against event featuring properties for sale in occupied West Bank is the second protest in six months.

stories.title: UN demands Israel release Gaza flotilla activists, investigate abuse claims
stories.summary: Israel must 'immediately and unconditionally' release Saif Abu Keshek and Thiago de Avila, rights office spokesman says.

stories.title: Bus and oil tanker collide in Indonesia, killing at least 16 people
stories.summary: A passenger bus and a fuel tanker collided head-on on the Trans-Sumatra Highway in South Sumatra province, Indonesia, killing at least 16 people and injuring four others.

stories.title: Crew rescued after cargo ship sinks off Greece, coast guard says
stories.summary: Greece rescued all nine crew members — eight Turkish nationals and one Azerbaijani — from a cargo ship that struck rocks and sank off the island of Andros early Wednesday, according to the Greek coast guard.

stories.summary: All cash and bullion held by Hungarian special services for two months are back on Ukrainian soil, the president confirmed on 6 May.

stories.title: London Jews celebrate Lag B’Omer amid fear and uncertainty over spate of attacks
stories.summary:

stories.title: Does China’s YJ-20 hypersonic sea-based missile give Beijing an edge over US carriers?
stories.summary: China's YJ-20, its first sea-based hypersonic anti-ship missile, has entered mass production and is designed for the Type 055 destroyer's vertical launch system. The missile's range and speed are intended to give China a strike advantage against rival surface combatants.

stories.title: Anti-Zionism in America and the shifting debate over support for Israel - opinion
stories.summary: A commentary examines anti-Zionism in the United States, arguing that the debate over Israel within the Democratic Party reflects deeper fractures in American political identity.

stories.title: Enemy attacks village in Kharkiv region with drone, three injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the village of Pysarivka in the Bohodukhiv district of Ukraine's Kharkiv region with a drone on Wednesday morning, injuring three people.

stories.title: Iran says it wants a 'comprehensive agreement' with U.S.
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi stated in Beijing that Iran seeks a comprehensive agreement with the United States and will protect its legitimate rights and interests in negotiations. Araqchi made the remarks after meeting with Chinese top diplomat Wang Yi, according to Iranian media.

stories.title: Tai Po fire: inspectors failed to anticipate firms’ deception, inquiry hears
stories.summary: A public inquiry into a deadly fire at a Tai Po residential estate in Hong Kong heard that government inspectors failed to detect engineering firms colluding to use substandard, flammable renovation materials, citing systemic defects in oversight.

stories.title: Trump says it is 'too early' for in-person talks with Iran
stories.summary: President Trump told The New York Post that it is "too early" for face-to-face talks with Iran, describing direct discussions as "too far off" despite reports of Washington and Tehran nearing a memorandum of understanding.

stories.title: South Africa: Finance Minister Warns Joburg Is in 'Severe Financial Distress' in Letter to Mayor Morero
stories.summary: South Africa's Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana warned that Johannesburg is in "severe financial distress" and ordered Mayor Morero to halt a budget-exceeding wage deal, citing potential harm to the national economy.

stories.title: Lockheed taps Skunk Works boss as new aeronautics chief
stories.summary: Greg Ulmer, who has led Lockheed’s aeronautics arm since 2021, is retiring. OJ Sanchez will take over in June.

stories.title: South Sudan: Civilians Starving in South Sudan's Conflict Areas
stories.summary: A new Human Rights Watch report documents severe food shortages affecting civilians in conflict-affected areas of South Sudan, highlighting the impact of fighting and restrictions on humanitarian aid.

stories.title: Gaza rebuild priced at $71 billion, with most homes and nearly all businesses destroyed

stories.title: Moscow Court Orders Seizure of Stake in Farming Giant Rusagro
stories.summary: A Moscow court ordered the seizure of a stake in Rusagro, a major Russian agricultural company. The firm's owner, Vadim Moshkovich, ranked 51st on Forbes' Russian wealth list, was arrested in March 2025 on fraud and bribery charges.

stories.title: Wang Fuk Court administrator schedules talks after residents’ legal threats
stories.summary: The government-appointed administrator of Wang Fuk Court in Hong Kong scheduled two online meetings with displaced residents after 240 flat owners threatened legal action. Hop On Management Company will hold the Zoom sessions following a deadly fire that devastated the estate last November.

stories.title: Araghchi in Beijing: How China could shape the direction of the US-Iran war
stories.summary: Analysts say shared US and Chinese interests in reopening the Strait of Hormuz could create a path towards peace.

stories.title: ‘Defeated by conspiracy’: West Bengal chief minister refuses to resign after election loss
stories.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee refused to resign after her Trinamool Congress party lost state elections to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's BJP, ending 15 years in power. Banerjee alleged the election was "forcefully captured" by Modi's party.

stories.title: Iran 'slopaganda': We tried recreating viral Lego-style AI videos
stories.summary: After Donald Trump announced a pause to the US operation in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's online propaganda machine was quick to declare victory. Explosive Media, one of the groups behind Lego-style vi

stories.title: Court rejects appeal by Gaza flotilla activists, keeps them in detention until Sunday
stories.summary: An Israeli court rejected an appeal filed by legal group Adalah on behalf of Gaza flotilla activists Thiago Ávila and Saif Abu Keshek, keeping them in detention until Sunday. A further hearing was scheduled to address the case.

stories.title: Russian drone hits kindergarten in Ukraine
stories.summary: A Russian drone strike has hit a kindergarten in Ukraine’s Sumy region.

stories.title: Here’s what’s behind the US Army’s $2.1B R&D funding increase
stories.summary: The U.S. Army's fiscal year budget request of $253 billion includes a proposed 12.9% increase in research and development spending, amounting to roughly $2.1 billion in additional R&D funding.

stories.title: Trump pauses Hormuz plan 50 hours after he announced it - what happened?
stories.summary: The US president pauses the military operation to get ships through the Strait of Hormuz two days after he announced it.

stories.title: Zelensky: Russian army violates ceasefire 1,820 times
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky reported that as of 10 a.m. Wednesday, Russian forces had committed 1,820 ceasefire violations, including shelling, assault attempts, airstrikes, and drone attacks, despite Ukraine's unilateral ceasefire declaration.

stories.title: Burkina Faso junta dissolves over 200 associations
stories.summary: Burkina Faso's military government ordered the dissolution of approximately 200 associations on Tuesday, continuing a pattern of restrictions on civic organizations in the West African country.

stories.title: Fire breaks out in multi-storey building in Tehran
stories.summary: A fire broke out in a multi-storey commercial building in Andisheh, in Iran's Tehran province, killing at least eight people and injuring 41 others, according to Iranian state media.

stories.title: Iran war may have motivated would-be Trump assassin, US intelligence report finds
stories.summary: A U.S. intelligence report suggests the war with Iran may have motivated Cole Tomas Allen, the suspect in the attempted attack on President Trump. Prosecutors allege Allen wanted to "fight back" against government policies he found objectionable.

stories.title: Elderly man rescued from rubble after Israeli strike on Lebanon
stories.summary: An 80-year-old man has been pulled out from under the rubble of his house in the south.

stories.title: 4 killed in post-poll unrest in India's West Bengal
stories.summary: Four people were killed in political violence in India's West Bengal state following the Bharatiya Janata Party's first-ever electoral victory there, winning 206 of 294 assembly seats. The unrest followed the defeat of longtime Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee's party.

stories.title: UK local elections: What does it mean to be Scottish today?
stories.summary: Voters across the United Kingdom head to polls on May 7 for local elections in England and devolved parliament elections in Scotland and Wales. Polls predict the ruling Labour Party may suffer its worst results in decades, with Reform UK and the Greens expected to gain.

stories.title: Pakistan's response to any future miscalculation will be more intense, warns Asif in Marka-i-Haq message
stories.summary: Pakistan's Defence Minister Khawaja Asif warned in a Marka-i-Haq anniversary message that any future military miscalculation would be met with a more intense response. The statement marked the anniversary of the 2025 military escalation with India that ended with a May 10 ceasefire.

stories.title: US and Iran finalising 14-point memorandum to end war: Report
stories.summary: The U.S. and Iran are reportedly close to finalizing a 14-point, one-page memorandum to end the war, with Pakistan mediating. The deal would address the Strait of Hormuz transit, U.S. sanctions relief, and other issues.

stories.title: Trump’s commerce chief Lutnick to face Epstein grilling in closed-door interview – US politics live
stories.summary: U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is set to face questioning about his ties to Jeffrey Epstein in a closed-door interview. Lutnick previously acknowledged visiting Epstein's island with his family in 2012 despite earlier claiming he severed ties in 2005.

stories.title: Russian man sets himself on fire at war memorial on anniversary of Ukraine invasion, authorities suppress news of it
stories.summary: A 37-year-old Kaliningrad resident, Alexander Okunev, set himself on fire at the 1,200 Guardsmen memorial on February 24, 2025, the third anniversary of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Russian authorities suppressed news of the protest, according to investigations by iStories, Delfi Estonia, and Lithuanian broadcaster LRT.

stories.title: Tunisia temporarily bans prominent rights group
stories.summary: Tunisian authorities temporarily banned the local branch of Avocats Sans Frontières, an international legal rights NGO. The move follows a similar measure against another leading civil society group days earlier.

stories.title: Two hikers injured in US bear attack on Yellowstone trail
stories.summary: Two hikers were injured in a bear attack on Monday on the Mystic Falls trail near Old Faithful in Yellowstone National Park. The National Park Service closed surrounding areas and is investigating the incident.

stories.title: US cancels visas for board of Costa Rica newspaper critical of Trump ally
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department cancelled tourist visas for more than half of the board members of Costa Rica's leading newspaper, La Nación. The paper has been critical of Costa Rican President Rodrigo Chaves, a Trump ally, and called the action an "indirect attack on press freedom."

stories.title: Living in the shadow of Israel's 'yellow line' in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel is entrenching its occupation of southern Lebanon behind a so-called 'yellow line,' with villages being systematically demolished and residents displaced from the area.

stories.title: Two women injured in Sumy after Russian strike on kindergarten
stories.summary: Two women were injured in the Ukrainian city of Sumy after Russian forces struck a kindergarten building with two drones.

stories.title: North Korea revises Constitution to drop references to unification of Korean Peninsula
stories.summary: North Korea revised its constitution to define its territory as bordering South Korea, effectively dropping all references to Korean Peninsula unification. The revised document also strengthens and codifies leader Kim Jong Un's nuclear role.

stories.title: Spanish PM urges Brussels protect ICC judges from US sanctions
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez urged the European Union to protect International Criminal Court judges and UN officials from U.S. sanctions related to investigations into the conflict in Gaza.

stories.title: If Iran does not agree to US deal, Trump says 'bombing starts'
stories.summary: President Trump stated on Truth Social that if Iran agrees to the proposed deal, the war and Hormuz blockade could end. He threatened that bombing would resume if Tehran does not comply with the terms.

stories.title: South Korea suspends review of Trump's call to participate in 'Project Freedom'
stories.summary: South Korea suspended its review of participation in the U.S.-led "Project Freedom" initiative after President Donald Trump placed the operation on hold.

stories.title: America needs next-gen solutions to counter modern air and missile threats
stories.summary: A sponsored article discusses the need for advanced sensing, communications, and interception technologies to defend the United States against evolving air and missile threats.

stories.title: Vietnam, India seek closer ties to hedge against dependence on superpowers
stories.summary: Vietnamese President To Lam arrived in New Delhi for a three-day visit, his first trip to India since taking office. The visit aims to deepen Vietnam-India ties as both nations seek to reduce dependence on superpowers and hedge against China amid maritime disputes.

stories.title: War in Ukraine: Russia attacks east and south Ukraine with over 100 drones
stories.summary: Russia launched over 100 drones against eastern and southern Ukraine, rejecting Kyiv's unilateral ceasefire. President Zelensky said Russia had chosen to continue fighting rather than halt hostilities and save lives.

stories.title: Pope Leo rejects claim he supports nuclear weapons after Trump tirade
stories.summary: Pope Leo rejected claims that he supports nuclear weapons after U.S. President Trump accused him of "endangering a lot of Catholics" over his stance on the Iran war. The first U.S.-born pontiff said those criticizing him need to speak the truth.

stories.title: UN demands Israel 'immediately' release Gaza flotilla activists
stories.summary: A UN spokesperson called on Israel to immediately release Gaza flotilla activists Saif Abu Keshek and Thiago Avila from detention, stating that their activism is not criminal.

stories.title: What happened to Trump’s ‘Project Freedom’?
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced 'Project Freedom,' a military operation to escort stranded ships through the Strait of Hormuz, but subsequently paused the initiative amid evolving diplomatic developments.

stories.title: Russia wanted a 9 May ceasefire. Kyiv announced one starting earlier. Russia killed a woman in a kindergarten, and hit 1,820 times
stories.summary: The Ukrainian Air Force reported intercepting or jamming 89 Russian drones during continued attacks that struck eight locations across Ukraine with nine drones, two ballistic missiles, and one air-launched missile. A woman was killed in a strike on a kindergarten.

stories.title: Russia is making military training a mandatory school subject in occupied Donbas. Kyiv asks the ICC to act
stories.summary: Russia plans to introduce mandatory military training, including "Cossack classes," in schools across occupied Donbas starting September 1. Ukraine's ombudsman has called the measure a crime against humanity and urged the International Criminal Court to intervene.

stories.title: Liechtenstein joins Special Tribunal for Crime of Aggression against Ukraine, says Sybiha
stories.summary: Liechtenstein has joined the expanded partial agreement to establish a Special Tribunal for the Crime of Aggression against Ukraine, as announced by Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha.

stories.title: Italy: Femen and Pussy Riot protest Russia’s return to Venice Biennale
stories.summary: Activists from Femen and Pussy Riot staged protests outside the Russian pavilion at the 2026 Venice Biennale press preview on Wednesday. The demonstrations marked Russia's return to the event since Moscow's 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: London police set up specialist Jewish protection team
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police announced a dedicated team of 100 officers, including counter-terrorism specialists, to protect Jewish communities following a series of anti-Semitic attacks, including a stabbing of two men. Commissioner Mark Rowley cited sustained threats from hostile state actors and extremists. A 35-year-old man was arrested after rocks were thrown at a Jewish community ambulance.

stories.title: Party boss of China’s emerging tech hub under  investigation for corruption
stories.summary: Fei Gaoyun, the Communist Party chief of Hefei, capital of China's Anhui province, has been placed under corruption investigation. China's top anti-corruption watchdog announced the probe, making the 54-year-old the latest senior official caught in President Xi Jinping's long-running campaign.

stories.title: US must be transparent about Israel's nuclear programme, Democrat lawmakers say
stories.summary: Thirty Democratic members of the U.S. House of Representatives sent a letter to Secretary of State Rubio urging Washington to end decades of ambiguity over Israel's nuclear weapons program and hold Israel to the same nonproliferation standards as other nations.

stories.title: Sudan recalls ambassador to Ethiopia amid rising tensions
stories.summary: Sudan recalled its ambassador to Ethiopia amid rising tensions between the two neighboring countries. No specific details on the immediate cause of the diplomatic escalation were provided.

stories.title: Reform-led Lancashire county council to quit refugee resettlement scheme
stories.summary: The Reform UK-led Lancashire county council announced plans to withdraw from the UK government's refugee resettlement scheme. Councillor Joshua Roberts made the announcement, which would make Lancashire the first local authority to leave the program.

stories.title: Israel kills several in Gaza, death toll rises to 72,619
stories.summary: The Palestinian Ministry of Health in Gaza reported that Israeli forces killed three more people over the past 24 hours, raising the official death toll to 72,619, with thousands more missing and presumed dead.

stories.title: Iran says Strait of Hormuz passage to be ensured after US pauses operation
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy stated it would ensure safe transit through the Strait of Hormuz, announcing that new procedures would be implemented following the U.S. pause of its escort operation.

stories.title: More charges filed against WH correspondents' dinner attacker
stories.summary: Cole Tomas Allen, accused of targeting President Trump at the White House Correspondents' Dinner, faces additional charges for allegedly firing at a Secret Service officer during the incident.

stories.title: What is the FDD, the pro-Israel think tank shaping Trump’s Iran policy?
stories.summary: The Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD), a Washington-based pro-Israel think tank, has reportedly influenced the Trump administration's Iran policy, with its talking points on the U.S.-Israel military campaign against Iran being adopted by senior officials.

stories.title: Hong Kong pledges deeper ties with Uzbekistan as China signs bilateral agreements
stories.summary: Hong Kong Chief Executive John Lee met with Uzbek Prime Minister Abdulla Aripov to strengthen trade ties. China and Uzbekistan signed 15 bilateral agreements covering infrastructure, healthcare, and metal production during the visit.

stories.title: Pakistan again turns to spot LNG market, seeks bids for 2 cargoes
stories.summary: Pakistan LNG Limited issued urgent tenders for two spot LNG cargoes for mid-to-late May delivery as rising temperatures increase power demand. The purchase follows unmet expectations that the Middle East crisis would ease and the Strait of Hormuz would reopen.

stories.title: How India uses remote island to show strength against China
stories.summary: India is developing Great Nicobar Island, located at the edge of the Indian Ocean, into a strategic military and trade hub. New Delhi intends the facility to strengthen its position along key shipping routes and counter China's expanding regional influence.

stories.title: European Commission warns Italy that Russia’s Venice Biennale pavilion violates sanctions, Financial Times reports
stories.summary: The European Commission warned Italy's government and Venice Biennale organizers that opening Russia's national pavilion would violate EU sanctions by providing services to the Kremlin, the Financial Times reported.

stories.title: IRGC announces 'safe and stable' transit through Hormuz with the end of US threats
stories.summary: Iran's IRGC Navy announced that "safe and stable" transit through the Strait of Hormuz would be ensured now that U.S. threats are ending, stating new procedures would be implemented without specifying details.

stories.title: Russian oil revenue jumped 52%—Moral Rating Agency lays out how to make Russia poor
stories.summary: A report from the Moral Rating Agency indicated that Russian oil revenue increased by 52%. The agency argued that while some sanctions measures have been implemented, significant gaps remain in efforts to curtail Moscow's energy income.

stories.title: Airlines among companies using fuel surcharges to cover surge in costs, UK survey shows
stories.summary: A UK survey found that airlines and other service-sector companies are increasingly using fuel surcharges to cover soaring energy and wage costs. Businesses raised prices at the fastest rate in over three years in April, driven partly by Iran war-linked inflation.

stories.title: Protests erupt over Israeli settlement sales in New York
stories.summary: Hundreds of demonstrators gathered outside an Israeli real estate event in New York City to protest the sale of properties linked to settlements in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Amputee football empowers Rwandan women on and off the pitch
stories.summary: Amputee football is growing in Rwanda, providing women with opportunities for physical rehabilitation, social inclusion, and self-acceptance through organized competitive play.

stories.title: China’s chipmakers rush to embrace DeepSeek’s V4. Which names stand out?
stories.summary: Multiple Chinese semiconductor manufacturers are racing to adopt DeepSeek's latest large language model, V4, on domestic hardware platforms. Huawei was among the first to adapt the model, as geopolitical tensions over advanced chips drive efforts to localize AI capabilities.

stories.title: Gulf banks tightens digital oversight to curb Iran crypto flows
stories.summary: Gulf banks are tightening digital oversight to curb cryptocurrency flows linked to Iran. A Chainalysis report found illicit crypto flows grew 694 percent over the past year, reaching $154 billion in total value.

stories.title: Turkish exercise sees Libya’s rival forces train together for second time within weeks
stories.summary: Turkey hosted a military exercise bringing together forces from Libya's rival factions, marking the second such joint training event in recent weeks. The initiative falls under Ankara's "One Army, One Libya" policy aimed at unifying Libyan military structures.

stories.title: US and Iran nearing one-page war-ending agreement
stories.summary: The United States and Iran are reportedly nearing a one-page agreement to end the war. Key terms include mutual lifting of Strait of Hormuz blockades, US sanctions removal, and Iran committing to a 15-year moratorium on uranium enrichment.

stories.title: Varus distribution center damaged in Dnipro due to Russian attack; fatalities reported
stories.summary: A Russian attack on Dnipro on May 5 damaged the distribution center of the Varus grocery store chain, resulting in fatalities among staff members.

stories.title: Iran struck over 228 US structures, equipment across region: Report
stories.summary: The Washington Post reported, using satellite imagery, that Iranian air strikes have damaged or destroyed at least 228 U.S. structures and pieces of equipment across the region since the war began in late February.

stories.title: Climate shocks and Hormuz crisis deepen MENA food insecurity
stories.summary: The Middle East and North Africa region faces a deepening food security crisis as climate shocks and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz strain import-dependent supply chains across the area.

stories.title: US offers $10m reward for Iraq armed group leader Akram al-Kaabi
stories.summary: The U.S. government designated Iraqi militia leader Akram al-Kaabi as a terrorist and offered a $10 million reward for information leading to his capture or identification.

stories.title: China condemns Japan’s first overseas ‘offensive missile’ test since WWII
stories.summary: China condemned Japan's firing of a Type 88 surface-to-ship missile in the Philippines during the U.S.-led Balikatan 2026 joint drill. Beijing called it Japan's first overseas "offensive missile" test since World War II, warning it threatened regional stability.

stories.title: Cuba says US Secretary of State Rubio lying about oil blockade
stories.summary: Cuba's foreign minister accused U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio of lying about an oil blockade, saying Rubio is fully aware of the harm his policies are causing to the Cuban people.

stories.title: Lessons from the war: A call for strategic reckoning in West Asia
stories.summary: The Israeli-U.S. war on Iran has disrupted longstanding assumptions about security, deterrence, and regional stability in West Asia, prompting analysts to call for a strategic reassessment of the conflict's broader implications.

stories.title: Trump pauses 'Project Freedom' amid potential deal with Iran
stories.summary: President Trump paused 'Project Freedom,' the U.S. military operation escorting ships through the Strait of Hormuz, amid progress toward a potential deal with Iran. The U.S. said its blockade on Iran would remain in place.

stories.title: Coyote swam 2 miles to Alcatraz Island, going farther than scientists expected
stories.summary: A coyote that swam to Alcatraz Island in San Francisco Bay earlier this year actually traveled approximately 2 miles from Angel Island, farther than biologists initially estimated. Scientists had originally guessed it swam the shorter distance from San Francisco.

stories.title: Alaska’s 2025 mega tsunami highlights risk to cruise lines as glaciers retreat
stories.summary: A 481-metre mega tsunami struck Tracy Arm fjord in southeast Alaska in August last year, triggered by a massive rockslide near a glacier. Researchers warn the event highlights growing risks from coastal rockslides and glacier retreat linked to climate change.

stories.title: Reform and Plaid Cymru likely to benefit from polarisation of Welsh politics
stories.summary: Polls suggest Reform UK could win the most seats in the Welsh Senedd election under a new proportional voting system, though it is unlikely to form a government. The polarization of Welsh politics is also expected to benefit Plaid Cymru.

stories.title: Has the US accepted Iran’s demand to settle Hormuz first, nuclear later?
stories.summary: The United States paused its Strait of Hormuz escort operations after Pakistan-led mediation between Washington and Tehran gained traction, suggesting a possible shift toward addressing Hormuz transit issues before nuclear negotiations.

stories.title: Two Russian drones strike kindergarten in Sumy
stories.summary: Two Russian drones struck a kindergarten building in the central part of the city of Sumy, Ukraine. No immediate details on casualties were provided.

stories.title: Looking ahead to the UK's local elections with British politics expert Colm Murphy
stories.summary: UK local elections are being held on Thursday, with polls predicting significant losses for the ruling Labour Party. Reform UK and the Green Party are expected to make gains in English council races and devolved parliament elections in Scotland and Wales.

stories.title: Israel to supply Germany with jet fuel amid shortages caused by Iran war
stories.summary: Israel will supply Germany with jet fuel to help address shortages caused by the Iran war. Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar communicated the decision to Germany's Economic Affairs and Energy Minister during a visit to Berlin.

stories.title: Thailand vows strict tourist oversight after public sex incidents
stories.summary: Thailand announced it would tighten oversight of tourist behavior following multiple incidents of foreigners caught having sex in public. The prime minister's office warned that inappropriate conduct, including illicit drug use, would face prosecution.

stories.title: Israel kills four in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley
stories.summary: An Israeli strike on the town of Zellaya in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley killed four people, including two women and an elderly man. Several others, including a child, were injured in the attack.

stories.title: Was former synagogue targeted in London arson attack a mosque?
stories.summary: A former synagogue in east London was targeted in an arson attack. The building has been disused since 2020, and a Muslim community group had been making plans to purchase the property.

stories.title: Russia ignores Ukraine's unilateral ceasefire and attacks kindergarten
stories.summary: Russia continued attacks on Ukrainian targets despite Ukraine's unilateral ceasefire declaration, including a strike on a kindergarten. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated Russia had "spurned the ceasefire" and said Kyiv was considering its response.

stories.title: Cruise passengers tell of life on board ship stranded off Cape Verde after hantavirus outbreak
stories.summary: Passengers aboard the MV Hondius cruise ship remain stranded off Cape Verde following a hantavirus outbreak on board. While passengers report calm conditions, officials warn the disease may have spread, and the ship faces additional days at sea.

stories.title: Russia strikes Ukraine with over 100 drones as Zelensky’s ceasefire takes effect
stories.summary: Russia launched three missiles and 108 drones at Ukraine in the early hours of May 6, coinciding with the start of a ceasefire declared by President Zelensky, according to Ukraine's Air Force.

stories.title: Indonesian captain among crew held as Somali pirates strike again in Horn of Africa
stories.summary: Somali pirates seized the Palau-flagged tanker MT Honour 25 near the Horn of Africa, taking hostage its crew including Indonesian captain Ashari Samadikun. The captain sent a voice note to his wife warning of the impending attack on April 21.

stories.title: Met sets up specialist unit as antisemitic hate crimes in London hit two-year high
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police announced a specialist community protection team of 100 extra officers after antisemitic hate crimes in April reached a two-year high. The unit will combine neighbourhood policing with counter-terrorism capabilities to protect Jewish communities.

stories.title: Hantavirus: Latest updates on the ongoing outbreak aboard the MV Hondius
stories.summary: South Africa confirmed that the hantavirus strain identified from the MV Hondius cruise ship outbreak can spread among humans. The ship, marooned off Cape Verde with nearly 150 people aboard, was heading to Spain as investigations continued.

stories.title: Ukrainian Attack Kills 5 in Annexed Crimea as Kyiv Accuses Russia of Violating Its Ceasefire
stories.summary: Kremlin-installed officials reported that a Ukrainian attack on the town of Dzhankoi in northern Crimea killed five people on Tuesday night. Dzhankoi is home to a military airbase. Kyiv accused Russia of violating its declared ceasefire.

stories.title: China calls for a ‘complete’ end to war on Iran
stories.summary: China has called for a complete end to the war on Iran, signaling its diplomatic position on the ongoing conflict in the region.

stories.title: United Russia coaches deputies to justify internet restrictions by citing an ‘information-psychological war’
stories.summary: Russia's ruling United Russia party prepared a pamphlet coaching deputies and campaign workers on how to justify internet restrictions by framing them as responses to an "information-psychological war," according to Russian newspaper Kommersant.

stories.title: Can Hezbollah dominate the lower air battlefield against Israel?
stories.summary: An analysis examines Hezbollah's use of fibre-optic-guided drones against Israel, noting that while not a decisive weapon, the technology exposes vulnerabilities in Israel's low-altitude air defenses.

stories.title: New weapons charges filed against suspect in deadly shooting at Bondi Beach Hanukkah festival
stories.summary: Naveed Akram faces new weapons charges in addition to 59 existing counts, including murder, attempted murder, and committing a terrorist act, after two gunmen opened fire at a Hanukkah festival at Bondi Beach in Sydney in December 2025.

stories.title: United States: Los Angeles fire suspect had grudge against wealthy
stories.summary: Federal prosecutors said the man accused of deliberately setting the deadly Los Angeles fire last year harbored a grudge against the wealthy and admired Luigi Mangione, who is accused of fatally shooting a health insurance CEO.

stories.title: Enemy shelling causes new power outages in three regions, says Ukrenergo
stories.summary: Russian shelling on the morning of May 6 caused power outages affecting consumers in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhzhia, and Kharkiv regions, according to the national grid operator Ukrenergo.

stories.title: German police raid neo-Nazi criminal youth groups
stories.summary: German police conducted coordinated raids against neo-Nazi criminal youth groups, searching locations across 12 of the country's states. Prosecutors said the operations were concentrated mainly in eastern and southern Germany.

stories.title: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi meets Chinese counterpart Wang Yi in Beijing
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Chinese counterpart Wang Yi in Beijing during a one-day visit. The meeting took place a week before U.S. President Donald Trump's scheduled summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing on May 14–15.

stories.title: Iran Nobel winner Narges Mohammadi at risk of dying in custody
stories.summary: Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi is reportedly at risk of dying while in custody in Iran. Concerns about her health and treatment in prison have been raised by international observers.

stories.title: Local elections could hasten the exit of Britain’s embattled Prime Minister
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces political pressure ahead of local elections, with his popularity declining due to a weak economy and repeated questions about his judgment.

stories.title: Sick crew members evacuated from hantavirus cruise ship | First Thing
stories.summary: Three passengers have died and crew members have been medically evacuated from the cruise ship MV Hondius following a suspected hantavirus outbreak. Spain has granted permission for the vessel, carrying close to 150 people, to dock at the Canary Islands.

stories.title: US announces phased closure of Peshawar consulate, says operations will shift to Islamabad
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department announced the phased closure of its consulate in Peshawar, Pakistan, with operations transferring to the embassy in Islamabad. The decision was attributed to personnel safety and resource management. Diplomatic engagement with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province will continue from Islamabad.

stories.title: Breathe Pakistan: Ministry official says govt ‘very actively engaged’ with all provinces on climate change
stories.summary: The second Breathe Pakistan International Climate Change Conference, organized by DawnMedia, is being held in Islamabad. A ministry official stated the government is actively engaging all provinces on climate change policy. Pakistan remains among the most climate-vulnerable nations despite contributing minimally to global emissions.

stories.title: Cuba says Rubio lying about oil blockade
stories.summary: Cuba accused U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio of lying about an oil blockade on the island. Rubio had previously stated there was no oil blockade on Cuba "per se."

stories.title: ‘Operation Epic Fury’ has ended: Is the Iran war over?
stories.summary: Analysts suggest that President Trump's pause of 'Project Freedom' and the end of 'Operation Epic Fury' could mark the beginning of the end of the U.S.-Iran war, though uncertainty remains about a final resolution.

stories.title: Arms deliveries and Africa Corps training: How Russia is bolstering its presence in Madagascar
