stories.summary: An explosion at a fireworks factory in China killed at least 21 people and wounded 61 others. President Xi Jinping called for a thorough investigation into the blast.

stories.title: US destroys six Iranian boats while opening Strait of Hormuz to trade amid threatened ceasefire
stories.summary: U.S. military forces destroyed six Iranian Revolutionary Guard fast boats and intercepted cruise missiles and drones on the first day of "Project Freedom," an operation to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping. The destroyers USS Truxtun and USS Mason transited the strait without being struck despite what U.S. Central Command called a sustained barrage of Iranian threats.

stories.title: IMF chief Georgieva warns of 'much worse outcome' if Middle East war drags into 2027
stories.summary: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned of a "much worse outcome" for global GDP if the Middle East war extends into 2027. The IMF outlined three scenarios ranging from a baseline reference forecast to a severe downturn.

stories.title: Russia lost ground in Ukraine in April, a first since mid-2023, analysis shows
stories.summary: Analysis shows that Russia lost territory in Ukraine during April, marking the first time Moscow has ceded ground since mid-2023. Contributing factors include Ukrainian strikes, Russia's blocking of Starlink access, and Kremlin restrictions on Telegram, all of which have compounded existing Russian military difficulties.

stories.title: Nearly 85% of Ukraine’s cheese imports come from Poland – expert
stories.summary: In 2025, Ukraine imported up to 16,000 tonnes of hard cheese, with Polish products accounting for 80–85% of total imports, according to industry experts.

stories.title: Canadian fiddler sues Google after AI Overview wrongly claimed he was a sex offender
stories.summary: Canadian fiddle player Ashley MacIsaac has filed a $1.5 million civil lawsuit against Google in Ontario's superior court, alleging that the company's AI Overview feature falsely identified him as a sex offender. The three-time Juno award winner says the inaccurate AI-generated summary led to concert cancellations.

stories.title: US intelligence indicates limited new damage to Iran's nuclear program, sources say
stories.summary: US intelligence sources indicate that the timeline for Iran to develop a nuclear weapon has not changed since last summer. Analysts suggest that significantly impeding Tehran's nuclear program may require destroying its stockpile of highly enriched uranium.

stories.title: Putin declares May 8-9 ceasefire with Ukraine to mark World War II anniversary
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin declared a two-day ceasefire with Ukraine on May 8–9 to mark the anniversary of the end of World War II. Russia's defence ministry warned it would launch a massive missile strike on Kyiv if Ukraine violated the truce.

stories.title: US, Gulf Arab nations draft new UN resolution on Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The United States and Gulf Arab nations are drafting a U.N. Security Council resolution to condemn Iran for blocking the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz announced the effort on Monday, describing Iran's actions as a response to a U.S.-Israeli bombing campaign.

stories.title: Israeli strike sparks fire in northern Gaza City
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike in northern Gaza City sparked a fire, with video showing flames rising from the targeted area. Reports indicate the strike hit a group of civilians.

stories.title: Energy prices surge, stocks and gold fall amid escalation
stories.summary: Oil prices surged roughly 5% after reported attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz raised fears of supply disruptions. Brent crude rose 4.98% and US West Texas Intermediate climbed 3.05%, while gold, silver, and US stock indices all declined.

stories.title: Qatar condemns Iran attack on UAE, pledges support
stories.summary: Qatar's Emir Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani condemned Iranian attacks on civilian sites in the UAE during a phone call with UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan. Qatar's foreign ministry affirmed full solidarity with the UAE and support for its sovereignty measures.

stories.title: US deploys jets, helicopters to support escort operation
stories.summary: US Central Command announced that "Project Freedom," launched by President Donald Trump, involves more than 100 aircraft and approximately 15,000 personnel escorting ships through the Strait of Hormuz. The USS Abraham Lincoln is among two aircraft carriers enforcing a blockade on Iranian ports.

stories.title: Naftogaz reports UAH 5.8B profit in 2025
stories.summary: Ukraine's state energy company Naftogaz reported a consolidated profit of 5.83 billion Ukrainian hryvnias for 2025.

stories.title: Why the Falkland Islands are British
stories.summary: Reports emerged that U.S. President Trump asked the Pentagon to review Britain's claim to the Falkland Islands, possibly as leverage over the UK's reluctance to support his policy on Iran. The Falklands, a British Overseas Territory in the South Atlantic, have long been subject to competing sovereignty claims from Argentina.

stories.title: Hong Kong should study how Singapore awards infrastructure contracts
stories.summary: An analysis suggests Hong Kong should study Singapore's approach to awarding infrastructure contracts as the city prepares a major public works push, including HK$150 billion in funding for the Northern Metropolis and other projects.

stories.title: Ukraine and Russia declare separate truces
stories.summary: Russia declared a unilateral ceasefire for May 8–9 to mark Victory Day, threatening a massive missile strike on Kyiv if violated. Ukraine countered with its own truce for May 5–6, dismissing Moscow's proposal. US-led diplomacy has stalled as Washington focuses on the Middle East.

stories.title: Rescuers among three dead after yacht sinks off Australian coast
stories.summary: Two volunteer marine rescuers, aged 78 and 62, died after their boat rolled in treacherous conditions while responding to a yacht sinking off the Australian coast.

stories.title: US destroys six Iranian small boats, shoots down missiles, drones, admiral says
stories.summary: The U.S. military announced an operation involving approximately 15,000 troops, navy destroyers, over 100 aircraft, and undersea assets. During the operation, American forces destroyed six Iranian small boats and shot down missiles and drones, according to a U.S. admiral.

stories.title: China fireworks factory explosion kills 21, injures more than 60 people
stories.summary: An explosion at the Huasheng Fireworks Manufacturing and Display Company in Liuyang, Hunan province, China, killed 21 people and injured 61 others. President Xi Jinping ordered all-out search-and-rescue efforts for those still unaccounted for.

stories.title: AI helps Singapore’s Grab woo tough Southeast Asian crowd, exceed expectations
stories.summary: Singapore-based Grab reported first-quarter profits exceeding analyst estimates, aided by AI-enhanced features in its superapp and resilient demand for ride-hailing and delivery services across Southeast Asia.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it hit Israeli Merkava tank in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah claimed it struck an Israeli Merkava tank with a guided missile in the town of Biyyada in southern Lebanon on Monday night, reporting the tank was seen burning. The group said the attack was in response to Israeli ceasefire violations.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Saudi Arabia calls for de-escalation after US-Iran clashes
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia called for de-escalation in the Middle East following military clashes between the United States and Iran that rattled a fragile ceasefire. The UN Security Council was scheduled to hold a closed-door meeting on Lebanon later in the day.

stories.title: China’s fight to keep Darwin Port could help fragile Sino-Australian relations: analysts
stories.summary: Chinese company Landbridge Group filed a legal case at the World Bank's ICSID tribunal over Australia's actions regarding Darwin Port, marking the first such international arbitration case against Australia. Analysts say the multi-year proceeding could serve as a buffer for Sino-Australian relations.

stories.title: Ex-China soldier escapes Myanmar fraud centre by scaling wall, masking scent with cow dung
stories.summary: A former Chinese soldier named Yang Lei recounted escaping a fraud center in Myanmar by scaling a wall, masking his scent with cow dung, and subduing an armed guard before returning safely to China.

stories.title: Man to plead guilty in Colorado firebombing attack on rally for Israeli hostages
stories.summary: Mohamed Sabry Soliman plans to plead guilty in a Colorado state case related to a firebombing attack on a rally for Israeli hostages. He faces a possible life sentence and has pleaded not guilty in a separate federal case.

stories.title: Turkey and Qatar discuss US-Iran talks in phone call
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan and Qatari counterpart Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani held a phone call to discuss Middle East developments, including ongoing US-Iran talks and regional de-escalation efforts.

stories.title: Iran warns US of ‘crushing’ response over Hormuz
stories.summary: IRGC Deputy Political Officer Yadollah Javani warned that any US intervention in the Strait of Hormuz would be met with a "decisive and crushing response." He claimed American efforts to reopen the strait had failed despite extensive attempts.

stories.title: Svyrydenko: 25 companies join Ukraine's private air defense initiative
stories.summary: Twenty-five Ukrainian companies have joined an experimental government initiative to create private air defense units, according to First Deputy Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko.

stories.title: Fujairah oil zone hit by fire after drone attack as UAE says it intercepted Iran missiles
stories.summary: A drone attack from Iran struck the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone in the UAE, causing a fire. Three Indian citizens sustained moderate injuries and were hospitalized. The UAE military said it intercepted Iranian missiles during the incident.

stories.title: What the public inquiry into deadly Tai Po blaze has revealed so far
stories.summary: An independent inquiry into the deadly November 2024 fire at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, Hong Kong, has completed 21 evidential hearings revealing multiple regulatory failures in overseeing the estate's renovation and fire safety supervision.

stories.title: Mother convicted for locking up daughter in Germany
stories.summary: A German woman was convicted for confining her daughter in her grandparents' house for seven years, completely isolating the child from the outside world. The case resulted in criminal charges and a court sentencing.

stories.title: Drones shatter months of relative calm in Khartoum, hit airport
stories.summary: Drone strikes hit Khartoum airport on Monday, May 4, breaking months of relative calm in Sudan's capital. The attacks were part of a sudden series of assaults three years into the country's civil war, according to witnesses.

stories.title: Newborn born in Nablus a day after his father was killed in Israeli raid
stories.summary: A Palestinian newborn was delivered in Nablus one day after Israeli forces fatally shot his father during a raid in the city.

stories.title: Germany's Merz marks a year in office facing deep transatlantic crisis
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz marks his first year in office amid a major transatlantic crisis. U.S. President Donald Trump has threatened 25% tariffs on European auto imports and announced plans to withdraw thousands of American troops from Germany.

stories.title: Iran no further to nuclear weapon than it was before war, US intel agencies assess
stories.summary: US intelligence agencies assess that Iran is no closer to building a nuclear weapon than it was before the war, estimating Tehran remains approximately one year away from that capability — a timeline unchanged since June 2025.

stories.title: China’s robots step into real-world roles, from cleaning to directing traffic
stories.summary: Robots powered by embodied artificial intelligence are increasingly performing real-world tasks in China, including home cleaning, traffic direction, and hazardous factory repairs, as the country accelerates deployment of AI-equipped machines.

stories.title: Iran war live: Washington, Tehran trade threats over Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Lebanon's Health Ministry reported that Israeli attacks have killed 2,696 people in Lebanon since March 2, amid ongoing tensions between Washington and Tehran over the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Six Indian nationals among sailors rescued by navy, maritime security agency in Arabian Sea: security sources
stories.summary: The Pakistan Navy and Pakistan Maritime Security Agency rescued seven sailors, including six Indian nationals and one Indonesian, from the vessel MV Gautam after it experienced a technical fault in the Arabian Sea while traveling from Oman to India.

stories.title: War update: 132 clashes on front lines, Ukrainian forces neutralize nearly 70 Russian troops in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 132 combat engagements with Russian troops on May 4, with the heaviest fighting in the Pokrovsk sector of the front line, where Russia launched 21 attacks. Ukrainian forces neutralized nearly 70 Russian soldiers in that sector.

stories.title: NAB recovers 80 acres of govt land illegally allotted to Bahria Town
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Accountability Bureau recovered 80 acres of government land in Hyderabad's Deh Ganjo Takkar, valued at approximately 6 billion rupees, that had been illegally allotted to the Bahria Town housing development for a fraction of its worth.

stories.title: Support among American Jews for US-led war on Iran declines: survey
stories.summary: A survey by the Jewish People Policy Institute shows declining support and rising opposition among engaged American Jews toward the US-led war against Iran, reflecting growing reservations as the campaign has progressed.

stories.title: Two dead after car runs into crowd in German city of Leipzig, reports local broadcaster
stories.summary: Two people were killed and two severely injured when a car drove into a crowd in the center of Leipzig, Germany, according to local broadcaster MDR citing police.

stories.title: Iran restarts attacks on UAE as US fights to restore traffic in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran launched 15 missiles and 4 drones at the UAE, sparking a fire at an oil facility in the first major attack since a prior ceasefire. The US reported sinking 6 small Iranian boats as it worked to restore shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: US and UAE report Iran attacks as military pushes to reopen Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: U.S. forces opened a passage through the Strait of Hormuz on Monday by sinking Iranian boats and escorting merchant ships, while fresh attacks struck vessels and facilities in the UAE. The escalation has raised concerns about global energy supplies and threatens a fragile regional ceasefire.

stories.title: Air Force clears T-7A Red Hawk for low-rate production
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force approved low-rate initial production of the T-7A Red Hawk advanced trainer jet. The decision authorizes a $219 million contract covering the manufacture of the first 14 aircraft.

stories.title: Chevron chief warns Strait of Hormuz closure will soon lead to oil shortages
stories.summary: Chevron CEO Mike Wirth warned that a closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which carries roughly 20 percent of global crude oil, would lead to physical supply shortages. He said Asia would be hit first and that economies could contract as demand adjusts to constrained supply.

stories.title: ‘Extensive brutality’: Rebel attacks reap hell on Congolese civilians
stories.summary: An ISIL-linked armed group has carried out torture, killings, and abductions of civilians, including children, in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

stories.title: Russian forces devastate Kostiantynivka with overnight air bomb strikes
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out overnight air bomb strikes on the city of Kostiantynivka in Ukraine's Donetsk region. Aerial reconnaissance from Ukraine's State Border Guard Service documented the devastation caused by the attacks.

stories.title: Mali leader Goita assumes role of defence minister after attacks, state media says
stories.summary: Mali's military leader Assimi Goita assumed the role of defense minister after his predecessor was killed in coordinated attacks on April 25 by al-Qaeda-linked militants and Tuareg separatists, state television reported from Bamako.

stories.title: Europe, Canada pull together in Yerevan in Trump's shadow
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney addressed fellow leaders at a gathering in Yerevan, Armenia, calling for resistance to what he described as a more transactional and insular global order. The summit brought together European and Canadian officials amid tensions over U.S. foreign policy under President Trump.

stories.title: Haredi masses breach Meron, flouting wartime Lag B’Omer restrictions
stories.summary: Thousands of ultra-Orthodox worshippers reportedly breached security restrictions to reach the Meron shrine in the Galilee for Lag B'Omer celebrations during wartime. Israeli police denied reports of mass illegal entry, while National Security Minister Ben Gvir praised officers for acting gently.

stories.title: Birthday girl, 10, among 3 dead in Colombia monster truck crash
stories.summary: A monster truck veered into spectators at an exhibition in Popayán, southwestern Colombia, on Sunday, killing three people. Among the dead was 10-year-old Hellen Velarde, who was attending the event as a birthday celebration. A second girl and a young woman were also killed in the incident.

stories.title: Ukraine and Russia Declare Separate Temporary Ceasefires
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia each declared separate temporary ceasefires. The Russian Defense Ministry threatened a "massive missile strike on the center of Kyiv" if Ukraine violated the terms of its ceasefire.

stories.title: Ukraine and Russia Declare Separate Truces
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia declared separate truces around the same period, with overlapping but distinct timeframes. The Russian Defense Ministry warned of a massive missile strike on central Kyiv if Ukraine violated Moscow's ceasefire.

stories.title: Three Indians injured after fire breaks out in UAE’s Fujairah due to drone attack
stories.summary: Three Indian nationals were injured after a fire broke out at the Fujairah Petroleum Industries Zone in the United Arab Emirates following a drone attack originating from Iran, according to local media reports.

stories.title: Armenia turns 'towards Europe' as Macron highlights shift from Russia
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron declared during a visit to Yerevan on Monday that Armenia has chosen a path toward Europe, underscoring the country's gradual shift away from Russian influence. European leaders gathered in the Armenian capital for regional summits focused on security and EU cooperation.

stories.title: Ukraine, Slovakia to prepare joint government meeting – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukraine and Slovakia agreed to prepare a joint government meeting to be held in either Kyiv or Bratislava, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

stories.title: Iran says no military solution to Hormuz crisis, warns against escalation
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that the Strait of Hormuz crisis cannot be resolved militarily, citing recent US provocations. He said Pakistan is mediating ongoing diplomatic talks and warned the US and UAE against deeper involvement in the conflict.

stories.title: UK eyes joining EU’s €90 billion Ukraine loan to tap defence orders
stories.summary: The United Kingdom is in discussions with the European Commission about joining the EU's €90 billion loan to Ukraine. Participation would allow Britain to qualify for Ukrainian defence procurement contracts financed by the loan but would require the UK to cover some interest payments on the borrowing.

stories.title: Modern slavery at record levels in UK and expected to worsen, report warns
stories.summary: The UK government's independent anti-slavery commissioner warned that modern slavery in Britain has reached record levels and is expected to worsen over the next decade. Referrals to the national referral mechanism nearly doubled in five years, rising from 12,691 in 2021 to 23,411 in 2025.

stories.title: Chinese start-up ZYT eyes mass production of semi-autonomous trucks this year
stories.summary: Shenzhen-based start-up ZYT, a spin-off from drone maker DJI, plans to begin mass production of semi-autonomous trucks this year. The company has partnered with China's top six heavy-truck manufacturers to produce vehicles equipped with its navigation-on-autopilot systems, aiming to improve fuel efficiency and reduce logistics costs.

stories.title: Organizers tout uptick in pilgrims to Tunisia Lag B’Omer fest 3 years after attack
stories.summary: Around 200 Jewish pilgrims from abroad attended the annual Lag B'Omer festival at Africa's oldest synagogue in Djerba, Tunisia, marking an increase in attendance three years after an attack. Previous years had seen only several dozen participants.

stories.title: Suicide attack foiled on army check post in South Waziristan; civilian martyred, 15 injured
stories.summary: An attempted suicide attack on a Pakistan Army checkpoint near Azam Warsak Bazaar in South Waziristan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, was foiled on Monday. The explosives-laden vehicle was destroyed before reaching the post, but the blast killed one civilian and injured 15 others, damaging nearby buildings.

stories.title: Two killed after car hits bystanders in Leipzig driver arrested
stories.summary: A car struck bystanders in the German city of Leipzig, killing at least two people. Several others were seriously injured. The driver was arrested by authorities.

stories.title: Secret Service shoots armed suspect near White House after brief lockdown
stories.summary: U.S. Secret Service agents shot and wounded an armed suspect near the White House on Monday after he opened fire, prompting a brief lockdown. The incident occurred shortly after Vice President JD Vance's motorcade passed through the area, though officials said Vance was not believed to be a target.

stories.title: Russian strikes kill 14 across Ukraine on Monday, nearly 60 injured – interior minister
stories.summary: Russian strikes killed 14 people and injured nearly 60 others across Ukraine on Monday, according to Interior Minister Ihor Klymenko. The attacks continued amid broader hostilities between Russia and Ukraine.

stories.title: Trump’s Germany troop cuts show limits of NATO efforts to keep US on board
stories.summary: President Trump's decision to cut US troop levels in Germany highlights the limits of NATO allies' efforts to persuade Washington to maintain its commitment to the alliance.

stories.title: IMF warns prolonged Israeli-US war could worsen global growth outlook
stories.summary: The IMF warned that a prolonged war involving Iran could significantly worsen the global economic outlook. Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said earlier projections of limited impact have been overtaken by events, with oil prices potentially reaching $125 per barrel through 2027.

stories.title: Pakistan has sufficient POL reserves till third week of June, says petroleum ministry
stories.summary: Pakistan's petroleum ministry informed Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar that the country holds sufficient petroleum, oil, and lubricant reserves to ensure uninterrupted supply through the third week of June 2026, factoring in incoming shipments.

stories.title: Ukraine announces ceasefire from May 6, awaits reciprocal steps from Russia – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that Ukraine would declare a ceasefire starting May 6 and called on Russia to take reciprocal steps. The move came amid competing truce proposals from both sides surrounding the Victory Day period.

stories.title: Saudi crown prince condemns Iran attacks in call with UAE president
stories.summary: Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman spoke with UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan to address recent Iranian missile and drone strikes on the UAE. Riyadh issued a strong condemnation of the attacks and reaffirmed its support for the Emirates.

stories.title: Bessent urges China to step up diplomacy on Iran ahead of Trump-Xi summit
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called on China to increase diplomatic engagement on the Iran conflict ahead of an expected summit between President Trump and President Xi Jinping.

stories.title: Jewish authors borrow from the past in new ‘mini-genre’ of ‘how-to’ activism literature
stories.summary: Three new books by Jewish authors offer practical guides for activism, drawing on historical traditions of dissent. The works arrive amid widespread protest fatigue and political polarization in the United States.

stories.title: Iranian sailors evacuated to Pakistan return home, state media confirms
stories.summary: Fifteen of 22 Iranian sailors, released by the United States and evacuated to Pakistan, crossed back into Iran on Monday via the Rimdan border terminal in Sistan-Baluchistan province. Iranian state media outlet IRNA confirmed their return, while Pakistan's Foreign Office described the evacuation as a US confidence-building measure.

stories.title: Pulitzers honour damning coverage of Trump and his policies
stories.summary: The 2025 Pulitzer Prizes heavily recognized reporting on the Trump administration, including coverage of immigration crackdowns and alleged enrichment of political allies. The Pulitzer committee criticized President Trump's efforts to restrict press freedom.

stories.title: For Christians in Israel and Jerusalem, intolerance is becoming normal
stories.summary: A French nun was assaulted in East Jerusalem, highlighting a pattern of intolerance toward Christians in Israel and Jerusalem that local communities say has become increasingly normalized despite official rhetoric.

stories.title: Russia declares unilateral 'ceasefire' on May 8-9
stories.summary: Russia's Ministry of Defense announced a unilateral ceasefire on May 8–9, framing it as honoring the Soviet victory in World War II. The declaration was made without prior coordination with Ukraine.

stories.title: UAE declares situation safe after missile threat alert
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates declared the security situation safe following a missile threat alert, the first such warning issued by UAE authorities since early April. No further details on the source of the threat were immediately provided.

stories.title: Fujairah oil zone hit by drone attack as UAE says it intercepted Iranian missiles
stories.summary: A drone attack originating from Iran struck the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone in the UAE, sparking a fire and moderately injuring three Indian citizens. The UAE Defence Ministry reported that its forces intercepted three Iranian cruise missiles, while a fourth fell into the sea.

stories.title: UAE Defence Ministry says four cruise missiles fired from Iran
stories.summary: Authorities in Fujairah, UAE, reported on May 4 that a fire erupted at the Fujairah Oil Industry Zone following what they described as a drone attack originating from Iran. The UAE Defence Ministry stated that four cruise missiles had been fired from Iranian territory.

stories.title: Norwegian fish farms polluting fjords with waste likened to ‘raw sewage of millions of people’
stories.summary: A report by the Sunstone Institute found that Norwegian fish farms release 75,000 tonnes of nitrogen and 13,000 tonnes of phosphorus annually into fjords and coastal waters, creating nutrient pollution equivalent to the raw sewage of a country the size of Australia.

stories.title: How the Middle East crisis is expanding China’s agrochemical influence
stories.summary: The Middle East conflict is disrupting global agricultural supply chains, creating openings for China to expand its agrochemical influence. Chinese fertiliser prices remain well below international levels, and domestic spring planting has proceeded normally.

stories.title: Belarus prepares training grounds, logistics routes that Russia could use at any time – border guard spokesman
stories.summary: A Ukrainian border guard spokesman reported that Belarus continues constructing military training sites and logistics routes that could be used by Russian forces. While Russia currently lacks sufficient troops in Belarus for an offensive, the infrastructure could be activated at any time.

stories.title: Armed man shot by US Secret Service near White House
stories.summary: US Secret Service agents shot an armed man near the White House and National Mall in Washington, triggering a brief lockdown. The incident occurred shortly after Vice President J.D. Vance's motorcade passed through the area, though officials said he was not believed to be the target.

stories.title: NRO awards three new contracts for commercial satellite data
stories.summary: The National Reconnaissance Office awarded three new contracts for commercial satellite data. NRO official Pete Muend indicated the agency could evaluate commercial satellite firms' ability to track airborne targets for the US Space Force.

stories.title: Pentagon seeks smarter, self-organizing drones as autonomous-warfare budget is poised to skyrocket
stories.summary: The Pentagon is pursuing new DARPA projects to develop smarter, self-organizing autonomous drones that require fewer human operators. The initiative comes as the U.S. military's budget for autonomous warfare systems is expected to increase significantly.

stories.title: A century since Dreyfus's wrongful conviction, a family member is promoted in the IDF
stories.summary: A descendant of Alfred Dreyfus, the French officer wrongfully convicted of treason in the 1890s in a landmark antisemitism case, has been promoted within the Israel Defense Forces. Uriel Dreyfus has now reached the same military rank his forefather once held.

stories.title: Ukrainian police raid dozens of draft officials over suspected corruption
stories.summary: Ukrainian police conducted searches across 16 regions on May 4, targeting current and former military draft officials suspected of corruption-related offenses. Dozens of searches were carried out as part of the nationwide operation announced by authorities in Kyiv.

stories.title: US president offers no clear answer on truce status with Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump declined to confirm whether the ceasefire with Iran remains intact, saying he was assessing reports of incidents involving commercial vessels near the Strait of Hormuz. Trump acknowledged some recent firing but offered no definitive statement on the truce's status.

stories.title: Blake Lively and Justin Baldoni settle lawsuit over acrimonious It Ends With Us production
stories.summary: Actors Blake Lively and Justin Baldoni settled their legal dispute stemming from the production of the 2024 film It Ends With Us, reaching an agreement just weeks before a scheduled trial. Settlement details were not disclosed.

stories.title: Zelensky on May 9 ceasefire: No official contact with Ukraine on proposal
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukraine received no official communication from Russia regarding the proposed May 9 ceasefire, indicating the announcement was made unilaterally.

stories.title: Opec+ set to raise output as Strait of Hormuz blockade disrupt oil flows
stories.summary: OPEC+ agreed to increase oil output by 188,000 barrels per day in June amid disruptions caused by restrictions around the Strait of Hormuz during the Israeli-US war on Iran. The UAE recently exited the group, citing interference in its production decisions, adding to market uncertainty.

stories.title: Zelensky says Russia never notified Ukraine of ceasefire or invited it to join, calls short-term halt meaningless
stories.summary: President Zelensky said Russia never notified Ukraine of the announced May 8–9 ceasefire or invited it to participate, calling such a short-term halt meaningless. Russia's Defense Ministry had declared the pause by order of President Putin.

stories.title: ‘A test of our values’: Starmer to call for whole-society response to rising antisemitism
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer will host a Downing Street roundtable calling for a whole-of-society response to rising antisemitism, following a knife attack on Jewish community members in Golders Green, arson attacks, and the Heaton Park terror incident.

stories.title: How US tech hegemony is locking out the Global South
stories.summary: An analysis argues that US actions including sanctions, export controls, and diplomatic pressure against China's technology sector amount to suppression rather than fair competition, with consequences that lock out Global South countries from technological advancement.

stories.title: Mobile carriers warn St. Petersburg residents of internet ‘difficulties’ ahead of May 9 parade
stories.summary: Mobile carriers MegaFon and Yota warned St. Petersburg residents to expect mobile internet disruptions during preparations for and the holding of mass events surrounding the May 9 Victory Day parade.

stories.title: Zohran Mamdani condemns ICE after police and protesters clash in Brooklyn
stories.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani condemned ICE after federal agents removed a detained man from a Brooklyn hospital, sparking a protest that led to clashes between demonstrators and police. The NYPD's response has also drawn scrutiny.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1531: Ukraine strikes Russia’s oil empire from Caspian to Baltic
stories.summary: On day 1,531 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, Ukraine carried out strikes targeting Russian oil infrastructure from the Caspian to the Baltic regions. Meanwhile, NATO has shifted to a posture described as CALM as European nations accelerate rearmament efforts.

stories.title: Israeli authorities ban Jewish pilgrimage near Lebanese border
stories.summary: Israeli authorities banned a Jewish pilgrimage event near the Lebanese border. Israeli media reported that thousands of people had already gathered at the pilgrimage site on May 4 before the ban was imposed.

stories.title: Can solar cars become mainstream?
stories.summary: The energy crisis driven by the Iran conflict has accelerated government efforts to promote electric vehicles, renewing interest in solar-powered cars. U.S. startup Aptera Motors plans to begin delivering solar cars to customers as early as this year, though the technology has long remained experimental due to technical challenges.

stories.title: US military accompanies commercial carrier through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The Maersk vessel Alliance Fairfax transited the Strait of Hormuz accompanied by US military forces. Maersk confirmed the passage was completed without incident and that all crew members were safe.

stories.title: Senegal's President Faye says ruling party, led by PM Sonko, risks 'collapse'
stories.summary: Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye warned in a state television address that the ruling party risks collapse, amid speculation of a rift with Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko. Faye said Sonko would remain in his post if he continues performing his duties properly. The comments come as Senegal faces economic challenges linked to debt and regional instability.

stories.title: Zelensky announces new aid packages after Yerevan summit
stories.summary: Following a summit in Yerevan, Armenian capital, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced new military aid packages and accelerated funding for drone and electronic warfare production.

stories.title: Two volunteers among three dead off NSW coast after rescue boat rolls while trying to help sinking yacht
stories.summary: Three people died, including two marine rescue volunteers, after a rescue boat rolled while responding to a sinking yacht at Ballina Bar on the northern New South Wales coast in Australia. Four others survived by making it to shore.

stories.title: Introducing ‘Project Freedom’
stories.summary: The US launched "Project Freedom," an initiative to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which has heightened tensions with Iran and threatened to destabilize the existing fragile ceasefire between the two countries.

stories.title: Project Freedom unlikely to pay off in Strait of Hormuz right away, analysts say
stories.summary: US Central Command launched "Project Freedom" in the Strait of Hormuz, with CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper reporting that six Iranian small boats were destroyed as the operation began. Analysts say the effort is unlikely to yield immediate results.

stories.title: Hormuz tensions push ceasefire to the brink as Trump threatens Iran
stories.summary: Tensions in the Strait of Hormuz have escalated as the US military encourages commercial ships to transit the waterway while Iran insists it maintains full control, pushing an existing ceasefire toward collapse amid threats from President Trump against Iran.

stories.title: Ukraine is building multi-layered shield along border with Russian-occupied Transnistria — 50 km from biggest port city
stories.summary: Ukraine is constructing a multi-layered defensive shield along its border with Russian-occupied Transnistria in Moldova, approximately 50 kilometers from its largest port city. Russian troops have been stationed in Transnistria since 1992.

stories.title: PTI accuses govt of ‘unprecedented economic crisis’, slams claims of stability
stories.summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) accused the Pakistani government in Islamabad of creating an unprecedented economic and governance crisis. PTI Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram cited an 11% year-on-year rise in the Consumer Price Index and a 15% increase in the Sensitive Price Indicator as evidence of returning inflation.

stories.title: 'It's an elite matter': UAE confirms it's in talks for swap line loan with US
stories.summary: The UAE confirmed it is in discussions with the United States over a currency swap line, describing it as part of an exclusive arrangement the US maintains with only five countries. UAE Trade Minister Thani al-Zeyoudi made the announcement at a conference in Abu Dhabi amid ongoing Iranian air strikes on the country.

stories.title: Maccabi Tel Aviv pulls away from Hapoel Jerusalem for overtime win
stories.summary: Maccabi Tel Aviv defeated Hapoel Jerusalem in overtime in Israeli basketball. Forward Lonnie Walker dislocated his finger during overtime and is expected to miss two to three weeks.

stories.title: 'Elephant in the room' Trump looms over European attempt at unity
stories.summary: European leaders gathered in Armenia acknowledged that their alliances are not as strong as desired, with the influence of US President Donald Trump described as a major factor. The meeting highlighted ongoing challenges in achieving European unity.

stories.title: Two killed after car hits bystanders in Leipzig, Germany, driver arrested
stories.summary: A 33-year-old German citizen was arrested in Leipzig, Germany, after driving a car into bystanders, killing two people. Police said there was no further danger to the public.

stories.title: Is Israel’s interception of the Global Sumud Flotilla legal?
stories.summary: Spain has accused Israel of abduction after Israeli forces intercepted the Global Sumud Flotilla and detained two activists, raising questions about the legality of the seizure under international maritime law.

stories.title: Strategic narratives reshape understanding of the US-Iran standoff - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece analyzes the US-Iran standoff, questioning whether strategic narratives in policy discourse are replacing objective assessments of the conflict's realities.

stories.title: Iran denies plan to target UAE, blames US for 'adventurism'
stories.summary: Iran denied that it planned an attack on oil facilities at Fujairah port in the UAE, with a military official attributing the incident to US military actions in the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran described the episode as a result of what it called US adventurism to create passage for unauthorized ship transit.

stories.title: Hantavirus: spread by rodents, potentially fatal, with no specific cure
stories.summary: A hantavirus outbreak aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius, traveling from Argentina to Cape Verde, has been confirmed by Dutch operator Oceanwide Expeditions. The virus, which circulates in rodents and can be fatal in humans, has no specific cure. The operator described the situation on board as serious.

stories.title: UDF strikes Russian drone warehouses, air defense systems in occupied territories
stories.summary: On May 3–4, Ukraine's Defense Forces struck Russian drone storage facilities and air defense systems in occupied territories, hitting multiple military targets.

stories.title: Israeli TV Academy Awards present their 2025 prizes, and honor the late Alon Aboutboul
stories.summary: The Israeli TV Academy presented its 2025 awards and honored the late actor Alon Aboutboul. For the first time in two years, the ceremony did not include special categories for crisis and wartime broadcasting.

stories.title: Video: Modi’s BJP poised to take control in India’s West Bengal
stories.summary: India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is positioned to gain control of the West Bengal state government, marking a significant political shift in the region.

stories.title: Opaque nature of US-Iran shadow war: Are they 'dancing their way out of a minefield' toward a deal?
stories.summary: Global defence commentator Peter Apps described U.S.-Iran tensions as a fluid situation where ceasefire negotiations and military escalation are occurring simultaneously. The Strait of Hormuz has emerged as both a critical global shipping chokepoint and a central battleground in the conflict.

stories.title: In world first, Israeli scientists map digital atlas of healthy human liver
stories.summary: Researchers from Israel's Weizmann Institute, Sheba Medical Center, and the Mayo Clinic have created the first digital atlas of a healthy human liver. The study revealed differences between human and mouse livers and may improve treatments for fatty liver disease.

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine declare competing ceasefires
stories.summary: Russia declared a unilateral ceasefire on May 9 to coincide with Victory Day, while Ukraine announced its own separate truce for May 5–6. Kyiv dismissed Moscow's gesture, citing the threat posed by Ukrainian drones as a factor behind Russia's move.

stories.title: Australia news live: four Australians among passengers on luxury cruise ship hit by deadly suspected hantavirus outbreak
stories.summary: The cruise ship MV Hondius remains off the coast of Cape Verde after a suspected hantavirus outbreak killed three passengers and left three others seriously ill. Four Australians are among nearly 150 people isolating onboard the vessel.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill at least two in Gaza, Wafa reports
stories.summary: At least two people were killed in Israeli strikes across Gaza on Monday, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa. A drone attack hit the Bureij refugee camp in central Gaza, while a separate air strike struck southeast of Gaza City. At least 834 people have been killed in Gaza since the October 10 ceasefire took effect.

stories.title: German defence ministry says no 'definitive cancellation' of US weapons deployment
stories.summary: Germany's defence ministry stated on May 4 that the United States had not definitively cancelled a plan, originally devised under former President Joe Biden, to deploy a battalion equipped with long-range Tomahawk missiles to German territory.

stories.title: Russia intensifies drone attacks on ports, Ukraine says
stories.summary: Ukraine reported that Russia has dramatically intensified drone attacks on its port infrastructure in 2026, launching more than 800 drones in the first four months of the year. That figure is more than ten times the number used in the same period a year earlier.

stories.title: Assimi Goita appoints himself defence minister
stories.summary: Mali's junta leader Assimi Goïta appointed himself defence minister following the killing of his predecessor amid a wave of attacks in the country. The move consolidates further military and political authority under Goïta's control.

stories.title: US decision not to deploy Tomahawks to Germany was even worse than withdrawal of 5,000 US troops. But Ukraine can help
stories.summary: A commentary argues that the US decision not to deploy Tomahawk missiles to Germany was more damaging than the withdrawal of 5,000 US troops from Europe. It also highlights that three years of full-scale war have made Ukraine's defense industry among the most combat-experienced globally.

stories.title: ADF neutralized 70 of 88 Russian drones since morning
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces neutralized 70 out of 88 Russian drones launched between 08:30 and 18:30 on Monday, May 4. A ballistic missile strike and 14 additional enemy strike UAVs were also recorded.

stories.title: Qatar emir condemns Iran attacks in call with UAE president
stories.summary: Qatar's Emir Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani condemned Iranian missile and drone attacks on the UAE during a phone call with UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed al-Nahyan. The emir said the strikes targeted civilian sites and infrastructure, and Doha expressed solidarity with the Emirates.

stories.title: Moscow rehearses V-Day parade marking WWII victory
stories.summary: Russia rehearsed its annual Victory Day military parade in Moscow commemorating the World War II anniversary and declared a ceasefire with Ukraine to cover the May 9 celebrations.

stories.title: Mysterious world beyond Pluto may have an atmosphere: astronomers
stories.summary: Japanese astronomers have found evidence that a roughly 500-kilometer-wide object beyond Pluto in the Kuiper Belt may possess an atmosphere, which would make it only the second trans-Neptunian object known to have one after Pluto.

stories.title: Ukrainian Ambassador to Israel warns 'Post' about country's 'growing frustration' - interview
stories.summary: Ukrainian Ambassador to Israel Yevgen Korniychuk expressed his country's growing frustration in an interview, stating that Ukraine aims to open criminal proceedings against traders, exporters, and offshore entities that may have enabled sanctions breaches.

stories.title: Feminism play Liberation and first world war novel Angel Down among Pulitzer winners
stories.summary: The Pulitzer Prize for fiction was awarded to Daniel Kraus for "Angel Down," a World War I novel written as a single sentence, while Bess Wohl's "Liberation," about 1970s feminist consciousness-raising groups, won the drama prize. Other winners included works by Jill Lepore on the US Constitution and Brian Goldstone on housing insecurity.

stories.title: India's Modi celebrates 'record' win in opposition-held West Bengal
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party won a decisive victory in West Bengal state elections, wresting the opposition stronghold with at least 124 seats won and leading in 83 others in the 294-member assembly.

stories.title: Senior IDF official: No change in home front rules despite Iran attack on UAE, Oman
stories.summary: A senior IDF official stated that Israel's home front guidelines remain unchanged despite Iranian attacks on the UAE and Oman. The official said Israeli air defense systems and offensive capabilities are maintained at a high level of readiness.

stories.title: 'It's an elite matter': UAE confirms it's in talks for swap line loan with US
stories.summary: The UAE confirmed it is in talks with the United States over a swap line loan arrangement. The announcement came shortly before Iran launched fresh strikes on the UAE, reportedly in retaliation for US military operations in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Israeli fintech startup partners with Elon Musk’s X to gauge market sentiment
stories.summary: Israeli fintech company BridgeWise has partnered with Elon Musk's social media platform X to integrate financial conversation data into its AI-powered investment analysis tool. The system will provide sentiment-based analysis across approximately 70,000 securities.

stories.title: Russian drone strikes sports facility in Kharkiv
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Kyivskyi district of Kharkiv with a drone, hitting a sports facility. No further details on casualties were immediately available.

stories.title: UAE says it intercepted 15 missiles and four drones launched from Iran
stories.summary: The UAE Ministry of Defence announced that its air defense systems intercepted 12 ballistic missiles, three cruise missiles, and four drones launched from Iran on Monday.

stories.title: Jailed Iranian Nobel laureate Mohammadi needs urgent heart treatment in Tehran, says brother
stories.summary: The brother of jailed Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi said she urgently needs heart treatment at a hospital in Tehran. He reported she is suffering from severe headaches, nausea, and chest pain.

stories.title: First Druze party launches ahead of elections, aims for independent representation
stories.summary: A new political party called Alliance of Brothers has launched in Israel ahead of upcoming elections, aiming to unite Druze citizens and provide them with independent political representation. The party seeks to empower the Druze community to influence Israel's public agenda.

stories.title: After Russia unilaterally announced 9 May ceasefire to hold parade, Zelenskyy set Ukraine’s silence regime to start three days earlier
stories.summary: After Russia unilaterally announced a May 9 ceasefire to hold its Victory Day parade, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy set Ukraine's own silence regime to begin three days earlier. Reports indicate Russia's announcement appeared on social media rather than through formal diplomatic channels.

stories.title: Trump threatens to 'blow Iran off face of the Earth' if US vessels attacked
stories.summary: President Trump threatened to "blow Iran off the face of the Earth" if US vessels are attacked, citing upgraded military equipment and ammunition. The remarks came amid escalating tensions between Washington and Tehran over the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: EU, PA announce program to support Palestinians facing settler violence in West Bank
stories.summary: The European Union and the Palestinian Authority announced a six-million-euro program to support Palestinians facing settler violence in the West Bank. The initiative focuses on documenting attacks and providing protective presence and equipment to threatened villages.

stories.title: Israel's greatest generations: Gen Zers, millennials who answered the call after Oct. 7 - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece highlighted the contributions of Israeli Gen Z and millennial generations who mobilized after the October 7 attacks. The article called on Israelis, Jews, and others to help these generations rebuild.

stories.title: UNFPA committed to supporting midwifery education, workforce development in Pakistan
stories.summary: UNFPA reaffirmed its commitment to supporting Pakistan in strengthening midwifery education, workforce development, and health systems, with Representative Dr. Luay Shabaneh issuing the statement in Islamabad to mark International Day of the Midwife on May 5.

stories.title: SA President Rhamaposa becomes first head of state to sign ‘Free Barghouti’ pledge
stories.summary: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa became the first head of state to sign a pledge calling for the release of Marwan Barghouti. Barghouti is a former leader of the Al-Aqsa Martyrs' Brigades, linked to attacks during the Second Intifada.

stories.title: Mali junta chief to take over killed defence minister's role
stories.summary: Mali's junta leader Assimi Goita assumed the additional role of defence minister by decree on Monday, following the killing of the previous minister in large-scale attacks. The move further consolidates military authority under Goita's leadership.

stories.title: Russian forces launch over 50 attacks on Dnipropetrovsk region in one day, leaving five injured
stories.summary: Russian forces launched over 50 attacks on the Nikopol and Synelnykove districts in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region in a single day, injuring five people. The strikes targeted civilian areas across the region.

stories.title: Gaza, Hamas, and the pre-Oct. 7 concept sources say Israel is still stuck in - analysis
stories.summary: Sources within Israel's defense establishment are questioning the foundational assumptions of Israel's current strategy toward Hamas for the first time since the October 7 attack, suggesting the country remains trapped in pre-attack strategic thinking.

stories.title: Belarus is building training grounds, transport hubs, and logistical routes — Ukraine says Russia could use them for offensive at any time
stories.summary: Ukrainian officials say Belarus is constructing training grounds, transport hubs, and logistical routes near the Ukrainian border that Russia could use for offensive operations. Kyiv warned the infrastructure could be activated at any moment.

stories.title: Austria expels three Russian diplomats over signals spying
stories.summary: Austria expelled three Russian diplomats, declaring them personae non gratae, over suspected signals intelligence operations involving satellite dishes installed on Russian diplomatic buildings in Vienna. The Austrian government said the antenna installations could be used for spying.

stories.title: War of words: Trump, Iran trade claims of missile strikes in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The US and Iran traded conflicting claims about military confrontations in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. President Trump announced "Project Freedom" to guide stranded ships through the waterway, while Iran claimed it struck a US frigate with two missiles — a claim Washington denied outright.

stories.title: Russia orders two-day ceasefire in Ukraine war to coincide with Victory Day
stories.summary: Russia ordered a two-day ceasefire on May 8–9 to coincide with Victory Day, marking the 81st anniversary of Nazi Germany's defeat. The Russian Defense Ministry said it expected Ukraine to observe the truce, following an order from President Vladimir Putin.

stories.title: Mali leader Goita takes defence post after minister killed
stories.summary: Mali's military leader Assimi Goita has appointed himself defence minister after the previous minister was killed in attacks linked to al-Qaeda and Tuareg separatist groups. The move consolidates Goita's control over the country's security apparatus.

stories.title: China consul in Mexico calls protectionism a ‘dead end’ as trade tensions with US escalate
stories.summary: China's Consul General Fu Xinrong in Tijuana, Mexico, denounced protectionism as a dead end, calling for trade relations based on sovereignty and mutual respect. The remarks came weeks before the US, Mexico, and Canada are set to review the USMCA trade agreement amid escalating US-China trade tensions.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia and its allies must curb the growing Israeli-Emirati axis
stories.summary: The article argues that Saudi Arabia and its allies should counter the growing strategic alignment between Israel and the UAE, amid escalating US-Iran tensions and the risk of a wider regional conflict involving the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Lebanon’s most senior Shi’ite politician says no to negotiations with Israel until war stops
stories.summary: Lebanon's parliamentary speaker Nabih Berri, the country's most senior Shi'ite politician, rejected negotiations with Israel until hostilities cease. His comments highlight challenges facing US-led efforts to broker peace between Lebanon and Israel.

stories.title: Missile strike on Merefa: Death toll rises to seven, 14 injured remain in hospitals
stories.summary: The death toll from a Russian missile strike on Merefa, Ukraine, rose to seven after a severely wounded man died in hospital. Fourteen other injured individuals remain hospitalized.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF destroys 30-meter-long Hezbollah tunnel in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces destroyed a 30-meter-long Hezbollah tunnel in southern Lebanon. Dozens of explosive devices and anti-tank missiles were found inside the tunnel, along with several weapons storage facilities in the surrounding area.

stories.title: At least 130 Nigerians seek repatriation from South Africa after protests, Abuja says
stories.summary: At least 130 Nigerian citizens in South Africa have requested repatriation from their government following anti-foreigner protests in South Africa. Nigeria's Foreign Minister Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu confirmed the requests from Abuja.

stories.title: Russia offers Ukraine May 8-9 ceasefire amid WWII anniversary, but threatens major reprisals in same breath
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin unilaterally declared a two-day ceasefire on May 8–9 to mark the 81st anniversary of the World War II victory, while Ukrainian President Zelenskyy proposed his own truce starting a couple of days earlier. Both sides issued the proposals independently without coordination.

stories.title: 'America has confirmed everything that Iran has been telling its population', analyst says
stories.summary: Analyst Emma Salisbury of the Foreign Policy Institute told FRANCE 24 that US actions toward Iran have reinforced the Iranian regime's longstanding narrative that America seeks to destroy the country. She argued President Trump has done nothing to counter Tehran's characterization of the US as a hostile power.

stories.title: Russia Lost Ground in Ukraine in April, a First Since Mid-2023 – AFP Analysis
stories.summary: An AFP analysis found that Russia lost ground in Ukraine in April, marking the Ukrainian army's first net territorial gains since mid-2023. The gains were marginal, representing only 0.02 percent of Ukrainian territory.

stories.title: Gangland wars killing dozens of bystanders, report Swedish police
stories.summary: Swedish police report that gang-related violence has killed dozens of bystanders, including people struck by stray bullets, victims of mistaken identity, and relatives of gang members targeted in ongoing turf wars across Sweden.

stories.title: UAE moves schools to remote learning as US-Israeli war on Iran threatens to restart
stories.summary: Authorities in the United Arab Emirates ordered all schools to transition to remote learning amid rising regional tensions linked to the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran. Officials said the situation would be reassessed on May 8.

stories.title: PSL 11’s highest scorer Babar Azam named captain of the edition’s Team of the Year
stories.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board named Peshawar Zalmi captain Babar Azam to lead the PSL 11 Team of the Year after he finished as the season's highest run-scorer. Peshawar Zalmi won their second PSL title by defeating Hyderabad Kingsmen by five wickets in Lahore.

stories.title: Austria expels three Russian embassy staff on suspicion of spying
stories.summary: Austria expelled three Russian embassy staff members on suspicion of espionage. The Russian embassy warned there would be a "harsh" response to the expulsions.

stories.title: Pakistani delegation attends US investment summit to expand global footprint
stories.summary: A delegation of 16 Pakistani entrepreneurs and business leaders is attending the SelectUSA Investment Summit in National Harbour, Maryland, seeking opportunities to invest in the United States and expand their global business presence.

stories.title: Iran-US clash over alleged warship attack in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran claims its navy forced a US warship to turn back from the Strait of Hormuz, while Washington denies any clash occurred. The competing accounts highlight escalating tensions over control of the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Effective cross-border payment solutions for IT and software businesses
stories.summary: The article discusses strategies for IT and software businesses to improve cross-border payment processes, emphasizing efficiency and globalization through appropriate solution selection.

stories.title: True Iranian regime change won't occur if the IRGC holds power - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that true regime change in Iran is unlikely as long as the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps retains power. The author contends that current developments represent a new form of IRGC control rather than genuine transformation.

stories.title: Cabinet ministers warn mutinous MPs over ousting Keir Starmer
stories.summary: Senior UK Labour cabinet ministers have warned backbench MPs against attempting to remove Prime Minister Keir Starmer following poor local election results. Several ministers told the Guardian that while Starmer intends to remain in office, the mood among Labour MPs is volatile and the situation could escalate.

stories.title: Rutte, Zelensky discuss PURL, Ukraine to continue to receive anti-ballistic missiles
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on the sidelines of the 8th European Political Community Summit in Yerevan, Armenia. Rutte confirmed that the PURL program is operational and that anti-ballistic missiles will continue to be supplied to Ukraine.

stories.title: Ukrainian soldier stumbled into a Russian dugout. Two weeks later he walked out with a POW
stories.summary: A wounded Ukrainian corporal spent 14 days unarmed in a Russian dugout alongside an armed Russian soldier. After two weeks, the Russian soldier surrendered and was taken as a prisoner of war.

stories.title: Fujairah oil zone hit by fire after drone attack as UAE says it intercepted Iran missiles
stories.summary: A fire erupted at a major oil industry zone in Fujairah, UAE, after a drone attack originating from Iran. The UAE military separately intercepted three Iranian missiles over its waters, while a fourth missile crashed into the sea.

stories.title: Lebanon death toll rises to 2,696 as Israeli attacks continue
stories.summary: Lebanon's National News Agency reported that the death toll from Israeli attacks since March 2 has reached 2,696, with 8,264 wounded. Israeli air strikes on Monday killed several civilians during intensive raids across towns in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Iran prevents entry of U.S. warships into Strait of Hormuz, Navy says
stories.summary: Iran's navy announced on May 4 that it had prevented enemy warships from entering the Strait of Hormuz by issuing what it described as a swift and decisive warning, according to Iranian state television. The statement did not name the warships involved.

stories.title: 56% of Russians want Western brands to return after war-driven exodus, survey finds
stories.summary: A survey by Russian research association Gruppa 7/89, conducted in February and March 2026, found that 56% of Russians want Western brands to return after their departure following the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, as reported by Vedomosti.

stories.title: Two arrested over Golders Green Iranian memorial wall arson
stories.summary: Two individuals were arrested in connection with an arson attack on an Iranian memorial wall in Golders Green, London. The memorial, which was not damaged by the fire, is dedicated to protesters killed by the Islamic Republic of Iran.

stories.title: Putin threatens 'massive missile strike' on Kyiv if Ukraine breaks two-day truce
stories.summary: Russia's defence ministry threatened a massive missile strike on Kyiv if Ukraine breached a two-day ceasefire declared by President Vladimir Putin. The truce was timed to coincide with World War II commemorations on May 8–9.

stories.title: Fire causes ‘substantial damage’ to Book of Mormon theater in New York
stories.summary: A fire broke out in an electrical room at the Eugene O'Neill Theatre on Broadway in New York, causing substantial damage and forcing the temporary closure of the long-running musical The Book of Mormon. The New York fire department described it as a deep-seated blaze, and the cause remains under investigation.

stories.title: Chloe Zhao, Stellan Skarsgard and Demi Moore among Cannes Film Festival jurors
stories.summary: Filmmaker Chloé Zhao, actress Demi Moore, and actor Stellan Skarsgård have been named among the jurors for the upcoming Cannes Film Festival on the French Riviera. The nine-person jury will award prizes including the Palme d'Or for best film. Organisers announced the selections on Monday.

stories.title: Russian forces strike market, church in Vilniansk, casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a market and a church in Vilniansk using drones, killing two people and injuring four others.

stories.title: Trump pleads with South Korea to join US mission to protect Gulf shipping
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump called on South Korea to participate in an international mission to protect shipping routes near Iran. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and General Dan Caine were set to provide further operational details at a Tuesday press conference.

stories.title: Tackling methane emissions key for climate change and energy security: IEA
stories.summary: The International Energy Agency published a report stating that reducing methane emissions is critical for both climate change mitigation and energy security, noting it could help offset the impact of the Iran crisis on global energy supply.

stories.title: Two dead as car ploughs into crowd in Germany's Leipzig
stories.summary: A car drove into a crowd on a street in Leipzig, eastern Germany, on Monday, killing at least two people and injuring several others. The driver was arrested. Germany has experienced multiple car-ramming attacks in recent years, including incidents in Magdeburg, Berlin, and Munich.

stories.title: Oil surges past $115 after reported drone strike on UAE port
stories.summary: Brent crude oil prices surged past $115 per barrel, rising more than five percent, after reports of a drone strike on the port of Fujairah on the UAE's eastern coast. Fujairah serves as a critical oil export point located outside the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Sberbank and T-Bank disable in-app chats between users
stories.summary: Russian banks Sberbank and T-Bank have disabled in-app messaging between users and comments on money transfers, according to the independent Russian outlet Verstka.

stories.title: Mali junta leader names himself defence minister after predecessor killed
stories.summary: Mali's military junta leader appointed himself as defense minister after former Defence Minister Sadio Camara was killed during a major offensive by combined jihadist and separatist forces.

stories.title: Support for Iran war among ‘connected’ US Jews falls again, poll finds
stories.summary: A poll found that support for the Iran war among politically connected American Jews has declined further, dropping to 60 percent after President Trump unilaterally announced a ceasefire on April 8. Support had already been falling in the weeks since the conflict began.

stories.title: Europe, Canada pull together in Yerevan in Trump's shadow
stories.summary: European leaders gathered in Yerevan, Armenia, for a European Political Community summit focused on defense independence amid US threats to cut military support. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney attended for the first time as a non-European leader, signaling closer transatlantic cooperation outside US frameworks.

stories.title: Russia names general sanctioned over Bucha killings as new Aerospace Forces commander
stories.summary: Colonel General Alexander Chaiko, who is under EU sanctions over the Bucha killings, has been appointed commander-in-chief of Russia's Aerospace Forces, replacing General Viktor Afzalov, according to RBC.

stories.title: Three Indian citizens wounded in Iranian drone attack on UAE oil facility
stories.summary: Three Indian citizens were wounded in an Iranian drone attack on an oil facility in the UAE. The UAE Defense Ministry said it intercepted three missiles, while a fourth fell into the sea.

stories.title: Career submariner selected to perform duties of under secretary of the Navy
stories.summary: Retired Navy Captain William Toti, a career submariner, has been selected to perform the duties of under secretary of the Navy. He is serving as the Navy's second-highest-ranking civilian.

stories.title: Iran says managing Strait of Hormuz is its ‘legitimate right’
stories.summary: Iranian First Vice President Mohammad Reza Aref declared that managing the Strait of Hormuz is Tehran's legitimate right, according to ISNA. He stated Iran is not seeking conflict but would respond forcefully if provoked, as tensions over the vital energy corridor continue.

stories.title: Rapper Kid Cudi fires MIA from tour after ‘offensive’ Republican rant
stories.summary: Rapper Kid Cudi removed British artist MIA from his tour after she was booed during a Dallas concert on May 2 for declaring herself a Republican voter. MIA's on-stage remarks went viral, prompting Cudi to end her participation in the tour.

stories.title: Iran fires 'warning shots' as US Navy says its ships entered Gulf via Hormuz
stories.summary: Tensions flared as the U.S. Navy moved ships through the Strait of Hormuz to guide hundreds of stranded commercial vessels, prompting Iran to fire warning shots and call the action a ceasefire violation. The UAE reported coming under attack for the first time since the early April ceasefire, and a British military monitor said two cargo vessels were ablaze off the UAE coast.

stories.title: Zelensky after meeting with Pashinyan: We restore active dialogue between our countries
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan in Yerevan on the sidelines of the 8th European Political Community Summit, marking the first visit by a Ukrainian president to Armenia in 24 years.

stories.title: Poking the bear? Armenia welcomes European leaders in Russia's backyard
stories.summary: Armenia hosted two back-to-back summits featuring European leaders and regional players, including a first-ever EU leaders' gathering in Yerevan. The European Political Community meeting also included Ukraine, NATO members such as the UK and Norway, and Canada. The events took place against a backdrop of U.S. troop drawdown plans for Germany and fresh tariff disputes.

stories.title: Firewalls won’t protect GEOINT companies. Cyber resilience will, if we act now.
stories.summary: Norman Laudermilch argues that geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) companies need to adopt cyber-resilience models that allow continued operations during attacks, rather than relying solely on traditional firewalls. He warns that cyberattacks are increasingly designed to disrupt operations, not just steal data.

stories.title: NYC Jews targeted in 60% of hate crimes last month; swastika sprayed on synagogue
stories.summary: The NYPD reported 30 confirmed anti-Jewish hate crime incidents in New York City during April, comprising roughly 60 percent of all hate crimes that month. A swastika was sprayed on a synagogue, and Nazi graffiti was found on a Kristallnacht memorial and Jewish homes in Queens.

stories.title: Germany positions navy for possible Strait of Hormuz deployment: Report
stories.summary: Germany is repositioning naval assets toward the Middle East in preparation for a possible Strait of Hormuz deployment. The minesweeper Fulda has departed Kiel, and the support vessel Mosel in the Aegean Sea is being readied. Berlin said any mission would require a ceasefire, legal mandate, and parliamentary approval.

stories.title: US destroys six Iranian small boats, shoots down missiles, drones, admiral says
stories.summary: US Admiral Brad Cooper announced that American forces destroyed six Iranian small boats and shot down Iranian missiles and drones in the Strait of Hormuz. Cooper said Iran was attempting to interfere with a US military operation to reopen the waterway to commercial shipping.

stories.title: Israel ramps up raids and incursions across southern Syria
stories.summary: Israeli forces carried out the second-highest number of military violations in southern Syria in April, including raids, incursions, and the establishment of checkpoints. The operations represent a continued pattern of Israeli military activity across Syria's southern border region.

stories.title: Russian missile attack kills five in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, officials say
stories.summary: A Russian missile attack on the town of Merefa in Ukraine's northeastern Kharkiv region killed five people and wounded several others on May 4, according to Ukrainian officials.

stories.title: UAE condemns Iran attacks, warns it reserves right to respond
stories.summary: The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs condemned Iranian missile and drone strikes, calling them a dangerous escalation and describing the attacks as treacherous. Officials warned that the UAE reserves its full and legitimate right to respond, citing a direct threat to national security.

stories.title: Shin Bet quietly reverses ban on Urich accessing Prime Minister’s Office – report
stories.summary: Israel's Shin Bet security agency reportedly reversed its ban on Eli Urich, a key aide to Prime Minister Netanyahu and suspect in several police investigations, granting him renewed access to the Prime Minister's Office after discussions with a senior PMO official.

stories.title: Zelensky, Costa discuss swift opening of all negotiation clusters
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky met European Council President António Costa and said Ukraine expects all six EU accession negotiation clusters to be opened within the current and following month.

stories.title: US says it destroyed Iranian boats, Iran denies naval losses
stories.summary: The United States said its forces destroyed six Iranian small boats and intercepted cruise missiles and drones during operations to secure shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran denied any naval losses, with state television quoting a military official directly contradicting the US account.

stories.title: Iran foreign ministry says US must ‘abandon its excessive demands’
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry called on the United States to abandon what it described as excessive demands. The statement came as President Donald Trump said Washington would begin escorting ships through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Finnish parliament strikes down initiative aimed at restricting weapons purchases from Israel
stories.summary: Finland's parliament rejected a citizens' initiative that sought to restrict weapons purchases from Israel. Finland has placed orders exceeding 800 million euros for Israeli weapons, including the David's Sling air defense system purchased in 2023 for 316 million euros.

stories.title: HRCP highlights severe contraction of civic space, erosion of judicial independence in 2025
stories.summary: The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan launched its 2025 annual report in Islamabad, documenting severe contraction of civic space and erosion of judicial independence. HRCP Chairperson Asad Iqbal Butt said human rights in Pakistan were in their worst state.

stories.title: Outgoing Indian envoy meets Bangladesh FM, discusses bilateral ties
stories.summary: India's outgoing envoy Verma met with Bangladesh's foreign minister to discuss bilateral ties. Verma reaffirmed India's commitment to strengthening people-centric cooperation with Bangladesh across all sectors.

stories.title: Senate Republicans prepare Iran authorisation bill: Report
stories.summary: A group of Senate Republicans is drafting an authorization for the use of military force against Iran, according to Semafor. The effort is proceeding behind closed doors as lawmakers anticipate possible renewed hostilities following President Trump's comments that the initial phase of conflict has ended.

stories.title: Former Qatari aircraft on track for summer Air Force One delivery
stories.summary: A former Qatari aircraft being modified under the Boeing VC-25B Bridge program is on track for delivery as Air Force One by summer. The plane has completed modifications and flight testing and is currently being painted in red, white, and blue livery.

stories.title: Iran drone hits UAE oil hub as Trump deploys navy to Hormuz
stories.summary: An Iranian drone struck a UAE oil facility, causing oil prices to surge. The attack came hours after President Trump deployed US warships to the Strait of Hormuz in an effort to weaken Iran's control over the strategic waterway.

stories.title: UAE quits OPEC: What next for oil, the Gulf, and geopolitics?
stories.summary: The UAE announced its departure from OPEC, a move with significant implications for global oil markets. The exit reflects a broader geopolitical shift and an intensifying rivalry between the UAE and Saudi Arabia over energy policy and regional influence.

stories.title: US’ Bessent urges China to help open Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged China to use its diplomatic leverage to pressure Iran into reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Speaking on Fox News, Bessent noted that China purchases roughly 90 percent of Iran's energy exports. He also asserted that the United States maintains absolute control over the strategic waterway.

stories.title: War update: 59 combat clashes since morning
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces reported 59 combat engagements with Russian troops since the start of the day, with the heaviest Russian activity concentrated on the Huliaipole, Pokrovsk, and Kostiantynivka sectors.

stories.title: Attacks on Belgorod Region Leave At Least 1 Dead, Multiple Wounded
stories.summary: Attacks on Russia's Belgorod region killed at least one person and wounded others. Meanwhile, Russian strikes against Ukraine on the same day killed at least seven people and injured dozens.

stories.title: Flights to Dubai and Sharjah diverted amid Iranian drone and missile attacks
stories.summary: Flights bound for Dubai and Sharjah in the UAE were held or diverted due to Iranian drone and missile attacks disrupting regional airspace, according to Flightradar24. Multiple aircraft experienced delays as the escalation affected flight paths across the area.

stories.title: Sweden arrests Chinese captain of suspected Russia-linked vessel
stories.summary: Swedish authorities arrested the Chinese captain of a seized oil tanker suspected of having Russian links. The captain faces allegations of carrying false documents and violating seaworthiness laws, according to a Swedish prosecutor.
