stories.title: Italy probes detention by Israel of Gaza flotilla activists aboard Italian-flagged vessel
stories.summary: Italian prosecutors opened an unlawful detention investigation after Israeli forces raided a Gaza-bound aid flotilla involving an Italian-flagged vessel. Spanish citizen Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian Thiago Avila were detained and taken to Israel for questioning.

stories.title: Russia and “those sympathetic to it” will try to force Ukraine into capitulation this summer – source in Ukraine’s presidential circle
stories.summary: A source in Ukraine's presidential circle warned that Russia and its sympathizers will attempt to force Ukraine into capitulation during the summer. Russia is demanding control over the Donbas region, where approximately 200,000 civilians still reside.

stories.title: Fatal 2022 China Eastern Airlines plane crash points to deliberate fuel cut-off
stories.summary: Newly released findings from the U.S. National Transportation Safety Board indicate that fuel supply levers on the China Eastern Airlines jet that crashed in 2022 were switched off mid-flight. All 132 people on board were killed when the plane struck a hillside. The evidence supports the theory that the crash was deliberate; China has not yet issued a final report.

stories.title: Iraqi court sentences 4 to prison for promoting Baath Party
stories.summary: An Iraqi court sentenced four individuals to prison for promoting the Baath Party, which was outlawed after the fall of Saddam Hussein. Iraq's de-Baathification policy continues, and while convictions remain rare, investigations still lead to the disqualification of political candidates.

stories.title: Clashes erupt in Suweida between Syrian forces and Druze militia
stories.summary: Armed clashes erupted in Suweida, southern Syria, between Syrian government security forces and a local Druze militia. The fighting marks a renewed escalation in the area's fragile security situation.

stories.title: Death toll from strike on Merefa rises to six, 31 injured
stories.summary: The death toll from a Russian strike on Merefa in the Kharkiv region has risen to six, with 31 people injured.

stories.title: Iran executes three men over involvement in anti-govt protests
stories.summary: Iran executed three men convicted of involvement in anti-government protests that erupted across the country in December and January.

stories.title: Israeli doctors use 3D printer to lengthen woman’s leg for vanishing bone disease
stories.summary: Surgeons at Hadassah Medical Center in Israel used a 3D printer to lengthen a woman's leg by eight centimeters in the country's first such procedure. The patient suffered from Gorham-Stout disease, a rare condition that causes bone tissue to disintegrate.

stories.title: Narendra Modi’s BJP win election in West Bengal for first time
stories.summary: Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won assembly elections in West Bengal for the first time, defeating opposition forces in a state that had been a rare stronghold against Modi's party. The result further consolidates BJP's dominance across India's political landscape.

stories.title: Navy F/A-18Gs over Iran, Venezuela show rise in aerial electronic attack
stories.summary: US Navy F/A-18G Growler electronic warfare aircraft have been deployed over Iran and Venezuela, signaling an increase in aerial electronic attack operations. The missions highlight the expanding role of the Navy's jamming capabilities.

stories.title: Page of Theodore Roosevelt speech hit by bullet in 1912 assassination attempt uncovered
stories.summary: A presidential historian in Pennsylvania has uncovered the first page of a manuscript that helped save Theodore Roosevelt's life during a 1912 assassination attempt. The thick document, carried in Roosevelt's breast pocket, slowed a bullet that struck him while he was campaigning for another presidential term. The signed page had not been seen publicly in over a century.

stories.title: Atmosphere spotted on celestial body in far reaches of solar system
stories.summary: Astronomers detected an atmosphere on a trans-Neptunian object designated (612533) 2002 XV93, an icy body approximately 500 kilometers across in the far reaches of the solar system. The atmosphere is over five million times thinner than Earth's.

stories.title: Oil surges as Strait of Hormuz tensions escalate after UAE drone strike
stories.summary: Oil prices surged sharply following a reported drone strike on a UAE energy facility amid rising Strait of Hormuz tensions. Brent crude rose over 5 percent to $113.78 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate climbed 3.1 percent to $105.11.

stories.title: UAE says missile and drone strikes launched from Iran
stories.summary: The UAE defense ministry reported that four cruise missiles were launched from Iran, and a drone attack caused a fire at an energy facility in Fujairah. The strikes targeted infrastructure near the Strait of Hormuz, a critical corridor for global oil shipments.

stories.title: Missiles fired at U.S. frigate in Strait of Hormuz, claims Iranian media
stories.summary: Iranian media claimed missiles were fired at a U.S. frigate in the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran asserted it had forced a U.S. warship to turn back. U.S. Central Command stated on May 4 that no U.S. Navy ships had been struck.

stories.title: All mainstream Norwegian Jewish organizations condemn Holocaust Center for Holocaust revitalization
stories.summary: An open letter to the HL Center stresses that the Holocaust represents "an industrial, ideologically driven genocide whose aim was the total extermination of the Jewish people."

stories.title: Putin Replaces Aerospace Commander With EU-Sanctioned General Amid Drone Surge, Reports Say
stories.summary: Russia replaced Aerospace Forces commander General Viktor Afzalov with Colonel General Alexander Chaiko, who is under EU sanctions, according to RBC and the pro-war Telegram channel Fighterbomber.

stories.title: Opinion: 'How Pakistan became the ultimate peacemaker between the US and Iran'
stories.summary: An opinion piece discusses Pakistan's role as a mediator between the United States and Iran following U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran in late February. The strikes, conducted without UN Security Council authorization, raised concerns about international law violations and global economic harm.

stories.title: India's Modi eyes important win in opposition-held West Bengal
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's BJP appeared poised for victory in West Bengal state elections as votes were counted under tight security. The state of 100 million people is one of several opposition-held territories where the BJP sought to expand its presence.

stories.title: This Mysterious Occult Healer Is Behind Some of Russia’s Biggest Wartime Protests
stories.summary: Svetlana Lada-Rus, described as a mysterious occult healer in Russia, has emerged as a figure behind some of the country's largest wartime protests against President Putin's government.

stories.title: Three Russian diplomats expelled from Austria over spying accusations
stories.summary: Austria expelled three Russian diplomats over accusations of espionage. The foreign minister said the diplomats gathered intelligence using a network of antennas installed atop Russian diplomatic buildings in Austria.

stories.title: Nepal lodges protest against India over long-running border dispute
stories.summary: Nepal formally protested to India after India and China reached an agreement to resume a religious pilgrimage through a disputed Himalayan mountain pass, reigniting a long-standing border dispute between Nepal and India.

stories.title: Italy probes ‘abduction’ after Israel intercepts Gaza aid flotilla
stories.summary: Italian prosecutors in Rome opened an abduction investigation after Israeli forces intercepted 22 boats from the Global Sumud Flotilla in international waters near Crete. Israel detained 175 activists; most were released, but Spanish national Saif Abu Keshek and Brazilian Thiago Avila were taken into custody in Ashkelon.

stories.title: Here is how you can protect yourself from extreme heat
stories.summary: Karachi, Pakistan, experienced temperatures reaching 44°C on Monday, with the Pakistan Meteorological Department warning that very hot and dry conditions will persist across southern Pakistan. The May outlook indicates above-normal temperatures nationwide with potential for heat spikes.

stories.title: UAE to get 10 C-390 aircraft, up to 10 more in the future
stories.summary: The UAE announced a deal to acquire 10 Embraer C-390 military transport aircraft, with options for up to 10 additional units. Vice President Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan noted it marks the C-390's first entry into the Middle East market and supports the UAE's defense industry localization goals.

stories.title: Russian forces increase combat activity in southern regions – Voloshyn
stories.summary: Ukrainian military spokesperson Voloshyn reported that Russian forces intensified combat activity in southern sectors during April, particularly near Prydniprovske and Oleksandrivka, with the heaviest assaults recorded near Huliaipole.

stories.title: ‘Project Freedom’ marks a classic Trump flip from warmonger to humanitarian
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump shifted from escalatory rhetoric toward Iran to announcing "Project Freedom," a humanitarian initiative promising to free marooned ships. The pivot has been characterized as a move from wartime posturing to pursuing a Nobel Peace Prize narrative.

stories.title: Israeli-Turkish tensions continue to grow as Ankara prepares to launch new flotilla
stories.summary: Diplomatic officials are working behind the scenes to defuse tensions, and Israel is currently utilizing diplomatic channels with Turkey to try to prevent the flotilla from setting sail.

stories.title: Oil jumps, stocks mixed amid Iran, US claims of attack in Strait
stories.summary: US crude was last up 0.1 percent to $102.03 a barrel and Brent rose to $110.36 per barrel, up 2 percent on the day

stories.title: South Korean ship attacked near Strait of Hormuz, South Korea's government confirms

stories.title: Lebanon’s Hezbollah-allied parliament speaker: No talks with Israel until war ends
stories.summary:
US envoy to Beirut says meeting between Lebanon’s President Aoun and Netanyahu would not be a 'loss or concession' for Beirut, but rather an opportunity to ensure Lebanese sovereignty
The post Lebanon

stories.title: US Centcom: Two US-flagged ships have passed through Hormuz
stories.summary: US Central Command announced that two US-flagged merchant vessels safely transited the Strait of Hormuz with escorts from US Navy guided-missile destroyers, contradicting Iranian claims that a US ship was forced to turn back.

stories.title: Belgian driver faces murder trial over 2022 carnival crash that killed seven
stories.summary: A Belgian driver is facing a murder trial over a 2022 crash at a carnival that killed seven people. Investigators found that the driver was filming a social media post and was not watching the road at the time of the incident.

stories.title: Modi’s party poised for big wins in Indian state elections
stories.summary: The ruling BJP's lead in two of four key states is expected to significantly weaken the opposition.

stories.title: What is hantavirus, the illness suspected to have killed several people on an Atlantic cruise ship?
stories.summary: A Dutch cruise ship carrying nearly 150 people of 23 nationalities, including 17 Americans, was waiting for assistance off the coast of Cape Verde after a suspected hantavirus outbreak killed three passengers. At least three others were reported seriously ill, and the World Health Organization is investigating.

stories.title: Russian forces attack Kharkiv and its suburbs with drones; three people injured
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the Kholodnohirskyi district of Kharkiv and its suburbs using drones, injuring at least three people.

stories.title: Cruise ship waiting for help off Cape Verde amid suspected deadly hantavirus outbreak
stories.summary: A Dutch cruise ship with 149 passengers of 23 nationalities remains under strict isolation off Cape Verde following a suspected hantavirus outbreak that killed three passengers and left others seriously ill. The World Health Organization and health authorities are investigating the incident.

stories.title: Philippines: Massive ash cloud fills sky as volcano erupts
stories.summary: Mayon Volcano in the Philippines erupted over the weekend, sending a massive ash cloud into the sky. The eruption forced more than 5,400 people to evacuate to emergency shelters in the surrounding area.

stories.title: Nigerian, Beninese militias kill dozens of Fulani herders in border raid
stories.summary: A state-backed Nigerian militia, operating alongside the military, killed scores of ethnic Fulani herders in a cross-border raid near the Nigeria-Benin border, according to local sources cited by AFP.

stories.title: ‘The death zone’: How Russia is luring Africans to Ukraine
stories.summary: Nine African countries have reported cases of men being recruited and sent to fight on behalf of Russia in the war in Ukraine. The reports highlight Russia's efforts to draw foreign fighters from the African continent into the conflict zone.

stories.title: Russian strikes kill at least eight in Ukraine, drones hit Moscow
stories.summary: Kharkiv and Kherson targeted by missiles, while Russian capital suffers rare hit from drones.

stories.title: Magnitude 6 earthquake strikes Philippines' Samar region
stories.summary: A magnitude 6 earthquake struck the Samar region of the Philippines at a depth of 73.3 kilometers, centered approximately nine kilometers from the coastal town of San Julian.

stories.title: Japan PM says oil crisis has 'enormous impact' in Asia-Pacific
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister stated that the ongoing oil crisis stemming from the Strait of Hormuz tensions is having an "enormous impact" across the Asia-Pacific region. Japan also emphasised the need to secure stable supplies of critical minerals.

stories.title: Hunted by drones it should have seen coming, Israel now sees its Lebanon strategy at risk
stories.summary: Years after drone warfare transformed other battlefields, the IDF seems caught off guard by Hezbollah's effective use of first-person and fiber-optic UAVs, leaving troops in southern Lebanon exposed y

stories.title: Driver injured after truck was struck by United plane landing at Newark airport
stories.summary: A delivery truck driver sustained minor injuries after a United Airlines Boeing 767, arriving from Venice, Italy, struck the tractor trailer while landing at Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey on Sunday. The aircraft also clipped a light pole, which in turn hit a nearby Jeep.

stories.title: Russians request exchange of two North Korean POWs twice – Coordination Headquarters
stories.summary: Russia has twice requested the exchange of two North Korean prisoners of war captured by Ukrainian troops in the Kursk region, according to Ukraine's Coordination Headquarters. Russia has shown no interest in exchanging other foreign fighters who served alongside Russian forces.

stories.title: UAE says Opec exit 'not directed against anyone'
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates stated that its decision to leave Saudi-dominated OPEC was not directed against any country. UAE minister and ADNOC CEO Sultan Al Jaber said the move focused on national priorities, following months of tensions with Saudi Arabia over oil output and foreign policy.

stories.title: Is the West missing the real war behind October 7?
stories.summary: A panel at a New York conference plans to explore the influence, ideology, and geopolitical dynamics behind the October 7 attack, examining aspects that organisers argue Western analysis has overlooked.

stories.title: Israeli attacks kill dozens within days in Lebanon despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported that Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon have killed 77 people since Thursday, despite an existing ceasefire agreement between the two sides.

stories.title: Dagestan Leader Steps Down, Putin Names High Court Judge as Successor
stories.summary: Dagestan's leader stepped down, and Russian President Vladimir Putin named a High Court judge as his successor. The leadership change came weeks after deadly floods struck the North Caucasus region.

stories.title: Iran did not hit a US Navy ship near Strait of Hormuz, US official tells 'Post'
stories.summary: A US official told the Jerusalem Post that no American Navy ship was hit near the Strait of Hormuz, denying claims by Iran's IRGC-aligned Fars News Agency that two missiles struck a US frigate and forced it to turn back.

stories.title: Project Freedom: What we know about Trump's bid to reopen Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump announced that the US Navy would help ships stranded in the Persian Gulf exit through the Strait of Hormuz under a plan called "Project Freedom," though many operational details remain unanswered.

stories.title: Musk vs. Altman: Battle of the tech bros underway in California courthouse
stories.summary: Elon Musk and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman are facing off in a federal courthouse in Oakland, California, in a trial being described as one of Silicon Valley's most consequential legal battles. The case centers on disputes related to artificial intelligence development.

stories.title: War preparations under way in Iran as Hormuz tensions with US escalate
stories.summary: Amid stalled talks and sparring over key waterway, Iranian media say US warship struck, but Washington denies incident.

stories.title: Gaza's hospitals struggle to diagnose as labs shut down
stories.summary: Doctors Without Borders reported that approximately 90 percent of Gaza's health infrastructure has been destroyed or damaged during the war, severely hampering hospitals' ability to conduct diagnostic laboratory work.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone strikes residential tower in Moscow less than 10 kilometers from Kremlin
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone struck one of the towers of the House on Mosfilmovskaya residential complex in Moscow, less than 10 kilometers from the Kremlin. Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin said air defense forces repelled an attack by two drones, and no casualties were reported.

stories.title: Iranian British man who chased Golders Green terrorist: ‘Maybe I can save someone’s life’
stories.summary: Ashkan Asadian, an Iranian-British man in London's Golders Green, recounted chasing and confronting a knife attacker, kicking him and grabbing for his weapon, which allowed a badly wounded Jewish victim to escape.

stories.title: Trump’s ‘Project Freedom’: Can US navy ‘guide’ stuck ships out of Hormuz?
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced "Project Freedom," a plan for the US Navy to escort ships stranded in the Persian Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz, though details on implementation remain unclear.

stories.title: How child soldiers in Sudan become influencers on TikTok
stories.summary: Some child soldiers in Sudan have gained large followings on TikTok, with millions of users celebrating their social media accounts. Psychologists and experts have warned that this trend is dangerous.

stories.title: Most shipping blocked at Hormuz despite US assurances
stories.summary: Despite US assurances under "Project Freedom," vessel tracking data showed most commercial shipping remained blocked at the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, with only a few ships permitted passage into the Gulf of Oman.

stories.title: NATO chief says Europeans have 'gotten message' from Trump on defence
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said European leaders have "gotten the message" from President Trump regarding frustration over the Iran war and are increasing defence contributions. His comments came after Washington announced the withdrawal of 5,000 troops from Germany, ahead of a European Political Community summit in Armenia.

stories.title: UAE says OPEC exit 'not directed against anyone'
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates said its recent exit from OPEC was "not directed against anyone," following months of tensions with Saudi Arabia, the cartel's de facto leader and the world's largest oil exporter.

stories.title: Decoding China: Beijing courts Europe amid US dysfunction
stories.summary: China is working to strengthen ties with European nations as the transatlantic partnership between the United States and European powers faces growing strain, seeking allies for a future multipolar world order.

stories.title: Shares of eBay take off on a $56 billion buyout bid from GameStop's Ryan Cohen
stories.summary: GameStop, led by Ryan Cohen, is pursuing an approximately $56 billion takeover bid for eBay, aiming to compete with Amazon in online retail. The proposal includes using GameStop's roughly 1,600 US stores as drop-off and shipping locations, as well as hosting live sales broadcasts featuring eBay products. eBay shares surged on the news.

stories.title: The loyal, lonely keepers of Sudan's pyramids
stories.summary: At the ancient site of Bajrawiya on Sudan's Island of Meroe, a guard continues to protect 140 pyramids built during the Kingdom of Kush's Meroitic period roughly 2,400 years ago. Three years into Sudan's war between the army and the Rapid Support Forces, the hereditary groundskeeper remains committed to safeguarding the site.

stories.title: Over 100 explosions heard in Chernihiv region; casualties and damage reported
stories.summary: The Chernihiv region of Ukraine recorded 108 explosions over 24 hours from Russian shelling, with enemy forces firing on border areas 56 times. Casualties and damage were reported across the region.

stories.title: Does Shaibani's Cairo visit signal a thaw in Egypt-Syria ties?
stories.summary: Syrian Foreign Minister Ahmad al-Shaibani visited Cairo for talks with Egyptian officials, potentially signalling a cautious thaw in Egypt-Syria relations after a rupture in 2024, amid broader regional tensions.

stories.title: Netanyahu testimony canceled overnight after defense cites security schedule
stories.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's scheduled court testimony was cancelled overnight after his defence team cited security-related scheduling conflicts. The cancellation is the latest in a series of interruptions linked to wartime developments.

stories.title: North Korea ramps up executions over foreign media, says NGO
stories.summary: An NGO reports that North Korea has increased executions of people caught consuming foreign media. Children of North Korean elites are reportedly consuming smuggled South Korean and American entertainment despite the risk of severe punishment under Kim Jong Un.

stories.title: Kirsty, 11, seeks more Kirstys to help raise money for brain tumour research
stories.summary: An 11-year-old girl named Kirsty Waugh from Tunbridge Wells, Kent, who is being treated for a paediatric brain tumour, has tracked down over 10,000 people who share her name worldwide to help raise money for brain tumour research. The namesakes span locations from Colombia to Malaysia to Antarctica.

stories.title: Reform government could cause Truss-style chaos, says renewables industry
stories.summary: Britain's renewable energy industry chief lobbyist Tara Singh warned that a Reform UK government stripping renewable projects of subsidy contracts could trigger economic chaos comparable to the Liz Truss era. RenewableUK said such policies proposed by Nigel Farage's party would severely undermine investor confidence across the UK economy.

stories.title: US tech can use China as ‘listening post’ for global edge, Washington think tank explains
stories.summary: The Information Technology and Innovation Foundation, a Washington-based think tank, argued that US technology companies should maintain their presence in China rather than exit. The ITIF said firms can capitalize on Chinese market revenue, monitor consumer trends, and reinvest profits into US-based research and development to sustain American innovation leadership.

stories.title: First Thing: Trump says US navy will ‘guide’ trapped ships through strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced "Project Freedom," a plan to guide commercial ships trapped in the Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz amid the Iran war. Trump claimed US representatives were having "very positive" discussions with Iran, while Iranian military officials insisted foreign armed forces would not be permitted in the waterway.

stories.title: Congo’s forests under strain from overlapping land use
stories.summary: The Congo Basin's forests, among the world's most important carbon sinks, face growing threats from overlapping land-use pressures. The concerns persist despite renewed global attention on ecosystem protection around Earth Day.

stories.title: Extreme heat could pose threat to players and fans at 2026 FIFA World Cup
stories.summary: Researchers are warning that extreme heat could threaten players, fans, and staff at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Games will take place across the United States, Canada, and Mexico during June and July, among North America's hottest months.

stories.title: ‘Far beyond’ EU and NATO: Armenia hosts EPC summit cast as ‘gateway’ in shifting diplomatic order
stories.summary: Armenia hosted the European Political Community summit, gathering approximately 50 leaders from Europe and Canada in the country's first-ever such event. Analysts described the summit as symbolically significant but structurally limited, serving as an informal platform to address transatlantic tensions, shifting US engagement, and shared security concerns.

stories.title: Europe must face up to ‘tensions’ with Trump, Keir Starmer says
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer acknowledged high "tensions" between Donald Trump and Europe at the European Political Community summit in Armenia. Starmer said Britain would use the summit to begin negotiations on joining the EU's loan scheme for Ukraine, as European leaders grapple with concerns over waning US interest in the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran.

stories.title: Welcome to Breaking Defense Europe. Here’s what you need to know.
stories.summary: Breaking Defense launched a European edition focused on delivering defense news for European audiences, produced by European journalists and analysts.

stories.title: Missile strike on Ukraine's Kharkiv region kills five, destroys infrastructure
stories.summary: A Russian Iskander-type ballistic missile struck the town of Merefa in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, killing five people and wounding at least 18. The strike damaged homes, businesses, and public buildings in an area far from the front lines. There was no immediate comment from Moscow.

stories.title: How the US-Israel war has cemented the IRGC's grip on Iran
stories.summary: Analysts argue that the US-Israeli war against Iran has strengthened the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' grip on power rather than weakening it, pushing Iran further toward a military-dominated state with clerical oversight.

stories.title: ‘Golden week’: Hong Kong draws more mainland Chinese visitors but spending uneven
stories.summary: Hong Kong recorded 714,765 mainland Chinese visitor entries between May 1 and 3 during the Labour Day Golden Week holiday, a 4.8 percent increase over the same period last year. However, industry figures cautioned that uneven spending patterns and more flexible travel habits could limit business gains despite hotel occupancy rates nearing 90 percent.

stories.title: Passenger traffic at Dubai International Airport drops 66% in March amid Iran war
stories.summary: Passenger traffic at Dubai International Airport fell 66 percent in March amid the ongoing Iran war. The airport was forced to shut down multiple times due to drone incidents in its vicinity.

stories.title: Iran's navy warns seafarers amid US effort to 'guide' stranded ships
stories.summary: Iran's navy warned that ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz must coordinate with Iranian authorities. The statement came after the United States announced efforts to guide stranded ships and open the strategic waterway.

stories.title: High Court freezes Second Authority council after state misses response deadline
stories.summary: Israel's High Court Justice Alex Stein froze the Second Authority council after the state missed a response deadline. Stein rejected new extension requests submitted on Sunday, calling them unacceptable regardless of the petitioners' positions.

stories.title: 5.2-magnitude earthquake jolts Islamabad, Pindi
stories.summary: A 5.2-magnitude earthquake struck near the Tajikistan-Xinjiang border region at a depth of 128 kilometers, with tremors felt in Islamabad and Rawalpindi on Monday morning.

stories.title: Wall Street dips, oil prices rise on reports of strike on US Navy vessel near Iran
stories.summary: Wall Street futures declined and oil prices surged on Monday amid conflicting reports of a strike on a US Navy vessel near the Strait of Hormuz. S&P 500 futures fell 0.2 percent and Dow futures dropped 0.5 percent. Oil initially jumped 5 percent before moderating after the US military denied the reports.

stories.title: Israel to buy more F-35 and F-15 warplanes
stories.summary: Israel announced plans to purchase additional F-35 and F-15 warplanes as part of a decade-long military modernization plan valued at $118 billion. The government confirmed the acquisitions as part of its broader defense investment strategy.

stories.title: Iran executes three men in relation to January anti-regime protests
stories.summary: Iran executed three men charged in connection with political protests that took place in January, as part of a wave of near-daily executions. Activists have denounced the killings as an attempt to instil fear amid the ongoing war with the US and Israel and domestic tensions.

stories.title: Hong Kong police launch investigation after elderly couple found dead in flat
stories.summary: Hong Kong police launched an investigation after an elderly couple—an 89-year-old man and his 87-year-old wife—were found dead in their flat at Lok Seen Lau in the Lok Man Sun Chuen estate in To Kwa Wan. A security guard reported a strange smell, and firefighters forced entry to discover both unresponsive on a bed.

stories.title: New alliances shakes up Nigerian political landscape
stories.summary: Nigerian opposition figures Peter Obi and Rabiu Kwankwaso, who finished third and fourth respectively in the last presidential elections, have switched parties. The realignment is reshaping Nigeria's political landscape ahead of future contests.

stories.title: Nigeria to evacuate 130 citizens from South Africa amid xenophobia fears
stories.summary: Nigeria announced plans to evacuate 130 citizens from South Africa amid rising xenophobia fears. Previous outbreaks of anti-foreigner violence in South Africa in 2008, 2015, and 2019 have strained relations between the two countries.

stories.title: Hezbollah chief rejects direct talks with Israel, says move would 'serve Netanyahu and Trump'
stories.summary: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem rejected direct negotiations with Israel, saying such talks would benefit Netanyahu and Trump. He accused Israel of violating the ceasefire agreement more than ten thousand times.

stories.title: Lebanon: Israel deploys new system to intercept Hezbollah drones
stories.summary: The Israeli military has deployed a new interception system in Lebanon designed to counter Hezbollah's explosive-laden drones, as tensions between the two sides continue to escalate despite the ceasefire.

stories.title: Michigan University professor praises anti-Israel student activists in commencement speech
stories.summary: A University of Michigan professor reportedly praised anti-Israel student activists during a commencement speech, deviating from prepared remarks. University President Domenico Grasso said the comments did not reflect the institution's position of neutrality.

stories.title: Labor extends EV tax break to encourage cheaper vehicles amid soaring fuel prices
stories.summary: Australia's Labor government announced it will extend its electric vehicle tax discount in full for another year, after which the benefit will apply only to EVs costing under A$75,000. The move comes amid surging fuel prices linked to the Iran war and rising EV demand, though the government plans to scale back support over the following three years.

stories.title: ‘Made in Europe’ law sets stage for an economic showdown with China
stories.summary: The European Union is moving toward introducing 'Made in Europe' protectionist measures that could trigger an economic confrontation with China, one of its largest trading partners. The push comes as EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has accused Beijing of undermining the rules-based international system, making a stand-off appear increasingly likely amid the ongoing US-China trade war.

stories.title: Army awards AV LASSO award, joining Textron, Uvision in prototyping competition
stories.summary: The US Army awarded an AV LASSO contract, adding a new competitor to a prototyping competition that includes Textron and Uvision. The awarded company will provide its Switchblade 400, a portable anti-armor loitering munition with medium range.

stories.title: Reuters: Senior Iranian official says Iran fired warning shot at US warship
stories.summary: A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Iran fired a "warning shot" toward a US Navy vessel to prevent its entry into the Strait of Hormuz, though it remains unclear whether the ship sustained any damage. US Central Command denied reports of an attack.

stories.title: UAE condemns Iranian attack on Adnoc tanker transiting Hormuz
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates condemned an Iranian drone attack on an Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (Adnoc) tanker attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz. Two drones targeted the vessel, but no injuries were reported. The UAE called the action "piracy" by Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps.

stories.title: Africa’s telecom towers turn to solar as diesel costs surge
stories.summary: Rising diesel prices, linked in part to the Iran conflict, are accelerating a shift across Africa's telecom industry from fuel-powered generators to solar energy systems. Operators are adopting solar to keep mobile networks running while controlling costs.

stories.title: France’s Jean-Luc Mélenchon announces 2027 presidential bid
stories.summary: Jean-Luc Mélenchon, the 74-year-old leader of France's radical left party La France Insoumise, announced he will run for the French presidency for a fourth time in the 2027 election. He cited the urgency of opposing wars waged by the US and Israel in the Middle East as motivation for his candidacy.

stories.title: Trump says US will 'guide' ships in Hormuz despite Iran warnings
stories.summary: President Trump reiterated that the US Navy would guide ships through the Strait of Hormuz despite Iranian warnings. A tanker near the UAE reported being struck by a projectile shortly after Trump's announcement.

stories.title: Shropshire council staff met with rising ‘abuse and intimidation’ over removal of flags
stories.summary: Shropshire council in England reported rising abuse, harassment, and intimidation of staff and councillors linked to the removal of unauthorised Union Jack and St George's flags. The authority said workers have been threatened while carrying out routine duties including street lighting repairs.

stories.title: ‘Hegemonic power’: How Modi’s BJP won India’s Bengal for the first time
stories.summary: India's ruling BJP, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, won seats in West Bengal for the first time, leveraging religious polarisation and anti-incumbency sentiment against the state's ruling party.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Komyshuvakha with guided bombs; one person killed
stories.summary: Russian forces conducted a guided bomb airstrike on Komyshuvakha in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, killing one man. The strike is part of continued Russian aerial attacks on communities in the region.

stories.title: Israel seizes nearly 60 percent of Gaza as it plans to resume war, report says
stories.summary: Israeli Army Radio reported that Israel has expanded control over nearly 60 percent of the Gaza Strip despite the ceasefire. Senior military officials are pushing to resume fighting, with operational plans completed and awaiting political approval.

stories.title: No US Navy ships struck by Iran, says US Central Command
stories.summary: US Central Command denied Iranian state media claims that two missiles struck a US warship in the Strait of Hormuz, stating no US Navy ships were hit. Centcom said US forces are supporting "Project Freedom" and enforcing a naval blockade on Iranian ports.

stories.title: Russia hit a record oil revenue month—yet the federal budget still came up short
stories.summary: Russia recorded a record month for oil revenue, but its federal budget still ran a deficit. Sberbank's CFO forecasts the ruble will fall to 90 per dollar, and three Russian ports have seen cargo drops of 13–43%.

stories.title: Russia’s oil revenue nearly doubled in March. Its own bankers still expect a crash
stories.summary: Russia's oil revenue nearly doubled in March, but Sberbank's chief financial officer forecasts the ruble will weaken to 90 per dollar. Three Russian ports have already recorded cargo volume drops ranging from 13 to 43 percent.

stories.title: A diary of America's wars with photographer Peter van Agtmael
stories.summary: Photographer Peter van Agtmael has spent over two decades documenting US wars in Iraq and Afghanistan and their domestic repercussions. His photo book "Look at the U.S.A.: A Diary of War and Home" pairs battlefield images with snapshots of post-9/11 American life to illustrate the connection between distant conflicts and their impact at home.

stories.title: Japan, Australia agree to deepen cooperation on energy, defence and critical minerals
stories.summary: Japan and Australia agreed to deepen cooperation on energy, defense, and critical minerals. Australia supplies nearly half of Japan's liquefied natural gas, while Japan is among Australia's top five suppliers of refined gasoline and diesel.

stories.title: All 8 Miners Confirmed Dead After Coal Mine Collapse in Russia’s Far East
stories.summary: All eight miners were confirmed dead after a coal mine collapse in Russia's Far East. The mining company's CEO attributed the collapse to melting permafrost.

stories.title: Likud activist, a convicted felon, tells Knesset panel that teens ‘didn’t mean to kill’ pizza worker
stories.summary: Likud activist and convicted felon Rafi Kedoshim sparked outrage at a Knesset committee hearing on teen violence by claiming that teenagers involved in the killing of a pizza worker "didn't mean to kill."

stories.title: Cruise ship at centre of suspected hantavirus outbreak blocked from docking in Cape Verde
stories.summary: Cape Verde authorities refused to allow a cruise ship suspected of harboring a hantavirus outbreak to dock in its ports, citing public health concerns. Three passengers aboard the Atlantic cruise ship have died, and the outbreak is under investigation by global health officials. Hantavirus is a rare respiratory infection primarily transmitted by rodents.

stories.title: Green group warns of disturbance to uninhabited island known for breeding seabirds
stories.summary: A Hong Kong environmental group reported that people were landing on an uninhabited island in southern Hong Kong waters during mainland China's Labour Day Golden Week holiday. The island is a known breeding site for terns, and the disturbance coincides with the seabirds' breeding season.

stories.title: South Africa: South Africa's Road Rage Problem Goes Deeper Than Bad Drivers
stories.summary: A report by South Africa's Institute for Security Studies highlights a growing road rage problem linked to accumulated stress, inequality, and normalized violence. The presence of firearms can escalate road incidents to fatal outcomes.

stories.title: Lebanon warned against direct meeting with Netanyahu amid war
stories.summary: Reports that Lebanese President Joseph Aoun may meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the White House triggered sharp criticism in Lebanon and across the Arab world, amid Israel's ongoing military operations.

stories.title: New power outages reported in four regions due to enemy shelling, says Ukrenergo
stories.summary: Russian attacks caused new power outages affecting consumers in Ukraine's Donetsk, Dnipropetrovsk, Kharkiv, and Kherson regions, according to state grid operator Ukrenergo. The outages were reported as of the morning of May 4.

stories.title: NATO is dead. Meet CALM.
stories.summary: A commentary piece discusses alternatives to NATO, proposing a new alliance concept referred to as CALM. The article notes that open debate about replacing the Alliance, long considered taboo, shifted after 2026.

stories.title: Lift technician dies after 10-metre fall down shaft at Hong Kong luxury estate
stories.summary: A 26-year-old lift technician died after falling 10 metres down a lift shaft he was repairing at Pacific View, a luxury residential estate on Tai Tam Road in Stanley, Hong Kong. The worker suffered fatal head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene. Police are investigating the cause of the accident.

stories.title: Austria expels 3 Russian diplomats over signals spying
stories.summary: Austria declared three Russian diplomats personae non gratae over an array of satellite dishes—described as an "antenna forest"—on rooftops of Russian diplomatic buildings in Vienna. Austrian domestic intelligence had long warned the installations could be used to intercept other states' satellite communications.

stories.title: FO says 22 crew members on Iranian ship seized by US have been evacuated to Pakistan
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office confirmed that 22 crew members of the Iranian vessel M/V Touska, seized by U.S. forces, were evacuated to Pakistan for repatriation as a confidence-building measure by the United States.

stories.title: Hezbollah deploys hard-to-jam fibre optic drones, shifting battlefield tactics
stories.summary: Hezbollah has shifted battlefield tactics in its conflict with Israel by deploying fibre optic drones that can evade Israeli electronic jamming systems. The escalation followed exchanges of rockets and airstrikes linked to broader regional tensions involving Iran. A US-brokered ceasefire took effect in mid-April but remains fragile amid ongoing clashes in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Republicans split with Trump and back Haitians – to save their seats
stories.summary: Several Republicans in Ohio are breaking with President Trump's stance on Haitian immigrants, recognizing the community's role in reviving local economies. In Springfield, Ohio, where an estimated 10,000 Haitians reside, vulnerable Republican lawmakers are reluctant to follow Trump's hardline immigration rhetoric ahead of elections.

stories.title: What’s behind the KMT’s internal splits over Taiwanese defence spending?
stories.summary: Taiwan's main opposition party, the Kuomintang, faces widening internal divisions over a proposed NT$1.25 trillion (US$40 billion) special defence budget put forward by the ruling Democratic Progressive Party. The US de facto ambassador in Taipei, Raymond Greene, has pressured the KMT on the issue ahead of upcoming local elections.

stories.title: Modi's BJP conquers Bengal, one of India's toughest political frontiers
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party made significant electoral gains in West Bengal, traditionally an opposition stronghold. The result in the state of 100 million people could reshape regional politics and the BJP's national trajectory.

stories.title: Boeing faces civil trial over 737 MAX crash
stories.summary: Boeing is facing a civil trial related to a 737 MAX crash. The company has acknowledged that its anti-stall software, known as MCAS, was implicated in the accident that led to the litigation.

stories.title: More than 300 families evacuate in Philippines due to ashfall from volcano
stories.summary: More than 300 families in the Philippines evacuated after massive ashfall from a volcano scattered over 87 villages in three towns. No deaths or injuries were reported, but poor visibility affected motorists.

stories.title: Italian prosecutors open investigation into kidnapping of Gaza flotilla activists
stories.summary: Prosecutors in Rome opened a kidnapping investigation after two activists aboard a Gaza-bound aid flotilla flying an Italian flag were seized by Israeli forces in international waters. The activists are currently imprisoned in Israel.

stories.title: Africa: Turkey Raises Residence Permit Fee By 930 Percent for Nigerians, 36 Other African Countries
stories.summary: Turkey's Directorate General of Migration Management announced residence permit fee increases of up to 930 percent for nationals of Nigeria and approximately 36 other African countries.

stories.title: Sudan: Cabinet Underscores Combating Corruption, Smuggling, and Narcotics
stories.summary: Sudan's cabinet met in Khartoum under the chairmanship of Dr. Kamil Idris to review anti-corruption, anti-smuggling, and anti-narcotics efforts. The meeting emphasized the role of the Ministry of Interior and General Intelligence Service in combating these issues.

stories.title: Coordination Headquarters hopes to resolve “Chechen issue” regarding POWs soon
stories.summary: Ukraine's Coordination Headquarters for the Treatment of Prisoners of War expressed hope for the near-term repatriation of all Ukrainian prisoners currently held in Chechnya. The statement addressed what officials termed the "Chechen issue" regarding POW treatment and return.

stories.title: Europe will not submit to an ‘insular and brutal world’, says Carney
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, the first non-European leader to attend a European Political Community meeting, said Europe will not submit to a more "brutal world" and can serve as the foundation for rebuilding a new international order. He spoke in Armenia amid tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and doubts about US commitment to NATO.

stories.title: Car show turns to tragedy as monster truck drives into crowd in Colombia
stories.summary: A monster truck lost control during a car show in Colombia and drove into a crowd of spectators, turning the event into a tragedy as onlookers captured the incident.

stories.title: ‘Israel is not implementing the ceasefire agreement in Gaza’
stories.summary: Accusations have emerged that Israel is failing to implement the terms of the ceasefire agreement in Gaza, raising concerns about compliance with the deal's provisions.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drone Slams Into Skyscraper Near Central Moscow
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone struck a skyscraper near central Moscow. The attack occurred days before Russia's annual Victory Day military parade on Red Square.

stories.title: US denies ship hit by Iranian missiles, Axios reporter says
stories.summary: A senior US official denied that any American vessel was struck by Iranian missiles near the Strait of Hormuz, responding to reports from Iran's Fars news agency that two missiles hit a US warship near Jask.

stories.title: Bulls in control as PSX gains 4,000 points during intraday trade
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 stock index surged approximately 4,000 points during intraday trading on Monday, driven by investor reaction to developments surrounding Iran-U.S. tensions and efforts to stabilize global energy routes.

stories.title: Interview: Gen. Ronald Clark, US Army Pacific commander
stories.summary: US Army Pacific commander Gen. Ronald Clark discussed the 41st iteration of the Balikatan military exercises, describing them as a "full-circle event." Clark has led USARPAC since November 8, 2024.

stories.title: US to 'guide' stranded ships from Hormuz: What we know about 'Project Freedom'
stories.summary: The United States launched "Project Freedom" on Monday to guide commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing blockade caused by the Iran war. The US-led Joint Maritime Information Center advised vessels to transit through Omani waters via an enhanced security area, potentially involving guided-missile destroyers, over 100 aircraft, and 15,000 service members.

stories.title: Dubai airport passenger traffic drops 66 percent over Iran war
stories.summary: Dubai's airport reported a 66 percent decline in passenger traffic linked to the Iran conflict, with first-quarter 2026 figures falling 21 percent to 18.6 million passengers as Iranian retaliatory strikes disrupted regional air travel.

stories.title: Hong Kong puts its own spin on DeepSeek with China-chip AI push abroad
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Generative AI Research and Development Centre, a government-backed lab, is preparing to launch HKGAI-V3, a new AI model built on DeepSeek V4 architecture and optimized to run entirely on Chinese-made chips. The centre plans to unveil the model in the first half of this year and export its capabilities to overseas markets.

stories.title: Russian strike on Merefa in Kharkiv region: Death toll climbs to four, 16 injured
stories.summary: A Russian strike on the town of Merefa in Ukraine's Kharkiv region killed four people and injured at least 16 others, according to reports as of the morning of the attack.

stories.title: What is the Ukrainian anti-drone system Sky Map being used in the Gulf?
stories.summary: Ukraine's "Sky Map" anti-drone system, which uses thousands of acoustic sensors and interceptors to detect and destroy incoming drones, is reportedly being deployed in the Gulf region.

stories.title: US close to delivering Israeli 'Gideon' KC-46 refueling aircraft for future Iran attacks
stories.summary: The US is close to delivering the first KC-46 aerial refueling aircraft, designated "Gideon," to Israel. The tanker completed its maiden test flight in the US and is expected to arrive in Israel within approximately one month, potentially supporting future operations against Iran.

stories.title: ‘Scarlet Swan’ chat member says Russia’s FSB forced her to read prepared script in staged terrorism video
stories.summary: Sofia Chepik, a member of the "Scarlet Swan" Telegram chat group, was released from a Moscow detention facility on May 3 after serving 15 days on a hooliganism charge. She alleged that Russia's FSB compelled her to read a prepared script for a staged terrorism video.

stories.title: Sea of Galilee trail plan that keeps parts of shore off-limits to public sparks outcry
stories.summary: A proposed 32-kilometre hiking trail around Israel's Sea of Galilee has drawn criticism from environmental groups, who oppose plans to include fences, locked gates, and bypass routes that would restrict public access to parts of the shoreline.

stories.title: Survey finds fewer than 25% of Gaza border residents feel safe, 40% don’t trust state
stories.summary: A survey by the Tekuma Directorate found that fewer than 25 percent of residents near the Gaza border feel safe and 40 percent distrust the state, though life satisfaction and optimism about the future have increased.

stories.title: Winning peace in Lebanon is harder than winning war
stories.summary: Analysts note that achieving a lasting peace in Lebanon remains more difficult than military operations, requiring consideration of the country's complex history and shifting geopolitical dynamics in the region.

stories.title: Iran warns of ceasefire violation as U.S. plans to escort Hormuz ships
stories.summary: Iran's parliamentary national security commission warned that any US interference in the new maritime regime of the Strait of Hormuz would be considered a violation of the ceasefire between the two countries.

stories.title: Iranian media: Two missiles hit US warship which ignored Iran’s warnings
stories.summary: Iran's Fars news agency reported that two missiles struck a US warship near Jask in the Strait of Hormuz after it ignored Iranian warnings, and that the vessel subsequently turned back from the area.

stories.title: Iran says ships being ‘guided’ by US through Hormuz must work with its armed forces
stories.summary: Iran declared that any commercial ships being "guided" by the US through the Strait of Hormuz must coordinate their transit with Iranian armed forces. Tehran warned it would attack any foreign military forces entering the waterway under the US plan, as hundreds of ships remain trapped in the Gulf due to the Iran war.

stories.title: Iranian military commander warns ‘supporters’ of US over Hormuz
stories.summary: Iranian Major-General Ali Abdollahi warned that nations supporting the United States should exercise caution before entering the Strait of Hormuz to escort commercial vessels. He accused the US military of jeopardizing vessel security and threatening global trade stability through aggressive actions in the waterway.

stories.title: Over thousand Ukrainians held captive by Russia since 2022 – Coordination Headquarters
stories.summary: Ukraine's Coordination Headquarters reported that over one thousand Ukrainian military personnel and civilians have been held captive by Russia since 2022.

stories.title: Money, power, exile: Inside an Iranian exile’s war on regime-linked wealth in Canada
stories.summary: An investigation profiled an Iranian exile in Canada working to expose regime-linked wealth. The activist began blogging under a pseudonym at age 15 and has since focused on tracking financial assets tied to the Iranian government.

stories.title: In the PR battle for AI data centres, tech giants have a blue-collar ally
stories.summary: Building trades unions in the United States have emerged as allies for tech companies in the public relations effort surrounding the construction of AI data centres.

stories.title: Village braces itself for closure of Spain's largest nuclear plant
stories.summary: A village in Spain is preparing for the closure of the country's largest nuclear plant. No additional details were provided in the source material about the timeline or specific community impacts.

stories.title: Hantavirus: Three cruise ship passengers die in suspected outbreak
stories.summary: Three passengers on a cruise ship in the Atlantic Ocean have died in a suspected hantavirus outbreak, with three more passengers ill. Hantavirus, which is primarily spread to humans through contact with rodent urine, droppings, and saliva, has a fatality rate of approximately 40 percent.

stories.title: Trump administration claims food aid fraud but critics say ‘there’s no evidence’
stories.summary: US Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins claimed without evidence that 14,000 SNAP food aid recipients included owners of luxury vehicles such as Ferraris and Bentleys. Critics called the assertion part of a disinformation campaign aimed at undermining the 87-year-old nutritional assistance program that supports tens of millions of low-income Americans.

stories.title: Nigeria: Dangote Denies Rift With Tony Elumelu, Rejects Refinery Funding Claims
stories.summary: Dangote Group denied allegations of a rift between its president, Aliko Dangote, and businessman Tony Elumelu. The company also rejected claims that the Dangote Petroleum Refinery was financed through personal borrowing from friends.

stories.title: Trump’s War Exposes the Weakness of Middle Powers
stories.summary: An analysis argues that collective action by middle powers will not be sufficient to shape the global order amid the challenges posed by the Trump administration's war policies. The assessment suggests that lesser powers lack the leverage needed to influence major geopolitical outcomes.

stories.title: Iran says it fired missiles at US warship to prevent it entering Hormuz
stories.summary: Iranian state media reported that Iran's forces fired two missiles at a US Navy destroyer near the Strait of Hormuz to prevent it from entering the waterway, though accounts of the incident are disputed.

stories.title: Shooting at lake near Oklahoma City in U.S. injures at least 10
stories.summary: A shooting at a gathering of young people near Arcadia Lake in Edmond, Oklahoma, injured at least 10 people. Authorities received multiple reports of gunfire at approximately 9 p.m.

stories.title: Shooting at US party sends at least 13 to hospital
stories.summary: A shooting at a gathering of young people near Arcadia Lake outside Oklahoma City on Sunday night sent at least 13 people to hospitals. Edmond police said they received reports of gunfire around 9 pm. No arrests had been made as of late Sunday.

stories.title: Russian forces carry out airstrike on Shostka, city council building and houses damaged
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out an airstrike on the city of Shostka in Ukraine, damaging the city council building and private homes. Three women were injured in the attack.

stories.title: Israeli commander boasts of West Bank killings unseen since 1967
stories.summary: The head of Israel's Central Command said Israeli troops are killing Palestinians in the West Bank at levels not seen since 1967. The statement referenced ongoing military operations across the occupied territory.

stories.title: India's Modi faces key test as vote count underway
stories.summary: Vote counting began in key Indian state elections, with particular focus on West Bengal, where Prime Minister Narendra Modi's BJP sought to unseat Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee's Trinamool Congress. Elections took place across five states and territories in April and May.

stories.title: 18 Peruvians deceived into fighting for Russia return home, with more repatriations expected
stories.summary: Eighteen Peruvian citizens who were deceived into traveling to Russia and forced to fight against Ukraine have been repatriated over the past two weeks, according to Peru's Foreign Ministry. Additional repatriations are expected.

stories.title: Europe, Canada leaders hold Yerevan talks in Trump’s shadow
stories.summary: European and Canadian leaders held talks in Yerevan, Armenia, under the shadow of U.S. President Donald Trump's foreign policy. The ongoing Iran war has deepened divisions in transatlantic relations, adding urgency to the discussions.

stories.title: Death toll from Turkey school shooting rises to 10
stories.summary: The death toll from a school shooting in Turkey rose to 10, sparking public outrage. President Erdogan responded by dismissing a deputy education minister and pledging to introduce new gun restrictions.

stories.title: Two killed in Israeli attack on southern Lebanon
stories.summary: At least two people were killed in Israeli air strikes on the town of Shhour in southern Lebanon, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The strikes followed Israeli military evacuation warnings issued to residents in several towns in the Tyre and Bint Jbeil districts.

stories.title: Russian officials bar women from helping clean oil-fouled beaches, citing concern for reproductive health
stories.summary: Officials in Tuapse, Russia, and Emergency Situations Ministry representatives barred female volunteers from participating in cleanup of oil-fouled beaches, citing concerns about reproductive health, according to a Kommersant correspondent.

stories.title: No ceasefire in Lebanon while Israeli attacks ongoing, says Hezbollah
stories.summary: Hezbollah Secretary General Naim Qassem stated there is no ceasefire in Lebanon while Israeli attacks continue. He criticized direct talks between Lebanese and Israeli authorities and called for security guarantees before negotiations. Qassem reaffirmed Hezbollah's commitment to armed resistance to prevent Israeli gains in Lebanon.

stories.title: Dar and Iran's Araghchi discuss regional situation, Pakistan's ongoing diplomatic efforts
stories.summary: Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar spoke with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi about the regional situation and Pakistan's diplomatic efforts for peace. Araghchi praised Pakistan's constructive mediation role between involved parties.

stories.title: Massive search continues for two missing US soldiers in Morocco
stories.summary: US, Moroccan, and allied forces launched a large-scale land, air, and sea search operation in the Cap Draa Training Area of Morocco after two US service members went missing during activities in the region.

stories.title: 30 students celebrating end of high school hospitalized with eye injuries from foam spray
stories.summary: Thirty Israeli high school students were hospitalised with eye injuries, including cornea damage, after using foam spray during end-of-school celebrations. Doctors warned against using foam spray without eye protection.

stories.title: Iran threatens to attack US warships that enter Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran warned that any US military vessels entering the Strait of Hormuz will be attacked, according to Ali Abdollahi, head of the unified command of the Iranian military. The threat came after President Trump announced the US Navy would accompany trapped ships out of the strait.

stories.title: Daily Briefing May 4 – ‘One big failure’: An IDF official on the Iran war so far
stories.summary: An IDF official described Israel's war with Iran as "one big failure," while military correspondent Emanuel Fabian reported on the fragile ceasefire in southern Lebanon, preparations for further Gaza operations, and internal IDF tensions.

stories.title: Oil spill from refinery struck by Ukraine has contaminated 60 kilometers of Russian coastline, ecologist says
stories.summary: An oil spill following Ukrainian drone strikes on a refinery has contaminated approximately 60 kilometers of Russian coastline near Tuapse. Municipal district head Sergei Boyko said the city beach would be cleaned by June 1 in time for resort season.

stories.title: Pitch perfect diplomacy? North Korean footballers head to South Korea
stories.summary: North Korea's Naegohyang Women's FC confirmed participation in the 2025–2026 AFC Women's Champions League, which will require travel to South Korea. The visit would mark the first time North Korean athletes have set foot on South Korean soil in eight years, raising hopes that sports diplomacy could help ease bilateral tensions.

stories.title: Any vessel violating Iran’s rules will be stopped by force, says IRGC
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps stated that any vessel passing through the Strait of Hormuz in violation of Iran's blockade will be met with military force. The IRGC Navy also issued a new map delineating the areas of the strait under Iranian armed forces' control.

stories.title: Russia adds nearly 100 professions to list eligible for alternative civilian service
stories.summary: Russia's Labor Ministry expanded the list of professions eligible for alternative civilian service by nearly 100 positions, raising the total from 271 to 363.

stories.title: Russian forces attack Kharkiv-Chuhuiv road with drone, leaving two people injured
stories.summary: On the morning of May 4, Russian forces struck the Kyiv-Kharkiv-Dovzhanskyi highway in Chuhuiv district with a drone, targeting vehicles on the road and injuring two people.

stories.title: Reform UK plan to set up migrant detention centres in Green-voting areas condemned by other parties – UK politics live
stories.summary: Reform UK proposed placing migrant detention centres in areas that elected Green Party council leaders or MPs. Other parties and commentators condemned the plan, with the British Future thinktank calling it potentially illegal and logically contradictory.

stories.title: ‘No pilgrims’: Regional war hushes Iraq’s holy cities
stories.summary: Iraq's holy cities have seen pilgrim visits virtually disappear due to the regional war. The cities previously drew pilgrims from Iran, Lebanon, Gulf states, India, Afghanistan, and other countries.

stories.title: Transgender student sues Hong Kong school over ‘discriminatory’ hair policy
stories.summary: A transgender student named Oscar Fung King-ho filed a lawsuit against a Hong Kong secondary school, alleging discrimination over a policy requiring short hair conforming to her sex assigned at birth. Her lawyers sought damages, citing public humiliation by teachers.

stories.title: Two worlds collide: the regulatory battlefield hanging over the EU’s ties with China
stories.summary: Cybersecurity tests conducted in a decommissioned Norwegian mine on Chinese-made Yutong electric buses revealed vulnerabilities including potential remote access, contributing to new EU regulations affecting EU-China relations.

stories.title: China ‘Madman of Science’ believes budget space travel is viable after low-cost rocket launch
stories.summary: Chinese self-taught innovator Lu Yulong and his five-person team built and launched the Shenzhen Pioneer rocket in Qinghai province in February. The 12-meter liquid rocket reached 3,700 meters altitude, setting a regional record and demonstrating low-cost space launch feasibility.

stories.title: Punjab cops in a bind over transfer to ‘hard areas’
stories.summary: Pakistan's Establishment Division transferred 10 Punjab police officers to postings in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, designated as "hard areas." Concerns were raised because many of the transferred officers are near retirement age, contrary to a rotation policy meant for younger officers.

stories.title: Iran threatens to attack US warships that enter Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran warned it would attack US warships attempting to enter the Strait of Hormuz, as President Trump announced plans for the US Navy to guide ships trapped in the strait to safety.

stories.title: Africa: African Groups Push for Stronger Disease Surveillance Systems
stories.summary: More than 20 civil society and community organizations across Africa urged governments to prioritize epidemic preparedness and strengthen disease surveillance systems, warning that weak infrastructure could undermine responses to future outbreaks.

stories.title: Southern Africa: Misa Launches Sixth Edition of the Southern Africa Press Freedom Report
stories.summary: The Media Institute of Southern Africa launched the sixth edition of its Southern Africa Press Freedom Report, which highlights a widespread crisis of technology-facilitated gender-based violence.

stories.title: NATO chief says Europeans have ‘gotten the message’ from Trump on defence
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General stated that European allies have received President Trump's message on increasing defence spending, amid US criticism that some NATO members are not contributing enough to support the US-Israel conflict with Iran.

stories.title: South Africa: Fuel and Fertiliser Costs Drive Up the Price of a Basic Food Basket
stories.summary: Rising fuel and fertiliser costs, partly linked to the U.S.-Iran conflict, are driving up the price of a basic food basket in South Africa. Analysts noted potential opportunistic pricing by processors and retailers even when producer prices stabilized.

stories.title: NATO's Rutte: Europeans are ensuring agreements with US on military bases are implemented
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said European nations are ensuring agreements with the US on military bases are being implemented. He added that an increasing number of European countries are pre-positioning naval assets, including minehunters and minesweepers, near the Gulf for potential future operations.

stories.title: Kenya: Duale Backs Kenya-Somalia Border Reopening to Boost Trade
stories.summary: Kenya's Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale expressed support for reopening the Kenya-Somalia border, stating the move would enhance trade and ease the movement of people and goods between the two nations.

stories.title: Israeli minister's 'disgusting noose cake' draws widespread criticism
stories.summary: Israeli Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir drew widespread condemnation over a birthday cake featuring a noose design. Separately, Amsterdam became the first capital city to ban advertising for meat and fossil fuels, and The Washington Post reported on a Ukrainian soldier trapped in a combat kill zone.

stories.title: Drone gun-running ring from Jordan to West Bank busted, five suspects indicted
stories.summary: Israel's Shin Bet, IDF, and police dismantled a cross-border weapons smuggling network that used drones to transport arms from Jordan into the West Bank. Five suspects were indicted after dozens of weapons were trafficked into Israeli-controlled territory.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone hits upmarket Moscow high-rise ahead of Victory Day celebrations
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone struck a high-rise residential building in an upscale Moscow neighborhood ahead of Russia's Victory Day celebrations. The attack came as the Kremlin prepared for a scaled-back military parade on May 9.

stories.title: UAE says it left Opec on good terms, Iran criticises exit
stories.summary: UAE Energy Minister Suhail Al Mazrouei said the UAE departed Opec and Opec+ on good terms and would continue cooperating with member states. Iran criticized the UAE's exit, with Iranian officials calling negative reactions toward fellow members unconstructive.

stories.title: Air Defense Forces shoot down 135 of 155 Russian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Defense Forces intercepted 135 of 155 Russian drones launched against Ukraine since the evening of May 3, leaving 20 drones unaccounted for.

stories.title: ‘I can’t feel my leg’: Israeli gunfire disables teenagers in West Bank
stories.summary: Al Jazeera reported from a refugee camp in the occupied West Bank where Israeli soldiers have shot and injured multiple teenagers, leaving some with permanent disabilities. The report documents cases of young people killed or maimed by Israeli gunfire in the territory.

stories.title: Iranian ship, crew seized by US transferred to Pakistan: report
stories.summary: The United States transferred the Iranian vessel M/V Touska and its 22 crew members to Pakistan for repatriation after seizing the ship for failing to comply with a US-imposed blockade on Iranian ports. Six other passengers had been transferred to another country earlier.

stories.title: Iran foreign ministry: US must abandon ‘excessive demands’
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei blamed the United States for the slow pace of diplomacy to end the war, describing US negotiating demands as "excessive." He called on Washington to adopt a more reasonable approach and said all countries involved directly or indirectly bear responsibility.

stories.title: Iran threatens American ships if they enter Hormuz, as US kicks off ‘Project Freedom’
stories.summary: Iran threatened to attack American ships entering the Strait of Hormuz as the US launched "Project Freedom" to move stranded commercial vessels. US officials indicated the initiative may not necessarily involve direct Navy escorts, while France said it would not participate in the "unclear" operation.

stories.title: In Moscow, drone strikes high-rise building 6 kilometers from Kremlin
stories.summary: Moscow Mayor Sergey Sobyanin reported that a drone struck a high-rise building in Moscow on the night of May 4, approximately six kilometers from the Kremlin. No further details on casualties were immediately provided.

stories.title: Iran's navy attacks US ship with missiles, CENTCOM denies strike
stories.summary: Iran's navy reportedly fired missiles at a US ship near the Strait of Hormuz, while US Central Command denied any American vessel was struck. The incident occurred as President Trump announced plans for the Navy to escort ships through the waterway.

stories.title: Iran warns US entry into Strait of Hormuz 'will be attacked'
stories.summary: Iran warned that any US forces entering the Strait of Hormuz would be attacked, after President Trump announced the US Navy would guide commercial ships through the waterway. The threat was issued by Iran's unified military command.

stories.title: Russian missile turns Monday morning in Kharkiv Oblast into a mass-casualty scene — 5 dead, 19 injured in Kharkiv Oblast
stories.summary: A Russian missile strike in Kharkiv Oblast on Monday morning killed five people and injured 19 others. The attack damaged an auto service station, four shops, and residential buildings in the region.

stories.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 66 as Trump announces Hormuz mission?
stories.summary: On day 66 of the Iran conflict, US President Donald Trump announced a new naval mission in the Strait of Hormuz. The announcement came after Iran said it had received a US response to its peace proposal, though diplomatic progress remains uncertain.

stories.title: This Energy Crisis Is Undoing the Last Ones
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the Western-led global order established after the 20th century's major energy crises is weakening. The current energy crisis is described as undermining the institutional and geopolitical frameworks that emerged from previous shocks.

stories.title: Iran warns US Navy to keep out of Hormuz after Trump says US will help stranded ships
stories.summary: Iran warned the U.S. Navy to stay out of the Strait of Hormuz after President Trump announced plans to assist stranded ships. Vessels have reportedly been trapped in the strait for over two months and are running low on food and supplies.

stories.title: Trump says US operation will aid ships stranded in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced the U.S. would begin efforts on Monday to free ships stranded in the Strait of Hormuz as a humanitarian gesture. He said hundreds of vessels and around 20,000 seafarers have been trapped with dwindling food and supplies as Iran blocks passage through the waterway.

stories.title: Europe, Canada leaders hold Yerevan talks in Trump's shadow
stories.summary: European leaders and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney gathered in Yerevan, Armenia, for a European Political Community meeting. The summit agenda focused on the war in Ukraine and the Middle East, with U.S. President Trump's unpredictable foreign policy looming over the discussions.

stories.title: Oil tanker hijacking stokes fears of new disruption in Gulf region
stories.summary: An oil tanker hijacking in the Gulf region has heightened concerns about potential collaboration between Somali pirates and Yemen's Houthi forces. The attack stoked fears of new disruptions to maritime shipping in the area.

stories.title: Australian inquiry opens public hearings into Bondi Beach shooting
stories.summary: A federal royal commission opened public hearings in Australia into the December shooting at a Hanukkah festival near Bondi Beach in Sydney that killed 15 people. The inquiry heard that Sydney's Jewish community had feared a catastrophic attack as antisemitic incidents rose. Two gunmen carried out the attack.

stories.title: Asia View: Taiwan’s President reaches Eswatini after China-linked travel hurdles
stories.summary: Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te arrived in Eswatini, one of Taiwan's few diplomatic allies in Africa. The trip was delayed after several countries reportedly withdrew overflight permission under pressure from China.

stories.title: China says to ignore US sanctions even as Trump visit nears
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce ordered Chinese companies to ignore U.S. sanctions imposed on five oil refiners accused of purchasing Iranian crude, calling the measures a violation of international law. The directive came less than two weeks before a scheduled presidential summit.

stories.title: Can Malaysia’s Umno reclaim role as pillar of Malay political power with solo election bid?
stories.summary: Malaysia's UMNO, led by President Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, announced that its Barisan Nasional coalition is "almost certain" to contest the next general election independently, ending its junior partnership role after more than three years as it seeks to rally Malay-Muslim support.

stories.title: China, Indonesia launch cross-border QR payments – a boost for the global yuan?
stories.summary: China and Indonesia launched a cross-border QR payment system allowing users of apps like Alipay and Indonesia's QRIS to make retail payments in either country using home currencies. The initiative advances Beijing's efforts to internationalize the yuan and reduce U.S. dollar dependence.

stories.title: ‘Point of no return’: New Orleans relocation must start now due to sea level, study finds
stories.summary: A new study warns that New Orleans has reached a "point of no return" due to sea-level rise and wetland erosion in southern Louisiana. The authors say the city could be surrounded by the Gulf of Mexico before the end of the century and urge immediate relocation planning.

stories.title: Jailed for Palestine, Amu Gib is running for local UK elections
stories.summary: Amu Gib, a UK-based activist jailed for pro-Palestine activism, is running as a candidate in local UK elections. The candidacy follows a tradition of imprisoned individuals contesting elections to challenge state authority.

stories.title: German chancellor downplays row with Trump after troop drawdown announced
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz downplayed tensions with President Trump after the U.S. announced a withdrawal of 5,000 troops from Germany, its largest European base. Merz denied any link between his criticism of U.S. war planning in Iran and the drawdown, reaffirming Germany's commitment to the transatlantic alliance.

stories.title: 'Project freedom': Trump says the US will 'guide' stranded ships from the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump announced "Project Freedom," a U.S. effort to guide stranded ships out of the Iran-controlled Strait of Hormuz, involving hundreds of vessels and some 20,000 seafarers. Iran denounced the operation as a ceasefire violation. Few operational details were provided.

stories.title: Defence in focus at European Political Community Summit in Yerevan
stories.summary: Leaders from nearly 50 countries, including the EU's 27 member states and partners, convened in Yerevan, Armenia, for the eighth European Political Community summit. Discussions focused on economic and energy security, with the Ukraine war and the Middle East situation topping the agenda.

stories.title: War update: 148 clashes on front lines, fiercest fighting near Pokrovsk, Kostiantynivka, Huliaipole
stories.summary: Ukraine's military recorded 148 combat engagements with Russian forces along the front lines on May 3. The fiercest fighting was concentrated near Pokrovsk, Kostiantynivka, and Huliaipole.

stories.title: Three cruise ship passengers die in suspected hantavirus outbreak
stories.summary: Three passengers died and three others fell ill on a Netherlands-based cruise ship due to a suspected hantavirus outbreak. The ship departed from Argentina roughly three weeks earlier with around 150 passengers and had stopped in Antarctica and other locations en route to Cape Verde.

stories.title: Lebanon's food security crisis and displacement 'going to have a lasting effect'
