stories.title: Rebels take key military camp in Mali's north
stories.summary: Rebel forces captured the Tessalit military camp in northern Mali without any reported clashes. A security source in the city of Gao, located south of Tessalit, confirmed the takeover occurred peacefully.

stories.title: Trump says Iran war 'terminated,' as war powers deadline arrives
stories.summary: President Trump sent a letter to congressional leaders on the 60-day War Powers deadline stating that there has been no exchange of fire with Iran since the ceasefire. Trump characterized the Iran war as "terminated."

stories.title: Israel's death penalty law perpetuates racial discrimination: UN watchdog
stories.summary: A UN watchdog committee stated that Israel's recently enacted death penalty law is effectively applicable only to Palestinians, constituting racial discrimination. The law establishes a 90-day deadline for carrying out executions after a final judgment is issued.

stories.title: 13 terrorists killed in Pakistan’s Khyber Pakhtunkhwa along Afghanistan border
stories.summary: Pakistani security forces killed 13 militants in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province near the Afghanistan border. In Mohmand district, troops detected and engaged a group of fighters attempting to infiltrate across the Pakistan-Afghanistan frontier.

stories.title: US Treasury warns shippers not to pay Hormuz tolls, even in form of charity
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department warned shipping companies that paying tolls to Iran for passage through the Strait of Hormuz, including in the form of charitable donations to organizations like the Iranian Red Crescent Society, could trigger punitive sanctions.

stories.title: New film profiles Jewish feminist who is NYC Sanitation Department’s official artist
stories.summary: A new documentary titled "Maintenance Artist" profiles Mierle Laderman Ukeles, a Jewish feminist artist who has served as the official artist-in-residence at New York City's Sanitation Department for 50 years. The film explores her belief, rooted in Jewish identity, that people transcend their societal roles.

stories.title: US to close its flagship Gaza mission as Trump plan stalls, sources say
stories.summary: The Trump administration plans to close a U.S. military-run monitoring center near Gaza that was tasked with overseeing the Israel-Hamas ceasefire and facilitating aid flows to Palestinians. Critics said the center had failed in its mission.

stories.title: US to withdraw 5,000 troops from Germany, fulfilling Trump threat
stories.summary: The Pentagon confirmed the US will withdraw about 5,000 troops from Germany within six to 12 months, following President Trump's threat after German Chancellor Friedrich Merz criticized Washington's lack of strategy in the Iran war. Merz had said Iran was "humiliating" the US in talks.

stories.title: Jailed Iranian Nobel winner Mohammadi hospitalized in ‘catastrophic’ condition
stories.summary: Imprisoned Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi has been hospitalized in what her rights foundation described as "catastrophic" condition. Her family said the health crisis followed 140 days of systematic medical neglect in prison, including a severe cardiac episode.

stories.title: Trump 'not satisfied' with Iran's latest proposal to end war with U.S.
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said he was not satisfied with Iran's latest peace proposal, which was conveyed through Pakistani mediators. Trump did not specify what shortcomings he found in the offer, and negotiations between Washington and Tehran remain stalled.

stories.title: Israeli authorities taking 2 activists who led Gaza-bound flotilla to Israel for questioning
stories.summary: Israeli authorities detained two activists who led a Gaza-bound flotilla and transported them to Israel for questioning. Solidarity protests erupted in several cities, including Rome, Athens, and Istanbul.

stories.title: USS Gerald R. Ford aircraft carrier leaves Middle East
stories.summary: The USS Gerald R. Ford aircraft carrier departed the Middle East. Approximately 20 U.S. Navy ships, including two other carriers, remain deployed in the region.

stories.title: US said to be withdrawing 5,000 troops from Germany over Iran war spat
stories.summary: President Donald Trump is reportedly withdrawing approximately 5,000 US troops from Germany following disagreements with European allies over their level of support for Washington's war against Iran.

stories.title: Gaza aid flotilla activists, including former Pakistani senator Mushtaq, released after Israeli interception
stories.summary: Over 100 activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla, including former Pakistani senator Mushtaq Ahmad, were released and transferred to the Greek island of Crete after Israeli forces seized their Gaza-bound aid ships. The flotilla had departed from Barcelona on April 12 before being intercepted in international waters near Greece.

stories.title: Russian hacker pleads guilty to cyberattacks on US, Ukrainian oil and gas facilities
stories.summary: A Russian hacker pleaded guilty to cyberattacks that damaged critical oil and gas infrastructure in the United States, Ukraine, and other countries. The charges carry a maximum sentence of 27 years in prison.

stories.title: Washington to pull some 5,000 US troops from Germany as rift over Iran war widens
stories.summary: The United States plans to withdraw around 5,000 troops from Germany over the next year amid a widening rift between Washington and Berlin over the Iran war. The move follows German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's statement that Tehran was "humiliating" Washington. NATO said Saturday it is consulting with the U.S. on the details.

stories.title: Ukraine says a strike hit Tuapse oil terminal, the fourth attack on the region in 2 weeks
stories.summary: Ukraine reported that a strike hit the Tuapse oil terminal in Russia, marking the fourth attack on that region in two weeks. Separately, Russia struck the western Ukrainian city of Ternopil with over 50 drones, according to Mayor Serhii Nadal.

stories.title: Five killed in small plane crash near Austin
stories.summary: Five people were killed when a small plane crashed near Austin, Texas, on Thursday evening. Local authorities confirmed the fatalities on Friday.

stories.title: Trump says he is 'not satisfied' after Iran delivers new proposal for peace talks
stories.summary: Iran submitted a new peace proposal to the United States through Pakistan, with the text delivered to Islamabad on Thursday. U.S. President Donald Trump responded from the White House that he was "not satisfied" with the offer, describing Iran's leadership as "disjointed."

stories.title: US withdrawing 5,000 troops from Germany, US officials say
stories.summary: The United States is withdrawing 5,000 troops from Germany, according to U.S. officials. The drawdown comes amid a growing rift between President Donald Trump and European allies over the Iran war.

stories.title: Trump considering option to ‘blast the hell out of’ Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated he is considering intensified military action against Iran, saying he is "not happy" with Tehran's latest peace proposal.

stories.title: Trump's proposed 2027 defense budget excludes military aid to Ukraine – Senator King
stories.summary: President Trump's proposed fiscal year 2027 defense budget does not include military assistance for Ukraine, according to U.S. Senator Angus King.

stories.title: Hegseth orders 5,000 US troops to withdraw from Germany
stories.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered the withdrawal of 5,000 U.S. troops from Germany. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the decision followed a review of U.S. force posture in Europe based on theater requirements and conditions on the ground.

stories.title: KP CM Afridi warns of protests against drone attacks
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi warned of protests against drone attacks in the province, citing collateral damage to civilians. Speaking at a cabinet meeting in Peshawar, Afridi condemned the strikes and hinted at legislation to criminalize collateral damage from such operations.

stories.title: Trump says he’ll place 25% tariff on automobiles from EU, accusing bloc of not complying with trade deal
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced he will impose a 25 percent tariff on automobiles imported from the European Union, accusing the bloc of failing to comply with the Turnberry Agreement trade framework.

stories.title: Why Beijing now wants its spies executed in Taiwan to come in from decades in the cold
stories.summary: China's Fujian province is framing the historical executions of Communist Party spies in Taiwan within a reunification narrative. A former residence in Fuzhou has become a national pilgrimage site tied to Beijing's messaging toward Taiwan.

stories.title: US believes Iran has lost $4.8 billion in oil earnings due to blockade — report
stories.summary: The United States believes Iran has lost approximately $4.8 billion in oil revenue due to a blockade. Separately, the U.S. reportedly told European allies to expect delays in arms deliveries as the Iran conflict drains stockpiles. Hezbollah fired at least four drones at northern Israel, all intercepted by the IDF.

stories.title: Why Bennett, Lapid's union actually strengthens Netanyahu's hand in next elections - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion analysis argues that the merger between Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid's political movements, while intended to unify Israel's opposition, could inadvertently push right-wing voters back toward Prime Minister Netanyahu.

stories.title: Can Bennett become Israel’s Peter Magyar in the fight for democracy? - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece examines whether former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett could replicate the political realignment achieved by Hungary's Peter Magyar and break Netanyahu's ruling bloc.

stories.title: Injury toll from Russian drone attack on Ternopil rises to 12
stories.summary: The number of people injured in a Russian drone attack on the western Ukrainian city of Ternopil has risen to 12. Ukrainian police established an emergency response hub in the city to coordinate relief efforts following the strike.

stories.title: Syria relies on Russia's oil despite pivot to the West
stories.summary: Syria's oil imports from Russia have surged 75% to approximately 60,000 barrels per day in the current year, making Moscow the country's dominant crude supplier. The increase follows the fall of the Assad government in December 2024, despite Syria's broader diplomatic pivot toward the West.

stories.title: Russia pounds Ukraine with drones in daytime attack
stories.summary: Russia launched over 400 drones at Ukraine in a daytime attack, injuring 10 people in the western city of Ternopil. Ukrainian officials reported the large-scale assault on Friday.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1528: Ukraine’s “long-range sanctions” cost Russia $7 billion this year — and counting
stories.summary: On day 1,528 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, Ukrainian drones struck a Su-57 stealth fighter base near the Urals, a refinery in Perm, and Buk-M3 air defenses in occupied Donetsk. A Russian drone swarm hit Ternopil, Rivne, Vinnytsia, Cherkasy, and Odesa, knocking Ternopil offline and injuring 10 people.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s population policy is still trapped in a city state mindset
stories.summary: Hong Kong faces calls to develop a comprehensive population policy amid rapid ageing, low fertility, and a shrinking labor force. Academics and policymakers advocate strategies focused on boosting birth rates and attracting immigrants, though critics argue this reflects a limited city-state mindset.

stories.title: China’s UN envoy blasts US ‘bullying’ as sanctions widen before Trump-Xi talks
stories.summary: China's UN envoy criticized U.S. "bullying" and sanctions against Chinese vessels and firms as Beijing assumed the rotating presidency of the UN Security Council. Washington simultaneously sanctioned a China-based petroleum terminal operator as part of efforts to cut Chinese funding to Iran.

stories.title: Iran offers new proposal amid stalled US peace talks
stories.summary: Iran submitted a new peace proposal to Pakistan on the evening of April 30 as negotiations with the United States remained stalled.

stories.title: Palestinian FA chief hits out at Israeli federation VP at FIFA Congress
stories.summary: At the FIFA Congress, Palestinian Football Association chief Jibril Rajoub publicly criticized the Israeli federation's vice president. FIFA President Gianni Infantino had called both officials to the podium and gestured for the Palestinian leader to approach the Israeli representative.

stories.title: Zelensky announces strengthening of air defense: Decisions made for Dnipro and Odesa
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced the reinforcement of air defenses following a large-scale Russian drone attack. Specific decisions have been made to strengthen protection for the cities of Dnipro and Odesa, with intensified work with international partners underway.

stories.title: Board of Peace denies plans to shut down ceasefire coordination HQ in Israel’s south
stories.summary: The Board of Peace denied a Reuters report alleging plans to shut down a ceasefire coordination headquarters in southern Israel. The report claimed the center would be folded into a yet-to-be-formed International Stabilization Force as the ceasefire frays and Hamas disarmament efforts stall.

stories.title: Trump claims hostilities have ended in Iran in letter to congressional leaders
stories.summary: President Trump sent a letter to congressional leaders claiming hostilities with Iran have "terminated," suggesting the 60-day War Powers Act deadline to seek congressional approval no longer applies. Democrats are pushing back against Trump's interpretation. The deadline fell 60 days after the U.S. and Israel launched strikes on Iran on February 28.

stories.title: Tessalit army base taken by rebels
stories.summary: Rebels captured the strategic Tessalit military base in northern Mali near the Algerian border, forcing the army and its Russian mercenary allies to surrender. Separately, in the DRC, former president Joseph Kabila rejected U.S. accusations of backing rebel fighters.

stories.title: US to shut centre intended to monitor Gaza ceasefire as peace plans stall: Report
stories.summary: The United States plans to close a military-run center established to monitor the Israel-Hamas ceasefire in Gaza. Diplomats say the facility has failed to prevent Israeli violations, and broader peace plans have stalled.

stories.title: Trump expands red snapper fishing as critics warn of overfishing
stories.summary: The Trump administration approved red snapper fishing permits granting anglers in Florida, Georgia, and the Carolinas greater control over the fishery. Critics have raised concerns about potential overfishing as a result of the expanded access.

stories.title: Fractures rock Gulf alliance as UAE quits OPEC during Iran war - analysis
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates has withdrawn from OPEC amid the ongoing Iran war, exposing deepening fractures in the Gulf alliance. A summit snub and public criticism have highlighted a widening Saudi-Emirati split with significant implications for energy policy and regional security coordination.

stories.title: At least 12 killed in latest Israeli attacks on Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on Lebanon have continued, killing at least 12 people in the latest attacks. More than 2,600 people have been killed since March 2, despite an ongoing ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Watch: TMC, BJP lock horns over EVM tampering claims | Above the Fold | 01.05.2026
stories.summary: In India, the Trinamool Congress and the Bharatiya Janata Party clashed over allegations of electronic voting machine tampering in West Bengal. Other major stories included rising LPG prices and the Bargi Dam tragedy.

stories.title: Iranian Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi hospitalised as health deteriorates
stories.summary: Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi has been hospitalized after losing consciousness twice and suffering a severe cardiac crisis. Her foundation announced the deterioration of her health.

stories.title: Trump: 60-Day War Powers Deadline ‘Totally Unconstitutional’
stories.summary: President Trump called the 60-day War Powers deadline "totally unconstitutional" as the timeframe for congressional authorization of the Iran conflict expired. The White House argues that the U.S.-Iran ceasefire effectively paused the legal clock.

stories.title: Drone attack on Ternopil: fire contained, nine hits on industrial facilities reported
stories.summary: Rescuers in the western Ukrainian city of Ternopil contained a fire caused by Russian drone strikes that hit nine industrial facilities. The attack targeted the city's industrial infrastructure overnight.

stories.title: The great disconnect: Why Israel is losing America while winning in Iran - opinion
stories.summary: An analysis argues that Israel maintains strong support among U.S. policy circles but is experiencing a steady erosion of public and generational backing in America. The piece highlights a growing disconnect between official U.S.-Israel relations and shifting American public opinion.

stories.title: US criticises Zambia for lack of engagement as $1 billion health deal stalls
stories.summary: The United States criticized Zambia for failing to engage on a new health aid agreement covering more than $1 billion in US funding. Washington said its repeated outreach was ignored as an April 30 deadline passed without a deal.

stories.title: “Just reaching the front line has become very risky”: Ukraine’s AI drones are hunting Russia’s supply vans
stories.summary: Ukraine is deploying AI-guided drones that can bypass Russian electronic warfare to target supply vehicles heading to the front lines. The technology is reportedly disrupting Russian logistics and making resupply operations increasingly dangerous.

stories.title: Post-Assad Syria still dependent on Russian oil despite shift to the West – Reuters
stories.summary: Despite Syria's post-Assad political shift toward the West, the country remains heavily dependent on Russian oil imports. Domestic crude production stays far below demand, and alternative suppliers have not filled the gap.

stories.title: China drops tariffs on all African nations except Eswatini
stories.summary: A new Chinese trade policy granting tariff-free market access to African nations took effect on Friday. The two-year deal covers 53 of Africa's 54 countries, excluding only Eswatini due to its diplomatic ties with Taiwan.

stories.title: Will the Next Fed Chairman Be More Compliant With Trump?
stories.summary: Kevin Warsh, a potential next Federal Reserve chairman, is expected to face significant pressure from President Trump to cut interest rates. The article examines whether a new Fed leader would be more compliant with the administration's monetary policy preferences.

stories.title: Palestinian football boss refuses Israeli handshake at FIFA event
stories.summary: Palestine Football Association President Jibril Rajoub refused to shake hands with an Israeli FA representative at a FIFA event. Rajoub publicly explained his reasons for the refusal.

stories.title: URIF aims to sign its first three investment agreements by end of 2026
stories.summary: The United States-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund, established one year ago, plans to finalize its first three investment agreements by the end of 2026. The fund is designed to support reconstruction efforts in Ukraine.

stories.title: Marine Corps fields 3,500 first-person view attack drones
stories.summary: The U.S. Marine Corps has fielded 3,500 first-person-view attack drones, a rapid buildup from zero such systems in service as of October 2025.

stories.title: Climate colonialism: Why Pakistan pays the price
stories.summary: The article argues that the climate crisis disproportionately affects countries like Pakistan despite their minimal contribution to global emissions. It notes that G20 nations produce roughly 80 percent of annual greenhouse gas emissions while vulnerable regions in South Asia bear the harshest consequences.

stories.title: New US sanctions are 'collective punishment', Cuba's FM says during May 1 marches
stories.summary: Cuban Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez condemned a new round of US sanctions as "collective punishment" during May 1 marches outside the US embassy in Havana. Cuba's economic crisis has worsened since US President Donald Trump imposed a severe fuel blockade on the island in January.

stories.title: USF hits four Russian aircraft in Russia's Chelyabinsk region
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces struck four Russian aircraft at the Shagol airfield in Russia's Chelyabinsk region. The targeted aircraft included at least one Su-57 stealth fighter and one Su-34 fighter-bomber.

stories.title: Your Taxes: Israel’s lower mid-market is tempting international M&A buyers
stories.summary: Israel's lower mid-market is attracting international buyers for mergers and acquisitions. Several factors, including favorable bargaining conditions, are contributing to increased interest in Israeli companies from foreign investors.

stories.title: Somali piracy resurfaces in the lightly-protected waters
stories.summary: Piracy is resurging off the coast of Somalia as the Somali government lacks the capacity to patrol its extensive coastline, leaving shipping lanes largely unprotected.

stories.title: Iran delivers new proposal for US talks, Trump says ‘not satisfied’ with offer
stories.summary: Iran delivered a new proposal to Pakistani intermediaries for negotiations with the United States. President Trump said he was not satisfied with the offer, though he confirmed that talks were continuing by phone.

stories.title: Over 100 Gaza aid flotilla activists taken to Crete after Israeli interception
stories.summary: Israeli forces intercepted aid ships from the second Global Sumud Flotilla in international waters near Greece, seizing vessels bound for Gaza that had departed from Barcelona on April 12. More than 100 activists were transferred to Greek boats and taken to Crete.

stories.title: Iran submits new proposal to end war; Trump says he’s ‘not satisfied’
stories.summary: Iran submitted a new proposal through Pakistan that envisions the U.S. unwinding its blockade at the start of Strait of Hormuz negotiations rather than as a precondition, and suggests nuclear talks in exchange for sanctions relief. President Trump said he is not satisfied with the offer.

stories.title: BoP denies rumors of Kiryat Gat base closure, says it will establish 'transitional Gaza gov't'
stories.summary: The U.S. Bureau of Planning denied rumors that the Kiryat Gat base in Israel would close and announced plans to establish a transitional government for Gaza. The U.S. military-run center's potential closure would have been a setback for President Donald Trump's Gaza plan, which has already been undermined by Hamas's refusal to disarm.

stories.title: Daytime Russian drone swarm hits western Ukraine, knocking Ternopil offline and injuring 10
stories.summary: A daytime Russian drone swarm struck western Ukraine, knocking the city of Ternopil offline and injuring at least 10 people. Impacts were also reported in the Rivne, Vinnytsia, Cherkasy, and Odesa oblasts.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz says regulatory system for virtual assets should be operationalised at the earliest
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shahbaz Sharif directed the swift operationalization of a regulatory framework for virtual assets meeting international standards. The directive came during a meeting with Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority Chairman Bilal Bin Saqib in Lahore.

stories.title: No unfunded requirements in FY27, say some services, COCOMs
stories.summary: The U.S. Army, Navy, and Air Force submitted approximately $3 billion in unfunded requirements for the fiscal year 2027 budget, all for military construction projects. U.S. Southern Command included $229.9 million in additional requests.

stories.title: US judge bars Trump from ending protected status for Yemeni nationals
stories.summary: A U.S. federal judge blocked the Trump administration from terminating Temporary Protected Status for Yemeni nationals. The administration had sought to cancel protections for people from 13 countries as part of a broader immigration crackdown.

stories.title: Russia’s Prosecutor General’s Office sues to seize assets of agribusiness giant Rusagro founder, worth $2.9 billion
stories.summary: Russia's Prosecutor General's Office filed a lawsuit in a Moscow court to seize the assets of Vadim Moshkovich, founder of the agribusiness giant Rusagro. Moshkovich's assets are reportedly valued at approximately $2.9 billion.

stories.title: Russians attack Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 50 times since morning, leaving four injured
stories.summary: Russian forces launched nearly 50 attacks using drones and artillery on two districts of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region, injuring four people. The strikes began in the morning and continued throughout the day.

stories.title: Man convicted of attempting terrorist attack at London’s Israeli embassy
stories.summary: A man was convicted of attempting a terrorist attack at the Israeli embassy in London. He tried to breach the embassy's perimeter in April 2025 while armed with two knives.

stories.title: Russian drones set fire to 2 apartment buildings in Odesa, damage port infrastructure
stories.summary: Russian drone strikes overnight on May 1 set fire to two residential apartment buildings in the Ukrainian city of Odesa and damaged port infrastructure. Odesa military administration head Serhiy Lysak reported the attacks.

stories.title: Norway informed it may face weapons delivery delays from US
stories.summary: Norway's Ministry of Defence has been formally notified by U.S. authorities that delays in deliveries of American weapons systems may occur. The notification was confirmed by the ministry on Friday.

stories.title: Ukraine says drones hit Su-57 fighters, Su-34 bomber at Russian airfield
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed that its drones struck several Su-57 fighter jets and an Su-34 fighter-bomber at the Shagol airfield in Russia's Chelyabinsk region on May 1. The strike targeted one of Russia's key military aviation facilities deep inside Russian territory.

stories.title: LNG ship from India heading towards Hormuz drops anchor
stories.summary: An LNG tanker named Umm Al Ashtan, sailing from India toward the Strait of Hormuz, dropped anchor near Oman. The vessel's route close to the Omani coast deviated from typical Iran-approved transit paths that follow the Iranian coastline.

stories.title: Taiwan expresses concern after China calls island biggest risk in U.S.-China relations
stories.summary: Taiwan expressed concern after China characterized the island as the biggest risk in U.S.-China relations. The statement came roughly two weeks before a planned summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping, where Taiwan is expected to be a central topic.

stories.title: Iran offers latest proposal to U.S. via Pakistan: state media
stories.summary: Iran transmitted its latest diplomatic proposal to the United States through Pakistan, according to Iranian state media. Oil prices remain more than 50 percent above pre-war levels as traders face the prolonged closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Pentagon reaches agreements with top AI companies, but not Anthropic
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced agreements with seven AI companies—including Amazon Web Services, Google, Microsoft, NVIDIA, OpenAI, SpaceX, and Reflection—to deploy their tools on classified military networks. Notably excluded is Anthropic, which the Pentagon labeled a supply-chain risk due to disputes over guardrails for military use of its AI.

stories.title: US to close its flagship Gaza mission as Trump plan stalls
stories.summary: The U.S. military-run body tasked with monitoring the Israel-Hamas ceasefire and coordinating aid to Gaza is set to be shut down, according to seven diplomats. The closure comes as President Trump's broader peace plan has stalled.

stories.title: Rebel checkpoints reported around Mali’s capital, northern town seized
stories.summary: JNIM militants and Tuareg separatist groups have established checkpoints around Mali's capital and seized a northern town, continuing their offensive against Mali's military government.

stories.title: New foreign components have again been found in Russian drones – Vlasiuk
stories.summary: Ukrainian official Vlasiuk reported that new Western-manufactured components produced in 2025 have been found in Russian drones used to attack Ukraine. The discovery indicates ongoing sanctions evasion and calls for strengthened enforcement of export controls on Russia.

stories.title: Trump 'not satisfied' with latest Iranian proposal, says leadership is 'fully disjointed'
stories.summary: President Trump told reporters outside the White House that he is "not satisfied" with the latest Iranian negotiation proposal, calling Iran's leadership "fully disjointed." Trump asserted that Iran wants a deal "because they have no military left."

stories.title: Putin’s approval rating falls to its lowest point since Russia’s full-scale invasion began
stories.summary: Vladimir Putin's approval rating has fallen to 73%, its lowest level since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, according to a poll by the Public Opinion Foundation (FOM). The decline marks a significant shift in Russian public sentiment.

stories.title: AI actors and writers will not be eligible for Oscars, Academy says
stories.summary: The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences issued new rules stipulating that acting and writing performed by artificial intelligence will not be eligible for Oscar consideration. The updated rules also expand international film category eligibility to include top award winners from major festivals such as Cannes, Venice, and Toronto.

stories.title: Can Iran withstand the US naval blockade?
stories.summary: The Trump administration is attempting to pressure Iran into concessions by imposing a naval blockade aimed at cutting off Iranian oil exports. Questions remain about whether Tehran can withstand the sustained economic pressure.

stories.title: Trump repeats that he is 'not happy' with Iran as deadline to seek approval for war looms
stories.summary: President Trump said on Friday that said a deal has been hard to reach in part because Iranian leadership was "very confused".

stories.title: Iran told Saudi Arabia it planned to 'crush the UAE': Report
stories.summary: Iran reportedly informed Saudi Arabia and Oman of its plans to "crush" the United Arab Emirates, according to a media report. Tehran allegedly boasted about its attacks on the UAE while seeking to exploit divisions among Gulf states.

stories.title: Iran crisis hampering aid to refugees as supply chain costs soar, UN warns
stories.summary: The United Nations warned that the ongoing Iran crisis is disrupting aid supply chains for refugees, with deliveries taking 25 additional days and transport costs more than doubling.

stories.title: Trump expands Cuba sanctions with global reach, targeting foreign banks and firms
stories.summary: President Trump signed an executive order significantly expanding U.S. sanctions on Cuba, authorizing penalties against foreign companies and financial institutions that do business with the island. The order extends Washington's reach to third-country actors, potentially affecting global firms including those in China.

stories.title: Cloudflare removes ‘spyware’ label from Russia’s state-backed messaging app Max
stories.summary: Cloudflare Radar removed a "spyware" designation from the domains of Max, a Russian state-backed messaging application. The labeling change was noted in the web infrastructure company's publicly available data.

stories.title: Ukrenergo forecasts no power outages for Saturday
stories.summary: Ukraine's grid operator Ukrenergo announced no planned electricity consumption restrictions for Saturday, May 2. The forecast indicates stable power supply across the country.

stories.title: Navy looks to resume purchasing P-8A aircraft
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy is seeking to resume purchases of P-8A Poseidon maritime patrol aircraft. The request follows the P-8A Increment 3 Block 2 variant reaching initial operating capability.

stories.title: Oscar statuette belonging to Russian documentary filmmaker found at Frankfurt airport, Lufthansa says
stories.summary: An Oscar statuette belonging to Russian documentary filmmaker Pavel Talankin, co-creator of the film Mr. Nobody Against Putin, was found at Frankfurt am Main airport. German airline Lufthansa confirmed the discovery to Deutsche Welle.

stories.title: Oscars changes allow for double acting nominations while banning AI
stories.summary: The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences announced major Oscars rule changes, including allowing actors to receive multiple nominations in one category and barring AI-generated performances and screenplays from eligibility.

stories.title: US warns shippers that paying Iran to traverse Hormuz may incur sanctions
stories.summary: Iran is demanding payments from commercial vessels for safe passage through the blockaded Strait of Hormuz, including in the form of charitable donations. The U.S. Treasury has warned shippers that complying with these payments may trigger American sanctions.

stories.title: Trump tears up part of EU tariff deal to raise import duties on cars and lorries
stories.summary: President Trump announced he would raise tariffs on cars and lorries imported from the EU from 15% to 25%, accusing Brussels of non-compliance and slow ratification of the tariff deal struck at his Scottish golf course. The move blindsided European leaders on a public holiday.

stories.title: US sanctions China-based operator, others over alleged Iran oil trade links
stories.summary: The United States imposed new sanctions on entities and individuals allegedly involved in Iranian petroleum trade, including China-based Qingdao Haiye Oil Terminal Co. and a Chinese national. The State Department said the terminal operator imported tens of millions of barrels of sanctioned Iranian crude.

stories.title: Photos: Cuba holds May Day celebrations amid US threats
stories.summary: Cuba held May Day celebrations in Havana marking International Workers' Day. The event coincided with the announcement of additional U.S. sanctions targeting the island nation.

stories.title: Florida prosecutors launch criminal investigation into deaths of 31 sloths
stories.summary: Florida prosecutors launched a criminal investigation into the deaths of 31 sloths imported from South American rainforests in Peru and Guyana. The animals, destined for a planned theme park called Sloth World in Orlando, died in an unheated warehouse between December 2024 and February 2025.

stories.title: Zelensky orders Ukraine military reform that would allow phased discharge of mobilized soldiers
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky ordered a military reform set to launch in 2026 that will include phased demobilization of some mobilized Ukrainian soldiers. The reform aims to restructure how troops are discharged from service.

stories.title: Ukrainian Jewish school and orphanage struck in overnight Russian drone attack
stories.summary: A Jewish school and orphanage in Ukraine sustained serious damage during an overnight Russian drone attack, though no injuries were reported. Russia launched over 600 drones at Ukraine in under 24 hours.

stories.title: As Gaza is destroyed, a VR project preserves what Israel tried to erase
stories.summary: A virtual reality project is working to digitally preserve sites across Gaza that have been destroyed during Israeli military operations. The immersive experience allows viewers to explore reconstructed Gazan environments and serves as a form of documentation of the enclave's destruction.

stories.title: At least four killed in a train crash in Indonesia
stories.summary: At least four people, including two minor girls, were killed in a train crash in Indonesia. The driver and remaining passengers sustained injuries in the incident.

stories.title: Russian shelling in Kherson region leaves one killed, five injured
stories.summary: Russian shelling in Ukraine's Kherson region killed one person and injured five others, including a police officer. The attacks targeted areas within the southern Ukrainian region.

stories.title: Iran judiciary chief says Tehran open to US talks but against policy ‘imposition’
stories.summary: Iran's judiciary chief stated that Tehran is open to negotiations with the United States but would not accept the imposition of external policies, affirming that Iran would not "back down" in any talks.

stories.title: The future of unmanned surface vessels includes ISR and counter-UAS
stories.summary: Red Cat, known for its aerial drones, launched a new company called Blue Ops to mass-produce unmanned surface vessels. The USVs are intended to support intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, and counter-drone operations.

stories.title: Al Qaeda-linked insurgents call on Malians to rise up, establish Sharia law
stories.summary: Al Qaeda-linked insurgents in Mali issued a rare French-language statement calling on Malians to rise up against the military-led government and establish Sharia law. The statement followed a series of unprecedented attacks carried out across the country.

stories.title: Trump says Iran seeks terms he ‘can’t agree to’ in latest peace proposal
stories.summary: President Trump stated that Iran's latest peace proposal, transmitted via Pakistan, contains terms he cannot agree to. Negotiations are reportedly continuing by phone.

stories.title: Saffron’s Last Gasp
stories.summary: The ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict is disrupting the global supply of saffron, the world's most expensive spice, much of which originates from Iran.

stories.title: Russia Fired Record Number of Drones at Ukraine in April – AFP Analysis
stories.summary: An AFP analysis found that Russia fired a record number of drones at Ukraine in April. Moscow significantly increased daytime long-range drone launches, a tactic Kyiv condemned as intended to maximize civilian casualties.

stories.title: While Asia and Europe scramble for natural gas, the US glut has nowhere to go
stories.summary: The U.S. war on Iran has disrupted approximately 20 percent of global LNG supply, damaging Qatari LNG facilities and halting tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. While import-dependent countries in Europe and Asia face surging prices, a natural gas glut in West Texas has left U.S. producers paying to offload surplus gas.

stories.title: Injury toll after Russian attack in Ternopil rises to 11
stories.summary: The number of people injured in a Russian attack on the western Ukrainian city of Ternopil has risen to 11. Authorities continue to assess the damage from the strike.

stories.title: India raises cooking gas, jet fuel prices as supply pressures mount
stories.summary: India raised prices for commercial liquefied petroleum gas and international jet fuel as supply disruptions linked to the Middle East war continue to pressure the import-dependent nation. The country relies on imports for roughly 60 percent of its LPG supply.

stories.title: Iran’s largest crypto exchange enables IRGC to move millions despite sanctions
stories.summary: Nobitex, Iran's largest cryptocurrency exchange, has allegedly enabled the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps to move millions of dollars despite international sanctions. The platform was founded in 2018 by brothers with reported ties to a powerful family connected to the Khamenei and Khomeini clans. Nobitex denies receiving government support.

stories.title: Gaza flotilla activists return despite Israel's sea interception
stories.summary: Activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla are regrouping in Greece for a second attempt to deliver aid to Gaza by sea. The effort follows Israel's interception of an earlier flotilla, during which 175 activists were detained.

stories.title: UK man appears in court over stabbing of two Jewish men in London
stories.summary: A 45-year-old man, Essa Suleiman, appeared in a London court charged with attempted murder after two Jewish men were stabbed in Golders Green, north London. Officers have described the incident as a suspected terrorist attack.

stories.title: Russian attack in Rivne region leaves five injured, civilian infrastructure damaged
stories.summary: Five people were injured and civilian infrastructure was damaged in a Russian strike on Ukraine's Rivne region. Authorities reported the attack caused harm to non-military targets in the western Ukrainian area.

stories.title: Mali attacks spotlight the growing reach of militants across West Africa
stories.summary: Simultaneous attacks in Mali on April 25 by al Qaeda-linked militants and separatist Tuareg rebels demonstrated the expanding reach and coordination of armed groups across West Africa. The assaults struck at the heart of the country's military government.

stories.title: Pentagon freezes out Anthropic as it signs deals with AI rivals
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense announced deals with seven artificial intelligence companies but excluded Anthropic from the agreements. The contracts signal the Pentagon's expanding engagement with commercial AI firms for defense applications.

stories.title: What in the World?
stories.summary: A weekly news quiz covers events from the week of April 25, including Iran's offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the UAE's departure from OPEC, and a conference hosted by Colombia.

stories.title: Trump heads to Florida stronghold in first public event since foiled attack
stories.summary: President Donald Trump traveled to The Villages, Florida, for his first public event since a foiled assassination attempt. The trip comes amid heightened security scrutiny and increasing political pressure on the administration.

stories.title: Trump's attacks on Europe's leaders worsen transatlantic frost
stories.summary: Relations between the United States and European allies have further deteriorated in recent weeks under President Donald Trump's leadership. Tensions with European leaders have deepened the existing transatlantic rift.

stories.title: US Navy turns to AI firm Domino for options to counter Iranian mines
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy awarded a contract to AI firm Domino to develop capabilities for detecting and countering Iranian mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The strait is one of the world's most critical shipping lanes for global energy supplies.

stories.title: Gaza aid flotilla activists taken to Crete after Israeli interception
stories.summary: More than 100 pro-Palestinian activists aboard aid ships heading to Gaza were taken to the Greek island of Crete after Israeli forces intercepted and seized their vessels in international waters near Greece. Flotilla organizers confirmed the activists' transfer to the town of Atherinolakkos.

stories.title: ‘Peace has become a dirty word’: Israel’s peace camp gathers
stories.summary: Israeli peace activists gathered in Tel Aviv to advocate for a resolution to the conflict amid diminishing prospects for peace negotiations.

stories.title: PM Svyrydenko: Russian drones targeted power facilities, critical infrastructure, and homes for 12 hours
stories.summary: Ukrainian Prime Minister Svyrydenko reported that Russia launched more than 400 drones over a 12-hour period targeting Ukrainian power facilities, critical infrastructure, and residential buildings. The sustained aerial assault struck energy systems across the country.

stories.title: Russians strike Zhytomyr region with drones, damaging sports and educational infrastructure
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out a drone attack on Ukraine's Zhytomyr region, including the regional capital. The strikes damaged sports and educational infrastructure in the area.

stories.title: 'Iran's most potent weapon': Telegraph's Adrian Blomfield offers rare frontline glimpse of Hormuz
stories.summary: The Telegraph's Adrian Blomfield reported from the Strait of Hormuz, describing the waterway's complex maritime environment. He noted approximately 300 small speedboats operating at high speeds, creating an ambiguous ecosystem where smugglers, civilians, and military actors are difficult to distinguish.

stories.title: Oscar goes missing after director forced to check it on flight: ‘could be used as weapon’
stories.summary: Director Pavel Talankin's Academy Award went missing after a TSA agent at New York's JFK Airport required him to check the statuette on a transatlantic flight to Frankfurt, citing it as a potential weapon. The airline located the Oscar two days later. Talankin co-directed the best documentary winner Mr Nobody Against Putin.

stories.title: IDF official says Iran war will be ‘one big failure’ if enriched uranium not removed
stories.summary: A senior IDF official warned that the war with Iran will be "one big failure" unless Tehran's enriched uranium stockpile is removed through negotiations. The officer also said the IDF's ability to counter Hezbollah drone threats remains constrained by the terms of the existing truce.

stories.title: UAE says Iran cannot be trusted over Hormuz, peace efforts at an impasse
stories.summary: A senior UAE official stated that Iran cannot be trusted regarding any unilateral arrangements for the Strait of Hormuz, reflecting deep regional mistrust. Diplomatic efforts to end the Iran war remain at an impasse, with Washington and Dubai both expressing frustration.

stories.title: Zayn Malik’s family urge fans to donate to Palestine
stories.summary: The family of British-Pakistani singer Zayn Malik, currently recovering in hospital, has urged fans to donate to Palestinian charities rather than send flowers. The former One Direction member's relatives directed supporters toward humanitarian aid for Palestinians.

stories.title: Poll finds 61 percent of Americans believe attacking Iran was a mistake
stories.summary: A recent poll indicates that 61 percent of Americans consider the attack on Iran a mistake. Respondents expressed concern about the war's impact on the cost of living and voiced skepticism about the campaign's success so far.

stories.title: Small plane crash in Texas Hill Country leaves five dead
stories.summary: A Cessna 421C crashed among trees at night in Wimberley, Texas, approximately 40 miles southwest of Austin, killing all five people onboard. Hays County Judge Ruben Becerra confirmed the crash occurred late Thursday night.

stories.title: Pakistan sees decline in militant violence for 2nd straight month: PICSS
stories.summary: The Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies reported that militant attacks in Pakistan fell 42 percent in April 2026, dropping from 146 in March to 85. Fatalities from militant attacks also declined from 106 to 60, marking a second consecutive month of improved security.

stories.title: Oscar statuette for award-winning Mr Nobody Against Putin documentary goes missing on flight
stories.summary: The Oscar statuette awarded for the documentary "Mr. Nobody Against Putin" went missing after the 3.8-kilogram award was checked into hold luggage on a flight. Director Pavel Talankin was unable to carry the statuette in the cabin.

stories.title: Gazans face years of untreated fractures amid health collapse
stories.summary: Thousands of residents in Gaza are living with untreated bone fractures due to severe medical shortages and a collapsed healthcare system. Supply shortages, restricted movement, and lack of surgical capacity have delayed necessary operations and long-term orthopedic care.

stories.title: Israel delivers Tamir interceptors to US Marine Corps for MRIC program
stories.summary: Israel delivered Tamir interceptor missiles to the U.S. Marine Corps for the Medium Range Intercept Capability program. The MRIC system uses a truck-mounted Iron Dome launcher paired with Tamir interceptors.

stories.title: Netanyahu posts AI video of political rivals turning into Arabs
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu posted an AI-generated video on X depicting political rivals transforming into Arabs, drawing widespread accusations of anti-Arab racism. The post also received a community note on the platform that was itself criticized as racist.

stories.title: Elbit subsidiary Fuse, Mistral to provide US Army THOR  drones
stories.summary: Elbit Systems subsidiary Fuse and partner Mistral will supply the US Army with THOR Group 2 drones. The backpack-portable, fully autonomous multirotor aircraft will provide American units with organic aerial reconnaissance and operational capabilities.

stories.title: London stabbing suspect left hospital, 'attacked Muslim friend'
stories.summary: London police identified Essa Suleiman as the suspect in a Golders Green stabbing. He allegedly attacked an acquaintance, Ishmail Hussein, described as a Muslim friend, on the same day two Jewish men were also stabbed in the area. Suleiman had reportedly left a hospital before the attacks.

stories.title: War update: 55 combat engagements since morning, Pokrovsk direction remains most active
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces engaged in 55 combat clashes with Russian troops since the morning, with the Pokrovsk direction in eastern Ukraine remaining the most active sector. Russia continues to concentrate its main offensive efforts in that area.

stories.title: Trump ‘not satisfied’ with Iran’s latest peace proposal as talks stall
stories.summary: President Donald Trump expressed dissatisfaction with Iran's latest peace proposal, saying he was not satisfied with what Tehran offered. Iranian state media reported that Tehran submitted a new plan aimed at ending the conflict that began with US-Israeli strikes on February 28. Negotiations remain stalled despite a weeks-long ceasefire.

stories.title: Al-Qaeda-linked insurgents establish check points around Bamako
stories.summary: Al-Qaeda-linked insurgents have established checkpoints around Mali's capital, Bamako, and seized a northern town. The Islamist fighters called on Malians to rise up against the military-led government and transition to Sharia law.

stories.title: Russian forces have attacked Naftogaz facilities 96 times since start of year
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked Naftogaz Group facilities 96 times between January and April, targeting energy production, gas transportation infrastructure, thermal power plants, and gas stations across Ukraine.

stories.title: Ukraine hits both Russia’s military and the infrastructure funding it – from a refinery in Perm to air defenses in occupied Donetsk
stories.summary: Ukraine conducted coordinated overnight strikes hitting a refinery in Russia's Perm region, air defense systems, and multiple ammunition and drone storage sites across Russian-occupied territories. The operation targeted both military assets and infrastructure funding Russia's war effort.

stories.title: Mass grave containing 55 bodies found in Syria’s Aleppo province
stories.summary: A mass grave containing the bodies of 55 men and women has been discovered in the village of Mazra'et Al-Raheb, southeast of Aleppo in Syria's Aleppo province. The circumstances surrounding the deaths have not yet been fully detailed.

stories.title: Ukraine plans army pay hikes, phased discharge — Zelenskyy
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced planned reforms including military pay increases and a phased discharge system for soldiers. The measures aim to boost morale and address complaints about exhaustion and uneven workloads on the frontline.

stories.title: King Charles wins praise for deft handling of Trump on US state visit
stories.summary: King Charles received praise for his diplomatic handling of a state visit to the United States, during which President Trump lifted some tariffs on Scotch whisky. Charles balanced praise for his host with subtle criticism, though the visit's long-term impact on US-UK relations remains uncertain amid divisions over issues including the Iran war.

stories.title: US warns shippers against paying Strait of Hormuz tolls, ‘donations’
stories.summary: The United States issued a warning to international shipping companies not to pay tolls or donations demanded in the Strait of Hormuz. The advisory came as Iranian state media reported that Tehran had submitted a new peace proposal to Washington.

stories.title: Residential building on fire in Rivne following Russian drone attack
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack struck a residential building in the city of Rivne, Ukraine, causing damage and igniting a fire that spread across approximately 100 square meters of the roof.

stories.title: ‘It’s the little things’: Israeli mother juggles war, parenthood as her husband serves
stories.summary: An ongoing photojournalism series by Chen G. Schimmel documents the lives of Israeli soldiers' wives managing family responsibilities during wartime. The second installment profiles a mother navigating parenthood while her husband serves in the military.

stories.title: Israel’s death penalty law perpetuates racial discrimination: UN watchdog
stories.summary: A United Nations committee has criticized Israel's death penalty law, calling it a grave erosion of human rights that perpetuates racial discrimination.

stories.title: Sacked Russian Deputy Minister Flees to U.S. Amid Fraud Probe, Sources Say
stories.summary: Former Russian Deputy Minister Denis Butsayev reportedly fled to the United States amid a fraud investigation. He was dismissed from the Natural Resources and Environment Ministry shortly after leaving Russia.

stories.title: Israeli general says 'Jewish terrorism' risks West Bank uprising
stories.summary: A senior Israeli general warned that violent settler attacks in the occupied West Bank risk triggering a Palestinian uprising. The general described the phenomenon as "Jewish terrorism" and said tensions in the territory are rising.

stories.title: RAF chief calls Falklands defence 'non-negotiable' as Rubio plays down Pentagon memo
stories.summary: RAF Air Chief Marshal Sir Harv Smyth declared the defense of the Falkland Islands "non-negotiable," stating the UK remains on high alert following the leak of a Pentagon memo that considered reviewing US support for British sovereignty over the archipelago. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio played down the significance of the memo.

stories.title: Once the left wing of US Jewry, is J Street now the new center?
stories.summary: J Street, long considered the left wing of the American Jewish political lobby, is increasingly viewed as occupying a centrist position. The shift reflects declining Democratic support for Israel, with J Street's pushback against anti-Zionism placing it closer to the mainstream.

stories.title: Iraq starts work on Basra-Haditha oil pipeline: state media
stories.summary: Iraq has begun construction on an oil pipeline connecting the southern city of Basra to the western city of Haditha, according to state media. The pipeline is planned to have a capacity of 2.5 million barrels per day.

stories.title: Workers in land-trades sector call for total boycott of Israel
stories.summary: Members of the UK-based Solidarity Across Land Trades (SALT) union called on agricultural workers to boycott organizations linked with Israel. The appeal targets workers across the land-trades sector to take collective action.

stories.title: Warm, wild weather puts Europe on storm and drought watch in May
stories.summary: European weather forecasters warn that May will bring a mix of storms and unseasonably warm, dry conditions across the continent, raising concerns about both severe weather events and drought.

stories.title: Army plans fast follow-up to AI cyber wargame with industry: Officials
stories.summary: The U.S. Army plans to rapidly follow up on an AI-focused cyber wargame conducted with cybersecurity executives from 14 technology firms, exploring a Pacific-war scenario. Officials said the Army aims to fast-track new AI tools and develop policies allowing greater autonomy for AI agents in cyber operations.

stories.title: Average price of gas in California edges past $6 a gallon, highest level in four years
stories.summary: The average gasoline price in California reached $6.06 per gallon, the highest level in four years, while the national average hit $4.39 according to the American Automobile Association. Analysts attributed rising fuel costs partly to the impact of the US war on Iran, noting Americans have paid $21.7 billion more at the pump since the conflict began.

stories.title: IDF: Iron Beam laser saw limited use in Iran war due to lack of batteries, 14 needed
stories.summary: The IDF revealed that Israel's Iron Beam laser defense system saw limited deployment during the Iran conflict due to a shortage of batteries, with 14 units needed. Officials noted Iron Beam's per-shot cost is negligible compared to Arrow and Iron Dome interceptors, which cost millions and tens of thousands of shekels respectively.

stories.title: No magic way to stop Hezbollah's FPV drones from striking, IDF admits
stories.summary: The IDF acknowledged it has no reliable method to fully counter Hezbollah's first-person-view drones striking Israeli positions. However, military officials suggested that removing US-imposed restrictions on IDF operations in northern Lebanon could reduce the drone threat by approximately 80 percent.

stories.title: IDF shifts focus to Iranian nuclear threat as ballistic missiles, regime change fall by the wayside
stories.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces are shifting strategic focus toward Iran's nuclear program, moving away from prioritizing ballistic missile threats or regime change. IDF officers clarified the military never promised regime change in Iran, only the possibility of creating conditions for such an outcome.

stories.title: Trump to put 25% tariffs on EU cars, says bloc not complying with trade deal
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced he would raise tariffs on European Union cars and trucks to 25 percent, accusing the bloc of not complying with a trade deal reached last July with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. The previous agreement had set tariffs at 15 percent on most goods.

stories.title: Israeli Air Force says it dropped 135,000 bombs in recent wars, warns of Syrian military rebuild
stories.summary: The Israeli Air Force disclosed it dropped 135,000 bombs during recent conflicts, including 23,860 munitions requested directly by ground forces for close support in Gaza and Lebanon. The IAF also warned about ongoing Syrian military rebuilding efforts.

stories.title: Andy Burnham has plan to return to Westminster ‘within weeks’, allies say
stories.summary: Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham reportedly has a plan to return to the UK Parliament within weeks through a byelection, with allies saying several Labour MPs are prepared to step aside. Burnham was previously blocked by Labour's ruling body from running in February's Gorton and Denton byelection.

stories.title: Air defense forces shot down 388 of 409 Russian drones
stories.summary: Ukrainian air defense forces intercepted 388 of 409 Russian attack drones launched on the morning of May 1. The drones included Shahed, Gerbera, Italmas, and other types used by the Russian military.

stories.title: Israeli police arrest man suspected of attacking nun near Jerusalem’s Old City
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested a man captured on video attacking a nun near Jerusalem's Old City. The incident is part of a pattern of recent attacks targeting Christians in the area.

stories.title: White House declines to comment on Iran’s negotiation proposals
stories.summary: White House Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly declined to comment on the latest Iranian negotiation proposals submitted through Pakistan, stating the administration does not detail private diplomatic conversations. She reiterated President Trump's position that Iran must never possess a nuclear weapon and that negotiations continue.

stories.title: Pakistan's successful US-Iran mediation reflects South Asia rise
stories.summary: Pakistan's mediation between the United States and Iran reflects a growing South Asian role in Middle Eastern diplomacy. Analysts say the effort highlights shifting regional power balances amid ongoing Iran-US tensions and broader geopolitical realignment.

stories.title: Sabastian Sawe receives hero’s welcome in Kenya after sub-two hour marathon feat
stories.summary: Kenyan marathon runner Sabastian Sawe received a hero's welcome in his home region of western Kenya after becoming the first person to run an official marathon in under two hours, clocking 1 hour 59 minutes 30 seconds at the London Marathon. He was flown to Eldoret on a Kenyan military plane.

stories.title: Zayn Malik cancels all US dates of upcoming tour following illness
stories.summary: Former One Direction member Zayn Malik cancelled all US dates for his upcoming tour following hospitalization for an unspecified illness. Malik said in an Instagram post that he is recovering at home and thanked fans for their support.

stories.title: Woman charged over death of two eight-year-old girls after Wimbledon car crash
stories.summary: Claire Freemantle has been charged with two counts of causing death by dangerous driving and seven counts of causing serious injury after her car crashed into The Study Prep school in Wimbledon, south London, in July 2023. Two eight-year-old girls were killed in the incident.

stories.title: DRC's ex-president Joseph Kabila dismisses US sanctions as "politically motivated"
stories.summary: Former Democratic Republic of Congo president Joseph Kabila rejected newly imposed U.S. sanctions against him, calling them "unjustified and politically motivated." The sanctions were recently levied by Washington against the former Congolese leader.

stories.title: Russia may be able to sustain intensity of its offensive for another one to two years – Pivnenko
stories.summary: Ukrainian military intelligence chief Oleksandr Pivnenko assessed that Russia can sustain its current offensive intensity for one to two more years. However, he noted Russia lacks the capacity to form significant reserves for large-scale operations, particularly in northern Ukraine.

stories.title: Video of attack on French nun in Jerusalem causes widespread condemnation
stories.summary: A video showing an attack on a French Catholic nun and archaeological researcher on a Jerusalem street drew widespread condemnation. Israel's foreign ministry denounced the assault as a "shameful act" after footage showed a man pushing the woman to the ground and kicking her.

stories.title: Iranian Foreign Minister: Israel’s war has cost US $100bn
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi claimed on X that the US-Israeli war on Iran has cost the United States $100 billion, four times what the Pentagon has publicly stated. Araghchi accused the Pentagon of lying about the war's costs and criticized the financial burden on American taxpayers.

stories.title: Foreign Office cuts will weaken oversight of international law, MPs warn
stories.summary: A cross-party group of British MPs warned that the closure of the Foreign Office's international humanitarian law unit will weaken the UK's ability to monitor and respond to violations of international law. The issue was raised with Prime Minister Keir Starmer during parliamentary questions.

stories.title: How Iranian monarchists have targeted anti-war activists
stories.summary: Iranian-British engineer Arjang Alidai, based in the UK, has received hundreds of threatening messages from Iranian monarchists after voting in the 2024 Iranian presidential election. Anti-government Iranians who boycotted the vote have targeted voters and those opposing military action against Iran.

stories.title: Cubans mark May Day amid rising humanitarian crisis
stories.summary: May Day demonstrations took place worldwide, with notable events in several cities. In Istanbul, police used tear gas and arrested around 400 people. In Havana, a large march gathered amid Cuba's ongoing humanitarian crisis, while protests also began in Paris at Place de la République.

stories.title: ‘What’s our red line?’ British Jews question their safety
stories.summary: Jewish communities in Britain are increasingly discussing whether rising antisemitic incidents have reached a tipping point that might prompt them to leave the country. Some are considering Israel or other destinations as potential refuges.

stories.title: Zelensky announces launch of military reforms with higher pay and updated contracts
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky announced military reforms set to begin in June, including higher pay and updated contracts for soldiers, non-commissioned officers, and commanders. Initial results, particularly regarding financial support for service members, are expected this month.

stories.title: Activists on Gaza aid flotilla detained by Israel disembark in Crete
stories.summary: Activists detained by Israel after attempting to deliver aid to Gaza by flotilla have disembarked in Crete, Greece. Several European governments with nationals among those arrested have called on Israel to release them.

stories.title: Russian State Prosecutors Seek Forfeiture of Jailed Billionaire’s Assets
stories.summary: Russian state prosecutors are seeking to seize the assets of jailed billionaire Vadim Moshkovich. He is the first Forbes-listed billionaire to be arrested in Russia since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine began.

stories.title: Power minister declares end to month-long loadshedding following arrival of LNG shipment
stories.summary: Pakistan's Power Minister Awais Leghari announced the end of a month-long period of electricity loadshedding following the arrival of a liquefied natural gas shipment. He attributed the outages to a gas shortage linked to the US-Iran war rather than system failures.

stories.title: Tribal chiefs lack legal authority to attest documents, Federal Constitutional Court rules
stories.summary: Pakistan's Federal Constitutional Court ruled that tribal chiefs nominated by their communities do not have legal authority to attest documents such as domicile certificates or national identity card applications. The ruling came while rejecting a petition by a self-proclaimed sardar of the Kharoti tribe seeking official recognition.

stories.title: Attack on Ternopil: About 20 Shahed drones explode over city, 10 people reported injured
stories.summary: Approximately 20 Russian Shahed drones exploded over the city of Ternopil in western Ukraine, injuring at least 10 people. More than 50 Shahed drones were detected approaching the city during the attack.

stories.title: Iranian official calls Strait of Hormuz Iran’s “natural right”
stories.summary: Iranian Deputy Parliament Speaker Ali Nikzad declared that the Strait of Hormuz is Iran's "natural right" rather than an international waterway, according to comments reported by Tasnim news agency. The statement follows President Masoud Pezeshkian's characterization of the American naval blockade on the strait as "intolerable."

stories.title: Hezbollah drones wound 4 troops; IDF urges civilians to leave south Lebanon town
stories.summary: Hezbollah drone attacks wounded four Israeli soldiers near the Lebanese border, prompting the IDF Home Front Command to tighten security guidelines in border communities. Lebanese state media reported four people, including a woman, were killed in IDF strikes in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: How Iranian monarchists have targeted anti-war activists
stories.summary: Supporters of Reza Pahlavi, the exiled son of Iran's last shah, have reportedly targeted anti-war activists through intimidation and violent attacks. The monarchist campaign has sought to silence critics opposed to their political agenda.

stories.title: Two injured, car destroyed by Hezbollah drone attack against northern Israel border town
stories.summary: A Hezbollah drone crossed into northern Israel and struck a border town, injuring two people and destroying a car. The IDF confirmed the incident and called it a violation of ceasefire understandings by Hezbollah.

stories.title: Russian drones hit food processing plant in Bohodukhiv, injuring four workers
stories.summary: Russian drones struck a food processing plant in Bohodukhiv in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, injuring four workers. The attack targeted a manufacturing facility in the city.

stories.title: Iranian-linked drones target opposition camp in Iraqi Kurdistan
stories.summary: Drones linked to Iran struck an opposition camp in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq. The attack is part of a broader escalation in Iraqi Kurdistan, which has been increasingly drawn into regional tensions connected to the US-led war against Iran.

stories.title: EU trade deal with South America’s Mercosur bloc takes provisional effect
stories.summary: The EU-Mercosur free trade agreement has provisionally taken effect, creating one of the world's largest free trade zones encompassing approximately 720 million potential consumers across Europe and South America.

stories.title: WHO recorded 149 attacks on health care in Lebanon
stories.summary: The World Health Organization recorded 149 attacks by the Israeli military on healthcare facilities and workers in Lebanon since February 28. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus also reported 26 attacks on healthcare in Iran and 6 in Israel during the same period.

stories.title: Trump says he will raise tariffs on EU autos to 25% for 'not complying' with trade deal
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced he will raise tariffs on European Union vehicles to 25 percent the following week, accusing the bloc of not complying with the 2025 trade agreement.

stories.title: Army reform in Ukraine to boost combat pay and reshape how troops are recruited and retained
stories.summary: Ukraine announced military reforms to restructure combat pay and troop recruitment and retention policies. The changes will link pay more closely to combat exposure and frontline responsibility, with infantry roles receiving the largest increases.

stories.title: Iran war hampering aid to refugees as costs soar, UN warns
stories.summary: The United Nations warned that the Iran war has more than doubled the cost of delivering humanitarian aid to war-torn Sudan by disrupting shipping routes. Rising transport costs and delivery delays are hampering relief efforts for Sudanese refugees.

stories.title: Commander of National Guard does not believe in potential offensive from Belarus
stories.summary: The commander of Ukraine's National Guard stated he does not believe Belarus will launch an offensive against Ukraine. He noted that strong Ukrainian defense units with significant drone capabilities are now deployed along the Belarusian border, making a rapid breakthrough like the 2022 invasion unlikely.

stories.title: Pro-Trump commentator snaps and drops F-bomb on CNN when asked to justify Iran war
stories.summary: CNN commentator Scott Jennings swore on live television after being repeatedly pressed by progressive commentator Adam Mockler to name a concrete political concession the U.S. had gained from its war with Iran. Jennings was unable to provide an answer during the exchange on NewsNight With Abby Phillip.

stories.title: Fifa Congress: Infantino tried to stage an Israel-Palestine handshake. He failed
stories.summary: FIFA President Gianni Infantino attempted to arrange a handshake between Israeli and Palestinian representatives at the FIFA Congress but failed. Palestinian Football Association chief Jibril Rajoub reportedly refused, saying he could not shake hands with someone brought to "whitewash" Israeli actions.

stories.title: Pentagon announces deal with seven AI companies for classified systems
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced agreements with seven artificial intelligence companies to develop classified military systems. The deal comes amid a reported standoff with AI firm Anthropic and growing debate over AI use in the context of the Iran war.

stories.title: Israel’s Slow War on the West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli leaders appear increasingly comfortable with the potential collapse of the Palestinian Authority as Israel continues gradual military and political pressure in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: US Hormuz coalition ‘not in competition’ with France-Britain mission, says French minister
stories.summary: France's defense minister stated that the US-led naval coalition in the Strait of Hormuz is not competing with the separate Franco-British maritime mission in the area, describing the two efforts as complementary.

stories.title: Lebanese Health Ministry: Israel has killed 2618 since March
stories.summary: The Lebanese Ministry of Public Health reported that 2,618 people have been killed and 8,094 wounded by Israeli attacks between March 2 and May 1. The toll includes casualties from ongoing Israeli strikes in Lebanon following a ceasefire agreement reached on April 17.

stories.title: Israeli police arrest man after nun attacked in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested a man in Jerusalem after a French nun was pushed and kicked near the Old City in an apparently unprovoked assault. The incident comes amid increasing harassment of Christians in Jerusalem by Jewish extremists.

stories.title: Israeli forces assault Palestinian child with Down syndrome
stories.summary: Armed Israeli forces chased and briefly detained a Palestinian child with Down syndrome in occupied East Jerusalem, according to footage that went viral online. The incident drew widespread attention and condemnation.

stories.title: General Staff confirms destruction of Su-57 and Su-34 aircraft in strikes on Shagol airfield
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed the destruction of Russian Su-57 and Su-34 aircraft at the Shagol airfield in Chelyabinsk Oblast on April 25. The strikes targeted one of Russia's advanced fighter jet bases deep inside Russian territory.

stories.title: Power minister declares end of month-long loadshedding following arrival of LNG shipment
stories.summary: Pakistan's Power Minister Awais Leghari announced the end of a month-long period of electricity loadshedding following the arrival of a liquefied natural gas shipment. Leghari attributed the outages to a gas shortage linked to the US-Iran conflict rather than systemic failures.

stories.title: Artist from war-torn north relocates to Tel Aviv, discovers success with works of kibbutz views
stories.summary: Israeli artist Doron Adorian, evacuated from northern Israel after October 7, 2023, relocated to Tel Aviv where she found success in the art community. Her paintings of kibbutz landscapes now hang in prominent collections, including that of former US Ambassador to Israel Jack Lew.

stories.title: Azerbaijan summons EU envoy in row over treatment of Karabakh Armenians
stories.summary: Azerbaijan's Foreign Ministry summoned the EU envoy over a resolution concerning the treatment of Karabakh Armenians. Baku dismissed the resolution as "unfounded and biased," maintaining that Karabakh Armenians left the region voluntarily.

stories.title: Spirit Airlines prepares to cease operations amid financial struggles and high oil prices
stories.summary: Spirit Airlines is preparing to cease operations after running out of cash, with a rescue attempt by the Trump administration apparently stalling. The airline had struggled with post-pandemic demand before the war in Iran drove up jet fuel costs.

stories.title: General Staff confirms new strikes on oil refineries in Tuapse and Perm
stories.summary: On the night of May 1, Ukraine's defense forces struck oil refineries in Tuapse and Perm, Russia. The operation also targeted a Buk-M3 air defense system in occupied Donetsk region and Russian military warehouses.

stories.title: Israeli forces conduct raids and seize land in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli forces raided Burqa village near Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, firing rubber-coated bullets, live ammunition, and gas canisters at Palestinians leaving Friday prayers, wounding a young man. Several young men and children were detained. Forces also seized land near the village of Kharsa close to Hebron.

stories.title: US sends 30 planeloads of military equipment to Middle East
stories.summary: The United States sent 30 planeloads of military equipment to the Middle East and delivered 6,500 tons of materiel to Israel. The shipments come amid concerns that the conflict with Iran could resume.

stories.title: Microbes coordinate activity to reduce competition, Israeli researchers discover
stories.summary: Israeli researchers led by Dr. Sarah Moraïs discovered that microbes coordinate their activity to reduce competition with neighboring organisms. The findings show microbes respond not only to environmental conditions but also to the presence and identity of other microbes nearby.

stories.title: US Navy turns to AI firm for options to counter Iranian mines
stories.summary: The US Navy awarded a contract to an artificial intelligence firm to develop capabilities for detecting and countering Iranian naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. The effort is part of a broader push to enhance AI-driven mine countermeasures in the region.

stories.title: $7 billion lost from Russia’s war economy this year through Ukraine’s “long-range sanctions” on oil sector – Zelenskyy
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Ukraine's long-range strikes on Russian oil processing and export facilities have cost Russia $7 billion in lost revenue this year. The damage has reduced Russia's capacity to export oil at full volume.

stories.title: Rebel alliance seizes key Tessalit military camp in northern Mali
stories.summary: A rebel alliance of Tuareg separatists and jihadist fighters seized the key military camp at Tessalit in northern Mali. The groups have been waging a joint campaign against Mali's ruling military junta.

stories.title: Pentagon inks deals with AI giants, but not Anthropic
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense signed agreements with OpenAI, Google, and SpaceX, among others, to deploy advanced AI models on the military's classified networks. Anthropic was notably excluded from the deals.

stories.title: Youssou N'Dour and Fatoumata Diawara headline FEMUA 2026
stories.summary: The 2026 edition of FEMUA, the major music festival in Ivory Coast, features headliners Youssou N'Dour and Fatoumata Diawara. Founded by Magic System's A'Salfo, the festival takes place in Anoumabo and Dimbokro, with Gabon as this year's special guest country.

stories.title: Russian drone crash in Vinnytsia region leaves one injured
