stories.summary: An estimated 8 million children in Sudan have been unable to attend school since the civil war began in April 2023. Displaced Sudanese children are now participating in programs to catch up on lost years of education.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones 4–0 Tuapse oil: refinery ablaze again after fourth strike last night
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Rosneft's refinery and terminal complex in Tuapse, Russia, for the fourth time, igniting another section of the facility on May 1. Cleanup from earlier strikes was still ongoing, involving removal of fuel and contaminated soil from the site.

stories.title: All Pakistan Newspaper Employees Confederation calls for restoration of Dawn ads
stories.summary: The All Pakistan Newspaper Employees Confederation called for the immediate restoration of government advertisements to Dawn newspaper, citing a severe financial crisis affecting thousands of media workers. The demand was made at a meeting held at the Pakistan Herald Workers' Union office in Karachi.

stories.title: Labour rights
stories.summary: An editorial on May Day argues that Pakistan's observance of Labour Day should move beyond rhetoric to address workers' job insecurity, safety hazards, and inadequate wages. It notes that most Pakistani workers are in the informal sector, with only 2–3 percent of the workforce organized.

stories.title: Air Defense Forces shoot down 190 of 210 Russian drones
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Defense Forces intercepted 190 of 210 drones launched by the Russian military in an overnight attack. Enemy strikes were recorded at 14 locations across the country.

stories.title: Aung San Suu Kyi moved from prison to house arrest in Myanmar
stories.summary: Myanmar's military authorities moved former leader Aung San Suu Kyi from prison to house arrest as part of a prisoner amnesty marking the Buddhist Full Moon Day of Kason. Her sentence was reduced as part of the amnesty honoring Buddha's birthday.

stories.title: Lifetime arrest warrants issued against Malik Riaz, son and co-accused in Bahria Town Karachi landgrab case
stories.summary: A Pakistani accountability court issued perpetual non-bailable arrest warrants against property tycoon Malik Riaz, his son, and co-accused in the Bahria Town Karachi land grab case. The National Accountability Bureau filed a reference alleging the illegal conversion and transfer of government land for the Bahria Town Karachi project.

stories.title: Stand with Afeka College in Engineering Israel’s Future - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: American Friends of Afeka College is promoting engineering education in Israel, supporting IDF reservists, and developing a new engineering campus. The sponsored content highlights the organization's innovation and educational mission.

stories.title: Amnesty urges probe into deaths at Nigerian military-run camp
stories.summary: Amnesty International called on Nigerian authorities to investigate the reported deaths of 150 members of the Fulani ethnic group at a military-run camp. The human rights organization issued its appeal on Thursday.

stories.title: Trump threatens to withdraw US troops from Italy and Spain – Europe live
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened to withdraw American troops from Italy and Spain, broadening a review of US military presence in Europe following public criticism from European leaders over the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: PTCL ‘remains closely engaged’ with e&
stories.summary: Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL) stated that its managing shareholder e& (formerly Etisalat) remains closely engaged with the company. PTCL responded to reports suggesting the Emirati telecom giant was considering exiting its Pakistan investment, saying shareholders remain committed to the company's long-term strategy.

stories.title: Met police chief denies ‘intervening in politics’ after open letter to Zack Polanski – UK politics live
stories.summary: London Metropolitan Police Commissioner denied intervening in politics after writing an open letter to Green Party leader Zack Polanski, who had shared footage appearing to show officers kicking the suspect in the Golders Green antisemitic stabbing attack.

stories.title: Malignant non-disclosure: PM’s belated cancer revelation subverts public’s right to know
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu belatedly disclosed a prostate tumor diagnosis, with vague details from his doctors raising questions about the timeline of his treatment, including whether he received cancer care during the conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Lights, camera, traction: film-projecting headlights steer China’s EV feature fight
stories.summary: At Beijing's Auto China show, Chinese electric vehicle makers showcased innovations including ultra-fast battery charging and film-projecting headlights. Domestic carmakers are recasting vehicles as AI-powered mobile living spaces and expanding export efforts to compete globally.

stories.title: Iran offers new proposal amid stalled US peace talks
stories.summary: Iran submitted a new peace proposal to the United States through mediator Pakistan, Iranian state media reported. The move comes after weeks of stalemate in negotiations between Tehran and Washington.

stories.title: Iran activates air defences as Trump faces Congress war deadline
stories.summary: Iran activated its air defense systems against incoming projectiles as the White House signaled it would disregard a congressional deadline regarding authorization for military action. Tensions between Washington and Tehran continue to escalate.

stories.title: Enemy launches drone attack on Kharkiv
stories.summary: Russian forces launched a drone strike on the Kholodnohirskyi district of Kharkiv, Ukraine. Details on casualties and damage from the attack were being assessed.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s East Dam draws thousands for ‘golden week’ as lawmaker floats entry fee
stories.summary: Thousands of visitors traveled to Hong Kong's East Dam at the High Island Reservoir Geopark during the Labour Day golden week holiday to view rare volcanic rock columns. A lawmaker proposed charging an entrance fee to help maintain the UNESCO-listed site.

stories.title: London police charge man with attempted murder in antisemitic Golders Green stabbing attack
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police charged a man with attempted murder in connection with an antisemitic stabbing attack in Golders Green, north London. In response to the attack, Britain raised its national terrorism threat level from 'substantial' to 'severe.'

stories.title: Russian forces launch nearly 20 overnight attacks on Dnipropetrovsk region, one wounded
stories.summary: The Russian military launched nearly 20 drone and artillery attacks overnight on three districts in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region, injuring one person. The strikes targeted multiple areas across the region.

stories.title: UK house prices jump despite impact of Middle East conflict
stories.summary: UK house prices rose 3% year-on-year in April, the fastest annual pace in 11 months, bringing the average property value to £278,880 according to Nationwide, surprising economists despite the broader economic impact of the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Hezbollah’s latest challenge to Israeli forces: A stealthier drone
stories.summary: Hezbollah has deployed a new type of drone against Israeli forces that is guided by thin fibre-optic cables rather than radio signals, making the aircraft harder to detect and jam.

stories.title: Trump insists Iran would use a nuclear weapon if it had one, praises Epic Fury's military successes
stories.summary: President Donald Trump told Newsmax that Iran would use a nuclear weapon if it possessed one and praised the military successes of Operation Epic Fury. Trump stated that while Iran's military has been heavily damaged, a guarantee against nuclear development is necessary for lasting peace.

stories.title: London assailant charged with attempted murder over terror stabbing of two Jews
stories.summary: London authorities charged Essa Suleiman with attempted murder for the stabbing of two Jewish individuals in what is being treated as a terror attack. He was also charged with attempted murder in a separate incident the same day and had a prior conviction for stabbing a police officer in 2008.

stories.title: Could a prolonged conflict between the US and Iran threaten another vital link?
stories.summary: Tensions between the United States and Iran have raised concerns about the vulnerability of undersea internet cables running through the Strait of Hormuz, which serves as both a critical oil chokepoint and a key corridor for Middle Eastern digital communications.

stories.title: China’s manufacturing rise is here to stay. The West must recalibrate
stories.summary: Columbia University professor Adam Tooze argues that China's expanded manufacturing dominance — dubbed "China shock 2.0" — extends across sectors including aviation, AI, telecoms, and robotics, requiring Western economies to recalibrate their strategies.

stories.title: U.S. official says Iran war truce ‘terminated’ hostilities for war powers deadline
stories.summary: A U.S. official stated that the truce with Iran has "terminated" hostilities for purposes of the War Powers Resolution deadline. There has been no exchange of fire between U.S. armed forces and Iran since a fragile ceasefire began more than three weeks ago.

stories.title: Russian military loses another 1,420 troops in war against Ukraine
stories.summary: According to Ukrainian military estimates, Russian forces have lost approximately 1,331,710 personnel since the full-scale invasion began on February 24, 2022. An estimated 1,420 Russian troops were killed in the most recent 24-hour period ending May 1, 2026.

stories.title: Russians crawl through a gas pipeline from Sudzha for two weeks to attack Ukraine’s Sumy Oblast
stories.summary: Six Russian soldiers were killed on April 29 while attempting to infiltrate Ukraine's Sumy Oblast by crawling through a gas pipeline from Russia's Sudzha. Ukrainian military officials described it as the latest failed incursion on the Northern-Slobozhansky front.

stories.title: Governance gaps weaken Pakistan’s climate disaster response, report warns
stories.summary: A report by the Jinnah Institute warns that persistent governance failures and weak community-level systems continue to undermine Pakistan's climate disaster response. The findings follow the devastating 2025 floods, which displaced millions and exposed critical gaps in preparedness despite existing policy frameworks.

stories.title: Russian nighttime attack damages high-rise buildings in Odesa, injures civilians
stories.summary: A Russian nighttime attack struck residential high-rise buildings in the Khadzhibey district of Odesa, Ukraine, injuring civilians. The strikes caused damage to multiple residential structures.

stories.title: Weather tracker: Tornadoes and giant hail in central US
stories.summary: A series of severe thunderstorms struck the central United States early in the week, producing eight tornadoes on Monday — including an EF2 tornado in Sycamore, Kansas — and a stronger tornado in Mineral Wells, Texas, where a disaster was declared. Extreme rainfall also caused flooding in China.

stories.title: US congress member says 'imminent' military strikes on Iran still on the table
stories.summary: US Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal told CNN that imminent military strikes on Iran remain a possibility. He cited classified briefings with military leaders but declined to provide specific timing or operational details.

stories.title: Ukraine begins to flex muscle as an emerging air power, angering Russia
stories.summary: Ukraine has expanded its air capabilities with strikes into Russian territory, prompting Russian officials to label the attacks as terrorism and call for heightened vigilance among the public.

stories.title: IHC upholds Capital Development Authority’s decision of canceling One Constitution Avenue lease
stories.summary: The Islamabad High Court upheld the Capital Development Authority's cancellation of the lease for the One Constitution Avenue skyscraper due to multi-billion-rupee payment defaults. IHC Chief Justice Sardar Mohammad Sarfraz Dogar announced the decision on appeals filed by BNP (Private) Limited and flat occupants.

stories.title: Israeli public believes Bennett, Eisenkot are more suitable as prime minister than Netanyahu - poll
stories.summary: A new Israeli poll found that the public considers Naftali Bennett and Gadi Eisenkot more suitable as prime minister than Benjamin Netanyahu. The poll also showed that the Together Party, formed by Bennett and Yair Lapid, dropped from 31 to 28 seats compared to the previous week's results.

stories.title: Venice Biennale jury resigns against participation of Russia and Israel
stories.summary: The entire international jury of the Venice Biennale resigned on Thursday over the continued participation of Russia and a decision to bar prizes for countries accused of crimes against humanity, including Russia and Israel. The winners' announcement has been postponed until November.

stories.title: Former DR Congo President Joseph Kabila hit with US sanctions
stories.summary: The United States imposed sanctions on former Democratic Republic of Congo President Joseph Kabila, accusing him of supporting the Rwanda-backed M23 rebel group and its political-military wing, the Congo River Alliance.

stories.title: Countries mark May Day with mass street demonstrations
stories.summary: Mass demonstrations marked International Workers' Day worldwide, with activists demanding higher wages and improved labor rights. In France, unions rallied under the slogan "bread, peace and freedom," linking worker concerns to the conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East.

stories.title: US considers reducing troops in Germany
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened to withdraw American troops from Germany after Chancellor Friedrich Merz remarked that the US was being "humiliated" by Tehran. Merz has maintained that the transatlantic partnership remains strong despite the tensions.

stories.title: UK raises national terror threat level following antisemitic incidents
stories.summary: The United Kingdom raised its national terror threat level from substantial to severe, indicating an attack is considered likely within six months. The decision followed recent antisemitic incidents including the stabbing of two Jewish men in north London, prompting the government to pledge increased security for Jewish communities.

stories.title: At least 15 killed in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon reportedly killed at least 15 people on Thursday, with unconfirmed reports suggesting the toll could exceed 30. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun condemned the attacks as violations of a nearly two-week-old ceasefire, while the US embassy in Beirut called for a meeting between Aoun and Israeli PM Netanyahu.

stories.title: Deadline for US Congress on war in Iran
stories.summary: US Central Command has reportedly drafted plans for "short and powerful" military strikes against Iran to break the stalemate in negotiations, according to Axios. The report briefly pushed oil prices up nearly 7%, surpassing $126 per barrel on Thursday.

stories.title: Housing snapshot April 2026: Home prices continue slide, bringing yearly drop to 1.7%
stories.summary: Home prices in Israel continued to decline in April 2026, with an annual drop reaching 1.7 percent, according to a Times of Israel market analysis.

stories.title: ‘Journalists compelled to self-censor to avoid legal trouble’
stories.summary: Press freedom watchdog Freedom Network warned that the weaponization of Pakistan's cybercrime laws, particularly amendments to the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) 2016, is creating a climate of fear among journalists. The report, released ahead of World Press Freedom Day on May 3, said journalists are compelled to self-censor to avoid legal repercussions.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: Over 80 Congolese Soldiers Face Trial for Fleeing Battles Against Rebels
stories.summary: Eighty-four Congolese soldiers are facing military trial in Kinshasa for allegedly fleeing combat against AFC/M23 rebels in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The charges include violating military orders, according to the Congolese army.

stories.title: Nigeria: When Even Water Needs a Second Look - Nigeria's Dangerous Dance With Fake Products
stories.summary: Nigeria faces a growing counterfeit-product crisis that threatens consumer safety, undermines legitimate businesses, and weakens the country's appeal as a foreign investment destination.

stories.title: Iran’s Supreme Leader defies US blockade as oil prices soar
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei defied the US naval blockade and predicted a future for the Persian Gulf region without American presence, as oil prices continued to rise amid the conflict.

stories.title: Labour Day in Lebanon starts amid heavy Israeli shelling
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes were reported flying over Tyre in south Lebanon on Labour Day, while heavy shelling struck several towns and villages in the south, including Wadi al-Hujeir, Qalaouiyah, and Al-Ghandouriyah, according to Lebanon's National News Agency.

stories.title: Iran vows ‘long, painful’ response if US renews attacks
stories.summary: Iran has threatened a prolonged and painful response if the United States resumes military strikes. Diplomatic negotiations to resolve the conflict have stalled, though a ceasefire established on April 8 remains in effect.

stories.title: Modern Combat Requires Warrior Medics Modeled After Machaon
stories.summary: An analysis argues that modern peer-to-peer combat, as demonstrated in Ukraine, has rendered the concept of protected medical units obsolete. Russian forces have systematically targeted Ukrainian aid stations and evacuation routes, highlighting the need for combat medics to receive tactical training under fire.

stories.title: Enemy attacks port infrastructure in Izmail district
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked port infrastructure in the Izmail district of Ukraine's Odesa region. The strike targeted facilities in the district, which is a key area for Ukrainian grain exports along the Danube River.

stories.title: UN chief warns Hormuz closure ‘strangling’ global economy
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres warned that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is "strangling the global economy" and could push tens of millions into poverty. He said restrictions on passage through the vital waterway are impeding delivery of oil, gas, fertilizer, and other critical commodities, risking a global recession.

stories.title: Crane truck driver runs the red signal at Lviv crossing — the train engineer he killed was a war veteran
stories.summary: A crane truck driver ran a red signal at a railway crossing in Lviv, Ukraine, causing a collision that killed a train engineer who was a war veteran. Two other people were hospitalized, though passengers on the train were uninjured.

stories.title: A Tale of Two Sisters - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A sponsored story profiles two sisters in their eighties who become unexpected roommates during wartime in Israel.

stories.title: Facing 60-day deadline, Trump administration claims Iran war ‘terminated’
stories.summary: The Trump administration argues that the US war in Iran has effectively ended due to the early-April ceasefire, a legal interpretation that would allow the White House to bypass a congressional authorization requirement. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth testified to the Senate that the ceasefire constituted a pause in hostilities.

stories.title: Fuel hits Rs400 per litre as govt passes on global impact
stories.summary: Pakistan's government raised petrol prices by Rs6.59 and diesel by Rs19.39 per litre, with IMF concurrence, to address rising global oil costs. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif extended fuel subsidies for motorcyclists and the transport sector by one month. Officials warned parliament of a potential $10–68 billion economic fallout from the Middle East crisis.

stories.title: Hongkongers flock to Shenzhen for ‘better’ Labour Day dining and attractions
stories.summary: Hong Kong residents crossed into Shenzhen during the Labour Day golden week holiday, attracted by more affordable dining, dental services, and family entertainment, with many budgeting around HK$1,000 for a full day.

stories.title: Why Lebanon Is Nonnegotiable for Iran
stories.summary: During US-Iranian ceasefire talks mediated by Pakistan in Islamabad in early April, Lebanon emerged as a key sticking point. Iran insisted that Lebanon and Hizballah were part of the ceasefire agreement, while the US and Israel initially rejected that interpretation, with President Trump calling Israeli operations in Lebanon a "separate skirmish."

stories.title: Palestinian football chief refuses to pose with Israeli counterpart at Fifa event
stories.summary: Palestine Football Association President Jibril Rajoub refused to pose for a photo or shake hands with Israeli Football Association Vice-President Basim Sheikh Suliman at a FIFA event. Rajoub cited Palestinian suffering and accused Israel of using the occasion to 'whitewash' its actions. FIFA President Gianni Infantino had called both officials to the stage.

stories.title: Breathe Pakistan conference  to be held at Serena
stories.summary: The Breathe Pakistan International Climate Change Conference has been relocated from the Jinnah Convention Centre to the Sheesh Mahal Hall at Serena Hotel in Islamabad. The May 6–7 event's agenda, dates, and session timings remain unchanged despite the venue change.

stories.title: Trump likely among 287 candidates for Nobel Peace Prize
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump is likely among 287 candidates being considered for the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, according to the Norwegian Nobel Committee. The list includes 208 individuals and 79 organizations, with the winner to be announced on October 9. The committee also raised alarm over the health of jailed Iranian laureate Narges Mohammadi.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz stated that Tel Aviv might resume its war on Iran 'soon' to achieve its objectives, despite a pause in fighting. Separately, a senior US official told NBC News that US hostilities against Tehran that began in late February have been 'terminated,' citing a two-week ceasefire agreed on April 7 that has since been extended.

stories.title: Pakistan commissions first Chinese attack submarine in ‘historic milestone’ for navy
stories.summary: The Pakistan Navy commissioned its first Chinese-built Hangor-class attack submarine, PNS/M Hangor, at a ceremony in Sanya, Hainan Island. Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari and Naval Chief Admiral Naveed Ashraf attended alongside senior Chinese officials.

stories.title: Mozambique: Small Increase in Minimum Wage, But No Hikes for Health, Govt Workers
stories.summary: Mozambique's Council of Ministers approved modest minimum-wage increases for the private sector on 28 April following negotiations among the government, employers, and the Consilimo trade union federation. Health-sector and government workers were excluded from the wage hikes.

stories.title: Veteran election czar Orly Adas resigns, throwing committee into turmoil
stories.summary: Orly Adas, the long-serving director of Israel's Central Elections Committee, resigned amid a reported dispute over extending her term. A Supreme Court deputy said he attempted to persuade her to stay, and her departure has created turmoil within the committee.

stories.title: US judge rejects Trump administration's halt on immigration applications
stories.summary: A federal judge in Boston ruled that Trump administration policies making it harder for people from travel-ban countries to obtain green cards and work permits are discriminatory and unlawful.

stories.title: Russia hammers targets across Ukraine overnight
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out overnight strikes targeting towns along the Black Sea coast and in central Ukraine, killing at least one person and injuring several others.

stories.title: Man arrested in Japan for burning wife’s body in zoo incinerator
stories.summary: Japanese police in Hokkaido arrested Tatsuya Suzuki on suspicion of incinerating his wife Yui Suzuki's body using an incinerator at the zoo where he worked, after human remains were discovered at the facility.

stories.title: After 25 years of negotiation, the Mercosur-EU agreement takes effect this Friday
stories.summary: The trade agreement between the Mercosur bloc and the European Union provisionally enters into force on Friday, May 1, after more than 25 years of negotiations. The final signing occurred on January 17 in Asunción, Paraguay. Provisional implementation allows immediate tariff reductions covering 95% of traded goods, though European Parliament ratification remains pending.

stories.title: White phosphorus reportedly used in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli forces reportedly carried out strikes using white phosphorus munitions in Nabatiyeh, southern Lebanon, according to circulating footage and reports. White phosphorus ignites on contact with oxygen and can rapidly spread fires. Human rights organizations have condemned Israel's use of such munitions as unlawful.

stories.title: 'Military force unable to solve Mali crisis': Is political solution only 'viable path forward'?
stories.summary: Following the death of Malian Defence Minister Sadio Camara, thousands attended tributes as analysts warned that military force alone cannot resolve Mali's deepening crisis. Chatham House expert Paul Melly assessed the situation within the context of a shifting geopolitical landscape in the Sahel.

stories.title: Ukraine and Netherlands plan to launch joint drone production this year
stories.summary: Ukraine and the Netherlands announced plans to begin joint production of drones, specifically the Baton and K4 models, as early as this year. The terms of the agreement remain confidential, with further project details undisclosed.

stories.title: UK police charge man with attempted murder for stabbing two Jewish Londoners
stories.summary: British police charged a 45-year-old British national on Friday with attempted murder in connection with the stabbing of two Jewish men in north London. Both victims are reported to be in stable condition.

stories.title: What do Ukraine’s robot soldiers mean for the future of warfare?
stories.summary: Ukraine's military has increasingly deployed remote-controlled and AI-assisted robotic weapons on the battlefield. The technology raises questions about the future role of artificial intelligence in autonomous combat decision-making.

stories.title: Police fire at stolen car after checkpoint breach in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli police opened fire at the wheels of a stolen vehicle in the West Bank after the driver crashed through a checkpoint, struck a patrol car, and sped toward IDF forces. The incident prompted a security response at the scene.

stories.title: Israeli attack in Nabatiyeh kills two, wounds several others
stories.summary: An Israeli strike on Nabatiyeh al-Faouqa in southern Lebanon killed two people and wounded at least 10 others, according to Lebanon's state-owned National News Agency. The attack occurred despite an April ceasefire, as Israel has continued military operations across southern Lebanon targeting infrastructure and residential areas.

stories.title: News live: Albanese rejects speculation about CGT discount changes; Israel says six detained Australians being moved to Crete
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Albanese rejected speculation about changes to capital gains tax discounts. Separately, Israel stated that six detained Australians are being transferred to Crete. In an unrelated incident, police in South Sydney reported a man allegedly stole nearly $3,000 worth of diesel from a service station.

stories.title: On May Day, Gaza’s workers find whatever source of income they can
stories.summary: Gaza's economic collapse has driven workers to take dangerous and precarious jobs to survive. Unemployment has surged amid continuing devastation in the territory, with residents seeking any available source of income on May Day.

stories.title: Friday briefing: How rising antisemitism is striking fear into the everyday lives of British Jews
stories.summary: A 45-year-old man was charged with attempted murder after two Jewish men were stabbed in Golders Green, north London, on Wednesday. The attack is part of a pattern of rising antisemitic incidents in the UK that has prompted many British Jews to fear for their safety.

stories.title: ‘Profoundly distressing’: record number of deaths in custody and police operations in NSW
stories.summary: New South Wales recorded a record 66 deaths in custody and police operations in 2025, an increase of 18 over the previous year. A coroners court report found nearly a quarter of prisoner deaths were attributed to self-harm, mostly by hanging, despite investment in removing ligature points from facilities.

stories.title: Opening Hormuz 'not a humanitarian gesture': Essential to keeping global food system operating
stories.summary: International Chamber of Commerce Secretary General John Denton warned that keeping the Strait of Hormuz open is essential to the global food system, not just oil and gas supply. He identified deteriorating access to fertiliser as the sharpest immediate concern, linking it to "cataclysmic risk" for global food security.

stories.title: Why is piracy rising off Somalia again — and is the Iran war responsible?
stories.summary: At least four vessels have been hijacked off the coast of Somalia in recent weeks, raising concerns about a resurgence of piracy in the region. The spike has prompted questions about whether the ongoing Iran war and related disruptions to naval patrols may be contributing factors.

stories.title: US official says Iran war truce 'terminated' hostilities for war powers deadline
stories.summary: A US official stated that for War Powers Resolution purposes, hostilities against Iran that began on February 28 have been 'terminated.' The declaration references the ongoing US-Iran ceasefire, which has been in effect since early April.

stories.title: Sheryl Sandberg announces scholarship fund for Camp Ramah in honor of late husband
stories.summary: Former Meta COO Sheryl Sandberg announced a scholarship fund for Camp Ramah in honor of her late husband Dave Goldberg. Sandberg said Goldberg's Jewish identity took root and grew during his time at the camp.

stories.title: Workers across the world march for peace and better pay in May Day rallies
stories.summary: May Day rallies took place worldwide on Friday, with workers from Islamabad to Istanbul protesting rising energy prices linked to the US-Israeli war on Iran. Demonstrators also called for better pay and peace amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: BAE faces £120m lawsuit over decision to scrap support for aid aircraft
stories.summary: Kenya-based aid cargo operator EnComm Aviation is suing BAE Systems for £120 million, alleging the British defense firm scrapped support for aircraft used to deliver humanitarian aid. EnComm claims the decision forced cancellation of contracts and reduced supplies to South Sudan, Somalia, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

stories.title: Editor's Notes: Israel turned right after Oct. 7, Bennett turned left - comment
stories.summary: A commentary piece argues that Israeli society shifted further right after the October 7 attack, while former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett moved in a more centrist or leftward direction. The analysis suggests Bennett's new political vehicle is misaligned with the current cultural and political mood in Israel.

stories.title: Tame the phenomenon: The frightening increase in youth crime needs to be handled - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial addressed the alarming rise in youth crime, calling for urgent action to address the phenomenon. The piece cited multiple studies warning that prolonged instability, trauma, isolation, and disrupted schooling harm children's mental health and can lead to violence.

stories.title: How China is using AI – and state funding – to transform the micro drama industry
stories.summary: South Korean micro drama company Vigloo is spending roughly 30 percent of its budget on AI-driven production workflows, reducing show production time from three months to one and cutting costs to one-fifth. China is using state funding and AI to transform its micro drama industry.

stories.title: Man charged with attempted murder in connection with Golders Green attack
stories.summary: Metropolitan Police charged Essa Suleiman, 45, with two counts of attempted murder and possession of a bladed article after two Jewish men were stabbed in Golders Green, north London, on Wednesday.

stories.title: Visitors warned over removing crabs, shells from Hong Kong’s Sharp Island
stories.summary: Conservation officers and volunteers confronted about a dozen visitors removing crabs and shells from a tombolo on Hong Kong's Sharp Island during the first day of mainland China's Labour Day holiday. The activity prompted warnings about the ecological impact on the protected coastal habitat.

stories.title: South Africa: Two Dead, Multiple Injured in Eastern Cape Crash - South African News Briefs - May 1, 2026
stories.summary: Two people were killed and multiple others injured in a vehicle crash in South Africa's Eastern Cape province. Further details about the circumstances of the accident were not immediately available.

stories.title: Labour Day: Hong Kong records 208,790 trips by mainland Chinese visitors so far
stories.summary: Hong Kong recorded over 208,790 trips by mainland Chinese visitors on the first day of the Labour Day golden week holiday. Many arrivals headed to the countryside for hiking and scenic views, while others explored urban areas on foot.

stories.title: Turkish activist describes Israeli navy's raid of Gaza-bound flotilla as 'unlawful'
stories.summary: A Turkish activist aboard a Gaza-bound aid flotilla described the Israeli navy's interception of several vessels in international waters as 'unlawful' and 'brutal.' The raid took place overnight as the humanitarian convoy attempted to deliver aid to Gaza.

stories.title: UN votes to cut the peacekeeping force in South Sudan from 17,000 to 12,000
stories.summary: The UN Security Council voted 13-0, with Russia and China abstaining, to reduce the peacekeeping force in South Sudan from 17,000 to 12,000 troops. The US-drafted resolution extends the mission's mandate until April 30, 2027.

stories.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 63 as Trump signals possible attacks
stories.summary: On day 63 of the US-Iran conflict, Iranian President condemned the US naval blockade as 'intolerable.' President Donald Trump signaled that military operations against Iran could resume, raising uncertainty about the future of the existing ceasefire.

stories.title: Slain Malian defence minister's state funeral broadcast on television
stories.summary: Mali held a televised state funeral for Defense Minister Sadio Camara, who was killed during coordinated attacks by jihadist militants and Tuareg separatist allies on military positions across the country. The assault was described as the largest such attack in Mali in over a decade.

stories.title: Gold, cruises and Dior: how Hong Kong lenders are enticing wealthy mainland China visitors
stories.summary: Hong Kong's major banks, including HSBC, Standard Chartered, and Bank of China (Hong Kong), are offering incentives such as gold bars, cruises, and luxury vouchers to attract wealthy mainland Chinese visitors during the golden week holiday. Several lenders have extended branch hours to capture clients.

stories.title: Some US troops cite benefits of Germany presence as Trump threatens pullback
stories.summary: Some senior US Army officers at a training facility in Hohenfels, Germany, highlighted the benefits of the American military presence there, one day after President Trump said he was reviewing whether to reduce troop numbers in Germany.

stories.title: Sweden confiscates ship with stolen Ukrainian grain – President’s Office calls to scale up this practice
stories.summary: Sweden confiscated the cargo ship Caffa, which was carrying grain stolen from Ukrainian occupied territories. Ukraine's President's Office called for scaling up such seizures to systematically prevent illegal exports from Russian-occupied areas.

stories.title: Trump backs FIFA letting Iran play at World Cup in US
stories.summary: FIFA confirmed that Iran will be allowed to compete in the upcoming World Cup hosted in the United States, with matches remaining on US soil. President Donald Trump expressed support for the decision after months of debate and campaigning over Iran's participation.

stories.title: Palestinian soccer chief refuses to shake hands with Israel federation VP at FIFA event
stories.summary: Palestine Football Association President Jibril Rajoub refused to shake hands with Israeli Football Association Vice-President at a FIFA event. Rajoub accused FIFA President Gianni Infantino of failing to understand the 'deep suffering' of the Palestinian people after Infantino urged the two to 'give hope to the children.'

stories.title: Israel receives 6,500 tons of US ammunition and military equipment
stories.summary: Israel's Ministry of Defense announced it received 6,500 tons of US ammunition and military equipment within a 24-hour period. The shipment included air and ground munitions, military trucks, and Joint Light Tactical Vehicles. Since the launch of Operation Roaring Lion, Israel has received over 115,600 tons of military equipment via 403 airlifts and 10 sealifts.

stories.title: Africa: African Nations to Benefit From China's Two-Year Zero-Tariff Regime
stories.summary: China's zero-tariff treatment for African nations with which it has diplomatic relations takes effect from May 1, 2026, through April 30, 2028. The policy is expected to benefit trade across the continent, with implementation beginning immediately.

stories.title: ‘Public health time bomb’: How France allowed cadmium to poison its crops and soil
stories.summary: France faces a public health crisis as its residents are three to four times more likely than other Europeans to have unsafe cadmium levels in their bodies. Experts attribute the contamination to government inaction, farming practices, and a historic reliance on North African phosphate-based fertilisers rooted in the colonial era.

stories.title: Israeli Defense Minister says war on Iran might resume 'soon'
stories.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz stated during a ceremony that Israel might resume its war against Iran 'soon' to achieve its objectives. Katz said Iran had received 'very severe blows' over the past year and indicated that Israel faces intensifying challenges alongside historic opportunities to reshape the regional situation.

stories.title: Nigeria: 150 Displaced Persons Died in Military Detention Camp in Kwara - Amnesty International
stories.summary: Amnesty International has alleged that 150 displaced persons died while held in a military detention camp in Nigeria's Kwara state. The organization also cited broader abuse of detainees at the facility.

stories.title: Caracas and Washington launch direct flights after seven years and sign two oil deals
stories.summary: The United States and Venezuela inaugurated their first direct flights since 2019 and signed two new oil agreements on Thursday. The White House described the moves as part of a three-stage bilateral plan designed by President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio following the capture of former President Nicolás Maduro by US forces on January 3.

stories.title: Malaysia’s angry culture war brigade tries to dampen water festival over ‘moral harm’
stories.summary: A government-backed water rave music festival in Kuala Lumpur's Bukit Bintang drew criticism from conservative and religious groups in Malaysia. The controversy highlights tensions between Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's tourism promotion goals and growing cultural conservatism in the country.

stories.title: Uganda: Museveni Launches Uganda's First Anti-Tick Vaccine
stories.summary: President Yoweri Museveni launched Uganda's first locally developed anti-tick vaccine. The vaccine is intended to combat tick-borne diseases that affect livestock in the country.

stories.title: Liberia: Sirleaf Says 'Filthy' Monrovia Reflects Governance Failures Under Boakai
stories.summary: Former Liberian President Ellen Johnson Sirleaf publicly criticized conditions in Monrovia, describing the capital as "filthy." She warned that the city's deterioration reflects deeper governance and accountability failures under President Joseph Nyuma Boakai's administration.

stories.title: Mozambique: Mozambique and U.S. Sign Agreement Valued At Over U.S.$500 Million
stories.summary: Mozambique and the United States signed a memorandum of understanding in Maputo valued at $537.5 million under the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC). The agreement was finalized on Wednesday.

stories.title: British couple jailed in Iran: 'We're likely to be here for a long time'
stories.summary: British nationals Lindsay and Craig Foreman face a 10-year prison sentence in Iran after being arrested during a motorcycle tour in the country last year. The couple have acknowledged they are likely to remain imprisoned for a prolonged period.

stories.title: Man who pocketed tiles from medieval priory as boy returns them 60 years later
stories.summary: Simon White returned fragments of medieval clay tiles to Wenlock Priory in Shropshire, nearly 60 years after pocketing them as a nine-year-old during a family visit. The decorative pieces date from the late 13th to early 14th century and had been stored in a toffee tin since the late 1960s.

stories.title: Nearly twice as many men as women standing in May elections in UK
stories.summary: Research ahead of UK elections on May 1 reveals nearly twice as many men as women are standing as candidates across local, mayoral, and devolved elections. Democracy campaigners warned that women remain "massively underrepresented" on ballot papers across all political parties.

stories.title: Uganda: Amnesty Urges Probe Into Alleged Security Force Abuses During January 15 Polls
stories.summary: Amnesty International has called for investigations into alleged human rights abuses by Ugandan security forces during the January 15 presidential and parliamentary elections. The allegations include unlawful killings, arbitrary arrests, enforced disappearances, and torture.

stories.title: Mali: Russia Vows to Keep Forces in Mali Despite Warning From Separatists to Withdraw
stories.summary: Russia declared that its forces would remain in Mali to continue supporting the country's military rulers, rejecting withdrawal demands from Tuareg separatists. The statement followed surprise attacks by separatists that forced Russian troops out of a key northern town.

stories.title: UN Chief warns consequences of Middle East crisis 'grow dramatically worse'
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned that the Middle East crisis is worsening with each passing hour and called for a pathway to peace. He noted that restrictions on movement in the Strait of Hormuz have disrupted global energy supplies, transport, manufacturing, and food markets.

stories.title: Sudan: Sudanese Refugees Injured in Sixth Armed Attack On Camp in Ethiopia
stories.summary: Sudanese refugees were injured in an armed attack on Aftit camp in Ethiopia's Amhara province on Tuesday evening. It was the sixth such armed incident at the camp, raising concerns about deteriorating security conditions for refugees in the settlement.

stories.title: Sudan: 17 Sudanese Refugees Drown Off Tobruk, Libya
stories.summary: The UNHCR confirmed that at least 17 Sudanese refugees drowned after a shipwreck in the Mediterranean Sea off the coast of Tobruk, Libya. Of the 33 people believed to have been on board, only seven survived, and nine remain missing.

stories.title: Brent touches $126 amid US military plan for 'short and powerful' strikes on Iran
stories.summary: Brent crude surged to $126.41 a barrel on Thursday after reports that US Central Command was preparing "short and powerful" strikes on Iranian infrastructure. Prices later settled near $114. The European benchmark has risen more than 60% since the US-Iran war began on February 28.

stories.title: Report: Cost of war on Iran closer to $50 billion
stories.summary: A CBS News report citing US officials estimated the total cost of the Iran war at approximately $50 billion, double the $25 billion figure previously announced by Pentagon official Jules Hurst for 'Operation Epic Fury.' The discrepancy reportedly stems from the initial estimate not accounting for damaged or destroyed military equipment.

stories.title: Sheryl Sandberg endows scholarship at Camp Ramah in California in honor of late husband
stories.summary: Sheryl Sandberg, the author of "Lean In" and a prominent philanthropist, endowed a scholarship at Camp Ramah in California in honor of her late husband. Sandberg has been a longstanding donor to Jewish and Israeli causes.

stories.title: Trump says ‘probably’ when asked if he might pull US troops out of Italy, Spain
stories.summary: President Trump indicated he would "probably" consider withdrawing US troops from Italy and Spain when asked about the possibility. The remarks follow earlier US statements about potentially reducing military personnel stationed in Germany.

stories.title: Trump says 'probably' when asked if he might pull US troops out of Italy, Spain
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said "probably" when asked whether he might withdraw U.S. troops from Italy and Spain. The comment followed his announcement that Washington was considering reducing military personnel stationed in Germany.

stories.title: Panama president says port caught in US-China dispute
stories.summary: Panamanian President Jose Raul Mulino said his country maintains a positive relationship with China despite being caught in a US-China dispute. He defended Panama's takeover of port contracts previously held by Hong Kong's CK Hutchison.

stories.title: ‘Even 1 case is too many’: experts warn of lasting harm after alleged dog cage child abuse
stories.summary: Psychologists in Hong Kong warned of lasting mental harm to children after two toddlers were allegedly confined in a dog cage, sparking public outrage. More than 100 reports have been filed since a mandatory child abuse reporting requirement took effect in January.

stories.title: NBU downgrades 2026 GDP growth forecast
stories.summary: Ukraine's National Bank downgraded its GDP growth forecast for 2026, projecting more restrained economic expansion than previously anticipated.

stories.title: Trump says Secret Service agent at dinner was not hit by friendly fire
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated that the Secret Service agent injured during an attack at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner was not struck by friendly fire.

stories.title: GOP lawmaker pushed to add a Holocaust denier to New Hampshire’s Holocaust panel
stories.summary: A Republican lawmaker in New Hampshire attempted to place a Holocaust denier on the state's Holocaust education commission. The effort drew condemnation from Jewish leaders and other lawmakers.

stories.title: Myanmar ex-leader Aung San Suu Kyi moved to house arrest, military says
stories.summary: Myanmar's military government announced that former leader Aung San Suu Kyi has been moved from prison to house arrest. The Nobel Peace Prize laureate has been in detention since the military coup that ousted her in 2021.

stories.title: Aung San Suu Kyi: The Myanmar democracy icon detained for years
stories.summary: Myanmar's former leader Aung San Suu Kyi has been largely out of public view since she was ousted in the 2021 military coup. Little information has emerged about her condition during her years of detention.

stories.title: Iran war may cause food shortages in Africa, world’s largest fertiliser firm says
stories.summary: Yara International CEO Svein Tore Holsether warned that the Iran war could cause food shortages and price rises in Africa's most vulnerable communities. The world's largest fertiliser company cautioned that soaring fertiliser prices could trigger a global bidding war, leaving the poorest countries unable to secure essential supplies.

stories.title: Danish treatment of Greenlandic mother may be ‘ethnic discrimination’, says UN
stories.summary: The United Nations warned Denmark that the removal of a Greenlandic Inuit mother's newborn child may constitute "ethnic discrimination." Keira Alexandra Kronvold's daughter was taken into foster care in November 2024, two hours after birth, based on parenting competency tests that have since been banned.

stories.title: Many Asian-Americans feel excluded from ‘true’ US identity, survey finds
stories.summary: A survey found that many Asian-Americans feel excluded from being seen as "truly" American by mainstream U.S. society. The findings highlight ongoing identity struggles among Asian-Americans despite being born and raised in the United States.

stories.title: King Charles’ gift amuses Chinese, anti-spy agency makes allegation: SCMP’s 7 highlights
stories.summary: A weekly roundup from the South China Morning Post highlights stories including projections that the U.S.-China economic gap will widen to $11 trillion by decade's end. Other topics covered include the Iran conflict's potential to bring the two powers closer and a gift from King Charles that amused Chinese audiences.

stories.title: Hegseth decries spread of 'falsehoods' regarding security of Kuwaiti base during Iran war
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth was questioned by Representative Patrick Ryan of New York about the security of a US base in Kuwait. Ryan pressed Hegseth on an Iranian drone attack in early March that killed six US Army Reserve soldiers.

stories.title: Scared and angry UK Jews demand government do more to address antisemitic violence
stories.summary: Following an antisemitic stabbing attack in the Golders Green area of north London, British Jewish community members demanded the government take stronger action against antisemitic violence. Residents expressed fear and skepticism about whether authorities would adequately respond to the rising threat.

stories.title: Ukraine returns 2,126 children abducted by Russia — Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that 2,126 children abducted by Russia have been returned to Ukraine through the Bring Kids Back UA initiative.

stories.title: Police say they will charge people with unrest in Alice Springs after arrest over death of Kumanjayi Little Baby
stories.summary: Northern Territory police in Australia said one person faces charges and more are expected over unrest in Alice Springs following the arrest of a man connected to the death of five-year-old Kumanjayi Little Baby. The child's body was found 5km from the Old Timers town camp. Her grandfather, a senior Warlpiri elder, appealed for calm.

stories.title: US determines hostilities against Iran have ended, says official
stories.summary: A senior US official told NBC News that US hostilities against Iran, which began on February 28, have been 'terminated.' The two sides agreed to a two-week ceasefire on April 7 that has since been extended, with negotiations restarting alongside the halt in fighting.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Iran briefly activates Tehran air defences against ‘reconnaissance drones’
stories.summary: Tehran briefly activated air defences for approximately 20 minutes late Thursday to counter what Iranian state news agencies Tasnim and Fars described as small aircraft and reconnaissance drones. Separately, the Trump administration signaled it would not be constrained by a congressional authorization deadline for the US-Israeli war against Iran.

stories.title: Oscar goes missing after Academy Award winner is blocked from taking it on flight
stories.summary: An Academy Award winner was prevented from carrying their Oscar statuette onto a flight, after which the award went missing. The airline issued an apology and launched an urgent internal search for the trophy.

stories.title: HK$1 minimum wage rise unlikely to significantly lift low-paid incomes, experts say
stories.summary: Hong Kong's minimum wage rose by HK$1 (13 US cents) effective May 1, but experts warned the increase is unlikely to significantly boost low-paid workers' incomes. Analysts said the rise broadly aligns with recent pay trends and should help preserve purchasing power under a new formula.

stories.title: Separate cities or shared space? Ministries divided over Negev housing plan for Haredim
stories.summary: Israeli government ministries are divided over plans to build three new cities in the Negev desert for the growing ultra-Orthodox (Haredi) population. The debate centers on whether to create separate Haredi communities or integrated shared spaces, reflecting broader tensions over economics and the future of Haredi life in Israel.

stories.title: Hong Kong slams attempts to sugarcoat Jimmy Lai’s criminal acts in press freedom index
stories.summary: The Hong Kong government condemned the use of a global press freedom index to criticize the jailing of former media owner Jimmy Lai Chee-ying. Authorities accused anti-China forces and foreign media of attempting to sugarcoat Lai's criminal acts and smear the city's press freedom record.

stories.title: New Banksy statue of man blinded by flag draws crowds in London
stories.summary: Street artist Banksy confirmed a new work in central London: a statue of a suited man blindly stepping off a plinth while holding a flag that blocks his view. The piece appeared on Wednesday near Pall Mall and has drawn large crowds.

stories.title: US prosecutors release new footage of Trump shooting suspect
stories.summary: The US Justice Department released previously unseen footage of the Trump shooting incident. Prosecutors presented the footage to demonstrate that the Secret Service agent injured during the attack was not struck by friendly fire.

stories.title: Kurdish militant says Turkey stalled peace talks over reforms
stories.summary: Kurdish militant leader Murat Karayilan accused Turkey of stalling peace negotiations despite steps taken toward a ceasefire. Karayilan said Turkey has failed to advance reforms necessary for the peace process.

stories.title: London assailant charged with attempted murder over terror stabbing of 2 Jews
stories.summary: A man in London has been charged with attempted murder in connection with the antisemitic stabbing of two Jewish individuals in Golders Green. Following the attack, Britain raised its national terrorism threat level from 'substantial' to 'severe.'

stories.title: ISW explains why Putin called Trump
stories.summary: The Institute for the Study of War reported that Russian President Vladimir Putin used an April 29 phone call with US President Trump to reaffirm his original military objectives in Ukraine. Putin sought to portray Russia's victory as inevitable.

stories.title: US imposes sanctions on former Congo President Joseph Kabila
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department imposed sanctions on former Democratic Republic of Congo President Joseph Kabila. The action was announced on April 30.

stories.title: Israeli group asks high court to order release of Gaza doctors
stories.summary: Israeli rights groups petitioned the high court to order the release of Gaza doctors, alleging Israel is detaining healthcare workers without charge. Hundreds of health workers reportedly remain in Israeli custody.

stories.title: Trump congratulates Zaidi on his nomination to be next Iraqi prime minister
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump congratulated Ali al-Zaidi on his nomination to become Iraq's next prime minister. Trump said he looked forward to a productive new relationship with the incoming Iraqi leader.

stories.title: Condemnation and protests against Israel’s raid of Gaza aid flotilla
stories.summary: Israel intercepted Gaza-bound aid boats in international waters, drawing widespread international condemnation and sparking protests. The raid on the humanitarian flotilla has intensified diplomatic criticism of Israel's actions regarding the blockade of Gaza.

stories.title: US urges meeting between Lebanese president, Israeli PM
stories.summary: The US Embassy in Lebanon urged a meeting between the Lebanese president and Israeli Prime Minister amid ongoing hostilities. Israeli strikes killed 17 people in Lebanon despite a ceasefire being in effect.

stories.title: Israel said bracing for Iran fighting to resume soon, as Trump briefed on military options
stories.summary: Israel is reportedly preparing for a possible resumption of fighting with Iran, with Defense Minister signaling conflict could resume soon. US Central Command has reportedly requested a hypersonic missile be sent to the Middle East. Iran's president condemned the US naval blockade as 'intolerable,' while President Trump was briefed on military options.

stories.title: Trump, Fox News praise UAE decision to leave Opec
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump praised the United Arab Emirates' decision to leave OPEC amid the ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran. Trump expressed approval of UAE ruler Mohamed bin Zayed's move, suggesting it could help lower oil prices.

stories.title: Italy condemns 'unlawful' Israeli interception of Gaza flotilla
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni condemned Israel's interception of an aid flotilla bound for the Gaza Strip as "unlawful." Meloni called for the release of Italian nationals who were aboard the vessels.

stories.title: UN climate body presses on after US quits, while China leads with renewables
stories.summary: The UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change is continuing its work despite the US government's withdrawal, with IPCC chair Jim Skea noting the US is just one of 195 member countries. China is meanwhile leading in renewable energy development.

stories.title: Some US troops cite benefits of Germany presence as Trump threatens pullback
stories.summary: Germany hosts approximately 35,000 active-duty U.S. military personnel, making it the largest American military footprint in Europe. Some U.S. troops stationed there have highlighted the strategic benefits of the German presence amid President Trump's threats to reduce the deployment.

stories.title: Russian city faces toxic aftermath of refinery attack
stories.summary: Residents of a Russian city were warned to limit outdoor activity and keep windows shut after elevated benzene levels were detected in the air following an attack on a local oil refinery.

stories.title: Georg Baselitz, the German painter who turned postwar art upside down, dies at 88
stories.summary: German painter Georg Baselitz, known for his provocative upside-down compositions that challenged postwar art conventions, has died at the age of 88.

stories.title: US suffered 'disgraceful defeat', Iran’s Supreme Leader says
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei declared that the United States suffered a "disgraceful defeat" in the region, according to a written message broadcast on Iranian state television.

stories.title: Pakistan, 10 other nations condemn Israeli assault on Gaza aid flotilla, 'unlawful detention' of activists
stories.summary: Pakistan, Türkiye, Brazil, Jordan, Spain, Malaysia, Bangladesh, Colombia, Maldives, South Africa, and Libya jointly condemned Israel's assault on the Global Sumud Flotilla. Their foreign ministers called the interception and detention of humanitarian activists in international waters a flagrant violation of international law.

stories.title: Scientology ‘speed running’ trend has LA abuzz and church unhappy
stories.summary: A viral trend of young people rushing Church of Scientology buildings in Los Angeles has drawn large crowds to Hollywood Boulevard. The Church of Scientology said it is "reviewing all available remedies" in response to the so-called speed-running raids.

stories.title: Why governments beyond Hong Kong are wary of prediction markets
stories.summary: Hong Kong's government paused a plan to allow the Hong Kong Jockey Club to offer basketball betting after the rise of prediction markets prompted officials to reassess the regulatory landscape. Governments globally are examining the challenges posed by these online platforms.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Air Force reports efficiency problems: 170 crews report no shootdowns in year
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Force disclosed significant efficiency problems among drone-interceptor crews. Of more than 300 crews, 170 failed to shoot down a single enemy UAV over the past year.

stories.title: Palestinian FA chief blasts Israeli VP at FIFA Congress
stories.summary: Palestinian Football Association chief Jibril Rajoub confronted Israel FA Vice-President Basim Sheikh Suliman at the FIFA Congress. The clash centred on the ongoing war in Gaza.

stories.title: German lawmaker says 'trust in this White House' not the same
stories.summary: German European Parliament member Marie-Agnes Strack-Zimmermann said trust in the current US administration to protect Berlin has diminished. She acknowledged that US troop presence in Germany remains mutually beneficial but expressed concern over President Trump's unpredictability.

stories.title: Lebanon's internal splits over talks with Israel trip up Saudi mediation efforts
stories.summary: Internal divisions among top Lebanese officials are disrupting Saudi Arabia's mediation efforts to help Lebanon present a unified position in historic negotiations with Israel. Lebanese sources and foreign officials told Reuters that the growing rift has complicated diplomatic progress in Beirut.

stories.title: Fema employees who criticized Trump cuts reinstated after months on leave
stories.summary: Fourteen FEMA employees were reinstated after spending eight months on administrative leave for signing a public letter criticizing Trump administration funding cuts. The "Katrina declaration" warned that the cuts left the US dangerously unprepared for natural disasters.

stories.title: ‘Love relay’: lonely China cancer patient orders ‘company’ via food delivery platform
stories.summary: A 24-year-old cancer patient named Little Li in Foshan, Guangdong province, China, ordered "companionship" through a food delivery platform while hospitalized. The story went viral, sparking a widespread outpouring of support online.

stories.title: UAE refers Sudan general and others to court over ammunition shipment for Sudanese army
stories.summary: The UAE referred the chief of staff of Sudan's army along with 12 other defendants and six companies to its State Security Court. The charges relate to an alleged attempt to move ammunition through UAE territory destined for the Sudanese army.

stories.title: US urges Lebanese president to meet Netanyahu, suggests sit-down could lead to IDF pullout
stories.summary: The US Embassy in Lebanon urged Lebanese President to meet Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu, suggesting direct engagement could lead to an Israeli military withdrawal. Political leaders in Beirut remain divided over the proposed talks with Jerusalem.

stories.title: Iran ‘dying to make a deal’, US war costs soar: here’s what happened overnight
stories.summary: The US-Israeli war on Iran entered its third month with diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran remaining stalled. President Trump claimed Iran is "dying to make a deal" but acknowledged uncertainty about the Iranian leadership and the status of negotiations.

stories.title: One of Khmelnytskyi NPP power units resumes operation after repairs
stories.summary: A power unit at the Khmelnytskyi Nuclear Power Plant in Ukraine resumed operation after completing scheduled maintenance that began on April 28.

stories.title: Uganda court sentences man to death for killing four young children at nursery school
stories.summary: A Ugandan court sentenced a man to death on Thursday for killing four young children at a nursery school earlier in April. The attack in the East African country sparked widespread public outrage and heightened concerns about the safety of pupils in schools.

stories.title: Pivotal US-Iran war deadline approaches with no end in sight for conflict
stories.summary: A key U.S. deadline related to the conflict with Iran is approaching, with no resolution in sight. Prospects for ending the war remain highly unlikely.

stories.title: US combatant chiefs want more amphibious ready groups, Marine commandant says
stories.summary: U.S. combatant command leaders have all requested amphibious ready groups and Marine Expeditionary Units, according to the Marine Corps commandant. The demand underscores the continued importance of amphibious capabilities across multiple geographic commands.

stories.title: FIFA head announces no changes to Iran's World Cup schedule as protestors demand team ban
stories.summary: Protesters gathered outside the FIFA Congress in Vancouver demanding Iran's national team be banned from the upcoming World Cup over alleged ties to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. FIFA president Gianni Infantino announced no changes would be made to Iran's schedule.

stories.title: UK PM Starmer says Jews are scared, promises action after London stabbings
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer pledged action to protect Britain's Jewish community, acknowledging widespread fear following the stabbing of two men in the Golders Green area of north London. The attack followed a series of antisemitic incidents in the capital.

stories.title: Russia bans imports of foreign satellite terminals, including Starlink
stories.summary: Russia has banned the import of foreign satellite communication terminals, including SpaceX's Starlink devices.

stories.title: Key deadline looms in US-Iran war as conflict drags on
stories.summary: A key deadline is approaching in the US-Iran conflict as the war continues. Democrats in Congress are pushing for a war powers vote, while Republican lawmakers continue to support President Trump's approach to the conflict.

stories.title: China scraps tariffs for all but one African nation
stories.summary: China announced the removal of tariffs on imports from all African nations with which it has diplomatic relations, except one. The zero-tariff regime boosts China's soft power on the continent, though analysts warn it may lead to uneven economic gains among African countries.

stories.title: It's not just oil: Iran war also threatens Asia's food security
stories.summary: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz due to the Iran conflict is threatening Asia's food security by disrupting fertilizer supply chains. Chinese restrictions have compounded the problem as planting season begins across the region.

stories.title: Japan survey finds sexual abuse at 15% of hospitals. Is the true scale higher?
stories.summary: A Japanese government survey found that more than 15% of hospitals and long-term care facilities have recorded cases of sexual assault or abuse of patients. The first-of-its-kind survey received responses from 1,113 of 5,000 invited institutions, with many incidents involving psychiatric care staff.

stories.title: Iran war live: Tehran says US ports siege ‘intolerable’; Trump mulls action
stories.summary: Israeli military strikes on Lebanon have killed at least 2,586 people and wounded more than 8,000 since March 2, according to local media reports.

stories.title: Evening update
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on Lebanon killed at least 32 people on Thursday as Israeli ground operations expanded. Air defence systems were activated over Tehran against small drones and surveillance aircraft. The UAE banned travel to Iran, Lebanon, and Iraq, urging its citizens to leave those countries immediately.

stories.title: Jihadists urge united front against Mali junta as Bamako blockade begins
stories.summary: Jihadist groups in Mali have called for a unified uprising against the ruling military junta, coinciding with a blockade of key roads leading into the capital, Bamako. The escalation follows coordinated attacks on junta positions and raises fears of deepening instability in the conflict-affected country.

stories.title: Russia conducts psychological operation in Kharkiv border region – CCD
stories.summary: Russia's forces are conducting a psychological operation in border areas of Ukraine's Kharkiv region, dropping leaflets from drones that encourage local residents to collaborate, according to Ukraine's Center for Countering Disinformation.

stories.title: Georg Baselitz, the German painter who turned postwar art upside down, dies at 88
stories.summary: German painter Georg Baselitz, known for his provocative postwar art including his signature upside-down paintings, has died at the age of 88. Baselitz was a major figure in contemporary European art who often challenged conventions of artistic expression.

stories.title: Venice Biennale jury resigns days before start of top art exhibition
stories.summary: The jury for the Venice Biennale resigned days before the opening of the prestigious art exhibition. The resignations followed tensions over Russia's return to the event for the first time since its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Man accused in Trump assassination attempt agrees to remain in custody
stories.summary: The man accused of attempting to assassinate President Donald Trump at a press gala in Washington agreed on Thursday to remain in custody while his case proceeds. The incident occurred at a black-tie event in the U.S. capital.

stories.title: War update: 109 combat clashes on frontline
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces reported 109 combat clashes with Russian troops along the frontline since the start of the day.

stories.title: Lebanon death toll from Thursday reaches 32, Israeli troops hit
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on the town of Harouf in southern Lebanon's Nabatieh district killed one woman and injured three, including a child, bringing Lebanon's 24-hour death toll to 32. Hezbollah said its fighters attacked Israeli forces operating up to 10 kilometers inside Lebanese territory.

stories.title: Top general in West Bank warns ‘Jewish terrorism’ could spark Palestinian uprising — report
stories.summary: Israeli Central Command chief Avi Bluth reportedly warned that settler violence in the West Bank amounts to "Jewish terrorism" and could trigger a Palestinian uprising. Bluth cautioned that Palestinians "won't remain indifferent forever" and said the violence is causing significant damage to Israel.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Mykolaiv again, damage reported in private sector
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the southern Ukrainian city of Mykolaiv again using drones, causing damage to the private residential sector.

stories.title: Trump says Secret Service agent not shot by friendly fire, as attack video is released
stories.summary: President Trump and the Secret Service stated that a federal agent injured during an attack at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner was not hit by friendly fire. Authorities released video footage showing the suspect shooting the officer while rushing through security.

stories.title: 214 robots take the field at US national competition for Jewish schools
stories.summary: The Center for Initiatives in Jewish Education hosted its annual national robotics competition in New York, featuring 214 robots from Jewish schools across the United States. The event highlighted the growing role of STEM programs in Jewish education.

stories.title: Lebanon says Israeli strikes kill 9 people, including 2 children
stories.summary: Lebanese authorities reported that Israeli strikes killed nine people, including two children. President Joseph Aoun condemned what he called continuing Israeli violations in southern Lebanon during a meeting with a delegation from the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.

stories.title: Amnesty urges Nigeria to investigate deaths in army-run camp, military says report baseless
stories.summary: Amnesty International called on Nigeria to investigate reports that at least 150 people, mostly children, died in an army-run camp in Kwara state. The Nigerian military dismissed the reports as baseless.

stories.title: 13 terrorists killed as bids to infiltrate Pak-Afghan border in KP foiled: ISPR
stories.summary: Pakistan's Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) reported that security forces killed 13 Fitna al Khawarij (Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan) militants during two foiled infiltration attempts along the Pak-Afghan border in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Mohmand district. ISPR described the militants as Indian-sponsored terrorists.

stories.title: Dutch authorities evacuate Kempen Airport as wildfires break out near military training areas
stories.summary: Dutch authorities evacuated Kempen Airport in southern Netherlands on Thursday after a large wildfire broke out near a military training area. The blaze is the latest in a series of fires amid exceptionally dry conditions in the country.

stories.title: Graham Platner becomes presumptive Dem. nominee as opponent Janet Mills drops out of race
stories.summary: Graham Platner became the presumptive Democratic nominee for US Senate in Maine after opponent Janet Mills dropped out of the race. His anti-Israel rhetoric and past Nazi tattoo have drawn concern from Jewish organizations.

stories.title: Tony Blair’s thinktank urges Labour to scrap ‘unaffordable’ pension triple lock
stories.summary: The Tony Blair Institute urged the UK Labour government to scrap the state pension triple lock, calling it "unaffordable" amid mounting fiscal pressure partly driven by the Iran war. The thinktank recommended a broader overhaul of the pension system.

stories.title: Under-fire British PM Starmer heckled after Jewish-targeted stabbings
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer was heckled during a visit following a series of knife attacks targeting Jewish communities in the UK. Crowds shouted hostile slogans at the prime minister, reflecting public anger over the government's response.

stories.title: Hong Kong public hospitals to extend time for daily visits from 5 to 9 hours by July 31
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Hospital Authority announced that all rehabilitation and palliative wards in public hospitals will extend daily visiting hours from five to nine hours by July 31. Paediatric wards will also allow round-the-clock visits by the same deadline.

stories.title: Russian archaeologist Butyagin plans to resume illegal excavations in Crimea
stories.summary: Russian archaeologist Alexander Butyagin announced plans to resume the Myrmekion archaeological expedition near Kerch in Russian-occupied Crimea, which Ukraine and international observers consider illegal excavation on occupied territory.

stories.title: U.K. calls antisemitism an emergency as police investigate stabbing attack on 2 Jewish men
stories.summary: British police arrested a 45-year-old man on suspicion of attempted murder after a stabbing attack on two Jewish men in the United Kingdom. Authorities classified the incident as an act of terrorism and are investigating possible motives, including any potential link to Iranian proxies.

stories.title: KP CM Afridi hints at legislation against collateral damage in drone strikes
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi indicated plans to introduce provincial legislation criminalizing collateral damage from drone strikes. The move follows public anger from his constituency and a meeting of district lawmakers who pledged a united effort to protect civilians.

stories.title: US embassy in Beirut says Lebanon is at ‘crossroads’, calls for meeting with Netanyahu
stories.summary: The US embassy in Beirut called for a direct meeting between Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, saying Lebanon stands at a "crossroads." The embassy stated that US-facilitated engagement between the two countries could begin a "national revival" for Lebanon.

stories.title: Former Spandau Ballet singer jailed for 14 years for multiple rapes and sexual assaults
stories.summary: Former Spandau Ballet singer Ross Davidson, 38, was sentenced to 14 years in prison after being convicted of multiple rapes and sexual assaults. The offences were committed against six women between August 2013 and December 2019 across two separate trials.

stories.title: Ceasefire ‘stops’ War Powers clock on Iran, Hegseth claims
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth claimed that a ceasefire pauses the 60-day clock under the War Powers Resolution of 1973, which governs unauthorized military deployments. However, the relevant provisions of the law make no mention of a ceasefire halting the timeline.

stories.title: Medical bus destroyed in Russian attack near Dnipro
stories.summary: A vaccination bus operated by Ukraine's Ministry of Health was destroyed in a Russian strike in the suburbs of Dnipro, belonging to the regional Center for Disease Control and Prevention.

stories.title: Syrian pilot confessions reveal centralized bombing orders during war
stories.summary: Confessions from Syrian pilots revealed that bombing orders during the Syrian war were centralized. Some officers received special trust from the leadership and were assigned intensive bombing missions.

stories.title: Pezeshkian, Ghalibaf look to fire FM Araghchi over allegiance to IRGC commander - report
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf are reportedly seeking to dismiss Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, alleging he has been acting primarily on behalf of IRGC commander Ahmad Vahidi rather than the civilian government.

stories.title: Russia conducts first Soyuz-5 rocket launch, Roscosmos says
stories.summary: Russia's space agency Roscosmos announced the first launch of the Soyuz-5 expendable rocket on April 30 from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.

stories.title: Iranian media: Iran’s air defence engaging drones over Tehran
stories.summary: Iran's air defense systems engaged small drones and surveillance UAVs over Tehran, according to the Tasnim news agency. Air defense sirens were heard across western, central, and southeastern areas of the Iranian capital.

stories.title: Mexico's Sheinbaum says proof needed after US charges Sinaloa governor for cartel ties
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum responded to U.S. charges against Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha alleging cartel ties, demanding "clear evidence" from Washington. Sheinbaum suggested the charges announced on Wednesday could be politically motivated if proof is not provided.

stories.title: Ukraine builds system to counter Russia's shadow grain fleet – Zelensky
