stories.summary: The Lufthansa airline group extended the cancellation of all flights to Israel through June, citing security concerns. The decision followed warnings from an EU aviation agency about risks to aircraft amid uncertainty over an Iran truce.

stories.title: Starmer calls on public to ‘open their eyes to Jewish pain’ in wake of Golders Green attack
stories.summary: Prime Minister Keir Starmer visited Golders Green in north London after a stabbing attack targeting Jewish men, urging the public to recognize antisemitic violence. He accused individuals marching alongside Hamas supporters of condoning violence against Jews, delivering his strongest remarks on antisemitism to date.

stories.title: IDF major charged with aiding enemy, taking bribe in alleged Gaza smuggling scheme
stories.summary: An IDF major was charged with multiple offenses including aiding the enemy, bribery, and aggravated smuggling in connection with an alleged contraband operation into Gaza. The officer's identifying details remain under a publication ban.

stories.title: Golders Green attack suspect named as Essa Suleiman, 45
stories.summary: The suspect in the Golders Green stabbing attack in north London has been identified as Essa Suleiman, 45, arrested on suspicion of attempted murder. Suleiman had been referred to the UK's Prevent counter-radicalisation programme in 2020 but was cleared and his case closed within six weeks.

stories.title: Wada investigation finds 300 Russian doping cases
stories.summary: The World Anti-Doping Agency said its investigation into data seized from a Moscow laboratory in 2019 has resulted in more than 300 sanctions against Russian athletes for doping violations.

stories.title: Britain pledges extra $43m for Jewish security after London stabbings
stories.summary: The British government pledged an additional £43 million for Jewish community security following two stabbing attacks targeting Jewish individuals in London. The funding announcement came one day after the knife assaults in the city.

stories.title: 'Damage control mode': Reputations of Mali junta & Russian mercenaries 'hang in balance'
stories.summary: Analysts say Mali's ruling military junta and its Russian mercenary partners face a reputational crisis following recent attacks by an alliance of Tuareg separatists and jihadist forces. Ulf Laessing of the Konrad Adenauer Foundation described the junta as struggling to maintain control while relying on an increasingly compromised Russian partner in the Sahel region.

stories.title: Neo-Nazi who planned mass gun attack convicted after MI5 undercover sting
stories.summary: Alfie Coleman, a young neo-Nazi from Great Notley in Essex, was convicted of planning a mass gun attack after being caught in an undercover MI5 operation. Coleman had compiled a hate-list of targets including colleagues and customers and wrote a manifesto identifying potential victims. A senior police officer warned of increasing youth radicalisation.

stories.title: Shahed attack damages apartment building and private home in Mykolaiv
stories.summary: A Russian Shahed drone attack damaged an apartment building, a private home, and a car in the Ukrainian city of Mykolaiv.

stories.title: Russian May Holiday Hotel Bookings Slump as Drone Attacks Hit Black Sea Tourism
stories.summary: Hotel bookings in Russia's Krasnodar region dropped 20.7% year-on-year for the May holiday period. The decline is attributed to ongoing drone attacks affecting Black Sea tourism destinations.

stories.title: Ukraine’s army chief orders two-month time limit for front-line troops
stories.summary: Ukraine's army chief issued an order limiting front-line combat deployments to a maximum of two months. The directive also mandates medical evaluations for troops serving on the front lines.

stories.title: Mexico’s Sheinbaum seeks ‘irrefutable’ evidence for US charges against Sinaloa governor
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum demanded that the United States provide "irrefutable" evidence compliant with Mexican law before pursuing extradition of Sinaloa's sitting governor on charges linking him to drug cartels. The statement came in response to U.S. charges announced against Governor Rubén Rocha.

stories.title: Marine commandant: Every combatant command has requested an amphibious ready group
stories.summary: Marine Corps Commandant Gen. Eric Smith said every U.S. combatant command has requested an amphibious ready group. The demand is roughly double the Marines' current goal of maintaining three deployed groups at any given time.

stories.title: Man charged with trying to kill Trump agrees to remain in custody
stories.summary: Cole Allen, 31, accused of attempting to assassinate President Donald Trump outside the White House Correspondents' Dinner in Washington, agreed during a court hearing on Thursday to remain in custody. Allen allegedly fired a shotgun at a security checkpoint during the event. His lawyer said he would not immediately contest prosecutors' arguments that he posed a danger.

stories.title: Peruvian President claims Jews pushed Germany into war because 'they controlled banks'
stories.summary: Peruvian President made antisemitic remarks during a speech at the 138th anniversary ceremony of the Lima Chamber of Commerce. He claimed that Jewish people pushed Germany into war because they controlled the banks.

stories.title: Lahore court grants interim pre-arrest bail to PM's daughter, son-in-law in Saaf Pani case
stories.summary: An anti-corruption court in Lahore granted interim pre-arrest bail to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's daughter Rabia Imran and her husband Ali Imran Yousaf in a case involving alleged irregularities in the Punjab Saaf Pani Company. The couple had previously been declared proclaimed offenders due to their absence from Pakistan.

stories.title: Louisiana claims supreme court voting rights decision means it cannot carry out primaries with current electoral maps – live
stories.summary: Louisiana's governor and attorney general moved to postpone the state's 2026 midterm primaries following a Supreme Court ruling that gutted the Voting Rights Act. The decision prompted states to rush to redraw electoral districts, with Democrats denouncing the postponement as causing mass voter confusion.

stories.title: Bank of England holds rates and spells out inflation risks from Iran war
stories.summary: The Bank of England held interest rates steady while highlighting inflation risks stemming from the US-Israeli war on Iran. Concerns are growing in the UK over potential sharp declines in economic growth linked to the conflict.

stories.title: Zelenskyy asks Trump whether Putin’s 9 May ceasefire means more than hours of safety for his own propaganda parade
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky questioned whether Russian President Putin's proposed May 9 ceasefire was anything more than a propaganda gesture. Russia has previously used temporary pauses to regroup forces, resupply positions, and resume offensive operations.

stories.title: Admin mum on whether Trump will seek to legalize Iran war
stories.summary: The Trump administration has not indicated whether the president will seek congressional authorization for the ongoing military conflict with Iran. The 60-day window under the War Powers Resolution is expiring, though Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth contends a ceasefire has paused the timeline.

stories.title: South Sudan president fires foreign, trade ministers in latest government changes
stories.summary: South Sudan's President Salva Kiir dismissed his foreign and trade ministers along with senior security officials, according to a presidential decree issued on Wednesday. The changes are part of a broader series of recent government reshuffles in the country.

stories.title: Zelensky signs laws extending martial law and general mobilization in Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky signed laws extending martial law and general mobilization in Ukraine for an additional three months.

stories.title: Italian author Erri De Luca to take part in International Writers Festival in Jerusalem
stories.summary: Italian author Erri De Luca will participate in the International Writers Festival in Jerusalem. The event, supported by the Jerusalem Foundation, will feature prize-winning writers alongside Israeli authors, poets, and journalists.

stories.title: Air Force’s top general: Supplemental funding needed to replace US aircraft lost in Iran
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force's top general said supplemental funding is needed to replace American aircraft destroyed during Operation Epic Fury in Iran. The fiscal year 2027 budget request was submitted before those losses occurred.

stories.title: New York officials return more than 650 antiquities valued at $14m to India
stories.summary: New York officials, led by Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg Jr., returned 657 antiquities valued at $14 million to India, some connected to alleged art smuggler Subhash Kapoor. The return coincided with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani raising the issue of the Koh-i-noor diamond's ownership.

stories.title: With unmanned systems in the forefront, Marine Corps evolves how it operates
stories.summary: The U.S. Marine Corps is integrating unmanned systems into its operations, with plans to begin operational testing of drone wingmen by 2029. Officials at the Modern Day Marine conference in Washington indicated Marines could eventually conduct their own intelligence and reconnaissance missions instead of relying on contractors.

stories.title: What a Post-Orbán Hungary Means for Hungarians and Europe
stories.summary: Hungary's opposition leader Péter Magyar has won a landslide election victory, ending Viktor Orbán's 16-year rule. The result marks a significant political shift for Hungary, which under Orbán pursued anti-Ukrainian, pro-Russian policies and frequently clashed with the European Union.

stories.title: Lebanon says Israeli strikes kill 9 people, including 2 children
stories.summary: Lebanese authorities reported that Israeli strikes killed nine people, including two children. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun condemned what he described as continuing Israeli violations in southern Lebanon, including the demolition of homes and places of worship.

stories.title: UN chief warns Hormuz closure 'strangling' global economy
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned that the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz due to the Iran war is strangling the global economy. He noted that even if restrictions were lifted immediately, supply chain recovery would take months, prolonging lower output and higher prices.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Air Force fundamentally changes how it tracks Russian Shaheds
stories.summary: Ukraine's Air Force has overhauled its tracking system for Russian-made Shahed drones. The previous model allowed drones to disappear from statistics when they crossed between regions, creating gaps in monitoring.

stories.title: Gaza flotilla organisers say 211 activists 'kidnapped' by Israel
stories.summary: Organizers of a Gaza-bound aid flotilla said 211 activists were detained by Israel. They reported that Israeli military speedboats approached the vessels and pointed lasers and semi-automatic weapons at the activists on board.

stories.title: Zelensky says Ukraine wants a long-term ceasefire, not ‘a few hours of safety for a parade in Moscow’
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine seeks a long-term ceasefire rather than a brief pause, dismissing Russia's Victory Day proposal. He directed his team to contact U.S. officials for details on the Russian offer.

stories.title: Man, machine and AI combine in battle to clear Ukraine of mines
stories.summary: Demining efforts in Ukraine are combining human operators, machines, and artificial intelligence to clear vast areas contaminated by mines and unexploded ordnance left from years of fighting.

stories.title: France top arms exporter to Israel in 2024, according to EU data
stories.summary: European Union data revealed that France was the top arms exporter to Israel in 2024. This occurred despite Israel later pledging in March to halt procurement from France, citing what it called a hostile attitude from Paris.

stories.title: Report: ICE detains Russian Buddhist lama who spoke out against war in Ukraine, deportation possible
stories.summary: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement detained Baldan Bazarov, a Russian Buddhist lama and former abbot from Buryatia who had spoken out against Russia's war in Ukraine. He was detained on April 29 and may face deportation.

stories.title: Starmer heckled with ‘Jew harmer’ shouts after London knife attack
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer was heckled with shouts of "Jew harmer" during a visit to London's predominantly Jewish Golders Green neighbourhood after two men were stabbed in a knife attack. The incident followed a series of attacks targeting Britain's Jewish community.

stories.title: In Mauritania, Malian refugees hope to return home
stories.summary: Approximately 300,000 Malian refugees have fled to Mauritania's Hodh Chargui region since 2012, driven by violence from jihadist groups, criminal gangs, and pro-independence movements. Many express hope of eventually returning to Mali.

stories.title: Yesh Atid MKs to 'Post': Lapid-Bennett alliance boosts opposition bloc, party to remain intact
stories.summary: Yesh Atid members of Knesset described the alliance between Yair Lapid and Naftali Bennett as a boost to Israel's opposition bloc. MK Ben Ari, the opposition coordinator, called the merger encouraging for citizens.

stories.title: First direct US-Venezuela commercial flight in 7 years heads to Caracas
stories.summary: The first direct commercial flight between the United States and Venezuela in seven years departed for Caracas on Thursday. The resumption follows the U.S. capture of former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in a January raid on his residence in Caracas.

stories.title: Calls grow to ban Palantir in Australia after manifesto described by UK MP as ‘ramblings of a supervillain’
stories.summary: Calls are growing in Australia to ban new government contracts with US surveillance technology firm Palantir, following a company manifesto that one UK MP described as the "ramblings of a supervillain." Palantir has responded by describing itself as simply "a software company."

stories.title: Queensland rejects key Bondi report recommendation as Albanese’s gun buyback flounders
stories.summary: Queensland's police minister rejected a key recommendation from the Bondi royal commission's interim report, led by Commissioner Virginia Bell, opposing a national gun buyback plan. The state argued the buyback would not keep guns away from terrorists and criminals, leaving New South Wales as the only clear supporter.

stories.title: Active-duty US soldiers to receive psychedelic drugs for PTSD next year
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Defense is funding two studies in which 186 active-duty soldiers with PTSD will undergo MDMA-assisted therapy sessions, likely beginning next year. The program aims to help service members process trauma using psychedelic-assisted treatment.

stories.title: Australians will pay more if Albanese fast-tracks fossil fuel projects, former oil and gas leaders warn
stories.summary: Former senior oil and gas executives from companies including BP, Shell, and Woodside warned the Albanese government that prioritising fossil fuel development could lead to ongoing price shocks for Australians. The 16 ex-industry leaders urged the government to back renewable energy projects instead.

stories.title: Is China’s Manus block a warning for other AI firms with global ambitions?
stories.summary: China blocked Meta Platforms' proposed acquisition of AI firm Manus, though Chinese state media characterized the decision as not a restriction on foreign investment. State broadcaster CCTV's social media account noted the deal reflected the AI industry transcending simple commercial logic.

stories.title: Trump tells Germany's Merz to stop interfering over Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump criticized German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, telling him to focus on ending the Russia-Ukraine war and spend less time interfering with US efforts to address what Trump called Iran's nuclear threat.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia to end LIV Golf funding, while league appoints new chairman
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia announced it will end its direct funding of LIV Golf, with the league planning to transition to a multi-partner investment model built around team franchises. A new chairman has also been appointed to oversee the restructuring.

stories.title: Iran, protests, human rights – all to know about the 76th FIFA Congress
stories.summary: The 76th FIFA Congress, held ahead of the World Cup, is expected to address geopolitical tensions involving Iran, human rights concerns, and logistical challenges related to the tournament.

stories.title: Russians attempt to gain foothold on islands near Kherson, mine Dnipro riverbanks – Voloshyn
stories.summary: Russian forces intensified attempts to land on islands near the Ukrainian city of Kherson and establish positions, while also increasing mining of the Dnipro River's shoreline. Ukrainian Defense Forces reported disrupting these efforts and destroying enemy assets.

stories.title: Banksy confirms statue of man blinded by flag in London is his work
stories.summary: The street artist Banksy confirmed that a new statue of a man with his face covered by a flag, erected overnight in London's Waterloo Place, is his work. The large sculpture was first spotted on Wednesday with Banksy's signature at the base.

stories.title: Israel’s top Jewish religious body 'refuses to condemn' smashing of Jesus statue
stories.summary: Israel's Chief Rabbinate reportedly declined to condemn an incident in which an Israeli soldier smashed a statue of Jesus. The Israeli army had sought a statement from the religious body denouncing the act as contrary to Jewish law amid widespread backlash.

stories.title: Kommersant reports Russia spent billions developing Russian social network VK’s video platform as it moves to designate it a ‘national’ service
stories.summary: Russia's Digital Development Ministry spent approximately 39.5 billion rubles in 2025 developing VK's video platform as a national service, according to Kommersant. An additional four billion rubles went toward a multifunctional information exchange service.

stories.title: Ukraine expands oil strikes on Russia as Putin proposes brief ceasefire
stories.summary: Ukraine expanded its strikes on Russian oil infrastructure as President Putin proposed a brief ceasefire during a phone call with President Trump. Putin suggested the ceasefire coincide with May 9, the anniversary of the defeat of Nazi Germany.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz launches Rs10m housing loans under Rs3.2tr 'Apna Ghar Programme'
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif launched the "PM Apna Ghar Programme," offering housing loans of Rs10 million on easy installments. The scheme aims to construct 500,000 housing units with a total allocation of Rs3.2 trillion, covering all provinces, Gilgit-Baltistan, and Azad Jammu and Kashmir.

stories.title: US military commanders to brief Trump on military options against Iran
stories.summary: Top U.S. military leaders, including CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper, are set to brief President Trump on potential military options against Iran. The briefing was scheduled for Thursday.

stories.title: Thousands pay tribute to Mali's slain defence minister under tight security
stories.summary: A tribute ceremony for Mali's slain defence minister Sadio Camara was held in the capital Bamako on Thursday under tight security. Camara was killed in a recent attack.

stories.title: ‘Act of piracy’: World reacts to Israeli interception of Gaza aid flotilla
stories.summary: World leaders condemned Israel's interception of a humanitarian aid flotilla bound for Gaza, with multiple governments describing the action as a violation of international law. The incident was characterized by some as an act of piracy.

stories.title: The hills of Samaria: The northern West Bank between politics and daily life
stories.summary: A reporter's notebook examines daily life and political dynamics in the northern West Bank, in the hills of Samaria, exploring the intersection of Israeli settlement activity and Palestinian communities.

stories.title: United States faces crossroads in Iraq as new prime minister is appointed - analysis
stories.summary: A new prime minister has been appointed in Iraq as the United States navigates its relationship with Baghdad. Washington announced new rewards for information on several key Iraqi militia leaders.

stories.title: Chechen PACE Member Suspended After LGBTQ+ and ‘Honor Killing’ Comments
stories.summary: Ruslan Kutayev, a Chechen member of the Platform for Dialogue with Russian Democratic Forces at PACE, was suspended after dismissive comments about LGBTQ+ people and women fleeing violence in Chechnya, including remarks on so-called honor killings.

stories.title: Russians cross 'kill zone' of up to 10 km to launch assaults in Zaporizhzhia sector – Voloshyn
stories.summary: In the Zaporizhzhia sector, Russian forces are attempting to cross an exposed zone of up to 10 kilometers to reach Ukrainian forward positions. Ukrainian defense forces report striking Russian troop concentration points and destroying equipment.

stories.title: IDF major allegedly smuggled $2.3m of contraband into Gaza, charged with aiding enemy
stories.summary: An Israel Defense Forces major responsible for the Kerem Shalom crossing area has been charged with aiding the enemy after allegedly smuggling $2.3 million worth of contraband into Gaza. The contraband reportedly included two tons of tobacco, car batteries, and hundreds of electronic devices.

stories.title: UK terror watchdog urges 'moratorium' on pro-Palestine marches
stories.summary: UK independent reviewer of terrorism legislation Jonathan Hall called for a moratorium on pro-Palestine marches in Britain. The comments followed a stabbing attack on two Jewish people in the Golders Green area of London.

stories.title: Chinese firms face pressure on AI investments as US peers’ spending keeps soaring
stories.summary: U.S. tech giants are on track for over $700 billion in AI capital expenditures this year, far exceeding Chinese counterparts. Analysts say China's growing demand for AI applications will pressure its tech companies, including those competing with Google and Microsoft, to increase spending.

stories.title: Pioneers of Bashan: The Israeli settlers eyeing land in Syria
stories.summary: A group called Pioneers of Bashan, founded in 2025, represents the expanding ambitions of Israel's settler movement into Syrian territory. The group embodies a growing push toward creating what proponents call a "Greater Israel."

stories.title: Regions Calling: Who Is Indigenous in Russia, Anyway?
stories.summary: Researcher Dr. Ekaterina Zibrova discussed how most of Russia's more than 180 ethnic groups are denied indigenous status under Russian law, examining the legal and political reasons behind this classification.

stories.title: UAE oil exit from OPEC signals focus on domestic priorities
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates exited OPEC, signaling a shift in its geopolitical priorities and sending a pointed message to Saudi Arabia. Analysts are assessing the ripple effects on the UAE's relationships with Riyadh, the United States, and Israel.

stories.title: Wang calls Taiwan ‘biggest risk factor’ in Beijing-Washington ties in Rubio call
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in a phone call that Taiwan is the biggest risk factor in China-U.S. relations. The call was aimed at preparing for a summit between President Trump and President Xi Jinping in Beijing in mid-May.

stories.title: ‘Tell God the truth’: The Ukrainian priest confronting the toll of war
stories.summary: Ukrainian Reverend Mykola Bagirov continues to minister to communities amid the ongoing war, confronting the daily toll of the conflict on his congregation while working to sustain religious faith.

stories.title: National Bank keeps key policy rate at 15%
stories.summary: The National Bank of Ukraine decided to maintain its key policy rate at 15 percent.

stories.title: Israel arrests 175 activists from Gaza flotilla far from its waters
stories.summary: Israel's military intercepted approximately 175 activists aboard more than 20 boats from a Gaza-bound aid flotilla in international waters off the coast of Greece. The activists were being transported to Israel. The flotilla had been organized by pro-Palestinian groups seeking to break Israel's blockade on Gaza.

stories.title: Will Gaza national committee succeed amid a fragmented reality?
stories.summary: A newly formed national committee in Gaza is attempting to address governance challenges in the territory. Analysts note the effort faces significant structural constraints amid political fragmentation.

stories.title: Twelve IDF soldiers wounded in drone strike as fighting escalates along Lebanon border
stories.summary: Twelve Israeli soldiers were wounded when a Hezbollah explosive drone struck an armored vehicle near the northern community of Shomera along the Lebanon border. Two soldiers sustained moderate injuries and ten had light wounds.

stories.title: Lahore Bar Association moves SC against 27th Amendment following transfer of IHC judges
stories.summary: The Lahore Bar Association filed a petition with Pakistan's Supreme Court challenging the constitutionality of the 27th Constitutional Amendment. The move followed the government's transfer of three Islamabad High Court judges to other high courts, approved by the Judicial Commission of Pakistan.

stories.title: Russians strike Chernihiv, leaving tree injured, administrative building damaged
stories.summary: A Russian attack on Chernihiv on April 30 struck an administrative building, injuring three people.

stories.title: Gaza was the scandal that should have ended Keir Starmer’s political career
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces intensifying political pressure over his stance on the Gaza conflict. Critics argue his support for Israel's military operations has caused lasting damage to his political standing.

stories.title: CH-53K gears up for first deployment with 26th Marine Expeditionary Unit
stories.summary: The U.S. Marine Corps' CH-53K King Stallion heavy-lift helicopter is preparing for its first operational deployment with the 26th Marine Expeditionary Unit. Program manager Col. Kate Fleeger stated the Corps is methodically completing training, personnel, and preparation checklist items to reach deployment readiness.

stories.title: The death of a Lebanese village
stories.summary: The Lebanese border village of Kfar Kila has been extensively destroyed. Israeli forces say the village and other leveled communities in southern Lebanon served as havens for Hezbollah.

stories.title: Ghalibaf says Strait of Hormuz will be 'free from American presence'
stories.summary: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf declared that Iran's control over the Strait of Hormuz would ensure a future free of American military presence. He made the remarks on the national Persian Gulf day.

stories.title: 'Growing sense in international community' that Trump doesn't have an Iran exit strategy
stories.summary: Analysts and commentators note a growing international perception that President Trump lacks a clear exit strategy for the U.S. conflict with Iran. European allies are described as strained between engagement and uncertainty over the administration's unpredictable approach.

stories.title: PSX plunges over 3,000 points during intraday trade as bears maintain control
stories.summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange's KSE-100 index plunged over 3,000 points during intraday trading on Thursday, dropping to an intraday low of 160,391 points. The sell-off marked a third consecutive session of losses as investors remained wary of the economic outlook and corporate earnings.

stories.title: Mali holds tribute for assassinated defence minister under tight security
stories.summary: Mali held a tribute ceremony in Bamako under tight security for assassinated defence minister Sadio Camara, who was killed in a rebel bomb attack. The assault was carried out by Tuareg separatist fighters and an al-Qaeda-linked jihadist group targeting the ruling military junta.

stories.title: The US Army wants to manufacture meatless proteins in combat zones
stories.summary: The U.S. Army is exploring alternative-protein manufacturing capabilities for use in combat zones. The initiative aims to enhance food supply chain resilience by producing meatless proteins in forward-deployed settings.

stories.title: Commissioning ceremony of Pakistan Navy’s first Hangor-class attack submarine held in China
stories.summary: Pakistan commissioned its first Hangor-class attack submarine, PNS Hangor, at a ceremony in Sanya, China. President Asif Ali Zardari and Chief of Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf attended. Zardari called the commissioning a historic milestone in Pakistan's naval modernization.

stories.title: Booker Prize nominee Chigozie Obioma on being an African writer today
stories.summary: Nigerian writer Chigozie Obioma, twice shortlisted for the Booker Prize for "The Fishermen" and "An Orchestra of Minorities," spoke at the Marrakech African Book Festival in Morocco. He discussed his experience as an African writer in the contemporary literary landscape.

stories.title: Why is China warning the UN of a Japanese ‘nuclear breakout’?
stories.summary: China issued a position paper urging the United Nations to address Japan's potential capability to produce nuclear weapons. Beijing called on the UN to make Japan's possible pursuit of nuclear arms an important agenda item at an ongoing convention in New York.

stories.title: If you were a Palestinian, could you see a way forward for peace with Israel? - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Israelis must acknowledge that, from the Palestinian perspective, the political horizon for peace has effectively disappeared if a different future is to be achieved.

stories.title: SSU drones hit one of Russia's largest oil refineries more than 1,500 km from Ukraine
stories.summary: Drones operated by Ukraine's SSU Alpha Special Operations Center struck the Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez oil refinery in Russia's Perm region, located more than 1,500 kilometers from Ukraine's border.

stories.title: Starmer booed at site of Golders Green terror; promises to tackle antisemitism, extremism
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer was booed while visiting the site of a terror stabbing in Golders Green, London, that wounded two Jewish people. He pledged to tackle antisemitism and extremism, and the government announced an additional $33 million for community security.

stories.title: Ukraine is striking Tuapse — Russian refinery town founded by general who engineered Caucasus genocide
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces have carried out three strikes in two weeks on Tuapse, a Russian refinery town and Black Sea port, causing fires, evacuations, and oil contamination. The city was historically a staging ground for a 19th-century Caucasus genocide carried out under a Russian general.

stories.title: Economic risks have 'intensified' since Iran war, says ECB
stories.summary: The European Central Bank warned that economic risks to eurozone growth and inflation have intensified due to the war involving Iran and its effects on global energy supplies. The ECB held its benchmark deposit rate at two percent.

stories.title: Global press freedom falls to lowest level in 25 years, RSF warns
stories.summary: Reporters Without Borders reported that global press freedom has fallen to its lowest level in 25 years, with only 1 percent of the world's population living in countries with a "good" media environment. Norway ranked first while Eritrea remained last, amid rising violence against journalists and growing legal and political pressures.

stories.title: US economy grows 2% in January–March; Iran war clouds outlook
stories.summary: The U.S. economy grew at a 2 percent annualized rate in the first quarter of 2026, recovering from a 0.5 percent expansion in late 2025 following a 43-day federal government shutdown. The Commerce Department noted the rebound, though the ongoing Iran war clouds the economic outlook.

stories.title: US military equipment worth billions of dollars destroyed in Iran war
stories.summary: The United States lost military aerial equipment valued at up to $2.8 billion during the war with Iran, according to a US-based think tank. The losses underscore the significant material cost of the conflict.

stories.title: Indonesian soldiers accused of acid attack. What happened and why?
stories.summary: Indonesian soldiers have been accused of carrying out an acid attack, which analysts say fits a broader pattern of military repression in the country. Concerns are growing over the expanding role of the Indonesian military in domestic affairs.

stories.title: PMDC announces closure of admissions for academic session 2025–2026
stories.summary: The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council announced the closure of admissions for the 2025–2026 academic session, stating students admitted after April 15 will not be registered. All recognized medical and dental colleges were directed to comply, with violations subject to the PMDC Act, 2022.

stories.title: Namibia: Traut Tackles Crime Through Collaboration
stories.summary: Newly elected Windhoek East councillor Jochen Traut in Namibia has identified fighting crime through stronger collaboration between communities and law enforcement as a short-term priority of his tenure.

stories.title: Namibia: May Day Takes Tripartite Turn ... Govt, Unions and Employers Join Forces for Opuwo Event
stories.summary: Namibia is preparing to mark International Workers' Day with a new tripartite approach, bringing together government, trade unions, and employers for a joint commemoration event in Opuwo.

stories.title: Russian drones strike Ukraine's Odesa overnight, wounding 18, officials say
stories.summary: Russian drones struck the southern Ukrainian city of Odesa overnight on April 30, wounding at least 18 people and damaging residential buildings. It was the second drone attack on Odesa that week.

stories.title: Russians try to advance toward Zaporizhzhia — Voloshyn
stories.summary: On the Huliaipole axis in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, Russian forces have sustained approximately 35 to 40 daily clashes for about two weeks while unsuccessfully attempting to push deeper toward the city of Zaporizhzhia.

stories.title: Palestinian Authority continues to pay terrorists, US State Department report confirms
stories.summary: A US State Department report confirmed that the Palestinian Authority continues payments to individuals convicted of terrorism-related offenses. Under the Taylor Force Act of 2018, such payments block US economic aid to Ramallah.

stories.title: Hormuz effect? How US, China are ramping up tensions over the Panama Canal
stories.summary: Tensions between the United States and China are escalating over control and influence regarding the Panama Canal. The dispute reflects a wider power struggle over global shipping routes and strategic waterways.

stories.title: Was Israeli PM’s Lebanon destruction video a snub to Trump?
stories.summary: Hours after US President Trump asked Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu to halt the destruction of buildings in Lebanon, Netanyahu posted a video montage showcasing the demolitions. The move was widely interpreted as a possible rebuff of Trump's request.

stories.title: Pakistan, the country that almost ended polio 30 years in a row
stories.summary: A four-year-old boy in Sindh's Sujawal became Pakistan's first reported polio case of 2026 on March 5, despite having a complete vaccination record. He contracted non-paralytic polio, a form that can go unnoticed. Pakistan continues to struggle with eradicating the disease after decades of effort.

stories.title: Iran supreme leader issues defiant statement on strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei issued a defiant statement asserting Tehran's control over the Strait of Hormuz and vowing to protect the country's nuclear and missile programmes. He described recent U.S. military deployments in the region as a disgraceful defeat.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia to pull investment from LIV Golf tour
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund plans to withdraw its investment from the LIV Golf tour. The move is part of broader scaling back of major projects funded by the kingdom.

stories.title: Ukraine to allow drone sales abroad, with caveats
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced plans to ease restrictions on Ukrainian arms manufacturers to permit drone exports abroad. The new regulations will require that Ukraine's own national defense needs are met first before manufacturers can sell to foreign buyers.

stories.title: Mali crisis: Who are the key leaders to know about?
stories.summary: Mali is facing one of its most severe security crises in years, involving multiple government and armed group leaders. Al Jazeera profiled key figures from both the Malian government and various armed factions involved in the conflict.

stories.title: Anti-immigrant attacks and protests in South Africa
stories.summary: South Africa has experienced a wave of anti-immigrant attacks and protests targeting foreign nationals. The violence reflects ongoing tensions over immigration in the country.

stories.title: 2 armed suspects arrested in KP's Karak for 'attacking' police team
stories.summary: Police in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Karak district arrested two armed suspects after a patrol came under fire in the Tor Dhand area. The suspects, traveling by motorcycle, opened fire when signaled to stop, triggering a gun battle. One suspect was arrested in an injured condition.

stories.title: Romania picks Rheinmetall’s Lynx combat vehicle in $4 billion acquisition
stories.summary: Romania selected Rheinmetall's Lynx infantry fighting vehicle in an acquisition valued at approximately $4 billion. Romanian defense officials intend to finance the purchase through European Union-backed loans.

stories.title: European Parliament urges sanctions on Venezuela to remain until verifiable democratic progress
stories.summary: The European Parliament passed a resolution with 507 votes in favor urging the EU Council to maintain sanctions on Venezuelan officials responsible for human rights violations. The sanctions are to remain until Venezuela adopts significant measures toward a democratic transition under acting President Delcy Rodríguez's government.

stories.title: Iran warns US of return to lengthy conflict if attacked, says report
stories.summary: A senior Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps official warned that any U.S. attack on Iran would trigger prolonged strikes against American regional positions and warships. The statement responded to reports that the U.S. military has prepared a plan for strikes on Iran.

stories.title: Russian nighttime attack in Odesa's Prymorskyi district leaves 22 buildings damaged
stories.summary: A Russian nighttime attack on April 30 damaged 22 buildings in Odesa's Prymorskyi district, which bore the heaviest impact from the shelling.

stories.title: UAE oil break exposes deepening Saudi rift as Gulf power shifts
stories.summary: The UAE's decision to break from OPEC production agreements has exposed a deepening rift with Saudi Arabia. Analysts say Abu Dhabi is prioritizing autonomy over deference to Riyadh, signaling a broader shift in Gulf power dynamics.

stories.title: Nun assaulted in Jerusalem amid 'pattern' of anti-Christian attacks by Israelis
stories.summary: A 48-year-old nun was physically assaulted while walking in occupied East Jerusalem on April 28, 2026. Israeli police arrested a suspect, and the incident was described as part of a pattern of anti-Christian attacks in the city.

stories.title: Some Ukrainian soldiers have been on position for 502 days. Syrskyi cappes frontline deployments at two months
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi capped frontline deployments at two months after reports emerged that some soldiers had been on position for 502 days. The decision followed a scandal involving inadequate food supplies to troops in the 14th Separate Mechanized Brigade.

stories.title: Netanyahu presses Trump on Lebanon while Washington builds Hormuz coalition
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pressed U.S. President Donald Trump on Lebanon-related issues while Washington simultaneously worked to build a multinational coalition for operations in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: 12 soldiers injured by Hezbollah drone in northern Israel; IDF strikes in Lebanon
stories.summary: A Hezbollah drone struck an Israeli artillery position near the northern border, injuring 12 soldiers, two of them moderately. The IDF carried out retaliatory strikes in Lebanon, which Lebanese authorities said killed nine people, including two children.

stories.title: Energy fears drive Gulf mediation in US-Iran conflict
stories.summary: Gulf countries are quietly mediating between the United States and Iran as the ongoing conflict disrupts vital oil exports. Working through intermediaries including Pakistan, Gulf states are attempting to revive negotiations from Doha despite tensions with Tehran.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian teen in West Bank raid
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed a 16-year-old Palestinian boy during a military raid in Hebron in the occupied West Bank. Medics reported the teen, Ibraheem Khayyat, was shot in the abdomen by Israeli troops.

stories.title: Sudden focus on teen violence underscores neglect of record bloodletting in Arab society
stories.summary: Two deadly stabbing incidents in Jewish cities in Israel prompted a swift government response, drawing criticism from Arab citizens who say authorities have long neglected a crime wave affecting their communities.

stories.title: US intervention forces end to decade of statistical opacity at Venezuela's Central Bank
stories.summary: Venezuela's Central Bank has begun publishing economic indicators withheld for at least a decade, following the U.S. military intervention that led to the capture of former president Nicolás Maduro on January 3. Newly released data showed monthly inflation reached 32 per cent in January before declining to 13.1 per cent in March.

stories.title: Russia’s role in Mali questioned as rebels push for exit
stories.summary: Rebel groups in Mali have called for the withdrawal of Russian forces, with a pullback from the northern city of Kidal highlighting growing pressure on Moscow's Sahel presence. Analysts note this reflects a broader questioning of Russia's military role across the region despite Moscow's claims of success.

stories.title: White House quiet as China ramps up trade leverage before Trump-Xi summit
stories.summary: The White House has remained unusually quiet as China increases its trade leverage ahead of a planned summit between President Trump and President Xi. Observers noted the Trump administration's response has been uncharacteristically muted.

stories.title: Deadly migration route leaves Horn of Africa migrants stranded
stories.summary: Migrants from the Horn of Africa, primarily Ethiopia, are returning to Djibouti after failed attempts to cross the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait to reach Gulf countries. More than 900 deaths were recorded on this route in 2025, making it the deadliest year on record.

stories.title: Viral pro-Iran AI memes blur lines between propaganda and entertainment
stories.summary: Iranian-American creator Mahdi Hemmat is generating millions of views with AI-generated, Lego-style rap videos that promote pro-Iran narratives and criticize President Trump amid the U.S.-Iran-Israel conflict. The content illustrates how digital creators are using entertainment formats to shape political opinion among younger Western audiences.

stories.title: Tai Po fire: tendering system can’t stop firms manipulating market, inquiry hears
stories.summary: A public inquiry into Hong Kong's deadly Tai Po fire heard that the official tendering system cannot prevent engineering firms from colluding to manipulate the building maintenance market. Three Urban Renewal Authority officials testified that the statutory body lacked the capacity to combat bid-rigging.

stories.title: Why are Western feminists silent on the war on Iranian women?
stories.summary: Western feminist organizations that previously supported Iranian women protesting compulsory hijab laws have been largely silent as Iranian women are reportedly being killed amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: China’s Tiangong space station to double in size as Nasa phases out ISS
stories.summary: China confirmed plans to expand its Tiangong space station, potentially more than doubling its size to accommodate growing scientific demand and international cooperation. The expansion comes as NASA prepares to retire the International Space Station in early 2031.

stories.title: Xi-Trump summit unlikely to revive Chinese investment in US, report warns
stories.summary: A Rhodium Group report warns that Chinese foreign direct investment in the United States is unlikely to recover significantly even if Presidents Xi Jinping and Donald Trump reach a deal at their planned Beijing summit. Chinese FDI in the U.S. has remained at low levels since collapsing from its 2016 peak.

stories.title: Telegraph and Politico owner says journalists must support Israel or resign
stories.summary: Axel Springer CEO Mathias Döpfner told staff at Politico and the Telegraph that supporting Israel is a core value of employment at the outlets and that journalists unwilling to comply should resign. The remarks prompted concerns about editorial independence.

stories.title: DR Congo creates paramilitary mining guard
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo announced the creation of a paramilitary mining guard backed by U.S. and UAE funding. The force is expected to grow to over 20,000 personnel by 2028 to secure mining operations and strengthen state control over critical mineral resources.

stories.title: Spectator owner’s son calls for mine-laden ‘floating wall’ to stop Channel crossings
stories.summary: Winston Marshall, son of Spectator owner Paul Marshall and a former member of Mumford & Sons, proposed constructing a mine-laden "floating wall" in the English Channel to stop small boat crossings. He described those crossing as economic migrants rather than refugees.

stories.title: Russians shell Donetsk region over 1,400 times in one day, leaving one killed, several injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out over 1,400 shelling attacks in Ukraine's Donetsk region in a single day, damaging 21 civilian structures. One person was killed and three were injured.

stories.title: $25bn or $1 trillion: How much has Iran war really cost the US?
stories.summary: U.S. lawmakers clashed on Capitol Hill over the true cost of the war with Iran, with estimates ranging from $25 billion to $1 trillion, highlighting concerns about a lack of transparency in military spending.

stories.title: Israel says intercepted 175 Gaza flotilla activists on 20 boats
stories.summary: Israel's Foreign Ministry confirmed it intercepted approximately 175 activists from more than 20 boats attempting to deliver aid to Gaza. The activists were taken aboard an Israeli navy vessel and transported to Israel.

stories.title: World’s top media outlets urge Israel to allow independent access to Gaza
stories.summary: Major international media organizations have called on Israel to grant independent journalists access to the Gaza Strip. Israel continues to block foreign reporters from entering the territory despite a ceasefire being in place.

stories.title: Army requests funds to speed development, production of EW systems
stories.summary: The U.S. Army's fiscal year 2027 budget request includes funding to accelerate the development and production of electronic warfare and signals intelligence systems, enabling faster fielding and continued experimentation.

stories.title: UK police arrest 'mahdi' claimant's followers over rape claims
stories.summary: British police deployed hundreds of officers in raids on properties in Crewe, Cheshire, linked to the Ahmadi Religion of Peace and Light. The operation targeted followers of a self-proclaimed mahdi over rape allegations.

stories.title: Rwanda: Who Is Eligible for Rwanda's $100m SME Fund?
stories.summary: Rwanda announced a $100 million fund for small and medium enterprises, offering eligible SMEs a grace period of up to 24 months to stabilize and expand their operations.

stories.title: Israel kills nine people in southern Lebanon despite ‘ceasefire’
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed nine people in southern Lebanon despite an active ceasefire agreement. The Lebanese government condemned the attacks as violations of the ceasefire terms.

stories.title: US weighs training Lebanese army unit to disarm Hezbollah
stories.summary: The United States is considering a plan to arm and train Lebanese army units to disarm Hezbollah in southern Lebanon. The initiative comes as Israeli military strikes in the region continue to escalate.

stories.title: South Africa: March and March Anti-Immigrant Protest Ends in Chaos
stories.summary: An anti-immigrant protest march in South Africa descended into chaos after demonstrators deviated from the agreed route and attacked immigrants.

stories.title: Shahed drones begin maneuvering when interceptor drones approach — 'Flash'
stories.summary: Russian Shahed-type drones have begun performing evasive maneuvers when approached by Ukrainian interceptor drones. The behavioral change is attributed to the likely installation of cameras on the Shahed drones, enabling real-time threat detection.

stories.title: Russia has given Iran something more important than weapons
stories.summary: Russia has provided Iran with significant political backing and diplomatic support opposing escalation, which analysts say has been more consequential in shaping the conflict than weapons transfers.

stories.title: South Africa: Mthatha Residents Block N2 Over Water Crisis
stories.summary: Residents of Mthatha, South Africa, blocked the N2 highway to protest a prolonged water crisis. Locals reported going months without access to running water.

stories.title: Iran's leader accuses US of driving Middle East insecurity, defends Iran’s military capabilities
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei accused the United States of driving instability across the Middle East, citing the presence of US military bases in the Persian Gulf region. He also defended Iran's military capabilities amid ongoing tensions.

stories.title: African oil producers defend need to drill at fossil fuel exit talks
stories.summary: Oil-producing African nations at fossil fuel phaseout talks in Colombia stated they would continue drilling to support economic growth, underscoring tensions between climate commitments and the fiscal needs of developing producers.

stories.title: Hong Kong homebuyers flock to new launches as flats sell out swiftly
stories.summary: Hong Kong homebuyers purchased most newly released residential units on Thursday, with all 120 flats at One Victoria Cove I in Hung Hom selling out. Developers are ramping up new construction launches amid sustained housing demand.

stories.title: Mali: Mali Junta Leader to Attend Funeral of Defence Minister Killed in Rebel Attacks
stories.summary: Mali's junta leader Assimi Goïta is expected to attend the funeral of Defence Minister Sadio Camara, who was killed in a rebel assault on his home. The attacks have destabilised the military government's hold on power.

stories.title: 'Next Iran'?: Turkey accelerates 60,000-tonne aircraft carrier amid Israel tensions
stories.summary: Turkey is accelerating construction of a 60,000-tonne aircraft carrier amid rising tensions with Israel. As Israel compares Turkey to Iran and strengthens ties with Greece and Cyprus, Ankara is investing in naval power to reassert its regional position.

stories.title: 'Next Iran'?: Turkey accelerates 60,000 tonnes aircraft carrier amid Israel tensions
stories.summary: Turkey is accelerating construction of a 60,000-tonne aircraft carrier as tensions with Israel escalate. The move comes as Israel strengthens ties with Greece and Cyprus, and Ankara seeks to reassert its naval power in the region.

stories.title: A world adrift looks to China for institutional anchors. Enter Hong Kong
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Hong Kong could serve as an institutional anchor amid growing strain on the international order, as unilateralism and protectionism erode confidence in rules-based global frameworks.

stories.title: South Africa: Ramaphosa Picks 4 November for Local Government Elections
stories.summary: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa announced 4 November as the date for local government elections during a meeting with mayors and premiers at the Birchwood Hotel in Ekurhuleni. Voters will elect representatives to councils across the country.

stories.title: Pakistan’s IMF-backed recovery under pressure as US-Iran mediation stalls
stories.summary: Pakistan's efforts to mediate between the United States and Iran have placed Islamabad near the centre of Middle East diplomacy, but the ongoing conflict is straining its fragile economy. Soaring oil prices and disrupted Strait of Hormuz flows are hitting Pakistan especially hard given its thin foreign exchange reserves.

stories.title: US seeks new coalition to get ships moving again in Strait of Hormuz, internal cable says
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department and Pentagon are jointly seeking to build a new international coalition to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, according to an internal diplomatic cable. The initiative aims to address disruptions caused by the ongoing conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Nigeria: 'My Enemies Want Me Out Using Insecurity' - Tinubu
stories.summary: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu characterised the country's rising insecurity as a politically motivated tool wielded by his opponents. He framed the violence as being weaponised against his administration rather than solely a national security challenge.

stories.title: Two months on, Qatar gas disruption jolts global supply
stories.summary: Two months after disruptions to Qatar's gas exports, the crisis is raising questions about global energy supply stability. Doha's financial reserves have helped it absorb the economic shock so far.

stories.title: Russia’s close ally now has enough nuclear warheads and delivery systems to breach US missile defense
stories.summary: North Korea, a close Russian ally, is reported to possess enough nuclear warheads and delivery systems to potentially breach U.S. missile defense capabilities.

stories.title: 'How are we going to get back home?' Islamist group tightens blockade on Mali capital
stories.summary: An Islamist group has tightened its blockade around Mali's capital, disrupting movement and supplies. The escalation follows the recent assassination of Mali's defense minister in a series of nationwide attacks.

stories.title: Russians attack Dnipropetrovsk region, leaving one killed, four injured
stories.summary: A Russian attack on the Dnipro district in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region killed one person and wounded four others.

stories.title: Tariffs on digital displays could help avoid US military dependence on China, policy group says
stories.summary: A US policy group argued that tariffs on digital displays could reduce American military dependence on Chinese technology. President Trump previously signed legislation requiring the Pentagon to plan for ending reliance on adversary-sourced technology by 2027.

stories.title: An Ayatollah for the Aggrieved
stories.summary: An analysis examines why Iran's Supreme Leader continues to draw support from Sunni admirers despite sectarian divisions, arguing that Iran's stance of resistance against Western powers remains the primary appeal.

stories.title: Israel intercepts and detains crews of Gaza aid flotilla near Crete
stories.summary: Israeli forces intercepted at least 22 boats from the Global Sumud Flotilla near the Greek island of Crete and detained their crews. The flotilla of approximately 58 vessels carrying people from 70 countries had departed from Italy to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza in an attempt to break Israel's maritime blockade.

stories.title: Nations urged to 'go further' as fossil fuel exit talks wrap up in Colombia
stories.summary: Fossil fuel exit negotiations concluded in Colombia, with participants urging nations to accelerate their transition away from fossil fuels. The push gained momentum as the war on Iran triggered a global energy crisis.

stories.title: Israeli maps outline expanded zone of military control in Gaza
stories.summary: Israel has quietly published new maps showing an expanded restricted military zone in Gaza, effectively placing at least 64 percent of the territory under Israeli military control.

stories.title: Iran says ‘new chapter’ in Strait of Hormuz after US ‘shameful failure’
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei declared a 'new chapter' in the Strait of Hormuz, claiming a shift in the strategic balance following what he called America's 'shameful failure' in its military campaign in the region.

stories.title: Ship Ukraine says carries stolen grain will not offload in Israel after diplomatic row
stories.summary: A ship that Ukraine alleges was carrying grain stolen from Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory will not offload its cargo in Israel following a diplomatic dispute. An Israeli official said the decision was made by the importer, not the government.

stories.title: Israel just quintupled its PR budget to $730 million; experts say it won’t work
stories.summary: Israel increased its public relations budget fivefold to $730 million. Experts expressed skepticism that the spending would significantly improve the country's international image given ongoing government policies.

stories.title: Soaring fuel prices in Pakistan threaten economic and political crises
stories.summary: Pakistan's monthly fuel import bill surged from $300 million to $800 million, placing severe strain on the country's economy and raising concerns about potential political instability.

stories.title: Uncovering Roots podcast: Israel's Paraguay scheme exposed
stories.summary: A podcast investigation examines a scheme linked to Israel involving Paraguay, exploring its impact on victims and the lasting trauma they have carried for decades.

stories.title: Report: United Russia sets turnout targets for party primaries, mobilizes public-sector workers to meet them
stories.summary: Russia's ruling United Russia party and the Kremlin's political bloc have set turnout targets exceeding 10% of voters for upcoming party primaries. Regional administrations are reportedly mobilizing public-sector and state-company workers to meet these targets ahead of the State Duma campaign. Russians have complained on social media about being coerced into participating.

stories.title: Russians attempting to break through to Kupiansk from two directions – military
stories.summary: Russian forces are attempting to advance toward the city of Kupiansk in Ukraine's Kharkiv region from both banks of the Oskil River. Ukrainian military officials reported the dual-axis offensive aimed at breaking through to the strategically important town.

stories.title: Africa: Amine Laghidi, the First Moroccan and African to be Awarded a Prize at the Trieste Summit
stories.summary: Professor Amine Laghidi of Morocco received a Special Award at the Trieste Summit, becoming the first Moroccan and African to be honoured at the event. Laghidi heads several global organisations.

stories.title: China’s US experts are falling short in the ‘great power game’, top scholar argues
stories.summary: A prominent Chinese academic argued that China's U.S. experts must better study America's internal crises, including political culture shifts, racial tensions, and fiscal unsustainability, to help Beijing navigate the rivalry with Washington.

stories.title: 'The world deserves food sovereignty and more secured food access for everybody'
stories.summary: At a high-level summit in Colombia, Delphine Lévi Alvarès of the Center for International Environmental Law argued that Middle East instability underscores the urgent need to decouple global food and energy systems from fossil fuels. She called for greater food sovereignty and secured food access worldwide.

stories.title: Press freedom at lowest level in 25 years: RSF
stories.summary: Reporters Without Borders reported that global press freedom has reached its lowest level in 25 years. The organization noted that the average score for all countries and territories worldwide has never been so low.

stories.title: Galilee man who swore loyalty to ISIS, planned attack on soldiers, indicted on terror charges
stories.summary: Israeli authorities indicted a man from the Galilee region on terror charges after he allegedly swore loyalty to ISIS and planned an attack on soldiers. Authorities noted a pattern of Arab citizens of Israel pledging allegiance to ISIS in recent years.

stories.title: Tracking the shadow fleet: How Iran evaded the US naval blockade in Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran has employed a shadow fleet of vessels using fake flags and transponder-darkening techniques to evade the U.S. naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: What does the UAE walking out of OPEC mean for Russia’s war on Ukraine?
stories.summary: The UAE's departure from OPEC is expected to reduce oil revenue flowing to Moscow, weakening but not collapsing Russia's financial capacity to sustain its war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Media orgs call on Israel to allow foreign reporters into Gaza
stories.summary: Editors from more than two dozen media organizations called on Israel to permit foreign journalists to enter Gaza, challenging the rationale behind the ban on independent press access to the territory.

stories.title: Iran war tests India’s Brics leadership as ‘political relevance’ questions mount
stories.summary: India's leadership of Brics is being tested by the bloc's failure to agree on a common position regarding the Middle East conflict. A meeting of Brics officials in New Delhi last week exposed divergent interests among the group's ten members.

stories.title: Starmer calls for ‘swift and visible’ response to attacks on Jews
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer called for a 'swift and visible' response to antisemitic attacks during a Downing Street meeting following an assault in north London that wounded two people.

stories.title: When the US and Israel bombed Tehran, I did not flee. Here’s why
stories.summary: A first-person account describes the decision of an Iranian resident to remain in Tehran during US and Israeli bombing, reflecting on Iranians' deep connection to their homeland despite the strikes.

stories.title: Russians unable to create buffer zone on border – SBGS spox
stories.summary: Ukraine's State Border Guard Service reported that Russian forces have been unable to significantly expand their zone of control along the northern border area, failing to establish a meaningful buffer zone.

stories.title: Manchester United’s Kobbie Mainoo signs new five-year deal
stories.summary: Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo signed a new five-year contract with the club. The England international had been linked with a departure after losing his starting place under manager Ruben Amorim.

stories.title: Chemical Emergency Alert Issued in Perm After Ukraine Strikes Industrial Sites
stories.summary: Authorities in Russia's Perm region issued a chemical emergency alert following Ukrainian strikes on industrial sites. Regional officials later claimed the warning was a test, despite residents reporting large smoke clouds and a chemical odor in the area.

stories.title: 'Piracy': Israel raids Gaza-bound aid flotilla off Greek coast
stories.summary: Israeli naval forces intercepted a Gaza-bound aid flotilla in international waters off the Greek coast, raiding at least 15 boats. Israel's foreign ministry said approximately 175 activists from over 20 vessels were taken into Israeli custody.

stories.title: Former Bnei Brak principal wanted in Israel for sex crimes against children arrested by ICE
stories.summary: A former principal from Bnei Brak wanted in Israel on charges of sex crimes against children was arrested by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Farkas appeared before a federal courthouse in Trenton, New Jersey, and was ordered to remain in custody.

stories.title: Cambridge A-level paper leak brings distress to bright students
stories.summary: Pakistan's Inter-Board of Coordination Commission is seeking a report from Cambridge after an alleged leak of the A-level Mathematics (9709) exam paper. Students and parents raised concerns about the transparency of the examination system, with reports of the paper circulating before the test.

stories.title: Zelensky orders talks with U.S. to verify details of Russia’s temporary truce proposal
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky ordered Ukrainian representatives to consult with the US president's team to clarify details of Russia's proposal for a short-term ceasefire. The directive signals Ukraine's willingness to examine the terms before responding formally.

stories.title: U.S. charges governor of Mexican state of Sinaloa with drug trafficking
stories.summary: The U.S. Justice Department charged Sinaloa state Governor Ruben Rocha with drug trafficking, alleging links to the Sinaloa Cartel. Rocha denied the charges on April 29, calling them politically motivated.

stories.title: PSX plunges over 4,700 points as bears maintain control
stories.summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange experienced a sharp selloff, with the KSE-100 index plunging over 4,700 points—a drop of roughly 2.89 percent—during Thursday's intraday trading. The decline marked a third consecutive session of losses, driven by investor concerns over the economic outlook, disappointing corporate earnings, and rising global oil prices amid geopolitical tensions.

stories.title: Gaza genocide death toll rises to 72,601
stories.summary: Medical officials in Gaza reported that the death toll from Israel's war on the enclave has reached 72,601, with 172,419 wounded since October 7, 2023. Since a ceasefire in October of the previous year, at least 824 additional people have been killed.

stories.title: Keir Starmer demands ‘swift, agile and visible’ response to London attack
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer convened a Downing Street meeting following a suspected terrorist stabbing attack in Golders Green, north-west London, a neighborhood with a large Jewish community. Starmer called the incident an attack on Britain's Jewish community and demanded a swift response from the government and criminal justice system.

stories.title: US military commanders to brief Trump on new options against Iran, Axios reports
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command has prepared a plan for 'short and powerful' military strikes against Iran and is set to brief President Trump on the new options, according to Axios. The development comes amid the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict.

stories.title: Will the Iran war reshape the global energy order?
stories.summary: Amid the Iran conflict, global energy dynamics are shifting as OPEC faces weakening influence, US oil exports increase, and China accelerates its transition toward renewable energy sources.

stories.title: Wang Fuk Court resident finds charred HK$100,000 inheritance after opening safe
stories.summary: Residents returning to the fire-damaged Wang Fuk Court estate in Tai Po, Hong Kong, discovered charred banknotes worth approximately HK$100,000 each inside safes retrieved from the wreckage. Several local storage companies offered free services to affected residents as a gesture of support.

stories.title: Mali crisis deepens as separatists and jihadists step up attacks
stories.summary: Mali's military launched strikes on the city of Kidal after separatist Azawad Liberation Front fighters claimed control. Jihadist group JNIM has intensified coordinated attacks and announced a blockade of roads leading to the capital Bamako, deepening the country's security crisis.

stories.title: Xi Jinping urges ‘disruptive innovation’ to boost China amid high-stakes US tech race
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping called for "disruptive innovation" and stronger basic research capabilities at a symposium in Shanghai. He emphasized expanding China's talent pool and fostering tolerance for failure amid an intensifying global technology competition with the United States.

stories.title: Daily Briefing Apr. 30 – Siege warfare? Who’ll blink first in tense Iran blockade
stories.summary: A briefing covers multiple Middle East developments including a new aid flotilla heading to Gaza, Israel's posture in Lebanon, and the tense standoff around the Iran blockade, alongside the appointment of a special envoy to the Christian world.

stories.title: Former CSRC chairman Yi Huiman to face trial for taking bribes, abusing power
stories.summary: Former China Securities Regulatory Commission chairman Yi Huiman will face trial on charges of accepting large bribes and abusing power. Prosecutors allege he used his position to provide benefits in job promotions, company listing approvals, and loan acquisitions.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz blockade: 'Who will blink first' ?
stories.summary: The US has discussed extending its blockade of Iranian ports through the Strait of Hormuz for months, pushing Brent crude to its highest level since March 2022. Both Washington and Tehran appear locked in a standoff, with neither side willing to make concessions.

stories.title: Bank of England warns ‘higher inflation is unavoidable’ after leaving interest rates on hold
stories.summary: The Bank of England held interest rates at 3.75% in an 8-1 vote but warned that higher inflation is unavoidable due to the Middle East conflict. The bank signaled that rate hikes could come later in the year.

stories.title: China sparks backlash with plan to send jobless graduates to vocational school
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security announced plans to expand vocational training for young jobseekers, aiming to upskill one million youth for emerging industries like robotics and AI. The policy, which encourages university graduates to attend technical schools, has drawn criticism amid China's ongoing youth unemployment crisis.

stories.title: Middle East ceasefires: A fragile peace on the brink | The Deep Dive
stories.summary: An analysis examines fragile ceasefires across the Middle East, from Tehran to Gaza and Lebanon, assessing the risk that unstable truces could trigger a new regional crisis.

stories.title: Defense Business Brief: Satellite firm’s ‘secret sauce’ | 3D-print factory in a box | Ship-lobby ad
stories.summary: The article covers defense industry developments including a satellite firm's technology, a 3D-printing factory system, and a ship-lobby advertisement. No specific conflict-related details were provided.

stories.title: Bodycam footage shows police detaining London stabbing suspect
stories.summary: Metropolitan Police bodycam footage shows officers detaining a suspect following a knife attack near a synagogue in Golders Green, London. Two men were stabbed in the incident, which occurred amid a series of recent arson attacks targeting Jewish sites in the area.

stories.title: Hungary has fired Netanyahu's pal Orbán but is Magyar different?
stories.summary: Peter Magyar won Hungary's elections after 16 years of Viktor Orbán's rule, promising reforms on rule of law and anti-corruption. However, analysts note Magyar's stance on Israel is not expected to differ significantly from Orbán's.

stories.title: ‘They’re as lost and inauthentic as us’: the Oscar winner who made a Farage satire – and released it on WeTransfer
stories.summary: Oscar-winning filmmaker Aneil Karia has released a satirical short film called "Vote Gavin Lyle," starring Jack Lowden as a Reform-style parliamentary candidate. The film was distributed via WeTransfer.

stories.title: SBU drones hit Lukoil’s Perm refinery — 1,500 km from Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine's SBU security service conducted a drone strike on the Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez oil refinery in Russia's Perm region, located more than 1,500 kilometers from the Ukrainian border. The facility processes nearly 13 million tons of crude oil annually.

stories.title: Press freedom at lowest level in 25 years: RSF
stories.summary: Reporters Without Borders reported that global press freedom has reached its lowest level in 25 years, with the average score across all countries and territories hitting a record low.

stories.title: Russian tanker hit in Black Sea left adrift after Ukrainian strike – Navy spox
stories.summary: A Russian tanker struck by the Ukrainian Navy in the Black Sea on April 29 reportedly lost propulsion and was left adrift. Ukrainian officials indicated the vessel likely did not sink after the attack.

stories.title: Mamdani says he would encourage King Charles to return the Koh-i-Noor diamond
stories.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he would encourage King Charles to return the Koh-i-Noor diamond to the Indian subcontinent during the monarch's state visit. India has indicated it will continue to pursue the return of the diamond from the United Kingdom.

stories.title: War fears mount as Trump mulls Iran strikes, blockade continues
stories.summary: Oil prices surged as President Trump reportedly moved away from negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz in favor of economic pressure and military threats against Iran. The escalation has heightened fears of a broader conflict.

stories.title: Telegraph and Politico owner says journalists must support Israel or resign
stories.summary: Mathias Döpfner, CEO of Axel Springer and owner of the Telegraph and Politico, reportedly told journalists they must support Israel or resign. Journalists at the outlets have accused Döpfner of editorial interference through his pro-Israel directives.

stories.title: Up seven in a year, up 50 since 2022. Ukraine climbs RSF press freedom rankings as global score hits 25-year low
stories.summary: Ukraine rose seven places in Reporters Without Borders' annual press freedom rankings, climbing 50 spots since 2022. Meanwhile, the United States dropped to 64th place as the global press freedom score hit a 25-year low.

stories.title: In 1946, Hong Kong’s governor Sir Mark Young returns after WWII – SCMP archive
stories.summary: A 1946 archival report describes the return of Hong Kong Governor Sir Mark Young to the colony on April 30, 1946, after being held as a prisoner of war by the Japanese during World War II. He paid tribute to those who fell defending Hong Kong.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill at least nine in south Lebanon, in breach of ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes killed at least nine people across multiple locations in southern Lebanon, including Jebchit, Toul, and Harouf. Residential buildings were destroyed in the attacks, which Lebanon says breach the existing ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Israel intercepts Gaza aid ships in international waters, organisers say
stories.summary: Israel intercepted humanitarian aid ships bound for Gaza in international waters, according to organizers from the Global Sumud Flotilla. The vessels were reportedly seized hundreds of miles from the Gaza coast.

stories.title: UK pledges extra £25mn for Jewish security after London stabbings
stories.summary: The UK government announced an additional £25 million in security funding for Jewish communities following a series of stabbing attacks in London. The allocation is part of broader efforts to protect the community.

stories.title: 'Sickening': British papers react to anti-Semitic attack in London
stories.summary: British newspapers led with coverage of the Golders Green stabbing attack targeting London's Jewish community. Other front-page stories included King Charles's speech to the US Congress and tensions between the US president and the German chancellor.

stories.title: Eurozone inflation soars to 3% as Iran war drives up energy prices
stories.summary: Eurozone inflation rose to 3% in April, up from 2.6% in March and 1.9% in February, driven largely by energy price increases linked to the Iran conflict. The European Central Bank faces pressure as growth stumbles and a key interest rate decision approaches.

stories.title: Mexico’s cartel crackdown hits top ranks – but will it fuel Jalisco violence?
stories.summary: Mexican special forces arrested Audias Flores, alias "El Jardinero," a potential successor to late Jalisco New Generation Cartel leader "El Mencho," after finding him hiding in a drainage pipe at a ranch in Nayarit state. The arrest raises concerns about possible cartel infighting and escalating violence in Jalisco.

stories.title: Russia strikes Odesa with drones, injuring 20 people and damaging homes, kindergarten, hotel
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the city of Odesa with a series of drones overnight, injuring at least 16 people including a 17-year-old. Residential homes, a kindergarten, and a hotel were damaged in the attack, according to Odesa military administration head Serhiy Lysak.

stories.title: Belarusian defectors tell Euromaidan Press: US sanctions relief unlocks the bank funding shells Russia fires at Ukraine
stories.summary: Belarusian defectors told Euromaidan Press that U.S. sanctions relief on Belarus has enabled bank funding that supports ammunition production ultimately used by Russia against Ukraine. Former security officers described it as a direct investment in weaponry fired across the border.

stories.title: CinC Syrskyi signs order on mandatory rotation of frontline troops
stories.summary: Ukraine's Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi signed an order mandating rotation for frontline servicemen. The order establishes clear time limits for deployment at forward positions and sets requirements for rest and support.

stories.title: Under Ukraine pressure, Israel blocks suspect Russian grain ship
stories.summary: Under pressure from Ukraine, Israel blocked a Russian grain ship from unloading its cargo at an Israeli port. Israel's Grain Importers Association said the Russian supplier would need to find an alternative destination.

stories.title: Why is China banning drone sales in Beijing?
