stories.summary: US Senator Bernie Sanders hosted a panel on Capitol Hill with leading Chinese scientists to advocate for international cooperation in regulating artificial intelligence. Sanders warned of societal risks if AI development continues without adequate safeguards.

stories.title: Video game-loving China monk defends hobby, says gaming, religion serve similar life purposes
stories.summary: Venerable Huayan, a senior Buddhist monk at Mingjiao Temple in Hefei, China, drew social media attention for his enthusiasm for video games, particularly Counter-Strike, arguing that gaming and religion serve similar life purposes.

stories.title: Russia blocks news site it accuses of promoting LGBT content
stories.summary: Russia's media regulator restricted access to an independent news outlet on April 29, accusing it of distributing propaganda promoting what authorities term "non-traditional sexual relations," the legal phrase Russian officials use to describe LGBT content.

stories.title: Attacks on hospitals and medics rising, driven by Middle East conflict, says World Health Organization
stories.summary: The World Health Organization reported on April 29 that attacks on healthcare facilities and medical staff are rising worldwide. The agency noted a significant increase linked to the recent conflict in the Middle East.

stories.title: Fire Watch Services for Texas Businesses: Staying Compliant and Operational
stories.summary: The article discusses fire watch services and fire safety compliance requirements for businesses in Texas. It does not contain conflict or security news content.

stories.title: Trump, Putin talk Iran and Ukraine, US energy exports up: here’s what happened overnight
stories.summary: President Trump spoke with Russian President Putin about the wars in Ukraine and Iran, calling the conversation "very good." Trump said the US would reach a solution on Iran "relatively quickly" and discussed US energy exports.

stories.title: Occupiers want to 'nationalize' nearly 8,000 apartments in Luhansk
stories.summary: Russian occupation authorities in Luhansk declared nearly 8,000 apartments ownerless, making them subject to seizure through so-called nationalization. The move targets properties in the temporarily occupied Ukrainian city.

stories.title: Israeli troops seize aid vessels bound for Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli forces seized control of aid vessels bound for Gaza in Greek waters west of Crete, more than 1,000 kilometers from Israel's coast.

stories.title: London cops ID Golders Green terrorist as a UK national from Somalia, don’t name him
stories.summary: London police identified the Golders Green attacker as a UK national of Somali origin but did not release his name. Separately, a royal commission urged Australia to strengthen security at Jewish events following the Bondi mass terror shooting.

stories.title: Will top Hong Kong civil servants pay price for blunders under new system?
stories.summary: Hong Kong's government unveiled a new accountability system targeting department heads. Senior civil servants questioned where responsibility lies, citing the deadly Tai Po fire at Wang Fuk Court estate as an example of systemic failures.

stories.title: Geely joins Chery, BYD in profit slide as reduced incentives decimate China car sales
stories.summary: Chinese automakers Geely, Chery, and BYD all reported double-digit net profit declines in the first quarter of 2025 amid reduced domestic purchase incentives. Geely's net profit fell 27% year-on-year to 4.17 billion yuan.

stories.title: Navy begins intercepting Gaza flotilla hundreds of miles from the Strip
stories.summary: Israeli naval forces began intercepting the Gaza-bound flotilla near Crete, hundreds of miles from the Gaza Strip. Tracking data showed vessels were confronted by Israeli forces as they attempted to breach the naval blockade on Hamas-run Gaza.

stories.title: Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla approached by warships, activists claim
stories.summary: Activists aboard the Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla reported that warships approached their vessel. They said security personnel boarded the ship and ordered passengers to line up at the front.

stories.title: US charges Sinaloa governor and other Mexican officials with drug trafficking offences
stories.summary: The US Department of Justice indicted the governor of Sinaloa and nine other current and former Mexican officials for alleged ties to the Sinaloa cartel, accusing them of drug trafficking, weapons offences, and kidnapping. Some of the charged officials belong to Mexico's ruling Morena party, complicating President Claudia Sheinbaum's relations with the Trump administration.

stories.title: Amid furore on social media, Cambridge says 'aware' of reports about question paper leak
stories.summary: Cambridge International Education (CIE) acknowledged reports of a question paper leak affecting its June 2026 exam series, prompting widespread concern on social media. CIE said it is investigating the reports and will update exam centers as needed. The organization administers internationally recognized exams across more than 160 countries, including Pakistan.

stories.title: Oil spikes while stocks slip ahead of US Fed rate decision
stories.summary: Oil prices surged nearly six percent on Wednesday amid fears of an extended US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, after President Trump warned Iran to accept nuclear controls. US stock markets mostly declined as investors awaited a Federal Reserve interest rate decision and major tech earnings reports.

stories.title: US Navy to extend service life of amphibious assault ship USS Wasp by 5 years
stories.summary: The US Navy plans to extend the service life of the amphibious assault ship USS Wasp by five years. The decision follows a completed study of Wasp-class ships, with a separate review of amphibious dock landing ships currently underway.

stories.title: UK groups urge trade suspension over Israel death penalty law
stories.summary: Leading UK humanitarian and rights organizations called on the British government to suspend its trade agreement with Israel over a new Israeli death penalty law. The move was described as significant.

stories.title: Brics to push for intra-currency payments as ‘immunity’ against Western clout
stories.summary: BRICS nations are evaluating a digital payments framework proposed by India's central bank that would allow cross-border transactions in local currencies, aiming to reduce exposure to Western sanctions, tariffs, and US dollar volatility.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump urges Tehran to give up; Ghalibaf mocks US strategy
stories.summary: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf mocked the US economic pressure campaign as oil prices surged and the standoff in the Strait of Hormuz continued.

stories.title: Student’s alleged jailing in China over Australian pro-democracy protests sparks calls for inquiry
stories.summary: Australia's Human Rights Commissioner Lorraine Finlay called for scrutiny after reports that a Chinese student was jailed for six years by Chinese authorities for participating in pro-democracy protests in Sydney. Finlay said the case highlights growing risks of transnational repression affecting people in Australia, including international students.

stories.title: Russia losing influence in Trans-Caspian region, Ukraine’s intelligence reports
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence reports that Russia is losing influence in the Trans-Caspian region. Moscow is no longer viewed as a guarantor of stability in the area, according to the assessment.

stories.title: Congress confronts Hegseth for the first time since Iran war started
stories.summary: Democratic members of Congress confronted Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in his first congressional appearance since the start of the U.S. war with Iran. Lawmakers raised concerns about rising war costs, the depletion of critical U.S. munitions stockpiles, and a bombing that struck a school and killed children.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1526: Ukraine’s drone campaign reached major oil pipeline hub near Perm
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck a major oil pipeline hub near Perm, Russia, on day 1,526 of the Russo-Ukrainian war. Separately, the Kyiv Security Forum reached consensus that Russia poses an existential threat to Europe.

stories.title: World’s largest aircraft carrier to return to US after record deployment
stories.summary: The USS Gerald R. Ford, the world's largest aircraft carrier, will return to its home port in Virginia in mid-May after a record deployment exceeding 300 days. During the deployment, the carrier participated in operations related to the conflict with Iran and the capture of Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro.

stories.title: Hormuz shipping traffic remains at a trickle as US-Iran deadlock deepens
stories.summary: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has dropped to a trickle, with only about six vessels crossing in the past 24 hours compared to normal traffic levels, as US-Iran negotiations over reopening the critical waterway remain deadlocked.

stories.title: Israeli study finds plants absorb nutrients from airborne dust, challenging root-only theory
stories.summary: An Israeli study found that plants can absorb nutrients such as iron and phosphorus through their leaves from airborne dust. The findings challenge the long-held scientific understanding that plants depend solely on their roots and soil for mineral intake.

stories.title: Trump may cut US troops in Germany after Merz’s ‘humiliating’ Iran comment
stories.summary: President Trump announced the US is reviewing a possible reduction of troops in Germany, which numbered over 35,000 in 2024. The move followed a dispute with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who said the US was being humiliated by Iran.

stories.title: Florida approves US House map meant to boost Republicans in midterms
stories.summary: The Florida legislature approved a new congressional redistricting map designed to maximize Republican seats ahead of the midterm elections, just two days after Governor Ron DeSantis unveiled the proposal. The vote coincided with a US Supreme Court decision rolling back a key provision of the Voting Rights Act.

stories.title: Islamic State-linked insurgents leave Mali town as army tries to reassert control
stories.summary: Malian forces regained control of a town near the Niger border that Islamic State-linked insurgents had entered earlier in the week. Residents confirmed the military's return as it worked to reassert authority following coordinated attacks over the weekend.

stories.title: Elon Musk returns to witness stand in trial over OpenAI's future
stories.summary: Elon Musk returned to the witness stand in Oakland, California, on April 29 in his lawsuit against OpenAI. Musk alleges the company abandoned its original mission of responsibly developing AI for humanity in favor of pursuing profits.

stories.title: Ultra-Orthodox protests over draft law spread across Israel
stories.summary: Ultra-Orthodox Jews staged protests across multiple Israeli cities, including Jerusalem and Ashkelon, against military conscription laws. Police deployed stun grenades to disperse demonstrators in Jerusalem. The unrest intensified after recent arrests of yeshiva students accused of evading mandatory military service.

stories.title: Trump threatens to reduce troop numbers in Germany amid growing row with Nato allies
stories.summary: President Trump announced the US is reviewing a possible reduction of troops in Germany, posting the statement on Truth Social. The move follows remarks by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz suggesting that the Trump administration was being outplayed in its negotiations with Iran.

stories.title: Trump threatens US troop cuts in Germany
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said the United States is considering reducing its troop presence in Germany, days after German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said the US was being "humiliated" by Iran's leadership.

stories.title: Israeli military intercepts Gaza-bound aid vessel off Greek coast
stories.summary: Israeli military speedboats intercepted a Gaza-bound humanitarian vessel off the Greek coast. Activists on board the Global Sumud Flotilla reported that personnel aimed lasers and semi-automatic weapons at them and ordered passengers to their knees.

stories.title: US lawmakers warn China is top space rival as race to the moon intensifies
stories.summary: US lawmakers warned at a congressional hearing that China is America's most significant competitor in space as both nations race to land astronauts on the moon. China targets a crewed lunar landing by 2030, while the US pursues its Artemis programme.

stories.title: War update: 137 clashes on frontline, intense fighting in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: On April 29, Ukrainian and Russian forces clashed 137 times along the frontline, with the most intense fighting concentrated in the Pokrovsk sector. Russian forces attempted 31 attacks in that sector alone.

stories.title: U.S. war in Iran has cost $25 billion so far, says Pentagon official
stories.summary: A senior Pentagon official stated on April 29 that the U.S. war in Iran has cost approximately $25 billion to date. This represents the first official military cost estimate for the conflict provided by the Department of Defense.

stories.title: Putin backs Chechen leader’s bid for another term at Kremlin meeting
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov at the Kremlin and expressed support for Kadyrov's bid for another term as head of the Chechen Republic. The meeting was announced by the Kremlin.

stories.title: HKMA holds base interest rate at 4%, following Fed as war inflation worries persist
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority held its base interest rate at 4%, following the US Federal Reserve's decision to maintain rates at 3.5–3.75%. Analysts said inflationary pressures from the US-Israel war with Iran reduced the likelihood of a rate cut this year.

stories.title: Senior diplomat meets Russian envoy, spurns EU rep amid stolen Ukraine grain fight
stories.summary: A senior Israeli diplomat met with Russia's envoy while declining to meet an EU representative amid a dispute over stolen Ukrainian grain. Israel said social media posts from Kyiv were insufficient proof that Russian-seized grain was reaching Israel, while Ukraine worked with the EU on sanctions.

stories.title: Israeli maps outline expanded zone of military control in Gaza
stories.summary: Israel quietly released new maps of Gaza roughly a month ago that expand the military's restricted zone, placing thousands of displaced Palestinians within its boundaries. Israeli military officials indicated the boundaries of the controlled area remain subject to further changes.

stories.title: Europe air quality improves but falls short of 2030 targets, EEA warns
stories.summary: The European Environment Agency reported that air quality across Europe has improved but remains insufficient to meet the EU's 2030 pollution targets. Pollution levels still exceed limits at up to 20% of monitoring stations across 39 countries surveyed.

stories.title: Russia’s Senate speaker asks country’s richest man to ‘pull some offshore money back’ to Russia
stories.summary: Federation Council Speaker Valentina Matvienko publicly called on Alexei Mordashov, co-owner of Russian steelmaker Severstal and one of Russia's richest individuals, to repatriate money held in offshore accounts back to Russia.

stories.title: Putin Says Russia Seeks Deeper Economic Ties With Congo
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed interest in deepening economic ties with the Republic of the Congo. Russia is pursuing stronger relationships across Africa through trade, investment, and debt relief initiatives.

stories.title: Prosecutors release detailed description of how D4vd allegedly killed teen girl
stories.summary: Prosecutors filed a court document alleging that singer D4vd, legally named David Anthony Burke, fatally stabbed 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez to prevent her from revealing sexual abuse. According to the brief, Burke began a sexual relationship with the victim when she was 13 and he was 18.

stories.title: King Charles to visit New York to commemorate 9/11 victims
stories.summary: Britain's King Charles and Queen Camilla arrived in New York on April 29 to commemorate victims of the September 11, 2001, al Qaeda attacks. The visit is part of a four-day state visit to the United States.

stories.title: Putin, Trump discuss Iran war, Ukraine ceasefire in call
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump held a phone call discussing Iran's nuclear conflict and the war in Ukraine. Putin proposed ideas to resolve the Iran situation and suggested a temporary ceasefire in Ukraine timed to the anniversary of the end of World War II.

stories.title: Firing from across Afghan border injures 5 in KP's South Waziristan: security sources
stories.summary: Mortar shells fired from across the Afghan border struck homes in Angoor Adda village in South Waziristan Lower, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, on Wednesday, injuring four children and a woman. The injured were transported to the district headquarters hospital in Wana. Security sources attributed the shelling to Afghan Taliban and affiliated elements.

stories.title: Genome study reveals what happened after the Roman Empire fell
stories.summary: A genomic study analyzing remains from a Roman frontier site in southern Germany challenges the widely held narrative of a violent "barbarian invasion" following the fall of the Roman Empire, suggesting a more complex demographic transition.

stories.title: Strike on passenger bus in Russia’s Belgorod region kills 3, wounds 8
stories.summary: A strike on the village of Voznesenovka in the Shebekino district of Russia's Belgorod region killed three people and wounded eight on April 29. The attack targeted a passenger bus, according to preliminary reports.

stories.title: Zelensky: Middle strikes among Ukraine’s top priorities in coming months
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky identified so-called 'middle strikes' as one of the country's top military priorities in the coming months. He did not elaborate on specific targets or timelines.

stories.title: Israel just quadrupled its PR budget to $730M, experts claim it won’t work
stories.summary: Israel quadrupled its public diplomacy budget to $730 million. However, experts argue the increased spending is unlikely to reverse reputational damage caused by Israeli policy and the ongoing war in Gaza.

stories.title: In interview blitz, Bennett vows to fire politicized officials if elected PM
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett pledged to dismiss politicized officials if elected, citing concerns about the Israel Police. He also urged former IDF chief Gadi Eisenkot to join a political union and warned that ultra-Orthodox draft evasion was endangering soldiers.

stories.title: Russian emergency workers in Tuapse say they’ve extinguished the third fire at an oil refinery struck by Ukrainian drone debris
stories.summary: Russian emergency workers extinguished a fire at the Tuapse oil refinery caused by Ukrainian drone debris. It was the third fire at the facility, according to the Emergency Situations Ministry.

stories.title: Ukraine to go after Russia’s shadow grain fleet and its enablers – FM Sybiha
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha announced that Ukraine will target Russia's shadow grain fleet and entities enabling it across all geographic areas. The initiative aims to counter Russian grain exports circumventing sanctions.

stories.title: UN bloated, costly, but China fears should keep US involved, House committee told
stories.summary: Witnesses before a US House oversight committee argued that while the United Nations is bloated and costly, a full American withdrawal would allow China to expand its influence. The testimony came as the Trump administration's "America first" approach has significantly reduced US engagement with the UN over the past 18 months.

stories.title: Gaza-bound aid ship intercepted by Israeli forces
stories.summary: The Global Sumud Flotilla reported that Israeli military speedboats intercepted its humanitarian vessel attempting to break the Gaza blockade. Activists said personnel pointed lasers and weapons at them, and communications were jammed. Israeli Army Radio confirmed Israel had begun seizing Gaza-bound aid ships far from its shores.

stories.title: US pledges $128m towards restoring Chernobyl protection
stories.summary: The United States pledged $128 million toward restoring protective infrastructure at the Chernobyl nuclear site in Ukraine. The contribution is notable given the Trump administration's broader skepticism toward international aid commitments.

stories.title: Moscow says Putin proposed a Victory Day ceasefire to Trump, but Trump says the idea was his
stories.summary: A dispute emerged between Moscow and Washington over who proposed a Victory Day ceasefire. Putin's aide Yuri Ushakov said Putin suggested the ceasefire during a phone call with Trump, while Trump claimed the idea was his own.

stories.title: Mexico to require federal projects to use local steel in response to US tariffs
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum announced on April 29 a new rule requiring all federal construction projects to use domestically produced steel. The measure comes after negotiations to lift U.S. steel tariffs on Mexico failed to produce an agreement.

stories.title: Carney, ‘strong and resolute’ in first year, now has to deliver on promises
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has spent his first year in office refocusing Ottawa's foreign policy in response to President Trump's adversarial stance toward traditional allies. Carney now faces pressure to deliver on the policy commitments he has made.

stories.title: Russian forces must withdraw from Mali: Tuareg spokesman
stories.summary: A Tuareg rebel spokesman demanded that Russian forces withdraw from Mali following some of the largest rebel attacks in nearly 15 years. Rebels captured the key northern town of Kidal, and Malian Defence Minister Sadio Camara was killed during the fighting.

stories.title: Raise tax on alcohol and junk food to cut deaths from liver disease, experts say
stories.summary: A European expert report recommended that governments across Europe significantly raise taxes on alcohol and unhealthy food to address 284,000 annual deaths from liver disease. The authors urged that tax revenue should be sufficient to cover the associated costs to health services, criminal justice, and social services.

stories.title: Russia’s media regulator demands Apple and Google remove iStories app from their stores
stories.summary: Russia's media regulator Roskomnadzor demanded that Apple and Google remove the mobile app of iStories, an independent Russian investigative journalism outlet, from their app stores. iStories reported the demand itself.

stories.title: PACE suspends member of Russian opposition platform over defense of ‘honor killings’ in North Caucasus
stories.summary: The Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe suspended a member of the Russian opposition platform after the individual effectively defended 'honor killings' in the North Caucasus. PACE President Petra Bayr issued a statement confirming the suspension.

stories.title: US Supreme Court curbs race-based voting maps in landmark ruling
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court issued a ruling that raises the legal threshold for minorities seeking to challenge electoral district maps as racially discriminatory, effectively making it harder to bring race-based challenges to voting maps.

stories.title: US Supreme Court undermines key provision of Voting Rights Act
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court on April 29 raised the legal threshold for racial minorities to challenge electoral maps as discriminatory under the Voting Rights Act. The ruling favored Louisiana Republicans and the Trump administration.

stories.title: UK demands Iran stop posting 'sacrifice' calls on embassy sites
stories.summary: The UK Foreign Ministry and Middle East envoy Falconer demanded that Iran stop posting calls for "self-sacrifice" on its embassy websites. British officials described the posts as "unacceptable and inflammatory" amid the ongoing war.

stories.title: “Long-range sanctions”: Zelensky approves new operations against Russia
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky approved new Ukrainian operations designed to increase pressure on Russia and push it toward diplomatic engagement. Zelensky described the measures as 'long-range sanctions' against Russia.

stories.title: Lebanon President says Israel must fully implement truce as strikes continue
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun stated that Israel must fully implement the existing ceasefire before any further negotiations can proceed. He said ongoing Israeli attacks are incompatible with the truce agreement.

stories.title: Quarter of Americans, almost half of US youth, support Hamas over Israel, Harvard Harris poll finds
stories.summary: A Harvard Harris poll found that 74% of Americans support Israel over Hamas, but nearly half of young Americans polled back Hamas. The survey revealed significant generational divides in American views on the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Trump calls UAE exit from Opec ‘great’, says it could lower prices
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump praised the UAE's decision to leave OPEC, calling it "great" and predicting it could help lower oil and gasoline prices. He linked volatile energy markets to disruptions caused by the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Brown University shooter targeted symbolic victims tied to grievances, FBI says
stories.summary: The FBI released a behavioural assessment concluding that Brown University shooter Claudio Neves Valente, 48, a former Brown student, targeted victims symbolically tied to personal grievances. Investigators say he also killed an MIT professor, selecting institutions and individuals he associated with perceived failure and injustice.

stories.title: Trump warns Iran better 'get smart soon' and accept nuclear deal
stories.summary: President Trump warned Iran to "get smart soon" and accept a nuclear deal, as reports indicated he rejected Tehran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Officials told oil executives the US naval blockade of Iran could be extended for months.

stories.title: Iran FA leaves Canada before FIFA Congress over airport 'insult'
stories.summary: Iran's football federation left Canada before the FIFA Congress in Toronto, accusing immigration officials at the airport of inappropriate treatment. The delegation said the incident constituted an insult that prevented their attendance.

stories.title: The UAE’s exit from Opec could bring ‘even bigger trouble’: Chinese expert
stories.summary: A Chinese expert warned that the UAE's exit from OPEC could bring broader geopolitical consequences, reflecting a widening fracture within the Gulf Cooperation Council. The UAE, a member since 1971, announced its departure from both OPEC and the OPEC+ alliance effective Friday.

stories.title: Israel has begun intercepting Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla aid boats
stories.summary: Organisers of the Global Sumud Flotilla, a humanitarian aid mission bound for Gaza, reported that Israeli military speedboats intercepted their vessels as they attempted to break the naval blockade.

stories.title: Putin announces his readiness to declare ceasefire on May 9
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin told US President Donald Trump during a phone call that Russia is prepared to declare a ceasefire in Ukraine on May 9, the date Russia celebrates the Soviet Union's World War II victory.

stories.title: Israel intercepts Global Sumud boats, demands activists halt their mission
stories.summary: Israeli forces captured seven of 58 vessels belonging to the Global Sumud Flotilla near Crete. The flotilla was attempting to deliver humanitarian aid to Gaza, which remains under an Israeli naval blockade.

stories.title: Iran says US blockade not disrupting oil supply
stories.summary: Iran's Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad stated that the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, in place since April 13, has not disrupted the country's fuel supply or distribution. He said oil workers are operating around the clock, though concerns remain that Iran could run out of storage capacity.

stories.title: Families of Canadian mass shooting victims sue OpenAI, CEO Altman in US court
stories.summary: Families of victims of a February mass shooting in Canada that killed nine people, including several children, have filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman in a U.S. court.

stories.title: Russians attack Mykolaiv and region with drones, casualties reported
stories.summary: Five people were injured in the Mykolaiv region of Ukraine following a Russian attack using Shahed-type drones targeting the city and surrounding area.

stories.title: Where Is Iran’s Enriched Uranium?
stories.summary: The U.N. nuclear watchdog, the IAEA, suspects that approximately half of Iran's enriched uranium stockpile remains stored at its Isfahan facility. The location of Iran's nuclear material is a key concern amid ongoing tensions.

stories.title: ‘Resign Immediately’: Democrats Grill Hegseth on Iran War
stories.summary: Congressional Democrats publicly confronted U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth during a rare hearing, pressing him on the war with Iran and military spending. Some Democratic lawmakers called for his resignation during the contentious exchange.

stories.title: 2 Jewish men stabbed in 'terrorist' attack in London
stories.summary: Two Jewish men, aged 76 and 34, were stabbed in Golders Green, north London, in an attack declared a terrorist incident by Metropolitan Police. A 45-year-old suspect was arrested at the scene. UK King Charles III, Prime Minister Keir Starmer, and London Mayor Sadiq Khan condemned the attack.

stories.title: Trump: Iranian naval blockade stays until Tehran agrees to nuclear deal - Axios
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that the naval blockade on Iran will remain in place until Tehran agrees to a nuclear deal. CENTCOM is reportedly preparing for potential military strikes if diplomatic negotiations fail.

stories.title: EU chief says Kremlin imposing 'digital Iron Curtain' on Russians
stories.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen accused the Kremlin of imposing a "digital Iron Curtain" on the Russian population. She also noted that rising inflation and skyrocketing interest rates in Russia are forcing citizens to bear the economic costs of Moscow's war.

stories.title: From Japan to India, overtourism cries out for new success metrics
stories.summary: An analysis argues that traditional tourism success metrics focused on arrivals and revenue are insufficient. It calls for new measurements that account for the well-being of local communities and workers in destinations across Asia facing overtourism pressures.

stories.title: Mali turmoil threatens Russian push for influence and mineral wealth in Africa
stories.summary: A series of military setbacks for Mali's Moscow-backed military government has undermined Russia's role as a self-proclaimed security guarantor in Africa. The turmoil threatens Russia's broader strategic and economic interests on the continent, including access to mineral resources.

stories.title: Great excitement as first orangutan is born at Jerusalem Biblical Zoo
stories.summary: Jerusalem Biblical Zoo celebrated the birth of its first orangutan, named Cayaha, meaning "light" in Indonesian. The birth is part of a European zoo breeding programme for the critically endangered species.

stories.title: Ukraine asks Israel to seize vessel it says is carrying grain stolen by Russia
stories.summary: Ukraine asked Israel to seize a vessel it says is carrying grain stolen from Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory. Ukraine's top prosecutor made the request on April 29, amid a diplomatic dispute between the two countries over the shipment.

stories.title: Report: Russian general accused of Bucha killings survives assassination attempt
stories.summary: An assassination attempt targeted Russian Major General Azatbek Omurbekov, who has been accused of involvement in the Bucha killings, at a military garrison in Khabarovsk Krai. An explosive device planted in a mailbox detonated on April 28, killing one person and wounding several others.

stories.title: Trump says Iran is 'choking like a stuffed pig', as he mulls extending blockade
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump appeared to reject an Iranian proposal to end the war that would have deferred nuclear program talks. Trump described Iran as 'choking like a stuffed pig' and said he is considering extending the naval blockade.

stories.title: Russia scales down WW2 victory parade due to Ukrainian threat
stories.summary: Russia announced it will scale down its annual May 9 World War II victory parade on Red Square, excluding military hardware this year. The Kremlin cited the threat of Ukrainian retaliatory strikes as the reason, more than four years into the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: China to ban drone sales in capital over security fears
stories.summary: Beijing authorities announced new regulations banning the sale of drones and prohibiting unmanned aerial vehicles and their core components from being brought into the Chinese capital, citing public security concerns.

stories.title: Kyiv region installing additional 150 MW of distributed gas generation, regional chief says
stories.summary: The Kyiv region currently operates 81 distributed gas generation units with a combined capacity of 103 megawatts, with an additional 150 MW of capacity being installed to bolster the area's energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Iran officials skip FIFA congress after airport incident in Canada
stories.summary: Iranian football federation officials left Canada without attending the FIFA congress after what state media called 'inappropriate behaviour' by immigration officials at Toronto airport. Three officials who arrived with valid visas reportedly flew back to Türkiye on the next available flight.

stories.title: Knesset panel advances measure lowering bar to compensate workers furloughed by Iran war
stories.summary: An Israeli Knesset panel advanced legislation to shorten the qualifying period for unpaid-leave compensation from 10 days to five for workers furloughed due to the Iran war. The measure followed pressure from business groups.

stories.title: Over 1.2 million people in Lebanon to face acute hunger due to war: Report
stories.summary: A new report warns that over 1.2 million people in Lebanon are expected to face acute hunger due to the ongoing war. Nearly one in four of the population analysed are projected to experience food insecurity.

stories.title: Ukraine presses Israel on grain shipment as 'Twitter diplomacy' accusations fly
stories.summary: Ukraine and Israel clashed over a disputed grain shipment, with Ukrainian officials accusing Israel of engaging in "Twitter diplomacy" and failing to respond to legal requests regarding the vessel.

stories.title: Italy's Fincantieri and KAYO to work together on strengthening Albania's navy
stories.summary: Italian shipbuilder Fincantieri and Albania's KAYO have established a joint venture to build and maintain naval vessels in Albania. The partnership aims to modernise Albania's military infrastructure and deepen the country's ties with NATO.

stories.title: India Rethinks Energy Security Amid War
stories.summary: India is reassessing its energy security strategy amid the ongoing conflict disrupting global energy markets. Diplomatic discussions in Abu Dhabi have signaled potential expansion of green energy cooperation between India and the UAE.

stories.title: Golders Green attack claim highlights rise of shadowy Iran-linked group
stories.summary: An Iran-linked group called Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamia (HAYI) claimed responsibility for a knife attack on two British Jewish men in Golders Green, north London. UK counter-terror police are investigating the stabbing as a terrorism case, though analysts suggest the claim may be opportunistic rather than directly state-backed.

stories.title: Merz says relations with Trump are good despite spat over Iran
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated that his personal relationship with US President Trump remains good despite disagreements over the US approach to Iran, saying he had expressed doubts about the military campaign from the start.

stories.title: Syria arrests former Assad-era general accused of 2013 chemical attack involvement
stories.summary: Syria's Interior Ministry arrested former Assad-era general Adnan Abboud Hilweh, accusing him of involvement in the 2013 sarin nerve gas attack on the Damascus suburb of Ghouta that killed over 1,000 people.

stories.title: Assad regime trials are 'integral for Syria to move on' from civil war, atrocities
stories.summary: A Syrian court held its first hearing in the trial of ousted president Bashar al-Assad and senior regime figures, with one defendant appearing in person. The International Crisis Group described the transitional justice process as essential for Syria to move beyond its civil war and past atrocities, despite most defendants being tried in absentia.

stories.title: Putin, Trump Discuss Iran, Ukraine in Phone Call, Kremlin Aide Says
stories.summary: During a phone call between Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump, the two leaders discussed Iran and Ukraine. Putin proposed a ceasefire in Ukraine on May 9, coinciding with Russia's Victory Day celebrations.

stories.title: Russian disinformation network Storm-1516 is flooding the West with fake stories, and JD Vance repeated one of them
stories.summary: A Russian disinformation network called Storm-1516, believed to include former employees of Yevgeny Prigozhin's troll factory and linked to the GRU, has been spreading fabricated stories across Western countries since 2023. The network has been accused of election interference in the US, Germany, and Hungary. US Vice President JD Vance reportedly repeated one of its fake stories.

stories.title: Palestine Action ban is risk to free speech, watchdog says, as UK gov’t appeals to bar group
stories.summary: A UK free-speech watchdog warned that the British government's ban on Palestine Action poses risks to freedom of expression. The government argued that criminal measures alone would have been insufficient, while lawyers for the group contended the ban was disproportionate.

stories.title: Trump says Iran ‘has to say we give up’ to reach deal
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that Iran must fully concede to reach an agreement with Washington, saying Iran 'has to cry uncle.' He insisted there would be no deal without Iran agreeing to abandon nuclear weapons and described the US port blockade as 'genius' and 'foolproof.'

stories.title: IDF Chief Zamir says current soldiers are greatest generation since War of Independence
stories.summary: IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir praised current Israeli soldiers as the greatest generation since the War of Independence. He also pledged to eliminate security threats facing northern Israel.

stories.title: Haviv Rettig Gur: Political footballs and politicians’ fumbles
stories.summary: Times of Israel senior analyst Haviv Rettig Gur discussed Israeli election-year developments, including the announcement of a joint party by two former prime ministers. He also highlighted widening societal divisions in Israel.

stories.title: Trump: Putin offered to help settle Iranian nuclear enrichment impasse
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated that Russian President Vladimir Putin expressed a desire to be involved in resolving the dispute over Iran's nuclear enrichment programme.

stories.title: Australia news live: Penny Wong wins jet fuel pledge from China in Beijing visit; US lawmaker says Aukus price might go up
stories.summary: Australian Foreign Affairs Minister Penny Wong secured a commitment from China during a Beijing visit to facilitate jet fuel exports to address supply disruptions. Separately, a U.S. lawmaker suggested the cost of the AUKUS defense pact could increase beyond the current $3 billion benchmark.

stories.title: Why is the UAE quitting OPEC – and what’s the impact?
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced its departure from OPEC amid what has been described as the worst global energy crisis in modern times. The decision could have significant implications for oil markets and Gulf cooperation.

stories.title: 'Uncertainty but a lot of resilience' in Latin America, says IDB head
stories.summary: Inter-American Development Bank President Ilan Goldfajn said the Iran war's energy shock has increased economic uncertainty in Latin America but highlighted the region's resilience. He noted countries are seeking targeted support for energy diversification and fertilizer needs. Separately, Jerome Powell held his final press conference as Federal Reserve Chair ahead of Kevin Warsh's expected confirmation.

stories.title: Don’t call it a ‘quagmire’: defense secretary refuses to speculate on length of Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary declined to characterize the Iran conflict as a "quagmire" and refused to speculate on its duration. The remarks come as a 60-day deadline under the War Powers Act approaches on Thursday, raising questions about congressional authorization for the ongoing military operation.

stories.title: Colombia hosts climate talks in bid to lead global transition away from fossil fuels
stories.summary: Colombian President Gustavo Petro pledged to transition the country's economy away from oil and coal after his 2022 election. As Colombia hosts international climate talks, the plan remains largely unfulfilled ahead of a May 31 presidential election first round, with the country still dependent on fossil-fuel production.

stories.title: After rejecting Iran’s proposal to open Hormuz, Trump says talks ongoing over the phone
stories.summary: US President Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz but said phone talks with Iran are ongoing. Trump described Iran as 'choking like a stuffed pig,' while Iran's parliament speaker accused him of trying to make Iran 'collapse from within.' Defense Secretary Hegseth noted the war has cost $25 billion.

stories.title: Iranian football officials leave Canada before FIFA Congress due to airport 'insult'
stories.summary: A delegation of Iranian football officials departed Canada before the FIFA Congress began, citing what they called inappropriate treatment by immigration officials at Toronto's airport. The head of Iran's football federation is a former member of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, which Canada has designated a terrorist organization.

stories.title: South Africa: Crowds protest against illegal immigration
stories.summary: Large crowds protested in Johannesburg, South Africa, against high levels of illegal immigration. The demonstrations reflect growing tensions between local South Africans and foreign nationals in the country.

stories.title: Nigerian troops kill 18 militants in northeast operations, military says
stories.summary: Nigerian troops killed at least 18 Islamist militants and destroyed several insurgent enclaves during coordinated operations across Borno state in the northeast. The military said the operations are part of intensified pressure on Islamist groups in the region.

stories.title: Iran accuses Bahrain of rights violations over citizenship revocations
stories.summary: Iran accused Bahrain of violating the rights of 69 individuals whose citizenship was revoked over alleged support for Iranian attacks. Bahrain's interior ministry said the individuals were stripped of nationality for colluding with foreign entities. Iranian spokesperson Esmail Baghaei called the move discriminatory.

stories.title: What’s behind Israel’s plan to move the Bnei Menashe?
stories.summary: A new wave of members of the Bnei Menashe community from Northeast India has arrived in Israel under a 2026 government immigration plan. The programme involves relocating the community, which claims ancient Israelite descent.

stories.title: Tuareg rebels vow Mali junta will fall
stories.summary: Tuareg separatist rebels in Mali declared that the ruling military junta will fall, one day after the junta's leader said the security situation was under control. Separately, the Democratic Republic of Congo announced plans to deploy troops to protect its mining operations.

stories.title: Russian attacks in Dnipropetrovsk region kill two, wound one
stories.summary: Two people were killed and one was injured in the Dnipropetrovsk region of Ukraine as a result of Russian attacks on the area.

stories.title: Where Is Pakistan Again?
stories.summary: The World Bank has reclassified Pakistan from its South Asia grouping to its Middle East and North Africa regional column. The administrative change has drawn attention as potentially carrying broader geopolitical and institutional implications beyond a routine bureaucratic adjustment.

stories.title: King Charles commemorates 9/11 victims in New York visit
stories.summary: Britain's King Charles and Queen Camilla visited the 9/11 memorial in lower Manhattan, New York, laying a floral bouquet at the site of the former World Trade Center. The visit occurred amid tensions between the UK and US, with President Trump criticizing Prime Minister Starmer.

stories.title: Ukraine asks Israel to seize ship carrying grain ‘stolen’ by Russia
stories.summary: Ukraine formally requested that Israel seize a vessel allegedly carrying grain stolen by Russia. Kyiv asked Israeli authorities to take grain samples from the cargo and question the ship's crew members.

stories.title: PMDC directs institutions to implement mental health screening protocols amid uptick in suicide cases
stories.summary: Pakistan's Medical and Dental Council directed all medical and dental institutions to implement structured mental health screening protocols for students, citing growing concerns over increasing suicide incidents and psychological distress among medical students.

stories.title: Mali’s Tuareg rebels say Russian fighters must withdraw from country
stories.summary: Tuareg rebel forces in Mali have demanded the withdrawal of Russian fighters from the country. A rebel spokesperson predicted that Mali's military government, which is struggling to reassert control, would fall 'sooner or later.'

stories.title: Palestine football appeals Fifa decision to do nothing about Israeli clubs in illegal settlements
stories.summary: The Palestinian Football Association appealed FIFA's decision not to take action against Israeli football clubs operating in illegal settlements. The PFA said it felt compelled to act in what it described as an 'unjust' situation.

stories.title: Israeli maps outline expanded zone of military control in Gaza
stories.summary: Israel quietly released new maps of Gaza approximately one month ago that expand the military's restricted zone, placing thousands of displaced Palestinians within areas subject to ongoing operational control. The Israeli military indicated the boundaries of these zones can continue to change.

stories.title: Ultra-Orthodox protests over draft law spread across Israel
stories.summary: Ultra-Orthodox Jews staged protests across Israel against military conscription laws, with police using stun grenades to disperse demonstrations in Jerusalem. Protests also erupted in Ashkelon following the arrest of yeshiva students accused of draft evasion. Courts have pushed for mandatory service enforcement.

stories.title: IDF chief says there’s ‘no ceasefire’ in south Lebanon amid continued fighting with Hezbollah
stories.summary: Israel's IDF chief stated there is 'no ceasefire' in south Lebanon as fighting with Hezbollah continues. Trump is reportedly pushing back on Israeli efforts to limit negotiations with Beirut. A monitor warned that one million Lebanese face food insecurity in the coming months.

stories.title: Russia says it's scaling down WW2 victory parade due to Ukrainian threat
stories.summary: Russia announced it will hold a scaled-down version of its annual World War II victory parade, omitting the traditional display of military weaponry. The Kremlin cited an increased threat of Ukrainian attacks as the reason for the reduced celebration.

stories.title: Syria trial seen as first step on long road for Assad's victims
stories.summary: Former Syrian regime official Atef Najib appeared before a court in Damascus in an emotionally charged hearing. The trial is considered a landmark first step toward accountability for victims of the Assad government.

stories.title: Bennett unveils ‘Israeli Renaissance’ plan, says alliance will replace Netanyahu - exclusive
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett unveiled his "Israeli Renaissance" plan in an interview, proposing to bring one million new immigrants to Israel over the next decade. He described the initiative as an alternative political alliance to replace the current Netanyahu-led government.

stories.title: Trump says he discussed a Ukraine ceasefire with Putin
stories.summary: President Trump said he discussed a possible ceasefire in Ukraine during a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday. Trump described suggesting "a little bit of a ceasefire" to the Russian leader.

stories.title: Lebanese soldier and brother killed in Israeli strike, Lebanon army says
stories.summary: A Lebanese soldier and his brother were killed in an Israeli airstrike in Bint Jbeil in southern Lebanon on April 29, according to the Lebanese army.

stories.title: Russian drones injure seven people in Kherson in one day, including two hospital workers
stories.summary: Seven residents of Kherson, Ukraine, were injured in a single day by Russian drone strikes, including two hospital workers. All casualties in the regional capital resulted from enemy drone attacks.

stories.title: Trump and Putin discuss Iran war and float temporary Ukraine ceasefire in call
stories.summary: Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump held a phone call lasting over 90 minutes in which they discussed the war in Iran and a possible temporary ceasefire in Ukraine. Putin's foreign policy adviser Yuri Ushakov said Moscow viewed a potential U.S. ground operation in Iran as dangerous, while Russia welcomed an extended ceasefire in the region.

stories.title: Defense Minister: Counterterrorism law allows seizure of Gaza flotilla's property
stories.summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz invoked Section 56(b) of the Counterterrorism Law to justify the seizure of property linked to the Global Sumud Flotilla as it set sail for Gaza. Katz said the law permits confiscation of assets connected to terrorist activities.

stories.title: US lawmaker presses Hegseth over deaths of soldiers in Iran drone attack
stories.summary: Democratic Representative Pat Ryan confronted US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth over the deaths of six American soldiers killed in a drone attack on a base in Kuwait. Ryan cited survivors who said they were unprepared and called on Hegseth to resign. Hegseth said measures had been taken to protect forces.

stories.title: Space Force awards first contracts for satellite threat warning radar payloads
stories.summary: The U.S. Space Force awarded its first contracts for satellite-based threat warning radar payloads through the Space Rapid Capabilities Office. The office is already planning a follow-on effort to develop smaller threat warning sensors for deployment across a broader fleet of Space Force satellites.

stories.title: Law ministry notifies transfer of 3 IHC judges to other high courts
stories.summary: Pakistan's Ministry of Law and Justice notified the transfer of three Islamabad High Court judges to other high courts under Article 200 of the Constitution, following approval by the Judicial Commission of Pakistan. Lawyers' bodies criticized the move for lacking transparency.

stories.title: Erdogan rejects criticism of Turkey's peace efforts with Kurdish militants
stories.summary: Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan said the peace process aimed at ending Turkey's decades-long conflict with Kurdish militants is progressing in a "positive atmosphere." His remarks came after criticism from pro-Kurdish lawmakers regarding the government's approach to negotiations.

stories.title: What are the sticking points for the EU's new budget?
stories.summary: Negotiations over the EU's next long-term budget have begun, with EU institutions seeking significantly increased funding. The 27 member states will ultimately decide the final allocations, and multiple sticking points remain unresolved.

stories.title: Slovakia's Supreme Court upholds 21-year sentence for PM Fico's attacker
stories.summary: Slovakia's Supreme Court upheld a 21-year prison sentence for the man who shot at Prime Minister Robert Fico two years ago. The court rejected the attacker's appeal against terrorism charges.

stories.title: US lawmakers question Pete Hegseth over budget for war on Iran
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth testified before Congress regarding the Pentagon's budget for the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran. Lawmakers questioned Hegseth on spending priorities related to the conflict.

stories.title: Pentagon chief Hegseth first public hearing on Iran war: Key takeaways
stories.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth testified alongside General Dan Caine in his first public congressional hearing on the Iran war. The Pentagon stated the conflict has cost approximately $25 billion so far.

stories.title: Mali faces 'very high risk' of new coup d'état, analyst says, amid jihadist insurgence
stories.summary: Analyst Michael Shurkin of 14 North Strategies told FRANCE 24 that Mali faces a very high risk of another coup d'état. He said the jihadist group JNIM and the Tuareg rebel movement FLA clearly hold the initiative, while the Malian military government is on the defensive.

stories.title: Shomrim volunteer who helped subdue London attacker: 'I wanted to protect community' - interview
stories.summary: Shomrim volunteer Yonaton El-Kouby helped subdue the attacker in the London stabbing incident. In an interview, El-Kouby said he acted to protect his community and expressed pride in being able to contribute to its safety.

stories.title: Powell says he’ll stay at Fed after chair term ends, citing attacks by Trump team
stories.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell announced he will remain on the Fed's board after his term as chair ends next month. Powell cited 'unprecedented' legal attacks by the Trump administration against the central bank. The Fed kept its benchmark interest rate steady.

stories.title: Two Jewish men stabbed in London, Israeli president calls for urgent action
stories.summary: Two Jewish men were stabbed in London by an attacker who was seen running with a knife and targeting Jewish members of the public. Israeli President Isaac Herzog called for urgent action in response to the attack.

stories.title: Two Jewish men stabbed in London ‘terrorist attack’
stories.summary: Two Jewish men were stabbed in north London in what authorities are treating as a terrorist attack. A man armed with a knife was seen running through the area before the stabbing occurred.

stories.title: Hegseth says deadly Iran school strike still under investigation
stories.summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth stated that a strike on an Iranian girls' school that killed approximately 170 people, mostly children, remains under investigation. Preliminary US findings suggest the strike may have resulted from outdated intelligence used by the military.

stories.title: Lebanon: Over 1 million expected to face acute food insecurity
stories.summary: Over one million people in Lebanon are expected to face acute food insecurity as Israeli military operations have severely impacted farming and agricultural infrastructure across the country.

stories.title: ‘No longer a trustworthy humanitarian organization’: NGO Monitor releases report on MSF’s failings
stories.summary: NGO Monitor released a report accusing Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) of abandoning neutrality in its coverage of Gaza, alleging the organization favored Hamas narratives while downplaying the group's actions. The report called MSF no longer a trustworthy humanitarian organization.

stories.title: Syniehubov: Russians probing new directions for offensive in Kharkiv region
stories.summary: Kharkiv Oblast Governor Oleh Syniehubov reported that Russian troops are probing new directions for potential offensives in the Kharkiv region. Ukrainian forces said they remain in control of the situation and are repelling the attacks.

stories.title: Indonesian soldiers on trial after acid attack on activist
stories.summary: Four Indonesian soldiers are standing trial in Jakarta for carrying out an acid attack on a prominent activist. The case has drawn attention to allegations of military violence against civilians in Indonesia.

stories.title: Germany’s Merz says relations with Trump are good despite spat over Iran
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said relations with U.S. President Donald Trump remain good despite disagreements over Iran policy. Trump had previously criticised NATO allies for not deploying their navies to help open the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Iran war has cost $25 billion so far, Pentagon official says
stories.summary: Acting Pentagon comptroller Jules Hurst III told the House Armed Services Committee that the U.S. war in Iran has cost approximately $25 billion to date. He said the majority of that spending has gone toward ordnance and munitions.

stories.title: Three men on trial accused of arson attacks linked to UK PM Starmer
stories.summary: Three men with links to Ukraine are on trial in London, accused of carrying out arson attacks on property connected to British Prime Minister Keir Starmer. Prosecutors allege the attacks were carried out on behalf of an unidentified figure known as 'El Money.'

stories.title: Jewish man in Rome arrested for allegedly shooting left-wing protesters with airgun
stories.summary: A Jewish man in Rome was arrested for allegedly shooting left-wing protesters with an airgun. Italian media reported the suspect confessed to the act. The incident occurred amid rising tensions during celebrations related to Israel and has been widely condemned by Jewish leaders.

stories.title: Iran's security council unified on war decisions, minister says
stories.summary: Iranian Justice Minister Amin Rahimi said all state institutions are unified behind the Supreme National Security Council on decisions related to war and negotiations. He stated that the council sets policy based on national interests, with final approval from the supreme leader.

stories.title: Palestine Action ban disproportionately impacts Palestinians in UK, court hears
stories.summary: A UK court heard arguments that the Home Office's ban on the Palestine Action group disproportionately affects Palestinians living in Britain. The Home Office defended the ban as necessary for national security, while lawyers warned it threatens civil liberties. Protests against the ban have taken place in Trafalgar Square, London.

stories.title: CCTV footage shows moment Israeli strike targets Palestinians
stories.summary: CCTV footage captured the moment an Israeli airstrike struck a group of Palestinians in Gaza City on Friday. Surveillance cameras in the area recorded the impact of the strike.

stories.title: Greece says it agreed with Qatar to deepen trade, energy and defence ties
stories.summary: Greece announced on April 29 that it had reached an agreement with Qatar to deepen cooperation in trade, energy, and defense. The deal extends a partnership first established in 2024.

stories.title: Minister calls for national consensus on ensuring water security
stories.summary: Pakistan's Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal called for national consensus on water security at a Water Security Task Force session in Islamabad, citing concerns over India's alleged "weaponisation" of water and advocating for strategic water storage infrastructure.

stories.title: Trump vows to maintain Iran blockade, Tehran threatens ‘practical’ action
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump vowed to maintain the naval blockade of Iranian ports, calling it 'more effective than the bombing.' Tehran threatened 'practical' action in response as global oil prices surged.

stories.title: CinC Syrskyi: “Small-group” air defense units downed over 2,100 Russian attack drones in April
stories.summary: Ukraine's Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi reported that small-group air defence units destroyed more than 2,100 Russian attack drones during April. The decentralised defence approach has become a key element of Ukraine's counter-drone strategy.

stories.title: Armenia's FM hails peace, embraces future: EU, elections, trade, 'huge' infrastructure projects
stories.summary: Armenian Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan, speaking from Armenia's new embassy in Paris ahead of an EU-Armenia summit, declared that peace between Armenia and Azerbaijan is becoming a reality. He outlined plans to institutionalize the peace and discussed elections, trade, and large-scale infrastructure projects.

stories.title: Viral LEGO-style AI videos blur line between entertainment and propaganda
stories.summary: AI-generated videos in a LEGO-style format satirizing U.S. President Donald Trump's war in Iran have gone viral, accumulating millions of views on social media. A FRANCE 24 correspondent in Tehran interviewed the content creator behind the videos, which raise questions about the boundary between entertainment and propaganda.

stories.title: Haredi yeshivas with draft dodgers will no longer receive tax-exempt donations, AG says
stories.summary: Israel's Attorney General Baharav-Miara ruled that Haredi yeshivas enrolling military draft dodgers will no longer be eligible for tax-exempt donations. She determined that the tax exemption indirectly finances draft evasion, though she noted that implementation will take time.

stories.title: Pentagon leaders place $25 billon price tag on Operation Epic Fury
stories.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told the House Armed Services Committee that Operation Epic Fury, the U.S. military campaign against Iran, has cost an estimated $25 billion. Committee members also questioned Hegseth about the recent dismissals of senior Army and Navy leaders.

stories.title: Trump says he had ‘good talk’ with Putin on Iran and Ukraine
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump spoke by phone for over 90 minutes on Wednesday, discussing the Middle East conflict and the war in Ukraine. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov described the call as frank and businesslike. Trump told reporters it was a good conversation.

stories.title: UK’s ‘terrorism’ laws risk overreach, watchdog warns
stories.summary: A UK watchdog has cautioned that the country's counterterrorism laws risk being applied too broadly against activist groups, raising concerns about potential overreach in how such legislation targets non-violent organizations.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF destroys Hezbollah rocket launcher inside civilian building in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli Defence Forces released footage showing the destruction of a Hezbollah rocket launcher concealed inside a civilian building in southern Lebanon. Separately, an IDF drone struck a Hezbollah operative attempting to flee on a motorcycle.

stories.title: World Bank warns of 16% rise in commodity pricing over Hormuz closure
stories.summary: The World Bank warned that the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz could drive commodity prices up by 16 percent. The institution forecast a 24 percent rise in energy prices in 2026, driven by the Iran conflict and disruptions to global shipping routes.

stories.title: Marines to field light loitering munition to operational units in ‘June timeframe’: Official
stories.summary: The U.S. Marine Corps plans to field a light loitering munition, designated OFP-L, to operational units by June. Systems from three manufacturers are currently being tested by units at Dugway Proving Grounds outside Salt Lake City, Utah.

stories.title: Russia to remain in OPEC+, hopes UAE exit does not spell end of group
stories.summary: Russia confirmed it will remain a member of OPEC+ following the UAE's departure from the group. Russia is the second-largest oil producer in the alliance.

stories.title: EU’s new carbon tariff could cost Ukraine $6 billion in GDP and tens of thousands of industrial jobs through 2030
stories.summary: The European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) could cost Ukraine up to $6 billion in GDP and tens of thousands of industrial jobs by 2030, creating serious structural risks for the country's war-damaged economy.

stories.title: IHC to hear Imran, Bushra's pleas against conviction in £190m corruption reference on April 30
stories.summary: The Islamabad High Court scheduled hearings for April 30 on appeals filed by former Prime Minister Imran Khan and his spouse Bushra Bibi against their convictions in the £190 million corruption reference.

stories.title: Zelenskiy says Ukraine will continue extending range of strikes on Russia
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy announced that Ukraine will continue extending the range of its strikes into Russian territory. He posted footage of what he described as an attack on a target more than 1,500 kilometres from Ukraine.

stories.title: Putin, in call with Trump, put forward ideas on Iran, Kremlin says
stories.summary: During a phone call on Wednesday, Russian President Vladimir Putin proposed ideas to U.S. President Donald Trump on resolving the conflict over Iran's nuclear program. Putin also suggested a temporary ceasefire in Ukraine to coincide with the anniversary of the end of World War Two in May.

stories.title: Kuwait revokes journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin's citizenship
stories.summary: Kuwaiti-American journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin was arrested and had his Kuwaiti citizenship revoked after sharing images related to the Iran war. His lawyers said he was punished for doing his job. Shihab-Eldin had spent several weeks in jail in Kuwait.

stories.title: Haredi anti-draft protesters block entrance to Jerusalem, are dispersed after 2 hours
stories.summary: Hundreds of ultra-Orthodox protesters affiliated with the extremist Jerusalem Faction blocked the entrance to Jerusalem for about two hours in opposition to the arrest of military draft evaders. Police dispersed the demonstrators. The protest came a day after faction members breached the home of an IDF officer.

stories.title: Drones strike two helicopters in Russia’s Voronezh region
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces carried out drone strikes in Russia's Voronezh region, hitting two Russian military helicopters—a Mi-28 attack helicopter and a Mi-17 transport helicopter.

stories.title: WATCH: Israel promotes Lebanon peace message in Times Square amid ceasefire talks
stories.summary: Israel promoted a peace message on Lebanon in New York's Times Square amid ongoing ceasefire talks. Israeli Consul General Ofir Akunis called for the destruction of Hezbollah, describing it as an Iranian proxy responsible for Lebanon's devastation.

stories.title: Ukraine needs to build its own high-speed Mesh tech, as China is Russia’s supplier, and Western modems are too expensive
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense experts say the country urgently needs to develop its own high-speed mesh communication technology for controlling UAVs at distances of 300–400 kilometers. China currently supplies such technology to Russia, while Western modems remain prohibitively expensive for Ukraine.

stories.title: Trump urges Iran to sign a deal after report suggests US may extend blockade
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump urged Iran to agree to a deal amid reports that he had instructed aides to prepare for an extended blockade of Iranian ports.

stories.title: Trump’s War Is Damaging U.S. Arms Exports to Allies
stories.summary: U.S. arms export deals with allies are reportedly being canceled as American military stockpiles run short due to the ongoing war with Iran. The drawdown of munitions is affecting Washington's ability to fulfill defense commitments to partner nations.

stories.title: Tuareg rebels urge Russian forces to leave Mali
stories.summary: A spokesman for Tuareg rebels in Mali called on Russian forces to withdraw from the country, stating that the ruling military junta will eventually fall. The demand follows a series of attacks by Islamist insurgents and separatist groups that have further destabilized the West African nation.

stories.title: Hundreds of Dogs Perish in Nizhny Novgorod Fire
stories.summary: A fire broke out in an outbuilding in Nizhny Novgorod, Russia, killing hundreds of dogs that were kept inside. Russia's Emergency Situations Ministry confirmed the incident.

stories.title: Supreme Court examines Trump's move against Haitian and Syrian immigrants
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court is examining the Trump administration's efforts to strip humanitarian protections from hundreds of thousands of Haitian and Syrian immigrants. The case is part of President Trump's broader immigration crackdown.

stories.title: Pakistan in the middle: What benefits and risks from US-Iran mediator?
stories.summary: Pakistan is navigating risks and benefits as a mediator between the United States and Iran. The United Arab Emirates has demanded immediate repayment of a $3.5 billion loan from Pakistan, while also signaling its departure from OPEC, adding pressure on regional dynamics involving Saudi Arabia and Israel.

stories.title: Teenage bullying increases in Ukrainian schools
stories.summary: Reports indicate that teenage bullying is increasing in Ukrainian schools. Experts attribute the rise to war-related trauma and chronic stress experienced by young people amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: IHC to hear Imran, Bushra's pleas against conviction in £190m reference on April 30
stories.summary: The Islamabad High Court has scheduled hearings for April 30 on appeals filed by former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan and his wife Bushra Bibi against their convictions in the £190 million corruption reference.

stories.title: Ukraine should not advertise its new ballistic missiles until factories can mass-produce them, ex-security officer says
stories.summary: A former Ukrainian security officer advised that Ukraine should not publicly advertise its new ballistic missiles until factories can mass-produce them. Ivan Stupak compared premature announcements to Russia's experience with its troubled Armata tank program.

stories.title: Trump reportedly rejects Iran proposal, says US blockade will continue
stories.summary: President Donald Trump reportedly rejected Iran's peace proposal, which sought to end hostilities and reopen the Strait of Hormuz while deferring nuclear talks. Trump indicated the US naval blockade of Iranian ports would continue until Tehran agrees to a nuclear deal, according to Axios.

stories.title: Iran has executed 21 people, arrested 4,000 people since start of Iran war: UN
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that Iran has executed 21 people and arrested approximately 4,000 since the start of the Iran war. Many detainees have been subjected to forced disappearances, torture, and inhumane treatment.

stories.title: Sexual violence in Sudan triggers mental health crisis: UN
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that sexual violence, including rape used as a weapon of war, is fuelling a mental health crisis in Sudan. Aid organisations said survivors face severe trauma, social stigma, and a collapsing healthcare system.

stories.title: Norwegian MP is 'seriously worried' about country's Jews amid rising antisemitism - interview
stories.summary: Norwegian MP Joel Ystebø expressed serious concern about rising antisemitism in Norway, criticizing what he called biased media coverage and insufficient government action following the escalation of anti-Israel protests in Oslo.

stories.title: Germany Arrests Kazakh Man Accused of Spying for Russia
stories.summary: German authorities arrested a Kazakh national accused of spying for Russia. Prosecutors alleged he provided a Russian intelligence handler with information about German military aid to Ukraine and photographs of NATO military convoys on German motorways.

stories.title: Black lawmakers decry supreme court voting decision: ‘We’re going backwards’
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled 6-3 in Louisiana v. Callais, weakening a key provision of the Voting Rights Act. Alabama Representatives Terri Sewell and Shomari Figures, who represent the state's two Black congressional districts, said the decision sends the country backward and puts their seats at risk of elimination.

stories.title: Zelensky imposes new sanctions against Russia for abduction of children, against shadow fleet vessels
stories.summary: President Zelensky announced new sanctions targeting Russian officials and collaborators involved in the abduction of Ukrainian children from temporarily occupied territories. The sanctions also cover 23 vessels identified as part of Russia's shadow fleet.

stories.title: How do Israel, China view their dispute over Iran - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis examines how China has navigated its relationships with both Israel and Iran, maintaining significant trade ties with Jerusalem while holding strategic partnerships with Tehran amid the current conflict.

stories.title: Iran war, jet fuel concerns cloud airlines' summer holiday plans
stories.summary: European airlines face mounting challenges as the US-Israel war on Iran drives jet fuel prices up nearly 84 percent since the conflict began on February 28. Industry leaders warn of potential fuel rationing in Asia and Europe if the war continues.

stories.title: Pro-Russian Hacker Group Gamifies Cyberattacks on Europe With Crypto Rewards – Investigation
stories.summary: An investigation revealed that a pro-Russian hacker group is gamifying cyberattacks against European targets by offering cryptocurrency rewards to participants. The group's operations have continued despite a major Europol-led crackdown in July 2025 called Operation Eastwood.

stories.title: Ukraine asks Israel to seize vessel it claims is carrying grain stolen by Russia
stories.summary: Ukraine has asked Israel to seize a vessel it says is carrying grain looted from Russian-occupied Ukrainian territories. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy publicly stated the ship had arrived at an Israeli port and was preparing to unload, sparking a rare diplomatic dispute between Kyiv and Jerusalem.

stories.title: Russia’s “Russo-Balt” just unveiled almost-identical Tesla Cybertruck clone
stories.summary: Russian manufacturer Russo-Balt unveiled a vehicle closely resembling Tesla's Cybertruck, featuring an angular design, stainless-steel body, sharp body lines, and distinctive front lighting.

stories.title: Russia will remain in OPEC+, backs market stability
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov confirmed Russia has no plans to leave OPEC+, praising the group's role in stabilising energy markets during a period of turmoil. Peskov also acknowledged the UAE's decision to exit the group, saying Moscow respects the move.

stories.title: Sea drones hit Russian shadow fleet tanker as it waited for an at-sea oil rendezvous off Russia’s Black Sea coast
stories.summary: Two Ukrainian kamikaze sea drones struck a Cameroon-flagged tanker linked to Russia's shadow fleet in its engine room and propeller area off Russia's Black Sea coast on April 29. The empty vessel had its AIS transponder turned off while awaiting an at-sea oil transfer, according to Ukraine's General Staff.

stories.title: War update: 54 combat engagements on frontline since morning
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces reported 54 combat engagements with Russian troops along the frontline since the start of the day, reflecting sustained fighting across multiple sectors.

stories.title: Ukraine war flips Sweden’s Hagglunds fortunes from layoffs to billions
stories.summary: The war in Ukraine has dramatically boosted Sweden's defense industry, particularly armored vehicle manufacturer Hagglunds in the northern town of Örnsköldsvik. The company has shifted from facing layoffs to securing billions in orders, making Sweden one of Europe's fastest-growing weapons producers.

stories.title: The Global Economic Impact from the Iran Conflict
stories.summary: IMF Deputy Managing Director Gita Gopinath discussed the global economic impact of the conflict with Iran. She addressed strategies countries can adopt to build greater economic resilience amid the disruptions caused by the war.

stories.title: WATCH: Anti-draft haredi Jerusalem Faction holds protest at Chords Bridge
stories.summary: Members of the ultra-Orthodox Jerusalem Faction held an anti-IDF draft protest at Jerusalem's Chords Bridge, blocking traffic. Israeli police worked to clear the demonstrators and restore normal movement.

stories.title: IDF Brigade 7 commander: Hezbollah resistance in Lebanon stronger, but IDF strikes hard - interview
stories.summary: IDF Brigade 7's commander reported that Hezbollah resistance in southern Lebanon has intensified compared to previous operations. Israeli forces killed 130 Hezbollah fighters and destroyed a major tunnel network while operating with less air support than during the 2024 campaign.

stories.title: Man pleads guilty to plotting jihadist attack on 2024 Taylor Swift concert in Vienna
stories.summary: A 21-year-old man identified as Beran A. pleaded guilty in Vienna to plotting an ISIS-inspired jihadist bomb attack on a Taylor Swift concert scheduled in 2024. He stated he wanted to wage jihad. Two co-defendants, Arda K. and Hassan E., also face charges.

stories.title: Marine Corps considering Army’s MV-75 as an attack helo replacement
stories.summary: The U.S. Marine Corps is evaluating the Army's MV-75 tiltrotor as a potential replacement for its attack helicopter fleet. Bell presented an armed variant of the aircraft tailored to the Marines at the Modern Day Marine conference.

stories.title: 'Shoulder to shoulder': Israel and Serbia launch strategic dialogue, negotiate Free Trade Agreement
stories.summary: Israel and Serbia launched a strategic dialogue and began negotiating a Free Trade Agreement. Serbian Foreign Minister Marko Djuric said the deal would open opportunities for companies in both countries.

stories.title: US Supreme Court Hears case on Haitian, Syrian immigrants
