stories.summary: The US Supreme Court is reviewing Trump-era decisions to terminate Temporary Protected Status for Haitian and Syrian immigrants. The case concerns a key immigration protection programme that shields nationals of designated countries from deportation.

stories.title: Family of ailing Iranian Nobel laureate say keeping her in jail is a death sentence
stories.summary: The family of imprisoned Iranian Nobel Peace Prize laureate Narges Mohammadi says her life is at risk after a severe health deterioration, a suspected heart attack, and a weight loss of nearly 20 kilograms. The 54-year-old activist was re-arrested in December 2025 and is being held in Zanjan. Her lawyers say she has been denied medical leave.

stories.title: Behind Tehran’s calm, Iran faces deepening economic collapse
stories.summary: Iran faces deepening economic collapse as the rial continues to lose value, with citizens reportedly desperate to offload the currency. Despite an appearance of normalcy on Tehran's streets, widespread financial hardship persists.

stories.title: IAEA chief says Iran’s enriched uranium likely remains at Isfahan
stories.summary: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi stated that much of Iran's highly enriched uranium was stored at Isfahan during US and Israeli strikes in June 2025 and is believed to remain there. He noted that discussions with Russia and others about removing the material are ongoing but would require a political agreement or major military operation.

stories.title: 12-year-old boy neutralizes Russian FPV drone that was flying toward his brothers and sisters
stories.summary: In the town of Semenivka, 12-year-old Anatolii Prokhorenko disabled a Russian first-person-view (FPV) drone that was flying toward his younger siblings, neutralizing the threat.

stories.title: Bangladesh measles outbreak kills over 220 children since March
stories.summary: Bangladesh has recorded 227 child deaths and nearly 35,000 suspected measles cases since March in one of its worst outbreaks in decades. The Chittagong Hill Tracts, home to Indigenous communities near the Myanmar border, is among the hardest-hit areas.

stories.title: Iran war price tag hits US$25 billion as Hegseth defends record Pentagon budget
stories.summary: A Pentagon official told U.S. lawmakers that the two-month war with Iran has cost approximately US$25 billion, with most spending directed toward ammunition. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth appeared before the House Armed Services Committee to defend a record $1.5 trillion military budget facing Democratic opposition.

stories.title: US embassy congratulates Iraq PM-designate, backs stability
stories.summary: The US embassy in Baghdad congratulated Iraq's prime minister-designate Ali al-Zaidi and expressed support for stability. The appointment follows months of political deadlock in Iraq.

stories.title: Israeli-Turkish woman arrested in Turkey over IDF service rescued following US intervention
stories.summary: Jessica Becher, a 28-year-old Israeli-Turkish dual citizen, was arrested in Turkey after Islamist groups targeted her over her past IDF service. She was rescued following US diplomatic intervention and returned to Israel under security protection.

stories.title: Stranded whale ferried out of German waters in barge
stories.summary: Rescue teams in Germany used a barge to ferry a stranded whale out of German waters after earlier rescue attempts had failed. The final operation was closely followed by the public.

stories.title: Iran executed 21, arrested 4,000 since West Asia war began: U.N.
stories.summary: A United Nations report states that Iran has executed 21 people and arrested approximately 4,000 since the start of the West Asia war. The report details forced disappearances, torture, and inhumane treatment including forced confessions among detainees.

stories.title: Police treating stabbing of two men in Golders Green as terrorism
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police declared the stabbing of two men in Golders Green, north London, a terrorist incident. The suspect, described as hunting for anyone "visibly Jewish," was arrested. The attack follows a series of arson attacks targeting Jewish sites in London since March.

stories.title: Trump says US blockade could last for months, warns Iran to ‘get smart soon’
stories.summary: President Donald Trump warned Iran to "get smart soon" and accept Washington's demands for strict nuclear controls. Trump told oil executives the U.S. naval blockade of Iran could continue for months, after reportedly rejecting Tehran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Kemi Seba to remain in detention as hearing postponed
stories.summary: A court in an unspecified location postponed the hearing of Keli Seba, a prominent pan-African and anti-Western activist, who will remain in detention. Seba is wanted in Benin on charges of inciting rebellion after allegedly backing a coup attempt in December.

stories.title: Jean Reno publishes thriller novel Escape about Russia's abduction of Ukrainian children
stories.summary: French actor Jean Reno authored a crime-thriller novel titled "Escape," which centers on the abduction of Ukrainian children by Russia. The book was published in a thriller format.

stories.title: US defence secretary says Iran must be pushed to abandon nuclear ambitions
stories.summary: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth told lawmakers that Washington must pressure Iran into abandoning its nuclear ambitions as part of any future deal. He claimed US and Israeli strikes had severely damaged Iran's nuclear facilities but acknowledged Tehran retains nuclear ambitions and a significant missile arsenal.

stories.title: US supreme court sides with anti-abortion centers in New Jersey case
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court unanimously sided with First Choice Women's Resource Centers, a Christian faith-based operator of anti-abortion "crisis pregnancy centers" in New Jersey. The decision revived a federal lawsuit challenging a 2023 subpoena from the state attorney general investigating possible deceptive practices.

stories.title: France urges citizens to leave Mali 'as soon as possible' amid security risks
stories.summary: France issued a travel advisory urging its nationals in Mali to leave the country as soon as possible following coordinated attacks over the weekend, including in the capital Bamako. The advisory cited deteriorating security conditions in the West African nation.

stories.title: NJPMC issues guidelines for AI use in judicial institutions
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Judicial Policy Making Committee issued formal guidelines for the use of artificial intelligence in judicial institutions, establishing a framework for integrating AI as an assistive tool in courts nationwide.

stories.title: Man carries deceased sister into Indian bank amid paperwork difficulty
stories.summary: A man in India carried the body of his deceased sister into a bank after being unable to access her account due to paperwork requirements. The incident was recorded and drew public attention to bureaucratic hurdles faced by bereaved family members.

stories.title: Talks ongoing to free Syrians on ship hijacked by Somali pirates
stories.summary: Negotiations are underway to secure the release of Syrian nationals aboard a St. Kitts and Nevis-flagged tanker hijacked by Somali pirates and redirected into Somali waters. All Syrian crew members have been accounted for and are reported in good health.

stories.title: Safran, MBDA see delivery of French rocket artillery in 2029 as feasible
stories.summary: French defense firms Safran and MBDA stated that delivery of the Thundart rocket artillery system by 2029 is feasible. The companies emphasized that the system is fully designed and manufactured in France.

stories.title: Mali Rebel Group Demands Russia Leave Country Following Major Offensive
stories.summary: A rebel group in Mali's Azawad region demanded that Russia withdraw permanently from the country following a major rebel offensive. A spokesman told AFP the goal extends to removing Russian forces from all of Mali.

stories.title: Pete Hegseth denies Iran war is a ‘quagmire’ as cost to US hits $25bn
stories.summary: Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth told the House Armed Services Committee that the U.S.-Israel war on Iran is not a "quagmire" and requested approval for a $1.5 trillion military budget. President Trump simultaneously posted an AI-generated image of himself with a weapon captioned "NO MORE MR. NICE GUY."

stories.title: Artist, left-wing activist and writer Yair Garbuz dies at 80
stories.summary: Israeli artist, left-wing activist, and writer Yair Garbuz died at the age of 80. Known for his collages and a controversial remark at a 2015 political rally, Garbuz had largely withdrawn from public life over the past decade.

stories.title: Russia says it will stay in OPEC+, hopes U.A.E. exit does not spell end of group
stories.summary: Russia's Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed that Russia will remain in OPEC+, calling it an important organisation during current global market turmoil. Moscow expressed hope that the UAE's exit from the alliance would not lead to the group's dissolution.

stories.title: Israel president invites talks on Netanyahu pardon request
stories.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has invited legal discussions regarding a potential pardon for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as his long-running corruption trial continues in court.

stories.title: Bondi Beach Hanukkah terror attack teaches valuable lessons to volunteer medics
stories.summary: A clinical lead from a volunteer Jewish first responder charity discussed lessons learned from the Hanukkah terror attack at Bondi Beach. The organisation urged Jewish communities worldwide to improve disaster preparedness based on findings from the incident's medical response.

stories.title: Religious Zionist rabbis say students will not enlist in Armored Corps with women
stories.summary: Heads of Religious Zionist yeshivot across the Orthodox spectrum announced their students would not enlist in Israel's Armored Corps alongside women. The declaration followed a High Court ruling instructing the IDF to begin a pilot programme integrating women into co-ed tank units.

stories.title: Czechia should make greater use of Ukraine’s drone experience – Senate committee chair
stories.summary: The Czech Senate's Committee on Foreign Affairs and Security discussed leveraging Ukraine's battlefield drone expertise for Czechia's own counter-drone security. The committee also addressed the movement of Russian diplomatic passport holders across Europe.

stories.title: Interpol has issued red notices for property tycoon Malik Riaz, his son: NAB chief
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Accountability Bureau Chairman Lt General (retired) Nazir Ahmed announced that Interpol has issued Red Notices for Bahria Town owner Malik Riaz and his son Ali Riaz. NAB said it is sending a team to pursue their extradition, though the notices could not be independently verified through Interpol.

stories.title: Three women killed in Israeli strike on south Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on the village of Tayr Debba in southern Lebanon killed three women and wounded at least 11 others, according to Lebanon's health ministry. Since March 2, Israeli attacks have killed at least 2,534 people and displaced over 1.6 million.

stories.title: What does Chornobyl look like 40 years later?
stories.summary: Forty years after the 1986 nuclear disaster, Chornobyl in Ukraine remains a site where lingering radiation, abandoned cities, and the effects of the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war converge. The exclusion zone continues to draw attention as a symbol of overlapping crises.

stories.title: Breaking: Ukrainian drones hit Russia’s Mi-28 gunship and Mi-17 transport chopper 150+ km from the frontline
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone units and the SBU's Alpha special forces struck a Russian Mi-28 gunship and Mi-17 transport helicopter at a forward airstrip in Russia's Voronezh Oblast on 29 April. The attack occurred more than 150 kilometres from the front line while the aircraft were reportedly refuelling.

stories.title: UAE exits OPEC: What is OPEC+, its members, and what does the bloc do?
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates has announced its exit from OPEC. In 2025, OPEC+ members collectively produced nearly 50 percent of the world's oil and oil liquids, according to the International Energy Agency.

stories.title: Calls grow to free Abu Safiya after Israel extends detention
stories.summary: An Israeli court has extended the detention of Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya under the Unlawful Combatants Law after he spent over a year in custody. International calls for his release are growing.

stories.title: Madagascar detains French ex-serviceman over alleged destabilisation plot
stories.summary: Malagasy authorities detained French national and former serviceman Guy Baret along with a Malagasy army officer on allegations of conspiring to destabilise Madagascar. Details of the alleged plot have not been fully disclosed.

stories.title: Hungary’s new PM races to unlock EU’s frozen funds
stories.summary: Hungary's incoming Prime Minister Peter Magyar travelled to Brussels to seek the release of billions of euros in EU funds that had been frozen over rule-of-law concerns under the previous government led by Viktor Orbán.

stories.title: Growing Hezbollah drone threat shows Israel's innovation race is in its infancy - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis highlights Hezbollah's growing use of drones as a tactical threat against the IDF in Lebanon. The report examines whether Israeli defense innovation can keep pace with the evolving drone challenge.

stories.title: US war in Iran has cost $25 billion so far, says Pentagon official
stories.summary: A senior Pentagon official told the House Armed Services Committee that the US war on Iran has cost approximately $25 billion so far. Jules Hurst, performing the duties of comptroller, said most of the expenditure went toward munitions.

stories.title: Lebanese soldier and brother killed in Israeli strike: army
stories.summary: An Israeli strike in southern Lebanon killed a Lebanese soldier and his brother while they were traveling on a motorcycle. The Lebanese military confirmed the deaths, and Israel said it is reviewing the incident.

stories.title: Area of oil pollution in Black Sea reaches nearly 800 square kilometers after Russian attack — ecologist
stories.summary: An oil slick resulting from Russian attacks on the port of Chornomorsk on April 26 has spread to approximately 793 square kilometers in the Black Sea, contaminating the Odesa coastline, according to an ecologist.

stories.title: President Zardari invites investment in 'priority sectors' on China visit
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari, during a week-long visit to China's Hunan and Hainan provinces, invited Chinese investment in priority sectors. He met with the CEO of Hangzhou Jinjiang Group in Sanya, highlighting alternative energy, water treatment, and electric vehicle battery systems.

stories.title: FOIP at 10: Bridging the Indo-Pacific and the Middle East
stories.summary: Japan is marking the tenth anniversary of its Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP) strategy by expanding cooperation on security, supply chains, and sustainable development, with a growing focus on bridging the Indo-Pacific and Middle East regions.

stories.title: London police say stabbing of 2 Jewish men is declared a terrorist incident
stories.summary: Two Jewish men, aged 34 and 76, were stabbed and hospitalized in London's Golders Green area on Wednesday in what the Metropolitan Police declared a terrorist incident. A 45-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder in the suspected antisemitic attack.

stories.title: ‘Do we need to think about moving away?’: Jewish community fears for safety after Golders Green stabbings
stories.summary: Residents of Golders Green in north London expressed fears for their safety following the stabbing of two men in a suspected antisemitic attack. Community members called for stronger security measures, with some questioning whether the UK remains safe for Jewish people.

stories.title: US defense secretary defends $1.5 trillion budget in Congress hearing
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth testified before Congress for the first time since the war on Iran began, defending a proposed $1.5 trillion defense budget for fiscal year 2027. He said the budget reflects the administration's goal of returning the US defense industrial base to a wartime footing.

stories.title: How Iranian diplomats turned embassy accounts into viral meme machines
stories.summary: Several Iranian embassy accounts, including those in South Africa, Thailand, and the United Kingdom, have gained viral popularity on the platform X by posting memes, humor, and trolling of American politicians, attracting millions of views with a Gen Z-style approach.

stories.title: Private air defence takes off in Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defence Ministry confirmed that two private companies are now offering air defence operations in the country. The development marks a growing role for private-sector involvement in Ukraine's wartime defence capabilities.

stories.title: Mali: Goïta speaks as fractures appear within the junta
stories.summary: Malian junta leader Assimi Goïta broke his silence three days after a joint FLA and JNIM offensive that killed defense minister General Sadio Camara. The crisis has exposed divisions within Mali's ruling military regime.

stories.title: Estonian FM comments on President Karis's statements about dialogue with Russia
stories.summary: Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna publicly stated that President Alar Karis's remarks about dialogue with Moscow contradict Estonia's official foreign policy. Other Estonian politicians echoed Tsahkna's position.

stories.title: 6 terrorists killed as attack on Bannu police post thwarted
stories.summary: At least six terrorists were killed when Bannu police in Pakistan repelled a major attack on the Mazanga police post in the early hours of Wednesday. One attacker died on the spot, while the bodies of five others were retrieved by their associates after an intense firefight.

stories.title: Lebanon detains ex-Palestinian envoy over corruption allegations
stories.summary: Lebanese authorities detained former Palestinian ambassador Ashraf Dabbour based on an Interpol warrant related to corruption allegations.

stories.title: China’s zero‑tariff push wins backing from South Africa and Kenya
stories.summary: Officials and business leaders in South Africa and Kenya expressed support for China's new zero-tariff policy covering 53 African nations. They said the measure could open trade opportunities, reduce costs for small businesses, and strengthen economic ties across the continent.

stories.title: Likud minister contradicts Netanyahu, says US limiting Israel's actions in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Security Cabinet member and Likud minister Avi Dichter publicly contradicted Prime Minister Netanyahu, stating that the United States is limiting Israel's military actions in Lebanon. His remarks offered a rare look at decision-making constraints on the northern front.

stories.title: Senate panel advances Kevin Warsh’s nomination for US Fed chair
stories.summary: The US Senate Banking Committee advanced Kevin Warsh's nomination to replace Jerome Powell as Federal Reserve chair. The vote proceeded along party lines after Warsh was nominated by President Donald Trump.

stories.title: Russia hits two hospitals, kills one woman overnight in strikes on Ukrainian cities
stories.summary: Russian strikes overnight hit two hospitals in Ukrainian cities, including the destruction of a reception ward at a hospital in Izmail. A 60-year-old woman died of smoke inhalation when her apartment in Shostka caught fire during the attacks.

stories.title: Russia to hold Victory Day parade without weaponry display
stories.summary: Russia announced it will hold its Victory Day parade without a military weaponry display, a scaled-back format not seen since 2007. The decision comes amid increasing Ukrainian drone and missile strikes deep into Russian territory, including Moscow.

stories.title: Kyiv Security Forum agreed Russia’s threat is existential. It did not discuss how to defeat Moscow.
stories.summary: The Kyiv Security Forum reached consensus that Russia poses an existential threat to Ukraine. However, participants reportedly did not discuss concrete strategies for defeating Moscow, with observers noting the unspoken issue of shifting US support.

stories.title: Ukraine urges Israel to seize ship over 'stolen' grain
stories.summary: Ukraine's top prosecutor submitted a formal request to Israel to detain a ship allegedly carrying grain taken from Ukrainian territories occupied by Russia.

stories.title: UK expels Russian diplomat in tit-for-tat move
stories.summary: The United Kingdom expelled a Russian diplomat in a retaliatory move. Moscow had not yet commented on the expulsion at the time of reporting.

stories.title: Rachel Zegler’s award-winning Evita to hit Broadway in 2027
stories.summary: The Olivier Award-winning revival of Evita, starring Rachel Zegler and directed by Jamie Lloyd, will transfer from London's West End to Broadway in spring 2027. Zegler won an Olivier for her lead performance in the Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber musical.

stories.title: Republic of Congo president holds talks with his Russian counterpart
stories.summary: Republic of Congo President Denis Sassou N'Guesso visited the Kremlin in Moscow on Wednesday for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Details of the discussions were not immediately disclosed.

stories.title: Death toll from Indonesia train crash rises to 16, all women
stories.summary: The death toll from a train crash in Indonesia has risen to 16, with all victims being women. Forty-four other passengers were treated at hospitals and subsequently discharged.

stories.title: Gulf summit urges pipelines, regional missile defence system
stories.summary: Leaders at a Gulf summit called for the rapid construction of oil pipelines and a regional missile defense warning system. The summit also rejected Iran's disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: US lawmakers to grill Pentagon chief on Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. lawmakers are set to question the Pentagon chief about the war with Iran. President Donald Trump has not yet publicly outlined a plan for winding down the conflict.

stories.title: Russia attacks port infrastructure in Ukraine's south, hits hospital
stories.summary: Russia struck port infrastructure in Ukraine's southern Odesa region with overnight drone attacks on April 29. The strikes also damaged residential buildings and a hospital, wounding two people, according to Ukrainian officials.

stories.title: Sweden targets social media giants over ‘murder adverts’ recruiting children
stories.summary: Sweden's government announced plans for legislation requiring social media platforms such as TikTok and Snapchat to remove criminal gangs' "murder adverts" within one hour or face significant fines. The ads increasingly recruit children under 15 for violent acts.

stories.title: EU launches battlefield technologies testing platform for Ukraine
stories.summary: The European Commission launched a new platform designed to test battlefield military technologies in real combat scenarios, aimed at supporting Ukraine's defense efforts.

stories.title: Navy releases list of ships it plans to inactivate this year
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy released a list of ships it plans to inactivate this year, intending to remove 14 vessels from its fleet.

stories.title: Oil prices hit highest levels since 2022 on Iran war fears
stories.summary: Oil prices climbed to their highest levels since 2022 amid reports that the United States could escalate military action to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The surge reflects growing market fears over the widening US-Iran conflict.

stories.title: Oil prices jump as Iran, US continue standoff over Hormuz strait
stories.summary: Oil prices surged to their highest levels in over three weeks after the Wall Street Journal reported that President Trump is planning an extended blockade on Iran. The increase reflects the ongoing US-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Over 1.2m in Lebanon expected to face acute hunger: UN-backed report
stories.summary: A joint report by the FAO, WFP, and the Lebanese government projects that 1.24 million people in Lebanon will face food insecurity at crisis levels or worse due to the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Iran’s currency falls to new low as US blockade, sanctions impact trade
stories.summary: Iran's currency has fallen to a record low as US sanctions and a blockade disrupt trade with major partners, including China and the United Arab Emirates.

stories.title: Netanyahu trial cross-examination interrupted as PM leaves for urgent security meeting
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's corruption trial cross-examination was interrupted when he left the courtroom for an urgent security consultation at the Kirya, the IDF's headquarters. The court had declined his request to delay the start time by three hours. He returned hours later.

stories.title: Panama reaffirms ‘neutrality’ of canal amid Middle East war
stories.summary: Panama reaffirmed the neutrality of the Panama Canal amid the ongoing Middle East war. Approximately five percent of global maritime trade transits through the canal.

stories.title: Nigeria: I Was Never Married to Rosy Meurer' - Olakunle Churchill Debunks Divorce Rumours
stories.summary: Nigerian public figure Olakunle Churchill publicly denied that he was ever legally married to Rosy Meurer, disputing divorce rumours. He also addressed his previous relationship with actress Tonto Dikeh.

stories.title: Russian drone strikes village in Kharkiv region, leaving three injured
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck the village of Petrivka in the Izium district of Ukraine's Kharkiv region, injuring three people.

stories.title: REPLAY: US lawmakers grill Pentagon chief Hegseth over Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth faced congressional questioning for the first time since the launch of the war against Iran. Democrats challenged the conflict as a costly war of choice undertaken without congressional authorization.

stories.title: US embassy congratulates Iraq’s PM-designate, says hopes for peaceful future
stories.summary: The U.S. embassy congratulated Iraq's newly designated prime minister and expressed hopes for a peaceful future. The incoming premier is expected to address Washington's demand that Baghdad disarm Iran-backed armed groups operating in the country.

stories.title: Malawi: Ecama Demands Fuel Levy Cuts As Prices Soar, Shortages Bite
stories.summary: The Economics Association of Malawi (ECAMA) president Bertha Bangara has called for the removal of non-essential levies on fuel as Malawi faces soaring fuel prices and supply shortages. She warned the current pricing structure is straining households and deepening economic distress.

stories.title: “Oil rain” reported in Perm after Ukrainian drones set Transneft pumping station ablaze 1,500 km from the war zone
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck a Transneft oil pumping station in Russia's Perm region, roughly 1,500 kilometers from the front lines, setting it ablaze and reportedly causing "oil rain" in the area. The Orsk oil refinery and a machine-building plant in Orenburg Oblast were also hit overnight.

stories.title: US Supreme Court hears Haiti, Syria TPS case with wide-ranging implications
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court is hearing a case on whether the Trump administration can terminate Temporary Protected Status for nationals of Haiti and Syria, a decision that could affect approximately 1.3 million people currently residing in the United States.

stories.title: Eritrea: Sovereignty Vs. Hegemonic Ambition - Ethiopia's Expansionist Quest for Outlet to the Sea
stories.summary: Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed reiterated in recent state media remarks that sovereign sea access is an existential and irreversible national objective for Ethiopia. Eritrean state media characterized the rhetoric as expansionist and a threat to regional sovereignty.

stories.title: Rioters who broke into IDF police chief’s home charged with assault, trespassing
stories.summary: Israeli authorities charged individuals who broke into the home of the IDF military police chief with assault, trespassing, property damage, and unlawful assembly. An Ashkelon court extended the detention of 10 suspects who had staged an anti-conscription protest at the officer's residence.

stories.title: How the Iranian street mobilises over nuclear negotiations
stories.summary: Public mobilization in Iran, particularly during the most intense phases of the current war, has been characterized as a significant factor in reinforcing domestic solidarity and the internal front.

stories.title: Crewe religious group raided by police investigating allegations of serious sexual offences
stories.summary: Approximately 500 police officers raided the headquarters of the Ahmadi Religion of Peace and Light in Crewe, England, as part of an investigation into allegations of serious sexual offenses, modern slavery, and forced marriage. Nine people were arrested and taken into custody.

stories.title: Lula's Supreme Court nominee defends limits on judicial power in Brazilian Senate hearing
stories.summary: Jorge Messias, President Lula's nominee for Brazil's Federal Supreme Court, testified before the Senate's Constitution and Justice Committee on April 29. He advocated for limits on judicial power and made overtures to the Bolsonarist right-wing opposition ahead of an expected close confirmation vote.

stories.title: US targets 35 individuals, firms in Iran evasion crackdown
stories.summary: The US Treasury imposed new sanctions on 35 individuals and firms accused of helping Iran evade existing sanctions. Washington also warned banks about transactions linked to shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Israeli officers say Lebanon mission focused on 'systematic destruction' of buildings
stories.summary: Israeli military officers told Haaretz that their mission in southern Lebanon has focused on the systematic destruction of buildings in predominantly Shia villages. The account describes widespread demolitions across the area.

stories.title: Sixty days in, Pentagon estimates $25B spent on Iran war
stories.summary: The Pentagon estimates that approximately $25 billion has been spent on the U.S. war with Iran in its first 60 days. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and the Joint Chiefs chairman testified before Congress for the first time since military strikes began on February 28.

stories.title: Israel is building homes, but not the homes Israelis need, Shoresh study warns
stories.summary: A study by Shoresh Institution researcher Yael Mishly found that Israel's housing market suffers from a structural mismatch rather than a simple shortage, arguing that the homes being built do not align with what most Israelis need.

stories.title: Mali: Moscow claims footage shows fighting with Tuareg rebels
stories.summary: Russia's defence ministry released footage it claims shows its troops fighting Tuareg rebels in Mali. The release follows the forced withdrawal of Moscow's Africa Corps paramilitary unit from the northern town of Kidal after attacks by Tuareg rebels and jihadist groups.

stories.title: One big FAMMily: Air Force eyes huge boost for low-cost cruise missile
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force is pursuing a major expansion of its Family of Affordable Mass Missiles (FAMM) program, envisioning production of nearly 30,000 low-cost cruise missiles. The planned procurement stands out even amid broader increases in munitions spending.

stories.title: Guardian Essential poll: Australians want higher tax on gas exports and extension of petrol excise cut
stories.summary: A Guardian Essential poll found that a majority of Australians support higher taxes on gas export profits and extending the petrol excise cut amid a fuel crisis. The poll also indicated growing public preference for shifting to renewable energy over continued reliance on fossil fuels, despite Prime Minister Albanese ruling out new taxes on existing gas export contracts.

stories.title: Chips, oil and Iran: why US is raising pressure on China before Xi-Trump talks
stories.summary: The United States is intensifying pressure on China over semiconductor exports, oil trade, and Iran policy ahead of a planned mid-May meeting between Presidents Trump and Xi Jinping. US House lawmakers advanced 20 new export control measures this month.

stories.title: Ukraine formally requests Israel to arrest Russian vessel carrying stolen grain
stories.summary: Ukraine's Office of the Prosecutor General formally requested Israel to arrest a Russian vessel suspected of transporting stolen Ukrainian grain, submitting a package of legal documents to Israeli authorities.

stories.title: In Gaza, life flickers as power cuts shatter livelihoods and healthcare
stories.summary: Severe electricity shortages in Gaza under Israeli siege are disrupting healthcare, collapsing businesses, and forcing families into dire survival conditions. Operations are delayed and livelihoods destroyed as power cuts deepen across the territory.

stories.title: China Southern Airlines orders Airbus jets worth US$21b as Boeing deal remains rumour
stories.summary: China Southern Airlines and its subsidiary Xiamen Airlines ordered 137 Airbus A320neo jets in a deal worth approximately $21 billion, strengthening Airbus's position in the Chinese market while Boeing awaits a rumored competing deal with Beijing.

stories.title: Who Is ‘El Jardinero,’ the CJNG Power Broker Arrested in Mexico?
stories.summary: Mexican authorities arrested an influential Jalisco Cartel New Generation (CJNG) boss known as "El Jardinero," described as a key power broker within the organization. The capture comes roughly two months after the cartel's top leader was killed, marking a significant blow to Mexico's most powerful criminal network.

stories.title: UK police say London stabbing of 2 Jewish men is terrorist incident
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police declared the stabbing of two Jewish men in the Golders Green area a terrorist incident. The victims, aged 34 and 76, were hospitalized, and a 45-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of attempted murder. Police are investigating possible links to recent synagogue arson attacks.

stories.title: Pakistan's weekly oil bill reached $800m amid Middle East war: PM Shehbaz
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif said the country's weekly oil bill has reached $800 million due to skyrocketing global fuel prices caused by the U.S.-Israel military campaign against Iran. He commended Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik's handling of the resulting fuel crisis.

stories.title: Loyal groundskeepers guard Sudan's ancient Nubian pyramids
stories.summary: Groundskeepers continue to protect Sudan's ancient Nubian pyramids, including those at the UNESCO-protected site of Meroe, which have endured sand erosion, rain, armed conflict, and neglect over the years.

stories.title: Anxiety, resentment around AI spur violence against tech’s figureheads
stories.summary: A series of attacks against prominent figures in the artificial intelligence industry have raised concerns about public anxiety and resentment toward AI technology. Authorities have found no demonstrable connections linking the incidents to one another.

stories.title: Report: St. Petersburg to cut May 9 parade attendance from 5,600 to 310
stories.summary: St. Petersburg authorities plan to drastically reduce spectator attendance at the May 9 Victory Day military parade at Palace Square from 5,600 to just 310, according to local outlet Fontanka.

stories.title: Watch: There's a ceasefire in Lebanon - but the fighting hasn't stopped
stories.summary: Israel and Hezbollah have continued exchanging fire in Lebanon despite a US-brokered ceasefire that took effect 12 days ago. Both sides have traded blame for violations of the truce.

stories.title: Russia is trying to block Ukraine’s defense deals with Gulf, and just added 8,000 troops to Africa
stories.summary: Ukraine's President Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine will continue operations targeting Russia's export capacity, amid reports that Moscow is attempting to obstruct Ukrainian defense agreements with Gulf states and has deployed approximately 8,000 additional troops to Africa.

stories.title: Lebanese soldier said killed in Israeli strike, Hezbollah fires 2 rockets at north amid truce
stories.summary: A Lebanese soldier was reportedly killed in an Israeli strike in southern Lebanon, while Hezbollah fired two rockets at northern Israel in the latest ceasefire violation. Lebanese media reported dozens of Israeli strikes and home demolitions across the south as Israel's security cabinet convened.

stories.title: Wounded Starmer limps on to meet his fate at elections next week
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces a critical test with local elections scheduled for the following week. The results are expected to be a key flashpoint for determining his political future amid ongoing challenges to his leadership.

stories.title: Armed forces destroy Afghan Taliban posts, vehicles in Chaman sector: security sources
stories.summary: Pakistani armed forces destroyed several Afghan Taliban posts and vehicles in Balochistan's Chaman sector as part of Operation Ghazab lil-Haq. Security sources said the operations responded to unprovoked aggression by Afghan Taliban forces along the Pak-Afghan border.

stories.title: Zelensky: Ukraine has documents indicating Russia’s plans to disrupt “Drone Deals” with partners
stories.summary: President Zelensky disclosed that Ukraine has obtained Russian documents detailing plans to disrupt Ukraine's defense partnerships under the Drone Deals framework with international partners.

stories.title: Mystery ‘El Money’ figure offered to pay men to set fire to property linked to Starmer, court hears
stories.summary: A London court heard that a Russian-speaking figure using the pseudonym "El Money" allegedly organized arson attacks on property linked to UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer in May of the previous year. Three defendants—two Ukrainian nationals and one Romanian national—deny plotting the attacks on two homes and a car.

stories.title: Police arrest another teen suspect in Independence Day murder at Petah Tikva pizzeria
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested another teenage suspect in connection with a murder at a Pizza Hut in Petah Tikva on Independence Day, bringing the total detained to 11. The primary suspect has not yet appeared before a judge.

stories.title: Over 1.2m people in Lebanon to face acute hunger due to war
stories.summary: A UN-backed report by the FAO, WFP, and Lebanon's agriculture ministry warned that over 1.24 million people in Lebanon—nearly one in four of the analyzed population—face acute hunger at crisis levels or worse between April and August 2026 due to the ongoing war.

stories.title: Kevin Warsh clears key Senate hurdle to replace Fed chair Powell
stories.summary: Kevin Warsh, President Trump's nominee to lead the Federal Reserve, was advanced by a Senate committee in a 13-to-11 party-line vote on April 29. The procedural approval clears the way for Warsh to succeed Jerome Powell amid concerns over White House efforts to influence the central bank's independence.

stories.title: The long shock: How the Iran war is remaking the global economy
stories.summary: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz due to the Iran conflict represents a major disruption to the post-1970s global energy order. Analysts say the consequences may fundamentally reshape how the global economy functions.

stories.title: Britain to create joint naval force with nine European countries as ‘complement’ to Nato
stories.summary: Britain agreed to establish a joint naval force with nine European countries to deter Russian threats from northern sea routes. The Royal Navy chief stated that despite the ongoing Middle East crisis, including the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, Russia remains the gravest security threat.

stories.title: How to Be a Dissident - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Author Gal Beckerman discussed his new book on dissidence in a conversation exploring its relevance for countries facing political uncertainty, including Israel as it approaches another election cycle.

stories.title: France's public holidays: The art of the long weekend
stories.summary: France's public holidays in May were examined, including the cultural tradition of "ponts" or extended long weekends. An ongoing political debate surrounds the May 1 bank holiday, alongside research into the ideal number of public holidays.

stories.title: The little-known clause that Europe’s security may now depend on
stories.summary: The EU's mutual defense clause, Article 42.7, has gained renewed attention as U.S. President Donald Trump has raised doubts about America's commitment to NATO. The provision requires EU member states to aid any member that comes under armed attack, functioning as a potential complement or alternative to NATO's Article 5.

stories.title: Inside Tehran’s main airport as more flights take off during ceasefire
stories.summary: Al Jazeera's correspondent Tohid Asadi reported increased flight activity at Tehran's main international airport during a period of ceasefire, suggesting a partial resumption of normal air travel in Iran's capital.

stories.title: King Charles’s US visit ‘about future generations, not just the current administration’
stories.summary: King Charles's state visit to the United States is intended to focus on future generations and long-term transatlantic ties rather than the current political administration. Analysts note the U.S.-UK relationship faces unprecedented friction over uncertainty regarding America's NATO commitments and the "special relationship."

stories.title: Report: Abramovich tied to Russian payment platform created to evade sanctions, serving drone makers
stories.summary: An investigation by the Russian outlet Proekt found that billionaires Roman Abramovich and Viktor Kharitonin may be linked to A7, a payment platform created in 2024 to help Russian entities circumvent Western sanctions. Sources describe A7 as the dominant player in Russia's cross-border payments market, serving clients including drone manufacturers.

stories.title: Ukraine opens international register of damage for Russian aggression, as reconstruction needs hit at $587.7 billion
stories.summary: Ukraine has launched an international register of damage caused by Russian aggression, operating under the Council of Europe framework. Reconstruction needs are estimated at $587.7 billion.

stories.title: The West’s sanctions wall on Russia is eroding. Ukrainians are holding it up with drones and dossiers.
stories.summary: Western sanctions against Russia are reportedly weakening as Moscow employs strategies to divide allied nations. Ukrainian forces are using drones and intelligence dossiers to help sustain sanctions enforcement amid growing fuel shortages in Russia.

stories.title: Young Palestinian artists from Gaza exhibit work shaped by war
stories.summary: In Gaza's Bureij refugee camp, 64 young Palestinian artists exhibited works reflecting their experiences of years of war and conflict in the territory.

stories.title: Russia will not display military equipment at Victory Day parade due to Ukraine threat
stories.summary: Russia announced on April 29 that its annual Victory Day parade on Red Square marking the defeat of Nazi Germany will not feature a military hardware display for the first time in nearly two decades. The Kremlin attributed the scaled-back event to Ukraine's "terrorist activity."

stories.title: Novosibirsk Veterinary Official Involved in Mass Cattle Cull Found Dead
stories.summary: Sergei Tur, the head of animal disease control at the Novosibirsk regional veterinary agency in Russia, was found dead. Tur had been responsible for organizing quarantines and the mass culling of livestock on farms affected by a recent cattle disease outbreak.

stories.title: Hungary’s incoming PM Magyar visits Brussels seeking to unblock EU billions
stories.summary: Hungary's incoming Prime Minister Péter Magyar visited Brussels seeking to unlock billions of euros in frozen EU funds. Magyar aims to demonstrate that his pledge to reset Hungary's relationship with the European Union can deliver quick, tangible benefits.

stories.title: Mali jihadists threaten to impose blockade on Bamako
stories.summary: Jihadist group JNIM announced a blockade on all roads leading into Mali's capital, Bamako, escalating the country's security crisis. Junta leader Assimi Goïta made a public appearance claiming the situation was under control.

stories.title: SSU drones strike Russian oil pumping station in Perm, over 1,500 km from Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service Alpha special operations center used drones to strike the Perm linear production dispatch station in Russia's Perm region, located more than 1,500 kilometers from the Ukrainian border. The facility is an oil pumping station.

stories.title: ‘We saw terrible things’: Mali refugees tell of atrocities amid attacks
stories.summary: Thousands of Malians have fled the country after attacks by multiple armed groups, including the national army. Refugees have described witnessing severe atrocities during the violence.

stories.title: “Russia has never seen this”: Russia’s central bank chief admits a 2.5 million worker deficit
stories.summary: Russia's central bank chief acknowledged a labor deficit of 2.5 million workers, a shortfall attributed to the state's pressure on small businesses and programs retraining war widows for the workforce.

stories.title: Two wounded in London knife attack against Golders Green Jews
stories.summary: Two people were wounded in a knife attack targeting Jewish individuals in the Golders Green area of London. The Community Security Trust reported that the Metropolitan Police, the Shomrim neighborhood watch, and the Hatzola emergency service responded quickly. Authorities urged witnesses to come forward with information.

stories.title: Kenya: Govt Issues Urgent Flood Warning to Tana River Residents
stories.summary: The Kenyan government issued an urgent flood warning to residents along the Lower Tana River after water levels in the Seven Forks dams rose significantly due to heavy upstream rainfall.

stories.title: Ukraine’s new heavy drones reportedly penetrate Soviet-era Iskander shelters in Crimea
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces reportedly used new heavy drones to penetrate Soviet-era bunkers in Crimea that were originally designed to protect Iskander missile systems from Cold War-era ballistic strikes. The target site had long been identified by Ukrainian intelligence.

stories.title: RBC reports Russia’s tax service and central bank are developing criteria to automatically flag undeclared business income from money transfers
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Tax Service and central bank are jointly developing criteria to automatically detect undeclared business income from money transfers, according to the Russian outlet RBC. The system would flag individuals earning unreported revenue from commercial activity.

stories.title: South Africa: No, Cape Town Not 'Officially' a US Province. Old Fabricated Audio Strikes Again
stories.summary: A video claiming Cape Town has officially become a US province after South Africa's Democratic Alliance secured a loan from the "Bezos Foundation" is circulating online. Africa Check confirmed the claim is false and the accompanying audio evidence was fabricated.

stories.title: US Marines help gun down beach invaders in simulated Philippines defense
stories.summary: U.S. Marines participated in a simulated beach defense exercise in the Philippines, helping repel a mock enemy invasion. The exercise concluded with the use of an explosive-laden first-person-view drone to strike the withdrawing simulated adversary.

stories.title: Belarus says it bars Russian military draftees from crossing its border
stories.summary: Belarus announced that Russian citizens barred from leaving Russia after receiving military draft notices will not be permitted to exit through Belarusian territory. Reports indicate a Russian man listed in a conscription database was recently prevented from flying out of Minsk National Airport.

stories.title: Nigeria: Lagos Bets On Local Power Amid Incessant Grid Collapses
stories.summary: Lagos state is expanding state-backed electricity generation and distribution after securing 400 megawatts of new supply, as Nigeria's national power grid continues to experience frequent collapses and fails to meet demand.

stories.title: Hot weather and hungry datacentres lift Australia’s energy demand to record highs but batteries quell prices
stories.summary: Australia's electricity demand reached a record 25 gigawatts in the first quarter of 2026, driven by growing datacentre usage and warmer weather. The Australian Energy Market Operator reported demand rose 1.2% year-on-year, though record rooftop solar output and battery storage growth helped moderate wholesale prices.

stories.title: UK: Starmer condemns 'antisemitic attack' after two Jewish men stabbed in London
stories.summary: A man was arrested in London's Golders Green neighborhood after allegedly stabbing two Jewish men on April 29, 2026. UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer condemned the incident as an antisemitic attack.

stories.title: Are US agents around Trump armed with Chinese red dot sights?
stories.summary: A press photo of a US Secret Service agent responding to a security breach at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner sparked debate after what appeared to be a Chinese-made Holosun red dot sight was spotted on her service pistol.

stories.title: No troop build-up near Ukraine’s border with Belarus, says SBGS
stories.summary: Ukraine's State Border Guard Service reported no observed buildup of troops or military equipment near the Ukrainian-Belarusian border on the Belarusian side. The statement aimed to address concerns about potential threats from Belarus.

stories.title: Abuse at French after-school programmes: Parents sound the alarm
stories.summary: Parents in Paris have raised alarms over mounting reports of physical and sexual abuse of nursery school children during after-school care and lunch breaks supervised by non-teaching staff. In 2026 alone, 78 youth workers were suspended in Paris, with 31 suspected of sexual abuse.

stories.title: Belgian defense minister meeting with firms lined up for slice of $1.3B counter-drone pie
stories.summary: Belgium's defense minister met with companies competing for a share of a $1.3 billion counter-drone contract. The Belgian Ministry of Defense confirmed the tender will combine active and passive measures, including detection sensors and a command-and-control system linking all effectors.

stories.title: Fresh Ethiopia-Tigray friction as leaked audio suggests shift in regional loyalty
stories.summary: A leaked audio recording allegedly featuring a senior Tigray People's Liberation Front official suggests willingness to engage in trade with Eritrea and coordinate with domestic armed groups against Ethiopia's federal government. The TPLF has denied the recording's authenticity.

stories.title: Two Jewish men badly wounded in terrorist stabbing attack in London’s Golders Green; assailant arrested
stories.summary: A 45-year-old man stabbed two Jewish men in London's Golders Green neighborhood, seriously wounding both, including a septuagenarian struck in the throat. London's Metropolitan Police declared the incident a terrorist attack and arrested the assailant. UK Prime Minister Starmer condemned it as appalling.

stories.title: Rwanda: Rwanda Considers Restricting Social Media Use for Children Under 16
stories.summary: Rwanda's government is considering legislation to restrict children under 16 from using social media platforms, as part of efforts to strengthen child protection in the digital space.

stories.title: Israel heads toward its most fateful elections, with law and order, governance and morality at stake
stories.summary: Israel is heading toward elections amid escalating internal security crises, including violence by Jewish extremists in the West Bank, deadly teen gang activity in central Israel, and ultra-Orthodox youth unrest nationwide. The political climate is shaped by governance and law-and-order concerns.

stories.title: Indian man takes sister's exhumed body to bank for withdrawal
stories.summary: In Odisha, India, a man named Jitu Munda exhumed his deceased sister's body and carried it to an Indian Overseas Bank branch after being denied access to her account without a death certificate.

stories.title: Long-sought arrest in Toronto’s anti-Jewish shootings leaves unanswered questions
stories.summary: Canadian police arrested Mohamed Mahdi in Toronto in connection with a series of shootings targeting Jewish establishments, including a restaurant riddled with bullets. Questions remain about whether the wave of attacks is linked and what long-term security measures are needed.

stories.title: UK government borrowing costs rise to their highest since 2008 financial crisis
stories.summary: UK government borrowing costs rose to their highest level since the 2008 financial crisis. The increase is attributed to Britain's exposure to the energy shock caused by the Iran war and growing fears of rising inflation.

stories.title: Tanzania: Dodoma Readies for Ruto's Tour of Tanzanian Parliament
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto is scheduled to address Tanzania's Parliament in Dodoma on May 5, 2026, in a visit aimed at strengthening regional cooperation between the two East African nations.

stories.title: Iran's rial drops to record low
stories.summary: Iran's currency fell to a record low of 1,810,000 rials per US dollar on Wednesday, losing nearly 15 percent in two days. The decline followed a period of relative stability during a US-Iran ceasefire and Iranian New Year holidays.

stories.title: US/Iran war lifting oil prices, but benefiting countries such as Australia, Norway and Brazil
stories.summary: The U.S.-Iran conflict has driven up global oil prices, benefiting energy-exporting nations such as Australia, Norway, and Brazil. Currencies of these countries have outperformed the U.S. dollar due to windfall profits from oil, gas, and metals exports.

stories.title: Rainforest loss eases in 2025, but El Nino and fires a looming threat: US study
stories.summary: A US study indicated that tropical rainforest loss eased in 2025, but El Niño conditions and fire risks remain significant threats. Tropical rainforests play a critical role in regulating the global climate and absorbing carbon dioxide.

stories.title: Israel engineered 'special' rats to attack Palestinians in Gaza, radical Fatah officials claim
stories.summary: A senior Fatah official in Gaza, Jamal Obeid, accused Israel of engineering rats to attack Palestinians in previously uninfested areas of the Gaza Strip. The claim was reported by Palestinian Media Watch, which monitors Palestinian media and official statements.

stories.title: Suspect in child murder case killed in police ‘encounter’ in Punjab’s Hafizabad
stories.summary: A suspect wanted for the kidnapping and murder of a six-year-old boy was killed during a police encounter in Hafizabad district, Punjab, Pakistan. The child's body was recovered from nearby fields during a search operation in Pindi Bhattian tehsil.

stories.title: DIU reports elimination of Akhmat unit fighters in coordinated strike
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Intelligence (DIU) special forces carried out a coordinated strike that eliminated a group of mercenaries from Russia's National Guard Akhmat unit. No further details on the location or scale of the operation were provided.

stories.title: Belarus Closes Transit Route for Russian Military Conscripts
stories.summary: Belarus confirmed it is blocking Russian military conscripts from using its territory as a transit route to leave Russia. A Russian man in a military conscription database was reportedly prevented from flying out of Minsk National Airport this week while trying to reach Georgia and Armenia.

stories.title: When one of these hits the ocean’s surface at 100Gs, enemy submarines better hide
stories.summary: A sponsored report highlights the development of next-generation sonobuoys designed for anti-submarine warfare. The advanced sonobuoys are engineered to detect increasingly quiet Russian and Chinese submarines and can withstand impacts of up to 100Gs upon hitting the ocean surface.

stories.title: Ugandan authorities arrest dozens of foreigners in possible human trafficking case
stories.summary: Ugandan authorities arrested dozens of foreigners since Monday in operations targeting suspected human trafficking. The crackdown focused on groups in northern Uganda and another group living in a closed compound.

stories.title: Britain created the template for Israel's occupation. It must own up to its crimes in Palestine
stories.summary: A commentary argues that British Mandate-era policies in Palestine—including collective punishment and coercive interrogation—served as a template for Israel's occupation and calls on Britain to apologize for its colonial role.

stories.title: Israel's execution law is a war on Palestinian prisoners
stories.summary: A commentary highlights the treatment of Palestinian prisoners in Israeli detention, arguing that long before any execution law, detainees faced death through torture, neglect, and abuse.

stories.title: Last Kenyan police officers leave Haiti after unsuccessful security mission
stories.summary: All Kenyan police officers deployed to Haiti as part of the UN-authorized Multinational Security Support Mission have departed the country. Despite Kenya's leadership of the mission since late 2023, armed gangs continue to control significant territory and inflict widespread violence in Haiti.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills five family members in Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike in Lebanon killed five members of the same family. The strike is part of ongoing Israeli military operations in the country.

stories.title: US forces board ship suspected of heading to Iran port
stories.summary: U.S. Marines boarded the commercial vessel M/V Blue Star III in the Arabian Sea on Tuesday on suspicion it was attempting to violate the American blockade of Iranian ports. Central Command said the ship was released after a search confirmed it was not heading to an Iranian port.

stories.title: Global forest loss slows but El Niño fires could threaten progress
stories.summary: New analysis shows the rate of global tropical rainforest loss slowed last year. However, scientists caution that deforestation remains rapid and warn that El Niño-driven fires could reverse recent progress.

stories.title: As war nears two months, displaced Lebanese families sink into despair
stories.summary: Displaced Lebanese families, including those from the southern town of Khiyam, are facing deepening despair nearly two months after a new conflict erupted. Fighting began on March 2 when Hezbollah fired into Israel, prompting mass displacement to Beirut and other areas.

stories.title: Top US diplomat in Kyiv to resign after Trump conflict-report
stories.summary: The top US diplomat in Kyiv, serving as acting ambassador, announced plans to resign following a Trump administration conflict report. A State Department spokesman denied that policy disagreements were behind the departure.

stories.title: Social media abuzz as bees colonise bike outside the Louvre Museum
stories.summary: A video posted by a cyclist in Paris showed tens of thousands of bees colonising a bicycle parked outside the Louvre Museum. Experts note that such bee swarm events are not uncommon in Paris.

stories.title: French film show: 'The Silent Run' tells a tragic migrant story
stories.summary: Director Marta Bergman's film "The Silent Run" depicts a harrowing real incident faced by migrants and refugees. The French film show also reviewed Alain Gomis's "Dao," set in Guinea-Bissau, and a comedy starring Laure Calamy and Vincent Macaigne.

stories.title: Mali junta chief makes first appearance since rebel attacks
stories.summary: Mali's military junta leader made his first public appearance since large-scale weekend attacks by jihadists and Tuareg separatists destabilised the regime, visiting wounded personnel and meeting Russia's ambassador. Insurgent forces remain positioned in northern Mali, with Moscow acknowledging the situation remains difficult.

stories.title: Ukrainian Navy unit strikes sanctioned tanker MARQUISE
stories.summary: A Ukrainian Navy unit struck the sanctioned tanker MARQUISE, sailing under a Cameroonian flag, using two kamikaze unmanned surface vessels. The attack targeted a vessel already subject to international sanctions.

stories.title: Drone diplomacy wins Ukraine valuable allies, but now it must deliver
stories.summary: Analysts say the Iran war has underscored the centrality of drones in modern warfare, giving Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy a valuable diplomatic asset. Ukraine's drone expertise has helped it win allies, but delivering on partnerships remains a challenge.

stories.title: World Boxing allows Russian, Belarusian boxers to compete as neutrals
stories.summary: World Boxing announced that Russian and Belarusian athletes will be permitted to compete in its events as neutral participants, without national flags, anthems, logos, or uniforms.

stories.title: Two Jewish men stabbed in north London as Starmer condemns ‘appalling antisemitic attack’ – latest updates
stories.summary: A 45-year-old man was arrested after two Jewish men were stabbed in Golders Green, north London. Counter Terrorism Policing is leading the investigation to establish the full circumstances and any potential links to terrorism. Prime Minister Starmer condemned the incident as an "appalling antisemitic attack."

stories.title: Palestinian couple nabbed on suspicion of living under fake Israeli identity for 20 years
stories.summary: Israeli police detained a Palestinian couple suspected of living under a stolen Israeli identity for approximately 20 years. The pair allegedly purchased an Arab Israeli woman's ID and maintained a double life between the West Bank and the city of Rahat.

stories.title: Revenue jumps for China’s Cambricon, MetaX amid thirst for domestic AI chips
stories.summary: Chinese AI chip designers Cambricon and MetaX reported strong first-quarter revenue growth, driven by surging domestic demand for home-grown computing power. Cambricon's revenue rose 160 percent year-on-year to 2.89 billion yuan amid US export-control concerns and China's self-sufficiency push.

stories.title: “Unyielding resolve is needed for the defense of Ukraine”: King Charles to US Congress
stories.summary: King Charles addressed the US Congress, invoking the historic US-UK wartime alliance to call for sustained support for Ukraine's defense. He warned against nations turning 'ever more inward looking.'

stories.title: Price of oil rises as Iran talks remain stalled and Strait of Hormuz closed
stories.summary: Oil prices have risen as US-Iran nuclear negotiations remain stalled and the Strait of Hormuz continues to be blockaded by the US. Qatar has warned of a 'frozen conflict' if no resolution is reached.

stories.title: Mapping the armed groups and alliances in Mali
stories.summary: Mali's security landscape includes numerous armed political organizations with varying tribal, ethnic, and ideological affiliations. A mapping effort details these groups and their alliances across the country.

stories.title: More Ukrainian drones are hitting Russian supply lines. The hardened targets are fine.
stories.summary: Ukraine has expanded its drone strikes deeper into Russian territory, targeting vulnerable supply and logistics lines. However, many of the drones reportedly lack sufficient destructive power against hardened targets.

stories.title: Inside Ukraine's drive to defeat the dreaded Shahed drone
stories.summary: In Ukraine's Kharkiv region, soldiers operate from a van equipped with screens and interceptor drones to counter Russian Shahed drones. The effort reflects Ukraine's ongoing drive to develop defences against the Iranian-made unmanned aerial vehicles that have been used extensively in the conflict.

stories.title: Kosovo set for another snap election after failure to elect president
stories.summary: Kosovo is headed for another snap election after its parliament failed to elect a new president on Tuesday. The political crisis plunges Europe's youngest nation into renewed uncertainty as lawmakers in Pristina were unable to reach agreement on a candidate.

stories.title: Afghanistan: Shiite and other minorities living in fear
stories.summary: An attack on a Shiite place of worship in Herat, Afghanistan, killed at least 11 people. Despite Taliban pledges to protect minorities, Shiite communities report growing feelings of structural vulnerability.

stories.title: UK refineries asked to maximise jet fuel production amid supply fears
stories.summary: The UK government asked British refineries to maximise jet fuel production as part of contingency planning amid fears that the Iran war could cause supply disruptions grounding aircraft. Energy minister Michael Shanks said the government is monitoring jet fuel stocks and coordinating with airlines, airports, and fuel suppliers.

stories.title: Colombian election reflects on ‘total peace’ promise as violence surges again
stories.summary: Colombia's upcoming election is forcing a reckoning with President Gustavo Petro's "total peace" promise as guerrilla violence surges again. The 2016 peace deal with the FARC reduced conflict but was rejected by dissident factions, and subsequent administrations slowed its implementation.

stories.title: ‘Ceasefire on paper’: Conricus warns Iran, Hezbollah, and Hamas are using the pause to prepare
stories.summary: Former IDF spokesperson Jonathan Conricus warned that Iran, Hezbollah, and Hamas are using the current ceasefire period to regroup and prepare for future conflict. He argued that Israel faces unresolved fronts in Iran, Lebanon, and Gaza, and that degraded adversaries could recover if not decisively defeated.

stories.title: Ukraine faces risk of tougher EU loan terms to get aid payouts
stories.summary: Ukraine faces the prospect of tougher conditions on EU loans needed to secure continued aid payouts. Discussions have focused on potential changes to a preferential tax regime currently benefiting some Ukrainian companies.

stories.title: Why has the UAE left Opec and what impact will its departure have?
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced its departure from OPEC, dealing a significant blow to the oil cartel amid the Iran war energy crisis. The move challenges Saudi Arabia's leadership of the organization at a time of historic disruption in global energy markets.

stories.title: Russia scales back Moscow Victory Day parade, blaming threat from Ukraine
stories.summary: Russia announced it will scale back its annual Victory Day military parade in Moscow, excluding military vehicles and cadets. Officials cited a security threat from Ukraine as the reason.

stories.title: Families sue OpenAI over failure to report Canada mass shooter’s behavior on ChatGPT
stories.summary: Families of seven victims of a mass shooting at a secondary school in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia, are suing OpenAI and its CEO in a San Francisco federal court. The lawsuits allege OpenAI employees flagged shooter Jesse Van Rootselaar's troubling ChatGPT conversations months before the attack but failed to alert authorities.

stories.title: Why China may benefit from the UAE’s Opec withdrawal amid Iran war oil crisis
stories.summary: The UAE, OPEC's third-largest producer, will formally leave the bloc on May 1. Analysts suggest China could benefit from additional oil supply as global markets face strain three months into the US-Israeli war in Iran. UAE Energy Minister Suhail Mohamed al-Mazrouei stated it was the "right time" to exit.

stories.title: Israel and Lebanon’s complicated talks: Is Hezbollah’s disarmament possible? - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece examined the prospects for Hezbollah's disarmament amid ongoing Israel-Lebanon negotiations. The author argued that direct face-to-face talks between the two countries are long overdue.

stories.title: Ukraine’s border guards curb draft evasion routes, bust 80 smuggling rings
stories.summary: Ukraine's border guards dismantled 80 criminal smuggling networks and detained approximately 3,000 people in the first three months of 2026. The operations targeted groups facilitating illegal border crossings, largely linked to men attempting to evade military conscription.

stories.title: India, U.K. need to simplify their regulatory mechanisms: London’s Lady Mayor
stories.summary: London's Lord Mayor Dame Susan Langley, during her first visit to India, emphasized that both India and the United Kingdom need to simplify their regulatory mechanisms and understand each other's markets more strategically.

stories.title: New petition seeks 'accountability' from UK over role in Israel-Palestine
stories.summary: A 400-page legal petition has been filed in the UK seeking reparations, a formal apology, and the release of historical documents related to Britain's role in the creation of Israel and its impact on Palestinians.

stories.title: Hegseth to be grilled by Congress for first time since Iran war began
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth faces his first congressional questioning since the Iran war began. Democrats are expected to press him on the war's escalating costs, depletion of critical munitions, and a school bombing that killed children.

stories.title: Iphigenia: A brutal reckoning with war, power, and sacrifice
stories.summary: A review of the play 'Iphigenia' at London's Arcola Theatre describes how the production reinterprets Euripides' ancient Greek tragedy of sacrifice as a reflection on modern warfare and power.

stories.title: Robert Mugabe's son to be deported from South Africa over firearms offence
stories.summary: Robert Mugabe's 28-year-old son faces deportation from South Africa over a firearms offence. He was arrested in February after a shooting incident at his home in Johannesburg.

stories.title: Ugandan authorities arrest dozens in crackdown on illegal migration
stories.summary: Ugandan authorities have arrested dozens of foreigners since Monday in an intensified crackdown on illegal migration. Operations targeted groups in the north of the country and a closed compound.

stories.title: US lawmakers to grill Pentagon chief on Iran war
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is set to face questioning from lawmakers on Wednesday, marking his first congressional testimony since the Trump administration launched military operations against Iran.

stories.title: US gas prices hit $4.23 high as Hormuz fears drive oil surge
stories.summary: Average US gasoline prices reached $4.23 per gallon, the highest since 2022 and a record since the start of the war with Iran, according to AAA. Brent crude rose to $114.60 per barrel, up nearly 25 percent from mid-April lows, driven by fears of a blockade at the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Rains revive Iraq’s wetlands after years of drought
stories.summary: Heavy rainfall is restoring Iraq's Huwaizah Marshes, an ancient wetland ecosystem that had suffered years of severe drought and environmental degradation.

stories.title: Israelis divided over outcome of recent wars, political leadership - study
stories.summary: A new study found that a plurality of Israeli citizens view Israel as stronger following recent wars, though nearly a third believe the country has been weakened. Respondents were also divided in their assessments of Israel's political leadership during the roughly five-week conflict.

stories.title: Shell CEO says blockade may mean energy shortages last into 2027
stories.summary: Shell's CEO warned that energy shortages caused by the ongoing blockade could persist into 2027. Brent crude rose 2.8 percent as US-Iran negotiations showed little sign of progress.

stories.title: Indian Muslims say they're being targeted as millions of voters deleted from rolls
stories.summary: India's Election Commission deleted over 55 million voters from electoral rolls as part of a Special Intensive Revision aimed at removing duplicates and deceased voters. The exercise has become a political flashpoint in West Bengal, where 9 million voters were removed ahead of a crucial state election, with Indian Muslims alleging they are being disproportionately targeted.

stories.title: Israel accused of using 'water as a weapon' against Palestinians in Gaza
stories.summary: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) has accused Israel of deliberately depriving Palestinians in Gaza of water access, describing the practice as an integral part of what the organization calls Israel's genocide.

stories.title: Von der Leyen confirms first EUR 6 billion tranche for Ukraine to procure drones
stories.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen confirmed that Ukraine will receive EUR 6 billion by the end of the second quarter of 2026 to procure domestically produced drones for its Defense Forces. The funding is part of a broader €90 billion loan package.

stories.title: Purdue Pharma to be dissolved as judge approves criminal sentence in opioid case
stories.summary: A federal judge approved a criminal sentence for Purdue Pharma, the maker of OxyContin, clearing the way for a sweeping legal settlement resolving thousands of opioid-related lawsuits. The company is set to be dissolved by week's end and replaced by a new entity focused on combating the opioid crisis.

stories.title: South Africa deports and fines Mugabe’s son after employee shot at family home
stories.summary: A South African court fined and ordered the deportation of Bellarmine Chatunga Mugabe, the youngest son of former Zimbabwean president Robert Mugabe, over immigration and firearms-related offences. The charges were unrelated to an earlier incident in which an employee was shot at the Mugabe family home in Johannesburg.

stories.title: Iran war squeezes India's pharma supply chain
stories.summary: The US-Israel war on Iran has disrupted India's pharmaceutical supply chain, raising energy and freight costs. India's reliance on Chinese active pharmaceutical ingredients compounds the risk of higher drug prices and potential shortages.

stories.title: Israeli defence minister sanctions Gaza aid flotilla
stories.summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz signed an order imposing sanctions on the fundraising campaign behind the Global Sumud Flotilla, a convoy of approximately 100 vessels that departed from Turkey, Spain, and Italy heading toward Gaza. The ministry stated the flotilla violates UN resolutions and undermines regional settlement efforts.

stories.title: Sudan’s sexual violence as weapon of war triggers huge mental health crisis: UN
stories.summary: UN agencies and local aid groups warned that widespread use of rape and sexual violence as a weapon of war in Sudan has caused a massive mental health crisis. The conflict between the Sudanese army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces, ongoing since April 2023, has killed tens of thousands and displaced around 11 million people.

stories.title: Hit from memory costs spreads from phones to EVs as China’s BYD raises driving-tech price
stories.summary: China's BYD announced a 21 percent price increase for its DiPilot 300 high-end driver-assistance system, raising the cost to 12,000 yuan. The company attributed the hike to sharply rising global storage hardware costs, reflecting how surging memory chip prices are spreading from smartphones to electric vehicles.

stories.title: Why an era of managed Hormuz disruption wouldn’t bode well for Asia
stories.summary: Analysts warn that even if active conflict in the Gulf subsides, the Strait of Hormuz may no longer function as a reliable and politically neutral shipping route. For China and other major Asian energy importers, concerns center on whether energy flows and shipping routes will remain free from geopolitical coercion.

stories.title: Italian convicted of adultery in Egypt amid custody battle
stories.summary: Italian citizen Nancy Guerra was convicted of adultery in Egypt while engaged in a custody dispute with her dual Egyptian-Italian ex-husband over their three-year-old daughter. The child is currently unable to leave Egypt due to a travel ban.

stories.title: Paradiso 17: Hannah Lillith Assadi's novel of Palestinian exile
stories.summary: Hannah Lillith Assadi's novel "Paradiso 17" explores Palestinian exile through the character Sufien, who is based on the author's refugee father. The book examines themes of displacement and identity across generations.

stories.title: Why Beijing’s weaponised cargo ship could be a crucial player in the Taiwan Strait
stories.summary: A mainland Chinese military magazine highlighted the Zhong Da 79, a medium-sized civilian cargo ship converted to carry containerised vertical missile launchers, radar sensors, and self-defence systems. First spotted at Hudong-Zhonghua Shipbuilding's yard in Shanghai, the vessel could serve as a low-cost deterrent against foreign intervention in a Taiwan Strait conflict.

stories.title: Is Iran’s oil storage nearly full – and will it have to cut production?
stories.summary: Analysts warn that Iran may be forced to gradually reduce oil production as its storage capacity nears its limits, particularly if the US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz continues.

stories.title: Tehran's downfall: The ayatollah regime will end by October 2028 - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece predicted the collapse of Iran's clerical regime by October 2028, contrasting Tehran's public countdown clock to Israel's destruction in 2040 with what the author described as the regime's own accelerating internal decline.

stories.title: War Is Killing Ukraine’s Oligarchy
stories.summary: Analysis suggests that the ongoing war with Russia is dismantling Ukraine's oligarchic power structures. The conflict is reportedly achieving what years of anti-corruption efforts could not in reducing the influence of powerful business elites.

stories.title: Russia declares nearly 8,000 Luhansk apartments “ownerless” for “nationalization”
stories.summary: Russian occupation authorities in Luhansk have declared nearly 8,000 apartments 'ownerless,' making them eligible for seizure. Properties missing from the state registry, with unpaid utilities, or vacant for three months can be confiscated.

stories.title: Zelensky announces new phase of long-range strikes
