stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukrainian long-range weapons can now strike targets beyond 1,500 kilometers and stated that Ukraine intends to continue extending this capability.

stories.title: How Hezbollah’s fibre optic drones test Israel’s sophisticated radar system
stories.summary: Hezbollah has deployed low-cost fibre-optic-guided drones that are reportedly immune to electronic jamming and difficult for radar to detect, posing a challenge to Israel's advanced air-defense systems.

stories.title: ‘No more Mr Nice Guy’: Trump warns Iran to ‘get smart’ over stalled talks
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump criticized Iran's negotiating proposal on Truth Social, warning Tehran to 'get smart' as uncertainty grows over a fragile ceasefire between the two countries.

stories.title: Trump said prepping for extended Iran blockade, says Tehran ‘better get smart soon’
stories.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly preparing for an extended naval blockade of Iran, with the president declaring 'No more Mr. Nice Guy.' Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is set to testify before Congress for the first time since the war began.

stories.title: At least three killed, more than 10 injured in Russian attacks on Ukraine
stories.summary: Russian forces launched at least 19 attacks on Ukraine's Donetsk region and 833 across the Zaporizhia region, killing at least three people and injuring more than 10, according to Ukrainian authorities.

stories.title: What role has Russia played in Mali’s security and the Sahel region?
stories.summary: Russia has expanded its influence in Mali and the broader Sahel region through defence partnerships and military cooperation, but its role now faces growing international scrutiny.

stories.title: Terrorist killed as attack on Bannu police post thwarted
stories.summary: Police in Bannu, Pakistan, repelled an attack on the Mazanga police post early Wednesday, killing one terrorist and injuring several others. The wounded attackers were carried away by accomplices under cover of darkness.

stories.title: Skies Turn Black in Perm Region After Ukraine Reportedly Strikes Oil Pipeline Facility
stories.summary: Unverified Ukrainian media reports suggest that a Transneft oil pumping station was targeted in a morning drone attack in Russia's Perm region, causing thick black smoke to fill the skies.

stories.title: 'It's Green all the way, darling': The coming political earthquake in East London
stories.summary: The Green Party is campaigning to unseat Labour in traditionally safe seats across east London boroughs, including Newham, in upcoming local elections. Green councillors and activists say they expect significant gains. Party leader Zack Polanski has been campaigning alongside local candidates.

stories.title: Hungary inspires Israeli opposition bid to defeat Netanyahu
stories.summary: Two Israeli opposition figures have formed a joint effort to unseat Prime Minister Netanyahu, drawing inspiration from the recent ousting of Hungary's long-serving leader Viktor Orbán.

stories.title: Tropical forest loss eases in 2025 from record high, report shows
stories.summary: A report released Wednesday showed that destruction of the world's tropical forests declined in 2025 from a record high. The findings, reported from São Paulo, underscore how decisive policy measures can help protect forests despite pressures from climate change and agricultural expansion.

stories.title: Africa: China's Zero-Tariff for African Products Takes Effect May 1 - Envoy
stories.summary: China's zero-tariff policy for African products is set to take effect on May 1, 2026, as confirmed by China's Ambassador to Nigeria, Yu Dunhai. The policy was announced by President Xi Jinping in February.

stories.title: From sirens to song: Friendship forged in Israel’s shared loss - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece recounts the story of two Israeli soldiers, Yossi and Moshe, who fought together, were killed in action, and are now buried side by side on Mount Herzl in Jerusalem. Their families formed a friendship through shared grief.

stories.title: Oil prices ease after rally as UAE exits OPEC; Iran conflict, Hormuz blockade keep supply concerns high
stories.summary: Brent crude futures for June fell 1% to $111.25 per barrel after a seven-session rally, following the UAE's exit from OPEC. Ongoing concerns over the Iran conflict and the Hormuz Strait blockade continue to weigh on supply outlooks.

stories.title: Hong Kong Law Society closes firm linked to crash-for-cash scams
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Law Society ordered the immediate closure of Raymond Lam & Associates, a solicitors' firm under investigation for alleged involvement in crash-for-cash insurance scams. The society appointed Robertsons as the intervention agent to handle matters related to the closure.

stories.title: ‘Might over right’ imperils international justice, Wang Yi tells UN’s Baerbock
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met UN General Assembly President Annalena Baerbock in Beijing and called for unity in safeguarding international justice. Wang warned that multilateralism faced severe challenges from powers prioritising "might over right," in what was widely seen as a veiled critique of Washington.

stories.title: Trump pushes for extended Iran blockade, two IDF soldiers wounded
stories.summary: A Jerusalem Post news roundup reported that the Trump administration is pushing for an extended naval blockade of Iran. The briefing also noted that two IDF soldiers were wounded in a recent incident.

stories.title: Mali's Tuareg rebels vow regime 'will fall', urge Russian forces to withdraw
stories.summary: A spokesperson for Mali's Tuareg rebel group, the Azawad Liberation Front, pledged that the country's ruling military junta "will fall" following weekend attacks by Islamist insurgents and Tuareg separatists on major cities. The group called for Russian forces to withdraw from all of Mali.

stories.title: Investigations launched into young Lebanese student who asked IDF spox. to bomb her school
stories.summary: Lebanese authorities launched investigations into a young student, reportedly 14 years old, who asked an Israeli military spokesperson to bomb her school. The student alleged that Hezbollah was storing weapons beneath the school, according to Lebanese media outlet L'Orient Today.

stories.title: Israeli 'double-tap' strike kills three rescue workers in Lebanon, officials say
stories.summary: Israeli forces carried out successive airstrikes in Lebanon on Tuesday, killing three rescue workers in what officials described as a 'double-tap' strike. Five people in total were reported killed in the attacks.

stories.title: How US and Iran are playing a crypto cat-and-mouse game over sanctions
stories.summary: Iranian authorities and citizens are increasingly turning to cryptocurrencies to circumvent US sanctions, while American officials work to catch up with enforcement and tracking measures.

stories.title: Suspect arrested after two Jewish men stabbed in London's Golders Green
stories.summary: London police arrested a man after two people were stabbed in Golders Green, a largely Jewish neighbourhood in north London. The victims were treated by emergency services at the scene. The attack is the latest in a series of incidents targeting the Jewish community, including attempted arson attacks on synagogues.

stories.title: Lebanon army says Israeli strike in south kills two
stories.summary: Lebanon's army reported that an Israeli airstrike in the southern town of Khirbet Selm, in the Bint Jbeil district, killed a Lebanese soldier and his brother on Wednesday. The two were traveling by motorbike from the soldier's military post. The strike occurred despite an active ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon.

stories.title: UK: London stabbing being treated as 'terrorist incident'
stories.summary: Two men were stabbed in Golders Green, a predominantly Jewish area of north London, in an attack that UK police declared a "terrorist incident." A 45-year-old suspect was arrested after also attempting to stab officers. The victims, aged 76 and 34, are in stable condition in hospital.

stories.title: UK: 2 people stabbed in north London, suspect arrested
stories.summary: British police arrested a man after two people were stabbed in Golders Green, a north London area with a significant Jewish population. A Jewish community security organization confirmed the wounded were receiving medical treatment.

stories.title: Kim praises North Korean soldiers who blew themselves up to evade Ukraine capture
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un praised soldiers who detonated grenades to kill themselves rather than be captured while fighting alongside Russian forces in the Kursk region of western Russia. His remarks mark the first official acknowledgment of the self-detonation policy reported through intelligence and defector testimonies.

stories.title: Russia’s shadow fleet continues passing UK waters despite boarding threat
stories.summary: Despite UK Prime Minister Starmer's March 25 threat to board Russian shadow-fleet vessels, at least 98 sanctioned Russian ships transited UK waters in the following month. That figure is roughly consistent with traffic levels over the preceding three months, suggesting little deterrent effect.

stories.title: Russian forces shell 43 settlements in Sumy region over past 24 hours, casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled 43 settlements in Ukraine's Sumy region over a 24-hour period, killing one person and wounding eight others.

stories.title: Russian paramilitary carried out air strikes in Mali as rebels advanced, footage shows
stories.summary: Footage emerged showing that Russian paramilitary forces, identified as the Africa Corps, conducted air strikes in Mali as rebel forces advanced. The attacks coincided with the Africa Corps' withdrawal from a key base in northern Mali.

stories.title: Iranian officials absent from pre-World Cup football events in Canada
stories.summary: It remains unclear whether Iranian football officials received Canadian visas to attend the AFC and FIFA congresses held in Canada ahead of the 2026 World Cup. Their absence from the pre-tournament events has raised questions about potential visa restrictions.

stories.title: The UAE’s OPEC exit is not about oil; it is the end of Gulf solidarity
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced its departure from OPEC, a move widely interpreted as reflecting a deepening rift with Saudi Arabia rather than a purely oil-market decision. Analysts say the exit signals a fundamental realignment of Gulf alliances and erodes longstanding regional solidarity.

stories.title: Southeast Asia’s Mekong River being poisoned by rare earth mining
stories.summary: Rare earth mining upstream is contaminating the Mekong River and its tributaries with toxic runoff, threatening millions who depend on the waterway across Southeast Asia. In Chiang Saen, northern Thailand, fisherman Sukjai Yana reports declining catches and falling demand due to contamination fears.

stories.title: Hong Kong throws SMEs lifeline with raft of measures, HK$450 billion in loans
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities announced a package of measures to support small and medium-sized enterprises facing the global fuel crisis and Middle East geopolitical tensions. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority increased available bank lending for SMEs by 21 percent to HK$450 billion (US$78.43 billion).

stories.title: Despite everything, 'the Palestinians have not given up': Historian Rashid Khalidi
stories.summary: Palestinian-American historian Rashid Khalidi spoke to FRANCE 24 in Paris, arguing that a future basis for peace exists because millions of Palestinians will not leave their land. Khalidi, appearing at events including the Arab World Institute, emphasized that the two peoples will need to negotiate a resolution despite the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill Gaza paramedic, raid West Bank villages
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed at least two Palestinians on Wednesday in separate incidents in the occupied West Bank and the Gaza Strip. One of those killed was a paramedic in Gaza. Raids were also conducted in West Bank villages.

stories.title: America's only 'special relationship' is Israel: UK envoy to US
stories.summary: The UK ambassador to the United States stated that America's "special relationship" now lies with Israel rather than Britain. The remarks were subsequently disowned by officials in London.

stories.title: Ukrainian “Shamanbat” unit, including free Ichkeria fighters, just took out dozens of Kadyrov’s men in single operation
stories.summary: Ukraine's special unit "Shamanbat," coordinating with the 104th Territorial Defense Brigade "Horyn" and military intelligence networks, carried out drone and artillery strikes against Russia's Akhmat forces. The operation reportedly destroyed enemy transport and armored vehicles and killed several dozen Akhmat personnel.

stories.title: Liberia: National Security Advisor Fires Back At Office of War Crimes Court Chief, Denies Sabotage Claims, Warns Against 'Misinformation Campaign'
stories.summary: In Liberia, the Office of the National Security Advisor has rejected allegations by OWECC-L Executive Director Jallah A. Barbu that National Security Advisor Samuel K. Woods II obstructed and undermined the country's transitional justice process, including the establishment of a war and economic crimes court.

stories.title: King Charles visits New York after Trump says UK monarch ‘agrees with me’ on Iran – US politics live
stories.summary: King Charles III visited New York amid remarks by President Donald Trump claiming the British monarch agreed that Iran should not possess nuclear weapons. Separately, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is set to testify before the House Armed Services Committee regarding Trump's $1.5 trillion defense budget request, facing questions about the ongoing Iran conflict and its global economic impact.

stories.title: Iran rial hits record low against dollar amid US blockade
stories.summary: The Iranian rial fell to a record low of approximately 1.8 million rials per dollar on the black market, according to currency-tracking websites Bonbast and AlanChand. The decline has been driven by a continuing US naval blockade of Iranian ports. Two months ago, before the war began, the rate was about 1.7 million rials per dollar.

stories.title: EU farmers and hauliers to get up to €50,000 to cover extra costs of Iran war
stories.summary: The European Union announced emergency measures subsidising up to 70 percent of extra fuel and fertiliser costs caused by the Iran war for farmers, fishing businesses, and road hauliers. Individual companies can claim up to €50,000 each through the end of the year under loosened state aid rules.

stories.title: The EU Is the New Go-To Middle Power
stories.summary: Analysis characterises the European Union as an increasingly attractive partner for countries seeking stability in a disordered geopolitical landscape. The bloc's institutional predictability is drawing interest from nations navigating great-power competition.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia Restores Diesel Supply to Pre-Crisis Levels
stories.summary: The Ethiopian government announced it has fully restored daily diesel supply to pre-crisis levels, reaching 9 million litres per day. The announcement was made in Addis Ababa.

stories.title: Before Trump’s visit, China touts mineral dominance, fortifies resource security
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Natural Resources announced that the country holds the world's largest reserves of 14 essential minerals, including rare earths and graphite. Beijing pledged to accelerate mineral exploration during the 15th five-year plan period from 2026 to 2030, ahead of President Trump's visit.

stories.title: Nigeria: Mercedes Benz Sues Osimhen for Alleged ₦142m Debt
stories.summary: German automaker Mercedes-Benz has filed a complaint with Italian Carabinieri against Nigerian football striker Victor Osimhen. He is accused of failing to complete payments totalling approximately ₦142 million for a leased vehicle.

stories.title: France urges citizens to leave Mali as security crisis deepens
stories.summary: France has urged its nationals in Mali to leave the country immediately, citing an 'extremely volatile' security situation. The warning follows coordinated attacks that struck several Malian cities, including the capital Bamako.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones reportedly strike oil facilities in Russia, sparking fires
stories.summary: Perm Krai Governor Dmitry Makhonin confirmed that a Ukrainian drone struck an industrial site in the Perm municipal district, starting a fire. The attack targeted facilities in Russia's Perm region.

stories.title: France urges citizens to leave Mali after rebel attacks
stories.summary: France urged its citizens to leave Mali following rebel attacks in the country. The United Kingdom issued similar travel advice, warning nationals who choose to remain that they do so at their own risk.

stories.title: South Africa: Treasury Drops Diesel Levy to Zero for May
stories.summary: South Africa's Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana announced the government will drop the diesel levy to zero for May to shield drivers from a major wholesale price increase. A R3 per litre relief on petrol will also be maintained.

stories.title: Drones strike Orsk and Perm region, reports suggest oil refinery hit
stories.summary: On the night of April 29, Ukrainian drones struck an oil refinery in Orsk, Russia, and an industrial facility in the Perm Krai region. Reports suggest the attacks targeted energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Report: Katz hired unqualified political allies as consultants at Defense Ministry
stories.summary: An investigation by Israel's Channel 12 alleges that Defence Minister Israel Katz appointed unqualified political allies as consultants at the Defence Ministry. Among them was Likud operative Yair Shalom, who is reportedly suspected of credit card fraud. The hirings are linked to internal Likud primary maneuvering.

stories.title: Daily Briefing Apr. 29 – The case of the ‘stolen’ Ukrainian wheat
stories.summary: A Times of Israel daily briefing covered stalled US-Iran negotiations, a rare Palestinian vote in Gaza and the West Bank, and a former Biden administration official's use of the term "genocide." The briefing also addressed a story involving allegedly stolen Ukrainian wheat.

stories.title: Officials warn of deepening crisis amid South Sudan’s hunger emergency
stories.summary: Almost two-thirds of South Sudan's population — approximately 7.9 million people — now face severe hunger, according to new figures released Tuesday. Renewed fighting between government and opposition forces is accelerating the humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: Israel-Iran war LIVE: Tehran labels U.S. ship seizures 'piracy' in formal protest to UN Secretary-General
stories.summary: Iran formally protested to the UN Secretary-General over U.S. seizures of ships in the Strait of Hormuz, labeling the interceptions as "piracy." Tehran's envoy argued Washington's justification lacks legal standing under international law.

stories.title: U.S. Senate blocks bid to prevent Trump from military action against Cuba
stories.summary: The U.S. Senate voted to block a measure that would have prevented President Trump from taking military action against Cuba. Senator Tim Kaine argued that U.S. actions toward Cuba could themselves be considered acts of war.

stories.title: WATCH: Israel Police arrest man for attacking nun near King David's Tomb
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested a 36-year-old man in Jerusalem on Tuesday after he allegedly attacked a nun near King David's Tomb. He is being questioned on suspicion of committing a racist assault.

stories.title: Berehove’s mayor tells Magyar what Ukraine actually provides its Hungarian community
stories.summary: The mayor of Berehove addressed Hungarian politician Péter Magyar, detailing the state support Ukraine provides to its ethnic Hungarian community. The mayor outlined assistance provided at national and local government levels.

stories.title: Trump tells aides to prep for lengthy Strait of Hormuz blockade: Report
stories.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly directing aides to prepare for a prolonged blockade of the Strait of Hormuz as the US seeks to intensify economic pressure on Iran. The war between the US and Iran has entered its third month.

stories.title: Buddhist monks-in-training caught with 110kg of cannabis in Sri Lanka
stories.summary: Sri Lankan authorities arrested 22 Buddhist monks-in-training at Colombo airport after they were found carrying 110 kilograms of cannabis. The incident was highlighted in an international press review that also covered topics including internet restrictions in Russia and generational burnout trends.

stories.title: 'You'd be speaking French': King Charles roasts Trump at state dinner
stories.summary: During a White House state dinner, King Charles III joked to President Trump that without British involvement in history, Americans "would be speaking French," responding to Trump's earlier remarks that Europeans would speak German without US help in World War II.

stories.title: Russia to hold Victory Day parade without military hardware due to fears of Ukraine attack
stories.summary: Russia's defence ministry announced that the annual Victory Day parade on May 9 in Moscow's Red Square will not feature armoured vehicles or missile systems for the first time in nearly two decades. The decision was made due to concerns over potential long-range Ukrainian drone attacks.

stories.title: Watchdog urges Hong Kong Observatory to better explain typhoon warning decisions
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Audit Commission has urged the Hong Kong Observatory to improve its communication around typhoon warning decisions. The watchdog cited increasing public demand for advance notification of signal changes as extreme weather events become more frequent due to climate change.

stories.title: IDF says senior Hamas intel operative who helped plan Oct. 7 killed in Gaza strike
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces announced that Iyad Shambari, described as a senior Hamas intelligence operative who served as operations chief and helped plan the October 7 attack, was killed in a strike in Gaza. In a separate incident, a nine-year-old was killed in a strike targeting a man the IDF said posed an immediate threat to troops.

stories.title: Why UAE's OPEC exit is a blow to Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates is withdrawing from OPEC to pursue independent oil production, weakening Saudi Arabia's position within the cartel. The departure removes a key Gulf partner from the organization and adds uncertainty to OPEC's ability to manage global oil supply.

stories.title: Nigeria: Peter Obi's Running Mate to Quit Labour Party Today, Joins PRP
stories.summary: Datti Baba-Ahmed, the 2023 vice-presidential running mate of Peter Obi in Nigeria, announced his departure from the Labour Party to join the People's Redemption Party. He cited internal wrangling and a drift from the party's founding ideals as reasons for leaving.

stories.title: Nigeria: Gunmen Invade Ekiti Church, Kill Pastor, Kidnap Worshippers
stories.summary: Gunmen attacked a church on the outskirts of a community in Ekiti State, Nigeria, during a crusade. The assailants killed the presiding pastor and kidnapped several worshippers.

stories.title: Europe climate report signals rising extremes
stories.summary: A European climate report highlighted rising weather extremes across the continent, signaling an urgent need to adapt to global warming. The findings also stressed the importance of accelerating the transition to clean energy sources.

stories.title: Has Russia lost influence in Mali after rebel advances in Kidal?
stories.summary: Rebel advances in Kidal, Mali, have raised questions about Russia's influence in the country following the withdrawal of its Africa Corps forces. The developments follow weekend clashes that challenged Moscow's military and political foothold in the West African nation.

stories.title: Ikea to open first small-format Beijing store to tap China’s changing consumer trends
stories.summary: Ikea is opening its first small-format store in Beijing, shifting strategy toward convenience and efficiency in China. The move follows the closure of seven large outlets across mainland China in early February amid changing consumer trends and a sluggish property market.

stories.title: Unexploded landmines a hidden threat for residents in Sudanese capital
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of residents have returned to Khartoum, Sudan, since the army recaptured the capital from the Rapid Support Forces in March of the previous year. Unexploded landmines scattered across the city now pose a serious hidden threat to returning civilians.

stories.title: Trump says King Charles does not want Iran to have nuclear weapon
stories.summary: At a White House state dinner honoring King Charles and Queen Camilla, President Trump claimed the British monarch agreed that Iran should never possess nuclear weapons. King Charles did not address Iran or the war in his own public remarks at the event.

stories.title: US denies funding DR Congo paramilitary mine guard
stories.summary: The United States denied funding paramilitary units tasked with securing mines in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The denial came one day after Kinshasa announced the creation of a dedicated mining guard force.

stories.title: Swearing banned by one in five councils in England and Wales, finds report on ‘busybody’ fines
stories.summary: A report by the Campaign for Freedom in Everyday Life found that one in five local councils in England and Wales now ban swearing through public spaces protection orders, up from one in twenty in 2022. The orders, originally designed to address serious anti-social behaviour, are reportedly being used to criminalise activities such as standing in groups, shouting, and picking up stones.

stories.title: Russian attacks injure two in Odesa region, spark fire in nature reserve
stories.summary: A massive Russian attack on the southern Odesa region injured two people and sparked a fire in a nature reserve.

stories.title: Report: Russian veterinary official who oversaw livestock seizures found dead
stories.summary: The head of a department at the Novosibirsk regional veterinary authority, who oversaw livestock seizures, has been found dead. The Novosibirsk outlet Sibirsky Express reported the death, which was confirmed by his wife, Yelena Tur.

stories.title: Trump says Iran 'better get smart soon'
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump warned Iran to "get smart soon" as diplomatic efforts between Washington and Tehran to end hostilities remained at a standstill. Trump posted the message on Truth Social, criticizing Iran's inability to agree to a non-nuclear deal.

stories.title: Technology Russia and Ukraine refined on their battlefield just hit Israeli Black Hawk in Lebanon
stories.summary: A fiber-optic guided drone, using technology refined on the Russia-Ukraine battlefield, reportedly struck an Israeli Black Hawk helicopter in Lebanon. Fiber-optic drones transmit signals through a physical wire, making them immune to electronic warfare jamming.

stories.title: European Commission president calls for diplomacy to end Iran war
stories.summary: The president of the European Commission called for a diplomatic resolution to the ongoing war involving Iran. The statement emphasized the need for negotiations to bring the conflict to an end.

stories.title: Germany arrests Kazakhstan citizen accused of spying for Russia
stories.summary: German authorities arrested a Kazakhstani citizen identified only as Sergej K. on suspicion of espionage for Russia. Prosecutors allege the suspect maintained continuous contact with Russian intelligence services.

stories.title: Evidence of what may be world’s oldest cremation found in Ethiopia, new study reveals
stories.summary: Researchers in Ethiopia have discovered burnt bone fragments that may represent the world's oldest known cremation. The Homo sapiens fossils were found in sediment at the Faro Daba beds in the Dawaitoli Formation.

stories.title: ‘You'd be speaking French’: King Charles roasts Trump at state dinner
stories.summary: At a White House state dinner, King Charles III quipped to President Trump that without Britain, Americans would be speaking French — a retort to Trump's previous remarks that Europeans would speak German without U.S. intervention in World War II.

stories.title: Is the Kremlin losing its grip on Mali and the Sahel?
stories.summary: A joint offensive by Tuareg separatists and the Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) in Mali has highlighted the limitations of Russia's security guarantees to Assimi Goïta's military junta and the broader Alliance of Sahel States.

stories.title: Pentagon faces scrutiny over lack of details on Minab girls' school strike in Iran
stories.summary: The Pentagon faces growing scrutiny over its lack of transparency regarding a strike on a girls' school in Minab, Iran, on February 28 during Operation Epic Fury. Iranian officials say the strike killed 168 people, including approximately 110 children.

stories.title: Trump says Iran seeks blockade end, Gulf pushes to reopen Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump stated that Iran has asked to lift the US blockade and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, but Washington plans to maintain pressure. Gulf leaders are simultaneously pushing for the restoration of shipping through the vital waterway.

stories.title: Ukraine claims to have intercepted 30,000 drones in March
stories.summary: Ukraine claimed to have intercepted 30,000 Russian drones in March alone. Ukrainian interceptor drones have emerged as one of the most cost-effective defensive tools, turning Russia's aerial campaign into a costly war of attrition.

stories.title: Iran war drives jet fuel surge, disrupts travel routes, testing European airlines
stories.summary: The Iran war has caused a surge in jet fuel prices, disrupting travel routes and straining European airlines. Willie Walsh, head of the International Air Transport Association, warned of potential fuel rationing in Asia and Europe.

stories.title: Russia to mark war anniversary with parade, but no equipment
stories.summary: Russia's Defence Ministry announced it will hold a military parade on Moscow's Red Square next month to mark victory over Nazi Germany but will not display military equipment, citing the operational situation related to the ongoing war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Russia says burning oil spill at refinery struck by Ukrainian drones has been contained
stories.summary: Russian authorities said they have contained a burning oil spill in Tuapse caused by Ukrainian drone strikes on an oil refinery there. Emergency Situations Ministry head Alexander Kurenkov confirmed the containment at an operational headquarters meeting in the city.

stories.title: Russia’s Victory Day parade goes without armor in 2026 after losing 24,486 combat vehicles in Ukraine
stories.summary: Russia's 2026 Victory Day parade in Moscow proceeded without armored vehicles, after having lost 24,486 combat vehicles in the war in Ukraine. The parade has traditionally served as a major display of Russian military power.

stories.title: DNA links Florida man in Philippines to 1989 child abduction
stories.summary: Young Tom Talmadge, 69, was arrested in the Philippines in connection with the 1989 kidnapping and sexual abuse of a 7-year-old girl in the Tampa, Florida, area. Investigators used preserved DNA evidence and genealogical research to identify Talmadge as the suspect decades after the crime.

stories.title: CEOs of US’s top energy firms received average pay raise of $12.3m, review finds
stories.summary: A review of financial documents found that CEOs of major US utility companies received an average pay raise of 16% last year, bringing average compensation to $12.3 million. Meanwhile, utility bills have risen as much as 40% in some regions since 2021, driven by inflation, the Iran war, and datacenter growth, and utilities disconnected power to customers 13 million times in 2025.

stories.title: In a fragmenting global order, former Japanese leader urges pivot to China
stories.summary: Former Japanese Prime Minister Yukio Hatoyama called on Japan and China to jointly confront what he described as 'US arrogance' under President Donald Trump. Speaking at an event in Hong Kong, Hatoyama urged both nations to manage bilateral relations and prevent a collapse of the world order.

stories.title: China boy, 6, discovers lump in throat that was initially thought to be ‘undeveloped twin’
stories.summary: A six-year-old boy in China named Xiaoliang was found to have an egg-sized tumour in his throat after months of heavy snoring and difficulty eating. He was referred to the Children's Hospital of Fudan University in Shanghai after his local hospital was unable to treat the condition.

stories.title: Enemy drones strike Kharkiv and suburbs overnight, injuring six people
stories.summary: Six people were injured in Kharkiv and its surrounding suburbs during a Russian drone attack on the night of April 29.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills 5 family members in Lebanon despite truce
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike on the town of Jebchit in southern Lebanon killed five members of the same family despite a ceasefire with Hezbollah. Israel has reportedly violated the truce on a daily basis since April 16, launching repeated airstrikes and demolishing villages in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill five people across Gaza in last 24 hours
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed at least five people and injured seven across Gaza in the past 24 hours despite an ongoing ceasefire, according to the Palestinian health ministry. Since the ceasefire began in October, 823 people have been killed and 2,308 wounded. The overall death toll since October 2023 has reached at least 72,599.

stories.title: Afghan women’s refugee team allowed to play in FIFA tournaments
stories.summary: FIFA granted the Afghan Women United team permission to represent Afghanistan in international football tournaments, including the upcoming Los Angeles Olympics. The team is composed of Afghan women refugees.

stories.title: Palestinian football body appeals FIFA ruling on Israel at top sports court
stories.summary: The Palestinian Football Association filed an appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport against a FIFA ruling concerning Israel. Separately, visa issues are reportedly affecting Palestinian and other delegations traveling to the upcoming FIFA Congress.

stories.title: Rights groups hail Indonesia’s ‘new chapter’ for domestic workers, warn of long road ahead
stories.summary: Indonesia's House of Representatives passed a domestic worker protection bill into law on April 21, twenty-two years after it was first proposed. Rights groups praised the legislation as a "new chapter" for millions of domestic helpers but cautioned that implementation challenges remain.

stories.title: Middle power moment
stories.summary: Pakistan's role as a mediator in the US-Iran conflict has drawn international attention and recognition as a middle power. However, analysts question the sustainability of this diplomatic position given deep geopolitical fault lines.

stories.title: Airlines worldwide cancel flights, raise fares amid Middle East conflict
stories.summary: Low-cost airlines including Ryanair, Transavia, and Volotea are canceling flights and raising fares due to soaring jet fuel prices caused by the Middle East conflict. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has removed a significant portion of global oil supplies from the market, triggering fuel shortage fears across the aviation industry.

stories.title: King Charles, Trump toast ties despite Iran tensions
stories.summary: King Charles III and President Donald Trump celebrated U.S.-UK ties at a White House state dinner on Tuesday. However, the event was shadowed by Trump's claim that the monarch agreed with his position on preventing Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Russian forces kill two residents and wound three others in Donetsk region over past 24 hours
stories.summary: Russian forces killed two residents and wounded three others in Ukraine's Donetsk region over a 24-hour period on April 28.

stories.title: Mali's embattled junta chief says situation 'under control'
stories.summary: Mali's military leader Assimi Goïta made his first public address since unprecedented coordinated attacks by jihadists and Tuareg separatists over the weekend, insisting the situation was "under control." He acknowledged the attacks constituted a situation of "extreme gravity," with armed groups still positioned in the country's north.

stories.title: United Arab Emirates will leave OPEC in a blow to the oil cartel
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced it will leave OPEC effective May 1, removing the cartel's third-largest producer. The UAE had been pushing back against production quotas it considered too restrictive, wanting to sell more oil on the global market.

stories.title: Indian billionaire's son offers home for Escobar's hippos
stories.summary: Anant Ambani, son of Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani, formally requested Colombia's government to halt the killing of hippos descended from Pablo Escobar's collection. He offered to relocate the animals, which have caused ecological damage to Colombian rivers.

stories.title: U.S. imposes sanctions on 35 individuals, entities for aiding Iran's sanctions evasions
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department imposed sanctions on 35 individuals and entities for helping Iran evade existing sanctions. The designations target mechanisms Tehran uses to receive payments for oil and other commodities.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill 8 in Lebanon: Violence continues despite ongoing ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed eight people on Tuesday, including civil defense rescuers, and wounded two soldiers, according to Lebanon's health ministry, despite an ongoing ceasefire. The Israeli military said it discovered and destroyed a large Hezbollah tunnel network used by elite fighters in the area.

stories.title: King Charles highlights US-UK bond during busy day of diplomacy with Trump and Congress
stories.summary: King Charles III addressed a joint session of the U.S. Congress, marking the 250th anniversary of American independence and celebrating the U.S.-UK alliance. He urged against isolationism while highlighting historical and cultural ties, delivering nuanced warnings alongside optimistic rhetoric.

stories.title: Somalia: Somaliland Elders Extend Parliament Terms, Draw Criticism
stories.summary: Somaliland's House of Elders approved a 27-month extension of the mandates of the House of Representatives and local councils. The extension exceeds timelines proposed by both the government and the National Electoral Commission, drawing criticism.

stories.title: Inside France’s role in countering Iranian drone and missile attacks
stories.summary: French fighter pilots deployed in the Middle East have been intercepting Iranian drones and missiles as part of an expanded mission. Commanders initially sent for counterterrorism operations saw their role shift after the conflict escalated on February 28. Several pilots spoke publicly about their experience for the first time.

stories.title: Trump tells aides to prepare for extended blockade of Iran, WSJ reports
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that President Trump has instructed aides to prepare for an extended blockade of Iran. Trump reportedly believes maintaining the blockade carries less risk than either withdrawing or restarting active military conflict.

stories.title: Why is the UAE choosing to leave OPEC?
stories.summary: OPEC faces a dual crisis from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the UAE's departure from the cartel effective May 1. The UAE's exit removes a major producer from the organization amid an ongoing energy shock caused by the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Ukrainian Navy “Angels” extract Russian-tortured civilian helper from occupied Zaporizhzhia Oblast
stories.summary: Ukrainian Navy special operations personnel extracted a civilian from Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia Oblast who had hidden wounded Ukrainian troops and passed intelligence. The man had been detained, tortured, and sentenced to over five years by Russian occupation authorities.

stories.title: New Zealand officials reject statue remembering Japan’s WWII sex slaves
stories.summary: New Zealand officials rejected an application to install a statue commemorating World War II "comfort women" after Japan suggested it could harm diplomatic relations. Japan forced up to 200,000 women from Korea, China, and Southeast Asia into sexual slavery from 1932 to 1945.

stories.title: Trump says King Charles does not want Iran to have nuclear weapon
stories.summary: During King Charles III's state visit to Washington, President Trump claimed the British monarch agreed that Iran should not possess nuclear weapons. The visit came amid strained UK-US relations, with Trump criticizing Prime Minister Keir Starmer over the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Pentagon chief to testify on Iran war
stories.summary: US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth is set to testify before the House Armed Services Committee on President Trump's $1.5 trillion defense budget request. The hearing comes as lawmakers from both parties seek answers on the unresolved Iran war and its global economic impact.

stories.title: Consequences of Iran war ‘may echo for months or years to come,’ EU chief warns – Europe live
stories.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen warned that the consequences of the Iran war may reverberate for months or years. Separately, EU officials in Brussels expressed cautious optimism about Hungary's new leader Péter Magyar and his efforts to reset ties and unlock frozen EU funds.

stories.title: Ukraine targets Druzhba pipeline to sever Russian oil, influence in EU
stories.summary: Ukraine is targeting the Druzhba oil pipeline to cut off Russian oil supplies still flowing to Hungary and Slovakia. Kyiv sees an opportunity to pressure Brussels as both EU member states continue purchasing Russian crude despite broader European efforts to reduce dependence on Moscow's energy exports.

stories.title: None more deserving of FIFA Peace Prize than Trump, says White House
stories.summary: The White House endorsed President Trump for FIFA's Peace Prize, claiming his "Peace through Strength foreign policy" had ended eight wars in less than a year.

stories.title: Growth to stability
stories.summary: Pakistan's State Bank raised its key policy rate by 100 basis points to 11.5 percent, shifting focus from growth support to macroeconomic stability amid re-emerging inflation and external risks linked to the Gulf crisis.

stories.title: Hungary's Magyar meets EU's von der Leyen in high-stakes Brussels visit
stories.summary: Hungarian opposition leader Peter Magyar met European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in Brussels ahead of taking office as prime minister. Magyar is seeking to unlock €10 billion in frozen EU funding before an August deadline as part of a post-Orbán reset of Hungary-EU relations.

stories.title: White House drafts guidance to bypass Anthropic's risk flag for new AI models: Report
stories.summary: The White House reportedly drafted guidance to bypass a safety risk flag raised by AI company Anthropic for its new models. Anthropic had previously clashed with the Pentagon after refusing to remove guardrails against using its AI for autonomous weapons or domestic surveillance.

stories.title: Youth hostel scheme falls short as only 44% of expected flats offered: audit
stories.summary: A Hong Kong Audit Commission report found that only 44% of expected flats under the Youth Hostel Scheme were offered, falling well short of government supply and construction targets. The review covered seven hostels, including two that were completed and operational.

stories.title: Trump warns aides US planning for 'extended blockade of Iran'
stories.summary: The United States is reportedly preparing for an extended blockade of Iran, with President Trump favoring sustained economic pressure over renewed military strikes or disengagement. The Wall Street Journal reported that Trump views maintaining the blockade as less risky than the alternatives.

stories.title: Two dead after small plane crashes into Australia airport hangar
stories.summary: A small plane crashed into a hangar at Parafield Airport in Adelaide, Australia, killing two people. The aircraft burst into flames upon impact.

stories.title: Lloyds takes £151m hit from Iran war as it forecasts rise in UK unemployment
stories.summary: Lloyds Banking Group reported a £151 million financial hit linked to the economic fallout from the Middle East conflict. The bank forecast UK GDP growth of just 0.5% for the year, below the IMF's 0.8% prediction, citing stagflationary pressures including rising unemployment and inflation.

stories.title: Israel in Lebanon: Is the 'security buffer zone' legal?
stories.summary: Israel has maintained a security buffer zone in southern Lebanon, raising questions about its legality. International humanitarian law provides limited clarity on the rules governing such zones in contemporary warfare.

stories.title: British Muslims oppose the war on Iran? No kidding, so do most Brits
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that opposition to the war on Iran among British Muslims reflects broader British public sentiment, with a recent march drawing half a million participants. Right-wing think tanks have been accused of attempting to frame Muslim opposition as disloyal rather than representative of mainstream opinion.

stories.title: 3-year-old rescued after falling into 18-metre-deep well in Syria
stories.summary: A three-year-old child was rescued after falling into an 18-metre-deep well in Syria. Details of the rescue operation and the child's condition were not immediately elaborated upon.

stories.title: Minister dismisses Labour rebels as ‘usual suspects’; Starmer prepares for final PMQs before recess – UK politics live
stories.summary: The UK Treasury is reportedly considering a one-year rent freeze on private sector homes as part of its response to economic disruption caused by the Iran war. Chancellor Rachel Reeves declined to rule out the measure, while Downing Street said there were "no plans" for such a policy.

stories.title: The Taiwan Evacuation Trap
stories.summary: On April 25, armed groups including jihadist organization JNIM and Tuareg separatist forces launched near-simultaneous attacks on military installations across Mali, striking targets in Bamako, Gao, Mopti, and Kidal. Analysts describe the coordinated offensive as the result of a deteriorating security trajectory in the Sahel following Western military withdrawal.

stories.title: US supreme court to hear whether protected status of Haitians and Syrians can be revoked
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court will hear oral arguments on whether the Trump administration can revoke Temporary Protected Status for hundreds of thousands of Syrians and Haitians. TPS allows people to live and work in the U.S. when their home countries are deemed unsafe due to war, instability, or natural disasters.

stories.title: King Charles, Trump toast ties despite Iran tensions
stories.summary: At a White House state dinner, Britain's King Charles III and President Donald Trump toasted bilateral ties, though tensions over the US-Israeli conflict with Iran loomed. Trump publicly claimed Charles agreed with him that Iran should not possess nuclear weapons.

stories.title: War update: 189 combat engagements on front line over past day
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces recorded 189 combat engagements with Russian invaders along the front line over the past day on April 28. The clashes occurred across multiple sectors of the front.

stories.title: Indonesia puts four soldiers on trial over acid attack on activist
stories.summary: Indonesia has put four soldiers on trial for an acid attack on activist Andrie Yunus that burned approximately one-fifth of his body. The accused military personnel face up to 12 years in prison if convicted.

stories.title: Hong Kong surplus hits HK$11 billion as finance chief ‘monitors’ Mideast war
stories.summary: Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan revised the city's previous-year fiscal surplus to HK$11 billion, nearly four times the original estimate. Chan said the ongoing Middle East conflict had limited economic impact, with GDP growth remaining strong in the first quarter.

stories.title: Moscow’s Victory Day Parade to Be Held Without Military Vehicles for First Time in Nearly 20 Years
stories.summary: Russia's Defense Ministry announced that Moscow's Victory Day parade will be held without military vehicles for the first time in nearly 20 years, citing "the current operational situation" as the reason.

stories.title: Russia Will Not Display Military Hardware at WWII Victory Parade
stories.summary: Russia's Defense Ministry announced that no military hardware will be displayed at this year's May 9 Victory Day parade on Red Square, the first such absence since 2008, citing the operational situation in Ukraine.

stories.title: Two Israeli soldiers wounded in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed one Palestinian man, Abdul Halim Rawhi Abdul Halim Hammad, during a raid in Silwad in the occupied West Bank. The Israeli military said two soldiers were wounded during the operation and that one Palestinian was arrested. Local sources provided additional details on the overnight raid.

stories.title: Early closures hit retail sales hard
stories.summary: Pakistan's government-imposed early market closures at 8–9 PM have caused a 25–30 percent drop in formal retail sales across 35,000 outlets, amounting to a weekly Rs100 billion decline in recorded economic activity. The Chain Store Association of Pakistan warned of layoffs and business losses.

stories.title: US in tough spot as it tries to avoid deal that highlights its failures in Iran
stories.summary: The United States faces difficult options as the U.S.-Israel war in Iran extends past its eighth week, twice as long as President Trump initially predicted. Washington must choose between a prolonged economic war or risky military action to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which has become strategically valuable to Iran.

stories.title: DR Congo president orders audit of cobalt and copper export revenues
stories.summary: Democratic Republic of Congo President Felix Tshisekedi ordered an audit of cobalt and copper export revenues, citing poor oversight and capital flight as barriers preventing the country from fully benefiting from record mineral sales.

stories.title: ADF neutralizes 154 out of 171 Russian drones overnight
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces neutralized 154 of 171 Russian drones used in overnight attacks. The interception rate represented approximately 90% of the incoming unmanned aerial vehicles.

stories.title: Last Kenyan officers leave Haiti as new international security initiative begins
stories.summary: The last contingent of Kenyan police officers has departed Haiti, ending the UN-backed Multinational Security Support Mission that had been in place since 2024. A new international security initiative is set to begin.

stories.title: Netanyahu trial: Judges refuse defense request to delay testimony hearing
stories.summary: Judges in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's corruption trial rejected a defense request to delay a testimony hearing. Netanyahu's attorney Amit Hadad had asked the court to shorten Wednesday's session, citing a security matter.

stories.title: Housing policy out of sync with shifting demand, especially for smaller homes, study finds
stories.summary: A research study found that housing policy is failing to account for growth in the number of households, driving prices out of reach and pushing more families into rentals. The report highlights a particular mismatch in demand for smaller homes.

stories.title: European airlines face biggest crisis since COVID as Iran war drives up fuel costs
stories.summary: European airlines are facing their most severe crisis since the COVID-19 pandemic as the Iran war has driven jet fuel prices up nearly 84 percent. Aviation experts warn that carriers may begin rationing fuel supplies during the summer holiday season.

stories.title: ‘Particularly badly exposed’: How the Iran war is hitting the UK
stories.summary: The ongoing war with Iran is increasingly affecting the United Kingdom's economy, with growing concerns about economic disruption and potential civil unrest. The conflict shows no sign of ending, leaving British officials grappling with its widening domestic fallout.

stories.title: South Sudan: Over Half of South Sudan's Population Faces Acute Hunger Crisis
stories.summary: UN agencies reported that 7.8 million people in South Sudan face high levels of acute food insecurity, while 2.2 million children suffer from acute malnutrition. Conflict and displacement are intensifying the hunger crisis across more than half the country's population.

stories.title: Mali's leader says situation 'under control' in first address since attacks
stories.summary: Malian junta leader Assimi Goita addressed the nation for the first time since a weekend wave of attacks, declaring that "the situation is under control."

stories.title: Tehran says it reserves right to counter US ‘state-sponsored piracy’
stories.summary: Iran's UN ambassador Amir-Saeid Iravani sent a letter to the UN Secretary-General and Security Council president accusing the United States of "state-sponsored piracy" for seizing Iranian commercial vessels. He said the seizures violate international law, the UN Charter, and maritime conventions, and warned that Iran reserves the right to respond.

stories.title: Russia loses 1,180 troops, two air defense systems in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Russia's total combat losses in Ukraine from February 2022 to April 29, 2026, reached approximately 1,328,820 personnel, including 1,180 in the past day. Russian forces also lost two air defense systems during the same period.

stories.title: TotalEnergies says it has reopened Saudi refinery closed after attacks
stories.summary: French oil company TotalEnergies announced it restarted its Satorp refinery in Saudi Arabia in mid-April after the facility was shut down due to damage from air strikes during the Iran war. The refinery is now operating at a capacity of 230,000 barrels per day following repairs to undamaged units.

stories.title: France urges citizens to leave 'extremely volatile' Mali 'as soon as possible'
stories.summary: France urged its citizens to leave Mali as soon as possible, describing conditions as "extremely volatile" following weekend attacks on government targets across the country. Jihadist group JNIM and Tuareg separatists launched the coordinated strikes in multiple cities.

stories.title: IHC judge transfers draw criticism from Islamabad bar
stories.summary: The Islamabad Bar Council criticized the transfer of three judges from the Islamabad High Court, calling the move opaque and warning it could undermine judicial independence. The council demanded a structured, uniform rotation policy for judges.

stories.title: Afghanistan women can return to competition
stories.summary: FIFA approved the return of Afghanistan's women's national team to international competition. Former captain Khalida Popal said the players will become a "symbol of resilience."

stories.title: Moscow State University opens AI school tied to Putin’s daughter, with links to China and FSB oversight
stories.summary: Moscow State University presented a new artificial intelligence school as part of its broader AI ecosystem, which includes a supercomputer and an AI institute officially headed by Katerina Tikhonova, identified as Vladimir Putin's daughter. The program reportedly has links to Chinese partners and FSB oversight.

stories.title: The evolving China-Pakistan space cooperation
stories.summary: China and Pakistan are expanding their space cooperation as part of their broader strategic partnership. The collaboration reflects the longstanding "all-weather" relationship between Beijing and Islamabad.

stories.title: U.S., allies release joint statement supporting Panama's sovereignty
stories.summary: The United States and allied nations issued a joint statement supporting Panama's sovereignty, accusing China of attempting to politicize maritime trade and infringe on the sovereignty of nations in the Western Hemisphere.

stories.title: Pentagon’s Department of War name change will cost $63.8 million
stories.summary: The Pentagon's renaming from the Department of Defense to the Department of War is projected to cost $63.8 million. Critics have questioned both the expense and the symbolism of adopting a more aggressive-sounding name.

stories.title: PM meets European Union business delegation
stories.summary: A high-level European Union delegation met Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad, praising Pakistan's Middle East de-escalation efforts and pledging to strengthen trade ties. The delegation was led by Peteris Ustubs of the European Commission's Directorate-General for International Partnerships.

stories.title: Tasnim: Iranian negotiations guided by Mojtaba Khamenei, led by Qalibaf
stories.summary: Iran's Tasnim News Agency reported that ongoing negotiations are being directed by Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, with Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf personally managing the process. Qalibaf has become a central figure in Iran's wartime decision-making and diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: Aligning the U.S. and Canadian Defense Industrial Bases
stories.summary: Bellingcat geolocated and verified two new videos showing missile strikes that hit an Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps compound and an adjacent school in the city of Minab in late February. The footage, released by Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, revealed two distinct waves of bombing hitting the complex.

stories.title: Russians carry out 833 attacks on Zaporizhzhia region in one day, leaving three injured
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 833 strikes on 43 settlements in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region over 24 hours, injuring three people. The attacks targeted the city of Zaporizhzhia and surrounding areas.

stories.title: President pays tribute to Chairman Mao  in his hometown
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari visited Shaoshan, China, the hometown of Chairman Mao Zedong, during an official trip. He laid a wreath at Mao's statue and was received by senior Hunan provincial officials.

stories.title: Avdija’s breakout NBA season ends as Trail Blazers knocked out of playoffs
stories.summary: Israeli basketball player Deni Avdija scored 22 points for the Portland Trail Blazers in a playoff loss to the San Antonio Spurs, ending his breakout NBA season. The defeat eliminated the Trail Blazers from the postseason.

stories.title: J.D. Salinger asked publishers to remove mention of Jewish-Irish heritage, letters show
stories.summary: Newly revealed letters show that author J.D. Salinger asked his publishers to remove references to his Jewish-Irish heritage from the jacket of "The Catcher in the Rye" ahead of its 1951 publication.

stories.title: On last day in IHC, Justice Kayani warns of summoning PM
stories.summary: On his final day at the Islamabad High Court before his transfer, Justice Mohsin Akhtar Kayani warned he would summon Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif if the finance member of the PTA tribunal was not appointed by May 18.

stories.title: Ultra-Orthodox draft protesters storm Israel military police chief’s home
stories.summary: Ultra-Orthodox draft protesters in Israel stormed the home of the military police chief. The incident drew strong condemnation from senior military officials and political leaders across the country.

stories.title: Lagos to Abidjan: Zenith Bank’s high-stakes gamble on the WAEMU market
stories.summary: Nigeria's Zenith Bank, holding a $22.4 billion balance sheet, is expanding into the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU) market in francophone West Africa, focusing on corporate finance to overcome barriers that have stalled other Nigerian lenders in the region.

stories.title: King Charles agrees with me on Iran nuclear weapon ban, claims Trump
stories.summary: President Donald Trump claimed at a White House state dinner that King Charles agreed Iran should never be allowed nuclear weapons. The remarks are likely to cause concern among royal aides, as the British monarch traditionally maintains political neutrality. Charles did not publicly address Iran.

stories.title: UK ambassador says only special relationship US has is 'probably' with Israel
stories.summary: British Ambassador to the United States Sir Christian Turner said America's only "special relationship" is "probably Israel" rather than Britain. The remarks, made in February and reported by the Financial Times during King Charles' US visit, could embarrass the British government amid already strained UK-US relations.

stories.title: Is India’s Chabahar dream in Iran dead?
stories.summary: India's strategic investment in the Chabahar port in southeastern Iran faces growing uncertainty amid the ongoing conflict. The port has long been central to India's regional connectivity and trade ambitions, but those plans are now in serious jeopardy.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill eight in south Lebanon: Health ministry
stories.summary: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed eight people and wounded two Lebanese soldiers, according to Lebanon's Health Ministry.

stories.title: Israeli forces carry out arrests across West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli forces conducted a series of raids and arrests across multiple locations in the occupied West Bank, including Kafr Qaddum, Iktaba near Tulkarem, and Beit Ummar in the Hebron area. Multiple Palestinians were detained, including three brothers and a son in Kafr Qaddum and eight people in Beit Ummar.

stories.title: Jirga resolves to raise ‘drone deaths’ in KP Assembly
stories.summary: Lawmakers from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's merged tribal districts met at the Chief Minister's House in Peshawar and resolved to raise the issue of civilian casualties from drone strikes in the provincial assembly. The KP cabinet was scheduled to discuss the matter, followed by a grand tribal jirga.

stories.title: Bristol launches summer of activist events to become UK civil rights capital
stories.summary: Bristol launched a program of activist events on the anniversary of the 1963 Bristol bus boycott, aiming to position itself as the UK's capital of civil rights. The campaign seeks to build on the city's long history of activism and create a new social manifesto.

stories.title: Russians strike Shostka community with drones and missile, leaving one dead, others injured
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked civilian infrastructure in Ukraine's Shostka community using drones and a missile, causing large-scale fires in residential areas. One person was killed and two others were injured in the strikes.

stories.title: Ukraine, Israel trade barbs over ‘stolen’ grain
stories.summary: Ukraine and Israel entered a diplomatic row after Kyiv accused Tel Aviv of accepting shipments of grain that Russia allegedly stole from occupied Ukrainian territory. Ukraine summoned Israel's ambassador to protest the alleged deliveries.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills five from same family in southern Lebanon town
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike on the town of Jebchit in southern Lebanon killed five members of the Bahjat family overnight. The strike destroyed a residential building in the Jabal neighbourhood, and rescue teams worked through the night to recover the bodies from the rubble.

stories.title: Jewish continuity needs you. Donate to Jewish higher education - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: This article is sponsored content promoting donations to Jewish higher education institutions. It frames supporting these programs as a means of ensuring Jewish cultural continuity and developing future community leaders.

stories.title: Western Withdrawal, Jihadist Expansion: How the Sahel Became Ground Zero for Global Terrorism
stories.summary: A policy analysis highlights Washington's lack of viable options for evacuating American citizens from Taiwan during a potential crisis. The assessment underscores the strategic challenges the U.S. faces in contingency planning for the region.

stories.title: China’s EV makers to cut charging times; Tesla rival Li Auto’s expansion: 7 EV reads
stories.summary: Chinese EV and battery manufacturers showcased technologies at the Beijing Auto Show aimed at reducing charging times to under 10 minutes. The push was triggered by competition from BYD and Contemporary Amperex, with Tesla rival Li Auto also announcing expansion plans.

stories.title: Microsoft removes Israeli names for occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Microsoft updated its digital mapping services, including Bing, to replace Israeli designations such as "Judea and Samaria, Israel" with "West Bank" for locations in the occupied Palestinian territory, aligning with international law. The Arab Center for the Advancement of Social Media confirmed the changes.

stories.title: Slovenia broadcaster to skip Eurovision over Israel participation
stories.summary: RTV Slovenia announced it will not broadcast the Eurovision Song Contest this year due to Israel's participation. The broadcaster will instead air a film series titled "Voices of Palestine." Slovenia joins several other countries that withdrew after organizers decided in December to allow Israel to compete.

stories.title: Iran expected to make new offer  to ‘reluctant’ US
stories.summary: Iran is expected to present a new diplomatic proposal to the United States through Pakistani intermediaries, even as Tehran publicly maintains a defiant posture. President Trump claimed Iran asked him to lift a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran's military said it remains in a state of war.

stories.title: Which hidden gems are mainland Chinese tourists chasing this Labour Day ‘golden week’?
stories.summary: Hong Kong expects approximately 980,000 mainland Chinese visitors during the Labour Day holiday from May 1 to 5, a 7% increase from the previous year. Many travelers are opting for curated itineraries focused on exhibitions and neighborhood walks, driven by social media trends on platforms like RedNote.

stories.title: Latvian court fines businessman for attempting to violate EU sanctions against Russia
stories.summary: A Riga City Court in Latvia fined a businessman 10,140 euros for attempting to violate European Union sanctions imposed against Russia. The case involved an effort to circumvent trade restrictions.

stories.title: South Korea’s Yoon given longer sentence for obstructing justice
stories.summary: A South Korean appeals court increased former President Yoon Suk-yeol's sentence for obstructing justice from five to seven years. Yoon was convicted of using presidential security agents to block his own arrest; both he and prosecutors had appealed the original ruling.

stories.title: Hong Kong taxis, minibuses to get 2-month LPG subsidy amid soaring fuel prices
stories.summary: Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po announced a two-month subsidy of 50 HK cents per litre on liquefied petroleum gas for taxis, minibuses, and school buses starting in May. The measure aims to ease operational costs amid rising fuel prices. A separate diesel subsidy was also set to take effect.

stories.title: From the oceans into our bodies: Plastic pollution 'associated with obesity and dementia'
stories.summary: Biologist and activist Merijn Tinga, known as the Plastic Soup Surfer, discussed research linking plastic pollution to health conditions including obesity and dementia. He highlighted the disconnect between experiencing nature directly and the pervasive throwaway culture on land.

stories.title: Nine suspects killed, two cops injured in ‘CCD encounters’ across Punjab
stories.summary: Nine suspects were killed and two police officers injured in multiple encounters conducted by Punjab's Crime Control Department across the Pakistani province on Tuesday. Six of the killings occurred in Lahore's Sundar area during a raid targeting wanted robbery suspects.

stories.title: US, allies release joint statement supporting Panama’s sovereignty
stories.summary: The United States and allied nations issued a joint statement supporting Panama's sovereignty. They accused China of attempting to politicize maritime trade and infringe on the sovereignty of nations through recent actions.

stories.title: Calls for humanitarian corridor through strait of Hormuz as Iran war hits vital aid
stories.summary: Aid organizations are calling for a humanitarian corridor through the Strait of Hormuz as the U.S.-Israel war on Iran disrupts vital supply routes. Soaring oil prices and the blockade are preventing food, fuel, and medicine from reaching millions of people in need, according to NGOs.

stories.title: Indian billionaire’s son offers to house Pablo Escobar’s hippos at his private zoo
stories.summary: Anant Ambani, son of Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani, offered to transport approximately 80 hippos descended from Pablo Escobar's original collection from Colombia to his private zoo in India. He formally requested Colombia's government to halt plans to cull the animals, which have disrupted local ecosystems.

stories.title: Gene study reveals unknown human migration into South America as late as 720AD
stories.summary: A genomic study published in Nature revealed evidence of a previously unknown human migration into South America occurring around 720 AD. The migrants carried genetic markers similar to indigenous populations of Australia and the Pacific Islands. The international research team included scientists from the University of São Paulo.

stories.title: Two Kashmir brothers: One killed by rebels, another by army 26 years later
stories.summary: Two brothers from a family in Kashmir were killed decades apart — one by armed rebels and the other by Indian army forces 26 years later. The killings reflect the protracted cycle of violence in the region, leaving the family with unresolved grief and unanswered questions.

stories.title: King Charles III calls for unwavering resolve to defend Ukraine in US Congress
stories.summary: King Charles III addressed the US Congress during his visit to the United States, calling for unwavering resolve in defending Ukraine. He emphasized the need for decisive action to support Ukraine and achieve a just peace.

stories.title: Life in limbo: How Iranians navigate a state of ‘no war, no peace’
stories.summary: Residents of Tehran are navigating daily life under a fragile truce with deep economic uncertainty. The Iranian capital exists in a state described as neither full war nor genuine peace, leaving citizens in prolonged limbo.

stories.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 61 as UAE exits OPEC?
stories.summary: On day 61 of the Iran war, the UAE announced its exit from OPEC as Gulf leaders convened in Saudi Arabia. US President Donald Trump declared that Iran is in a "state of collapse" amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Two IDF soldiers wounded in West Bank overnight ops.
stories.summary: Two Israeli soldiers were wounded during overnight operations in the occupied West Bank. According to Israeli media, the attackers reportedly stabbed the soldiers, though the IDF did not confirm the exact method of attack.

stories.title: Haaretz: Israeli civilian contractors paid per building destroyed in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli newspaper Haaretz reported that civilian contractors have been carrying out demolition operations in southern Lebanon, with payment based on the number of buildings destroyed. Soldiers said army units provided protection during the work.

stories.title: 'Over-dependence on military solutions: Mali struggling in its effort to regain peace and security'
stories.summary: Political scientist Dr. Folahanmi Aina of SOAS London analyzed Mali's security crisis, arguing that Colonel Assimi Goïta's junta has over-relied on military solutions to a fundamentally multidimensional conflict. He cited the interplay between militarized governance, external partnerships, and persistent insurgent violence in the Sahel.

stories.title: US Senate blocks bid to prevent Trump from military action against Cuba
stories.summary: The Republican-led US Senate on Tuesday blocked a Democratic resolution that would have required congressional approval before President Trump could take military action against Cuba.

stories.title: After years in limbo, court lets Syrian convert live in Israel with husband, a disabled vet
stories.summary: An Israeli court ruled that a Syrian woman who converted to Judaism can live in Israel with her husband, a disabled military veteran. The Interior Ministry had repeatedly denied the couple's efforts to establish residency despite the woman's conversion and her severing of ties to Syria.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian man during raid in Silwan
stories.summary: Israeli forces shot and killed 37-year-old Abdul Halim Rawhi Abdul Halim Hammad during a dawn raid on Silwan in the occupied West Bank, according to the Palestinian health ministry. The military also conducted a wide-scale campaign of raids and arrests across the West Bank.

stories.title: Libyan court jails four human traffickers for up to 22 years, attorney general says
stories.summary: A criminal court in Tripoli, Libya, convicted four members of a trafficking gang involved in human trafficking, abductions for ransom, and torture. The attorney general's office announced sentences of up to 22 years in prison.

stories.title: SSU shows footage of massive strikes on Russian positions in Luhansk region
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service (SSU) and Defense Forces conducted large-scale strikes against Russian military positions in occupied areas of Luhansk region, releasing footage of the operation.

stories.title: Video: Netanyahu says Israel destroyed ‘massive’ tunnel in Lebanon
stories.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced in a video statement that Israel destroyed a large tunnel in Lebanon, claiming the operation targeted Hezbollah infrastructure. A Haaretz report noted that Israel has been systematically demolishing civilian buildings in southern Lebanon during the ceasefire that began on April 17.

stories.title: Europe named ‘fastest-warming continent’ in latest climate change report
stories.summary: A United Nations climate report has identified Europe as the fastest-warming continent on Earth. The continent faces severe impacts including intensifying heatwaves, more frequent wildfires, and shrinking ice cover.

stories.title: Hosting British king, Trump says Charles agrees Iran cannot have nuclear bomb
stories.summary: During a state dinner hosting British King Charles, US President Trump said Charles agreed that Iran cannot be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon. Trump declared Tehran "militarily defeated," and both leaders praised the US-UK special relationship despite tensions over the Iran war.

stories.title: Trump administration labels Australia’s media bargaining laws ‘foreign extortion’
stories.summary: The Trump administration labeled Australia's proposed media bargaining laws as "foreign extortion." The Australian plan would require Meta, Google, and TikTok to negotiate payment deals with news publishers or face a 2.25% levy. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese defended the legislation as protecting media outlets.

stories.title: US ambassador to Ukraine to step down amid stalled talks to end Ukraine war
stories.summary: Acting US Ambassador to Ukraine Julie Davis is stepping down from her post amid stalled negotiations to end the Russia-Ukraine war. She had reportedly become frustrated with President Trump's decreasing support for Ukraine.

stories.title: US ambassador to Ukraine to step down amid stalled talks to end Ukraine war
stories.summary: Acting U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine Julie Davis announced she will step down from her post and retire. Her departure comes amid stalled U.S.-brokered negotiations aimed at achieving a ceasefire and ending Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Israeli military raids towns in West Bank, injures woman
stories.summary: Israeli forces raided the villages of al-Mufaqara, at-Tuwani, and Khirbet al-Dab'a in Masafer Yatta, south of Hebron in the occupied West Bank. A Palestinian woman was injured during the raid, and soldiers reportedly entered homes and seized money from a resident.

stories.title: Malaysian Indians least likely to be scammed as they ask too many questions: police
stories.summary: Malaysian police reported that ethnic Indian Malaysians are the least likely demographic to fall victim to scams because they tend to ask extensive questions that frustrate scammers. Malaysia lost an estimated 2.7 billion ringgit ($684 million) to online scams last year, a 76 percent increase.

stories.title: Russia to hold equipment-free Victory Day parade as Ukraine war grinds on
stories.summary: Russia announced its May 9 Victory Day parade on Moscow's Red Square will proceed without military equipment for the first time since 2008, citing operational demands of the ongoing war in Ukraine. The parade marks the 81st anniversary of victory over Nazi Germany.

stories.title: Can Russia serve as an economic lifeline for Iran amid the Hormuz blockade?
stories.summary: Analysts are assessing whether Russia could serve as an economic lifeline for Iran during the US-led Hormuz blockade. While Moscow could offer some support, significant logistical challenges and high costs limit the viability of sustained Russian assistance to Tehran.

stories.title: Rightwing provocateur’s plan to register ‘Free Palestine party’ renews concern over Victoria’s voting system
stories.summary: Right-wing figure Avi Yemini announced plans to register a "Free Palestine party" in Victoria, Australia, intending to use it to funnel preferences to conservative parties in the state election. The move has renewed pressure on Labor to scrap Victoria's group voting ticket system.

stories.title: China social media account banned for forcing women to stay in tank with crocodile
stories.summary: Chinese authorities permanently banned a social media account with over 11 million followers for forcing young female live-streamers to stay in a tank with a crocodile and hold their breath underwater. The account, @Yebali, had operated for five years on the platform.

stories.title: Memorial ceremony for fallen IDF lone soldier held in US hometown, marking 30 days since passing
