stories.summary: A memorial ceremony marking 30 days since the death of IDF lone soldier Sgt. Moshe Yitzchak HaKohen Katz was held in his US hometown of New Haven, Connecticut. The 22-year-old was killed while fighting in Lebanon on March 29.

stories.title: Nigeria: Lawmakers Approve Tinubu's $516m Loan Request for Road Project
stories.summary: Nigeria's House of Representatives approved President Bola Tinubu's request for a $516 million loan to fund a road construction project. The request was conveyed in a letter read by Speaker Abbas Tajudeen during Tuesday's plenary session.

stories.title: Nigeria: UAE Withdraws From Opec, Opec+
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced its withdrawal from both OPEC and OPEC+. The UAE energy ministry confirmed the decision in a statement issued on Tuesday.

stories.title: Pentagon may be understating severity of US missile stockpile shortage - report
stories.summary: The Atlantic reported that the Pentagon may be understating the severity of a US missile stockpile shortage. Vice President Vance reportedly discussed the issue with President Trump, warning that a weapons shortfall would be extremely detrimental to American interests.

stories.title: Nigeria: Suspected Meningitis Outbreak Kills Several People in Sokoto Village
stories.summary: A suspected meningitis outbreak has killed several people in a village in Sokoto State, Nigeria. Sokoto Health Commissioner Faruk Wurno said the state government deployed health officials to investigate and provide free medications.

stories.title: Anthony Albanese rules out gas export tax on existing contracts and criticises ‘populist’ campaign
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese ruled out imposing a new tax on existing gas export contracts, saying the middle of a global fuel crisis is the wrong time to jeopardize trade partnerships with Asian nations. He criticized the campaign for a 25 percent levy on gas exports as populist.

stories.title: Israeli forces attack town in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes destroyed several houses in the southern Lebanese town of Hanin at dawn, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The strikes followed Israeli attacks on the towns of Naqoura and Khiam.

stories.title: Wednesday briefing: Where Starmer stands after another precarious day in Parliament
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces growing pressure within the Labour Party after surviving a bruising parliamentary session over his appointment of Peter Mandelson as US ambassador. With heavy local election losses expected next week, senior Labour figures are signaling unease about his leadership.

stories.title: Government vows action as landlord-tenant rows block access at Wang Fuk Court
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities pledged to intervene in landlord-tenant disputes preventing residents from retrieving belongings from fire-damaged Wang Fuk Court. Deputy Chief Secretary Warner Cheuk said the government would make alternative arrangements if access agreements were not reached.

stories.title: Peace efforts stall as US examines latest Iran proposal
stories.summary: U.S. peace efforts with Iran have stalled as Washington examines Tehran's latest proposal. President Trump has indicated reluctance to remove the Strait of Hormuz blockade without first resolving the dispute over Iran's nuclear program.

stories.title: 'You'd be speaking French': King Charles pokes fun at Trump during state dinner
stories.summary: At a White House state dinner on Tuesday, King Charles III quipped to President Trump that without Britain, Americans would be speaking French. The joke was a response to Trump's January remark that European leaders would be speaking German without US aid in World War II.

stories.title: China targets ‘zombies’ with regulatory headshots to kill off subsidised laggards
stories.summary: China's State Administration for Market Regulation launched a pilot program in seven economic hubs to force the exit of debt-laden "zombie companies" — unprofitable firms propped up by subsidies or bank loans. The initiative aims to combat local protectionism and wasteful competition.

stories.title: Burkina Faso: Burkina Faso's Dubious Military Reserve Plan
stories.summary: Burkina Faso's military government is pursuing a rapid mobilization plan to build military reserves. Human Rights Watch warned the initiative risks fueling abuses and weakening civilian protections.

stories.title: UN sanctions brother of Sudan's RSF leader, Colombian mercenaries
stories.summary: The United Nations imposed sanctions on Algoney Hamdan Daglo Musa, the younger brother of Sudan's Rapid Support Forces leader, along with three Colombian mercenaries accused of recruiting former Colombian military personnel to fight in Sudan's conflict.

stories.title: Sudan: Remembering El Fasher and Those Still Detained
stories.summary: Six months after the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) seized El Fasher, capital of North Darfur State, in a raid the UN fact-finding mission described as bearing the "hallmark of genocide," many people remain detained or missing. The violent six-day assault occurred last October.

stories.title: Mali’s junta leader says situation ‘under control’ in first appearance since attacks
stories.summary: Mali's military leader Assimi Goita made his first public appearance since coordinated insurgent attacks over the weekend, vowing to neutralize those responsible. Al-Qaeda's West African affiliate and Tuareg separatists struck Mali's main army base near Bamako and pushed Russian-backed government forces out of the strategic town of Kidal.

stories.title: Afghan students recount harrowing university strike
stories.summary: Afghan students described a missile strike on their university on Monday. Afghan officials attributed the attack to Pakistan, though details on casualties were not provided in the initial accounts.

stories.title: Hormuz crisis revives Thailand’s land bridge plan but business case still lacking
stories.summary: The Strait of Hormuz crisis has revived interest in Thailand's proposed land bridge — a road and rail corridor connecting the Gulf of Thailand to the Andaman Sea — as an alternative trade route. However, critics question the project's business case and environmental impact.

stories.title: 'Funding war crimes': HRW accuses Israel over Syria's Golan settlement plan
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch accused Israel of funding war crimes by approving a $334 million plan to settle thousands of Israeli civilians in the occupied Golan Heights. The group called on the EU, the UK, and other states to suspend trade agreements with Israel and impose restrictions on settlement-linked business.

stories.title: US Senate blocks bid to stop Trump using military against Cuba
stories.summary: The US Senate rejected an effort to prevent President Trump from using military force against Cuba. Senator Tim Kaine argued that actions the US is taking against Cuba would be considered an act of war if directed at the United States.

stories.title: ‘People assume we’re grifters’: disabled Britons report rise in abuse over blue badges
stories.summary: Disabled blue badge holders in the United Kingdom report a rise in harassment, filming, and threats from strangers who accuse them of faking their disabilities. About 3 million people in the UK hold blue badges, and growing anti-benefits rhetoric has fueled public hostility toward users of the parking scheme.

stories.title: Why Mali’s future hinges on the battle of Kidal
stories.summary: Tuareg rebels and JNIM forces recaptured the northern Malian city of Kidal, exposing vulnerabilities in Bamako's military junta and the limits of Russian military support in the Sahel region.

stories.title: DRC central bank chief André Wameso: ‘Confidence has returned’
stories.summary: Democratic Republic of Congo central bank governor André Wameso discussed the country's recent eurobond issuance, anti-money-laundering efforts, and plans to improve transparency in the national financial system.

stories.title: Sudan: Unicef Warns of Catastrophe Facing Darfur's Children 20 Years After Crisis First Shocked World
stories.summary: UNICEF warned that children in Sudan's Darfur region face a new humanitarian catastrophe two decades after the crisis first drew global attention. Violence has displaced millions across Sudan, but international focus and support remain far below previous levels.

stories.title: Tehran-Moscow flights resume after two-month suspension
stories.summary: Flights between Tehran and Moscow resumed on Tuesday after a two-month suspension caused by the US-Israeli war, according to IRNA. Iran's Mahan Air operated the first flight, with regular service set to run three times weekly. The restart followed a meeting between Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi and President Vladimir Putin.

stories.title: UN aid chief says situation in Somalia worsened by US war on Iran
stories.summary: UN relief coordinator Tom Fletcher criticized the US war on Iran during a visit to Somalia, saying the conflict has worsened conditions in the country. Fletcher highlighted the humanitarian impact of the broader regional crisis on Somali civilians.

stories.title: Trump prepares for long-term blockade of Iran, report says
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that President Trump instructed aides to prepare for a prolonged blockade of Iran aimed at pressuring its economy and oil exports. The strategy focuses on restricting shipping rather than resuming military strikes, with Trump insisting Iran commit to suspending uranium enrichment for at least 20 years.

stories.title: Trump says King Charles backs stance on Iran nuclear issue
stories.summary: President Trump stated during a White House state dinner that King Charles III supports Washington's position that Iran must not obtain a nuclear weapon. Trump said his administration was engaged in Middle East diplomacy and described the situation as progressing well.

stories.title: Iran urges UN to act over US seizure of Iranian ships
stories.summary: Iran's UN ambassador Amir-Saeid Iravani sent a letter to the UN secretary-general and Security Council president protesting the US seizure of Iranian vessels, describing the actions as piracy. He called the seizures illegal coercion and interference in lawful international trade.

stories.title: GCC holds emergency talks on security, Hormuz reopening
stories.summary: Gulf Cooperation Council leaders held an extraordinary summit in Jeddah, their first in-person meeting since the start of the war involving Iran. Discussions focused on regional security, missile and drone threats, and efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Galilee resident arrested after police seize Palestinian flags, military uniforms from his home
stories.summary: Israeli security forces arrested a 51-year-old man from the Galilee region after a search of his home uncovered Palestinian flags and military uniforms. The raid was conducted following a tip about illegal weapons possession.

stories.title: King Charles promotes US-UK unity in speech to Congress amid Iran tensions
stories.summary: King Charles III addressed the U.S. Congress, emphasizing unity between the United States and the United Kingdom amid ongoing tensions with Iran. He stressed the shared commitment to upholding democracy despite any disagreements between the two nations.

stories.title: Latvia to transfer additional CVR(T) armored combat vehicles to Ukraine
stories.summary: Latvia announced it will transfer additional CVR(T) tracked armored combat vehicles to Ukraine to support its defense efforts.

stories.title: Amber rainstorm warning issued as thunderstorms hit Hong Kong
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Observatory issued an amber rainstorm warning on Wednesday as intense thunderstorms and strong gusts hit the city. Residents were urged to seek safe shelter as heavy showers associated with upper-air disturbances persistently affected the area.

stories.title: US, Latin America countries criticise China’s retaliation over Panama Canal
stories.summary: China detained nearly 70 Panamanian-flagged ships following a Supreme Court ruling related to the Panama Canal, according to US officials. The United States and several Latin American countries publicly criticized China's retaliatory measures.

stories.title: Challenges ahead for Wang Fuk Court homeowners who reject buy-back offer
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities warned that homeowners in the undamaged Wang Chi House block of Wang Fuk Court who reject the government's buy-back offer will face long-term difficulties managing and maintaining their properties. Deputy Financial Secretary Michael Wong said invoking legislation to acquire all property titles remained a possibility.

stories.title: India’s major airlines on ‘verge of closing down’ as high fuel costs sting
stories.summary: The Federation of Indian Airlines, representing carriers including IndiGo, Air India, and SpiceJet, warned in a letter to India's Civil Aviation Ministry that major airlines are on the verge of suspending operations due to extremely high jet fuel costs. The group called for pandemic-era cost caps and fuel price reductions.

stories.title: ‘It will never cover what’s authentic’: African music industry weighs up AI risks and rewards
stories.summary: At a music industry event in Cape Verde, African delegates discussed AI's impact on the continent's music scene. Nigerian singer-songwriter Fave's experience with an unauthorized AI-generated version of her track was cited as an example, with Lagos-based entertainment lawyer Oyinkansola Fawehinmi praising her decision to release her own remix incorporating the AI elements.

stories.title: Will Israel’s use of Iron Dome to aid Arab neighbour recalibrate Mideast defence?
stories.summary: Israel reportedly deployed an Iron Dome missile defence battery and troops to the United Arab Emirates early in its war with Iran, according to Axios, citing Israeli and US officials. Analysts describe the move as a watershed moment in Middle Eastern security alignments, highlighting the growing importance of air defence cooperation.

stories.title: Rebel Wilson rejects ‘absolutely outrageous’ phone-dumping accusation as defamation trial continues
stories.summary: Actor Rebel Wilson rejected accusations in a Sydney defamation trial that she dumped her phone to avoid handing over communications. Wilson is being sued by Charlotte MacInnes, the lead actor of Wilson's directorial debut film The Deb.

stories.title: US soldier charged for threatening to ‘kill every single Jew’ inside a synagogue
stories.summary: A US soldier stationed at a base in Louisiana was charged with threatening to kill Jewish people inside a synagogue. The soldier allegedly made the threats on a messaging platform, expressing violent white supremacist views.

stories.title: Germany’s Merz ‘doesn’t know what he’s talking about’ on Iran: Trump
stories.summary: President Trump criticized German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, saying he "doesn't know what he's talking about" regarding Iran. Merz had previously criticized the U.S. strategy in Iran, claiming that Tehran was "humiliating" Washington.

stories.title: Germany’s Merz ‘doesn’t know what he’s talking about’ on Iran: Trump
stories.summary: US President Trump dismissed German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's criticism of the US strategy in Iran, saying Merz "doesn't know what he's talking about." Merz had accused Washington of being "humiliated" by Tehran during the conflict.

stories.title: Army Command: BMT program has evolved significantly over four years of war
stories.summary: Ukraine's basic military training program has been significantly overhauled since the outbreak of full-scale war, with updates occurring nearly every year. The current focus is on personnel survival and execution of assigned combat missions.

stories.title: US imposes fresh sanctions targeting Iran's covert 'shadow banking' financial network
stories.summary: The United States imposed new sanctions targeting Iran's covert shadow banking financial network. The action followed earlier sanctions on an independent refinery in China for purchasing billions of dollars' worth of Iranian oil.

stories.title: Google allows Pentagon to use its AI in classified military work
stories.summary: Google has agreed to provide the U.S. Department of Defense with API access to its artificial intelligence tools for classified military applications. Full details of the arrangement have not been disclosed.

stories.title: UK King Charles roasts Trump with colonial quip: ‘you’d be speaking French’
stories.summary: At a White House state dinner on Tuesday, UK King Charles III joked to US President Donald Trump that without the British, Americans would be speaking French. The quip referenced Trump's earlier comments suggesting European allies would be speaking German without US intervention in World War II.

stories.title: Why UAE’s exit from Opec is good news for Asia’s energy security
stories.summary: Analysts say Asia's oil-importing economies stand to benefit from the UAE's exit from OPEC, though the ongoing closure of the Strait of Hormuz limits immediate price relief. Brent crude surged to US$111 per barrel and WTI approached US$100, up sharply from pre-war levels of around US$70 and US$65 respectively.

stories.title: U.S. Marines board merchant ship in Arabian Sea suspected to be headed to Iran
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command reported that Marines boarded a merchant vessel in the Arabian Sea suspected of heading to an Iranian port. After conducting a search and confirming the ship's voyage would not include an Iranian port call, U.S. forces released the vessel.

stories.title: Tehran calls on UN Security Council to act against Israel
stories.summary: Iran's UN ambassador Amir-Saeid Iravani urged the UN Security Council to compel Israel to uphold the ceasefire in Lebanon and halt attacks on civilian infrastructure. He also called for the withdrawal of Israeli forces from Lebanon and condemned Israeli operations in Gaza, the West Bank, and the Golan Heights.

stories.title: Gaza situation remains precarious, Tony Blair tells UN
stories.summary: Former UK Prime Minister Tony Blair told the UN Security Council that Gaza's situation remains precarious despite a ceasefire and reduced violence. He noted that ceasefire violations continue but food assistance has improved and the Rafah Crossing is partially open for medical evacuations.

stories.title: Lebanon’s PM slams Israel’s ‘war crimes’ as attack kills 3 rescue workers
stories.summary: An Israeli attack in Lebanon killed three rescue workers. Lebanese Prime Minister condemned the strikes as war crimes, while President Joseph Aoun accused Israel of violating international law protecting civilians and humanitarian workers.

stories.title: US conditions for paying UN dues include China curbs, report says
stories.summary: The U.S. has reportedly set conditions for paying its United Nations dues, including measures to curb China's influence within the organization. Among the demands is blocking China from channeling funds to the office of the UN Secretary-General.

stories.title: UAE quits OPEC as oil cartel takes blow during war on Iran
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced its departure from OPEC, citing national interests. The decision deals a significant blow to the oil cartel amid the ongoing war involving Iran and broader shifts in energy policy.

stories.title: Houthis say their support for Iran is 'clear, public and explicit'
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement declared its support for Iran is unambiguous, backing Iran's restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz. The Houthis warned they are not neutral in the broader conflict involving Iran, Lebanon, and Palestine.

stories.title: The Mediterranean: Warmer, saltier, more acidic, and rising fast — report
stories.summary: An annual monitoring report found that the Mediterranean Sea is becoming warmer, saltier, more acidic, and rising faster due to climate change. The report noted that invasive species are displacing local marine life across the region.

stories.title: Europe hit by record heat, glacier loss and marine extremes per climate report
stories.summary: Europe recorded its hottest year on record in 2025, with unprecedented heatwaves, rapid glacier melt, record sea temperatures, and expanding wildfires, according to a major climate report. The continent is warming at twice the global average rate, with extremes stretching from the Mediterranean to the Arctic.

stories.title: Jerusalem hills finally recovering from devastating 2025 wildfires
stories.summary: The Jerusalem hills are showing signs of recovery from devastating wildfires that struck in 2025. With the Lag Ba'omer holiday approaching, Israel's Fire and Rescue Authority issued a ban on unsanctioned bonfires.

stories.title: Amnesty: Israel must halt ‘unlawful destruction of civilian property’ in Lebanon
stories.summary: Amnesty International called on Israel to stop destroying civilian property in Lebanon after footage emerged showing Israeli bulldozers demolishing solar panels in southern Lebanon. The organization said the incident reflects a broader pattern of damage to non-military infrastructure along the border.

stories.title: Mali’s military leader emerges after alleged coup attempt
stories.summary: Mali's military leader made a public appearance following what was described as an attempted coup. He stated that the country is under control, though details about the alleged coup attempt remained limited.

stories.title: Trump rebukes Merz after German leader says Iran ‘humiliating’ US over talks
stories.summary: President Trump rebuked German Chancellor Friedrich Merz after Merz said Iran was humiliating the United States during nuclear negotiations. Trump accused Merz of believing it is acceptable for Iran to possess a nuclear weapon.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone strike on Russian port causes fire, toxic smoke as locals fault officials for withholding public health information
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck oil-loading infrastructure at the Russian port of Tuapse in Krasnodar Krai, sparking a large fire. Satellite images showed smoke spreading at least 140 kilometers, while local residents criticized officials for withholding public health information.

stories.title: Russian agents planning assassination attempt on AFU general detained in Zhytomyr region
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service and National Police detained two agents of Russian special services in the Zhytomyr region who were planning to assassinate a major general of the Ukrainian Armed Forces.

stories.title: Resistance to new mosques exposes tensions over Japan’s growing Muslim communities
stories.summary: Plans to build a mosque in Fujisawa, a city southwest of Tokyo, have become a flashpoint amid resistance from some local residents. Muslim community leaders and scholars said the opposition reflects a broader pattern in Japan, where negative overseas media coverage of Islam and social media narratives fuel resistance to new mosques.

stories.title: Israeli strike on Lebanese troops, rescuers wounds two soldiers, Lebanon says
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on April 28 in the village of Majdal Zoun in southern Lebanon wounded two Lebanese soldiers during a rescue operation, according to the Lebanese army. The strike targeted Lebanese troops and rescuers engaged in the operation.

stories.title: US imposes sanctions on 35 individuals, entities for aiding Iran's sanctions evasions
stories.summary: The U.S. government on April 28 imposed sanctions on 35 entities and individuals accused of supporting Iran's shadow banking network. Washington alleges the targets facilitated the movement of tens of billions of dollars tied to sanctions evasion and Iran's sponsorship of terrorism.

stories.title: US spy agencies examine how Iran would react to Trump declaring victory
stories.summary: US intelligence agencies are analyzing how Iran might respond if President Trump were to declare victory in the ongoing conflict. The assessment aims to understand implications of a potential pullback ahead of US midterm elections.

stories.title: US spy agencies examine how Iran would react to Trump declaring victory
stories.summary: U.S. intelligence agencies are assessing how Iran might respond if President Donald Trump were to declare a unilateral victory in the ongoing U.S.-Iran war, which has lasted roughly two months and resulted in thousands of deaths. The conflict has become a political liability for the White House.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Trump says Iran has been 'militarily defeated' at state dinner
stories.summary: At a White House state dinner on Tuesday, President Donald Trump declared that Iran has been "militarily defeated," marking his first public comments on the topic during King Charles III's royal visit to Washington.

stories.title: Putin says Ukraine has intensified attacks on civilian targets in Russia
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin stated on April 28 that Ukraine has intensified attacks on civilian infrastructure within Russia. He cited a recent Ukrainian drone strike on an oil refinery in the southern Russian city of Tuapse as an example.

stories.title: Chechen political figure says ‘honor killings’ are a private family matter, calls LGBTQ+ people ‘outcasts and perverts’
stories.summary: Chechen political figure Ruslan Kutayev, president of the Assembly of Peoples of the Caucasus and a PACE platform member, called honor killings a private family matter and used derogatory language against LGBTQ+ people. His remarks have generated widespread debate in Russia's opposition.

stories.title: King Charles avoids direct Iran reference and hails 'most consequential alliance' between UK and US
stories.summary: King Charles III addressed a joint session of the US Congress on Tuesday during his state visit to Washington, calling the UK-US relationship one of the most consequential alliances in history. The 28-minute speech avoided direct references to the war against Iran or the Epstein case, both of which have recently strained transatlantic relations.

stories.title: Argentina expects to raise $2 billion from privatizations this year, says Minister Caputo
stories.summary: Argentina's Economy Minister Luis Caputo announced the government expects to raise approximately $2 billion by year-end through privatizations and concessions of public companies. The plan is a key element of President Javier Milei's economic program and a central commitment to the IMF.

stories.title: Former US officials criticise Pentagon silence on deadly Iran school attack
stories.summary: Former US officials have criticized the Pentagon for providing almost no information about a deadly strike on a school in Iran. Two months after the incident, the Pentagon has stated only that the matter remains under investigation.

stories.title: Chinese team pioneers path to turn carbon dioxide into jet fuel as prices soar
stories.summary: Chinese scientists at the Shanghai Advanced Research Institute are scaling up technology to convert carbon dioxide into jet fuel as global aviation fuel prices surged past $200 per barrel amid the Iran conflict, causing airlines to cancel flights.

stories.title: Kim Jong Un praises troops who 'self-blasted' to avoid capture by Ukraine
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un praised soldiers who detonated their own grenades to avoid capture while fighting in Ukraine. The statement confirms reports that North Korean troops are instructed to kill themselves rather than be taken prisoner.

stories.title: Russia developing fees for international internet traffic
stories.summary: Russia's Digital Development Ministry is developing a mechanism to impose additional charges on international internet traffic. The plan was disclosed in a written response to the Association of Telecommunications Companies.

stories.title: US sanctions 35 entities over Iran ‘shadow banking’ network
stories.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced sanctions on 35 entities and individuals linked to Iran's shadow banking networks, describing them as a critical financial lifeline for Iran's armed forces and a source of funding for what Washington calls terrorist operations in the Middle East.

stories.title: How South Korea’s Samsung clan made a US$45 billion financial comeback in 1 year
stories.summary: The Samsung founding family, led by Jay Y. Lee, achieved a $45 billion financial recovery within one year after facing a massive inheritance tax bill following patriarch Lee Kun-hee's death in 2020 and Jay Y. Lee's imprisonment for bribery.

stories.title: US boards vessel but allows passage in Iran blockade
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command said Marines boarded the commercial vessel Blue Star III during enforcement of the Iran blockade but allowed it to continue after confirming it was not heading to an Iranian port. It was the first boarded ship released since the blockade began over two weeks ago.

stories.title: 349 artists and media workers killed in Ukraine after beginning of full-scale war
stories.summary: Since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion, 349 artists and 137 Ukrainian and foreign media professionals have been killed in Ukraine.

stories.title: Inflation jumps to 4.6% in Australia as Iran war fuel shock begins to bite
stories.summary: Australia's inflation rate jumped to 4.6 percent in the year to March, up from 3.7 percent the previous month, driven by fuel price increases linked to the Iran war. Financial markets are pricing in a third consecutive interest rate hike by the Reserve Bank at its next meeting.

stories.title: Why more Singapore graduates are choosing jobs below their qualifications: ‘it’s meaningful’
stories.summary: A growing number of university graduates in Singapore are choosing jobs below their formal qualifications, citing personal fulfillment. One Nanyang Technological University business graduate chose to become a full-time barista rather than pursue a corporate career.

stories.title: A remilitarised Japan threatens more than just China
stories.summary: An analysis examines concerns that Japan's remilitarization under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi poses broader regional implications beyond the China-Taiwan dynamic, particularly following her remarks about potential military intervention in a Taiwan crisis.

stories.title: Boiling oil spills onto street outside Russian refinery after drone strike ignites storage tank
stories.summary: A storage tank at an oil refinery in Tuapse, Krasnodar Krai, boiled over following a drone strike on April 28, sending oil spilling onto a nearby street. The regional Emergency Situations Ministry confirmed the incident to the governor.

stories.title: Chief of staff remarks spark concern over looting by Israeli forces
stories.summary: Israel's Haaretz newspaper reported growing concerns over discipline within the Israeli military after Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir acknowledged incidents of looting by soldiers. The report warned that such conduct could undermine operational effectiveness.

stories.title: UCLA student government censured after condemning event with ex-hostage Omer Shem Tov
stories.summary: UCLA's student government faced censure from the university, Jewish organizations, and a sitting regent after it condemned a campus event featuring freed Israeli hostage Omer Shem Tov, claiming the talk amplified a one-sided narrative.

stories.title: US spy agencies examine how Iran would react to Trump declaring victory: sources
stories.summary: U.S. intelligence agencies are analyzing how Iran might respond if President Donald Trump declared a unilateral victory in the ongoing two-month conflict. Senior administration officials requested the assessment amid concerns that the war, which has killed thousands, could lead to significant Republican losses in upcoming midterm elections.

stories.title: Putin says there are ‘no serious threats’ from Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refinery as oil spills into city street
stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin downplayed Ukrainian drone strikes on oil infrastructure in Tuapse, claiming there were "no serious threats." His comments came as boiling oil spilled onto city streets following attacks on the refinery.

stories.title: Trump approval sinks to record low as war with Iran drives cost-of-living concerns
stories.summary: President Donald Trump's approval rating has fallen to a record low amid growing public dissatisfaction with his handling of cost-of-living issues and the war with Iran.

stories.title: Palestinian Football Association appeals to sports court over FIFA ruling on Israel
stories.summary: The Palestinian Football Association has appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport over a FIFA ruling regarding Israel. The association has long argued that Israeli clubs based in the occupied West Bank should not compete in leagues run by the Israel Football Association.

stories.title: Crude oil climbs above $111 as diplomacy falters
stories.summary: Brent crude oil rose to approximately $111.18 per barrel amid ongoing uncertainty surrounding the U.S.-Iran conflict. Analysts attributed the rally to stalled diplomacy and continued restrictions around the Strait of Hormuz, with rising energy costs also affecting U.S. consumers.

stories.title: US economic gap over China to widen, but Iran might bring them closer: former UN official
stories.summary: Former UN Security Council president Kishore Mahbubani has projected that the US-China GDP gap will widen to $11 trillion by decade's end. However, he suggests that geopolitical tensions, including the war in Iran and the Strait of Hormuz crisis, could serve as a stabilizing force for US-China bilateral relations.

stories.title: China boy grabs public attention by ‘handcrafting’ turbojet engine in family’s living room
stories.summary: A 14-year-old boy named Che Jingang from Hainan Island in southern China has attracted widespread attention on social media after state media outlets reported he had handcrafted turbojet engines in his family's living room. His social media account, managed by his mother, has around 30,000 followers.

stories.title: US-backed mining guard to secure Congolese cobalt sites, says Kinshasa
stories.summary: The DRC government announced the creation of a 20,000-strong mining guard unit to secure cobalt extraction and transport sites, aligning with American industrial interests in critical minerals. The US embassy denied providing direct funding for the initiative.

stories.title: Lebanon condemns Israeli strike killing rescue workers
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun condemned an Israeli air strike on the town of Majdal Zoun that killed at least five people, including three civil defence workers responding to an earlier attack. Aoun said the strike was part of a pattern of assaults targeting relief and first aid workers.

stories.title: ‘No fundraising launched’ after father’s death, paralysed dancer Mo Li warns of scams
stories.summary: Hong Kong dancer Mo Li Kai-yin, who was paralysed after being struck by a falling screen during a Mirror concert in 2022, warned supporters about fundraising scams following the death of his father, Reverend Derek Li Shing-lam. Mo clarified on Instagram that neither he nor his family had launched any fundraising efforts.

stories.title: Hungary's Magyar proposes meeting with Zelenskiy on minority rights
stories.summary: Hungarian election winner Peter Magyar proposed a meeting with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy in western Ukraine to discuss minority rights of ethnic Hungarians. Magyar announced the proposal in a Facebook post on April 28 from Budapest.

stories.title: US agents raid 22 Minnesota sites in social-welfare fraud probe
stories.summary: U.S. law enforcement agencies raided more than 20 locations across Minnesota on April 28 as part of investigations into social-welfare program fraud. The probe reflects a priority of the Trump administration.

stories.title: Libyan court jails four human traffickers for up to 22 years
stories.summary: A court in Tripoli, Libya, convicted four members of a criminal gang involved in human trafficking, abductions for ransom, and torture, handing down sentences of up to 22 years in prison.

stories.title: Ultra-Orthodox protesters storm home of Israeli military police chief
stories.summary: Ultra-Orthodox Jewish protesters stormed the home of Israeli military police chief Brigadier-General Yuval Yamin in Ashkelon, protesting enforcement measures against draft evasion. The incident followed a High Court ruling ordering benefit cuts and legal action against those refusing conscription. Prime Minister Netanyahu condemned the act.

stories.title: ‘Wartime’ in Iran, Trump’s fury and the UAE: here’s what happened overnight
stories.summary: As the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran enters its third month, no breakthrough between Washington and Tehran appears imminent. President Trump criticized German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on social media following a meeting with Britain's King Charles III in Washington.

stories.title: Russia officially acknowledges forced recruitment of students for war
stories.summary: Russia's Ministry of Defense issued a statement responding to reports that university students were being expelled and coerced into signing military contracts for service in unmanned units. The ministry's response effectively acknowledged the existence of forced recruitment cases.

stories.title: NYC Hinds Hall Palestinian eatery has good hummus, wipes Israel off its menu maps
stories.summary: A Palestinian restaurant called Hinds Hall opened on New York City's Upper West Side, named after a child killed in Gaza. The eatery has drawn attention for displaying maps that omit Israel while associating with the anti-Zionist protest movement.

stories.title: UK summons Iranian ambassador over embassy’s ‘unacceptable’ comments on social media
stories.summary: The United Kingdom summoned Iran's ambassador after the Iranian embassy in Britain posted a statement on social media calling on Iranians in the UK to declare their willingness to sacrifice their lives in the ongoing war. The UK government described the comments as unacceptable.

stories.title: Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refinery send smoke across Black Sea coast as state of emergency is declared
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck oil infrastructure in Tuapse for the third time in two weeks on April 28, hitting previously untargeted sections of the refinery and the marine terminal. A state of emergency was declared as smoke spread across the Black Sea coast. Previous fires at the site burned for days.

stories.title: Energy prices expected to surge 24pc, reaching highest level since 2022 Russia-Ukraine war: World Bank assessment
stories.summary: The World Bank projects global energy prices will surge 24 percent in 2026, reaching their highest level since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The increase is driven by the Middle East war's impact on commodity markets, with overall commodity prices forecast to rise 16 percent.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill eight in south Lebanon, including rescuers
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed eight people across southern Lebanon on Tuesday, including rescue workers. The Israeli military said it also destroyed a large Hezbollah tunnel during the operations.

stories.title: ​Battle of wills: On the U.S. war on Iran
stories.summary: The article discusses the U.S.-Iran confrontation and calls for the United States to lift its blockade so Iran can reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The standoff reflects an escalating battle of wills between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump says Tehran wants end to blockade; Israel kills medics
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated that Iran has reached out to Washington requesting the lifting of the naval blockade on Iranian ports, suggesting Tehran wants an end to the restrictions.

stories.title: Romania's two largest parties call no-confidence vote in pro-European government
stories.summary: Romania's leftist Social Democrats and the far-right opposition submitted a no-confidence motion against the minority government of pro-European Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan on Tuesday in Bucharest. The motion could bring down the government in early May, following a split between the two largest parties and their former coalition arrangement.

stories.title: People linked to top Orban aide were blocked trying to send funds abroad, Hungary's Magyar says
stories.summary: Hungarian election winner Peter Magyar said tax authorities in Hungary blocked transfers of funds abroad by individuals linked to a top aide of outgoing Prime Minister Viktor Orban. The identities of those involved were not disclosed.

stories.title: US envoy says Belarus may free more prisoners in next month
stories.summary: U.S. special envoy John Coale, speaking in Warsaw, said he expects additional prisoners to be released from Belarus within the next month. He added that further sanctions relief for Minsk could follow if the releases occur.

stories.title: Israeli strike on Jebchit kills two as Lebanon toll rises
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on the town of Jebchit in the Nabatieh district of southern Lebanon killed two people and wounded 13 others. Across Lebanon on Tuesday, Israeli strikes killed at least 11 people and injured 30, including women and children.

stories.title: Palestinian football body appeals to sports court over FIFA Israel ruling
stories.summary: The Palestinian Football Association has appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport over FIFA's decision not to sanction Israel. The appeal concerns Israeli football clubs based in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Russian ‘shadow fleet’ undeterred by Starmer’s threat as nearly 100 ships cross UK waters
stories.summary: An analysis found that at least 98 Russian vessels subject to UK sanctions transited through British waters in the past month. The movements occurred despite threats by Prime Minister Keir Starmer to crack down on Russia's so-called shadow fleet.

stories.title: Russians launch drone attack on rescue workers in Marhanets, damaging depot
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out a drone attack targeting rescue workers in Marhanets, Dnipropetrovsk region of Ukraine. The strike damaged a depot and emergency equipment in what was described as a deliberate attack on first responders.

stories.title: Trump reportedly tells aides to prepare for extended blockade of Iran
stories.summary: President Trump reportedly instructed aides to prepare for an extended naval blockade of Iran. While hosting King Charles, Trump said the British monarch agreed that Iran must not obtain nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Iran talks stall amid Hormuz tensions and ceasefire violations in Lebanon
stories.summary: Diplomatic efforts to address the broader Middle East conflict have stalled as the US evaluates Iran's latest proposal on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Tensions in Lebanon continue to rise despite a fragile ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah.

stories.title: A faraway conflict threatens livelihoods in India's glass hub
stories.summary: Supply chain disruptions caused by Middle East tensions have driven up costs in India's glass manufacturing hub, threatening the livelihoods of workers dependent on the industry.

stories.title: Hezbollah carries out wave of attacks on Israeli forces in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced multiple attacks on Israeli forces operating in southern Lebanon. The group claimed it shot down a Hermes 900 drone over al-Qantara, struck a Merkava tank with an explosive drone, and targeted Israeli troops with drone swarms in al-Taybeh and Bint Jbeil.

stories.title: SpaceX ties Elon Musk's compensation to Mars colonisation goal
stories.summary: SpaceX's board approved a compensation plan for CEO Elon Musk tied to goals including Mars colonization and operating data centers in space. The details were disclosed in a confidential registration statement filed with the SEC as SpaceX prepares for a public offering.

stories.title: Israeli contractor killed, his son wounded by Hezbollah drone in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli contractor Amer Hujirat was killed and his son wounded by a Hezbollah explosive drone while operating an excavator in southern Lebanon. The Israeli prime minister said a special project is underway to counter the growing drone threat.

stories.title: Iraqi president nominates Ali al-Zaidi as PM-designate
stories.summary: Iraqi President Abdul Latif Rashid nominated Ali al-Zaidi as prime minister-designate. The nomination comes after U.S. President Trump earlier threatened to cut support for Iraq if former premier Nouri al-Maliki, who has close ties to Iran, returned to power.

stories.title: The tragedy of recurring Rohingya refugee deaths
stories.summary: A fishing trawler carrying Rohingya refugees capsized, drawing renewed attention to the deadly risks faced by displaced Rohingya and the human cost of their protracted displacement from Myanmar.

stories.title: Explosions rock Kyiv, six killed in Russia, Ukraine
stories.summary: Explosions struck Kyiv as both Russia and Ukraine intensified aerial attacks, with six people killed across both countries. Both sides have primarily targeted energy infrastructure in recent months as the conflict continues.

stories.title: UK faces £35bn hit and risk of recession this year over impact of Iran war, thinktank warns
stories.summary: The UK's National Institute of Economic and Social Research warned that Britain faces a £35 billion economic hit and possible recession this year due to fallout from the Iran war. Even under a best-case scenario, NIESR projected slower economic growth through 2026 and 2027.

stories.title: Pair of Hong Kong luxury homes sells for US$41m as market sizzle increases
stories.summary: Mainland Chinese property tycoon Zhao Zhijun sold two adjoining units at 8-12 Peak Road in Hong Kong for a combined HK$320 million (US$40.8 million), realizing an 86 percent gain over 16 years. The sale reflects renewed demand from mainland buyers restoring liquidity to Hong Kong's luxury property market.

stories.title: UN sanctions brother of Sudan's RSF leader, Colombian mercenaries
stories.summary: The United Nations imposed sanctions on Algoney Dagalo, the younger brother of Rapid Support Forces leader Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, as well as Colombian mercenaries linked to Sudan's conflict. The sanctions target individuals involved in the ongoing civil war in Sudan.

stories.title: Mali military leader Goita meets Russian ambassador after attacks, office says
stories.summary: Malian military leader Assimi Goita met with the Russian ambassador on Tuesday in Bamako, according to his office. It was Goita's first public appearance since insurgents carried out simultaneous attacks across Mali on Saturday.

stories.title: Zelensky: We have information on which areas will be main targets for Russian forces this spring and summer
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy said Ukraine has intelligence on which areas Russian forces plan to target this spring and summer. He stated that Ukraine would share this information with its partners, including details about potential Russian operations in NATO countries.

stories.title: UN court orders medical review of jailed Bosnian Serb general Mladic amid release bid
stories.summary: The UN war crimes court in The Hague ordered an independent medical assessment of Ratko Mladic, the 84-year-old Bosnian Serb general serving a lifetime sentence. The order follows Mladic's request for early release on health grounds, according to court documents published Tuesday.

stories.title: Israel using water access as 'weapon' in Gaza: MSF
stories.summary: Médecins Sans Frontières accused Israel of using water access as a weapon in Gaza. The medical charity documented multiple incidents in which its clearly marked water trucks and boreholes were shot at or destroyed.

stories.title: 'Empowered': UAE's exit from Opec appeases Trump, delivers blow to Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates has withdrawn from OPEC amid the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The move is seen as a gesture toward the Trump administration and a strategic challenge to Saudi Arabia's leadership of the oil-producing bloc.

stories.title: Amer Hujirat, Defense Ministry civilian contractor, killed in Hezbollah drone attack in Lebanon
stories.summary: Amer Hujirat, a civilian contractor with Israel's Defense Ministry, was killed in a Hezbollah drone attack in southern Lebanon. The incident highlights evolving threats from Hezbollah, which has been deploying fiber optic-guided drones against Israeli forces.

stories.title: Israeli soldier shows Gaza’s Beit Hanoon completely flattened
stories.summary: A video recorded by an Israeli soldier revealed widespread destruction in the town of Beit Hanoon in northern Gaza, showing the area has been almost completely flattened during military operations.

stories.title: Trump’s Ukraine envoy stepping down amid stalled peace talks with Russia
stories.summary: Acting US Ambassador to Ukraine Julie Davis is stepping down and retiring amid stalled US-brokered ceasefire talks to end Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Reports indicate Davis had grown frustrated with President Trump's policies and his diminishing support for Kyiv.

stories.title: Pro-Kurdish party criticises Turkey's 'hesitant' steps toward PKK peace
stories.summary: Turkey's pro-Kurdish DEM Party issued one of its strongest criticisms of the government's handling of the peace process with the PKK on Tuesday. The party highlighted a growing stand-off between Ankara and Kurdish militants over next steps to end the decades-long conflict.

stories.title: Trump approval rating falls to lowest level amid Iran war
stories.summary: President Donald Trump's approval rating has dropped to 34 percent, the lowest of his current term, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll. The decline has accelerated since the US-Israeli war on Iran began on February 28, with rising fuel prices compounding public dissatisfaction.

stories.title: Democrats urge Trump to keep ban on Chinese cars in US as Xi meeting looms
stories.summary: More than 70 House Democrats, led by Representative Debbie Dingell, sent a letter urging President Trump to maintain restrictions on Chinese automakers entering the U.S. market. The appeal comes weeks before Trump's planned trip to Beijing for a meeting with President Xi Jinping.

stories.title: US not funding Congo's $100 million mine guard, embassy says
stories.summary: The United States said on Tuesday it is not funding any security units tasked with policing or guarding mines in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The statement from the US embassy in Kinshasa came after Congo announced plans to launch a $100 million paramilitary force to secure mining sites.

stories.title: ‘Alpha’ troops and more ships: Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao outlines vision for service
stories.summary: Acting U.S. Navy Secretary Hung Cao outlined his vision for the service in one of his first public addresses, calling for "alpha" troops and an expanded fleet. He emphasized a shift in priorities and made controversial remarks about personnel standards.

stories.title: Trump hails British as ‘friends’ as King Charles III visits amid Iran tensions
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump hosted King Charles III at the White House, praising the British as friends. The state visit aimed to demonstrate allied unity despite reported divisions between the U.S. and UK over the Iran conflict.

stories.title: President on winter preparations: Ukraine must build reserves to ensure people have what they need
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy emphasized the need to build energy reserves ahead of the next heating season. He said every community in Ukraine must have sufficient reserves to ensure electricity and heating regardless of circumstances.

stories.title: Iran’s Guards seize wartime power, blunting Supreme Leader’s role
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has seized wartime executive powers amid the country's ongoing conflict, diminishing the role traditionally held by Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. Reports indicate that with Khamenei absent, no other actor within the Iranian system has the capacity to resist the Guards' expanded authority.

stories.title: Ultra-Orthodox draft protesters storm Israel military police chief's home
stories.summary: Ultra-Orthodox anti-conscription protesters in Israel stormed the home of the military police chief. The incident was in response to government moves to enforce penalties against those who refuse military service.

stories.title: Beyond the headlines: Finding an anchor in the shelter - opinion
stories.summary: The article offers a personal reflection on life in Israel beyond the headlines of conflict, providing a weekly glimpse into everyday experiences including moments in shelters.

stories.title: Trump hits back at German chancellor over Iran war remarks
stories.summary: President Donald Trump criticized German Chancellor Friedrich Merz after Merz said Iran was humiliating the US in war-related negotiations. Trump accused Merz of supporting Iran's nuclear ambitions, though Merz has publicly stated Iran must not acquire nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Report: Qatar offered to ‘look after’ ICC prosecutor who issued warrants for Israeli leaders
stories.summary: A Wall Street Journal editorial cited a recording in which the manager of a private intelligence operation alleged that Qatar offered to support ICC prosecutor Karim Khan. The operation reportedly sought to discredit a woman who accused Khan of sexual abuse. Khan had issued arrest warrants for Israeli leaders.

stories.title: Bangladesh starts fuelling its first nuclear power station
stories.summary: Bangladesh began fuelling its first nuclear power station as the country faces annual electricity shortages during summer heat waves. The Rooppur plant is expected to help alleviate strain on Bangladesh's overstretched power grid.

stories.title: EU says it has approached Israel over Russian grain boat that docked in Haifa
stories.summary: The European Union has contacted Israel regarding a Russian vessel that docked at the port of Haifa carrying what Ukraine described as stolen Ukrainian grain. An EU foreign affairs spokesperson confirmed the approach on Tuesday.

stories.title: Mali junta leader vows crackdown after insurgent attacks shake Bamako and north
stories.summary: Mali's military leader Assimi Goita made his first public appearance following coordinated insurgent attacks in Bamako and northern regions over the weekend. He pledged to "neutralise" those responsible as jihadist and separatist groups escalated violence across the country.

stories.title: King Charles III Delivers Pointed Message in Address to U.S. Congress
stories.summary: King Charles III addressed the US Congress during his Washington visit, delivering remarks that praised multilateral institutions, warned about climate change, and championed diversity.

stories.title: Gold miners set to stay in Mali despite attacks, industry sources say
stories.summary: International mining companies are expected to continue investing in Mali despite Saturday's insurgent attacks that killed the country's defence minister. Industry executives and analysts said the attacks have raised concerns about supply routes but are unlikely to drive firms out of one of Africa's most resource-rich countries.

stories.title: Suspected members of Nigeria-linked Black Axe crime gang arrested in Switzerland
stories.summary: Suspected members of the Nigeria-linked Black Axe crime gang were arrested in Switzerland on accusations of involvement in romance scams and cyberfraud. Europol announced the arrests on Tuesday.

stories.title: Flying cars and 5-minute charges: China's EV industry sees opportunity in Iran crisis
stories.summary: China's electric vehicle industry sees a commercial opportunity arising from the U.S.-Iran conflict, as the global scramble for fuel accelerates interest in alternatives. Companies are promoting advanced EV technologies including rapid-charging systems.

stories.title: US spy agencies examining how Iran would react to Trump declaring victory
stories.summary: US intelligence agencies are analyzing how Iran might respond if President Trump declares victory in the ongoing conflict. The assessment aims to understand implications of a potential US pullback, amid concerns the war could hurt Republican prospects in midterm elections.

stories.title: As US-Iran talks remain ‘stalled’, experts warn of ‘long-term disruptions’
stories.summary: US-Iran negotiations remain stalled, with no breakthrough reported. The standoff between Washington and Tehran has contributed to rising global oil prices, raising concerns among experts about long-term disruptions to energy markets.

stories.title: Hungary's outgoing PM Orban offers to quit as Fidesz party chief, local media say
stories.summary: Hungary's outgoing Prime Minister Viktor Orban offered his resignation as leader of his right-wing Fidesz party on Tuesday. A Fidesz party congress scheduled for June will decide whether to accept his resignation, according to a party lawmaker.

stories.title: Drone diplomacy wins Ukraine valuable allies, but now it must deliver
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy has leveraged Ukraine's drone warfare expertise into diplomatic agreements during visits to the Middle East and Europe. Kyiv is using its military technology capabilities to strengthen its diplomatic position and secure new partnerships.

stories.title: Mexico's military captures top cartel leader in another blow to the Jalisco New Generation Cartel
stories.summary: Mexico's military captured a top leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, dealing another blow to the organization. The cartel was designated a foreign terrorist organization by U.S. President Trump along with five other Mexican cartels.

stories.title: How China’s reported ban on sulphuric acid exports could have overseas buyers reeling
stories.summary: China has reportedly moved to ban exports of sulphuric acid, a key ingredient in fertilizer production and metal processing. The squeeze on the commodity was initially triggered by the U.S.-Israel conflict in Iran and the effective blockage of the Strait of Hormuz, which disrupted shipments from a region accounting for a quarter of global production.

stories.title: US lawmakers move to mandate first comprehensive review of China’s AI capabilities
stories.summary: U.S. lawmakers introduced a draft bill that would require the State Department to produce the first comprehensive assessment of China's artificial intelligence capabilities. The proposed legislation calls for identifying specific AI leaders in China and evaluating Beijing's progress using independent benchmarks.

stories.title: Watch: Elderly woman rescued by robot from Ukraine's frontline
stories.summary: The Ukrainian army used a drone to locate an elderly woman stranded near the frontline and dispatched a ground robot to rescue her. She was attempting to leave her war-torn village when the military intervened.

stories.title: New-generation Ukrainian FPV drones tested at proving ground
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Defense and the Brave1 defense-tech cluster tested new-generation strike FPV drones from eight domestic manufacturers at a proving ground.

stories.title: New-generation Ukrainian FPV drones tested at proving ground
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Defense, working with the Brave1 defense innovation cluster, tested new-generation strike first-person-view drones from eight Ukrainian manufacturers at a proving ground. The tests evaluated next-generation FPV drone capabilities for battlefield use.

stories.title: US spy agencies examine how Iran would react to Trump declaring victory
stories.summary: US intelligence agencies are examining how Iran might respond if President Trump declared a unilateral victory in the two-month-old war. The assessment aims to gauge Tehran's potential reactions to such a move.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills five in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: An Israeli air strike on the southern Lebanese town of Majdal Zoun killed at least five people, including three paramedics trapped under rubble from an earlier attack, according to Lebanon's health ministry. At least two Lebanese soldiers accompanying a rescue team were also wounded.

stories.title: UAE OPEC departure 'a manifestation of dissatisfaction vis à vis Saudi Arabia', expert says
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced its departure from OPEC and OPEC+, effective May 1, citing national interests. An expert described the move as a "manifestation of dissatisfaction" with Saudi Arabia, OPEC's de facto leader, amid longstanding tensions over production quotas.

stories.title: Trump says Iran in ‘state of collapse’, wants US to open Hormuz Strait as soon as possible
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated on social media that Iran is in a "state of collapse" and wants the United States to reopen the Strait of Hormuz as soon as possible. It was unclear how Iran had allegedly communicated that message.

stories.title: Iran and US allowed Russian superyacht to cross Strait of Hormuz, source says
stories.summary: A superyacht owned by Russian billionaire Alexey Mordashov was permitted to transit the blockaded Strait of Hormuz after maintenance in Dubai because neither Iran nor the United States objected. A source close to Mordashov confirmed the passage on Tuesday.

stories.title: Watch: UAE shocks world with dramatic OPEC exit | Above the Fold | 28.04.2026
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced a dramatic exit from OPEC, shocking global energy markets. The development was among several major international stories including an Indian heatwave, an SCO summit, and a Jakarta train crash.

stories.title: At UN, China denounces Japan and EU over South China Sea remarks
stories.summary: At the United Nations, China's deputy UN ambassador Sun Lei condemned remarks by Japan and the European Union regarding the South China Sea. Sun called Japan's statements unwarranted and accused them of distorting the facts.

stories.title: The biggest military spenders
stories.summary: Global military spending has increased for the 11th consecutive year, according to the latest report by the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI). The data highlights a sustained upward trend in defense budgets worldwide.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1525: Tuapse burns again, Crimea’s Iskander bunkers cracked open, and Washington loses another envoy
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy unveiled a "Drone Deals" export framework as Ukrainian strikes hit Russian missile bunkers in Crimea and reignited a fire at the Tuapse refinery on day 1,525 of the war. The same day, the Financial Times reported that the US ambassador in Kyiv is resigning.

stories.title: US-Israel talks to discuss shifting military aid funding to joint defense partnership
stories.summary: The United States and Israel are set to begin talks in May on restructuring their military relationship, potentially shifting from traditional aid funding to a joint defense partnership model.

stories.title: Finance minister says no plans of seeking more bilateral financing after recent inflows from Saudi Arabia
stories.summary: Pakistani Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said the government has no plans to seek additional bilateral financing after receiving $3 billion from Saudi Arabia. He made the remarks at the first EU-Pakistan Business Forum in Islamabad, stating Pakistan's external position had stabilized.

stories.title: Netanyahu trial: President’s legal team invites prosecution, defense to preliminary plea-deal talks
stories.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog's legal team invited both the prosecution and Netanyahu's defense lawyers to preliminary talks on a possible plea deal. The discussions are meant to test whether an agreement can be reached before Herzog considers a formal pardon request from Prime Minister Netanyahu.

stories.title: Turkey offering to broker agreement between US, Lebanon on Hezbollah, sources tell 'Post'
stories.summary: Turkey has offered to broker an agreement between the United States and Lebanon regarding Hezbollah, according to sources cited by the Jerusalem Post. The Lebanese government has reportedly been hesitant about the initiative due to concerns over expanding Turkish influence in the country.

stories.title: FIFA introduces new World Cup red-card rules to combat racism
stories.summary: FIFA announced new red-card rules for the upcoming World Cup aimed at combating racism. Players who cover their mouths during confrontations or walk off the pitch in protest of refereeing decisions may be sent off under the new measures.

stories.title: Canadian PM invited to attend European Political Community summit in May
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has been invited to attend the European Political Community summit in Armenia next month. European Council President Antonio Costa said this marks the first time a non-European country has been invited to participate in the EPC gathering.

stories.title: Trump administration blocks US wind energy projects in switch to oil and gas
stories.summary: The Trump administration canceled two previously permitted U.S. wind energy projects and agreed to pay millions in refunds to the developers, on the condition the funds be reinvested in oil and gas. Representatives Jared Huffman and Jamie Raskin had called the agreements unlawful.

stories.title: Cao says industry needs to ‘move forward’ in first speech as acting SecNav
stories.summary: Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao delivered his first public remarks since assuming the role, urging the defense industry to accelerate progress. He outlined priorities for the service going forward.

stories.title: Trump's threats to steal Iran's oil continue a long history of US pillage
stories.summary: US President Trump has threatened to seize Iran's oil resources amid the ongoing military conflict. The rhetoric has drawn comparisons to a broader history of US economic coercion in countries such as Zimbabwe and Venezuela.

stories.title: Israel says has ‘no territorial ambitions’ in Lebanon, despite evacuations
stories.summary: Israel stated it has no territorial ambitions in Lebanon despite issuing evacuation warnings to residents of over a dozen villages and towns located outside or along the so-called "Yellow Line" in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: EU climate chief says energy crisis boosts case to ditch fossil fuels
stories.summary: European Commissioner for Climate Action Wopke Hoekstra said the energy crisis caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran strengthens the case for phasing out fossil fuels. He cited the closure of the Strait of Hormuz as a major driver of global energy price increases and Europe's vulnerability to import dependence.

stories.title: US-Iran ceasefire can’t paper over fires in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Despite ongoing U.S.-Iran peace negotiations in Islamabad, hostilities continue in the Strait of Hormuz, where ships have been attacked. Israel continues striking Lebanon, and disagreements over Iran's nuclear program remain unresolved, undermining ceasefire efforts.

stories.title: Zelensky: AFU will have priority access to sufficient weapons despite exports
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that the Ukrainian Armed Forces will retain priority access to sufficient weapons, even as Ukraine moves to export domestically produced arms. Any surplus beyond military needs will be made available for international sale.

stories.title: Continuing hostilities in Lebanon as 1.2 million displaced sink into despair
stories.summary: Despite a U.S.-brokered ceasefire, Israel has continued military strikes in Lebanon and occupies a strip of the south, while Hezbollah has maintained attacks against Israeli forces. The ongoing hostilities have displaced approximately 1.2 million people, creating a severe humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: China Pulls the Plug on Meta’s AI Acquisition
stories.summary: China blocked Meta's planned artificial intelligence acquisition, reflecting Beijing's shifting national security concerns. The decision represents a reversal that could affect Meta's AI development strategy.

stories.title: Israeli strikes on Gaza kill five, including 9-year-old boy, medics say
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on the Gaza Strip on Tuesday killed five Palestinians, including a 9-year-old boy, according to health officials in Gaza. The strikes were reported by medics in the territory.

stories.title: US intel agencies examining how Iran would react if Trump declares victory in war
stories.summary: US intelligence agencies are analyzing how Iran might respond if President Trump were to declare victory in the ongoing conflict. Early assessments concluded Tehran would likely interpret such a declaration as a win for Iran. The White House says negotiations are continuing.

stories.title: 'Victory to the resistance': CAIR allegedly cosponsored event writing letters to terrorists
stories.summary: The Council on American-Islamic Relations' Washington chapter allegedly co-sponsored an event that involved writing letters to imprisoned individuals described by critics as terrorists. The event drew scrutiny as CAIR's executive director is running for state office.

stories.title: Mali leader says situation under control
stories.summary: Mali's military leader Assimi Goita addressed the nation in a video statement following coordinated attacks across the country. Separately, the Islamic State claimed responsibility for an attack in Nigeria's Adamawa State that killed at least 29 people.

stories.title: King Charles calls for NATO unity, Ukraine support in US Congress speech
stories.summary: King Charles III addressed the US Congress during a four-day visit to the United States, calling for NATO unity and continued support for Ukraine. The British monarch praised the US-UK relationship while delivering pointed messages to lawmakers.

stories.title: UAE leaves OPEC in a blow to oil cartel
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced it will leave OPEC and OPEC+ effective May 1, stating the decision serves its national interests. The UAE had long expressed frustration with production quotas, and its relationship with Saudi Arabia, OPEC's de facto leader, had grown increasingly strained.

stories.title: Drone strike in southern Sudan kills 11: medical source
stories.summary: A drone strike on the city of Rabak in southern Sudan killed 11 people, according to medical sources. A second drone strike was also reported further north in Khartoum state.

stories.title: FO says Cambodia has agreed on early repatriation of 54 Pakistanis arrested following scam centre raid
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office announced that Cambodian authorities agreed to the early repatriation of 54 Pakistani nationals arrested during a raid on a scam center. Reports indicated that over 200 Pakistanis were held in overcrowded Cambodian facilities with inadequate conditions.

stories.title: Oil tycoons deny paying bribes to former Nigerian minister
stories.summary: Several oil tycoons denied paying bribes to former Nigerian Petroleum Minister Diezani Alison-Madueke. She is accused of receiving luxury accommodations and lavish spending sprees in the United Kingdom, charges she also denies.

stories.title: Mountaineer climbs Everest for Palestinian children
stories.summary: Mountaineer Mostafa Salameh is attempting to summit Mount Everest while carrying letters written by children in Gaza. The climb is intended to draw attention to the plight of Palestinian children in the territory.

stories.title: Armed group announces siege on Mali capital
stories.summary: The armed group JNIM has declared the start of a "total siege" on Mali's capital, Bamako. The announcement signals a significant escalation by the al-Qaeda-linked group against the Malian government.

stories.title: US ambassador to Ukraine Julie Davis to resign amid “frustration” with Trump – FT
stories.summary: US Ambassador to Ukraine Julie Davis plans to resign in the coming weeks, the Financial Times reported. Her departure adds to significant turnover among senior US diplomats in Kyiv during the ongoing war.

stories.title: Britain challenges court decision that Palestine Action ban was unlawful
stories.summary: The British government on Tuesday challenged a court ruling that its ban on pro-Palestinian group Palestine Action was unlawful. Britain had designated Palestine Action a terrorist organisation, but a court found the move unlawfully interfered with freedom of expression.

stories.title: ICC orders $8.5 million in compensation for victims of Timbuktu Islamist who imposed sharia law
stories.summary: International Criminal Court judges in The Hague ordered 7.25 million euros ($8.5 million) in compensation for more than 65,000 victims of a Malian Islamist who helped impose sharia law on Timbuktu in 2012. The defendant was a key figure in the police force that ordered public floggings and other punishments.

stories.title: Melnyk suggests IAEA Chief Grossi could be next UN Secretary-General
stories.summary: Ukraine's Permanent Representative to the UN, Andrii Melnyk, suggested that IAEA Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi could be a candidate for the next UN Secretary-General. The proposal highlights Grossi's international profile amid ongoing nuclear safety concerns.

stories.title: Israeli court extends detention of Gaza hospital director without charge
stories.summary: An Israeli court approved the continued detention of Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya, director of Kamal Adwan Hospital in Gaza, without filing charges. The Beersheba District Court upheld his detention under the "Unlawful Combatants Law." Physicians for Human Rights said he is held in harsh conditions and denied medical care.

stories.title: US and Nato faced with frustrating ‘marriage crisis’, Belgian defence minister says
stories.summary: Belgian Defence Minister Theo Francken described the U.S.-NATO relationship as a "marriage crisis" during a think tank event in Washington. He cited growing frustrations on both sides of the Atlantic and urged the United States to stand with its allies.

stories.title: Beverley Martyn, spirited British folk singer, dies aged 79
stories.summary: British folk singer-songwriter Beverley Martyn has died at age 79. She was known for collaborations with her former husband John Martyn, as well as solo work spanning from 1960s singles to a 2014 comeback album. Her family said she died peacefully at home.

stories.title: New pirate group behind latest Somali hijacking: officials
stories.summary: Security officials said a recent pirate attack off the coast of Somalia was carried out by a newly identified group of "opportunistic criminals." The hijacking has renewed attention on piracy in the region.

stories.title: US conditions for paying UN dues include China curbs, report says
stories.summary: The United States has conditioned the release of billions of dollars in unpaid UN dues on specific reforms, including cost-cutting and measures to counter China's influence within the organization. Diplomatic notes circulated by the US outlined nine "quick-hit" reforms required before further funding is released.

stories.title: News live: King Charles praises ‘ambitious’ Aukus and expresses pride in Australia in speech to US Congress
stories.summary: King Charles III addressed the U.S. Congress and praised the Aukus nuclear submarine partnership, emphasizing defense ties between the UK, the U.S., and Australia. Separately, the Australian federal government announced A$45 million in funding to fast-track environmental approvals for mining, energy, and housing projects.

stories.title: JNF halts most funding for at-risk youth in West Bank over settler violence links
stories.summary: The Jewish National Fund has halted most of its funding for at-risk youth programs in the West Bank over links to settler violence. JNF's chairman said the money had been supporting activities that led to the expulsion of Palestinians and vowed not to fund extremist outposts.

stories.title: King Charles praises Nato and urges defence of Ukraine in key speech during Trump visit
stories.summary: King Charles III addressed the U.S. Congress, emphasizing the importance of NATO, the defense of Ukraine, and the transatlantic "special relationship" between Britain and the United States. The speech, marking the 250th anniversary of American independence, was widely interpreted as an implicit appeal to President Trump to uphold traditional European alliances.

stories.title: Anti-Israel protesters shout “child killers” at Oslo Independence Day celebration
stories.summary: Anti-Israel protesters disrupted an Israeli Independence Day celebration in Oslo, Norway, shouting chants including "child killers" and "Death to the IDF." The incident prompted calls for police action against the demonstrators.

stories.title: Zelensky: Export of Ukrainian weapons will become reality, all details agreed
stories.summary: President Zelensky announced that all details regarding the export of Ukrainian weapons have been agreed upon and approved at the state institutional level. Ukraine plans to make arms exports a reality while ensuring its own military needs are met first.

stories.title: Gantz warns Bennett-Lapid alliance could harm chances of replacing government
stories.summary: Israeli opposition figure Benny Gantz warned that a political alliance between Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid could undermine efforts to replace the current government. Gantz released a campaign video calling for a broad bloc representing all of Israel, accusing Bennett and Lapid of prioritizing internal leadership rivalries.

stories.title: A-G moves to press criminal charges against Israel Prison Service commissioner
stories.summary: Israel's Attorney-General moved to press criminal charges against Israel Prison Service Commissioner Yaakobi. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir denounced the attorney-general, calling her actions anti-democratic and accusing her of attempting to frame the commissioner.

stories.title: UAE leaves Opec in huge blow to global oil producers' group
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced its withdrawal from OPEC, dealing a significant blow to the oil producers' group amid an energy crisis linked to the Iran war. UAE Energy Minister Suhail Mohamed al-Mazrouei said the decision followed a strategic review of the country's energy policies.

stories.title: Russia's FSB says archaeologist Butyagin released by Poland in prisoner swap, TASS reports
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Security Service confirmed that archaeologist Alexander Butyagin was released by Poland as part of a prisoner swap, according to state news agency TASS. The exchange was announced on Tuesday.

stories.title: Iraq air defences fire at drone over Baghdad's Green zone
