stories.summary: Iran partially eased internet restrictions for businesses after a three-month blackout, with the Supreme National Security Council approving an "Internet Pro" system designed to preserve commercial activity during the crisis.

stories.title: Nigeria: 'I Was Misquoted' - Kenyan President Backtracks On Comments About Nigerians' English-Speaking Proficiency
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto walked back comments he made about Nigerians' English-speaking proficiency, saying four days later that he had been misquoted.

stories.title: Accelerating space power through software-defined mission dominance
stories.summary: A sponsored article discusses the need to accelerate space power through software-defined capabilities. As space-based threats evolve, the piece argues that existing satellites require new defensive and protective capabilities that can be updated even after launch.

stories.title: What is the Azawad Liberation Front, part of the Mali attacks?
stories.summary: The Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) is the latest group representing Tuareg independence aspirations in northern Mali. Tuareg communities have waged multiple rebellions over decades seeking autonomy in the region.

stories.title: Explosions heard in Kyiv; air defense systems activated
stories.summary: Explosions were heard in Kyiv as air defense systems activated during an air raid alert triggered by the threat of incoming Russian drones.

stories.title: Alleged drug trafficking kingpin deported from Türkiye to India
stories.summary: 59-year-old accused Salim Dola was handed over to the Narcotics Control Bureau and taken to its headquarters in Delhi

stories.title: UK appeals ‘overstated and wrong’ court ruling that Palestine Action ban is unlawful
stories.summary: The UK government appealed a court ruling that deemed the banning of Palestine Action unlawful. The group was designated a terrorist organization in 2025 after activists broke into an air force base and damaged military aircraft.

stories.title: Third Ukrainian strike hits Russian oil refinery and prompts evacuations
stories.summary: A third Ukrainian strike hit a Russian oil refinery in Tuapse, prompting evacuations of nearby residents. The Kremlin accused Kyiv of attempting to destabilize global energy markets.

stories.title: The cost of 76 years of US wars, from Korea to Iran
stories.summary: Al Jazeera published an analysis of the human and financial costs of U.S.-led wars spanning 76 years, from the Korean War through the current conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Russian oligarch’s superyacht allowed through strait of Hormuz, source says
stories.summary: A superyacht named Nord, owned by sanctioned Russian billionaire Alexei Mordashov and valued at over $500 million, was permitted to transit the blockaded Strait of Hormuz after maintenance in Dubai. A source close to Mordashov said neither the US nor Iran objected to the vessel's passage through the contested waterway.

stories.title: With Meta-Manus AI deal ‘difficult’ to undo, how will Beijing exert its authority?
stories.summary: Meta Platforms' approximately $2 billion acquisition of Chinese-origin AI startup Manus faces obstacles after Beijing ordered the deal blocked. Analysts said unwinding the acquisition would be complex and time-consuming given how far the transaction has progressed.

stories.title: Iran bans steel exports
stories.summary: Iran banned exports of steel products, including slab, sheet, and strip, after U.S.-Israeli airstrikes reportedly destroyed approximately 70 percent of the country's steel production capacity during the conflict.

stories.title: Ex-Mossad chief says Israeli settler violence reminds him of the Holocaust
stories.summary: Former Mossad chief Tamir Pardo said Israeli settler violence in the occupied West Bank reminded him of the Holocaust. He warned that efforts to curb settler assaults could potentially trigger a civil war in Israel.

stories.title: Russians attack facility in Konotop; five people wounded
stories.summary: Five civilians were injured in a Russian attack on the Konotop community in Ukraine's Sumy region.

stories.title: Volunteers work to restore damaged Great Omari Mosque library in Gaza
stories.summary: Palestinian medical students in Gaza launched a volunteer initiative to clean and restore the damaged library of the Great Omari Mosque, one of Gaza's historic sites, after it sustained destruction from Israeli shelling.

stories.title: ‘We were left alone’: Along Israel's ‘Yellow Line’, Lebanese feel abandoned by the state
stories.summary: Residents of southern Lebanon near Israel's "Yellow Line" expressed feelings of abandonment by the Lebanese state. Israeli troops have advanced to positions near the coastal town of Naqoura, visible from the city of Sour.

stories.title: Gaza residents return to gym in devastated Khan Younis amid widespread destruction
stories.summary: Residents of Khan Younis in Gaza reopened a partially destroyed basement gym beneath war-damaged buildings, restoring equipment to create a training space amid the lack of functioning recreational facilities in the area.

stories.title: U.S. no longer in position to ‘dictate’ policy to other nations, says Iran
stories.summary: While a ceasefire has halted the fighting between Iran, the U.S. and Israel, talks on bringing a permanent conclusion to the conflict have been inconclusive

stories.title: ICC orders $8.5 million compensation for victims of Malian jihadist
stories.summary: The International Criminal Court ordered €7.2 million (approximately $8.5 million) in compensation for victims of Al Hassan, a former Malian jihadist leader convicted of war crimes and crimes against humanity in 2024.

stories.title: UAE to exit Opec, dealing blow to oil cartel’s unity
stories.summary: The UAE announced its departure from OPEC and OPEC+ effective May 1, following a comprehensive review of its production policy. The Ministry of Infrastructure said the decision was based on national interests and a commitment to meeting global market needs.

stories.title: Swarm of 10,000 bees settles on bike outside Louvre in Paris
stories.summary: A swarm of approximately 10,000 bees settled on a bicycle locked to the railings of a metro station outside the Louvre museum in Paris. The bees clustered beneath the bike's saddle.

stories.title: UAE leaves OPEC and OPEC+ in blow to global oil producers' group
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates has withdrawn from both OPEC and OPEC+, a move that comes amid tensions related to the Iran conflict. The departure has unsettled oil markets and weakened cohesion among global oil-producing nations.

stories.title: Iranian embassies openly recruit for ‘sacrificing life’ campaign in the West
stories.summary: Iranian embassies in the United Kingdom, Germany, Australia, and Sri Lanka have openly recruited individuals for a martyrdom campaign amid the conflict with the US and Israel.

stories.title: Japan’s revised security policy to get ‘more aggressive’: Chinese expert
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi initiated a review of Japan's major security policies, arguing for increased military power to address geopolitical threats including those from China. A Chinese expert characterized the move as a fundamental shift toward a more aggressive security posture.

stories.title: Russia urges stability in Mali amid escalating violence
stories.summary: Russia called for a return to peace and stability in Mali following a wave of attacks by jihadist and separatist groups across the country.

stories.title: Iran war is latest blow to Somalia's malnourished children
stories.summary: Aid agencies warn that the US-Israeli war on Iran is worsening conditions for malnourished children in Somalia, where looming famine and deep cuts in foreign aid have already created a humanitarian crisis. Rising fuel prices caused by the conflict are threatening supply chains critical to delivering life-saving assistance.

stories.title: Canada’s push to rebuild ties with China hits a snag: a lack of direct flights
stories.summary: Canada announced plans to increase direct flight connections to China as part of efforts to rebuild bilateral ties. However, airlines may be reluctant to add routes due to high jet fuel costs and restricted access to Russian airspace.

stories.title: Kazakhstan to Reroute German Oil Exports Following Russian Pipeline Suspension
stories.summary: Kazakhstan announced it will reroute oil exports to Germany after Russia suspended pipeline access. Crude will now be transported through the Baltic Sea port of Ust-Luga and a joint Russian-Kazakh oil pipeline.

stories.title: Recording reveals Qatar promised to 'look after' ICC prosecutor Khan if he pursued Netanyahu - WSJ
stories.summary: A Wall Street Journal report citing a witness and audio recording alleges that Qatar promised to protect ICC prosecutor Karim Khan if he pursued charges against Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu. Qatar reportedly ordered an investigation to discredit sexual assault allegations against Khan.

stories.title: UAE says it will withdraw from OPEC and OPEC+, in historic blow to global oil cartel
stories.summary: The UAE announced its withdrawal from both OPEC and OPEC+, with its energy minister stating no direct consultations were held with other members, including Saudi Arabia. Gulf oil producers are already struggling with exports due to Iran's Hormuz blockade.

stories.title: Philippines says Czech authorities released key suspect in corruption scandal
stories.summary: The Philippines announced that Zaldy Co, a key suspect in a corruption scandal, has been released from Czech custody. Authorities said Co is now believed to be somewhere within Europe's Schengen area.

stories.title: BREAKING: UAE walks out of OPEC after six decades. Russia’s oil revenue takes the hit.
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced its withdrawal from OPEC and OPEC+ after approximately six decades of membership, a move linked to energy market turmoil caused by the Iran war. The departure is expected to undermine Russia's oil revenue by weakening OPEC's ability to maintain price floors.

stories.title: Army releases commercial solutions opening for rapid EW and signals intelligence capabilities
stories.summary: The US Army has released a commercial solutions opening to rapidly acquire electronic warfare and signals intelligence capabilities. The initiative aims to build a library of options that allows individual units to select capabilities suited to their specific structure and mission requirements.

stories.title: Gulf leaders meet in S. Arabia to discuss Iran strikes response
stories.summary: Gulf state leaders convened in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, to coordinate a collective response to the Iran conflict. The summit addressed regional attacks, damaged infrastructure, and fragile ceasefire negotiations.

stories.title: Ukraine accuses Israel of receiving shipments of grain 'stolen' by Russia
stories.summary: Ukraine accused Israel of receiving grain shipments allegedly stolen by Russia from occupied Ukrainian territory. Israel's foreign minister denied the claim, stating no evidence had been provided that a vessel carrying such grain reached the port of Haifa.

stories.title: Who is Ali al-Zaidi, the businessman named as Iraq’s PM-designate?
stories.summary: Ali al-Zaidi, a political outsider and businessman, was designated as Iraq's new prime minister to resolve a months-long political deadlock in the country.

stories.title: Five labourers injured after unknown attackers hurl hand grenade in Dalbandin
stories.summary:
QUETTA: Five labourers were injured in a grenade attack in the Dalbandin area of Chagai district late on Monday night, police said.
According to police officials, unidentified assailants on motorcycle

stories.title: Photos show demolition of Christian churches by Azerbaijan in Nagorno-Karabakh
stories.summary: Satellite imagery revealed the demolition of Christian churches in Nagorno-Karabakh by Azerbaijan, including the Holy Mother of God Cathedral and Church of St. Jacob in the city of Khankendi, known to Armenians as Stepanakert.

stories.title: Zelensky blasts Israel over purchase of stolen Ukrainian grain, threatens sanctions
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned Israel's purchase of grain originating from Russian-occupied Ukrainian territories, calling it illegitimate. He warned that Ukraine could impose sanctions over the transactions.

stories.title: Drones have range of 1,750 kilometers: Ukraine increases its deep-strike range against Russia by 2.5 times
stories.summary: Ukraine announced that its domestically developed long-range drones can now strike military targets at distances of approximately 1,750 kilometers into Russian territory, representing a 2.5-fold increase in deep-strike range since 2022.

stories.title: One year after Spain’s blackout, its shift to renewables and grid evolution power on
stories.summary: One year after a massive blackout struck Spain and much of Portugal, the country's transition to renewable energy continues to advance. Solar energy was initially and incorrectly blamed for the cascading grid failure. Renewables have since helped insulate Spain from rising gas prices driven by conflict in the Middle East.

stories.title: UAE to quit Opec and Opec+
stories.summary: The UAE announced it will leave both OPEC and OPEC+ effective May 1, citing long-term strategic and economic considerations. The decision comes amid disruptions to Gulf oil exports caused by the Iran conflict and tensions with Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: “Next major step”: Ukraine plans 50,000 ground robots to keep troops out of danger on drone-saturated front
stories.summary: Ukraine announced plans to deploy up to 50,000 ground robots along the front lines to reduce troop exposure. The robotic systems are already being used for logistics and casualty evacuations in high-risk zones on the drone-saturated battlefield.

stories.title: United Arab Emirates says it is leaving Opec and Opec+
stories.summary: The UAE announced its departure from both OPEC and OPEC+ effective May 1, describing the move as reflecting its evolving energy strategy. Gulf oil producers have already been struggling with exports due to disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: UAE to quit global oil cartel OPEC, citing 'national interests'
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced on Tuesday it will leave OPEC and OPEC+, citing national interests. The decision comes as energy prices continue to rise amid the ongoing conflict involving Iran.

stories.title: UAE quits Opec in win for Trump as oil cartel weakened
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates has withdrawn from the OPEC oil cartel, dealing a significant blow to the organization and its de facto leader, Saudi Arabia. The departure comes amid a global energy shock caused by the Iran war. Analysts say the move could weaken OPEC's ability to present a united front on production policy.

stories.title: Britain's King Charles meets Trump in bid to salvage ties
stories.summary: Britain’s King Charles III met Donald Trump at the White House early Tuesday, kicking off a high-stakes state visit shadowed by transatlantic tensions and a new alleged attempt to assassinate the US p

stories.title: Drone attack causes fire at Russia's Tuapse refinery, authorities say
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Russia's Tuapse oil refinery on the Black Sea coast, causing a fire, according to Russian authorities. The attack was reported on Tuesday, April 28.

stories.title: Europe’s smaller airports ‘under threat’ if fuel shortages cause many cancellations
stories.summary: The Airports Council International has warned that Europe's smaller airports face existential threats as the Middle East crisis drives up jet fuel prices. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has doubled jet fuel costs, prompting some carriers to cancel routes. The EU's new Entry-Exit System is also causing passenger delays.

stories.title: Lahore court grants interim bail to PM's daughter, son-in-law in money laundering case
stories.summary:
LAHORE: A special court (central) on Tuesday granted interim pre-arrest bail to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s daughter, Rabia Imran and her husband Imran Yousaf in a money laundering case.
The coupl

stories.title: EU’s strategic gas reserve may be stored in Ukrainian storage facilities, says Lithuanian energy minister
stories.summary: Lithuania's energy minister suggested that Ukraine's gas storage facilities could serve as a storage site for the European Union's strategic gas reserve, potentially contributing to the EU's energy balance after Ukraine joins the bloc.

stories.title: Lapid said willing to drop to third spot on ticket with Bennett if Eisenkot joins
stories.summary: Israeli opposition leader Yair Lapid reportedly expressed willingness to accept third position on a joint electoral ticket with Naftali Bennett if former military chief Gadi Eisenkot joined. Eisenkot has resisted the invitation, focusing on building his own Yashar party.

stories.title: Independence Day killing puts spotlight on youth violence wracking Petah Tikva’s streets
stories.summary: The fatal stabbing of a Pizza Hut employee by a group of teenagers during Israel's Independence Day highlighted a growing youth violence problem in Petah Tikva and other central Israeli cities.

stories.title: Uganda detains 231 foreigners in crackdown on possible human trafficking
stories.summary: Ugandan authorities detained 231 foreign nationals in a crackdown on illegal migration. The internal affairs ministry linked the detentions to suspected human trafficking and cyberscam operations.

stories.title: Israel using water access as ‘weapon’ in Gaza: MSF
stories.summary: Médecins Sans Frontières accused Israel of using control over water access as a weapon in Gaza, describing the practice as a campaign of collective punishment against Palestinians.

stories.title: Iran war: Who in Tehran could shape talks with the US?
stories.summary: Negotiations between the United States and Iran remain uncertain, with a breakthrough appearing unlikely in the near term. Analysts are examining which officials in Tehran hold the most influence over the direction of any potential talks.

stories.title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy rebukes Israel for buying grain 'stolen' by Russia
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy accused Israel of purchasing grain stolen by Russia from occupied Ukrainian territories. Ukraine summoned Israel's ambassador and reported that another ship carrying such grain has docked at an Israeli port.

stories.title: Pakistan, Sri Lanka commence two-week joint counter-terrorism exercise: ISPR
stories.summary: Pakistan and Sri Lanka launched a two-week joint counter-terrorism exercise called "Shake Hands-II" in Tarbela, involving Pakistan's Special Services Group and Sri Lankan Army Special Forces, aimed at enhancing professional military cooperation.

stories.title: Trial over foiled attack on Taylor Swift’s Vienna concert set to open
stories.summary: The trial of a 21-year-old suspect accused of plotting an attack on Taylor Swift's Vienna concert is set to open. The defendant's lawyer said he will plead guilty to the main charges.

stories.title: Antiquities dealer who exposed thefts at British Museum dies aged 61
stories.summary: Danish academic and antiquities dealer Ittai Gradel, who exposed the theft of hundreds of artefacts from the British Museum, has died of renal cancer at age 61. Gradel had alerted the museum and police after purchasing dozens of stolen museum items on eBay over several years. The museum recently awarded him a medal for his contributions.

stories.title: French parliamentary inquiry becomes far-right attack against public media
stories.summary: A French parliamentary inquiry into public broadcasters, led by 32-year-old lawmaker Charles Alloncle, has drawn criticism for amplifying far-right attacks on public media outlets including FRANCE 24. Critics warn the hearings, which have gone viral on social media, risk undermining trust in public broadcasting and may support far-right efforts to privatize the sector ahead of 2027 elections.

stories.title: UAE quits OPEC in shock move amid energy turmoil
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced its withdrawal from OPEC and OPEC+ amid energy market disruption driven by the Iran war. The departure marks a historic shift in Gulf energy politics and global oil market dynamics.

stories.title: Leading by example or showmanship? Singapore politicians’ train rides split opinion
stories.summary: Singapore politicians posting about their public transport use during the global energy crisis drew mixed reactions online. The trend followed Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong's call for citizens to use public transport as an energy-saving measure.

stories.title: What’s in Iran’s latest proposal – and how has the US responded?
stories.summary: Iran submitted a new diplomatic proposal to the United States, but the Trump administration signaled its rejection, citing an incomplete resolution of Tehran's nuclear ambitions as a key concern.

stories.title: Netanyahu helped 'create a genocide in Gaza', top Biden official says
stories.summary: Former senior Biden administration official Wendy Sherman stated that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu helped "create a genocide in Gaza" and led the United States down a path that destabilized the region.

stories.title: Somalia: Somalia Vows Stronger Protection for Commercial Shipping Amid Maritime Security Concerns
stories.summary: Somalia pledged to strengthen security for commercial vessels along its coastline amid growing concerns over the safety of key international shipping routes, officials announced at the United Nations.

stories.title: Lithuania ready to push for decision to ban Russian oil during its EU presidency, minister says
stories.summary: Lithuania's government announced its readiness to push for a full ban on Russian oil imports during its upcoming presidency of the Council of the European Union, as part of efforts to tighten sanctions against Moscow.

stories.title: Dozens of Gaza children arrive in Jordan for medical care
stories.summary: Eighty-one wounded or ill Palestinian children from Gaza, accompanied by 108 family members, arrived in Jordan for medical treatment through the King Hussein border crossing. Jordan's army confirmed this is the 26th group of children transported to the kingdom since the war in Gaza began in October 2023.

stories.title: ‘War crime’: Afghan-Pakistan truce under strain after university strike
stories.summary: Civilian casualties from a strike in Afghanistan's Kunar province have strained a ceasefire between Afghanistan and Pakistan. Pakistan denied involvement, casting doubt on ongoing peace talks.

stories.title: EBRD signs €54 million to keep trains in Ukraine moving through blackouts
stories.summary: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development signed a €54 million financing package to support Ukraine's state rail operator, aiming to keep train services running despite ongoing power blackouts. The agreement came one day after new sleeper cars were introduced in Kyiv.

stories.title: Why French banks are swapping the high street for high finance in Africa
stories.summary: French banks, including Société Générale, are withdrawing from retail banking operations across Africa. A new strategy emerging from Paris prioritises sovereign debt management and strategic financial corridors over maintaining local branch networks on the continent.

stories.title: Mali PM urges 'not to panic' after coordinated attack by jihadists, separatists
stories.summary: An alliance of al-Qaeda-linked militants and Tuareg separatists carried out the largest coordinated attack in over a decade in Mali. Mali's prime minister urged the public not to panic following the assault, which represents a significant escalation of extremist violence in the region.

stories.title: King Charles in US for state visit amid differences over Iran war
stories.summary: King Charles and Queen Camilla arrived in the United States on Monday for a four-day state visit, welcomed by President Donald Trump despite differences between Washington and London over the Iran war. The visit marks the 250th anniversary of the US Declaration of Independence and is the first by a British monarch in two decades.

stories.title: Gulf leaders to meet in Saudi Arabia to discuss Iran war
stories.summary: Gulf Cooperation Council leaders convened an exceptional meeting in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, to discuss their response to Iranian missile and drone attacks that have struck infrastructure across all six GCC member states during the Iran war.

stories.title: Violence escalates in Colombia with dozens of attacks before presidential vote
stories.summary: Rebel groups in Colombia's southwestern region staged 26 attacks using explosives and drones since Friday, including a highway bombing between Cali and Popayán that killed at least 21 people. The violence has heightened security concerns ahead of Colombia's May presidential election, where crime is expected to be a dominant issue.

stories.title: Trump unhappy with Iran, IDF takes down over 1,000 Hezbollah sites
stories.summary: The Jerusalem Post published a news roundup covering President Trump's dissatisfaction with Iran and the IDF's destruction of over 1,000 Hezbollah sites.

stories.title: UAE leaves OPEC in blow to oil cartel during war on Iran
stories.summary: The UAE announced its withdrawal from OPEC amid the ongoing conflict with Iran, as Gulf oil producers face significant difficulties shipping exports through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Gaza's bread crisis deepens with 50% production cuts
stories.summary: Gaza's Government Media Office warned that bread production in the territory has fallen by roughly 50 percent due to a sharp decline in flour deliveries entering the strip.

stories.title: Chinese industrial robot maker Inovance joins Hong Kong IPO queue
stories.summary: Chinese industrial automation company Shenzhen Inovance Technology filed for an IPO in Hong Kong, joining a wave of mainland tech firms seeking international capital. The Shenzhen-listed company has a market capitalization of approximately 175.3 billion yuan ($25.6 billion).

stories.title: China orders maritime security research as Strait of Hormuz crisis exposes trade risks
stories.summary: China has commissioned leading enterprises and academic institutions to research the protection of critical sea lanes and overseas port holdings. The initiative responds to vulnerabilities exposed by crises at maritime chokepoints, including the Strait of Hormuz blockade linked to the US-Israeli war in Iran.

stories.title: Facing US and Chinese pressure, the EU must forge its own strategy
stories.summary: A Tsinghua University scholar argued in Foreign Affairs that China wants Europe to act as an independent pole in the global order, but that Europe lacks strategic autonomy. The article contends that the EU must develop its own coherent strategy amid pressure from both the US and China.

stories.title: Forterra, Polaris tout new autonomous vehicle for CASEVAC, logistics
stories.summary: Forterra and Polaris have unveiled the MESA, a new autonomous vehicle designed for casualty evacuation and logistics operations. The vehicle is intended to operate up to the "last tactical mile," supporting both supply transport and CASEVAC missions in forward areas.

stories.title: 'Iranians believe they have upper hand because they can endure double blockade better than US'
stories.summary: Ali Vaez, Director of the Iran Project at the International Crisis Group, argued that Tehran believes it holds a strategic advantage over the United States because Iran can better endure the economic pressures of a prolonged double blockade. He noted that Washington faces mounting political and economic constraints that shape its negotiating behavior.

stories.title: General Staff confirms another strike on Tuapse Refinery
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed that Ukrainian Armed Forces units carried out a new strike on the Tuapse Refinery in Russia's Krasnodar region on the night of April 28.

stories.title: Exclusive: ICC Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan to address Oxford Union next week
stories.summary: ICC Chief Prosecutor Karim Khan is scheduled to speak at the Oxford Union, marking his first public appearance since judges cleared him of misconduct charges. His future role at the court remains uncertain.

stories.title: South Africa: Level 2 Warning for the Eastern Cape
stories.summary: South Africa's Weather Service issued Yellow Level 2 warnings for the Eastern Cape province, alerting residents to expected damaging winds and waves in the area.

stories.title: $60 million gone: Russian early-warning radar burns in Belgorod Oblast as Ukraine’s anti-air hunt continues
stories.summary: A Ukrainian kamikaze drone struck the antenna module of a Russian early-warning radar system in Belgorod Oblast, likely rendering it inoperable. The radar installation is estimated to be worth approximately $60 million and may require extensive repairs.

stories.title: Nigeria's leader battles security, political crises
stories.summary: Nigeria faces a worsening security crisis as politicians prepare for 2027 elections. Analysts say President Bola Tinubu's recent cabinet reshuffle is aimed at rebuilding public trust amid widespread insecurity affecting millions.

stories.title: Ghana's military hunts those behind convoy attack on northern highway
stories.summary: Ghana's military launched a search operation after an attack on a convoy along a northern highway killed three civilians and seven gunmen. The violence occurred in an area affected by a long-running chieftaincy dispute.

stories.title: Mali’s PM urges public 'not to give in to panic' after Kidal fall
stories.summary: Mali's Prime Minister Abdoulaye Maiga urged citizens not to panic after jihadist fighters and Tuareg separatists seized the strategic northern town of Kidal in coordinated attacks that also killed the country's defence minister.

stories.title: Posthumous parenthood: After loss of loved ones, Israeli widows choose to bring new life
stories.summary: A growing number of Israeli widows are choosing posthumous conception using their fallen partners' genetic material in the aftermath of October 7. The trend raises significant legal and ethical questions about posthumous parenthood in Israel.

stories.title: UK will tax soaring BP profits from Iran war, says Ed Miliband
stories.summary: UK Energy Minister Ed Miliband announced plans to tax windfall profits of companies like BP, whose earnings more than doubled due to oil price spikes caused by the Iran war, to address the cost-of-living crisis.

stories.title: Australia’s top diplomat visits China to talk energy security
stories.summary: Australia's top diplomat traveled to China for discussions focused on energy security, though specific details of the talks were not immediately disclosed.

stories.title: Israeli families vow to stay in North: 'If we're not here, Hezbollah will be here'
stories.summary: Israeli families living near the northern border with Lebanon say they are determined to remain in their homes despite an unstable ceasefire. Residents expressed concern that leaving would allow Hezbollah to establish a presence in the area.

stories.title: US Treasury chief says businesses working with Iranian airlines risk sanctions
stories.summary: The US Treasury secretary warned that businesses working with Iranian airlines risk facing sanctions. Iran has reportedly resumed commercial flights from Tehran's international airport.

stories.title: 'Totally lost': Israel's next generation faces rising wartime trauma, study warns
stories.summary: A new study warns of rising wartime trauma among Israeli children living in northern and southern border regions. The research documents deepening psychological harm to the next generation as conflict continues.

stories.title: Through a mother's eyes: The wartime struggle of Israelis with special needs - comment
stories.summary: An analysis examines the wartime struggles faced by Israelis with special needs and their families. The piece highlights the mental and physical challenges confronting this population amid ongoing conflict in the region.

stories.title: Imran brought to Pims for follow-up treatment, undergoes fourth eye procedure
stories.summary: Former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan received his fourth intravitreal anti-VEGF injection at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences in Islamabad for right central retinal vein occlusion and was discharged on Tuesday morning.

stories.title: Aliyah under fire: The new immigrants who chose Israel despite war and uncertainty
stories.summary: Five new immigrants made aliyah to Israel despite the ongoing conflict, choosing to settle in the country amid sirens and missile threats. They described the move as fulfilling a lifelong dream.

stories.title: Migrants in hiding as Mauritania pushbacks drastically cut Europe arrivals
stories.summary: Following an agreement with the European Union, Mauritanian authorities have rounded up and deported thousands of migrants to Mali and Senegal, drastically reducing the number of arrivals reaching Europe via Atlantic routes.

stories.title: 'Israel destroyed houses, roads, even trees': People return to destruction in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Residents returning to southern Lebanon after a ceasefire have documented widespread destruction by the Israeli army, including demolished houses, roads, and infrastructure. Israel has been creating a buffer zone along the border. Observers describe finding empty villages and razed homes throughout the area.

stories.title: Beyond the strikes: How healthcare is holding Israel’s displaced together
stories.summary: As missile strikes displace thousands of Israelis, the country's healthcare system has adapted by establishing medical care services inside hotels housing displaced populations.

stories.title: Russia’s War Boom Masks an Economic Implosion
stories.summary: Russia's wartime economy shows record-low unemployment, but analysts say this masks deeper structural problems. The labor shortage is attributed to millions of missing workers, suggesting the apparent economic boom conceals significant underlying damage to Russia's workforce and long-term economic capacity.

stories.title: Nigeria: In Borno, Cash Transfers Are Helping Families Treat Malnutrition Beyond the Clinic
stories.summary: In Borno State's Konduga area, cash transfer programs are helping families treat childhood malnutrition outside clinical settings, supporting vulnerable households struggling to afford food and basic necessities.

stories.title: Kenya: Ruto Says English Comments Taken Out of Context As Nigeria Responds to Viral Remarks
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto said his recent remarks on English usage were taken out of context, claiming a private conversation was recorded and circulated widely online, prompting a diplomatic response from Nigeria.

stories.title: Why Japan is now opening its door to lethal weapons exports
stories.summary: Japan is shifting away from its longstanding pacifist weapons export policies amid rising tensions with China and North Korea. Australia and the Philippines are expected to be among the first partners for Tokyo's new lethal weapons exports.

stories.title: Japan looks to woo allies with new weapons deals
stories.summary: Japan has scrapped a decades-old ban on exporting lethal weapons, seeking to strengthen alliances through new arms deals. The policy shift comes amid growing security tensions with China and North Korea.

stories.title: China testing truck-mounted nuclear reactor that could power AI data centre
stories.summary: Chinese scientists are testing a prototype truck-mounted nuclear reactor described as the world's first 10-megawatt vehicle-mounted nuclear power unit. The reactor, which has been in development for several years, could generate enough electricity to power a medium-sized AI data centre. The team is now seeking practical deployment opportunities.

stories.title: Mali: Malian Official Accuses Russian Forces of 'Betrayal' After Kidal Falls to Rebels
stories.summary: Russian paramilitary forces withdrew from the northern Malian city of Kidal, allowing jihadist and Tuareg rebels to seize the strategic stronghold. A senior Malian official accused Russian forces of "betrayal," as coordinated attacks across the country also killed Mali's defence minister.

stories.title: Iraq appoints businessman Ali Al-Zaidi as prime minister
stories.summary: Iraq's ruling Coordination Framework coalition named businessman Ali Al-Zaidi as the country's new prime minister. The appointment follows nearly five months of complex political deadlock.

stories.title: Police launch major operation to combat youth violence after deadly stabbings
stories.summary: Israeli police launched a major operation to address youth violence following deadly stabbings, including increased law enforcement presence and deployment of the controversial National Guard in Tel Aviv. The main suspect in the Petah Tikva killing reportedly refused to cooperate with investigators.

stories.title: Life in Tehran since the ceasefire: How Iranian society is evolving
stories.summary: Since a ceasefire took effect, daily life in Tehran has largely returned to normal despite the ongoing stalemate in the Strait of Hormuz and stalled peace talks between the US and Iran. FRANCE 24 correspondents report that Iranian society is undergoing a significant transformation, a process that began months ago and has intensified during the war.

stories.title: Greece man, 89, arrested after Athens shooting injures 5 people
stories.summary: An 89-year-old man opened fire with a hunting rifle at a social security office in Athens, Greece, on Tuesday, wounding an employee in the leg. He then carried out a second shooting at an Athens courthouse, lightly injuring four more people. The suspect, reportedly motivated by pension disputes, was later arrested in Patras.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Chuhuiv this morning, resulting in two dead
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the city of Chuhuiv in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, killing two people. One man died at the scene and another was seriously wounded before dying in the hospital.

stories.title: In Israel’s Arab sector, war exposes a dual threat of rampant crime and no shelter
stories.summary: Arab Israeli communities face a dual threat of ongoing conflict and rampant domestic crime, with residents reporting a lack of bomb shelters and government neglect. Community members say long-standing underinvestment has left them especially vulnerable during wartime.

stories.title: Iran war begins to hit China’s economy as costs surge
stories.summary: The war in Iran is negatively affecting China's economy, with surging energy and plastic prices contributing to declining car sales, factory closures in the toy sector, and worker protests across the country.

stories.title: Is it wrong to show Taiwan army officers a film about KMT forces fighting Japan in WWII?
stories.summary: A Taiwanese army officer was disciplined for screening The Eight Hundred, a mainland Chinese film depicting Kuomintang forces fighting Japanese troops in World War II. The punishment sparked a political controversy on the island, with ruling Democratic Progressive Party lawmaker Wang Ting-yu raising concerns about Beijing's state-led messaging and its influence on military education in Taiwan.

stories.title: A generational crisis: Israel's most vulnerable children pay war's steepest price
stories.summary: Research highlights the severe impact of the Israel-Iran conflict on at-risk Israeli children and youth. The study describes a generational crisis in which the most vulnerable young people are bearing the heaviest toll of the ongoing war.

stories.title: From Start-Up Nation to recovery nation: How Israel is rebuilding mental health at scale - analysis
stories.summary: Israel is scaling up mental health technology and services in response to a surge in trauma cases across the country. The effort aims to expand access to psychological care and build national resilience, leveraging the country's tech sector expertise.

stories.title: Even in ceasefire, Israelis are still living with the war - from the editor
stories.summary: The article examines how Israelis continue to navigate loss, trauma, and rebuilding even during ceasefire conditions. It highlights both resilience and underlying strain affecting Israeli society amid ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Northern officials, residents denounce Lebanon truce: ‘Stop using our kids as sitting ducks’
stories.summary: Officials and residents in northern Israel criticized the Lebanon ceasefire, with one council head urging decision-makers to experience conditions firsthand. Security cabinet member Miri Regev acknowledged the situation resembled a "porous ceasefire" rather than a stable truce.

stories.title: Rubio defends daily Israeli strikes in Lebanon despite ceasefire
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended ongoing daily Israeli airstrikes in Lebanon despite a ceasefire being in place. Rubio claimed that both Israel and Lebanon view Hezbollah as the central problem.

stories.title: North Korea’s executions for watching K-dramas, foreign content surge during Covid-19: report
stories.summary: A report by the Transition Justice Working Group found that North Korean executions for consuming South Korean cultural content—including K-dramas, films, and K-pop—surged by 250 per cent during the Covid-19 pandemic. The Pyongyang-based crackdown also targeted religious practices, according to the North Korea-focused human rights organisation's findings released Tuesday.

stories.title: Israeli army kills child in Gaza, settlers burn Palestinian home
stories.summary: Gaza's post-ceasefire death toll has reached 818 after a boy was killed by Israeli forces in Khan Younis. In the West Bank, Israeli settlers set fire to a Palestinian home as settler violence continued.

stories.title: Plane crash in South Sudan kills 14
stories.summary: A plane crash near Juba, South Sudan, killed 14 people. Bad weather is reported to have been a contributing factor, underscoring ongoing aviation safety and infrastructure challenges in the country.

stories.title: BYD, China’s EV king, posts a 55% slump in first-quarter profit
stories.summary: BYD, China's largest electric vehicle maker, reported a 55 per cent year-on-year decline in first-quarter net profit to approximately 4.09 billion yuan (US$590 million). Revenue fell 11.8 per cent to 150.2 billion yuan, as weakness in the domestic Chinese market offset rising exports.

stories.title: Europe makes mistake regarding war in Ukraine back in 2022, says Estonian president
stories.summary: Estonian President Alar Karis said Europe missed an opportunity to begin peace talks with Moscow at the start of the full-scale war in Ukraine in 2022, calling it a strategic mistake.

stories.title: Lapid to be allocated 10 out of top 24 mandates in Together Party's Knesset list, sources tell KAN
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid have agreed that Lapid's Yesh Atid party will receive 10 of the top 24 spots on their joint Together Party Knesset list, with provisions enabling the factions to split after the election.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Russian oil refinery causes major fire, officials say
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike caused a large-scale fire at the Rosneft-owned Tuapse oil refinery on Russia's Black Sea coast on Tuesday, prompting evacuations of nearby buildings. The refinery had already halted operations since April 16 following a previous drone attack. Kyiv has intensified strikes on Russian infrastructure since March.

stories.title: Google breaks ground on AI megahub in India
stories.summary:
Tech giant Google on Tuesday marked the ceremonial start of work on its largest artificial intelligence hub outside of the United States with a groundbreaking ceremony in India.
The firm promised in O

stories.title: How a surgeon kept a Sudan hospital functioning on the war’s front line
stories.summary: Dr. Jamal Eltaeb led Al Nao hospital in Omdurman, near Khartoum, keeping it operational as control of the area shifted between the Sudanese army and paramilitary Rapid Support Forces fighters on the war's front line.

stories.title: Russia is killing journalists and jailing them as “terrorists,” Ukraine tells UN
stories.summary: Ukraine's delegation to the United Nations reported that at least 26 Ukrainian media workers are being held in Russian captivity and 147 have been killed since the full-scale invasion began. Ukraine accused Russia of killing journalists and jailing them on terrorism charges.

stories.title: White House to review presidential security; spotlight on line of succession
stories.summary: The White House announced a review of presidential security following a foiled attack at the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents Association Dinner, an event attended by several cabinet secretaries, raising questions about the presidential line of succession.

stories.title: Authorities Order Evacuations Following Third Ukrainian Strike on Tuapse Refinery
stories.summary: Authorities ordered evacuations following a third Ukrainian strike on the Tuapse refinery. Separately, at least three people were killed in overnight attacks on Russia's Belgorod region.

stories.title: Displaced women in Lebanon face period poverty amid Israel's war
stories.summary: Women displaced by Israeli military operations across Lebanon are struggling to access menstrual hygiene supplies. The situation highlights a hidden crisis of poverty, stigma, and neglect among displaced populations.

stories.title: Amnesty calls for US strike on Yemen to be investigated as war crime
stories.summary: Amnesty International called for an investigation into a U.S. airstrike on a migrant detention facility in Yemen, which killed at least 68 people, arguing it may constitute a war crime.

stories.title: Israel-Iran war LIVE: Budget airlines first to cut flights as jet fuel prices soar
stories.summary: Budget airlines began cutting flights as jet fuel prices surged amid the Israel-Iran war, while US and Iranian officials clashed over Tehran's nuclear program at a UN review of the atomic treaty. Iran's foreign minister praised Russia's diplomatic support.

stories.title: U.S. Trade Representative's Office to hear investigations on Trump’s new import taxes
stories.summary: The U.S. Trade Representative's Office scheduled hearings on new temporary import taxes that President Trump imposed after the Supreme Court struck down his preferred tariffs in February.

stories.title: BP reports huge profit rise in first quarter amid Iran war
stories.summary: BP reported a significant rise in first-quarter profits driven by higher oil prices linked to the Middle East conflict. Strong trading performance and market volatility also contributed to the surge.

stories.title: Russians attack infrastructure facility in Kryvyi Rih again; one person injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck an infrastructure facility in Kryvyi Rih, Ukraine, for the second time in one morning, injuring one person in the attack.

stories.title: How the US-Israeli war is collapsing the sanctions regime on Iran
stories.summary: The ongoing U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran is undermining international sanctions enforcement on Tehran. Analysts note that circumvention mechanisms already exist and the conflict is encouraging more entities to exploit them.

stories.title: Mapping the destruction: How Israel ‘wiped out’ Lebanon’s Bint Jbeil
stories.summary: An Al Jazeera visual investigation mapped systematic demolition of the Lebanese border town of Bint Jbeil by Israeli forces, drawing comparisons to the devastation seen in Gaza.

stories.title: When will Strait of Hormuz be ‘safe’ for commercial shipping again?
stories.summary: Analysts warn that even if the Strait of Hormuz reopens to commercial shipping, insurance costs could rise to 20 times pre-war levels, posing lasting economic consequences for global trade.

stories.title: ‘Back to what he used to be’: Babar Azam’s unlearning journey
stories.summary: Pakistan cricket captain Babar Azam trained at the Hanif Mohammad High-Performance Centre in Karachi ahead of Peshawar Zalmi's HBL Pakistan Super League qualifier against Islamabad United, with observers noting a return to his earlier batting form.

stories.title: Mossad chief says agency’s operations penetrated ‘core’ of Iran, Lebanon secrets
stories.summary: Mossad Director David Barnea stated that the agency's operations penetrated the "core" of Iranian and Lebanese intelligence secrets. He commended ten operations for outstanding achievements in 2025 and highlighted enhanced cooperation with the Israeli military.

stories.title: Sydney concert to benefit Bondi terror victims canceled after choir opposes singing with Jewish group
stories.summary: A planned benefit concert in Sydney for Bondi terror victims was canceled after more than half of the Australian Hellenic Choir voted against performing alongside the Sydney Jewish Choral Society, prompting accusations of antisemitism.

stories.title: Mexican cartel leader found hiding in a ditch
stories.summary: Mexican authorities captured Audias Flores Silva, a key leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, who was found hiding in a ditch. His arrest comes approximately two months after the cartel's top leader was killed.

stories.title: 'Firmly committed' to Iran-US peace, Pakistan tells UN Security Council
stories.summary: Pakistan's UN representative Asim Iftikhar Ahmad told the Security Council that Islamabad remains committed to a peaceful resolution of the US-Iran conflict, warning that the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz could trigger severe global economic and security consequences.

stories.title: Iran's Araghchi says US requested new round of talks
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi stated that the United States has requested a new round of talks with Tehran. Reports indicate Trump is dissatisfied with Iran's latest proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz while postponing nuclear discussions.

stories.title: Shelling causes new power outages in three regions, says Ukrenergo
stories.summary: Russian shelling caused power outages across three Ukrainian regions as of the morning of April 27. The Sumy region was the hardest hit, with additional outages reported in the Zaporizhzhia and Kharkiv regions, according to Ukrenergo.

stories.title: Why Moody’s has raised China’s credit outlook amid Iran war shocks
stories.summary: Moody's Ratings upgraded China's sovereign credit outlook from "negative" to "stable," signalling increased confidence in the world's second-largest economy. The move came amid energy shocks from the US-Israel war in Iran and broader concerns about the global economic trajectory. Moody's had previously downgraded China's sovereign rating from Aa3 to A1 in 2017.

stories.title: Energy security comes first for Indonesia as it defies EU over Russian oil
stories.summary: Indonesia is proceeding with plans to import 150 million barrels of Russian oil despite new EU sanctions targeting the Karimun Oil Terminal in Indonesia for alleged connections to Russia's shadow fleet and circumvention of the oil price cap. The European Commission announced the sanctions as part of its 20th package of measures against Russia.

stories.title: China upgrades maritime rescue range and depth as ambitions on high seas expand
stories.summary: China's maritime rescue authorities have expanded their deep-sea search and rescue capabilities beyond 4,000 metres, according to state media outlet People's Daily. The Nanhai Rescue Bureau, responsible for operations in China's southern waters, credited the development of high-tech equipment for enabling practical operations at such depths.

stories.title: Middle East crisis could cost world $1tn while oil firms make ‘obscene’ profit, analysis finds
stories.summary: An analysis cited by climate campaigners estimates the Middle East oil and gas crisis could impose up to $1 trillion in additional costs on the global economy. Petroleum companies are reportedly earning substantial profits from elevated fuel prices. Campaigners called for urgent windfall taxes at a conference in Colombia.

stories.title: African cotton: Governments step back in as markets falter
stories.summary: The cotton sector across the CFA franc zone is undergoing major restructuring. Mali faces a sharply weaker season, Benin has recorded a record year, and Burkina Faso has moved toward nationalisation, as governments intervene amid falling global cotton prices.

stories.title: Hong Kong urged to shift focus from tourist numbers to increasing spending
stories.summary: Researchers from Hong Kong Polytechnic University and consultancy Think China urged Hong Kong to prioritise increasing tourist spending over boosting visitor numbers. Their preliminary findings show mainland Chinese visitor arrivals have recovered to about 88 per cent of pre-pandemic 2018 levels, but high-income travellers are spending less and adopting more selective consumption habits.

stories.title: Is capitalism fuelling today’s wars? Varsha Gandikota & Jason Hickel
stories.summary: Political economist Jason Hickel and Varsha Gandikota-Nellutla discussed whether capitalism drives modern conflicts and whether Global South nations can reclaim sovereignty in the current global order.

stories.title: Mossad head Barnea highlights operational capabilities, strategic success against Iran, Hezbollah
stories.summary: Mossad Director David Barnea praised the agency's operational capabilities during a citation ceremony, highlighting what he described as strategic successes in operations against Iran and Hezbollah carried out in target countries.

stories.title: Mikhail Piotrovsky runs Russia’s Hermitage Museum. EU just sanctioned him for legitimizing Russia’s occupation of Ukraine
stories.summary: The European Union sanctioned Mikhail Piotrovsky, director of Russia's Hermitage Museum in St. Petersburg, for his role in legitimizing Russia's occupation of Ukraine.

stories.title: Austria Islamic State man admits plot on Taylor Swift concert in Vienna
stories.summary: A man accused of pledging allegiance to Islamic State and plotting an attack on Taylor Swift's Vienna concerts in August 2024 pleaded guilty as his trial began on Tuesday in Austria. Austrian authorities had cancelled Swift's three scheduled Eras Tour performances after the plot was thwarted.

stories.title: Mali reeling after coordinated attacks expose security cracks
stories.summary: Mali faced widespread instability after coordinated attacks by jihadist fighters and rebel groups resulted in the seizure of multiple towns and military bases over the weekend, exposing significant security vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Turkish Airlines: Rising fuel costs and regional conflict force African retreat
stories.summary: Turkish Airlines is suspending routes to 10 African destinations after a decade of expansion on the continent. Rising fuel costs and regional geopolitical conflicts are cited as the primary factors driving the retreat.

stories.title: US startups explore genome editing in human embryos, raising ethical concerns
stories.summary: A press review covered multiple global stories, including US startups exploring genome editing in human embryos, raising ethical concerns. Other topics included photos of starving soldiers in Ukraine, the controversial Alloncle report on French public broadcasting, and President Trump's renewed call to fire talk show host Jimmy Kimmel.

stories.title: Military base in Crimea, where Russia stores Iskander missiles, catches fire following a nighttime attack
stories.summary: A military base in Russian-occupied Crimea used to store Iskander operational-tactical missile systems caught fire following a nighttime attack on April 27–28.

stories.title: Mali: Rebels Now in Control of Key Mali Town After Attacks
stories.summary: Jihadist and Tuareg separatist forces seized control of the key northern Malian town of Kidal following coordinated attacks on military junta positions across the country, according to local sources and an ally of the local governor.

stories.title: King Charles to promote British-US unity in speech to Congress
stories.summary: King Charles III is scheduled to address the US Congress with a speech emphasizing British-American unity, shared values, and global security cooperation, amid ongoing tensions related to the Iran conflict and transatlantic defense ties.

stories.title: Israel orders Lebanese to flee over a dozen towns and villages
stories.summary: Israel's military ordered residents in more than a dozen towns and villages in southern Lebanon to evacuate northward immediately, citing Hezbollah's violation of a ceasefire agreement. Israeli artillery and air strikes on southern Lebanon have continued despite a ceasefire signed on April 16.

stories.title: Trump not happy with latest Iran proposal to end the war, U.S. official says
stories.summary: A US official said President Trump was dissatisfied with Iran's latest proposal to end the war, as oil prices continued to climb in early Asia trading on April 28, 2026, reflecting the distance between the two sides in negotiations.

stories.title: The cost for Ukraine of Trump’s deal with Lukeshenka
stories.summary: Three rounds of US sanctions relief over six months freed more than 400 prisoners and partially reopened Belarus's financial system as part of a Trump-Lukashenko deal. However, the Belarusian regime continues to support Russia's war effort in Ukraine, raising questions about the cost to Kyiv.

stories.title: The evolving China-Pakistan space cooperation
stories.summary: The article examines the evolving space cooperation between China and Pakistan, framing it as an extension of their longstanding "all-weather" strategic partnership.

stories.title: Daily Briefing Apr. 28 – Untangling the Iran-Russia-Hezbollah web
stories.summary: Mideast expert Ksenia Svetlova analyzed the Tehran-Moscow-Hezbollah relationship and assessed that Gulf states face a critical juncture as they plan for the possibility of a nuclear-armed Iran.

stories.title: What does a $1 billion default look like? In Ukraine, it looks like six new sleeper cars.
stories.summary: Ukraine's state rail operator, which has defaulted on its debt, introduced six new sleeper cars despite ongoing destruction of its rolling stock. Russia is reportedly destroying rail carriages at a rate approximately forty times faster than Ukraine can build replacements.

stories.title: Iran Is More Unified Than Ever
stories.summary: Analysts argue that the war with the US and Israel has deepened unity among Iranian officials and strengthened connections between the government and the public. The conflict has reportedly consolidated internal cohesion across Iran's political and security establishment.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Patriot systems are on a “starvation ration,” Air Force spox says
stories.summary: A Ukrainian Air Force spokesperson stated that Ukraine's Patriot air defense systems are operating on a "starvation ration" of interceptors. Russia fired more than 700 missiles at Ukraine over the past winter, a significant portion of which were ballistic missiles.

stories.title: Sudan: Darfur - Two Decades On, a New Generation of Children Faces 'Horrific Violence'
stories.summary: A UN report warned that children in Sudan's Darfur region face a renewed cycle of violence, hunger, and displacement two decades after the conflict first drew international attention. The agency said the current crisis is receiving insufficient global notice.

stories.title: Russians strike infrastructure facility in Kryvyi Rih, one person killed, five wounded
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck an infrastructure facility in Kryvyi Rih, Dnipropetrovsk region, killing one man and wounding five others.

stories.title: Security fears mount for Ghana’s border economy after convoy attack
stories.summary: Three civilians were killed in an attack on a military-escorted convoy along the Bawku-Bolgatanga corridor in northern Ghana. The corridor is a key commercial route linking Accra with Burkina Faso and Togo, and the incident has heightened security concerns for the border economy.

stories.title: Israel's policy of endless war is fuelled by the crisis of Zionism
stories.summary: An opinion piece by Andrew Hammond argues that Israel's pursuit of continuous military campaigns is driven by internal insecurity and a crisis within Zionism, contending the approach has failed to achieve regional stability or hegemony.

stories.title: Hafiz Saeed's close aide and key LeT figure Sheikh Yousaf Afridi shot dead in Pakistan
stories.summary: Sheikh Yousaf Afridi, a close aide to Hafiz Saeed and key figure in the Lashkar-e-Taiba militant group, was shot dead in Pakistan. Afridi reportedly played a role in recruitment and coordination of the group's activities in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

stories.title: Tel Aviv’s ‘Open Houses’ offers fresh peek at private and public spaces
stories.summary: Tel Aviv's annual 'Batim Mibifnim' (Homes from the Inside) event, which opens private and public spaces to visitors, begins registration on May 1.

stories.title: Iraq names little-known banker Ali al-Zaidi as PM after five-month deadlock
stories.summary: Iraq named Ali al-Zaidi, a little-known banker, as prime minister-designate following a five-month political deadlock. Reports suggest al-Zaidi was a largely unknown figure whom Iraq's political factions settled on as a compromise candidate.

stories.title: Attack against Ghana military convoy kills three civilians
stories.summary: A military-escorted civilian convoy in northern Ghana was attacked on Monday, killing three civilians and injuring one, according to the Ghana Armed Forces.

stories.title: French researcher cracks 4,000-year-old Elamite script from Iran
stories.summary: French archaeologist François Desset has made significant progress in deciphering Linear Elamite, a 4,000-year-old script from what is now Iran that has long eluded researchers. His work has drawn comparisons to Jean-François Champollion, who deciphered ancient Egyptian hieroglyphics in the 19th century.

stories.title: Who is Iyad Ag Ghali, Mali’s most wanted man?
stories.summary: Iyad Ag Ghali, leader of the al-Qaeda-linked group JNIM (Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin), is Mali's most wanted man. His organization, allied with Tuareg separatists, carried out the largest coordinated attack in Mali in over a decade. French forces, Malian authorities, and Russian mercenaries have all failed to capture him.

stories.title: Starmer says 'people might change their habits' because of Iran war

stories.summary: Pakistan's Economic Coordination Committee approved the export of donkey meat and hides from Gwadar Port to China, acting on a summary submitted by the Food Security Division for disposal of existing inventory under export protocols.

stories.title: Pro-Kremlin blogger admits role in Navalny persecution, says he now plans to lead Russia’s opposition
stories.summary: Pro-Kremlin blogger Ilya Remeslo, known for his role in pursuing criminal cases against the late opposition leader Alexei Navalny, publicly criticized Vladimir Putin in a Telegram post in mid-March and was subsequently placed in a psychiatric hospital for a month. After his release, Remeslo told journalist Ksenia Sobchak he had changed his political stance and intends to lead Russia's opposition.

stories.title: Iran slams EU sanctions, condemns US tanker seizures
stories.summary: Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei condemned new EU sanctions as reflecting 'double standards' and criticized US seizures of Iranian-linked tankers, calling them 'piracy on the high seas.'

stories.title: Trump and team renew attacks on adversaries after gala shooting
stories.summary: President Trump and members of his administration renewed attacks on political adversaries following a shooting at a gala event. The administration's tone shifted quickly after the incident.

stories.title: Trolleybus overhead lines dismantled in Sloviansk to protect them from shelling
stories.summary: Authorities in Sloviansk, Donetsk region, dismantled trolleybus overhead contact lines and removed the equipment from the city to protect it from increasing Russian shelling.

stories.title: Northern council head, five others arrested on suspicion of bribery
stories.summary: A northern Israeli council head and five others were arrested on suspicion of bribery. Police allege the suspects participated in a scheme involving computer service contractors who offered kickbacks to secure municipal tenders.

stories.title: ‘Zero enrichment’ stance complicates talks, analyst says
stories.summary: Geopolitical analyst Giorgio Cafiero told Al Jazeera that Washington's insistence on 'zero enrichment' complicates diplomatic efforts with Iran. He suggested accepting limited uranium enrichment could open a path to a new agreement.

stories.title: Estonia proposes barring Russian and Belarusian citizens without permanent residency from buying property
stories.summary: Estonia's Internal Affairs Ministry has drafted legislation that would prohibit Russian and Belarusian citizens without permanent residency from purchasing real estate in the country.

stories.title: ‘Book Van’ and ‘Science Ride’  bring learning to Balochistan villages
stories.summary: In Balochistan, Pakistan, the education department launched 'Book Van' and 'Science Ride' mobile learning projects with UNICEF support, delivering educational materials door-to-door to children across 14 districts in remote areas of the province.

stories.title: Rights group seeks removal of Russian opposition platform member at PACE who called ‘honor killings’ a family matter
stories.summary: The human rights group SK SOS, which assists North Caucasus residents fleeing violence, has called for the removal of Ruslan Kutayev from the Russian opposition platform at the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe after he reportedly justified so-called honor killings in Chechnya.

stories.title: Iranian defence official holds talks with Russian, Belarusian ministers
stories.summary: Russian Defence Minister Andrei Belousov met with Iran's Deputy Defence Minister Reza Talaei-Nik on the sidelines of talks in Kyrgyzstan on Monday. The meeting, reported by Russia's TASS news agency, also involved discussions with Belarusian officials.

stories.title: Iran clashes with US, UAE, over position in UN nuclear non-proliferation conference
stories.summary: Iran clashed with the United States and the UAE at a UN nuclear non-proliferation conference over Tehran's nomination for a leadership role. The US representative called Iran's selection an 'affront to the Non-Proliferation Treaty itself.'

stories.title: Drone attack in south Lebanon, Israeli troops reported injured
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported two soldiers were injured in a Hezbollah drone attack in southern Lebanon. One soldier was described as severely injured. Both were evacuated for hospital treatment.

stories.title: At least 20 killed in Colombia highway blast
stories.summary: At least 20 people were killed in an explosion on a highway in Colombia. President Gustavo Petro attributed the attack to a narco-terrorist group led by a former FARC fighter.

stories.title: Jewish continuity needs you. Donate to Jewish higher education - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A sponsored appeal encourages donations to Jewish higher education institutions, arguing that supporting such programs helps sustain Jewish heritage and develop future community leaders.

stories.title: Every third apartment building in Zaporizhzhia damaged by shelling – city authorities
stories.summary: Zaporizhzhia city authorities reported that 1,405 apartment buildings — roughly one in three across the city — have been damaged by enemy shelling.

stories.title: After blows to his anti-protest laws, Minns considers retreat from ‘globalise the intifada’ ban
stories.summary: New South Wales Premier Chris Minns indicated he may not pursue a ban on the slogan "globalise the intifada," saying he would only act if a constitutional challenge to a similar ban in Queensland fails. The proposed ban followed the Bondi terror attack but has faced legal setbacks.

stories.title: Outgoing Mossad chief reportedly says Qatargate affair didn’t seem to harm state security
stories.summary: Outgoing Mossad chief David Barnea reportedly said the Qatargate affair did not appear to harm Israeli state security. His assessment contradicts the position of former Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar.

stories.title: US, Iran clash at UN after Tehran gets nuclear non-proliferation role
stories.summary: The United States and Iran clashed at the United Nations after Tehran was selected for a role related to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty. Washington called Iran's appointment an "affront" to the treaty's principles.

stories.title: New Zealand spy plane reports possible North Korea sanctions breach at sea
stories.summary: A New Zealand Defence Force surveillance aircraft observed a North Korean vessel engaging in a suspected illicit transfer of goods at sea, potentially breaching United Nations sanctions imposed on North Korea.

stories.title: Tech giants face new levy to pay for Australian news as Meta calls position ‘simply wrong’
stories.summary: The Australian government under Prime Minister Anthony Albanese unveiled a draft news bargaining scheme that would impose a 2.25 percent levy on local revenues of Google, Meta, and TikTok unless they strike deals with Australian media outlets. Both Google and Meta criticized the proposed reform.

stories.title: Taking power in Mali might be a stretch but insurgents can force hand of weakened regime
stories.summary: Al-Qaida-affiliated group JNIM and Tuareg insurgents launched coordinated attacks on military bases and towns in Mali, inflicting significant casualties on government forces and Russian auxiliary fighters. While observers note tactical gains by the militants, analysts say seizing full power remains unlikely despite the weakened state of the ruling regime.

stories.title: Lebanon accuses Israel of committing ‘ecocide’ in country since 2023
stories.summary: Lebanon's environment minister accused Israel's military of committing "ecocide" in a report detailing ecological damage during the 2023-2024 invasion. The report found that Israeli military operations damaged 5,000 hectares of forest cover and reshaped southern Lebanon's physical and ecological landscape.

stories.title: Calls for ‘student premium’ to support disadvantaged young people after GCSEs
stories.summary: A coalition of 14 social mobility organisations in the UK is urging the government to create a "student premium" to support disadvantaged young people after age 16. They warn that a post-16 funding gap risks young people falling out of education, employment, and training.

stories.title: The next Knesset should belong to those who choose to serve - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial argued that the next Knesset should prioritize representatives from communities that serve Israel, framing mandatory service as a nonpartisan Zionist principle.

stories.title: Iran oil shipments plunge as Hormuz blockade tightens, data shows
stories.summary: Iranian oil shipments have fallen sharply as the Strait of Hormuz blockade tightens, according to Kpler data cited by the Wall Street Journal. Analysts warn Iran's crude production could drop to around 1.2–1.3 million barrels per day by mid-May if restrictions persist.

stories.title: Philippines’ Sara Duterte hits back against wealth allegations as impeachment looms
stories.summary: Philippine Vice-President Sara Duterte-Carpio and her spouse are pushing back against allegations of ill-gotten wealth as the House of Representatives prepares to submit Articles of Impeachment to the Senate, potentially by early May.

stories.title: Doctor arrested on suspicion of threatening Channel 12 journalist Mohammad Magadli
stories.summary: A 40-year-old doctor from northern Israel was arrested on suspicion of repeatedly threatening Channel 12 journalist Mohammad Magadli by phone from an unknown number.

stories.title: Hong Kong adds spared Wang Fuk Court block to resettlement plan as most opt to sell
stories.summary: The Hong Kong government will include Wang Chi House — the only block undamaged in the November 26 Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po that killed 168 people — in its resettlement plan after three-quarters of homeowners indicated they preferred to sell their flats to authorities. The block had originally been excluded from long-term resettlement proposals.

stories.title: Video: Iran’s UN envoy says Tehran ‘not bound’ by UN Law of the Sea
stories.summary: Iran's UN envoy Amir Saeid Iravani declared that Tehran is 'not bound' by the UN Law of the Sea and defended Iran's maritime actions in the Strait of Hormuz. He accused some nations of 'double standards' regarding the US-imposed maritime blockade.

stories.title: U.S., Iran clash over Tehran's nuclear programme as review of atomic treaty begins at UN
stories.summary: The United States and Iran clashed over Tehran's nuclear programme as a review of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty opened at the United Nations. Russia's Ambassador-at-Large Andrey Belousov objected to singling out Iran, calling the criticism politicisation and expressing hope it would not derail the conference.

stories.title: Top Jalisco cartel leader 'El Jardinero' arrested in Mexico, minister says
stories.summary: Mexican special forces arrested Audias Flores, known as "El Jardinero," a top commander of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel, in the western state of Nayarit. Security Minister Omar García Harfuch announced the operation on Monday.

stories.title: China’s Politburo steps up policy response as Iran war shakes global economy
stories.summary: China's Politburo pledged a holistic policy response to external shocks from the US-Israel war on Iran, emphasizing energy security, technological self-reliance, and control over industrial supply chains. The meeting, led by President Xi Jinping, addressed the conflict's widening impact on the global economy.

stories.title: Trump fires independent board overseeing National Science Foundation
stories.summary: The Trump administration fired members of the National Science Board, which independently oversees the National Science Foundation. Board members received an email from the Presidential Personnel Office stating their positions were terminated effective immediately, a move critics called a dangerous attack on US innovation.

stories.title: Around 20,000 seafarers stranded in Persian Gulf as Hormuz stays shut despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Approximately 20,000 seafarers, mostly from India, remain stranded in the Persian Gulf as the Strait of Hormuz stays shut despite a ceasefire. The mariners have endured missile blasts and food shortages since the Iran war began two months ago.

stories.title: Asean’s natural leader, Bali on edge over Japanese earthquake: 7 Asia highlights
stories.summary: The South China Morning Post highlighted seven Asia stories from the past week, including Indonesia ceding its role as ASEAN's natural leader to Singapore, concerns in Bali over a potential magnitude-9 megathrust earthquake following a Japanese quake, and a deadly Japanese Type 10 tank explosion that killed three.

stories.title: Oil prices rise despite Iran’s proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Brent crude prices rose more than 1 percent even as Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for deferring nuclear negotiations.

stories.title: Mexico captures top cartel leader ‘El Jardinero’ hiding in roadside ditch
stories.summary: Mexican military forces captured Audias Flores Silva, known as "El Jardinero," a top regional commander of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG), in northwestern Mexico. He was considered a possible successor to the cartel's recently killed leader. The United States had offered a $5 million reward for information leading to his arrest.

stories.title: Supply shock from Iran war drives electronics component prices up globally
stories.summary: Supply disruptions from the US-Israeli war on Iran have sharply increased global prices of printed circuit boards, Reuters reported. An Iranian strike on the Jubail petrochemical complex halted production of high-purity polyphenylene ether resin, which accounts for about 70 percent of global supply.

stories.title: US challenges Iran’s role in UN nuclear talks, Tehran rejects accusations
stories.summary: The US and Iran clashed at a UN conference reviewing the Non-Proliferation Treaty after Tehran was selected as a vice president of the meeting. Washington called the move an 'insult,' accusing Iran of failing its nuclear obligations. Iran rejected the accusations.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Trump not happy with Iran's latest peace proposal, US official says
stories.summary: A US official said President Trump is unhappy with Iran's latest peace proposal, which would set aside Iran's nuclear programme until the war ends and shipping disputes through the Strait of Hormuz are resolved. Washington and Tehran remain in a standoff over the critical waterway through which a fifth of the world's traded oil and gas normally passes.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Marian Marinica Resigns As Warriors Head Coach
stories.summary: Zimbabwe's senior men's national football team head coach Marian Marinica has resigned from his position, as confirmed by the Zimbabwe Football Association (ZIFA).

stories.title: Gambia: Gender Gaps Deepen Climate Crisis As New Report Calls for Urgent Action in Gambia
stories.summary: A study conducted under a Food and Agriculture Organization project found that climate and disaster risks in The Gambia disproportionately affect women due to structural inequalities in access to resources, decision-making, and livelihoods.

stories.title: Kenya: Ruto Blames Cartels for Attempts to Derail Social Health Authority Rollout
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto accused cartels of attempting to derail the rollout of the Social Health Authority, while asserting that the country is pursuing universal health coverage through legislation designed to outlast political cycles.

stories.title: Mali's PM urges public to remain calm during visit to victims of coordinated attacks
stories.summary: Mali's transitional Prime Minister General Abdoulaye Maiga visited victims of coordinated attacks by jihadi and rebel forces that took place on Saturday and killed the country's defence chief. He urged the public to remain calm.

stories.title: Media freedom ‘under sustained attack’ across EU as public trust drops, report finds
stories.summary: The Civil Liberties Union for Europe reported that media freedom across the EU is under sustained attack, with journalists facing rising harassment, threats, and violence.
