stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Presidential Library in St. Petersburg on April 27. Putin pledged to do "everything" to promote peace in the Middle East during the meeting, according to the Russian news agency Interfax.

stories.title: Smotrich confirms Finance Ministry hasn’t transferred any tax revenues to PA for past year
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich confirmed that his ministry has not transferred any tax revenues to the Palestinian Authority for the past year. The PA prime minister said the policy is intended to destroy Palestinian state institutions, leaving the authority unable to pay its employees.

stories.title: Risk as design input: The Eight-Factor Risk Framework for cognitive operations
stories.summary: A sponsored analysis introduces the Eight-Factor Risk Framework for cognitive operations, describing a theoretical model that identifies three simultaneous zones held by every target audience.

stories.title: Romania's largest party teams up with far-right opposition to topple pro-European coalition
stories.summary: Romania's Social Democrats announced they would partner with the hard-right Alliance for Uniting Romanians to attempt to topple the country's pro-European coalition government. The Social Democrats had left the coalition earlier in April. The move could put Romania's EU funding at risk.

stories.title: US, Iran clash during UN nuclear weapons conference
stories.summary: US and Iranian officials clashed at the opening of the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty review conference in New York City. The dispute centered on Iran's appointment as a vice-president of the conference. The US, Australia, and the UAE opposed the move, while the UK, France, and Germany raised concerns.

stories.title: US Navy’s unmanned MQ-25A Stingray notches first successful test flight
stories.summary: The US Navy and Boeing completed the first test flight of the MQ-25A Stingray unmanned aerial refueling drone on Saturday. The aircraft demonstrated autonomous taxi, takeoff, flight, and landing capabilities.

stories.title: At least four killed and dozens injured in Indonesia train crash
stories.summary: A commuter train and a long-distance train collided on the outskirts of Jakarta, Indonesia, on Monday. Officials report at least four people were killed and dozens more were injured in the crash.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz signs off on letting fans attend PSL playoffs
stories.summary: Pakistan's Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif approved public attendance at all three Pakistan Super League playoff matches. PCB Chairman and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi announced the decision, adding that fans were strongly encouraged to use public transport.

stories.title: King Charles lands in Maryland for state visit as ‘special relationship’ comes under strain – US politics live
stories.summary: King Charles and Queen Camilla arrived in Maryland for a four-day U.S. state visit. The royal couple met President Trump at the White House, though any meeting between the king and president was kept off-camera amid tensions in the U.S.-UK relationship.

stories.title: Zelensky: Deliveries of anti-ballistic missiles in May must meet promised levels
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky urged international partners to ensure that deliveries of anti-ballistic missile systems in May meet previously promised levels. The statement underscored Ukraine's ongoing need for air defense capabilities.

stories.title: Ukraine summons Israeli ambassador — for second Russian stolen-grain vessel to reach Haifa
stories.summary: Ukraine summoned Israel's ambassador for a second time over a Russian vessel carrying stolen Ukrainian grain arriving at the port of Haifa. Ukrainian officials accused Russia of looting grain from occupied Ukrainian territories and Israel of facilitating the trade by unloading it.

stories.title: Putin tells lawmakers that fixating on bans and restrictions is counterproductive
stories.summary: President Vladimir Putin addressed lawmakers and senators at a Legislative Council meeting in St. Petersburg. He urged them to move beyond a focus on punitive legislation, arguing that fixating on bans and restrictions is counterproductive.

stories.title: ‘Chonkers’ the large sea lion charms the San Francisco Bay area
stories.summary: A 2,000-pound Steller sea lion nicknamed "Chonkers" has become a local celebrity after taking up residence at Pier 39 in San Francisco Bay approximately a month ago. The unusually large animal has drawn attention from visitors and social media users.

stories.title: Iran's leadership is humiliating the United States, Germany's Merz says
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz accused Iran's leadership of humiliating the United States and said he could not identify Washington's exit strategy in the Iran war. His comments underscored deep divisions between the US and its European NATO allies.

stories.title: Mali junta destabilized by 'unprecedented' insurgency
stories.summary: Mali's ruling military junta faces what analysts describe as an unprecedented insurgency after jihadist attacks killed the country's defense minister and struck several cities. The unrest poses a serious threat to junta stability.

stories.title: Mali on edge as insurgency tests junta's resolve
stories.summary: Mali faces a serious security challenge as coordinated insurgent assaults on several cities killed Defence Minister Sadio Camara. Analysts say the attacks are testing the resolve of the military junta governing from Bamako.

stories.title: Iran’s FM Araghchi calls his Islamabad visit ‘successful'’ after arriving in Russia
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi described his visit to Islamabad as successful before arriving in Russia. The trip followed diplomatic engagements in Pakistan.

stories.title: Navy’s MQ-25 Stingray carrier drone completes first test flight
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy's MQ-25 Stingray unmanned carrier-based drone completed its first test flight from Boeing's facility at MidAmerica Airport in Mascoutah, Illinois. The approximately two-hour flight marked a milestone for the carrier-based refueling drone program.

stories.title: Report: Top Yandex manager dies in Russia after boat capsizes on Volga River during storm
stories.summary: Sergei Loyter, a senior manager at Russian technology company Yandex, was found dead in the Svetloyarsky district of the Volgograd region. He was among a group of fishermen who went missing after their motorboat capsized on the Volga River during a storm.

stories.title: Russians may ramp up artillery shelling on southern front in coming days – Voloshyn
stories.summary: Ukrainian military spokesman Voloshyn reported that Russian forces have received additional artillery ammunition and may intensify shelling on the southern front in the coming days. A temporary lull in attacks was attributed to adverse weather conditions.

stories.title: Russian Court Outlaws Top LGBTQ+ Rights Group as 'Extremist'
stories.summary: A Russian court designated a leading LGBTQ+ rights organization as "extremist." The ruling means that anyone associated with the group could face years of imprisonment for supporting an extremist organization.

stories.title: White House says Iran proposal under review
stories.summary: White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said senior US officials are reviewing an Iranian proposal to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The proposal reportedly includes reopening the waterway in exchange for future talks on Iran's nuclear program. President Trump has met with his national security team to discuss the offer.

stories.title: Iran looking into Trump's request for negotiations, foreign minister says
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in Russia that Iran is examining a request from President Trump for negotiations. Araghchi told reporters the US sought talks because it has not achieved any of its objectives in the conflict.

stories.title: China blocks Meta's $2B acquisition of AI startup Manus
stories.summary: Chinese authorities blocked Meta's approximately $2 billion acquisition of AI startup Manus, forcing the US tech company to unwind the deal. Analysts say the decision could set a new precedent for Chinese regulatory intervention in cross-border tech transactions.

stories.title: US Air Force looks to launch cheap missiles from cargo aircraft
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force is pursuing development of inexpensive, long-range missiles designed to be launched in large volleys from cargo aircraft. The initiative aims to leverage existing transport platforms for mass strike capability.

stories.title: Russia’s Digital Development Ministry claims VPN blocking protects user data
stories.summary: Russia's Digital Development Ministry has ordered internet services to block users who have VPNs enabled. The ministry justified the measure by citing security concerns, claiming that VPN blocking helps protect user data.

stories.title: Hezbollah disarmament ‘must happen’, senior Lebanese minister tells US think tank
stories.summary: Lebanese Social Affairs Minister Haneen Sayed told a U.S. think tank that the disarmament of Hezbollah is a government demand and "must happen." She acknowledged the process would not be instant, describing Hezbollah as a "community" rather than solely a militant organization, and said a political settlement would take time.

stories.title: Court doesn’t order state inquiry into Oct. 7, gives government 2 months to decide on probe
stories.summary: Israel's Supreme Court declined to order an official state inquiry into the October 7 attack but gave the government two months to decide on a probe framework. Bereaved families criticized the ruling, while judges acknowledged the government's failure to investigate the onslaught.

stories.title: Netanyahu's rivals are joining forces. Can they shift Israel's security policy?
stories.summary: Former Israeli leaders Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid announced a joint party called "BeYachad" to challenge Prime Minister Netanyahu's coalition in upcoming elections. While focused on domestic issues like ultra-Orthodox military conscription, the alliance is expected to maintain a security posture on Iran, Gaza, and Lebanon similar to Netanyahu's.

stories.title: Insurgent alliance strikes at heart of Mali’s junta, exposing limits of Russian protection
stories.summary: A coordinated offensive by separatist and al-Qaeda-linked jihadist groups struck multiple locations across Mali, sparking two days of intense fighting. The attacks represent the most serious challenge to Mali's ruling military junta since a 2012 rebel offensive, exposing the limits of Russian-backed security support.

stories.title: US Army eyes a heavier, hybrid-powered Infantry Squad Vehicle
stories.summary: The U.S. Army is developing a heavier, hybrid-powered variant of the Infantry Squad Vehicle, designated ISV-H. Unlike the original ISV designed to transport a nine-soldier squad across rugged terrain, the new version is intended to fulfill additional operational roles beyond troop movement.

stories.title: US is being ‘humiliated’ by Iran’s leadership, says Friedrich Merz
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz publicly stated that Iran's leadership is "humiliating" the United States, suggesting the Trump administration is being outwitted in negotiations with Tehran. His comments followed Trump's cancellation of a planned round of indirect talks with Iran in Islamabad, after a previous session led by Vice President JD Vance ended without progress.

stories.title: Ukraine confirms major refinery hits: 24 oil tanks destroyed in Tuapse
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff confirmed strikes against Russian oil infrastructure in Tuapse and Yaroslavl. The attacks on the Tuapse refinery destroyed 24 oil storage tanks. The strikes were carried out by Ukraine's Defense Forces targeting Russian refining capacity.

stories.title: WATCH: Israel's Defense Ministry detonates 700 landmines near Syrian border
stories.summary: Israel's National Mine Action Authority detonated 700 landmines near the Syrian border as part of ongoing demining operations. The effort aims to reclaim mined areas for civilian and industrial use.

stories.title: As New Mexico probes Epstein, local survivors come forward
stories.summary: Authorities in New Mexico are investigating the late Jeffrey Epstein's Zorro Ranch compound to determine how many people were abused there. Local survivors have come forward as the probe continues.

stories.title: One Ukrainian drone maker carried out 11,473 strikes in March, and took out 43% of Russia’s Molniya drones
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone unit known as "General Chereshnia" carried out 11,473 strikes during March and destroyed 43% of Russia's Molniya reconnaissance drones. The unit's operations reflect Ukraine's expanding use of unmanned aerial vehicles against Russian forces.

stories.title: Dollar blockade: Will US pressure on Iraq's militias backfire?
stories.summary: The United States has halted dollar shipments to Iraq as a pressure measure targeting Baghdad over Iran-backed militias operating in the country. Analysts warn the move could have catastrophic consequences for Iraq's government and economy.

stories.title: US press gala shooting suspect charged with attempting to kill Trump
stories.summary: Cole Thomas Allen has been charged with attempting to assassinate US President Donald Trump following a shooting at a press gala on Saturday. Prosecutors allege Allen carried out the attack targeting the president.

stories.title: Hezbollah drones pose challenge to Israeli forces in Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah has been launching suicide drones against Israeli forces operating in Lebanon, posing a significant tactical challenge. The group says its attacks are a response to Israeli ceasefire violations.

stories.title: Iranian intel service attempts to recruit London-based journalist for anti-Israel display
stories.summary: Iran's intelligence service allegedly attempted to recruit a London-based journalist to stage an anti-Israel display. The journalist's employer, LBC, reported the recruitment attempt to British counter-terrorism police and shared the full exchange with officials.

stories.title: Four killed, 70 injured in attacks by Pakistan: Afghan Taliban
stories.summary: The Afghan Taliban government reported that Pakistani mortar and rocket attacks on Afghanistan killed four people and injured 70 on Monday. The cross-border strikes targeted Afghan territory.

stories.title: Birmingham council leader says end of city’s bin strike ‘within sight’
stories.summary: Birmingham city council leader John Cotton announced that the resolution of a long-running refuse workers' strike, which began in January 2025, is "within sight." An improved offer is being prepared for the workers in an effort to end the dispute.

stories.title: Rachel Reeves considering rent freeze to limit Iran war fallout
stories.summary: UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves is considering a one-year rent freeze on private sector homes in England to shield household budgets from the economic impact of the Iran war. The proposal is being debated within government as part of a broader cost-of-living package expected in coming weeks.

stories.title: 3 women take Chief Rabbinate exam for first time in history, after delay ended by court order
stories.summary: Three women sat for a Chief Rabbinate exam in Israel for the first time in history, taking a test on laws of mourning after a court-issued emergency injunction ended years of delays. The women were tested at a separate location from male candidates.

stories.title: Dinesh Trivedi appointed India's next Envoy to Dhaka
stories.summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs announced the appointment of Dinesh Trivedi as the country's next envoy to Dhaka. Trivedi is expected to take up the assignment shortly.

stories.title: Security, politics and protest: top stories in {Africanews Today}
stories.summary: Life is gradually returning to normal in Mali following a jihadist attack that killed General Sadio Camara, the country's defence minister. The incident was among the top security and political stories across the African continent.

stories.title: Rubio says Iran ‘serious’ about deal, sets nuclear condition
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that Iran appears serious about reaching an agreement with Washington, citing Tehran's worsening economic conditions. However, Rubio emphasized that any deal must include guarantees preventing Iran from developing a nuclear weapon.

stories.title: Experts call for halt of AI chip exports to China after White House distillation warning
stories.summary: An AI policy group argues the move is necessary after the White House warned that Beijing is attempting to use U.S. AI systems to build similar capabilities.

stories.title: War update: Russians launch 76 attacks, Pokrovsk sector sees fiercest battles
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 76 attacks against Ukrainian Defense Forces positions in a single day. The fiercest fighting was concentrated in the Pokrovsk sector, while Russian troops also showed increased activity in the Huliaipole sector.

stories.title: Russia MFA Expands Entry Ban List in Response to New EU Sanctions
stories.summary: Russia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs expanded its entry ban list in retaliation for new European Union sanctions. Moscow did not disclose the number of individuals added to the list or their identities.

stories.title: UAE ties with Gulf, Pakistan strained over stance on Iran
stories.summary: The UAE has applied financial pressure on Pakistan and publicly criticized fellow Gulf monarchies over their positions regarding the war on Iran. The tensions mark an unusual rift within Gulf diplomatic relations.

stories.title: 4 killed and dozens injured in train crash outside Jakarta
stories.summary: Two trains collided near Bekasi Timur station, approximately 25 kilometers from Jakarta, Indonesia, killing at least four people and injuring dozens. Rescuers conducted a mass evacuation at the scene, carrying survivors from the wreckage into waiting ambulances.

stories.title: US 'used to' school shootings: Gun violence 'inevitably turned to the political arena as well'
stories.summary: Legal analyst and former U.S. federal prosecutor Eric Lisann discussed how mass shootings and political violence have become normalized in American society. He attributed this to the convergence of mass violence normalization, escalating violent political rhetoric since 2015, and easy access to firearms.

stories.title: Central bank increases policy rate by 100bps to 11.5pc
stories.summary: The State Bank of Pakistan raised its key policy rate by 100 basis points to 11.5 percent, effective Tuesday. The Monetary Policy Committee cited risks from rising oil prices linked to the Middle East conflict. This marks the first rate hike in nearly three years.

stories.title: Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant worker killed in Ukraine drone attack, management says
stories.summary: An employee of the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in Ukraine was killed in a Ukrainian drone attack, according to the Russian-installed management of the facility. The plant has been under Russian control. The announcement was made via Telegram on Monday.

stories.title: Bruised by Trump, NATO alliance considers end to annual summits
stories.summary: NATO is considering ending its practice of holding annual summits, a shift that could help avoid potentially tense encounters with US President Donald Trump. The move reflects ongoing strains within the transatlantic alliance.

stories.title: The insurgent groups battling Mali's military-led government
stories.summary: April 27 - Mali's government is facing new questions about how long it can hold on to power two days after insurgents launched attacks across the country, hitting the main army base outside the capita

stories.title: Mexico warns US involvement in anti-drug operation should not to be repeated
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum sent a diplomatic note to the United States demanding that unauthorized U.S. participation in anti-narcotics operations in Chihuahua state not be repeated. The incident came to light after two U.S. and two Mexican officials were killed in a car crash on April 19 following the operation.

stories.title: Pakistan opens new transit routes to facilitate Iran trade
stories.summary: Pakistan has authorized new transit routes enabling Iran to import goods from third countries through Pakistani territory. The routes link the ports of Karachi, Port Qasim, and Gwadar to border crossings in Balochistan. The policy took effect during a visit by Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.

stories.title: Tanks couldn’t take Chasiv Yar. So Russia’s reaching for the playbook that took Pokrovsk.
stories.summary: Russian forces have been unable to capture the Ukrainian city of Chasiv Yar using armored assaults and are reportedly shifting to encirclement tactics similar to those used at Pokrovsk. Chasiv Yar remains one of the last major obstacles to a Russian advance toward Kramatorsk in the Donetsk region.

stories.title: Several Russian units cancel leave until May 9 due to expectations of intensified fighting, says Voloshyn
stories.summary: Ukrainian military spokesperson Voloshyn reported that units of Russia's 19th Motorized Rifle Division have canceled all leave until May 9. The move is linked to concerns about ongoing Ukrainian Armed Forces operations and may indicate Russian preparations for intensified fighting.

stories.title: State attorney rejects request by Israeli NGOs to take steps against OnlyFans
stories.summary: Israel's state attorney rejected a request by Israeli NGOs to take legal steps against the OnlyFans platform. The NGOs had cited international cases where indictments were filed against the platform over allegations of sexual abuse and exploitation.

stories.title: Russia’s mercenaries left Malian city under escort by rebels they came to fight
stories.summary: Russian mercenaries from the Wagner-linked forces withdrew from a strategic city in northern Mali under escort by the very rebels they had been deployed to fight. Mali had severed ties with Ukraine in 2024 to maintain its relationship with Russia's military contractors.

stories.title: UK information commissioner steps back amid workplace investigation
stories.summary: UK Information Commissioner John Edwards stepped back from his role after the Information Commissioner's Office launched an independent workplace investigation into unspecified "HR matters." Edwards stated he is fully cooperating with the inquiry.

stories.title: Mild heatwave conditions likely in southern parts of Pakistan from April 29 to May 3: PMD
stories.summary: The Pakistan Meteorological Department forecast mild heatwave conditions across southern Pakistan from April 29 to May 3. A westerly wave is expected to lower temperatures by 2–4°C in northern areas from April 27–29 and May 3–5. The department also warned that El Niño conditions could emerge during May–July.

stories.title: Rubio rejects new Iranian proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz, with future of talks in limbo
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio rejected Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, calling Iran's approach exploitative. Tanker traffic through the strait remains limited as Iran asserts control over the waterway. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Iran was humiliating the US in negotiations.

stories.title: Ukraine drone forces expand kill zone into occupied regions, commander says: Russia’s trains, comms towers, and depots struck
stories.summary: Ukraine's drone forces expanded operations into Russian-occupied areas of Donetsk, Luhansk, and Zaporizhzhia oblasts between April 23 and 25, striking trains, communications towers, and supply depots. An SBS commander said mid-range FP-2 drones carried out the attacks.

stories.title: Hezbollah leader rejects Lebanon-Israel direct talks, vows to confront Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah's leader rejected direct Lebanon-Israel negotiations and vowed to confront Israel. Meanwhile, the Lebanese and Israeli ambassadors to the United States held two meetings in Washington in recent weeks, marking the first such direct diplomatic contacts in decades.

stories.title: Suspected pirates steer cargo vessel towards Somalia, security groups say
stories.summary: Suspected pirates boarded a St. Kitts and Nevis-flagged cargo vessel off Somalia's coast and were sailing it toward the Somali coastline. British maritime security groups Vanguard and Ambrey reported the incident from Garowe, Somalia.

stories.title: High Court gives Israeli gov't two months to establish framework for Oct. 7 state probe
stories.summary: Israel's High Court of Justice gave the government two months to establish a framework for a state probe into the October 7 attack. The court said it would decide on further handling of related petitions after receiving the government's update.

stories.title: Ceasefire at risk as Pakistan and Afghanistan report cross-border attacks
stories.summary: Pakistan and Afghanistan reported cross-border strikes, the first since both nations agreed to a ceasefire during peace talks the previous month. The incidents threaten to unravel the recently negotiated halt to violence between the two countries.

stories.title: KP CM Afridi meets with TTAP's Achakzai and Abbas amid reports of rift within opposition
stories.summary: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi met with Tehreek Tahaffuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan leaders Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas at Achakzai's Islamabad residence. The meeting followed reports of a rift between PTI and TTAP over decision-making within the opposition alliance. Former NA speaker Asad Qaiser and other leaders also attended.

stories.title: St. Petersburg court declares Russian LGBT Network an ‘extremist organization,’ bans it from operating in Russia
stories.summary: A court in St. Petersburg declared the Russian LGBT Network an "extremist organization" and banned it from operating anywhere in Russia. The ruling was announced by the Joint Press Service of St. Petersburg Courts.

stories.title: Gunmen kidnap 23 children from Nigerian orphanage
stories.summary: Gunmen kidnapped 23 children from an orphanage in Nigeria. Mass kidnappings remain a widespread tactic used by gangs and armed groups across the country to generate ransom payments.

stories.title: Defense Forces strike ammunition depot, Tornado-S system, and command posts of Russian troops, says General Staff
stories.summary: Ukraine's General Staff announced that Defense Forces struck a Russian ammunition depot, a Tornado-S multiple launch rocket system, and several command posts belonging to the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation.

stories.title: Trump weighs Iran’s ‘red lines’ as Tehran’s top diplomat engages Russia’s Putin
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg following mediation efforts in Islamabad. The diplomatic activity coincided with President Trump convening his national security team to evaluate a new Iranian peace proposal, delivered via Pakistan, aimed at resolving the Middle East crisis and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: 14 Killed in crash near Juba as poor weather suspected
stories.summary: A Cessna aircraft crashed on the outskirts of Juba, South Sudan's capital, killing 14 people. Poor weather conditions are suspected as a contributing factor in the aviation accident.

stories.title: Leaked Report Ranks Russia’s Prison System Among Top State Agencies for Quality of Service
stories.summary: A leaked government evaluation ranked Russia's Federal Penitentiary Service among the top state agencies for quality of service, scoring 94% out of 62 ministries and agencies assessed. The findings were reported by Russian newspaper Kommersant.

stories.title: India names BJP leader envoy to Bangladesh as ties thaw
stories.summary: India appointed veteran BJP politician Dinesh Trivedi as its next high commissioner to Bangladesh, a rare choice of a non-foreign service officer. The move aims to rebuild ties that deteriorated after former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina fled to New Delhi following a 2024 uprising. India faces competition from China for influence in Bangladesh.

stories.title: Venice opera house drops incoming music director after nepotism remarks
stories.summary: Venice's La Fenice opera house dismissed incoming music director Beatrice Venezi following controversy over nepotism remarks. Her appointment last September had prompted orchestra members to go on strike.

stories.title: Bahrain revokes citizenship of 69 people in connection with Iran war
stories.summary: Bahrain's government revoked the citizenship of 69 individuals over allegations of glorifying Iranian actions and aiding foreign entities during the Iran war. The measure also affects the families of those stripped of their nationality.

stories.title: Putin pledges support for Iran in talks with Araghchi in Russia, says he wants peace soon
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin pledged support for Iran during talks with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Russia, expressing a desire for peace soon. Moscow has offered to mediate in the Middle East following its condemnation of US and Israeli strikes on Iran.

stories.title: The costs of Israel's mishandling of Hamas-linked Gaza hospital chiefs - analysis
stories.summary: Questions have been raised about Israel's handling of Gaza hospital chiefs allegedly linked to Hamas, with critics asking why the doctors have not been formally indicted and given standard criminal trial due process protections.

stories.title: White House says US will not negotiate with Iran through the media
stories.summary: The White House stated that the United States will not conduct negotiations with Iran through the media, calling the diplomatic discussions sensitive. A spokesperson reiterated that any deal must prioritize American interests and prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon.

stories.title: Congo plans paramilitary unit for mines with US, UAE funding
stories.summary: The agency declined to name the source of the US and Emirati funds.

stories.title: Bahrain strips dozens of citizenship over Iran support
stories.summary: Bahrain's interior ministry announced it revoked the citizenship of 69 individuals for supporting Iran during the ongoing war. The decision was disclosed on Monday by the Gulf kingdom's government.

stories.title: Archaeologists at Pompeii use AI to reveal the face of one of the victims
stories.summary: Archaeologists at Pompeii used artificial intelligence for the first time to digitally reconstruct the face of a victim of the AD 79 eruption of Mount Vesuvius. The portrait depicts an older man who was among two victims discovered while apparently fleeing toward the coast.

stories.title: Russian Forces reinforce front line near Velyka Novosilka following losses near Ternuvate, says Voloshyn
stories.summary: According to spokesperson Voloshyn, Russian forces lost offensive capability near Ternuvate in the Zaporizhzhia region and withdrew units of the 29th Army to training grounds. New forces were redeployed to the Velyka Novosilka area to reinforce front-line assault operations.

stories.title: Mass Layoffs, Unpaid Wages Hit Coal Mines in Occupied Luhansk as Operator Nears Bankruptcy
stories.summary: Coal mines in Russian-occupied Luhansk are experiencing mass layoffs and unpaid wages as the operating company nears bankruptcy. Non-payment of wages has become a recurring problem for miners in occupied eastern Ukraine.

stories.title: Negotiating with Israel 'not treason,' Lebanon's Aoun says, stressing goal is to end war
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun stated that negotiating with Israel is "not treason," emphasizing the goal is to end the war. He accused Hezbollah of treason, saying the group took Lebanon to war for external interests.

stories.title: Can King Charles III help heal the US-British rupture?
stories.summary: Britain’s refusal to take part in the United States’ war with Iran has deeply strained relations.

stories.title: Africa: Africa's Path to Lasting Peace: Multilateral Security Cooperation
stories.summary: A report from Nairobi describes 2026 as a pivotal moment for African security, noting that while the continent hosts some of the world's fastest-growing economies and a youthful population, persistent security challenges continue to overshadow its progress. The analysis calls for multilateral security cooperation.

stories.title: Pakistan accused of attacking Afghan university
stories.summary: Air attacks on Afghanistan's Kunar province killed at least seven people and injured 75, with sources telling the BBC that Pakistan was responsible. Pakistan's information ministry denied the allegations, calling Afghan media reports a "blatant lie" intended to cover up Afghan Taliban support for militants.

stories.title: Slain soldier’s girlfriend says at his funeral that she saw his death in Lebanon in real time
stories.summary: Idan Fooks, a 19-year-old Israeli soldier, was killed in a Hezbollah drone attack in Lebanon and laid to rest. His girlfriend, serving as an IDF surveillance soldier, reportedly witnessed his death in real time while on duty.

stories.title: India, New Zealand sign free trade deal, cutting fruit tariffs, boosting exports and visas
stories.summary: India and New Zealand signed a free trade agreement on Monday following negotiations concluded in December 2025. India gains greater market access for engineering goods, machinery, and textiles while protecting its dairy sector. New Zealand's Commerce Minister and India's Piyush Goyal signed the deal, which is expected to facilitate $20 billion in investment into India.

stories.title: Where is the counter-drone tech in Israel's North? - analysis
stories.summary: Hezbollah continues launching drones at northern Israel and Israeli troops in southern Lebanon, and while many are intercepted, some penetrate defenses with lethal effect. The situation has raised questions about gaps in Israel's counter-drone capabilities.

stories.title: Buy airline tickets now, Spain urges as Iran war lifts oil prices
stories.summary: Spain's government urged citizens to purchase airline tickets promptly as rising oil prices driven by the Iran war push up costs. Global oil prices have increased by roughly 50 percent since February 28 due to supply disruptions.

stories.title: UK PM Starmer faces possible parliament probe over Mandelson
stories.summary: British lawmakers are set to vote on whether Prime Minister Keir Starmer should face a parliamentary investigation related to a scandal involving Peter Mandelson. The probe could add to the political pressure on Starmer's leadership.

stories.title: Malians respond to the death of defence Minister Sadio Camara
stories.summary: Mali's Minister of Defence Sadio Camara, 47, was killed on Saturday in a car bomb attack at his home in Kati. Camara was a key member of Mali's ruling military junta, and the government confirmed his death in a statement issued on Sunday.

stories.title: Analysis: Bennett-Lapid alliance attempt to unseat Israel’s Netanyahu
stories.summary: Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid have reunited in a joint political effort to challenge Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's hold on power in Israel. Analysts note the alliance is unlikely to produce significant policy changes for Palestinians.

stories.title: Encircling Jenin: How Israel's new settlement push is closing in
stories.summary: Israel is advancing new settlement expansion around the Palestinian city of Jenin in the northern West Bank. The construction plans would effectively encircle the city, fragmenting Palestinian territory and consolidating Israeli control in the area.

stories.title: Confronting the Past and Present, Lessons from Chornobyl
stories.summary: The Ukraine Compass, a weekly digest for War on the Rocks members, examined Ukrainian commentary around the legacy of the Chornobyl disaster. The series curates Ukrainian media perspectives on politics, daily life, and public debate beyond battlefield coverage.

stories.title: Suspected pirates steer cargo vessel towards Somalia
stories.summary: A cargo vessel has reportedly been hijacked by suspected pirates and is being steered toward Somalia. The incident occurs as maritime traffic is being rerouted away from the Strait of Hormuz, which is described as effectively closed.

stories.title: Rubio rejects Iranian proposal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, calling the conditions unacceptable. Rubio argued that Tehran's offer would effectively give Iran control over access to the international waterway.

stories.title: Bruised by Trump, Nato alliance considers end to annual summits
stories.summary: NATO is considering ending its practice of holding annual summits, according to six sources, potentially avoiding a tense encounter with President Trump. The move follows repeated criticism by the Trump administration of allied nations for not contributing more to U.S. military operations against Iran.

stories.title: Voloshyn explains why Russian paratroopers redeployed from Kursk region to Kherson region
stories.summary: Spokesperson Voloshyn reported that several Russian Airborne Forces units are being redeployed from the Kursk region to the Kherson region. The forces are moving to the Dnipro River area to reinforce Russian positions and intensify assault operations in the river's island zone.

stories.title: King Charles to meet Donald Trump off camera to avoid awkwardness
stories.summary: King Charles is set to meet U.S. President Donald Trump at the White House with no cameras present. British officials requested the private format to avoid a potential repeat of the public confrontation Trump had with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

stories.title: UK police make another arrest in relation to attacks on Jewish-linked premises
stories.summary: British police arrested another man in connection with a series of attacks targeting Jewish-linked premises in northwest London. The arrest is part of an ongoing investigation into the incidents.

stories.title: Nations to discuss fossil fuel exit as Strait of Hormuz blockade drives up prices
stories.summary: Ministers and officials are gathering in Santa Marta, Colombia, to discuss practical steps for transitioning economies away from fossil fuels. The meeting comes as a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has driven up global energy prices.

stories.title: Tornadoes, hail and high winds forecast to hit midwest and Mississippi valley
stories.summary: Severe storms including tornadoes, large hail, and high winds are forecast to hit the mid-Mississippi valley and midwest United States on Monday, putting nearly 50 million people at risk. The Storm Prediction Center issued a level 4 out of 5 risk for areas including St. Louis. The storms follow a deadly weekend tornado that killed two people in Texas.

stories.title: First protest filed against the Army’s troubled MAPS contract
stories.summary: Some in industry are calling the $50 billion professional services vehicle "still a hot mess" as the Army works to answer thousands of questions.

stories.title: Constable martyred in terrorist attack on police checkpost in Balochistan's Pishin
stories.summary: A police head constable was killed in a militant attack on a checkpost in the Huramzai area of Pishin district, Balochistan. Armed assailants on a motorcycle opened fire with automatic weapons, and police returned fire. The attackers fled the scene, and security forces subsequently arrived to respond.

stories.title: Germany: Trial of 'Ulm Five' protesters accused of Elbit break-in postponed
stories.summary: The trial of five activists known as the "Ulm Five," accused of breaking into an Elbit Systems weapons factory in Ulm, Germany, on 8 September 2025, has been postponed. The delay followed the defendants being placed behind a glass barrier that prevented contact with their lawyers.

stories.title: Defense Forces launch counterattacks near Charivne in Zaporizhzhia region; no Russian advancement in south, says Voloshyn
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces are conducting counterattacks near Charivne in the Zaporizhzhia region, according to spokesperson Voloshyn. No Russian advances or Ukrainian loss of positions have been recorded in the southern sector in recent days.

stories.title: Will the Iran war push millions back into poverty?
stories.summary: The ongoing US-Israeli military campaign against Iran is driving up global fuel and food prices. An estimated 32.5 million people worldwide are at increased risk of being pushed into poverty as a result of the conflict's economic fallout.

stories.title: Chinese automaker BYD’s new-generation fast chargers to hit Israel later this year
stories.summary: Chinese automaker BYD plans to introduce its new-generation fast-charging technology in Israel later this year. The company's latest batteries and charging stations are designed to charge electric vehicles from 10% to 97% in under 10 minutes.

stories.title: Clashes over water resources in Chad kill over 40 people
stories.summary: Community clashes over water resources in Chad killed more than 40 people in violence centered around a water well that spread across a wide area. Extreme weather has intensified such disputes, prompting military intervention.

stories.title: Israeli press review: Teens murder of pizzeria worker sparks lawlessness fears
stories.summary: Israeli media reported on the murder of a pizzeria worker by teenagers, raising concerns about lawlessness. Separately, a sharp rise in suicides among Israeli soldiers and police officers was documented, and Israel was found to have been purchasing stolen Ukrainian wheat from Russia.

stories.title: Egyptian foreign minister holds talks with US’ Witkoff
stories.summary: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty spoke by phone with US Middle East envoy Steve Witkoff, discussing US-Iran negotiations and regional tensions. Abdelatty stressed the importance of reinforcing ceasefire efforts and working toward ending the war through coordination with regional and international partners.

stories.title: Melania Trump urges ABC to ‘take a stand’ against Jimmy Kimmel over monologue
stories.summary: First lady Melania Trump accused comedian Jimmy Kimmel of "hateful and violent rhetoric" and called on ABC to "take a stand" against him. Her comments came after the White House correspondents' dinner shooting, though the Kimmel monologue she referenced aired on Thursday before the Saturday attack.

stories.title: Redbridge Independents defy Labour minister Wes Streeting's 'sectarian' accusation
stories.summary: Vaseem Ahmed, leader of the Corbyn-endorsed Redbridge Independents party, criticized UK Health Secretary Wes Streeting for branding the party "sectarian." The dispute comes ahead of local elections scheduled for 7 May, with Jeremy Corbyn campaigning alongside the Redbridge Independents.

stories.title: ‘Sense of disbelief’: how White House press dinner attack unfolded – The Latest
stories.summary: A gunman breached security at the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents' Dinner on Saturday, getting close to where President Donald Trump and senior officials were gathered before being stopped by law enforcement. The suspect is set to be charged. The incident occurred less than two years after previous assassination attempts against Trump.

stories.title: DR Congo to establish US-backed paramilitary guard for mines
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo plans to establish a US-backed paramilitary guard to protect its mining operations. The initiative aims to secure access to critical minerals in areas where the DRC government is competing with rebel groups for territorial control.

stories.title: EU faces ‘China shock’ as EV imports drive Beijing’s record surplus with bloc
stories.summary: China's trade surplus with the European Union reached a record $83 billion in the first quarter of 2026. Chinese EV exports were a major driver, with China selling approximately $148 billion in goods to the EU while importing only $65 billion from the bloc.

stories.title: Alex Sinclair: Why I wear my kippah with Israeli and Palestinian flags - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece by Alex Sinclair discusses his decision to wear a kippah bearing both Israeli and Palestinian flags, arguing that multiple truths about the Israeli-Palestinian conflict must be acknowledged simultaneously.

stories.title: Sabotage, provocations, contract killings: International network operating under supervision of Russian intelligence agencies foiled
stories.summary: Prosecutors from Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office, the National Police, and law enforcement agencies from multiple countries dismantled an international network operating under Russian intelligence supervision. The group was planning contract killings and sabotage operations on European Union territory.

stories.title: Beijing Is Using Influencers to Burnish Its Image
stories.summary: The term "Chinamaxxing" has become an online phenomenon as Beijing uses social media influencers to improve its international image. The campaign represents a broader effort by China to shape public perception through digital content creators.

stories.title: Iran’s Foreign Minister Meets With Putin in St. Petersburg
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg. Putin reaffirmed Moscow's strategic partnership with Tehran and praised Iran for what he described as fighting for its independence.

stories.title: Chris Ndikumana, the Michael Jackson disciple ministering to Africa’s elite
stories.summary: Chris Ndikumana, originally from the streets of Lubumbashi in the Democratic Republic of Congo, has built a digital prayer ministry called Kanguka. He now fills stadiums in Abidjan and counts footballer Samuel Eto'o and heads of state among his followers.

stories.title: Iran’s lawfare strategy: a long-term threat to Israel and the US in international forums - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Iran is pursuing a long-term lawfare strategy aimed at weakening Israel and the United States by leveraging legal challenges in international forums to shape global perceptions and undermine their legitimacy.

stories.title: Ukraine just uncovered Russian-coordinated plot to assassinate Russian dissident and Ukrainian supporter in Lithuania
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence uncovered a Russian-coordinated assassination plot targeting a Russian opposition figure living in exile and a pro-Ukraine Lithuanian citizen in Lithuania. The network had conducted long-term covert surveillance of both targets.

stories.title: Archbishop of Canterbury praises Pope Leo for speaking powerfully on injustice
stories.summary: Archbishop of Canterbury Sarah Mullally praised Pope Leo for speaking "powerfully about the many injustices" in the world after a private meeting at the Vatican. The remarks appeared to reference the pontiff's recent outspokenness, particularly his criticism of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Congo creates paramilitary mining guard backed by US-UAE funding
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo announced the creation of a paramilitary guard to protect its mining operations, funded by US and Emirati investments. The new force is intended to secure the country's vast mineral resources.

stories.title: Israel 'deployed Iron Dome and troops' to UAE during Iran war
stories.summary: Israel reportedly deployed its Iron Dome missile defense system and troops to the United Arab Emirates during the war with Iran. The deployment revealed deepening military cooperation between Abu Dhabi and Tel Aviv.

stories.title: Canadian antisemitism ‘metastasized’ in 2025 with record 6,800 incidents, mostly online — report
stories.summary: B'nai Brith Canada reported a record 6,800 antisemitic incidents in Canada in 2025, the majority occurring online. The annual report also documented 10 violent incidents and hundreds of cases of vandalism, describing the situation as a national crisis.

stories.title: Suspects in Scot's murder in Kenya charged over attack on another man
stories.summary: Four suspects in the murder of a Scottish man in Kenya have been charged and pleaded not guilty to an alleged attack on an American man at a holiday apartment.

stories.title: Iran offers Hormuz deal without nuclear talks, as it seeks broader buy-in
stories.summary: Iran has proposed a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz without linking it to nuclear negotiations, seeking broader international and regional support. The diplomatic push comes as indirect talks between Tehran and Washington remain uncertain.

stories.title: Eisenkot invites most opposition chiefs to meet, coordinate path to ‘Zionist majority’ victory
stories.summary: Israeli opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot invited most opposition leaders, including Bennett and Lapid, to coordinate a strategy aimed at ousting Prime Minister Netanyahu. Eisenkot did not extend invitations to Arab parties or his former colleague Benny Gantz, and does not plan to join Bennett and Lapid's merged Together party.

stories.title: Russia Summons German Ambassador Over CDU Lawmaker’s Meeting With Exiled Chechen Separatist Leader
stories.summary: Russia summoned the German ambassador after CDU lawmaker Roderich Kiesewetter met with an exiled Chechen separatist leader. Moscow accused the politician of expressing support for the self-proclaimed Chechen Republic of Ichkeria, which Russia recently designated a terrorist organization.

stories.title: Iran foreign minister says Islamic Republic is 'stable, solid' in meeting with Putin
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Saint Petersburg and declared the Islamic Republic "stable, solid and powerful." Araghchi said the war with the United States and Israel had demonstrated Iran's true strength to the world.

stories.title: Germany’s Merz says US has no strategy in Iran war
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz publicly criticized the United States, stating it lacks a clear exit strategy in its war against Iran. The remarks highlight growing divisions between Washington and its European NATO allies.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone strikes Kasta-2E radar station in Belgorod region
stories.summary: Crews from Ukraine's 429th Separate Regiment of Unmanned Systems, known as Achilles, struck a Russian Kasta-2E radar station in Volotovo, Belgorod region. The target was located approximately 80 kilometers from the Ukrainian border.

stories.title: Gunmen raid Nigerian orphanage and kidnap children
stories.summary: Gunmen attacked an orphanage in Kogi state in central Nigeria on Saturday, kidnapping 23 children and the facility's proprietress. Nigerian security forces later rescued 15 of the abducted pupils.

stories.title: ‘Staged’: Conspiracy theories spread online after thwarted shooting at White House press gala
stories.summary: Conspiracy theories spread online after a gunman rushed past security at the White House Correspondents' Dinner on Saturday, with some claiming the incident was staged in response to President Donald Trump's poll numbers. The dinner was cut short following the security breach.

stories.title: Russia’s military spending hits $190 billion in 2025. Ukraine’s reached $84 billion at 40% of GDP
stories.summary: Russia's military spending rose 5.9% to $190 billion in 2025, reaching 7.5% of GDP, among the highest shares globally. Ukraine's military expenditure reached $84 billion, consuming approximately 40% of its GDP.

stories.title: Timeline: How Mali went from democracy beacon to instability
stories.summary: Mali has experienced a series of political and security crises since 2012, transitioning from what was once considered a democratic model in West Africa to a state of persistent instability.

stories.title: Israel and Syria’s Shared Fight Against Hezbollah
stories.summary: An analysis examines how Israel and Syria share a common interest in countering Hezbollah. The piece argues that Washington should facilitate cooperation between the two estranged neighbors against the militant group.

stories.title: Syria tries prominent Assad-era security official
stories.summary: A Syrian court held its first hearing in the trial of ousted ruler Bashar al-Assad and senior figures from his government. Former security official Atif Najib appeared in the dock in handcuffs, marking a significant step in accountability for the Assad era.

stories.title: Plane crashes near South Sudan’s Juba, killing all 14 on board
stories.summary: A Cessna aircraft crashed near Juba, South Sudan, killing all 14 people on board. Preliminary reports suggest bad weather and low visibility may have caused the crash.

stories.title: What Five Decades of Summits Reveal About U.S.-China Relations
stories.summary: An analysis of over five decades of U.S.-China summits explores patterns in the bilateral relationship. The piece argues that the real test of the Trump-Xi meeting will come in the implementation of any agreements reached afterward.

stories.title: King Charles jets to US for trip overshadowed by Iran quarrel and shooting
stories.summary: LONDON/WASHINGTON, April 27 - Britain's King Charles and Queen Camilla arrive in the United States later on Monday for a four-day trip, a tour which has taken on even greater prominence after the Whit

stories.title: Who are the Russian mercenaries operating in Mali?
stories.summary: Africa Corps, a Russian paramilitary group controlled by Russia's Defence Ministry, confirmed it withdrew from the northern Malian town of Kidal after fierce fighting. The group has supported Mali's military junta since deploying in 2025, though Russia's military presence in Mali dates back to 2021.

stories.title: IDF striking Hezbollah terror infrastructure in southern, eastern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military stated it struck Hezbollah infrastructure in southern and eastern Lebanon. Separately, IDF soldiers in southern Lebanon were attacked by a Hezbollah explosive drone on Monday, causing no injuries.

stories.title: Ukraine’s new B-2 drone is a mystery. Its kills aren’t.
stories.summary: Ukraine's new B-2 drone has been striking Russian targets at distances up to 200 kilometers, contributing to the degradation of Russian air defenses. Details about the drone's specifications remain largely undisclosed.

stories.title: The oil, gas and arms companies profiting from the war on Iran
stories.summary: Campaigners are highlighting the significant profits being made by fossil fuel and weapons companies amid the war on Iran. Rising energy costs worldwide have drawn attention to the firms benefiting from the conflict.

stories.title: Plane crash in South Sudan kills all 14 on board
stories.summary: A plane crash on the outskirts of South Sudan's capital Juba killed all 14 people on board, including 13 passengers and the pilot. Authorities are investigating, with early reports pointing to bad weather and poor visibility as likely causes.

stories.title: 14 killed in plane crash on outskirts of South Sudan’s capital
stories.summary: A Cessna aircraft crashed on the outskirts of Juba, South Sudan's capital, killing all 14 people on board, including two Kenyan nationals and 12 South Sudanese. The civil aviation authority said adverse weather and poor visibility likely caused the crash, and a team was dispatched to the site roughly 20 km from the capital.

stories.title: Orikhiv under constant Russian airstrikes, no street fighting in the city, says Voloshyn
stories.summary: Ukrainian military spokesperson Voloshyn reported that the city of Orikhiv in Zaporizhzhia region is under constant Russian airstrikes and shelling but no street fighting has occurred. He noted Russian forces would need to breach several defensive lines to advance toward the city.

stories.title: Stalled US-Iran talks show limits of Pakistan’s mediation drive
stories.summary: Mr Trump on April 25 called off a planned trip by his special envoys to Islamabad for negotiations.

stories.title: Eisenkot calls on opposition to secure 'Zionist' majority against Netanyahu
stories.summary: Former IDF Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot called on opposition parties he termed the "Hope Bloc" to form a unified "Zionist" majority against Prime Minister Netanyahu, following the Bennett-Lapid political merger.

stories.title: Shipping traffic through Hormuz remains muted with no US-Iran deal in sight, data shows
stories.summary: Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains severely limited amid the US-Iran standoff. The US Central Command has redirected 37 vessels since imposing a blockade on Iran on April 13.

stories.title: Sudan army strike on Darfur camp kills 6: rights group
stories.summary: A Sudanese army airstrike hit a displaced persons camp in western Darfur, killing six civilians and wounding dozens, according to a rights group.

stories.title: Israeli troops launch mass detention campaign in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli forces conducted a mass detention campaign in the West Bank, carrying out raids and arrests in the Qalandia refugee camp on Monday.

stories.title: Iran blames US for failure of talks as FM meets with Putin
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg on Monday, blaming Washington for the failure of Middle East peace negotiations. Putin pledged Moscow's support in efforts to bring the regional conflict to a close.

stories.title: NATO’s top military officer: Russia is trying to reclaim Soviet territory, and threat extends beyond Baltics
stories.summary: NATO's top military officer has warned that Russia is attempting to reclaim former Soviet territory, citing threats to countries including Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Bulgaria, Romania, Moldova, Albania, and Slovakia. The officer indicated the threat extends beyond the Baltic states.

stories.title: Pakistan, China sign 3 MoUs to boost desalination, agri technology, tea sector cooperation
stories.summary: Pakistan and China signed three memoranda of understanding to strengthen cooperation in water desalination, agricultural technology, and the tea industry during President Asif Ali Zardari's week-long visit to China.

stories.title: Putin Fires Head of Russia’s Cultural Diplomacy Agency
stories.summary: Russian President Putin dismissed the head of Rossotrudnichestvo, Russia's cultural diplomacy agency. Yevgeny Primakov was replaced by Igor Chaika, the son of Russia's former chief prosecutor.

stories.title: US supreme court reinstates Texas electoral map favoring Republicans
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court formally reinstated a redrawn Texas electoral map designed to benefit Republicans, potentially flipping up to five US House seats. The decision by the 6-3 conservative-majority court formalizes an interim ruling from December as Republicans seek to maintain control of Congress.

stories.title: Putin pledges support for Iran in talks with FM Araghchi
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin told Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi that Iran would navigate the "difficult period" of war and expressed hope for peace. Araghchi visited Russia while US-Iran negotiations remain on hold.

stories.title: UAE criticises 'weak' response to Iran from other Gulf countries
stories.summary: UAE presidential advisor Anwar Gargash criticized the Gulf Cooperation Council for what he called its historically weak collective response after Iran launched retaliatory attacks against Gulf states. Gargash said he had expected such a weak stance from the Arab League but not from the GCC.

stories.title: Indigenous woman dies weeks after giving birth and being evicted from public housing: ‘She was failed completely’
stories.summary: Noongar woman Mary Ann Miller, a mother of seven, died of sepsis at Fiona Stanley Hospital in Western Australia on March 28, two weeks after giving birth. Her family says the Western Australian government knew she was experiencing domestic violence and had been evicted from public housing while trying to flee an allegedly abusive former partner.

stories.title: Why tougher US visa rules for skilled foreign workers may end in exodus to Asia, Europe
stories.summary: Tighter US visa rules for skilled foreign workers, including H-1B holders, are creating uncertainty that may drive an exodus of talent to Asia and Europe. Workers like Chinese content creator Yoyo Yue describe growing instability in long-term immigration prospects under President Trump's administration.

stories.title: Russian sabotage groups trying to infiltrate Ukrainian lines on southern front – Voloshyn
stories.summary: On Ukraine's southern front, Russian sabotage groups are using foliage as cover to infiltrate Ukrainian defensive lines, particularly near the Velykomykhailivka forest. Ukrainian spokesperson Voloshyn said defense forces are conducting search-and-strike operations to contain the infiltration attempts.

stories.title: Brazilian platform to track commodity chains ahead of EU deforestation rules
stories.summary: A new Brazilian digital platform launched on Monday to cross-reference social and environmental data, supporting the tracing of commodity supply chains linked to deforestation and land conflicts. The system was established ahead of the implementation of European Union deforestation regulations.

stories.title: Israeli gov't limits Lag Ba’omer celebration on Mount Meron amid security concerns
stories.summary: Israeli authorities limited Lag Ba'omer celebrations at Mount Meron to a maximum of 1,500 people across nearby communities including Safsofa, Or HaGanuz, Bar Yochai, and Meron, citing security concerns.

stories.title: Somalia: Somalia, Oman Discuss Stronger Cooperation in Transport and Digital Infrastructure
stories.summary: Somalia and Oman held discussions on strengthening cooperation in transport, communications, and information technology. The talks took place in Muscat as Mogadishu seeks to accelerate digital transformation and expand regional economic ties.

stories.title: Germany's Merz says Iran is humiliating US as talks stall
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz accused Iran's leadership of humiliating the United States, citing stalled negotiations in which US officials traveled to Pakistan and left without results.

stories.title: Global military spending rises 2.9% to $2.89 trillion
stories.summary: Global military spending rose 2.9 percent to $2.89 trillion, according to a conflict think-tank report released Monday. US military expenditure declined 7.5 percent as President Trump halted new financial military aid to Ukraine.

stories.title: Mali under pressure as coordinated attacks aim to 'destabilise' state [Interview]
stories.summary: Political analyst Josiasse Assemon said Mali faces growing pressure from coordinated attacks targeting major cities. The attacks have employed covert infiltration tactics and brought together rival armed groups seeking to destabilize the state.

stories.title: Palestinians in Gaza’s Deir al-Balah elect local leaders in first election in two decades
stories.summary: Palestinians in the Gaza community of Deir al-Balah and the Israeli-occupied West Bank voted in local elections over the weekend. For Gazan participants, it was their first local vote in more than two decades. Palestinian authorities called the election a success and said it could pave the way for future votes in the war-torn enclave.

stories.title: Iran offers to end chokehold on Strait of Hormuz, asks U.S. to end blockade
stories.summary: Iran also wants the U.S. to end its blockade of the country as part of its proposal, said the two officials, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss the closed-door negotiations

stories.title: Lebanon Latest: Israel’s deadly attacks amid ceasefire breaches
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes struck southern Lebanon despite a ceasefire, killing at least 14 people and triggering further civilian displacement from the affected areas.

stories.title: Hezbollah enhances drone capabilities by learning from Ukraine war tactics - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis indicates Hezbollah is upgrading its drone capabilities by incorporating fiber-optic technology and tactics observed in the Ukraine war, aiming to enhance its capacity for attacks against Israel despite supply shortages.

stories.title: Syria Quneitra families protest for relatives detained by Israel
stories.summary: Families of dozens of Syrians detained by Israel protested outside the Syrian foreign ministry in Quneitra, demanding information about their relatives' whereabouts and conditions.

stories.title: Buoyed by European rearmament boost, global military spending jumps to $2.89 trillion
stories.summary: Global military spending reached $2.89 trillion, driven largely by a 14 percent increase in European defense expenditure amid the continent's rearmament push. US military spending declined by 7.5 percent over the same period.

stories.title: Foreign missions delay return to Iraq amid US-Iran tensions
stories.summary: Several foreign diplomatic missions have delayed their return to Iraq due to ongoing US-Iran tensions. Armed factions known as the "Islamic Resistance in Iraq" continue to issue threats, contributing to the security concerns.

stories.title: Rival armed groups join forces against the Malian state: What next?
stories.summary: Armed groups with differing ideologies have launched coordinated attacks against the Malian state across multiple areas. Analysts are questioning whether the coalition can maintain its unity given the groups' divergent goals.

stories.title: Beijing’s new project 956EM takes Soviet ship design and strips every Russian weapon from it
stories.summary: China's Project 956EM adapts a Soviet-era warship design by removing all Russian-origin weaponry and replacing it with Chinese systems. Upgrades include new 324 mm torpedo tubes and modern Chinese electronic countermeasure systems intended to improve the vessel's survivability in contemporary naval combat.

stories.title: UK, EU 'push back strongly' on US foreign policy: Will Charles' visit 'soften' transatlantic divide?
stories.summary: Chatham House analyst Laurel Rapp noted that King Charles's planned visit to the United States now carries heightened diplomatic significance amid tensions between Washington and its allies over trade, NATO, Iran, Ukraine, and other strategic issues. The UK and EU have reportedly pushed back strongly on current US foreign policy positions.

stories.title: NPT summit: Can nuclear pact survive US-Israel war on Iran?
stories.summary: Analysts attending the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty review conference say the summit is unlikely to compel nuclear-armed states to comply with the treaty's obligations, particularly amid the ongoing US-Israel conflict with Iran.

stories.title: IDF strikes Lebanon’s Beqaa Valley for first time in 3 weeks as towns in north cancel school
stories.summary: Israeli forces struck Lebanon's Beqaa Valley for the first time in three weeks, following continued Hezbollah rocket fire. Schools in northern Israeli towns were canceled. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun criticized Hezbollah for waging war serving "foreign interests."

stories.title: Suspect in shooting at Trump's press dinner to appear in court
stories.summary: A California man accused of storming a gala dinner attended by President Donald Trump was to appear in court on Monday over a shooting that marks the latest spasm of political violence in deeply divid

stories.title: Argentine economy ministry secretary resigns over seven undeclared properties in Miami
stories.summary: Argentine Infrastructure Coordination Secretary Carlos Frugoni resigned after a media investigation revealed he failed to declare seven apartments in Florida to Argentine tax authorities, acquired through two Delaware-based LLCs. Economy Minister Luis Caputo accepted the resignation, and Frugoni now faces a complaint for alleged illicit enrichment.

stories.title: King Charles jets to US for four-day trip amid Iran conflict, media gala shooting
stories.summary: Britain’s King Charles and Queen Camilla will arrive in the United States later on Monday for a four-day trip, a tour which has taken on even greater prominence after the White House Correspondents’ d

stories.title: Military ombudsman: Up to 1.6 million could potentially join Ukraine’s Armed Forces
stories.summary: Ukraine's military ombudsman stated that up to 1.6 million people could potentially join the Ukrainian Armed Forces, which would allow for troop rotation. The statement comes amid an ongoing mobilization crisis in Ukraine.

stories.title: Relative calm returns to many parts of Mali following weekend's attacks
stories.summary: A fragile calm returned to Bamako and the military stronghold of Kati on Monday after two days of fierce fighting between Mali's army and jihadists allied with Tuareg separatists. The weekend attacks raised uncertainty about the ruling military junta's future.

stories.title: Russian troops resort to cannibalism on front lines as supplies dwindle, Ukraine intelligence claim
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence claims that Russian troops on the front lines have resorted to cannibalism due to dwindling supplies. The Sunday Times reported it could not independently verify the claims, but noted at least 12 separate reports of Russian infantrymen allegedly eating fellow soldiers have surfaced.

stories.title: Simultaneous attacks signal new phase of conflict in Mali-analyst
stories.summary: Political analyst Josiasse Assemon said coordinated attacks targeting major cities in Mali signal a new phase of conflict. The attacks involved covert infiltration tactics and brought together rival armed groups in simultaneous operations.

stories.title: Cool as a cucumber: man calmly ate salad as press dinner shooting unfolded
stories.summary: Michael Glantz, a senior talent agent with Creative Artists Agency, was filmed calmly eating his salad at the White House correspondents' dinner on Saturday after gunfire was heard outside and Secret Service agents entered the ballroom at the Washington Hilton hotel.

stories.title: Mali’s militant attacks expose limits of Putin’s power in Africa
stories.summary: Rebel fighters in Mali struck significant blows against the ruling military junta despite the presence of approximately 2,000 Russian troops supporting the regime. The attacks highlight the limits of Moscow's military backing for junta leader Assimi Goïta, who met with President Putin in the Kremlin last summer as part of Russia's broader Sahel influence campaign.

stories.title: Alibaba gets approval to spin off warehouse park as Reit in pivot for logistics assets
stories.summary: Alibaba Group received approval from the Hong Kong stock exchange to spin off the Jiaxing Park, a logistics and warehousing hub in Zhejiang province, as a real estate investment trust listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. The move comes two years after Alibaba withdrew listing plans for its logistics arm Cainiao.

stories.title: Putin: I will do 'everything' possible to ensure Middle East peace
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin told Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi during a meeting in Saint Petersburg that Russia would do "everything" possible to help bring peace to the Middle East. The pledge came amid the ongoing US-Israeli conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Iran war disrupts the circuit board supply chain, raises costs for tech firms
stories.summary: The disruption is a fresh blow to electronics manufacturers which are already grappling with soaring memory chip ‌costs and highlights the broadening impact of the Iran war

stories.title: 'We represent a new force': Nearly 60 nations push ahead with fossil fuel exit
stories.summary: Nearly 60 countries gathered in Santa Marta, Colombia, for the first global conference dedicated to accelerating a fossil fuel phaseout. The summit aims to break a long-standing deadlock on the issue that has stalled progress at UN COP climate summits.

stories.title: Only 23% voted in Gaza's Deir al-Balah for local elections
stories.summary: Local elections in Gaza's Deir al-Balah recorded a turnout of only 23%, the lowest participation rate among all districts. By contrast, turnout in the occupied West Bank reached approximately 56%.

stories.title: Back to the 90s: Tate exhibition to explore decade’s art and fashion
stories.summary: Tate Britain announced an upcoming exhibition exploring 1990s British art and fashion, curated by former British Vogue editor Edward Enninful. The show will feature works including Steve McQueen's first major film and a Chris Ofili painting honoring Doreen and Stephen Lawrence.

stories.title: Iran offers to reopen Strait of Hormuz without nuclear deal
stories.summary: Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz without requiring a nuclear deal. A standoff continues at the waterway, through which one-fifth of the world's oil and gas transits, as Iran has restricted access and the US has imposed a blockade on Iranian ports.

stories.title: Russian forces intensify small-unit assaults near Huliaipole but fail to gain foothold – Voloshyn
stories.summary: Russian forces have intensified small-unit assault operations south and west of Huliaipole in the Zaporizhzhia region. Ukrainian spokesperson Voloshyn said Russian troops have been unable to establish positions due to Ukrainian search-and-strike resistance operations.

stories.title: Did this tiny Caribbean island’s Jewish community help win the US Revolutionary War?
stories.summary: A new exhibition titled "The First Salute" at the Weitzman National Museum of American Jewish History explores the role of a Caribbean island's Jewish community in supporting the American Revolution. The exhibit marks America's 250th birthday.

stories.title: Iran says its army should have authority over the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: A proposed Iranian law would grant the country's armed forces authority over the Strait of Hormuz, including the power to block hostile vessels. Parliament's national security committee chairman Ebrahim Azizi said the legislation also requires transit fees to be paid in Iranian rials.

stories.title: Smashing a figure of Jesus is part of Israel's ongoing erasure of Christians
stories.summary: An article examines the treatment of Christian communities and sites in the context of Israeli military operations, citing an incident involving the destruction of a figure of Jesus as part of a broader pattern.

stories.title: Russian Army Denies University Students Face Pressure to Join Drone Forces
stories.summary: A senior Russian defense official denied that university students face pressure to join the military's drone forces. The official also stated that commanders are explicitly prohibited from transferring drone recruits to other military branches without written consent.

stories.title: Street battles and withdrawal of Russian mercenaries: Inside the 48-hour fall of Mali’s Kidal
stories.summary: The Azawad Liberation Front and the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM) launched an offensive on April 25 against several Malian towns, recapturing the northern city of Kidal after a three-year presence of Russian and Malian forces. Verified footage documented street battles and the withdrawal of Russian mercenaries over 48 hours.

stories.title: DRC creates paramilitary mining security unit backed by US and UAE funding
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo announced the creation of a paramilitary mining security unit to protect its vast mining operations. The new force is backed by funding from the United States and the United Arab Emirates.

stories.title: 2 months into the Iran war, who holds the upper hand?
stories.summary: Two months into the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, the conflict has reached a costly stalemate. A fragile Pakistan-brokered ceasefire has paused fighting, but the Strait of Hormuz remains blocked and direct talks have collapsed after Tehran demanded the US end its naval blockade of Iranian ports.

stories.title: US teens place high in Israel’s annual Bible Quiz
stories.summary: American teenagers participated in Israel's annual Bible Quiz, earning praise from judges for their Hebrew fluency. The US participants traveled to Israel during a tenuous ceasefire with Iran.

stories.title: Optical chipmaker’s profit soars 1,153% on AI demand, China’s tech self-reliance push
stories.summary: Shanghai-listed Yuanjie Semiconductor Technology reported a 1,153 percent year-on-year increase in first-quarter net profit to 179 million yuan, while revenue rose 321 percent to 355 million yuan. The gains were driven by surging demand for computing power amid China's AI boom and its push for technological self-reliance.

stories.title: Chinese supercomputers help crack the mystery of Yellowstone’s volcanic plumbing: paper
stories.summary: Chinese researchers using domestic supercomputers published findings proposing that Yellowstone's magma channels were not forced open by rising magma but were instead created by tectonic forces tearing apart the lithosphere. The study aims to resolve a longstanding scientific debate about the volcanic plumbing beneath the world's largest active volcanic system.

stories.title: Russian forces attempting to advance and entrench near Hryshyne and Rodynske – military
stories.summary: Fighting has escalated near the settlements of Hryshyne and Rodynske in Ukraine's Donetsk region, where Russian forces are attempting to advance and establish positions. Ukrainian military officials said their units are holding defensive lines and inflicting losses on the attackers.

stories.title: Walid Jumblatt: The hidden obstacle to Israeli-Lebanese rapprochement - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece examines Lebanese Druze leader Walid Jumblatt's role as an obstacle to Israeli-Lebanese rapprochement. The analysis argues his opposition is rooted in personal motivations and a long history of political survival maneuvering in Lebanon.

stories.title: Iran proposes to reopen Strait of Hormuz without nuclear agreement
stories.summary: Iran FM in Saint Petersburg blames U.S. for failure of Pakistan talks, state media said

stories.title: Night light disrupts antibody production rhythms, may raise risk of death, Israeli study finds
stories.summary: Researchers at Tel Aviv University found that nighttime artificial light, even from common sources like streetlights, disrupts antibody production rhythms in mice. The findings suggest potential implications for human immune function and mortality risk.

stories.title: Former Israeli PMs Bennett and Lapid merge parties ahead of elections
