stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid announced a merger of their political parties into a new bloc called Beyahad, meaning "Together" in Hebrew, to challenge Benjamin Netanyahu in Israel's October elections.

stories.title: Kenya: Former governor Mike Sonko is back, but what does he want?
stories.summary: Former Nairobi governor Mike Sonko has re-emerged in Kenyan politics after a court victory that unlocked millions in assets and the launch of his own political party. His intentions ahead of the 2027 elections remain unclear.

stories.title: Iranian health minister: US-Israeli attacks targeted 240 medical facilities
stories.summary: Iran's Health Minister Mohammad Reza Zafarghandi stated that US-Israeli attacks targeted 240 medical facilities, including approximately 50 hospitals and 50 emergency centers that were damaged in the bombardment.

stories.title: Fire risks not spotted due to old inspection guidelines, Tai Po blaze inquiry told
stories.summary: A public inquiry into Hong Kong's deadly Tai Po fire at Wang Fuk Court heard that government surveyors failed to detect major fire risks because outdated inspection guidelines did not require in-person checks of renovation works. Illegal alterations to emergency passages during the HK$336 million exterior overhaul reportedly went unnoticed as a result.

stories.title: 'You should have become soaps': Pro-Palestine protesters kick Jews out of Milan Liberation march
stories.summary: During Italy's April 25 Liberation Day march in Milan, pro-Palestine protesters reportedly expelled Jewish participants and directed antisemitic remarks at them, including Holocaust-related slurs.

stories.title: New Bennett-Lapid party weakens compared to separate runs, Netanyahu maintains lead - poll
stories.summary: A new poll shows the merged Bennett-Lapid party performing weaker than when the two ran separately, with the opposition bloc dropping to 59 seats from 61. Netanyahu's coalition rose from 49 to 51 seats, regaining a lead.

stories.title: Israel-backed militias' bid to seize control of Gaza from Hamas
stories.summary: A new report details how Israeli-backed armed militias are operating inside the besieged Gaza Strip, attempting to challenge Hamas's control while fragmenting the territory's political landscape.

stories.title: Gunmen abduct 23 children from orphanage in central Nigeria
stories.summary: Gunmen raided an unregistered orphanage in Nigeria's Kogi state and abducted at least 23 children. A partial rescue operation recovered some of the children, but eight remained missing as of Monday.

stories.title: How the Iran war is bringing back 'citizenship as a weapon'
stories.summary: Some Gulf states have begun revoking the citizenship of nationals deemed "traitors" amid the ongoing conflict involving Iran, Israel, and the United States. Questions have been raised about whether the measures serve genuine security purposes or are being used to suppress political dissent.

stories.title: Bureau defends Hins Cheung mentor role after mainland China online backlash
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Security Bureau defended appointing singer Hins Cheung as a mentor in a rehabilitation program for roughly 7,000 people arrested during the 2019 protests but not prosecuted. The decision drew criticism from internet users in mainland China, but the bureau said it welcomes individuals from all backgrounds to share positive life experiences.

stories.title: 5.7-magnitude earthquake jolts Islamabad, parts of KP: PMD
stories.summary:
Tremors were felt in Islamabad and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on Monday as an earthquake of 5.7 magnitude struck the Afghanistan-Tajikistan border region, the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) said.
In

stories.title: Ukrainian drones to be produced in Norway as countries sign agreement
stories.summary: The defense ministries of Norway and Ukraine signed an agreement in Kyiv to manufacture Ukrainian drones in Norway. The project is the first under the Build with Ukraine initiative, establishing Norwegian-Ukrainian defense production cooperation.

stories.title: Iran FM Araghchi says he discussed conditions for continuing US talks with ‘friends in Pakistan’
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said he discussed conditions for continuing U.S.-Iran talks with Pakistani officials during recent visits to Islamabad. He also traveled to Oman before arriving in Russia as part of a regional diplomatic tour.

stories.title: Rabbinate accused of defying court as Israeli women left waiting for exams
stories.summary: Israel's Chief Rabbinate has been accused of defying a court order, leaving Israeli women waiting hours for religious examinations. Rabbi Seth Farber of the organization ITIM said staff were trying to provide food for the women left waiting.

stories.title: Dara Horn, Joseph Finder among visiting authors at annual writer’s festival
stories.summary: Authors Dara Horn and Joseph Finder are among the visiting guests at an upcoming annual writers' festival in Jerusalem. Organizers acknowledged difficulties in securing participants due to boycotts and Israel's low favorability in the literary world.

stories.title: Zambia: CPJ Calls On Zambian President to Champion the Media As World Press Freedom Day Host
stories.summary: The Committee to Protect Journalists wrote to Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema raising concerns about attacks on journalists and restrictive media legislation. The letter was sent as Zambia prepares to host the United Nations' World Press Freedom Day 2026 Global Conference on May 3.

stories.title: Chinese robotaxi firms accelerate global roll-outs as cost edge drives expansion
stories.summary: Chinese robotaxi companies Pony AI and WeRide are accelerating global fleet deployments, citing cost advantages from China's new energy vehicle supply chain. Pony AI's seventh-generation robotaxi, including vehicle, battery, and autonomous driving kit, now costs below 230,000 yuan, benefiting from improved operational efficiency.

stories.title: As Hamas prepares to choose 1st leader since Sinwar, postwar Gaza’s fate hangs in the balance
stories.summary: Hamas is preparing to select its first leader since Yahya Sinwar, with two leading contenders representing divergent strategies for the group's future. One candidate favors continued armed resistance in Gaza while the other prioritizes the organization's political survival.

stories.title: Mali's defence minister killed as armed groups launch countrywide offensive
stories.summary: Mali's Defence Minister Sadio Camara and family members were killed in a car bomb attack as Tuareg separatists and an al-Qaeda affiliate launched a coordinated countrywide offensive, with fighting reported in the capital Bamako.

stories.title: China seeks Southeast Asia gains as US influence falters
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi visited Southeast Asia as Beijing seeks to expand its regional influence. The trip aimed to position China as a stable partner amid regional concerns over war, tariffs, and questions about Washington's reliability.

stories.title: Russia ramping up assaults on southern axis, Ukraine holding line – Voloshyn
stories.summary: Russian forces are increasing the intensity of their attacks along Ukraine's southern axis, according to Ukrainian spokesperson Voloshyn. Ukraine's Defense Forces are holding the line and have regained control of positions in some areas.

stories.title: Nigeria: Family Counters Army's Account, Alleges Unlawful Killing of Corps Member in Abuja
stories.summary: A Nigerian family disputed the army's account of the killing of a National Youth Service Corps member in Abuja. The family called the military's claim of an exchange of gunfire during pursuit of armed robbers "false, misleading, and an affront to the memory of an innocent young man."

stories.title: Nigeria: Terrorists Attack Katsina Community, Kill 10, Injure Several Others
stories.summary: Terrorists attacked a community in Nigeria's Katsina state, killing 10 people and injuring several others. Local vigilante group members prevented the attackers from fully entering the village.

stories.title: China’s CATL touts landmark order in ‘DeepSeek moment’ for sodium-ion batteries
stories.summary: China's CATL signed a landmark contract to supply 60 gigawatt-hours of sodium-ion batteries to Beijing HyperStrong Technology over three years. The deal marks a major step in commercializing sodium-ion battery technology amid rising demand for energy storage infrastructure following the global oil shock.

stories.title: Russian drone attack on Odesa wounds 10, officials say
stories.summary: An overnight Russian drone attack on the southern Ukrainian city of Odesa on April 27 wounded 10 people, including two children. Residential buildings were also damaged in the strike, according to Ukrainian officials.

stories.title: Sadiq Khan may try to stop Scotland Yard signing Palantir contract
stories.summary: London Mayor Sadiq Khan may seek to block the Metropolitan Police from signing a contract with US technology firm Palantir for AI-based criminal intelligence processing. Khan's office cited concerns about using public funds to support companies whose activities may conflict with London's values, noting Palantir's links to US immigration enforcement and Israel's military.

stories.title: The arms Ukraine outgrew in two years are now its potential export catalogue
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence chief Budanov identified older first-person-view drones, 2022–2023-era long-range drones, sea drones, and bombers as weapons Ukraine has outgrown and could now export. Potential buyers include countries in Asia and Africa.

stories.title: Tens of thousands flock to French kite festival as record smashed
stories.summary: The 39th International Kite Festival in Berck-sur-Mer, northern France, drew tens of thousands of visitors and set a world record for the longest kite ever flown at 100 metres. The event featured spectacular kites and favorable weather conditions.

stories.title: Syria’s first public trial of Assad and allies opens in Damascus
stories.summary: Syria's first public trial of officials linked to former President Bashar al-Assad's government opened in Damascus on Sunday. Assad and his brother Maher, former commander of the 4th Armored Division, were charged in absentia alongside other former security officials. They face accusations including killings, torture, extortion, and drug trafficking.

stories.title: Who are the groups behind unprecedented Mali attacks?
stories.summary: Al-Qaeda-linked group JNIM and Tuareg rebels joined forces to launch attacks across Mali, killing the country's defence minister. Two days of national mourning were declared. The Malian army, supported by Russian mercenaries, faces an alliance between the jihadist group and separatist fighters despite their historical disagreements.

stories.title: Court martial of Nigerian officers over coup plot to resume in May
stories.summary: The court martial of approximately three dozen Nigerian military officers charged with plotting to overthrow the government is set to resume in May. Local officials confirmed the proceedings would continue next month.

stories.title: Mali's junta in crisis as defence minister killed, key city 'caputred'
stories.summary: Mali's military junta faced a major security crisis after coordinated attacks by jihadist fighters and separatist rebels over the weekend killed Defence Minister Sadio Camara and reportedly left a key northern town under rebel control. The assaults targeted multiple locations nationwide.

stories.title: Parachinar Airport becomes operational after long hiatus
stories.summary: Parachinar Airport in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Kurram District has been reactivated after a long hiatus, following renovation work by the Frontier Works Organisation and Pakistan Airports Authority. Pakistan Army Aviation conducted operational trials on April 26.

stories.title: King Charles' US visit overshadowed by Iran quarrel and shooting
stories.summary: King Charles and Queen Camilla arrive in the United States for a four-day visit, with the trip overshadowed by tensions over the ongoing war in the Middle East involving Iran.

stories.title: Israeli army says it launched attack on Lebanon's Beqaa Valley
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced it launched strikes on what it described as Hezbollah positions in Lebanon's Beqaa Valley, while also attacking the southern towns of Tibnin and Yater. The death toll since the April 16 ceasefire has reached 38.

stories.title: Russia launches nearly 1,900 drones, 60 missiles at Ukraine over past week – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky reported that Russia launched approximately 1,900 strike drones, nearly 1,400 guided aerial bombs, and about 60 missiles at Ukraine over the past week. Ukrainian air defenses achieved over 90% effectiveness in destroying the incoming drones.

stories.title: How does targeting water supply during war worsen the scarcity crisis?
stories.summary: Water infrastructure is increasingly targeted during armed conflicts worldwide, exacerbating scarcity crises for civilian populations dependent on these systems.

stories.title: Why anti-US sentiment is quietly growing in India
stories.summary: Anti-US sentiment is growing in India as the population faces economic fallout from the US-Israel war with Iran. Public opinion toward President Donald Trump has turned increasingly negative, though analysts say underlying tensions predate the current conflict.

stories.title: Palantir manifesto draws global criticism over 'technofascist' and militarist vision of the West
stories.summary: Palantir Technologies published a 22-point manifesto on X that has drawn international criticism for its ultranationalist and militarist tone. The document, which has accumulated over 32 million views, is based on a book by CEO Alex Karp and corporate affairs head Nicholas Zamiska. Critics have labeled the vision "technofascist."

stories.title: Germany's Merz questions US strategy in Iran war, says nation 'humiliated'
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz questioned the US exit strategy in the Iran war, saying Iran's leadership has humiliated the nation and that Iranian negotiators proved "clearly stronger" than expected. He urged a swift end to the conflict, citing economic impacts on Germany.

stories.title: Russian drone attack on Odesa wounds 10, officials say
stories.summary: Russia struck ​port infrastructure on ‌the Black ​Sea ⁠in Odesa, which damaged ​an ‌energy facility within the cargo terminal

stories.title: ‘Clearly stronger’: Germany’s Merz says Iran ‘humiliated’ US in its war
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated that Iran has "humiliated" the United States in the ongoing war, warning that Washington risks becoming mired in a prolonged conflict similar to its experiences in Iraq and Afghanistan.

stories.title: Badenoch says parliament ‘right place to hold Starmer to account’ in bid to win support from Labour MPs for inquiry – UK politics live
stories.summary: UK Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch urged Labour MPs to support a parliamentary inquiry to hold Prime Minister Keir Starmer accountable. Separately, Downing Street said the UK is well-positioned to handle global supply disruptions caused by the unresolved Iran war, citing forward-planning by the government.

stories.title: Data reveals limited shipping traffic through Hormuz
stories.summary: Shipping data shows only seven vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours amid stalled US-Iran negotiations. This represents a sharp decline from the average 140 daily passages before the war began on February 28.

stories.title: Have US-Iran talks failed? Why no deal yet doesn’t mean diplomacy is dead
stories.summary: US-Iran diplomatic negotiations have reached a deadlock, but analysts assess that neither side is likely to resume military hostilities, suggesting diplomacy remains a viable path forward.

stories.title: Patterns of influence: Inside Prof. Yaniv Dover’s physics-inspired view of marketing
stories.summary: Professor Yaniv Dover of the Hebrew University Business School discussed his physics-inspired approach to marketing in a video conversation hosted by Israeli director Maor Zaguri.

stories.title: Lebanon cannot be bombed into sovereignty
stories.summary: Analysts argue that achieving a sovereign Lebanon and the demilitarization of Hezbollah requires a credible political transition rather than military intervention alone.

stories.title: Junta leader’s silence adds to Mali’s deepening political crisis
stories.summary: Mali's military junta faces a deepening political crisis after coordinated jihadist and rebel attacks killed Defence Minister Sadio Camara and left key northern towns contested. Junta leader General Assimi Goïta has been conspicuously absent from public view following the attacks.

stories.title: Kyiv and Warsaw to develop “Polish model” for defense cooperation by June – Kamyshin
stories.summary: Kyiv and Warsaw announced plans to develop a "Polish model" for defense-industry cooperation by the Ukraine Recovery Conference in Gdańsk at the end of June 2026, where the first defense-sector contracts are expected to be signed.

stories.title: Global military spending surges and reaches record high
stories.summary: The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) reported that global military spending has surged to a record high. Researchers also raised concerns about declining transparency in military expenditure reporting.

stories.title: Iranian foreign minister heads to Russia, Trump says 'call us' to negotiate
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Russia on Monday to seek support from President Vladimir Putin as U.S.-Iran negotiations remain stalled. U.S. President Donald Trump said Iran could call if it wants to negotiate an end to their two-month conflict.

stories.title: Russian fighters confirm withdrawal from northern Mali city after separatist attacks
stories.summary: Russian fighters confirmed their withdrawal from the northern Malian city of Kidal following attacks by separatist forces. Ethnic Tuareg fighters claim control of the city after a weekend of coordinated nationwide attacks carried out alongside Islamist groups.

stories.title: Poll projects dead heat between Fujimori and Sánchez in Peru runoff as count nears completion
stories.summary: An Ipsos Peru poll shows right-wing candidate Keiko Fujimori and left-wing candidate Roberto Sánchez tied at 38 percent in a simulated runoff for Peru's presidential election scheduled for June 7. The survey has a margin of error of ±2.8 percentage points. The official count from the April 12 first-round election remains inconclusive.

stories.title: UK spring sunshine prompts warnings over unsafe fake designer sunglasses
stories.summary: UK experts warned that counterfeit designer sunglasses lack proper UV filters and pose risks of eye damage. The College of Optometrists urged shoppers to check for safety marks when purchasing sunglasses during spring sunshine.

stories.title: 'Struggling to process': One person tried to defend Yemanu Zalka during Independence Day eve attack
stories.summary: A Petah Tikva Magistrate's Court extended by five days the detention of the main suspect and three teenage suspects in the murder of Yemanu Zalka during an Independence Day eve attack. Reports indicate one person attempted to defend Zalka during the incident.

stories.title: Pro-choice campaigners in Malta create lockboxes containing abortion pills
stories.summary: Pro-choice campaigners in Malta installed 15 lockboxes containing abortion pills at locations across the country to protest its near-total abortion ban, the strictest in western Europe. Women less than nine weeks pregnant can email to receive location codes and access the pills.

stories.title: Israel bombs southern Lebanese town of Taybeh
stories.summary: Israeli forces bombed the southern Lebanese town of Taybeh. Earlier Israeli attacks in the country killed two people, raising the total death toll since the April 16 ceasefire to 38.

stories.title: Guangdong’s rule as China’s GDP king faces an unprecedented threat to the crown
stories.summary: China's Jiangsu province is narrowing its GDP gap with Guangdong, which has been the country's largest provincial economy since the late 1980s. Both provinces have GDPs comparable to G7 members Italy and Canada. The latest economic data shows the rivalry reflects shifting economic dynamics within China.

stories.title: Reopen Strait of Hormuz by reframing Iran’s tolls as reconstruction
stories.summary: The Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil and gas trade passes, has become a critical flashpoint amid Gulf tensions. Disruptions have driven up prices, shipping costs, and military tensions beyond the region. The article proposes reframing Iran's tolls as reconstruction contributions to help resolve the standoff.

stories.title: Court martial of Nigerian officers accused of coup plot to resume in May
stories.summary: The court martial of approximately three dozen Nigerian military officers accused of plotting to overthrow the government is set to resume in May. The charges stem from an alleged coup plot uncovered last year.

stories.title: Rare April Snowstorm Shatters Record in Moscow, Leaves At Least 3 Dead in Samara
stories.summary: An unusual April snowstorm struck Moscow, breaking records for the period. In Samara, the severe weather left at least three people dead, and city authorities warned residents to prepare for additional wet snow and strong wind gusts.

stories.title: Late-April Snowfall Shatters Record in Moscow
stories.summary: Moscow experienced record-breaking late-April snowfall. City authorities warned residents to prepare for additional wet snow and strong wind gusts in the coming days.

stories.title: UK: Starmer to hold meeting about economic impacts of Iran war
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer announced a meeting for Tuesday involving Cobra and Bank of England representatives to assess the economic impact of the US-Israeli war on Iran, warning that economic consequences could persist for some time.

stories.title: Russian attack triggers large oil spill in Odesa region port
stories.summary: A Russian attack on the Odesa region on April 26 caused a sunflower oil spill in the waters of the port of Chornomorsk.

stories.title: Iran’s foreign minister arrives in St. Petersburg to meet with Putin
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in St. Petersburg in the early hours of April 27 to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin, according to Iranian agencies Mehr and Irna.

stories.title: Venice opera house fires government-linked music director after months of protests
stories.summary: Venice's Teatro La Fenice opera house fired incoming music director Beatrice Venezi after she made statements the foundation deemed "repeated offensive," including insinuations about nepotistic hiring practices. The dismissal followed months of protests over her appointment. La Fenice cancelled all future collaborations with the 36-year-old conductor.

stories.title: Assimi Goïta silent, rebels seize northern stronghold: What we know about the Mali attacks
stories.summary: Rebel forces from the FLA seized the northern stronghold of Kidal in Mali, while defence chief Sadio Camara was killed. President Assimi Goïta has remained silent as the military junta faces mounting pressure and isolation from the territorial losses.

stories.title: How one surgeon maintained hospital care amid Sudan's conflict
stories.summary: Amid Sudan's ongoing conflict and the near-collapse of its healthcare system, surgeons including Dr. Jamal Eltaeb and Dr. Osman Ismail Osman are working under extreme conditions to maintain hospital operations and treat patients.

stories.title: PSG vs Bayern Munich: Champions League – preview, team news, start, lineups
stories.summary: Bayern Munich travel to Paris to face defending champions Paris Saint-Germain in the first leg of a Champions League semifinal.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia Snooker Masters 'cancelled' leaving players furious
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia cancelled its major snooker tournament, the Saudi Arabia Snooker Masters, as part of a broader effort to restrict spending on high-cost sporting events, leaving players frustrated.

stories.title: Aoun defends Israel-Lebanon talks amid Hezbollah criticism
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun defended direct negotiations with Israel amid criticism from Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem. Aoun vowed not to accept a "humiliating agreement" while responding indirectly to Hezbollah's objections to the talks.

stories.title: Hezbollah rejects Lebanon-Israel talks, vows confrontation
stories.summary: Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem rejected Lebanon's direct talks with Israel, vowing the group's confrontational actions against Israel will continue. He criticized the Lebanese government's decision to engage in negotiations.

stories.title: Iran war disrupts the circuit board supply chain, raises costs for tech firms
stories.summary: The conflict in the Middle East has disrupted supplies of crucial raw materials and pushed up prices of the printed circuit boards (PCB) used in almost all electronic devices, from smartphones and com

stories.title: Mbappe could miss El Clasico after Real Madrid confirm thigh injury
stories.summary: Real Madrid confirmed that forward Kylian Mbappé sustained an injury to the semitendinosus muscle in his left thigh, putting his participation in the upcoming El Clásico in doubt.

stories.title: Exclusive: Lebanon truce deadline tied to Hezbollah disarmament
stories.summary: Diplomatic sources told The New Arab that the United States has given Lebanon a three-week deadline to present a plan for disarming Hezbollah, warning that failure to comply could result in expanded Israeli military operations.

stories.title: Nigeria: Court Martial Over Coup Plot to Resume May 8 - Dhq
stories.summary: Nigeria's Defence Headquarters confirmed the court martial related to last year's foiled coup plot will resume on May 8. Approximately three dozen military officers face charges in connection with the alleged plot to overthrow the government.

stories.title: Taiwan completes US tank deal as final Abrams shipment reaches port
stories.summary: Taiwan received its final shipment of 28 US-made M1A2T Abrams tanks at the Port of Taipei, completing a long-delayed modernization order. The tanks were transported under military and police escort to the Armour Training Command in Hsinchu county. The delivery aims to bolster Taiwan's defenses amid growing military pressure from Beijing.

stories.title: Massive Russian attack on Odesa: Injury toll climbs to 14
stories.summary: Fourteen people were injured in Odesa following a nighttime Russian drone attack on the city.

stories.title: Israeli gun fire kills Palestinian child, wounds another
stories.summary: Israeli gunfire killed 15-year-old Ayham al-Omari and wounded another civilian in Beit Lahia in northern Gaza, according to the Palestinian Wafa news agency.

stories.title: Daily Briefing April 27: Success of Bennett-Lapid merger hinges on Eisenkot role in race
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid announced they will run on a joint list in the 2026 elections, with analysts suggesting the merger's success may depend on former IDF Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot's role in the race.

stories.title: Somalia: Senior Somali Presidential Adviser Resigns Amid Political Tensions
stories.summary: A senior adviser to Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud resigned on Sunday, citing growing political disputes that could threaten the country's stability and security. The resignation was announced from Mogadishu.

stories.title: Somalia: UN Humanitarian Chief Arrives in Somalia for High-Level Aid Talks
stories.summary: UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs Tom Fletcher arrived in Mogadishu on Monday for a high-level mission. His visit focuses on Somalia's urgent humanitarian needs and long-term aid financing strategies.

stories.title: Malawi: Malawi Secures U.S.$80 Million Lifeline As Government Turns to Local Councils to Fix Service Delivery
stories.summary: Malawi secured an $80 million grant from the World Bank following Finance Minister Joseph Mwanamvekha's meetings in Washington DC. The funds are expected to ease foreign exchange pressures and address governance challenges at the local council level.

stories.title: U.S. says three killed in boat strike as campaign toll hits 185
stories.summary: The US military's Southern Command reported three people were killed in a boat strike, stating the vessel was operated by designated terrorist organizations along known narco-trafficking routes, bringing the campaign's total toll to 185.

stories.title: Hamas organizing pro-Palestinian protests, raising funds in Netherlands, Dutch intelligence says
stories.summary: Dutch intelligence agency AIVD reported that Hamas has been organizing pro-Palestinian protests and raising funds in the Netherlands. The agency also warned about Iran's offensive cyber programs targeting Europe, including influence operations, sabotage, and espionage.

stories.title: Israel-Iran LIVE: Meeting with Vladimir Putin will be a good opportunity to discuss war developments, says Iran FM Araghchi
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Saint Petersburg for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Reports indicate Iran has presented a proposal to the US for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and ending the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: First Thing: White House correspondents’ dinner suspect to be charged as motive examined
stories.summary: A 31-year-old suspect identified as Cole Tomas Allen from Torrance, California, is due in court after a shooting at the White House correspondents' dinner on Saturday. He faces charges including assault of a federal officer and attempting to kill a federal officer. A manifesto reportedly found listed Trump administration officials.

stories.title: Fighting over access to water in Chad kills at least 42, army intervenes
stories.summary: At least 42 people were killed in Chad after a dispute over water access escalated into reprisal attacks between communities. The Chadian army intervened, and the government stated the situation is under control.

stories.title: Iran offers U.S. deal to end war and reopen Strait of Hormuz — Axios
stories.summary: Iran has presented the United States with a proposal to restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and end hostilities, while suggesting that nuclear program negotiations be deferred to a later stage, according to Axios.

stories.title: 10 things to know about Taiwo Oyedele, Nigeria’s new finance minister
stories.summary: Nigerian President Tinubu appointed Taiwo Oyedele, formerly the country's tax reform adviser, as finance minister. The appointment signals a shift toward data-driven fiscal policy and technocratic governance in Nigeria.

stories.title: Israel appoints first ambassador to Somaliland
stories.summary: Israel appointed its first ambassador to Somaliland, the self-declared independent region in the Horn of Africa, months after formally recognizing it.

stories.title: Mali in turmoil after insurgents seize towns and kill defence minister
stories.summary: Mali was hit by coordinated attacks from al-Qaida-affiliated JNIM and the Tuareg-led Azawad Liberation Front, which seized several towns and military bases. The country's defence minister and military intelligence chief were reportedly killed in the assaults. The attacks represent an unprecedented collaboration between formerly opposing insurgent groups.

stories.title: North Korea strengthens nuclear push as US flails in Middle East
stories.summary:
North Korea is taking advantage of the Middle East war to speed up its weapons development and cement its nuclear status in a world where international norms have broken down, analysts say.
Since US-I

stories.title: The cost of bringing down inflation in India, U.S. and U.K. | Data
stories.summary: The U.S. Federal Reserve managed to reduce inflation with minimal economic impact, while the United Kingdom experienced a recession during its disinflation effort. India avoided a downturn but now confronts a currency crisis as a consequence of its anti-inflation measures.

stories.title: Colombia offers record $1.4m-reward for rebel it blames for deadly bomb attack
stories.summary: Colombia offered a record $1.4 million reward for a rebel leader known as "Marlon," blamed for a bomb attack that killed 20 people. The blast occurred on the Pan-American Highway in the south-western Cauca department and injured 36 others. A dissident FARC faction is blamed for the attack.

stories.title: She opposed US-Israeli bombs on Iran. The monarchists lost it | Ariana Jasmine
stories.summary: Iranian-American content creator Ariana Jasmine discussed divisions within the Iranian diaspora over the US-Israeli war on Iran, describing backlash she received from monarchist groups after opposing the military campaign.

stories.title: Awash Bank listing tests Ethiopia’s new exchange
stories.summary: Awash Bank became the first company listed on the Ethiopian Securities Exchange, serving as a test for the country's nascent capital market. High investor demand was constrained by limited liquidity and the absence of formal pricing mechanisms.

stories.title: Russian drones strike Odesa, injuring 13 people across multiple districts
stories.summary: Russian forces launched a massive overnight drone attack on Odesa on April 27, injuring 13 people across multiple districts, according to the city's military administration head, Serhiy Lysak.

stories.title: Why Iran plays the Sicilian Defence
stories.summary: On Friday, April 11, while Pakistani officials were arranging the seating plan for ceasefire talks in Islamabad, the USS Frank E. Peterson and USS Michael Murphy entered the Strait of Hormuz. Murphy s

stories.title: WuXi AppTec posts record first-quarter revenue on strong global demand
stories.summary: Shanghai- and Hong Kong-listed WuXi AppTec reported record first-quarter revenue of 12.44 billion yuan ($1.72 billion), up 28.81 percent year on year. Net profit rose nearly 27 percent to 4.65 billion yuan. Strong global pharmaceutical demand and a robust order backlog drove the growth.

stories.title: Pakistani president seeks to bolster ‘full spectrum’ of ties with China on visit
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari began a week-long visit to China focused on economics and trade. He arrived on Saturday and is visiting Changsha in Hunan province before heading to Sanya in Hainan. Zardari plans to meet provincial leaders to review the full spectrum of Pakistan-China relations.

stories.title: US supreme court to hear case that could weaken consumers’ ability to sue for failure to warn of product risks
stories.summary: The US Supreme Court will hear arguments on Monday in a case that could limit consumers' ability to sue companies for failing to warn about product risks. The case involves glyphosate, the active ingredient in Roundup herbicide, which has been linked to cancer in multiple studies and classified as a probable carcinogen by a WHO agency.

stories.title: Bomb blast on Colombia highway leaves at least 20 dead ahead of May elections
stories.summary: A bomb blast on the Pan-American Highway in Colombia's Cauca department killed at least 20 people and injured 36 others. A dissident FARC faction is blamed for the Saturday attack, which destroyed buses and vans. The violence comes ahead of presidential elections next month.

stories.title: Oil rises, stocks swing as US-Iran peace talk hopes wobble
stories.summary: Oil prices rose on Monday while global stock markets showed mixed results as the US and Iran remained no closer to ending their eight-week-old war, with stalled peace talks dampening hopes for a resolution.

stories.title: Teva honored for gender equality as women reach 43% of senior management in Israel
stories.summary: Israeli pharmaceutical company Teva was recognized for advancing gender equality, with women now comprising 43% of senior management positions in Israel. The award cited the company's efforts in women's representation, equal pay, and inclusive workplace policies.

stories.title: Crimea under massive attack overnight, says ATESH
stories.summary: The partisan network ATESH reported that Russian-occupied Crimea came under a massive attack overnight on April 26–27. Details of the strikes and damage were not immediately specified.

stories.title: At least 42 people killed in eastern Chad during clashes over water resources
stories.summary: At least 42 people were killed and 10 injured in intercommunal clashes over water resources in eastern Chad. Officials confirmed the violence on Sunday.

stories.title: Sanctioned Russian steel tycoon’s superyacht crosses blocked Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The 142-meter superyacht Nord, owned by sanctioned Russian steel tycoon Alexei Mordashov of Severstal, crossed the Strait of Hormuz, according to vessel-tracking service Vesselfinder.

stories.title: Russia’s overnight target list in Odesa: a hotel, the funicular, the port, three districts, 14 civilians
stories.summary: Russian forces struck Odesa overnight, hitting a hotel, the funicular, the port, and three city districts, killing 14 civilians. Ukraine's Air Force reported shooting down 74 of 94 drones, though 20 struck 15 locations across the country.

stories.title: Too early to drop sanctions against Iran, says EU's von der Leyen
stories.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen stated in Berlin that it is too early to lift sanctions on Iran, citing the country's suppression of its own population and calling for fundamental change before any sanctions relief.

stories.title: IDF locates Hezbollah weapons cache in children’s bedroom during op. in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces reported discovering a Hezbollah weapons cache hidden in a children's bedroom during operations in southern Lebanon. The cache contained explosives, Kalashnikov rifles, grenades, RPGs, machine guns, and other combat equipment.

stories.title: Global military spending continues to rise as European and Asian expenditures surge
stories.summary: Global military spending reached $2,887 billion in 2025, up 2.9 percent from 2024, according to SIPRI data. European spending rose 14 percent and Asia-Oceania spending increased 8.1 percent, while US spending declined. The US, China, and Russia together accounted for 51 percent of the global total.

stories.title: White House shooting, US-Iran talks, and IDF controversy: What you need to know
stories.summary: A news recap covered several major developments including a shooting at the White House, ongoing U.S.-Iran diplomatic talks, and a controversy involving the Israel Defense Forces.

stories.title: Iran war fertilizer squeeze could spell trouble for next year’s grain harvests
stories.summary: The ongoing conflict with Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz have driven up nitrogen-based fertilizer prices, potentially threatening next year's global grain harvests as farmers struggle to afford rising input costs amid low staple crop prices.

stories.title: PLA showcases YJ-20 hypersonic missiles as Balikatan drills heat up South China Sea
stories.summary: The Chinese People's Liberation Army released footage of YJ-20 hypersonic anti-ship missile launches, though the timing and location were unspecified. The video appeared on social media as joint US-Philippines-Japan Balikatan military exercises were underway in the disputed South China Sea, heightening regional tensions.

stories.title: Varoufakis on Palantir, AI warfare, and the rise of tech lordism
stories.summary: Former Greek finance minister Yanis Varoufakis discussed Palantir's new manifesto, AI-driven weapons systems, and the growing ideological influence of major technology companies in an interview with journalist Redi Tlhabi.

stories.title: South Africa: 'Every Rand Stolen is an Attack on our Democracy' - Ramaphosa on Freedom Day
stories.summary: President Cyril Ramaphosa marked South Africa's 32nd Freedom Day in Bloemfontein, calling on citizens to protect the Constitution and renew the social contract forged in 1994. He acknowledged that progress toward full economic freedom and social justice remains incomplete.

stories.title: India, New Zealand sign ‘once-in-a-generation’ free-trade deal
stories.summary: India and New Zealand signed a free trade agreement on Monday to deepen economic ties and expand market access. India seeks to diversify exports amid US tariffs and disruptions from the Iran war, while New Zealand aims to reduce reliance on China. The deal covers a range of goods and market access provisions.

stories.title: Israel sent air defence system and troops to UAE during Iran war, report says
stories.summary: According to an Axios report, Israel deployed an Iron Dome air defense battery and troops to the United Arab Emirates during the Iran war, marking the first time Israel has sent such a system to another country.

stories.title: Two killed in Israeli attacks in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: At least two people were killed in Israeli attacks in southern Lebanon, according to Al Jazeera.

stories.title: Liberia: Tweah - Investigators Lack Understanding of Govt Operations in U.S.$6.2m Case
stories.summary: In Liberia, former Finance Minister Samuel D. Tweah testified in Criminal Court 'C,' rejecting charges that he and four other former officials personally diverted $6.2 million in government funds. Tweah argued that investigators lacked understanding of government operations.

stories.title: South Africa: Dry Tap Reality - the Growing Water Infrastructure Crisis in SA
stories.summary: South Africa faces a growing water infrastructure crisis, with unreliable supply, unsafe water, and prolonged service interruptions reported across all provinces. The situation reflects systemic failures and weak oversight in the country's water management systems.

stories.title: Liberia: Liberia, Sierra Leone Face Renewed Scrutiny Over 'Crackdowns On Dissent' Following Lawmaker's Expulsion, Activist Sentencing
stories.summary: Liberia and Sierra Leone face renewed international scrutiny over perceived crackdowns on political dissent. Civil society groups and regional observers have raised concerns about a possible rollback of free speech following a lawmaker's expulsion in one country and an activist's sentencing in the other.

stories.title: Hezbollah chief 'enemy reached a dead end'
stories.summary: Hezbollah chief Naim Qassem declared that Israel's attacks on Lebanon aimed at destroying the group have "reached a dead end." He called on Lebanon's government to stop direct negotiations with Israel and reverse its March decision criminalizing the resistance.

stories.title: Australians will call ‘bullshit’ on green energy without clearer benefits, Rudd warns
stories.summary: Former Australian Prime Minister Kevin Rudd warned that public support for green energy policies could collapse without tangible benefits such as lower energy prices. He described US President Trump's cuts to green industry support as "unfortunate." Rudd made the comments after finishing his tenure as Australia's ambassador to the United States.

stories.title: Hong Kong police arrest 9 men in joint Asia-wide crackdown on child pornography
stories.summary: Hong Kong police arrested nine men as part of a coordinated seven-jurisdiction operation across Asia targeting child sexual exploitation material. The crackdown involved Singapore, Malaysia, Japan, South Korea, Thailand, and Brunei, resulting in more than 300 suspects detained. The operation targeted production, distribution, and possession of such material.

stories.title: Russian forces attempt to advance on all front sectors – Defense Forces
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces reported that Russian troops are attempting offensive operations across all front-line sectors, varying the intensity of their assaults along the front.

stories.title: Malaysia’s jailed ex-PM Najib withdraws appeal on house arrest, local media reports
stories.summary: Former Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak has withdrawn his appeal for house arrest, according to local media. Najib was sentenced to an additional 15 years in prison and fined $2.8 billion in December for abuse of power and money laundering linked to the 1MDB scandal.

stories.title: Iranian FM Arrives in St. Petersburg for Talks With Putin
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in St. Petersburg for talks with Russian President Putin, following diplomatic visits to Oman and Pakistan where he met officials mediating regional conflicts.

stories.title: Japan’s Takaichi faces women-led backlash over constitution reform push, arms build-up
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi faces a growing backlash from women protesters opposing her government's push to revise Japan's pacifist constitution and expand arms exports. Demonstrations outside the National Diet in Tokyo have grown from thousands in late February to tens of thousands. Many participants are new to political activism.

stories.title: Tens of thousands flood US cities in massive show of support for Israel
stories.summary: The Israeli-American Council organized 27 pro-Israel rallies across 21 communities in U.S. cities, held between April 23 and May 3. Tens of thousands of participants attended the events in a large-scale show of support for Israel.

stories.title: Territorial integrity is ‘red line’ for Europe, Finland warns after US Greenland threats
stories.summary: Finnish Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen declared that Europe's territorial integrity is a "red line" in Finland's relations with the United States and other powers. Her comments came in response to US threats regarding Greenland. She affirmed Finland's defense of the UN Charter, national sovereignty, and territorial integrity.

stories.title: UAE 'aggressively' lobbying US to designate Yemen's Islah as a terror group, sources say
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates has been aggressively lobbying Washington to designate Yemen's Islah party as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist group. The move could inflame tensions with Saudi Arabia, which has historically maintained ties with Islah.

stories.title: Somalia hunger crisis worsens as drought displaces more than 500,000 people
stories.summary: In Somalia, drought has displaced more than 500,000 people, worsening a hunger crisis as humanitarian funding decreases and displaced communities face starvation with diminishing international assistance.

stories.title: Beersheba college ordered to compensate educator fired over Oct. 7 social media posts
stories.summary: An Israeli court ordered Kaye College in Beersheba to compensate educator Dr. Warda Sada after finding the institution violated her academic freedoms by firing her over social media posts related to October 7. The college plans to appeal.

stories.title: Amsterdam becomes world's first capital to ban fossil fuel ads
stories.summary: Amsterdam became the first national capital to approve a legal ban on fossil fuel advertisements, including ads for flights, cruise ships, and petrol cars. Dutch activists are now pushing for the restrictions to be implemented at the national level as part of a growing global movement among cities to curb such advertising.

stories.title: Iran's Araghchi in Russia after Pakistani delivers message to US
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi arrived in Russia after Pakistan conveyed a message to the United States on Tehran's behalf. Iran submitted a new proposal pushing to reopen the Strait of Hormuz while postponing nuclear negotiations to a later stage.

stories.title: Massive frigate buy from Japan jolts Australian warship program
stories.summary: Australia is pursuing a major frigate acquisition from Japan, aiming to minimize local modifications to avoid delaying ship deliveries. The purchase represents a significant shift in Australia's warship procurement program.

stories.title: Oil prices jump as US-Iran talks stall
stories.summary: Oil prices surged nearly three percent as U.S.-Iran peace talks stalled and shipments through the Strait of Hormuz remained constrained. Brent crude rose to $108.36 per barrel, its highest level in three weeks, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate climbed to $96.85.

stories.title: Iran offers deal to US to reopen Strait of Hormuz, delay nuclear talks: Report
stories.summary: Iran has reportedly offered the United States a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and delay nuclear talks. The proposed plan calls for extending the ceasefire to allow both parties to work toward a permanent end to hostilities.

stories.title: Prison officer admits brutal assault on inmate after baby powder bingo game
stories.summary: A former Hong Kong prison officer, Tam Lik-chung, pleaded guilty to severely wounding an inmate at Pik Uk Prison in Sai Kung by thrusting a stick into the victim's rectum. An inmate, Ho Lik-wun, also pleaded guilty to helping restrain the victim. The assault occurred in December after a baby powder incident during a game.

stories.title: Polish influencer’s nine-day, non-stop live stream raises £50m for cancer charity
stories.summary: A 23-year-old Polish social media influencer known as Łatwogang raised more than £50 million for a children's cancer charity during a nine-day nonstop live stream from Warsaw. Celebrity guests including musician Chris Martin, tennis player Iga Świątek, and footballer Robert Lewandowski participated in the fundraiser.

stories.title: UK’s King Charles heads to Washington to help mend frayed ties with US
stories.summary: UK King Charles is traveling to Washington for a four-day visit aimed at strengthening US-UK relations. President Trump told the BBC the visit could help repair ties, though some observers characterize it primarily as a media event.

stories.title: U.S. State Department orders global warning about alleged AI thefts by DeepSeek, other Chinese firms
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department issued a global cable warning about alleged artificial intelligence theft by Chinese firms, including DeepSeek. The directive comes weeks before President Donald Trump is scheduled to visit Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing.

stories.title: Michael Jackson: 'Untouchable' icon, sexual predator or both?
stories.summary: Michael Jackson's biopic opened to strong box-office numbers despite ongoing sexual abuse allegations against the late pop star. Media outlets also covered conspiracy theories surrounding a shooting at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner.

stories.title: Iran FM in Russia for high-stakes war talks as tensions with US persist
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi traveled to St. Petersburg for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The visit is part of Tehran's intensified diplomatic efforts amid ongoing regional tensions and disputes with the United States.

stories.title: Gunman sought to kill Trump, cabinet at gala dinner
stories.summary: Investigators revealed that Cole Allen, 31, who attempted to storm a gala dinner attended by President Donald Trump, planned to assassinate the president and multiple senior officials. A note shared with his family before the attack indicated he intended to target officials ranked from highest to lowest.

stories.title: US says three killed in boat strike as campaign toll hits 185
stories.summary: The U.S. military said it struck a boat "engaged in narco-trafficking operations" in the Eastern Pacific Ocean, killing three people. The strike brings the total death toll from the U.S. anti-narcotics campaign to 185.

stories.title: Eleven arrested in coordinated op. targeting alleged protection racket in central Israel
stories.summary: Israeli police unit Lahav 433 arrested eleven suspects in central Israel as part of an operation targeting an alleged protection racket. Investigators set up a front construction company during the covert phase of the investigation to gather evidence.

stories.title: Finland detains 2 Russians who aided Ukrainians as deportation proceeds after asylum denials
stories.summary: Finnish authorities detained and are deporting Olga and Nikita Belov, a Russian mother and son who fled to Finland after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and had aided Ukrainians. Their asylum applications were denied.

stories.title: Israel, Hezbollah trade accusations over Lebanon truce violations
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon killed 14 people on Sunday, marking the deadliest day since a ceasefire in the Israel-Hezbollah conflict took effect over a week ago. Both sides exchanged accusations of violating the truce, with Prime Minister Netanyahu saying Israel was targeting Hezbollah and the group vowing to respond to violations.

stories.title: As some hijabs come off in Iran, restrictions still in place
stories.summary: Despite reduced enforcement of hijab rules in Iran, women can still face legal consequences for not wearing one. Authorities continue to summon women who appear in public without the mandatory head covering.

stories.title: Man with Iranian flag shirt charged in Brooklyn hate crime assaults on three Jews
stories.summary: New York police charged 41-year-old Andrze Wnuk with three hate crime assaults against Jewish individuals in Brooklyn. The suspect was reportedly wearing a shirt bearing an Iranian flag at the time of the attacks.

stories.title: How long can EU's 'Zionist Veto' block Israel's accountability?
stories.summary: Analysis of the EU–Israel Association Agreement examines European credibility on human rights accountability following events in Gaza. The article discusses how EU member-state dynamics have blocked measures aimed at holding Israel accountable.

stories.title: Caught between wars, US Afghan allies trapped in Qatar without safe exit
stories.summary: Afghan allies of the United States remain stranded at a defunct camp in Qatar, awaiting processing for potential resettlement in the U.S. The site has served as a holding facility for Afghans hoping to be relocated.

stories.title: Putin signs laws giving widows and widowers of fallen Russian soldiers free university enrollment and extending other war benefits
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin signed three laws on April 25 extending benefits to families of soldiers killed in the war, seriously wounded Rosgvardiya personnel, and workers returning from military service, including free university enrollment for widows and widowers.

stories.title: Iran’s foreign minister in Russia for talks
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister traveled to Russia for diplomatic talks. No further details on the agenda were immediately disclosed.

stories.title: Attack on Odesa: 13 people injured, residential and port infrastructure damaged, merchant ship hit
stories.summary: A massive Russian attack on Odesa damaged residential buildings, a hotel, vehicles, and port infrastructure, and struck a merchant ship. At least 13 people were injured, including two children.

stories.title: 'This keeps happening': US press gala shooting latest sign of rising political violence
stories.summary: A California man accused of storming a gala dinner attended by President Trump was set to appear in court Monday. The shooting represents at least the third attack or threat targeting Trump in three years, intensifying concerns about rising political violence in the United States.

stories.title: Colombia's ruling left set to extend time in power as Cepeda leads, poll shows
stories.summary: A poll released on Sunday shows Colombia's ruling left-wing coalition is poised to retain power, with presidential candidate Iván Cepeda leading at 44.3% support. Cepeda is expected to continue President Gustavo Petro's agenda against a divided right-wing opposition.

stories.title: Families of Indonesian helpers who died in Tai Po fire struggle to break news to kids
stories.summary: Families of Indonesian domestic helpers killed in a fire at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, Hong Kong, have struggled to inform victims' children of their deaths. A workers' rights advocate from the Association for the Rights of Industrial Accident Victims visited Indonesia to meet relatives of eight helpers who died. Families have also faced scammers targeting their compensation.

stories.title: Kommersant reports Syria plans to convert Russia’s Khmeimim air base into military training and humanitarian hub
stories.summary: Syria's interim president Ahmed al-Sharaa plans to convert Russia's Khmeimim air base into a military training and humanitarian hub, according to the Russian business daily Kommersant, citing a Syrian source.

stories.title: Iran Foreign Minister arrives in Russia as U.S. talks remain stalled
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi traveled to Moscow for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The visit comes as U.S.-Iran negotiations remain stalled, with both Russian and Iranian state media confirming the meeting.

stories.title: Buy airline tickets now, Spain urges as Iran war lifts oil prices
stories.summary: Spain's government urged consumers to purchase airline tickets immediately to avoid potential fare increases driven by rising oil prices. The advisory came as the ongoing Iran conflict continued to push global energy costs higher.

stories.summary: An analysis of South Africa's agricultural sector 32 years after apartheid notes significant advancements alongside ongoing challenges, with debate over whether the farming sector is under siege or making meaningful progress.

stories.summary: A Kenyan appeals court overturned a landmark ruling that had recognized access to abortion as a fundamental right. The decision could push more women toward unsafe procedures in a country where abortion is legal but widely stigmatized.

stories.summary: The injury toll from the overnight Russian attack on Odesa rose to 11 people, including two children.

stories.title: At least 42 killed in Chad after water well dispute escalates
stories.summary: At least 42 people were killed in Chad after a dispute over a water well between two families escalated into a cycle of reprisal attacks.

stories.summary: Hopes that Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi's visit to Pakistan would restart direct US-Iran talks did not materialize. President Trump cancelled the trip of US envoys to Islamabad but left the diplomatic door open, while Pakistani leaders continued mediation efforts.

stories.title: Russia attacks Odesa, claims Ukraine hit Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant
stories.summary: Russia launched attacks on the Ukrainian city of Odesa while accusing Ukraine of striking the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant. Russian-installed managers at the facility reported one worker was killed in the Ukrainian attack.

stories.title: Portugal's arms industry is taking off
stories.summary: Portugal has significantly expanded its domestic arms industry over the past five years, developing a surprisingly large independent defense manufacturing sector. Questions remain about how autonomous it can be given its alliance with the United States.

stories.summary: Analysis examines how Israel and the U.S. miscalculated on regime change in Iran. Critics argue that networks of think tank operatives and native informants, similar to those involved in the Iraq War, helped draw Washington into the conflict.

stories.title: King Charles' visit to US goes ahead despite Washington shooting

stories.summary: A Karachi court ordered the release of five women, including Baloch Yakjehti Committee activist Fozia Baloch, who were arrested for protesting outside the Karachi Press Club against the alleged enforced disappearance of Baloch's brother, Daad Shah. They had been charged under sedition laws.

stories.title: Russia blacked out Europe’s largest nuclear plant 15 times since occupying it in 2022
stories.summary: Russia's Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, Europe's largest, has experienced 15 blackouts since Russian forces occupied it in 2022. The most recent outage occurred on the 40th anniversary of the Chornobyl disaster, with state operator Energoatom reporting a 90-minute loss of external power.

stories.summary: North Korea opened a museum in Pyongyang commemorating its troops killed while fighting alongside Russian forces. The memorial reflects deepening military cooperation and strengthening ties between Pyongyang and Moscow.

stories.summary: The article analyzes the role of Pakistan's Roshan Digital Account (RDA) program beyond dollar inflows, noting that workers' remittances exceeded $38 billion in FY25 and now cover more than 100 percent of the country's trade deficit, serving as a critical external-sector stabilizer.

stories.summary: The death of Raja Liaquat Khan, 50, in Indian-held Kashmir prompted an emotional scene as his relatives in Azad Jammu and Kashmir watched his funeral from across the Line of Control, highlighting the enduring pain of divided Kashmiri families.

stories.title: Iran says will end Strait of Hormuz chokehold if US siege ends
stories.summary: Iran proposed ending its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for the lifting of the U.S. siege, without addressing its nuclear program. The offer represents a new diplomatic approach focused on reopening the vital waterway.

stories.summary: Pakistan faces significant fiscal challenges ahead of its next federal budget, with government debt rising by Rs1.99 trillion to Rs79.9 trillion between July 2025 and February 2026. stories.title: The war on Iran is eroding nuclear non-proliferation
stories.summary: U.S. and Israeli military operations against Iran, framed as efforts to prevent a nuclear weapons program, are reportedly undermining international confidence in the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty framework.

stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid announced they will run on a joint electoral list under a new party called Beyahad (Together), led by Bennett, in a bid to unseat incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in upcoming elections.

stories.summary: Chinese automakers are equipping car headlights with projection capabilities that can display movies, similar to drive-in theaters. The feature reflects the intense competition and rapid innovation in China's domestic automotive market.

stories.title: PA loyalists win big in Palestinian municipal polls
stories.summary: Loyalists of Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas won most seats in municipal elections held across the West Bank and, for the first time in nearly two decades, in Gaza's Deir al-Balah. Hamas boycotted the vote; turnout reached 56 percent in the West Bank but only 23 percent in Gaza.

stories.title: Remembering Raghu Rai: The photographer who showed India to itself
stories.summary: Renowned Indian photographer Raghu Rai has died. He was widely regarded as a visual historian who chronicled India's most defining and often painful moments throughout his career.

stories.title: Russian military loses another 810 soldiers and 26 artillery systems in war against Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine's military reported that Russia lost approximately 810 soldiers in a single 24-hour period, bringing estimated total Russian combat losses since February 2022 to around 1,326,460 personnel. Twenty-six Russian artillery systems were also destroyed.

stories.summary: Israeli defense firm Elbit Systems was awarded $200 million in defense contracts during the Iran war. CEO Bezhalel Machlis said the contracts underscore the company's technological leadership in air-launched weapon systems.

stories.title: Ambode comeback talk tests Tinubu’s grip on Lagos succession
stories.summary: Speculation about a political comeback by former Lagos governor Ambode is testing President Tinubu's control over succession in Lagos state's ruling APC party. Party elders appear to be coalescing behind deputy governor Obafemi Hamzat instead.

stories.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 59 amid diplomatic push to end conflict?
stories.summary: On day 59 of the Iran conflict, Tehran engaged regional partners in discussions on diplomatic solutions. U.S. President Trump stated that Iran could telephone if it wished to negotiate.

stories.title: Lebanon says Israel strikes kill 14 in deadliest day since truce
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported that Israeli strikes killed 14 people in southern Lebanon on Sunday, making it the deadliest day since the ceasefire took effect. At least 36 people have been killed by Israeli strikes since the truce began, according to an AFP tally.

stories.title: Trump opts for talks with Iran over the phone
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump indicated a preference for phone-based talks with Iran, praising Pakistan's role in facilitating dialogue. Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi stopped in Islamabad en route to Moscow, while the IRGC stated it has no plans to lift its Strait of Hormuz blockade.

stories.title: The Importance of the Battle of Savo Island
stories.summary: On the night of Aug. 9, 1942, an Allied fleet of 17 warships guarded the approaches to Guadalcanal. The fleet was newer, larger, and better equipped than the Japanese force bearing down on it. It had

stories.title: Hebrew University – Olim’s 1st Choice in Israel - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Hebrew University in Jerusalem promoted its support for new immigrants to Israel, highlighting scholarships and academic programs. The university announced a Campus Open Day scheduled for May 8.

stories.title: Iran said to offer US deal to reopen Hormuz, end war and put off nuclear talks
stories.summary: Iran reportedly offered the United States a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end hostilities while deferring nuclear negotiations. President Trump was expected to meet with his national security and foreign policy teams to discuss the offer as oil prices continued to rise.

stories.title: Odesa hit by massive drone attack, at least nine injured
stories.summary: Russian drones struck Odesa in a massive attack, damaging residential buildings, a hotel, and vehicles. At least nine people were injured in the assault on the Ukrainian port city.

stories.title: Jewish continuity needs you. Donate to Jewish higher education - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A sponsored appeal called for donations to Jewish higher education institutions, describing such contributions as tax-deductible investments in future community leaders.

stories.title: Pirates seize another vessel off Somali coast as threat level increased
stories.summary: The UK's maritime monitoring authority reported at least four suspected piracy incidents off the coast of Somalia in the past week, including the seizure of another vessel, prompting an increase in the regional threat level.

stories.title: Kim Jong Un opens memorial for N Korean soldiers killed in Ukraine war
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and Russian Defence Minister Andrey Belousov unveiled a memorial in Pyongyang honoring North Korean soldiers killed while fighting alongside Russian forces in the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Jewish continuity needs you. Donate to Jewish higher education - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: This is a sponsored advertisement promoting donations to Jewish higher education institutions, not a news article.

stories.title: Japan’s bathhouses struggle to stay afloat as oil prices spike, supply dwindles
stories.summary:
Customers of Ikesu Onsen, a traditional Japanese bathhouse in Tsushima in Aichi prefecture, have had to delay their daily dips due to the Iran war.
The sento, or public bathhouse, has been forced to p

stories.title: White House: US will not negotiate through the media
stories.summary: White House spokesperson Karoline Leavitt stated that the United States will not conduct negotiations with Iran through public media channels, emphasizing the sensitivity of diplomatic discussions and reiterating that Washington will not allow Iran to possess nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Video: Student shuts down Israeli soldier event at Rutgers University
stories.summary: A Jewish student at Rutgers University disrupted an event featuring an Israeli soldier, publicly condemning Israel's military operations in Gaza. The confrontation reflected growing campus opposition to hosting Israeli military figures.

stories.title: Araghchi: Pakistan played important role, US approach stalled progress
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi credited Pakistan with playing an important role in mediating talks between Tehran and Washington. He said the United States' approach had stalled progress despite earlier diplomatic advances.

stories.title: Activists accused of raiding Israeli weapons factory face trial in Germany
stories.summary: Five European nationals known as the "Ulm Five" are standing trial in Germany, accused of raiding a facility linked to Israeli defense company Elbit Systems. The defendants are charged with targeting the weapons-related site.

stories.title: Sirens sound in Galilee after drone infiltration from Lebanon
stories.summary: Air raid sirens were activated across parts of the Galilee in northern Israel, including Maalot-Tarshiha, after the Israeli military detected a suspected hostile drone entering from Lebanon. The incident is under investigation.

stories.title: Intercepted communication: Russian troops in Pokrovsk direction leaving wounded at positions
stories.summary: Ukrainian military intelligence intercepted communications indicating that Russian troops in the Pokrovsk direction are abandoning wounded soldiers at their positions rather than evacuating them.

stories.title: Netanyahu testimony, set to resume after monthslong break, canceled at last minute
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's scheduled testimony in his ongoing corruption trial was canceled at the last minute. His lawyer cited security concerns, preempting cross-examination after President Herzog reportedly rebuffed a pardon request.

stories.title: Israel destroys power and water systems in Christian town in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli forces bulldozed solar panels in Debel, a predominantly Maronite Christian town in southern Lebanon, cutting electricity and water supply. Roads, homes, and olive groves were also destroyed, leaving civilians without essential services.

stories.title: Chinese refiner Hengli denies Iran ties after US sanctions hit shares
stories.summary: Shares in Chinese refiner Hengli Petrochemical fell 10 percent after the US Treasury imposed sanctions over alleged Iranian oil purchases. Hengli denied ties to Iran, while China condemned the sanctions as illegal.

stories.title: North Korea, Russia boost anti-West ‘powerful bulwark’ as Ukraine war drags on
stories.summary: North Korea and Russia are deepening their military alliance amid the ongoing Ukraine war. A memorial museum honoring North Korean soldiers was unveiled in Pyongyang on Sunday. Observers say the partnership reflects converging needs, including Russia's demand for manpower and materiel.

stories.title: Global military spending surges on insecurity: Report
stories.summary: Global military spending surged due to rising insecurity, with the United States, China, and Russia spending a combined $1.48 trillion, accounting for just over half of the worldwide total, according to a new report.

stories.title: Everest climbers left hanging after giant ice chunk blocks path to summit
stories.summary: A large serac — a block of glacial ice — above the Khumbu Icefall has blocked the climbing route to Mount Everest's summit for nearly two weeks. Nepalese rope-fixing teams known as "icefall doctors" have been unable to complete preparations for the spring climbing season, risking significant delays.

stories.title: China old folk custom sacrificed young women to become ‘Cave God’ brides who starved to death
stories.summary: An ancient folk custom known as Luo Hua Dong Nv from Miao communities in Xiangxi, western Hunan province, China, involved sending unmarried girls to live in caves as brides of a legendary "Cave God," where they fasted to death. The practice no longer exists, and its origins remain unclear.

stories.title: The kippah controversy: when Israel's overreach becomes a global issue - editorial
stories.summary: Israeli police confiscated a kippah bearing Palestinian flags in the city of Modi'in, sparking controversy over police overreach and limits on free expression in Israel.

stories.title: IDF probe: Infiltrating Hamas terrorists devastated Kibbutz Holit on October 7
stories.summary: An IDF investigation into the October 7 Hamas attack on Kibbutz Holit found that infiltrating terrorists killed 13 civilians and took 9 hostages. The probe detailed the devastating impact on the border community.

stories.title: Kim reaffirms North Korean support for Russia's 'sacred' Ukraine war
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un reaffirmed support for Russia's invasion of Ukraine and vowed to help Moscow achieve victory in its "sacred war", state media reported Monday, after Russian Defence Min

stories.title: Iran's Araghchi visits Russia as talks with US on hold
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi visited Russia to continue diplomatic efforts amid the war against Iran, following the cancellation of planned US-Iran talks that were to be held in Pakistan.

stories.title: Video: Drone narrowly misses Israeli soldiers and helicopter in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli soldiers in southern Lebanon were targeted by drone strikes while evacuating wounded troops, with video showing an explosion landing meters from the group. A helicopter was forced to depart quickly as additional drones approached the area.

stories.title: Four Israeli troops injured at military base in southern Israel
stories.summary: Four Israeli soldiers were injured in an operational accident at a military base in southern Israel. One was seriously wounded and another moderately injured, while two sustained light injuries. The military released no further details.

stories.title: Taiwan court hands down jail terms in TSMC trade secrets case
stories.summary: A Taiwan court sentenced a former Tokyo Electron employee to 10 years in prison for stealing TSMC trade secrets. Four other defendants received sentences ranging from 10 months to six years.

stories.title: Record bear sightings in Japan cause alarm as hibernation ends
stories.summary: Bear sightings across northeastern Japan are outpacing 2025's record levels as animals emerge from hibernation. A woman's body was found in Iwate prefecture, shortly after a police officer was injured in a nearby bear attack. Authorities have urged caution ahead of the Golden Week holidays.

stories.title: Malaysian state in crisis after Umno pulls support for chief minister in royal row
stories.summary: Malaysia's Negeri Sembilan state government faces collapse after the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO) withdrew support for the chief minister. The crisis highlights growing tensions within Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim's coalition government ahead of national elections due within two years.

stories.title: 'Green coal' offers Chad a cleaner and cheaper alternative to coal and wood
stories.summary: Consumers in Chad are increasingly adopting 'green coal' as a cheaper and cleaner alternative to traditional wood and coal for fuel.

stories.title: Somalia: Somaliland President Condemns White House Dinner Shooting, Backs Trump
stories.summary: Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdillahi Irro condemned a shooting at the White House Correspondents' Dinner, expressing solidarity with the United States and voicing support for former President Donald Trump.

stories.title: Kenya: Batuk Soldiers Join Charity Run to Support Girls' Menstrual Hygiene in Laikipia
stories.summary: Soldiers from the British Army Training Unit Kenya (BATUK) participated in a 10-kilometre charity run in Laikipia County alongside volunteers to raise awareness about menstrual hygiene and support vulnerable girls and women.

stories.title: Kenya: Police Nab Four Drug Peddlers in Major Crackdown in Molo
stories.summary: Police in Nakuru County, Kenya, arrested four suspected drug peddlers during a major security operation targeting illicit brew and narcotics in Molo town.

stories.title: Kenya: Garissa Female Aspirant Arrested Over Incitement Linked to Deadly Tseikuru Attack
stories.summary: A female political aspirant from Garissa County, Kenya, was arrested on allegations of incitement to violence following a deadly attack in Tseikuru, Kitui County, that killed seven people.

stories.title: West Africa: The Enduring Resilience of Children of the Central Sahel in the Midst of Crisis
stories.summary: A UNICEF representative completed a 14-day visit to the Central Sahel region, highlighting the resilience of children amid ongoing insecurity, climate shocks, and socio-economic crises affecting Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger.

stories.title: Nigeria: 10 Villagers Die As Katsina Community Foils Bandit Attack
stories.summary: Residents of Gurbi community in Kankara local government area of Katsina State, Nigeria, repelled an armed bandit attack, but at least 10 people were killed in a nearby settlement during the incident.

stories.title: Nigeria: Army Orders Probe As NYSC Member Killed in Cross Fire With Armed Robers in Abuja
stories.summary: Nigeria's Guards Brigade has ordered an investigation into the death of National Youth Service Corps member Abdulsamad Jamiu, who was killed in crossfire during a confrontation with armed robbers in the Dei Dei area of Abuja.

stories.title: Focusing on the manufacturing sector
stories.summary: The article examines Pakistan's manufacturing sector, noting increased domestic petroleum production during the first eight months of fiscal year 2026 but warning that fragile external demand and high costs continue to threaten investment and export-oriented growth.

stories.title: CORPORATE WINDOW: Industry prepares budget wishlist
stories.summary: As Pakistan prepares its national budget amid double-digit inflation, corporate sectors are lobbying policymakers with their policy wish lists while ordinary citizens remain skeptical about the prospect of economic relief.

stories.title: AJK laws tweaked  to facilitate refugee voting
stories.summary: The Azad Jammu and Kashmir government promulgated an electoral amendment ordinance in 2026 to facilitate voting by post-1989 refugees from Indian-held Kashmir who have relocated between camps, while also extending political party restrictions in line with Pakistani law.

stories.title: Araghchi arrives in Russia for talks with Putin on war, diplomacy
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in St. Petersburg for talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin. He said the visit focuses on consultations between Tehran and Moscow regarding regional developments and the ongoing war.

stories.title: Mozambique: Humanitarian Aid Under Pressure in Cabo Delgado
