stories.summary: Mozambique's National Disaster Management Institute (INGD) has warned that humanitarian aid in Cabo Delgado province is under severe pressure from the combined effects of terrorist attacks and climate-related disasters affecting the same communities.

stories.title: Kenya: Gachagua Vows Fresh Court Battle Over Impeachment, Claims Process Was Illegal
stories.summary: Former Kenyan Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua, now leader of the Democracy for the Citizens Party, has announced he will file a new court challenge against his impeachment, alleging the process was unconstitutional and unlawful.

stories.title: Kenya: Ruto Urges National Unity in Fight Against Rising Youth Drug and Alcohol Crisis
stories.summary: Kenyan President William Ruto has pledged a renewed national campaign against drug and alcohol abuse, describing rising substance use among youth as a growing threat to the country's future.

stories.title: Kenya: Ruto Blasts Mt Kenya 'Political Cartels' Over 2027 Succession Politics During Murang'a Tour
stories.summary: During a tour of Murang'a, Kenyan President William Ruto criticized political figures he accused of acting as gatekeepers of Central Kenya's political direction ahead of the 2027 general election, vowing not to be controlled by regional power brokers.

stories.title: Uganda’s Somalia bill: Who pays the ‘security dividend’?
stories.summary: Uganda is questioning why countries and entities profiting from stability in Somalia, including Turkey which is expanding into Somalia's energy sector, are not contributing to the security costs that Kampala bears through its troop deployments.

stories.title: Nigeria: FCT Teachers Suspend Strike
stories.summary: The Nigeria Union of Teachers' Federal Capital Territory wing suspended its seven-day strike and directed public primary and secondary school teachers to resume classes.

stories.title: Nigeria: Govt Approves N10bn Housing Loan Scheme for Civil Servants
stories.summary: Nigeria's federal government has approved a 10-billion-naira housing loan scheme aimed at bridging the national housing deficit and providing affordable housing for low- and middle-income civil servants.

stories.title: Nigeria: Flights Delayed, Rescheduled As Jet Fuel Shortage Deepens
stories.summary: Airlines across Nigeria are experiencing widespread flight delays and rescheduling due to a deepening shortage of Jet A1 aviation fuel, disrupting operations at major airports nationwide.

stories.title: Nigeria: The Trust Deficit - Cyber Risk As a Structural Threat to Nigeria's Digital Economy
stories.summary: Nigeria faces growing cybersecurity incidents that are eroding public trust in its digital economy, posing a structural threat to the country's ongoing digital transformation efforts.

stories.title: Nigeria: NDLEA Intercepts 'Terror Drug' Captagon in Kwara, Arrests Suspects Nationwide in Major Anti-Narcotics Sweep
stories.summary: Nigeria's National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) intercepted a consignment of the stimulant Captagon in Kwara State and carried out a nationwide crackdown resulting in multiple arrests, major drug seizures, and recovery of explosive materials.

stories.title: Rwanda: What AfCFTA Means for Entrepreneurs Looking to Grow Beyond Borders
stories.summary: Despite Rwanda having signed and ratified the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) agreement in 2018, awareness among local entrepreneurs remains limited, with some trade professionals only learning about the framework in 2025.

stories.title: Rwanda: Ruhango - 35 Genocide Victims Given Decent Burial
stories.summary: The remains of 35 victims of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi were given a dignified burial on April 26 at the Kinazi Genocide Memorial Site in Ruhango District, Rwanda.

stories.title: Lebanon reports Israeli strikes kill 14 in deadliest day since truce
stories.summary: Lebanon reported 14 people killed in Israeli strikes, marking the deadliest day since the ceasefire agreement took effect. Hezbollah stated it would not halt attacks on Israeli troops as long as Israel continued what it described as ceasefire violations.

stories.title: Iran gives US proposal for reopening Strait of Hormuz, ending war - Axios
stories.summary: Axios reported that Iran submitted a proposal to the United States for reopening the Strait of Hormuz and ending the war. President Donald Trump is expected to hold a situation room meeting with his top national security and foreign policy team to discuss the matter.

stories.title: From Australia to Vietnam, the Iran war is fuelling demand for EVs
stories.summary: Electric vehicle sales are rising across markets from Australia to Vietnam as the Iran war drives up petrol and diesel costs, making EVs more economically attractive to consumers.

stories.title: China-Japan tensions a boon to Hong Kong tourism for ‘golden week’, expert says
stories.summary: Sino-Japanese tensions and an appreciating yuan are redirecting mainland Chinese tourists to Hong Kong ahead of the Labour Day "golden week" holiday. Hotel prices in the city have risen by up to 8 percent, according to an industry representative.

stories.title: Indonesian migrant smugglers target Malaysia entry via Singapore, Thailand
stories.summary: Malaysian immigration authorities dismantled an Indonesian migrant-smuggling syndicate that rerouted people through Singapore and southern Thailand instead of traditional sea crossings. A pre-dawn raid at two Kuala Lumpur transport terminals led to 11 arrests, including a suspected transporter, and the seizure of a vehicle used to move migrants.

stories.title: DJI-Insta360 rivalry, nuclear hint for China’s next carrier: 5 weekend reads you missed
stories.summary: A weekend roundup highlights several developments across Asia, including intensifying rivalry between Chinese drone makers DJI and Insta360, speculation that China's next aircraft carrier may be nuclear-powered, a fatal Japanese Type 10 tank blast, and the death of Reverend Derek Li in Hong Kong.

stories.title: President: Some Chernobyl defenders still held in Russian captivity
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that some defenders of the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant, including National Guard soldiers, remain in Russian captivity. The personnel were captured during Russia's seizure of the site early in its invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran loads 4.6 million barrels despite US blockade, tracker says
stories.summary: Maritime analytics firm TankerTrackers reported that Iran loaded approximately 4.6 million barrels of crude oil at export terminals despite an active US naval blockade. The assessment was based on satellite imagery tracking tanker movements and port operations.

stories.title: Axios: Tehran proposal via Pakistan aims to end blockade, reopen Hormuz
stories.summary: Axios reported that Iran submitted a proposal through Pakistani mediators offering to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end hostilities with the United States, while postponing nuclear negotiations to a later stage.

stories.title: Displaced Lebanese flee again as strikes hit evacuation route
stories.summary: Thousands of displaced civilians in southern Lebanon who had returned home under a ceasefire were forced to flee again after fresh Israeli evacuation orders. A missile struck a roadside coffee stand in the Tyre District during the evacuation, killing at least one person.

stories.title: Magnitude 6.1 earthquake strikes in northern Japan
stories.summary: A magnitude 6.1 earthquake struck 18 kilometers west of the town of Sarabetsu in Hokkaido, northern Japan, at a depth of 81 kilometers, according to the U.S. Geological Survey.

stories.title: Pro-Palestine activists face trial for attack on Israeli arms factory in Germany
stories.summary: Five pro-Palestinian activists from Britain, Ireland, Germany, and Spain face trial in Germany for an alleged break-in at an Elbit Systems arms facility in Ulm, Baden-Württemberg, on September 8. The activists have been held in pre-trial detention in separate prisons since their arrest, with families alleging extreme conditions.

stories.title: Deadly Israeli attacks worsen Gaza’s water shortage crisis
stories.summary: Israeli forces in Gaza killed a water engineer and two water transport drivers over four days in mid-April, worsening severe clean water shortages. Israeli restrictions on hygiene products entering Gaza have driven up prices, compounding the spread of preventable diseases among displaced populations.

stories.title: King Charles visits Trump: what are the potential pitfalls for the monarch?
stories.summary: King Charles III begins a four-day state visit to the United States on Monday, navigating diplomatic tensions over the Iran conflict and the aftermath of a shooting at the White House correspondents' dinner. The visit aims to reaffirm U.S.-UK bilateral ties on the 250th anniversary of American independence.

stories.title: People in UK spend fewer years in good health than a decade ago, study finds
stories.summary: A Health Foundation study found that people in the United Kingdom are spending fewer years in good health than a decade ago. The decline in healthy life expectancy contrasts sharply with improvements in most other wealthy nations, prompting warnings that Britain's population health is deteriorating.

stories.title: China unveils ultra-cheap ‘all-iron flow battery’ for renewable energy storage
stories.summary: Chinese scientists at the Institute of Metal Research under the Chinese Academy of Sciences have developed an "all-iron flow battery" that could drastically cut renewable energy storage costs. Iron costs over 80 times less than lithium as a raw material, potentially addressing a major bottleneck in the global energy transition.

stories.title: As some hijabs come off in Iran and enforcement eases, locals fear it’s temporary
stories.summary: Some women in Iran have stopped wearing hijabs as enforcement has eased, but residents in Tehran fear the relaxation is temporary. Locals believe authorities are distracted by the US-Israeli war and may resume crackdowns later.

stories.title: Netanyahu’s biggest rivals join forces for Israel’s coming election
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid announced they are merging their parties — Bennett 2026 and There is a Future — to challenge Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition in an expected election later this year.

stories.title: McDonald’s to open on Melbourne street once dubbed ‘world’s coolest’ after winning legal challenge
stories.summary: Melbourne's Victorian civil and administrative tribunal upheld McDonald's application to open a 24/7 takeaway outlet on Smith Street in the Darebin council area, previously dubbed the "world's coolest" street. The tribunal ruled the fast food chain could not be denied solely because it didn't suit the location's character.

stories.title: Men accused of raping cellmates mistakenly allowed to stay in shared cells by Queensland prison staff
stories.summary: A Queensland ombudsman report found that corrections staff at Brisbane Correctional Centre violated strict protocols by allowing men charged with alleged prison rapes to remain in shared cells. Staff mistakenly believed the sexual assault cases were "closed" and the accused posed no risk.

stories.title: Ukraine’s MFA condemns shooting during White House Correspondents Dinner
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha condemned a shooting that occurred during the White House Correspondents' Dinner in Washington. Sybiha stated that such violence has no justification.

stories.title: Russian lawmaker says US ‘unprepared’ for Iran war
stories.summary: Senior Russian lawmaker Alexey Pushkov told TASS that the United States was unprepared for war with Iran, arguing Washington relied on a misguided belief that military force could quickly achieve its objectives. He said Iran had extensively prepared its missile infrastructure.

stories.title: Cross-border fire continues in Lebanon despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Hezbollah carried out drone and rocket attacks against Israeli troops in southern Lebanon and across the border despite an extended ceasefire. The group said Israeli military operations during the truce, including airstrikes and demolitions, would be met with resistance.

stories.title: Brent crude holds above $107 as tensions persist
stories.summary: Brent crude climbed above $107 per barrel as hopes for renewed US-Iran diplomatic talks faded. The price gains reflect ongoing supply disruption concerns linked to tensions around the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: US strike kills three on alleged narco boat as campaign death toll hits 185
stories.summary: The U.S. military struck a boat in the Eastern Pacific Ocean it claimed was involved in narco-trafficking, killing three people. The strike brings the campaign's total death toll to at least 185, according to an AFP tally, following dozens of similar attacks in recent months.

stories.title: Window blocking ‘inappropriate’ but outside building authority’s remit, Tai Po probe told
stories.summary: An independent committee investigating the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire in Hong Kong's Tai Po district heard that window-blocking was deemed "inappropriate" but fell outside the Buildings Department's authority. Four witnesses from the Buildings Department and Home Affairs Department were scheduled to testify on Monday.

stories.title: China warns EU over ‘Made in Europe’ plan, vows countermeasures
stories.summary: China criticized the European Union's proposed "Made in Europe" rules, which would require companies seeking public funds in sectors such as cars, green technology, and steel to meet local content thresholds. Beijing warned it would take countermeasures if the measures are adopted.

stories.title: Hungary's incoming PM says Orbán-linked oligarchs are moving funds to Uruguay and other destinations
stories.summary: Hungary's incoming prime minister Péter Magyar alleged that oligarchs linked to outgoing leader Viktor Orbán are transferring tens of billions of forints to Uruguay, the UAE, the US, and other countries. Magyar described it as a coordinated effort to move capital abroad ahead of the government transition scheduled for May 9.

stories.title: Kibbutz Holit was left to fight Hamas alone for hours on October 7 — IDF probe
stories.summary: An IDF investigation found that 60 Hamas terrorists attacked Kibbutz Holit on October 7, killing 16 people and abducting 9 to Gaza. Military backup arrived only in the afternoon after troops were diverted to fight elsewhere.

stories.title: Iran minister heads to Russia as Middle East peace talks remain stalled
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister traveled to Russia amid stalled Middle East peace negotiations. Iran reportedly sent written messages to the United States through Pakistan acting as a mediator, indicating that indirect diplomatic efforts were continuing.

stories.title: Israel restores some restrictions in north amid Hezbollah fire, nixes major pilgrimage
stories.summary: Israel's Home Front Command reimposed restrictions in northern border towns, capping gatherings at 1,500 people amid renewed Hezbollah fire from Lebanon. Prime Minister Netanyahu ordered the Lag B'Omer pilgrimage at Meron to be held in a symbolic fashion only.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Putin receives Iran’s foreign minister amid stalled US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Moscow on Monday amid stalled U.S.-Iran negotiations. Moscow and Tehran have deepened their relationship in recent years, with both nations subject to heavy Western sanctions.

stories.title: Satellite images show scale of Israeli destruction of south Lebanon towns
stories.summary: Satellite imagery reveals extensive destruction caused by the Israeli military in towns across southern Lebanon, showing widespread damage to civilian infrastructure.

stories.title: Police come under fire while evacuating civilians in Dnipropetrovsk region
stories.summary: Police officers in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region came under Russian fire while traveling to the settlement of Pokrovske to evacuate civilians. The incident occurred during ongoing Russian attacks targeting the region.

stories.title: US turns back 38 ships as Iran port blockade continues
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command said its forces have turned back 38 commercial vessels as part of an ongoing blockade of Iranian ports, preventing ships from entering or leaving Iranian waters. Centcom stated it is continuing to enforce maritime restrictions by directing ships to change course.

stories.title: Islamabad signals progress toward broader regional agreement
stories.summary: Officials in Islamabad indicated that a preliminary framework for U.S.-Iran negotiations may be taking shape, with Pakistan serving as mediator. Gulf countries are also seeking inclusion in any broader regional agreement. Pakistan remains hopeful of convening a second round of talks.

stories.title: Father and four children escaped blaze that killed two others at home in Blue Mountains foothills
stories.summary: Two bodies, believed to be children, were found inside a home destroyed by fire in Bowen Mountain in the Blue Mountains foothills of New South Wales. A father and four other children escaped the blaze and were taken to hospital.

stories.title: Russian envoy urges Washington to drop ‘blackmail’ tactics
stories.summary: Russia's envoy to international organizations in Vienna, Mikhail Ulyanov, called on the United States to abandon what he described as ultimatums and blackmail in its negotiations with Iran. He argued on X that Washington's approach of threatening military force or tighter sanctions is ineffective with Tehran.

stories.title: Oil prices rise amid stalled US-Iran peace talks
stories.summary: Brent crude oil prices rose more than 2 percent after the United States and Iran failed to hold a second round of negotiations in Pakistan, stalling diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: Chinese EVs make inroads in South Korea, one of world’s most competitive auto markets
stories.summary: Chinese-manufactured electric vehicles now account for one in three new EV registrations in South Korea, driven largely by Tesla's Shanghai-built models. Analysts said higher fuel prices linked to the U.S.-Israeli war in Iran and looser market restrictions support further expansion, though tightening subsidies could slow growth.

stories.title: ​Turning point: On the U.S. and India’s independent foreign policy
stories.summary: An analysis examined how U.S. policies are constraining India's ability to maintain an independent foreign policy. The piece framed the dynamic as a turning point in the bilateral relationship.

stories.title: Iran said to offer US deal to reopen Hormuz and end war, delay talks on nuclear program
stories.summary: Iran reportedly offered the United States a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the war while delaying discussions on its nuclear program. Separately, Israel reimposed gathering restrictions in the north amid Hezbollah attacks, and Prime Minister Netanyahu canceled mass Lag B'Omer festivities on Mount Meron.

stories.title: Lebanon reports bloodiest day since ceasefire as Israel targets Hezbollah
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported that Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon killed 14 people on Sunday, the deadliest day since the Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire began. Israel and Hezbollah exchanged accusations of truce violations, with Prime Minister Netanyahu saying the military was targeting Hezbollah and the group vowing continued responses.

stories.title: Trump says China ‘could help more’ on Iran conflict
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said China could play a larger role in addressing the conflict with Iran, while noting he was not overly disappointed with Beijing's current stance. Trump is scheduled to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing on May 14, where the issue is expected to be discussed.

stories.title: Araghchi set to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is set to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg, according to Iran's state news agency IRNA. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov is also expected to join discussions focused on the status of negotiations to end the war.

stories.title: North Korea’s Kim vows continued support for Russia at memorial for fallen troops
stories.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un pledged continued support for Russia's policies during a meeting with Russian Defence Minister Andrei Belousov. The Russian delegation attended a ceremony in North Korea for a memorial honoring North Korean soldiers killed fighting in Russia's Kursk region.

stories.title: Iran's Araghchi visits Pakistan for 2nd time in two days; envoy says trip undertaken to discuss regional developments
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi visited Pakistan twice in two days as part of a tri-nation tour that also included Oman, before heading to Moscow. The visits occurred amid Pakistani-led diplomatic efforts to facilitate talks between Tehran and Washington over the conflict triggered by US-Israeli strikes on Iran beginning February 28.

stories.title: Netanyahu meets Christians serving in IDF amid controversy over treatment of Lebanese Christians
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu met with Christian soldiers serving in the IDF amid controversy over Israel's treatment of Lebanese Christians. Netanyahu praised the Christian service members, saying they fill important positions across the military.

stories.title: King Charles III begins US visit despite press gala shooting, transatlantic tensions
stories.summary: Britain's King Charles III and Queen Camilla began a four-day visit to the United States on Monday to honour historic ties between the two countries as the US marks its 250th anniversary. The trip wil

stories.title: British royals begin four-day US visit despite shooting
stories.summary: King Charles III began a four-day state visit to the United States on Monday despite a shooting two days earlier at a dinner attended by his host, President Donald Trump. The visit proceeds amid transatlantic tensions over the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it targeted troops, tank with drones and missile
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced it launched a series of attacks on Israeli forces in southern Lebanon using drones and missiles. The group said it struck an artillery position in Biyyada, soldier gatherings in Taybeh, and a Merkava tank near Kfar Kila.

stories.title: Syrian court begins proceedings against Assad and allies
stories.summary: A Syrian court opened proceedings against ousted president Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher al-Assad, both tried in absentia after fleeing the country. A former security official and relative of the Assads, identified as Atif Najib, appeared in the courtroom in handcuffs.

stories.title: Hindu temple caretaker found dead in Bangladesh, minority group demands strong action
stories.summary: The body of a Hindu temple caretaker named Nayan was found in Cox's Bazar, Bangladesh, three days after he went missing. The Bangladesh Puja Celebration Council's local general secretary Jony Dhar indicated the death was a murder and called for strong action by authorities.

stories.title: What Is Chinlon, and Why Is It Important to Myanmar’s Culture
stories.summary: Chinlon is a traditional Myanmar sport that blends athletic skill, performance, and cultural expression into a continuous flowing motion emphasizing balance and control. The activity, which does not rely on competitive scoring, has been a significant part of Myanmar's cultural identity across multiple generations.

stories.title: UKMTO flags ongoing threat to shipping in Gulf
stories.summary: The UK Maritime Trade Operations reported no incidents in the Strait of Hormuz during the latest reporting period ending April 26. However, the agency warned that the broader security environment across the Gulf and the Gulf of Oman remains volatile due to ongoing military activity.

stories.title: Oil jumps as Iran-US talks stall, Hormuz flows constrained
stories.summary: Oil prices rose sharply amid stalled U.S.-Iran negotiations and constrained transit through the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude climbed to approximately $107.55 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate reached around $96.42. Analysts cited reduced Gulf shipments and diplomatic uncertainty as drivers of energy market pressure.

stories.title: China launches war on Alzheimer’s that may affect 10% of population by 2050
stories.summary: China has launched a national campaign to combat Alzheimer's disease, mobilizing scientific institutions, biotech firms, and experts to develop new treatments. Projections suggest the disease could affect nearly 10 percent of China's population by 2050, posing a significant public health and economic challenge.

stories.title: China city dwellers adopt chickens as pets, treating them like babies, walking them in prams
stories.summary: Residents of major Chinese cities are increasingly keeping chickens as household pets, with social media posts about pet chickens accumulating over 3.1 billion views. The trend is reshaping perceptions of pet culture in urban China, even in regions like Guangdong province traditionally known for poultry consumption.

stories.title: Traffic restrictions around Islamabad's Red Zone, Serena Hotel lifted: Ishaq Dar
stories.summary: Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar announced that traffic restrictions around Islamabad's Red Zone and the Serena Hotel have been lifted. The restrictions had been imposed in anticipation of US-Iran talks that were subsequently cancelled. Dar thanked residents of Islamabad and Rawalpindi for their patience.

stories.title: Araghchi says neighbours ‘priority’ after Oman talks
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said neighboring countries remain a priority following talks in Oman on bilateral relations and regional developments. He emphasized discussions on ensuring safe transit through the Strait of Hormuz for the benefit of all littoral states.

stories.title: Indian national arrested in Nepal for possessing prescription drug in large quantity
stories.summary: Nepalese authorities arrested Indian national Mohmad Sahanewajak, 29, from Bihar, in Itahari Sub-metropolitan city in Sunsari district. He was found in possession of 50,000 capsules of Tramadol and 9,520 capsules of Dicyclomine, both prescription drugs held in large quantities.

stories.title: Belarus plans to introduce new financial restrictions for citizens – CCD
stories.summary: Belarus is planning to introduce new financial restrictions for citizens, including limits on the number of payment cards individuals can hold and tighter rules for blocking bank accounts, according to reporting by the CCD.

stories.title: Israel court orders gov’t to penalise ultra-Orthodox who refuse draft
stories.summary: An Israeli court has ordered the government to impose penalties on ultra-Orthodox men who refuse military conscription. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had sought to delay legislation on drafting ultra-Orthodox citizens.

stories.title: Trump says U.S., Iranian officials can talk by phone
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated that US and Iranian officials could conduct negotiations by phone rather than in person. In separate remarks, Trump expressed strong disappointment with NATO and suggested the United States might consider leaving the military alliance.

stories.title: ESF reserves reach HK$3.75 billion, even as government subsidies shrink
stories.summary: Hong Kong's English Schools Foundation (ESF) has seen its reserves more than triple over the past decade, reaching HK$3.75 billion (US$480.8 million), despite declining government subsidies. The organization noted in its 2024-25 annual report that it expects increased competition for students and plans to modernize its marketing efforts.

stories.title: Wagering on a plea deal for Netanyahu, Herzog takes a risky bet on his pareve approach
stories.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog is pursuing a possible plea deal for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, wagering on his consensus-building approach to resolve the long-running criminal trial. Observers note the effort could either defuse the issue or damage public confidence in the presidency if it fails.

stories.title: Lebanon health ministry says Israeli strikes kill 14 in deadliest day since ceasefire began
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported that Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed 14 people on Sunday, including two women and two children, making it the deadliest day since the Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire began over a week ago. Thirty-seven others were wounded, and Israel reported one soldier killed.

stories.title: Magnitude 6.2 quake strikes Japan’s Hokkaido, JMA warns of more to come
stories.summary: A magnitude 6.2 earthquake struck southern Hokkaido, Japan, at 5:23 a.m. local time on Monday at a depth of 83 kilometers. The Japan Meteorological Agency revised the magnitude upward from an initial estimate of 6.1. No tsunami alert was issued.

stories.title: 'Great respect' for Pakistan and they will stay involved, but we are going to do it by phone: Trump on Iran talks
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said Iran talks would be conducted remotely by phone rather than in-person meetings. He praised Pakistan's mediatory role between Washington and Tehran, saying Islamabad would remain involved in the diplomatic process.

stories.title: Trump says he speaks with Putin and Zelensky: Fox News
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump told Fox News he has been in communication with both Putin and Zelenskyy, expressing optimism about resolving the Russia-Ukraine conflict.

stories.title: Iran war live: Araghchi to meet Putin; Trump says Tehran can call for talks
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi traveled to Russia for diplomatic meetings, while U.S. President Donald Trump stated that Iranian leaders could contact him by phone if they wished to initiate talks.

stories.title: Video: Israeli ‘ceasefire’ violations on the rise in Gaza
stories.summary: Al Jazeera reported that Israel has violated the Gaza ceasefire more than 2,400 times since it took effect. Correspondent Hala Al Shami detailed the rising number of violations in a video report.

stories.title: WATCH: IDF helicopter evacuates wounded soldiers amid heavy fire, drone impacts meters away
stories.summary: Video footage showed an Israeli Air Force helicopter evacuating wounded soldiers under heavy fire, with a drone impacting just meters from the aircraft. The helicopter departed the scene within seconds after detecting additional drones launched into the area.

stories.title: Home Front Command tightens security guidelines in northern Israel as Hezbollah tensions increase
stories.summary: Israel's Home Front Command issued tightened security guidelines for northern Israel, limiting gatherings in communities along the confrontation line with Lebanon to no more than 1,500 people. The restrictions took effect Sunday evening amid increased Hezbollah tensions.

stories.title: Sumy region under drone attack: Infrastructure hit, power outages reported
stories.summary: Russia launched drone attacks on Ukraine's Sumy region, striking several communities and damaging infrastructure. The attacks caused power outages and injuries were reported across the affected areas.

stories.title: Adalah petitions Israel’s Supreme Court to release bodies of Palestinian citizens of Israel
stories.summary: The legal advocacy group Adalah filed a petition with Israel's Supreme Court demanding the release of the bodies of six Palestinian citizens of Israel that authorities have withheld. Adalah called the policy of withholding hundreds of Palestinian bodies as bargaining chips inhumane.

stories.title: Pakistan lifts Islamabad security lockdown as talks stall
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar announced the lifting of a security lockdown around a high-security zone in Islamabad that had been in place for over a week. The restrictions were imposed amid hopes of hosting a second round of U.S.-Iran talks, but Dar's remarks suggest no immediate plans for further direct negotiations.

stories.title: Trump tells Fox News Iran can call US if it wants to negotiate
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated that Iran is welcome to contact the United States if it wishes to negotiate, saying 'they can come to us, or they can call us.'

stories.title: Peru's Fujimori, leftist Sanchez deadlocked in presidential runoff poll
stories.summary: A new poll shows right-wing candidate Keiko Fujimori and leftist Roberto Sanchez locked in a virtual tie in Peru's presidential runoff. The result remains uncertain as vote counting continues amid allegations of fraud.

stories.title: Israel kills three in Gaza attacks, civil defence says
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed at least three people in attacks on Gaza, according to the territory's civil defense. Gaza's health ministry reported that at least 811 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces since the ceasefire began.

stories.title: Nuclear energy to remain backbone of Ukraine’s power generation – Shmyhal
stories.summary: Ukraine's updated energy strategy through 2050 envisions nuclear power remaining the backbone of its electricity generation, with at least half of production coming from nuclear plants, according to Prime Minister Shmyhal.

stories.title: Taiwan will not 'bow its head': FM hits out at China during visit to Eswatini
stories.summary: Taiwan's foreign minister, during a visit to Eswatini, declared that Taiwan would not yield to pressure from China. He stated that no blockade could weaken Taiwan's resolve to maintain its dignity and international engagement.

stories.title: Iran loads 4.6m barrels as more crude slips past US blockade
stories.summary: A maritime analytics firm reported that Iran loaded approximately 4.6 million barrels of crude oil at its export terminals despite the US naval blockade. TankerTrackers said an additional four million barrels appear to have moved past the blockade line.

stories.title: Trump says shooting proves need for his White House ballroom
stories.summary: Following a shooting incident at the White House Correspondents' Dinner held at the Washington Hilton, President Donald Trump argued the event underscored the need for his proposed White House ballroom. The dinner took place a few blocks north of the White House.

stories.title: Suspect in Washington dinner attack spent several years acquiring guns
stories.summary: The suspect in the armed attack at the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents' Dinner had spent several years acquiring firearms. He purchased a shotgun in California eight months prior and a semi-automatic pistol two years before the incident.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill 14 in deadliest day in Lebanon since truce
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed 14 people in Lebanon on Sunday in the deadliest day since the truce was established. Lebanon's health ministry said the dead included two women and two children, with 37 others wounded.

stories.title: UAE-Iran differences and India’s plans to dilute language on Israel-Palestine derail joint statement at BRICS meet
stories.summary: A BRICS deputy foreign ministers' meeting in Delhi failed to produce a joint statement due to UAE-Iran disagreements and India's reported attempt to soften language on the Israel-Palestine issue. India instead issued a Chair's Statement summarizing the topics discussed.

stories.title: Iranian FM Araghchi lands in Pakistan after Oman visit, next stop Moscow: diplomatic source
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi returned to Pakistan on Sunday after visiting Oman as part of a tri-nation diplomatic tour that will also take him to Moscow. The trip comes amid Pakistani-led efforts to facilitate negotiations between Tehran and Washington to end the conflict sparked by US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February.

stories.title: Israeli fire injures Palestinian in Jabalia camp in Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli forces seriously injured a Palestinian man after opening fire in the Al-Faluja area of Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza on Sunday evening, according to the Wafa news agency. Medical sources reported the overall Gaza death toll has reached 72,587 since October 7, 2023.

stories.title: Launching joint slate, Bennett and Lapid promise ‘the era of division is over’
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett and opposition leader Yair Lapid announced a joint electoral slate, pledging to unite Israel's political center. Lapid stated the goal is to win elections and establish what he called a Zionist government with Bennett at the helm.

stories.title: War update: 161 clashes on frontline, fiercest fighting in Pokrovsk, Huliaipole sectors
stories.summary: On April 26, Ukrainian forces reported 161 combat engagements along the frontline, with the fiercest fighting in the Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors. Russian forces launched more than 60 attacks on Ukrainian positions in those areas.

stories.title: Iran FM to meet Putin on Russia trip, says Tehran's ambassador
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is scheduled to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin during his visit to Moscow, according to Tehran's ambassador. The planned meeting reflects the deepening relationship between Russia and Iran in recent years.

stories.title: Netanyahu’s biggest rivals join forces for Israel’s next election
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid announced they are merging their respective right-wing and centrist parties ahead of Israel's next election. The alliance unites two of Prime Minister Netanyahu's most prominent political rivals.

stories.title: Renewable energy will boost national security and protect UK from sabotage, minister says
stories.summary: UK Energy Minister Michael Shanks stated that renewable energy infrastructure such as wind farms and solar panels would strengthen national security by being harder to target than centralized fossil fuel power stations. He argued renewables also reduce vulnerability to supply shocks like those caused by geopolitical conflicts.

stories.title: Indian Dalit man's alleged custodial death and a family's wait for justice
stories.summary: The death of Akash Delison in Tamil Nadu, India, has revived concerns about alleged custodial killings, with his Dalit family continuing to seek justice and accountability from authorities.

stories.title: Oman urges diplomacy to secure Strait of Hormuz navigation
stories.summary: Oman's Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi called for diplomatic efforts to ensure freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz following US-Israeli attacks on Iran. He said he held productive talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Muscat on Saturday.

stories.title: Mali defence minister killed amid flurry of insurgent attacks
stories.summary: Mali's defence minister Sadio Camara was killed on Sunday when a suicide car bomb struck his residence in the town of Kati. The attack occurred during coordinated assaults by insurgent groups, including al-Qaida's West African affiliate, according to a government spokesperson.

stories.title: Syrian court begins proceedings against Assad and allies
stories.summary: A Syrian court has begun proceedings against former President Bashar al-Assad and his allies. Assad and his brother Maher, who fled Syria, will be tried in absentia. Their relative Atef Najib, a former security official, appeared in the courtroom in handcuffs.

stories.title: North Ireland police suspect dissident republicans in latest car bombing
stories.summary: Police in Northern Ireland are investigating a recent car bombing and suspect dissident republican groups are responsible for the attack.

stories.title: In China, President Zardari expresses interest in closer collaboration in seed technology, agricultural research
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari, on a week-long visit to China's Hunan and Hainan provinces, met with a senior Chinese Communist Party official. He expressed Pakistan's interest in closer collaboration with China on seed technology, agricultural research, and modern farming practices.

stories.title: Russian strike on Novomykolaivka in Zaporizhzhia region leaves thousands without power
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the village of Novomykolaivka in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, leaving more than 4,400 consumers without electricity across several settlements. The strike damaged local power infrastructure.

stories.title: PA leader Abbas’s loyalists win local elections, including in Gaza’s Deir al‑Balah
stories.summary: Loyalists of Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas won local elections held in several locations, including Deir al-Balah in Gaza. The vote was described as the first election of any kind in the Gaza Strip in over two decades, with Ramallah calling it a step toward full independence.

stories.title: Global military spending hits record $2.9 trillion in 2025 amid growing insecurity
stories.summary: Global military spending reached nearly $2.9 trillion in 2025, marking the 11th consecutive year of growth, according to SIPRI. The United States, China, and Russia together accounted for over half the total at $1.48 trillion, driven by rising insecurity and rearmament efforts worldwide.

stories.title: Israel PM says Hezbollah 'dismantling' ceasefire with Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accused Hezbollah of undermining the ceasefire agreement with Lebanon. Under the recently extended truce, Israel has reserved the right to respond to imminent threats and has been conducting near-daily strikes in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Jordan’s king warns against Israeli escalation in Gaza, West Bank
stories.summary: Jordan's King Abdullah II warned against Israeli attempts to exploit regional developments to impose new realities in Gaza and the occupied West Bank. He made the remarks during a meeting with Kuwait's foreign minister in Amman.

stories.title: Transavia cancels flights as fuel costs surge amid Iran war
stories.summary: Dutch low-cost airline Transavia announced it would cancel some flights in May and June due to rising jet fuel costs linked to disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. The cancellations affect about two percent of its schedule, and affected passengers will be offered rebooking, vouchers, or refunds.

stories.title: Zelenskyy accuses Russia of 'nuclear terrorism' on Chernobyl anniversary
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia of 'nuclear terrorism' on the anniversary of the Chernobyl disaster. Five people were killed across Ukraine after Russia launched over 100 drones overnight, continuing its nearly nightly aerial bombardment campaign.

stories.title: Ukraine signs deal to open special fund for Chornobyl Confinement restoration
stories.summary: Ukraine signed an agreement with international partners to open a special fund for restoring the New Safe Confinement structure at the Chornobyl Nuclear Power Plant. The facility was damaged in a previous Russian drone strike.

stories.title: Australia news live: Wong heads to Japan, China and South Korea to secure fuel supply; new ADF armoured vehicles ordered
stories.summary: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong departed on a diplomatic tour to Japan, China, and South Korea aimed at securing fuel and energy supply chains. Separately, Australia's Defence Force announced orders for new armoured vehicles.

stories.title: Qatar, Saudi Arabia discuss US-Iran crisis
stories.summary: Qatar's Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani and Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan discussed the fragile US-Iran ceasefire in a phone call. Both sides emphasized de-escalation efforts to support regional security and stability.

stories.title: Trump has ‘good conversations’ with Putin, Zelenskyy: report
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters he had 'good conversations' with both Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Trump called the animosity between the two leaders 'ridiculous' but declined to say when he last spoke with Putin.

stories.title: SIPRI: Record arms spending, again
stories.summary: The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute reported that global military spending reached a new record high in 2025. SIPRI warned the upward trend is likely to continue and carries additional security risks.

stories.title: Flotilla sets sail from Italy to challenge Gaza blockade
stories.summary: A convoy of 65 vessels called the Global Sumud Flotilla 2026 Spring Mission departed from Sicily, Italy, aiming to break the Israeli blockade on Gaza and deliver humanitarian aid. Palestinian flags were raised on many of the boats.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill 14 in Lebanon amid ongoing ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes killed 14 people in Lebanon despite an ongoing ceasefire that the United States extended by three weeks following negotiations.

stories.title: Trump factor drives up Asia-Pacific military spending at fastest pace since 2009
stories.summary: Military spending in the Asia-Pacific rose at its fastest pace since 2009, driven by uncertainty among US allies over Washington's security commitments under President Trump. Global military expenditure reached $2.89 trillion in 2025, marking the 11th consecutive annual increase, according to SIPRI.

stories.title: Daniel Gros on what China can learn from the euro as it works towards a global yuan
stories.summary: Daniel Gros, director of the Institute for European Policymaking at Bocconi University, analyzed the structural tensions in EU-China economic relations and drew lessons from the euro's development to assess China's push toward internationalizing the yuan.

stories.title: Palestinian leader’s loyalists win local elections, including some seats in Gaza
stories.summary: Loyalists of the Palestinian Authority leadership won local elections held on April 25, including some seats in Gaza. The vote marked the first elections of any kind conducted in Gaza since 2006.

stories.title: Syria begins first trial of Bashar al-Assad and allies after his ouster
stories.summary: A Syrian court held its first hearing in the trial of ousted president Bashar al-Assad and senior officials from his former government. Assad and his brother Maher al-Assad are being tried in absentia, while former security official Atif Najib appeared in court in handcuffs.

stories.title: Trump says he has “good conversations” with Zelensky and Putin
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said he has had "good conversations" with both Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Russian President Vladimir Putin, suggesting ongoing diplomatic engagement regarding the war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Israel deployed Iron Dome system to UAE during Iran war
stories.summary: Israel secretly deployed an Iron Dome air defense system along with operating crews to the United Arab Emirates early in the war with Iran, according to Israeli and US officials cited by Axios. The UAE has reportedly been targeted by approximately 550 Iranian ballistic and cruise missiles and over 2,200 drones.

stories.title: Anti-Trump sentiment being examined as motive for White House press dinner shooting
stories.summary: Investigators are examining anti-Trump sentiment as a possible motive behind a shooting near the White House Correspondents' Dinner in Washington, DC. A manifesto reportedly written by the suspect listed Trump administration officials as targets. President Donald Trump and senior officials were present at the event.

stories.title: Death toll in Colombia highway bus bomb attack rises to 20
stories.summary: A bus bombing on a highway in Colombia killed at least 20 people, with the death toll rising from earlier reports. The attack occurred amid escalating political violence in the country ahead of next month's presidential election.

stories.title: Pakistan notifies 6 land routes for transportation of goods to Iran amid blockade of Hormuz, Iranian ports
stories.summary: Pakistan has officially notified six overland routes for transporting goods to Iran, including corridors through Gwadar, Karachi, and Taftan. The move, formalized under a new statutory order, responds to disruptions caused by the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and Iranian ports, with thousands of Iran-bound containers reportedly stranded at Pakistani ports.

stories.title: IMF executive board to meet on May 8 to approve disbursement of over $1.2bn to Pakistan
stories.summary: The IMF's executive board is scheduled to meet on May 8 to approve disbursement of over $1.2 billion to Pakistan. The funds come under the $7 billion Extended Fund Facility and the Resilience and Sustainability Facility, following successful program reviews.

stories.title: UK government move to delay social media ban faces pushback in Lords
stories.summary: The UK government tabled an amendment to the children's wellbeing and schools bill that could delay restrictions on children's access to social media by up to three years. Peers in the House of Lords and child-safety campaigners pushed back, saying the move breaks earlier promises of swift action.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1523: Forty years after Chornobyl, Russia has struck Ukraine’s nuclear infrastructure 155 times
stories.summary: On day 1,523 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, Moldovan President Maia Sandu visited Kyiv on the 40th anniversary of the Chornobyl disaster. Ukraine's Prime Minister Shmyhal disclosed that Russia has struck Ukraine's nuclear infrastructure 155 times, and Ukrainian forces hit three Russian warships in Sevastopol and a refinery in Yaroslavl.

stories.title: Lebanon says Israeli strikes on south kill 14 people
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported that Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon on Sunday killed 14 people, including two women and two children, and wounded 37 others. The strikes occurred despite an extended ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon.

stories.title: Iran FM to visit Moscow for talks on ceasefire and negotiations
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is set to travel to Moscow on Monday for talks covering ceasefire negotiations and regional developments. Iran's ambassador to Russia noted that President Pezeshkian and Vladimir Putin have held several calls since the war began.

stories.title: Severe weather hits Ukraine leaving three killed, several injured
stories.summary: Severe weather struck 13 regions across Ukraine, killing three people and injuring several others, including a child. Emergency services are conducting response operations in the affected areas.

stories.title: Drone attack hits Sudan aid truck: UN
stories.summary: A UNHCR-operated vehicle was struck by a drone attack on Friday while transporting emergency shelter kits to Tawila in Sudan, which hosts more than 700,000 displaced people. The United Nations confirmed the incident.

stories.title: Russia’s nuclear sector remains unsanctioned, helping turn Ukraine’s nuclear sites into war zones – Zelenskyy
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy called for stronger international sanctions on Russia's nuclear sector, arguing that Moscow is weaponizing the Chornobyl and Zaporizhzhia nuclear sites as part of its war against Ukraine.

stories.title: Deputy PM Shmyhal: Russia has attacked nuclear-critical substations 155 times since start of full-scale war
stories.summary: Ukrainian Deputy Prime Minister Shmyhal reported that Russia has attacked substations critical to nuclear safety 155 times since the start of the full-scale invasion. The strikes target infrastructure essential to the safe operation of Ukraine's nuclear power plants.

stories.title: Israel issues forced evacuation orders for seven Lebanese towns
stories.summary: Israel issued evacuation orders for seven towns in southern Lebanon north of the Litani River after one of its soldiers was killed. The Israeli military directed residents to move north and west, extending operations beyond its previously established buffer zone.

stories.title: Chinese EV firm Nio accused of exploiting Better Place patents in $250 million suit
stories.summary: Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer Nio faces a $250 million lawsuit accusing it of infringing on patents originally developed by Israeli company Better Place. The patents are now held by Charge Peak, which acquired them after Better Place folded. Nio has rejected the claims.

stories.title: London Marathon hails ‘greatest day’ as Sawe breaks two hours and records tumble
stories.summary: Sabastian Sawe became the first man to break the two-hour barrier in an official marathon race at the London Marathon. Both the men's and women's-only world records were broken, and organisers expected to surpass 59,226 finishers, potentially setting a new global record.

stories.title: Iran’s foreign minister leaves Pakistan, heads to Russia for more talks
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi departed Pakistan and traveled to Moscow to hold talks with senior Russian officials, according to Iran's Foreign Ministry.

stories.title: Netanyahu's biggest rivals join forces for Israel's next election
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid announced a joint political alliance to challenge Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in upcoming elections. They cited Netanyahu's failure to achieve strategic victories regarding Iran and Gaza as motivation for their partnership.

stories.title: Russia hit Ukraine’s nuclear energy infrastructure 155 times, creating serious risks for nuclear safety – Shmyhal
stories.summary: Ukrainian Prime Minister Shmyhal reported that Russia has struck Ukraine's nuclear energy infrastructure 155 times. Officials warned that repeated strikes on substations linked to nuclear plants threaten the stability of Ukraine's power grid.

stories.title: ‘You’re lucky you’re not soap bars’: Jews forced to leave rally marking WWII end in Italy
stories.summary: In Italy, members of Jewish organizations participating in a rally marking the end of World War II were insulted and forced to leave the march. Participants reportedly faced antisemitic slurs during the commemoration event.

stories.title: Zelensky: Strike on Chernobyl NPP shows Moscow cannot be trusted as international partner
stories.summary: President Zelensky condemned a Russian drone strike on the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant's containment structure, calling Russia an irresponsible power that cannot be trusted as an international partner. He argued Russia must be restrained for global safety.

stories.title: Fatah leading in West Bank municipal elections
stories.summary: Palestinian President Mahmud Abbas's Fatah movement led municipal council races in several major West Bank cities, including Hebron, with about 95 percent of ballots counted. Voting also took place in Deir el-Balah in central Gaza, marking the first elections since the Gaza war began.

stories.title: Bennett-Lapid reunion jolts electoral race, but path to unseating Netanyahu elusive as ever
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid revived their 2021 alliance to challenge Prime Minister Netanyahu. Their path to power may depend on whether former IDF chief Gadi Eisenkot joins their slate or runs independently, and whether a breakaway Likud faction emerges.

stories.title: Israeli settler attacks Hebron activist’s home as soldier looks on
stories.summary: In Hebron, an Israeli settler was filmed throwing rocks and attempting to break into the home of Palestinian activist Issa Amro while an Israeli soldier stood by without intervening.

stories.title: What’s driving attacks against gov’t and Russian forces in Mali?
stories.summary: In Mali, opposition armed groups, including an al-Qaeda-linked faction, have joined forces to carry out attacks against government and Russian forces operating in the country.

stories.title: Iranian FM Araghchi back in Pakistan after Oman visit, to head to Moscow after short stay: diplomatic source
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi returned to Pakistan's Nur Khan air base in Rawalpindi on Sunday after a day-long visit to Oman, continuing a tri-nation tour. His travel comes amid Pakistani-led diplomatic efforts to facilitate talks between Tehran and Washington over the conflict that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28.

stories.title: Iran minister leaves Pakistan, heads to Russia for more talks
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi departed Pakistan for Moscow after US President Trump canceled the trip of his negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Islamabad.

stories.title: Bomb attack on Colombia highway kills 19 ahead of election
stories.summary: A bomb attack on a highway in Colombia's Cauca department killed 19 people and injured dozens. The attack occurred amid a surge of violence ahead of next month's elections.

stories.title: Pope Leo says those who wage war are thieves stealing away our peaceful future
stories.summary: Pope Leo on Sunday condemned those who wage wars and exploit the earth's resources, calling them thieves who rob the world of a peaceful future. Speaking on the 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl disaster, he also issued a warning about the use of nuclear power.

stories.title: Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi returns to Islamabad as Pakistan races to save talks with U.S.
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi returned to Islamabad as Pakistan works to sustain diplomatic channels between Iran and the United States. Pakistani officials have not disclosed when American representatives might return to the region following recent face-to-face talks.

stories.title: Iran minister leaves Pakistan, heads to Russia for more talks
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi departed Islamabad for Moscow on Sunday to meet senior Russian officials. The visit covers bilateral Iran-Russia relations and regional developments as mediators work to sustain peace talks between Tehran and Washington.

stories.title: Ukrainian officials and foreign representatives honor Chernobyl cleanup workers
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky, Moldovan President Maia Sandu, Ukrainian government representatives, and foreign delegations honored Chernobyl disaster cleanup workers on the anniversary of the 1986 nuclear accident.

stories.title: Eisenkot welcomes Bennett-Lapid union but says: To win, we need to bring in more votes
stories.summary: Former IDF chief and Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot welcomed the Bennett-Lapid alliance but said broader voter outreach is needed to win. Eisenkot has not joined their slate, though Bennett said the door remains open. Netanyahu's Likud criticized the partnership.

stories.title: Netanyahu attacks Bennett, Lapid's joint party list announcement with inflammatory video
stories.summary: Members of Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's coalition and opposition figures reacted to the announcement by former prime ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid that they will form a joint list for the 2026 Knesset elections. Netanyahu responded with an inflammatory video attacking the new alliance.

stories.title: Rabbinic diplomacy between Israel and US explored in new exhibition
stories.summary: A new exhibition marks 100 years of rabbinic diplomacy between Israel and the United States. It showcases key meetings, letters, and diplomatic exchanges between Israeli Chief Rabbis and American presidents over the past century.

stories.title: Former Israeli PMs Bennett, Lapid unite to challenge Netanyahu in elections
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid announced a political alliance aimed at unifying the fragmented opposition to challenge Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in upcoming elections.

stories.title: California measure requiring photo ID at polls will be on November ballot
stories.summary: A ballot measure requiring photo identification to vote will appear before California voters in November. Republican state representative Carl DeMaio of San Diego championed the initiative, which garnered nearly one million signatures. The measure faces strong opposition from Democrats.

stories.title: Hungary's incoming PM says Orbán-linked oligarchs are moving funds to Uruguay and other destinations
stories.summary: Hungary's incoming Prime Minister Péter Magyar alleged that oligarchs linked to outgoing leader Viktor Orbán are transferring tens of billions of forints to Uruguay, the United Arab Emirates, the United States, and other countries. Magyar described it as a coordinated effort to move capital abroad ahead of the government transition scheduled for May 9.

stories.title: Has Iran exposed the limits of what US can achieve by force?
stories.summary: Political scientist Vali Nasr argued that US and Israeli military options against Iran have proven insufficient, suggesting that force alone cannot achieve Washington's strategic objectives in the region.

stories.title: Israel’s president says he wants a deal reached in Netanyahu case before pardon decision
stories.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog stated he wants a deal reached in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's legal case before making a decision on a pardon request. Netanyahu submitted the pardon request in November.

stories.title: Highlighting their differences, old-new partners Bennett and Lapid try, again, to oust Netanyahu
stories.summary: Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid formally announced their renewed political alliance to unseat Prime Minister Netanyahu in Israel's upcoming elections. Bennett expressed confidence in a major victory, while Lapid was more cautious, as the two emphasized their complementary strengths.

stories.title: Palestinian authorities call local elections in a Gaza community and the West Bank a success
stories.summary: Palestinian authorities held municipal elections in the occupied West Bank and in the Deir el-Balah area of central Gaza, calling the vote a success. Gaza voters said they were motivated to participate despite a near-total absence of public services after over two years of Israeli military operations.

stories.title: Israeli settlers uproot hundreds of olive trees near Ramallah
stories.summary: Israeli settlers from the Adi Ad outpost uprooted approximately 400 olive trees on Palestinian farmland near Turmus Ayya, northeast of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank. Residents also reported recent arson attacks on a house and a vehicle in the area.

stories.title: Hezbollah and Israel escalate attacks, accusing each other of violating ceasefire
stories.summary: Hezbollah and Israel escalated military operations, with each side accusing the other of violating the ceasefire. The intensification of strikes continued despite ongoing diplomatic efforts to maintain the truce.

stories.title: Washington shooting suspect sent anti-Trump writings to family before attack
stories.summary: Cole Tomas Allen, the suspect in a Washington shooting, reportedly sent anti-Trump writings to his family before the attack, calling himself the 'Friendly Federal Assassin.' His sister described him as someone prone to making radical statements.

stories.title: Family of Correspondants' Dinner shooting suspect alerted police before attempted attack - report
stories.summary: Family members of the suspect in the shooting near the White House Correspondents' Dinner alerted police before the attempted attack. They reported that the individual had frequently made radical statements and referenced a vague plan to "fix issues in the world."

stories.title: Ukraine opens special fund to restore Chernobyl shelter damaged in Russian drone strike
stories.summary: Ukraine launched a special fund aiming to raise more than €500 million to restore the Chernobyl nuclear shelter, which was damaged in a Russian drone strike. The initiative seeks international contributions for the critical infrastructure repair.

stories.title: Israel issues evacuation warning for seven Lebanese towns beyond ‘buffer zone’
stories.summary: Israel issued evacuation warnings for seven towns in Lebanon located north of the Litani River, beyond the buffer zone in southern Lebanon currently occupied by Israeli forces. The warnings signal a potential expansion of Israeli military operations deeper into Lebanese territory.

stories.title: 'Last Letters from Heroes of the October 7th War': Nobody taught them how to do this - review
stories.summary: A new book titled "Last Letters from Heroes of the October 7th War" compiles final messages written by soldiers who faced the possibility of death during the conflict. The collection offers personal accounts from those who served during the October 7 war.

stories.title: Iran’s top diplomat leaves Pakistan for Russia, Trump says Tehran can talk by phone
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi departed Pakistan for Moscow after making stops in Oman and returning to Pakistan as part of intensive diplomatic efforts to restart US-Iran negotiations. President Trump, who cancelled a planned envoy trip to Pakistan, said Iran and the US could instead communicate by phone.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Dnipropetrovsk region over 20 times in day, three injured
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked three districts in Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region more than 20 times in a single day using drones and artillery. Three people were injured in the strikes.

stories.title: Iran minister returns to Pakistan despite US cancelling talks
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi returned to Pakistan despite the cancellation of a planned US diplomatic visit. President Trump had called off envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner's trip to Islamabad, where they had been scheduled to hold talks.

stories.title: Shas-backed candidate Zevadia Cohen appointed new chief rabbi of Tel Aviv
stories.summary: Rabbi Zevadia Cohen, backed by the Shas party, was appointed as the new chief rabbi of Tel Aviv. He was selected by a 64-member committee after receiving the support of Tel Aviv Mayor Ron Huldai.

stories.title: Pope says atomic energy must be used only for peace
stories.summary: Pope Leo stated that atomic energy must be used exclusively for peaceful purposes. His remarks came as the 40th anniversary of the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster was commemorated on April 26.

stories.title: Did Trump save eight Iranian women from execution?
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump claimed he saved eight Iranian women from execution, but Iranian authorities have disputed the assertion. The competing claims highlight ongoing tensions between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Argentine court orders execution of Cristina Kirchner's assets for about $480 million in Vialidad case
stories.summary: Argentina's Federal Court of Cassation confirmed the confiscation and ordered execution of assets belonging to former President Cristina Kirchner in the Vialidad fraudulent administration case. The amount totals approximately 684.99 billion pesos, or about $480 million, representing damages from public works contracts awarded in Santa Cruz province during the Kirchner administrations.

stories.title: West Africa: Mali - Guterres Calls for International Solutions to Curb Spread of Violent Extremism in the Sahel
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for international solutions to curb violent extremism in the Sahel following coordinated attacks in Mali. Clashes between extremists, northern separatist rebels, and government forces continued across the landlocked West African nation.

stories.title: Israel issues forced evacuation orders for southern Lebanon in escalation
stories.summary: Israel issued forced evacuation orders for areas in southern Lebanon, marking an escalation in tensions. Hezbollah rejected Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's allegations that it was undermining the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire.

stories.title: London venue cancels ‘grotesque’ antisemitic art exhibition following UKLFI complaint
stories.summary: A London venue canceled an art exhibition after UK Lawyers for Israel filed a complaint about antisemitic imagery in the works. The exhibition reportedly featured grotesque caricatures of Jews and blood libel imagery.

stories.title: Iran sends US message via Pakistan outlining ‘red lines’
stories.summary: Iranian state media reported that Tehran sent messages to the United States through Pakistani diplomatic channels outlining its key red lines. The messages reportedly address Iran's positions on nuclear issues and the Strait of Hormuz. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is said to be operating within established diplomatic parameters.

stories.title: Sgt. Idan Fooks, 19, killed in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Sergeant Idan Fooks, 19, from Petah Tikva was killed while serving in southern Lebanon. He was a member of the 7th Armored Brigade's 77th Battalion.

stories.title: Trump, administration officials likely targets of shooting at White House correspondents' dinner: US official
stories.summary: A suspect opened fire at a security agent near the White House Correspondents' Association dinner at the Washington Hilton in Washington, D.C. U.S. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche said President Donald Trump and administration officials were the likely targets of the attack.

stories.title: IDF Lt. Col. (res.) Ido Frommer killed in civilian parachuting accident
stories.summary: IDF Lieutenant Colonel (res.) Ido Frommer was killed in a civilian parachuting accident. Frommer was the CEO and co-founder of a UAV company and had previously managed technological, economic, and educational development in the Israeli town of Yeruham.

stories.title: Syrian court begins proceedings against Assad and allies
stories.summary: A Syrian court opened proceedings against associates and allies of former President Bashar al-Assad. Defendants include Wassim al-Assad and former Grand Mufti Ahmed Badreddin Hassoun, along with other arrested military officials.

stories.title: Pakistan eases restrictions on twin cities with no possibility of U.S.-Iran talks
stories.summary: Pakistani authorities eased movement restrictions in the twin cities of Islamabad and Rawalpindi, though police and law enforcement deployments remain active. The relaxation came amid reports that prospects for U.S.-Iran diplomatic talks had stalled.

stories.title: Gunman believed to be targeting Trump administration officials: U.S. Attorney General
stories.summary: U.S. federal prosecutors announced that the suspect who fired at a federal officer near the White House Correspondents' Association dinner would be formally charged in federal court on Monday with assault of a federal officer and discharging a firearm in an attempt to kill a federal officer.

stories.title: Hungary's Magyar to meet EU's von der ​Leyen for talks on EU funds this week
stories.summary: Hungary's incoming prime minister Peter Magyar announced he will travel to Brussels on Wednesday for informal talks with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. The discussions aim to unblock EU funds that were frozen over disputes with Magyar's predecessor.

stories.title: Mali's defence minister reported dead in major weekend assault
stories.summary: Mali's Defence Minister Sadio Camara was reportedly killed in an attack on his residence at the Kati military base outside Bamako on Saturday. The assault was carried out by the al-Qaeda-linked group JNIM, according to France's RFI radio.

stories.title: Washington in shock after White House press dinner shooting: ‘an angry, polarized nation’
stories.summary: A man targeted a Secret Service agent at a security checkpoint during the White House Correspondents' Dinner at the Washington Hilton hotel before being tackled and arrested. President Donald Trump and First Lady Melania Trump were rushed from the event. The incident prompted wide discussion about political violence, security, and gun control.

stories.title: Global Sumud Flotilla embarks from Sicily, aiming to disrupt Gaza blockade
stories.summary: The Global Sumud Flotilla, comprising over 60 Italian and Spanish vessels, set sail from Sicily aiming to challenge Israel's naval blockade of Gaza. The flotilla seeks to raise international awareness and mobilize activist support for Palestinians in the territory.

stories.title: Hezbollah says Israel violating truce, rejects Netanyahu accusation
stories.summary: Hezbollah rejected Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's accusation that it was undermining the ceasefire agreement. The group stated that Israel was the party violating the truce through its continued military operations in Lebanon.

stories.title: Mali junta in crisis after defence minister is killed and key city ‘captured’
stories.summary: Mali's military junta faced a major security crisis after coordinated attacks by jihadist fighters and Tuareg separatist rebels killed the defense minister and reportedly captured a key northern town. Junta leader General Assimi Goita had not been seen publicly since the offensive began.

stories.title: Israeli attacks kill over 2,500 in Lebanon since March
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry reported that at least 2,509 people have been killed and 7,755 wounded in Israeli attacks since fighting with Hezbollah resumed on March 2. The toll reflects months of escalating cross-border hostilities between Israel and the Lebanese armed group.

stories.title: Severe weather in Ukraine leaves two dead, two injured
stories.summary: Two people died and two others, including a child, were injured due to severe weather across Ukraine. Rescue workers are responding to weather-related emergencies in 13 regions of the country.

stories.title: Netanyahu's biggest rivals join forces for Israel's next election
stories.summary: Former Israeli prime ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid announced a merger of their parties—Bennett 2026 and There is a Future—to challenge Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition in upcoming elections expected later this year.

stories.title: UK faces higher prices for eight months after war in Iran ends, says minister
stories.summary: UK minister Darren Jones warned that prices for energy, food, and flights will remain elevated for at least eight months after the conflict in Iran ends. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which carries roughly a fifth of global oil and gas, has driven oil prices sharply higher since US and Israeli strikes on Iran began in February.

stories.title: IDF soldier killed in south Lebanon drone attack as Israel, Hezbollah trade blame
stories.summary: An Israeli soldier was killed and six others were wounded in a drone attack inside Israel's declared security zone in southern Lebanon. Prime Minister Netanyahu accused Hezbollah of undermining the ceasefire, while Hezbollah described its actions as a legitimate response to Israeli violations.

stories.title: Switzerland angers Italy by claiming costs of treating Crans-Montana fire victims
stories.summary: Switzerland announced it will bill Italy for the healthcare costs of treating Italian nationals injured in the New Year's Eve fire at the Crans-Montana ski resort, which killed 41 people. The decision has drawn criticism from Rome.

stories.title: Drones, drones, and more drones: Ukraine sets spending priorities for €90B EU package
stories.summary: Ukraine announced that the first tranche of a €90 billion EU loan package will be directed primarily toward scaling up drone production. Energy infrastructure protection was identified as the second spending priority.

stories.title: Mali Defence Minister killed, fresh fighting between army and rebels
stories.summary: Mali's Defence Minister Sadio Camara, his second wife, and two grandchildren were killed in a car bomb attack at his home in the town of Kita, outside the capital Bamako. The attack occurred amid renewed fighting between the Malian military and rebel groups.

stories.title: Israeli politics shaken as Bennett and Lapid join forces again - analysis
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett and opposition leader Yair Lapid have formed a renewed political alliance. Despite ideological differences, analysts note the personal trust between the two leaders serves as their central campaign promise.

stories.title: Frontier Works Organisation resumes construction of BRT Red Line project on Karachi's University Road
stories.summary: Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab announced that the Frontier Works Organisation has resumed construction on a section of the long-delayed BRT Red Line project along University Road in Karachi. The Sindh government had cancelled the previous contractor's agreement days earlier, citing execution delays, and planned to re-award the contract on an emergency basis.

stories.title: Israel kills three in Gaza, civil defence says
stories.summary: Gaza's Civil Defence agency reported that Israeli forces killed three people in the territory, including two men struck by a drone-fired missile near Kuwait roundabout while among a group of civilians.

stories.title: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard pledges continued support for Hezbollah
stories.summary: Esmail Qaani, commander of Iran's IRGC Quds Force, pledged continued support for Hezbollah and allied groups within the "Resistance Front." In remarks carried by Tasnim news agency, he claimed unity among the groups is stronger than ever and predicted Israel would fail to achieve its objectives in Lebanon.

stories.title: Another attack on Trump ? A post analysis of the White House correspondents' dinner shooting
stories.summary: President Donald Trump and other officials were evacuated from the White House Correspondents' Dinner at the Washington Hilton after a man attempted to breach security with firearms. The individual was subdued at the scene.

stories.title: Israel High Court demands government enforce draft law, revoke benefits from evaders
stories.summary: Israel's High Court ordered the state to revoke benefits from ultra-Orthodox (Haredi) individuals who evade military conscription. The ruling represents a significant step toward enforcing draft law compliance amid an ongoing manpower shortage in the Israeli military.

stories.title: Chernobyl: Two Takes, Then & Now. On the Ground 40 years on
stories.summary: The 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl nuclear disaster is being marked in Ukraine. The 1986 explosion at the Chernobyl power plant remains the worst nuclear catastrophe in history.

stories.title: 16 dead in strikes as Chernobyl anniversary highlights nuclear risks of Russia-Ukraine war
stories.summary: Strikes across Ukraine, Russian-occupied territory, and Russia killed at least 16 people, including nine in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro from Russian drone and missile attacks. The violence coincided with the 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl nuclear disaster, renewing warnings about combat near nuclear facilities.
