stories.title: Ukraine to take part in NATO summit in Turkey, Zelensky says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine will participate in the upcoming NATO summit in Turkey. The specific format and level of Ukrainian representation at the summit have not yet been determined.

stories.title: Forging new alliances: Israel appoints first ever ambassador to Somaliland
stories.summary: Israel appointed its first-ever ambassador to Somaliland, a self-declared republic in the Horn of Africa. Ambassador Lotem will initially serve in a non-resident capacity, reflecting the early stages of diplomatic engagement between the two sides.

stories.title: No headway in Middle East peace efforts as US and Iran refuse to yield
stories.summary: Diplomatic efforts to end the nearly two-month-old conflict between Iran and the United States showed no progress, with neither Washington nor Tehran willing to make concessions. No new negotiations are scheduled, deepening the sense of deadlock despite active regional diplomacy.

stories.title: First trial of Assad-era Syrian official starts in Damascus
stories.summary: Syria held its first public trial of a former Assad-era official in Damascus, with ex-security chief Atef Najib appearing in court. The proceedings mark a significant step in accountability efforts following the fall of the Assad government.

stories.title: Russia confirms Iran foreign minister to visit for talks
stories.summary: Russia's foreign ministry confirmed that Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi would visit Moscow for talks. Iran's ambassador to Russia said Araghchi was expected to meet President Vladimir Putin on Monday to consult on regional developments.

stories.title: Israel police confiscate Hungary flag over Palestine resemblance
stories.summary: Israeli police confiscated a Hungarian flag from an anti-government protester near Haifa, citing its resemblance to the Palestinian flag. Authorities said the flag's display could lead to provocation.

stories.title: Adalah petitions High Court to return bodies of six Arab citizens withheld by Israel
stories.summary: Palestinian legal organization Adalah petitioned Israel's High Court to compel the return of bodies of six Arab citizens being withheld by the state. The petition challenges Israel's longstanding policy of holding deceased individuals' remains as leverage.

stories.title: Israel carries out strikes in south Lebanon despite ceasefire
stories.summary: The Israeli military conducted artillery and air strikes in southern Lebanon, claiming it targeted Hezbollah fighters and weapons sites. Hezbollah said it attacked Israeli troops inside Lebanon. The strikes occurred despite a US-mediated ceasefire in place since April 16.

stories.title: War update: 53 combat clashes since morning, with heaviest fighting in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 53 attacks on Ukrainian defense positions since the start of the day. The heaviest fighting was concentrated in the Pokrovsk sector, with heightened Russian activity also reported along the Huliaipole sector.

stories.title: Israel army says soldier killed in south Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced that Sergeant Idan Fooks, 19, was killed during combat in southern Lebanon. An officer and three other soldiers were severely injured in the same incident, with one soldier moderately injured and another lightly injured.

stories.title: Israeli officials, residents alarmed by Egypt army border drills
stories.summary: Israeli officials and residents near the Egyptian border expressed alarm over Egyptian military drills conducted close to the frontier. Despite Israel having approved the exercises, communities living in the border area said the activity was very worrying.

stories.title: Syria begins trial of first Assad-era official in Damascus
stories.summary: Syria opened its first trial of an Assad-era official at the Palace of Justice in Damascus. Atef Najib, a cousin of former president Bashar al-Assad and ex-head of political security in Deraa province, is accused of orchestrating the repression of the initial 2011 protests.

stories.title: Royal Mail investigating claims that postal worker ‘binned Reform UK election leaflets’
stories.summary: Royal Mail is investigating claims that a postal worker discarded Reform UK campaign leaflets ahead of Thursday's local elections in the United Kingdom. A post on a private Facebook group for Royal Mail staff reportedly included an admission of binning the materials.

stories.title: “We have done everything”: Ukraine’s EU membership talks expected to start in June, Zelenskyy says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that Kyiv has completed all necessary preparations for EU membership talks and expects formal negotiations to begin in June. Ukraine is now awaiting a decision from EU leaders.

stories.title: Russia, North Korea agree 'long-term' military cooperation
stories.summary: Russia's defense minister and the chairman of the State Duma visited North Korea to formalize long-term military cooperation. During the visit, a memorial to North Korean soldiers killed fighting in Ukraine was inaugurated, and a new defense agreement was negotiated between the two countries.

stories.title: Japan deploys 1,400 firefighters to battle raging wildfires in the north
stories.summary: Japan deployed 1,400 firefighters and 100 Self-Defence Force personnel to combat mountain wildfires in its northern regions, now burning for a fifth consecutive day. The fires consumed over 1,373 hectares and continued to threaten the coastal town of Otsuchi in Iwate Prefecture on the Pacific coast.

stories.title: On the ascendant
stories.summary: Pakistan played a key diplomatic role in facilitating a ceasefire between the United States and Iran and subsequently hosted high-level delegations from both countries in Islamabad for talks. The effort came amid escalating global conflicts and the aftermath of a 40-day US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Russia's air defense already experiences missile shortage — Syrskyi
stories.summary: Ukraine's Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi reported that Russia's air defense systems are experiencing missile shortages. He shared the assessment during a briefing with Canadian Chief of the Defence Staff Jennie Carignan.

stories.title: Medical supply shortages loom in Iran as civilians bear the cost of ongoing conflict, UN warns
stories.summary: The United Nations warned of looming medical supply shortages in Iran as the ongoing conflict disrupts access to critical healthcare resources. Civilians are bearing the brunt of the crisis, with the effects of the war on Iran's medical infrastructure being felt both domestically and globally.

stories.title: Abbas loyalists win Palestinian local elections, some Gaza seats
stories.summary: Loyalists of Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas won Palestinian local elections, including some seats in Gaza. Voter turnout was 23 percent in Gaza and 56 percent in the West Bank, according to the Central Elections Commission chairman.

stories.title: Four Palestinians killed by Israeli fire in Gaza
stories.summary: At least four Palestinians were killed by Israeli forces across the Gaza Strip on Sunday. Two men were shot near the Kuwait roundabout in Gaza City, one man was killed near the Saqqa mosque in central Gaza, and a woman was shot dead in Khan Younis. Health authorities say at least 800 Palestinians have died since the ceasefire began.

stories.title: President Zardari underscores industrial cooperation, technology partnership during visit to China
stories.summary: Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari visited Sany Heavy Industry Co. Ltd. in Changsha, China, during a week-long trip focused on economic and trade cooperation. Zardari emphasized strengthening industrial and technological partnerships between Pakistan and China during engagements in Hunan and Hainan provinces.

stories.title: Texas tornado kills at least one person as wildfires still rage in parts of Georgia
stories.summary: A powerful tornado struck Wise County in northern Texas on Saturday night, killing at least one person and causing significant damage across multiple neighborhoods. The extreme weather coincided with ongoing wildfires in parts of Georgia, affecting millions across the southern and midwestern United States.

stories.title: Israel sent Iron Dome system, dozens of IDF soldiers to UAE during Iran war
stories.summary: Israel deployed an Iron Dome air defense system and dozens of IDF soldiers to the United Arab Emirates during the Iran war. This marked the first operational use of the Iron Dome system outside of Israel and the United States.

stories.title: Iran shifts economic focus to essentials during war uncertainty
stories.summary: Iran's government is partially reversing a previous currency policy for basic goods and drawing on its sovereign wealth fund. The measures aim to stabilize access to essential items amid economic uncertainty linked to ongoing regional tensions.

stories.title: Trump says Iran can call the US if it wants to negotiate
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that Iran can contact the United States by phone if it wishes to negotiate an end to the conflict between the two countries. He made the remarks during a Fox News interview. Trump also cancelled a trip by envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Pakistan, setting back peace efforts.

stories.title: SSU strikes three ships, MiG-31 aircraft, air defense facilities in Crimea
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service struck several key Russian military targets in Crimea, including three military ships, a MiG-31 fighter jet, and air defense installations.

stories.title: Abbas loyalists sweep Palestinian elections, including some seats in Gaza
stories.summary: Supporters of Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas won a decisive majority in Palestinian local elections, including some seats in Gaza. Voter turnout in Gaza was notably low, attributed to the continuing impact of the conflict there.

stories.title: The afterlife of antisemitism – with Flora Cassen - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Historian Flora Cassen discussed differences between European and American Jewish life, the role of Holocaust memory, and the resurgence of antisemitism in a podcast conversation. The discussion examined historical and contemporary patterns of anti-Jewish hostility.

stories.title: Final steps taken before audacious plan to tow whale stranded in Germany to North Sea
stories.summary: A millionaire-funded operation is in its final stages to tow a 12-tonne humpback whale named Timmy, stranded on Germany's Baltic Sea coast for nearly a month, approximately 400 kilometers to the North Sea using a barge-mounted steel aquarium. The plan has drawn criticism from some who call it 'pure animal cruelty.'

stories.title: Israel gives warning to seven towns beyond Lebanon 'buffer zone'
stories.summary: Israel issued warnings to seven towns located north of the Litani River and beyond the buffer zone in southern Lebanon. Israeli troops continue to occupy southern Lebanon and have maintained military operations in the area.

stories.title: Greggs rolls back self-service cabinets in shoplifting hotspots
stories.summary: UK bakery chain Greggs has removed self-service display cabinets in stores most affected by shoplifting, replacing them with staff-served, theft-proof counters. The move follows record shoplifting figures in England and Wales, which surpassed half a million offences last year.

stories.title: Rebuilding Justice For Jews- Adela Cojab - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Adela Cojab discussed her landmark lawsuit against New York University, which became a key case in efforts to apply Title VI of the Civil Rights Act to protect Jewish students from discrimination on campus.

stories.title: UK says cooperating closely with US on security ahead of King Charles' visit
stories.summary: The British government said it is cooperating closely with U.S. security services ahead of King Charles' visit to the United States, following the shooting at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner in Washington.

stories.title: Hope for Israel’s 78th Birthday - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Donniel Hartman and Yossi Klein Halevi offered reflections on Israel's 78th Independence Day, discussing themes of mourning, blessing, and national resilience in a special podcast segment.

stories.title: Syria opens first public trial of former Assad regime official, Atef Najib
stories.summary: Syria opened its first public trial of former Assad regime official Atef Najib in Damascus, focusing on crimes committed in Dara'a and Damascus. The trial marks a significant step toward accountability for abuses under the former regime.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz will not return to pre-war conditions, Iranian MP says
stories.summary: Senior Iranian lawmaker Ali Nikzad declared that the Strait of Hormuz will not return to pre-war conditions, citing directives from Iran's leadership. Iran has maintained control over the strait since the war began on 28 February, while the US imposed a naval blockade on 13 April. Talks in Islamabad failed to produce a breakthrough.

stories.title: What’s left of Russia’s Black Sea Fleet in Crimea comes under fire as Ukraine hits three warships in Sevastopol strike
stories.summary: Ukraine's SBU intelligence service struck three Russian warships in Sevastopol harbor in Crimea. The operation also targeted Belbek airfield, hitting a MiG-31 fighter jet and airfield infrastructure.

stories.title: After October 7: Rethinking Israel’s Grand Strategy - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Barak Seener discussed findings from the Henry Jackson Society's "Israel 2048" report, outlining a proposed shift in Israeli grand strategy from reactive deterrence to proactive power projection following the October 7 attack.

stories.title: Zelensky: Three more countries contribute about EUR 400M to PURL
stories.summary: President Zelensky announced that three additional countries contributed approximately EUR 350–400 million to the PURL program during a meeting in Cyprus. The first tranche of a EUR 90 billion loan will fund domestic weapons production and energy infrastructure protection.

stories.title: Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid announce united run under Bennett in 2026 elections
stories.summary: Former Israeli prime ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid announced they will run on a joint party list in the 2026 Knesset elections, with Bennett leading the ticket. Bennett also invited former IDF chief Gadi Eisenkot to join the new unified party.

stories.title: Pakistani exports to major European markets slow down amid ME conflict despite GSP+ status
stories.summary: Pakistan's exports to major Western and Northern European markets declined in the first nine months of the fiscal year despite retaining GSP+ trade status. The downturn is linked to weakening demand and disruptions caused by the US-Iran conflict, which has affected global shipping and goods transport through the Middle East.

stories.title: Nigeria: Exclusive - Inside Nigeria's Deal to Write Off $32.8 Million Fine Against Meta
stories.summary: Nigeria reached an undisclosed deal with Meta that includes writing off a $32.8 million fine previously imposed on the company. The agreement also softened other regulatory obligations Nigeria had placed on the tech giant.

stories.title: Nigeria: For the Record - Ibadan Declaration: What Major Opposition Parties Agreed Ahead 2027
stories.summary: At a national summit in Ibadan, major Nigerian opposition parties issued a communiqué pledging to unite behind one presidential candidate for the 2027 elections. The declaration commits all participating parties to agree on and support a single nominee to challenge the ruling party.

stories.title: Nigeria: 2027 Election - Opposition Parties Agree to Field One Candidate Against Tinubu
stories.summary: Several Nigerian opposition parties announced an agreement to field a single presidential candidate against incumbent President Tinubu in the 2027 election. The decision was made at a national summit held in Ibadan and formalized in a joint communiqué issued on Saturday.

stories.title: Trump claims gala shooting gives urgency to White House ballroom plan
stories.summary: President Donald Trump used the shooting at the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents' Dinner to press his case for constructing a 1,000-seat ballroom at the White House, a project estimated at $400 million. An armed attacker was arrested after rushing toward the hotel ballroom where Trump was attending the event.

stories.title: Egypt's foreign minister speaks with his Qatari and Iranian counterparts
stories.summary: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty held separate phone calls with his Qatari and Iranian counterparts to discuss relaunching US-Iran negotiations. Abdelatty emphasized the importance of diplomacy to sustain the ceasefire and work toward ending the war.

stories.title: Sandu, Zelensky discuss specific terms of Moldova's assistance within Coalition of the Willing
stories.summary: Moldovan President Maia Sandu and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky discussed Moldova's potential contribution to the Coalition of the Willing, despite Moldova's neutral status.

stories.title: Iranian and Saudi foreign ministers discuss regional developments
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan Al Saud spoke by phone about regional and diplomatic developments. Araghchi briefed his Saudi counterpart on ceasefire progress and Iran's efforts to end the war and reduce tensions.

stories.title: Syria’s first public trial of Assad-era officials begins in Damascus
stories.summary: Syria's first public trial of Assad-era officials opened in Damascus with defendant Atef Najib, a former general and cousin of ousted president Bashar al-Assad. Najib is accused of ordering the torture of children during the 2011 uprising. Bereaved families at the proceedings demanded the death penalty.

stories.title: Iran diplomacy stalls as Hormuz becomes focal point of mediation efforts
stories.summary: Diplomatic efforts over the Strait of Hormuz have stalled as President Trump stated that Iran's most recent proposal was "not enough" despite offering concessions. Tehran is reportedly attempting to persuade Oman to support a mechanism for collecting tolls in the strait, making Hormuz a central focus of mediation.

stories.title: Former PMs Bennett, Lapid join forces under unified party ahead of next Israeli elections
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid announced they are merging their parties ahead of the next elections. Space has reportedly been left for Yashar! party leader Gadi Eisenkot to join the unified party.

stories.title: Ukraine warns of energy funding gap despite €100M partner pledge for winter preparations
stories.summary: Ukraine warned of a gap in energy funding despite a €100 million pledge from international partners for winter preparations. Officials noted that Ukrainian teams have already identified usable equipment from decommissioned power plants in several EU countries for transfer.

stories.title: French FM: Russian attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure create risk of radiological consequences
stories.summary: France's foreign minister warned that Russian strikes on Ukraine's civilian and energy infrastructure pose a risk of serious radiological consequences.

stories.title: Explosive device kills 13, injures 38 on bus in southwestern Colombia as violence persists
stories.summary: An explosive device detonated on a bus traveling along the Panamerican Highway in Cajibio municipality, Cauca region, southwestern Colombia, killing 13 people and injuring 38. Governor Octavio Guzman confirmed the incident.

stories.title: Colombia highway bomb attack kills at least 19
stories.summary: Suspected guerrilla fighters detonated explosives on the Pan-American Highway in southwest Colombia, killing at least 19 people. The attack occurred amid a period of intensified violence in the region.

stories.title: Colombia highway bomb attack kills 19
stories.summary: Suspected guerrillas detonated explosives on a bus traveling the Pan-American Highway in southwest Colombia, killing 19 people. The region has experienced intensifying violence in recent days. Dashcam footage of the attack has been released.

stories.title: Israeli attacks kill at least four Palestinians in Gaza, medics say
stories.summary: Israeli military strikes killed at least four Palestinians in the Gaza Strip on Sunday, according to health officials in the enclave. The report was relayed from Cairo on April 26.

stories.title: Hezbollah says Israel violating truce and vows retaliation
stories.summary: Hezbollah rejected Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's claim that it was jeopardizing the Lebanon ceasefire. The group described its attacks on Israeli targets in southern Lebanon and northern Israel as legitimate responses to Israel's persistent violations of the truce and continued occupation of southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Gaza couples marry in mass wedding in rare moment of joy
stories.summary: Couples in Gaza celebrated a mass wedding ceremony on Friday organized by a UAE-based charity. The event provided a rare moment of joy amid ongoing Israeli military violence in the territory.

stories.title: Netanyahu says Hezbollah 'dismantling' ceasefire with Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accused Hezbollah of effectively dismantling the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon through its violations. Speaking at a weekly cabinet meeting, Netanyahu pledged to target Hezbollah vigorously. Under the extended truce terms, Israel claims the right to respond to planned or imminent attacks.

stories.title: Zelensky: Russia strikes infrastructure due to lack of success on battlefield
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia has resorted to massive strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure due to its lack of battlefield success. He characterized the attacks as part of an information campaign designed to project strength and pressure Ukraine.

stories.title: New footage shows moment of deadly bus bombing in Colombia
stories.summary: Newly released dashcam footage captures the moment a bomb-laden bus detonated in Colombia. The explosion was deadly, though specific casualty figures were not immediately detailed in the footage release.

stories.title: High Court orders government to impose financial sanctions on Haredi draft evaders
stories.summary: Israel's High Court unanimously ordered the government to impose financial sanctions on ultra-Orthodox (Haredi) men who evade military conscription. The court found the government had failed to implement previous rulings and called police refusal to arrest draft dodgers an "unacceptable mass violation of law."

stories.title: Mali's defence minister reported dead in major weekend assault
stories.summary: Mali's defense minister was reportedly killed during major assaults that took place on Saturday. The United Nations called for an international response to the escalating violence and terrorism in the West Africa Sahel region.

stories.title: ‘State of war’: Why Israel has escalated attacks in Gaza
stories.summary: Israel has escalated military operations and expanded its control within the Gaza Strip, sidelining a new US-backed technocratic administration established there. The intensified campaign has drawn renewed scrutiny of Israel's strategic objectives in the territory.

stories.title: Ukraine is holding Russian forces away from Moldova, Sandu says
stories.summary: Moldovan President Maia Sandu visited Kyiv for talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on security, EU integration, and regional cooperation. Sandu stated that Ukraine's defense efforts are helping hold Russian forces away from Moldova.

stories.title: Russian mercenaries to withdraw from Mali city after attacks
stories.summary: Russian mercenaries are set to withdraw from the city of Kidal in Mali following coordinated attacks by armed groups across the country on Saturday. Clashes resumed in Kidal in the aftermath of the large-scale weekend assaults.

stories.title: Swiss International says 5 injured after flight aborts takeoff in New Delhi
stories.summary: Swiss International Airlines flight LX147 from New Delhi to Zurich aborted takeoff on April 26 after an engine issue, injuring four passengers and one crew member. Reports indicated one engine caught fire on the runway, prompting an emergency evacuation at Delhi's airport.

stories.title: Mali Defence Minister killed in car bomb as nationwide fighting intensifies
stories.summary: Mali's Defence Minister Sadio Camara was killed in a car bomb attack at his home near Bamako. The assassination occurred as intense fighting spread across the country for a second consecutive day.

stories.title: Russian shelling of Kramatorsk leaves two killed, several injured
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled the city of Kramatorsk in Ukraine's Donetsk region, killing two people who were on the street and injuring several others.

stories.title: Berlin’s farce: How Germany failed Iran’s Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi - comment
stories.summary: Iran's Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi visited Berlin, where he rejected claims of foreign influence. The visit raised concerns about security failures and Germany's political ties with Iran's Islamic regime.

stories.title: Chinese FM tells Myanmar leader Beijing will back its security, sovereignty
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met Myanmar junta leader Min Aung Hlaing and pledged Beijing's firm support for Myanmar's national sovereignty and security. The meeting took place during Wang's three-country tour of Southeast Asia, which also included stops in Cambodia and Thailand.

stories.title: One of the greatest tragedies of this war has been the collateral damage inflicted on Iran's medical facilities
stories.summary: Since the US-Israeli joint strike on Iran's Supreme Leader's office in Tehran's Pasteur neighborhood on 28 February 2026, which killed Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, the war has caused significant collateral damage to Iran's medical facilities, including the nearby Pasteur Institute.

stories.title: In pictures: How the shooting at White House correspondents' dinner unfolded
stories.summary: A gunman opened fire at the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents' Association dinner on Saturday evening. Secret Service agents rushed President Donald Trump and his cabinet from the ballroom. The suspect was subsequently taken into custody.

stories.title: The Assad regime's true interest in Palestine was domination
stories.summary: On the anniversary of the 2018 Yarmouk refugee camp attack, analyst Alexander Bustos argues the Assad regime used the Palestinian cause to consolidate power while undermining Palestinian liberation movements.

stories.title: Russian official says oil market needs months to recover from Hormuz closure
stories.summary: Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak stated that the oil market will need several months to recover even after the Strait of Hormuz reopens, citing the deep disruption caused by the closure and the backlog of ships.

stories.title: War, the Gulf & Rethinking Money in Sport
stories.summary: Journalist Samantha Johnson examines how geopolitical tensions, including ongoing conflicts, could reshape the business of sport in the Gulf region. The analysis considers the intersection of war, Gulf state influence, and financial investment in global sports.

stories.title: Trump, cabinet officials were likely targets of Washington shooting, acting AG says
stories.summary: The acting US Attorney General said President Trump and cabinet officials were likely targets of a shooting in Washington, DC, that occurred outside the White House correspondents' dinner. Trump stated officials believe the suspect was a "lone wolf." A Secret Service member who was shot is reportedly in good shape.

stories.title: Cheap spirits, pricey condoms: how war in the Middle East is shifting the way Australians spend
stories.summary: Rising petrol prices linked to the Middle East conflict are altering Australian household spending patterns. Consumers have cut back on driving and made deeper budget reductions, with some reportedly forgoing healthcare amid already high living costs.

stories.title: Zelensky to discuss peaceful de-occupation of Zaporizhzhia NPP with Grossi
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced plans to discuss the peaceful de-occupation of the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant with IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi. The talks aim to restore Ukrainian control over the facility and strengthen diplomatic efforts for its safety.

stories.title: Russian Parliament Speaker Thanks North Korea’s Kim for ‘Liberation of Kursk'
stories.summary: Russian Parliament Speaker visited Pyongyang, where he thanked North Korean leader Kim Jong Un for assistance in what he called the liberation of Russia's Kursk region. A Russian delegation attended the opening of a memorial complex honoring North Korean personnel killed while supporting Moscow's war against Ukraine.

stories.title: State Duma Speaker Thanks North Korea’s Kim for ‘Liberation of Kursk’
stories.summary: Russian State Duma Speaker thanked North Korean leader Kim Jong Un for North Korea's role in the recapture of Russia's Kursk region. A Russian delegation visited Pyongyang for the opening of a memorial honoring North Korean soldiers killed supporting Russia's war against Ukraine.

stories.title: Rescuers find body of boy swept away while swimming in Karachi water line
stories.summary: Rescue teams in Karachi recovered the body of 12-year-old Zahid Mohammed Khan on the third day of a search operation. The boy had been swept away while swimming in a Karachi Water and Sewerage Corporation line in Scheme 33 near Al-Azhar Garden. Rescue 1122 and Edhi services confirmed the recovery.

stories.title: Outrage after man dressed as Hitler, standing on Israeli flag, salutes Boston Marathon runners
stories.summary: A man dressed as Adolf Hitler stood on an Israeli flag and gave a Nazi salute to runners at the Boston Marathon. Israeli Consul to New England Benjamin Sharoni condemned the incident as an attempt to intimidate Jewish runners.

stories.title: The week in pictures: Trump evacuated at media dinner, Leo XIV in Africa and robots race in Beijing
stories.summary: Key events of the week included the evacuation of President Trump after shots were fired at the White House Correspondents' Dinner in Washington, the killing of Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil in an Israeli strike, Pope Leo XIV's visit to a prison in Equatorial Guinea, and a robot half-marathon in Beijing.

stories.title: Zelensky, Sandu discuss security, EU integration, economic cooperation
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Moldovan President Maia Sandu discussed deepening cooperation in security, infrastructure, and energy. Both leaders reaffirmed their countries' joint pursuit of European Union membership, with negotiation clusters expected to open soon.

stories.title: Syria: First trial of Assad-era officials opens in Damascus
stories.summary: A court in Damascus opened the first trial of Assad-era officials, with defendant Atef Najib appearing in person and several others, including former president Bashar al-Assad and his brother, being tried in absentia. Assad and his brother are believed to have fled to Russia.

stories.title: Russian mercenaries in Mali: Limited gains, reports of abuse
stories.summary: Russian paramilitary forces operating in Mali have achieved limited success against jihadist groups, according to journalist Philip Obaji. Reports of abuses by the Moscow-backed fighters have mounted, raising questions about the effectiveness of Russia's military support for Mali's ruling junta.

stories.title: UNRWA’s West Bank schools drop to four-day weeks over funding issues, UN agency confirms to ‘Post’
stories.summary: UNRWA has reduced its West Bank school schedule to four-day weeks due to funding shortages. The agency laid off 571 staff members in January amid declining donations and ongoing criticism from Israel and monitoring organizations.

stories.title: UK blocks donation designated for the welfare of Ukrainian children in Israel
stories.summary: The United Kingdom blocked an $80,000 donation designated for the welfare of Ukrainian children in Israel, with the UK Treasury citing the risk of diverting funds from the Russia-Ukraine conflict.

stories.title: After week of killings, police chief says some murders ‘impossible to prevent’ as anger grows
stories.summary: Israeli Police Chief Danny Levi stated that some murders are impossible to prevent, following one of the bloodiest weeks in Israel this year with multiple killings across Jewish and Arab communities.

stories.title: New IRA suspected over car explosion outside Belfast police station
stories.summary: A car exploded outside a police station in Dunmurry, on the outskirts of Belfast, Northern Ireland, in an attack that caused no injuries. Police said they believe the New IRA dissident republican paramilitary group was responsible and are treating the incident as attempted murder.

stories.title: Ukraine calls on world to stop Russia’s nuclear blackmail on Chornobyl anniversary
stories.summary: On the 40th anniversary of the Chornobyl nuclear disaster, Ukraine's Foreign Ministry called on the international community to counter Russia's nuclear threats. The statement urged states committed to global stability to take action against what Kyiv described as nuclear blackmail.

stories.title: Environmental activists threaten High Court petition over data wipe
stories.summary: Israel's Environmental Protection Ministry removed all pollution permit data from its website, citing an emergency request related to Iran's alleged efforts to target industrial sites. Environmental activists are threatening a High Court petition over the data wipe.

stories.title: Attacks in Mali: Malian Defense Minister Sadio Camara killed by rebels
stories.summary: Mali's Defence Minister Sadio Camara was killed in a rebel attack, according to reports from France24. The killing occurred amid a broader escalation of violence between the Malian military and armed rebel groups operating in the country.

stories.title: Pogacar beats French teen Seixas to win 4th Liege-Bastogne-Liege
stories.summary: World cycling champion Tadej Pogačar won his fourth Liège-Bastogne-Liège classic and third consecutive title on Sunday, edging French teenager Paul Seixas in a closely contested finish in Belgium.

stories.title: Wildfires in Japan’s north worsen, 1,400 firefighters deployed
stories.summary: Japan deployed approximately 1,400 firefighters and Self-Defence Force personnel to combat mountain wildfires that have burned for five days in the country's north, threatening the coastal town of Otsuchi. Additional blazes broke out in Kitakata city and Nagaoka, straining firefighting resources across the region.

stories.title: Russia must return control of Zaporizhzhia NPP to Ukraine, halt attacks on energy infrastructure – European Commission
stories.summary: The European Commission marked the 40th anniversary of the Chornobyl disaster by calling on Russia to return control of the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant to Ukraine. The EU also demanded that Russia cease attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Iran foreign minister to return to Pakistan despite Trump cancelling envoys’ trip
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is expected to return to Pakistan for peace talks despite US President Donald Trump cancelling his envoys' planned trip to Islamabad. Araghchi previously met Pakistani officials before traveling to Oman.

stories.title: US-Iran conflict: What’s the latest as the Islamabad talks stall?
stories.summary: Washington and Tehran remain at an impasse during negotiations in Islamabad, Pakistan, as mediators seek a diplomatic breakthrough amid the ongoing US-Israeli military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: Florida is latest US state to enter redistricting war ahead of 2026 election
stories.summary: Florida's Republican-controlled legislature began a special session in Tallahassee to redraw congressional district maps ahead of the 2026 elections. The effort follows Virginia's redistricting and pressure from former President Trump on Republicans to protect their House majority, though no proposed map was previewed before the session.

stories.title: Scientists in China create a predator-like material to hunt for uranium in the ocean
stories.summary: Researchers at the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Qinghai Institute of Salt Lakes developed a light-powered metal-organic framework micromotor that can autonomously swim through water and capture uranium ions. The technology could advance nuclear fuel extraction from seawater and aid in radioactive pollution cleanup.

stories.title: Iran foreign minister returns to Pakistan despite Trump cancelling envoys’ trip
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Islamabad after visiting Oman, resuming peace talks with Pakistani officials including Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, despite the US cancelling its envoys' trip. He is also planning a visit to Moscow.

stories.title: Renewed violence in Mali raises fears of escalating Sahel crisis
stories.summary: Fresh fighting erupted in the northern Malian city of Kidal between Tuareg rebels backed by jihadists and government forces supported by Russian mercenaries. The violence follows coordinated nationwide attacks, including explosions and gunfire in the capital Bamako.

stories.title: Philippine officials say two Americans among suspected communist rebels killed in clash with troops
stories.summary: Philippine military forces killed suspected communist rebels in a clash, with officials confirming two Americans were among those killed. A government task force warned Americans of Filipino descent in the U.S. about recruitment by left-wing activist groups supporting Filipino insurgents, describing the process as "terror-grooming."

stories.title: One of the greatest tragedies of this war has been the collateral damage inflicted on Iran's medical facilities
stories.summary: US and Israeli strikes have damaged major Iranian medical facilities, including the century-old Pasteur Institute and the Tofigh Daru pharmaceutical complex in Tehran. The destruction has erased decades of global research and pharmaceutical innovation. Iranian medical staff have protested in front of destroyed hospitals in the capital.

stories.title: Netanyahu vows police, education action following ‘heinous’ Petah Tikvah killing
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu pledged police and education reforms after teenagers fatally stabbed a pizzeria worker in Petah Tikvah. Israel's police chief described the attack as an unpredictable incident difficult to prevent.

stories.title: Tickets for HBL PSL 11 final to go on sale from April 27
stories.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board announced that tickets for the HBL PSL 11 final would go on sale starting April 27. The final is scheduled for May 3 at Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore, with May 4 designated as a reserve day.

stories.title: Education Ministry says Finance Ministry data gaps blocked High Court update in haredi funding case
stories.summary: Israel's Education Ministry told the High Court that data gaps from the Finance Ministry prevented it from providing a required update in a case involving ultra-Orthodox (haredi) education funding. The ministry said it had requested relevant material but had not received all necessary data.

stories.title: Former Israeli ambassador to the UK appointed as head of PMO National Public Diplomacy Directorate
stories.summary: Israel's government unanimously approved former UK ambassador Tzipi Hotovely to lead the National Public Diplomacy Directorate within the Prime Minister's Office. Hotovely served as Israel's ambassador to the United Kingdom from 2020 to 2025.

stories.title: Here's how Lebanon can escape the US-Israeli peace process trap
stories.summary: Analyst Mona Deeley argues that Lebanon must establish clear objectives and leverage in negotiations with Israel to avoid an outcome similar to the Palestinian Authority's experience with US-Israeli peace frameworks.

stories.title: Mali rattled by ongoing armed attacks: What to know
stories.summary: Mali's security situation has worsened significantly in recent years, with armed groups carrying out coordinated attacks across the country targeting military and civilian sites.

stories.title: 40 years since the world’s worst nuclear disaster in Ukraine
stories.summary: April 2026 marks the 40th anniversary of the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster in Ukraine, which remains the worst nuclear accident in history.

stories.title: Israel feared Amal Khalil, just as it did Shireen Abu Akleh
stories.summary: Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil was killed by Israel, drawing comparisons to the 2022 killing of Palestinian-American journalist Shireen Abu Akleh. Both were targeted for their reporting on the conflict.

stories.title: Mali: Mali - Fresh Battle Breaks Out Between Tuareg Rebels, Government Forces in Kidal
stories.summary: Fresh fighting broke out in the northern Malian city of Kidal between Tuareg rebels and government forces backed by Russian mercenaries. Both rebel sources and a local politician confirmed the clashes to AFP.

stories.title: U.S. State Department emphasizes priority of nuclear safety on Chornobyl anniversary
stories.summary: The US State Department issued a statement on the 40th anniversary of the Chornobyl disaster emphasizing the importance of nuclear safety worldwide. The statement addressed safety concerns both at the Chornobyl site and at nuclear facilities globally.

stories.title: Ryanair to shut Berlin base as it blames rise in German aviation tax
stories.summary: Ryanair announced it will close its Berlin operating base and cut winter passenger numbers from 4.5 million to 2.2 million annually, citing increased German aviation taxes. The airline plans to relocate seven aircraft to other centers, with Berlin flights served by planes based at other airports from October onward.

stories.title: Mali defence minister killed after coordinated attacks
stories.summary: Mali's Defence Minister Sadio Camara was killed following coordinated attacks by armed groups on multiple military sites and his residence.

stories.title: Ukraine hits Russian military trains, oil refinery, air defense assets overnight
stories.summary: On April 25–26, Ukraine's Defense Forces struck an oil refinery in the Russian city of Yaroslavl and targeted Russian air defense assets in temporarily occupied Ukrainian territories. Ukrainian forces also hit Russian military trains during the overnight operations.

stories.title: Israel sent Iron Dome and troops to help defend UAE during Iran war – report
stories.summary: According to an Axios report, Israel deployed its Iron Dome missile defense system and troops to help defend the UAE during the Iran war, marking the first time the system has been used outside Israel and the United States.

stories.title: Syria's first trial of Assad-era officials opens in Damascus
stories.summary: Syria's first trial of officials from the Assad era opened in Damascus. Former President Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher were charged in absentia, along with several other high-ranking former security officials.

stories.title: Father, six-year-old son found dead in suspected murder-suicide
stories.summary: A father and his six-year-old son were found dead in Israel in a suspected murder-suicide involving a family member's firearm. Separately, a teenager was stabbed to death in northern Israel, prompting the police chief to acknowledge limits on preventing such killings.

stories.title: What lies ahead for Gaza after ceasefires in Iran and Lebanon?
stories.summary: With ceasefire agreements reached in the Iran and Lebanon conflicts, attention is shifting to Gaza, where negotiations remain deadlocked over Hamas's weapons and future governance arrangements.

stories.title: Brawny shekel threatens to knock out exporters, tech firms dependent on almighty dollar
stories.summary: The Israeli shekel has strengthened significantly, dropping below 3 NIS to the US dollar. Israeli exporters and tech companies paid in dollars warn they may need to cut costs, lay off workers, or relocate without government assistance.

stories.title: Israel appoints first ambassador to Somaliland after recognition of breakaway region
stories.summary: Israel appointed Michael Lotem, currently a roving economic envoy to Africa, as its first ambassador to Somaliland. Israel became the first country to recognize Somaliland's independence from Somalia.

stories.title: Global aid fleet sets sail from Italy to break Gaza siege
stories.summary: A multinational aid fleet departed from Italy bound for Gaza, aiming to break Israel's siege and deliver humanitarian assistance to the territory. The flotilla seeks to reach the devastated coastal enclave directly by sea.

stories.title: Death toll from Russian strikes on Dnipro rises to nine
stories.summary: The death toll from Russian evening strikes on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro rose to nine after another victim died in hospital. The strikes targeted the central Ukrainian city as part of ongoing Russian aerial attacks.

stories.title: Mali: Defense Minister Sadio Camara killed after jihadist attack
stories.summary: Mali's Defence Minister Sadio Camara was killed following attacks carried out by jihadist groups on April 25. The killing occurred amid a wave of coordinated violence across the country.

stories.title: Gunfire and blasts rock Mali: Army claims situation is under control
stories.summary: Gunfire and explosions were reported across Mali as the country experienced a wave of attacks. The Malian military claimed the security situation was being brought under control amid the escalating violence.

stories.title: Ukraine takes aim at Russia’s fuel lifeline, hits major refinery in Yaroslavl
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck a major oil refinery in Yaroslavl, Russia, which processes approximately 15 million tons of oil annually. The facility is a key supplier of fuel for Russian military logistics.

stories.title: Chernobyl 40th anniversary: A zone that must be sheltered
stories.summary: Commemorations marked the 40th anniversary of the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster in Ukraine. The exclusion zone around the former power plant remains a restricted area requiring ongoing containment and monitoring efforts.

stories.title: Israeli warplanes strike southern Lebanon, says state media
stories.summary: Israeli warplanes struck the town of Kfar Tibnit in southern Lebanon on Sunday, with reports of casualties, according to Lebanon's state-run National News Agency. The strikes occurred despite a ceasefire that took effect on 17 April. Israeli forces continue to occupy parts of southern Lebanon within a self-designated buffer zone.

stories.title: Toxins plus climate harms likely cause of reduced fertility, study finds
stories.summary: A new peer-reviewed study found that simultaneous exposure to endocrine-disrupting chemicals and climate change impacts such as heat stress likely produces additive or synergistic effects on reproductive harm. Researchers warned of alarming fertility declines observed across multiple global species, including humans.

stories.title: Lonely at the top: who are Keir Starmer’s allies as daunting May elections loom?
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces questions about his political support network as local elections in Scotland, Wales, and England approach in May. Many Labour MPs reportedly doubt he will lead the party into the next general election, though allies say he retains genuine friendships in and out of government.

stories.title: Iran must rollback its nuclear, missile program - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that a ceasefire with Iran is insufficient for lasting security and that Iran must dismantle both its nuclear program and missile development capabilities.

stories.title: Sri Lanka seeks investors for loss-making Mattala airport in Hambantota
stories.summary: Sri Lanka is seeking investors for the loss-making Mattala Rajapaksa International Airport in Hambantota, widely known as the "world's emptiest airport." India has previously expressed interest in operating the facility, including through a possible joint venture with a Russian company.

stories.title: Zelensky Accuses Russia of ‘Nuclear Terrorism’ on Chernobyl Anniversary
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accused Russia of "nuclear terrorism" during commemorations of the 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl disaster. The anniversary was marked amid continued Russian drone attacks on Ukrainian territory.

stories.title: President of Moldova arrives in Kyiv
stories.summary: Moldovan President Maia Sandu arrived in Kyiv on April 26 for a visit marking the 40th anniversary of the Chornobyl nuclear disaster. The trip underscored continued diplomatic engagement between Moldova and Ukraine.

stories.title: Pakistan PM dials Iranian President, discusses evolving regional situation
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister spoke with Iranian President Pezeshkian in a 50-minute phone call, discussing the evolving regional situation and ongoing efforts to promote peace and stability. Pakistan's Prime Minister's office described the conversation as warm and cordial.

stories.title: Lebanese prisons emptied of Hezbollah terrorists after two released on bail
stories.summary: Two Hezbollah suspects were released on bail from Lebanese prisons, reportedly leaving no remaining Hezbollah detainees in custody. The suspects had admitted to transporting 21 Grad missiles, 3,000 rounds of ammunition, and eight machine guns from the Bekaa Valley to southern Lebanon for use against the IDF.

stories.title: Iran's Araghchi discusses efforts to end war and Hormuz security with Oman
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met with Oman's Sultan Haitham bin Tariq al-Said in Muscat on Sunday. The talks focused on security in the Strait of Hormuz, broader Gulf stability, and diplomatic efforts to end the war on Iran. Araghchi called for a regional security framework without outside military presence.

stories.title: Shots fired at White House, prompting Trump's evacuation, as IDF strikes Hezbollah in Lebanon
stories.summary: Shots were fired near the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner, prompting the evacuation of President Trump. Separately, the IDF carried out strikes against Hezbollah targets in Lebanon.

stories.title: Drones attack Crimea overnight
stories.summary: Temporarily occupied Crimea was hit by a large-scale Ukrainian drone attack overnight on April 26. Explosions were reported near the Kacha and Belbek airfields, in Balaklava, near Sevastopol, and in the Bakhchysarai district.

stories.title: China launches Pakistani satellite
stories.summary: China launched Pakistan's PRSC-EO3 satellite at 8:15 p.m. Beijing Time using a Long March-6 carrier rocket. The satellite successfully entered its planned orbit.

stories.title: Syria puts first Assad-era official on trial in Damascus
stories.summary: Syria has opened its first public trial of a former Assad-era official in Damascus. Atef Najib, the former head of political security in Deraa province, faces charges of crimes against the Syrian people.

stories.title: New fighting in Mali's Kidal between army and rebels
stories.summary: Tuareg rebels of the Azawad Liberation Front coalition claimed to have seized the northern city of Kidal on Saturday, sparking renewed fighting with Mali's military. The clashes mark a fresh escalation of conflict in Mali's volatile northern region.

stories.title: Middle East shipping crisis elevates China-Europe railway’s profile
stories.summary: The China-Europe railway network, linking 235 cities across 26 European countries with over 120 Chinese cities, is gaining strategic importance following the US-Israel war on Iran. Middle East shipping disruptions have elevated the overland rail route as a key alternative for transcontinental supply chains.

stories.title: White House correspondents’ dinner shooting latest: Trump unharmed and suspect in custody after attack at Washington Hilton
stories.summary: A shooting occurred at the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents' Dinner, with a suspect taken into custody. President Trump was unharmed. A Secret Service officer injured in the attack was discharged from hospital, with officials noting a ballistic vest helped prevent a more serious outcome.

stories.title: China's Hengli Petrochemical denies trade with Iran in response to US sanctions
stories.summary: Chinese independent refiner Hengli Petrochemical denied any trade dealings with Iran after the United States sanctioned one of its subsidiaries for allegedly purchasing Iranian oil. In a stock exchange filing, Hengli stated that all its crude oil suppliers guaranteed their shipments fell outside the scope of US sanctions.

stories.title: Herzog pushes for new plea deal talks, says he won’t consider Netanyahu pardon request yet
stories.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog is pushing for new plea deal negotiations in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's corruption trial, according to reports confirmed by the president's office. Herzog indicated he wants to mediate between the attorney general and Netanyahu's lawyer but will not yet consider a pardon request.

stories.title: Suspect in Independence Day murder is son of senior figure in defense establishment
stories.summary: A 21-year-old named Zalka was killed in Israel last Tuesday in what is being investigated as a murder case. The Petah Tikva Magistrate's Court extended the detention of the main suspect, identified as the son of a senior figure in Israel's defense establishment, by five days.

stories.title: Video: Iranian-American activist speaks about diaspora split over US-Israeli war
stories.summary: Iranian-American political content creator Ariana Jasmine discussed the Iranian diaspora's divisions over Western intervention in an interview with Middle East Eye. She addressed the Pahlavi monarchist movement and her experience of opposing the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Israel kills four Palestinians across Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli attacks across the Gaza Strip killed at least four Palestinians on Sunday. The strikes were described as the latest violation of the ceasefire agreement reached in October.

stories.title: Shlomo Group turns to Indian technicians in NIS 50m service-center expansion
stories.summary: Israeli automotive conglomerate Shlomo Group opened a new service center in Holon as part of a NIS 50 million expansion. The company is employing trained Indian technicians alongside local staff to address a labor shortage in Israel's automotive service sector.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Defense Forces strike oil refinery in Yaroslavl
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces struck an oil refinery in the Russian city of Yaroslavl overnight on April 26. The attack was part of Ukraine's continuing campaign targeting Russian energy infrastructure deep inside Russian territory.

stories.title: Japan deploys 1,400 firefighters to battle raging wildfires in the north
stories.summary: Japan deployed approximately 1,400 firefighters to combat wildfires threatening residential districts in Otsuchi, on the Pacific Coast. As of early Sunday, April 26, 2026, the fires had consumed 1,373 hectares, a 7% increase from the previous day.

stories.title: Russian Strikes Kill Three, Wound Four in Ukraine
stories.summary: Russian strikes killed three people and wounded four in Ukraine, with casualties reported in the Sumy border region and the city of Dnipro. The attacks were part of ongoing Russian bombardment of Ukrainian civilian areas.

stories.title: Russian Strikes Kill Three, Wound 4 in Ukraine
stories.summary: Russian strikes killed three people and wounded four in Ukraine, with casualties reported in the border region of Sumy and the city of Dnipro.

stories.title: Tel Aviv  to choose new chief rabbi after High Court delays, political fight over representation
stories.summary: Tel Aviv is set to elect a new chief rabbi after the position has been vacant for nearly nine years since former chief rabbi Israel Meir Lau left office in 2017. The selection process has been delayed by High Court proceedings and political disputes over representation.

stories.title: 40 years since Chernobyl disaster: Soviet Union's 'top-down culture' partly to blame
stories.summary: Ukraine commemorated the 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl nuclear disaster on Sunday. Michael Bluck, Director of the Centre for Nuclear Engineering at Imperial College London, told FRANCE 24 that the Soviet Union's top-down authoritarian culture was among the factors that contributed to the 1986 explosion.

stories.title: China is poised to reap rewards as energy shock heats up the race for renewables
stories.summary: China's solar panel exports have helped Cuba increase solar power's share of national electricity generation from 6 percent to over 20 percent within a year, amid a US energy blockade. The development is cited as a model for reducing fossil fuel dependence during what analysts call the worst global energy crisis in history.

stories.title: Nighttime Russian attack sparks fire at infrastructure facility in Zhytomyr region
stories.summary: A Russian overnight attack on the Zhytomyr region of Ukraine caused a fire at an infrastructure facility. Ukrainian emergency services extinguished the blaze; no casualties were immediately reported.

stories.title: Russian strikes kill three, wound four in Ukraine
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack killed two civilians in the northeastern Ukrainian border region of Sumy, according to the head of Sumy's regional military administration. Across Ukraine, Russian strikes killed a total of three people and wounded four.

stories.title: Israeli forces storm West Bank polling station, injure six
stories.summary: Israeli forces raided a polling station in the occupied West Bank during local elections, injuring six people. The incident occurred amid an escalation of military raids and settler attacks across the territory.

stories.title: Voters contend with ‘grotesque’ leaflets and ‘dodgy’ data in English elections
stories.summary: A Full Fact investigation for the Guardian found that election leaflets distributed by local politicians across England contain misleading tactical voting claims for the May local elections. The leaflets use national polling data and questionable bar charts to assert that rival parties cannot win locally, despite lacking evidence to support such claims.

stories.title: Mali’s unholy alliance: Separatists and jihadists join forces to de-seat the junta
stories.summary: In Mali, separatist group FLA and jihadist organization Jnim have formed an unprecedented alliance against the ruling military junta. Strategic towns have fallen and Defence Minister Sadio Camara's residence was destroyed, signaling a dangerous escalation for President Goïta.

stories.title: Syria begins long-awaited first trial of Assad-era officials
stories.summary: The first public trial of an Assad-era official opened in Damascus on Sunday. Atef Najib, a former brigadier general who headed the Political Security Branch in Daraa province and is a cousin of Bashar al-Assad, appeared in court facing charges related to crimes against the Syrian people.

stories.title: China warns EU to remove firms and citizens from Russian sanctions list
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce demanded the European Union remove Chinese companies and individuals from its latest Russia-related sanctions list. Beijing warned it would take necessary measures to protect the rights and interests of its citizens and firms, urging dialogue to resolve the dispute.

stories.title: Israeli embassy worker in Washington describes 'shouting, panic' at White House dinner shooting
stories.summary: Israeli Embassy spokesperson Tal Naim described hearing shouting and widespread panic at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner in Washington after shots were fired. Naim said she was seated approximately 200 meters from the stage when the incident occurred.

stories.title: Cabinet approves ex-UK envoy Hotovely to lead National Public Diplomacy Directorate
stories.summary: Israel's cabinet unanimously approved former UK ambassador Tzipi Hotovely to head the National Public Diplomacy Directorate within the Prime Minister's Office, a position vacant for two years. Ministers also approved Doron Cohen as civil service commissioner.

stories.title: Pakistan PM dials Iranian President, discusses evolving regional situation
stories.summary: Pakistan's Prime Minister held a 50-minute phone call with Iran's President to discuss the evolving regional situation. The two leaders exchanged views on ongoing efforts to promote peace and stability in the region, according to Pakistan's Prime Minister's office.

stories.title: How the shooting at White House Correspondents' Dinner unfolded
stories.summary: A gunman opened fire at the Washington Hilton during the White House Correspondents' Association dinner on Saturday evening. Secret Service agents evacuated President Donald Trump and his cabinet from the ballroom. The suspect was subsequently taken into custody at the scene.

stories.title: Kenya’s Sawe is world’s first man to run a sub-two-hour marathon in London
stories.summary: Kenyan runner Sebastian Sawe became the first person to complete a marathon in under two hours, breaking Kelvin Kiptum's previous world record of 2:00:35 at the London Marathon. Ethiopia's Tigst Assefa retained her women's title at the same event.

stories.title: Zelensky on Chernobyl anniversary: Russia again putting world at risk of man-made disaster
stories.summary: On the 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl nuclear disaster, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called on the international community to prevent what he termed nuclear terrorism by Russia. Zelensky drew parallels between the 1986 catastrophe and current Russian threats to nuclear safety in Ukraine.

stories.title: Ukrainian Drone Attack on Sevastopol Kills 1 – Moscow-Installed Governor
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone struck the port city of Sevastopol in Russian-annexed Crimea, killing one person, according to the Moscow-installed governor. The attack damaged several homes and a dance school across multiple neighborhoods.

stories.title: UAE to establish $272m national fund for industrial resilience
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced a one-billion-dirham ($272 million) national fund to strengthen industrial resilience. Prime Minister Mohammed bin Rashid al-Maktoum said the fund will support localization of vital industries, supply chain resilience, and AI adoption in production and planning.

stories.title: China’s Li Auto targets BMW and Mercedes with premium SUVs in Middle East, Asia-Pacific
stories.summary: Beijing-based electric vehicle maker Li Auto is expanding into the Middle East and Asia-Pacific markets with premium SUVs designed to compete with BMW, Mercedes-Benz, and Audi. Company president Ma Donghui said overseas deliveries are expected to account for 30 percent of total sales by 2030.

stories.title: Taliban govt says Afghans in Qatar can return 'with confidence'
stories.summary: The Taliban government urged Afghan nationals in Qatar to return home, stating they could do so "with confidence." However, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned of ongoing arbitrary arrests and torture of former government officials in Afghanistan.

stories.title: Trump says shooting at press dinner 'won't deter him' from Iran war
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump was evacuated from the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner at the Washington Hilton after shots were fired outside the venue. Trump later told reporters the incident would not deter him from pursuing the war on Iran, adding the shooting was likely unrelated to the conflict.

stories.title: Fatah says it claimed ‘sweeping victory’ in local elections, despite democratic shortcomings
stories.summary: The Palestinian faction Fatah claimed a sweeping victory in local council elections, including in Jenin, where the Palestinian Authority had previously been accused of losing control to Hamas-linked Palestinian Islamic Jihad. The elections faced criticism over democratic shortcomings.

stories.title: Russian forces shell 18 settlements in Kharkiv region over past 24 hours, casualties reported
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled 18 settlements in Ukraine's Kharkiv region over a 24-hour period, resulting in civilian casualties. No further details on the scale of damage or specific locations were immediately provided by Ukrainian authorities.

stories.title: Lebanon won’t disarm Hezbollah, but will attack a 'generator owner'
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam criticized security forces for what he called unacceptable harsh actions following the arrest of a generator owner. The incident drew attention to a perceived double standard, as the Lebanese state has not moved to disarm Hezbollah.

stories.title: Mali’s Defence Minister Sadio Camara killed amid coordinated attacks
stories.summary: Mali's Defence Minister Sadio Camara was killed during coordinated attacks by armed groups. His death is considered a significant blow to Mali's ruling military government, which continues to fight insurgent forces across the country.

stories.title: Suspect at White House correspondents’ dinner shooting had multiple weapons, bulletproof vest: Trump
stories.summary: The suspect in the shooting at the White House correspondents' dinner has been identified as Cole Tomas Allen from California. President Trump described Allen as a "would-be assassin" who was carrying multiple weapons and a bulletproof vest.

stories.title: Ukrainians gather to remember Chernobyl disaster despite Russia’s war
stories.summary: Residents of Slavutych, Ukraine, gathered in the early hours of Sunday to commemorate the 40th anniversary of the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster, placing candles on a radiation hazard symbol in the central square. The annual vigil took place despite wartime curfews and warnings against large gatherings during Russia's ongoing war.

stories.title: Trump says shooting at press dinner 'won't deter him' from Iran war
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that a shooting incident at the White House Correspondents' Dinner on 25 April 2026 would not deter him from pursuing the war with Iran. A suspect armed with a shotgun, handgun, and multiple knives was detained. Trump said the incident was unlikely linked to the conflict.

stories.title: China backs Myanmar’s push to ease diplomatic isolation, stamp out telecoms scams
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi pledged support for Myanmar's new government to engage with multilateral platforms and combat telecoms scam operations. During a meeting with junta leader Min Aung Hlaing, Wang reaffirmed China's backing for Myanmar's sovereignty and territorial integrity.

stories.title: Rescuers show aftermath of shelling in Chernihiv region
stories.summary: Firefighters in Ukraine's Chernihiv region extinguished fires in Chernihiv city and the Borzna and Horodnia communities following Russian attacks on April 25 and the early morning of April 26. Rescuers documented the aftermath of the shelling.

stories.title: Daily Briefing April 26 – As both sides keep striking, is there still a Lebanon ceasefire?
stories.summary: Times of Israel military correspondent Emanuel Fabian discussed the IDF's readiness regarding Iran, the fragile state of the Lebanon ceasefire amid continued strikes by both sides, and the case of two Israeli Air Force technicians accused of spying for Iran.

stories.title: Death of Mali defence minister Sadio Camara deals a heavy blow to junta
stories.summary: Mali's defence minister Sadio Camara, a key ally of Russia in the Sahel, was killed in a car bomb attack at his residence in the garrison town of Kati. His death is a significant blow to the ruling military junta.

stories.title: Israel threatens residents in south Lebanon in leaflets dropped over Sour
stories.summary: The Israeli army dropped leaflets over Mansouri village in the Sour district of southern Lebanon, warning civilians against entering nearly two dozen villages in the area. Army spokesperson Avichay Adraee also renewed warnings against accessing areas around the Litani River and villages within an Israeli-established zone roughly 10 kilometers inside southern Lebanon.

stories.title: US intercepts sanctioned merchant vessel in Arabian Sea, Central Command says
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command announced it intercepted a sanctioned merchant vessel in the Arabian Sea on Saturday, April 25. The ship was reportedly attempting to breach the U.S. blockade on Iran.

stories.title: Netanyahu, Herzog among world leaders ‘shocked’ by shooting at gala attended by Trump
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu, President Herzog, and other world leaders expressed shock at the shooting outside the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner attended by President Trump. Multiple leaders condemned political violence and sent well-wishes to U.S. officials and attendees.

stories.title: At least four people killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza despite ‘ceasefire’
stories.summary: Israeli forces continued advancing into western Gaza, expanding their area of control in the east. At least four people were reported killed in Israeli attacks despite an ostensible ceasefire being in place.

stories.title: Salah to miss rest of Liverpool season, says Egypt team director
stories.summary: Egypt national team director Hassan announced that Liverpool forward Mohamed Salah will miss the remainder of the club's season due to injury. Hassan added that Salah is expected to be fit for the 2026 World Cup, where Egypt is drawn in Group G alongside Belgium, New Zealand, and Iran.

stories.title: Israel destroys solar panels in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli forces destroyed solar panels in southern Lebanon. No further details on the specific location or scale of the destruction were immediately available.

stories.title: ‘Coolcation’ trend heats up as travellers flee rising temperatures
stories.summary: A growing travel trend dubbed "coolcation" is seeing tourists choose cooler-climate destinations to escape rising temperatures. The shift is driven by intensifying global warming affecting traditional warm-weather vacation spots.

stories.title: Donald Trump says shooting won’t ‘deter’ him from Iran war
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump declared that a shooting incident would not deter him from pursuing the war with Iran. Trump had previously cancelled his envoys' trip to Pakistan, where peace talks with Iran were being arranged.

stories.title: Deadly Israeli strikes hit Lebanon despite ceasefire extension
stories.summary: Israeli forces carried out strikes in at least four locations in southern Lebanon late Saturday, reportedly killing six people despite a recently extended ceasefire. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the attacks on Hezbollah positions, citing alleged ceasefire violations.

stories.title: Israeli attacks kill 2,490 people in Lebanon since 2 March
stories.summary: The Lebanese health ministry reported that Israeli attacks on Lebanon since 2 March have killed 2,496 people and wounded at least 7,725. Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed four people on Saturday despite a ceasefire that had been extended by three weeks.

stories.title: Donald Trump says suspect was armed with multiple weapons at White House correspondents’ dinner
stories.summary: A suspect armed with multiple weapons opened fire near the White House correspondents' dinner in Washington, D.C. One law-enforcement officer was struck but survived thanks to a bulletproof vest. President Donald Trump reported the suspect carried several firearms.

stories.title: Loud bangs and a Trump evacuation: chaos at correspondents' dinner
stories.summary: The Secret Service evacuated President Trump from the White House correspondents' dinner at the Washington Hilton after loud gunshots erupted. Hundreds of guests ducked under tables as authorities swarmed the banquet hall to secure the venue.

stories.title: China unveils world’s first coal fuel cell that can produce electricity with zero emission
stories.summary: Chinese scientists have developed a direct coal fuel cell that generates electricity from coal without combustion, reportedly achieving higher energy efficiency than conventional coal-fired power while producing zero carbon dioxide emissions.

stories.title: Teen arrested in Louisiana shooting got ride from scene from grandmother
stories.summary: Markel Lee, 17, was arrested in connection with a mass shooting at a Louisiana mall that killed a high school senior and wounded five others. Investigators used surveillance video and license plate readers to track a car driven by Lee's grandmother, who had unknowingly given him a ride from the scene.

stories.title: China Gen Z snipers nicknamed ‘Sweetheart’, ‘Gun Queen’ challenge gender stereotypes
stories.summary: Two female Gen Z snipers in China's People's Armed Police have gained attention for their marksmanship. Liu Jiangtao, 26, from Chongqing, broke the women's record in a sniper selection test by firing three rounds through a single hole on a coin-sized target at hundreds of metres.

stories.title: Shelling in Donetsk region over past 24 hours kills two, wounds five
stories.summary: Two people were killed and five wounded by Russian shelling in the Donetsk region over the past 24 hours. The attacks struck the areas of Druzhkivka and Oleksievo-Druzhkivka.

stories.title: Above-normal temperature forecast in Punjab
stories.summary: Pakistan's Meteorological Department forecast hot and dry weather across Punjab on Sunday, with temperatures expected to remain above normal in the central and southern plains. A weakening westerly wave has reduced the chance of rain, leaving dry and humid conditions across the province.

stories.title: Preserving Israel’s military edge: Strategic steps for the MOD - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that shifting regional alliances, major arms deals, and rising threats are placing unprecedented pressure on Israel's qualitative military edge. The analysis calls for a new strategy by Israel's Ministry of Defense to preserve its technological and military advantages.

stories.title: Punjab to export livestock
stories.summary: Punjab province in Pakistan signed memorandums of understanding with seven institutions, including China's Global Meat Company, to export livestock and meat. Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz presided over the meeting, which outlined plans to export one million livestock and install a boiler unit in collaboration with the Punjab Agriculture and Meat Company.

stories.title: Bus blast in Colombia kills 13 amid rising violence
stories.summary: An explosive device detonated on a bus in southwestern Colombia on Saturday, killing 13 people and injuring at least 38. Colombia's army chief described the attack as a terrorist act, amid escalating violence linked to drug trafficking in the region.

stories.title: Measles claims lives of 71 children across country in four months
stories.summary: Seventy-one children have died of measles across Pakistan in the first four months of the year, including 40 in Sindh province. The deaths were reported as the country observed World Immunisation Week, with experts calling for local vaccine manufacturing to reduce dependence on imports.

stories.title: US cancels envoy travel, shifts from talks to pressure as Iran’s divisions deepen - analysis
stories.summary: The United States canceled planned envoy travel related to Iran diplomacy, signaling a shift from negotiations to a pressure-based strategy. The White House indicated willingness to sustain a long-term posture in its conflict with Iran, while Tehran also showed no urgency to resume talks.

stories.title: Yemen’s landmine crisis endures despite truce and de-mining efforts
stories.summary: Landmines across Yemen continue to cause civilian deaths and injuries despite an ongoing truce and active de-mining operations. The crisis persists as a legacy of the country's prolonged conflict.

stories.title: Iran FM heads to Russia for talks, as US cancels Islamabad visit
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi headed to Russia for diplomatic talks after the US canceled a planned visit to Islamabad. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that Iran would not negotiate under threats and blockade.

stories.title: Iran FM returns to Islamabad, as US envoys cancel visit
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi returned to Islamabad after US envoys canceled their planned visit to Pakistan. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that Iran would not negotiate under threats or blockade conditions.

stories.title: Iran refuses 'imposed' talks with US as envoys cancel visit
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that Iran would not engage in negotiations under threats and blockade, rejecting what Tehran characterized as imposed talks with the United States. U.S. envoys reportedly canceled a planned visit amid the impasse.

stories.title: Raghu Rai, legendary Indian photographer, dies at 83
stories.summary: Raghu Rai, the acclaimed Indian photographer and Magnum Photos member, has died at the age of 83. His decades-long career documented pivotal moments in India's modern history.

stories.title: 2 US citizens killed in raid on Philippines communist stronghold
stories.summary: Two U.S. citizens were among 19 people killed in a military raid on an alleged communist stronghold in the Toboso municipality of Negros Island, Philippines, on April 19. Over 300 residents fled their homes during the operation, and the Philippines Commission on Human Rights has launched a probe.

stories.title: First section of Fanling Bypass to open soon. So how will Hongkongers benefit?
stories.summary: The eastern section of Hong Kong's Fanling Bypass is set to open on May 3, marking the first major transport infrastructure project completed under the Northern Metropolis development plan. The 4-kilometer roadway is expected to reduce travel times by 10 minutes and serve the Fanling North New Development Area.

stories.title: Tel Aviv Museum of Art reimagines exhibitions amid wartime conditions
stories.summary: The Tel Aviv Museum of Art is adapting its programming amid wartime conditions in Israel, bringing art experiences into safe rooms and bomb shelters. The changes come as museums face closures and ongoing air-raid sirens disrupt normal operations.

stories.title: War, memory, and metal: Yaacov Dorchin’s latest Tel Aviv exhibition
