stories.summary: An editorial commentary discusses India's position one year after the Pahalgam attack in Indian-administered Kashmir, noting that India has not achieved the diplomatic isolation of Pakistan it sought. Pakistan's Information Minister Ataullah Tarar stated India has not presented solid evidence regarding the Pahalgam incident.

stories.title: Two bodies recovered from rubble in Dnipro, injury toll rises to 21
stories.summary: Rescuers in the Ukrainian city of Dnipro recovered two bodies from the rubble of a residential building destroyed during a nighttime Russian attack. The injury toll rose to 21, with up to five more people possibly trapped under debris.

stories.title: Watch: Iran says no direct talks with U.S. in Islamabad planned
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi visited Pakistan but Tehran ruled out direct face-to-face talks with the United States in Islamabad. Iran said Pakistan would serve as a mediator rather than a venue for direct US-Iran negotiations.

stories.title: Palestinians to vote in first elections since Gaza war
stories.summary: Palestinians are set to vote in their first elections since the Gaza war, with nearly 1.5 million people registered in the West Bank and approximately 70,000 registered in Gaza's Deir el-Balah area.

stories.title: Trump cancels US envoys' trip to Pakistan for Iran talks
stories.summary: President Trump cancelled the trip of U.S. envoys to Pakistan that had been planned for Iran-related negotiations. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi had already departed Pakistan after holding key talks with Pakistani officials as mediation efforts intensified.

stories.title: Iran's Araghchi exits Pakistan before US envoys for talks
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi departed Pakistan after holding talks in Islamabad, leaving before U.S. envoys were due to arrive. The diplomatic activity was part of intensifying mediation efforts between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Iran FM lands in Islamabad as fragile peace efforts resume
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Islamabad for diplomatic talks that could help revive US-Iran peace negotiations. Regional tensions remain elevated amid ongoing conflicts.

stories.title: Iran defence ministry says US seeks 'face-saving' way out of war
stories.summary: Iran's defence ministry stated that the United States is seeking a "face-saving" exit from the ongoing war. A ministry spokesperson said Iran's military power is now a dominant force, according to the ISNA news agency.

stories.title: Displaced Lebanese remain skeptical despite extended truce
stories.summary: Displaced Lebanese families sheltering in the coastal city of Sidon expressed skepticism about an extended truce between Lebanon and Israel. Despite expressions of optimism from U.S. President Donald Trump, ongoing strikes and deep mistrust prevent many civilians from returning home.

stories.title: Scan, switch, sanction—the app turning Western shoppers into Russia’s exit enforcers
stories.summary: A new consumer app allows Western shoppers to scan products and identify companies still operating and paying taxes in Russia. Approximately 2,300 large Western firms continue to have a tax-paying presence in Russia despite the conflict in Ukraine.

stories.title: “We don’t need voters, we need consumers”: Inside the app squeezing Western companies out of Russia
stories.summary: A mobile application is helping squeeze Western companies out of the Russian market by redirecting consumers to domestic alternatives. Approximately 2,300 large Western firms continue to pay taxes in Russia despite international sanctions.

stories.title: US envoys to travel to Islamabad despite Iran ruling out direct negotiations with US
stories.summary: U.S. envoys are expected to travel to Islamabad to attempt to salvage ceasefire talks with Iran, even as Tehran has ruled out direct negotiations with American representatives. An indefinite ceasefire has paused most fighting, but the closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues to disrupt global energy shipments.

stories.title: Mali live: Army says armed 'terrorist' groups launch attacks on military positions nationwide
stories.summary: Mali's army reported on Saturday that unidentified armed groups attacked military positions in the capital Bamako and several towns in the country's interior. Journalists reported hearing gunfire near Mali's international airport, with fighting described as ongoing.

stories.title: Russian strikes leave four civilians killed, 17 injured in Kherson region
stories.summary: In Ukraine's Kherson region, Russian air and artillery strikes killed four civilians and injured 17 others on April 24. The attacks continued a pattern of Russian bombardment targeting populated areas in the southern region.

stories.title: Israel threatens residents against returning to south Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli army, through spokesperson Avichay Adraee, warned Lebanese residents against returning to their homes in southern Lebanon. Israel said access to areas near the Litani River, Wadi Salhania, and Saluki is prohibited, and that Israeli forces continue to occupy large swaths of southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Peru police raid ex-election chief’s home amid widening probe
stories.summary: Peruvian police raided the homes of former elections chief Piero Corvetto and five other officials on Friday as part of a probe into ballot shortages and irregularities during the April 12 presidential election. Corvetto resigned on Tuesday, taking responsibility for the shortcomings while denying wrongdoing.

stories.title: West Bank and part of Gaza vote in first municipal elections since war
stories.summary: Municipal elections were held in the occupied West Bank and central Gaza, marking the first vote since the Gaza war. Fatah-linked candidate lists were dominant, while Hamas did not participate in the elections.

stories.title: Social media post lands citizen in jail amid security alert in Islamabad
stories.summary: Police in Islamabad arrested a citizen for posting a social media joke comparing the Tarnol railway crossing to the Strait of Hormuz during a heightened security alert. Charges were filed under multiple sections of the Pakistan Penal Code.

stories.title: Who pays and how?
stories.summary: An opinion piece discusses the international law of torts and state liability for transboundary harm, citing historical cases including Poland's reparations to Germany over a seized factory and Canada's compensation to the United States for cross-border smelter damage. The article frames military aggression as the most severe form of such harm.

stories.title: The US protected Hormuz shipping from Iranian attacks in the ’80s. Could it again?
stories.summary: Analysts say replicating the US Navy's 1980s "Tanker War" protection of Hormuz shipping would be challenging today due to small IRGC gunboats and ambitious US strategic objectives in the context of the current Iran conflict.

stories.title: U.S. military strike on alleged drug boat kills 2 in eastern Pacific
stories.summary: A US military strike on an alleged drug-trafficking vessel in the eastern Pacific killed two people. The incident is part of an ongoing Trump administration campaign targeting suspected narcotics boats in Latin American waters that has killed at least 183 people since early September.

stories.title: Gunmen stage simultaneous attacks across Mali, army says
stories.summary: The Malian army reported that gunmen staged apparently coordinated simultaneous attacks in the capital Bamako and several other locations, involving multiple armed groups.

stories.title: Spain PM brushes of reported Pentagon email on punishing NATO members
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez dismissed reports that the Pentagon is considering punishing NATO members who do not support U.S. operations in the Iran war. Spain has refused to allow U.S. forces involved in the conflict to use its bases or airspace, citing violations of international law.

stories.title: Araghchi’s Islamabad visit ‘bodes well’ for US dialogue
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Islamabad carrying Tehran's formal response to US proposals conveyed through Pakistan. US envoys Witkoff and Kushner are preparing to travel to Islamabad as diplomatic activity intensifies amid the US-Iran conflict.

stories.title: War update: 236 combat clashes on frontline over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces reported 236 combat engagements with Russian troops along the frontline over the past day on April 24. The clashes occurred across multiple sectors of the front.

stories.title: Lebanon truce
stories.summary: An editorial comments on the three-week extension of the Israel-Lebanon truce, which was negotiated under US mediation in Washington. The piece questions Israel's long-term intentions in Lebanon and the broader Middle East, suggesting the ceasefire may not reflect a genuine pursuit of peace.

stories.title: 🔴 Mali military says armed 'terrorist groups' launch attacks on positions nationwide
stories.summary: Mali's military reported that armed groups it described as "terrorist" launched attacks on military positions across the country, including in the capital Bamako.

stories.title: Tunisia suspends rights group amid widening repression
stories.summary: Tunisian authorities ordered one of Africa's oldest human rights organizations to suspend its activities for one month. Critics say the move is part of a widening crackdown as the country shifts toward authoritarian governance.

stories.title: Mojtaba Khamenei remains out of the spotlight in Iran
stories.summary: Mojtaba Khamenei, named Iran's new supreme leader after the death of his father, has remained out of public view, fueling speculation he was seriously injured in the strike that killed Ayatollah Ali Khamenei nearly two months ago. The New York Times reported he is living in hiding and communicates through handwritten notes.

stories.title: Eyewitnesses say gunfire and explosions rock several districts in Mali
stories.summary: Eyewitnesses reported gunfire and explosions across several districts in Mali, including near the main military base in Kati. Kati is the hometown of junta leader General Assimi Goïta.

stories.title: Court cancels bail of YouTuber Rajab Butt over his absence
stories.summary: A sessions court in Karachi cancelled the interim bail of Pakistani YouTuber Rajab Butt due to his absence from proceedings in a case alleging he hurt religious sentiments under Section 295-A of the Pakistan Penal Code.

stories.title: ‘Astonishing’ discovery could help save children from deadly disfiguring condition
stories.summary: Researchers have identified a previously unknown species of bacteria in patients with noma, a neglected tropical disease that destroys facial tissue and is fatal in 90% of untreated cases. The discovery may lead to improved methods for preventing, detecting, and treating the childhood condition.

stories.title: Criminalisation of climate protesters in UK is counterproductive, research finds
stories.summary: A UK study of 1,300 climate campaigners found that criminalizing direct-action protests through arrests, fines, and prison sentences is counterproductive. Researchers concluded that such measures increase activists' determination to undertake disruptive demonstrations and may contribute to radicalization.

stories.title: US State Dept orders global warning about alleged China AI thefts by DeepSeek, others
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department issued a global advisory alleging that Chinese AI companies, including DeepSeek, have engaged in intellectual property theft. The Chinese Embassy in Washington rejected the accusations, stating that China is committed to protecting intellectual property rights.

stories.title: Injuries, widespread damage reported as Russia attacks Odesa region overnight
stories.summary: Russian forces conducted a large-scale drone attack on Ukraine's Odesa region overnight, injuring two people and causing widespread damage. The attack targeted civilian areas of the southern Ukrainian region.

stories.title: A city back on its feet after a month of war: The 2026 Jerusalem Marathon experience
stories.summary: The 2026 Jerusalem Marathon took place as the city sought to recover after a month of war. Organizers and participants highlighted a spirit of persistence and resilience despite the recent conflict.

stories.title: Top Iranian and Pakistani officials meet in Islamabad
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi traveled to Islamabad for talks with Pakistani officials. US envoys were also expected to arrive in the Pakistani capital for separate discussions.

stories.title: First batch of Gul Plaza traders receives compensation
stories.summary: Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah distributed Rs511.7 million in compensation to 200 of 1,209 shopkeepers affected by the January 17 fire at Gul Plaza in Karachi. He pledged accountability based on findings of a Judicial Commission investigating the blaze.

stories.title: Palestinians in West Bank and some in Gaza vote in local elections
stories.summary: Local elections were held across the occupied West Bank and in one city in Gaza. Hamas and several other Palestinian factions did not participate in the vote.

stories.title: US accuses civil rights group of defrauding donors with payments to extremist informants
stories.summary: The US government has accused the Southern Poverty Law Center of defrauding donors through payments to extremist informants under a now-defunct program. The charges follow the FBI's decision to cut ties with the organization after it listed slain conservative activist Charlie Kirk's group as extremist.

stories.title: Overnight Russian attacks on Ukraine kill five, injure 30
stories.summary: Russia launched over 600 drones and 47 missiles targeting eight regions across Ukraine, with the city of Dnipro among the hardest hit. The overnight attacks killed at least five people and injured 30.

stories.title: Russian drone attack on Mykolaiv region leaves two injured, power line damaged
stories.summary: In Ukraine's Mykolaiv region, Russian drone attacks injured two people and damaged a power transmission line, causing power outages. The strikes continued Russia's pattern of targeting both civilians and energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Stranded seafarers face peril in Hormuz
stories.summary: Indian seafarer Ankit Yadav and three fellow mariners have been stranded at an inland Iranian port for roughly two and a half weeks, surviving on limited rations. They are among thousands of seafarers from multiple nations stuck in and around the Strait of Hormuz as conflict in Iran disrupts one of the world's busiest shipping routes.

stories.title: Polls open in Gaza area in first municipal election in 20 years
stories.summary: Gaza's city of Deir el-Balah held its first municipal election in roughly 20 years, described by officials as a pilot vote. The occupied West Bank also conducted its first local polls since the 2023 war.

stories.title: Man whose coexistence kippa was carved up by Israel Police asks ‘what is in store for us’
stories.summary: Israeli police detained writer and peace activist Alex Sinclair after he wore a kippa featuring both Israeli and Palestinian flags. Officers reportedly cut up the head covering, prompting Sinclair to warn publicly about the country's direction toward illiberalism.

stories.title: JUI-F to boycott CM Bugti-led govt over madressah action
stories.summary: Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI-F) Balochistan leader Senator Maulana Abdul Wasay announced a boycott of Chief Minister Bugti's coalition government, alleging provincial operations against madressahs across Balochistan. The provincial government has moved to strengthen madressah registration and identified around 300 unregistered seminaries.

stories.title: Only essential goods exempt as twin cities on high alert
stories.summary: Islamabad's district administration granted special passage to vehicles carrying petroleum products, food, and medicines amid heightened security for foreign delegates arriving for US-Iran talks. Deputy Commissioner Irfan Memon said authorities were coordinating with food distributors, pharmaceutical companies, and petrol pump owners across the twin cities.

stories.title: Pakistan gains from global ‘Big Catch-Up’ vaccination drive
stories.summary: Gavi, the WHO, and UNICEF announced the "Big Catch-Up" vaccination drive has reached an estimated 18.3 million children across 36 countries, administering over 100 million vaccine doses. Pakistan was among the countries that benefited significantly from the initiative.

stories.title: Ukraine downs 610 aerial targets used by Russia in overnight attack
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 610 aerial targets during a Russian overnight attack beginning on the evening of April 24, including 30 missiles and 580 drones. The large-scale assault represented a significant wave of Russian aerial bombardment.

stories.title: ‘Racism is a cancer’: Indigenous leaders condemn orchestrated booing at Anzac Day ceremonies
stories.summary: Indigenous speakers were booed during welcome to country ceremonies at Anzac Day dawn services in Sydney, Melbourne, and Perth. Indigenous leaders and army captain Uncle Jack Pearson condemned the heckling as racist and contrary to the Anzac spirit.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Witkoff and Kushner head to Pakistan for talks; Israel strikes Lebanon despite ceasefire
stories.summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner traveled to Islamabad for talks, while Iran's foreign minister also arrived in Pakistan. Iran's foreign ministry stated there would be no direct negotiations with the US. Separately, Israel carried out strikes in Lebanon despite an existing ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: SCMP scoops 74 awards, led by Hong Kong fencing infographic in design competition
stories.summary: The South China Morning Post won 74 awards at the 47th Best of News Design Creative Competition organized by the Society for News Design. An infographic on Hong Kong's fencing boom was the leading entry, earning three silver and one bronze medal.

stories.title: US imposes sanctions on Chinese ‘teapot’ refinery for buying Iranian oil
stories.summary: The United States imposed sanctions on a Chinese independent "teapot" refinery for purchasing Iranian oil. China's government called on Washington to cease what it described as abusing sanctions to target Chinese companies.

stories.title: Ireland to demand Israel pay for settler demolition of Palestinian school
stories.summary: Ireland plans to demand that Israel reimburse the cost of a Palestinian school demolished by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Karachi’s collective trauma
stories.summary: A report describes the severe deterioration of University Road in Karachi, a major arterial route now largely reduced to dirt and rocks. The piece highlights the daily hazards faced by commuters and pedestrians, including students, who must navigate the damaged roadway.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: Islamabad remained under security lockdown as US and Iranian envoys arrived in Pakistan's capital. Iran stated no direct meeting with US officials was planned and would only convey its position through Pakistani mediators. Tensions over the Strait of Hormuz continued to affect global trade and energy markets.

stories.title: ‘Athens cannot operate as a giant hotel’: mayor vows to rescue capital from overtourism
stories.summary: Athens mayor Haris Doukas warned that the Greek capital, home to 700,000 residents hosting 8 million tourists annually, faces over-saturation from mass tourism. The socialist mayor pledged to reclaim congested city-centre neighbourhoods for local residents as tourist season begins.

stories.title: Russia’s war casualty toll in Ukraine up by 1,230 over past day
stories.summary: Russia's cumulative combat losses in Ukraine reached approximately 1,324,690 personnel from February 24, 2022, to April 25, 2026, according to Ukrainian military reports. Russian forces lost an estimated 1,230 troops in the most recent 24-hour period.

stories.title: US freezes $439 million in cryptocurrency linked to Iran: Treasury chief
stories.summary: U.S. Treasury officials announced the freezing of $439 million in cryptocurrency linked to Iran. Washington said the action targets both traditional sanctions evasion methods and newer technologies used to circumvent financial restrictions.

stories.title: Hezbollah says ceasefire ‘meaningless’ as fighting continues
stories.summary: Hezbollah declared the US-mediated ceasefire with Israel "meaningless" following its three-week extension, as Lebanese authorities reported two people killed by an Israeli strike and Hezbollah downed an Israeli drone. The Israeli military said its forces killed six Hezbollah fighters during a clash in the southern Lebanese town of Bint Jbeil.

stories.title: Pentagon claims full Hormuz blockade as world feels fuel crunch
stories.summary: Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth claimed a full blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, saying 34 ships had been turned around, though Hapag-Lloyd reported one vessel passed through. EU leaders met in Cyprus seeking a diplomatic resolution to the shipping crisis.

stories.title: Iran hangs man for role in protests, claims he was working for Mossad
stories.summary: Iran executed a man linked to anti-regime protests, claiming he was an operative working for Israel's Mossad intelligence agency. Since mid-March, Iran has put to death nine people connected to the protest movement amid its escalating conflict with Israel and the United States.

stories.title: Pakistan among top 10 countries facing acute food crisis
stories.summary: A UN-backed report identified Pakistan among the top 10 countries facing acute food insecurity, with over nine million Pakistanis in crisis conditions. Severe monsoon flooding destroyed crucial cropland and livelihoods, worsening hunger across the country.

stories.title: Trump seeks to bring back  firing squads  for executions
stories.summary: The US Justice Department announced plans to expand federal death penalty methods to include firing squads, electrocution, and gas alongside lethal injection. Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche said the move aims to enforce capital punishment against the most dangerous criminals.

stories.title: Injury toll in Russia’s massive overnight attack on Dnipro rises to 14, including minor
stories.summary: The injury toll from a massive Russian overnight attack on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro rose to 14, including a child. Homes, vehicles, and businesses across the city sustained damage from the strikes.

stories.title: US uses unusual routes to send jet fuel to Japan, Philippine bases amid Hormuz closure
stories.summary: The US Defense Logistics Agency issued a request to ship 235,000 barrels of military-grade jet fuel from Cherry Point in Blaine, Washington, to Subic Bay in the Philippines. The unusual Pacific routing reflects disruptions to global oil supply chains caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz amid the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Palestinian Authority local elections start for first time in years, including voters from Gaza
stories.summary: The Palestinian Authority held local elections in the West Bank and the Gazan city of Deir al-Balah, the first such vote since the October 7, 2023, attacks. The elections mark a significant political event for Palestinians in both territories.

stories.title: Could hair or cosmetics be make-or-break factors for China’s would-be civil servants?
stories.summary: China's state media issued appearance guidelines for civil service exam candidates, advising modest dress, light makeup for women, and short hair for men. The guidance comes as competition for government positions has intensified, with civil service jobs long regarded as secure employment in China.

stories.title: Major Russia drone and missile attack kills several, wounds dozens in Ukraine
stories.summary: Russia launched more than 660 drones and missiles at Ukraine overnight on Friday, killing four people and injuring over 30. The eastern city of Dnipro suffered major strikes that damaged buildings, prompting rescue teams to search for survivors trapped under rubble on Saturday morning.

stories.title: Lessons in mediation
stories.summary: An analysis examines Pakistan's evolving role in US-Iran diplomacy, noting that Islamabad shifted from quietly passing messages between the two adversaries to hosting delegations and publicly positioning itself as a mediator. The escalation to all-out war at the end of February prompted this more ambitious diplomatic engagement.

stories.title: Islamabad locked down as envoys arrive for talks
stories.summary: Large parts of Islamabad were placed under tight security lockdown for over a week as uncertainty surrounded a potential second round of US-Iran talks. Key roads and the Red Zone were sealed. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were expected, but Iranian officials said no direct talks were planned.

stories.title: ‘Exodus’: When Hollywood still loved the Jewish state
stories.summary: The article discusses the 1960 film "Exodus," starring Paul Newman, and its portrayal of Israel. It reflects on a period when Hollywood expressed strong support for the Jewish state.

stories.title: Iran says deep-buried 'bunker-buster' bomb neutralised
stories.summary: Iranian authorities announced they safely neutralized an unexploded bunker-buster bomb in Yazd Province that had been buried approximately 13 meters underground in a residential area after failing to detonate. The operation was carried out jointly by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and local bomb disposal units.

stories.title: Russian strikes hit residential building, transport infrastructure in Kharkiv
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a multi-story residential building in the Saltivskyi district of Kharkiv, Ukraine, damaging civilian infrastructure and transport facilities in the city.

stories.title: Iran war is tearing the polyester fabric of fast fashion – and shoes could be next
stories.summary: Rising fossil fuel prices linked to the Iran conflict are increasing costs for polyester feedstocks such as PTA and MEG by nearly 30 percent. Indian producer Filatex and garment makers in India and Bangladesh face squeezed margins, threatening higher prices for fast-fashion retailers including Zara and H&M.

stories.title: West Bank scepticism as Palestinians doubt local elections will change much
stories.summary: Palestinians in the West Bank are expressing widespread apathy ahead of local municipal elections, citing frustration with the Palestinian Authority and the ongoing Israeli occupation as reasons for low voter enthusiasm.

stories.title: US sanctions China’s ‘teapot’ refinery for buying Iranian oil
stories.summary: The United States has imposed sanctions on China's Hengli refinery for purchasing Iranian oil. The US Treasury stated the refinery has generated hundreds of millions of dollars in revenue for Iran's military.

stories.title: China acquired capacity to build 50 nuclear power reactors simultaneously: Official report
stories.summary: China's total installed nuclear power capacity has reached 125 million kilowatts, ranking first globally, according to a China Nuclear Energy Association report cited by state broadcaster CCTV. Officials say China has acquired the capacity to build 50 nuclear reactors simultaneously.

stories.title: Russian strike spotter in Odesa jailed for 15 years for treason
stories.summary: A court in Ukraine sentenced a Russian intelligence agent to 15 years in prison with confiscation of property for directing missile and drone strikes on the city of Odesa.

stories.title: Africa: 'We Are at a Critical Point in the Fight Against Malaria' #WorldMalariaDay
stories.summary: Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, reported that the rollout of malaria vaccines across Africa is the fastest in its history. Twenty-five African countries have introduced malaria vaccines into routine immunization programs, with early data showing reduced severe disease and hospital admissions.

stories.title: Cory Bernardi repays more than $40,000 for flying on Gina Rinehart’s plane during SA election campaign
stories.summary: Former Liberal senator Cory Bernardi, now One Nation's South Australian leader, repaid more than A$40,000 to Gina Rinehart's company S Kidman & Co for private flights taken during the state's recent election campaign. The reimbursement was made to comply with new South Australian laws prohibiting electoral donations from individuals.

stories.title: India-Germany defence road map ‘good template’ for wider EU cooperation
stories.summary: India and Germany signed a Defence Industrial Cooperation Road Map in Berlin, with Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and German counterpart Boris Pistorius agreeing to deepen collaboration in development, production, and niche technologies. Experts say the agreement could help India modernize its submarine fleet and expand Europe's security role in the Indo-Pacific.

stories.title: Flood of small parcels from China pushes Belgian airport’s capacity to limit
stories.summary: Liege airport in Belgium is receiving more than 4 million small parcels daily from China, overwhelming its 80-member customs inspection team. Belgium's top customs official Kristian Vanderwaeren noted the facility was built partly to serve e-commerce platforms such as Shein, Temu, and Alibaba but faces an explosion in parcel volumes.

stories.title: Voting underway in West Bank, parts of Gaza
stories.summary: Palestinians in the West Bank and parts of the Gaza Strip began voting in municipal elections, the first since the war that started in October 2023. Nearly 1.5 million people were registered to vote in the West Bank and about 70,000 in Gaza's Deir el-Balah area.

stories.title: France voices concern about the spread of Islamist extremism in Sahel
stories.summary: France expressed concern about the spread of Islamist extremism in the Sahel region. Military regimes in Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger had previously forced the withdrawal of French troops that were involved in counterterrorism operations.

stories.title: Israel-Iran war LIVE: Iran says no direct talks with U.S. in Islamabad planned
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson said no direct talks with the United States are planned in Islamabad. Pakistani officials will serve as intermediaries, conveying messages between the Iranian and American delegations.

stories.title: Ukraine’s envoy urges global sanctions on Russia’s nuclear industry at UN Commemoration of Chornobyl
stories.summary: Ukraine's Permanent Representative to the UN, Andrii Melnyk, called on countries to impose coordinated sanctions on Russia's nuclear energy sector at a UN commemoration of the Chornobyl disaster, citing Moscow's actions involving Ukrainian nuclear facilities.

stories.title: Palestinians vote in municipal elections in Gaza, West Bank
stories.summary: Palestinians voted in municipal elections in the occupied West Bank and part of Gaza, marking the first vote since the Gaza war began. The elections took place amid widespread political disillusionment.

stories.title: U.S. won't renew Iranian, Russian oil waivers: Bessent
stories.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced Washington will not renew oil waivers for Iran and Russia as global energy markets face disruption from the US-Israeli war in Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Capture of ships by US, Iran violates international law, shipping body says
stories.summary: The International Chamber of Shipping stated that the seizure of vessels by both the United States and Iran violates international law. The organization's director called on both countries to immediately release the crews of the captured ships.

stories.title: PA holds local elections, including first in parts of Gaza since 2007 Hamas takeover
stories.summary: The Palestinian Authority held local elections in the West Bank and in Deir al-Balah in Gaza, marking the first such vote in parts of Gaza since Hamas took control in 2007. Only President Abbas's Fatah faction fielded a party slate, and the Gaza vote was largely symbolic.

stories.title: India to exit Chabahar port stake amid sanctions pressure
stories.summary: India is reportedly planning to sell its stake in Iran's Chabahar Port to an Iranian company following the expiration of a US sanctions exemption. An interim arrangement may allow an Iranian operator to manage the port during the sanctions period, with India potentially resuming operations afterward.

stories.title: Israeli court uncovers covert Hamas funding network, key figures sentenced
stories.summary: An Israeli court exposed a covert financial network that funnelled millions of dollars to Hamas through intermediaries operating within Israel. Key figures in the network, which supported activities in Gaza and the West Bank, were sentenced.

stories.title: Russian attack on Dnipro leaves four people injured, house destroyed
stories.summary: A combined Russian missile-and-drone attack on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro partially destroyed a residential building and injured four people.

stories.title: ‘Toughest stance’: Hong Kong launches 18 operations against illegal fuel stations
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities launched 18 joint operations against illegal refuelling stations in 2025 amid a global energy price surge. Customs Commissioner Chan Tsz-tat said the practice has become more common in urban areas but is not yet widespread locally.

stories.title: As Iran tries to wipe Israel off the map, a museum charts those who first put it on
stories.summary: The Israel Museum in Jerusalem reopened an exhibition exploring maps produced from the 15th to 19th centuries that blended geography with biblical beliefs and contemporary politics. The exhibition charts the historical cartographic representation of the region.

stories.title: Russia's Lavrov says US discarding international conventions, pursuing its own interests
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov accused the United States of abandoning internationally recognized diplomatic conventions to pursue its own interests, particularly in dominating global energy markets.

stories.title: British professor uncovers location of Shakespeare’s London home using previously unknown documents
stories.summary: British professor Munro identified the location of William Shakespeare's London home using previously unknown documents. The discovery challenges prior assumptions about where the playwright spent his later years.

stories.title: How the Walsall rapist John Ashby exposed his misogyny rapping online
stories.summary: John Ashby, 32, of Walsall, England, was sentenced to life in prison with a minimum of 14 years for a racially motivated sexual attack on a Sikh woman. Investigators found he had posted hate-filled and misogynistic content online through rap videos prior to the attack.

stories.title: 7,000-year history of China stilted houses celebrates human ingenuity, offers insights
stories.summary: Stilted houses known as ganlan, with a 7,000-year history in China, are highlighted as a significant element of East Asian architectural heritage. The fishing village of Tai O on Lantau Island in Hong Kong is cited as a notable destination where visitors can experience these traditional structures.

stories.title: Malaysia gets new anti-corruption chief as protests mount against outgoing head
stories.summary: Malaysia appointed a former judge as its new anti-corruption chief amid mounting protests against outgoing Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission head Azam Baki. The move follows months of political turbulence over alleged misconduct, including a share ownership scandal linked to Baki, that has drawn criticism of Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.

stories.title: Elections without sovereignty: What Palestine’s local vote really represent
stories.summary: Palestinians participated in local municipal elections in the West Bank and parts of Gaza. Analysts note the vote offers a form of political participation but lacks real power, highlighting how Israeli occupation continues to shape and constrain Palestinian political life.

stories.title: Iran says large share of missile capability remains unused
stories.summary: Iran's defense ministry stated that a significant portion of the country's missile capabilities remains unused despite recent conflict with the United States and Israel. Spokesman Reza Talaei-Nik highlighted domestic production of over 1,000 types of weapons supported by thousands of companies across the country.

stories.title: Thousands of sailors stranded as maritime standoff at Hormuz continues
stories.summary: Thousands of sailors from India and other countries remain stranded in the Strait of Hormuz amid escalating military tensions disrupting one of the world's busiest shipping routes. Iran's IRGC seized a vessel called "Epaminodes" suspected of US military links, while US Central Command reported intercepting another ship.

stories.title: Punjab snubs officers applying directly to Centre for Haj duties
stories.summary: The Punjab government reprimanded BS-18 officers of the Pakistan Administrative Service and Provincial Management Service for applying directly to the federal religious affairs ministry for Haj duty without obtaining prior permission. The Services and General Administration Department issued a letter expressing "serious concern" over the bypassing of provincial authority.

stories.title: The Middle East’s new power brokers? Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Egypt unite
stories.summary: Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, and Egypt are forming a coalition of regional powers seeking influence in shaping the post-war Middle East order. The grouping spans from the Persian Gulf to Central and South Asia, with members sharing the view that the new regional framework should not be dictated solely by the U.S.-Israel alliance or Iran.

stories.title: Ukraine to fund nationwide resilience services in 2027 budget, PM says
stories.summary: Ukrainian Prime Minister announced that pilot resilience support services in local communities have proven effective and will become permanent, with dedicated funding allocated in the 2027 state budget.

stories.title: Hypersonic weapon startup Castelion wins $105 million Navy contract for F/A-18 integration
stories.summary: California-based defense startup Castelion has secured a $105 million U.S. Navy contract to integrate its Blackbeard hypersonic missile with carrier-based F/A-18 fighter jets. The deal moves the weapon from development toward operational readiness, with battlefield deployment anticipated as early as next year.

stories.title: Arrests reported amid Israeli operations in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli forces conducted raids across the occupied West Bank, arresting several Palestinians in Nablus, Salem, al-Mughayyir near Ramallah, and Tuqu near Bethlehem. Settlers also reportedly set fire to two vehicles in the village of Qusra.

stories.title: Middle East war live: US envoys expected in Islamabad as Iran rules out direct talks
stories.summary: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Islamabad for peace talks related to Iran, though Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, already in Pakistan, ruled out direct negotiations with American representatives. The effort represents the latest U.S. attempt to broker a deal with Iran.

stories.title: The High Court is treading a dangerous path by delaying an October 7 state inquiry
stories.summary: Israel's High Court is reportedly considering deferring the establishment of a state commission of inquiry into the October 7 attacks to the next government. Critics argue the delay, driven by concerns about political backlash, undermines the rule of law.

stories.title: ‘Cries of delight’ as Sumatran orangutan filmed using canopy bridge to cross road for first time
stories.summary: Conservationists in the Pakpak Bharat district of North Sumatra, Indonesia, filmed a critically endangered Sumatran orangutan using a canopy bridge to cross a road for the first time. The bridge was built in 2024 over the Lagan-Pagindar road to help wildlife navigate habitat fragmentation caused by the roadway.

stories.title: Inside Chornobyl: 40 years after disaster, nuclear site still at risk in Russia’s war
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck Chornobyl's confinement shelter in February 2025, raising concerns about the safety of the site of the world's worst nuclear disaster. Workers warn that the facility, protected by the massive "new safe confinement" steel structure, remains vulnerable amid Russia's ongoing war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Hanged under the cover of war: letters and videos tell stories of Iran’s death row victims
stories.summary: Testimony and writings from Babak Alipour, who spent three years on death row at Rajai Shahr prison in Karaj, Iran, before being executed in March, have emerged publicly. His letters describe fellow death row inmates, including 69-year-old Behrouz Ehsani and Mehdi Hassani, a father of three.

stories.title: 'Animals are traumatised too': Pet rescuers under fire in Ukraine
stories.summary: Animal rescue teams operating in eastern Ukraine described the dangers they face while saving dogs, cats, and other animals affected by the war. Rescuers said animals in the conflict zone are also suffering from trauma caused by ongoing hostilities.

stories.title: Hong Kong to step up crackdown on coerced shopping, scams during Labour Day ‘golden week’
stories.summary: Hong Kong announced increased enforcement against coerced shopping, unlicensed tour guides, and unfair sales practices targeting visitors during mainland China's Labour Day golden week holiday. Tourism Secretary Rosanna Law said hotel occupancy rates were expected to exceed 90 percent, with an estimated 980,000 mainland visitors anticipated.

stories.title: Colombia, Venezuela hold  key talks in post-Maduro visit
stories.summary: Colombian President Gustavo Petro visited Caracas in the first visit by a foreign leader since Nicolás Maduro's removal from power. Colombia and Venezuela announced military cooperation to combat criminal organizations operating along their shared border.

stories.title: Xpeng sets August goal to overtake Tesla’s self-driving tech in China
stories.summary: Chinese electric vehicle maker Xpeng has set an August deadline to surpass Tesla's self-driving capabilities in China, according to CEO He Xiaopeng. The target reflects an intensifying technology race in the world's largest car market as manufacturers increasingly rely on advanced software for growth.

stories.title: US Democrats look to rein in Trump's war powers, this time on Cuba
stories.summary: U.S. Senate Democrats are pushing for a vote as early as next week on a measure to restrict President Donald Trump's authority to launch military action against Cuba. The effort responds to Trump's recent threats of military intervention against the island nation.

stories.title: Oil tanker arrives at Iraq’s ports: Official
stories.summary: An oil tanker has arrived at Iraqi ports, marking the second such delivery since wartime disruptions affected shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Israel's Remembrance, Independent days did not change - we did - comment
stories.summary: A commentary reflects on how personal experiences of loss and connection have changed the way Israelis relate to Remembrance Day and Independence Day over the course of their lives.

stories.title: US says Iran open to talks, Tehran denies meeting plans
stories.summary: The White House said Iran is open to direct talks and that US officials Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff will travel to Islamabad. Iran's foreign ministry denied any planned meeting with the US, saying its position would be conveyed through Pakistan.

stories.title: Second phase of “Easter exchange” returns defenders born in 2000s
stories.summary: During the second phase of the "Easter exchange" between Ukraine and Russia, young defenders born in the 2000s and wounded servicemen were successfully returned.

stories.title: US imposes sanctions on Chinese 'teapot' refinery for buying Iranian oil
stories.summary: The United States imposed sanctions on Chinese independent refineries, known as 'teapots,' for purchasing Iranian oil. Sanctioned firms include Hebei Xinhai Chemical Group, Shandong Shouguang Luqing Petrochemical, and Shandong Shengxing Chemical.

stories.title: What’s at stake for Iran and the US in Islamabad?
stories.summary: Iran's foreign minister traveled to Islamabad for diplomatic discussions, while US envoys were also en route to the Pakistani capital. The simultaneous visits raised questions about the possibility of indirect or direct engagement between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Tehran denounces Israeli remarks on targeting leadership
stories.summary: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf condemned remarks by Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz about potentially targeting Iran's leadership. Ghalibaf warned that Iranian forces would defend the country and said internal unity would counter external threats.

stories.title: Iran’s foreign minister arrives in Pakistan, raising hopes for US peace talks
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Pakistan, fueling speculation about possible US-Iran peace talks. However, Pakistani sources indicated that Araghchi was not scheduled to meet with US negotiators in Islamabad.

stories.title: Hong Kong Aberdeen marina project attracting local and overseas interest
stories.summary: Hong Kong's planned Aberdeen marina-residential tourism project has drawn interest from local and international parties, including the city's leading yacht club and a Singapore-based operator. Real estate and boating industry experts said developers would likely partner with marina operators and called on the government to improve surrounding infrastructure.

stories.title: China and Mozambique to map critical minerals in insurgency-hit Cabo Delgado
stories.summary: Mozambique and China agreed to conduct a geological survey of critical mineral deposits in Mozambique's northern provinces, including insurgency-affected Cabo Delgado. The announcement followed talks between Chinese President Xi Jinping and Mozambican President Daniel Chapo in Beijing, as Maputo seeks Chinese investment and security expertise.

stories.title: UK political reaction to Pentagon leak: 'Falklands sovereignty is not up for debate'
stories.summary: The UK government and opposition parties jointly reaffirmed British sovereignty over the Falkland Islands after an internal Pentagon email surfaced suggesting the US could reconsider diplomatic support for London over the archipelago. The email reportedly framed the move as possible retaliation for Britain's refusal to join the military offensive against Iran.

stories.title: AFP: Journalist held in Kuwait over war footage released
stories.summary: Kuwaiti-American journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin was released by Kuwait and allowed to leave the country after being detained for weeks over sharing war footage. US State Department officials said his release followed intervention by the Trump administration.

stories.title: Aoun says Lebanon won’t be used as bargaining chip
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun stated Lebanon would not be used as a bargaining chip in regional conflicts. Hezbollah's Mohammad Raad urged authorities to withdraw from direct negotiations, while Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel is pursuing peace with Lebanon.

stories.title: Israel escalates attacks in Gaza, killing 12 people
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed 12 Palestinians, including six police officers, in multiple attacks across the Gaza Strip.

stories.title: EU aims for closer ties with Syria after Nicosia talks
stories.summary: EU leaders meeting in Nicosia pledged closer ties with Syria following the ouster of former President Bashar al-Assad. The bloc backed reconstruction efforts and new cooperation talks with Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa.

stories.title: Trump tells Reuters he will discuss digital tax, NATO with King Charles
stories.summary: President Donald Trump told Reuters he plans to discuss Iran, NATO, and the United Kingdom's digital services tax with King Charles during the monarch's upcoming visit to Washington next week.

stories.title: Iran to make offer aimed at satisfying US demands, Trump tells Reuters
stories.summary: President Trump told Reuters that Iran intends to present an offer aimed at satisfying US demands, though he said he did not yet know the details of the proposed offer.

stories.title: Just what the doctor ordered: how AI could help China bridge the medical resources gap
stories.summary: A doctor at the First Hospital of Lanzhou University in Gansu province purchased an Apple Mac Mini to run the open-source OpenClaw AI agent. He used the program to develop an application that extracts and organizes information from doctor-patient conversations and lab reports, reflecting broader AI adoption in China's healthcare sector.

stories.title: Hormuz blockade drives Panama Canal fees up to $4m
stories.summary: Shipping companies are paying up to $4 million for priority transit through the Panama Canal as the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz disrupts global shipping routes. Auction prices for fast-track canal slots have surged due to vessels rerouting to avoid the Gulf.

stories.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 57 as US envoys head to Pakistan?
stories.summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to travel to Pakistan as Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Islamabad for diplomatic discussions amid the ongoing US-Iran conflict.

stories.title: US will not renew Iranian, Russian oil waivers, Treasury Secretary tells Associated Press
stories.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told the Associated Press that Washington will not renew oil waivers originally granted for Iranian and Russian oil to ease strain on global energy markets caused by the Russia-Ukraine and US-Iran conflicts.

stories.title: Zelensky arrives in Azerbaijan for 'security and energy' talks
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky visited Azerbaijan for talks on energy and security cooperation. The trip followed a visit to Saudi Arabia as Ukraine continues to deepen ties with Gulf states and expand defence partnerships.

stories.title: Russia says US prioritising energy dominance over diplomacy
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov accused the United States of abandoning international agreements and pursuing energy dominance, particularly in regions like Iran and Venezuela. He warned that such policies risk undermining international law.

stories.title: Sheltering in Tel Aviv’s bus station, foreign workers face unique plight in wartime
stories.summary: Hundreds of foreign laborers in Tel Aviv are sheltering in tents beneath the central bus station, highlighting difficult conditions faced by third-country workers during wartime in Israel.

stories.title: SSU detains Russian agent coordinating shelling of Kramatorsk
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service detained a Russian GRU agent in the Donetsk region who had been coordinating shelling of Kramatorsk and tracking Ukrainian armored vehicles for destruction.

stories.title: Iranian delegation led by FM Araghchi lands in Islamabad; US officials to also arrive in Pakistan
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Islamabad and was received by Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar and military chief Field Marshal Asim Munir. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner were also heading to Pakistan, though Iran stated it would not meet directly with US officials.

stories.title: Altman apologizes after OpenAI failed to alert police before fatal Canada shooting
stories.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman issued an apology after the company failed to alert law enforcement about the online behavior of a person who subsequently shot and killed eight people in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia. OpenAI said its abuse detection systems flagged the account but determined at the time it did not meet the threshold for a legal referral.

stories.title: OpenAI’s Sam Altman apologises over failure to report Canadian mass shooter
stories.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman apologised after it emerged that ChatGPT's parent company had suspended a Canadian mass shooter's account before the attacks but failed to report the activity to law enforcement.

stories.title: US soldier charged with Maduro bets was blocked from opening account on Kalshi, source says
stories.summary: A U.S. soldier was charged in connection with bets placed on the political prediction market Polymarket, where he allegedly earned approximately $400,000. A source revealed that the soldier had previously been blocked from opening an account on the rival platform Kalshi.

stories.title: US soldier charged with Maduro bets was blocked from opening account on Kalshi, source says
stories.summary: U.S. Army soldier Gannon Ken Van Dyke, charged with placing bets on Polymarket tied to the capture of Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro using classified information, was previously blocked from opening an account on rival prediction market Kalshi.

stories.title: US military kills two more people in strike on alleged drug boat in Pacific
stories.summary: The US Southern Command announced that a lethal strike destroyed a small boat in the eastern Pacific, killing two people in what it described as a counter-narcotics operation. The strike was directed by Gen. Francis L. Donovan through Joint Task Force Southern Spear, continuing a campaign that has killed at least 178 people since September.

stories.title: Default in our stars: China’s banks use satellites to track assets with sky-high scrutiny
stories.summary: Several Chinese banks, including China Merchants Bank and Shanghai Pudong Development Bank, have begun using satellite remote-sensing technology to evaluate clients' physical assets and guard against credit risks. The trend follows earlier adoption by Ping An Bank in 2022 and Zhejiang E-Commerce Bank in 2020, with Postal Savings Bank of China also joining.

stories.title: 'Fighting the Hate': Melanie Phillips’s guide to confronting anti-Israel narratives - review
stories.summary: A review discusses Melanie Phillips's book "Fighting the Hate," which offers guidance on confronting anti-Israel narratives that have become prevalent in the Western world.

stories.title: Washington rules out oil waivers, freezes $344m in Iran-linked assets
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury froze $344 million in digital assets linked to Iran and sanctioned several digital wallets as part of an economic pressure campaign. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also announced Washington would not renew oil waivers previously granted for Iranian and Russian oil.

stories.title: Multiple Israeli strikes reported across Gaza, woman and child among killed
stories.summary: More than 11 Palestinians, including a woman and a child, were killed in separate Israeli strikes across the Gaza Strip on Friday. A drone strike near a police checkpoint in Gaza City hit targets reported by Al-Shifa Hospital, while another strike in the south killed at least seven, according to Nasser Hospital.

stories.title: US legal adviser says Iran war justified by Tehran’s ‘aggression’ over decades
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department's top legal adviser argued that President Trump's military campaign against Iran was justified as self-defense and in defense of ally Israel, characterizing it not as a new war but as a continuation of an ongoing conflict driven by decades of Iranian aggression.

stories.title: Argentina court orders seizure of ex-president Kirchner's assets
stories.summary: An Argentine appellate court upheld a lower court order to seize the assets of former President Cristina Kirchner in connection with a corruption conviction. Kirchner is currently serving a six-year sentence.

stories.title: Pentagon chief Hegseth says US blockade on Iran 'going global'
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the American naval blockade on Iran is expanding globally, increasing pressure on Tehran ahead of renewed nuclear talks in Pakistan.

stories.title: American flags raised in Metula to protest US influence amid anger over ceasefire extension
stories.summary: Residents of Metula, an Israeli town near the Lebanese border, raised American flags in protest against perceived U.S. influence amid anger over a ceasefire extension. Israeli officials have reported multiple Hezbollah violations of ceasefire terms, including rocket fire toward border communities.

stories.title: Witkoff and Kushner headed to Pakistan for Iran talks, White House says
stories.summary: U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are traveling to Islamabad for talks with Iran mediated by Pakistan, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt announced. The visit follows earlier rounds of U.S.-Iran negotiations.

stories.title: Severe weather leaves more than 100 communities in 10 regions without power
stories.summary: Severe weather left more than 100 communities across 10 Ukrainian regions without power as of April 24. Separately, Russian attacks caused power outages affecting users in five additional regions.

stories.title: Israel charges F-15 fighter jet technicians with spying for Iran, report says
stories.summary: Two Israeli Air Force technicians who worked on F-15 fighter jets have been charged with spying for Iran. The servicemen were indicted on charges including aiding the enemy and passing information to a foreign agent after a joint investigation by Shin Bet, police, and military authorities.

stories.title: Japanese military seeks answers for fatal Type 10 tank blast that should not have happened
stories.summary: A turret explosion inside a Japanese Type 10 tank during military maneuvers killed three crew members, causing shock in defense circles. Japan's defense ministry is investigating the virtually unprecedented incident before allowing the advanced tank to return to training.

stories.title: China’s AI token drive is really about upgrading inland economies
stories.summary: Chinese policymakers are promoting a "token economy" concept that links artificial intelligence with energy, infrastructure, and digital services. The initiative aims to restructure economic interactions in China's inland regions and position the country competitively in the next phase of digital development.

stories.title: Russia accuses US of using coups, kidnappings to ‘defend its well-being’ at any cost
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov accused the United States of abandoning international diplomatic conventions to dominate energy markets. In a Russian state television interview, Lavrov alleged that Washington's actions in Latin America and the Middle East undermine international law in pursuit of its own interests.

stories.title: The moral eclipse of politics in the modern age
stories.summary: A commentary discusses Pope Leo XIV's anti-war stance as a reminder that political leadership was historically expected to carry moral weight, arguing against moral neutrality in modern governance.

stories.title: Palestinians vote in local elections as polls open for the first time since Gaza war
stories.summary: Palestinians voted in municipal elections on Saturday, the first polls held since the Gaza war. No Hamas candidates appeared on the electoral lists, which were mostly aligned with President Mahmoud Abbas's Fatah party or ran as independents.

stories.title: UAE says rebuilding trust with Iran will take 'ages'
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates said rebuilding trust with Iran will take years following recent attacks. Tensions persist despite a ceasefire, with ongoing regional disputes over security and energy routes.

stories.title: Iran says it won't meet US, will convey position to Pakistan amid mediation
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said no meeting with the United States is planned in Islamabad. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Pakistan's capital to meet Pakistani officials, with Iran's position to be conveyed through Pakistani mediation channels.

stories.title: Iranian delegation led by FM Araghchi lands in Islamabad; arrival of US representatives expected as well
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Islamabad and was received by Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir. The visit focuses on regional developments and peace efforts ahead of expected US-Iran talks in Pakistan.

stories.title: 'We cried together': Trump's deportation drive forces tough decisions for couples
stories.summary: The Trump administration's deportation drive is forcing spouses of undocumented immigrants to choose between family separation or relocating abroad. Affected couples face difficult decisions as enforcement intensifies.

stories.title: Australian women and children leave Syrian detention camp for Damascus – and potentially home
stories.summary: Four Australian women and nine of their children and grandchildren departed the al-Roj detention camp in northeastern Syria, traveling by road toward Damascus. The group is seeking repatriation to Australia after a previous attempt in February was turned back. The Albanese government stated it is not directly assisting the effort.

stories.title: Why China will see India’s latest defence deal with South Korea as ‘inevitably sensitive’
stories.summary: India and South Korea agreed to expand defence industry cooperation in areas including artillery and anti-aircraft systems following a meeting between Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and South Korean President Lee Jae Myung during his three-day visit to India. Analysts say China views the deal as sensitive given its ongoing Himalayan border dispute with New Delhi.

stories.title: US, EU sign critical minerals plan to counter China reliance
stories.summary: The United States and European Union signed a critical minerals partnership plan aimed at reducing reliance on China. Beijing has restricted exports of critical minerals needed for key industries including defense.

stories.title: China’s ‘most pampered child’ interred in palace-like coffin with treasures 1,400 years ago
stories.summary: Archaeologists have documented the 1,400-year-old tomb of Li Jingxun, a young Sui dynasty aristocrat from Longxi in what is now Gansu province, northwest China. She was buried in an elaborate palace-like stone coffin filled with treasures, reflecting her high-ranking family status during the transition from the Northern dynasties.

stories.title: Ukraine, Russia swop 193 prisoners of war each in US, UAE-facilitated exchange
stories.summary: Ukraine and Russia exchanged 193 prisoners of war each in a swap facilitated by the United States and the United Arab Emirates. The exchange is the latest in a series of prisoner swaps conducted over four years of war.

stories.title: Moscow and Abu Dhabi push for renewed diplomacy
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov and UAE Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed called for the resumption of negotiations to address the Middle East crisis during a phone conversation. Both sides stressed the need for talks toward a long-term, sustainable resolution for the region.

stories.title: Australian families reattempt repatriation from Syria’s Roj camp
stories.summary: Four Australian families departed Syria's Roj camp in an attempted repatriation to Australia. Authorities are coordinating the return amid security concerns over alleged links to the Islamic State group.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it carried out attacks on Israeli forces in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah claimed it carried out several attacks on Israeli forces in southern Lebanon, targeting troops and military vehicles in al-Qantara with drones. The group also said it shot down an Israeli Hermes 450 drone over Tyre and struck an armored personnel carrier in Ramyah.

stories.title: Romania tests AI-powered drone interceptors as Ukraine war gets closer
stories.summary: Romania tested a U.S.-made, AI-powered drone defense system at the Capu Midia base on the Black Sea coast. The trial comes as the conflict in neighboring Ukraine increasingly raises security concerns for the NATO member.

stories.title: Kremlin ramping up war propaganda ahead of May 9 celebrations
stories.summary: Ukraine's Center for Countering Disinformation reported that the Kremlin is intensifying propaganda campaigns ahead of May 9 Victory Day celebrations, including expanding the "Victory Dictation" initiative and deploying other influence tools.

stories.title: From soft toys to bandages, Iran war may drive up cost of petroleum-derived goods
stories.summary: Experts warn that the Iran conflict could drive up costs of petroleum-derived consumer goods—from soft toys to bandages—if oil prices hold above $90 per barrel, pressuring global supply chains beyond the already visible rise in travel costs.

stories.title: UK PM vows legislation to ban Iran Guards: report
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer is reportedly preparing legislation to ban Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The move follows arson attacks in Britain and rising concerns over Iranian state-backed threats.

stories.title: Katya Adler: Europe's Nato allies push back at reported US threat to Spain
stories.summary: European NATO allies pushed back against a reported US threat directed at Spain, further straining transatlantic relations. BBC Europe editor Katya Adler reported the incident highlighted ongoing tensions between Europe and the United States.

stories.title: Merz floats sanctions relief for Iran peace deal, other EU leaders cautious
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz suggested at an EU meeting in Nicosia, Cyprus, that the European Union could ease sanctions on Iran as part of a comprehensive deal to end the Iran war. Other EU leaders expressed more cautious positions on the proposal.

stories.title: Ukrainian commander sacked after troops left starving at front
stories.summary: A Ukrainian military commander was dismissed after troops under his command were left without adequate food at the front lines. The situation came to light after a soldier's wife posted photos that provoked widespread public anger across Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran war live: Tehran’s FM in Islamabad; US says envoys to travel for talks
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes and tank shelling across Gaza killed at least 12 Palestinians, including six police officers, according to reports from the territory.

stories.title: Leo Terrell’s civil rights roots fuel his fight against antisemitism
stories.summary: Leo Terrell, who leads a federal task force targeting antisemitism, described the fight against threats to the Jewish community as personally important to him, drawing on his civil rights background.

stories.title: Estonian PM urges EU to impose tariffs on Russian goods to fund Ukraine’s reconstruction
stories.summary: Estonian Prime Minister called on the European Union to impose tariffs on Russian goods, proposing that the revenue be used to finance Ukraine's postwar reconstruction.

stories.title: Thousands at risk after multi-million dollar Everest flood warning system left to rust
stories.summary: A multi-million-dollar flood warning system installed at Imja glacial lake near Mount Everest has not been maintained since 2016. Local residents expressed fear about the risk to thousands of people living downstream from the deteriorating system in Nepal.

stories.title: Watch: Raghav Chadha, six AAP MPs join BJP | Above the Fold | 24.04.2026
stories.summary: Six Aam Aadmi Party MPs, including Raghav Chadha, have joined India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party in a significant political realignment. The development marks a major shake-up in India's opposition landscape.

stories.title: UN says Israeli strikes in Lebanon, Hezbollah rockets into Israel may breach international law
stories.summary: The UN human rights office in Geneva reported documented patterns of attacks on civilians in populated areas and residential buildings in both Lebanon and Israel. The office said strikes by Israel in Lebanon and Hezbollah rockets into Israel may constitute serious violations of international humanitarian law.

stories.title: Kedrion warns Iran war may delay plasma supplies to Iran
stories.summary: Italian pharmaceutical company Kedrion warned that the ongoing Iran conflict may disrupt delivery of vital plasma-derived medicines, as rising fuel costs threaten global supply chains and patient access.

stories.title: Police raid Peru’s election authorities after outcry over slow vote count
stories.summary: Anticorruption police in Peru raided the homes of former election office head Piero Corvetto and other officials, seizing material amid public outcry over a slow vote count following recent elections.

stories.title: US vice president absence from Iran talks ‘in line with protocol’: Report
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance did not attend the Iran-related talks in Islamabad, which the Washington Post reported was consistent with standard diplomatic protocol requiring meetings between counterparts of similar rank. Envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are leading the US side.

stories.title: Kosovo court jails three men for 2023 terror attack near Serbia's border
stories.summary: A court in Pristina, Kosovo, convicted three men on terrorism charges related to a 2023 attack in northern Kosovo near the Serbian border. Serb gunmen had stormed a village and clashed with police in a shootout that killed four people, including a police officer.

stories.title: UN Deputy Secretary-General: Chernobyl became mega-crisis that transformed approaches to disaster response
stories.summary: UN Under-Secretary-General for Disarmament Affairs Izumi Nakamitsu highlighted the lasting significance of the Chernobyl disaster, calling it a mega-crisis that fundamentally transformed international approaches to disaster response and emergency management.

stories.title: Germany launches spying probe into Signal attacks targeting MPs
stories.summary: Germany has launched a spying investigation into cyberattacks targeting members of parliament via the Signal messaging application. Details of the probe's scope and suspected actors have not yet been fully disclosed.

stories.title: US mulls expelling Spain from Nato for failing to back war on Iran
stories.summary: An internal Pentagon email seen by Reuters outlined potential punitive measures against NATO allies for insufficient support in the US conflict with Iran, including possible expulsion of Spain from the alliance and recognition of Argentina's claims over the Falkland Islands to pressure the UK.

stories.title: Justice Dept to close investigation into Fed Chair Powell, US Attorney Pirro says
stories.summary: The U.S. Justice Department is closing its investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro announced on Friday. The decision removes an obstacle to Senate confirmation of Kevin Warsh, President Trump's nominee to lead the central bank.

stories.title: Syria accuses Hezbollah-linked cells of plotting attacks, signaling break from Assad-era alliance
stories.summary: Syria's post-Assad government accused Hezbollah-linked cells of plotting assassinations, bombings, and rocket attacks on Syrian territory. Damascus is moving against these networks, signaling a break from the former Assad regime's alliance with Hezbollah.

stories.title: Syria says it arrested ex-intel officer filmed taking part in 2013 Damascus massacre
stories.summary: Syrian authorities announced the arrest of former intelligence officer Amjad Yousef, who appeared in leaked video footage showing officers shooting dozens of prisoners into a trench in a Damascus suburb near the Yarmouk Palestinian refugee camp during a 2013 massacre.

stories.title: Germany’s Merz says no ‘immediate’ Ukraine EU membership, floats Kyiv joining meetings
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stated there would be no immediate EU membership for Ukraine but suggested Kyiv could participate in EU meetings. Ukraine continues to push for an accelerated accession process as it fights Russia's invasion.

stories.title: UN peacekeeper dies of wounds suffered in Lebanon last month: UNIFIL
stories.summary: A United Nations peacekeeper serving with UNIFIL in Lebanon has died from wounds sustained the previous month, bringing the total death toll to six. Indonesia has called on the UN to conduct a thorough investigation into the incidents.

stories.title: White House says Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner to head to Pakistan for talks with Iran
stories.summary: White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt announced that U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and presidential adviser Jared Kushner would travel to Pakistan for a second round of direct talks with Iranian representatives, with Pakistan serving as mediator.

stories.title: As Pensacola’s oldest synagogue turns 150, locals celebrate the community’s rich history
stories.summary: Pensacola, Florida, is celebrating the 150th anniversary of its oldest synagogue. The city's Jewish community of roughly 1,800 significantly predates other southern Florida Jewish populations, and locals say the community is poised for a renaissance.

stories.title: Azov fighters present Duke and Duchess of Sussex with gift in appreciation of support for Ukraine
stories.summary: Soldiers from Ukraine's 12th Special Forces Brigade "Azov," part of the National Guard, met with Prince Harry and presented the Duke and Duchess of Sussex with a symbolic gift. The gesture expressed gratitude for their support of Ukraine.

stories.title: Her life on the home front: How war is reshaping life for Israel’s wives and mothers
stories.summary: A report profiles how the ongoing war is reshaping daily life for Israeli women whose husbands are serving in the military. The piece highlights the emotional and logistical challenges faced by wives and mothers managing households while their partners are deployed.

stories.title: Lebanon confirms six killed in Israeli strikes despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Lebanon's health ministry confirmed that Israeli air strikes killed six people and injured two others in southern Lebanon on April 24, despite an ongoing ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah.

stories.title: China slaps export curbs on European firms over Taiwan arms sales
stories.summary: China imposed export restrictions on dual-use items targeting seven European entities, citing their involvement in arms sales to Taiwan. The curbs also prohibit foreign organizations and individuals from transferring China-originated dual-use goods to the named firms.

stories.title: Leaders of Colombia, Venezuela expected to discuss security at Caracas meeting
stories.summary: Colombian President Gustavo Petro traveled to Caracas on Friday to meet Venezuelan counterpart Delcy Rodriguez. The two leaders, both under pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump, were expected to discuss bilateral security issues.

stories.title: Minister seeks details on reports of hijacking of tanker with Pakistani crew near Somali coast
stories.summary: Pakistan's Maritime Affairs Minister Junaid Anwar Chaudhry requested a detailed report on the reported hijacking of an oil tanker by pirates near the Somali coast. The vessel's crew reportedly includes 11 Pakistani nationals. The ministry said it is coordinating with the Foreign Office and Somali authorities.

stories.title: U.S. soldier charged with using classified intel to win $400K Polymarket bet on Maduro raid
stories.summary: U.S. Army soldier Gannon Ken Van Dyke was charged with using classified intelligence to place approximately $400,000 in bets on the prediction market Polymarket regarding a raid on Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro. Most bets were allegedly placed hours before missiles struck Caracas.

stories.title: Citizen taken into custody for likening Tarnol Railway Crossing to Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Police in Islamabad arrested a citizen for allegedly mocking the Tarnol Railway crossing by comparing it to the Strait of Hormuz, which has been disrupted by the Middle East conflict. An FIR was registered under multiple sections including disobedience to a public servant's order.

stories.title: US justice department steps in on behalf of xAI in Colorado regulation case
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice has intervened in a lawsuit filed by Elon Musk's xAI against a Colorado law regulating artificial intelligence systems. The department argued the state law violates the 14th Amendment's equal protection guarantee, setting up a conflict between state regulation and the Trump administration's push for a federal AI framework.

stories.title: Indigenous speakers booed at Anzac Day services as Ben Roberts-Smith attends Gold Coast event
stories.summary: Anzac Day commemorations in Melbourne and Sydney were disrupted by booing during Indigenous acknowledgement of country segments. One man was arrested at the Sydney dawn service at Martin Place. Separately, Victoria Cross recipient Ben Roberts-Smith, who faces five war crime murder charges he denies, attended the dawn service at Currumbin Beach on the Gold Coast.

stories.title: Israel reportedly agreed to, but did not implement US request to curb Gaza strikes
stories.summary: Hamas-run authorities reported that 13 people were killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza. Israel reportedly agreed to a US request to curb strikes in Gaza but did not implement the commitment. Tehran said no direct meeting with US officials was planned during the Islamabad talks.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills three in Gaza, medics say
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike killed at least three people in Gaza on Friday, according to Palestinian health officials. The strike was reported from Cairo, with medics confirming the casualties.

stories.title: The Kashmir town trying to win back tourists after a deadly attack
stories.summary: One year after a deadly attack in Pahalgam, the town in Indian-administered Kashmir is struggling to revive its tourism industry. The slowdown has severely affected local livelihoods and the broader regional economy.

stories.title: As DJI duels Insta360, China sharpens global hardware edge amid US scrutiny
stories.summary: Shenzhen-based rivals DJI and Insta360 are intensifying competition across consumer drones and cameras, sharpening China's global hardware edge even as both companies face growing US regulatory scrutiny.

stories.title: Drones hit Kuwait border posts as Iraq orders investigation
stories.summary: Kuwait's military reported that two drones launched from Iraqi territory struck northern border posts on Friday, causing damage but no casualties. Iraq's prime minister ordered an investigation, and Baghdad condemned the attack during a call with Kuwaiti officials.
