stories.summary: U.S. Army Master Sergeant Gannon Ken Van Dyke, a Special Forces soldier, was charged with placing wagers on the prediction platform Polymarket using confidential government information regarding the removal of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro. He allegedly earned $400,000 from the bets.

stories.title: Tai Po fire probe: water pressure could only reach 20th floor, commander says
stories.summary: Hong Kong Fire Services Department Director Andy Yeung Yan-kin is set to testify before an independent committee investigating the deadly Tai Po fire. A fire commander revealed that water pressure during the blaze could only reach the 20th floor of the building. Yeung is the most senior official to give evidence in the inquiry into Hong Kong's deadliest fire in decades.

stories.title: How fake military job ads in Philippines led to alleged spy recruitment pipeline
stories.summary: An investigation revealed that fake job advertisements bearing the emblem of defense publisher Janes were posted on Philippine military Facebook forums in 2023, offering up to $5,000 for security researchers. The fraudulent ads, which included Viber and WhatsApp contact details, were traced to an alleged spy recruitment pipeline targeting Philippine military personnel.

stories.title: Report: Iran War 'drained' essential US ammunition supplies
stories.summary: According to a New York Times report, the war in Iran has significantly depleted the US military's global ammunition stockpile, forcing the Pentagon to redirect equipment from commands in Asia and Europe. Independent estimates place the cost between $28 billion and $35 billion, roughly $1 billion per day.

stories.title: Couple discovers Lebanon home destroyed by Israel from satellite image
stories.summary: Joe Elias, a Lebanese national, discovered through satellite imagery that his home village had been destroyed by Israeli forces. He contacted BBC Verify after reports emerged that several villages in Lebanon had been leveled.

stories.title: US to deploy election observers in The Bahamas
stories.summary: The US State Department announced plans to deploy election observers to The Bahamas ahead of next month's election, following a request from the Caribbean nation's opposition leader amid concerns about potential voter fraud.

stories.title: Oil rises above $106 per barrel as US, Iran deadlocked in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Oil prices rose above $106 per barrel amid a standoff between the United States and Iran over the Strait of Hormuz. President Donald Trump stated that vessels would need permission from the US Navy to transit the key waterway.

stories.title: Italian peacekeepers replace crucifix desecrated in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Italian UN peacekeepers in southern Lebanon replaced a crucifix statue of Jesus Christ that had been vandalized by Israeli soldiers, according to Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni.

stories.title: SSU detains Russian agent preparing airstrikes on Kramatorsk and Druzhkivka
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service counterintelligence detained a Russian military intelligence (GRU) agent in the Donetsk region. The agent was preparing target coordinates for Russian airstrikes on the cities of Kramatorsk and Druzhkivka in eastern Ukraine.

stories.title: Trump says US in no rush but 'clock is ticking' for Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump warned that time is running out for Iran as diplomatic talks have stalled. A third American aircraft carrier arrived in the Middle East, reinforcing the U.S. military presence in the region. Trump said the U.S. is in no rush but that the 'clock is ticking.'

stories.title: Japan injects new life into Fukushima with nuclear plant ‘hope tourism’
stories.summary: Fifteen years after the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster, tour buses are bringing visitors to the barely inhabited coastal towns near the wrecked plant in Japan. The phenomenon, dubbed "hope tourism," draws people to areas still marked by empty lots, restricted-access signs, and ongoing radioactive cleanup operations.

stories.title: Jewish groups protest as California sends out antisemitic conspiracies in voter guide
stories.summary: Jewish organizations protested after California distributed an official voter guide containing a candidate statement with antisemitic conspiracy theories. The statement blamed Israel for the assassination of Charlie Kirk, attacked the Talmud, and included links to white supremacist websites.

stories.title: European states accuse Russia of trying to erase memory of Stalin's crimes after monument disappears
stories.summary: Four European states accused Russia of attempting to erase the memory of Soviet leader Josef Stalin's crimes after a monument honoring victims executed by his secret police was dismantled in Siberia.

stories.title: US says Iran players welcome at World Cup amid Italy uproar
stories.summary: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that Iranian footballers will be welcome to participate in the 2026 World Cup held in the United States. He denied reports that Washington had asked Iran not to send its national team, addressing an uproar involving Italy's potential replacement of Iran in the tournament.

stories.title: Israel awaiting US green light to ‘return Iran to Stone Age’, says defence minister
stories.summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz stated that Israel is prepared to resume war against Iran and is awaiting a green light from the United States to, in his words, return Iran to the "Stone Age."

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon extend ceasefire as Trump hopes for deal
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced an extension of the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon after the two countries' ambassadors to Washington met at the White House. Trump expressed hope that the truce could lead to a broader deal between the parties.

stories.title: Pope condemns killing of protesters in Iran, reaffirms stance against war
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV condemned the killing of protesters in Iran during a press conference aboard the papal flight, after US President Donald Trump had criticized him the previous week for not addressing the issue while speaking out against the US-Israel war with Iran.

stories.title: Pope Leo decries migrants being treated 'worse than house pets'
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV sharply criticized the global treatment of immigrants, saying migrants and refugees fleeing violence or poverty are often treated "worse than house pets or animals."

stories.title: Israel Police arrest Jerusalem rioter who assaulted officer, waved Israeli flag with swastika
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested a rioter in Jerusalem who assaulted an officer and waved an Israeli flag bearing a swastika. Police deployed dispersal measures to control the situation during the unrest.

stories.title: Iran fast-boat swarms add to Hormuz threats for shipping
stories.summary: Iran deployed a swarm of small fast boats to seize two container ships near the Strait of Hormuz, raising concerns about the viability of reopening the critical oil export route despite US claims of having neutralized Iran's naval capabilities.

stories.title: Man dies after fainting on Cathay Pacific flight from UK to Hong Kong
stories.summary: A 51-year-old man died after fainting on Cathay Pacific flight CX216 from Manchester to Hong Kong. The aircraft landed at Hong Kong International Airport on Friday morning, and police said the deceased had a history of illness.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire continues as Trump hopes for peace deal
stories.summary: President Trump announced a three-week extension of the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire and expressed hope for a permanent peace deal this year. He said he expected Israeli and Lebanese leaders to meet with him in the coming weeks to advance negotiations.

stories.title: Trump says he will ‘probably put a big tariff on the UK’ if it doesn’t drop digital services tax
stories.summary: President Trump threatened to impose tariffs on the United Kingdom if it does not drop its digital services tax, a 2% levy on revenues of major US tech companies introduced in 2020. Trump accused the UK of trying to "make an easy buck" from American technology firms.

stories.title: Trump orders US Navy to destroy boats laying mines in Hormuz strait
stories.summary: President Donald Trump ordered the US Navy to destroy any Iranian boats caught laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz, escalating pressure on Tehran to reopen the crucial waterway.

stories.title: Three police officers injured in Kherson after drone detonated
stories.summary: Three police officers were injured in the southern Ukrainian city of Kherson after an unexploded drone detonated. The incident occurred as Kherson continues to face regular drone and shelling attacks from Russian forces.

stories.title: Fake app drains Filipino retiree’s life savings via ‘malware-as-a-service’
stories.summary: A 68-year-old retiree in the Philippines lost his life savings after being tricked into installing a fake Social Security System app. A caller posing as a government pension fund employee sent the man a malicious link via the Viber messaging app, deploying malware-as-a-service to drain his accounts.

stories.title: Engine dilemma lies at heart of successful take-off for China’s C919
stories.summary: China's Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China (Comac) delivered only three C919 narrowbody jets in the first quarter of 2025, far behind its annual target of over 30. Engine supply challenges remain a central obstacle to scaling production of China's domestically developed airliner.

stories.title: Group of over 250 Bnei Menashe immigrants from India lands in Israel
stories.summary: A group of over 250 members of the Bnei Menashe community from India arrived in Israel as immigrants. They are the first members of the community to immigrate since the Israeli government decided last year to bring approximately 4,600 Bnei Menashe to the country.

stories.title: French, UK defence chiefs eye 'real progress' in Hormuz plan
stories.summary: French and British defense chiefs expressed optimism that military plans to secure the Strait of Hormuz are making progress. The initiative aims to restore trade flows through the strategically vital waterway, which has been disrupted by the regional conflict.

stories.title: Israeli army launches air strikes on southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military carried out air strikes on southern Lebanon, stating it targeted rocket launchers. Shortly before, Hezbollah fired rockets at northern Israel, triggering sirens in Shtula, despite a ceasefire in effect. U.S. President Trump announced a three-week extension to the truce following White House talks between Israeli and Lebanese delegations.

stories.title: Russia’s Investigative Committee releases Eksmo publishing house executives without charges, orders them to return for questioning
stories.summary: Russia's Investigative Committee released Eksmo publishing house CEO Yevgeny Kapyev and three other senior executives on April 23 after detaining them in a criminal "extremism" case related to the sale of queer literature. The executives were ordered to return for further questioning.

stories.title: UK’s Starmer worried by foreign-backed proxy attacks in Britain
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer expressed growing concern over foreign states using proxies to carry out attacks in the United Kingdom and pledged to introduce new legislation to address the threat.

stories.title: Man stabs, seriously wounds 2 doctors at Russian hospital
stories.summary: A man armed with a knife attacked and seriously wounded two doctors at a hospital in Makhachkala, the capital of Russia's Dagestan republic, on April 23. The Dagestan branch of Russia's Investigative Committee confirmed the stabbing.

stories.title: 'A nuclear weapon should never be allowed to be used by anybody': Trump
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump ruled out using nuclear weapons against Iran, responding to reporters at the White House. His remarks followed earlier threats regarding the destruction of Iranian civilization. Trump called the question about a potential nuclear strike 'stupid.'

stories.title: ‘Phone booth princess’: China grandma dedicates 33 years to managing public telephone booth
stories.summary: Shen Yuxiu, a Shanghai grandmother in her 80s, has managed the city's last staffed public telephone booth on Fuzhou Road for 33 years. She operates two landline phones daily from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m., earning minimal income despite the booth's location between popular tourist spots.

stories.title: ‘Unacceptable abuse’: UK health data of 500,000 people listed for sale in China
stories.summary: The data was downloaded legitimately by three research institutions in China.

stories.title: Trump declares 3-week truce extension after hosting 2nd round of Israel-Lebanon talks
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump declared a three-week extension of the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire after hosting a second round of talks at the White House. Trump indicated that Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and Lebanese President Aoun would likely meet at the White House in coming weeks. He acknowledged being unaware of a Lebanese law banning contact with Israelis but predicted it would be repealed.

stories.title: Congress members join protest against ‘oligarch’s dinner’ for Trump thrown by Ellisons
stories.summary: Dozens of protesters, including members of Congress, gathered along the National Mall in Washington to oppose a dinner hosted by Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison honoring the Trump White House. Critics view the event as emblematic of close ties between the Ellison family and the administration amid Paramount's pending $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery.

stories.title: Lubinets calls for appeal against Italian court ruling on adoption of Ukrainian child
stories.summary: Ukraine's Parliamentary Commissioner for Human Rights, Dmytro Lubinets, called for an appeal against an Italian court ruling that permitted a foreign family to adopt a Ukrainian child. Lubinets demanded the child's return to Ukraine.

stories.title: India voices anger after Trump shares comments calling it a ‘hellhole’
stories.summary: India's foreign ministry condemned a Truth Social post by President Trump sharing comments by podcast host Michael Savage calling India a "hellhole." The criticism comes ahead of a planned visit to India by Secretary of State Marco Rubio aimed at easing bilateral tensions.

stories.title: Chinese EV makers bet on in-house chips to make cars smarter and more autonomous
stories.summary: Chinese EV makers including Xpeng, Nio, and lidar producer Hesai Group are showcasing in-house chip designs at the Auto China show in Beijing. The companies are developing chips for autonomous driving and in-car entertainment with computing power comparable to leading international products.

stories.title: Meta to cut workforce by ten per cent as artificial intelligence spending surges
stories.summary: Meta announced plans to cut approximately 8,000 jobs as it increases spending on artificial intelligence. The layoffs are part of a broader tech-sector trend toward cost control, with Microsoft also reportedly considering voluntary buyouts.

stories.title: US soldier involved in Maduro raid charged over alleged bets on capture
stories.summary: US soldier Gannon Ken Van Dyke, who participated in the January military operation to capture Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, has been charged with allegedly making over $400,000 in wagers on prediction market Polymarket related to Maduro's removal. He faces up to 60 years in prison.

stories.title: At least 17 Somali migrants die after boat capsizes off Algeria
stories.summary: At least 17 Somali migrants died after their boat capsized in waters between Algeria and Spain. Somalia's ambassador to Algeria confirmed the death toll on Thursday. The migrants were attempting the dangerous sea crossing toward Europe.

stories.title: Top UK rights groups condemn conviction of Palestine activists
stories.summary: Leading UK human rights groups issued a joint statement condemning the conviction of Palestine solidarity activists Ben Jamal and Chris Nineham. The organizations described the prosecution as an 'attack on civil society' and a threat to the right to political activism in Britain.

stories.title: Australia’s US$7 billion Japan warship deals signals shift from US overreliance
stories.summary: Australia and Japan announced a warship deal valued at approximately US$7 billion. Defence Ministers Richard Marles and Shinjiro Koizumi confirmed the agreement, which analysts say will help Australia address navy shortfalls and reduce its overreliance on the United States for defence technology.

stories.title: Iran war live: Lebanon truce extended; Trump says time not on Tehran’s side
stories.summary: Gaza's Health Ministry reported that the death toll from Israel's ongoing military campaign in Gaza has reached 72,568, with 172,338 people injured. Separately, the Lebanon ceasefire has been extended, and U.S. President Donald Trump stated that time is not on Iran's side.

stories.title: Zelensky meets Danish PM in Cyprus to discuss joint drone production
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky met with Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen in Cyprus to discuss expanding joint defense production, with a focus on drone manufacturing. The meeting underscored the two countries' growing military cooperation.

stories.title: WATCH: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire to extend by three weeks, Trump says, after talks at White House
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced a three-week extension of the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon during White House talks. Discussions on Hezbollah's disarmament are continuing as part of the broader diplomatic effort.

stories.title: Trump extends Lebanon ceasefire, hails ‘historic’ White House talks
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced a three-week extension of the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire after hosting Israeli and Lebanese delegations at the White House. Trump said the talks went well and expressed hope for future meetings with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and Lebanese President Joseph Aoun.

stories.title: US judge orders release of family of Egyptian attack suspect
stories.summary: A U.S. federal judge ordered the immediate release of the family members of a man accused of carrying out a firebomb attack on a Jewish protest march in Colorado last year. The ruling pertains to the detained relatives of the Egyptian suspect.

stories.title: Russia warns European states against hosting French nuclear bomber planes
stories.summary: April 23 - Russia warned on Thursday that any European countries that accepted deployments of French nuclear-capable strategic bombers would make themselves targets for attack by Moscow's forces in th

stories.title: Pakistan, 7 other Muslim nations reject attempts to alter historic, legal status quo in Jerusalem, at its holy sites
stories.summary: Foreign ministers of Pakistan and seven other Muslim-majority countries issued a joint statement rejecting any changes to the historic and legal status quo in Jerusalem and its Islamic and Christian holy sites, condemning Israeli settler incursions into Al-Aqsa Mosque under police protection.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia appoint Donis as coach ahead of World Cup
stories.summary: The Saudi Arabian football federation announced the appointment of Georgios Donis as the national team's new head coach ahead of the 2026 World Cup. The announcement was made on Thursday as Saudi Arabia prepares for the upcoming tournament.

stories.title: Drone deal: Zelensky, Nausėda discuss expanding defense cooperation
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda discussed expanding defense cooperation, focusing on the Drone Deal initiative. The talks centered on opportunities for joint defense manufacturing between the two nations.

stories.title: Trump’s ‘gold card’ visa granted to just 1 person so far
stories.summary: The Trump administration's "gold card" visa program, which charges at least US$1 million for the right to live and work in the United States, has been approved for only one person so far. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick disclosed the figure, falling short of earlier claims of US$1.3 billion in sales.

stories.title: A rumour, a lynching in India and a long wait for justice
stories.summary: An Indian court has convicted 20 people for the 2018 mob lynching of two men who were falsely accused of kidnapping children. The case highlighted concerns about rumor-fueled vigilante violence in India.

stories.title: Russia reports toxic rain, orders locals to stay home after Ukrainian oil strike
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck oil facilities in the southern Russian town of Tuapse on April 20, causing a large fire and toxic smoke. Russian authorities reported toxic rain in the area and ordered residents to stay indoors.

stories.title: Trump says nuclear weapons 'should never be allowed,' will not be used against Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated that nuclear weapons "should never be allowed" and confirmed they would not be used against Iran. He expressed a desire to negotiate a lasting deal rather than a quick agreement with Tehran.

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon envoys hail ‘historic’ moment at White House
stories.summary: Israeli Ambassador Yechiel Leiter and Lebanon's envoy praised U.S.-brokered progress during talks at the White House, calling it a historic moment. Speaking alongside President Donald Trump, Leiter said Israel and Lebanon had never been closer, and expressed hope for continued peace efforts.

stories.title: In Orban’s rule, Israelis saw a model for their own country. Will he also be one in defeat?
stories.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, whom Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu called a 'true friend,' suffered a major electoral defeat. The loss comes six months before Israel's own elections, prompting speculation about whether it could foreshadow a similar leadership change in Israel.

stories.title: Two Russian LGBT groups say courts declared them 'extremist'
stories.summary: Two Russian LGBT organizations announced on Thursday that separate courts had designated them as "extremist." The rulings are part of a broader crackdown on gay and transgender communities in Russia.

stories.title: Argentina blocks media access to Casa Rosada citing espionage complaint
stories.summary: Argentina's government under President Javier Milei blocked accredited journalists from entering the Casa Rosada government house in Buenos Aires on Thursday. Officials cited an incident of alleged illegal espionage as the reason for restricting media access.

stories.title: Trump shares right-wing anchor’s rant against Indians, MEA terms it ‘inappropriate’
stories.summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs called a right-wing media rant against Indians shared by US President Donald Trump 'inappropriate,' after opposition members and former diplomats criticized the government for not responding more forcefully.

stories.title: US soldier charged with using Polymarket to bet on Nicolas Maduro abduction
stories.summary: Gannon Ken Van Dyke, a 38-year-old U.S. soldier, has been charged with using the prediction market platform Polymarket to place bets on the abduction of Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro. He allegedly earned $400,000 by leveraging insider knowledge of a planned operation against Venezuela.

stories.title: Pentagon says top Navy official to leave office ‘immediately’
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced that the US Navy's top civilian official would leave office immediately, without providing a reason. The departure comes as the Navy is conducting a blockade of Iranian ports.

stories.title: At least 10 wounded in shooting at Mall of Louisiana
stories.summary: A shooting at the Mall of Louisiana wounded at least 10 people on Thursday. City police said the attack occurred at approximately 2 p.m. near the food court.

stories.title: Days before King Charles's state visit, Trump says it could help mend ties with London
stories.summary: President Trump said the upcoming state visit of King Charles III and Queen Camilla, beginning Monday, could help repair US-UK relations strained by tensions over the Iran war and other disputes. Trump made the remarks in a BBC telephone interview broadcast on Thursday.

stories.title: Tanzania inquiry says over 500 killed in last year's election violence
stories.summary: A government-appointed commission of inquiry in Tanzania reported on Thursday that at least 518 people were killed during violence surrounding the country's elections last October. This marks the first official acknowledgment of the scale of the deadly unrest that accompanied the vote.

stories.title: Brazil beckoned: China now has stock and bond ‘connect’ schemes in these 5 regions
stories.summary: China launched a bond-market-connect scheme with Brazil, marking the first such link between two emerging markets. China now maintains at least five offshore capital-market connect schemes across three continents, allowing investors to trade across borders without special permits or capital-flow controls.

stories.title: MoE Shmyhal: Ukraine restores 1 GW of TPP capacity out of planned 3.8 GW
stories.summary: Ukrainian Prime Minister Denys Shmyhal reported that Ukraine has restored 1 gigawatt of thermal power plant capacity out of a planned 3.8 GW, as the country works to rebuild energy infrastructure damaged in the conflict.

stories.title: LATAM and Aerolíneas Argentinas aircraft collide on the ground at Santiago airport with no injuries reported
stories.summary: A LATAM Airlines Airbus A321 struck a stationary Aerolíneas Argentinas Boeing 737 on the ground at Santiago's Arturo Merino Benítez International Airport on Wednesday evening. No injuries were reported, but both affected flights were rescheduled following the collision on the airport apron.

stories.title: In letter to UNSC president, Dar draws attention to 'grave' consequences of Indus Waters Treaty suspension by India
stories.summary: Pakistan's UN Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad delivered a letter from Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar to the UN Security Council president, urging the body to address India's unilateral suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty and warning of grave peace, security, and humanitarian consequences for South Asia.

stories.title: US Navy Secretary Phelan fired by Pentagon, say sources
stories.summary: US Navy Secretary John Phelan was fired from his position effective immediately, according to officials familiar with the matter. The Pentagon did not provide a reason for his departure, which follows recent dismissals including the Army's top general by Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth.

stories.title: Higher fuel costs due to Iran war mean fewer people will receive aid globally, NRC says
stories.summary: The head of the Norwegian Refugee Council warned on Thursday that the Iran war is driving up global energy prices, increasing costs for humanitarian operations. Higher fuel expenses are making it more expensive to transport aid, pay staff, and purchase food for displaced populations, meaning fewer people will receive assistance worldwide.

stories.title: Trump says Israel-Lebanon ceasefire to be extended by three weeks
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced that the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire would be extended by three weeks. Envoys from both countries met in Washington as the fragile truce had been set to expire on Sunday.

stories.title: Hezbollah fires rocket salvo at northern Israel shortly before ceasefire extended
stories.summary: Hezbollah fired a salvo of rockets at northern Israel shortly before the ceasefire was extended, marking the first such attack since the truce began. The attack occurred while Israeli and Lebanese envoys were meeting at the White House. An IDF reservist in southern Lebanon was lightly injured by an explosive-laden drone.

stories.title: IRGC commander backs Iran ‘unity’ after Trump division claims
stories.summary: Iran's Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani pushed back against U.S. President Donald Trump's claims of internal divisions within Iran's leadership. Qaani emphasized national cohesion, describing the unity between Iran's public and its officials as the backbone of the country's strength.

stories.title: Teenager becomes first Congo virus fatality in Pakistan's Karachi
stories.summary: A teenager in Karachi became Pakistan's first fatality from Congo virus, raising concern among health officials ahead of the Eid al-Adha festival next month.

stories.title: Heavy weapons use in Iran war sparks concerns over US readiness in Taiwan: Report
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that the volume of munitions the U.S. has expended in its war with Iran has raised concerns about a short-term gap in readiness to defend Taiwan against a potential Chinese invasion. Officials worry the shortfall could expose American forces to increased risk.

stories.title: Vlasiuk discusses next sanctions package targeting energy, finance, and weapons components
stories.summary: Ukrainian sanctions commissioner Vlasiuk discussed the EU's upcoming 21st sanctions package against Russia, which will target Russia's financial system, impose additional energy export restrictions, and introduce new controls on dual-use goods.

stories.title: EU leaders to discuss mutual assistance pact amid NATO doubts
stories.summary: European Union leaders are set to discuss the bloc's mutual assistance clause at a summit in Cyprus on Thursday. The talks come amid growing doubts about US President Donald Trump's commitment to NATO, as his criticism of traditional allies raises concerns about collective security during a period of increasing instability.

stories.title: US soldier charged with using inside info to win US$400,000 bet on Maduro’s capture
stories.summary: U.S. Army senior enlisted soldier Gannon Ken Van Dyk has been charged by federal prosecutors in New York with using classified information from the operation to capture Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro to place bets on the prediction market platform Polymarket, allegedly winning US$400,000.

stories.title: Hezbollah fires rockets, citing Israeli ceasefire violations
stories.summary: Hezbollah launched rockets toward the northern Israeli settlement of Shtula, describing the attack as a response to Israeli violations of the ceasefire, specifically strikes on the southern Lebanese city of Yater. The Israeli military said it detected and intercepted several projectiles originating from Lebanon.

stories.title: Trump ally to visit China as US turns up pressure before May summit
stories.summary: Senator Steve Daines of Montana will lead a bipartisan five-member U.S. delegation to Shanghai and Beijing starting May 1. The visit comes as Washington increases pressure on China over trade, technology competition, and its ties to Iran, ahead of a leaders' summit scheduled for May 14–15.

stories.title: Chechen woman flees Russia after abduction attempt in Siberia
stories.summary: Aishat Khizriyeva, a 21-year-old Chechen woman, fled Russia after an abduction attempt in Siberia, according to the human rights group SK SOS, which reported her departure on April 23.

stories.title: Boy George speaks out against critics who condemned his pro-Israel stance
stories.summary: British singer Boy George publicly defended his pro-Israel stance amid criticism. The 70th Eurovision Song Contest in Vienna faces a boycott call from over 1,000 musicians protesting Israel's participation.

stories.title: ‘China or India or some other hellhole’: Trump reposts anti-immigrant rant
stories.summary: President Donald Trump reposted social media content from a conservative commentator describing India as a "hellhole," prompting India's government to call the remarks "inappropriate." The incident comes ahead of a planned visit to India by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio aimed at easing recent bilateral tensions.

stories.title: DRC: first eurobond draws massive demand [Business Africa]
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo raised $1.25 billion in its first-ever Eurobond issuance, marking a major debut in international financial markets. Investor demand was nearly four times the amount offered, reflecting strong interest in the DRC's sovereign debt.

stories.title: EU approves large loan to Ukraine and 20th sanctions package against Russia after Hungary drops opposition
stories.summary: The European Union approved a large loan to Ukraine and adopted its 20th sanctions package against Russia after Hungary withdrew its opposition, clearing the way for the measures to proceed.

stories.title: At least one dead and five people injured in Louisiana mall shooting, police say
stories.summary: At least one person was killed and five others were injured in a shooting inside the food court at the Mall of Louisiana in Baton Rouge on Thursday. Baton Rouge police said two groups exchanged gunfire following an argument, and several individuals fled the scene.

stories.title: EU formally approves Ukraine loan and 20th sanctions package against Russia
stories.summary: The European Union formally approved a loan for Ukraine and its 20th package of sanctions against Russia. EU ambassadors had already given their approval to both measures on April 22.

stories.title: ‘Undeniable reality’: why China should be wary of US focus on global maritime chokepoints
stories.summary: A Chinese policy adviser at East China Normal University warned Beijing that U.S. confrontations with Iran over the Strait of Hormuz signal Washington's intent to contain China through control of global maritime chokepoints. The adviser recommended that China strengthen its naval presence in the region.

stories.title: Milei administration in Argentina blocks journalist access to Casa Rosada
stories.summary: Argentina's Milei administration has restricted journalist access to the Casa Rosada presidential palace. Press freedom advocates have raised concerns about increasingly hostile rhetoric toward media and tightening access policies under President Javier Milei's government.

stories.title: First tranche of European defense loan for Ukraine to total EUR 6B, source says
stories.summary: The first tranche of a European defense loan to Ukraine is expected to total 6 billion euros by the end of June 2026. The funds will be allocated to purchase a batch of Ukrainian-made drones.

stories.title: UK Jews are under siege, and Iran faces no consequences - comment
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police and Counter Terrorism Policing have arrested 25 people in connection with attacks on Jewish sites in the UK. Eight have been charged, one convicted, and the rest remain under investigation.

stories.title: Trump’s Iran War Approaches a Fresh Legal Hurdle
stories.summary: Congressional pressure is expected to mount on Republican lawmakers to vote on ending the US military campaign in Iran as the conflict approaches a legal time limit under war-powers provisions.

stories.title: Israel prepared to renew Iran war, awaiting 'green light' from Trump, Katz says
stories.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said the IDF is prepared to resume military operations against Iran and is awaiting authorization from US President Donald Trump. Katz warned that future strikes would target "the most painful places" and be "different and deadly."

stories.title: Heavy weapons use in Iran war sparks concerns over US readiness in Taiwan: Report
stories.summary: A report raises concerns that heavy U.S. munitions expenditure in the Iran conflict could create shortages that would increase risks for American forces in a potential defense of Taiwan against a Chinese invasion. The assessment highlights the strain on U.S. military readiness across multiple theaters.

stories.title: Trump declares 3-week truce extension as Israel and Lebanon hold talks at White House
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced a three-week extension of the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire, shortly after Hezbollah fired rockets at Israel for the first time during the truce. Trump said Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and Lebanon's president would meet in Washington in the coming weeks.

stories.title: Nausėda: Lithuania backs consistent EU integration approach for Ukraine and Moldova
stories.summary: Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda expressed support for a consistent EU integration approach for both Ukraine and Moldova, stating he sees no reason to differentiate between the two countries on their paths to European Union membership.

stories.title: Trump rules out using nuclear weapons against Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated at the White House on Thursday that nuclear weapons should never be used, ruling out their deployment against Iran. The remarks marked a reversal from earlier threats of overwhelming force against the country.

stories.title: An Economic War of Attrition
stories.summary: The United States and Iran have shifted from direct military confrontation to economic warfare. Both sides are now focused on inflicting financial pressure on each other in what has become an economic war of attrition.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1520: EU unlocks €90 billion for Ukraine and adopts 20th sanctions package
stories.summary: The European Union approved a €90 billion loan for Ukraine and adopted its 20th sanctions package against Russia on April 23, with the first tranche expected by May or June for weapons, budget support, and energy defense. The new sanctions target 20 Russian banks, 46 shadow fleet tankers, and cryptocurrency platforms used to evade oil-price caps.

stories.title: FIA set to fast track money laundering probes
stories.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) is set to fast-track money laundering probes under a new rulebook that fixes deadlines for inquiries and creates dedicated desks nationwide.
FIA Direc

stories.title: Pentagon says US forces boarded tanker in Indian Ocean carrying Iran oil
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced that US forces boarded a tanker in the Indian Ocean carrying Iranian oil. The operation was described as aimed at disrupting illicit networks providing material support to Iran.

stories.title: Russian blogger Victoria Bonya accepts invitation to appear on propagandist Solovyov’s broadcast
stories.summary: Russian blogger Victoria Bonya announced she accepted an invitation to appear live on a broadcast hosted by the team of Vladimir Solovyov, a prominent Russian state propagandist.

stories.title: Funeral held for journalist killed in targeted Israeli strike
stories.summary: Mourners in south Lebanon attended the funeral of journalist Amal Khalil, who was killed in a targeted Israeli airstrike. The strike has drawn attention to the dangers faced by media workers operating in conflict zones along the Israel-Lebanon border.

stories.title: In Orban’s rule, Israelis saw a model for their own country - will he also be one in defeat?
stories.summary: Hungary's upcoming election is being closely watched in Israel, where voters are preparing for their own election within six months. Observers are assessing whether opposition candidate Péter Magyar would maintain Viktor Orbán's supportive stance toward Israel.

stories.title: Iran’s exiled former crown prince splattered with red liquid in Berlin
stories.summary: Iran's exiled former crown prince Reza Pahlavi was splattered with a red liquid, believed to be tomato sauce, during an incident in Berlin. The substance struck his coat and neck.

stories.title: Italy ready to deploy two minesweepers in Hormuz Strait, navy chief says
stories.summary: Italy's navy chief announced the country is prepared to deploy two minesweepers to the Strait of Hormuz. The vessels would require approximately four weeks to reach the area.

stories.title: Dnipro Jewish community leader’s home damaged in Russian strike, wounding child
stories.summary: A Russian strike damaged the home of the Jewish community leader in Dnipro, Ukraine, wounding a child who is now recovering. The city has endured an intense barrage of Russian drone and missile attacks over the past week.

stories.title: EU formally approves 90bn euro Ukraine loan and new sanctions on Russia
stories.summary: The European Union formally approved a 90-billion-euro loan package for Ukraine along with a new round of sanctions targeting Russia. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy welcomed the decision and urged that the first tranche be disbursed by May or June.

stories.title: Pope decries migrants and refugees being treated ‘worse than house pets’
stories.summary: Pope Leo criticized the treatment of migrants and refugees globally, saying they are treated worse than household pets. The pontiff has previously directed criticism at U.S. President Donald Trump's immigration policies and called for more humane treatment of displaced people.

stories.title: War-driven demand boosts profits for weapons and aircraft manufacturers
stories.summary: Boeing reported a reduced first-quarter loss as its defense division's earnings rose, bolstered by a $2.3 billion U.S. Pentagon contract. The broader weapons and aircraft manufacturing sector has seen increased profits driven by heightened global demand linked to ongoing conflicts.

stories.title: Will complex EU loan deal intensify conflict?
stories.summary: Ukraine has received a multibillion-dollar loan from the European Union as part of Western efforts to support Kyiv. Meanwhile, Russia continues to generate significant oil revenue, raising questions about whether the financial dynamics could prolong the conflict.

stories.title: Trump says he is keeping Strait of Hormuz closed, not Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump claimed that he, not Iran, is the one keeping the Strait of Hormuz closed. The statement comes amid heightened tensions in the Persian Gulf region, where the strategic waterway is critical to global oil shipments.

stories.title: Ukraine launches new level of air defense — Fedorov
stories.summary: Ukraine's Minister of Digital Transformation Mykhailo Fedorov announced the launch of a new level of "small" air defense capability aimed at enhancing protection against aerial threats.

stories.title: US sanctions Cambodian senator over purported scam network links
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department imposed sanctions on Cambodian Senator Kok An, accusing him and his associates of using political influence to protect a network of fraud centers. The action targets what Washington describes as a scam network operating with high-level political cover in Cambodia.

stories.title: Peter Beinart’s ‘Being Jewish After the Destruction of Gaza’ wins PEN America award
stories.summary: Peter Beinart's book "Being Jewish After the Destruction of Gaza" won a PEN America award. Judges praised it for offering a model for rewriting narratives, noting that PEN America's CEO departed in 2024 after the organization published a report accusing Israel of genocide.

stories.title: EU leaders, Zelensky to celebrate unblocked funds for Kyiv in Cyprus
stories.summary: EU leaders and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky are meeting in Cyprus to mark the release of previously blocked funds for Kyiv. The two-day summit will also include discussions on the Middle East conflict and its broader consequences.

stories.title: White House accuses China of industrial-scale theft of AI technology
stories.summary: The White House accused China of stealing intellectual property from US artificial intelligence laboratories on an industrial scale. Beijing denied the allegation.

stories.title: With travel chaos looming, Brittany Ferries vows no price hikes
stories.summary: Brittany Ferries CEO Christophe Mathieu announced the company has sufficient maritime fuel supplies for the summer season and pledged not to raise ticket prices despite the global energy crisis. The statement comes amid expectations of widespread travel disruption for European holidaymakers.

stories.title: US boards ship carrying Iran oil as Trump threatens mine-laying vessels
stories.summary: U.S. Central Command boarded a ship carrying Iranian oil as part of an ongoing blockade. CENTCOM stated it has intercepted 33 vessels since imposing restrictions on maritime traffic to and from Iran, while Trump threatened mine-laying vessels.

stories.title: Romania's ruling coalition loses majority after its biggest party walks out
stories.summary: Seven ministers from Romania's Social Democrats, the country's largest party, resigned from Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan's pro-European coalition government on Thursday. The departures stripped Bolojan of his parliamentary majority and put access to EU funds at risk.

stories.title: Prominent activist’s chilling jail-time manifesto details rationale for Oct. 7 hate in US
stories.summary: Casey Goonan, imprisoned for firebombings in California, authored a manifesto while incarcerated detailing his rationale for violence inspired by Hamas's October 7 attack. The document frames the Hamas invasion as the launch of a broader worldwide struggle.

stories.title: A Jewish Iranian Expat Watches the War Unfold - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Journalist Roya Hakakian, a Jewish Iranian expatriate, discussed the Iran conflict and her hopes for the Iranian people in an interview. She also reflected on what Western feminists can learn from Iranian women's experiences.

stories.title: Hungary, Slovakia get Russian oil from repaired Ukraine pipeline
stories.summary: Hungary and Slovakia resumed receiving Russian oil through the Druzhba pipeline after Ukraine completed repairs. The pipeline had been damaged in a Russian attack in January.

stories.title: Son of former Shah of Iran appeals to Western countries for support
stories.summary: Reza Pahlavi, son of Iran's former Shah, appealed in Berlin on Thursday for Western countries to join the conflict against Iran. He also criticised the German government's decision not to meet with him during his visit.

stories.title: Trump to host Israel-Lebanon talks at White House
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump will host Israeli and Lebanese representatives at the White House for a second round of ambassador-level negotiations aimed at easing tensions between the two sides, according to a White House official.

stories.title: Trump, in absentia, becomes first non-Israeli to receive Israel’s top civilian honor
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump became the first non-Israeli to receive Israel's top civilian honor, though he was not present at the ceremony. He had reportedly planned to accept via a videotaped address after an invitation from Israel's Education Minister.

stories.title: Meeting in Cyprus: Joint statement by Zelensky, Costa and von der Leyen
stories.summary: At a meeting in Cyprus, Ukrainian President Zelensky, European Council President Costa, and European Commission President von der Leyen welcomed the approval of a €90 billion EU loan for Ukraine. They called on third countries to help close remaining financing gaps and endorsed the 20th sanctions package against Russia.

stories.title: Woman charged with plotting attack on Houston synagogue ‘to kill as many Jews as possible’
stories.summary: An 18-year-old woman from North Carolina was charged with plotting a car-ramming attack on Congregation Beth Israel in Houston, Texas, intended to kill as many Jewish people as possible. She is held on a $10 million bond; two male co-conspirators remain at large.

stories.title: Australia news live: Andrew Hastie says US alliance weakened Australia; Sri Lanka hackers steal millions owed to Australia
stories.summary: Australian Liberal frontbencher Andrew Hastie argued that deepening reliance on the US alliance has eroded Australia's sovereign capabilities, including its defence industry. He urged the country to strengthen its national security posture. Separately, Sri Lankan hackers reportedly stole millions of dollars owed to the Australian government.

stories.title: Israel appoints new envoy to Christian world after Lebanese Jesus statue, Pizzaballa controversies
stories.summary: Israel appointed George Deek as its new envoy to the Christian world, following recent controversies involving a Lebanese Jesus statue and Latin Patriarch Pierbattista Pizzaballa. Deek, formerly Israel's ambassador to Azerbaijan, is noted as Israel's first Christian ambassador.

stories.title: Iran dismisses Trump’s claim of leadership rift, says nation is ‘one soul’
stories.summary: Iranian officials dismissed U.S. President Donald Trump's claims of a leadership rift within Iran, asserting that the nation remains unified. Multiple officials emphasized what they described as the "iron unity of the nation and government."

stories.title: Lebanon Seeks to Extend Israel-Hezbollah Cease-Fire
stories.summary: Lebanon is working to extend the ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah, but Hezbollah's opposition to negotiations and ongoing Israeli military strikes are complicating diplomatic progress.

stories.title: Sudan refugee crisis driving Chad measles, meningitis outbreaks: MSF
stories.summary: Médecins Sans Frontières reported that eastern Chad is experiencing simultaneous outbreaks of meningitis and measles, driven by large numbers of refugees crossing the border from Sudan.

stories.title: The Pentagon replicated a Ukrainian-style drone attack in Florida. Now it’s changing its counter-drone strategy
stories.summary: The Pentagon conducted a military exercise in Florida replicating Ukrainian-style drone attack tactics. The results are informing changes to the US military's counter-drone strategy, with the exercise distinguished by novel technology and participants.

stories.title: Indian seafarer among crew of ship held by Iran in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran is holding two vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, including the ship Epaminondas with a crew of 21 that includes at least one Indian seafarer.

stories.title: EU loan allows us to increase air defense production and protect energy infrastructure – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky expressed gratitude for progress on the €90 billion EU loan, stating it will allow Ukraine to increase air defense production and protect critical energy infrastructure. He also welcomed the new EU sanctions package against Russia.

stories.title: US blockade of Hormuz successful despite media reports suggesting otherwise, maritime expert says
stories.summary: A maritime expert said the US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz is succeeding despite contrary media reports. Seven large container ships detected near Iran's Chabahar Port were not evidence of Iran shifting operations east of Hormuz, as initially speculated.

stories.title: Amal Khalil: The fearless journalist, killed by Israel, who embodied southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Amal Khalil, a veteran Lebanese journalist from southern Lebanon, was killed by Israeli forces in the region where she was born during an earlier Israeli occupation. Her brother described her as a figure present in every Lebanese home.

stories.title: LaGuardia firefighter heard ‘stop’ before crash but didn’t know who it was for, report says
stories.summary: The National Transportation Safety Board released a preliminary report on the March 22 collision at New York's LaGuardia Airport between a fire truck and an Air Canada jet that killed both pilots. A firefighter on the truck heard an air traffic controller say "stop, stop, stop" but did not know the warning was directed at him. The airport's crash prevention system failed to generate an alert.

stories.title: Blood diamonds, crypto: Hezbollah’s financial operations in Europe serve as major terror lifeline
stories.summary: A report by the Democratic Procedures Institute found that Hezbollah maintains extensive financial operations across Europe, including involvement in blood diamonds and cryptocurrency. The network is concentrated in wealthier nations such as France and Germany and serves as a major funding source for the group.

stories.title: Pakistan rejects Indian propaganda on Pahalgam attack, deplores 'weaponisation of false narrative'
stories.summary: Pakistan rejected India's allegations linking it to the April 22, 2025, Pahalgam attack in which 26 people were killed, calling the claims a false narrative. Pakistan denied involvement and called for a neutral investigation into the deadliest armed attack in the disputed Kashmir region since 2000.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill four in Gaza, medics say
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed four people in Gaza, according to medics. Since the ceasefire began, four Israeli soldiers and more than 780 Palestinians have been killed in the territory.

stories.title: “A surprise for the enemy”: Budanov says Ukraine’s AI weapons are ready as drone numbers hit their ceiling
stories.summary: Ukraine's military intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov announced that AI-powered weapons systems are ready for deployment, as both Ukrainian and Russian forces approach the limits of current drone control technology. The head of the Presidential Office confirmed that AI represents the next frontier.

stories.title: Israel, Hezbollah trade ceasefire violation accusations as IDF tries to block civilians' return
stories.summary: Israel and Hezbollah exchanged accusations of ceasefire violations as the IDF continued efforts to prevent Lebanese civilians from returning to southern Lebanon. Israel has conditioned civilian return on progress toward a broader agreement involving Hezbollah's disarmament.

stories.title: Starting from the end: Resolving Israeli-Palestinian conflict is key to regional peace - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that resolving the Israeli-Palestinian conflict should be the central focus of regional peace efforts, suggesting that moderate Arab states could help re-center the broader agenda around this goal.

stories.title: Former Syrian rebel leader returns home after UAE detention
stories.summary: Former Syrian rebel leader Issam Buwaydani returned to Damascus on Thursday after being detained for nearly a year in the United Arab Emirates for undisclosed reasons.

stories.title: US deploys third aircraft carrier to Middle East, Centcom says
stories.summary: The United States has deployed a third aircraft carrier, the USS George HW Bush, to the Middle East, joining the USS Abraham Lincoln and USS Gerald R. Ford already in the region. US Central Command confirmed the carrier entered its area of responsibility in the Indian Ocean amid escalating regional tensions.

stories.title: Costa: Next step is to open first cluster of negotiations on Ukraine's EU accession
stories.summary: European Council President António Costa said the next step following the €90 billion loan and 20th sanctions package is to open the first cluster of accession negotiations for Ukraine's EU membership.

stories.title: What is Europe's plan to secure the Strait of Hormuz?
stories.summary: France and the United Kingdom are leading efforts to establish a multinational naval mission to safeguard shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Questions remain about the operation's scope and whether it can bring lasting stability to the strategic waterway.

stories.title: NDMA warns of intense heatwave in several regions across country till May 5
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Disaster Management Authority issued a nationwide alert warning of an intense heatwave in several regions through May 5, along with forecasts of rain, windstorms, and thunderstorms between April 24 and 29.

stories.title: Both Trump and Iran share false information about 8 women facing execution by the regime
stories.summary: Donald Trump claimed Iran agreed to spare eight Iranian women facing execution as a gesture of respect toward him, but accusations quickly emerged that the women were AI-generated. Iran gave conflicting responses, and two NGOs confirmed that all parties—both the U.S. and Iran—shared incorrect information about the cases.

stories.title: Police detain Modiin man for wearing kippa with Palestinian flag, cut it out
stories.summary: Israeli police in Modiin detained Alex Sinclair for wearing a kippa featuring a Palestinian flag, cutting the flag image from the religious headcovering. Sinclair filed a complaint, noting that officers falsely claimed displaying the Palestinian flag is illegal.

stories.title: EU Commission reveals details of 20th sanctions package against Russia
stories.summary: The European Commission published technical details of the 20th sanctions package against Russia, which for the first time includes an anti-circumvention tool. The measures were adopted by EU member states to further restrict Russia's ability to evade existing sanctions.

stories.title: Israeli fire kills five in Gaza and the West Bank, medics say
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes killed at least four Palestinians in Gaza on Thursday, according to medics. In a separate incident, Israeli soldiers shot and killed a Palestinian teenager in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Dutch facing biggest security threat in decades, intelligence agency says
stories.summary: The Netherlands' intelligence agency warned that the country faces its largest security threat in decades. The agency identified Russia and China as the primary sources of these threats.

stories.title: Trump to meet Lebanon and Israel envoys, as Beirut seeks truce extension
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump will meet Lebanese and Israeli envoys at the White House on Thursday for a new round of peace talks, with Beirut seeking a one-month extension of a ceasefire set to expire. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is leading the diplomatic effort.

stories.title: Lebanon Is Done With Hezbollah
stories.summary: Lebanon and Israel are reportedly engaged in discussions centered on countering Hezbollah, which both neighboring states view as a mutual adversary. The talks signal a potential shift in Lebanon's posture toward the Iran-backed group.

stories.title: Iranian ex-shah’s son says talks with Tehran are ‘appeasement’
stories.summary: Reza Pahlavi, son of Iran's former Shah, characterised diplomatic engagement with Tehran as appeasement. He urged European governments not involved in the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran to take alternative measures against the Iranian government.

stories.title: Iran takes seized ships to port, countries check on seafarers’ safety
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps seized multiple ships on April 22 and transported them to port. Several countries are now checking on the safety of their seafarers aboard the seized vessels.

stories.title: Iran's economy looks set to withstand US naval blockade
stories.summary: Analysts say the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports will likely reduce Iran's oil output but is unlikely to cause immediate economic collapse. The standoff centers on the Strait of Hormuz, which normally carries about a fifth of global oil and LNG traffic.

stories.title: Ukrainian Navy destroys Russian unmanned sea craft near Odesa port
stories.summary: Ukraine's Naval Forces destroyed a Russian unmanned surface vessel that attempted to approach a port in the Odesa area, according to a military announcement.

stories.title: US says it redirected 33 ships under Iran naval blockade
stories.summary: US Central Command announced it has redirected 33 vessels since enforcing a naval blockade on Iran, up from 31 earlier the same day. The US military also reported intercepting and boarding a sanctioned vessel allegedly carrying Iranian oil in the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Palestinian teen shot dead, Israeli child lightly hurt in rock-throwing as West Bank roils
stories.summary: A Palestinian teenager was shot dead and an Israeli child was lightly injured in rock-throwing incidents as violence escalated in the West Bank. Separately, Israeli forces thwarted an attempted car-ramming attack, and France's foreign minister warned the EU may impose sanctions on Israelis linked to violent settler attacks.

stories.title: Amid spate of arson attacks on Jewish sites, Starmer warns of ‘malign state actors’
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer visited a targeted synagogue amid a series of arson attacks on Jewish sites in the United Kingdom. He expressed growing concern about "malign state actors" using proxies to stage attacks domestically.

stories.title: Trump may talk of regime infighting, but Iran seems united by strategy born of war
stories.summary: Despite President Donald Trump's claims of intense infighting within Iran's leadership, multiple analysts said Tehran has displayed notable institutional cohesion. Experts suggested that US-backed assassinations of senior Iranian commanders, including more pragmatic figures, may have inadvertently unified the country's leadership rather than fracturing it.

stories.title: IDF uncovers Hezbollah stronghold 25 m. underground in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces reported uncovering a Hezbollah stronghold approximately 25 meters underground in southern Lebanon. Soldiers found weapons and multiple rooms inside the complex that had been used for Hezbollah's operational management.

stories.title: Iran Is Calling the Shots Now
stories.summary: Analysts suggest Iran is adopting a strategic approach likened to Ho Chi Minh's playbook during the Vietnam War, positioning Tehran as a driving force in shaping regional dynamics amid ongoing tensions with the United States.

stories.title: Trump orders U.S. military to 'shoot and kill' Iranian small boats choking Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump ordered the U.S. military to shoot and kill Iranian small boats operating in the Strait of Hormuz. The Pentagon denied a news report claiming the Defense Department assessed it could take six months to clear Iranian-laid mines from the waterway.

stories.title: 'Shame, disgrace': Israeli diplomat in US heckled at Silicon Valley Memorial Day ceremony
stories.summary: Israeli Ambassador Marco Sermoneta was heckled by attendees at a Silicon Valley Memorial Day ceremony in the United States. A group began singing the Israeli national anthem in protest as the diplomat denounced critics of the IDF and the State of Israel.

stories.title: How Trump’s Iran war is driving military dissent
stories.summary: Dissent is reportedly growing within the United States military over the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, manifesting in both public protests and quieter forms of resistance among service members.

stories.title: Air defences activated in Tehran as ‘hostile targets’ reported
stories.summary: Air defense systems were activated across parts of Tehran on Thursday after Iranian media reported attempts to intercept "hostile targets" over the capital. Authorities did not specify the nature of the threat, and no immediate damage or casualties were reported.

stories.title: US Navy is reviewing cost of future Ford-class carriers to ensure they ‘make sense’
stories.summary: The US Navy is reviewing the cost and capabilities of future Ford-class aircraft carriers to determine whether they justify their expense compared to older Nimitz-class vessels. Recently ousted Navy Secretary John Phelan said the service is evaluating how much more capable the Ford-class ships truly are.

stories.title: The scourge that is anti-Israel US politicians - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece criticizes Drew Warshaw, a candidate for New York City comptroller, for allegedly misrepresenting facts about Israel bonds in public statements. The article characterizes certain anti-Israel positions among US politicians as harmful.

stories.title: DoJ inspector general to audit department’s compliance with Epstein Files Transparency Act
stories.summary: The US Department of Justice's Office of the Inspector General announced an audit of the department's compliance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act. Deputy Inspector General William M. Blier said the review will evaluate processes for releasing mandated files, which have been plagued by missed deadlines, leaked victims' information, and excessive redactions.

stories.title: British delegation visits units defending Zaporizhzhia direction
stories.summary: Deputy Head of Ukraine's Presidential Office Pavlo Palisa and a British delegation led by UK National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell visited Ukrainian military units defending positions on the Zaporizhzhia front.

stories.title: Channel One host Pimanov, sanctioned for propaganda, dies at 64, network reports
stories.summary: Alexei Pimanov, a host on Russia's state-controlled Channel One who had been sanctioned internationally for propaganda, died of heart failure on April 23 at the age of 64, the network reported.

stories.title: War update: 32 clashes on front line since morning, with highest activity in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 32 attacks on Ukrainian Defense Forces positions since the morning, with the Pokrovsk sector experiencing the heaviest combat activity along the front line.

stories.title: US-Iran stalemate running out of time as risks for Trump and Tehran grow
stories.summary: U.S.-Iran negotiations remain stalled, with growing risks for both sides as time runs short. Analysts suggest Iran must either return to talks or face a potential new flare-up in military hostilities.

stories.title: Lebanon leaders accuse Israel of war crime after journalist killed
stories.summary: Lebanon's president and prime minister accused Israel of committing a war crime after an Israeli airstrike in southern Lebanon killed Amal Khalil, a 42-year-old journalist working for the Lebanese daily Al-Akhbar.

stories.title: Record demand can’t save US airlines from Iran war fuel shock
stories.summary: U.S. airlines face declining profits despite record travel demand as fuel costs surge due to the Iran war. Rising expenses are forcing carriers to cut routes and capacity.

stories.title: Israel defense minister says awaiting US green light to 'return Iran to Stone Age'
stories.summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz declared that Israel is prepared to resume its war against Iran and is waiting for US approval to return Iran to "the Stone Age," according to a report from Jerusalem.

stories.title: Palestine Action defendant wounded by taser and sledgehammer in raid, court hears
stories.summary: A court in England heard that Palestine Action defendant Leona Kamio, a 30-year-old nursery school teacher, sustained taser wounds, bruises, and a sledgehammer injury to her hand during her arrest at an Israeli-owned arms factory. A medical report documented wounds to her arm, hip, and chin.

stories.title: Iran war pushing more than 30 million back into poverty, UN development chief says
stories.summary: The UN development chief warned that the Iran war is pushing more than 30 million people back into poverty worldwide. The conflict is also straining humanitarian operations in regions already facing severe emergencies.

stories.title: Slovenia to air films about Palestine instead of Eurovision song contest
stories.summary: National broadcasters in Slovenia, Ireland, and Spain announced they will not air the Eurovision song contest this year, boycotting the event over Israel's participation. Slovenia's RTV said it would broadcast films about Palestine instead.

stories.title: Baby died after NHS trust failed to warn mother of ‘unsafe’ home birth, coroner finds
stories.summary: A coroner in the UK found that NHS trust Barnet Hospital failed to warn a mother about the risks of a home birth, leading to the death of seven-day-old Poppy Hope Lomas at University College Hospital London in October 2022.

stories.title: Iran flaunts its grip over the Strait of Hormuz with commandos storming cargo ship
stories.summary: Iran demonstrated its control over the Strait of Hormuz by deploying commandos to storm a cargo ship, shifting the conflict's arena to the Persian Gulf in an apparent strategy to inflict maximum economic pain on its adversaries.

stories.title: PM meets Pakistanis selected for China's space mission, hopes it will 'usher in era of space research'
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met astronaut candidates Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud, selected for China's manned space programme, expressing hope the mission would launch a new era of space research in Pakistan.

stories.title: Russian-controlled court jails woman for buying Ukrainian war bonds
stories.summary: A court in Russian-controlled southern Ukraine sentenced a woman to 14 years in prison for treason after she purchased Ukrainian war bonds to support the Ukrainian military.

stories.title: ‘Dirty f***ing Jew:’ Thames Police arrest Slough man after assault on Orthodox Jew
stories.summary: Thames Valley Police arrested a 48-year-old man from Slough on suspicion of racially or religiously aggravated assault and public order offenses after an attack on an Orthodox Jewish individual. The suspect has been in custody since Thursday evening.

stories.title: Italy says energy crisis puts its plans for defence spending in doubt
stories.summary: The Italian government indicated it may be unable to increase defense spending as planned due to economic difficulties and surging energy prices. A government document cited the need to address the energy crisis as a competing priority.

stories.title: What the Palantir CEO’s ‘manifesto’ tells us about the changing face of war
stories.summary: Palantir CEO Alex Karp's published manifesto called for mandatory military service and deeper ties between Silicon Valley and the Pentagon, while warning of an AI arms race. Critics note the growing entanglement of tech companies with military operations is outpacing oversight.

stories.title: Israeli troops carrying out large-scale looting in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli troops conducted large-scale looting of homes and businesses in southern Lebanon, according to a report by Haaretz. The report alleged that military commanders were aware of the looting but took no action to stop it.

stories.title: US drivers turn to EV rentals as gasoline prices surge
stories.summary: U.S. gasoline prices have risen by more than a third since the Iran war began on February 28, prompting growing numbers of American drivers to turn to electric vehicle rentals as a cheaper alternative.

stories.title: EU’s 20th sanctions package hits 20 Russian banks, 46 shadow fleet tankers, and crypto platforms
stories.summary: The European Union adopted its 20th sanctions package against Russia, targeting 20 Russian banks, 46 shadow fleet tankers, and cryptocurrency platforms. The measures also address oil transport and re-exports via Kyrgyzstan, bringing the total number of sanctioned shadow fleet ships to 632.

stories.title: IDF searches for suspects following attempted ramming attack against soldiers in West Bank
stories.summary: The IDF is searching for suspects after an attempted vehicle-ramming attack against soldiers in the West Bank. No soldiers were reported wounded in the incident.

stories.title: Dutch intelligence says security threats at their highest level in 80 years
stories.summary: The Dutch intelligence service AIVD assessed that the Netherlands faces its most serious national security threat in 80 years, the highest level since the end of World War II.

stories.title: Putin Defends Mobile Internet Outages as Necessary Measure in Fight Against Terrorism
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin publicly defended mobile internet shutdowns across the country as a necessary counterterrorism measure, marking his first personal comments on the disruptions that have caused widespread confusion.

stories.title: Israel seeks ‘green light’ from US to kill remaining Khamenei family members
stories.summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz stated that Israel is seeking US approval to target remaining members of the late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei's family, including his son Mojtaba Khamenei, who has assumed the role of supreme leader.

stories.title: In first, Ukrainian unmanned vessel launches interceptor to knock out Shahed drone
stories.summary: Ukraine deployed an unmanned surface vessel that launched an interceptor missile to shoot down a Russian Shahed drone, marking the first known use of such a capability. The development could strengthen Ukraine's air defenses and complicate Russia's leverage in potential future negotiations.

stories.title: Woman killed by bear in Polish forest, son and local government say
stories.summary: A 58-year-old woman was killed by a bear while walking in a mountainous forested area in Poland, in an extremely rare fatal encounter. Her son reported the incident to rescuers.

stories.title: Trump says he ordered US Navy to ‘shoot and kill’ boats mining the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said he ordered the US Navy to "shoot and kill" boats mining the Strait of Hormuz. Separately, reports indicate the IRGC has taken control in Iran amid claims Khamenei was "gravely injured," while Israel's Katz said he awaits US approval to strike Iranian nuclear sites.

stories.title: Trump orders Iran mine-layers sunk, as Iran tolls tankers
stories.summary: President Trump ordered the US Navy to sink any Iranian vessel caught laying mines in the Strait of Hormuz, further straining a fragile ceasefire as Gulf disruptions continued to impact the global economy.

stories.title: Extended naval blockade is admission US military escalation poses even greater risk
stories.summary: President Trump's decision to extend the US naval blockade of Iran indefinitely may reflect recognition that further military escalation risks breaching the nominal ceasefire. A third US carrier strike group, the George H.W. Bush, is expected to arrive in the Middle East imminently.

stories.title: Russia says it's maintaining oil supplies but has no new OPEC+ initiatives
stories.summary: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov stated that Russia continues its oil supplies and is contributing to price stabilization amid the global energy crisis. He said Moscow has no new OPEC+ initiatives to propose at this time.

stories.title: U.S. military says it seizes another oil tanker associated with Iran
stories.summary: The U.S. military seized another oil tanker associated with Iran, one day after Iranian forces attacked three cargo ships in the Strait of Hormuz and captured two of them. The escalation intensified disruptions to the waterway through which roughly 20% of the world's traded oil passes.

stories.title: Truce without talks: What room for diplomacy between US and Iran?
stories.summary: Diplomatic efforts between the US and Iran remain stalled despite a unilateral ceasefire, with Iran seeking accountability for the killing of its leader and the US sending mixed signals. Ship seizures in the Strait of Hormuz and unclear chains of command on both sides complicate mediation.

stories.title: Israeli Air Force technicians indicted for spying on IDF chief, Ben-Gvir at Iran's behest
stories.summary: Two Israeli Air Force technicians were indicted for spying on behalf of Iran, including conducting surveillance of the IDF chief and National Security Minister Ben-Gvir. The indictment states one soldier sent training materials to an Iranian agent.

stories.title: Dutch are facing biggest security threat in decades, intelligence agency says
stories.summary: The Dutch intelligence agency AIVD reported that the Netherlands faces its greatest security threat in decades, identifying Russia and China as the primary sources of concern.

stories.title: Mixed views in Lebanon ahead of controversial talks with Israel
stories.summary: Lebanon remains divided over upcoming negotiations with Israel, with segments of the population supporting Hezbollah's armed resistance while others favor diplomatic engagement.

stories.title: Pope Leo departs Equatorial Guinea after wrapping up his 11-day trip to Africa
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV held an open-air mass in Equatorial Guinea before tens of thousands of followers, concluding an 11-day African tour that was marked by criticism from US President Donald Trump over the Pope's stance on Iran.

stories.title: Ceasefire extended: What's next in the Iran war?
stories.summary: The United States and Iran are negotiating to protect their respective interests amid an extended ceasefire with no fixed deadline, though several major sticking points remain unresolved.

stories.title: UK prepared to deploy RAF Typhoons to keep strait of Hormuz open after Iran war
stories.summary: The United Kingdom offered to deploy RAF Typhoons based in Qatar and mine-hunting drones to help patrol and clear the Strait of Hormuz as part of a multinational mission once the Iran war ends. The proposal was made during a 30-country meeting jointly organized by France.

stories.title: King Charles on US mission to bolster UK's special relationship with royalist Trump
stories.summary: Britain's King Charles will travel to the United States for the most high-profile trip of his reign, aimed at strengthening the UK-US "special relationship." The Iran war has strained bilateral ties to their lowest point in 70 years.

stories.title: Trump poised to expand refugee program for white South Africans
stories.summary: The Trump administration is considering more than doubling the annual refugee limit to increase admissions of white South Africans to the United States, according to three people familiar with the discussions.

stories.title: Israel is drawing closer to the Middle East — while the West turns a cold shoulder
stories.summary: Israel is engaging in diplomatic talks with regional adversaries including Lebanon and Syria, while traditional European allies are distancing themselves and seeking to loosen ties with Jerusalem.

stories.title: Palestine Action defendant wounded by taser and sledgehammer in raid, court hears
stories.summary: At Woolwich Crown Court in London, Palestine Action defendants Leona Kamio and Samuel Corner described being wounded by a taser and struck with a sledgehammer during a police raid. The pair also recounted altercations with security guards and police during the incident.

stories.title: Who are the Lebanese journalists killed by Israel since 2 March?
stories.summary: Multiple Lebanese journalists have been killed by Israeli strikes since 2 March while on assignment in Lebanon. The ongoing Israeli assault has been described as catastrophic for the country's media industry and press community.

stories.title: Could Italy replace Iran at the 2026 World Cup?
stories.summary: FIFA has no plans to replace Iran with Italy at the 2026 World Cup, according to sources, after the idea was proposed by a special envoy of US President Donald Trump.

stories.title: Florida student arrested over 'Netanyahu, drop bombs' joke
stories.summary: A Florida International University student named Gabriela Saldana was arrested after a social media joke referencing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu prompted a police investigation and criminal charges.

stories.title: Grenade explodes in apartment building in Mykolaiv: One dead, one injured
