stories.title: Russia’s Culture Ministry denies distribution license for film about woman who leaves North Korea
stories.summary: Russia's Culture Ministry denied a distribution license for the film 'Hana Korea,' which tells the story of a woman who leaves North Korea, according to its Russian distributor U Films.

stories.title: Nigeria: Tinubu Seeks Senate Approval for Fresh $516m Loan
stories.summary: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu submitted a request to the Senate seeking approval to borrow an additional $516.3 million in external loans. The purpose of the fresh borrowing was not detailed in the initial report.

stories.title: Iran’s exiled crown prince Pahlavi splashed with red substance in Berlin
stories.summary: Reza Pahlavi, Iran's exiled crown prince, was splashed with a red liquid as he left Germany's federal press conference building in Berlin on Thursday. The incident occurred after he had criticised the US-Iran ceasefire at a news briefing. He appeared unhurt and departed by car; police investigated the substance.

stories.title: Russian troops intensify attempts to advance toward Kupiansk from north, says Tregubov
stories.summary: Russian forces have intensified offensive operations aimed at advancing toward the city of Kupiansk in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, particularly from the northern direction, according to Ukrainian military spokesperson Tregubov.

stories.title: Philippines’ ex-president Rodrigo Duterte to face trial for crimes against humanity
stories.summary: The International Criminal Court confirmed charges of crimes against humanity against former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte over his anti-drugs crackdown. Pre-trial judges unanimously found substantial grounds to believe Duterte was responsible for murder and attempted murder in operations that killed thousands of people. He will now face trial at the ICC.

stories.title: Why Indian Muslim voters say they’ve been frozen out of this state election
stories.summary: Millions of voters in West Bengal, India, are participating in state elections, but more than 9 million names — many belonging to Muslim voters — have been deleted from electoral rolls.

stories.title: Plan for healthier school meals in England will hit services, say caterers
stories.summary: A UK trade body representing school caterers warned that proposed government rules for healthier school meals in England could have a devastating effect on catering services. The proposals would increase the use of lentils, pulses, and beans while limiting desserts and grab-and-go items such as pizzas and sausage rolls.

stories.title: Daily Briefing April 23 – Netanyahu’s campaign enters high gear at state ceremonies
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu intensified political campaigning at state ceremonies, while talks in Washington, D.C., continued regarding potential peace arrangements for Israel-Lebanon and the Iran conflict.

stories.title: China must ‘strengthen education’ of Tibetan Buddhists, Beijing official says after tour
stories.summary: Li Ganjie, head of the Chinese Communist Party's United Front Work Department and Politburo member, called for strengthening the education, training, and management of Tibetan Buddhist personnel during a visit to Tibetan areas in western China. The remarks were reported by state news agency Xinhua on Wednesday.

stories.title: Republican lawmakers attempt to shield big oil from climate lawsuits in ‘alarming’ bills
stories.summary: Republican lawmakers in the US House and Senate introduced bills that would grant oil and gas companies broad legal immunity from climate-related lawsuits and policies. The House bill is led by Representative Harriet Hageman of Wyoming, and the Senate version by Senator Ted Cruz of Texas. Environmental advocates warned the legislation would shield polluters from accountability.

stories.title: Why Anthropic’s Mythos has energised China’s cybersecurity industry
stories.summary: Anthropic's unreleased AI model, Claude Mythos Preview, has attracted significant attention from China's cybersecurity and finance industries. The model is reportedly capable of autonomously identifying and exploiting cybersecurity vulnerabilities at levels surpassing conventional enterprise tools. It has not been made publicly available.

stories.title: Chinese hackers are using everyday devices to hack UK firms, warns watchdog
stories.summary: The UK's National Cyber Security Centre and agencies in nine other countries warned that Chinese state-backed hackers are targeting everyday devices such as wifi routers to conduct espionage against British businesses. Companies were urged to increase vigilance against persistent cyber-attack attempts linked to Beijing.

stories.title: Nigeria: Amupitan - What God Told Me Before I Accepted INEC Job
stories.summary: Prof. Joash Amupitan, newly appointed chairman of Nigeria's Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), said he accepted the role after receiving what he described as a divine conviction. He expressed confidence that God would strengthen him in office.

stories.title: Naqvi, US envoy discuss diplomatic efforts for holding 2nd round of US-Iran talks in Islamabad
stories.summary: Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi met US Chargé d'Affaires Natalie Baker in Islamabad to discuss diplomatic efforts toward hosting a second round of US-Iran negotiations in the Pakistani capital. Naqvi praised US President Donald Trump's initiative to extend a ceasefire, calling it a welcome development.

stories.title: Zelensky appoints heads of SSU departments in Kyiv and Kyiv region, Kherson and Kharkiv regions
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky appointed new heads of Security Service of Ukraine (SSU) departments in Kyiv, the Kyiv region, and the Kherson and Kharkiv regions, as part of ongoing leadership restructuring.

stories.title: How the Philippines became Japan’s closest security partner in Southeast Asia
stories.summary: The Philippines and Japan have deepened military cooperation, with Japanese forces participating for the first time in this year's Balikatan exercises hosted by the Philippines. Tokyo also eased its defence export rules on Tuesday, paving the way for expanded bilateral partnerships in joint drills and defence technology.

stories.title: Supreme Court hears petitions demanding October 7 state inquiry, bereaved families disrupt
stories.summary: Israel's Supreme Court heard petitions to compel the government to establish a state commission of inquiry into the October 7 Hamas attack, more than two and a half years after the massacre. Bereaved families disrupted proceedings.

stories.title: Iranian women held by US immigration not Qassem Soleimani's relatives: Report
stories.summary: Hamideh Soleimani Afshar and her daughter Sarina, arrested in the US in early April after their residency permits were rescinded, are reportedly not relatives of slain Iranian Quds Force commander Qassem Soleimani, contrary to earlier claims circulated by far-right campaigner Laura Loomer.

stories.title: Israel at 78 still believes it can live by the sword alone. A reckoning is due
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Israel, marking its 78th year, continues to rely on military force while liberal Israeli nostalgia for an earlier, better state overlooks the Nakba and occupation that existed from the country's founding.

stories.title: Israel at 78 still believes it can live by the sword alone. A reckoning is due
stories.summary: Writing on Israel's 78th Independence Day, columnist Gideon Levy argues that liberal Israeli nostalgia for an earlier, better version of the state is an illusion, citing the Nakba and occupation as foundational elements.

stories.title: The economic winners & losers in the US-Israel war on Iran
stories.summary: Analysts are assessing the economic impact of the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran, identifying sectors and countries that stand to gain or lose from the conflict.

stories.title: Trust trumps everything else: Anthropic’s India chief Irina Ghose
stories.summary: At the AWS Summit in Bengaluru, Anthropic's India Managing Director Irina Ghose emphasized the importance of customer trust and building reliable AI products that serve all users.

stories.title: Hong Kong airport staff offered free measles jabs in bid to prevent outbreak
stories.summary: Hong Kong health authorities announced free measles vaccinations for airport workers starting Friday after three cases were detected among aircraft maintenance staff. The Centre for Health Protection cited a high risk of transmission at the airport due to heavy traveller volumes and a significant proportion of non-local-born workers who may lack childhood immunisation.

stories.title: Trump calls Chinese shipment to Iran a 'gift,' Israeli technicians charged with espionage
stories.summary: A news roundup reported that President Trump characterized a Chinese shipment to Iran as a "gift." Separately, Israeli technicians were charged with espionage, though further details were not elaborated in the brief.

stories.title: Iranian women held by US immigration not Qassem Soleimani's relatives: Report
stories.summary: A report by Drop Site found that two Iranian women detained by US immigration authorities are not relatives of slain Quds Force commander Qassem Soleimani, contradicting claims made by a far-right activist on X.

stories.title: Iran attacks ships in Hormuz as Trump extends ceasefire without conditions and faces domestic backlash
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump extended the ceasefire with Iran on Tuesday without setting a deadline, just hours before his two-week truce was set to expire. Iran attacked two container ships in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, but the White House declined to call it a ceasefire violation since neither vessel was American or Israeli.

stories.title: Israeli battery-swapping IP owners demand $250 million from Chinese EV giant for patent infringemen
stories.summary: Israeli-owned Charge Peak, which holds intellectual property from the defunct Israeli company Better Place, filed a $250 million patent infringement claim against Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer Nio over battery-swapping technology shipped to Europe.

stories.title: Russia’s Investigative Committee opens review of children’s author Grigory Oster’s books after lawmaker’s complaint
stories.summary: Russia's Investigative Committee opened a review of books by prominent children's author Grigory Oster after a State Duma deputy filed a formal complaint criticizing the works, according to the Russian business daily Kommersant.

stories.title: ICC confirms crimes against humanity trial of ex-Philippine leader Duterte
stories.summary: The International Criminal Court confirmed charges of crimes against humanity against former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte, clearing the way for a trial related to his "war on drugs" campaign.

stories.title: Indian physicists voice solidarity with Iran, Palestine, Lebanon academics
stories.summary: Prominent Indian physicists, including leading string theorists, issued a statement condemning attacks on universities in Iran, Palestine, and Lebanon, expressing solidarity with academics in those countries.

stories.title: “No nation benefits from these deaths”: Prince Harry at Kyiv Security Forum
stories.summary: Prince Harry made an unannounced visit to Kyiv on 23 April and addressed the Kyiv Security Forum. He directed remarks at Russian President Vladimir Putin, stating there is still an opportunity to stop the war and that no nation benefits from the ongoing deaths.

stories.title: Humanitarian worker Mike Penrose on the 'Food from Ukraine' programme
stories.summary: Veteran humanitarian worker Mike Penrose discussed the "Food from Ukraine" programme in an interview with FRANCE 24, describing how it increases the value of aid distributed amid declining funding. He noted the programme also operates effectively in Africa, with a regional food distribution hub recently launched in Accra, Ghana.

stories.title: Ghana: Foreign Affairs Minister Engages South Africa Over Xenophobic Attacks
stories.summary: Ghana's Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa engaged South Africa's Minister of International Relations and Cooperation regarding reported xenophobic attacks on Ghanaian nationals in South Africa. The diplomatic engagement aimed to address the safety concerns of Ghanaians living there.

stories.title: Lebanon's choice: Disarm Hezbollah or accept an Israeli buffer zone - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis piece examines Lebanon's strategic choice between disarming Hezbollah or accepting an Israeli buffer zone in the south. The discussion frames the decision in terms of Lebanese sovereignty and long-term regional stability.

stories.title: Behind the 'secret sauce' of Israeli resilience Americans cannot grasp - comment
stories.summary: The article discusses Israeli societal resilience in the face of constant security threats, noting how daily life resumes quickly after rocket sirens. It suggests this pattern reflects a collective adaptation to persistent danger that outside observers find difficult to understand.

stories.title: First Thing: ‘Impossible’ to reopen strait of Hormuz amid ‘flagrant’ ceasefire breaches, Iran says
stories.summary: Iranian forces seized two ships in the Strait of Hormuz as both the US and Iran maintained separate blockades of the critical waterway. President Trump announced an extension of the ceasefire with Iran, demanding a unified proposal from Tehran's leadership, which he described as seriously fractured.

stories.title: Meet the lionesses of Iran leading the fight for freedom
stories.summary: The article highlights Iranian women who are leading activism and resistance efforts inside Iran despite government repression.

stories.title: Iran's Islamic republic: The regime that hangs protesters is now a Gen Z mascot - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Iran's government is gaining sympathy in parts of the West despite its record of mass executions and repression of protesters, attributing the trend to propaganda and distorted narratives.

stories.title: Trump's Iran strategy: Not narcissism, but a blueprint against China - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that President Trump's actions against Iran reflect a coherent global strategy aimed at countering China rather than political impulse. The article frames the Iran policy as part of a broader geopolitical blueprint.

stories.title: Understanding Arab paradoxical positions in the Iran war - opinion
stories.summary: An analysis examined how Arab states are navigating the Iran conflict by avoiding direct military engagement while using economic pressure and strategic distance to weaken Iran as a regional rival without escalation.

stories.title: To stop Hezbollah, Israel must pressure the Lebanese system that sustains it - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Israel must exert pressure on the broader Lebanese political system to counter Hezbollah's influence. The commentary contends that Lebanon risks forfeiting its sovereignty and stability by shielding the militant group.

stories.title: Nigeria: Troops Repel Midnight Terror Attack in Yobe, Kill 24, Recover Weapons - - Official
stories.summary: Nigerian Army troops of Operation Hadin Kai repelled a coordinated midnight terrorist attack on Kukareta in Yobe State, killing at least 24 insurgents. Security forces also recovered a large cache of arms and ammunition during the operation.

stories.title: Woman recruited by Russians poisons soldier in Uzhhorod, says prosecutor’s office
stories.summary: Ukrainian prosecutors announced the detention of a woman in the Zakarpattia region suspected of poisoning a soldier in Uzhhorod on behalf of Russian intelligence agencies.

stories.title: Moscow claims G20 invitation at highest level as US prepares December summit in Miami
stories.summary: Russia's deputy foreign minister stated that Moscow received a G20 invitation at the highest level for the December 2026 summit in Miami. The claim came weeks after the Kremlin denied any visit by President Putin was being discussed, as the United States prepares to host the summit.

stories.title: Lebanon's president calls Israeli killing of journalist a 'war crime'
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun condemned the Israeli strike that killed journalist Amal Khalil, 43, in al-Tayri as a 'war crime,' accusing Israel of deliberately targeting journalists to conceal its actions in Lebanon.

stories.title: Syrian President al-Sharaa says he loves basketball but was distracted by war
stories.summary: Syrian President Ahmad al-Sharaa discussed his love of basketball, noting he had been distracted by years of war. His comments came amid a revival of international basketball competitions across Syrian provinces.

stories.title: Liberia: Gold Rush Chaos Threatens Rivers, Power, and Governance
stories.summary: A report warns that Liberia's artisanal and small-scale gold mining sector is escalating into an unregulated semi-industrial gold rush. The crisis threatens rivers, power infrastructure, economic stability, and governance institutions across the country.

stories.title: 1 Killed in Ukrainian Drone Strike on Industrial City in Russia’s Samara Region
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike killed one person at an industrial facility in Novokuybyshevsk in Russia's Samara Region. The attack follows recent strikes that reportedly forced a nearby oil refinery to halt operations.

stories.title: 3 Killed in Ukrainian Drone Strikes Across Russia
stories.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes across Russia killed three people, including in the Samara region. The attack followed earlier strikes that reportedly forced an oil refinery in Samara to halt operations.

stories.title: Washington uses Iraq's own oil money to bend Baghdad to its will
stories.summary: The Trump administration blocked a shipment of nearly $500 million in cash to Iraq, pressuring Baghdad to dismantle powerful Iranian-backed armed groups. Analysts warned the move risks destabilising Iraq's already fragile economy.

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon set for new round of US talks; Hezbollah fires at IDF troops again
stories.summary: Israeli Ambassador Yechiel Leiter and Lebanese counterpart Nada Hamadeh Moawad were set to meet in Washington for a new round of US-mediated talks, with Beirut seeking a one-month extension of the existing truce. Hezbollah meanwhile fired again at IDF troops.

stories.title: In Tehran, money is short and a return to war looms over daily life
stories.summary: The BBC's Lyse Doucet reported from Tehran, where busy shopping streets mask widespread economic hardship and deep public uncertainty. Residents face financial strain and growing anxiety over a possible return to open conflict.

stories.title: ‘Seriously fractured’? Scepticism over Trump’s Iran leadership split claim
stories.summary: Analysts expressed skepticism over President Trump's claim that Iran's leadership is seriously fractured, noting that key Iranian decision-makers have been completely absent from public view, creating confusion rather than confirming internal divisions.

stories.title: How Iran raised Hormuz stakes by capturing ships
stories.summary: Following the launch of a US-Israeli military campaign against Iran on February 28, Tehran responded by blocking the Strait of Hormuz and seizing ships transiting the waterway.

stories.title: Israeli strike near mosque kills five in Gaza, including three children
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike near a mosque in Gaza killed at least five Palestinians, including three children.

stories.title: Gaza to hold first election in over 20 years amid Israel attacks
stories.summary: The city of Deir al-Balah in Gaza is set to hold the territory's first election in over 20 years, even as Israeli strikes continue despite a ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Air quality in Russian port city deteriorates as fire from drone strike burns for 3rd day
stories.summary: Air quality in the Russian port city of Tuapse in Krasnodar Krai has sharply deteriorated as a fire at the city's marine terminal, ignited by a Ukrainian drone strike three days earlier, continued to burn.

stories.title: Nigeria: 10 Contacts Traced, Isolated As Covid-19 Case Hits Cross River
stories.summary: A COVID-19 case was confirmed in Nigeria's Cross River State, with authorities tracing and isolating 10 contacts. Officials said the patient, a Chinese national, is stable and there are no signs of community spread.

stories.title: Nigeria: U.S. Issues Warrant for Nigerian Woman After Skipping Prison Term
stories.summary: A U.S. federal warrant has been issued for Nigerian-born fraud convict Emuobosan Emanuella Hall after she failed to surrender to begin serving an eight-year prison sentence. The sentence was linked to a romance scam, and her failure to appear could add up to ten additional years of imprisonment.

stories.title: US seizes Iran-linked vessel, mine clearing could take 'months'
stories.summary: The US seized an Iran-linked vessel as a deadlock over the Strait of Hormuz continues. Pentagon officials reportedly estimate that clearing mines from the strait could take months.

stories.title: Iran tightens grip on Hormuz, mine clearing could take 'months'
stories.summary: Iran and the United States remain in a standoff over the Strait of Hormuz, with the Pentagon reportedly estimating that clearing Iranian mines from the waterway could take months.

stories.title: Russian drone attack on Dnipro kills 3, wounds 10 and damages residential building
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro in the early hours of April 23 killed at least two people and wounded 10, according to Dnipropetrovsk Region Governor Oleksandr Hanzha. A residential building was damaged.

stories.title: China’s Russia ties mean EU trade deal is off the table, Finland says
stories.summary: Finland's Foreign Minister Elina Valtonen said China's close ties with Russia should disqualify Beijing from launching free-trade agreement talks with the European Union. Her remarks counter recent signals from some European leaders, including German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, who suggested a trade pact with China could be possible.

stories.title: Iran executes man for alleged links to Israel and membership in banned opposition group
stories.summary: Iran executed Sultan-Ali Shirzadi-Fakhr, claiming he was a member of the banned People's Mujahedeen of Iran and had collaborated with Israel's Mossad. Rights groups have accused the regime of escalating executions as a tool of repression.

stories.title: Iran defies US blockade to claim tolls from Hormuz shipping
stories.summary: Iran's deputy parliament speaker announced that the country has received its first revenues from transit fees collected from ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Iran receives first revenue from Strait of Hormuz tolls
stories.summary: Iran's deputy speaker of parliament announced the country has received its first revenue from transit fees imposed on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Top US Navy official to leave office 'immediately:' Pentagon
stories.summary: US Navy Secretary John Phelan was directed to leave office immediately, following the recent removal of top US Army officer General Randy George and two other senior military officials earlier in the month.

stories.title: US Treasury chief says Gulf allies request currency swap lines
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said several Gulf and Asian allies have requested currency swap lines from Washington to manage the economic fallout from the war with Iran.

stories.title: Rival party workers fight on election day in India’s West Bengal
stories.summary: Clashes broke out between rival political party workers on election day in West Bengal, India.

stories.title: Iran war: How big is the global energy shock?
stories.summary: The conflict involving Iran has disrupted more than 500 million barrels of oil in a matter of weeks, significantly reshaping global energy supply flows.

stories.title: What the Iran-Iraq war taught today’s Iranian leaders - and why that matters
stories.summary: An analysis argues that Iran's current political and military response to the US-Israeli war is shaped by lessons its leadership drew from the 1980-1988 Iran-Iraq war, which defined the country's governing and defense structures.

stories.title: Watch: Donald Trump should lift the blockade | The Hindu Editorial
stories.summary: An editorial argues that US President Donald Trump should lift the blockade on Iran in exchange for Tehran easing restrictions on the Strait of Hormuz. It also urges Iran to make concessions on its nuclear program in return for sanctions relief and security guarantees.

stories.title: Dia al-Azzawi on his Excursion Across Time London exhibition
stories.summary: British-Iraqi artist Dia al-Azzawi discussed his exhibition 'Excursion Across Time' in London, which presents a historical overview of his decades-long artistic career.

stories.title: Pakistan seeks three spot LNG cargoes in first tender since Dec 2023
stories.summary: Pakistan LNG Limited issued a spot tender—its first since December 2023—seeking three LNG cargoes of approximately 140,000 cubic metres each for delivery between late April and mid-May at Port Qasim in Karachi. Power Minister Awais Leghari said the move aims to meet rising electricity demand and reduce dependence on costlier diesel.

stories.title: Trump's Op. Economic Fury pressure campaign on Iran expands beyond Hormuz blockade - report
stories.summary: The Trump administration's Operation Economic Fury has expanded beyond the initial blockade of Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz. The campaign now targets ships providing support to the Iranian regime in international waters.

stories.title: Hong Kong set for intense thundery showers, gusts in the evening
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Observatory issued special weather alerts on Thursday evening warning of intense thundery showers and gusts associated with an approaching cold front. Local temperatures were expected to drop to as low as 19 degrees Celsius.

stories.title: Iran continues crude exports despite US blockade: analysis
stories.summary: Data analytics firm Vortexa reported that approximately 10.7 million barrels of Iranian crude exports passed through the Strait of Hormuz between April 13 and April 21, despite an ongoing US Navy blockade enforced roughly 300 miles west of Iran's coast.

stories.title: Ukrainian drones kill 1, injure others at petrochemical plant in Russia
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike on an industrial facility in Novokuybyshevsk, in Russia's Samara Region, killed one person and injured others. The regional governor did not identify the specific facility targeted.

stories.title: Russians shell Chernihiv region more than 40 times; one person injured, and damage reported
stories.summary: Russian troops shelled settlements in Ukraine's Chernihiv region 42 times over a 24-hour period, injuring one woman and damaging residential homes across the area.

stories.title: Somalia: Somalia - Seventy-Two Press Freedom Violations Documented in 2025
stories.summary: A report documented 72 press freedom violations in Somalia during 2025, including 69 attacks on journalists, two attacks on media outlets, and the killing of journalist Mohammed Abukar Mohammed on 18 March 2025.

stories.title: RFK Jr agenda suffers another loss as trans advocates hail ‘huge step forward’
stories.summary: A US federal judge overturned the Trump administration's ban on gender-affirming care for children, citing Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s "wanton disregard" for the law. Transgender advocates and medical experts called the ruling a significant step forward for patients' rights.

stories.title: Malaysia’s durian growers in ‘survival mode’ as early glut and Iran war hit export trade
stories.summary: Malaysian durian growers report being in "survival mode" as an early bumper harvest coincides with surging fuel and freight costs linked to the Iran war. Rising transport and energy expenses are squeezing the premium fruit export trade to China.

stories.title: Africa’s abandoned workers in Lebanon
stories.summary: African migrant workers in Lebanon are caught in the crossfire of the ongoing war, facing dangerous conditions and limited options for evacuation or assistance.

stories.title: Liberia: Sen. Konneh Outlines Redtapes On Proposal to Print New Money
stories.summary: Liberian Senator Amara Konneh, who chairs the Senate Committee on Public Accounts and Audit, released an analysis of the Central Bank of Liberia's proposal to print new banknotes. He outlined potential negative economic consequences if macroeconomic stabilization measures are not implemented.

stories.title: South Korea’s air force apologises after audit blames 2021 jet collision on mid-air selfies
stories.summary: South Korea's air force apologized for a 2021 mid-air collision between two fighter jets after auditors determined pilots were taking selfies and filming during the flight. One pilot was suspended from flying duties and faced severe disciplinary action.

stories.title: Kenya: Weak Asset Systems Undermining Anti-Corruption Fight, Unodc Warns
stories.summary: The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime called for urgent reforms to asset management systems in Eastern Africa. UNODC warned that persistent weaknesses and lack of real-time cross-border cooperation continue to undermine anti-corruption efforts in the region.

stories.title: Nigeria: Katsina Stakeholders Back Buhari's Son for House of Reps Seat
stories.summary: Stakeholders in Nigeria's Katsina State expressed support for former President Buhari's son to contest a House of Representatives seat. The endorsement was made during a visit to Governor Dikko Radda at the Government House.

stories.title: Nigeria: Terrorists Target, Kidnap Medical Doctor in Niger Community
stories.summary: Armed groups in Niger State, Nigeria, kidnapped a medical doctor from a local community. Residents suspect the doctor was specifically targeted to provide medical treatment to wounded or ill fighters.

stories.title: Iran says it won’t reopen Strait of Hormuz as long as US is blockading ports
stories.summary: Iranian Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf stated that Iran will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz while the United States continues to blockade Iranian ports, calling the blockade a violation of ceasefire terms.

stories.title: Lavrov claims Russia fights for Orthodox “honor and dignity” — while its troops detain priests in occupied Ukraine, ISW notes
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov claimed that protecting Orthodox Christianity is a Russian war goal in Ukraine. The Institute for the Study of War noted that Russian forces have detained clergy and destroyed churches in occupied Ukrainian territories.

stories.title: Senate Republicans bypass Democrats to advance $70bn ICE and border patrol plan in ‘vote-a-rama’– US politics live
stories.summary: U.S. Senate Republicans used budget reconciliation to advance a $70 billion plan funding ICE and Border Patrol without Democratic support during an extended late-night vote. DHS funding had lapsed over nine weeks ago amid disputes over imposing new operational constraints on immigration enforcement agencies.

stories.title: Failed car bomber released in Oct 7 deal gave video speech at Berkeley classroom
stories.summary: A woman released in the November 2023 hostage deal following the October 7 attack, who had previously been convicted of a failed car bombing, delivered a video speech to a classroom at the University of California, Berkeley.

stories.title: Trump looks for way out on war, but Iran may not oblige
stories.summary: The Iran conflict has proven politically damaging for President Trump, drawing opposition from within his own Republican base. Trump is reportedly seeking an exit from the war, though Iran may not cooperate with his efforts to de-escalate.

stories.title: Malawi: Zamba Snubs PAC Again, Defies Summons As Lawmakers Question 'Above the Law' Conduct
stories.summary: Former Malawi Secretary to the President and Cabinet Colleen Zamba again refused to appear before Parliament's Public Accounts Committee despite a formal summons. Lawmakers and analysts described her repeated defiance as a troubling challenge to parliamentary oversight.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Zimbabwe, Botswana Seal 11 Deals to Strengthen Bilateral Cooperation
stories.summary: Zimbabwe and Botswana signed eleven bilateral agreements during the fifth session of their Bi-National Commission held in Harare on Wednesday. The deals aim to strengthen cooperation across key sectors.

stories.title: The unfolding tragedy of Gaza's missing children amid genocide
stories.summary: Thousands of children in Gaza remain missing beneath collapsed buildings and in areas inaccessible to rescue teams, leaving families in prolonged uncertainty about their fate.

stories.title: More than 500 people killed in Tanzania election violence, inquiry finds
stories.summary: An inquiry into Tanzania's election violence found that more than 500 people were killed. Opposition parties accused security forces of killing protesters, but the official report did not assign responsibility for the deaths.

stories.title: Nigeria: Parents Urge Wike to End FCT Teachers' Strike
stories.summary: Parents in Nigeria's Federal Capital Territory, organized under the Parents Teachers Association, called on FCT Minister Nyesom Wike to intervene in an ongoing teachers' strike affecting primary and secondary schools.

stories.title: AI robot beats elite table tennis players in 'pivotal breakthrough'
stories.summary: Sony's AI-powered table tennis robot, named Ace, defeated elite human players in an experiment described as a pivotal breakthrough. The development was highlighted alongside other stories, including a criminal complaint filed in France against UberEats and Deliveroo for alleged human trafficking, and the role of priests in the ongoing war in Ukraine.

stories.title: Explosions heard in Kryvyi Rih
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the Ukrainian city of Kryvyi Rih with drones, with explosions reported across the city. No immediate casualty figures were provided.

stories.title: Migrants deported from US stranded, 'scared' in DR Congo
stories.summary: The first group of migrants deported from the United States arrived in the Democratic Republic of Congo under a controversial U.S. program that sends undocumented foreign nationals to third countries. Deportees described being stranded and scared.

stories.title: Lufthansa cuts 20,000 flights as Iran war causes jet fuel shortage
stories.summary: Lufthansa announced it would cut 20,000 short-haul flights from its schedule through October, citing a jet fuel shortage caused by the ongoing war involving Iran.

stories.title: Russia’s 1950s tanks are massing for Zaporizhzhia. Ukrainian drones are killing them in their sheds.
stories.summary: Russian field armies are stockpiling Soviet-era tanks and vehicles, including 1950s-era models, for a planned offensive in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region. Ukrainian drone units are targeting the staging areas to disrupt the buildup.

stories.title: Spanish conservatives revive regional pacts with far-right Vox party
stories.summary: Spain's conservative People's Party is reviving regional coalition agreements with the far-right Vox party by adopting a harder line on immigration. The renewed alliances come ahead of next year's general election, after earlier pacts collapsed over policy disagreements in 2023.

stories.title: Dutch intelligence: Russia could strike NATO within a year after Ukraine war ends
stories.summary: The Dutch military intelligence service MIVD reported that Russia could be prepared for a regional conflict with NATO within a year of the Ukraine war ending, aiming to split the Alliance politically rather than defeat it militarily.

stories.title: Iran war shipping disruption impacts medicine availability in Sudan
stories.summary: Aid organizations warn that shipping disruptions caused by the Iran war are impeding the delivery of food and medicine to Sudan, where millions already depend on humanitarian assistance.

stories.title: Enemy strikes railway in Zhytomyr region; woman killed
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked transport infrastructure in Ukraine's Zhytomyr region, killing a woman. The strike targeted railway facilities in the area.

stories.title: Repeatedly deferring to Trump, Netanyahu subjects Israeli security to US president’s whim
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has repeatedly deferred to US President Donald Trump on security decisions, but Trump's reported preference for premature ceasefires and engagement with adversaries is seen as posing risks to Israeli security.

stories.title: Sainsbury’s boss urges government to help ease rising energy costs for food producers
stories.summary: Sainsbury's CEO Simon Roberts called on the UK government to help ease rising energy costs for farmers, food producers, and retailers driven by the Iran war. He said controlling industry energy prices is the most important step to prevent further food price increases.

stories.title: UGV makers Tencore of Ukraine and Shark Robotics of France sign joint venture
stories.summary: Ukrainian unmanned ground vehicle maker Tencore and French robotics firm Shark Robotics signed a joint venture to combine combat robotics and civil protection robotics capabilities.

stories.title: Prince Harry arrives in Ukraine on unannounced visit
stories.summary: Prince Harry made an unannounced visit to Kyiv, Ukraine, where he paid tribute to the country for what he called bravely and successfully defending Europe against Russia.

stories.title: What we know about Israel killing Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil
stories.summary: Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil was killed and freelance photographer Zeinab Faraj was injured in what Lebanese officials described as a 'double-tap' Israeli strike in the town of al-Tayri, southern Lebanon.

stories.title: How fire safety failures worsened Hong Kong’s deadly inferno
stories.summary: A report examines fire safety failures that contributed to a deadly building fire in Hong Kong.

stories.title: Philippine ex-president Duterte to stand trial as ICC confirms crimes against humanity charges
stories.summary: The International Criminal Court confirmed crimes against humanity charges against former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte. He is accused of the extrajudicial killing of thousands during his anti-drug campaign and will stand trial.

stories.title: Chinese military experts take stock of US munitions weak spot exposed by Iran war
stories.summary: Chinese military analysts assessed that the U.S. war with Iran has significantly depleted American munitions stockpiles, including roughly half of Patriot and THAAD interceptors over 39 days of fighting. They identified limited U.S. production capacity as a critical vulnerability against stronger adversaries.

stories.title: Wealthy young Chinese gain popularity for founding companies with relaxed work environments
stories.summary: Young wealthy Chinese, known as fuerdai or "second-generation rich," are gaining popularity by founding companies with relaxed work cultures. Once associated with spoiled lifestyles, they are reshaping their public image in contemporary China.

stories.title: Democrats say cuts to social security have caused ‘customer service chaos’ for American seniors
stories.summary: A report led by Senator Elizabeth Warren found that Trump administration cuts to the Social Security Administration have caused severe customer service disruptions for older Americans and people with disabilities. Phone wait times were found to be more than ten times higher than the agency claimed on its website.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills five Palestinians in northern Gaza, medics say
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike near a mosque in Beit Lahia, northern Gaza, killed five Palestinians on Wednesday evening, including three children, according to medics.

stories.title: Israeli forces levelling Lebanese villages behind ‘yellow line’
stories.summary: Israeli forces have been demolishing villages in southern Lebanon behind a designated 'yellow line' as part of their military operations in the border region.

stories.title: Around the world, from paint to flights, Iran war raises costs and darkens outlooks
stories.summary: Dozens of companies worldwide have withdrawn financial guidance or warned of price increases since the Iran war began, citing disrupted supply chains and reduced consumer confidence affecting sectors from paint manufacturing to aviation.

stories.title: A longer Iran conflict could boost risk for Ukraine securing missile defences, Zelensky says
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that a prolonged Iran conflict could increase risks to Ukraine's ability to secure missile defense systems. He noted that Kyiv has received limited quantities of such weaponry but has not yet experienced disruptions in supply.

stories.title: Warner Bros. shareholders set to vote on Paramount takeover bid
stories.summary: Warner Bros. Discovery shareholders are voting on Thursday on a $110 billion acquisition offer from Paramount Skydance. The proposed takeover faces significant opposition from Hollywood workers. The vote takes place amid broader economic developments, including US consideration of currency swap deals with Middle Eastern and Asian allies.

stories.title: Pakistan hopeful for US-Iran talks despite Strait of Hormuz ship seizures
stories.summary: Pakistan remains optimistic about facilitating US-Iran diplomatic talks despite recent ship seizures in the Strait of Hormuz. A former Pakistani ambassador stated that the ceasefire has created sufficient space for diplomacy to resume.

stories.title: How it ends
stories.summary: An opinion piece draws parallels between the lengthy Paris negotiations that ended the Vietnam War and current diplomatic challenges. It references five years of talks beginning in 1968, including 68 rounds of secret discussions between Henry Kissinger and Le Duc Tho representing the Viet Cong.

stories.title: Who is John Phelan, the US Navy Secretary fired by Pete Hegseth?
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fired Navy Secretary John Phelan amid reported turbulence in American military leadership during the ongoing US-Israeli war with Iran.

stories.title: Attock refinery operations normalise as transport links restored
stories.summary: Pakistan's Attock Oil Refinery resumed operations after road transport of petroleum crude and products was restored with intervention from Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and military headquarters. The refinery, which serves central and northern Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and other regions, had been forced to shut down due to road closures.

stories.title: War update: 159 battles on front lines; 36 enemy assaults repelled in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 159 combat engagements with Russian troops along the front lines on April 22. The Pokrovsk sector saw the heaviest activity, with 36 Russian assaults repelled.

stories.title: Two Pakistanis to be China’s first foreign astronauts: reports
stories.summary: Reports indicate two Pakistani astronauts are set to become China's first foreign astronauts, potentially reaching orbit before any Indian astronaut accomplishes a similar feat.

stories.title: No Fifa plans for Iran-Italy swap at World Cup
stories.summary: FIFA confirmed there are no plans to replace Iran with Italy at the upcoming World Cup, standing by President Gianni Infantino's statement that the Iranian team will participate as scheduled.

stories.title: Pakistan should clamp down on terror groups like LeT, JeM: U.S. lawmaker
stories.summary: US Congressman Brad Sherman called on Pakistan to take action against militant groups Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed. His remarks came on the first anniversary of the Pahalgam attack, during which he commemorated the victims.

stories.title: Cause of death revealed for teen who authorites say was killed by D4vd
stories.summary: A medical examiner's report determined that a teenager allegedly killed by the musician known as D4vd died from multiple penetrating injuries caused by objects.

stories.title: India to Iran: How two wars shaped the rise of Pakistan’s Asim Munir
stories.summary: Pakistan's General Asim Munir was elevated to the rank of field marshal following last year's war with India. He is now reportedly playing a peacemaking role amid the broader Iran conflict.

stories.title: The economic connection
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has created urgent need for direct trade and energy cooperation between India and Pakistan. Eighty-one percent of Pakistan's oil imports and a significant share of India's energy supplies pass through the strait, making alternative regional economic integration increasingly necessary.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s Langham group among first to invest in Beijing’s ‘city of the future’ Xiongan
stories.summary: Hong Kong-based Langham Hospitality Group signed a management agreement to operate in Xiongan New Area, a state-backed development zone southwest of Beijing. The deal marks one of the first private Hong Kong investments in the planned hi-tech hub.

stories.title: Ex-Philippine president Duterte to stand trial at ICC over deadly ‘war on drugs’
stories.summary: The International Criminal Court confirmed crimes against humanity charges against former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte on Thursday, clearing the path for a trial. Duterte faces charges of murder and attempted murder connected to his anti-drugs campaign, representing a major test for the ICC amid political pressure.

stories.title: Russians strike Komyshuvakha in Zaporizhzhia region with guided bombs; one person killed
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the settlement of Komyshuvakha in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region with guided bombs, killing a woman.

stories.title: DTEK commits €1.2 billion to 650 MW Poltava wind farm as Ukraine’s grid faces next winter without buffer
stories.summary: Ukrainian energy company DTEK committed €1.2 billion to build a 650-megawatt wind farm in the Poltava region, one of Europe's largest onshore wind projects, as Ukraine's power grid faces critical shortfalls ahead of next winter.

stories.title: Iran has a long history of defying bullies. Trump has reaped the whirlwind
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Iran has a historical pattern of resisting foreign pressure. A rally in Tehran on April 22, 2026, saw Iranians waving national flags during the ceasefire in the US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: EU risks fallout with US over Trump-linked Balkans pipeline plan
stories.summary: The European Union sought to stall a Balkans pipeline contract linked to a company fronted by Donald Trump's personal lawyer, risking a confrontation with the U.S. president. Documents show Brussels intervened in the Southern Interconnection pipeline project, marking its first challenge to a commercial venture tied to those close to Trump.

stories.title: Ceasefire extension
stories.summary: The United States has extended a ceasefire with Iran, with Pakistani diplomacy credited for preventing renewed hostilities. However, tensions persist over dueling blockades—Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the US blockade of Iranian ports—with neither side willing to lift restrictions first, stalling planned peace talks in Islamabad.

stories.title: Sindh records year’s first death from Congo fever
stories.summary: Sindh province in Pakistan recorded its first death from Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever this year. The victim was a 17-year-old cattle farm worker from Tando Adam who was treated at Jinnah Postgraduate Medical Centre in Karachi before being referred to the Sindh Infectious Diseases Hospital.

stories.title: Israeli settlers raise flag over occupied Syrian village
stories.summary: Members of the "Pioneers of Bashan" settler movement raised an Israeli flag in an occupied Syrian village in the Golan Heights. The Israeli army subsequently arrested the settlers involved in the unauthorized action.

stories.title: Trump says Israel-Lebanon ceasefire extended by three weeks
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced a three-week extension of the ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon during talks in Washington. The announcement came as representatives from both countries met at the White House amid ongoing diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: Trump to attend Lebanon-Israel talks at White House
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump will personally attend negotiations between Lebanese and Israeli ambassadors at the White House, as separate US-led talks with Iran remain stalled.

stories.title: Iran-US talks stall over Hormuz; Lebanon, Israel to meet in US
stories.summary: US-Iran negotiations have stalled over the Strait of Hormuz, with Washington refusing to lift its blockade on Iranian ports and Tehran maintaining control over the waterway. Separately, Lebanon and Israel are scheduled to meet in the United States for talks.

stories.title: Gaza’s second front: The battle against disease-carrying rats
stories.summary: Palestinian families in displacement camps across Gaza are facing a severe rat infestation amid unsanitary living conditions. The rodent problem poses a growing public health threat as access to pest control and humanitarian aid remains limited.

stories.title: South Korean army removes poster depicting man-hating hand gesture
stories.summary: The South Korean army removed a recruitment poster after a female model's hand gesture was identified as resembling the "Megalian hand," associated with a radical feminist group and perceived as anti-male. The gesture, with thumb and index finger pinched together, prompted public scrutiny.

stories.title: Russia's Vladimir Putin hosts Seychelles President Patrick Herminie at Kremlin
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted Seychelles President Patrick Herminie at the Kremlin on Wednesday. The two leaders discussed bilateral relations and international issues.

stories.title: Criminal gangs profiting as child sexual abuse websites double, experts say
stories.summary: The Internet Watch Foundation reported that commercial child sexual abuse websites doubled from about 7,028 in 2024 to over 15,000 in 2025. Experts say criminal gangs are profiting significantly from online exploitation, with abusive content found across major social media platforms.

stories.title: China’s premium EVs mount tech-powered challenge to BMW, Mercedes-Benz at expo
stories.summary: Chinese EV makers including BYD, Geely, Leapmotor, and Nio are showcasing premium electric models at Auto China in Beijing, the world's largest car show. The event marks an intensified challenge to European automakers such as BMW and Mercedes-Benz through rapid technological advancement.

stories.title: ‘This is not the country I moved to’: the British Indians showing support for Nigel Farage
stories.summary: Savitha Prakash, a first-generation Indian immigrant and NHS doctor in London's Harrow borough, is running in local elections for Reform UK. She drew comparisons between party leader Nigel Farage and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, saying both aim to make a difference for their countries.

stories.title: Turkey passes bill to restrict social media access for under-15s
stories.summary: Turkey's parliament passed a bill restricting social media access for children under 15. The legislation followed a school shooting in Kahramanmaras that killed nine students and a teacher, prompting investigation into the 14-year-old perpetrator's online activity.

stories.title: Zelensky to join EU leaders in Cyprus after 90-bn-euro loan unblocked
stories.summary: EU leaders are meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Ayia Napa, Cyprus, on Thursday following the unblocking of a 90-billion-euro loan for Kyiv. The funds had been stalled due to a dispute between Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban and Zelensky. Final approval of the loan is expected by Thursday.

stories.title: Second French peacekeeper dies in Lebanon after ambush blamed on Hezbollah
stories.summary: A second French UN peacekeeper died on Wednesday from wounds sustained in a weekend ambush in Lebanon attributed to Hezbollah. The first soldier, Staff Sergeant Florian Montorio, was killed in the Saturday attack. Hezbollah has denied responsibility.

stories.title: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon kill Lebanese journalist, wound another
stories.summary: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon on Wednesday killed Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil of Al-Akhbar newspaper and wounded a photographer. The day's total death toll of five made it the deadliest day since the April 16 ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah.

stories.title: Iran says Strait of Hormuz won’t be reopened as long as US blockade remains
stories.summary: Iran declared it will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz as long as the United States maintains its naval blockade. Although a ceasefire between the two sides has been extended, the strategically vital waterway remains closed to shipping.

stories.title: Defense forces strike oil facilities in Samara and Nizhny Novgorod regions
stories.summary: On the night of April 23, Ukrainian Armed Forces struck an oil refinery in Russia's Samara region and attacked the Gorky oil pumping station in the Nizhny Novgorod region.

stories.title: US accuses China of 'intimidation campaign' to block Taiwan president’s Africa trip
stories.summary: The United States accused China of pressuring African nations to revoke overflight permits to block a planned visit by Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te. Beijing denied the allegations and expressed appreciation for the African states that refused the transit.

stories.title: EU set to sign off €90bn loan for Ukraine and fresh Russia sanctions – Europe live
stories.summary: The EU is set to approve a €90 billion loan for Ukraine and new sanctions against Russia after Hungary and Slovakia dropped their opposition following the Druzhba oil pipeline's reopening. Separately, a head-on collision between two local trains in Denmark injured at least 17 people, four critically.

stories.title: Hong Kong fire services declined Tai Po alert over confusion fears, inquiry hears
stories.summary: A Hong Kong public inquiry heard that fire services declined to activate an emergency mobile phone alert during the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire, citing concerns it would confuse trapped residents. The blaze was the city's deadliest inferno in decades.

stories.title: Dnipro apartment block in flames: Russian overnight strike kills 2, injures 10 including two children
stories.summary: Russia launched 155 drones at Ukraine overnight on April 23, striking a residential apartment block in Dnipro. The attack killed at least two people and injured 10, including two children.

stories.title: New round of talks in Washington: Lebanon, Israel to discuss truce extension
stories.summary: Lebanese and Israeli envoys are meeting for a second time in Washington on Thursday to discuss extending the 10-day US-mediated ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah, which is set to expire on Sunday. Lebanon is pushing for a truce extension amid fragile conditions.

stories.title: Iran tightens control of Hormuz after US calls off renewed attacks
stories.summary: Iran seized two ships in the Strait of Hormuz, tightening its control of the strategic waterway after US President Trump indefinitely suspended attacks. The status of a two-week-old ceasefire remained unclear with no sign of peace talks restarting.

stories.title: Personal info of 9,045 people compromised in Hong Kong private club data breach
stories.summary: A data breach at Hong Kong's Yau Yat Chuen Garden City Club compromised personal information of 9,045 people, according to the city's Privacy Commissioner. The watchdog urged organizations to review security measures and update software to address vulnerabilities.

stories.title: Chihuahua operation: Mexico, US trade harsh words over deaths of two US agents
stories.summary: The US and Mexican governments exchanged sharp words over the deaths of two Americans in Chihuahua state, reportedly CIA personnel, during an anti-drug operation. The two Americans and two Mexican investigators died in a car crash on Sunday in northern Mexico.

stories.title: Uganda: Fuel Crisis Hits Tororo As Prices Surge
stories.summary: A deepening fuel crisis in Tororo, Uganda, has led to surging prices and severe shortages. Motorists are resorting to purchasing fuel in jerrycans as they struggle to sustain daily transportation needs.

stories.title: Southern Africa: Global Fund Launches Regional Malaria Grant for Southern Africa, Bolsters Response to Rising Risk From Extreme Weather Events in Mozambique
stories.summary: The Global Fund launched a US$24 million regional malaria grant for southern Africa through the MOSASWA partnership based in Maputo. The investment includes emergency funding to address a malaria surge following devastating floods in Mozambique.

stories.title: In Gaza, first local vote in years offers gauge of Hamas popularity
stories.summary: Palestinians in Deir al-Balah, one of the few Gaza cities not overrun by Israeli ground forces, will vote in municipal elections this weekend. The vote, featuring some pro-Hamas candidates, will serve as a rare gauge of the group's popularity and is part of broader Palestinian Authority elections.

stories.title: Iran war makes green hydrogen viable in Asia as fossil fuel prices soar
stories.summary: Rising oil and gas prices caused by the Iran war have narrowed the cost gap between green hydrogen and fossil fuels across Asia. Iran's closure of the Strait of Hormuz and strikes on Qatar's Ras Laffan LNG complex have driven fuel price surges, making zero-emission hydrogen more economically competitive.

stories.title: Russian military loses another 1,100 troops and 58 artillery systems in war against Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine's military reported approximately 1,100 Russian troops were killed or wounded in the past 24 hours, bringing total estimated Russian combat losses since February 2022 to roughly 1,322,550 personnel. An additional 58 Russian artillery systems were destroyed.

stories.title: CM Bugti vows to follow president’s directives amid political turmoil
stories.summary: Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti stated in Quetta that his government would implement President Asif Ali Zardari's directives amid political turmoil over potential changes to the province's leadership. Bugti spoke during the inauguration of a road between Chaman Phatak and Koyla Phatak, noting the president had contacted him before and after meetings with lawmakers.

stories.title: Why Japan’s central bank is caught between a rock and a hard place
stories.summary: The Bank of Japan faces a policy dilemma as inflationary pressures persist after its first interest rate hike since 2007 in March 2024. The central bank raised rates out of negative territory to address inflation that had exceeded its 2% target for 22 consecutive months.

stories.title: How Iran responded to Trump’s claimed role in saving 8 women from execution
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump claimed Iran agreed not to execute eight women protesters as a sign of respect for him, while Iranian officials denied the executions were ever planned. Trump said four women would be released immediately, with the announcement coming a day after a unilateral US ceasefire in the conflict.

stories.title: Govt advised against ratifying Unesco maritime heritage pact
stories.summary: Pakistan's National Institute of Oceanography has advised against ratifying the UNESCO 2001 Convention on underwater cultural heritage, citing national security concerns. The institute warned that compliance could expose sensitive maritime data including naval routes and offshore installations.

stories.title: Rise of the ‘ghost owner’: 18,000 UK vehicles in use without proper records
stories.summary: Over 18,000 vehicles in the UK lack proper owner address records with the DVLA, registered instead to the agency's own address. A Labour MP has called for action against these "ghost owners" who cannot be held accountable for traffic offenses and other crimes.

stories.title: Russian attack triggers fire in apartment block in Ukraine's Dnipro, seven injured
stories.summary: A Russian air attack on Thursday struck an apartment block in the southeastern Ukrainian city of Dnipro, triggering multiple fires. Regional authorities reported seven people were injured, including two children.

stories.title: Israeli airstrike kills journalist in south Lebanon: civil defence
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike in the southern Lebanese town of al-Tiri killed journalist Amal Khalil and wounded another journalist on Wednesday. Khalil worked for the Lebanese daily Al-Akhbar. Lebanon's civil defence recovered her body from the rubble of a targeted house.

stories.title: Judicial Commission of Pakistan ‘likely’ to recommend transfer of five IHC judges
stories.summary: Pakistan's Judicial Commission is expected to recommend transferring five Islamabad High Court judges to provincial high courts at its April 28 meeting. The 27th Constitutional Amendment empowered the commission to recommend such transfers without requiring the judges' consent.

stories.title: Extreme heat pushes global agrifood systems to brink, UN report warns
stories.summary: A joint UN report by the World Meteorological Organisation and the Food and Agriculture Organisation warns that extreme heat is pushing global agrifood systems to critical thresholds. Rising temperatures threaten crop yields, livestock, and fisheries, disproportionately affecting women farmers. The report urges adoption of early warning systems and proactive measures.

stories.title: South Africa: Teen Pregnancies Are Dramatically Dropping. But Researchers Aren't Sure Why
stories.summary: New research across South Africa's nine provinces shows a steep decline in adolescent pregnancy rates between 2021 and 2025, reversing a previous upward trend. Researchers have not yet identified the specific causes behind the drop.

stories.title: Telegram founder says summons addressed to ‘suspect’ arrives at his former Russian apartment
stories.summary: Telegram founder Pavel Durov reported that a summons addressed to "suspect Durov P.V." was delivered by mail to his former apartment in Russia.

stories.title: Rinehart’s $200m donation to convert homes for veterans welcomed by RSL – as it happened
stories.summary: Australian mining billionaire Gina Rinehart donated A$200 million to convert homes for military veterans, a move welcomed by the RSL. Separately, Australia's Health Minister Mark Butler acknowledged public unease about NDIS cuts amid $53 billion in new defense spending.

stories.title: Russian attack on Dnipro: number of wounded rises to seven
stories.summary: The number of people wounded in a Russian attack on the Ukrainian city of Dnipro rose to seven, including two children.

stories.title: Fire after Ukrainian attack at Russia's Tuapse refinery hits air quality
stories.summary: Russian firefighters battled a blaze for a third consecutive day at the Tuapse oil refinery on the Black Sea coast following a Ukrainian drone strike. Officials in Tuapse reported that air quality in the city had sharply deteriorated as a result of the ongoing fire.

stories.title: Seeing the Cyber in Economic Statecraft
stories.summary: An analysis in the War on the Rocks series highlights the intersection of cybersecurity and economic statecraft, noting that Americans lost nearly $21 billion to cybercrime in 2025. The article urges better US integration of cyber threats into national security and economic strategy.

stories.title: China calls on Cambodia for ‘shared security and risks’ during global turmoil
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi called for closer solidarity with Cambodia during the first China-Cambodia 2+2 strategic dialogue in Phnom Penh. The meeting aimed to deepen political and security cooperation, with Wang urging both sides to manage development and security challenges independently.

stories.title: Iran behind low-level ‘hybrid warfare’ attacks in UK and Europe, analysts say
stories.summary: Analysts and security officials say Iranian intelligence services and Revolutionary Guards operatives are recruiting teenagers through criminal intermediaries to carry out low-level "hybrid warfare" attacks in Europe and the UK. Targets have included Jewish community sites in Belgium and the Netherlands and US banks.

stories.title: KP Assembly breaks tradition with open-air sitting
stories.summary: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Assembly held its first-ever open-air session, during which Chief Minister Sohail Afridi criticized the federal government for an alleged baton charge against PTI founder Imran Khan's sisters. The opposition boycotted the session except for PPP members. The house formed a committee on gas rights under Article 158.

stories.title: Israel signs major $200m deal with Elbit Systems
stories.summary: Israel's Ministry of Defence signed a $200 million contract with Israeli defence firm Elbit Systems to purchase new aerial munitions. Defence Minister Israel Katz said the deal aims to strengthen the independence of Israel's munitions supply chain.

stories.title: Ben Roberts-Smith planned to leave Australia and researched buying wellness business in Spain, court documents show
stories.summary: Court documents reveal that former Australian soldier Ben Roberts-Smith, accused of war crimes, had planned to leave Australia and had researched buying a wellness business in Spain. He had a business class flight booked when he was arrested at Sydney airport and was subsequently granted bail under strict conditions.

stories.title: US plans to send 1,100 stranded Afghans to ‘unstable’ Democratic Republic of Congo
stories.summary: The Trump administration is in discussions with the Democratic Republic of Congo to resettle approximately 1,100 Afghans stranded at a Qatar base while awaiting US visas. Many of the evacuees have ties to US military and aid operations in Afghanistan. Advocacy groups have condemned the plan as unacceptable.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills five in Gaza, including three children
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike killed five people in Gaza, including three children. Gaza officials report that Israel has committed approximately 2,400 violations of the ceasefire agreement reached with Hamas in October.

stories.title: Libya rescues 404 migrants on 10 boats, Red Crescent says
stories.summary: Libya's eastern-based coast guard, operating under the Libyan National Army, rescued at least 404 migrants from 10 boats at sea. The Tobruk Red Crescent reported that the migrants had faced harsh conditions during their journey.

stories.title: Israel kills and wounds several Palestinians in Khan Younis
stories.summary: Israeli shelling in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, killed one Palestinian man identified as Yahya Abu Shalhoub and wounded several others on Thursday morning. Three people injured in a drone strike were admitted to the Nasser Medical Complex.

stories.title: How a dropped sexual assault case cost an aspiring South Korean police officer her life
stories.summary: Over 80,000 people signed a petition demanding a renewed investigation after a 19-year-old South Korean woman died by suicide following police dismissal of her sexual assault case. The petition surpassed the 50,000-signature threshold requiring formal review by the National Assembly.

stories.title: ‘Strict security’ triggers food, fuel shortages in twin cities
stories.summary: Suspension of goods transport in Rawalpindi and Islamabad due to strict security measures has caused shortages of food and fuel in Pakistan's twin cities. Traders and transporters have demanded the district administration reopen roads, warning of price hikes from supply chain disruptions. Fuel supply to Islamabad and Peshawar airports may also be affected.

stories.title: US Navy Secretary John Phelan fired amid Pentagon shakeup
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced that U.S. Navy Secretary John C. Phelan was removed from his position effective immediately. No reason was given for his departure, and the statement did not clarify whether the decision was voluntary.

stories.title: Will another film star be able to sway the election in India’s Tamil Nadu?
stories.summary: Actor C. Joseph Vijay is entering electoral politics in India's Tamil Nadu state. Political commentators assess that Vijay could at best act as a disruptor in what has become a three-cornered contest in the upcoming state election.

stories.title: US optimistic about Iran talks ‘this week’
stories.summary: The United States expressed optimism about resuming negotiations with Iran, with President Trump suggesting talks could restart in Islamabad within 36 to 72 hours. Iran's President Pezeshkian welcomed dialogue but cited blockades and threats as obstacles, while Iran seized two cargo ships attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Dozens of Israeli settlers cross into Syria to demand settlement
stories.summary: Dozens of Israeli settlers crossed into Syrian territory in the Golan Heights area and barricaded themselves on a rooftop, demanding the establishment of a settlement. The incursion represents an escalation of settler activity in occupied Syrian land.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: Israeli media reports claim Washington informed Tel Aviv that the ceasefire with Iran will expire on Sunday, though White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said President Trump has not set a timeline. Meanwhile, Israeli attacks and demolitions continue in Lebanon despite a 10-day truce.

stories.title: High Court convenes to hear petitions demanding Oct. 7 state inquiry, without audience
stories.summary: Israel's High Court convened to hear petitions demanding a state commission of inquiry into the October 7 Hamas attack. Bereaved families clashed outside the courthouse, and the session was broadcast live but closed to the public to prevent disruptions.

stories.title: Head-on train collision near Copenhagen leaves four critically injured
stories.summary: Two local trains collided head-on near Copenhagen, Denmark, injuring at least 17 people, four of whom are in critical condition. Images showed both trains with significant frontal damage in a wooded area north of the capital.

stories.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 55 after Trump extended ceasefire?
stories.summary: On day 55 of the US-Iran conflict, following Trump's extension of a ceasefire, Iran expressed willingness to negotiate but blamed US "breach of commitments, blockade and threats" for stalling diplomatic progress.

stories.title: Zelensky warns Iran war could threaten Ukraine access to US air defenses
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that a potential U.S.-Iran war could threaten Ukraine's access to American air defense systems. He noted Ukraine has been securing U.S. weapons through the PURL program, under which NATO countries finance arms purchases for Kyiv.

stories.title: Enemy attack on Dnipro wounds two, damages residential buildings
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked the Ukrainian city of Dnipro, causing fires and damaging residential buildings. At least two people were initially reported injured.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills Lebanese journalist despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil, 43, was killed by an Israeli airstrike in the southern Lebanese town of al-Tayri on 22 April 2026 while covering the aftermath of earlier attacks. The strike occurred despite an active ceasefire, with a second strike reportedly hitting an area where reporters were sheltering.

stories.title: Lebanon, Israel to meet today as truce hangs by a thread
stories.summary: Lebanese and Israeli envoys are scheduled to meet in Washington for a second round of US-mediated talks aimed at extending a ceasefire set to expire on Sunday. The meeting comes as Israeli strikes killed five people in southern Lebanon, including a journalist. Beirut seeks to use the extension as a step toward negotiating troop withdrawal and detainee returns.

stories.title: A Formal Defense Pact in the Indo-Pacific Is the Wrong Answer
stories.summary: Former Biden administration official Ely Ratner proposed a legally binding Pacific Defense Pact among the US, Japan, Australia, and the Philippines to deter China. Analysts counter that a formal multilateral defense treaty in the Indo-Pacific may not be the right approach despite valid concerns about China's military posture.

stories.title: To Iran, Trump blinked first by extending the ceasefire
stories.summary: Iranian leaders believe they have a greater willingness to endure the costs of the ongoing conflict than U.S. President Trump, viewing his decision to extend the ceasefire as a sign that Washington blinked first in the standoff.

stories.title: Despite snags, Pakistan works to keep channels open
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif met with Iran's ambassador and expressed hope for a peace deal to permanently end the conflict. Deputy Prime Minister Dar spoke with Turkish and UK counterparts to sustain diplomatic channels. Efforts are underway to facilitate a second round of Iran-US talks following a ceasefire extension.

stories.title: DeSantis signs bill banning DEI programs in Florida local governments
stories.summary: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis signed legislation banning diversity, equity, and inclusion programs in local governments across the state. Civil rights advocates argue that DEI practices help address historic inequities for marginalized groups.

stories.title: Israel-Iran LIVE: Iran attacks 3 ships in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iranian forces attacked three ships in the Strait of Hormuz amid ongoing tensions. Separately, Lebanese officials met with Israeli counterparts in Washington to request an extension of the truce.

stories.title: EU 'must' shift to renewables to end fossil fuel 'blackmail from war-driving authoritarian regimes'
stories.summary: German MEP Hannah Neumann argued that the EU must accelerate its shift to renewable energy to end dependence on fossil fuels from authoritarian regimes. She cited growing geopolitical instability around Iran and criticized the lack of clarity in ongoing international negotiations.

stories.title: Trains collide head-on in Denmark, causing multiple injuries
stories.summary: Two local trains collided head-on north of Copenhagen, Denmark, on a line between Hillerød and Kagerup, injuring at least 17 people, four critically. Emergency services responded to the scene in a wooded area, where both trains sustained visible front-end damage.

stories.title: Train collision in Denmark prompts massive emergency response near Copenhagen
stories.summary: Two trains collided near Copenhagen, Denmark, on Thursday, injuring at least 17 people and prompting a massive emergency response. Several passengers were airlifted to a hospital. The cause of the head-on collision is under investigation.

stories.title: How my modest love song was sucked into a chilling machine of political propaganda
stories.summary: Israeli songwriter describes how a personal love song was co-opted for political purposes during Israel's Independence Day torch-lighting ceremony, which the author says was turned into a display of support for Prime Minister Netanyahu.

stories.title: South Africa: Legendary Congolese Artist Ferré Gola Set To Perform In Joburg Next Month
stories.summary: Congolese music star Ferré Gola is scheduled to perform in Johannesburg, South Africa, next month in what will be his first-ever concert in the city.

stories.title: U.S. Navy Secretary John Phelan fired by Pentagon
stories.summary: U.S. Navy Secretary John Phelan was fired by the Pentagon. His removal follows the recent dismissal of the Army's top officer, General Randy George, and two other senior generals by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

stories.title: Hezbollah supporters defiant after sons killed in terror group’s fight against Israel
stories.summary: Mass funerals were held for Hezbollah operatives killed fighting Israel. Parents of slain fighters expressed defiance, calling their children's deaths an honor in defense of Lebanon and saying they would be willing to sacrifice more.

stories.title: Private secretary of billionaire Judith Neilson refused bail on $1m fraud charges
stories.summary: Annalouise Spence, 50, former private secretary to Australian billionaire philanthropist Judith Neilson, was charged with dozens of counts of fraud and refused bail in a local court on Thursday. She allegedly used a business credit card to make over A$1 million in unauthorized purchases of luxury clothing, artwork, and jewellery.

stories.title: UK media sidelined Palestinian voices in Gaza war, study finds
stories.summary: A new study found that BBC, the Guardian, and Sky News used language and framing that dehumanized Palestinians and downplayed Israeli violence during coverage of the Gaza war, effectively sidelining Palestinian voices.

stories.title: Mainland China’s ultra-wealthy numbers rise as Hong Kong tipped for faster growth
stories.summary: According to Knight Frank, mainland China's population of ultra-high-net-worth individuals—those with assets exceeding US$30 million—grew 23 per cent over five years to 121,677 and is projected to reach 144,602 by 2031. Despite the increase, China's share of global UHNWIs is expected to decline from 17 per cent to 15 per cent by 2031.

stories.title: Schools forced to cut back on support for Send pupils in England, poll finds
stories.summary: A poll found that more than two-fifths of school leaders in England have cut back support for children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) due to ongoing financial pressures. Seventy-one per cent reported reducing teaching assistants in the past year, and 81 per cent warned of further cuts ahead.

stories.title: Dutch analyst: Ukrainian army likely among best-trained in Europe
stories.summary: A Dutch analyst assessed that the Ukrainian military is likely among the best-trained armies in Europe due to its combat experience. The analyst also highlighted joint Ukrainian-Dutch drone production as a strategically important step for European security.

stories.title: 'This was a targeted assassination': Colleague of slain journalist Amal Khalil
stories.summary: Journalist Courtney Bonneau described the killing of Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil as a targeted assassination. Khalil, a correspondent for Al-Akhbar, was killed by an Israeli airstrike in the town of at-Tiri after reportedly sheltering inside a house following an earlier drone strike.

stories.title: Zelensky to join European leaders in Cyprus as EU unblocks €90bn Ukraine loan
