stories.title: ‘Hungry all the time’: US Navy deny food shortages after grim photos emerge
stories.summary: The US Navy denied claims of food shortages aboard warships maintaining the blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, after photos showing mostly empty food trays circulated online with reports that sailors were "hungry all the time."

stories.title: Lebanon hopes for extension of ceasefire at Washington meeting
stories.summary: Lebanon's government is seeking an extension of the 10-day US-mediated ceasefire with Israel, set to expire on April 26, during meetings in Washington. The ceasefire has provided a temporary halt to hostilities.

stories.title: Inquiry clears Bristol school of antisemitism for postponing Jewish MP’s visit
stories.summary: An independent inquiry into Bristol Brunel Academy found no evidence of antisemitism after the school postponed a visit by Jewish Labour MP Damien Egan. The review concluded the visit was delayed over safeguarding concerns rather than external influence.

stories.title: Israeli settlers kill Palestinian man in West Bank shooting
stories.summary: Israeli settlers shot and killed 29-year-old Palestinian Odeh Atef Odeh Awawdeh in Deir Dibwan, east of Ramallah, in the occupied West Bank. According to the Palestinian news agency Wafa, settlers surrounded the town and opened fire with live ammunition; Awawdeh was shot in the back and died at Ramallah Medical Complex.

stories.title: Trump among recipients of Israel Prize for ‘special contribution to the Jewish people’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is among the recipients of Israel's annual Israel Prize for "special contribution to the Jewish people." He is expected to receive the award during his next visit to Israel, alongside artists, researchers, and educators honored at the ceremony.

stories.title: Mexico’s Sheinbaum demands answers over CIA agents in Chihuahua
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum demanded an explanation after CIA officers were found to have participated in a drug raid in the state of Chihuahua without the federal government's knowledge.

stories.title: Spain is sending Ukraine 100 VAMTAC vehicles, same platform hosting Britain’s Rapid Ranger counter-drone system
stories.summary: Spain announced it is providing Ukraine with 100 VAMTAC armored vehicles, the same platform used by the United Kingdom for its Rapid Ranger counter-drone system. The vehicles offer personnel protection and enhanced mobility in field conditions.

stories.title: 'Character arc': Syrian leader watching dance performance to Missy Elliott song goes viral
stories.summary: A video of Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa watching a choreographed dance performance set to Missy Elliott's "Work It" in Damascus went viral online. The footage drew widespread attention given al-Sharaa's background as a former militant leader turned head of state.

stories.title: Zelensky meets Spain’s DM to discuss air defense missiles, SAFE expansion, and joint production
stories.summary: President Zelensky met with Spain's defense minister to discuss air defense missile supplies, expansion of the SAFE defense cooperation program, and joint weapons production initiatives.

stories.title: Temporary protected status holders add $29bn to US economy, report says
stories.summary: A report by FWD.us found that temporary protected status holders contribute approximately $29 billion annually to the U.S. economy. The findings were released ahead of a Supreme Court hearing on the Trump administration's bid to end protections for Syrians and Haitians.

stories.title: 'Right now both sides are testing each other', analyst says as Iran truce extended
stories.summary: Former National Security Advisor Negah Angha said the US and Iran are "testing each other" as a ceasefire was extended amid an ongoing standoff that has choked off traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. She noted Iran has signaled to Western allies its ability to impact the global economy.

stories.title: Critical roles of Eyal Zamir, Dan Caine, Brad Cooper in shaping the Iran war - exclusive
stories.summary: An exclusive report identifies Eyal Zamir, Dan Caine, and Brad Cooper as key IDF and US military figures shaping operational decisions in the Iran conflict. While US President Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu make the ultimate war decisions, these officials have been the next most influential players.

stories.title: Dollar gains, Iran war keeps central banks in wait-and-see mode
stories.summary: The US dollar edged higher as tensions from the Iran conflict and ceasefire uncertainty kept global markets cautious. Disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz continued to elevate energy risks, prompting central banks to maintain a wait-and-see approach.

stories.title: Iran blames Trump’s blockade for diplomatic impasse as fragile truce holds
stories.summary: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that the United States and Israel would not achieve their objectives through coercion, as a fragile truce between the parties continues to hold. He framed a US-led blockade as the primary obstacle to diplomatic progress.

stories.title: Over 50,000 Lebanon housing units damaged, destroyed in war
stories.summary: More than 50,000 housing units in Lebanon have been damaged or destroyed during the conflict with Israel. Despite a ceasefire being in place, Israeli forces continue to damage homes in southern Lebanese towns they still occupy.

stories.title: US saw record high of 5,668 books banned in libraries in 2025, says agency
stories.summary: The American Library Association reported a record 5,668 books were banned in U.S. libraries in 2025, representing 66% of all titles challenged. The most-banned book was Sold, a 2006 novel by Patricia McCormick about sex trafficking in India.

stories.title: Large Iranian missile fragment located in open area in central Israel
stories.summary: Israeli civilians found a large Iranian missile fragment in an open area near Ramat Hasharon in central Israel, believed to originate from Operation Roaring Lion. Police confirmed the fragment posed no immediate danger and urged public vigilance.

stories.title: Ukraine’s combat experience is entering NATO training curricula. This week it happened in Bydgoszcz
stories.summary: A NATO training course held in Bydgoszcz, Poland, incorporated Ukraine's combat experience into its curriculum. The program covered practical analytical skills including Operational Analysis, effectiveness metrics, and risk management for active combat planning.

stories.title: War with Pakistan halts school for Afghan border children
stories.summary: Fighting along the Afghanistan-Pakistan border has left the town of Barikot deserted, with schools destroyed and thousands of children displaced. The conflict has cut off access to education for children in the border region.

stories.title: Navy scientists seek tech breakthroughs in areas that companies ignore
stories.summary: The U.S. Office of Naval Research is focusing on technology breakthroughs in areas that private-sector companies tend to overlook. The shift comes as private R&D funding rises and the Navy adjusts to new budget priorities.

stories.title: Iran dissidents bemoan European silence after latest execution
stories.summary: Iran announced on April 22 that it executed a man convicted of spying for Israel's Mossad intelligence agency. Iranian dissident groups criticized European governments for remaining silent following the hanging. The execution is part of a broader pattern of capital punishment in Iran drawing international condemnation.

stories.title: Smotrich: US supports Israeli West Bank settlement expansion - interview
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich claimed in an interview that the United States supports Israeli settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank. However, past US policy has called for maintaining stability in the area, and President Trump has not backed total annexation.

stories.title: Pakistan moves towards one-window airport clearance with e-gates, smart scanners
stories.summary: Pakistan is developing a one-window airport clearance system using e-gates and smart scanners to modernize border control and reduce wait times. The plan was discussed jointly by the Ministries of Defence and Interior.

stories.title: Trump taps defense firm execs to lead space acquisition, NRO
stories.summary: The Trump administration selected Erich Hernandez-Baquero to serve as the U.S. Space Force's next acquisition chief and nominated Roger Mason as the next director of the National Reconnaissance Office. Both appointees come from defense industry backgrounds.

stories.title: Navy secretary leaving the Pentagon, ‘effective immediately’
stories.summary: Navy Secretary John Phelan departed the Pentagon effective immediately, a move that had been long rumored. His exit comes as the Navy is actively engaged in operations against Iran and in the process of rolling out its proposed budget.

stories.title: Russian drones strike agricultural enterprise in Chernihiv region, damaging warehouses and equipment
stories.summary: Russian drones struck an agricultural enterprise in the village of Ivanivka in Chernihiv region's Semenivka community. The attack damaged warehouses, equipment, and a combine harvester operating in the field.

stories.title: Iran war conflict could create systemic gas demand destruction, says top sector official
stories.summary: A senior energy sector official warned that the ongoing Iran conflict could cause systemic destruction of global gas demand. The Middle East conflict has been described as producing the largest energy supply disruption in modern history, with significant implications for global markets.

stories.title: Thousands of London commuters walk to work in underground strike
stories.summary: Thousands of London commuters walked to work on Wednesday due to a strike on the Underground. The industrial action by Transport for London workers was prompted by plans to condense the working week into four days. The disruption affected services across the capital.

stories.title: French soldier dies of wounds after attack on UN force in Lebanon
stories.summary: French President Macron confirmed that a second French soldier died from wounds sustained in an attack on UN peacekeepers in Lebanon last week, which France attributed to Hezbollah.

stories.title: Air Force pushes to fund upgraded refueling systems instead of new tanker development
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force is prioritizing funding for upgraded aerial refueling systems over the development of an entirely new tanker aircraft. A former military official has raised concerns that delays in replacing the current tanker fleet could negatively impact combat readiness.

stories.title: Iran denies women protesters facing execution after Trump calls
stories.summary: Iran denied that eight women detained over protests face execution, responding to US President Donald Trump's public calls for their release. Human rights organizations have warned that the detainees remain at risk of the death penalty.

stories.title: The Palestinian woman on the cover of L'Espresso speaks to MEE: "Israeli settlers were ready to kill us"
stories.summary: Palestinian lawyer Meead Abu al-Rub spoke to Middle East Eye about her appearance on the cover of Italian magazine L'Espresso after being filmed facing harassment by Israeli settlers during an olive harvest in the occupied West Bank in October 2025. The 35-year-old works with the Wall and Settlement Authority.

stories.title: IDF killed 20 Hezbollah terrorist, struck over 70 targets in op. prior to Lebanon ceasefire
stories.summary: The IDF reported killing 20 Hezbollah fighters and striking over 70 targets in an operation prior to a Lebanon ceasefire. The operation was conducted around Dibbin, approximately 12 kilometers inside Lebanese territory, by the 91st Division in coordination with the Israeli Air Force.

stories.title: Wheelchair shortage deepens crisis for disabled people in Gaza
stories.summary: Disabled residents in Gaza face a worsening humanitarian crisis due to severe wheelchair shortages, leaving many unable to move or access medical care. Families report elderly caregivers struggling with damaged or improvised chairs, while some individuals are forced to crawl or share a single wheelchair among several people.

stories.title: UK must brace itself for rise in state-backed cyberattacks, security chief says
stories.summary: A senior UK security official warned that Britain must prepare for an increase in state-backed cyberattacks. The official noted that the highest-impact cyber incidents are increasingly linked to government actors rather than criminal gangs alone. The warning highlights growing nation-state threats to UK infrastructure.

stories.title: US slams China after African countries block Taiwan leader’s eSwatini trip
stories.summary: The U.S. State Department criticized China after the Seychelles, Mauritius, and Madagascar revoked overflight clearances for Taiwanese leader William Lai Ching-te's aircraft en route to eSwatini. Washington called the move, allegedly made at Beijing's request, an abuse of the international civil aviation system.

stories.title: Sierra Leone signs offshore exploration deal with Shell
stories.summary: Sierra Leone signed a new offshore oil and gas exploration agreement with Shell, aiming to develop the country's untapped energy resources.

stories.title: Gaza worker restores stove burners as families adapt to fuel shortages
stories.summary: A worker in Gaza who restores and manufactures stove burners reported that families are increasingly relying on repaired and improvised cooking equipment amid ongoing fuel shortages. The craftsman, with over 30 years of experience, produces locally made burners to help residents cope with limited fuel access.

stories.title: Former Gaza hostage Eli Sharabi reflects on Independence Day, family loss
stories.summary: Former Gaza hostage Eli Sharabi reflected on Israel's Independence Day and the personal losses he suffered following the October 7 Hamas attack. Sharabi, who survived captivity, described how the holiday now carries deeper significance as he honors family members who were killed.

stories.title: The InSight Take: Does Kinahan’s Arrest Mark a New Chapter?
stories.summary: Daniel Kinahan, described as one of Europe's most influential drug traffickers, was arrested in Dubai. Analysts are examining the implications of his detention for the Kinahan cartel's cocaine trafficking operations across Europe.

stories.title: 3rd Army Corps refutes Russia’s claim of capturing Luhansk region
stories.summary: Ukraine's Third Army Corps denied Russian claims of having established full control over the Luhansk region. The unit directly contradicted statements by Russia's General Staff and Ministry of Defense asserting complete capture of the territory.

stories.title: Trump, Pakistani sources says US-Iran talks could begin Friday as ceasefire extended
stories.summary: Reports indicate that US-Iran talks could begin on Friday, with a ceasefire between the parties extended. President Donald Trump, asked by the New York Post about the possibility of Friday negotiations, responded that talks were possible.

stories.title: Italy lists Ukraine among top buyers for arms, while eyeing drone deal
stories.summary: Ukraine became the fourth-largest importer of Italian military equipment in 2025, with exports reaching €349 million. Kyiv rose from outside the top 10 the prior year. Italy is also reportedly exploring a drone deal with Ukraine.

stories.title: Russian journalist and politician calls for ‘home protest’ in support of free internet
stories.summary: Russian journalist and politician Yekaterina Duntsova called for a "home protest" in support of free internet access in Russia. The appeal comes amid increasing Russian government restrictions on online freedoms.

stories.title: Israeli army says it stopped settlers entering Syria buffer zone
stories.summary: The Israeli military intercepted approximately 40 settlers who attempted to cross into the Israeli-controlled buffer zone in Syria. The group, identified as members of the right-wing "Pioneers of Bashan" movement advocating settlements in Lebanon and Syria, was returned to Israel and handed to police.

stories.title: Schools in India’s capital told to ring regular bells to remind children to drink water
stories.summary: Authorities in New Delhi have ordered schools to ring regular bells reminding children to drink water as the city prepares for heatwave conditions. India recorded nearly 11,000 heat stroke deaths between 2012 and 2021.

stories.title: Three ships targeted in Hormuz, Iran seizes two
stories.summary: Iranian forces targeted three container ships and seized two in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's parliament speaker said the strait would remain closed as long as the US naval blockade continued, calling it a violation of the ceasefire.

stories.title: Bad optics? Israel jails soldiers who smashed Jesus statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli military authorities jailed soldiers who destroyed a statue of Jesus at a Christian site in Lebanon. Critics argue that Israeli attacks on Christian locations in Lebanon undermine claims of shared Judeo-Christian values and mutual respect between the communities.

stories.title: Did UK universities pay to ‘spy’ on pro‑Palestine students?
stories.summary: UK universities allegedly contracted a private security firm with links to military intelligence to conduct surveillance on pro-Palestine student activists. The revelations have raised questions about the extent of monitoring and the relationships between academic institutions and security companies.

stories.title: EU envoys poised to adopt 20th package of Russia sanctions, diplomats say
stories.summary: EU envoys are set to adopt a 20th package of sanctions against Russia after Slovakia and Hungary dropped their opposition. The shift followed the repair of the Druzhba oil pipeline, which had been a key point of contention among member states.

stories.title: 2 Pakistani astronauts selected as candidates for China’s space programme
stories.summary: China selected two Pakistani astronauts, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud, as candidates for its manned space programme. One will become the first foreign astronaut aboard China's space station.

stories.title: Telega developers file antitrust complaint with Russia’s Federal Antimonopoly Service over App Store removal
stories.summary: The developers of Telega, an unofficial Telegram client, filed an antitrust complaint with Russia's Federal Antimonopoly Service after Apple removed their app from the App Store. The complaint alleges anticompetitive practices in the app's removal.

stories.title: OMB director rebukes shipbuilders over production delays
stories.summary: Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought criticized U.S. shipbuilders over production delays, pointing to large backlogs as evidence that defense contractors are benefiting from program schedule slippages.

stories.title: Second French peacekeeper dies after ambush blamed on Hezbollah
stories.summary: A second French soldier died from wounds sustained in a weekend ambush against UN peacekeepers in Lebanon that has been attributed to Hezbollah. The first soldier killed was Staff Sergeant Florian Montorio, who was shot dead in the Saturday attack. Hezbollah has denied responsibility for the ambush.

stories.title: Suspect in slaying of Colombian presidential hopeful arrested in Argentina
stories.summary: A Colombian national suspected of involvement in organizing the killing of Colombian presidential hopeful Miguel Uribe was arrested in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Authorities confirmed the suspect's capture and his alleged role in coordinating the assassination.

stories.title: At least four killed in Israeli attacks on Lebanon, journalists wounded
stories.summary: Israeli attacks on the southern Lebanese town of at-Tiri killed at least four people and wounded journalists, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The strikes targeted areas where media personnel were present, resulting in multiple casualties.

stories.title: World's worst energy crisis? Iran war sparks scramble for alternatives to Gulf oil
stories.summary: The International Energy Agency declared the Strait of Hormuz disruption the biggest energy crisis in history, as Iran's seizure of ships compounded global fuel supply concerns. The blockade has led to rising fuel prices, cancelled flights, and a scramble for alternative oil and gas sources.

stories.title: Turkey’s foreign minister to visit Britain for talks on Iran, Ukraine, source says
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan will visit London this week for official talks with British counterparts on the wars in Iran and Ukraine. The discussions will also cover broader cooperation between Turkey and the UK as NATO allies.

stories.title: Japan: South Korean arrested outside Yasukuni Shrine ceremony for war dead
stories.summary: Japanese police arrested a South Korean national outside Tokyo's Yasukuni Shrine during a ceremony for war dead. The individual was holding a banner with political messages. Approximately 120 Japanese lawmakers attended the ceremony, though the prime minister did not.

stories.title: US turning to Ukrainian counter-drone tech after Iran attacks, sources say
stories.summary: The US military has deployed Ukrainian-developed counter-drone technology at a key American air base in Saudi Arabia following Iranian attacks. The move reflects Washington's interest in battle-tested Ukrainian drone defense systems. Sources say the adoption signals deeper US-Ukraine defense technology cooperation.

stories.title: Report: Russian schools hold classes warning students about dangers of VPN services
stories.summary: Schools across multiple Russian regions have begun holding classes warning students about the dangers of using VPN services, according to the independent outlet Verstka. The lessons were documented through posts on VKontakte pages of educational institutions.

stories.title: Teen pleads guilty to arson at London synagogue, says he has ‘no hate’ toward Jews
stories.summary: A 17-year-old pleaded guilty to committing arson at a London synagogue, claiming he did not know the building was a synagogue and expressed no hatred toward Jews. Police are still seeking two additional suspects in connection with the attack on the UK Jewish institution.

stories.title: How Israel used aid to advance its aims in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli-coordinated aid deliveries to the southern Lebanese village of Rmeish have drawn scrutiny over the involvement of Samaritan's Purse, a pro-Israel evangelical organization. Critics question whether Israel used humanitarian assistance to advance strategic aims in the area.

stories.title: The next wave of aliyah is coming, but Israel is still not ready - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that a major new wave of Jewish immigration to Israel is approaching, but the country remains unprepared. The author identifies bureaucratic and financial barriers, noting that Israel effectively taxes those attempting to make aliyah.

stories.title: Sweden Releases Russian Captain After ‘Shadow Fleet’ Ship Detention
stories.summary: Swedish prosecutors released the captain of a detained 'shadow fleet' vessel after being unable to disprove his claim that he did not know the ship's registration papers were fraudulent.

stories.title: Lebanese journalist trapped after Israeli strike in south
stories.summary: Reporters Without Borders called for international pressure on Israel to allow the rescue of Al-Akhbar journalist Amal Khalil, trapped near al-Tiri in southern Lebanon after an Israeli air strike. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun requested Red Cross coordination with the army and UN peacekeepers to facilitate her rescue.

stories.title: Iran dissidents bemoan European silence after latest execution
stories.summary: Iranian dissident leader Maryam Rajavi addressed the European Parliament, criticizing EU leaders and member states for their silence on what she described as a wave of political executions in Iran. She called their lack of response unjustifiable.

stories.title: Army unveils sweeping XM30 push, $4B bet on NGC2 in newly released budget materials
stories.summary: The U.S. Army revealed extensive plans for its XM30 infantry fighting vehicle program, committing approximately $4 billion to Northrop Grumman in newly released budget materials. Army officials described the effort as part of the service's most significant modernization push in over 40 years.

stories.title: Pakistan’s capital holds its breath with US-Iran talks in limbo
stories.summary: Islamabad closely monitored stalled US-Iran negotiations, with many in Pakistan's capital expressing pride in the country's mediating role. Pakistan has been involved in efforts to navigate a possible end to hostilities between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Druzhba pipeline restarts Russian oil flows to Europe, unblocking EU loan for Kyiv
stories.summary: Russian oil resumed flowing through the Ukrainian section of the Druzhba pipeline on Wednesday after a months-long halt, according to officials in Budapest and Prague. The restart unblocked a €90 billion EU loan urgently needed by Kyiv. The pipeline had been at the center of a standoff involving Hungary and Slovakia.

stories.title: Hodaya Cohen wins Israel's 78th Independence Day Tanach World Quiz for Youth
stories.summary: Hodaya Cohen won Israel's 78th Independence Day Tanach World Quiz for Youth, held at the Jerusalem Theater. The event was pre-recorded due to the security situation and featured 16 contestants from seven countries.

stories.title: India-bound ship among two vessels ‘seized’ by Iran Guards in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iranian Revolutionary Guards seized two vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, including the Liberia-flagged Epaminodas, which was headed to Gujarat's Mundra port in India. Both ships were directed to the Iranian coast.

stories.title: Major Russian book publisher's staff questioned over 'LGBT propaganda'
stories.summary: Russian authorities questioned staff at one of the country's largest book publishers over possible "LGBT propaganda" in its catalogue. The investigation, reported on April 22, is part of broader restrictions on gay and transgender rights under President Vladimir Putin's government.

stories.title: US blocked $500 mn cash shipment to Iraq over pro-Iran attacks
stories.summary: The United States halted a shipment of approximately $500 million in cash destined for Iraq and suspended portions of its security cooperation with Baghdad. The move was reportedly in response to pro-Iran attacks targeting US interests.

stories.title: Defendants plead not guilty over 2025 Nigeria coup plot
stories.summary: Six men pleaded not guilty to treason and terrorism charges in Nigeria in connection with an alleged 2025 coup plot. The case marks the first prosecutions related to the reported putsch attempt.

stories.title: Putin hosts Seychelles president at Kremlin
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted Seychelles President Patrick Herminie at the Kremlin for discussions on bilateral relations and international issues.

stories.title: Kharkiv TRC soldiers suspected of torturing civilians
stories.summary: Ukraine's State Bureau of Investigations uncovered evidence that military personnel at a Kharkiv district territorial recruitment and social support center tortured civilians. The case involves soldiers suspected of abusing their authority at the facility.

stories.title: Air defense wants to intercept 95% of Russian weapons but is running out of radars to spot them
stories.summary: Ukrainian air defense officials stated they aim to intercept 95% of Russian weapons but face a shortage of radar systems. A sergeant noted that all radar systems scheduled for production in 2026 have already been purchased.

stories.title: UAE-backed Colombian mercenaries aided RSF in El Fasher: report
stories.summary: A report alleges that Colombian mercenaries backed by the United Arab Emirates assisted Sudan's Rapid Support Forces in operations around El Fasher. Mobile phones belonging to the Colombian fighters were reportedly tracked to UAE-linked military hubs before being deployed to Sudan.

stories.title: ‘Impossible’ to reopen strait of Hormuz amid ‘flagrant’ ceasefire breaches, Iran says
stories.summary: Iranian forces seized two ships in the Strait of Hormuz as both Washington and Tehran maintained separate blockades of the critical waterway. Iran declared it impossible to reopen the strait amid what it called flagrant ceasefire breaches. The standoff threatens global oil and gas transit through the route.

stories.title: Trump's Gaza committee teeters as Israel obstructs peace process
stories.summary: A third of the 12-member Palestinian-led Gaza committee established under a Trump administration initiative have submitted resignations. The resignations came in protest of Israel's refusal to comply with ceasefire agreement terms, threatening the committee's viability.

stories.title: Europe Might Sit Out In An Indo-Pacific War — But It Can’t Escape the Fallout
stories.summary: A 2024 analysis by Paul van Hooft and Tim Sweijs argued that a US-China war over Taiwan would inevitably draw in and weaken Europe, even if European states attempted to remain neutral. The authors revisited their arguments amid heightened tensions in both the Indo-Pacific and European theaters.

stories.title: US aggression risks pushing a cornered Iran towards a global shadow war
stories.summary: Analysis suggests that increased US pressure on Iran risks driving Tehran toward asymmetric responses through its global network. Iran's international support base reportedly includes lone-wolf actors and sleeper cells that could be activated for proxy operations against American interests.

stories.title: Robotics and satellite communications: Joint venture agreements signed at Ukraine–EU Business Summit
stories.summary: Several joint venture agreements between Ukrainian and European companies were signed at the Ukraine–EU Business Summit in Brussels. The deals focused on robotics and satellite communications, reflecting deepening defense and technology cooperation between Ukraine and EU partners.

stories.title: From patriotic slogans to drones — Iran murals project defiance in war with US
stories.summary: Since the outbreak of the US-Israeli war on Iran, murals featuring themes of resistance and defiance have proliferated across Tehran and other major Iranian cities, continuing a tradition of political street art dating to the 1979 revolution.

stories.title: Not one-drone-fits-all: Admirals stress unmanned systems tailored to the mission
stories.summary: U.S. Navy admirals at the Sea-Air-Space conference emphasized that unmanned systems must be tailored to specific operational theaters. Rear Adm. Douglas Sasse noted that drone capabilities effective in EUCOM or CENTCOM may not suit the Pacific due to far greater distances.

stories.title: Gibraltar’s monkeys may be eating soil to cope with junk food from tourists
stories.summary: Researchers on the Rock of Gibraltar have documented Barbary macaques eating soil more frequently, a behavior scientists believe helps the monkeys cope with stomach upset caused by consuming junk food given or stolen from tourists.

stories.title: Rights groups deny fresh arrests of Palestinians in Damascus
stories.summary: A Palestinian rights group addressed reports of fresh arrests of Palestinians in Damascus, Syria, stating the situation remains unclear due to a lack of official clarification from Syrian authorities. The group said the circumstances surrounding the detentions are shrouded in ambiguity.

stories.title: Palestine Action defendants wanted to 'destroy as many weapons as possible', court told
stories.summary: Palestine Action defendants are on trial in London, where jurors were shown evidence including photos of a battle simulator and quadcopter military drones damaged during a raid on an Elbit Systems factory near Bristol. Prosecutors said the defendants aimed to destroy as many weapons as possible.

stories.title: Iran hangs former nuclear employee for allegedly spying for Israel, aid groups say
stories.summary: Iran executed Mehdi Farid, a former employee of Iran's Atomic Energy Organization, for allegedly spying extensively for Israel's Mossad intelligence agency. Farid was arrested in 2023, and aid organizations confirmed the execution, which the judiciary said was for "extensive cooperation" with Mossad.

stories.title: Iran says it is ready for 2026 World Cup despite security concerns
stories.summary: Iran announced it is fully prepared for its national football team to compete in the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States, scheduled from June 11 to July 19. FIFA President Gianni Infantino confirmed Iran is expected to participate, despite US President Donald Trump raising safety concerns about the team's attendance.

stories.title: The Navy will keep shrinking until the industrial base catches up
stories.summary: A commission examining the future of the U.S. Navy is exploring strategies to sustain the fleet as ships deteriorate faster than they can be replaced. The service is expected to continue shrinking until the industrial base can meet production demands.

stories.title: Extreme heat threatens global food systems, UN agencies warn
stories.summary: United Nations agencies warned that extreme heat is threatening global food systems as temperatures increasingly breach 30°C. Yields for most major crops are reportedly falling due to rising temperatures, raising concerns about food security worldwide.

stories.title: Iran fires on three ships in Strait of Hormuz, complicating efforts to resume U.S.-Iran talks
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired on a container ship and two other vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations Centre. The attacks complicated ongoing efforts to resume U.S.-Iran diplomatic talks.

stories.title: Israel stands together with India in fight against terrorism: Israeli FM
stories.summary: Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar expressed solidarity with India in combating terrorism. He pledged to strengthen bilateral cooperation to advance peace, security, and stability.

stories.title: Approximately 40 Israelis attempted to sneak over border into Syria, IDF confirms
stories.summary: Approximately 40 Israeli civilians from the Habashan Pioneers group attempted to cross from the Golan Heights into Syria. The IDF arrested the group, and police conducted questioning of those involved.

stories.title: From Belgian storage to Elbit subsidiary to Ukrainian air sefense: journey of 15 Gepard systems
stories.summary: Fifteen Gepard anti-aircraft systems were transferred from Belgian storage through an Elbit subsidiary to Ukraine's air defense forces. Belgium had originally operated 54 Gepard systems before decommissioning them in the 2000s as part of defense modernization.

stories.title: Economy Ministry: Druzhba pipeline filling resumes, Russian oil to reach Slovakia on Thursday
stories.summary: The Druzhba oil pipeline is being refilled following repairs on its Ukrainian section, with Russian oil expected to reach Slovakia on Thursday morning. Ukraine's Economy Ministry confirmed the resumption of pipeline operations.

stories.title: Olympic Committee of Israel honors fallen swimmer Eden Nimri
stories.summary: The Olympic Committee of Israel honored Eden Nimri, an IDF captain and former youth national team swimmer who was killed in service. Nimri was recognized for both her military and athletic achievements.

stories.title: No peace in sight: When will Sudan's war end?
stories.summary: International conferences aimed at ending Sudan's civil war have produced no lasting results, as external actors remain entrenched and neither the Sudanese Armed Forces nor the Rapid Support Forces shows willingness to stop fighting. Analysts see no peace agreement on the horizon.

stories.title: Indonesia denounces Israel ‘propaganda’ banner over Gaza hospital ruins
stories.summary: Indonesia accused Israel of flying a propaganda banner over the ruins of the Indonesia Hospital in northern Gaza, which was built with approximately $7.3 million in Indonesian donations and opened in 2015 before being destroyed.

stories.title: Roman Abramovich takes Jersey to European human rights court over criminal investigation
stories.summary: Russian-born oligarch Roman Abramovich has filed a case at the European Court of Human Rights challenging a criminal investigation by Jersey authorities into his financial affairs. His lawyers claim the freezing of £5.3 billion in assets was unfair and abusive. Abramovich is under UK sanctions over his ties to Vladimir Putin.

stories.title: French soldier dies of wounds after attack on UN force in Lebanon
stories.summary: A second French soldier died from wounds sustained in an April 18 attack on UN peacekeepers in southern Lebanon. President Emmanuel Macron blamed Hezbollah for the attack, which also killed another French soldier immediately.

stories.title: Pentagon just deployed Ukrainian anti-drone system at Saudi air base — less than month after Trump said Ukrainian help wasn’t needed
stories.summary: The Pentagon deployed Ukraine's Sky Fortress anti-drone system at a Saudi Arabian air base to counter aerial threats. The move came less than a month after former President Trump suggested Ukrainian assistance was unnecessary.

stories.title: Dozens of settler activists cross into Syria and Lebanon, are escorted out by IDF
stories.summary: Dozens of Israeli settler activists from fringe groups attempted to cross into Syrian and Lebanese territory held by the Israeli military. The IDF intercepted the groups, escorted them back to Israel, and condemned the incursions as criminal offenses.

stories.title: UAE envoy downplays Iran war impact amid US currency swap talk
stories.summary: The UAE's ambassador to the United States downplayed the economic impact of the Iran war, as President Trump indicated he is considering providing a currency swap line to the Emirati central bank to address liquidity concerns.

stories.title: PCB investigates all-rounder Mohammad Nawaz for alleged recreational drug use
stories.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board has launched an investigation into spin-all-rounder Mohammad Nawaz over alleged recreational drug use. Nawaz will continue playing for Multan Sultans in the Pakistan Super League pending the investigation's outcome.

stories.title: Palestinian March of Return reshaped by Israeli restrictions
stories.summary: Palestinians held small marches visiting villages depopulated during the Nakba, as Israeli restrictions reshaped the annual Palestinian March of Return. Events took place in areas including al-Mughayir village near Ramallah in the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Iran says ‘fully prepared’ for football team’s World Cup participation
stories.summary: Iran's government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani announced that Tehran has completed all necessary arrangements for the national football team's participation in the 2026 FIFA World Cup, co-hosted by the United States. The statement addressed concerns raised by US President Donald Trump about the team's attendance.

stories.title: Ships attacked in Strait of Hormuz as uncertainty clouds US-Iran peace talks
stories.summary: A Liberia-flagged container ship was struck by gunfire and rocket-propelled grenades in the Strait of Hormuz amid uncertainty surrounding US-Iran peace talks. The attack highlights the ongoing security risks in the critical waterway as diplomatic efforts remain unresolved.

stories.title: Ukraine to restart Russian oil pipeline to Europe ‘within a few hours’
stories.summary: Ukraine announced it would restart the flow of Russian oil through a pipeline to Europe within hours. The pipeline had been at the center of a standoff between Hungary and Slovakia over energy supplies and transit arrangements.

stories.title: Mali and Niger accuse neighbours of backing terrorism in Sahel rift
stories.summary: Mali and Niger accused neighboring states of supporting terrorism in the Sahel, deepening a diplomatic rift across West Africa.

stories.title: “They come out and die in about 10-15 minutes”: Ukrainian drone commander on Russia’s strange Sumy tactics
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone commander reported that Russian forces in the Sumy sector are being killed within 10 to 15 minutes of emerging from positions. The commander noted that heavy armored vehicles have not been observed in that area.

stories.title: A 42bn-euro dilemma: What is stopping EU from holding Israel to account?
stories.summary: The European Union faces internal divisions over whether to suspend its association agreement with Israel, a trade relationship valued at approximately 42 billion euros. Historical ties, divergent national positions, and commercial interests have created a deadlock among EU member states on holding Israel accountable.

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon face new risks even if US-Iran talks advance - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis warns that Israel and Lebanon face continued instability even if US-Iran negotiations progress. Hezbollah's entrenched position in southern Lebanon and Israel's insistence on long-term security arrangements could keep the northern front volatile.

stories.title: PA begins work to find 11,200 missing, disappeared Palestinians
stories.summary: The Palestinian Authority has begun efforts to locate approximately 11,200 missing Palestinians from Gaza, believed to be buried under rubble from Israeli bombardment or held in Israeli custody.

stories.title: Travel Agency Staff Arrested After 3 Tourists Die on Siberian Peak
stories.summary: Three tourists died during an expedition on Mount Munku-Sardyk, the highest peak in the Eastern Sayan range along the Russian-Mongolian border. Staff from the travel agency that organized the trip have been arrested.

stories.title: South Korean court cuts jail time for battery CEO over deadly plant fire
stories.summary: A South Korean court reduced the prison sentence for Aricell CEO Park Soon-kwan, who had been sentenced to 15 years in September for a deadly battery plant fire. The original ruling found the company had prioritised profit over worker safety.

stories.title: Lebanon says over 62,000 homes damaged or destroyed in Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Lebanese officials reported that Israeli strikes damaged or destroyed over 62,000 housing units, with approximately 21,700 homes destroyed and 40,500 damaged within about 45 days of fighting. Additional homes were destroyed during the first days of the ceasefire.

stories.title: Sindh govt cancels BRT Red Line construction contract, to re-award it on emergency basis: Sharjeel Memon
stories.summary: The Sindh government cancelled the construction contract for the Mosamiyat–Numaish section of Karachi's BRT Red Line project and plans to re-award it on an emergency basis. Senior Minister Sharjeel Memon confirmed the decision amid long delays affecting commuters on University Road.

stories.title: US and Iran in blockade standoff as Pakistan pushes for talks
stories.summary: Tensions remain high in the Strait of Hormuz despite President Trump's extension of a ceasefire with Iran. Pakistan is actively pushing for renewed diplomatic talks between Washington and Tehran amid the ongoing blockade standoff.

stories.title: Rheinmetall lands multibillion dollar FV-014 loitering munitions framework contract
stories.summary: German defense firm Rheinmetall secured a multibillion-dollar framework contract for its FV-014 loitering munitions system. The deal follows a February demonstration of the FV-014 conducted in collaboration with an undisclosed potential NATO customer.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz directs to accelerate efforts for promoting electric vehicles in Pakistan
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif directed officials to accelerate efforts to promote electric vehicles in the country. He cited reducing fuel imports and enhancing environmental protection and energy security as key objectives amid regional instability.

stories.title: Iran seizes ships in Strait of Hormuz after Trump halts attacks
stories.summary: Iran seized two ships in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, tightening its control over the strategic waterway. The seizures came after President Trump halted U.S. military attacks in the area.

stories.title: Alcoholism and mental disorders in Russia reach decade-high peak
stories.summary: Russia's rates of alcoholism and mental disorders have reached their highest levels in a decade. The Chukotka Autonomous Okrug recorded the worst figures nationally, with 391.4 cases per 100,000 residents.

stories.title: New Zealand minister slammed for ‘butter chicken tsunami’ comments about planned FTA with India
stories.summary: A senior New Zealand minister drew criticism for describing a planned free trade agreement with India as a "butter chicken tsunami." The coalition partner NZ First party withdrew support for the deal over concerns about immigration, even as the government prepared to sign the agreement in New Delhi.

stories.title: Ukraine restarts Russian oil to Europe, unblocking 90-billion-euro EU loan
stories.summary: Ukraine resumed the transit of Russian oil to Europe, enabling Hungary to lift its veto on an EU loan worth approximately 90 billion euros. All 27 EU member states are now expected to formally approve the financial package.

stories.title: Labour councillor defending seat in election posed with rifle in Israeli army uniform
stories.summary: Labour councillor Izzy Lenga, who represents South Hampstead ward in London's Camden and sits on Labour's London executive committee, was photographed posing with a rifle in an Israeli army uniform. She is linked to an organization that has helped establish illegal Israeli settlements.

stories.title: Ink and rubble: The systematic assault on Iran’s intellectual soul
stories.summary: The article discusses the impact of Israeli military strikes on Iran's intellectual and cultural institutions, framing the bombing as an assault on the country's academic and cultural heritage.

stories.title: US treasury to extend sanctions relief on Russian and Iranian oil
stories.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent extended sanctions relief on Russian and Iranian seaborne oil for 30 days, responding to requests from approximately 10 countries vulnerable to oil shortages caused by the closed Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Expert: 40 years after Chernobyl, world unprepared for new nuclear threats
stories.summary: Experts warn that 40 years after the 1986 Chernobyl nuclear disaster, the world remains unprepared for new nuclear threats, particularly amid Russia's full-scale war in Ukraine. The proximity of active combat to nuclear facilities raises renewed concerns about potential catastrophe.

stories.title: Second French soldier dies of wounds sustained in Hezbollah attack on UN peacekeepers
stories.summary: French Corporal Anicet Girardin became the second French soldier to die from wounds sustained in a Hezbollah attack on a UN peacekeeping base in southern Lebanon. President Emmanuel Macron confirmed Girardin succumbed to gunfire injuries after being evacuated to France for treatment.

stories.title: Islamabad’s Red Zone remains off-limits; other routes in twin cities reopen to public after days-long closure
stories.summary: Islamabad's Red Zone remained sealed on Wednesday due to security preparations for foreign delegations, though other routes in the twin cities reopened. The closures were linked to an expected visit by U.S. Vice President JD Vance, whose arrival plans were abruptly changed by the White House. Iran's negotiating delegation also delayed a decision on attending talks.

stories.title: How Israel is destroying Lebanon’s water infrastructure
stories.summary: Experts have accused Israel of deliberately targeting water infrastructure in southern Lebanon, with the aim of displacing or endangering the local population. The attacks have reportedly caused significant damage to essential water supply systems in the region.

stories.title: Mapping the environmental toll of the Middle East war
stories.summary: The ongoing U.S. and Israeli military campaign against Iran has caused significant environmental damage, including oil refinery fires, missile strikes on pesticide factories, and an oil slick in the Strait of Hormuz. Concerns are growing over the public health impact on local populations.

stories.title: Ukraine’s fifth minesweeper just arrived from Netherlands — named “Henichesk” after ship Russia sank in 2022
stories.summary: Ukraine received its fifth minesweeper from the Netherlands, named "Henichesk" after a ship Russia sank in 2022. The United Kingdom, Belgium, and the Netherlands have collectively donated similar vessels — named Cherkasy, Chernihiv, Mariupol, and Melitopol — to bolster Ukraine's naval fleet.

stories.title: IDF escalates robot wars against Hezbollah in southern Lebanon's Bint Jbail
stories.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces have intensified the use of ground robots in operations against Hezbollah in Bint Jbail, southern Lebanon. The robotic systems are being deployed to accelerate the destruction of Hezbollah weapons infrastructure as military operations in the area expand.

stories.title: Ukraine has asked Turkey to host a Zelensky-Putin meeting, minister says
stories.summary: Ukraine has asked Turkey to host a meeting between President Volodymyr Zelensky and Russian President Vladimir Putin, according to a Ukrainian minister. Zelensky has long sought direct talks to hasten a resolution to the war, which has lasted more than four years.

stories.title: Trump has not set a timeline for extension of Iran ceasefire, source says
stories.summary: A source briefed on the matter told Reuters that U.S. President Donald Trump has not set a specific timeline for extending the ceasefire with Iran.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz is hosting gunboat diplomacy as US and Iran vie for most effective blockade
stories.summary: The US and Iran are engaged in competing naval blockade efforts in the Strait of Hormuz following President Trump's decision to shelve plans to bomb Iranian infrastructure. Iran aims to maintain its chokehold on global oil flows, with some analysts warning it could run out of oil storage capacity imminently.

stories.title: Turkish firms boost defense ties with Malaysia in missiles, comms and AI
stories.summary: Turkish defense companies are expanding cooperation with Malaysia in the areas of missiles, communications systems, and artificial intelligence. Analysts note that Malaysia selected Turkish suppliers for their combat-proven technology, competitive pricing, fast delivery timelines, and willingness to establish long-term industrial partnerships.

stories.title: Israeli settlers block Palestinian children from school in the West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli settlers have been blocking Palestinian children from reaching their school near Umm al-Khair village in the occupied West Bank. Students, teachers, and families have responded by staging daily peaceful sit-ins at the site of a fence erected near the village.

stories.title: Israel cannot settle for another ceasefire with Lebanon, Alma Center head says - interview
stories.summary: Alma Center head Zehavi argued that Israel cannot accept another ceasefire with Lebanon without addressing what she views as two decades of failed security policy. She said the current debate requires revisiting those longstanding strategic shortcomings.

stories.title: Mother who lost three kids in Louisiana shooting hospitalized with bullet lodged in face
stories.summary: Christina Snow, the mother of three children killed in a mass shooting in Shreveport, Louisiana, is recovering in hospital with a bullet still lodged in her face. Police described the incident, in which eight people were killed, as a violent domestic incident.

stories.title: Iran’s leaders debate war and peace after Trump ceasefire extension
stories.summary: Iranian state television has promoted a pro-war narrative following a Trump-announced ceasefire extension, while other voices within Iran urge moderation and diplomatic engagement.

stories.title: Algeria: President Tebboune Welcomes Chadian Counterpart At Algiers International Airport
stories.summary: Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune welcomed Chadian President Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno at Algiers International Airport for an official visit on Wednesday.

stories.title: Lebanon said to seek one-month truce extension; Hezbollah again targets troops with drone
stories.summary: Lebanon is seeking a one-month extension of its ceasefire with Israel ahead of planned talks in Washington. Meanwhile, Hezbollah targeted Israeli troops with a drone in southern Lebanon, and the IDF reported killing two Hezbollah members who crossed the ceasefire line.

stories.title: Algeria: President Tebboune Holds Talks With Chadian Counterpart At Algiers International Airport Vip Lounge
stories.summary: Algerian President Tebboune held talks with Chadian President Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno in the VIP lounge at Algiers International Airport during the Chadian leader's official visit to Algeria.

stories.title: Uganda: Brutal Killing of Radiographer Sparks Security Fears in Mukono
stories.summary: Radiographer Peter Mubiru was fatally attacked by unknown assailants with a paver stone in Bugoba Village, Mukono Municipality, Uganda. The killing has sparked fear among local residents and calls for security agencies to restore order.

stories.title: Somalia: Somalia to Intensify Anti-Terror Operations, Defence Minister Says
stories.summary: Somalia's Defence Minister Ahmed Moallim Fiqi announced that the Federal Government will intensify military operations against militants while expanding stabilization efforts in recently recovered areas.

stories.title: Israelis blow up house in southern Lebanon 'in memory' of slain soldier
stories.summary: Israel released footage showing Battalion 7106 remotely destroying a home in the southern Lebanese village of Kfar Kila. The military said the demolition was carried out in memory of soldier Lidor Porat, who was killed during fighting in Lebanon.

stories.title: China condemns Japanese leaders' war shrine offerings, visits
stories.summary: China condemned Japanese leaders for making offerings and visits to the Yasukuni war shrine. A Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson called the actions a gross trampling of human conscience and issued a strong condemnation.

stories.title: Reuters: Third Russian oil refinery shuts down this week after drone attacks
stories.summary: Three Russian oil refineries have suspended operations this week following Ukrainian drone attacks, according to Reuters. The shutdowns represent a continued Ukrainian strategy of targeting Russia's energy refining infrastructure.

stories.title: Somalia: Somali President Opens New Ports Ministry Headquarters
stories.summary: Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud inaugurated the new headquarters of the Ministry of Ports and Marine Transport in Mogadishu, emphasizing government priorities of port modernization and maritime resource protection.

stories.title: Palestinians in Gaza to vote in municipal elections, offering view into support for Hamas
stories.summary: Palestinians in Gaza are set to participate in municipal elections, marking the territory's first vote since 2006. In that year, Hamas won legislative elections and subsequently seized control of Gaza after a brief civil war with Fatah, led by PA President Mahmoud Abbas.

stories.title: Ukraine has asked Turkiye to host a Zelenskiy-Putin meeting, Foreign Minister says
stories.summary: Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said Kyiv has asked Turkey and other capitals to host a meeting between President Volodymyr Zelenskiy and Russian President Vladimir Putin. The request reflects Ukraine's ongoing diplomatic efforts to arrange direct talks.

stories.title: Somalia: Former Somali President Raises Concerns Over Government Term Dispute
stories.summary: Former Somali President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed expressed concern over a dispute surrounding the current Federal Government's mandate, warning of political uncertainty in the country.

stories.title: Botswana: Officials Warn of Illegal Phane Harvesting
stories.summary: Officials in Botswana warned about illegal harvesting of Phane (mopane worms) near Tshimoyapula, where large crowds have been depleting the natural resource.

stories.title: Ghana: GIS Intensifies Crackdown On Exploitative Migrant Street Begging Networks in Ashanti Region
stories.summary: The Ghana Immigration Service conducted an intelligence-led operation in Kumasi, Ashanti Region, on April 21, 2026, to rescue undocumented migrants from exploitative street begging networks.

stories.title: Britain’s military dependence on US ‘no longer tenable’, says former Nato chief
stories.summary: Former NATO Secretary General Lord Robertson warned that Britain's high military dependence on the United States is "no longer tenable" and that the UK must become more strategically independent. He said the diplomatic tone from the White House is at a historic low and that divergence between the two allies is likely to continue beyond the Trump presidency.

stories.title: Niger junta says it suspended nearly 3,000 NGOs in 2025
stories.summary: Niger's military government announced it suspended approximately 2,900 of the country's 4,700 registered local and foreign NGOs and development agencies in 2025, according to the interior minister.

stories.title: Honoring soldiers, Herzog says they have fought ‘battles future generations will study’
stories.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog honored soldiers at an Independence Day ceremony, stating they fought battles that future generations would study. A freed hostage performed at the event, and the IDF chief warned Israel was ready to resume fighting if necessary.

stories.title: Russia to Cut Kazakh Oil Transit to Germany
stories.summary: Rosneft's German subsidiary informed German regulators that Russia's Energy Ministry ordered a suspension of Kazakh oil transit through Russian pipelines to Germany.

stories.title: Trump calls Iran’s leadership ‘fractured’. Is it, and who’s in charge?
stories.summary: Approximately 53 days into the conflict with Iran, analysts find little concrete evidence that Iran's government leadership is fragmented, contrary to claims by U.S. President Donald Trump describing it as 'fractured.'

stories.title: Palestine Action activist who hit officer with sledge hammer ‘panicked’, court told
stories.summary: Samuel Corner, 23, a Palestine Action activist, told a court he struck police Sgt Kate Evans with a sledgehammer to protect a co-defendant he believed was being seriously hurt during a raid on an Elbit Systems facility near Bristol in August 2024. He is charged with causing grievous bodily harm with intent.

stories.title: US spent up to 61% of its Patriot arsenal in 39 days — Ukraine looks at building its own ballistic defense
stories.summary: A report indicates the United States has expended up to 61% of its Patriot missile arsenal over 39 days of operations. In response to dwindling Western stockpiles, Ukraine is exploring the development of its own ballistic missile defense capabilities.

stories.title: ‘He was always smiling’: Sister of fallen soldier Shachar Fridman on Israel’s Remembrance Day
stories.summary: The sister of fallen IDF soldier Shachar Fridman spoke on Israel's Remembrance Day about her brother, who served in the 101st Battalion of the Paratroopers Brigade. Fridman had already completed his service but returned to duty after the October 7 outbreak of war.

stories.title: Fires ignited by Ukrainian drones rage at Russian oil refinery
stories.summary: Hundreds of firefighters are working to contain fires at Russia's Tuapse oil refinery after Ukrainian drone strikes ignited blazes at the facility.

stories.title: EU agrees to unblock €90bn loan for Ukraine after Hungary lifts veto
stories.summary: EU member states agreed to unblock a €90 billion loan for Ukraine and a new sanctions package against Russia after Ukraine resumed pumping Russian oil through the Druzhba pipeline to Hungary and Slovakia. Budapest subsequently lifted its veto, and formal approval is expected by Thursday.

stories.title: Nepal’s home minister resigns, second cabinet exit in one month
stories.summary: Nepal's Home Minister Sudan Gurung resigned after less than a month in office, citing questions about his investments and other matters. His departure marks the second cabinet exit in Nepal within one month.

stories.title: Russian national known as “Mexican” built 105-store drug network across Ukraine. It was even advertised in Kyiv metro
stories.summary: Ukrainian authorities dismantled a drug distribution network called "Khimprom" spanning 105 stores across the country. The network was built by a Russian national known as "Mexican" and was reportedly advertised in Kyiv's metro system.

stories.title: Blockchain billionaire Sun takes Trump family’s crypto firm to court
stories.summary: Blockchain billionaire Justin Sun has filed a lawsuit against World Liberty, the crypto firm linked to the Trump family. The company faces growing scrutiny from investors who have raised concerns about a lack of transparency.

stories.title: Russia’s Judicial Department removes conviction statistics from its website
stories.summary: Russia's Judicial Department, which operates under the Supreme Court, has removed conviction statistics from its website, according to independent Russian media outlets.

stories.title: Sexual violence by Israeli settlers and soldiers driving Palestinian displacement, report says
stories.summary: A report finds that sexual violence committed by Israeli settlers and soldiers in the occupied West Bank is driving Palestinian displacement, with threats against women and children forcing families to flee their homes.

stories.title: Prize-winning book 'Houris' brings prison term for French-Algerian author Kamel Daoud
stories.summary: French-Algerian author Kamel Daoud has been sentenced in absentia to three years in prison and fined in Algeria over his prize-winning novel "Houris," which revisits the country's civil war. The ruling raises concerns about freedom of expression and pressure on authors confronting Algeria's violent past.

stories.title: Mexico pledges World Cup safety after shooting at ancient pyramids
stories.summary: Mexican authorities pledged enhanced security for the upcoming World Cup after a shooting at the Teotihuacan archaeological site near Mexico City killed a Canadian tourist. The incident raised concerns about safety ahead of the major international sporting event.

stories.title: US in talks to resettle 1,100 Afghans in Congo, group says
stories.summary: The United States is in discussions to resettle approximately 1,100 stranded Afghan nationals in the Democratic Republic of Congo as visa processing has stalled, raising concerns about their safety and long-term prospects.

stories.title: As millions return to Sudan, UN calls for investment in essential services
stories.summary: The UN International Organization for Migration reported that nearly four million displaced people have returned to their homes across Sudan three years into the conflict, but face severe shortages of essential services.

stories.title: As internal divisions simmer, Lebanese see echoes of civil war
stories.summary: Lebanese citizens who lived through the 1975–1990 civil war warned of echoes of that conflict in current internal divisions. Rising tensions among different factions within Lebanon have fueled fears of renewed domestic fighting.

stories.title: Lufthansa cuts 20,000 summer flights as fuel prices surge
stories.summary: Lufthansa announced it is cutting 20,000 flights from its summer schedule as jet fuel prices surge due to the US-Israeli war with Iran. The German airline is among several carriers reducing operations in response to rising fuel costs driven by the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: Food security: Why Guterres’s UN plan to get fertiliser flowing in Hormuz is stalling
stories.summary: The United Nations is proposing a humanitarian corridor through the Strait of Hormuz to allow fertiliser and essential goods to pass through the waterway, which has been effectively blocked since the start of the Iran war. The plan has yet to be approved by several countries involved.

stories.title: Russian drones strike Ukraine's Odesa port, kill railway worker in south, deputy PM says
stories.summary: Russian drones struck infrastructure at Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa overnight, killing a railway worker in the south, according to Deputy Prime Minister Oleksiy Kuleba. The attack was reported on April 22 and targeted key port facilities.

stories.title: As Iran talks go nowhere, will Donald Trump still go to Beijing?
stories.summary: Stalled US-Iran peace talks are raising doubts about President Trump's planned visit to Beijing, though the war could elevate the diplomatic stakes if the trip proceeds. Trump extended a fragile two-week ceasefire with Iran just before it was set to expire.

stories.title: EU ambassadors approve €90 billion loan for Ukraine and 20th package of sanctions against Russia
stories.summary: EU ambassadors approved a €90 billion loan for Ukraine and the 20th package of sanctions against Russia at a COREPER II meeting in Brussels. The session also finalized amendments to the EU's multiannual financial framework, completing the legislative requirements for the loan.

stories.title: Pakistan out of women’s football tournament in India over political strife
stories.summary: The Pakistani government barred its women's football team from participating in the SAFF Women's Championship hosted in Goa, India, citing political tensions between the two countries.

stories.title: Kyiv mass shooter called himself  “general of Russian Army” and filmed himself killing seven people
stories.summary: A 58-year-old gunman named Dmytro Vasylychenkov carried out a mass shooting in Kyiv, killing seven people while filming the attack. He reportedly referred to himself as a "general of the Russian Army" during the incident.

stories.title: Oil falls after Iran says it received sign US will end blockade
stories.summary: Oil prices fell after Iran indicated it had received a signal that the United States would end its blockade. Brent crude declined as much as 2 percent to near $97 a barrel on the news, reflecting market expectations of eased tensions in the Middle East.

stories.title: Ukraine’s grid didn’t choose nuclear. Russia made this choice for Ukraine.
stories.summary: An analysis examines how Russian attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure have effectively pushed the country toward greater reliance on nuclear power. The shift is described as a consequence of attrition rather than a deliberate policy choice by Ukraine's grid planners.

stories.title: The war on Iran: Breaking down the words you’re hearing
stories.summary: An analysis examines the terminology used in coverage of the U.S.-Israel military campaign against Iran, tracing the linguistic origins of key terms commonly heard in reporting on the conflict.

stories.title: Patriot Park Deputy Director Arrested for Allegedly Accepting Bribe
stories.summary: Vitaly Melimuk, deputy director of Patriot Park, has been arrested on allegations of accepting a bribe. He is the latest park official to face criminal prosecution amid a broader shakeup in Russia's military establishment.

stories.title: No cartels involved - but Mexico's pyramid attack prompts new concerns
stories.summary: A deadly shooting at a popular pyramid tourist site in Mexico has raised new security concerns weeks before the country hosts the World Cup. Authorities say drug cartels were not involved in the attack.

stories.title: Iran hangs man convicted of links to Israel’s Mossad
stories.summary: Iran executed a man convicted of links to Israel's Mossad intelligence agency. The hanging came amid a series of executions in recent weeks of individuals connected to mass protests that erupted in January.

stories.title: US considers sending Afghan allies to DR Congo amid resettlement halt
stories.summary: The Trump administration is considering a plan to resettle more than 1,000 Afghans who supported U.S. forces to the Democratic Republic of Congo rather than bringing them to the United States.

stories.title: How Ireland’s war-driven fuel blockades revealed the true cost of Europe’s oil addiction
stories.summary: Disruptions to oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz caused by the Iran war have triggered fuel blockades and energy shortages in Ireland and across Europe. Electric vehicle sales in continental Europe rose 51% in March as the crisis accelerates the shift toward clean energy.

stories.title: Russia says will halt oil flow to Germany via Druzhba pipeline
stories.summary: Russia confirmed it will suspend shipments of Kazakh oil to Germany through the Druzhba pipeline starting May 1, cutting a key energy supply route to Europe.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Spider ground robot shoots +70°, hunting drones the way infantry can’t
stories.summary: Ukraine's Spider ground robot is capable of engaging aerial drones at elevation angles exceeding 70 degrees, providing anti-drone capabilities beyond what infantry can achieve. The autonomous system can operate alongside troops for up to three days without rotation.

stories.title: ICC chamber rules case against Rodrigo Duterte’s war on drugs killings to proceed
stories.summary: The ICC Appeals Chamber rejected former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte's challenge to the court's jurisdiction, allowing the crimes against humanity case related to his anti-drug campaign killings to proceed. Duterte has been held at The Hague since March 2025.

stories.title: Turkey and Pakistan discuss latest on ceasefire talks
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan and Pakistani counterpart Ishaq Dar discussed developments in U.S.-Iran talks during a phone call. The two ministers also reviewed joint Turkish-Pakistani efforts to mediate between the parties involved.

stories.title: Blue skies, white smoke: Israelis celebrate 78 years of independence
stories.summary: Israelis celebrated 78 years of independence at beaches, parks, and streets across the country, with barbecues, music, and gatherings marking the occasion.

stories.title: Italian PM responds to Russian propagandist Solovyov’s ‘fascist creature’ insult; Russia’s ambassador summoned
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni responded to Russian state TV presenter Vladimir Solovyov after he called her a "fascist creature" on his program. Italy summoned the Russian ambassador over the remarks.

stories.title: Ministers speak out in cabinet meeting over Keir Starmer’s sacking of Olly Robbins
stories.summary: UK Cabinet ministers expressed concern about Prime Minister Keir Starmer's decision to dismiss Olly Robbins as the Foreign Office's top official over the Peter Mandelson vetting scandal. Several ministers warned Starmer during a cabinet meeting against alienating the civil service.

stories.title: Northrop slated to deliver surface EW system to carriers in 2028
stories.summary: Northrop Grumman plans to deliver a surface electronic warfare system to U.S. Navy aircraft carriers by 2028. Company executive Montá Harrell stated that Northrop has developed SEWIP configurations for both destroyers and carriers.

stories.title: Unblocked EU loan provides relief to Ukraine's strained finances
stories.summary: EU ambassadors on Wednesday unblocked a €90 billion loan to Ukraine that had been halted by a Hungarian veto linked to a dispute over oil flows via the Druzhba pipeline. The loan, originally approved by the European Council in December, is considered critical for Kyiv's ability to sustain its fight against Russia.

stories.title: A stroll through Tel Aviv on Independence Day: Amid fragile calm, a city exhales
stories.summary: Crowds filled beaches and parks in Tel Aviv on Independence Day amid fragile ceasefires and weeks of conflict. Residents embraced barbecues and music in an atmosphere described as cautious relief.

stories.title: Three people injured in Kherson following drone attack
stories.summary: Three people were injured in Kherson's Korabelnyi district following a Russian drone attack on the city.

stories.title: Two hostages captured in Niger freed by Russia's Africa Corps in Mali
stories.summary: Russian national Oleg Greta and Ukrainian Yuri Yurov, held hostage in Mali for nearly two years, were freed by Russia's Africa Corps in what Moscow described as a special operation.

stories.title: Labour expected to suffer losses in London's local elections
stories.summary: A YouGov poll conducted for Sky News and Politico predicted that the Labour Party will suffer losses in London's upcoming local elections, with significant gains expected for the Green Party and the Reform Party.

stories.title: Second French peacekeeper dies in Lebanon after ambush blamed on Hezbollah
stories.summary: A second French UN peacekeeper, Corporal Anicet Girardin, died from wounds sustained in a weekend ambush in Lebanon blamed on Hezbollah. Staff Sergeant Florian Montorio was killed in the same Saturday attack, which Hezbollah has denied carrying out.

stories.title: Peru's electoral authority chief resigns as runoff still undecided ten days after first round
stories.summary: Piero Corvetto resigned as head of Peru's National Office of Electoral Processes (ONPE) ten days after the April 12 first-round presidential vote, amid judicial investigations and an institutional credibility crisis. The National Justice Board unanimously accepted his resignation as the runoff remains undecided.

stories.title: Nepal: Interior minister elected on anti-corruption platform steps down amid financial investigation
stories.summary: Nepal's Interior Minister Sudan Gurung resigned amid a financial investigation, saying he wanted to ensure a fair probe. His departure marks the second ministerial exit in weeks for a government elected on an anti-corruption platform after youth protests toppled its predecessor.

stories.title: 'Trump's high-stakes political theatre: US winning conventional war, Iran winning asymmetrical war'
stories.summary: Dr. William Lawrence, a former US diplomat and analyst at the National Council on US-Arab Relations, described the US-Iran confrontation as high-stakes political theatre. He argues the US is winning the conventional war while Iran is prevailing in the asymmetrical dimension of the conflict.

stories.title: Trump approval slips as polls show warning signs for Republicans ahead of midterms
stories.summary: Three major polls by Reuters-Ipsos, AP-NORC, and NBC show President Trump's approval rating hovering in the mid-30s, with public concern over the economy, the Iran conflict, and immigration. The declining numbers pose warning signs for Republican candidates ahead of the US midterm elections in six months.

stories.title: Iran targets three ships in Strait of Hormuz escalation
stories.summary: Iranian forces targeted three commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, escalating threats to one of the world's most important shipping routes.

stories.title: Israeli strike on car in southern Lebanon kills two, say medics
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike on a car in southern Lebanon killed two people, according to medics cited by Lebanese state media.

stories.title: Iraqi militias linked to Iran form 'joint operations' room
stories.summary: Iraqi militias linked to Iran have established a joint operations room in Baghdad amid fears of renewed conflict involving Iranian and U.S. forces. The move followed a visit to Baghdad by Iranian commander Qaani.

stories.title: Consequences of massive strike on Yampil community in Sumy region revealed
stories.summary: Rescue workers documented the aftermath of a large-scale Russian strike on the Yampil community in Ukraine's Sumy region.

stories.title: Ukraine says some Russian missiles fly near Chornobyl, risking major accident
stories.summary: Ukraine's top state prosecutor told Reuters that Russia has repeatedly launched drones and missiles on flight paths near the disused Chornobyl nuclear plant during attacks on Ukraine. Officials warned the practice elevates the risk of a major nuclear accident at the site.

stories.title: China’s battery makers stand to gain as Iran war reshapes energy storage demand: Fitch
stories.summary: Fitch Ratings says Chinese battery cell manufacturers stand to benefit from the US-Israeli war in Iran as high oil prices and expanding AI data centers drive rising global demand for energy storage solutions.

stories.title: Can ‘token exports’ give China an edge in the AI era?
stories.summary: Chinese AI models accounted for four of the top 10 models by token consumption on the OpenRouter marketplace between mid-March and mid-April, reflecting growing global adoption of Chinese artificial intelligence systems.

stories.title: Deputy director of Russia’s Defense Ministry ‘Patriot’ park arrested on bribery charges
stories.summary: A Russian court authorized the arrest of Vitaly Melimuk, deputy general director for operations and logistics at the Defense Ministry's Patriot park, on charges of accepting an 18-million-ruble bribe, according to the Russian Investigative Committee.

stories.title: Trump says he was 'surprised' by 'Chinese gift to Iran' found in seized tanker ship
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said during a CNBC interview that he was surprised by items found aboard a seized tanker ship, describing them as a possible "Chinese gift to Iran." Trump did not provide specific details about the cargo or the vessel's origin.

stories.title: Syria's Sharaa lands in Qatar as part of wider Gulf tour
stories.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa visited Qatar as part of a Gulf tour, meeting with Qatar's Emir in Doha. Discussions focused on strengthening regional ties, attracting investment, and advancing Syria's post-war reconstruction.

stories.title: What is uranium enrichment and how quickly could Iran build a nuclear bomb?
stories.summary: MIT professor Ted Postol discussed Iran's nuclear capabilities, including its stockpile of approximately 440 kilograms of 60 percent enriched uranium and the timeline for potentially developing a nuclear weapon.

stories.title: Prosecutors seek nearly 2 years in prison for film critic Anton Dolin over ‘foreign agent’ violations
stories.summary: Russian prosecutors asked a Moscow court to sentence film critic and journalist Anton Dolin in absentia to one year and 10 months in prison for allegedly failing to fulfill his legal obligations as a designated foreign agent.

stories.title: Iran war conflict could create systemic gas demand destruction
stories.summary: Analysts warn that the ongoing Iran war could cause systemic, long-term destruction of global gas demand as countries accelerate switching to alternative energy sources amid what is described as the largest supply disruption in modern history.
