stories.title: Russia and Libya revive joint commission after 15-year freeze
stories.summary: Russia and Libya reactivated their joint commission after a 15-year freeze, opening opportunities for Russian firms to participate in Libyan oil production, trade, and reconstruction projects.

stories.title: Zero net migration would shrink UK GDP by 15% by 2060, Oxford Economics warns
stories.summary: A report by Oxford Economics warns that a scenario of zero net migration would shrink the United Kingdom's GDP by 15% by 2060 and limit annual growth to 0.9%. The study was published amid intense political debate over immigration policy in the UK.

stories.title: Iran says U.S. naval blockade has little impact on food supply
stories.summary: Iran's Agriculture Minister Gholamreza Nouri stated that the U.S. naval blockade has had little impact on Iran's food supply. He said the country faces no problems in supplying basic goods and food despite the blockade.

stories.title: From grief to trepidation: This year’s fateful transition from Memorial Day to Independence Day
stories.summary: Israel's transition from Memorial Day to Independence Day carried heightened significance this year amid ongoing external threats and internal debate over Prime Minister Netanyahu's leadership and policies.

stories.title: FedEx targeted by French lawsuit over 'complicity' in Gaza genocide
stories.summary: The French Jewish Union for Peace filed a lawsuit in France accusing FedEx's French subsidiary of complicity in genocide by allegedly facilitating the transfer of military equipment to Israel.

stories.title: How the Iran war oil and gas supply shock compares with past disruptions
stories.summary: An analysis compares the current oil and gas supply disruption caused by the Iran war with past energy shocks. The conflict's impact on global energy markets has drawn parallels to previous major supply crises.

stories.title: Will Iraq’s Shia bloc overcome obstacles to pick the next PM?
stories.summary: Iraq's Shia-led Coordination Framework faces a constitutional deadline on Sunday to nominate a new prime minister, with internal negotiations continuing over the selection amid political obstacles.

stories.title: Iran tankers laden with crude go dark to sail past US blockade
stories.summary: At least two Iranian tankers carrying approximately nine million barrels of crude oil evaded the U.S. naval blockade by turning off their tracking systems. The vessels successfully delivered their cargo to market within the past week.

stories.title: In Semenivka, Chernihiv region, enemy Molniya drone strikes private houses, injuring woman
stories.summary: In Semenivka, Chernihiv region, a Russian Molniya combat drone struck a residential area, injuring an older woman and damaging private houses.

stories.title: Philippine lawmakers examine gap in Sara Duterte’s bank statements, declared wealth
stories.summary: Philippine lawmakers examining impeachment complaints against Vice-President Sara Duterte-Carpio were shown evidence of bank transactions totaling 4.4 billion pesos in inflows, far exceeding her and her husband's declared net worth.

stories.title: Woman and child killed in Russia's Syzran after Ukrainian drone hits building, official says
stories.summary: A woman and child were killed in the Russian city of Syzran after a Ukrainian drone strike caused a partial collapse of their apartment building on Wednesday. Twelve other people were injured in the attack, according to the regional governor.

stories.title: Russia could be ready for NATO conflict year after Ukraine, Dutch warn
stories.summary: A new Dutch intelligence report warns that Russia could be prepared for a conflict with NATO within a year after the Ukraine war ends. According to the assessment, Moscow's strategy would aim not at outright military defeat of the alliance but at dividing it through limited territorial gains.

stories.title: Ukraine says some Russian missiles fly near Chornobyl, risking major accident
stories.summary: Ukraine's Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko reported that some Russian missiles have flown near the Chornobyl nuclear site, raising the risk of a major accident. The disclosure came as Ukraine prepared to mark the 40th anniversary of the 1986 Chornobyl disaster on April 26.

stories.title: Iran hangs former nuclear employee on spying charges: NGOs
stories.summary: Iran executed Mehdi Farid, a former nuclear employee, on charges of spying for Israel's Mossad. Human rights organizations have warned of a sharp increase in politically charged executions in Iran during the ongoing war.

stories.title: Europol tracked 45 children Russia deported all the way to the military units that moved them — and passed the evidence to Kyiv
stories.summary: Europol tracked 45 children forcibly deported from Ukraine to Russia, tracing their movement to specific Russian military units involved in the transfers. The intelligence package, including routes, perpetrators, and destination facilities, was shared with Ukrainian investigators.

stories.title: High Court sets May 14 deadline for state update in Ras Ein al-Auja case
stories.summary: Israel's High Court extended the deadline for the state to provide an update on the Ras Ein al-Auja case to May 14. The extension came amid disputes over when the update was originally required.

stories.title: When the map turns red: Inside the lives upended by Israel’s expulsion orders
stories.summary: Israeli authorities issued evacuation orders marking buildings and districts in red on maps, triggering mass displacement as families, including schoolchildren, scrambled to flee on short notice amid clogged roads and chaos.

stories.title: Supreme Court adopts digital hearings across multiple cities
stories.summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court announced it has integrated digital technology enabling multi-location hearings across the country. The system connects benches, counsel, and litigants from different cities without geographical constraints, aiming to improve transparency and accessibility.

stories.title: ‘Do not forget the fighters’: Chaim Malespin marks Israel’s 78th Independence Day
stories.summary: Chaim Malespin marked Israel's 78th Independence Day by honoring 170 soldiers who fell over the past year, including Staff Sergeant Daniel Hamo, a paratrooper from Tiberias killed in Gaza.

stories.title: Attock refinery announces closure of main crude plant amid road closures
stories.summary: Attock Refinery Limited, the only oil refinery in northern Pakistan, shut down its main crude plant due to road closures imposed for security ahead of possible U.S.-Iran talks. The facility serves fuel needs across central and northern Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, and Gilgit-Baltistan.

stories.title: Residents pay the price as Afghanistan-Pakistan border remains closed
stories.summary: The Pakistan-Afghanistan border has been completely closed for six months due to the ongoing conflict between Kabul and Islamabad. Despite multiple mediation attempts, negotiations have failed, leaving tens of thousands displaced and causing significant civilian casualties.

stories.title: Beyond the desecrated statue: What truly demands our outrage
stories.summary: A statue of Jesus was destroyed in Lebanon, drawing public attention. The article contextualizes the incident within the broader ongoing Israeli military operations and their humanitarian impact.

stories.title: Russia's Planned VPN Traffic Charges Hit by Technical Delays – Vedomosti
stories.summary: Russian authorities' plan to have telecom providers charge extra for VPN traffic has been delayed by technical difficulties, with carriers unable to meet the original implementation timeline, according to Vedomosti.

stories.title: TikToker dressed as chief rabbi stirs confusion at Independence event
stories.summary: TikToker Eyal Tzionov, who styles himself as a messiah, caused confusion at an Israeli Independence Day event by dressing in the Sephardic chief rabbi's iconic robe and turban. He had previously ascended the Temple Mount and attended a rally supporting Minister Ben Gvir.

stories.title: The Navy’s plan for pilot training could add the first clean-sheet trainer aircraft since the 1950s
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy is exploring plans for a new pilot training aircraft, which could be the first clean-sheet trainer design since the 1950s. Sierra Nevada Corporation's Freedom trainer is designed to withstand the demanding landing conditions associated with naval aviation operations.

stories.title: Pakistan coach Adeel calls for more international matches after FIFA Series
stories.summary: Pakistan women's football team head coach Adeel Rizki called for regular training camps and more international matches after his team finished third in their first FIFA Series campaign in Ivory Coast. He emphasized that continuity is essential for sustained improvement.

stories.title: Polymarket forecast low chances of ceasefire being extended even after Trump's announcement
stories.summary: Prediction market Polymarket showed only a 20% chance that the Iran-related ceasefire would be extended by April 22. Users on the platform did not consider the current situation to constitute an official extension, even following Trump's announcement.

stories.title: Rare ancient charcoal shows how prehistoric ‘Israelis’ were already grilling 780,000 years ago
stories.summary: A study of rare ancient charcoal found at the Gesher Benot Ya'akov archaeological site in Israel reveals that hominins were using fire for grilling approximately 780,000 years ago, demonstrating advanced cognitive abilities.

stories.title: Son of Holocaust survivors and granddaughter of a Nazi confront their separate inheritances
stories.summary: Charlie Scheidt, son of Holocaust survivors, and Kat Rohrer, granddaughter of a Nazi, co-authored the memoir 'Inheritance' about confronting their families' opposing legacies during World War II.

stories.title: Nigeria's Tinubu sacks finance minister in surprise cabinet reshuffle
stories.summary: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu dismissed Finance Minister Wale Edun in a cabinet reshuffle, replacing him with former Minister of State for Finance Taiwo Oyedele. Oyedele played a central role in the administration's recent tax overhaul.

stories.title: Palestinian boy, 14, among two killed in settler attack near West Bank school
stories.summary: Two Palestinians, including 14-year-old Aws al-Naasan, were killed when Israeli settlers opened fire near a school in the West Bank village of al-Mughayyir. Witnesses and local officials said the attackers shot at students and then at those who came to help, wounding three others.

stories.title: Syrian minorities refused asylum in Europe as rejections surge
stories.summary: European countries are seeing a surge in asylum rejections for Syrian minorities. In one case, armed men in the Syrian city of Jableh forced a 20-year-old Alawite student and his father to the ground at gunpoint in March of last year, illustrating the ongoing threats minority communities face.

stories.title: Lebanon 'to request one-month truce extension' during Israel meeting
stories.summary: A Lebanese official told AFP that Lebanon will request a one-month extension of the ceasefire during its meeting with Israel in Washington on Thursday. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun confirmed contacts are underway as the current truce period nears expiration.

stories.title: US imposes new sanctions against suppliers of weapons to Iran
stories.summary: The United States imposed new sanctions targeting networks linked to Iran that are involved in rebuilding missile supplies. The measures come amid continued uncertainty over the ceasefire and ongoing tensions in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: In Bulgaria, passenger bus runs into group of Ukrainians, leaving several dead and injured
stories.summary: Near the Bulgarian-Turkish border, two Ukrainian citizens were killed and 16 others injured when their passenger bus rolled backward and crashed into a group of people standing behind it.

stories.title: What if China Succeeds?
stories.summary: An analysis poses the question of what global consequences could follow if China achieves its strategic ambitions. The piece argues that Beijing's success could have negative implications for other nations.

stories.title: Washington’s ‘psyop’ propaganda push could backfire, analysts say
stories.summary: A reported U.S. plan to have embassies collaborate with the military's psychological operations department to boost America's global image has drawn criticism from analysts who warn it could damage U.S. credibility and amount to propaganda.

stories.title: A year on, India has failed to substantiate allegations against Pakistan over Pahalgam attack: info minister
stories.summary: Pakistan's Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said India has failed to provide evidence linking Pakistan to the April 2025 Pahalgam attack, which killed 26 people, mostly tourists. Tarar made the remarks on the incident's first anniversary, calling India's allegations unsubstantiated.

stories.title: Houthis signal return, warn of broader regional escalation
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi movement warned it will not remain neutral in the broader Middle East conflict. The group signaled preparations to expand operations across the Red Sea, Arabian Sea, and Indian Ocean.

stories.title: Russian propaganda hailed Polish POW as defector — now Russia jails him for 13 years
stories.summary: Russia sentenced 47-year-old Polish citizen Krzysztof Flaczek to 13 years in prison for fighting on behalf of Ukraine. Russian state media had previously promoted Flaczek as a voluntary defector, but that propaganda narrative was quietly removed after his conviction.

stories.title: Nearly 8,000 migrants dead or missing in 2025
stories.summary: Nearly 8,000 people died or went missing on migration routes in 2025, according to the United Nations, underscoring the deadly risks faced by those seeking safety or opportunity.

stories.title: Slovakia held EU sanctions on Russia hostage to Druzhba pipeline. Ukraine just turned the tap back on
stories.summary: Slovakia had blocked EU sanctions on Russia over disruptions to the Druzhba oil pipeline running through Ukraine. After Ukraine resumed pipeline operations, Slovak Foreign Minister Blanár confirmed Bratislava would no longer obstruct the 20th EU sanctions package against Russia.

stories.title: Iran war drives up costs for Africa's airlines
stories.summary: The ongoing Iran war is driving up jet fuel prices, significantly increasing costs for African airlines. Carriers across the continent are raising ticket prices, canceling flights, and restructuring operations to remain financially viable.

stories.title: Iran war fuels crisis for Africa's aviation sector
stories.summary: The ongoing war in Iran is driving up jet fuel prices, forcing African airlines to raise ticket costs, cancel flights, and restructure operations to remain financially viable.

stories.title: EU plans to cut electricity taxes to shield households from Iran war energy crisis
stories.summary: The European Commission announced plans to cut electricity taxes and relax state aid rules to help households cope with the energy crisis caused by the Iran war. The measures aim to incentivize consumers to switch away from fuel-burning cars and boilers while reducing electricity bills.

stories.title: Over 2,100 abducted children returned to Ukraine since launch of Bring Kids Back UA, says Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky announced that over 2,100 Ukrainian children abducted by Russia have been returned since the launch of the Bring Kids Back UA initiative, including 150 returned since the beginning of this year.

stories.title: Iran: 'Going back to war is not in anyone's interest,' risk analyst says
stories.summary: A risk analyst speaking to FRANCE 24 said that resuming full-scale war between the US and Iran is not in anyone's interest, even as the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed during the ceasefire. The economic impasse continues despite the largely holding ceasefire.

stories.title: Iran hangs man convicted of links to Israel's Mossad
stories.summary: Iran executed Mehdi Farid, who was convicted of extensive cooperation with Israel's Mossad intelligence agency. The judiciary's Mizan Online website confirmed the hanging took place after a final verdict was approved.

stories.title: China names 2 Pakistani astronauts chosen to train for Tiangong space station mission
stories.summary: China named Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud as the two Pakistani astronauts selected to train for a mission to the Tiangong space station. One will become the first foreign astronaut to enter the station.

stories.title: Deadly Israeli settler attack on school kills two in Ramallah
stories.summary: Two people were killed when Israeli settlers opened fire on a school near Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, according to reports from the area.

stories.title: When the map turns red: Inside the lives upended by Israel’s expulsion orders
stories.summary: Israeli forces have been issuing expulsion orders to residents in southern Lebanon, forcing people from their homes. Evacuees have reported watching Israeli strikes subsequently destroy their properties.

stories.title: Russia to block Kazakh oil flows to Germany via key pipeline
stories.summary: Germany confirmed that Russia will block flows of Kazakh oil through a key pipeline to a German refinery starting May 1. The refinery supplies a significant portion of Berlin's energy needs.

stories.title: Russia to block Kazakh oil flows on key pipeline supplying Berlin
stories.summary: Germany confirmed that Russia will block flows of Kazakh oil through a key pipeline to a Berlin-area refinery beginning May 1, threatening a vital energy supply for the German capital.

stories.title: Russia and Libya vow to strengthen bilateral cooperation
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov met with Libya's acting foreign minister Taher Al-Baour in Moscow and pledged Russia's readiness to assist Libya in restoring unity and national reconciliation.

stories.title: Europe readies response to second energy crisis in four years
stories.summary: The European Union is preparing its response to a second energy crisis in four years, triggered by the Iran war's disruption of oil supplies. Draft proposals indicate EU officials plan to avoid major market interventions for now.

stories.title: Iran calls US ship seizure ‘piracy’: Is it?
stories.summary: Since the onset of the war on Iran, the United States has been seizing Iranian ships in international waters. Iran has characterized these actions as piracy, sparking debate over international maritime law.

stories.title: Tiny Pacific nations face tough choices on food, fuel posed by Iran war
stories.summary: Small Pacific island nations are struggling with a global fuel crisis caused by the disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz due to the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran. Prices for diesel, petrol, and kerosene have risen by as much as 70 percent in Papua New Guinea, affecting food costs and healthcare access.

stories.title: Oil prices rise despite ceasefire extension
stories.summary: Oil prices edged higher despite the extension of the US-Iran ceasefire, while European stock markets eased. Investors remain uncertain about the prospects for resumed peace talks, though both sides are broadly expected to seek an end to the conflict.

stories.title: Lebanon: Hezbollah responds to Israeli violations ahead of talks
stories.summary: One person was killed in an Israeli drone strike in eastern Lebanon as ceasefire violations increased. The incidents occurred ahead of rare Lebanon-Israel direct talks scheduled in Washington.

stories.title: Tough penalties planned to stop unapproved fire system shutdowns in Hong Kong
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities proposed new offenses with tougher penalties for fire installation contractors who deactivate firefighting systems without approval or fail to report malfunctions within 24 hours, following the city's deadliest fire in decades.

stories.title: China’s low-cost EVs to be fitted with lidar systems, usually reserved for luxury models
stories.summary: Chinese EV makers may introduce lidar-equipped intelligent driving systems in models priced as low as 60,000 yuan this year, according to tech firm Robosense. The development reflects intensifying competition and falling component costs in China's electric vehicle market.

stories.title: How China’s patient diplomacy can help secure peace in Iran
stories.summary: Abu Dhabi's crown prince and Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez discussed the Iran crisis with President Xi Jinping during separate Beijing visits. Xi also reiterated China's support for an immediate ceasefire in a call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.

stories.title: How China stands to gain from the US-Israel war on Iran
stories.summary: China has leveraged the US-Israeli war on Iran to advance its national interests and promote a multipolar world order. Beijing has positioned itself to assert greater influence as a global power during the conflict.

stories.title: UK Starmer says unaware of security lapse in Mandelson security vetting
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faced parliamentary questions over his appointment of Peter Mandelson as Britain's ambassador to Washington, amid security vetting concerns. Former top civil servant Olly Robbins testified there was an "atmosphere of pressure" from Downing Street to approve the appointment.

stories.title: Warning over Taiwan? PLA warships make rare transits off southwest Japan
stories.summary: Chinese PLA warships made two rare transits through international waterways near southwestern Japan this week, passing through the Yokoate Channel and the Yonaguni-Iriomote Waterway. The Eastern Theatre Command's 133rd Fleet conducted exercises in the western Pacific, with the movements widely interpreted as a warning to Tokyo over its stance on Taiwan.

stories.title: EU resumes aid to Ethiopia suspended over Tigray war
stories.summary: The European Union announced it will resume budgetary aid to Ethiopia, which had been suspended since December 2020 following the outbreak of civil war in the Tigray region. The conflict between Ethiopian government forces and Tigrayan rebels lasted two years and claimed approximately 600,000 lives.

stories.title: Nigeria faces jet fuel shortage as Strait of Hormuz disruption bites
stories.summary: Nigeria is experiencing a jet fuel shortage driven by disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz that have curtailed global supplies of middle distillates. The Major Energies Marketers Association of Nigeria said reduced availability of jet fuel and diesel passing through the waterway is pushing up prices and squeezing airlines.

stories.title: Italy Summons Russian Ambassador After Solovyov Insults Meloni
stories.summary: Italy summoned the Russian ambassador after state TV presenter Vladimir Solovyov directed a series of insults at Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, calling her derogatory names on air.

stories.title: Trump says US caught Chinese ‘gift’ for Iran, testing red line
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump claimed the United States intercepted a Chinese "gift" intended for Iran, testing a stated red line. The development is notable as Beijing generally avoids supplying weapons to overseas conflicts or openly violating U.S. sanctions.

stories.title: Cheri Cherin: Figure of the Congolese popular art movement honoured in Paris
stories.summary: A tribute exhibition in Paris honors Congolese painter Chéri Chérin, who passed away a few months ago. He was a leading figure in the Congolese popular art movement, known for socially engaged work that brought the genre to international audiences.

stories.title: Seven Palestinians killed as Israel continues attacks in Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed seven Palestinians in continued attacks in Gaza, disregarding the October ceasefire with Hamas. More than 3,000 Palestinians have been killed or injured since the ceasefire was declared.

stories.title: US blocks Iraq’s dollar shipments to squeeze Iran-backed militias, WSJ reports
stories.summary: The United States has blocked Iraq's dollar shipments in an effort to squeeze Iran-backed militias operating in the country, according to the Wall Street Journal. Washington is pressing Baghdad to dismantle Iranian-backed armed groups within its borders.

stories.title: Nepal minister quits amid financial scrutiny after just weeks in office
stories.summary: Nepal's Home Minister Sudan Gurung resigned on Wednesday amid scrutiny of his finances, less than a month after taking office on an anti-corruption platform. The 38-year-old, a prominent figure in the Gen-Z protests that toppled Nepal's previous government last September, said he stepped down to ensure a fair investigation.

stories.title: Syrskyi visits Pokrovsk sector and decides to reinforce units
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi visited the Pokrovsk sector, where 688 Russian attacks have been recorded since early April. After consulting with field commanders, Syrskyi decided to reinforce Ukrainian units in the area.

stories.title: EU unblocks €90 billion loan to Ukraine
stories.summary: EU member state envoys have unblocked a €90 billion loan to Ukraine that had been stalled by Hungary. They also approved a 20th package of sanctions against Russia over its invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: Gaza’s yellow line creeps forward as Israeli forces expand zone of control
stories.summary: Israeli forces have been gradually moving the agreed "yellow line" truce boundary in Gaza westward over six months since the ceasefire, expanding their zone of control. Palestinians report waking to find the line has shifted overnight, placing them in free-fire zones as ceasefire negotiations remain stalled.

stories.title: Tehran defiant as US–Iran talks remain in deadlock over Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran accused President Trump of using the ceasefire extension as a time-buying maneuver as US-Iran talks remained deadlocked over the Strait of Hormuz. Fears are growing that the pause may be a brief lull before renewed confrontations.

stories.title: “We will use all available methods” — Shoigu threatened Moldova over Transnistria. Available methods are limited: Ukraine is in the way
stories.summary: Russian Security Council Secretary Nikolai Shoigu threatened Moldova over the breakaway region of Transnistria, invoking the Donbas precedent and citing 220,000 Russian passport holders. Analysts note Russia's ability to act is constrained by Ukraine's geographic position between Russia and Moldova.

stories.title: Germany unveils strategy for becoming Europe’s strongest military by 2039
stories.summary: Germany has announced a new defense strategy aimed at making the Bundeswehr Europe's most capable military force by 2039. The plan shifts away from fixed hardware quotas for tanks, aircraft, and ships, adopting instead a flexible, effects-based planning model.

stories.title: Africa: Extreme Heat Pushing Global Food Systems to the Brink, UN Agencies Warn
stories.summary: A new UN report warns that extreme heat and increasingly frequent heatwaves are pushing global food and farming systems to the brink, threatening the livelihoods of over a billion people worldwide.

stories.title: Africa: The Ballot Box Illusion - How Authoritarians Repackaged the African Ballot
stories.summary: A report by CIVICUS documents how authoritarian leaders across multiple African countries have used elections as procedural ceremonies of democracy while maintaining firm control over power structures.

stories.title: Is Trump’s indefinite ceasefire with Iran the prelude to peace?
stories.summary: An analysis examines whether President Trump's indefinite ceasefire extension with Iran could lead to lasting peace. Observers note that in a frozen conflict scenario, both sides may frame compromises as victories.

stories.title: Israel risks Council of Europe suspension over death penalty law
stories.summary: Israel faces potential suspension from the Council of Europe's parliamentary assembly after passing a law imposing the death penalty on Palestinian detainees. The legislation has drawn sharp international criticism.

stories.title: Iran seizes two ships as UK pushes for Hormuz reopening
stories.summary: Iran seized two ships and fired on at least one other vessel in the Strait of Hormuz following U.S. President Trump's announcement that the ceasefire would be extended. The UK is pushing for the reopening of the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Ships targeted in Hormuz as UK pushes for strait's reopening
stories.summary: At least three vessels came under fire in the Strait of Hormuz following President Trump's announcement of a ceasefire extension. The United Kingdom is pushing for the strategic waterway's reopening.

stories.title: Ukrainian Defense Forces strike command post for Russian Black Sea Fleet warships in Sevastopol
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces struck the Striletsky command post of the Russian Black Sea Fleet in the occupied city of Sevastopol.

stories.title: EU gives preliminary approval to unblock €90 billion Ukraine loan
stories.summary: EU member states gave preliminary approval on Wednesday to unlock a €90 billion loan for Ukraine. The decision followed delays caused by a dispute with Hungary over oil flows through the Druzhba pipeline.

stories.title: Iranian economy: Layoffs, inflation add to sanctions pain amid war
stories.summary: The ongoing conflict involving the US and Israel has deepened Iran's economic crisis, with internet blackouts, soaring inflation, and rising layoffs compounding existing sanctions pressure. Uncertainty has gripped Iran's workforce as the war continues.

stories.title: In south Lebanon village, Hezbollah buries fighters killed in war with Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah held a mass funeral in the south Lebanon village of Kfar Sir on Tuesday for more than a dozen fighters killed during over six weeks of war with Israel. The ceremony took place days after a 10-day US-brokered ceasefire was announced by President Trump.

stories.title: Ukraine to restart oil flows via Druzhba pipeline, potentially unblocking EU's loan
stories.summary: Ukraine resumed pumping oil through the Druzhba pipeline on Wednesday after President Zelenskiy said repairs following a Russian attack on a pumping facility were complete. The resumption was key to persuading Hungary and Slovakia to lift their EU veto on a €90 billion loan to Ukraine.

stories.title: Estonian Holocaust memorial 'extensively damaged' by vandalism
stories.summary: The Ereda Holocaust memorial in Estonia's Ida-Viru County was extensively damaged by vandalism. Police reported the monument was dented, several pieces were broken off, and its fastenings were bent.

stories.title: Ukraine says Russian oil to Hungary, Slovakia has restarted
stories.summary: Energy companies in Ukraine and Hungary confirmed that oil flows through the Druzhba pipeline from Russia via Belarus have resumed. Hungary and Slovakia expect the first deliveries to arrive by Thursday.

stories.title: Devastated Gaza will need over $70 billion to rebuild, international report warns
stories.summary: A joint report by the United Nations, the European Union, and the World Bank estimates that rebuilding Gaza will require more than $70 billion over the next decade. The assessment follows over two years of conflict between Israel and Hamas, which began after Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack.

stories.title: Victor Wembanyama sustains concussion in Spurs' Game 2 loss
stories.summary: San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama sustained a concussion during Game 2 of the team's first-round NBA playoff series against the Portland Trail Blazers. He hit his face on the court after being knocked down while driving to the basket in the second quarter and left for the locker room.

stories.title: Starmer and Badenoch clash over Olly Robbins’ Mandelson evidence – UK politics live
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and opposition leader clashed in parliament over testimony by former official Olly Robbins. UK inflation rose to 3.3% in March after the Iran war triggered the largest fuel price increase in over three years. The Liberal Democrats blamed the cost-of-living pressures partly on what they termed "Trumpflation."

stories.title: Ukraine asks Turkey to host Zelenskiy-Putin peace talks amid stalled negotiations
stories.summary: Ukraine proposed Turkey as a neutral venue for peace talks between Presidents Zelenskiy and Putin. The proposal aims to restart stalled negotiations while avoiding meetings in Belarus or Russia.

stories.title: Five major issues affecting the FIFA World Cup with 50 days to go
stories.summary: With 50 days until the FIFA World Cup, organizers face multiple challenges including the impact of the U.S.-Israel war on Iran, high ticket prices, and security concerns related to violence in host nations.

stories.title: Israeli settlers set Palestinian home on fire in occupied West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli settlers set a Palestinian home on fire in the occupied West Bank, according to reports. No further details on casualties were immediately provided.

stories.title: Venezuela: 'Repressive apparatus remains in place,' says Amnesty International
stories.summary: Amnesty International warned that Venezuela's state repressive apparatus "remains intact" following the overthrow of Nicolás Maduro. The human rights organization cautioned that the structures of repression have not been dismantled despite the change in leadership.

stories.title: EU provisionally approves €90bn Ukraine loan as Hungary drops opposition after Druzhba pipeline reopens – Europe live
stories.summary: The EU provisionally approved a €90 billion loan to Ukraine after Hungary dropped its opposition following the reopening of the Druzhba oil pipeline. Formal procedures were expected to conclude on Thursday. Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico also criticized Hungary's incoming government led by Péter Magyar.

stories.title: Drugs and fraudulent call centers: Police foil Khimprom criminal group, operating in Ukraine and EU
stories.summary: Ukrainian police dismantled the Khimprom criminal group, which operated across Ukraine and the EU and was involved in fraudulent call centers, the U420 project, and illegal narcotics trafficking.

stories.title: Lebanon's direct talks with Israel will lead to strife not peace
stories.summary: Lebanon has entered direct talks with Israel, raising concerns among analysts that the US-sponsored negotiations could deepen internal divisions. Critics warn the talks risk fomenting domestic conflict rather than achieving lasting peace or ending Israeli occupation.

stories.title: Woman and Child Killed in Ukrainian Drone Strike on Samara Region
stories.summary: A woman and a child were killed in a Ukrainian drone strike on the city of Syzran in Russia's Samara Region. Ukraine had previously targeted an oil refinery in the same city.

stories.title: Pope Leo to visit prison in Equatorial Guinea on final leg of Africa tour
stories.summary: Pope Leo is scheduled to visit a prison in Equatorial Guinea on the final leg of his Africa tour. He will also pay tribute to victims of a deadly accident that struck the city of Bata in 2021.

stories.title: Settler arson attack reportedly wounds 8 Palestinians, including baby; police launch probe
stories.summary: Eight Palestinians, including a baby, were reportedly wounded in an arson attack by Israeli settlers in a village near Nablus in the West Bank. The IDF said troops arrived but found no suspects, as Israeli police launched an investigation.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Iran doesn’t want the Strait of Hormuz closed, says Trump
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump announced a ceasefire extension in the Iran-Israel conflict and stated that Iran does not want the Strait of Hormuz closed. Iran had not yet responded to the ceasefire announcement at the time of reporting.

stories.title: Rabbi who bulldozed Palestinian homes selected for Israel's national celebration
stories.summary: An extremist rabbi accused of involvement in demolishing Palestinian homes was selected to participate in Israel's Independence Day celebrations. Separately, reports examined LGBTQ laws in Hungary and Russia, and allegations of manipulation at a French meteorological station linked to insider betting on the Polymarket platform.

stories.title: Kyrie Irving changes Instagram photo to show solidarity with Palestine
stories.summary: NBA player Kyrie Irving changed his Instagram profile photo to an image of a Palestinian child being blocked from school by Israeli soldiers in the occupied West Bank, signaling solidarity with Palestinians.

stories.title: EU approves €90bn loan for Ukraine as pipeline is turned on ending deadlock
stories.summary: The European Union approved a €90 billion loan for Ukraine. Separately, Ukraine announced it had reopened the Druzhba oil pipeline after months of deadlock over stalled crude supplies to Hungary.

stories.title: US, Iran peace talks uncertain with Vance trip scrapped
stories.summary: Planned U.S.-Iran peace talks have been thrown into uncertainty after Vice President Vance's trip was scrapped. Iran informed the United States through Pakistan that it would not attend negotiations that had been scheduled for April 22.

stories.title: Iran seizes two vessels for 'maritime violations', says media
stories.summary: Iran's IRGC navy seized two vessels, identified as the MSC Francesca and the Epaminodes, for alleged maritime violations. The ships were detained for operating without authorization and manipulating navigation systems, then transferred to Iranian shores.

stories.title: Virginia congressional map vote could embolden Florida Republicans to push for boundary changes, says Jeffries – US politics live
stories.summary: A Virginia congressional redistricting vote could embolden Florida Republicans to pursue their own boundary changes, according to House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries. Jeffries warned that the result should serve as a caution to Governor Ron DeSantis. Separately, California held its first major gubernatorial debate featuring six candidates after frontrunner Eric Swalwell exited the race.

stories.title: Bringing babies into the world in Lebanon’s crammed shelters
stories.summary: Displaced Lebanese mothers are giving birth and raising newborns in cramped shelters near Beirut amid the Israel-Hezbollah war. One mother, Mariam Zein, described her distress at being unable to enjoy her first child's early weeks in normal conditions.

stories.title: Russian agent linked to Medvedchuk's project detained in Odesa over SOF officer murder plot
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service detained a Russian FSB agent in Odesa who was allegedly plotting the assassination of a Special Operations Forces commander. The suspect was linked to a project associated with Viktor Medvedchuk.

stories.title: Does William Lai’s cancelled eSwatini trip show Beijing’s reach in Africa?
stories.summary: Three African countries denied overflight clearance for Taiwanese President William Lai Ching-te's planned trip to eSwatini, forcing its cancellation. Beijing praised the decision, as the visit was intended to mark the 40th anniversary of King Mswati's accession. ESwatini remains the only African country with diplomatic ties to Taiwan.

stories.title: Liberia: War Crimes Court Body Accuses Senior Liberian Officials of Blocking Progress
stories.summary: The body responsible for establishing Liberia's War and Economic Crimes Court accused senior government officials of deliberately obstructing its progress. It named the justice minister, the president's legal advisor, and the national security advisor as key obstacles to the court's creation.

stories.title: Stern warning: one man’s mission to clear the rotting boats poisoning Cornwall’s creeks
stories.summary: A man in Cornwall named Steve Green is working to remove derelict boats from the county's waterways using a modified VW campervan equipped with a crane and winch. Abandoned vessels left to decay release fibreglass shards that harm marine life. Green's mission targets rotting boats polluting Cornwall's creeks and estuaries.

stories.title: China to fuse software and steel with US$14tr sector to fix weak links in world’s factory
stories.summary: China's State Council unveiled a plan to modernize its service sector and integrate it with advanced manufacturing, targeting a valuation of 100 trillion yuan (US$14.7 trillion) by 2030. The initiative aims to strengthen weak links in China's industrial supply chain by fusing software capabilities with traditional manufacturing.

stories.title: Iran's workers face waves of layoffs as war batters domestic economy
stories.summary: Iranian workers face mass layoffs and soaring inflation as the ongoing war damages domestic infrastructure and causes internet blackouts. The economic deterioration comes amid continued conflict, severely impacting Iran's labor market and daily life for ordinary citizens.

stories.title: Why is India’s Manipur burning for three years?
stories.summary: India's northeastern state of Manipur has experienced three years of ethnic clashes and remains on edge. There are growing fears that the ongoing conflict could escalate further.

stories.title: Drone strikes hit Iranian Kurdish rebels in Iraq, says exiled group
stories.summary: Drone strikes in Iraq's northern Kurdistan region wounded three Iranian Kurdish fighters belonging to the Kurdistan Freedom Party. The exiled opposition group blamed Tehran for launching four drones against its bases in the autonomous region.

stories.title: Chile closes ranks on Strait of Magellan sovereignty a week after Argentine admiral's remarks
stories.summary: Chile consolidated a unified stance defending its sovereignty over the Strait of Magellan, one week after remarks by Argentine Rear Admiral Hernán Montero about the waterway's eastern mouth went viral. Internal Chilean debate shifted toward how the executive branch handled its communications response to the Argentine admiral's comments.

stories.title: Libya, UAE fuelled Sudan war with Colombian mercenaries, reports find
stories.summary: Newly released reports indicate that Libya and the UAE facilitated the deployment of Colombian mercenaries to support Sudan's paramilitary Rapid Support Forces in their fight against the Sudanese army, as the civil war enters its fourth year.

stories.title: Ukraine Repairs Druzhba Pipeline, Clearing Way for Russian Oil Flows to Europe
stories.summary: Ukraine completed repairs to the Druzhba pipeline, which carries Russian crude oil to Hungary and Slovakia, ending a monthslong diplomatic standoff that had disrupted energy supplies to the two EU members.

stories.title: Searchers find body of 1 of 6 missing crew members after super typhoon overturns ship
stories.summary: Searchers recovered the body of one of six missing crew members from a cargo ship that overturned near the Northern Mariana Islands during a super typhoon. U.S. Air Force divers used an underwater remotely operated drone to locate the remains, and Japan Coast Guard divers conducted additional searches.

stories.title: Iran says it has seized two ships in Strait of Hormuz after vessels attacked
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps seized two ships in the Strait of Hormuz. A British maritime agency reported that one of the cargo vessels was heavily damaged by Iranian forces during the incident.

stories.title: Death sentences soar in DR Congo after moratorium lifted, report warns
stories.summary: A campaign group warned that death sentences in the Democratic Republic of Congo have surged since the government lifted a de facto moratorium on executions in 2024.

stories.title: President Herzog honors 120 outstanding soldiers in pre-recorded Independence Day ceremony
stories.summary: Israel's President Herzog honored 120 outstanding soldiers in a pre-recorded Independence Day ceremony. The event was pre-recorded due to the ongoing ceasefire and broader security situation, with attendance limited to soldiers' families.

stories.title: Is China a winner of the Iran war or facing economic risks?
stories.summary: China's economy has outperformed expectations despite disruptions caused by the Iran war, though analysts warn that weak domestic demand and structural risks continue to pose challenges.

stories.title: Russia’s Central Bank scolded live on TV—Iran war oil keeps funding the war anyway
stories.summary: Russia's Central Bank faced public criticism on live television, while intelligence assessments indicate that oil revenues—bolstered by Iranian war-related pricing—continue to fund Russia's war effort. Moscow is reportedly concealing the extent of economic damage from the conflict.

stories.title: The Russian economy is faltering. Oil windfalls are keeping Putin’s war alive
stories.summary: Intelligence agencies report that Russia is concealing the extent of economic damage caused by the war, while oil revenues continue to fund Moscow's military operations in Ukraine.

stories.title: Explosions heard in Sevastopol; strikes reported
stories.summary: Explosions were reported overnight and into the morning of April 22 in Russian-occupied Sevastopol. Two strikes were confirmed near Cape Fiolent, where an anti-aircraft missile regiment is based, and on Monastyrske Highway, the site of a Black Sea Fleet electronic intelligence unit.

stories.title: How QuitGPT is challenging AI use in modern warfare
stories.summary: The QuitGPT campaign has grown significantly since January, with 700,000 users pledging to cancel AI subscriptions. The movement is driven by concerns over the use of artificial intelligence in modern warfare.

stories.title: Somalia: Somali Opposition Rejects Any Term Extension for President
stories.summary: Opposition groups in Mogadishu issued a warning against any extension of President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's federal government mandate. The statement followed a series of meetings between the president and clans considered close to his administration.

stories.title: KP’s Maneri residents without water for four days as power cut off
stories.summary: Residents of the Maneri region in Swabi district, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, have been without water for five days after the Peshawar Electric Supply Company cut power to water supply pumps over Rs1.4 million in unpaid dues owed by the Tehsil Municipal Administration.

stories.title: Iran fires on 3 ships in Strait of Hormuz after Trump extends ceasefire
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired on three ships in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, shortly after President Trump announced an indefinite extension of the U.S.-Iran ceasefire. The attacks threatened global energy supplies and complicated diplomatic efforts to arrange talks between Washington and Tehran.

stories.title: Vedomosti reports Russian mobile carriers ask for more time to set up VPN traffic billing systems
stories.summary: Several Russian mobile carriers have told the Digital Development Ministry they will not be ready by the May 1 deadline to implement extra charges for VPN traffic on their networks, the business daily Vedomosti reported.

stories.title: Trump says Iran ‘collapsing’ over Hormuz blockade, as ships attacked in key waterway
stories.summary: President Trump claimed Iran is "collapsing" under the Strait of Hormuz blockade as ships were attacked in the waterway. Iran denied the blockade's effectiveness, while Trump extended the ceasefire indefinitely. Tehran also executed a man accused of working with Mossad.

stories.title: Moscow’s offensive has lost ground since it started — yet Russia’s top brass declared Luhansk Oblast fully seized for the fourth time
stories.summary: Russian Chief of General Staff Gerasimov claimed Russian forces seized 1,700 square kilometers in 2026 and control 70% of Lyman in Luhansk Oblast. However, the Institute for the Study of War found actual gains were roughly one-fifth of that figure, with no control over the city and territorial losses since March 1.

stories.title: Malawi: 'I Also Failed to Find Fuel in Zomba' - Govt Spokesperson Namalomba's Personal Ordeal Mirrors a Nation Running On Dry
stories.summary: Malawi's Information Minister Shadric Namalomba publicly acknowledged he was unable to find fuel in Zomba over the weekend. His admission highlighted the severity of a nationwide fuel crisis affecting both ordinary citizens and government officials.

stories.title: Nato 'will always defend' Turkey, says chief
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte stated the alliance would defend all members, including Turkey, after intercepting four missiles fired from Iran into Turkish airspace in recent weeks. Turkey, which borders Iran, had largely been spared direct Iranian retaliation before the ceasefire.

stories.title: Malawi: Court Order Ignored? Pregnant Rape Survivors Still Blocked From Safe Abortion Services Despite Landmark Ruling
stories.summary: Stakeholders in Malawi report that pregnant rape survivors continue to face barriers accessing safe abortion services despite a court ruling meant to guarantee those rights. Sexual and reproductive health services remain difficult to obtain for assault survivors.

stories.title: Baltic states ask Ukraine to help reduce tensions over Russian threats, says Sybiha
stories.summary: Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the Baltic states—Latvia, Lithuania, and Estonia—have asked Ukraine for help reducing tensions related to Russian information attacks and accusations about Ukrainian drone airspace access.

stories.title: One month phone-free: Young Americans try digital detox
stories.summary: A program encouraging young Americans to go phone-free for one month is gaining attention as a digital detox experiment. Participants reported the experience became increasingly liberating as the month progressed.

stories.title: Tui cuts profit forecast as effects of Iran war cost travel group €40m
stories.summary: Travel company Tui cut its profit forecast after the Iran war cost it approximately €40 million, including repatriating nearly 12,000 guests and staff. Evacuations included passengers from two cruise ships docked in Abu Dhabi and Doha. The losses were booked in March due to the Middle East conflict's impact on operations.

stories.title: The Devil Wears Prada 2 criticised for offending China with nerdy ‘Chin Chou’ character
stories.summary: The Hollywood sequel The Devil Wears Prada 2 faced accusations of racism in China over an Asian character named "Jin Chao," which many viewers said sounded similar to the derogatory slur "Ching Chong." The controversy erupted after a clip featuring the character was shared by a Chinese influencer.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone strike hits residential building in Russia, injuring 11
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone struck a four-story residential building in Syzran, Samara Region, in the early hours of April 22, destroying one entrance and injuring 11 people, according to Russia's Emergency Situations Ministry.

stories.title: Nearly half of US children are breathing dangerous levels of air pollution, report warns
stories.summary: An American Lung Association report found that nearly half of US children are exposed to dangerous levels of air pollution, including ground-level ozone and particle pollution. Experts warned that the Trump administration's rollback of environmental protections at the EPA will worsen conditions. The report is the organization's 27th annual air quality assessment.

stories.title: Confusion over government agencies’ roles in fire oversight, Tai Po probe reveals
stories.summary: A public inquiry into Hong Kong's deadliest fire in decades revealed confusion among government departments over responsibility for supervising large-scale renovation projects. A Fire Services Department assistant director said his agency lacked expertise in construction and was not responsible for handling complaints about flammable building materials.

stories.title: Daily Briefing April 22: Trump’s muddled messaging complicates talks with Iran
stories.summary: US bureau chief Jacob Magid reported on complications in US-Iran ceasefire talks caused by mixed messaging from the Trump administration. The briefing also covered a second round of Lebanon-Israel talks, stalled Hamas disarmament, and a settler attack that killed two Palestinians.

stories.title: Displaced Palestinians return to books as Gaza's Phoenix library rises from the rubble
stories.summary: Displaced Palestinians in Gaza opened the Phoenix Library in the Rimal neighbourhood, a youth-led initiative to revive cultural life during the war. Founder Omar Hamad and volunteers retrieved and cleaned books from rubble. The library includes literary, scientific, and children's sections.

stories.title: Video: Israeli soldier shares footage of burning village in Lebanon
stories.summary: A video reportedly shared by an Israeli soldier circulated online showing a tank driving through a village in southern Lebanon with buildings visibly burning. Middle East Eye reported it could not independently verify the exact location or timing of the footage.

stories.title: Russian, Libyan foreign ministers hold talks in Moscow
stories.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov held talks with Libya's acting foreign minister, Taher Al-Baour, in Moscow. Lavrov stated that Russia is ready to help Libya restore unity and achieve national reconciliation.

stories.title: Trump extends ceasefire, says giving Iran time to negotiate
stories.summary: President Donald Trump indefinitely extended the US ceasefire with Iran, citing a request from mediator Pakistan and the need to give Tehran's leadership time to formulate a proposal. However, Trump said the US naval blockade of Iran's ports would continue. Tehran had not publicly responded to the extension as of early Wednesday.

stories.title: Trump extends ceasefire with Iran, says Tehran regime 'seriously fractured'
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump extended a ceasefire with Iran, claiming Tehran was "collapsing financially" due to the Strait of Hormuz blockade. Iran did not publicly respond to the extension. An Iranian gunboat fired on a container ship off the coast of Oman, causing damage but no casualties, according to a British maritime security agency.

stories.title: IRGC seizes two ships, transfers them to Iranian shores
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards seized the MSC Francesca and Epaminodes for operating without authorization and manipulating navigation systems. Both vessels were transferred to Iranian shores.

stories.title: Khartoum slowly comes back to life, one year after recapture by military
stories.summary: One year after the Sudanese army recaptured Khartoum, the capital's center remains largely quiet and heavily damaged as the country's civil war continues into its third year.

stories.title: Russians strike agricultural enterprise in Velykyi Burluk, Kharkiv region
stories.summary: Russian forces struck an agricultural enterprise in the village of Velykyi Burluk in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, causing a fire at the facility.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz blockade drives up costs at Panama Canal
stories.summary: The Strait of Hormuz blockade resulting from the Iran war has driven up costs at the Panama Canal. One vessel reportedly paid US$4 million to skip the queue and avoid waiting up to five days for transit.

stories.title: Will Iran war reshape global trade more than COVID?
stories.summary: Trade experts are assessing whether the Iran conflict could reshape global supply chains more significantly than the COVID-19 pandemic. Companies are already adjusting strategies to mitigate revenue risks from the geopolitical disruption.

stories.title: Cargo ship leaving Iran 'fired upon and is now stopped in the water'
stories.summary: One person was killed and two others injured in an Israeli drone strike in Lebanon's western Bekaa Valley. Villages south of the Litani River saw renewed displacement toward Sidon and Beirut due to destruction and lack of basic services.

stories.title: French activists sue ‘deceptive’ laughing gas suppliers
stories.summary: The Antoine Alleno Association, a French road safety group, filed a lawsuit against companies selling nitrous oxide under the Cream Deluxe brand, alleging deceptive marketing targeting young people. The group is led by Michelin-starred chef Yannick Alleno, whose son was killed by a speeding driver in 2022.

stories.title: Iran’s gunboat fires on container ship off Oman coast
stories.summary: An Iranian Revolutionary Guard Corps gunboat fired on a container ship off the coast of Oman. The IRGC stated the action was in response to what it described as a US seizure of an Iranian commercial vessel.

stories.title: Trump declares Iran ceasefire extension with peace talks in doubt
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced an indefinite extension of the ceasefire with Iran on Tuesday, hours before the two-week truce was set to expire. It remained unclear whether Iran or Israel, the U.S. ally in the two-month war, would agree to the extension.

stories.title: Lesson interrupted
stories.summary: Pakistan's government shut down schools and shifted higher education online amid skyrocketing fuel prices triggered by the U.S.-Israel war on Iran. The disruption follows a pattern of repeated school closures affecting children's education across the country.

stories.title: SpaceX partners with AI start-up Cursor, may buy it for $76.4 billion
stories.summary: SpaceX has partnered with AI coding start-up Cursor and may acquire the company for $76.4 billion. The potential deal comes amid intensifying competition among AI firms seeking to become the preferred tool for software developers.

stories.title: Somalia: Ted Cruz Signals Trump May Recognize Somaliland
stories.summary: U.S. Senator Ted Cruz expressed confidence that President Donald Trump will formally recognize Somaliland before the end of his term. Cruz pointed to growing momentum in Washington for deeper engagement with the self-declared republic based in Hargeisa.

stories.title: Trumped again?
stories.summary: Pakistan mediated failed U.S.-Iran talks in Islamabad, but prospects for a second round remain uncertain. The U.S. seizure of an Iranian tanker during the process complicated diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: How China’s new AI carbon accounting model points the finger at the US
stories.summary: China's Shanghai Advanced Research Institute launched what it calls the world's first "panoramic" carbon accounting system. The model shifts emphasis toward consumer-based emissions responsibility, resulting in lower estimated emissions for China and higher estimates for the United States compared to other models.

stories.title: Russians attack railway facility in Zaporizhzhia; train engineer's assistant killed
stories.summary: A Russian drone attacked a marshaling yard at the Zaporizhzhia-Live railway station on the night of April 22, killing a train engineer's assistant in the strike on the railway facility.

stories.title: Hezbollah says attacked north Israel in response to Israeli truce violations
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced it attacked northern Israel in response to what it described as Israeli ceasefire violations, including attacks on Lebanese civilians and destruction of homes and villages.

stories.title: Trump extends Iran war ceasefire as Strait shutdown drags on
stories.summary: President Trump announced an indefinite extension of the U.S. ceasefire with Iran, citing a request from Pakistan, while the Strait of Hormuz remained disrupted. Trump downplayed reports about an intercepted ship allegedly carrying a "gift from China" to Tehran.

stories.title: Russia strikes Ukraine’s Odesa port, kills railway worker in Zaporizhia
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the port of Odesa and killed a railway worker in Zaporizhia, Ukraine. Ukraine's deputy prime minister condemned the attacks on civilian infrastructure.

stories.title: Israel attacks mosque in Lebanon in another ceasefire violation
stories.summary: Israeli forces attacked a mosque in Lebanon, which critics described as another violation of the existing ceasefire agreement between the two sides.

stories.title: Two more cases registered in  Italian boat capsize incident
stories.summary: Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency registered two additional cases related to a boat capsize tragedy off the Italian coast, bringing the total to seven. FIA offices in Gujrat and Sialkot are investigating human traffickers linked to at least 16 Pakistani victims.

stories.title: Punjab Assembly speaker ‘eats his words’ on agricultural income tax within 24 hours
stories.summary: The Punjab Assembly in Pakistan reversed its speaker's previous ruling and restored agricultural income tax notifications it had suspended just one day earlier. The House approved a motion to condone the delay in presenting the notifications.

stories.title: Iraq restricts Assad regime Syrian officers in Baghdad
stories.summary: Iraq's Defence Minister Thabet al-Abbasi acknowledged the presence of 130 Syrian military personnel from the former Assad regime in Baghdad. Iraqi authorities have moved to restrict the activities of these officers.

stories.title: Moment of truth
stories.summary: Islamabad was set to host a second round of U.S.-Iran talks, but Iranian participation remained uncertain due to the ongoing U.S. blockade of Iranian ports. No indications emerged that the American administration planned to ease the blockade to facilitate negotiations.

stories.title: Gaza’s unseen casualties: A surge in stillbirths and birth defects
stories.summary: Gaza has experienced a 140% rise in stillbirths and a doubling of congenital anomalies amid the ongoing war. Medical sources attribute the surge to the devastating humanitarian conditions in the territory.

stories.title: Assisting Jews worldwide this Independence Day
stories.summary: On Israel's Independence Day, Danyelle Neuman, Chief Development Officer of the Jewish Agency, discussed the organization's role in assisting Jewish communities worldwide during times of crisis.

stories.title: Gibraltar’s monkeys eat mud ‘to avoid upset stomachs from tourist junk food’
stories.summary: Researchers on Gibraltar observed that Barbary macaques living on the Rock have learned to eat soil, a behavior known as geophagy, apparently to settle their stomachs after consuming junk food from tourists. Soil consumption peaked during the holiday season and was highest among monkeys with the most tourist contact.

stories.title: UK firms to face tougher checks on export licences to bolster sanctions on Russia
stories.summary: The UK government announced plans to impose tougher export licence controls on British firms to prevent goods from reaching Russia via intermediary countries. Under the new measures, manufacturers will need licences to export to countries suspected of acting as staging posts for Russia-bound goods. The move aims to strengthen sanctions supporting Ukraine.

stories.title: Why Trump’s pick for Fed chair will not bring home the bank for the president
stories.summary: President Trump nominated Kevin Warsh to succeed Jerome Powell as chair of the Federal Reserve. However, analysts say Warsh faces significant challenges in persuading Fed board members to lower interest rates. Trump's desire to influence monetary policy is expected to meet institutional resistance at the central bank.

stories.title: Asia braces for food shortages as ‘super El Nino’, Iran war effects collide
stories.summary: Scientists warn that a potential "super El Niño" event combined with the Iran war's effects on energy and fertiliser costs could cause significant food shortages across Asia. India's Meteorological Department has forecast a below-average monsoon, while Australia's planting acreage has reportedly dropped to a seven-year low.

stories.title: 2,700 China-Japan flights axed in March as rift between Asian powers deepens
stories.summary: Nearly 2,700 flights between China and Japan were cancelled in March, bringing the cancellation rate to almost 50 percent amid deepening political tensions. Further cuts are expected during the upcoming Labour Day holiday period.

stories.title: War update: 231 combat clashes on frontline over past day, over 50 attacks in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Ukraine's defense forces recorded 231 combat engagements with Russian troops along the front line on April 21, with over 50 attacks concentrated in the Pokrovsk sector.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz tensions escalate ahead of Israel-Lebanon meet
stories.summary: Iranian forces seized two container ships and fired on a third in the Strait of Hormuz as tensions escalated. The incidents occurred ahead of Israeli-Lebanese talks in Washington, where Beirut planned to seek a ceasefire extension.

stories.title: Trump announces Iran ceasefire extension amid doubts over deal
stories.summary: President Trump announced an indefinite extension of the US-Iran ceasefire while peace talks remain uncertain. The US Navy blockade continues, and Iran has not confirmed its support for the extension.

stories.title: Biotech-led boom as 8 China firms flock to Hong Kong’s thriving stock market
stories.summary: Eight mainland Chinese companies, five of them in biotech, passed listing hearings on the Hong Kong stock exchange in April. The influx follows the China Securities Regulatory Commission's push for private firms to list in Hong Kong, with companies spanning AI-driven drug discovery, driverless technology, and industrial robotics.

stories.title: €1 bn from Madrid on the table — Spain’s defense chief opens her Kyiv visit
stories.summary: Spanish Defense Minister Margarita Robles opened her visit to Kyiv at the Wall of Memory and is set to receive the Order of Princess Olha from President Zelensky. Madrid has announced plans for €1 billion in military aid to Ukraine in 2026.

stories.title: As internal divisions simmer, Lebanese see echoes of last century’s civil war
stories.summary: Internal divisions in Lebanon are intensifying amid talks with Israel, with former civil war fighters warning the country is nearing a breaking point. Sectarian rifts are deepening between the government and Hezbollah over responsibility for Israeli strikes.

stories.title: Two cargo ships anchor at Gwadar Port
stories.summary: Two cargo ships docked at Pakistan's Gwadar Port, carrying 368.7 tons of machinery and general cargo and 5,000 metric tons of MOP fertiliser respectively. Port officials said the arrivals are contributing to increased economic activity at the facility.

stories.title: Trust Trump? Iran’s doubts shadow peace talks
stories.summary: An analysis examines deep Iranian skepticism toward U.S. trustworthiness as potential peace talks loom. Experts note that trust between Washington and Tehran, historically low, has reached its nadir amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Starmer says unaware of security lapse when appointing Mandelson
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer told parliament he was unaware that Peter Mandelson had been flagged by security checks before being appointed envoy to the United States. The statement followed testimony by fired senior foreign ministry official Olly Robbins, who said Starmer had a "dismissive attitude" toward security vetting.

stories.title: Air defense forces neutralize 189 out of 215 Russian drones since yesterday evening
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 189 of 215 Russian drones launched starting on the evening of April 21. The remaining drones were part of a large-scale aerial assault across Ukrainian territory.

stories.title: US halts dollar shipments to Iraq, freezes military aid over militia concerns
stories.summary: The United States halted $500 million in dollar shipments to Iraq and froze military cooperation programs, demanding Baghdad dismantle Iranian-backed militias following militia attacks against US interests.

stories.title: Iran war: Jet fuel crisis deepens as Lufthansa cuts flights
stories.summary: Lufthansa has canceled 20,000 flights due to jet fuel shortages caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz amid the Iran war. Experts warn of further cancellations and price increases across the aviation industry.

stories.title: Jet fuel crisis deepens as Lufthansa cuts 20,000 flights
stories.summary: Lufthansa canceled 20,000 flights due to jet fuel shortages caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Experts warn that further airline cancellations and price increases are likely as the supply disruption continues.

stories.title: US and Iran 'locked in war of words' says Lyse Doucet
stories.summary: The United States confirmed that Vice President's planned trip to Pakistan for a second round of US-Iran peace talks has been cancelled. The two sides remain locked in an escalating war of words over the Strait of Hormuz standoff.

stories.title: 'We cannot let Iran be our spokesperson': Lebanon charts own path in talks with Israel
stories.summary: Lebanon is seeking to chart an independent path in negotiations with Israel, separate from Iranian influence. Communications manager Jad Shahrour of the Samir Kassir Foundation emphasized the need for Lebanon to disentangle its decision-making from external actors while acknowledging deep historical tensions complicating stability.

stories.title: South Korean fighter jets collided due to pilots taking pictures, report finds
stories.summary: A South Korean military investigation found that two fighter jets collided because one of the pilots was taking photographs during flight. One pilot was fined thousands of dollars by the military to cover aircraft repair costs.

stories.title: EU envoys to weigh 20th Russia sanctions package alongside 90bn euro Ukraine loan
stories.summary: EU ambassadors are scheduled to meet on April 22 to approve a €90 billion loan for Ukraine and a 20th sanctions package against Russia. The measures still require consent from Hungary and Slovakia.

stories.title: Trump extends Iran ceasefire, yet blockade enforcement persists
stories.summary: President Trump announced an extension of a fragile ceasefire with Iran, citing a request from Pakistan and stating he awaits a "unified proposal" from Tehran. However, enforcement of the blockade continues despite the extension.

stories.title: America First Fed? Trump nominee Kevin Warsh signals ‘monetary sovereignty’ push: analysts
stories.summary: U.S. Federal Reserve chair nominee Kevin Warsh outlined a policy vision during his Senate confirmation hearing that Chinese analysts interpreted as extending "America First" principles into monetary policy. Analysts said his approach signals a shift from global liquidity provision toward prioritising domestic productivity and monetary sovereignty.

stories.title: Iran war reflects the false promise of US ‘energy dominance’
stories.summary: The article argues that the disruption of oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran war exposes the false promise of U.S. "energy dominance" rhetoric. Despite claims of energy independence, the U.S. remains a net crude oil importer, and its refineries depend on the medium sour crude that transits the strait.

stories.title: Israel’s ‘digital occupation’ of south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli drones are conducting persistent surveillance over southern Lebanon, a practice critics have labeled a "digital occupation." Al Jazeera reported on the impact of the drone presence on Lebanese communities.

stories.title: How China is gaining from Iran war by showing it is different from US
stories.summary: China has leveraged its economic relationships with the US, Israel, Iran, and Gulf states to protect its interests during the Iran conflict. Beijing has positioned itself as a diplomatic alternative to Washington.

stories.title: EU drafts entry ban on former Russian combatants — Kallas sets June deadline, Sybiha endorses
stories.summary: EU High Representative Kaja Kallas plans to propose an entry ban on former Russian combatants by the June European Council meeting. Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha has endorsed the initiative.

stories.title: Russian drone attack leaves port facilities damaged in Odesa region
stories.summary: Port infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region sustained damage during a large-scale overnight Russian strike drone attack on April 22.

stories.title: Why Japan’s earthquake has Bali on edge over magnitude 9 ‘megathrust’ risk
stories.summary: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake that struck Japan on Monday has raised concerns on the Indonesian island of Bali about the risk of a magnitude 9 "megathrust" event. Japan's Meteorological Agency issued a special advisory citing a slightly elevated 1 percent probability of a major quake in coming days.

stories.title: Pentagon to stop requiring members of US military to get flu vaccines
stories.summary: The Pentagon announced it will stop requiring U.S. military members to receive flu vaccines. The decision reportedly caught some Republican members of Congress off guard.

stories.title: Europe wanted a say on the Iran war, but it’s still on the sidelines
stories.summary: European nations seeking influence over the Iran war and the critical Strait of Hormuz remain largely sidelined. Iran and the United States continue to be the primary decision-makers regarding the vital waterway.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Zimbabweans Feared Dead After Bus Crash in South Africa
stories.summary: A cross-border bus carrying Zimbabwean passengers veered off the N1 highway near Makhado in South Africa's Limpopo Province on Wednesday, plunging into a ditch. Several passengers are feared dead in the crash.

stories.title: How Israel expands its control of south Lebanon border villages
stories.summary: Military sources reported that Israeli forces have expanded their occupation of border villages in southern Lebanon since the ceasefire took effect. The expansion represents a deepening of Israeli territorial control in the region.

stories.title: IRGC asserting themselves as Iran 'responds to Trump’s method of conducting diplomacy in kind'
stories.summary: Analysts suggest Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps is asserting itself as Tehran responds to Trump administration diplomacy with a dual strategy of rhetorical escalation and cautious pragmatism. Dr. Burcu Ozcelik of RUSI argued that Iran is simultaneously managing external pressures while safeguarding its nuclear program and regional influence.

stories.title: When the Rules Fail: Tax Incentives and Defense Sustainment
stories.summary: An analysis of US defense industrial policy argues that distorted tax incentives steer maintenance and sustainment work toward private vendors, even when government-owned facilities are well-positioned to perform it. The piece draws a parallel to soccer's adoption of video review technology to correct systemic oversights.

stories.title: Anthropic’s Mythos is stoking cybersecurity fears. What does it mean for China?
stories.summary: US-based Anthropic unveiled its Claude Mythos Preview AI model on April 7, drawing global attention for its ability to identify and exploit cybersecurity vulnerabilities. Rather than releasing it publicly, Anthropic provided Mythos to a select consortium. The model has raised concerns about implications for Chinese AI development and US-China technological competition.

stories.title: Russia loses 1,140 troops and 38 artillery systems in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: According to Ukrainian military reports, Russian forces lost approximately 1,140 personnel and 38 artillery systems in a single day. Cumulative Russian losses since February 24, 2022, are estimated at around 1,321,450 troops.

stories.title: Macron vows to help Lebanon prepare  for talks with Israel
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron pledged to help Lebanon prepare for negotiations with Israel. Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said the country needs €500 million to address the humanitarian fallout, while Hezbollah warned Israel would face resistance if troops remain in Lebanon.

stories.title: Coles adds 20c to the price of milk as war in the Middle East pushes up Australian grocery costs
stories.summary: Australian supermarket chain Coles raised home-brand milk prices by up to 20 cents per litre, with rival Woolworths expected to follow. The increases were driven by soaring diesel and fertiliser costs linked to the Middle East conflict. Some of the additional revenue will be temporarily passed on to dairy farmers.

stories.title: Ukraine is building a bigger deep-strike drone machine — middle- and deep-strike operations both scaling up, more units from May
stories.summary: Ukraine's drone forces report conducting over 100,000 combat sorties per month. The drone forces commander is now formally expanding units dedicated to middle- and deep-strike operations into Russian territory, with additional capacity expected from May.

stories.title: Independence Day celebrations marred by stabbings, fire as multiple Israelis injured
stories.summary: Several incidents across central Israel during Independence Day celebrations left multiple people injured, some critically. The incidents included stabbings and a residential fire in various locations.

stories.title: One killed in Israeli drone strike in Lebanon as displacement continues
stories.summary: A British maritime agency reported that a cargo ship departing Iran was fired upon and stopped in the water approximately eight nautical miles west of Iran. The crew was reported safe with no damage to the vessel, amid the ongoing US blockade of Iranian ports.

stories.title: Florida launches probe into OpenAI over ChatGPT’s alleged role in shooting
stories.summary: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier announced a criminal investigation into OpenAI after a deadly 2025 shooting at Florida State University. Authorities are examining claims that OpenAI's ChatGPT chatbot provided information to the suspect prior to the attack.

stories.title: The killer robots are coming. The battlefield will never look the same
stories.summary: An analysis explores how autonomous weapons systems and battlefield robots are transforming modern warfare. Military personnel note the potential to reduce human casualties, with one junior lieutenant stating that "human life is precious and robots don't bleed."

stories.title: Digital officers already operate in several AFU units — Ministry of Defense
stories.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Defense announced that digital officers have been selected and deployed in several key Armed Forces units. These officers are tasked with implementing digital solutions to support military operations.

stories.title: World urges restraint as US, Iran stick to guns
stories.summary: Global powers urged restraint as U.S.-Iran tensions escalated, with a U.S. blockade in the Strait of Hormuz derailing peace talks and sending energy prices soaring. An Iranian tanker was seized, which Tehran condemned as state terrorism, while the U.S. Senate prepared to vote on limiting presidential war powers.

stories.title: Iran’s UN ambassador responds to US ceasefire extension
