stories.summary: Iran's UN ambassador issued a response to US President Donald Trump's announcement extending the ceasefire between the two countries. The diplomatic exchange came amid uncertainty over broader peace negotiations.

stories.title: Resilience Without Capacity: The Fatal Flaw in America’s New Cyber Strategy
stories.summary: A critique of the White House's new cyber strategy argues it pairs a strong vision for resilience and competition with contradictory policy choices, including cuts to the very capabilities it depends on. The strategy treats cyberspace as a domain of sustained strategic competition and emphasizes national resilience and offensive cyber action.

stories.title: Iran ready for talks in Islamabad if US lifts blockade, UN envoy says
stories.summary: Iran's UN Ambassador Amir-Saeid Iravani said Tehran is ready to resume negotiations with the United States in Islamabad once Washington lifts its naval blockade. He added that the US must halt ceasefire violations before talks can proceed.

stories.title: USF strikes Russian Grad system in Zaporizhzhia region
stories.summary: The 429th Separate Unmanned Systems Brigade, known as Achilles, struck a Russian BM-21 Grad multiple launch rocket system in the Zaporizhzhia direction. The brigade is part of Ukraine's unmanned systems forces.

stories.title: US halts shipment of Iraq’s oil dollars to curb Iran-linked groups: WSJ
stories.summary: The US Treasury blocked a plane carrying nearly $500 million in US banknotes destined for Iraq, according to The Wall Street Journal. The move aimed to curb funding to Iran-linked groups operating in Iraq.

stories.title: Military planners to discuss Hormuz reopening in London
stories.summary: Military planners are scheduled to meet in London to discuss the potential reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. The talks will build on progress made during an earlier meeting held on April 17.

stories.title: Why Iran Metabolizes the Pressure that Broke Venezuela
stories.summary: An analysis argues that Iran's resilience under US pressure differs fundamentally from Venezuela's experience because of distinct internal and external factors. The Supreme Leader's authority is anchored in a theocratic order where religious legitimacy supports a sprawling economic system, making regime change through coercive pressure unlikely.

stories.title: World Cup host Mexico pledges security at tourist sites after shooting
stories.summary: Mexico's president acknowledged that the archaeological site outside Mexico City where a shooting occurred lacked adequate security. The government pledged enhanced security at tourist sites ahead of hosting the World Cup.

stories.title: ‘Creativity is the basis of Judaism’: Yaacov Agam, father of kinetic art, receives Israel Prize
stories.summary: Israeli artist Yaacov Agam, 97, considered the father of kinetic art, received the Israel Prize. The award ceremony took place in Jerusalem at the museum he helped design.

stories.title: Retail chains found to be charging over double what they pay for imported grapes
stories.summary: Israel's Agriculture Ministry is considering price controls after an audit revealed retailers charging over double what they pay for imported grapes. Grapes imported at 14 NIS per kilogram were being sold for 32 NIS.

stories.title: U.S. military pushes for boost in 2027 spending on drones and air defences used in Iran war
stories.summary: The U.S. Pentagon plans to triple drone spending to over $74 billion and invest more than $30 billion in critical munitions, including missile interceptors, for fiscal year 2027. The proposed increases respond to depleted stockpiles resulting from the ongoing war with Iran.

stories.title: The Strokes frontman says ‘privileged’ Zionists talk ‘like Black people during slavery’
stories.summary: The Strokes frontman Julian Casablancas said in a web series episode that "American Zionists" enjoy privileges of "white privileged people" but complain of oppression, comparing their rhetoric to that experienced by Black people during slavery.

stories.title: Ukraine to resume oil supplies via Druzhba pipeline on Wednesday — Reuters
stories.summary: Ukraine announced it would resume pumping oil through the Druzhba pipeline on Wednesday, April 22, according to Reuters.

stories.title: Iran executes civil defence official convicted of spying for Israel
stories.summary: Iran executed Mehdi Farid, a senior civil defence official convicted of spying for Israel's Mossad, after the Supreme Court upheld his conviction. Farid reportedly confessed to attempting to pass sensitive facility and personnel information to Israeli intelligence.

stories.title: Nigeria: Why Tinubu Fired Wale Edun As Finance Minister
stories.summary: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu approved the removal of Finance Minister Wale Edun and Housing Minister Ahmed Dangiwa. The announcement was made by Secretary to the Government of the Federation George Akume.

stories.title: Florida launches criminal probe into OpenAI and ChatGPT over deadly shooting
stories.summary: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier announced a criminal probe into OpenAI and its ChatGPT application over a deadly shooting at Florida State University that killed two people. Prosecutors are investigating whether artificial intelligence interactions with the suspected gunman contributed to the attack.

stories.title: Alan Dershowitz leaves Democratic Party, calling it the ‘most anti-Israel’ in US history
stories.summary: Attorney Alan Dershowitz announced he is leaving the Democratic Party, calling it the "most anti-Israel" in US history. He joined the Republican Party, which he said has kept antisemites on the sidelines.

stories.title: Singapore’s Balakrishnan warns Hormuz just a ‘dry run’ if US, China clash
stories.summary: Singapore Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan warned that any disruption in the Strait of Hormuz would pale in comparison to a potential US-China clash in the Pacific. He disclosed that Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia share a common interest in keeping the Strait of Malacca open, even amid speculation about tolls on the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Hongkongers flock to theatres to snap up HK$30 Cinema Day tickets in advance
stories.summary: Hong Kong residents queued as early as 10:30 a.m. at cinemas such as Star Cinema in Tseung Kwan O to purchase HK$30 tickets for Cinema Day. Sales opened at noon on Wednesday for Saturday screenings. Buyers called for more frequent discount events and family-friendly promotions.

stories.title: Russians strike transport infrastructure in Zaporizhzhia, leaving one killed, another injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck transport infrastructure in the city of Zaporizhzhia, killing one man and injuring another person.

stories.title: Why China is backing nuclear fuel rod production in Namibia
stories.summary: China pledged to support Namibia's domestic processing of critical minerals and uranium, moving beyond raw material exports. The commitment came in a joint communiqué issued after talks in Beijing between Foreign Minister Wang Yi and Namibian counterpart Selma Ashipala-Musavyi. Namibia has long exported unprocessed minerals and now seeks to develop higher-value downstream industries.

stories.title: Digital memory at stake: Why news outlets block the Wayback Machine
stories.summary: A growing number of news outlets are blocking the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine from archiving their content, raising concerns about the preservation of digital records and online historical memory.

stories.title: IRGC boat fires on vessel near Oman, report says
stories.summary: A container ship was fired upon near the coast of Oman by a boat linked to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, causing heavy damage to its bridge. Iran's Tasnim News Agency said the military had enforced maritime law on a vessel that ignored warnings.

stories.title: Nigeria: 350,000 Children Vaccinated Against Crippling Diphtheria Epidemic
stories.summary: Doctors Without Borders and the Borno State Ministry of Health completed a diphtheria vaccination campaign in Maiduguri Metropolitan Council, Borno State, Nigeria. The campaign targeted children up to 14 years old and reached approximately 350,000 children.

stories.title: Taiwan president cancels Eswatini trip after African countries close airspace
stories.summary: Taiwan's President Lai canceled a planned trip to Eswatini after several African countries closed their airspace to his aircraft. Taiwan accused Beijing of pressuring African nations to deny overflight rights.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: U.S. In Talks to Send Afghan Refugees to DR Congo
stories.summary: The United States is reportedly in talks to resettle Afghan allies who assisted U.S. forces in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The Afghan refugees face a choice between relocation to the conflict-affected DRC or return to Taliban-controlled Afghanistan.

stories.title: Russian drone attacks infrastructure facility in Kharkiv
stories.summary: Russian forces used a Molniya-type UAV to strike an infrastructure site in the Slobidskyi district of Kharkiv.

stories.title: 'Bid farewell to oil production': Iran cautions Gulf states against aiding attacks
stories.summary: Iran's IRGC aerospace commander Majid Mousavi warned Gulf states that oil production across the Middle East could be disrupted if their territory is used to launch attacks against Iran.

stories.title: Texas can require Ten Commandments be displayed in classrooms, US court rules
stories.summary: A US court ruled that Texas can require the display of the Ten Commandments in public school classrooms. Challengers plan to appeal to the Supreme Court, while conservatives hailed the decision as a victory for moral values.

stories.title: IRGC says forces ready for ‘surprises’ beyond enemy expectations
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said in a statement marking its founding anniversary that it is prepared to deliver battlefield surprises and use new capabilities in any future confrontation with adversaries.

stories.title: Delhi schools sound alarm – and water bell – as India sizzles in brutal heatwave
stories.summary: Authorities in New Delhi have ordered schools to ring regular "water bells" reminding students to drink water as the Indian capital braces for severe heatwave conditions. Government data shows nearly 11,000 people died from heatstroke across India between 2012 and 2021, with New Delhi previously recording temperatures as high as 49.2°C.

stories.title: US reviewing military footprint after Iran strikes, Pentagon says
stories.summary: The Pentagon said the US is reviewing its military presence in the Middle East following roughly 40 days of conflict with Iran. Officials noted that damage assessments of US bases are incomplete, and repair funding is not included in the 2027 budget request.

stories.title: World Cup co-host Mexico ramps up security at tourist sites after shooting
stories.summary: Mexico's government announced increased security at tourist sites after a lone gunman opened fire at the Teotihuacan pyramids near Mexico City, killing one Canadian tourist and injuring a dozen others. The shooting occurred less than two months before Mexico co-hosts the FIFA World Cup.

stories.title: Australia news live: independent candidate for Farrer says Coalition preferencing One Nation ‘not for the good of our community’
stories.summary: In Australia, the federal government struck a deal with two major companies to increase fertiliser imports for farmers amid a global supply bottleneck. Separately, an independent candidate in the New South Wales electorate of Farrer criticised the Coalition's decision to preference One Nation.

stories.title: Trump reads from Bible in America 250 event critics accuse of Christian nationalism
stories.summary: President Trump participated in an America 250 event featuring a marathon reading of the Bible's 66 Protestant-recognized books, reading a passage from 2 Chronicles. Critics accused the event of promoting Christian nationalism.

stories.title: UK inflation rises to 3.3% amid soaring fuel prices driven by Iran war
stories.summary: UK inflation rose to 3.3% in March, up from 3% in February, driven largely by surging fuel prices linked to the Iran war. The Office for National Statistics reported the increase matched City economists' forecasts, adding further pressure on household finances amid the ongoing cost of living crisis.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Trump extends ceasefire but blockade continues; Iran attacks container ship off Oman
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced an extension of the U.S. ceasefire with Iran at Pakistan's request while awaiting a proposal from Tehran, even as the U.S. military maintains its blockade of Iranian ports. Separately, Iran attacked a container ship off Oman. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Iran's Kharg Island storage facilities would soon be full and its oil wells forced to shut.

stories.title: Climbing lamp posts cross-legged challenge goes viral in China with players often needing rescue
stories.summary: A woman in Jiangsu province, eastern China, became stuck on a lamp post while attempting a viral "cross-legged climbing" challenge and had to be rescued by police. The trend requires participants to wrap their legs around a lamp post in a seated position and then try to free themselves, but many have found it unexpectedly difficult.

stories.title: Morning update
stories.summary: A morning briefing summarized ongoing US-Iran tensions, noting the ceasefire extension alongside a continued US blockade, mixed signals from Tehran on diplomacy, and shifting global energy and security dynamics from Washington to Beijing.

stories.title: Thirteen killed in second India fireworks blast in three days
stories.summary: A second fireworks explosion in India in three days killed thirteen people. Earlier in the week, a blast at a firecracker factory in the neighboring state of Tamil Nadu left at least 25 dead.

stories.title: US lawmakers condemn threats against Congresswoman Ansari
stories.summary: More than a dozen Democratic US lawmakers condemned threats and doxxing directed at Representative Yassamin Ansari after she criticized the war with Iran. Representative Gregory Meeks called the attacks on Ansari, her family, and staff unacceptable.

stories.title: Alan Dershowitz quits Democratic Party, calling it ‘most anti-Israel party in US history’
stories.summary: Attorney Alan Dershowitz announced he is leaving the Democratic Party, calling it the most anti-Israel party in US history. The move formalized a political shift that has seen him increasingly break with Democrats over Israel policy.

stories.title: South Africa: IEC Warns of 'Significant' Risks for Local Elections - South African News Briefs - April 22, 2026
stories.summary: South Africa's Independent Electoral Commission warned of "significant" risks ahead of upcoming local elections.

stories.title: First local dengue case could lead to outbreak in coming months, health official says
stories.summary: Hong Kong recorded its first locally transmitted dengue fever case in over a year, detected in Tai Po in a patient with no travel history. Albert Au Ka-wing of the Centre for Health Protection warned that undiagnosed imported cases could trigger an outbreak in the coming months but said the risk was preventable.

stories.title: Piers Morgan challenges Israel’s ‘most moral army’ claim
stories.summary: British broadcaster Piers Morgan questioned claims that the Israeli military is the most moral army in the world, citing recent Haaretz testimonies from Israeli soldiers describing killings of unarmed civilians in Gaza and incidents in Lebanon.

stories.title: PTCL returns to profit after years
stories.summary: Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd (PTCL) returned to profitability after more than four years, reporting a 58 percent revenue increase in Q1 2026. The company also announced plans to formally launch 5G services next month.

stories.title: Six terrorists killed in Khyber, Bannu operations
stories.summary: Pakistani security forces killed six terrorists in separate operations in Khyber and Bannu districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Five were killed during an operation in the Akkakhel area of Bara, and one was killed in Bannu.

stories.title: Supreme Court sets aside dismissal of ministry official
stories.summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court overturned the dismissal of a Ministry of Commerce officer who had been removed for unauthorized absence. The case was remanded to the Federal Service Tribunal for a fresh hearing within three months.

stories.title: Trump claims Iran ‘collapsing financially’ amid Hormuz standoff
stories.summary: President Trump claimed on Truth Social that Iran is collapsing financially and losing hundreds of millions of dollars daily due to the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, adding that Iran's military and police are not being paid.

stories.title: The Deb actor in feud with Rebel Wilson signed $150,000 record deal, court told
stories.summary: Actor Charlotte MacInnes is suing Rebel Wilson for defamation over social media posts alleging MacInnes made a sexual harassment complaint related to the musical film The Deb. A court heard that MacInnes secured a $150,000 record deal with a publicist representing international stars during the feud with Wilson.

stories.title: El Salvador holds mass trial for 486 alleged members of notorious MS-13 gang
stories.summary: A Salvadoran court began a mass trial of 486 alleged MS-13 gang members on Tuesday, one of the largest collective prosecutions under President Nayib Bukele's emergency powers crackdown. Prosecutors allege the defendants committed more than 47,000 crimes between 2012 and 2022. Human rights groups have warned the proceedings violate due process.

stories.title: Alleged Iranian front group calls on Americans to kill Trump, claims it could have killed Ivanka
stories.summary: An alleged Iranian front group issued calls for Americans to kill President Trump, claiming it could have targeted his daughter Ivanka. The group also directed appeals at US security personnel and alleged victims of Jeffrey Epstein.

stories.title: Police detain 17-year-old student who prepared two explosions in Kremenchuk
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service detained a 17-year-old student in the Poltava region who was allegedly preparing two explosions near a police department on orders from Russian special services in the city of Kremenchuk.

stories.title: US indefinitely extends ceasefire with Iran
stories.summary: President Donald Trump indefinitely extended the U.S. ceasefire with Iran, agreeing to a request from mediator Pakistan to allow more time for negotiations while maintaining a blockade of Iranian ports.

stories.title: Iran war: What’s happening on day 54 as Trump extends ceasefire?
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced an extension of the US ceasefire with Iran, stating it would remain in effect until a proposal is presented and negotiations conclude.

stories.title: Why Myanmar’s token amnesties are ‘no cause for celebration’
stories.summary: Myanmar's military government announced an amnesty for 4,335 prisoners and reduced Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi's 27-year sentence by a sixth. Analysts say the gestures, the regime's third amnesty in six months, reflect growing boldness rather than genuine mercy. Suu Kyi, 80, has not been seen publicly since her trials ended in December.

stories.title: Florida investigating ChatGPT role in mass shooting at university
stories.summary: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier announced a criminal investigation into whether OpenAI's ChatGPT played a role in a mass shooting at Florida State University that killed two people. Prosecutors reviewed exchanges between the suspected gunman and the chatbot. Uthmeier said that if ChatGPT were a person, it would face murder charges.

stories.title: Beijing deepens ties as Middle East energy crisis reshapes region
stories.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi is touring Southeast Asia, visiting Cambodia, Thailand, and Myanmar, as Beijing seeks to strengthen ties amid energy disruptions and trade pressures linked to Middle East tensions.

stories.title: MTR Corp’s HK$18.8 billion green bond sale sets local currency record
stories.summary: Hong Kong's MTR Corporation sold HK$18.8 billion (US$2.4 billion) in green bonds across five-, ten-, and thirty-year tranches, setting a record for Hong Kong dollar-denominated issuances. Each tranche was also the largest for its respective tenor. The offering marks MTR's first publicly offered bond in the local currency market.

stories.title: Russian official says Russians in Moldova’s Transdniestria under threat
stories.summary: Sergei Shoigu, secretary of Russia's Security Council, stated that the safety of Russian citizens in Moldova's breakaway Transnistria region is under threat and that Moscow will take all necessary steps to protect them.

stories.title: North Korea’s Lazarus suspected of stealing US$290 million in KelpDAO cyberattack
stories.summary: North Korea-linked hacking group Lazarus is suspected of stealing nearly US$290 million in cryptocurrency from online investment tool KelpDAO, making it the largest known crypto heist of the year. A United Nations panel has linked North Korea's cybercrime operations to funding the country's nuclear weapons program.

stories.title: US warns it will run out of money to pay airport security workers in coming weeks
stories.summary: Emergency funds allocated during a partial U.S. government shutdown in late March to pay airport security workers are expected to run out by early May, raising concerns about continued Transportation Security Administration operations.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: Peaceful Protesters Face Military Trial in DR Congo
stories.summary: In the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ituri Province, peaceful protesters are facing military trials under martial law that restricts free speech and assembly, according to Human Rights Watch.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Fears of Possible Escalation of Violence in Tigray
stories.summary: The Tigray People's Liberation Front in Ethiopia announced the restoration of a regional parliament, raising fears of possible escalation of violence. The election of such a parliament was previously one of the triggers for the war in northern Ethiopia.

stories.title: Nigeria: Oyedele in As Nigeria's Finance Minister, Edun Out
stories.summary: In a Nigerian cabinet reshuffle, Oyedele has been appointed as Finance Minister, replacing Edun. Oyedele previously served as Minister of State in the same ministry.

stories.title: Namibia: Namibia Targets 80% Reduction in Food Imports
stories.summary: Namibian President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah announced a target of reducing food imports by 80 percent. The government plans to boost local agricultural production and safeguard livestock health to sustain export markets.

stories.title: Sudan: Measles Surge Across Darfur and Kordofan Triggers Urgent Vaccination Response
stories.summary: A rapidly spreading measles outbreak across Sudan's Darfur and Kordofan regions has triggered emergency vaccination campaigns. Health systems are struggling with rising infections, child deaths, and severe medical supply shortages.

stories.title: Two arrested in possession of IDF weapons, ammunition, and illegal drugs
stories.summary: Israeli authorities arrested two suspects in possession of stolen IDF weapons, ammunition, and illegal drugs. An active-duty soldier allegedly stole the weapons and transferred them to a civilian who sold them to criminal elements.

stories.title: Why the Junta Released Myanmar’s President
stories.summary: Myanmar's military junta released the country's detained president, though the fate of former leader Aung San Suu Kyi remains uncertain. The reasons behind the junta's decision to free the president have drawn international attention.

stories.title: UK could face ‘hacktivist attacks at scale’, says head of security agency
stories.summary: Richard Horne, chief executive of the UK's National Cyber Security Centre, warned that the UK could face large-scale hacktivist attacks if drawn into a conflict, with potential disruption comparable to recent major ransomware incidents. He noted that nation states now account for the most significant cyber incidents the NCSC handles.

stories.title: Multinational pharmaceutical companies to benefit from new China guidelines: analysts
stories.summary: China's State Council published new guidelines on innovative drug pricing described by analysts as the most significant in a decade. The framework supports value-based pricing for patented innovative drugs while driving down generic drug prices through market competition, benefiting both domestic and multinational pharmaceutical companies.

stories.title: Heatwaves, floods and wildfires pose rising threat to democracy, report finds
stories.summary: A new report found that climate-related hazards such as heatwaves, floods, and wildfires disrupted at least 23 elections in 18 countries in 2024. Over the past two decades, 94 elections and referendums across 52 countries have been affected by extreme weather events linked to the climate crisis.

stories.title: US potentially facing 'near-term risk' of running out of key ammunition after Iran war - report
stories.summary: A Center for Strategic and International Studies analysis found the US may face a near-term risk of running out of key ammunition after the Iran war, estimating three to five years to replenish missile stockpiles to pre-war levels.

stories.title: Sudan: Millions of Desperate Sudanese Return Home Amid Dire Conditions As War Rages
stories.summary: The UN's International Organization for Migration reported that nearly four million displaced Sudanese have returned to their places of origin three years into the conflict but face dire conditions and a continued struggle for survival.

stories.title: Sudan: '4m Returnees in Sudan At Risk As Services Collapse' - IOM
stories.summary: The IOM warned that the return of millions of displaced Sudanese is at risk due to collapsing services and fragile conditions across the country, including in Khartoum, Omdurman, and Port Sudan.

stories.title: Africa: A Quiet U.S.-AU Deal That Could Reshape Investment in Africa
stories.summary: The Trump administration and the African Union have begun negotiations on a deal that could reshape U.S. investment and development cooperation in Africa, according to the Institute for Security Studies.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Tigray Party Restores Pre-War Parliament, Jeopardising Northern Ethiopia Peace
stories.summary: The Tigray People's Liberation Front announced it is reassuming control of Tigray's regional government and restoring its pre-war parliament, effectively voiding the peace deal with Ethiopia's federal government that ended the northern Ethiopian conflict.

stories.title: Guatemalan attorney general sanctioned internationally loses bid for third term
stories.summary: Guatemalan Attorney General Consuelo Porras, who has faced international sanctions and clashed with President Bernardo Arévalo, lost her bid for a third term and is set to leave office next month.

stories.title: US lifts or eases sanctions against Russia and Belarus about 16 times last year – Vlasiuk
stories.summary: Vladyslav Vlasiuk, Ukraine's Presidential Commissioner for Sanctions Policy, stated that approximately 16 instances were recorded over the past year in which the United States lifted or eased sanctions against Russian and Belarusian entities.

stories.title: The Onion signs new deal to take over Alex Jones’ Infowars
stories.summary: The Onion has signed a restructured deal to license the Infowars platform from its court-appointed manager, Gregory Milligan, rather than purchasing its assets outright. The agreement was submitted to Texas state Judge Maya Guerra Gamble. The satirical site's parent company, Global Tetrahedron, had initially attempted to buy Infowars for US$1.75 million at a 2024 auction.

stories.title: Millions in India stripped of vote before critical state election, as government seeks to ‘purify’ electoral roll
stories.summary: Approximately 9.1 million names were deleted from the electoral roll in the Indian state of West Bengal ahead of critical state elections, with about 2.7 million people reportedly stripped of their vote. Experts say Muslims and other minorities have been disproportionately affected by the revision, which critics have called mass disenfranchisement.

stories.title: Rights groups say EU ‘enabling’ Israel after trade deal decision
stories.summary: Human rights groups including Amnesty International criticized the EU after Germany and Italy blocked a proposal by Spain, Slovenia, and Ireland to suspend the EU-Israel trade agreement, accusing the bloc of enabling alleged Israeli violations.

stories.title: Iran adviser calls Trump ceasefire extension ‘meaningless’
stories.summary: An adviser to Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf dismissed Trump's ceasefire extension as meaningless, arguing Washington cannot impose conditions on Tehran. Disputes over the US naval blockade and stalled negotiations continue.

stories.title: Singaporean man charged after viral Lucky Plaza assault on Filipino woman
stories.summary: Singaporean man Andrew Suresh Markandan, 47, was charged with two counts of voluntarily causing hurt and two counts of mischief after a viral video showed him assaulting a Filipino woman, Alibutdan Vilma Litgio, at Lucky Plaza shopping centre. He is also accused of a prior assault on the same victim at Hotel 81 Bugis in March of the previous year.

stories.title: ‘Significant failures’ led two NSW foster children to be placed with serial killer, review finds
stories.summary: A review in New South Wales, Australia, found that "significant failures" by the Department of Communities and Justice led to two foster children, aged 12 and 14, being placed in a home with convicted triple murderer Regina Arthurell. Two department staff members have been suspended, and the review revealed the department had been warned about Arthurell's presence in the home in December.

stories.title: Phone tracking shows how Colombian mercenaries backed Sudan's RSF - report
stories.summary: A report by the Conflict Insights Group used phone tracking data to reveal how Colombian mercenaries supported Sudan's Rapid Support Forces. The research also highlights the extent of UAE involvement in the conflict.

stories.title: Shifting Saudi ties: what role could China take after Iran war is over?
stories.summary: Analysts say the Iran conflict is prompting Saudi Arabia to reconsider its U.S.-led security strategy, with China emerging in a limited but functional role. However, deep U.S.-Saudi defense ties are expected to constrain broader cooperation with Beijing. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman initiated a phone call amid shifting regional dynamics.

stories.title: Temporary accommodation linked to deaths of 104 children in England in six years
stories.summary: Data revealed that living in temporary accommodation contributed to the deaths of 104 children in England over six years, 76 of whom were under one year old. In 2024, there were 64 stillbirths and 27 neonatal deaths among mothers in temporary accommodation in the UK. Experts have called for urgent action on the housing crisis.

stories.title: Pollen season in UK and mainland Europe extended by climate breakdown
stories.summary: A study found that climate change has extended the pollen season in the UK and mainland Europe by one to two weeks since the 1990s. Researchers said the lengthened season affects tens of millions of allergy sufferers, adding to the broader health impacts of global heating beyond extreme weather events.

stories.title: Israel’s death penalty law could spell suspension from rights body role, says chief
stories.summary: The president of the Council of Europe's Parliamentary Assembly, Petra Bayr, said Israel's observer status could be suspended over its new law mandating the death penalty for Palestinians convicted of certain offences. Bayr stated that not using capital punishment is a requirement for holding observer status at the pan-European human rights body.

stories.title: Iran’s UN envoy says received signs US ready to end blockade
stories.summary: Iran's UN envoy Amir Saeid Iravani told reporters that Tehran has received indications the United States is prepared to lift its Strait of Hormuz blockade. He said Iran would then be ready to resume negotiations planned for Islamabad.

stories.title: El Salvador court tries over 400 alleged gang leaders for 47,000 crimes
stories.summary: A Salvadoran court began the mass trial of over 400 alleged leaders of the MS-13 gang, facing charges related to more than 47,000 crimes prosecutors say were committed between 2012 and 2022.

stories.title: White House looks to extend oil transport exemption
stories.summary: President Trump plans to extend a Jones Act waiver allowing oil to be shipped between US ports on non-American-flagged vessels, according to Axios. The measure, first introduced in March, aims to ease rising fuel costs linked to the Iran conflict.

stories.title: After surviving US-Israeli strikes, Iran regime faces fresh challenge in truce talks
stories.summary: Iran's leadership showed unity during US-Israeli strikes by taking a hard line, but upcoming truce negotiations with the US could expose divisions within the panel now running the country, according to analysis.

stories.title: US denies moving THAAD system from South Korea
stories.summary: A senior US military official denied that the THAAD missile defence system has been moved from South Korea, after reports suggested components were being shifted to the Middle East. General Xavier Brunson confirmed the system remains on the Korean Peninsula.

stories.title: US court allows Texas public schools to display Ten Commandments
stories.summary: The Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that Texas can require the Bible's Ten Commandments to be displayed in public school classrooms under Senate Bill 10. The 120-page decision responded to legal challenges from families of diverse faiths. The ruling represents a win for Christian conservatives advocating for religious expression in schools.

stories.title: Iran says 775 war-damaged schools repaired
stories.summary: Iran's Education Minister Alireza Kazemi said 775 of 1,300 schools damaged during the conflict have been repaired, with the worst damage in Tehran, Kermanshah, Isfahan, and Hormozgan provinces. Full repairs are expected by October.

stories.title: Kosovar teen charged for trying to kill teacher wanted to kill 'as many Jewish people as possible'
stories.summary: A Kosovar teenager identified as Erjon S. was charged with attempted murder, assault, and resisting arrest after allegedly trying to kill a teacher with the stated goal of killing as many Jewish people as possible.

stories.title: FIFA unlocks more World Cup tickets and adds new, more expensive categories
stories.summary: FIFA has released additional tickets for the upcoming World Cup but introduced new premium-priced categories, drawing criticism from some fans over the higher costs.

stories.title: Large-scale fire extinguished in Hlukhiv following nighttime Russian attack
stories.summary: Rescue workers in the Sumy region extinguished a large-scale fire in the Hlukhiv community caused by a massive nighttime Russian attack.

stories.title: Mexico disappearances climb as attacks on rights defenders persist, Amnesty says
stories.summary: Amnesty International reported that the number of disappearances in Mexico has risen to 133,500 cases as of 2025. The organization noted that attacks against human rights defenders, journalists, and activists searching for the disappeared continued throughout the country.

stories.title: World's biggest maker of condoms set to raise prices due to Iran war
stories.summary: Malaysia-based Karex, the world's largest condom manufacturer producing over five billion units annually, announced plans to raise prices due to disruptions caused by the Iran war. The company supplies global brands including Durex and Trojan.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Trump says Iran 'collapsing financially' as Washington prolongs ceasefire
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said Iran is "collapsing financially" due to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz as the U.S. maintains its blockade of Iranian ports. Trump announced an extension of the ceasefire with Iran while diplomatic efforts continue.

stories.title: Tehran held military parades as ceasefire was set to end
stories.summary: Videos circulated showing large crowds attending a military parade in Tehran on Tuesday as the US-Iran ceasefire deadline was approaching, signaling Iran's show of military readiness.

stories.title: ‘At the request of CDF Munir, PM Shehbaz’, Trump announces extension in ceasefire until Iran submits proposal
stories.summary: President Donald Trump announced an indefinite extension of the U.S. ceasefire with Iran at the request of Pakistani mediator PM Shehbaz and military chief General Munir, though a naval blockade of Iranian ports remains in place. Tehran has not yet officially responded.

stories.title: Israel and Hezbollah exchange fire, testing Lebanon truce as talks loom
stories.summary: Hezbollah fired rockets and drones into northern Israel on Tuesday, accusing Israeli forces of violating the ceasefire in southern Lebanon. Israel described the attack as a "blatant violation" of the truce agreement. The exchange of fire comes ahead of U.S.-mediated talks between the Israeli and Lebanese governments.

stories.title: Polyfoam use left unchecked amid gap in supervision, Tai Po fire probe hears
stories.summary: An independent committee investigating the Wang Fuk Court fire in Hong Kong's Tai Po district heard testimony from four fire department officers on the 17th day of hearings. The November 26 blaze, which broke out during a major renovation, killed 168 people, displaced approximately 5,000 residents, and destroyed seven of eight estate blocks. The probe is examining unchecked polyfoam use linked to a supervision gap.

stories.title: Centcom says US forces ‘rearming’ during Iran ceasefire
stories.summary: US Central Command chief Brad Cooper said American forces are rearming and retooling during the Iran ceasefire while remaining ready. He appeared alongside US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, emphasizing the military's ability to adapt.

stories.title: IAEA says nuclear monitoring key to lasting agreement
stories.summary: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi said any peace agreement involving Iran must include nuclear monitoring from the start, warning that omitting oversight would create only an illusion of an agreement. He welcomed the US ceasefire extension.

stories.title: Trump says Hormuz 'totally BLOCKADED’ by US, claims Iran wants it open
stories.summary: President Trump declared on Truth Social that the Strait of Hormuz is totally blockaded by the US and claimed Iran wants it reopened to sustain oil revenues, asserting that Iran loses hundreds of millions of dollars daily from the closure.

stories.title: Film director Ihor Malakhov killed in action
stories.summary: Ukrainian film director Ihor Malakhov was confirmed killed in action on the front lines. He had been listed as missing in action since 2023.

stories.title: Virginia redistricting vote could boost Democrats in US midterms
stories.summary: Virginia voters approved a new congressional map on Tuesday that could give Democrats up to four additional U.S. House seats ahead of the November midterm elections. The redistricting move is seen as a direct response to President Trump's push for mid-decade map redrawing, intensifying the national gerrymandering battle.

stories.title: Trump extends ceasefire until Iranian proposal is submitted, talks are over
stories.summary: President Donald Trump extended the U.S. ceasefire with Iran, citing a request from Pakistan, to allow Iranian leaders additional time to present a unified negotiating proposal.

stories.title: Trump effect? Taiwan poll reveals deep doubts about US military protection
stories.summary: A poll released by Taipei's Democracy Foundation found that 57 percent of Taiwanese respondents do not believe the United States would send troops to defend Taiwan in a cross-strait conflict. Half of those surveyed also questioned the effectiveness of American weapons. The results highlight growing skepticism about Washington's security guarantees.

stories.title: US Navy arming warships with Patriot missiles to counter China’s hypersonic threat
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy plans to deploy Patriot missiles aboard its warships for the first time, aiming to counter China's hypersonic weapons threat. This marks the first instance of the Patriot system being fielded at sea.

stories.title: After being sexually harassed by terrorists, female IDF reservists refuse to serve - report
stories.summary: Female IDF reservists reportedly refused to serve after being sexually harassed by detained terrorists. Israel's State Comptroller had previously criticized the IDF for ordering female officer cadets to guard Nukhba terrorists.

stories.title: Pacific Islanders skip food, medicine amid global fuel shortage from Iran war
stories.summary: Pacific Island nations are facing severe fuel shortages and rising costs for food and healthcare as the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran disrupts oil traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. The strait typically carries about 20 percent of global oil and liquefied natural gas flows. Aid agencies have warned of escalating prices across the region.

stories.title: Confronting Wexner’s Epstein ties, alumni of Jewish leadership programs launch new survivor fund
stories.summary: Alumni of Jewish leadership programs linked to Les Wexner launched a new survivor fund called ASHRU to support victims, citing a responsibility to confront Wexner's ties to Jeffrey Epstein.

stories.title: How Hong Kong can actively shape the foreign policy debate
stories.summary: A commentary argues that Hong Kong, despite being described as a "superconnector" between China and the world, remains underdeveloped as a hub for international relations study and practice. The author, who returned to Asia after years in the UK and US, suggests the city could play a more active role in shaping foreign policy debate.

stories.title: CATL to supercharge China’s EV sector with faster-charging, higher-performing batteries
stories.summary: CATL, the world's largest electric vehicle battery producer with over 40 percent global market share, unveiled upgraded technologies including lighter battery packs and faster charging capabilities. The company aims to accelerate global automotive electrification and strengthen Chinese EV manufacturers' international expansion strategies.

stories.title: US in talks to send Afghan refugees to DR Congo
stories.summary: The United States is in discussions to resettle Afghan allies who assisted U.S. forces in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The Afghan refugees face a choice between resettlement in the war-torn DRC or return to Taliban-controlled Afghanistan.

stories.title: Italy summons Russian ambassador over TV host insults to PM Meloni
stories.summary: Italy summoned the Russian ambassador in Rome after a pro-Kremlin Russian television host directed insults at Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni. Italian Foreign Minister announced the diplomatic protest on Tuesday, April 21.

stories.title: Iran war latest: Trump’s ceasefire reversal and tensions simmer with China
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump indefinitely extended the ceasefire with Iran hours before it was set to expire, at Pakistan's request, while maintaining the U.S. naval blockade. Uncertainty remains over how the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran will conclude. Tensions with China also continued to simmer amid the broader conflict.

stories.title: Japanese prefecture pays singles to use dating apps to battle low birth rates
stories.summary: Japan's Kochi prefecture announced it will subsidize dating app fees for residents aged 20 to 39, offering up to 20,000 yen (US$125) per person for the 2026 financial year. The initiative targets certified matchmaking platforms as the country confronts record-low birth rates.

stories.title: Virginia voters approve new congressional maps in blow to Trump
stories.summary: Virginia voters on Tuesday approved new congressional maps designed to boost Democratic representation, potentially gaining the party up to four additional U.S. House seats. The vote is part of a broader redistricting battle that began after President Trump pushed Texas's Republican legislature to redraw its congressional maps to unseat Democratic incumbents.

stories.title: Chinese New Year bamboo greeting cards date back over 2,000 years to Han dynasty
stories.summary: Researchers have traced the origin of Chinese New Year greeting cards back over 2,000 years to the Han dynasty (206 BC–AD 220). During that era, people inscribed their names, ages, hometowns, and official positions on bamboo or wood sticks called "ming ci," which served as early name cards.

stories.title: Argentina’s Milei sings and lights torch for Israeli national day
stories.summary: Argentine President Javier Milei participated in Israel's 78th Independence Day celebrations, singing and lighting a ceremonial torch at the event.

stories.title: Trump extends ceasefire and hopes for ‘unified proposal’
stories.summary: President Trump announced on social media that the ceasefire in the US war with Iran has been extended, expressing hope for a unified proposal from Tehran.

stories.title: Germany's ruling coalition at odds over reform push
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's coalition government faces internal disagreements over a reform package covering taxes, pensions, and the health system. The coalition is also seeking ways to address rising fuel prices linked to the Iran war.

stories.title: Israel punishes soldiers who desecrated crucifix in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military removed two soldiers from combat duty and sentenced them to 30 days in military detention after they destroyed a crucifix in a Christian village in southern Lebanon. One soldier used a sledgehammer to smash the statue while the other filmed the act.

stories.title: Indians slam New Zealand minister for ‘butter chicken tsunami’ remarks: ‘outright racism’
stories.summary: New Zealand First party minister sparked outrage by calling a planned free-trade agreement with India a "butter chicken tsunami." The New Zealand government has described the deal, set to be signed in New Delhi, as a "once in a generation" opportunity. The right-wing coalition partner pulled its support over fears about the agreement's impact.

stories.title: Trump buys time for Iran deal after frantic day of diplomacy
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump decided to back off escalation threats against Iran for the second time in two weeks, buying additional time for diplomatic efforts toward a potential deal.

stories.title: Scammers trick overseas students out of gold in fake money-laundering probes
stories.summary: Hong Kong police warned that fraudsters have scammed at least nine overseas students aged 19 to 26, studying in the UK, Australia, and other countries, out of up to HK$1.5 million each. The scammers accused victims of money laundering and lured them to Hong Kong to purchase gold for bogus law-enforcement investigations.

stories.title: Navy ‘going to study’ possibility of building ships outside US, Phelan says
stories.summary: U.S. Navy Secretary John Phelan said the Navy is exploring the possibility of building ships outside the United States to alleviate pressure on domestic shipbuilding, which faces significant labor capacity challenges.

stories.title: Italy summons Russian ambassador after TV host targets Meloni with stream of insults
stories.summary: Italy summoned Russia's ambassador after a Russian television presenter directed a stream of insults at Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni during a broadcast. Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani confirmed the diplomatic action, which was condemned across Italy's political spectrum and risks further straining Rome-Moscow relations amid the Ukraine conflict.

stories.title: Trump extends Iran ceasefire indefinitely as peace talks stall
stories.summary: President Trump announced Tuesday that the United States would indefinitely extend its ceasefire with Iran as peace talks remain stalled. Pakistan is mediating efforts to bring both sides back to negotiations, while Washington and Tehran have warned that hostilities could resume without a deal.

stories.title: Southern Poverty Law Center indicted on federal fraud charges
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice announced an 11-count federal fraud indictment against the Southern Poverty Law Center over past payments to confidential informants who infiltrated extremist groups including the Ku Klux Klan. SPLC chief executive Bryan Fair called the allegations false and condemned the prosecution.

stories.title: Battleship costs and sub timelines at Sea Air Space
stories.summary: At the Navy League's annual Sea Air Space conference, discussions focused on battleship costs and submarine construction timelines. Reporters Aaron Mehta and Diana Stancy covered highlights from the second day of the event.

stories.title: ‘Donnyland’? Ukraine proposes renaming part of the Donbas in Trump’s honour
stories.summary: Ukraine has proposed renaming part of the Donbas region in honor of U.S. President Donald Trump. Details of the proposal were not immediately elaborated upon.

stories.title: After Israeli flyers in NY high school placed in urinal, board president faces calls to resign
stories.summary: In a New York high school, flyers related to Israel were placed in a urinal, and photographs of the vandalism were posted online. The school board president is now facing calls to resign after her daughter was among those sharing the images.

stories.title: Report: Detained employees of Popcorn Books and Individuum implicate Eksmo executives in ‘extremism’ case over queer literature
stories.summary: Three former employees of Russia's Popcorn Books publishing house, detained over the sale of queer literature, have reportedly told investigators that executives at the Eksmo publishing group were involved in alleged "extremism," according to TASS.

stories.title: Iran to restart domestic flights; charts phased airspace reopening
stories.summary: Iranian government sources said Tehran plans to reopen its airspace in phases, starting with overflight operations, which would provide relief to international airlines connecting Europe with Asia, including Indian carriers.

stories.title: Israeli army jails soldiers for vandalising Jesus statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military sentenced two soldiers to 30 days of military detention and removed them from combat duty for destroying a statue of Jesus in the Christian village of Debl in southern Lebanon. The incident drew widespread condemnation after a photo was shared online.

stories.title: Indonesia’s state energy firm raises fuel prices, risking subsidy strain
stories.summary: Indonesia's state-owned energy company Pertamina raised prices on some non-subsidized fuel products. Economists warned the increase could push more households toward subsidized fuel grades, tightening supplies and adding pressure to a state budget already strained by politically sensitive energy costs.

stories.title: China’s shipyards secure wave of oil tanker orders as Iran war drives demand
stories.summary: Chinese shipyards are securing a wave of new oil tanker orders as the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran worsens crude transport bottlenecks through the Strait of Hormuz. The strait handles about a quarter of the world's seaborne oil. Shipping companies are racing to expand capacity, particularly in very large crude carriers (VLCCs).

stories.title: Iran war live: Trump says ceasefire extended as talks with Tehran in limbo
stories.summary: Lebanon's disaster management unit reported that weeks of Israeli attacks have killed 2,454 people and injured 7,658, as the US-Iran ceasefire was extended with talks remaining in limbo.

stories.title: Russian drone attack on Kharkiv region leaves 11 civilians injured
stories.summary: Eleven civilians were injured in Ukraine's Kharkiv region following a massive Russian drone attack on settlements in the Bohodukhiv district.

stories.title: Condom prices could rise 30% due to Iran war, says world’s top producer Karex
stories.summary: Malaysia-based Karex, the world's largest condom manufacturer, announced plans to raise prices by 20% to 30% due to supply chain disruptions caused by the Iran war. The company, which produces over 5 billion condoms annually for brands including Durex and Trojan, is also experiencing a surge in demand as freight costs and shipping delays reduce customer stockpiles.

stories.title: Trump reads from Bible after high-profile clash with pope
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump and prominent Christian supporters participated in the "America Reads the Bible" event, a marathon Bible reading live-streamed from the Museum of the Bible in Washington. Trump contributed a video reading from the Oval Office. The event was billed as encouraging a return to America's spiritual foundations ahead of the nation's 250th anniversary.

stories.title: Nigeria charges six over alleged coup plot to overthrow Tinubu
stories.summary: Nigeria's government filed 13 criminal charges against six former security officials in Abuja, accusing them of plotting the violent overthrow of President Bola Tinubu's government last year. Court documents detailing the charges were made public on Tuesday, April 21.

stories.title: Russian drones hit agricultural enterprise in Chernihiv region
stories.summary: Russian forces struck an agricultural enterprise in Ukraine's Chernihiv region using drones. The attack targeted civilian agricultural infrastructure.

stories.title: Trump remains ‘in a quandary’ despite Iran war ceasefire extension
stories.summary: Analyst Barbara Slavin described Trump's decision to extend the Iran ceasefire as a relief but cautioned that a diplomatic resolution remains far off, saying the president is still in a quandary.

stories.title: Trump officials consider sending 1,100 Afghans who aided US forces to Congo
stories.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly discussing sending up to 1,100 Afghans who assisted U.S. forces during the Afghanistan war to the Democratic Republic of Congo. The discussions follow President Trump's decision to end an initiative that allowed these Afghans to apply for resettlement in the United States.

stories.title: War update: 194 frontline clashes, Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors remain hottest
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces reported 194 Russian attacks on their positions in a single day, with the heaviest fighting concentrated in the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors of the front line.

stories.title: ‘Reprehensible’: Pakistan condemns storming of Al Aqsa Mosque compound, raising of Israeli flag in its courtyard
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Office condemned the storming of the Al Aqsa Mosque compound and the raising of an Israeli flag in its courtyard, calling the acts "reprehensible" violations of international law that risk escalating regional tensions.

stories.title: Magyar says Netanyahu will face arrest in Hungary
stories.summary: Hungarian opposition figure Péter Magyar stated that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu would face arrest if he visited Hungary, citing the ICC warrant issued in 2024 over alleged crimes against humanity and war crimes in Gaza.

stories.title: New York court rules in favor of Uruguayan fintech dLocal, dismisses investor class action
stories.summary: New York's Appellate Division unanimously upheld the dismissal of a class action lawsuit filed by investors against Uruguayan fintech company dLocal and the investment banks involved in its 2021 IPO. The court found no material omissions in the company's pre-IPO disclosures.

stories.title: Trump extends Iran truce, demands "unified proposal" from Tehran to negotiate
stories.summary: President Trump announced an indefinite extension of the ceasefire with Iran hours before the two-week truce was set to expire, while maintaining the naval blockade on Iranian ports. Trump conditioned further diplomatic progress on Tehran presenting a "unified proposal" to resume negotiations.

stories.title: Rachel Goldberg-Polin: Mother of murdered hostage Hersh ‘parcels out her pain’ in book
stories.summary: Rachel Goldberg-Polin, mother of murdered hostage Hersh Goldberg-Polin, has published a book titled 'When We See You Again,' providing a personal account of what happened to her son and her family.

stories.title: Black children in England and Wales almost eight times more likely to be strip-searched than white peers – report
stories.summary: A report by the children's commissioner for England found that Black children in England and Wales are almost eight times more likely to be strip-searched by police than white children. Commissioner Rachel de Souza noted that Black children are also overrepresented in incidents where officers use force, including handcuffs, firearms, or Tasers.

stories.title: Frozen Russian assets could fund Special Tribunal, Ukrainian lawmaker says
stories.summary: A Ukrainian lawmaker proposed using frozen Russian assets to fund a Special Tribunal on Russia's crime of aggression against Ukraine. Securing funding remains the primary obstacle to establishing the tribunal.

stories.title: Pakistan’s Sharif thanks Trump for ceasefire extension
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif publicly thanked US President Donald Trump for extending the ceasefire with Iran to allow diplomatic efforts to continue. Sharif expressed hope that both sides would uphold the truce and work toward a comprehensive peace agreement.

stories.title: US Southern Command stands up autonomous unit
stories.summary: U.S. Southern Command established a new unit dedicated to autonomous, semi-autonomous, and unmanned platforms. Once fully operational, the command will be tasked with countering threats across multiple domains using these systems.

stories.title: 'Godfather of denim’: an Italian designer whose Jewish father was murdered at Auschwitz
stories.summary: Italian designer Adriano Goldschmied, known as the godfather of denim and credited with founding or developing at least 50 jean brands, died on April 5 at age 82. His Jewish father was murdered at Auschwitz.

stories.title: Notification declaring local holiday in Rawalpindi on April 22 is fake: DC
stories.summary: Rawalpindi Deputy Commissioner Hassan Waqar Cheema dismissed as fake a notification circulating on social media that claimed a local holiday had been declared in the city for April 22.

stories.title: Russian police probe top publisher in ‘LGBT extremism’ case
stories.summary: Russian police have opened an investigation into a prominent publisher under the country's "LGBT extremism" laws. The case is part of the Kremlin's ongoing expansion of repressive legislation targeting the LGBTQ community in Russia.

stories.title: Russian strikes on Novomykolaivka in Zaporizhzhia region leave seven civilians injured
stories.summary: Russian troops carried out six strikes on the village of Novomykolaivka in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia district, injuring seven civilians.

stories.title: Russia says Africa Corps has freed Russian and Ukrainian nationals abducted in West Africa
stories.summary: Russia's defence ministry announced that its Africa Corps carried out a special operation in Mali that freed a Russian and a Ukrainian citizen. The two men had been abducted in neighbouring Niger in 2024.

stories.title: US says it intercepted ‘stateless sanctioned’ oil vessel in Asia-Pacific, amid Iran crackdown
stories.summary: The United States said it intercepted a stateless, sanctioned oil vessel in the Asia-Pacific region as part of its crackdown on Iranian oil exports. The vessel reportedly loaded approximately two million barrels of crude oil at Iran's Kharg Island on April 5.

stories.title: Chinese university student charged with illegally taking photos of US military planes
stories.summary: Chinese university student Tianrui Liang, 21, was charged with unauthorized photography of U.S. military aircraft in Nebraska. He was arrested at New York's JFK International Airport on April 7 while attempting to return to Scotland, where he studies in Glasgow. His road trip through several states included a stop at an air force base in South Dakota.

stories.title: Zelensky approves new “long-range sanctions” against Russia
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky approved a new set of "long-range sanctions" targeting Russia. The measures are part of Ukraine's ongoing economic pressure campaign against Moscow.

stories.title: IMO says seafarers killed as attacks on Gulf shipping mount
stories.summary: The International Maritime Organization reported that at least 10 seafarers have been killed and others seriously wounded in attacks on commercial vessels in the Persian Gulf since the US-Israeli war on Iran began. Approximately 20,000 civilian seafarers remain aboard vessels in the Gulf facing dwindling supplies and severe psychological stress.

stories.title: Son of Holocaust survivors, granddaughter of a Nazi confront their separate inheritances
stories.summary: A new book titled 'Inheritance: Love, Loss and the Legacy of the Holocaust' brings together the perspectives of a son of Holocaust survivors and the granddaughter of a Nazi, drawing on family letters, archival research, and visits to Europe.

stories.title: Trump extends Iran ceasefire with fate of Pakistan talks left uncertain
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump extended the ceasefire with Iran while ordering the continuation of a naval blockade. Maritime intelligence reports suggest dozens of vessels have evaded US warships enforcing the blockade.

stories.title: Iran foreign ministry spokesperson says Tehran yet to decide on participating in talks with US in Islamabad
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said Tehran had not yet decided whether to attend talks with the United States in Pakistan. He accused Washington of "piracy at sea and state terrorism" over actions against Iranian vessels.

stories.title: Ceasefire hangs in balance as Iranian, US delegations not attending next round of talks - report
stories.summary: Iran's Tasnim news agency reported that Tehran has decided not to attend the second round of US-Iran talks in Pakistan, casting further doubt on the future of the ceasefire as it nears expiration.

stories.title: Extension of US-Iran ceasefire gives 'breathing space'
stories.summary: The BBC's Lyse Doucet reported from Tehran as President Trump announced an extension of the US-Iran ceasefire. Observers said the extension provides breathing space for further negotiations.

stories.title: Russia just destroyed one of Ukraine’s best indoor athletics arenas
stories.summary: A Russian drone strike on April 21 destroyed the only specialized indoor track and field facility in Ukraine's Sumy Oblast, eliminating the region's best athletics arena.

stories.title: Amnesty warns that 'predator' leaders seek to impose new 'world order'
stories.summary: Amnesty International Secretary General Agnes Callamard warned that "predator" leaders including U.S. President Donald Trump, Russia's Vladimir Putin, and Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu are seeking to impose a new world order.

stories.title: In Tehran, Iranians try to enjoy ceasefire while it lasts
stories.summary: Residents of Tehran are attempting to enjoy daily life during the ceasefire in the Iran conflict while fearing its expiration. Many Iranians expressed concern over the war's economic impact and a strict internet blackout that remains in place.

stories.title: Eight arrested as British police probe suspected anti-Semitic arson attacks
stories.summary: British police arrested eight people in connection with suspected antisemitic arson attacks, including an alleged plot targeting a venue linked to the Jewish community. The arrests are part of a broader investigation into a wave of such incidents.

stories.title: Hotpot, bubble tea and sportswear: China's new exports take on the world
stories.summary: A new wave of Chinese consumer brands—including hotpot restaurant chains, bubble tea franchises, and sportswear companies—is expanding internationally. The trend marks a shift from China's traditional image as a producer of cheap, mass-produced goods.

stories.title: After extending truce, Trump claims Iran ‘collapsing financially’ over Hormuz closure
stories.summary: After extending the US-Iran ceasefire, Trump claimed Iran is collapsing financially due to the Hormuz closure. Pakistani PM thanked Trump and expressed hope for a comprehensive peace deal during planned talks in Islamabad. Reports also emerged of Palestinian homes being torched by settlers.

stories.title: Watch: Several killed in fireworks unit blast in Kerala | Above the Fold | 21.04.2026
stories.summary: A fireworks unit explosion in Thrissur, Kerala, killed several people. Separately, India conducted diplomatic outreach to West Asia including Saudi Arabia, while campaigning ended ahead of Tamil Nadu and West Bengal Assembly polls.

stories.title: Trump’s $1.9 trillion defence budget includes ships, jets and Golden Dome
stories.summary: President Donald Trump proposed a $1.9 trillion U.S. defence budget that includes funding for ships, jets, and the Golden Dome missile defence system. Senior officials described the budget as the largest investment in drone warfare and counter-drone technology in U.S. history.

stories.title: Zelensky on €90B EU loan: No grounds for blocking it anymore
stories.summary: President Zelensky stated that Ukraine has fulfilled all requirements to unlock €90 billion in EU support and said there are no remaining grounds for blocking the loan.

stories.title: Romanian PM says he'll lead minority government after leftist Social Democrats walk out
stories.summary: Romanian Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan announced he will lead a minority government after the leftist Social Democrats, the coalition's largest party, withdrew their support. Bolojan said the move is necessary to ensure reforms required to access European Union funds continue.

stories.title: China and Philippines taking ‘baby steps’ towards better relations: Manila’s ambassador
stories.summary: The Philippines is pursuing incremental steps to stabilize relations with China before addressing more contentious issues such as the South China Sea dispute, according to Manila's ambassador to Beijing, Jaime FlorCruz.

stories.title: Iran reportedly rejects Pakistan talks, citing US ‘excessive demands’
stories.summary: Iran has reportedly decided not to attend planned peace talks in Pakistan, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. Tehran cited what it called excessive US demands, with officials concluding the negotiations would be unproductive.

stories.title: Japan scraps a ban on lethal weapons exports in a change of its postwar pacifist policy
stories.summary: Japan scrapped its longstanding ban on lethal weapons exports on Tuesday, marking a significant departure from its postwar pacifist policy. The decision is aimed at strengthening Japan's arms industry amid growing security concerns over Chinese and North Korean military aggression.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1518: EU’s €90 billion loan for Ukraine set for Wednesday vote
stories.summary: The European Union is set to vote on a €90 billion loan package for Ukraine. Hungary has signaled it is preparing to lift its veto on the Ukrainian aid measure.

stories.title: 'Landmark' EU court ruling rejects Hungary anti-LGBTQ law
stories.summary: The European Court of Justice ruled Tuesday that Hungary's anti-LGBTQ legislation violates EU rules, in what has been called the largest human rights case in the bloc's history. The European Commission, 16 member states, and the European Parliament brought the case against Hungary before the court.

stories.title: Uncertainty clouds Iran talks as ceasefire deadline nears
stories.summary: As of 7:30 p.m. Pakistan time, Iran had not formally confirmed its participation in U.S.-Iran talks in Islamabad, according to Pakistan's Information Minister, as a ceasefire deadline approached.

stories.title: Can Israel’s economy sustain conflicts on multiple fronts?
stories.summary: The Bank of Israel estimates that Israel's war with Iran cost 35 billion shekels ($11.52 billion) in budgetary expenses. Operations in Gaza through 2025 consumed approximately 8.6% of the country's annual GDP.

stories.title: ‘World Parliament’ platform used by Russia to spread propaganda – Ukrainian Vice Speaker
stories.summary: Ukraine's Vice Speaker accused Russia of using the Inter-Parliamentary Union platform to spread propaganda and maintain international legitimacy. The IPU, sometimes called the "World Parliament," has been a venue for Russian narrative promotion.

stories.title: Navy expects construction on first Trump-class battleship to start in FY28
stories.summary: Secretary of the Navy John Phelan said construction on the first Trump-class battleship is expected to begin in fiscal year 2028, with the service currently in discussions with two potential vendors.

stories.title: Israel kicks off 78th Independence Day festivities with annual torch-lighting ceremony
stories.summary: Israel marked its 78th Independence Day with an annual torch-lighting ceremony. Among the torchbearers were Argentine President Javier Milei, a disabled IDF veteran, and an Iranian former judicial official. Prime Minister Netanyahu delivered a pre-recorded speech highlighting military achievements.

stories.title: United States Treasury Department imposes fresh sanctions against suppliers of weapons to Iran
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department imposed new sanctions targeting suppliers of weapons to Iran. The action came as a two-week ceasefire announced by President Trump was set to expire in the coming days.

stories.title: Russian social network VK removes diabetes mutual aid section at internet regulator’s request
stories.summary: Russian social network VK removed a mutual-aid section from a diabetes community called "Nyura Sharikova. Sakharny Diabet" at the request of internet regulator Roskomnadzor. The community's founder announced the removal on April 21.

stories.title: Trump extends ceasefire, orders military to maintain Iran blockade
stories.summary: President Trump posted on Truth Social that he directed the US military to continue the blockade of Iran while extending the ceasefire. The extension came at the request of Pakistan's Field Marshal Asim Munir and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to allow Iranian leaders time to formulate a unified proposal.

stories.title: From Africa, Pope Leo warns humanity’s future is ‘tragically compromised’
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV delivered forceful remarks during a 10-day tour of Africa, warning that humanity's future is "tragically compromised." The pontiff has adopted an assertive speaking style throughout the trip.

stories.title: Saildrone announces new USV class aimed at anti-submarine warfare
stories.summary: Saildrone announced Spectre, a new class of unmanned surface vessel designed for anti-submarine warfare. Sea trials for the platform are planned for early 2027.

stories.title: Hezbollah says attack on Israel was response to ceasefire violations
stories.summary: Hezbollah said it launched rockets and attack drones at a target in northern Israel in retaliation for what it called Israeli violations of a 10-day ceasefire. The group said the targeted site had been used to shell a town in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: At Senegal forum, Niger and Mali say neighbours sponsor terrorism
stories.summary: The foreign ministers of Niger and Mali, speaking at a forum in Diamniadio, Senegal, accused neighbouring countries of sponsoring terrorism. Both nations, which formally left the West African regional bloc ECOWAS last year, indicated willingness to cooperate with the organization on some matters.

stories.title: Israel to mark Independence Day with 'heads held high', says Bennett as opposition honors fallen
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett said Israel would mark its Independence Day with 'heads held high,' honoring families who lost loved ones. Opposition leaders also held ceremonies to remember fallen soldiers.

stories.title: US-China AI race must strike a balance between security and openness
stories.summary: The U.S. House Select Committee on China released a report alleging Beijing is aggressively acquiring frontier AI capabilities through both market access and theft. The findings are shaping Washington's policy approach to technology competition with China.

stories.title: Trump extends ceasefire, says giving Iran time to negotiate
stories.summary: President Trump indefinitely extended the U.S. ceasefire with Iran to allow more time for negotiations, crediting a request from mediator Pakistan, but maintained a naval blockade of Iranian ports.

stories.title: Florida to open criminal investigation into OpenAI over ChatGPT’s influence on alleged mass shooter
stories.summary: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier announced a criminal investigation into OpenAI to determine whether its ChatGPT tool offered "significant advice" to a gunman accused of carrying out a mass shooting in the state last year.

stories.title: War in Iran is causing biggest energy crisis in history, IEA says
stories.summary: The International Energy Agency declared that the war in Iran is causing the biggest energy crisis in history. IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol confirmed the severity of the disruption to global energy markets.

stories.title: Myanmar’s military government rebuffed on peace talks offer
stories.summary: Myanmar's military chief Min Aung Hlaing was elected president by parliament following elections widely criticized as illegitimate. His government's offer of peace talks has been rebuffed by opposition groups.

stories.title: Zelensky, Merz discuss current priorities in bilateral and international cooperation
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz discussed priorities for bilateral cooperation and coordination within multilateral formats with international partners.

stories.title: A Kashmir tourist hotspot became a deadly bloodbath. A year on, the pain remains unbearable
stories.summary: One year after militants killed 26 people at a tourist site in Indian-administered Kashmir, bereaved families continue to struggle with their losses.

stories.title: Air Force eyes massive boost for F-15EX fleet
stories.summary: The U.S. Air Force's fiscal 2027 budget proposal includes a significant expansion of the F-15EX fleet and increased funding for the F-35 Joint Strike Fighter, while slowing the planned retirement of A-10 Warthog aircraft.

stories.title: EU weighs more US jet fuel, cleaner aviation amid Iran war strains
stories.summary: The European Commission is evaluating increased imports of U.S. jet fuel, including Jet A grade, to address aviation fuel supply strains caused by the Iran war. The EU is also examining cleaner aviation fuel alternatives as part of its response.

stories.title: Macron says Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon key to stability
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron and Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam held a joint news conference in Paris ahead of Lebanon-Israel talks in Washington. Macron called for Israeli withdrawal from Lebanon, internationally backed Hezbollah disarmament, and reconstruction of southern Lebanon.

stories.title: China’s new Type 076 ‘drone carrier’ to take part in South China Sea training drills
stories.summary: China's new Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan, described as a "drone carrier," has departed Shanghai for sea trials in the South China Sea, where the U.S., Philippines, and Japan are simultaneously conducting joint military exercises.

stories.title: More than $71 billion needed over next decade to rebuild Gaza: UN, EU
stories.summary: A joint EU-UN assessment estimates that more than $71 billion will be needed over the next decade to rebuild war-ravaged Gaza. The report described unprecedented loss of life and a catastrophic humanitarian crisis in the Palestinian territory.

stories.title: Iran Foreign Ministry condemns arrests in UAE as 'baseless'
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry condemned arrests of Iranian nationals in the UAE as "baseless," while accusing Gulf states of allowing U.S. forces to launch attacks from their territory during the conflict.

stories.title: Minority rights resurface in Slovak-Hungarian relations after Magyar's win
stories.summary: The rights of Slovakia's ethnic Hungarian minority have re-emerged as a bilateral issue after Hungarian election winner Peter Magyar protested Slovak legislation reinforcing post-World War Two retribution acts. Magyar raised the concern in his first phone call with Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico.

stories.title: Ukraine reopens damaged Druzhba pipeline to unlock €90 billion EU loan
stories.summary: Ukraine announced it has repaired the damaged Druzhba oil pipeline, removing the final obstacle to receiving a long-delayed €90 billion EU loan. The repair forces Kyiv to resume Russian oil flows to Hungary and Slovakia despite its push for tighter sanctions on Moscow.

stories.title: France freezes some spending to offset €6 billion fallout from Iran war
stories.summary: France announced a freeze on some government spending to offset at least €6 billion in economic costs stemming from the Iran war. The fallout includes increased defense spending, business and household support measures, and rising borrowing costs.

stories.title: Michelle Bachelet hopes world is 'finally ready' for a female UN chief
stories.summary: Former Chilean President Michelle Bachelet said Tuesday she hopes the world is ready for the first female United Nations secretary-general as she campaigns to succeed António Guterres. Bachelet framed her candidacy as an opportunity to restore trust in the organization during a period of global crisis.

stories.title: Russia’s Investigative Committee orders review of children’s author Grigory Oster’s poetry collection
stories.summary: Alexander Bastrykin, head of Russia's Investigative Committee, ordered a review of books by children's author Grigory Oster over content deemed to raise "pedagogical concerns," the agency announced on April 21.

stories.title: Russia unable to sharply increase number of drones used in its strikes on Ukraine – expert
stories.summary: An expert assessment indicates Russia is unable to sharply increase the number of drones used in strikes on Ukraine. The main limiting factor, beyond munitions availability, is the number of launch sites accessible to Russian forces.

stories.title: 4 suspects arrested in Karachi in action against gangs involved in leaking matric exams
