stories.summary: Karachi's Special Investigation Unit arrested four suspects involved in leaking matriculation exam papers. Police identified at least eight WhatsApp groups used to share leaked exam content.

stories.title: Trump says he does not want to extend ceasefire with Iran
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated in a CNBC interview on Tuesday that he does not want to extend the ceasefire with Iran. Trump said the United States holds a strong negotiating position and predicted the outcome would be a favorable deal.

stories.title: China Doesn’t Always Win When the U.S. Loses
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the Iran war challenges zero-sum assumptions about great-power competition, suggesting that U.S. setbacks do not automatically translate into strategic gains for China.

stories.title: Pakistan says formal response from Iran regarding participation in 2nd round of talks ‘still awaited’
stories.summary: Pakistan's Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said Iran had not yet formally confirmed its participation in a second round of U.S.-Iran peace talks in Islamabad. He noted the ceasefire was set to expire on April 22 and urged Iran to respond before the deadline.

stories.title: Two Palestinians killed in West Bank village by Israeli settlers, say witnesses
stories.summary: Two Palestinians, aged 14 and 32, were killed by Israeli settlers in a West Bank village, according to witnesses and the Palestinian Health Ministry.

stories.title: Was Donald Trump 'blocked' from using the nuclear codes against Iran?
stories.summary: Former CIA analyst Larry Johnson alleged on a podcast that President Trump sought to use nuclear weapons against Iran during an emergency White House meeting but was stopped by Joint Chiefs Chairman General Dan Caine. The claim has fueled growing concerns among lawmakers about Trump's decision-making.

stories.title: Four Israeli children saved in organ transplant marathon
stories.summary: Four Israeli children received life-saving organ transplants in a medical marathon, including a liver transplant for a 9-year-old girl, two kidney transplants for an 18-year-old and a toddler, and a heart transplant for a 3-year-old.

stories.title: Trump extends ceasefire to give Iran more time to negotiate
stories.summary: President Trump announced he is extending the ceasefire with Iran to provide additional time for peace negotiations. The US military blockade of Iran remains in effect during the extension.

stories.title: Vance still in Washington as uncertainty mounts over US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Planned US-Iran talks in Pakistan remained in doubt as Tehran had not confirmed its participation and Vice President JD Vance's departure from Washington was delayed. The uncertainty arose as the two-week ceasefire neared expiration.

stories.title: US issues more Iran sanctions on eve of possible talks in Pakistan
stories.summary: The Trump administration imposed sanctions on 14 individuals and entities allegedly linked to Iran's arms industry. The sanctions were announced on the eve of possible diplomatic talks in Pakistan.

stories.title: Canadian who was detained by China warns against Carney’s electric vehicle deal
stories.summary: Michael Kovrig, a Canadian former diplomat detained in China from 2018 to 2021, warned that Prime Minister Mark Carney's electric vehicle deal with Beijing risks creating a strategic dependency that China could exploit for political coercion.

stories.title: In south Lebanon’s Nabatieh, residents fear a return to war
stories.summary: Residents of Nabatieh in south Lebanon expressed fears of a return to war amid ongoing tensions. Israeli strikes on Lebanon have killed more than 2,300 people and displaced over a million.

stories.title: Israel to compete in Cheerleading World Championship for first time in history
stories.summary: Israel will compete in the Cheerleading World Championship for the first time. Team manager Ludmila Yasinskaya-Demari, founder of the Israel Cheer Union, highlighted the symbolic connection between the sport and Israeli society's current needs.

stories.title: EU resumes aid to Ethiopia suspended over Tigray war
stories.summary: The European Union is set to resume budgetary aid to Ethiopia that was suspended when civil war erupted in the Tigray region in 2020. Separately, Nigeria is experiencing jet fuel shortages driven by disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Trump says U.S. in ‘very, very strong’ position for Iran talks
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said the United States is in a "very, very strong" position ahead of peace talks with Iran. He also called on Tehran to free eight women he said face execution to improve prospects for the negotiations.

stories.title: Zelensky discusses EUR 90B loan in conversation with von der Leyen
stories.summary: President Zelensky discussed unblocking a €90 billion support package for Ukraine in a conversation with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen.

stories.title: SC to function with minimal staff on Wednesday; no judicial work to be conducted at FCC for 2nd consecutive day
stories.summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court in Islamabad announced it would operate with minimal staff on Wednesday, while the Federal Constitutional Court suspended judicial work for a second day. The closures stem from heightened security measures for anticipated U.S.-Iran peace talks in the capital's Red Zone.

stories.title: Europe should focus on own security as global threats mount, Dutch intelligence agency says
stories.summary: The Dutch military intelligence agency MIVD said Europe must take greater responsibility for its own security, citing mounting global threats. The agency pointed to pressure on Western alliances and China's support for Russia's war in Ukraine as key concerns.

stories.title: EU eyes options as Iran conflict threatens jet fuel shortages
stories.summary: The European Union is exploring contingency options as a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz threatens jet fuel supplies. Europe is heavily dependent on imported jet fuel, making the disruption a significant concern for the bloc's aviation sector.

stories.title: Sudan refugees returning home face new ‘struggle for survival’: UN
stories.summary: The United Nations has warned that Sudanese refugees returning home face a severe humanitarian crisis. Returnees are encountering heavily damaged homes, water supplies, health facilities, and electricity infrastructure, with chronic underinvestment compounding the challenges.

stories.title: US imposes new sanctions against suppliers of weapons to Iran
stories.summary: The US Treasury imposed new sanctions on 14 individuals and companies, as well as aircraft, linked to supplying rocket and drone components to Iran. Treasury Secretary Bessent stated the Iranian regime would be held accountable.

stories.title: Taiwan president cancels Africa trip blaming Chinese pressure
stories.summary: Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te cancelled a planned trip to Africa after at least one country, Madagascar, denied overflight permission. Taipei attributed the denials to pressure from China.

stories.title: EU imposes sanctions on two Russian entities it says are linked to disinformation
stories.summary: The European Council imposed sanctions on two Russian entities it said were linked to propaganda and disinformation operations directed from Moscow. The sanctions were announced on Tuesday, April 21, in Brussels.

stories.title: Dozens of US lawmakers have been accused of sexual harassment, study finds
stories.summary: A study by the National Women's Defense League found that 53 workplace sexual harassment allegations have been made against at least 30 U.S. House and Senate lawmakers over the past two decades. Nine of the accused lawmakers still hold office.

stories.title: Trump announces Iran ceasefire extension but says blockade remains
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced an extension of the ceasefire with Iran but stated that the naval blockade would remain in place. Trump said military attacks would be paused until Iranian leaders present a unified proposal to end the war.

stories.title: Lebanon PM and Macron to discuss bolstering country’s position in Israel talks
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister and French President Emmanuel Macron are set to discuss strengthening Lebanon's negotiating position in talks with Israel. The United States will host ambassador-level discussions with Israel and Lebanon on April 23.

stories.title: Zelensky, Costa agree to meet to discuss cooperation in Drone Deal format
stories.summary: President Zelensky and European Council President António Costa agreed to meet to discuss cooperation under the Drone Deal format. They also discussed unblocking €90 billion in EU aid for Ukraine.

stories.title: Health minister says medicine stocks sufficient to meet demand for next 5 to 6 months
stories.summary: Pakistan's Health Minister Mustafa Kamal said the country holds sufficient medicine stocks for five to six months. The Drug Regulatory Authority and pharmaceutical industry coordinated to maintain supply amid international challenges.

stories.title: Kyiv court jails patrol officer who ran from mass shooting scene
stories.summary: A Kyiv court ordered the detention of 27-year-old patrol officer Mykhailo Drobnytsky, one of two officers who fled the scene during the mass shooting in Kyiv on April 18.

stories.title: Germany, Italy block bid to suspend EU-Israel trade agreement
stories.summary: Germany and Italy blocked an effort within the European Union to suspend the bloc's association agreement with Israel. The move prevented the EU from taking collective trade action against Israel.

stories.title: 6 Things I Wish I Knew About the U.S. and Israeli Positions on Iran
stories.summary: A commentary identifies six key knowledge gaps regarding U.S. and Israeli positions on the Iran conflict that make it difficult to assess how the war will conclude.

stories.title: Torture and beating photos seized during Lyons gang raids in Spain
stories.summary: Spanish police conducting raids against alleged members of the Lyons crime group on the Costa Del Sol seized photographs depicting torture and beatings linked to the organization.

stories.title: U.S., Iran signal they will return to Pakistan for ceasefire talks, officials say
stories.summary: Both the United States and Iran signaled they would return to Pakistan for ceasefire talks. President Trump had accused Iran of repeatedly violating the ceasefire in the broader West Asian conflict.

stories.title: Trump’s US Fed nominee Warsh vows independence, says he’s no ‘sock puppet’
stories.summary: Kevin Warsh, Donald Trump's nominee to lead the US Federal Reserve, testified at his confirmation hearing and pledged to maintain the institution's independence. His hearing drew scrutiny amid Trump's renewed calls for interest rate cuts.

stories.title: Teenager in Russia injured after picking up explosive device disguised as bundle of banknotes
stories.summary: A teenager in the Russian city of Perm sustained burns after picking up an explosive device disguised as a bundle of banknotes that detonated on contact, according to the regional Territorial Security Ministry and Interfax.

stories.title: Russia's Sergei Shoigu says safety of Russians in Transnistria under threat, TASS reports
stories.summary: Sergei Shoigu, secretary of Russia's Security Council, declared that Russian citizens in Moldova's breakaway Transnistria region face threats to their safety. Analysts note Russia is employing tactics similar to those used to justify intervention in eastern Ukraine and Donbas.

stories.title: Russia’s state-backed messaging app Max renamed ’Макс’ (Maks) in app stores amid law restricting foreign loanwords
stories.summary: Russia's state-backed messaging app Max has been renamed "Макс" (Maks) in the App Store and Google Play, reflecting compliance with a Russian law restricting the use of foreign loanwords.

stories.title: Houthi leader warns war likely to continue beyond ceasefire
stories.summary: Houthi leader Abdel-Malik al-Houthi warned in a televised speech that fighting is likely to continue beyond the current US-Iran ceasefire, describing the truce as merely a pause in a continuous conflict. He said the prospect of regional escalation remains high.

stories.title: Nuclear deal between Iran, US illusory if IAEA not involved, Director Grossi says - Telegraph
stories.summary: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi warned that any nuclear deal between Iran and the United States would be illusory without IAEA verification. He stressed that without monitoring, an agreement amounts to an unverifiable promise.

stories.title: Russian strike in Dnipropetrovsk region leaves three people injured, damages minibus
stories.summary: A Russian attack in the Pokrovske community of Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region damaged a scheduled minibus and injured three people.

stories.title: NATO criticises Russian and Chinese nuclear stances, urges cooperation with US
stories.summary: NATO criticized Russia and China's nuclear arms policies and urged both nations to engage with the United States to improve stability and transparency. The alliance made the remarks ahead of an upcoming international conference on nuclear arms.

stories.title: Israel will face resistance if troops stay in Lebanon, Speaker Berri says
stories.summary: Lebanese parliament speaker Nabih Berri warned that Israeli forces occupying parts of southern Lebanon would face resistance if they do not withdraw. The warning came ahead of U.S.-mediated talks scheduled for later in the week.

stories.title: Ukraine hits Russian oil pumping station, part of Druzhba pipeline
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck an oil-pumping and dispatch facility in Russia's Samara region that is part of the Druzhba pipeline network. An official from Ukraine's SBU security service confirmed the overnight attack on Tuesday.

stories.title: Two CIA agents reportedly killed in car crash in Mexican state of Chihuahua
stories.summary: Two CIA agents were reportedly killed in a car crash in the Mexican state of Chihuahua. Their presence in a law enforcement convoy has raised questions about US operations on Mexican soil and respect for Mexico's sovereignty.

stories.title: EU divided on suspension of Israel pact as Spain pushes for action
stories.summary: EU member states including Spain and Ireland pushed for suspending the bloc's association agreement with Israel, but the European Union remained divided on the issue. The debate took place at a meeting in Brussels on Tuesday.

stories.title: South Sudan to hold elections in December as fighting rages on
stories.summary: South Sudan has announced plans to hold elections in December after years of delays, even as the country faces ongoing fighting and the threat of renewed civil war.

stories.title: Israeli rabbi who bulldozed Gaza honoured as torchbearer
stories.summary: Rabbi Avraham Zarbiv, known for documenting his use of a bulldozer to destroy structures in Gaza, was honored as a torchbearer during Israel's Independence Day celebrations.

stories.title: Iran state TV says ceasefire ends at midnight GMT
stories.summary: Iranian state television announced the US-Iran ceasefire, in effect since April 8, would expire at midnight GMT on Wednesday. However, President Trump indicated a later deadline, and mediator Pakistan offered yet another timeline, ending at 23:50 GMT.

stories.title: Zelensky discusses areas of cooperation between Ukraine and Chile with President Kast Rist
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky held talks with Chilean President José Antonio Kast Rist to discuss areas of bilateral cooperation between Ukraine and Chile.

stories.title: Video: Israeli soldiers sing national anthem on ruins of Lebanese town
stories.summary: Israeli soldiers were filmed singing Israel's national anthem while standing on the ruins of a demolished town in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: My life inside Israel's panopticon
stories.summary: Palestinians in the West Bank face pervasive Israeli surveillance and rising settler violence, creating a climate of constant fear even within their homes, according to writer Falasteen Mansour.

stories.title: Significant 'overlap' between auto industry and arms manufacturing, expert says
stories.summary: European automobile manufacturers are increasingly pivoting toward producing combat drones and defense systems as the continent seeks to rearm against Russian threats. Experts note significant overlap in engineering expertise between the automotive and arms industries.

stories.title: India bats for greater Global South representation in UNSC
stories.summary: India called for greater Global South representation on the UN Security Council, particularly in the permanent member category, at Inter-Governmental Negotiations on UNSC reform.

stories.title: Lebanon war puts pregnant women at risk
stories.summary: Lebanon's healthcare system is under severe strain despite a temporary ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah. Thousands of displaced pregnant women face significant difficulties accessing medical services.

stories.title: IDF confirms Hezbollah drone caused sirens in northern Israel in violation of ceasefire
stories.summary: The Israeli military confirmed that a Hezbollah drone triggered warning sirens along the Lebanese border in northern Israel, constituting a violation of the existing ceasefire. However, the IDF initially classified the incident as a false identification.

stories.title: At 78, Israel’s defense-tech edge is reshaping modern warfare - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Israel's defense-technology sector, as the country marks 78 years of independence, has become deeply embedded in its national defense strategy and is reshaping modern warfare.

stories.title: Iran undecided on talks as ceasefire enters final hours; Trump: ‘They have to negotiate’
stories.summary: US-Iran ceasefire talks remained uncertain as Tehran had not confirmed participation and Vice President JD Vance delayed his planned trip to Pakistan. Israel was reportedly preparing for a possible resumption of war amid diminishing prospects for a deal.

stories.title: Nearly 8,000 people died or disappeared trying to migrate in 2025
stories.summary: The International Organization for Migration reported that nearly 8,000 people died or disappeared on migration routes in 2024, with sea routes to Europe being the deadliest. The UN agency noted many victims were lost in "invisible shipwrecks" that go unrecorded.

stories.title: Ukraine completes repairs on Druzhba oil pipeline, it can resume operations - Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky announced that Ukraine has completed repairs on a section of the Druzhba oil pipeline damaged by a Russian strike. The pipeline is now ready to resume operations.

stories.title: Kyiv shooter quarrelled with neighbour before attack, minister says
stories.summary: Ukrainian Interior Minister Ihor Klymenko said the gunman who killed seven people in a mass shooting in Kyiv on Saturday had quarrelled with a neighbour before opening fire on passersby. The information was reported by public broadcaster Suspilne.

stories.title: FedEx faces French ‘genocide’ complaint over Israel cargoes
stories.summary: FedEx faces a legal complaint in France accusing the company of transporting parts for Israeli aircraft involved in bombing Gaza. The complaint alleges complicity in what the plaintiffs characterize as genocide.

stories.title: Spain renews push to punish Israel after Orban’s loss
stories.summary: Spain renewed its push for EU sanctions against Israel following the electoral defeat of Hungarian leader Viktor Orban, who had consistently blocked any EU attempts to impose punitive measures on Israel.

stories.title: Lebanon says €500m needed for humanitarian response as ceasefire holds
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said Lebanon requires €500 million over the next six months to address humanitarian needs as a fragile ceasefire with Israel holds. At least 2,450 people have been killed and over 7,600 wounded in six weeks of fighting.

stories.title: U.S. forces board tanker in Indian Ocean, previously sanctioned for smuggling Iranian crude oil
stories.summary: U.S. forces boarded the tanker Tifani in the Indian Ocean between Sri Lanka and Indonesia. The vessel had previously been sanctioned for smuggling Iranian crude oil.

stories.title: Russian police raid book publisher accused of pushing ‘gay propaganda’
stories.summary: Russian police raided a book publisher in Moscow accused of promoting 'gay propaganda,' part of the Kremlin's broader crackdown on social liberalism and political dissent.

stories.title: Italian mail blunder and mistrust hinder crackdown on Chinese gangs
stories.summary: Italian authorities face difficulties cracking down on Chinese criminal gangs due to mistrust and bureaucratic failures, including a mail delivery blunder. The episode reflects broader paralysis surrounding Beijing's efforts to cooperate with Italian law enforcement.

stories.title: Cherfilus-McCormick is third lawmaker to quit, as wave of scandal swamps US Congress
stories.summary: Democratic Representative Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick of Florida resigned from the U.S. House ahead of a House Ethics Committee hearing over campaign finance violations, becoming the third lawmaker to step down in just over a week.

stories.title: Zelensky says Ukraine has completed repairs on Druzhba pipeline, which carries Russian oil to Europe
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on April 21 that specialists completed repairs on a section of the Druzhba oil pipeline, which carries Russian oil to Europe and which Kyiv says was damaged by a Russian military strike.

stories.title: US Navy to integrate PAC-3 MSE interceptor missile with Aegis Combat System
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy plans to integrate Lockheed Martin's PAC-3 MSE interceptor missile with the Aegis Combat System aboard its warships. The integration aims to enhance shipboard missile defense capabilities.

stories.title: 'No decision' on joining talks with US,  Iranian foreign ministry spokesman tells BBC
stories.summary: Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei told the BBC that Tehran has made "no decision" on joining talks with the United States. He expressed concern about the US naval blockade of Iranian ports and the seizure of an Iranian vessel.

stories.title: Pentagon seeks funds for Golden Dome, drones, AI in largest-ever budget request
stories.summary: The Pentagon submitted its largest-ever budget request, seeking funds for the Golden Dome missile defense shield, drones, artificial intelligence, data infrastructure, and the defense industrial base.

stories.title: Russians strike Bohodukhiv in Kharkiv region again, two people wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out a repeated strike on the city of Bohodukhiv in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, wounding two women.

stories.title: Russia Says Freed 2 Hostages Taken by Jihadists in Niger
stories.summary: Russia's Defense Ministry said its Africa Corps freed two hostages in Mali who had been captured by jihadists in Niger. The hostages were employees of a Russian geology company.

stories.title: EU expects first loan tranche to Ukraine end-May/early June - Dombrovskis
stories.summary: The EU expects to disburse the first tranche of its 90 billion euro loan to Ukraine by late May or early June, according to a senior EU official. Ukraine's funding needs for 2026 are covered, with other international donors providing bridging finance in the interim.

stories.title: Pentagon officials broadly detail $55 billion drone plan under DAWG
stories.summary: Pentagon officials outlined a $55 billion drone development plan under the Drone Augmented Warfighting Group (DAWG). The majority of the funding relies on reconciliation measures, similar to the approach used for the proposed Office of Strategic Capital loan program expansion.

stories.title: Nicaragua’s president says Trump ‘mentally deranged’ over war on Iran
stories.summary: Nicaraguan President Daniel Ortega called U.S. President Donald Trump 'mentally deranged' over the American military campaign against Iran.

stories.title: EU foreign ministers reject proposal to suspend association agreement with Israel
stories.summary: EU foreign ministers rejected a proposal by Ireland, Spain, and Slovenia to partially suspend the EU-Israel association agreement. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the proposal remains on the table but lacks sufficient support among member states.

stories.title: US-Iran talks are in doubt as ceasefire nears an end
stories.summary: U.S. officials announced that Vice President JD Vance's trip to Pakistan for peace talks with Iran has been put on hold as the two-week ceasefire nears expiration. Iran said it had not yet decided whether to send a delegation to the talks.

stories.title: US forces detain Iran-linked tanker Tifani with ceasefire talks on edge
stories.summary: U.S. forces detained the Iran-linked oil tanker Tifani, which is under sanctions for smuggling Iranian crude. The seizure was carried out under Washington's policy of intercepting all Tehran-linked vessels as ceasefire talks remain uncertain.

stories.title: Russian man fined for posting photo of cat that resembles Hitler
stories.summary: A district court in Sochi fined a Russian man 1,000 rubles for publicly displaying Nazi symbols after he posted a photo of a cat said to resemble Adolf Hitler. The case was reported by independent outlets Verstka and Mediazona.

stories.title: No Iran delegation sent to US talks yet as truce expiry nears
stories.summary: No Iranian delegation has been sent to Islamabad for talks with the United States as the fragile truce between the two countries nears expiration. Separately, Israel and Lebanon are scheduled to hold a second round of talks in Washington on April 23.

stories.title: Rats, fleas plague Gaza’s displaced as temperatures rise
stories.summary: Displaced residents in Gaza are facing infestations of rats and fleas as temperatures rise. Nearly all of Gaza's population has been displaced by Israeli evacuation orders and airstrikes during the war with Hamas.

stories.title: Secretary General of European Council names main obstacle to launching Special Tribunal for crime of aggression by Russia
stories.summary: The Secretary General of the European Council identified unclear cost estimates and lack of concrete budget commitments from participating countries as the main obstacles to launching the Special Tribunal for Russia's crime of aggression against Ukraine.

stories.title: Report: Russian authorities search homes of Eksmo publishing executives, detain CEO
stories.summary: Russian law enforcement searched the homes of executives at Moscow-based publishing house Eksmo, according to pro-Kremlin TV channel REN TV. The CEO was reportedly detained.

stories.title: School board president from New York faces calls to resign over daughter's antisemitic remarks
stories.summary: A school board president in Scarsdale, New York, faces calls to resign after her daughter made antisemitic remarks. Flyers for an 'IsraelFest' event celebrating Israel's Independence Day at Scarsdale High School were found placed in a bathroom urinal.

stories.title: Russia Removes 2 Decades of Court Statistics From Public Access
stories.summary: Russian authorities removed approximately two decades of court statistics from public access. The data had been used by researchers to track trends in cases involving treason, military-related offenses, sabotage, and terrorism justification.

stories.title: Ukraine says Druzhba pipeline running Russian oil to Europe can resume work
stories.summary: Ukraine announced that the Druzhba pipeline, which carries Russian oil to Europe, can resume operations. Kyiv expressed hope the pipeline's restoration would help unlock a pending EU loan, with the bloc's foreign policy chief signaling a 'positive decision.'

stories.title: 7,900 people died, disappeared on migration routes in 2025: UN
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that 7,900 people died or disappeared on migration routes in 2025. The cumulative total of dead and missing migrants since 2014 has surpassed 80,000.

stories.title: Nigeria: French Retailer Carrefour Enters Nigeria, Guinea in Franchise Deals
stories.summary: French retailer Carrefour announced franchise agreements with local partners to enter Nigeria and Guinea, expanding its presence in West Africa as part of its Carrefour 2030 emerging-markets growth strategy.

stories.title: Taiwan president blames China for forced cancellation of Eswatini trip
stories.summary: Taiwanese President Lai Ching-te cancelled a planned trip to Eswatini, Taiwan's sole diplomatic ally in Africa, after the Seychelles, Mauritius, and Madagascar revoked overflight permission. Taiwan's government attributed the revocations to intense pressure from China.

stories.title: Israel will face resistance if troops stay in Lebanon, Lebanese Parliament Speaker says
stories.summary: Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri, a senior Shi'ite statesman and Hezbollah ally, warned that Israel would face continued resistance if its troops remain in Lebanon.

stories.title: Gerasimov lies about 'complete occupation of Luhansk region' for second time – CCD
stories.summary: Ukraine's Center for Countering Disinformation reported that Russian General Gerasimov falsely claimed complete occupation of Luhansk region for the second time. The claim is part of a broader Russian information campaign supporting continuation of the war.

stories.title: PSX gains over 900 points amid geopolitical uncertainty
stories.summary: Pakistan's KSE-100 stock index gained 959 points, or 0.56 percent, closing at 173,155.79 amid geopolitical uncertainty. The index had surged as much as 3,100 points intraday before pulling back.

stories.title: Warsh's path to top Fed job entangled ahead of Senate confirmation hearing
stories.summary: Former Federal Reserve Governor Kevin Warsh appeared before the Senate Banking Committee on Tuesday as part of his confirmation process to lead the US central bank. His path to the role is complicated by a dispute over a Trump administration criminal probe of current Fed Chair Jerome Powell.

stories.title: Russia, North Korea connect road bridge ahead of summer opening
stories.summary: Russia and North Korea have connected a road bridge between the two countries ahead of a planned summer opening. Russia's Transport Ministry said the bridge can handle up to 300 vehicles and 2,850 people per day.

stories.title: Two US officials who died after Mexico drug raid reported to be CIA agents
stories.summary: Mexico opened an investigation into a possible constitutional breach after two U.S. embassy officials who died in a car accident in Chihuahua state were reported to be CIA agents. The officials were returning from a raid on a drug lab when their vehicle plunged down a 200-meter ravine.

stories.title: Trump weighs UAE currency swap as Abu Dhabi hints at yuan option
stories.summary: President Trump is reportedly considering a currency swap arrangement with the UAE as Abu Dhabi signals it may turn to the Chinese yuan. The UAE's oil-reliant economy has been significantly impacted by Iranian attacks during the Middle East war.

stories.title: Canadian military aims to show it can go it alone in the Arctic
stories.summary: Canadian soldiers completed a more than 5,000-kilometre snowmobile patrol over three months across the Arctic, traveling from Inuvik, Northwest Territories, to Churchill, Manitoba. The exercise, conducted in blizzards and temperatures reaching minus 60 degrees Celsius, was designed to demonstrate Canada's ability to independently defend its northern territory.

stories.title: Many Americans question Trump’s temperament amid Iran war, pope spat: Poll
stories.summary: A poll found that 51 per cent of Americans said President Trump's mental sharpness had worsened over the past year. The survey reflected broader public concerns about Trump's temperament amid the Iran war and a public dispute with the Pope.

stories.title: Swedish Intelligence: Russia’s economy is worse than its official data says
stories.summary: Swedish intelligence assessed that Russia's economy is performing worse than official data indicates. However, the agency noted this has not altered Moscow's military objectives.

stories.title: Russia to halt Kazakhstan’s oil flows to Germany via Druzhba, sources say
stories.summary: Russia is set to halt Kazakh oil exports to Germany via the Druzhba pipeline beginning May 1, according to three industry sources. The move would cut off a key transit route for Kazakh crude to European markets.

stories.title: Flu vaccine no longer mandatory for soldiers, says US military chief
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that flu vaccinations will no longer be mandatory for American military personnel, citing the principle of 'medical autonomy' and calling the previous mandate 'overreaching.'

stories.title: Push to bring US and Iran together for talks as ceasefire deadline looms
stories.summary: Efforts are under way to bring the U.S. and Iran together in Pakistan for a new round of talks before the two-week ceasefire expires. President Trump said the U.S. military was prepared to resume attacks if progress was not made, while Iran appeared reluctant to accept the terms.

stories.title: What are the sports impacted by the Saudi PIF's new strategy?
stories.summary: The Saudi Public Investment Fund announced a strategic shift that could affect its investments across multiple sports and clubs worldwide.

stories.title: Israeli settlers open fire on school, killing Palestinian child
stories.summary: Israeli settlers opened fire on a school in the West Bank, killing a Palestinian child. Eyewitnesses reported that Israeli forces prevented Palestinian residents from reaching the school to rescue their children during the attack.

stories.title: Israel jails soldiers for vandalising Jesus statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military sentenced two soldiers to 30 days of detention and removed them from combat duty for destroying a statue of Jesus Christ in the Christian village of Debl in southern Lebanon, following widespread condemnation of the incident.

stories.title: Trump turning negotiations into ‘table of surrender’, Iran's top negotiator says
stories.summary: Iran's top negotiator and parliament speaker Mohammad Ghalibaf accused President Trump of trying to turn negotiations into 'a table of surrender.' He said Iran rejects talks under threat and is prepared to reveal 'new cards on the battlefield,' adding uncertainty to possible US-Iran talks in Islamabad.

stories.title: Volunteer cook who pampers IDF troops under Hezbollah fire lights Independence Day torch
stories.summary: Ora Hatan, a volunteer cook who has continued feeding IDF soldiers on the Lebanese border despite Hezbollah rocket fire that destroyed her family restaurant, was chosen to light a torch at Israel's Independence Day ceremony.

stories.title: War update: 91 combat engagements since morning, greatest pressure in Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka directions
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 91 combat engagements against Ukrainian positions since morning, with the highest pressure concentrated in the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka directions in the Donetsk region.

stories.title: Russia Forced to Slash Oil Production After Ukrainian Strikes – Reuters
stories.summary: Ukrainian strikes on Russian energy infrastructure have forced Russia to cut oil production by an estimated 300,000 to 400,000 barrels per day, according to Reuters. The targeted infrastructure accounts for roughly a quarter of Russia's state revenue.

stories.title: US commander warns Taiwan not to ‘starve the chicken’ on defense
stories.summary: U.S. Indo-Pacific Command chief Admiral Samuel Paparo urged Taiwan not to underfund its defense, warning against what he called starving the chicken. He stressed the importance of Taiwan's legislature passing its stalled defense budget.

stories.title: Battered but not broken: How many missiles does Iran have left?
stories.summary: Analysts are assessing the state of Iran's missile arsenal following the US-Israeli military campaign, debating whether the strikes dealt a lasting blow to Iran's missile program or caused only a temporary setback.

stories.title: The US exit from Syria, explained
stories.summary: The United States has ended its military presence in Syria after roughly ten years. The withdrawal raises questions about the future of allied Kurdish forces, regional stability, and Syria's political trajectory.

stories.title: EU’s hybrid threats sanctions list grows to 88 names. Two Russian information networks has been added
stories.summary: The European Council expanded its hybrid-threats sanctions list to 88 names by adding two Russian information networks accused of conducting influence operations.

stories.title: Why supporters of Burkina Faso’s junta leader are campaigning against a Sky News journalist
stories.summary: Sky News journalist Yousra Elbagir has been targeted by a smear campaign from supporters of Burkina Faso's junta leader Captain Ibrahim Traoré. The campaign followed her reporting on security conditions and repression of free speech in the country.

stories.title: Kevin Warsh, Trump’s pick for Fed chief, calls for ‘regime change’ at US central bank
stories.summary: Federal Reserve chair nominee Kevin Warsh called for "regime change" at the U.S. central bank during his Senate confirmation hearing, proposing a new inflation-control approach and a communications overhaul. Republican Senator Thom Tillis indicated he would not vote for the nomination.

stories.title: Israeli soldiers use sexual violence for forcible displacement
stories.summary: A report found that Israeli forces are using sexual violence to terrorize Palestinians into leaving their communities in the West Bank. Legal experts say the practice may constitute the war crime of forcible transfer.

stories.title: Azerbaijan says it is ready to supply LNG to Pakistan
stories.summary: Azerbaijan's state energy company SOCAR said it is prepared to supply liquefied natural gas to Pakistan upon receiving a formal request. A framework agreement signed in 2025 between SOCAR Trading and Pakistan LNG Limited enables accelerated LNG purchases.

stories.title: Pentagon seeks $30bn boost for munitions amid war on Iran
stories.summary: The Pentagon's budget includes over $30 billion to replenish munitions stockpiles depleted during the US-Israeli war on Iran. Priority items include Patriot air defense systems, THAAD interceptors, Precision Strike Missiles, and Mid-Range Capability systems.

stories.title: 'Deviated from IDF values': Soldiers who smashed Lebanese Jesus statue removed from combat
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces removed soldiers from combat duty after they smashed a Jesus statue in Lebanon. The IDF expressed deep regret, stating its operations in Lebanon target Hezbollah and other armed groups, not Lebanese civilians.

stories.title: US Navy unmanned surface vessel fleet to grow sevenfold in Indo-Pacific
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy plans to expand its fleet of medium unmanned surface vessels in the Indo-Pacific region to at least 30, a sevenfold increase. The expansion will also include smaller unmanned surface vessels and unmanned aerial systems.

stories.title: US Navy unmanned surface vessel fleet to grow sevenfold in Indo-Pacific
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy's fleet of medium unmanned surface vessels in the Indo-Pacific is expected to grow sevenfold to at least 30 vessels. The expansion will also include smaller unmanned surface vehicles and unmanned aerial systems.

stories.title: European Union weighs more American jet fuel, cleaner aviation industry amid strains from Iran war
stories.summary: The European Commission is preparing a broader package of energy and transport measures as the Iran war strains aviation fuel supplies. The EU's transport chief noted there are currently no signs of widespread flight cancellations.

stories.title: Hezbollah to bury fighters killed in war with Israel
stories.summary: Hezbollah announced plans to bury fighters killed during its conflict with Israel in Lebanon. The group has not disclosed the total number of its fighters killed since Israel launched its attack.

stories.title: Zelensky approves list of Ukraine's next military operations
stories.summary: President Zelensky approved a list of upcoming Ukrainian military operations, citing reduced sanctions and political pressure on Russia as factors enabling increased Russian military ambitions. Ukraine plans to counter this by increasing drone use on the frontline.

stories.title: IDF says Hezbollah breached truce, launching rockets at troops, drone at Israel
stories.summary: The Israeli military said Hezbollah breached the ceasefire by launching rockets at Israeli troops and a drone toward Israel. Hezbollah claimed responsibility, saying its attacks were in response to Israeli ceasefire violations. The IDF said it struck the rocket launcher in response.

stories.title: How the War in Iran Is Affecting Its Northern and Eastern Neighbors
stories.summary: The U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, which began on February 28, has produced significant ripple effects beyond the immediate conflict zone, affecting Iran's northern and eastern neighbors with both security risks and potential strategic opportunities.

stories.title: Some 150 Jewish leaders denounce, apologize for IDF soldier's defacement of Lebanese Jesus statue
stories.summary: Approximately 150 Jewish leaders, including Orthodox, Conservative, and Reform rabbis, signed a letter denouncing and apologizing for the defacement of a Lebanese Jesus statue by IDF soldiers. The letter was organized by Israel365 Action, an NGO connecting evangelical Christian and Jewish communities.

stories.title: What’s the bill to rebuild Gaza, and who will pay?
stories.summary: A joint UN-EU report estimates that rebuilding Gaza will cost approximately $71 billion over a ten-year period. Questions remain over who will finance the reconstruction effort.

stories.title: 'Mood shifting' in Europe: Public opinion and governments 'turning against Israel'
stories.summary: Dr. Maya Sion-Tzidkiyahu of the Mitvim Institute noted that European public opinion and government positions are increasingly shifting toward a more critical stance on Israel. She highlighted potential economic, diplomatic, and cultural consequences for Israel as European sentiment evolves.

stories.title: Two Israeli soldiers jailed over smashing of Jesus statue in Lebanon village
stories.summary: The Israeli military sentenced two soldiers to 30 days in jail and removed them from combat duty after one used a sledgehammer to destroy a statue of Jesus in a Christian village in southern Lebanon while the other filmed. The IDF said the conduct deviated from military orders and values.

stories.title: UN: Libya fuelled Sudan war with Colombian mercenaries
stories.summary: A United Nations report found that a Libyan armed group sent Colombian mercenaries, weapons, and fuel to support Sudan's Rapid Support Forces. The intervention has fueled the ongoing war in Sudan and worsened the humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: Israeli soldiers jailed for damaging crucifix in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel's military sentenced two soldiers to 30 days in jail and removed them from combat duty for smashing a crucifix in southern Lebanon. The incident drew widespread condemnation from Christian religious leaders after images circulated globally.

stories.title: Downing Street exerted pressure to approve Mandelson’s appointment, sacked official tells MPs
stories.summary: Former UK Foreign Office official Olly Robbins told MPs that Downing Street applied persistent pressure to approve Peter Mandelson's appointment as UK envoy to Washington. Robbins said Prime Minister Keir Starmer's office showed a "dismissive attitude" toward security vetting concerns.

stories.title: Two Palestinians killed during settler attack on West Bank village, officials say
stories.summary: Two Palestinians, including a 14-year-old boy, were shot and killed during an Israeli settler attack on the West Bank village of al-Mughayyir, according to the village's mayor.

stories.title: Ukraine ready to postpone receiving some benefits from EU to speed up its accession – Kachka
stories.summary: Ukraine's trade representative Taras Kachka stated that Ukraine is willing to postpone receiving certain EU benefits in order to accelerate the country's accession process to the European Union.

stories.title: Russia keeps arresting Crimeans. The count just hit 520
stories.summary: The number of political prisoners detained by Russian authorities in occupied Crimea has reached 520, more than doubling since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Those detained include a welder, a human rights defender, and a father of four.

stories.title: 'Do them no harm!' Trump calls for Iran to stop execution of women as start to negotiations
stories.summary: President Trump publicly called on Iran to release imprisoned women and halt their executions, framing the appeal as a potential starting point for negotiations. He posted the request on Truth Social, urging Iranian authorities to "do them no harm."

stories.title: Around 3.3 million jobs may have been affected by 2025 floods in Pakistan: ILO
stories.summary: The International Labour Organisation estimated that approximately 3.3 million jobs may have been affected by the 2025 floods in Pakistan. The assessment covered 14 severely impacted districts in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, with Punjab bearing the majority of losses.

stories.title: Mass shooting reignites push to loosen gun laws in war-torn Ukraine
stories.summary: The mass shooting in Kyiv that killed seven people has reignited debate in Ukraine over loosening gun laws. Many Ukrainians took to social media to demand the right to carry handguns for personal protection.

stories.title: Ukraine has delivered 92% of last year’s fiber-optic drone total to Front in under four months
stories.summary: Ukraine has delivered 92% of last year's total fiber-optic drone output to the front lines in under four months, after resolving cost issues related to fiber-optic cable production.

stories.title: Israel must take sharply declining US public support seriously, think tank warns
stories.summary: Israel's Institute for National Security Studies warned that U.S. public support for Israel is sharply declining and urged Israeli leaders to take the trend seriously, cautioning that American backing may not last indefinitely.

stories.title: North Carolina officials to charge adults who allegedly ‘stood by’ teen fight that became mass shooting
stories.summary: North Carolina authorities in Winston-Salem announced plans to charge adults who allegedly stood by during a pre-planned teenage fight that escalated into a mass shooting. Two teenagers were killed and five others wounded in the incident on Monday.

stories.title: Lebanon’s Moment of Reckoning
stories.summary: Analysis focuses on Lebanon's ceasefire and strategies to ensure it weakens Hezbollah rather than strengthens the group. The discussion centers on Lebanon's political and security trajectory following the truce.

stories.title: Iranian citizen extradited to US under Iran-China smuggling indictment
stories.summary: Reza Dindar, a 44-year-old Iranian citizen, was extradited to the United States to face a nine-count indictment in Seattle. He is accused of attempting to evade US trade sanctions on Iran by routing illegal exports through third countries including China.

stories.title: Japan loosens arms exports rules in major shift
stories.summary: Japan announced a significant loosening of its arms export rules, clearing the way for weapons sales to partner nations and allies. The policy shift represents a major change in Tokyo's traditionally restrictive defense export posture.

stories.title: Russians strike Sloviansk with multiple launch rocket systems, leaving five injured
stories.summary: Russian troops struck the city of Sloviansk in Donetsk region using multiple launch rocket systems, wounding five civilians.

stories.title: Iran slams US seizure of cargo vessel, demands release
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry condemned the US Navy's seizure of the Iranian-flagged cargo ship Touska in the Gulf of Oman, calling it "extremely dangerous" and "criminal" and demanding the immediate release of the vessel and its crew.

stories.title: EU expects positive decisions on 90 billion euro loan to Ukraine on Wednesday
stories.summary: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said she expected "positive decisions" on a 90 billion euro (approximately $105.94 billion) loan for Ukraine to be made on Wednesday. The announcement was made in Luxembourg on April 21.

stories.title: US did not move defense system from Korea, general says
stories.summary: A U.S. general denied reports that a THAAD missile defense system was moved from South Korea to the Middle East. The Washington Post had reported in March that the Pentagon was relocating parts of the system.

stories.title: Lebanon PM and Macron to discuss bolstering country's position
stories.summary: French President Macron met with Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam to discuss strengthening Lebanon's negotiating position ahead of US talks with Israel. Discussions focused on ceasefire tensions, Hezbollah, and ongoing Israeli occupation issues.

stories.title: ‘He talks too much’: how Trump’s erratic commentary is the real block to an Iran deal
stories.summary: President Trump's contradictory public statements and threats regarding Iran have reportedly complicated Pakistan-mediated peace talks in Islamabad. Analysts say Tehran is increasingly wary of entering negotiations without guarantees of a binding agreement.

stories.title: Teenage boy charged after London synagogue arson attack, police say
stories.summary: British police charged a 17-year-old boy in connection with a counter-terrorism investigation into an arson attack on a synagogue in north London over the weekend. The incident occurred at a synagogue in the city's northern area.

stories.title: UK: Newham council investigates Labour mayoral candidate's past flat purchase
stories.summary: Newham council in east London is investigating a Labour mayoral candidate's past purchase of a council flat, ahead of local elections scheduled for 7 May.

stories.title: Two Palestinians killed, four wounded in West Bank settler attack on school
stories.summary: Two Palestinians, aged 14 and 32, were killed and four others wounded by gunfire in a settler attack on a school in the West Bank. The Palestinian Red Crescent Society confirmed the casualties.

stories.title: Syrian charged with planning attack on Jews and ‘infidels’ in Berlin
stories.summary: German prosecutors charged a Syrian national with planning an attack targeting Jews and 'infidels' in Berlin. The suspect allegedly purchased a knife and materials to build explosives and consumed online content about 'martyrdom' and 'jihad.'

stories.title: Israeli sexual violence helping push Palestinians from West Bank: Report
stories.summary: A report by an NGO documented at least 16 cases of conflict-related sexual violence attributed to Israeli settlers and soldiers in the West Bank. The findings suggest such violence is contributing to the displacement of Palestinians from the territory.

stories.title: Ukraine's defense minister adviser 'Flash' shows his house destroyed after Russian drone attack
stories.summary: Serhii Beskrestnov, known by the call sign "Flash" and an adviser to Ukraine's defense minister, showed his home destroyed by a Russian drone attack. He said five jet-powered drones were launched at his family's residence in an apparent targeted assassination attempt.

stories.title: British Rapid Ranger is downing Shaheds in Ukraine from Spanish armored vehicles
stories.summary: British-made Rapid Ranger air-defense systems, mounted on Spanish armored vehicles, are being used in Ukraine to intercept Iranian-designed Shahed drones, adding a new layer to the country's air defenses.

stories.title: US budget earmarks record funding for drones and counter-drone systems
stories.summary: A proposed $1.5 trillion US defence budget includes nearly $54 billion for military drones and unmanned systems, plus $21 billion for counter-drone technology. Pentagon officials cited the growing role of drones in modern warfare, including in the US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: Govt actively pursuing diversified capital markets strategy, finmin tells EU envoy
stories.summary: Pakistani Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb told EU Ambassador Raimundas Karoblis that Pakistan is pursuing a diversified capital markets strategy to strengthen external buffers. He highlighted the country's return to macroeconomic stability and growing investor confidence.

stories.title: Russia Is Making Bank on Trump’s Iran War
stories.summary: Analysis suggests Russia is benefiting financially from the U.S.-Iran conflict through elevated oil prices and relief from certain sanctions pressures. The situation has reportedly improved economic conditions for Moscow.

stories.title: UN agency prepares Hormuz evacuation plan for hundreds of ships
stories.summary: The International Maritime Organization is preparing an evacuation plan for hundreds of ships in the Strait of Hormuz amid the ongoing shipping crisis. The UN agency is coordinating with littoral states including Iran and Oman.

stories.title: After uproar, Kyrgyzstan hotel removes sign barring entry to ‘Jews and animals’
stories.summary: A hotel in the city of Osh, Kyrgyzstan, removed a sign barring entry to 'Jews and animals' after international outcry. Israel's ambassador welcomed the swift action by local authorities to take down the notice.

stories.title: Many Americans question Trump’s temperament amid Iran war
stories.summary: President Trump's approval rating remains at 36 percent as Americans express concerns about his temperament amid the Iran war, rising fuel costs, and his public feud with Pope Leo.

stories.title: Pakistan Navy conducts successful test of locally developed air-launched cruise missile: ISPR
stories.summary: The Pakistan Navy successfully test-fired the indigenously developed "Taimoor" air-launched cruise missile, an anti-ship weapon system. The military's media wing, ISPR, said the missile demonstrated exceptional precision and validated Pakistan's combat strike capability.

stories.title: China pledges deeper cooperation with Mozambique
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Mozambican President Daniel Chapo agreed during talks in Beijing to elevate bilateral ties and deepen cooperation between China and Mozambique.

stories.title: Rats, fleas plague Gaza’s displaced as temperatures rise
stories.summary: Displaced Palestinians living in tents across Gaza report surging infestations of rats, fleas, and other pests as spring temperatures rise. Residents near the southern city of Khan Younis told AFP that vermin are biting children and contaminating food. Aid agencies warned the situation poses a growing public health threat amid minimal sanitation infrastructure.

stories.title: How grievance turns to violence in a mass shooter's mind
stories.summary: An analysis of mass shootings, including last week's school shooting in Turkey, examines how a buildup of grievance and fixation often precedes the transition from violent thoughts to violent acts.

stories.title: Iran says World Cup decision hinges on player safety in US
stories.summary: Iran's Sport Minister Ahmad Donyamali said the government and the Supreme National Security Council will make the final decision on World Cup participation, contingent on guarantees for player safety in the US amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Syrskyi suspends heads of Odesa Regional and Peresyp District Territorial Recruitment Centers
stories.summary: Ukrainian Commander-in-Chief Oleksandr Syrskyi suspended the heads of the Odesa Regional Territorial Center for Recruitment and Social Support and the Peresyp District Territorial Recruitment Center from their duties.

stories.title: UK: No 10 had "dismissive attitude" to Mandelson's vetting
stories.summary: Former senior British Foreign Office official Olly Robbins told a parliamentary committee that Downing Street showed a dismissive attitude toward security vetting for Peter Mandelson's appointment as UK ambassador to the United States. Robbins said he faced constant pressure to expedite the process, deepening a political controversy around Prime Minister Keir Starmer.

stories.title: Trump says he does not want to extend ceasefire with Iran, will get 'great deal'
stories.summary: President Trump told CNBC he does not want to extend the ceasefire with Iran, expressing confidence that the US will secure a "great deal" to end the weeks-long war. He stated Iran has "no choice" but to negotiate.

stories.title: Macron to host Lebanon's PM Nawaf Salam
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam is scheduled to meet French President Emmanuel Macron at the Élysée Palace on Tuesday. Macron is expected to reaffirm support for the Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire, three days after a French peacekeeper was killed in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Top Lebanese official makes warning
stories.summary: Israel carried out an airstrike in the Wadi Houjeir valley in southern Lebanon on Tuesday despite a truce that took effect on Friday, according to L'Orient-Le Jour. The Israeli military accused Hezbollah of ceasefire violations, while Hezbollah held mass funerals for 44 fighters killed during weeks of fighting.

stories.title: Iran's participation in US talks unclear
stories.summary: Pakistan's information minister Attaullah Tarar said Islamabad has not yet received a formal response from Iran on whether it will send a delegation for a second round of U.S.-Iran talks. The decision is considered critical as the two-week ceasefire between the two sides nears expiration.

stories.title: 2 troops dismissed, jailed for smashing statue of Jesus in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military sentenced two soldiers to 30 days in military prison—one for smashing a statue of Jesus in southern Lebanon and another for photographing the act. Six additional troops who failed to intervene were called in for questioning.

stories.title: 7,900 people died, disappeared on migration routes in 2025: UN
stories.summary: The UN's International Organisation for Migration reported that approximately 7,900 people died or disappeared on global migration routes in 2025, pushing the total since 2014 beyond 80,000. The IOM urged countries to establish safer pathways for migrants.

stories.title: Israeli forces block Palestinian student protest after barring access to school
stories.summary: Israeli forces dispersed a Palestinian student protest in Umm al-Khair, near Hebron in the occupied West Bank, after barring students' access to a school. The crackdown comes amid increasing settler violence in the area.

stories.title: Iran sees mass redundancies from war with US and Israel
stories.summary: Manufacturers, retailers, and digital-sector companies in Iran are experiencing mass layoffs as a result of the ongoing war with the United States and Israel. Reports warn the economic damage could worsen if hostilities resume.

stories.title: Russia has taken 1,700 sq km of Ukraine in 2026, top general says
stories.summary: A senior general stated that Russia has captured 1,700 square kilometers of Ukrainian territory in 2026, though pro-Ukrainian mapping sources place the figure at 592 square kilometers.

stories.title: CEO of Russia’s Largest Book Publisher Detained in LGBTQ+ ‘Extremism’ Probe
stories.summary: Yevgeny Kapyev, CEO of Russia's largest book publisher Eksmo, was detained by police in Moscow following a search of the company's office. The detention is linked to an investigation into alleged LGBTQ+ "extremism."

stories.title: Rabbi who boasts of bulldozing Palestinian homes will light torch for Israel’s national  day
stories.summary: Rabbi Avraham Zarbiv, known for demolishing Palestinian civilian homes in Gaza, was selected to light a torch at Israel's independence day ceremony. Human rights organizations criticized the honor, saying it endorsed ethnic cleansing and war crimes.

stories.title: Northrop to invest $2.5B to hasten B-21 production
stories.summary: Northrop Grumman plans to invest $2.5 billion to accelerate production of the B-21 Raider stealth bomber. CEO Kathy Warden said the company will spend $200 million in 2026 as part of the effort to speed up delivery timelines.

stories.title: Haredi extremist vandalizes image of female Hatzalah volunteer killed in missile attack
stories.summary: An ultra-Orthodox extremist in Beit Shemesh vandalized an image of a female Hatzalah volunteer who was killed in a missile attack. Hatzalah head Eli Beer condemned the act as crossing a red line.

stories.title: AFU strikes three ammunition depots and other Russian logistical facilities
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces struck three Russian ammunition depots and other logistics facilities on April 20–21, targeting sites in occupied Ukrainian territories and inside Russia.

stories.title: Pass on the Flame!
stories.summary: Argentina's president became the first non-Israeli and non-Jewish leader to light an Independence Day Torch at an Israeli ceremony, marking a historic moment in diplomatic relations.

stories.title: Man and woman shot dead in suspected double homicide in north
stories.summary: A man and a woman were shot dead in a suspected double homicide in the Druze village of Yarka in northern Israel. Police are searching for suspects after both victims were pronounced dead at the scene.

stories.title: Robot chases wild boars off the streets of Warsaw
stories.summary: Warsaw has deployed a robot to chase wild boars from city streets after the population surged to over 3,000, a 20-fold increase since 2020 in the Polish capital.

stories.title: SC notifies SOPs to ensure uninterrupted functioning during ‘unforeseen public holidays’
stories.summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court issued standard operating procedures to ensure uninterrupted judicial functioning during unforeseen public holidays. The move comes amid heightened security arrangements in Islamabad ahead of expected US-Iran peace talks.

stories.title: Nicaragua President calls Trump mentally unstable over Mid-East war against Iran
stories.summary: Nicaraguan President Daniel Ortega publicly called U.S. President Trump mentally unstable in connection with the U.S.-led military campaign against Iran. Ortega and Washington have long maintained a contentious relationship.

stories.title: Ukraine lost 500 American battle taxis. Now it’s building a tougher one.
stories.summary: Ukraine has lost approximately 500 American M-113 armored personnel carriers, which are fast but lack sufficient protection. Ukrainian engineers are now developing a tougher domestically built replacement vehicle.

stories.title: Myanmar President seeks peace talks within 100 days, rebels reject offer
stories.summary: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing called on all armed groups to engage in peace talks by a July 31 deadline, setting a 100-day window for negotiations. Rebel groups rejected the offer, declining to participate in the proposed discussions.

stories.title: Occupied West Bank: Israeli forces uproot hundreds of olive trees
stories.summary: Israeli bulldozers uprooted dozens of olive and fruit trees in al-Lubban al-Sharqiya village south of Nablus in the occupied West Bank. Local landowner Fuad Daraghmeh said approximately 40 olive trees he had tended for 40 years were destroyed.

stories.title: Mobile clinic still barred from Gaza on Pope's death anniversary
stories.summary: A mobile clinic called the "Vehicle of Hope," intended to vaccinate children in Gaza as one of Pope Francis's last wishes before his death last year, remains barred from entering the territory.

stories.title: Video: US veterans protest Iran war
stories.summary: Dozens of US military veterans and family members of deployed soldiers stormed a congressional office building in Washington, DC, on Monday to protest the war on Iran.

stories.title: 'Blood libel repackaged': Israeli ambr. condemns Stockholm mock slaughter protest
stories.summary: Israel's ambassador to Sweden, Ziv Nevo Kulman, condemned a mock slaughter protest in Stockholm, calling it a repackaging of centuries-old antisemitic blood libels with the word "Zionists" substituted for "Jews."

stories.title: Russia to halt supplies of Kazakh oil to Germany via Druzhba pipeline — Reuters
stories.summary: Russia intends to halt the transit of Kazakh oil to Germany through the Druzhba pipeline beginning May 1, according to Reuters. The move could disrupt energy supplies to German refineries dependent on the route.

stories.title: Lavish Hasidic fundraising event held on Memorial Day eve, sparking condemnation
stories.summary: A lavish Hasidic fundraising event held on the eve of Israel's Memorial Day drew condemnation. Democrats chair Yair Golan criticized ultra-Orthodox draft exemptions, accusing attendees of showing contempt for those who died defending the country.

stories.title: Cost of war: Gaza development set back by 77 years, new report finds
stories.summary: A new report finds that Gaza's development has been set back by 77 years due to more than two years of war with Israel, requiring close to eight decades and tens of billions of dollars for recovery.

stories.title: Pakistan urges US and Iran to extend ceasefire
stories.summary: Pakistan's Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar urged both the US and Iran to extend their two-week ceasefire during a meeting with the US Chargé d'Affaires in Pakistan, Natalie A. Baker.

stories.title: Rabbi accused of war crimes selected for Israel’s national celebration
stories.summary: Rabbi Avraham Zarbiv, who filmed himself demolishing Palestinian buildings in Gaza while reciting religious verses, has been selected to participate in Israel's national independence day ceremony.

stories.title: Pakistan extends airspace closure for Indian planes till May 24
stories.summary: Pakistan extended its airspace closure to all Indian-registered aircraft and planes operated, owned, or leased by Indian airlines and operators, including military flights. The restriction, issued via a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM), remains in effect until May 24.

stories.title: Kenya: Met Department Issues Heavy Rainfall Advisory Across Coastal and Northern Kenya
stories.summary: The Kenya Meteorological Department issued a heavy rainfall advisory warning of intensified rainfall across coastal and northern Kenya between April 22 and April 27, 2026.

stories.title: European Union expects positive decisions on 90 billion euro loan to Ukraine on April 22
stories.summary: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said the European Union expects positive decisions on a 90 billion euro loan to Ukraine on April 22. The announcement signals progress in securing major financial support for Kyiv.

stories.title: Israeli soldiers punished over vandalism of Jesus statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel's military announced that two soldiers will be removed from combat duty and given 30 days of military detention for vandalizing a Jesus statue in Lebanon.

stories.title: Weaponized energy: Russia may cut off Kazakh oil to Germany on 1 May, risking Berlin-Brandenburg fuel shock
stories.summary: Russia may halt the transit of Kazakh oil to Germany starting May 1, potentially cutting 17% of feedstock to Germany's PCK refinery. The move risks a fuel supply shock in the Berlin-Brandenburg region.

stories.title: Middle East Eye documentary 'Soaked in Blood' wins Webby award
stories.summary: Middle East Eye's investigative documentary "Soaked in Blood" won a Webby award. The film revealed that Israeli forces killed a starving Palestinian walking along a route declared safe by the US and Israel-backed Gaza Humanitarian Foundation.

stories.title: Nigeria: Foundation Honours Nigerian Geneticist for Sickle Cell Research
stories.summary: A Nigerian geneticist, Ms. Falusi, was honored with a role model award for her research on Sickle Cell Disease and Alpha Thalassaemia in the field of human genetics.

stories.title: Nigeria: Court Adjourns Chinese Nationals' Illegal Mining Trial for Final Arguments
stories.summary: A court in Abuja adjourned the illegal mining trial of eight Chinese nationals for final arguments after the defendants called only one witness in their defense.

stories.title: Africa: AUC Chairperson This Morning Joined H.E. @tayeatske, President of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
stories.summary: African Union Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf joined Ethiopian President Taye Atske at the inaugural Africa-China Entrepreneurs meeting (CAES) in Addis Ababa.

stories.title: Africa: AUC Chairperson Today Received the Letters of Credence of H.E. Ambassador Nasir Aminu, Permanent Representative of the Federal Republic of Nigeria
stories.summary: AU Commission Chairperson Mahmoud Ali Youssouf received the letters of credence from Ambassador Nasir Aminu as Nigeria's new Permanent Representative to Ethiopia and to the African Union.

stories.title: What are the main points of contention between US and Iran?
stories.summary: Uncertainty persists over a second round of US-Iran negotiations in Islamabad as the fragile truce between the two countries nears expiration. A US delegation led by Vice President JD Vance is expected, but Iran has not confirmed participation. President Trump warned Iran could "face problems" if it refused to negotiate.

stories.title: Kenya: High Court Lifts Orders Blocking Arrest of Governors
stories.summary: Kenya's High Court in Kiambu lifted conservatory orders that had blocked the arrest or detention of governors and other public officials. Law enforcement agencies can now proceed with legal action.

stories.title: Trump says US likely to resume bombing Iran as ceasefire nears end
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said he expects to resume bombing Iran as the 14-day ceasefire approaches its Wednesday deadline with no deal reached. Trump told CNBC the military is "raring to go," while Tehran warned of a response and negotiators headed to Islamabad for talks.

stories.title: 2 Palestinians, one of them 14, killed in alleged settler attack in West Bank
stories.summary: Two Palestinians, one aged 14, were killed in an alleged settler attack outside a school in al-Mughayyir near Ramallah in the occupied West Bank. The IDF launched a probe after a reservist reportedly opened fire; villagers were said to have been throwing stones.

stories.title: Nigeria: No, Nigerian Army Did Not 'Recently' Arrest 488 Boko Haram Members in Abia State
stories.summary: A fact-check confirmed that the Nigerian Army did not recently arrest 488 Boko Haram members in Abia State, debunking a widely circulated claim.

stories.title: Japan PM Takaichi sends offering to Yasukuni war shrine
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi sent a ritual offering to Tokyo's Yasukuni Shrine, which honours approximately 2.5 million war dead including convicted war criminals. The shrine has long drawn criticism from neighbouring countries, particularly China and South Korea.

stories.title: Russian Businesses Helping Funnel Military Equipment to Wagner Successor Group in Mali – Report
stories.summary: A report indicates Russian businesses are helping ship military equipment to the Wagner successor group operating in Mali. The scale of the shipments suggests Russia may be seeking to establish a long-term military presence in the country.

stories.title: ‘Strangled’: Pakistan faces economic imperative in Iran war peace push
stories.summary: Pakistan's economy is feeling the strain of mediating between the United States and Iran, with business owners in Islamabad reporting devastating effects from rising fuel costs, rolling blackouts linked to the US-Israel war on Iran, and government-imposed restrictions on operating hours aimed at conserving electricity.

stories.title: Taiwan president postpones Eswatini trip after claims of China pressure
stories.summary: Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te postponed a planned trip to Eswatini after three African countries reportedly withdrew overflight permission. Taipei accused China of pressuring those nations to deny access.

stories.title: Memorial Day exposes widening rift between public and political leadership
stories.summary: Israel's Memorial Day has exposed growing divisions between the public and political leaders, with 2.5 years of war, a lack of accountability for October 7, and Haredi draft exemptions turning a day of unity into one of dissent.

stories.title: US-Iran talks: What are the sticking points as truce extended?
stories.summary: Major disagreements persist between the US, Israel, and Iran as President Trump announced the ceasefire extension. Key sticking points remain unresolved despite the additional time provided by the truce.

stories.title: US-Iran talks: What are the sticking points as truce ends?
stories.summary: Major disagreements between the US, Israel, and Iran remain unresolved as a two-week ceasefire approaches expiration. Fears of renewed conflict are growing amid uncertainty over whether diplomatic talks will continue.

stories.title: US-Iran talks: What are the sticking points as truce nears end?
stories.summary: Major disagreements persist between the US and Israel on one side and Iran on the other as a ceasefire nears expiration. Fears of renewed conflict are growing amid stalled negotiations over key sticking points.

stories.title: Iran foreign ministry condemns arrests in UAE as 'baseless'
stories.summary: Iran's foreign ministry condemned the arrests of individuals in the UAE whom Abu Dhabi accused of belonging to an Iran-linked group plotting terrorist acts. Tehran called the arrests "baseless" and urged the UAE to respect detainees' rights.

stories.title: Student allegedly jailed in China for six years after taking part in pro-democracy protests in Australia
stories.summary: A Chinese student who participated in pro-democracy protests in Australia was allegedly sentenced to six years in prison after returning to China in December 2024. The student lost contact with friends in Sydney following his return, prompting calls for the Australian government to strengthen protections for overseas students against political repression.

stories.title: Uber driver Michael was assaulted by passengers. He says the platform’s response added insult to injury
stories.summary: An Uber driver named Michael Thorn was assaulted by a passenger and hospitalized, after which the platform deactivated his account. Drivers removed from the Uber platform say they have limited recourse to appeal as the company increasingly relies on automated decision-making systems.

stories.title: ‘Not a personal attack’: gun lobby targets marginal Labor seats at NSW election over post-Bondi reforms
stories.summary: The Australian Recreation Union, a gun users' group, announced plans to target marginal Labor seats in the upcoming New South Wales election. The group is recruiting campaign managers across 17 electorates to support candidates opposing firearm laws enacted after the Bondi terror attack.

stories.title: Death of Sydney’s ‘birdman’ described as ‘beyond tragic’ by Albanese government
stories.summary: Bikram Lama, a 32-year-old homeless man, was found dead near St James tunnel in Sydney's Hyde Park in December. Australian federal and state housing ministers described his death as "beyond tragic" and said it highlights gaps in support for vulnerable people without residency status.

stories.title: Ketamine, psychedelics, GHB: is the US falling out of love with cocaine?
stories.summary: Data indicates that cocaine use has dropped significantly among Generation Z Americans compared with previous generations. The decline coincides with rising popularity of other substances including ketamine, psychedelics, and GHB in the United States.

stories.title: Trump’s military push confronts US lawmakers and China’s shipbuilding edge
stories.summary: President Trump's fiscal year 2027 budget requests $65.8 billion for 34 warships as part of a plan to rebuild the U.S. Navy into a "Golden Fleet." Analysts note the ambitious shipbuilding goals face challenges from China's superior shipbuilding capacity and congressional scrutiny.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Bohodukhiv in Kharkiv region; three people injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out a drone strike on the town of Bohodukhiv in Ukraine's Kharkiv region, injuring three women.

stories.title: Video: US forces board sanctioned tanker in Asia Pacific
stories.summary: The US Department of War released video showing American forces boarding a sanctioned tanker in the Asia Pacific region.

stories.title: US Navy successfully tests new long-range, winged JDAM out to 200 miles
stories.summary: The U.S. Navy conducted a successful test on April 1 of a new long-range, winged variant of the Joint Direct Attack Munition. The weapon was deployed from an F/A-18 Super Hornet, flew approximately 200 miles over 34 minutes, and struck within meters of its intended target.

stories.title: Trump says he opposes extending Iran ceasefire amid talks uncertainty
stories.summary: President Donald Trump stated he opposes extending the ceasefire with Iran, saying Tehran has "no choice" but to attend negotiations in Pakistan and accept a deal.

stories.title: Pakistan delivers weapons to Libya's Haftar as part of Saudi-financed deal, sources say
stories.summary: Sources report that at least five Pakistani cargo planes carrying weapons were unloaded at Benghazi airport in Libya in March, delivering arms to Khalifa Haftar's forces as part of a Saudi-financed deal.

stories.title: Gaza's Palestinian women bearing the brunt of Israel's genocide
stories.summary: UN Women estimates that around 11,000 women and girls in Gaza have sustained permanent disabilities from injuries or delayed medical access, highlighting the disproportionate impact of the conflict on Palestinian women.

stories.title: US military service members will no longer be required to get annual flu shot
stories.summary: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced that military service members will no longer be required to receive annual flu vaccinations. Hegseth called the existing mandate "overly broad" and "not rational," framing the policy change as eliminating overreaching requirements.

stories.title: Why is the EU under pressure to suspend its trade agreement with Israel?
stories.summary: EU member states are divided over whether to suspend the bloc's trade association agreement with Israel, amid mounting pressure related to rights violations in Gaza and the West Bank.

stories.title: Change or continuity? What a new president means for Iraq
stories.summary: Iraq's new president, Nizar Amidi, has taken office in a largely ceremonial role. Analysts are examining whether the balance of presidential power might begin to shift under his tenure.
