stories.title: Execution law entrenches 'horrific Israeli racism' say activists
stories.summary: Activists have condemned a new Israeli execution law as entrenching racism against Palestinians. More than 9,500 Palestinian prisoners are currently held in Israeli prisons, including 86 women and 350 children.

stories.title: US ‘restricts intelligence sharing with South Korea’ after minister identified suspected nuclear site
stories.summary: The United States has reportedly restricted intelligence sharing with South Korea after Unification Minister Chung Dong-young publicly identified Kusong as a suspected North Korean uranium enrichment site. The facility had not previously been officially confirmed alongside the known nuclear sites at Yongbyon and Kangson.

stories.title: Car said to belong to minister’s security detail strikes and kills Palestinian teen
stories.summary: A vehicle belonging to an Israeli minister's security detail struck and killed 16-year-old Palestinian Mohammad Majdi al-Ja'abari near Hebron in the occupied West Bank. The teen was riding his bicycle when hit. Minister Ben Gvir's office said he was not at the scene and claimed the teenager entered the road at a red light.

stories.title: Burn treatment for Gaza children threatened by Israeli restrictions
stories.summary: Medical treatment for children with burn injuries in Gaza is under threat due to Israeli restrictions on the entry of supplies and personnel. The limitations are hampering healthcare access for injured minors in the besieged territory.

stories.title: Russian forces attack power facility in Chernihiv region; 54,000 customers without power
stories.summary: A Russian attack damaged a power facility in the Nizhyn district of Ukraine's Chernihiv region, leaving approximately 54,000 customers without electricity.

stories.title: Ben-Gurion, Epilogue - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A documentary features newly uncovered footage of David Ben-Gurion, Israel's first prime minister. The material provides new perspectives on the historical leader's life and legacy.

stories.title: China calls for US ‘sincerity’ on Iran, warns of Japan’s ‘dangerous’ nuclear ambitions
stories.summary: China's latest Non-Proliferation Treaty report called on the United States to show "sincerity" in resolving the Iranian nuclear issue. The document, published by China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, also warned about Japan's discussions on possessing nuclear weapons, labeling them "dangerous" nuclear ambitions.

stories.title: Delicate moment
stories.summary: An editorial examines the uncertain status of US-Iran peace talks expected in Islamabad, noting Iran had not confirmed attendance due to mistrust of the US. Tehran cited three main grievances: America's blockade of Iranian ports, a US attack on an Iranian cargo ship, and delays in the Lebanon ceasefire.

stories.title: Confusion grips Rawalpindi amid strict security measures for US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Rawalpindi residents faced widespread confusion as authorities closed some roads and suspended public transport ahead of a possible second round of US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad. Several universities shifted to online classes while others remained open. Security measures were concentrated around Nur Khan Airbase.

stories.title: 2 teens killed and 5 injured in North Carolina shooting
stories.summary: Two teenagers were killed and five others injured in a shooting at a park in North Carolina. Authorities said the victims had gathered at the location for a pre-planned fight.

stories.title: Rachel Goldberg-Polin’s new memoir piercingly articulates the ordeal of losing a son
stories.summary: Rachel Goldberg-Polin published a memoir titled "When We See You Again" about her son Hersh Goldberg-Polin, who was taken hostage by Hamas and killed in captivity at age 23. The book chronicles her life before and after his abduction.

stories.title: Man who threatened to bomb US mission sent to prison in Karachi
stories.summary: A judicial magistrate in Karachi sent suspect Sharjeel Akbar to prison on judicial remand after he allegedly threatened to bomb the US consulate general. He was arrested and charged under Pakistan Penal Code sections covering criminal intimidation and intentional insult, as well as the Telegraph Act.

stories.title: Canadian killed in shooting at Mexico's ancient Teotihuacán pyramids
stories.summary: A Canadian tourist was killed and several others were injured in a shooting at the Teotihuacán archaeological site in Mexico on Monday. Mexican officials confirmed the incident at the popular tourist destination, which occurred weeks before the country hosts the FIFA World Cup.

stories.title: Netanyahu, Trump: On Gaza and the Iran war, the parallels with World War Two are clear
stories.summary: Scholars and commentators are drawing parallels between the US-Israeli war on Iran and the Gaza conflict with events from World War Two. The comparisons center on the actions of Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu and US President Trump in the broader regional military campaign.

stories.title: Israeli settler kills teenager in Hebron
stories.summary: An Israeli settler driving in a ministerial security detail struck and killed 16-year-old Palestinian Mohammad Majdi al-Ja'bari near Hebron in the occupied West Bank. The teenager was cycling to school on Route 60 near the Beit Einun junction at approximately 6 a.m. when the incident occurred.

stories.title: War update: 174 combat clashes over past day, fiercest fighting in Pokrovsk, Huliaipole sectors
stories.summary: Ukrainian and Russian forces engaged in 174 combat clashes along the front line on April 20, with the most intense fighting reported in the Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors.

stories.title: As Iran crisis drags on, fears of global food catastrophe grow
stories.summary: Analysts warn that the ongoing Iran crisis could trigger a global food catastrophe as the conflict's full impact on supply chains has yet to materialize. While global food prices have risen only modestly so far, further disruptions are anticipated.

stories.title: Japan’s Takaichi sends Yasukuni shrine offering, South Korea expresses ‘regret’
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi sent a ritual offering to Tokyo's Yasukuni Shrine, which honours war dead including convicted war criminals, prompting South Korea to express "regret." Takaichi did not visit the shrine in person. The shrine has long been a source of diplomatic tension with Japan's neighbours.

stories.title: Lebanon negotiating with Israel to obtain 'serenity, prosperity': Ghassan Salamé
stories.summary: Lebanon's Culture Minister Ghassan Salamé described negotiations with Israel as a necessity rather than a choice for Lebanon. He framed the talks as the only viable path toward stability and dignity for the Lebanese people after decades of conflict.

stories.title: US and Israel driving 'predatory' world order, Amnesty warns
stories.summary: Amnesty International has warned that the United States and Israel are driving a "predatory" world order. The organization's report covers Israel's actions in Gaza and what it describes as apartheid, alongside crackdowns in Tunisia, Egypt, and Gulf states.

stories.title: Russian drones hit Sumy hospital — 15 injured, three schoolgirls among wounded
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 143 drones and two Iskander missiles overnight on April 21, hitting a hospital in Sumy and injuring 15 people, including three schoolgirls. One person was killed in Kherson, and a school was destroyed in Sloviansk.

stories.title: US has turned back 27 ships since Strait of Hormuz blockade started
stories.summary: The US military has turned back 27 ships since imposing a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Personnel are currently searching containers aboard the Touska, an Iranian vessel seized by US forces.

stories.title: Trump claims Iran violated truce, doubt surrounds peace talks
stories.summary: President Trump accused Iran of violating a ceasefire, while peace talks have stalled with no Iranian delegation present. Tensions continue to escalate over the Strait of Hormuz and the ongoing US blockade.

stories.title: US positive on Iran deal, says blockade on Iranian ports to stay
stories.summary: The United States has expressed optimism about ongoing peace talks with Iran taking place in Pakistan as the ceasefire nears its expiration. However, Washington confirmed that the naval blockade on Iranian ports will remain in place until a deal is reached.

stories.title: Activist Kemi Seba faces extradition battle after arrest in South Africa
stories.summary: Activist Kemi Seba was arrested in South Africa, and Benin is preparing an extradition request. Prosecutors in Benin accuse him of inciting rebellion after he publicly supported a failed coup attempt in December.

stories.title: Injury toll in Sumy rises to 15 following nighttime drone attack
stories.summary: Fifteen people were injured in the Ukrainian city of Sumy following a Russian drone attack carried out overnight on April 21.

stories.title: Group to sue US government over destroyed homes in Lebanon
stories.summary: A group of Lebanese Americans announced plans to sue the US government over the destruction of their homes during Israel's military campaign in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Nepal resumes issuing permits for workers headed to Middle East
stories.summary: Nepal resumed issuing work permits for its nationals heading to the Middle East, six weeks after suspending the process due to the regional war. Approximately 75 percent of Nepali workers abroad are employed in Middle Eastern countries, and their remittances constitute over a quarter of Nepal's $42 billion economy.

stories.title: Sudan's military chief meets Saudi Crown Prince in Jeddah
stories.summary: Sudanese military chief Gen. Abdel-Fattah Burhan traveled to Jeddah to meet Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. The talks focused on the latest developments in Sudan and the broader region.

stories.title: Vance reportedly departing for Pakistan, but still unclear if Iran will join talks
stories.summary: US Vice President Vance reportedly departed for Pakistan for potential talks with Iran, though Iranian state media said no delegation had yet left Tehran. Iran reportedly received authorization from Mojtaba Khamenei to negotiate, while US officials told CNN that Trump's social media posts were undermining the diplomatic process.

stories.title: “No truth” in it: Estonia rejects Zelenskyy’s warning of a Russian mobilization aimed at the Baltics
stories.summary: Estonia's foreign minister rejected Ukrainian President Zelenskyy's warning that Russia may be mobilizing forces to attack a Baltic state. Tallinn said the claim does not align with its own intelligence or threat assessment.

stories.title: 2 women killed in separate traffic accidents involving goods vehicle and coach
stories.summary: Hong Kong police are investigating two separate traffic accidents on Tuesday that killed two women. In one incident near Yau Tong MTR station, a light goods vehicle struck a 30-year-old mainland Chinese woman crossing Cha Kwo Ling Road, causing serious head and limb injuries.

stories.title: Canadian tourist killed, 13 injured in Mexico pyramid shooting
stories.summary: A gunman opened fire at a popular pyramid tourist site in central Mexico, killing a Canadian tourist and injuring 13 others. The attacker, whose nationality was unknown, died by suicide after the shooting, according to Mexico state security secretary Cristobal Castaneda.

stories.title: Russian strikes hit Dnipropetrovsk region overnight, four injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out nearly ten strikes on Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region overnight, injuring four people. The attacks targeted the region with multiple rounds of bombardment.

stories.title: Fans flock to Hollywood premiere of Michael Jackson biopic
stories.summary: Fans and members of Michael Jackson's family attended the Hollywood premiere of a new biopic chronicling the late singer's rise from child star to global music icon. The film does not address the child sexual abuse allegations that marked his later life.

stories.title: China’s diplomacy succeeds even if it doesn’t bring Middle East peace
stories.summary: China's recent diplomatic engagement in the Middle East has prompted debate over whether Beijing is shifting its global strategy toward a peacemaker role. Analysts are divided, with some seeing China stepping into leadership while sceptics argue the US-Israel war on Iran has exposed the limits of Beijing's regional influence.

stories.title: Midtown Jerusalem: Where international luxury  meets the heart of the capital - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: This is a sponsored real estate advertisement for a luxury residential development in Jerusalem by Israel Canada. It is not a news article.

stories.title: ‘He didn’t fall in vain’: On Memorial Day, two young IDF widows discuss life after death
stories.summary: Two young IDF widows, Alma Levin Fridman and Revital Shamir, shared their experiences of loss on Israel's Memorial Day. They discussed their late husbands, families, and the grief they carry while honoring their partners' service.

stories.title: Seven arrested for disrupting ceremonies, tearing down flags during Memorial Day
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested seven people during Memorial Day for disrupting ceremonies and removing flags. Two men were detained in Beit Shemesh for tearing down flags, and a mother with four children was arrested for interrupting a ceremony in Lod. Far-right activists also disrupted a joint Israeli-Palestinian memorial event.

stories.title: My dreams in Iran were already dead before the ceasefire came
stories.summary: A personal account from Iran describes the devastation wrought by the conflict, even after bombing ceased under a ceasefire. The author says the damage to their life and prospects was already irreversible before the fighting paused.

stories.title: Egypt is trying to hold ceasefire in Lebanon together
stories.summary: Egypt's foreign minister met with his American counterpart and subsequently spoke by phone with the Lebanese prime minister as Cairo works to preserve the ceasefire in Lebanon.

stories.title: Rebel Wilson labelled ‘nuts’ by PR team she allegedly hired to attack colleague, court hears
stories.summary: Actor Rebel Wilson is being sued for defamation by colleague Charlotte MacInnes over social media posts alleging sexual harassment. A court heard that a PR team Wilson allegedly hired to attack a co-producer of her film The Deb described her as "nuts."

stories.title: PMDC advances probe into medical student suicides, video scandal
stories.summary: The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council held preliminary hearings on three cases, including suicides of two medical students reportedly linked to harassment at medical institutions. PMDC President Rizwan Taj emphasized a zero-tolerance policy toward harassment and referred the cases to the PMDC Disciplinary Committee for final adjudication.

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill five in Gaza, Hamas clashes with Israeli-backed militia
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed five people in Gaza, while Hamas clashed with an Israeli-backed militia in the territory. The violence is the latest to undermine an October ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Russia’s war casualty toll in Ukraine up by 1,040 over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine reported that Russia's total combat losses since the February 2022 full-scale invasion have reached approximately 1,320,310 personnel as of April 21, 2026. An additional 1,040 Russian casualties were recorded in the past day alone.

stories.title: Excitment in Equatorial Guinea's capital ahead of Pope Leo's visit
stories.summary: Equatorial Guinea is preparing for a visit by Pope Leo XIV on Tuesday. Local church leaders say the papal visit could strengthen faith and national unity in the country.

stories.title: PTI lambasts govt for ‘crippling farm sector’
stories.summary: Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram criticized the current government for allegedly damaging key economic sectors, particularly agriculture. He claimed anti-farmer policies had paralyzed the economy and warned of further national decline without immediate policy corrections.

stories.title: ‘The witches are back’: first look at Practical Magic 2 as Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman return for spooky sequel
stories.summary: A first teaser for Practical Magic 2 has been released, featuring Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman reprising their roles as the Owens sisters. Joey King and Maisie Williams join the cast as the next generation of the family in the sequel to the 1998 film.

stories.title: Macron to meet Lebanon's PM in Paris to 'reaffirm commitment' for Israel truce
stories.summary: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam met with French President Emmanuel Macron at the Élysée Palace on Tuesday. Macron was expected to reaffirm France's support for the Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire, three days after a French peacekeeper was killed in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Amnesty warns that ‘predator’ leaders seek to impose new ‘world order’
stories.summary: Amnesty International's chief warned that authoritarian leaders are attempting to impose a new world order, saying almost every world leader has demonstrated cowardice in the face of human rights abuses.

stories.title: UK to accelerate clean energy drive amid Iran war
stories.summary: The United Kingdom plans to accelerate its clean energy initiatives amid the ongoing conflict with Iran, seeking to reduce dependence on disrupted energy supplies.

stories.title: Federal Cons­titutional Court won’t hear cases today; staff to work from home
stories.summary: Pakistan's Federal Constitutional Court suspended all judicial proceedings on Tuesday due to extraordinary security measures in Islamabad ahead of anticipated US-Iran peace talks. Staff and lawyers were directed to work from home after movement restrictions were imposed across the capital.

stories.title: Iran will respond decisively to any renewed hostile action, senior commander says
stories.summary: A senior Iranian military commander, Ali Abdollahi of the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, warned that Iran's armed forces are prepared for an "immediate and decisive response" to any hostile action. The statement comes as a two-week US-Iran ceasefire is set to expire on Wednesday, with both sides accusing each other of violations.

stories.title: The United States Is Repeating Its Silicon Mistake with Gallium Nitride
stories.summary: China controls 99 percent of the world's primary gallium supply, a critical semiconductor material, and imposed an outright export ban to the United States in December 2024. The U.S. National Defense Stockpile held zero gallium reserves when the ban took effect, raising concerns about repeating past failures in semiconductor supply chain management.

stories.title: €90 billion for Ukraine—two-thirds of the 2026–27 budget gap—clears Brussels Wednesday
stories.summary: EU ambassadors are set to vote Wednesday on final approval of a €90 billion aid package for Ukraine covering two-thirds of its 2026–2027 budget gap. Separate measures on sanctions and military aid remain blocked in Brussels.

stories.title: Is Israel replicating Gaza’s ‘Yellow Line’ in south Lebanon?
stories.summary: Israel announced the establishment of a 10-kilometer-deep "Yellow Line" security zone along the border in southern Lebanon, where its forces continue operating despite a ceasefire with Hezbollah. The demarcation has drawn comparisons to a similar Israeli military line in the Gaza Strip and raises questions about Lebanon's sovereignty.

stories.title: US, Iran exchange threats as fragile ceasefire set to expire
stories.summary: The United States and Iran are exchanging threats as a two-week ceasefire between the two countries nears expiration. Tensions have escalated, with both sides accusing each other of violations during the truce period.

stories.title: Ukraine calls for tougher energy sanctions on Russia at UNSC
stories.summary: Ukraine's UN Permanent Representative Andrii Melnyk called on the United States and European partners to strengthen energy sanctions against Russia during a UN Security Council session. He also urged support for a new Security Council resolution on a ceasefire.

stories.title: Iranian commander says forces ready to give ‘decisive response’
stories.summary: Major General Gholam Ali Rashid Abdollahi of Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters said the country's armed forces are fully prepared to deliver a "decisive" response to any breach by adversaries. He cited Iran's strengthened missile and drone capabilities as bolstering its defensive position.

stories.title: Scam messages offering ships safe transit through Hormuz, security firm warns
stories.summary: Greek maritime risk firm Marisks warned that fraudulent messages offering ships safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for cryptocurrency have been sent to shipping companies with stranded vessels. Unknown actors claiming to represent Iranian authorities demanded transit fees in Bitcoin or Tether.

stories.title: 12 British varsities paid firm to ‘spy’ on pro-Palestine students: report
stories.summary: An investigation by Al Jazeera and Liberty Investigates found that 12 British universities paid Horus Security Consultancy Limited, a firm run by former military intelligence officials, to monitor student protesters and academics. The firm reportedly surveilled social media accounts and conducted secret counter-terrorism threat assessments targeting those expressing solidarity with Palestine.

stories.title: Tennis duo Sabalenka and Alcaraz sweep top Laureus sports honours
stories.summary: Tennis players Aryna Sabalenka and Carlos Alcaraz won the top Laureus World Sports Awards. Barcelona footballer Lamine Yamal was named Young Sportsperson of the Year, following his Breakthrough award in 2025.

stories.title: Israeli fire kills two more in Gaza; Hamas confronts pro-Israel militia
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed two Palestinians in separate incidents in the Gaza Strip on Monday — one in an airstrike at Bureij camp in central Gaza and another in Gaza City. Hamas fighters also clashed with gunmen from an Israeli-backed militia. The violence continues despite the US-brokered ceasefire deal signed in October.

stories.title: Trump Fed chair pick Kevin Warsh to vow interest rate independence at key hearing
stories.summary: Kevin Warsh, President Trump's nominee to chair the Federal Reserve, is expected to pledge independence on interest rate decisions at a key Senate confirmation hearing. He must clear this hurdle to succeed outgoing Fed Chair Jerome Powell.

stories.title: IRGC says three unexploded US bombs defused in Lorestan province
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reported that its bomb disposal unit defused three unexploded US-made MK-84 aircraft bombs in the western Lorestan province. Each 900-kilogram bomb is capable of creating craters up to 11 meters deep.

stories.title: US officials press Cubans for reforms at Havana meeting
stories.summary: US officials met with Cuban counterparts in Havana to press for reforms. An official said neither side set deadlines or made threatening statements during the discussions.

stories.title: India is violating its obligations under international law: Francesca Albanese
stories.summary: UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese stated that India is violating its obligations under international law. She addressed her latest report on human rights in the occupied Palestinian territories and raised legal and moral concerns about countries supporting Israel.

stories.title: A look back on Queen Elizabeth II’s life, 100 years since her birth – from the SCMP archive
stories.summary: Queen Elizabeth II was born 100 years ago on April 22, 1926, to the Duchess of York, with no expectation she would eventually ascend to the throne. She became Britain's longest-serving monarch, reigning for over 70 years. The South China Morning Post revisited its archival coverage of the queen's life.

stories.title: I’m Sorry, Dave. I’m Afraid I Can’t De-escalate: On (AI) Wargaming and Nuclear War
stories.summary: Researchers at King's College London found that large language models placed in simulated nuclear crisis scenarios frequently escalated conflicts. In 95 percent of simulated games across 21 match-ups between three frontier AI models, at least one side engaged in nuclear signaling, with tactical nuclear use following in most cases.

stories.title: Traitor sentenced to 15 years for passing Ukrainian defense positions in Kharkiv region to Russia
stories.summary: A Ukrainian court sentenced an FSB agent to 15 years in prison with property confiscation for passing Ukrainian defense positions near Kharkiv to Russia. The agent also called for renewed strikes on a local thermal power plant.

stories.title: Mughal-era pigeon training survives in heart of India’s capital
stories.summary: In Delhi, India, the centuries-old Mughal-era tradition of pigeon training and keeping continues to thrive. Residents practice the hobby as a form of therapy and communal bonding amid the pressures of life in the capital.

stories.title: Diplomatic flurry as US-Iran truce deadline nears
stories.summary: As the US-Iran ceasefire deadline approaches, a US negotiating team is heading to Islamabad while Iran is still considering whether to send its delegates. President Trump extended the truce by one day but called a further extension 'highly unlikely,' while Iranian President Pezeshkian criticized contradictory US messages.

stories.title: Trump’s Board of Peace holds Gaza reconstruction talks with UAE’s DP World
stories.summary: Trump's Board of Peace held discussions with UAE-based DP World regarding reconstruction efforts in Gaza. The talks occurred against the backdrop of continued Israeli military operations that have killed more than 700 people in Gaza since last year's US-brokered ceasefire.

stories.title: What the War Against Iran Means for the U.S.-South Korean Alliance
stories.summary: Analysts argue that the standoff over the Strait of Hormuz has direct implications for South Korea's security through energy imports, shipping, and economic stability. The situation highlights how the U.S.-South Korean alliance, originally built to deter North Korea, now extends beyond the Korean Peninsula.

stories.title: Punjab Assembly terms revised agriculture tax null and void
stories.summary: The Punjab Assembly in Pakistan declared government notifications revising agricultural income tax rates illegal, unconstitutional, and void, nullifying all collections under the disputed regime. Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan ruled that the Punjab government violated legal requirements by not presenting the rate changes during the FY 2025-26 budget.

stories.title: Singapore’s US-interest balancing act, viral Songkran clash: 7 Asia highlights
stories.summary: In a rare public protest, hundreds gathered at Singapore's Hong Lim Park to denounce the "US war machine," reflecting rising anti-American sentiment in the city-state. The demonstration highlighted Singapore's balancing act between national interests and public opinion amid regional geopolitical tensions.

stories.title: The Onion launches new bid to take over Alex Jones’ Infowars and turn it into a parody platform
stories.summary: The satirical news outlet The Onion has launched a new bid to acquire conspiracy theorist Alex Jones' Infowars platforms. The Onion intends to transform the Infowars properties into parody content.

stories.title: China’s vast nuclear power sector now able to build 50 reactors at a time
stories.summary: China announced it now has the capacity to build up to 50 nuclear reactors simultaneously, according to a report by the China Nuclear Energy Association. The capability spans the full project life cycle from design to construction, as Beijing pushes to rapidly expand nuclear power generation.

stories.title: Somalia: 72 Media Freedom Violations Reported in Somalia, Including One Journalist Killing
stories.summary: The National Union of Somali Journalists reported 72 media freedom violations in Somalia in 2025, including the killing of one journalist. The report describes a media environment of widespread and systematic repression with impunity for perpetrators.

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 53 of the US-Israel conflict?
stories.summary: On day 53 of the US-Israel military conflict with Iran, diplomatic efforts to end the war have stalled. Tehran has rejected entering negotiations under pressure, leaving prospects for a resolution uncertain.

stories.title: Ghassan Salamé: Lebanon negotiating with Israel 'to give serenity, prosperity to fellow countrymen'
stories.summary: Lebanon's Culture Minister Ghassan Salamé characterized negotiations with Israel as a necessity for achieving sovereignty and stability. He argued that peace requires full sovereignty over Lebanon's land, people, and waters, along with consistent application of international law.

stories.title: Melnyk at UNSC responds to another falsehood from Russia’s Nebenzya
stories.summary: Ukraine's UN Permanent Representative Andrii Melnyk countered statements by Russia's UN representative Nebenzya at the Security Council. Melnyk described the Russian delegation's remarks as distorted narratives about conditions in both Ukraine and Russia.

stories.title: Music executive behind K-pop group BTS faces arrest in South Korea
stories.summary: South Korean police are seeking an arrest warrant for Bang Si-Hyuk, the founder and chair of HYBE, the agency behind K-pop group BTS. He is accused of illegally gaining more than $100 million through an investor fraud scheme.

stories.title: As Singapore overtakes Indonesia in Asean leadership poll, is Prabowo to blame?
stories.summary: A survey by the ISEAS – Yusof Ishak Institute found that Singapore has overtaken Indonesia as the perceived leader of ASEAN among regional opinion leaders. Analysts attributed Indonesia's decline to President Prabowo Subianto's preference for pursuing Jakarta's ambitions outside the regional bloc.

stories.title: Uganda: Ugandan Military Reports Rescue of 200 ADF Hostages in DR Congo
stories.summary: Uganda's military announced that a joint operation with Democratic Republic of Congo forces freed approximately 200 hostages held by the Islamist militant group Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in eastern DRC.

stories.title: Iran remains undecided over second-round talks with US as Vance heads to Islamabad
stories.summary: Iran had not confirmed its participation in a second round of talks with the United States as of Tuesday, with the ceasefire between the two countries nearing expiration. Reporting from Tehran indicated the negotiations remain in the balance.

stories.title: Israeli police arrest two ultra-Orthodox Jews for removing Israeli flags
stories.summary: Israeli police arrested two ultra-Orthodox Jewish men in Beit Shemesh for tearing down Israeli flags. The incident occurred during a period of heightened tensions around national memorial ceremonies.

stories.title: Seized Iranian ship likely carrying equipment deemed dual-use by US, sources say
stories.summary: US forces boarded and seized the Iranian-flagged container ship Touska off the coast of Chabahar port in the Gulf of Oman. Maritime security sources said the vessel, part of the sanctioned IRISL group, likely carried dual-use equipment that Washington considers potentially military-applicable.

stories.title: Explosions rock Sumy: Medical facility hit, four people injured
stories.summary: Explosions struck the Ukrainian city of Sumy, hitting a medical facility, damaging residential buildings, and injuring four people. The attack was part of ongoing Russian strikes on Ukrainian urban areas.

stories.title: A digital Marshall plan: How Musk, Trump, and Pahlavi can free the Iranians - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece proposes a "Digital Marshall Plan" for Iran involving the covert distribution of hundreds of thousands of Starlink terminals across the country. The plan envisions using hybrid insertions and targeted drops to bypass regime internet controls and connect Iranian citizens.

stories.title: US Air Force says key Iran warplane, the A-10 Warthog, will live on to 2030
stories.summary: The US Air Force secretary extended the service life of the A-10 Warthog attack aircraft until 2030, sparing it from a planned 2026 retirement. The close air support plane has played a significant role in operations related to the Iran conflict.

stories.title: EU mulls ending trade agreement with Israel over human rights concerns
stories.summary: The EU is set to discuss its trade agreement with Israel amid concerns raised by some member states over potential human rights violations in Gaza, Lebanon, and the West Bank. A previous proposal to cut trade ties or sanction Israeli ministers failed to gain sufficient support among member states.

stories.title: After Xi, South Korea’s Lee brings Modi into ‘selfie diplomacy’ frame
stories.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and Samsung chairman Lee Jae-yong posed for a viral selfie during a Korea-India summit in New Delhi using Samsung's Galaxy Z Flip7. The image drew attention to "selfie diplomacy" months after Lee's earlier selfie with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

stories.title: Zelenskyy: leaving Donbas means losing war’s strongest shield — its cities
stories.summary: President Zelenskyy argued that withdrawing from the Donbas would constitute a strategic defeat for Ukraine, emphasizing that the region's urban defenses are far stronger than any fortifications built in open fields.

stories.title: Trump invokes wartime powers to fund new energy projects
stories.summary: President Trump invoked wartime powers to fund new energy projects amid rising oil, gas, and electricity costs driven by the Iran conflict. The move aims to expand domestic energy production to offset price pressures.

stories.title: Gunman kills Canadian tourist visiting Mexico's pyramids
stories.summary: A gunman killed a Canadian tourist and wounded several others at Mexico's Teotihuacán archaeological site, specifically at the Pyramid of the Moon. Authorities confirmed the shooting at the heavily visited pre-Aztec destination in central Mexico.

stories.title: Melnyk at UN Security Council: Ukraine rejects Russia’s ultimatums, will not abandon single millimeter of its soil
stories.summary: Ukraine's UN Permanent Representative Andrii Melnyk told the Security Council that Ukraine rejects Russia's ultimatums and will not cede any territory. He stated that Russia is suffering enormous battlefield losses while making only minimal territorial gains.

stories.title: UK’s Starmer says he’s sorry but won’t resign after facing MPs on Mandelson-Epstein scandal
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer apologized to MPs over his appointment of Peter Mandelson as US envoy, acknowledging it was a mistake given Mandelson's links to Jeffrey Epstein. Starmer refused to resign despite opposition pressure, and a sacked Foreign Office official was scheduled to address MPs.

stories.title: U.S. officials press Cubans for reforms at Havana meeting
stories.summary: US officials met with Cuban counterparts in Havana to press for reforms, signaling potential diplomatic progress between the two countries. The talks occurred despite President Trump's previous hints at possible military action against Cuba.

stories.title: Trump’s ‘Board of Peace’ held talks with DP World over Gaza reconstruction, report says
stories.summary: Representatives of Trump's "Board of Peace" held discussions with Dubai-based DP World about managing supply chains and infrastructure projects in Gaza, the Financial Times reported. The talks explored whether DP World could partner on logistics for humanitarian aid entering the territory.

stories.title: Egypt hosts US envoy as regional talks continue on Sudan, Lebanon, and Iran
stories.summary: Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sissi met in Cairo with US envoy Massad Boulos to discuss developments in Sudan and Lebanon. El-Sissi also praised US President Donald Trump's efforts to secure a ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Iran weighs Pakistan talks with US, and claims it has ‘new cards for battlefield’
stories.summary: Iran is weighing whether to join US-brokered peace talks in Pakistan, with officials stressing no decision has been made. US Vice President JD Vance is set to travel to Islamabad to lead the American delegation if Iran agrees to participate.

stories.title: Iran war forces job losses, reverse migration in India’s ceramic hub
stories.summary: Gujarat's Morbi ceramics industry has suffered widespread closures and layoffs due to a fuel crisis linked to the Iran war. Most production units in the region have shut down, forcing workers to lose their jobs and triggering reverse migration.

stories.title: Iran urges UN action over 'barbarous' US seizure, says crew families threatened
stories.summary: Iran filed formal complaints with the United Nations and the International Maritime Organisation over the US seizure of the vessel Touska, calling it an illegal act violating international law and a ceasefire agreement. Tehran alleged crew members and their families were subjected to intimidation and demanded the ship's immediate release.

stories.title: Trump says recovering Iran uranium 'will be a long and difficult process'
stories.summary: President Trump described the effort to recover uranium from Iran as a "long and difficult process" following US strikes on Tehran's nuclear sites. He referenced "Operation Midnight Hammer" on Truth Social, claiming it achieved total destruction of Iranian nuclear facilities.

stories.title: Israel's 78th Independence Day: Optimism, not pessimism, will rebuild the nation - editorial
stories.summary: Israel marked its 78th Independence Day amid ongoing conflict. The article highlights that new immigrants continue to arrive and Israel ranked high in the World Happiness Report, framing optimism as central to the nation's resilience and growth.

stories.title: China influencer tricked into Cambodia cyber scam recounts ordeal but live-stream was cut short
stories.summary: A 20-year-old Chinese influencer known as Umi live-streamed her account of being lured to Cambodia and forced into a cyber scam operation, but the broadcast was abruptly cut off and her social media account was banned. She had previously gained national attention after being rescued from Cambodia in January.

stories.title: Chinese scientists replicate eel’s 6,000km breeding journey inside research pool
stories.summary: Chinese researchers at the Chinese Academy of Fishery Sciences, led by Zhao Feng, successfully replicated the complete 6,000-kilometer breeding life cycle of eels within an artificial research pool. The breakthrough, which used satellite-tracking technology, could help save the migratory species from extinction.

stories.title: Nigeria: Peter Okoye Changes Birth Date Amid Rift With Twin Brother Paul
stories.summary: Nigerian musician Peter Okoye changed his official birth date amid an ongoing rift with his twin brother Paul. In June 2025, Peter publicly declared he had severed ties with his family, particularly his brothers.

stories.title: Iran accuses US of ‘terrorism’ over ship seizure
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Ministry condemned the US seizure of the vessel Tosca, calling it maritime piracy, terrorism, and a ceasefire violation. Tehran demanded the ship and crew's release and warned of dire consequences if they remain detained.

stories.title: After Iran war, attack on Gulf States, will the GCC withdraw from Arab League - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis explores whether Gulf Cooperation Council states might withdraw from the Arab League following the Iran war and attacks on Gulf states. Kuwaiti political journalist Abdullah Al-Khamis proposes an alternative Arab coordination council comprising Gulf states, Jordan, Morocco, and Syria.

stories.title: Trump criticizes US media over coverage of Iran war
stories.summary: President Trump accused CNN and other US media outlets of biased coverage of the Iran war, calling them "Anti-America Fake News Media." He claimed the outlets were rooting for Iran and failing to credit US military personnel.

stories.title: US, Iran warn they are ready for war as peace talks remain in limbo
stories.summary: The United States and Iran both warned they are prepared for war as peace talks remain uncertain. Tehran has accused Washington of violating a soon-to-expire ceasefire through its blockade of Iranian ports and seizure of a ship.

stories.title: US-Iran talks in limbo as Trump vows no let-up in blockade
stories.summary: Tehran accused the United States of violating a soon-to-expire ceasefire by maintaining a blockade of Iranian ports and seizing an Iranian ship. US President Donald Trump vowed no let-up in the blockade, leaving the status of US-Iran negotiations uncertain.

stories.title: Slain hostage’s mother aims to perpetuate life with son’s posthumously retrieved sperm
stories.summary: Iris Haim, mother of slain Israeli hostage Yotam Haim who was mistakenly killed by IDF troops after escaping captivity in Gaza, obtained a court ruling allowing the family to use his posthumously retrieved sperm for conception.

stories.title: Trump attacks US media over Iran war coverage
stories.summary: President Trump criticized CNN, The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, and The Washington Post for portraying the Iran conflict as a US loss. He claimed "Operation Midnight Hammer" was a complete success against Iranian nuclear sites.

stories.title: Tuesday briefing: What it might take for lasting peace between the US and Iran
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance is expected to fly to Pakistan if Iran agrees to further talks on ending the US-Iran conflict. Despite an existing ceasefire, both sides have escalated threats, leaving the prospect of lasting peace uncertain.

stories.title: Burkina Faso: Crackdown On Civil Society
stories.summary: Human Rights Watch reported that Burkina Faso's government has carried out a mass dissolution of civic groups and is enforcing repressive laws. The crackdown represents a significant escalation against civil society in the country.

stories.title: Iraqi Shi’ite leaders pick Bassem al-Badry as PM nominee, sources say
stories.summary: Leaders of Iraq's main Shi'ite Muslim political blocs selected government official Bassem al-Badry as their nominee for prime minister during a meeting in Baghdad on Monday. Two Shi'ite officials confirmed the decision, though no official public announcement was made.

stories.title: At soldiers’ graves, the rows keep growing: Remembrance Day is shaped by new loss
stories.summary: Families across Israel marked Memorial Day (Yom Hazikaron) amid continued fighting and a growing number of new casualties. The observances this year were shaped by the expanding rows of soldiers' graves reflecting ongoing losses.

stories.title: Ukrainian-Polish expedition begins search work at sites of two former villages in Volyn region
stories.summary: A joint Ukrainian-Polish search expedition has begun at the sites of former villages Ostrivky and Volia Ostrovetska in Ukraine's Volyn region. The operation aims to locate remains of local residents killed in August 1943.

stories.title: NBA: Victor Wembanyama named first unanimous defensive player of the year
stories.summary: San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama became the first unanimous NBA Defensive Player of the Year, receiving all 100 first-place votes. At 22, he is the youngest recipient of the award and led the league in blocks for a third consecutive season.

stories.title: US veterans arrested in Capitol during protest against the war on Iran
stories.summary: US military veterans were arrested inside the Capitol building in Washington, D.C., while staging a protest against the ongoing war on Iran.

stories.title: 5 arrested at Hong Kong pharmacies, anti-obesity pills and other dangerous drugs seized
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities arrested five men at registered pharmacies and seized thousands of unregistered anti-obesity medicines and dangerous drugs, including clonazepam and zolpidem. The Department of Health conducted the operation jointly with police at a pharmacy in Sha Tin district.

stories.title: Outlook for China stocks brightens on capital flows, rebounding home prices
stories.summary: Despite stronger-than-expected first-quarter GDP growth, China's urban youth unemployment rate for ages 16-24 rose to 16.9 percent in March from 16.1 percent in February, ending six months of decline. The increase comes as a record graduation season approaches, adding pressure to a job market already affected by deflation and external challenges.

stories.title: Malaysian sultan warns Asean staring at ‘economic crisis’ over Hormuz closure
stories.summary: Malaysia's Sultan Nazrin Shah of Perak warned that the closure of the Strait of Hormuz due to the Middle East conflict is pushing ASEAN nations toward an economic crisis. He cited surging energy, fertilizer, and transport prices driving up food costs and inflation across the region.

stories.title: Sudan war: Senior RSF commander defects to army in major blow to paramilitaries
stories.summary: A senior Rapid Support Forces commander in Sudan has defected to the Sudanese army, dealing a significant blow to the paramilitary group. The defection may signal new fractures within the RSF as Sudan's civil conflict enters its fourth year.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Mugabe Was 'Devastated' By Chiwenga's Illness After 2017 Ouster - Former Spokesperson
stories.summary: Former spokesperson for the late Robert Mugabe revealed that Mugabe was reportedly devastated by Vice President Constantino Chiwenga's illness following the 2017 military-led transition that ousted him. Despite Chiwenga's central role in removing him from power, Mugabe reportedly bore no ill will.

stories.title: Zimbabwe: Parliament Not for Sale - Zanu-PF Youth League
stories.summary: Zimbabwe's ruling ZANU PF youth league urged Parliament to reject a reported multi-million dollar donation from businessman Wicknell Chivayo. The youth wing warned against any perception of undue influence over state institutions.

stories.title: Palantir manifesto described as ‘ramblings of a supervillain’ amid UK contract fears
stories.summary: US tech company Palantir published a manifesto championing American military dominance and AI weapons, prompting alarm in the UK amid concerns over government contracts. CEO Alex Karp's posts implied some cultures are inferior to others, drawing criticism from British MPs who called the document "the ramblings of a supervillain."

stories.title: Israeli soldiers using sexual assault to force Palestinians out of West Bank, report says
stories.summary: A report alleges that Israeli soldiers and settlers are using sexual assault, forced nudity, and gendered violence to force Palestinians from their homes in the occupied West Bank. Experts say the attacks are causing girls to leave school and enter early marriages.

stories.title: Amnesty International slams ‘predatory world order’ led by US and Israel
stories.summary: Amnesty International Secretary General Agnes Callamard accused the United States, Israel, and Russia of waging war on civilians with impunity, describing the current global order as 'predatory.'

stories.title: Japan lifts ban on lethal weapons exports in major shift of pacifist policy
stories.summary: Japan is moving to lift its longstanding ban on lethal weapons exports, potentially allowing the sale of military hardware including fighter jets overseas. The policy shift marks a significant departure from decades of pacifist restrictions.

stories.title: Gunman kills Canadian woman, wounds four at Mexico’s Teotihuacan pyramids
stories.summary: A gunman killed a Canadian woman and wounded four others at the Teotihuacan pyramids near Mexico City on Monday before fatally shooting himself. Authorities confirmed the incident at one of Mexico's most visited tourist sites.

stories.title: Hezbollah MP calls for Lebanese president to withdraw from Israel talks
stories.summary: Hezbollah MP Hassan Fadlallah called on Lebanon's president to withdraw from direct negotiations with Israel. He said Hezbollah would reject any concessions to Israel and urged a return to national consensus on Lebanon's diplomatic approach.

stories.title: Sudan: Rising Civilian Toll in South Kordofan As Fighting Intensifies, Drone Strike Kills Three At West Darfur Hospital
stories.summary: At least 100 civilians have been killed in Delling, South Kordofan, Sudan, since February, with 35 killed in early April alone, according to a protection group of international organizations and UN agencies. A drone strike also killed three people at a hospital in El Geneina, West Darfur. Over 50,000 civilians are at severe risk from indiscriminate shelling and airstrikes.

stories.title: Hezbollah says it will break Israel’s ‘yellow line’ in Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah lawmaker Hassan Fadlallah declared the group would break the "yellow line" security zone established by Israel in southern Lebanon, despite an active 10-day ceasefire. He asserted Hezbollah's right to self-defense and rejected calls to disarm.

stories.title: Israeli airlines accused of reselling stranded customers’ seats for wartime windfall
stories.summary: Israeli airlines face accusations of refunding stranded travelers instead of rebooking them, then reselling the freed seats at inflated wartime prices. Critics allege the practice appears to violate Israeli law while profiting from high demand during the conflict.

stories.title: Work-from-home may not save as much energy as Southeast Asia hopes
stories.summary: Several Southeast Asian governments, including Indonesia and the Philippines, have implemented work-from-home policies for civil servants to reduce energy costs driven by the Iran war. However, analysts question the projected savings, noting the actual energy reduction calculations are more complex than initially estimated.

stories.title: Court ruling fails to ease aid flow into Gaza
stories.summary: Foreign aid organizations report continued difficulties operating in the Gaza Strip and occupied West Bank despite an Israeli Supreme Court decision freezing a government ban on dozens of NGOs. International staff and supplies continue to face access restrictions.

stories.title: Jerusalem's Assembly of Catholic Ordinances condemns destruction of statue of Jesus in s. Lebanon
stories.summary: The Assembly of Catholic Ordinances in Jerusalem condemned the destruction of a statue of Jesus in southern Lebanon. The statement described the act as a grave affront to the Christian faith and cited other reported incidents of IDF soldiers desecrating Christian symbols in the area.

stories.title: Vance to travel to Islamabad, Iranian delegation gets reported approval from supreme leader - Axios
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance is reportedly set to travel to Islamabad, according to Axios. Separately, Iran's negotiating team reportedly received approval from the supreme leader to engage in talks, though the team faced pressure from the IRGC to refuse negotiations without an end to the US blockade.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone forces hit Russian Tor-M2KM system, S-350 radar
stories.summary: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces struck a Russian S-350 air defense system's 50N6E radar and a Tor-M2KM surface-to-air missile system. The drone strikes targeted key Russian air defense assets on the battlefield.

stories.title: Palestinian woman killed by Israeli naval fire off Gaza coast
stories.summary: A Palestinian woman was killed by gunfire from Israeli warships off Gaza's northern coast, according to Al Jazeera Arabic. Gaza's health ministry also reported five Palestinians killed in separate Israeli strikes across the territory on Monday.

stories.title: Principal and three teachers plead not guilty to assaulting students at regional NSW school
stories.summary: A principal and three teachers at a regional New South Wales school have pleaded not guilty to charges of assaulting two students. Police allege the four educators—two men and two women—attacked the boys at the school between August 2024 and June 2025.

stories.title: US says 415 troops wounded in Iran war
stories.summary: The Pentagon reported that 415 US service members have been wounded in the war involving Iran. The casualties span multiple branches: 271 army, 63 navy, 62 air force, and 19 marines.

stories.title: US did not meet goals in Iran war, report says
stories.summary: A Politico report found that the US did not achieve its stated objectives in the Iran war and that the conflict weakened Washington's global influence. The report noted the US failed to inform some close allies about initial military decisions, and American popularity declined in Muslim-majority countries.

stories.title: China achieves a world first, updating stabilisers for renewable energy grids
stories.summary: China developed the world's first 35-kilovolt direct-connection high-voltage synchronous condenser, built by Dongfang Electric Machinery. The technology revives a century-old grid stabilization approach to support China's expanding renewable energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Why more Rohingya risk sea escapes to Malaysia, Indonesia: ‘some make it, some die’
stories.summary: Rohingya refugees continue to undertake dangerous sea crossings from Bangladesh toward Malaysia and Indonesia, with hundreds dying en route annually. Survivor Rahila Begum spent two days adrift in the Andaman Sea after her overcrowded boat capsized, a disaster that left 250 people missing and feared dead.

stories.title: China’s youth unemployment crunch deepens as record graduation season looms
stories.summary: China's urban youth unemployment rate for ages 16-24 rose to 16.9 percent in March, reversing six consecutive months of decline, even as overall first-quarter economic growth exceeded expectations. The worsening job market faces additional pressure from an approaching record university graduation season.

stories.title: Rahm Emanuel joins calls to end US ‘financial aid’ as Democratic support for Israel hits new lows
stories.summary: Former Chicago mayor Rahm Emanuel called for ending US financial aid to Israel, saying America should not spill blood for Israel's security. He asserted that Jerusalem dragged the US into the conflict in violation of a longstanding rule, as Democratic support for Israel reaches new lows.

stories.title: Police detain Russian agent who was preparing new strikes on Kyiv's heat and power plants
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service (SSU) detained an FSB agent near Kyiv who was preparing a new series of missile and drone attacks on the capital region. The agent was also spying on bases of Ukraine's Defense Forces.

stories.title: UN Economist says energy costs weighing down on China and India
stories.summary: A senior UN economist said rising oil prices are expected to slow economic growth in China from 5 percent to between 4.3 and 4.6 percent this year. India's growth is also forecast to ease from over 7 percent to about 6 percent due to energy costs.

stories.title: Amnesty warns of ‘primitive ferocity’ by 'voracious predators' in global order
stories.summary: Amnesty International's annual report identified Israel, Russia, and the United States as leading a global decline in human rights. Secretary General Agnes Callamard described their leaders as "voracious predators" fostering an environment of "primitive ferocity."

stories.title: US, Iran warn ready for war as talks in limbo
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned they would target any vessel attempting to pass through the Strait of Hormuz without permission, as both the US and Iran signaled readiness to resume fighting. Diplomatic talks remain in limbo.

stories.title: New jihadist group or Iranian proxy? Ashab al-Yamin attacks raise alarm across Europe - analysis
stories.summary: An analysis examines the emerging terror group Ashab al-Yamin, whose attacks across Europe have raised alarm. The group may function as an Iranian proxy, with Iran's regime allegedly using criminals, youth, and third-country nationals to carry out its agenda abroad.

stories.title: Israel kills more than 780 Palestinians in Gaza since ceasefire began, ministry says
stories.summary: Gaza's health ministry reported that more than 780 Palestinians have been killed in Israeli strikes since a ceasefire was agreed in October. Five people were killed on Monday in separate incidents across the territory, including shelling in Khan Younis and a drone strike in Bureij refugee camp.

stories.title: Michigan Democrats back pro-Palestinian candidate for university board
stories.summary: Michigan Democrats selected a pro-Palestinian candidate, Makled, for a university board position. The move reflects a broader trend in which Democratic voters increasingly disapprove of Israel, signaling the growing influence of the party's pro-Palestinian wing in Michigan.

stories.title: Canadian woman killed after gunman opens fire at Mexico’s Teotihuacán pyramids
stories.summary: A gunman opened fire at Mexico's Teotihuacán pyramids near Mexico City on Monday, killing one Canadian tourist and wounding six others. The shooting is the latest violent incident in Mexico as the country prepares to co-host the football World Cup in June.

stories.title: Cuba confirms talks with US officials, urges end to Trump energy blockade
stories.summary: Cuba's foreign ministry confirmed that Havana recently hosted talks with US officials, with delegations including US assistant secretaries and Cuba's deputy foreign minister. A senior Cuban diplomat urged an end to the Trump administration's energy blockade as the island faces a deep economic crisis.

stories.title: Over $90 billion needed over next decade to rebuild Gaza, study says
stories.summary: A study estimates that over $90 billion will be needed over the next decade to rebuild Gaza. Approximately $33 billion is required in the first 18 months to restore essential services, rebuild critical infrastructure, and support economic recovery.

stories.title: EU to host Taliban officials for talks on deporting Afghans
stories.summary: The European Union is planning to host Taliban officials for discussions on deporting Afghan nationals who lack legal residence in the bloc back to Afghanistan.

stories.title: Why leading Chinese scientists are rising to the top in the Communist Party
stories.summary: A new report found that the number of academicians from China's leading scientific and engineering institutes in the Communist Party's Central Committee doubled from 15 in 2012 to 30 in 2022. Scientists now account for roughly 8 percent of Central Committee membership, reflecting their growing political influence.

stories.title: Restrictions lifted, but war clouds put damper on Independence Day plans
stories.summary: Israeli cities are proceeding with Independence Day celebrations amid fragile ceasefires with Lebanon and Iran, though some have scaled back events. War-weary residents expressed caution and fatigue despite the lifting of public gathering restrictions.

stories.title: Israel hindering Gaza aid access despite court ruling, says NGO
stories.summary: Aid organizations say Israel continues to hinder access to Gaza despite an Israeli Supreme Court ruling that froze a government ban on dozens of NGOs. International groups report ongoing difficulties delivering assistance in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Gulf states worry US-Iran talks may cement Tehran’s ‘golden’ grip on Hormuz
stories.summary: Ongoing US-Iran negotiations are increasingly focused on the Strait of Hormuz, raising concerns among Gulf states that their broader regional security interests are being sidelined. Gulf leaders worry a potential deal could strengthen Tehran's strategic position over the critical waterway.

stories.title: China bets on RISC-V in global AI race
stories.summary: China is investing heavily in the open-source RISC-V chip architecture as part of its strategy in the global AI race. Researchers at the Chinese Academy of Sciences unveiled their latest Xiangshan processor, and experts at the Zhongguancun Forum in Beijing celebrated the establishment of a complete RISC-V ecosystem in China.

stories.title: A new F/A-XX timeline and many, many MUSVs at Sea Air Space Day 1
stories.summary: The first day of the Navy League's Sea-Air-Space conference featured a new timeline for the F/A-XX next-generation fighter program and extensive discussion of medium unmanned surface vessels. Reporters Aaron Mehta and Diana Stancy shared highlights from the event.

stories.title: US officials press Cubans for reforms at Havana meeting
stories.summary: US officials met with Cuban counterparts in Havana this month, both governments confirmed on Monday. Washington is pressing for reforms to Cuba's state-led economy amid an energy crisis on the island and a US blockade on oil shipments to Cuba.

stories.title: Tigray party to restore pre-war administration, jeopardising northern Ethiopia peace
stories.summary: Tigray's main political party announced from Nairobi on April 20 that it would reassert control over the region's government. The move effectively voids the peace agreement with Ethiopia's federal government that ended one of the century's deadliest conflicts, jeopardizing stability in northern Ethiopia.

stories.title: Strike on Russian army logistics: Partisans disable substation in Voronezh region
stories.summary: Partisans from the ATESH resistance movement sabotaged a substation in Russia's Voronezh region, disrupting logistics for a Russian army grouping operating on the Kharkiv axis. The operation directly targeted supply infrastructure supporting Russian forces.

stories.title: Cuba confirms talks with US officials, wants end to Trump’s energy blockade
stories.summary: Cuba confirmed it held talks with US officials, describing the exchange as respectful and professional. A Cuban Foreign Ministry official said the discussions were free of threats, and Havana called for an end to the Trump administration's energy blockade.

stories.title: Democrats push fifth vote to curb Trump’s Iran war
stories.summary: US Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer announced Democrats would force a fifth vote on a war powers resolution to halt President Trump's war with Iran. Schumer urged Senate Republicans to stop sitting on the sidelines while service members risk their lives.

stories.title: Pakistan urges Trump to tone down rhetoric ahead of talks
stories.summary: A Pakistani official told The Washington Post that Islamabad warned President Trump against using strong public rhetoric ahead of potential US-Iran talks. Pakistan is mediating between the two sides and said it received a positive signal from Iran regarding participation in negotiations.

stories.title: Axios: Vance to head to Pakistan as ceasefire deadline nears
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance is expected to travel to Islamabad for talks aimed at ending the war with Iran, Axios reported. The visit comes as a fragile ceasefire nears expiration, though Iran has not confirmed its participation in the negotiations.

stories.title: Apple says chief executive Tim Cook stepping down in September
stories.summary: Apple announced on Monday that CEO Tim Cook, 65, will step down on September 1. John Ternus, head of hardware engineering and an Apple employee since 2001, will succeed him. Cook will remain with the Cupertino-based company as executive chairman.

stories.title: Trump: New deal with Iran will be better than old one
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated that a new deal with Iran would be "far better" than the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, from which he withdrew the United States in 2018.

stories.title: Global Sumud Flotilla disrupts cargo ship bound for Israel
stories.summary: Activists from the Global Sumud Flotilla intercepted and disrupted a cargo ship they claimed was carrying materials destined for Israeli weapons production en route to Israel.

stories.title: ‘Another row’: Families of slain soldiers mark Memorial Day in shadow of continued war
stories.summary: Bereaved Israeli families marked Memorial Day while the country remains engaged in ongoing conflict. Parents of fallen soldiers gathered at military cemeteries, finding solace in shared grief as new rows of graves reflect the war's continuing toll.

stories.title: Right-wing activists disrupt joint Israeli-Palestinian Remembrance Day ceremony in Tel Aviv - KAN
stories.summary: Right-wing activists including Mordechai David, Rami Ben Yehuda, and Sheffi Paz attempted to disrupt a joint Israeli-Palestinian Remembrance Day ceremony in south Tel Aviv. Hundreds of attendees, including relatives of October 7 victims, were present at the event.

stories.title: Middle East war live: US, Iran warn they are ready for war as peace talks in limbo
stories.summary: The United States and Iran both warned they are prepared for war as peace talks announced by President Trump for Pakistan remain in limbo. A ceasefire between the two countries is set to expire overnight Tuesday.

stories.title: Who is John Ternus, Apple’s next CEO?
stories.summary: Apple announced that hardware engineering executive John Ternus will succeed Tim Cook as CEO, effective September 1. Cook will transition to executive chair of the board. Ternus is a longtime company insider, signaling continuity of Apple's strategy that has driven annual profits above $100 billion.

stories.title: Board of Peace envoy says Gaza plan needs quick progress, Hamas talks ‘not easy’
stories.summary: The lead envoy for Gaza on the Board of Peace said he is fairly optimistic about reaching an arrangement that works for all sides. He noted that the Gaza plan requires quick progress and acknowledged that talks with Hamas are "not easy."

stories.title: Chinese circuit-board supplier Victory Giant jumps 57% in Hong Kong share debut
stories.summary: Victory Giant, a Guangdong-based Chinese printed circuit board manufacturer and Nvidia supplier, surged 57 percent in its Hong Kong trading debut on Tuesday. The company raised HK$20 billion in its IPO, driven by investor demand tied to the global AI infrastructure boom.

stories.title: Iran pulling Hormuz ‘lever’ to maximum in US standoff
stories.summary: Iran is leveraging its control over the Strait of Hormuz to maximum effect in its standoff with the United States. However, using the critical waterway as a bargaining tool carries significant risks for the Islamic Republic.

stories.title: Neighbours shocked after ‘nice uncle’ arrested in Malaysia for gunning down 3
stories.summary: A 71-year-old man was arrested in Taman Kota Jaya, Johor, Malaysia, for fatally shooting three people at a food court. Neighbors expressed shock, describing the suspect as a friendly and polite community member who regularly shared produce from his orchard.

stories.title: US is ‘pretty far behind where they started’ the war on Iran
stories.summary: Analyst Daniel Benaim assessed that the United States is in a worse strategic position than when it began the war on Iran, arguing that Washington missed early opportunities to declare victory and pursue off-ramps.

stories.title: Global fallout grows over Israeli soldier smashing Jesus statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: International outrage is intensifying over a photograph showing an Israeli soldier smashing a statue of Jesus Christ in Lebanon. The incident has drawn widespread condemnation from religious and political figures globally.

stories.title: Which global firms are being attracted by Hong Kong’s strategic enterprise scheme?
stories.summary: Twenty-two strategic enterprises, including Pfizer, have signed agreements with Hong Kong's Office for Attracting Strategic Enterprises to open or expand operations in the city. This sixth cohort brings the total number of strategic partners to over 120 since the initiative launched in 2022.

stories.title: Maker of China’s C919 jet weighs supply chain weaknesses amid delivery delays
stories.summary: China's Commercial Aircraft Corporation (Comac) is reassessing geopolitical risks to its C919 passenger jet supply chain, particularly its reliance on foreign-sourced jet engines. The Shanghai-based manufacturer faces delivery delays this year due to both external supply constraints and internal manpower shortages.

stories.title: Hong Kong can advance AI beyond the confines of geopolitical rivalry
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that Hong Kong can play a meaningful role in advancing artificial intelligence development beyond the US-China rivalry. It contends the global AI landscape is more complex than a simple bipolar competition, with middle powers actively shaping the emerging order.

stories.title: Bot farm supplying fake accounts to Russian intelligence uncovered in Zhytomyr
stories.summary: Ukrainian authorities neutralized a bot farm in Zhytomyr that supplied over 3,000 fake accounts per month to Russian intelligence services. The accounts were used to spread Kremlin propaganda and disinformation about Ukrainian forces.

stories.title: Sub that sank Iranian warship reflects Navy’s drive to adapt, CNO says
stories.summary: The Chief of Naval Operations said a US submarine's sinking of an Iranian warship reflects the Navy's push to adapt to modern warfare. Admiral Caudle described the incident as "a glimpse of the future force" at the Sea-Air-Space conference.

stories.title: Pennsylvania court strikes down ban on use of Medicaid funds for abortions
stories.summary: A Pennsylvania commonwealth court ruled that the state constitution guarantees a right to abortion and struck down a decades-old ban on using state Medicaid funds for abortion costs. The decision is a major victory for Planned Parenthood and abortion clinic operators who sued in 2019.

stories.title: Plight of parentless China boy cared by grandpa attracts 46 million views, prompts government aid
stories.summary: A nine-year-old boy named Zichen in Taikang county, Henan province, China, gained widespread attention after his story of caring for his 73-year-old grandfather went viral with 46 million views. The boy brought meat from his school canteen home, fearing his grandfather might die without adequate nutrition, prompting local authorities to intervene with assistance.

stories.title: ‘Sailing over a ball of fire’: Iraqi captain keeps traversing Mideast waters amid threat of attack
stories.summary: Iraqi ship captain Rahman Al-Jubouri continues navigating Middle Eastern waters despite Iranian attacks on tankers amid the US-Iran standoff. He described the work as a serious risk, with crew members battling danger and homesickness.

stories.title: Iran will not negotiate under threat, bend to force, top officials say
stories.summary: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad-Bagher Ghalibaf accused US President Trump of violating a ceasefire by imposing what he called a siege. Senior Iranian officials stated that Iran will not negotiate under threat or yield to the use of force.

stories.title: Trump, Iran and the Strait of Hormuz: here’s what happened overnight
stories.summary: As a two-week US-Iran ceasefire neared its end, President Trump defended the war and insisted the Strait of Hormuz blockade would remain until a deal is reached. Uncertainty persists over whether negotiations will resume in Pakistan, with a US team prepared to travel to Islamabad.

stories.title: Lubinets calls for international missions to be granted access to Russian-occupied Oleshky
stories.summary: Ukraine's Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights, Dmytro Lubinets, called on the international community to grant humanitarian missions access to the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in the Kherson region. Lubinets cited a humanitarian catastrophe and inhumane living conditions, urging documentation of crimes and establishment of effective response mechanisms.

stories.title: Hong Kong retailers leverage scale, sourcing to offset war-driven cost pressures
stories.summary: Hong Kong's major retailers are employing direct sourcing and economies of scale to absorb rising logistics costs caused by the Middle East war. However, cosmetics chain Sa Sa International warned that shipping and airfreight costs have already risen by up to 15 percent, testing their ability to hold prices.

stories.title: Fitness influencer drowns during swimming portion of Ironman Texas
stories.summary: Brazilian fitness influencer Mara Flavia Souza Araujo, 38, drowned during the swimming portion of Ironman Texas at Lake Woodlands near Houston on Saturday. She was reported as a lost swimmer, and divers recovered her body approximately 90 minutes later in 10 feet of water.

stories.title: Vance to reportedly depart today for Pakistan as Iran’s top negotiator blasts US blockade
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance was reportedly set to depart for Pakistan for ceasefire talks, while Iran's top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf criticized the US blockade and threatened new battlefield actions if the war resumes.

stories.title: Six women win 2026 Goldman prize, world’s top environmental award
stories.summary: Six women from Colombia, Nigeria, Papua New Guinea, South Korea, the United Kingdom, and the United States won the 2026 Goldman Environmental Prize. It marks the first time an all-women cohort has received the award.

stories.title: Jewish man among first charged in pro-Palestinian slogan crackdown that reminds some of 1970s Queensland
stories.summary: Stephen Heydt, a 73-year-old Jewish clinical psychologist, was among the first people charged in Brisbane under a crackdown on pro-Palestinian slogans. He was arrested at a rally for wearing a custom-made T-shirt and chanting, facing two separate offences. Critics have compared the crackdown to authoritarian policing in 1970s Queensland.

stories.title: Victor Wembanyama wins NBA Defensive Player of the year in unanimous vote
stories.summary: Victor Wembanyama of the San Antonio Spurs unanimously won the NBA Defensive Player of the Year award, receiving all 100 first-place votes. At 22, he is the youngest winner and has led the league in blocks for three consecutive seasons.

stories.title: Chief conductor of St. Petersburg Symphony Orchestra dies after falling ill on flight to Istanbul
stories.summary: Sergei Stadler, chief conductor and artistic director of the St. Petersburg Symphony Orchestra, died at age 63 on April 20 after falling ill on a flight to Istanbul. Russian outlet Fontanka reported the death, citing the St. Petersburg governor's press service.

stories.title: Can Iran protect friendly shipping? Attack on Indian tankers raises safety questions
stories.summary: Iran's firing on two Indian-flagged oil tankers, the Jag Arnav and another vessel, in the Strait of Hormuz has raised questions about Tehran's ability to protect friendly shipping. The incident is particularly sensitive given India's non-adversarial relationship with Iran and its recent resumption of Iranian oil purchases under a US sanctions waiver.

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon to hold second round of talks in Washington on April 23
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon are scheduled to hold a second round of ambassador-level talks in Washington on April 23. The United States is hosting the negotiations between the two countries.

stories.title: Israel, Lebanon to hold second round of talks in Washington on April 23
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon will hold a second round of ambassador-level talks in Washington on April 23. The U.S. Department of State will host the negotiations between the two countries.

stories.title: Iran war live: Tehran spurns talks under threats; Trump says blockade stays
stories.summary: Iran declared it will not enter negotiations "under the shadow of threats," while President Trump said the US blockade in the Strait of Hormuz would continue. Diplomatic efforts remain stalled as both sides hold firm positions.

stories.title: Zelensky: Withdrawal from Donbas would be strategic defeat for Ukrainian Armed Forces
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that withdrawing forces from contested areas of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions in the Donbas would constitute a strategic defeat for the Ukrainian Armed Forces. Zelensky called any such withdrawal irresponsible given the military situation.

stories.title: Two killed after planned fight between youth  at North Carolina park escalates to shooting
stories.summary: Two people were fatally shot and several others injured at a North Carolina park after a planned confrontation between youth escalated into gunfire. The North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation confirmed the incident.

stories.title: ‘They’re not easy’: Board of Peace envoy admits Hamas disarmament talks stalled
stories.summary: Board of Peace envoy Nickolay Mladenov acknowledged that negotiations over Hamas disarmament have stalled after the group ignored an initial ultimatum. He said an agreement must be reached within two weeks before diplomatic momentum is lost.

stories.title: Iraq reopens Rabia border crossing after nearly 13 years to boost fuel oil exports via Syria
stories.summary: Iraq reopened the Rabia border crossing with Syria after nearly 13 years of closure to boost fuel oil exports. The crossing, formerly a major trade route, had been shut down following the emergence of the ISIS terrorist group.

stories.title: Another Democrat, Betty Yee, exits crowded race for California governor
stories.summary: Former California state controller Betty Yee suspended her campaign for governor, becoming the latest Democrat to exit the crowded race. Yee, who was vying to be the first woman to hold the office, cited lagging fundraising and low polling numbers.

stories.title: Putin signs decree letting importers defer VAT payments for up to 3 months
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree launching a pilot program allowing importers to defer value-added tax payments collected by customs authorities for up to three months. The program will run until June 30, 2027.

stories.title: ‘Predators’: Amnesty slams Netanyahu, Putin, Trump as human rights decline
stories.summary: Amnesty International's latest report singled out Israeli PM Netanyahu, Russian President Putin, and US President Trump as leaders behind devastating wars that have inspired other states to commit human rights abuses.

stories.title: Iraq reopens border crossing with Syria shut for nearly 13 years
stories.summary: Iraq reopened the al-Rabia border crossing with Syria, known as al-Yarubiyah on the Syrian side, after nearly 13 years of closure. All three border crossings between Iraq and Syria are now operational.

stories.title: Doval’s Riyadh visit on PM’s instructions, part of government outreach to Gulf: MEA
