stories.summary: Indian National Security Adviser Ajit Doval visited Riyadh on Prime Minister Modi's instructions as part of broader government outreach to the Gulf region. Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry said the talks reviewed India-Saudi cooperation and regional developments.

stories.title: US delegation expected in Islamabad but uncertainty prevails over talks amid mixed signals from Iran
stories.summary: U.S. President Trump confirmed an American delegation would arrive in Islamabad, Pakistan, for talks, with reports suggesting Vice President JD Vance would lead the visit. Uncertainty persisted as Iran said it had not decided whether to attend the next round of U.S.-Iran negotiations, and tight security measures were imposed in Islamabad.

stories.title: Over $71bn needed over next decade to rebuild Gaza: UN, EU
stories.summary: A joint EU and UN assessment estimated that more than $71.4 billion will be needed over the next decade to rebuild Gaza. The Gaza Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment, developed with World Bank coordination, described unprecedented loss of life and a catastrophic humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: War update: 139 clashes on front lines, most enemy attacks repelled in Pokrovsk sector
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 139 combat engagements along the front lines as of Monday evening, with the heaviest fighting in the Pokrovsk sector. There, Ukrainian troops repelled 25 Russian assaults and inflicted significant losses on attacking forces.

stories.title: Ukrainian prankster infiltrates Russian Industry and Trade Ministry drone meeting, hears official say 90% of electrical components are foreign
stories.summary: A Ukrainian prankster named Yevhen Volnov infiltrated a private video conference held by Russia's Industry and Trade Ministry discussing drone production. During the meeting, a Russian official acknowledged that 90% of electrical components used in the drones are of foreign origin. The Telegram channel Astra identified several participants.

stories.title: Jump in EU EV sales amid Iran war boosts Chinese brands’ fortunes
stories.summary: Battery electric vehicle sales in the EU surged 51 percent month-on-month in March 2025 across 15 key markets, driven by consumers shifting away from fossil fuels amid rising oil prices caused by the Middle East conflict. Chinese EV brands are positioned to benefit significantly from the trend, boosting their European expansion.

stories.title: Vance has not yet left for Iran talks in Pakistan, source says
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance had not yet departed the United States for Pakistan as of April 20, according to a source familiar with the matter, as prospects for a second round of US-Iran negotiations in Islamabad remain uncertain.

stories.title: US and Iran warn they are ready for war as clock ticks on ceasefire end
stories.summary: Both the United States and Iran signaled readiness for war as the ceasefire deadline approached on Tuesday. While US Vice President J.D. Vance was prepared to return to Islamabad for a second round of talks, Iran declined to confirm its participation, leaving the status of negotiations uncertain.

stories.title: Mexico to probe security role of US officials killed in Chihuahua car crash
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said she was unaware that US embassy officials had been working with Chihuahua state to combat drug cartels and announced her government would review whether national security law was broken after the officials died in a car crash.

stories.title: Zelensky holds first-ever leader-level call with president of Honduras
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky held his first phone call with Honduran President Nasry Asfura, marking the first leader-level contact between the two countries. The leaders discussed potential areas of bilateral cooperation.

stories.title: Watch: Can Iran and the U.S. find middle ground?
stories.summary: The latest episode of Above the Fold examines uncertainty surrounding the next phase of U.S.-Iran peace talks ahead of a Wednesday ceasefire deadline. The program also covers renewed violence in Manipur, India, a powerful earthquake in Japan, the deadliest mass shooting in Louisiana, and a fireworks factory explosion in Virudhunagar, India.

stories.title: Embattled Starmer says he was not told Mandelson failed vetting process
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer stated that he and other ministers were not informed until last week that Peter Mandelson had failed an independent vetting process. Starmer described the failure to notify him as "unforgivable."

stories.title: Seized Iranian ship likely carrying equipment deemed dual-use by US, sources say
stories.summary: The Iranian-flagged container ship Touska, seized by US forces on Sunday, is believed to have been carrying items Washington deems dual-use with potential military applications, according to maritime security sources.

stories.title: Hungary’s incoming PM says Netanyahu would be arrested if he visits
stories.summary: Hungary's incoming prime minister stated he would enforce the International Criminal Court arrest warrant against Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu if he visited the country, committing to detain him.

stories.title: UK shifts older wind and solar farms to fixed-price deals to reduce price shocks
stories.summary: The UK government confirmed plans to shift older wind and solar farms—comprising nearly a third of Great Britain's power market—onto fixed-price contracts. The move aims to protect households and businesses from volatile wholesale gas prices by replacing market-linked subsidy arrangements.

stories.title: Turning point? Clean energy met 100% of world’s new power needs in 2025: report
stories.summary: A report by London-based energy think tank Ember found that clean power generation in 2025 grew faster than global electricity demand, preventing any increase in fossil fuel generation. The milestone comes as the US-Israel war on Iran heightens global energy security concerns and accelerates interest in reducing dependence on oil and gas.

stories.title: Seven people injured in Russian drone strike on residential building in Kharkiv
stories.summary: A Russian drone strike hit a residential building in the Osnovianskyi district of Kharkiv, injuring seven people. The attack targeted civilian infrastructure in Ukraine's second-largest city.

stories.title: Defying Hezbollah, Lebanon’s president seeks end to hostilities with Israel talks
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun stated that upcoming talks with Israel aim to end hostilities and the occupation in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah has sharply criticized the negotiations, which are set to enter a second round on Thursday. US President Donald Trump announced a 10-day truce following the first round of talks last week.

stories.title: Iran does not accept negotiations with the US under threats, parliament speaker says
stories.summary: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf stated that Tehran will not accept negotiations with the United States conducted under threats. In a post on X, Qalibaf accused U.S. President Donald Trump of trying to turn the negotiating table into a "table of surrender."

stories.title: EU to widen Iran sanctions to those who block Hormuz
stories.summary: The European Union reached a political agreement to expand its Iran sanctions regime to include those who block shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Russian blogger whose angry appeal to Putin went viral hits back after state TV attack
stories.summary: A Russian celebrity blogger whose critical appeal to President Putin went viral pushed back after a prominent state TV presenter accused her of working for the West and called for an investigation into her activities.

stories.title: Nigeria police rescue 18 abducted bus passengers, including exam-bound students
stories.summary: Police in Nigeria's Benue state rescued 18 passengers abducted from a bus, including eight students traveling for university entrance examinations, and arrested seven suspects in connection with the kidnapping.

stories.title: Trump: Israel never talked me into war with Iran
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that Israel did not persuade him to go to war with Iran, pushing back against suggestions of Israeli influence on his Iran policy.

stories.title: Europol identifies 45 Ukrainian children taken to occupied territories, Russia, Belarus
stories.summary: Europol, working with the Netherlands, conducted a coordinated operation on April 16–17 to identify and trace 45 Ukrainian children forcibly transferred or deported to Russian-occupied Ukrainian territories, Russia, and Belarus. The findings were shared with Ukrainian authorities.

stories.title: Czechs want to discuss role in French nuclear deterrence initiative, PM Babis says
stories.summary: Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis announced on Monday in Prague that the Czech Republic wants to discuss potential participation in a French initiative to extend nuclear deterrence to European allies.

stories.title: Space Force kills OCX GPS ground control system, citing ‘insurmountable’ challenges
stories.summary: The US Space Force has canceled the OCX GPS ground control system, citing insurmountable technical challenges. The Pentagon will instead continue operating a current ground control system managed by Lockheed Martin.

stories.title: Ugandan and Congolese troops free 200 captives from IS-affiliated militants
stories.summary: Ugandan and Congolese military forces conducted a joint raid on an Islamic State-affiliated militant camp in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, freeing at least 200 civilian captives, according to Uganda's military.

stories.title: RSF commander defects to Sudan’s military as war enters 4th year
stories.summary: A Rapid Support Forces commander known as Adam defected to Sudan's military as the country's civil war entered its fourth year. Adam fled RSF-controlled Darfur earlier this month, bringing dozens of fighters and equipment with him to the Sudanese Armed Forces.

stories.title: Pro-Russian party entered Lithuania’s ruling coalition — and it’s already blocking defense projects on Suwalki Corridor
stories.summary: A pro-Russian party has entered Lithuania's ruling coalition and is already obstructing defense projects along the strategically important Suwalki Corridor, which connects Poland to the Baltic states. The report also notes that Latvia may be more vulnerable to similar political dynamics.

stories.title: British pharmacist fights Indian extradition for allegedly killing his ex-mother-in-law with arsenic
stories.summary: British pharmacist Ajith Kumar Mupparapu faces extradition proceedings to India over allegations that he poisoned his ex-mother-in-law, Sirisha Muttavarapu, and targeted her family using arsenic in 2023.

stories.title: Outcry grows over Israeli soldier smashing Jesus statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: Former MAGA allies of Donald Trump have publicly denounced an Israeli soldier's destruction of a Jesus statue in Lebanon. The growing outcry highlights tensions over the desecration of a Christian religious symbol.

stories.title: US labour secretary to leave Trump’s cabinet amid misconduct investigations
stories.summary: The Trump administration announced that US Labour Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer has left the cabinet amid allegations of misconduct, including an affair with a subordinate and drinking alcohol on the job. She is the third Trump cabinet member to depart, following the earlier removals of Kristi Noem and Pam Bondi.

stories.title: US firms dash to recover tariffs paid on Chinese imports as refund system launches
stories.summary: Lanca Sales, a New Jersey-based food-packaging importer-exporter, began filing for refunds on Monday after the US launched a system to recover tariffs paid on Chinese imports. The duties were imposed under President Donald Trump's broad tariff measures on nearly all imports, including those from China.

stories.title: Mudra: Next steps toward just peace for Ukraine discussed in Netherlands
stories.summary: Deputy Head of Ukraine's Presidential Office Iryna Mudra visited the Netherlands, where she met with Dutch Foreign Ministry officials to discuss next steps toward a just peace for Ukraine. The talks focused on accountability issues related to the conflict.

stories.title: Sacking former Royal Navy chief demonstrates challenge facing the Armed Forces
stories.summary: The Royal Navy's First Sea Lord said the sacking of the former head of the Royal Navy for inappropriate behaviour highlights broader challenges facing the British Armed Forces.

stories.title: Tim Cook to step down as Apple CEO
stories.summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook announced he will step down on September 1, handing leadership to John Ternus, the company's current head of hardware engineering.

stories.title: Fears over Ethiopia peace deal as TPLF restores Tigray government
stories.summary: The Tigray People's Liberation Front restored the regional government in Tigray, Ethiopia, raising concerns about the durability of the peace deal that ended the deadly civil conflict. The announcement has sparked fears of renewed fighting.

stories.title: How China is reinforcing its ‘legal shield’ against foreign pressure
stories.summary: China issued new regulations designed to counter what it calls the unjustified extraterritorial application of foreign laws. Analysts describe the move as a shift from diplomatic protests to legal warfare. The European Chamber of Commerce in China expressed concern over the rules' broad scope and vague language.

stories.title: British Army spring recruiting season in Nepal for future Gurkha soldiers
stories.summary: The British Army has begun its annual spring recruiting season in Nepal to select the next intake of Gurkha soldiers. Young Nepalese men, many still teenagers, compete for the opportunity to join the British military.

stories.title: Australia news live: Anthony Albanese says national cabinet to meet this week to discuss ‘long tail’ of fuel crisis
stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced that national cabinet will meet this week to discuss the ongoing fuel crisis, including options to increase domestic oil refining capacity. Shadow housing minister Andrew Bragg also defended the Coalition's new immigration policy, calling high migration a demand-side factor.

stories.title: Obama's visit to NYC preschool sparks memory of his bloody legacy
stories.summary: Former U.S. President Barack Obama visited a preschool in New York City alongside Mayor Zohran Mamdani, where they participated in a reading event. Social media users drew attention to Obama's record of authorizing drone strikes during his presidency that resulted in civilian casualties, including children.

stories.title: Trump says US will not lift Hormuz blockade until deal made with Iran
stories.summary: President Trump stated the US will maintain its naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz until a deal is reached with Iran. The remarks came as uncertainty persists over whether Iran will participate in upcoming peace talks scheduled in Pakistan.

stories.title: Canadian tourist killed in Mexico archaeological site shooting
stories.summary: A gunman fatally shot a Canadian woman and injured five others at Mexico's Teotihuacan archaeological site on Monday before killing himself. Cristobal Castaneda, security secretary for Mexico state, confirmed the attack at the popular tourist destination near Mexico City.

stories.title: Cuba confirms meeting with US officials on island, wants energy blockade lifted
stories.summary: Cuba's government confirmed Monday that it recently met with US officials on the island. Tensions remain high between Havana and Washington over the US energy blockade of Cuba. The meeting took place as the Caribbean nation faces a severe energy crisis.

stories.title: Falklands, King’s Baton Relay depicts multicultural handshake and marvelous wildlife
stories.summary: The King's Baton Relay for the upcoming Commonwealth event opened at Government House in Stanley, Falkland Islands. A locally designed baton was revealed for the first time, with children who helped create its design taking part in the ceremony.

stories.title: Moscow court fines Russian rapper Morgenshtern on ‘foreign agent’ charges
stories.summary: A Moscow court sentenced Russian rapper Alisher Morgenshtern (known as Morgenshtern) in absentia to a seven-million-ruble fine for failing to comply with obligations as a designated foreign agent. The case was reported by independent outlet Mediazona.

stories.title: Ukraine defines framework with EU to unblock aid – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine and the European Union have defined a cooperation framework aimed at unblocking a support package for Kyiv. The agreement also addresses extending restrictions on Russia.

stories.title: Ukraine’s drone operators are about to stop carrying five different controllers to front
stories.summary: Ukraine is working to standardize drone controllers for its front-line operators, who currently carry up to five different devices. The initiative aims to address a significant logistical burden faced by drone units deployed along the front lines of the war with Russia.

stories.title: Tim Cook to step down as Apple CEO, handing reins to firm’s hardware leader
stories.summary: Apple announced that CEO Tim Cook will hand over leadership to hardware engineering chief John Ternus on September 1. Cook will remain as executive chairman. During Cook's nearly 15-year tenure, Apple's market value grew by more than US$3.6 trillion.

stories.title: Israel talks aim to end hostilities, occupation: Lebanon President
stories.summary: Lebanon's president stated that ongoing negotiations with Israel are aimed at ending hostilities and the occupation. Iran-backed Hezbollah is not participating in the talks.

stories.title: The sights of Sea Air Space Day 1
stories.summary: The Navy League's Sea Air Space conference opened its first day, featuring exhibits on the show floor at the organisation's largest annual event.

stories.title: Israel at 78: Unbowed, strong, and determined as it swings between a miracle and a mess - comment
stories.summary: As Israel marks its 78th year of independence, the country reflects on a year marked by rocket sirens, extended reserve duty, and significant strain on families. The period has been defined by loss and uncertainty amid ongoing security challenges.

stories.title: EU eyes Ukraine loan, Israeli settler sanctions, after Hungarian election
stories.summary: The ouster of Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán in recent elections has removed a key obstacle to EU foreign policy decisions. The bloc is now moving forward on a loan package for Ukraine and sanctions targeting Israeli settlers. These steps had previously been blocked within the 27-member union.

stories.title: How new US-Indonesia defence pact sharpens China’s ‘Malacca dilemma’
stories.summary: The United States and Indonesia announced a major defence cooperation partnership on April 13, covering capacity building, exercises, and maritime cooperation. Analysts say the pact strengthens Washington's strategic position near the Strait of Malacca, compounding what is often called China's 'Malacca dilemma.' Indonesia maintains it is not choosing sides.

stories.title: Europol ‘hackathon’ traces 45 deported Ukrainian kids
stories.summary: A Europol-organized hackathon brought together investigators who traced the locations of 45 Ukrainian children who had been deported, partly using open-source information to find them.

stories.title: Govt forsees economic slowdown during current, next fiscal years due to Middle East war
stories.summary: Pakistan's government projected an economic slowdown during the current and next fiscal years due to a roughly 20% cut in the development budget redirected to fuel subsidies. Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal cited global supply chain disruptions from the Middle East war and rising oil prices as contributing factors.

stories.title: A-10s escape retirement once again amid continued use in Iran war
stories.summary: The US Air Force will extend three A-10 Warthog squadrons through 2030, sparing the aging close air support aircraft from retirement. The decision reflects the plane's continued operational use in the Iran conflict.

stories.title: Russia’s Interior Ministry proposes banning extradition of all foreigners granted asylum in the country
stories.summary: Russia's Interior Ministry proposed legislation that would ban the extradition of any foreigner granted asylum in Russia, regardless of the type of asylum. The measure would apply broadly to all forms of protected status within the country.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1517: Ukraine has reached security cooperation arrangement with India, with documents being finalized
stories.summary: On day 1,517 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, Ukraine announced it has reached a security cooperation arrangement with India, with documents currently being finalized. Separately, Ukrainian pork exports have entered markets in Vietnam, the Philippines, and Singapore as EU exporters lose ground in Asia.

stories.title: Stray bullet claims life of MQM-P MNA’s daughter in Karachi
stories.summary: A 19-year-old medical student and daughter of MQM-P MNA Iqbal Mehsud Khan was killed by a stray bullet in Karachi's Gulshan-i-Iqbal area. She was struck while standing on her home's terrace on Saturday night and died during hospital treatment the following day.

stories.title: Tim Cook to step down as Apple CEO in September after 15-year tenure
stories.summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook will step down on September 1 after nearly 15 years, with hardware chief John Ternus succeeding him. Cook, 65, will become executive chairman. Apple's market value grew by more than $3.6 trillion during his tenure.

stories.title: Tymoshenko in court says she does not know MPs named in bribery case
stories.summary: Former Ukrainian Prime Minister Yulia Tymoshenko appeared before Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court, stating she does not know the MPs named in a bribery case. The court is hearing an appeal against a suspicion notice alleging she offered undue benefits to parliamentarians.

stories.title: Kanye West shows nixed in Poland, Switzerland amid backlash over past antisemitism
stories.summary: Concerts by rapper Kanye West, also known as Ye, were canceled in Poland and Switzerland due to backlash over his past antisemitic remarks. A scheduled show in France was also postponed, with the French interior minister reportedly seeking to ban the event. West claimed a "commitment to make amends."

stories.title: Israeli ministers celebrate re-establishment of settlement in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli government ministers celebrated the re-establishment of a settlement in the occupied West Bank, reflecting the far-right ruling coalition's support for rapid settlement expansion in the territory.

stories.title: Why the US can’t copy Ukraine’s robot navy
stories.summary: Analysis suggests the US cannot simply replicate Ukraine's unmanned naval drone strategy for its own forces. Command and control of maritime operations will remain a fundamentally human endeavor even as autonomous vessels proliferate in the Pacific.

stories.title: How is the war on Iran affecting the Russia-Ukraine conflict?
stories.summary: The ongoing conflict between the U.S.-Israel coalition and Iran is affecting the Russia-Ukraine war through disruptions in global energy markets. The energy crisis created by the Middle East hostilities carries implications for both Moscow and Kyiv as each side navigates shifting supply dynamics and pricing.

stories.title: Board of Peace envoy optimistic about Gaza disarmament talks, but warns of delays
stories.summary: The Board of Peace is engaged in discussions on Gaza disarmament. Envoy Nickolay Mladenov expressed cautious optimism about progress but warned that delays could hamper the process.

stories.title: Fmr. IDF chief Eisenkot reflects on son’s death, says he ‘didn't cry' for decades until funeral
stories.summary: Former IDF Chief of Staff Gadi Eisenkot spoke publicly about the death of his son Gal during operations in Gaza, revealing he had not cried for decades until the funeral. Eisenkot has also launched the Yashar! political party focused on Israel's future.

stories.title: Russian designer tells host to ‘suck it’ on popular internet show, sparking backlash
stories.summary: Russian designer and pro-Kremlin figure Artemy Lebedev sparked backlash after making a vulgar remark to a host during a popular Russian internet show called Natalnaya Karta. The episode aired on April 17.

stories.title: US Air Force extends A-10 Warthog through 2030
stories.summary: The US Air Force has decided to extend the service life of the A-10 Warthog ground-attack aircraft through 2030. The decision follows the A-10's increased operational involvement during Operation Epic Fury in Iran.

stories.title: Elon Musk snubs Paris prosecutors' summons over X and Grok
stories.summary: Elon Musk did not appear Monday for a voluntary interview with Paris prosecutors investigating allegations that X's algorithm was used to interfere in French politics. The probe was expanded to include dissemination of Holocaust denial and sexual deepfakes generated by X's AI chatbot Grok.

stories.title: Indian politicians are campaigning while holding fish. What is going on?
stories.summary: Politicians campaigning in West Bengal's elections have been photographed holding fish as a campaign tactic. The practice symbolizes cultural identity and regional pride, reflecting the significance of fish in Bengali culture and politics.

stories.title: Trump boasts on ‘winning war’ on social media posts
stories.summary: Former U.S. President Donald Trump posted multiple statements on social media throughout the day claiming the U.S. is winning the war. The posts struck a boastful tone, though specific conflicts or operations were not clearly identified in the messages.

stories.title: Iran will keep lying, former Mossad chief Yossi Cohen warns
stories.summary: Former Mossad chief Yossi Cohen stated that Iran will continue to deceive the international community and that no agreement or ceasefire will change Tehran's ambitions. He emphasized the ongoing challenge of safeguarding Israel's security.

stories.title: German FM summons Russian ambassador in Berlin over threats to German companies
stories.summary: Germany's Foreign Ministry summoned Russian Ambassador Sergey Nechayev over direct threats by Russia to strike targets on German territory. Berlin characterized the threats as an attempt to weaken German support for Ukraine.

stories.title: Israel's Supreme Court orders renewed review on rape suspect's name publication
stories.summary: Israel's Supreme Court ordered a renewed review of whether to publish the name of a rape suspect, halting the release pending further judicial examination. The decision has prompted debate over balancing justice and privacy rights.

stories.title: China ‘has to be involved’ in new nuclear arms control talks, US senator urges
stories.summary: US Senator Deb Fischer, a Nebraska Republican chairing the Senate Armed Services Committee's strategic forces subcommittee, urged on Monday that China must be included in nuclear arms control negotiations alongside Russia. She also called for the US to accelerate nuclear modernisation, including deploying more bombers.

stories.title: Michigan Democrats back pro-Palestinian candidate for university board
stories.summary: The Michigan Democratic Party endorsed pro-Palestinian candidate Amir Makled for the University of Michigan Board of Regents, sidelining the incumbent pro-Israel Jewish board member. Makled has drawn scrutiny for retweeting memes and cartoons described as carrying antisemitic connotations.

stories.title: Rumen Radev, Russia-friendly ex-fighter pilot, sweeps Bulgaria's election
stories.summary: Former Bulgarian president and ex-fighter pilot Rumen Radev won Sunday's parliamentary election in a sweeping victory. Radev, seen as friendly toward Russia, had urged voters to reject what he called corrupt officials running the country.

stories.title: What to know about the next round of US-Iran talks in Pakistan
stories.summary: The United States and Iran are scheduled to hold another round of direct negotiations in Pakistan on Tuesday. Uncertainty surrounds whether the Iranian delegation will attend the talks. The discussions follow earlier rounds of diplomacy between the two nations.

stories.title: Tim Cook to step down as CEO of Apple: ‘the greatest privilege of my life’
stories.summary: Apple announced Monday that CEO Tim Cook will be succeeded by hardware engineering chief John Ternus on September 1. Cook, who called the role the greatest privilege of his life, will transition to executive chairman.

stories.title: Europol and partners trace 45 ‘forcibly transferred’ Ukrainian children
stories.summary: Europol announced it shared information with Ukraine on 45 children identified as having been forcibly transferred to Russia, Belarus, or Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory. The operation was conducted in coordination with the Netherlands on April 16–17 to trace and identify the displaced children.

stories.title: Canadian tourist killed, 6 people injured in shooting at Mexico archaeological site
stories.summary: A gunman opened fire at Mexico's Teotihuacan archaeological site on Monday, killing a Canadian woman and injuring four other people. The attacker fired from partway up the Pyramid of the Moon before killing himself. Cristobal Castaneda, security secretary for Mexico state, confirmed the incident.

stories.title: France to join Steering Committee of Special Tribunal on Russia's aggression – Barrot
stories.summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot announced that France will join the Steering Committee of a proposed Special Tribunal on Russia's crime of aggression against Ukraine. France also called on the Council of Europe to uphold the rule of law and democracy.

stories.title: Shooter at Mexico's Teotihuacan pyramid site kills Canadian tourist, wounds four others
stories.summary: A Canadian woman was killed and four others injured when a gunman opened fire at the Teotihuacan pyramids north of Mexico City on Monday. The attacker then killed himself, according to the Mexico state security secretary.

stories.title: Hungary’s Magyar says ICC-wanted leaders will be detained, despite invite to Netanyahu
stories.summary: Hungary's Prime Minister-elect Péter Magyar stated that individuals wanted by the International Criminal Court will be detained if they enter Hungary, despite his predecessor's invitation to Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu. Magyar also indicated he intends to reverse the previous government's decision to leave the ICC.

stories.title: IDF escalates efforts to prevent civilian return to southern Lebanon after ceasefire
stories.summary: The Israeli military has escalated efforts to prevent civilians from returning to their villages in southern Lebanon despite the ceasefire. Residents have attempted to cross into their homes in defiance of IDF warnings, raising questions about the truce's future.

stories.title: EU to gauge member states' willingness to take measures against Israel
stories.summary: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Monday that member states will discuss the bloc's cooperation agreement with Israel. Spain is leading a push to suspend the deal as attitudes harden among key EU members over Israel's actions in the Gaza Strip, Lebanon, and the occupied West Bank.

stories.title: Uncertainty prevails over talks amid mixed signals from Iran; Trump says US delegation en route to Islamabad
stories.summary: Uncertainty surrounds a potential second round of US-Iran direct talks in Islamabad, with Iran saying it has not decided on attending while Trump announced a US delegation led by JD Vance was heading to Pakistan. Islamabad sealed its Red Zone and suspended public transport as a security precaution.

stories.title: Venezuela’s melting 'permafrost' draws debt investors' optimism
stories.summary: At last week's IMF-World Bank meetings in Washington, investors and officials cited Venezuela as the biggest source of optimism despite the country facing Western sanctions and billions in outstanding debt.

stories.title: At Memorial Day ceremony, leaders warn of division, IDF chief says ‘all parts of nation’ must defend it
stories.summary: At Israel's Memorial Day ceremony, IDF Chief of Staff urged "all parts of the nation" to take part in defending the country, while leaders warned against internal division. Prime Minister Netanyahu struck a defiant tone at a separate event, declaring "superiority over the Iranian axis" and vowing continued military operations.

stories.title: France may take over protecting logistics hub that supplies Ukraine’s war effort
stories.summary: France may assume responsibility for protecting a key logistics hub through which most U.S. and allied heavy military equipment is routed before reaching Ukraine. The potential French role would help secure a critical supply node for Ukraine's war effort.

stories.title: Sudanese deminers scour shattered capital for hidden explosives
stories.summary: Demining teams in Sudan's capital, Khartoum, have been working to locate and clear hidden explosives left amid the ongoing conflict. Authorities reported clearing tens of thousands of explosive devices across the city.

stories.title: Israeli fire kills two in Gaza, Hamas clashes with Israeli-backed militia
stories.summary: Israeli fire killed two people in Gaza, and Hamas clashed with an Israeli-backed militia, marking continued violence that has overshadowed the US-brokered ceasefire deal signed in October.

stories.title: MQM-P MNA’s daughter dies after being shot by stray bullet in Karachi
stories.summary: A 19-year-old medical student and daughter of MQM-P MNA Iqbal Mehsud Khan died after being struck by a stray bullet while standing on her home's terrace in Karachi's Gulshan-i-Iqbal area. Police said the bullet came from an unknown direction on Saturday night.

stories.title: Russian forces strike residential building in Kharkiv with drone, leaving six injured
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a residential building in the Osnovianskyi district of Kharkiv on April 20, injuring at least six people. The attack targeted civilian infrastructure in Ukraine's second-largest city.

stories.title: Federal agents detain wife of another US army member: ‘ICE is out of control’
stories.summary: US Army Sergeant First Class Jose Serrano, a 27-year veteran who deployed to Afghanistan, said his wife Deisy Rivera Ortega was detained by ICE officers during a scheduled immigration appointment in El Paso, Texas. Serrano said the arrest occurred despite her having legal proceedings under way.

stories.title: US to host further G-20 talks on war’s impact on food and fertiliser
stories.summary: The United States plans to host additional G-20 discussions on the impact of war on global food and fertiliser supplies, following a push for coordinated action with the IMF and World Bank launched last week.

stories.title: Funerals held across Lebanon during 10-day ceasefire
stories.summary: Funerals are being held across Lebanon during a 10-day ceasefire in the war between Israel and Hezbollah. Mourners in multiple communities are burying victims of the conflict. The temporary halt in hostilities has allowed communities to carry out burials and mourn their dead.

stories.title: Slovenia PM Golob's party goes into opposition after coalition talks fail
stories.summary: Slovenian Prime Minister Robert Golob announced that his liberal Freedom Movement party would move into opposition after failing to form a majority coalition following its narrow victory in March's parliamentary elections. Centre-right parties are now expected to form a government.

stories.title: The World Is Paying the Price for America’s War
stories.summary: The US conflict with Iran is described as having severe economic consequences beyond American consumers, disproportionately affecting populations in the global south.

stories.title: Israel says it thwarted Iranian plan to attack Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan oil pipeline
stories.summary: Israel said it uncovered and thwarted an Iranian-directed cell that planned to attack the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan oil pipeline as well as Jewish and Israeli targets in Azerbaijan.

stories.title: IDF chief calls on haredim to serve as Israel marks Remembrance Day at Western Wall
stories.summary: During Israel's Remembrance Day ceremony at the Western Wall in Jerusalem, IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir called on ultra-Orthodox (haredi) citizens to serve in the military. He spoke about fulfilling the promise of a secure state for current and future generations.

stories.title: Pakistan increases Eurobond from $500m to $750m
stories.summary: Pakistan increased its Eurobond issuance from $500 million to $750 million by exercising a green-shoe option, marking its return to international capital markets after four years amid growing foreign exchange needs due to higher oil costs linked to the Middle East conflict.

stories.title: How Likely Are U.S.-Iran Peace Talks in Islamabad?
stories.summary: Planned US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad face uncertainty after the US seized an Iranian ship, potentially disrupting the negotiations.

stories.title: Russians attack Dnipropetrovsk region nearly 70 times in one day, leaving three killed, eight injured
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out nearly 70 attacks on Ukraine's Dnipropetrovsk region in a single day using drones, artillery, and an aerial bomb. The strikes targeted the Nikopol, Kryvyi Rih, and Synelnykove districts, killing three people and injuring eight.

stories.title: Israel confirms its soldier destroyed Jesus statue in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military confirmed that a viral photo showing one of its soldiers destroying a statue of Jesus with a sledgehammer in the southern Lebanese Christian village of Debel is authentic. The military said it has launched an investigation into the incident. Locals said the statue was on a crucifix outside a family home.

stories.title: Cuba confirms recent ‘respectful’ talks with visiting US delegation
stories.summary: Cuban diplomat Alejandro Garcia confirmed that delegations from Cuba and the United States recently held talks in Havana. The meeting included assistant secretaries from the US State Department. The discussions come as Cuba faces a deepening crisis linked to US President Donald Trump's pressure campaign.

stories.title: Qatar announces ‘gradual resumption’ of flights by foreign airlines
stories.summary: Qatar announced a gradual resumption of flights by foreign airlines after having shut its airspace during Iran's retaliatory drone and missile campaign against Gulf countries.

stories.title: US 'continued violations of ceasefire' obstacle to diplomatic process, Iran says
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Pakistani counterpart Ishaq Dar that US 'continued violations of the ceasefire' are a major obstacle to ongoing diplomacy. Araghchi said Iran would decide how to proceed after evaluating all aspects of the situation.

stories.title: One-third of 103 companies building Russia’s Su-57 used for launching Kh-69s are still not Sanctioned
stories.summary: A report found that one-third of the 103 companies involved in manufacturing Russia's Su-57 fighter jet, which carries Kh-69 cruise missiles, remain unsanctioned. The Su-57 is also expected to deploy UMPK glide bombs against Ukrainian targets.

stories.title: 'They will destroy Iran': Tehran's Ghalibaf denounces critics of Iran holding US talks - report
stories.summary: Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammed-Bagher Ghalibaf condemned hardline figures including Saeed Jalili and Amir-Hossein Sabeti for opposing ceasefire talks with the United States. He warned that their stance could "destroy Iran."

stories.title: Pakistan confident Iran will attend US talks: Report
stories.summary: A senior Pakistani government official said Pakistan is confident it can persuade Iran to attend talks with the United States. Islamabad reported receiving a positive signal from Tehran as President Trump's ceasefire deadline approaches, with Pakistan actively engaging both sides.

stories.title: Joint Israeli-Palestinian Memorial Day event held in secret amid far-right threats
stories.summary: A joint Israeli-Palestinian Memorial Day ceremony was held in secret in Jaffa, with a parallel event in Jericho, due to threats from far-right groups. Bereaved Israelis and Palestinians shared stories of loss from the October 7 attack, the Gaza war, and West Bank violence.

stories.title: Police investigate whether London arson attacks were planned for weeks
stories.summary: London police are investigating whether a series of arson attacks against synagogues and other Jewish targets were planned for weeks, with suspects allegedly conducting reconnaissance beforehand. Detectives believe the firebombings, which also targeted premises linked to Iranian dissidents, were carried out by criminals paid on behalf of Iran.

stories.title: Louisiana mass shooting: What we know about suspect, eight children killed
stories.summary: A mass shooting in Shreveport, Louisiana, killed eight children, making it the deadliest such attack reported in the United States in over two years. Authorities have identified a suspect in the attack. Investigations into the motive and circumstances are ongoing.

stories.title: Houthi official threw 13-year-old girl down well, killing her, after marital dispute
stories.summary: A Houthi official in Yemen allegedly killed his 13-year-old daughter by throwing her down a well following a marital dispute with his ex-wife. The incident has drawn attention to violence against minors in Houthi-controlled areas.

stories.title: 'Trump has boxed himself into a corner', expert says as fate of Iran peace talks uncertain
stories.summary: Middle East analyst Rosemary Kelanic of Defense Priorities told FRANCE 24 that President Trump "has boxed himself into a corner" regarding Iran. She argued the conflict has weakened the U.S. position relative to Iran, particularly after Tehran demonstrated its ability to close the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: UAE says dismantled Iran-linked group plotting 'terror' ops
stories.summary: The UAE announced it dismantled an Iran-linked group allegedly planning terrorist operations in the country. The operation took place after the UAE bore the brunt of Tehran's attacks on Gulf states prior to a two-week US-Iran ceasefire.

stories.title: Enemy increases pressure in Hryshyne, Donetsk region, situation worsens — 7th Corps of Air Assault Forces
stories.summary: Russian forces intensified pressure in the town of Hryshyne in Ukraine's Donetsk region, attempting to advance in the central and northern parts of the settlement. Ukraine's 7th Corps of Air Assault Forces reported a worsening situation in the area.

stories.title: 4 construction workers abducted by armed men in KP’s Tirah valley
stories.summary: Four road construction workers, including two excavator operators, were abducted at gunpoint by armed men in the Peer Mela area of Tirah valley in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Three of the abducted workers were from Balochistan, and security forces launched a search operation.

stories.title: Several military and police officers charged with corruption in multiple cases
stories.summary: Seven Israeli military and police officers were charged with corruption, including money laundering, as authorities seized 50 million shekels. A separate case involved an IDF officer charged with smuggling goods into Gaza.

stories.title: Cuba confirms meeting with US representatives in Havana, insists on lifting energy blockade
stories.summary: Cuba's government confirmed that a meeting with U.S. representatives recently took place in Havana. The diplomatic engagement comes amid a severe energy crisis on the island, which Cuba attributes to Washington's blockade of oil supplies.

stories.title: Taliban arrests senior co-founder Mullah Mutasim Agha Jan amid deepening internal rifts
stories.summary: The Taliban arrested senior co-founder Mullah Mutasim Agha Jan, a close associate of the late founder Mullah Mohammad Omar. Agha Jan had served as finance minister in the Taliban's pre-9/11 government. The arrest signals deepening internal rifts within the movement.

stories.title: Belarus warns its neighbors against “aggression” same week it was building artillery positions on Ukraine’s border
stories.summary: Belarus issued warnings to its neighbors against "aggression" during the same week it was observed constructing artillery positions near the Ukrainian border. A Belarusian official claimed the country possesses sufficient non-nuclear weaponry.

stories.title: US will provide dollar loan to UAE if economy is jolted by war on Iran, US official says
stories.summary: A US official said Washington would provide a dollar loan to the UAE if its economy is disrupted by the war on Iran. Trump ally Steve Bannon criticized the UAE for seeking the short-term financial arrangement.

stories.title: New deal with Iran will be better than old one, Trump says
stories.summary: President Donald Trump claimed on social media that a nuclear deal being negotiated with Iran would be far superior to the 2015 JCPOA agreed under President Obama. The statement came amid criticism from Democrats and nuclear experts who accused him of rushing negotiations.

stories.title: 1 dead, 6 hurt as trolleybus crashes into supermarket in Austria
stories.summary: A trolleybus veered off the road and crashed into a supermarket in Salzburg, Austria, on Monday, killing one person and injuring at least six others. Austria's Red Cross confirmed the fatality, and police identified the deceased as a 55-year-old bystander who died at the scene. The driver and several passengers were also injured.

stories.title: Report finds Gaza needs more than $71bn in next decade for recovery
stories.summary: A joint EU and UN report estimates that Gaza will require more than $71 billion over the next decade to rebuild. The assessment identifies housing, health, education, commerce, and agriculture as the most devastated sectors in the Palestinian enclave.

stories.title: Trump: Israel ‘never talked me into’ Iran war, cites Oct. 7 and nuclear threat
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated that Israel did not persuade him to pursue military action against Iran. He attributed his stance to the October 7 attacks and his longstanding position that Iran must never acquire nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Dutch government offers tax breaks for rising fuel costs
stories.summary: The Dutch government announced tax breaks to help offset rising fuel costs for citizens. Officials said they would prepare additional measures should the energy crisis worsen.

stories.title: Czech FM protests to Russian ambassador over threats to strike EU defense enterprises
stories.summary: The Czech Ministry of Foreign Affairs formally protested to the Russian ambassador over threats to strike EU defense enterprises, including targets in the Czech Republic. The ministry reminded Russia of its obligations under international law.

stories.title: The Strategic Aftershocks of Trump’s Iran War
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the strategic consequences of the Trump administration's military conflict with Iran will extend well beyond the end of active fighting.

stories.title: 2 dead after planned fight between young people escalates to a shooting in North Carolina
stories.summary: A planned fight among young people escalated into a shooting at Leinbach Park in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, on Monday morning, leaving two people dead. The park is near Jefferson Middle School. The North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation confirmed that several people were shot, including two fatally, and juveniles were involved.

stories.title: Uncertainty prevails over second round of U.S.-Iran talks in Pakistan
stories.summary: A second round of US-Iran talks is expected in Islamabad in the coming days, with Pakistani authorities implementing extensive security measures, though uncertainty remains over whether Iran will attend.

stories.title: Baby was sexually abused before being killed by man adopting him, court told
stories.summary: A court heard that 13-month-old Preston Davey was "routinely ill-treated, sexually abused and physically assaulted" before being killed by Jamie Varley, 37, a secondary school teacher who was in the process of adopting him. Varley and his partner John McGowan-Fazakerley, 32, face charges in connection with the child's death.

stories.title: Sri Lanka’s Dasun Shanaka handed one-year PSL ban for IPL switch
stories.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board imposed a one-year PSL ban on Sri Lankan cricketer Dasun Shanaka after he unilaterally withdrew from Lahore Qalandars during the 2026 tournament to join IPL franchise Rajasthan Royals, breaching player registration terms.

stories.title: Former PM Bennett backs civil marriage, public transport on Shabbat in Israel
stories.summary: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett publicly endorsed civil marriage and public transportation on Shabbat in Israel. His remarks drew praise from left-wing figures but sharp criticism from ultra-Orthodox (haredi) political parties.

stories.title: Russia Says It Can Take Iran’s Enriched Uranium. Will That Happen?
stories.summary: U.S. officials have rejected the idea of sending Iran's enriched uranium to Russia, but some experts argue the proposal could serve both countries' interests. The discussion centers on Russia's offer to take custody of Iran's enriched uranium as part of broader negotiations.

stories.title: Russians strike gas station in Kharkiv region, three injured
stories.summary: A Russian strike hit a gas station in Bohodukhiv, Kharkiv region, injuring three men. The attack targeted civilian infrastructure in the area.

stories.title: Army to rely on FMS, reinvesting to ensure helicopter manufacturers stay ‘healthy’
stories.summary: Following drastic cuts to helicopter procurement funding in the FY27 budget request, U.S. Army senior leaders and industry representatives say foreign military sales and reinvestment programs will sustain helicopter manufacturers. The approach aims to keep production lines viable despite reduced domestic orders.

stories.title: JD Vance to lead US delegation in Pakistan if Iran agrees to talks
stories.summary: U.S. Vice President JD Vance is expected to lead a diplomatic delegation to Islamabad on Tuesday if Iran agrees to further nuclear and peace talks. He will be accompanied by special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Pakistan is seeking to raise its global standing by facilitating Middle East peace negotiations as the current ceasefire deadline approaches.

stories.title: Czech PM Babis criticises Senate leader’s Taiwan trip for damaging China business ties
stories.summary: Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš criticized the Senate leader's trip to Taiwan, arguing it damaged the Czech Republic's business ties with China. Like most countries, the Czech Republic formally recognizes Beijing rather than Taipei.

stories.title: Berlin Summons Russian Envoy Over 'Threats'
stories.summary: Germany's Foreign Ministry summoned Russian Ambassador Sergey Nechayev in Berlin over unspecified threats. The ministry declined to provide additional details about the nature of the threats.

stories.title: In pictures: Islamabad on high security even as uncertainty looms over 2nd round of US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Islamabad implemented heightened security measures including sealing the Red Zone and suspending public transport ahead of possible foreign delegation arrivals, even as Iran has not confirmed its attendance at a second round of US-Iran negotiations.

stories.title: With eyes on future NASA moon base, Space Force launches cislunar acquisition task force
stories.summary: The U.S. Space Force has established a cislunar acquisition task force with an eye toward supporting a future NASA lunar base. Separately, the Air Force Research Laboratory is preparing to launch its experimental cislunar monitoring satellite, Oracle Prime, next year.

stories.title: Lebanon's Aoun says aiming to end hostilities with Israel talks
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun announced plans to hold direct talks with Israel aimed at ending hostilities and extending the ceasefire in Lebanon. The initiative drew criticism from Hezbollah.

stories.title: Russians increase assault activity in Huliaipole direction — Voloshyn
stories.summary: Ukrainian military spokesperson Voloshyn reported that Russian forces increased assault activity in the Huliaipole sector following the end of an "Easter truce." Approximately 80 assaults were recorded in the area over the past week, accompanied by a rise in airstrikes.

stories.title: Druzhba pipeline restart this week after Russian attack could unlock €90 billion in EU aid for Ukraine
stories.summary: The Druzhba oil pipeline is expected to restart this week following a Russian attack that had disrupted operations. The resumption may satisfy Hungary's precondition for supporting up to €90 billion in EU aid to Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran says 'no decision' on joining new talks, with US delegation set to depart
stories.summary: Iran stated it had not yet decided whether to attend a new round of peace negotiations with the United States, even as Washington's delegation prepared to depart for Pakistan on Monday. President Trump suggested he could resume military strikes if the current temporary ceasefire lapses in its final days.

stories.title: Ukrainian drone attack hits Russia’s Tuapse port
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck Russia's Black Sea port of Tuapse, sending plumes of black smoke into the sky. The attack targeted port infrastructure in the southern Russian city.

stories.title: 40 Israelis detained at Moscow airport, reportedly over war with Iran
stories.summary: Approximately 40 Israeli citizens were detained at a Moscow airport, reportedly in connection with the war between Israel and Iran. Israel said it contacted Russian authorities to secure their release; the travelers reported being told that enemies of Tehran are Russia's enemies as well.

stories.title: What exit strategy? Trump, Iranians send mixed signals as truce deadline looms
stories.summary: As the U.S.-Iran ceasefire deadline approaches, both sides are sending mixed signals about next steps. Tensions remain high following the seizure of a container ship in the Gulf, while rising oil prices add pressure on the Trump administration to pursue de-escalation. Proposals have ranged from threats of military action to a proposed Strait of Hormuz toll-sharing arrangement.

stories.title: Kremlin encouraged by Bulgarian Radev's desire to resolve issues with Russia via talks
stories.summary: The Kremlin expressed encouragement at Bulgarian politician Rumen Radev's stated desire to resolve issues with Russia through pragmatic dialogue, following his landslide election victory on Sunday.

stories.title: Op. Red Heart: Fallen soldier’s mother reveals son was killed in op. tied to Bibas rescue attempt
stories.summary: The mother of a fallen Israeli soldier revealed that her son was killed during Operation Red Heart, a mission linked to an attempt to rescue the Bibas family. The disclosure came over two years after the soldiers' deaths, and after Israel learned that Shiri Bibas and her children had already been killed in captivity.

stories.title: Russian authorities detain 40 Israelis landing in Moscow over 'involvement' in Iran war - report
stories.summary: Russian authorities at Moscow's Domodedovo Airport detained approximately 40 Israeli nationals, some holding dual Russian citizenship, upon their arrival. The detainees were reportedly told that Iran's enemy is Russia's enemy, linking the detention to Israel's involvement in the conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Mother, 6 children killed in explosion and fire at rural Pennsylvania home
stories.summary: An Amish woman and her six children, aged three to eleven, were killed in a house fire following an explosion at their home in Lamar Township, Clinton County, Pennsylvania. Firefighters responding on Sunday morning found seven people trapped but were unable to enter the engulfed structure. Pennsylvania State Police confirmed the seven deaths.

stories.title: Israel entrenches hold on south Lebanon, warns residents to stay out
stories.summary: Israel warned residents of southern Lebanon to stay out of a belt of territory along the border and not to approach the Litani River area. The move entrenches Israel's hold over southern Lebanon despite a ceasefire agreement in the war with Hezbollah.

stories.title: Milei signs deals with Israel, pledges embassy move to Jerusalem and calls Marxism "satanic"
stories.summary: Argentine President Javier Milei signed the "Isaac Accords" with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in Jerusalem on Sunday and reiterated his pledge to move Argentina's embassy to Jerusalem. Milei also voiced support for Israel's conflict with Iran and called Marxism "satanic" during a speech at Bar-Ilan University.

stories.title: MQ-9B SeaGuardian® offers Navy-Marine Corps a decisive edge in today’s battlespace
stories.summary: General Atomics promotes the MQ-9B SeaGuardian unmanned aerial system as offering the U.S. Navy and Marine Corps a significant advantage in modern operational environments. The sponsored content highlights the platform's suitability for current conflict scenarios.

stories.title: Ukraine denies reports of Russian forces capturing Zybyne in Kharkiv region
stories.summary: Ukraine's 16th Army Corps denied Russian claims of capturing the settlement of Zybyne in the Kharkiv region. Ukrainian servicemen stated they continue to repel Russian forces in the area and called the Russian media reports false.

stories.title: Bahraini king orders citizenship to be stripped from 'traitors'
stories.summary: Bahrain's King Hamad bin Isa ordered the stripping of citizenship from individuals he labeled as traitors. The decree came amid long-running sectarian tensions in the kingdom and the broader US-Israeli war on Iran.

stories.title: UAE reports dismantling of Iran-linked ‘terror’ cell
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates announced it had dismantled a cell linked to Iran that was allegedly plotting terrorist operations. The arrests were made after the UAE sustained Iranian attacks targeting Gulf states.

stories.title: Hezbollah remains the central barrier in israel-lebanon negotiations - opinion
stories.summary: An analysis argues that Hezbollah's parallel governance structures in Lebanon remain the primary obstacle to Israel-Lebanon peace negotiations. The piece contends that progress depends on Lebanon reclaiming sovereignty from the militant group.

stories.title: HUR’s “Ghosts” hit two Russia’s landing ships, $5 million radar, and fuel depot in one overnight peration
stories.summary: Ukraine's military intelligence directorate (HUR) "Ghosts" unit struck two Russian landing ships, a radar system valued at $5 million, and a fuel depot in a single overnight operation. The attacks further diminish Russia's amphibious capacity dating from the Soviet era.

stories.title: After watchdog slams understaffing, AI to vet Pentagon-backed professors’ China ties
stories.summary: The Pentagon plans to use artificial intelligence to vet the foreign ties of professors involved in Defense Department-backed research, following criticism from a watchdog about understaffing. Experts warn that AI errors in assessing the nature of research partnerships could mask genuine espionage if humans do not serve as final arbiters.

stories.title: Germany summons Russian ambassador, citing ‘direct threats’
stories.summary: Germany summoned the Russian ambassador to Berlin over what it described as direct threats. German officials characterized the threats as an attempt to undermine European support for Ukraine and test allied unity.

stories.title: Pakistan prepares for second round of US-Iran talks, even as uncertainty looms
stories.summary: Pakistan blocked off a sensitive Red Zone area in Islamabad and closed nearby hotels in preparation for a potential second round of US-Iran negotiations. The security measures reflect the high sensitivity surrounding the diplomatic talks.

stories.title: Israel condemns soldier’s desecration of crucifix in south Lebanon
stories.summary: Israel's military condemned the desecration of a crucifix by one of its soldiers in the southern Lebanese village of Debel. The cross was part of a small family shrine in the village.

stories.title: Boeing lands Chinook without a pilot at the controls
stories.summary: Boeing used its A2X autonomous software to guide a U.S. Army CH-47 Chinook helicopter through its final approach and landing without a pilot at the controls. The demonstration marks a step forward in autonomous flight capabilities for military rotorcraft.

stories.title: Ashab al-Yamin claimed responsibility for Skopje, Munich attacks on Jewish sites
stories.summary: A group called Ashab al-Yamin claimed responsibility for attacks on Jewish sites in Skopje, North Macedonia, and Munich, Germany. Surveillance footage shared by Israel's ambassador to North Macedonia showed two men scaling a fence and dousing a building with an accelerant.

stories.title: Woman charged in US with trafficking arms to Sudan for Iranian government
stories.summary: US authorities charged an Iranian citizen with trafficking arms to Sudan on behalf of the Iranian government. The accused allegedly brokered deals for drones and ammunition with Sudan's Ministry of Defence.

stories.title: Russia heavily mines Crimea coastline over fears of Ukrainian landing – military
stories.summary: Russian forces in occupied Crimea are conducting large-scale mining of the coastline and adjacent waters, according to Ukrainian military sources. The effort is intended to prevent a potential amphibious landing operation by Ukraine's Defense Forces.

stories.title: What a protest in Syria reveals about the country's divides
stories.summary: A protest called 'Law and Dignity' in Syria exposed deep divisions within the country, not only over policy but over who has the right to demand change and when. The event highlighted Syria's ongoing societal fractures.

stories.title: Magyar says would carry out ICC warrant against Netanyahu
stories.summary: Newly elected Hungarian leader Peter Magyar stated he would arrest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu if he entered Hungary, in compliance with the ICC arrest warrant. The announcement marks a shift from Hungary's previous stance under prior leadership.

stories.title: Estonia Dismisses Zelensky’s Claims of Russian Plans to Invade Baltics
stories.summary: Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna dismissed Ukrainian President Zelensky's claims that Russia is planning to invade the Baltic states. Tsahkna said available indicators suggest Russia is under significant military and economic strain.

stories.title: ‘Nothing left’: Hong Kong fire survivors return to burnt homes
stories.summary: Survivors of a devastating fire at Wang Fuk Court in Hong Kong returned to their destroyed homes five months after the blaze, which killed 168 people. Residents described finding nothing left of their possessions.

stories.title: Breakthrough Prizes award $18.75 million to 2026 research leaders
stories.summary: The Breakthrough Prizes announced $18.75 million in awards to 2026 research leaders, bringing the total awarded to scientists since the prizes' founding to more than $340 million over 14 years.

stories.title: Raging at ‘fake news,’ Trump denies Israel ‘talked me into the war with Iran’
stories.summary: President Trump denied reports that Israel persuaded him to launch strikes on Iran, insisting his decision was based on his conviction that Iran must not obtain nuclear weapons. He said the October 7 Hamas attack on Israel reinforced his view.

stories.title: Turkey jails 8 people in deadly 2024 cable car accident
stories.summary: A court in Antalya, southern Turkey, sentenced eight people to prison for a 2024 cable car accident that killed one passenger and injured seven. Four defendants received seven-and-a-half-year sentences for causing death and injury through negligence. The remaining four received sentences ranging from three years and four months to five years.

stories.title: Police gunfight with favela gang traps 200 tourists on hilltop
stories.summary: Approximately 200 tourists were trapped on Morro Dois Irmãos hill in Rio de Janeiro's Vidigal favela after a police gunfight with a gang blocked the access route. The stranded sightseers were left on the hilltop during the security operation.

stories.title: These are difficult times for the world, so what will Pakistan do?
stories.summary: Pakistan is mediating talks between the United States and Iran, which officials say have not collapsed but face significant challenges. The negotiations come amid broader regional tensions.

stories.title: UK Green Party suspends Jewish activist after Israel criticism
stories.summary: The UK Green Party suspended Jewish left-wing activist Tony Greenstein following his criticism of Israel. Greenstein had previously been expelled from the UK Labour Party over views on Israel that critics characterized as antisemitic.

stories.title: The limits of Bushra Bibi’s power
stories.summary: The article examines the political influence and limitations of Bushra Bibi, Pakistan's former first lady and wife of former Prime Minister Imran Khan, and the public debate surrounding her role in national politics.

stories.title: Biggest party in Romanian coalition set to demand PM's resignation, political crisis looms
stories.summary: Romania's Social Democrats are expected to withdraw support for Liberal Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan, likely triggering a political crisis that could affect the country's debt, credit ratings, and EU fund disbursements.

stories.title: Dutch government recognizes geopolitical necessity of Ukraine’s EU membership – FM Berendsen
stories.summary: Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen stated that the Netherlands recognizes the geopolitical necessity of Ukraine's membership in the European Union. The statement reflects the Dutch government's official position on Ukraine's EU accession path.

stories.title: Trump threatens to bomb Iran if ceasefire breaks down as Vance reportedly en route to Islamabad
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump warned he would bomb Iran if a ceasefire collapses, while Vice President J.D. Vance was reportedly traveling to Islamabad for talks. Trump told PBS News he was uncertain whether Iranian representatives would attend negotiations in Pakistan but insisted Tehran would not obtain nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Civil Groups Sue Mali Over Wagner Abuses
stories.summary: Civil society groups have filed a legal case before the African Court on Human and Peoples' Rights against Mali over abuses attributed to the Wagner private military group. It is reportedly the first known case at the court seeking to hold a state accountable for hosting and hiring private military contractors.

stories.title: Israeli soldier in Sri Lanka faces war crimes summons over Gaza
stories.summary: A Sri Lankan court issued a war crimes summons against Jake Burkons, an Israeli soldier and American citizen, over alleged complicity in Israel's military campaign in Gaza. He is reportedly the first US citizen accused of such complicity outside the United States.

stories.title: Syrian soldier dies in operation to detain Assad official
stories.summary: A Syrian soldier was killed during a security operation to detain an Assad-era official in Latakia province. Syrian government forces arrested additional former regime officials, while Israeli forces separately abducted two men in Quneitra.

stories.title: Lebanon, Israel to meet again Thursday for direct talks, US says
stories.summary: The United States confirmed that Lebanon and Israel will hold a second round of direct negotiations on Thursday. The talks are taking place as the Israeli military continues operations in Lebanese towns.

stories.title: Iran says US not serious about diplomacy, no plan for second round of negotiations
stories.summary: Iran stated that the United States is not serious about diplomacy and indicated it had no plans for a second round of negotiations, even as President Trump said he had ordered US negotiators to travel to Pakistan for further talks.

stories.title: Russia preparing to breach Ukrainian minefields for counterattacks on Oleksandrivka axis – military
stories.summary: Russian units on the Oleksandrivka axis have received engineering munitions for remote demining of Ukrainian positions, according to Ukrainian military officials. The preparations indicate Russia is attempting to breach minefields to resume counterattacks and regain initiative in the sector.

stories.title: ‘Everyone must calm down’, Macron urges as US-Iran talks near
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron urged all parties to calm down as US-Iran negotiations approach, calling for maintenance of the ceasefire involving the US, Israel, Iran, and Lebanon.

stories.title: Nigeria tightens broadcast rules to curb divisive content ahead of 2027 elections
stories.summary: Nigeria's broadcast regulator barred radio and television presenters from airing personal opinions, intimidating guests, or broadcasting divisive political content ahead of the 2027 general elections. Violators face sanctions from the regulatory body.

stories.title: Back to Basics at the U.N.
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the next United Nations secretary-general should prioritize conflict resolution over issues such as climate change, disease, or artificial intelligence.

stories.title: Hungary will abide by ICC over Netanyahu, says incoming PM
stories.summary: Hungary's incoming Prime Minister Peter Magyar announced he would halt Hungary's departure from the International Criminal Court and comply with the ICC arrest warrant for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who faces crimes against humanity charges.

stories.title: Israel kills 2 in Gaza, Hamas clashes with Israel-backed militia
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed two people in Gaza, and Hamas clashed with an Israel-backed militia in the territory. The incidents represent the latest violations of a months-long ceasefire in the Palestinian territory.

stories.title: SDF begins removing checkpoints, handing over prisons in Hasakah
stories.summary: The Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces began dismantling checkpoints and transferring control of prisons to the Syrian government in Hasakah. The moves are part of an integration agreement reached in January.

stories.title: Venezuela’s Machado plans to return home by end of 2026, urges swift elections
stories.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado announced plans to return home by the end of 2026 and called for swift elections. She warned that prolonged delays in holding elections would increase the risk of civil unrest in the country.

stories.title: Saildrone unveils new medium unmanned surface vessel for anti-sub warfare, ISR
stories.summary: Saildrone has unveiled a new medium unmanned surface vessel designed for anti-submarine warfare and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance missions. The vessel comes in two variants: the Spectre Silent Endurance and the Spectre Stealth Strike.

stories.title: Naqvi meets Iran, US envoys to discuss preparations for 2nd round of Islamabad Talks
stories.summary: Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi held separate meetings with the US Chargé d'Affaires Natalie Baker and Iran's Ambassador Reza Amiri Moghadam to discuss security and logistical arrangements for a possible second round of US-Iran talks in Islamabad.

stories.title: In Jerusalem, young composers partner with bereaved families to create musical memories
stories.summary: In Jerusalem, the Tarbut Movement paired families who lost loved ones on or after October 7, 2023, with local school music programs. Young composers created and recorded songs commemorating the deceased in musical styles they had loved.

stories.title: When Identity Means Everything
stories.summary: The Ukraine Compass, a weekly digest published by War on the Rocks, curates Ukrainian media commentary and analysis to provide perspectives on daily life, politics, and public debate in wartime Ukraine beyond battlefield coverage.

stories.title: Can we stop demonizing each other over the West Bank - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece calls on Israelis to stop demonizing one another over disagreements regarding the West Bank. The author emphasizes shared experiences of loss after October 7 and a common desire for safety.

stories.title: Japan warns of ‘huge’ earthquake after powerful tremor, records 80 cm tsunami wave
stories.summary: Japan's Meteorological Agency warned that the likelihood of a subsequent major earthquake is elevated following the 7.4-magnitude tremor off the northern coast. An 80-centimetre tsunami wave was recorded after the initial quake.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces thwart Russian breakthrough attempt via gas pipeline on Kursk axis
stories.summary: Ukraine's 71st Separate Airmobile Brigade and other units stopped a Russian breakthrough attempt along a gas pipeline on the Kursk axis. Russian forces reportedly used quad bikes and motorcycles in the assault, which was repelled by Ukrainian defenders.

stories.title: Naqvi meets US, Iran envoys to discuss preparations for 2nd round of Islamabad Talks
stories.summary: Pakistan's Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi held separate meetings with the U.S. and Iranian envoys in Islamabad to discuss preparations for a potential second round of talks between Washington and Tehran. The first round ended without an agreement.

stories.title: Iran PM: 'Deep historical mistrust' toward US remains
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated on X that "deep historical mistrust" toward the US persists in Iran. He accused Washington of sending contradictory signals aimed at forcing Iran's surrender, adding that "Iranians do not submit to force."

stories.title: Rosaviatsia Lifts Restrictions on Flights to Iran and UAE Ticket Sales
stories.summary: Russia's aviation authority Rosaviatsia lifted restrictions on flights to Iran and resumed ticket sales for UAE routes. Flights to Israel and Iran had been suspended in late February following U.S. and Israeli military strikes on Iran.

stories.title: At least 21 killed as bus crashes into Kashmir gorge
stories.summary: At least 21 people were killed when an overcrowded bus skidded off a sharp curve and plunged into a gorge in the mountainous Kashmir region.

stories.title: Ugandan and Congolese forces rescue 200 people from ISIL-linked ADF
stories.summary: Ugandan and Congolese military forces rescued approximately 200 civilian captives held by the Allied Democratic Forces, an armed group operating in the region with links to ISIL (ISIS).

stories.title: New round of Israel-Lebanon talks set for Thursday as US said trying to extend truce
stories.summary: A new round of Israel-Lebanon talks is scheduled for Thursday in Washington, with envoy Yechiel Leiter leading the Israeli delegation. The US is reportedly working to extend the truce, while Hezbollah insists it will remain armed and Lebanon's PM seeks an Israeli withdrawal.

stories.title: IDF officer indicted for attempting to smuggle goods into Gaza Strip through Kerem Shalom Crossing
stories.summary: An IDF lieutenant has been indicted for attempting to smuggle goods into the Gaza Strip through the Kerem Shalom border crossing. The officer allegedly used his military position to facilitate the operation in exchange for a bribe.

stories.title: Home Office bans Tommy Robinson ally from entering UK to attend far-right march
stories.summary: The UK Home Office banned Colombian-American activist Valentina Gomez, an ally of Tommy Robinson, from entering the country. Gomez had planned to speak at a Unite the Kingdom rally scheduled for 16 May. She was a 2025 Republican congressional candidate in Texas.

stories.title: Ukraine must stay in focus, Dutch FM tells Rubio during U.S. visit
stories.summary: Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen raised Ukraine's need for continued international support during meetings with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Washington. The discussions focused on sustaining military assistance to Ukraine and increasing pressure on Russia.

stories.title: Sudanese deminers scour shattered Khartoum for hidden explosives
stories.summary: Demining teams in Khartoum, Sudan, are working to clear hidden explosives from areas devastated by conflict, including a central park once frequented by families. Operatives in protective gear use metal detectors amid extreme heat to locate ordnance.

stories.title: Money, lobbyists, inertia: Why fossil fuels are so hard to quit?
stories.summary: The article examines why the global transition away from fossil fuels has stalled despite the 2023 COP28 agreement. It highlights the influence of lobbying, financial interests, and the ongoing Middle East conflict's impact on energy dependence, particularly the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: India, South Korea plan $50bn trade push with new deals
stories.summary: India and South Korea agreed to expand economic cooperation in energy, critical minerals, shipbuilding, semiconductors, and steel, aiming to double bilateral trade to $50 billion by 2030. South Korean President Lee Jae Myung visited India for a three-day state visit.

stories.title: US Army turns to Ukraine-tested drones to counter Iranian UAV threat
stories.summary: U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll told lawmakers the service has purchased 13,000 low-cost interceptor drones to counter Iranian-made Shahed unmanned aerial vehicles. The Army is drawing on drone technology tested in the Ukraine conflict to address the Iranian UAV threat.

stories.title: EU hosts Palestinian leader in conference about security and peace in Gaza and the West Bank
stories.summary: Palestinian Prime Minister Mohamed Mustafa spoke at an EU-hosted conference in Brussels on security and peace in Gaza and the West Bank. He stated that Gaza requires unified governance under one state, one government, and one law.

stories.title: Uncertainty prevails over Islamabad talks amid mixed signals from Iran
stories.summary: Uncertainty surrounded a planned second round of U.S.-Iran direct talks in Islamabad, as Iran said it had not decided whether to attend. Pakistan's capital tightened security and sealed its Red Zone ahead of the possible arrival of foreign delegations.

stories.title: Iran expands limited internet access but restrictions remain for most
stories.summary: Iran has expanded limited internet access to more citizens, selling it as a paid privilege. However, most Iranians still face significant online restrictions.

stories.title: More than 200 rescued from IS-linked group in DR Congo
