stories.summary: The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo and the AFC/M23 rebel coalition reached progress on a protocol covering humanitarian access, judicial protection, ceasefire oversight, and the release of prisoners.

stories.title: US animal rights activists clash with police over Wisconsin dog breeder
stories.summary: Approximately 1,000 animal welfare activists attempted to enter the Ridglan Farms beagle breeding and research facility in Blue Mounds, Wisconsin, on Saturday. Police used rubber bullets and pepper spray to disperse the crowd and arrested the group's leader. It was the second such attempt in recent months.

stories.title: Israeli settlers burn Palestinian home, car in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian property in the West Bank, burning a home and a car. In separate incidents, settlers stole 150 sheep from a Palestinian farmer and injured an elderly Palestinian woman.

stories.title: More than 18,000 patients wait to leave Gaza
stories.summary: More than 18,000 patients in the Gaza Strip are waiting for medical evacuation, but only a few hundred have been allowed to leave for treatment despite ceasefire commitments to facilitate such evacuations.

stories.title: “Rusty Dagger” built for Ukraine reportedly cleared F-16 integration testing
stories.summary: A cruise missile known as "Rusty Dagger," designed specifically for Ukraine, has reportedly passed F-16 integration testing. The affordable weapon could soon be deployed on Ukraine's F-16 fighter jets.

stories.title: ISW: Russia likely plans to exploit European telecom loopholes for Shahed guidance — as it already does near Poland, Romania, Belarus
stories.summary: The Institute for the Study of War reported that Russia likely plans to exploit European telecom network loopholes to guide Shahed drones. Ukraine's Defense Ministry adviser said Russia uses SIM cards from Rostelecom subsidiary T2, which switch to neighboring countries' networks when Ukrainian signals are blocked.

stories.title: Trump threatens to ‘blow up whole country’ if Iran does not sign deal
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump told Fox News he would 'blow up the whole country' if Iran does not sign a peace deal. Trump said Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner would lead talks in Islamabad.

stories.title: Damascus claims to arrest more Hezbollah-linked cell members behind plot to kill rabbi
stories.summary: Syrian state media reported the arrest of additional members of a Hezbollah-linked cell in Damascus accused of plotting to assassinate Rabbi Michael Khoury near the Maronite Church in the Bab Touma neighborhood on April 11.

stories.title: DR Congo, AFC/M23 group agree to facilitate aid, release prisoners within 10 days
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo government and the Rwanda-backed AFC/M23 group agreed on Sunday to facilitate humanitarian aid deliveries and release prisoners within 10 days. The AFC/M23 has seized large areas of eastern DR Congo since 2021.

stories.title: DRC government, M23 rebels commit to protect civilians, aid deliveries
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo's government and M23 rebels agreed during talks in Switzerland to protect civilians and facilitate aid deliveries. The two sides also advanced a protocol for monitoring the ceasefire.

stories.title: Former US vice president Harris accuses Netanyahu of dragging Trump into Iran war
stories.summary: Former US Vice President Kamala Harris accused Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu of drawing President Trump into the war with Iran. Harris said Americans do not want war and that US servicemen have been put at risk. Netanyahu has repeatedly denied the accusation.

stories.title: Islamabad police impose traffic restrictions ahead of further talks
stories.summary: Islamabad police announced traffic restrictions and a 'red zone' closure due to visiting foreign delegations, signaling that a new round of U.S.-Iran talks may resume in Pakistan's capital.

stories.title: Turkey 'optimistic' Middle East ceasefire will be extended
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan expressed optimism that the Middle East ceasefire between the U.S.-Israel coalition and Iran would be extended before its Wednesday expiration, saying no one wants to see the war continue.

stories.title: What to know about US-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump accused Iran of violating the ceasefire and announced plans to send US negotiators to Pakistan for further talks. Tensions center on the strategic Strait of Hormuz, a critical global shipping route.

stories.title: Canada Research Chair chemist Janusz Pawliszyn joins Chinese university
stories.summary: Janusz Pawliszyn, a 71-year-old Canada Research Chair chemist and fellow of the Royal Society of Canada, has joined Sun Yat-sen University in Guangzhou, China. He has supervised over 110 graduate students and nearly 200 postdoctoral researchers during his career.

stories.title: Rescuers show how they extinguished Shostka fire under threat of further Russian attacks
stories.summary: Rescuers from Ukraine's State Emergency Service extinguished fires in Shostka, Sumy region, caused by a Russian drone attack on the night of April 19, working despite ongoing threats of additional strikes.

stories.title: Iran claims it replenishes missile launchers faster than before Operation Roaring Lion - report
stories.summary: An Iranian Revolutionary Guards commander claimed Iran is replenishing its missile launchers faster than before Operation Roaring Lion. Separately, an Israeli report said the security establishment located missile launchers aimed at Israel, ready to fire if no Lebanon ceasefire was reached.

stories.title: Russia plans to move 114,000 of its citizens into occupied regions of Ukraine, skipping cities it destroyed
stories.summary: Russia plans to resettle approximately 114,000 of its citizens into occupied regions of Ukraine, excluding heavily destroyed cities such as Bakhmut, Avdiivka, Marinka, and Vuhledar from its reconstruction plans.

stories.title: North Korea launches ballistic missiles as UN warns of nuclear advances
stories.summary: North Korea fired multiple short-range ballistic missiles from its Sinpo area toward its eastern waters, with each traveling approximately 140 kilometers, according to South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff. The launches came days after the IAEA warned of Pyongyang's advancing nuclear capabilities.

stories.title: As Israel approaches 78th Independence Day, its population stands at 10.244 million
stories.summary: Israel's population stands at 10.244 million as it approaches its 78th Independence Day. Approximately 76% are Jews and 'others,' while 21.1% are Arabs. Over the past year, 177,000 were born, 48,000 died, and 21,000 immigrated.

stories.title: Oklahoma principal who disarmed gun-wielding intruder crowned prom king
stories.summary: Kirk Moore, principal of Pauls Valley High School in Oklahoma, was crowned prom king by students on Friday after he charged and disarmed a gun-wielding intruder at the school. Moore was shot during the incident while defending students.

stories.title: Turkey says Muslim countries concerned by Israel-Greece-Cyprus alliance
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan, speaking at the Antalya Diplomacy Forum, warned that an alliance between Israel, Greece, and Cyprus has clear military dimensions and has raised concerns among Muslim-majority countries.

stories.title: Trump managing Iran war based on conflicting caprices that blindside his aides — report
stories.summary: A Wall Street Journal report states that President Trump's advisers have urged him to curb improvised social media posts and interviews regarding the Iran war. Trump reportedly yelled at aides for hours after a U.S. jet was downed and was kept from the situation room.

stories.title: How a five-dollar gadget put a Dutch warship at risk for 24 hours, calling security into question
stories.summary: A five-dollar electronic gadget compromised the Dutch warship Evertsen for 24 hours while it operated as part of a strike group in the Mediterranean, potentially exposing the broader naval formation's movements to adversaries.

stories.title: Green in the valley: Israel’s abandoned fishponds are turning into a solar goldmine
stories.summary: A new solar energy project in northern Israel will convert abandoned fishponds in the Beit She'an valley into solar installations. The initiative aims to generate clean energy, restore natural habitats, and share profits between local kibbutzim and the city.

stories.title: France U-turns on visa ban for Palestinian rights defender
stories.summary: France reversed a visa ban on Shawan Jabarin, director of Palestinian rights organization Al-Haq, allowing him to travel to France. Rights groups had criticized the original ban as an attempt to silence scrutiny of Israel.

stories.title: North London synagogue hit in latest arson attack targeting Jewish community
stories.summary: A synagogue in North London was targeted in an arson attack, the latest in a series of incidents against Jewish community sites. The building sustained minor smoke damage to an internal room, with no injuries or significant structural damage reported.

stories.title: Russians launch drone attack on railway infrastructure in Poltava region
stories.summary: Russian forces launched a drone attack targeting railway infrastructure in Ukraine's Poltava region.

stories.title: Syrians fear Israel building base after Quneitra incursions
stories.summary: Residents near Quneitra in southern Syria fear Israel may be constructing a military base after Israeli forces brought prefabricated units and set up checkpoints during incursions into the area.

stories.title: Displaced Lebanese woman returns to find home destroyed after ceasefire
stories.summary: A displaced woman who returned to southern Lebanon following a ceasefire found her home had been completely destroyed, reduced to rubble during the conflict.

stories.title: UK's Starmer 'appalled' by spate of arson attacks against London Jewish sites
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer said Sunday he was "appalled" by a series of recent arson attacks targeting Jewish sites in northwest London, including a synagogue attacked overnight from Saturday to Sunday.

stories.title: As Iran war strains ties with Trump’s US, UK looks to Europe
stories.summary: The United Kingdom is preparing legislation to deepen ties with the European Union as the Iran war strains its relationship with the United States. President Trump's rhetoric toward Britain has accelerated Prime Minister Keir Starmer's efforts to move closer to the 27-nation EU bloc, a decade after the Brexit vote.

stories.title: 'Ceasefire in the Middle East, especially in Lebanon, are meant to be broken', analyst says
stories.summary: A 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon is under review as new talks take place in Washington. Analyst Aaron David Miller of the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace expressed skepticism about the truce's durability and noted growing frustration from President Trump over Israeli military activity, linking the Israel-Lebanon and U.S.-Iran dynamics.

stories.title: Bulgaria’s eighth election in five years is today — and the frontrunner could become the EU’s new Orbán on Ukraine
stories.summary: Bulgaria held its eighth parliamentary election in five years, with the frontrunner drawing comparisons to Hungary's Viktor Orbán for his stance on Ukraine. Rivals' refusal to form a coalition with left-leaning leader Radev makes a stable pro-Russian government unlikely.

stories.title: Residents in Lebanon refused to leave, despite Israel attacks
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed hundreds of civilians across southern Lebanon before a ceasefire took effect, but many residents refused to flee their homes despite the bombardment.

stories.title: Rob Bauer just named NATO’s alarming scenario involving Russia and Europe
stories.summary: Former NATO Military Committee Chair Rob Bauer outlined an alarming scenario for NATO involving both Russia and Europe, suggesting the threat chain begins with China rather than Moscow.

stories.title: Australia soldier charged with war crimes vows to clear his name
stories.summary: Australian special forces soldier Ben Roberts-Smith has been charged with war crimes allegedly committed in Afghanistan between 2009 and 2012. Roberts-Smith has maintained his innocence and vowed to clear his name.

stories.title: UK seeks EU deals on steel and EVs in push for closer economic ties
stories.summary: The UK government is seeking deals with the EU on steel and electric vehicles to shield British industry from new tariffs and stricter EV rules due in 2027. Prime Minister Keir Starmer is pursuing closer economic ties with the bloc amid uncertainty caused by the Middle East conflict and strained U.S. relations.

stories.title: ‘It was constant chaos’: ex-Infowars producer on life under Alex Jones
stories.summary: A new book by former Infowars producer Josh Owens details his experience working for far-right conspiracy theorist Alex Jones, describing the environment as "constant chaos." Meanwhile, Jones recently clashed with President Trump after Trump publicly disparaged several right-wing media figures.

stories.title: How hydrogen could help China cut natural gas use and carbon emissions
stories.summary: China has begun a large-scale project in Weifang, Shandong province, to blend hydrogen with natural gas to supply energy to 100,000 households, aiming to reduce natural gas consumption and carbon emissions as part of its green energy push.

stories.title: Defense forces repel Russian motorcycle-led assault in Zaporizhzhia region
stories.summary: Soldiers of Ukraine's 225th Separate Assault Regiment repelled a Russian motorcycle-led assault in the Zaporizhzhia region. The Ukrainian defense forces successfully prevented the attempted Russian advance.

stories.title: Why military brass kept Trump sidelined during high-stakes Iranian extraction operation - report
stories.summary: U.S. military officials reportedly kept President Trump out of the Situation Room during a high-stakes extraction operation to rescue an American airman in Iran, fearing his temper could disrupt the mission.

stories.title: Rat poison found in HiPP baby food jar in Austria, police say
stories.summary: Austrian police reported that rat poison was found in a jar of HiPP baby food in Austria. The brand warned consumers that consuming the affected purées could be life-threatening.

stories.title: US preparing to board Iran-linked vessels amid blockade
stories.summary: The United States is preparing to board Iran-linked vessels as part of its blockade operations, barring Iranian-linked ships from passing through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Russia runs out of T-72Bs to refurbish and is now cannibalizing T-72As from 1970s, says expert
stories.summary: Russia has exhausted its supply of refurbishable T-72B tanks and is now reactivating older T-72A models from the 1970s, according to an expert. Russia is reportedly losing approximately 100 tanks per month in the conflict.

stories.title: Two Indian men shot dead in Italy while leaving gurdwara
stories.summary: Two Indian men were shot dead outside the Gurdwara Mata Sahib Kaur Ji in an industrial area of an Italian town on April 17, shortly before midnight. The attack occurred as the victims were leaving the Sikh place of worship.

stories.title: Algeria gas windfall from Iran War: Short-term gain and no pain?
stories.summary: The U.S.-Israel war on Iran is driving European countries toward Algerian natural gas supplies, boosting Algeria's geopolitical influence despite the country's entrenched corruption issues.

stories.title: An Israeli columnist called American Jews ‘traitors,’ here's why he's wrong - comment
stories.summary: The article responds to Israeli columnist Haggai Segal, who wrote in Makor Rishon that American Jews were disloyal for not immigrating to Israel, arguing against characterizing the world's largest Jewish community as traitors.

stories.title: Trump says US negotiators to head to Pakistan for Iran talks
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced that American negotiators would travel to Islamabad, Pakistan, for talks with Iran. Trump accused Tehran of violating a truce and warned of severe repercussions.

stories.title: Iran asserts leverage in Hormuz ahead of new round of talks
stories.summary: Iran has partially reopened the Strait of Hormuz under strict authorization and designated routes as tensions with the United States persist. Pakistan is attempting to organize new negotiations, while Iranian officials insist on sanctions relief and reject U.S. demands to halt nuclear activities.

stories.title: Lebanon: Two Israeli soldiers killed in last 24 hours
stories.summary: Two Israeli soldiers were killed within 24 hours in southern Lebanon. The Israeli military expressed concern over the prevalence of improvised explosive devices in the area during the ongoing truce.

stories.title: Israel's double game between negotiations with Lebanon and occupation in the south
stories.summary: Hussein Ibish of the Arab Gulf States Institute in Washington analyzed Israel's approach to Lebanon as oscillating between ceasefire negotiations and continued military presence in the south. He described Israel's stated goal of pushing out Hezbollah as justification for expanding control toward the Litani River.

stories.title: Food security under threat as Middle East war disrupts fertiliser supply
stories.summary: Roughly one-third of global fertiliser production originates in the Gulf region, and ongoing Middle East conflict is disrupting supply chains through the Strait of Hormuz. Repeated disruptions to this critical transit route are raising concerns about fertiliser export delays and potential threats to worldwide food security.

stories.title: MLES: Legislative initiatives helping return soldiers who left units without permission
stories.summary: Ukraine's Military Law Enforcement Service reported that recent legislative initiatives have helped encourage the return of soldiers who left their units without authorization, including through the use of the 'Army+' mobile app. MLES units continue operating directly in combat zones.

stories.title: Can Iran fiasco help China edge out US in key arena of Southeast Asia?
stories.summary: Since the U.S. launched strikes against Iran on February 28, several NATO allies have distanced themselves from Washington. Analysts now suggest China could exploit the situation to expand its influence in Southeast Asia, drawing parallels to Russia's loss of standing in Central Asia following its invasion of Ukraine.

stories.title: UK looks to Europe as Iran war strains ties with Trump's US
stories.summary: The UK's reluctance to join the U.S.-Israel war on Iran has strained ties between London and Washington, prompting Prime Minister Keir Starmer to pursue closer relations with the European Union despite Brexit.

stories.title: Eric Robic, Tel Aviv hit-and-run perpetrator shot in Paris, had long history of financial crime
stories.summary: Eric Robic, the French-Jewish man who fatally struck Lee Zeitouni in a Tel Aviv hit-and-run and was later shot dead in Paris, had a lengthy history of financial crime with a dozen convictions since 1994.

stories.title: Turkey's Fidan says Iran and US 'has will' to continue talks to end the war
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said at the Antalya Diplomacy Forum that both Iran and the United States have the will to continue negotiations to end the war, though disagreements remain. He also called for extending the ceasefire due to expire next week.

stories.title: US Army is deploying $3,000 drones to shoot down Shaheds — because Ukraine proved they work
stories.summary: The U.S. Army is deploying low-cost drones, priced at around $3,000 each, to intercept Iranian-made Shahed drones, adopting a tactic that Ukrainian forces developed and proved effective on the battlefield.

stories.title: Minister affirms govt providing pilgrims best possible facilities as PIA launches Haj operation
stories.summary: Pakistan's Religious Affairs Minister Sardar Muhammad Yousuf confirmed the government is providing pilgrims with top facilities as Pakistan International Airlines launched its Haj operation from Islamabad International Airport. The Road to Makkah project has been expanded to Lahore, joining Karachi and Islamabad, and is expected to serve over 95,000 pilgrims this year.

stories.title: Iranian women's soccer players 'were misled,' in Australia, Pezeshkian says in video address
stories.summary: Iranian President Pezeshkian claimed in a video address that Iranian women's soccer players who sought asylum in Australia 'were misled.' Australia had granted humanitarian visas to six players and one staff member in early March after they expressed fears of persecution upon returning to Iran.

stories.title: Argentinian president Milei lands in Israel, set to meet with Netanyahu, announce new El Al flight
stories.summary: Argentine President Javier Milei arrived in Israel for meetings with Prime Minister Netanyahu and to announce a new El Al flight route. Argentina's foreign minister is also holding separate talks with Israeli officials focused on counterterrorism cooperation and technological collaboration.

stories.title: Bank bosses called to meeting with Reeves over impact of Iran war on UK economy
stories.summary: UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves has summoned the chief executives of HSBC, Barclays, Lloyds, NatWest, and Santander to an emergency meeting this week. The summit will focus on limiting the economic impact on the UK economy from the Middle East crisis triggered by U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iran.

stories.title: Iran turns back two tankers attempting to cross Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's armed forces turned back two tankers—flagged to Botswana and Angola—attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz, citing the ongoing U.S. maritime blockade on Iran, according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency.

stories.title: Iran says it is replenishing missile launchers faster than before the war
stories.summary: An Iranian Revolutionary Guards Aerospace Force commander claimed Iran is replenishing its missile and drone launchers faster than before the war with the U.S. and Israel. Majid Mousavi spoke while inspecting an underground missile facility.

stories.title: How the PLA may use stealth drones in a swarming boat attack from Taiwan
stories.summary: A Chinese military magazine, Defence Review, has proposed using the GJ-21 stealth attack drone to counter a potential Taiwanese swarm of unmanned combat boats crossing the Taiwan Strait. The GJ-21, a naval variant of the GJ-11 Sharp Sword, is described as having long endurance and high maneuverability suited for defeating such tactics inspired by Ukraine's naval operations.

stories.title: Supreme Court justices accuse Levin of abusing power to block judicial appointments
stories.summary: Israeli Supreme Court justices accused Justice Minister Yariv Levin of abusing his power by refusing to convene the judicial selection committee, thereby blocking needed appointments of district and magistrate court judges.

stories.title: New site offers travel by armchair to Eilat’s magnificent coral reefs
stories.summary: A new website offers virtual exploration of Eilat's coral reefs in the Gulf of Eilat, featuring virtual safaris through underwater habitats, a live reef camera, and access to scientific research aimed at raising awareness of the marine ecosystem.

stories.title: The factory that makes Russia’s killer drones burned again overnight — Neptune missile attack conformed
stories.summary: Ukrainian Neptune cruise missiles struck the Atlant Aero factory in Taganrog, Russia, where Molniia strike drones are manufactured. Local residents reported powerful explosions before dawn and thick black smoke rising from the plant.

stories.title: USF Operators shoot down Shahed drone from surface platform for first time
stories.summary: Operators of Ukraine's 412th Nemesis Brigade launched an interceptor drone from an unmanned surface platform and shot down a Russian Shahed-type drone. The Armed Forces of Ukraine described it as the first time such a surface-platform-based interception has been achieved worldwide.

stories.title: UN chief Guterres condemns killing of French peacekeeper in Lebanon
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned the killing of a French peacekeeper and wounding of three others in a small-arms attack on UNIFIL in southern Lebanon. France and UNIFIL blamed Hezbollah, which denied involvement.

stories.title: Trump backs US$50 million investment for South Africa rare earths
stories.summary: The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation is backing a US$50 million equity investment in the Phalaborwa Rare Earths Project in South Africa. The project aims to extract rare earth elements from industrial mining waste at an old chemical processing plant, as part of broader U.S. efforts to reduce dependence on China for critical minerals.

stories.title: Pope Leo tells Angola during huge Mass to ‘build hope’
stories.summary: Pope Leo, on the third leg of his Africa tour, celebrated a large Mass in Angola and urged the nation to 'build hope' and move beyond divisions rooted in its war-scarred history.

stories.title: Russia’s shadow fleet is moving $10 billion in oil right now — that’s budget for next week’s attacks on Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine's President Zelensky warned that Russia's shadow fleet is currently transporting approximately $10 billion worth of oil, arguing that easing sanctions enables Moscow to fund continued attacks on Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran war: 10 frequently used words and their meanings
stories.summary: As the U.S.-Israel war on Iran approaches its two-month mark, a glossary explains frequently used terminology associated with the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Humans far behind as robot breaks record at Beijing half marathon
stories.summary: A humanoid robot broke the world record at the Beijing half marathon on Sunday, competing alongside human runners. The event highlighted the rapid advancement of Chinese robotics, as humanoid robots have become increasingly visible in China's public spaces and media.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill one person in Gaza ahead of talks
stories.summary: Israeli forces fatally shot a young man in Jabalia, northern Gaza, early Sunday, marking another reported ceasefire violation in the devastated territory ahead of planned talks.

stories.title: Russia uses 3,740 aerial attack assets against Ukraine in one week – Zelensky
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky reported that Russia used approximately 3,740 aerial attack assets against Ukraine in one week, including nearly 2,360 strike drones, over 1,320 guided aerial bombs, and about 60 missiles.

stories.title: Does the world need new leaders? Varsha Gandikota & Naledi Pandor
stories.summary: Varsha Gandikota-Nellutla interviewed former South African Foreign Minister Naledi Pandor on whether global leadership is experiencing a crisis.

stories.title: Iran warns Hormuz will stay shut unless US lifts siege on its ports
stories.summary: Iran threatened to keep the Strait of Hormuz closed unless the United States lifts what Tehran describes as a siege on Iranian ports, escalating tensions over maritime access.

stories.title: Does Israel’s ‘Yellow Line’ violate the Lebanon ceasefire?
stories.summary: Israel's establishment of a so-called 'Yellow Line' in southern Lebanon has raised concerns that a temporary military zone could evolve into a longer-term occupation, potentially violating the Lebanon ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: “Together, We Remember”
stories.summary: Masa Israel Journey organized an international Yom HaZikaron (Remembrance Day) ceremony expected to be viewed by hundreds of thousands of Jewish participants from roughly 60 countries and Israel.

stories.title: Pakistan preparing for potential new talks in Islamabad: Al Jazeera
stories.summary: Pakistan is preparing for a potential second round of U.S.-Iran talks in Islamabad. Two major hotels, including the Serena, have reportedly evacuated guests and increased security, while local authorities restricted heavy transport in the city.

stories.title: Daily Briefing Apr. 19 – Five points of apparent failure in the Iran war
stories.summary: Times of Israel diplomatic correspondent Lazar Berman outlined five apparent failures in the U.S.-Israel war on Iran, including disagreements between Jerusalem and Washington on Iran and Lebanon policy, and IDF difficulties confronting Hezbollah.

stories.title: Hong Kong Sevens a treat for fans but local restaurants hungry for more trade
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Sevens rugby tournament concluded with a high-energy finale at Kai Tak Stadium on Sunday, drawing large crowds of costumed fans. However, some nearby restaurants reported lower revenue compared to last year, attributing the decline to increased competition from newly opened dining establishments in the area.

stories.title: General Staff confirms strike on Atlant Aero enterprise in Taganrog, number of other targets in temporarily occupied territories
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces struck the Atlant Aero defense-industrial enterprise in Taganrog, Russia, on the night of April 19, along with several other targets in Russian-occupied territories. The Ukrainian General Staff confirmed the strikes.

stories.title: North Korea fires ballistic missiles again, flexing muscle amid Iran war
stories.summary: North Korea fired ballistic missiles into the sea on Sunday, marking its fourth launch this month and seventh of the year. Analysts suggest Pyongyang is demonstrating self-defense capabilities amid the ongoing Iran war and ahead of possible diplomatic contacts with the United States and South Korea.

stories.title: Lebanese army restores road, bridge damaged by Israeli strikes
stories.summary: The Lebanese army reopened a road connecting Nabatieh with the Khardali area that had been damaged by Israeli strikes. Repair work on the Tayr Falsay-Tyre bridge remains ongoing.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: 'Bold and loyal', Trump praises Israel as 'great ally' of U.S.
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump publicly praised Israel as a 'bold and loyal' ally and a premier strategic partner during a period of heightened regional instability involving the Iran-Israel conflict.

stories.title: Humanoid robot breaks half marathon world record in Beijing
stories.summary: A humanoid robot built by Chinese smartphone maker Honor set a new half marathon world record in Beijing, finishing well ahead of human competitors.

stories.title: Nathalie Baye, prolific star of French and Hollywood cinema, dies aged 77
stories.summary: French film star Nathalie Baye has died at age 77 from Lewy body dementia at her home in France, her family confirmed. Baye appeared in approximately 80 films, won four César Awards for best actress, and starred in Steven Spielberg's Catch Me If You Can.

stories.title: Pakistan’s Nadia, Aqsa reflect on FIFA Series highs, heartbreak and the road ahead
stories.summary: Pakistan's women's football team competed in their first-ever FIFA Series, recording an 8-0 victory before losing 1-0 to Mauritania and 2-0 to hosts Ivory Coast. Forwards Nadia Khan and Aqsa Mushtaq highlighted both the team's potential and structural challenges.

stories.title: Falling fertility, debt and AI: is the US headed toward a population crisis?
stories.summary: Analysts warn the United States may be heading toward a population crisis driven by falling fertility rates, an aging population, and rising national debt. The demographic shift could strain social stability and economic systems, countering decades-old fears about overpopulation.

stories.title: China’s ‘land aircraft carrier’ charges flying drone with microwave beam
stories.summary: Chinese scientists have demonstrated a ground-based microwave wireless power transmission system capable of beaming energy to a drone in flight while both the vehicle and emitter are in motion. The technology, likened to a "land-based aircraft carrier," could allow drones to fly indefinitely by recharging mid-air.

stories.title: Blaze in Malaysia’s Sabah destroys 1,000 homes, displaces over 9,000
stories.summary: A fire in Sandakan district in Malaysia's Sabah state on Borneo destroyed approximately 1,000 homes and displaced over 9,000 people on Sunday. Authorities said strong winds, closely built houses, and low tide conditions that limited water access contributed to the rapid spread of the blaze in the coastal village.

stories.title: Zelensky Says Oil Sanctions Relief Provides Billions for Russian Military
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky argued that sanctions relief on Russian oil provides billions of dollars to fund Moscow's military operations. He stated that every dollar paid for Russian oil directly finances the war against Ukraine.

stories.title: Australia and Japan sign contracts for $7bn warships deal
stories.summary: Australia and Japan signed contracts for a $7 billion warships deal, reflecting deepening defense ties between Canberra and Tokyo amid shared concerns over China's growing military influence in the region.

stories.title: Insurgency-hit Nigeria strikes defence deal with Turkey
stories.summary: Nigeria and Turkey signed a defence agreement under which Turkey will train 200 members of the Nigerian army's special forces. The deal comes as Nigeria continues to face an ongoing insurgency.

stories.title: Defense Forces thwart enemy attempts to break through near Chasiv Yar for second consecutive day
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces repelled a large-scale Russian attempt to break through near Chasiv Yar in the Donetsk region for the second consecutive day.

stories.title: Late bloomer Salman Mirza sets sights on 2027 World Cup
stories.summary: Pakistani left-arm pacer Salman Mirza, who debuted internationally at age 31 in T20Is against Bangladesh in July 2025, has set his sights on making Pakistan's squad for the 2027 ODI World Cup. The Karachi-based bowler has quickly established himself as a reliable performer after years on the domestic circuit.

stories.title: Maria Corina Machado draws thousands of Venezuelans in Madrid, declares: "Today we begin the journey home"
stories.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize laureate María Corina Machado drew thousands of supporters to Madrid's Puerta del Sol on Saturday. She received the Gold Medal of the Community of Madrid from regional president Isabel Díaz Ayuso and declared the beginning of a new push for free elections in Venezuela.

stories.title: Syria may consider long-term talks with Israel on Golan Heights
stories.summary: Syrian leader Ahmed al-Sharaa indicated he would consider entering long-term negotiations with Israel over the Golan Heights, which Israel has occupied and annexed for decades.

stories.title: War on Iran: Why Israel and the US are the ultimate losers
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the US-Israeli military campaign aimed at weakening or destabilising the Iranian government appears to have had the opposite effect. Antiwar protests were reported internationally, including in the Philippines.

stories.title: Bangladesh raises fuel prices as conflict in West Asia drives up costs
stories.summary: Bangladesh raised fuel prices as the ongoing war on Iran pushed up crude oil prices, disrupted supply chains, and increased freight and insurance costs, making fuel imports significantly more expensive for the country.

stories.title: 'Who is the baby-killer, coward?' Far-right activist confronts Yair Golan after left-wing protest
stories.summary: A far-right activist confronted opposition politician Yair Golan following a left-wing protest at Habima Square in Tel Aviv. The protest, organized by the October Council, highlighted that this year marks the third Remembrance Day without answers regarding hostages and other unresolved issues.

stories.title: ‘I am going crazy’: Families of missing Gaza children endure agonising uncertainty
stories.summary: Approximately 2,900 Palestinian children remain missing following Israeli attacks in Gaza. Families, including a mother who has had no information about her 14-year-old son for 10 months, describe enduring severe anguish and uncertainty.

stories.title: Russians transfer troops from Rostov region through Mariupol – Andriushchenko
stories.summary: Russian forces reportedly spent nearly three days transferring troops from Russia's Rostov region through the occupied city of Mariupol toward the Berdiansk-Melitopol direction, according to Ukrainian official Andriushchenko.

stories.title: Allies back Starmer as Mandelson’s Epstein link leaves UK PM fighting for his job
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faces a political crisis as a scandal involving Lord Mandelson's links to Jeffrey Epstein threatens his tenure. Senior Labour allies have defended Starmer as a 'man of integrity' ahead of parliamentary questioning.

stories.title: Ghazal, youngest female Kurdish Peshmerga, dies after IRGC strike and medical neglect
stories.summary: Ghazal Molan, a 19-year-old Kurdish Peshmerga fighter described as the youngest female member of the force, died after being wounded in an IRGC drone strike. Reports allege she was denied urgent hospital care before her burial in Sulaymaniyah.

stories.title: The GCC has unity, it now needs joint defence and development
stories.summary: An analysis argues that Gulf Cooperation Council states, having achieved political unity, now need to pursue joint defense capabilities, energy security cooperation, and coordinated economic development.

stories.title: IDF reservist killed, nine wounded by explosive in southern Lebanon amid truce
stories.summary: IDF reservist Sgt. First Class Lidor Porat, 31, was killed and nine soldiers were wounded when an engineering vehicle struck an explosive device in southern Lebanon during the truce. The Israeli military carried out strikes following the incident.

stories.title: Russian drone attack leaves one killed, four injured in Chernihiv
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack on the city of Chernihiv killed a 16-year-old boy and injured four other people.

stories.title: Hong Kong urged to be more proactive in removing barriers with Shenzhen
stories.summary: Analysts are urging Hong Kong to take a more proactive role in removing barriers to cross-border flows of people, capital, goods, and data with Shenzhen. The calls follow the appointment of Jin Lei, an economist and former Sichuan province official, as Shenzhen's new Communist Party chief, succeeding Meng Fanli.

stories.title: LIVESTREAM: Reading of the Declaration of Independence at the Kotel - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A livestream event at the egalitarian section of the Western Wall in Jerusalem featured a reading of Israel's Declaration of Independence, with participants from Israel and around the world affirming shared values.

stories.title: Displaced Lebanese families return home despite Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Displaced Lebanese families returned to southern Lebanon to inspect their destroyed homes but remained uncertain about staying, as concerns about renewed Israeli attacks and further conflict persisted.

stories.title: US 'more coordinated' with China  amid Hormuz struggle than people assume, fmr. Navy commander says
stories.summary: A former US Navy commander stated that Washington and Beijing are more coordinated over the Strait of Hormuz situation than widely assumed. He also noted that Iran's longstanding claim of control over the strait is being challenged by American military superiority in the area.

stories.title: A petition called 'Lebanon will not be the next Gaza' calls on French leaders to take action
stories.summary: A petition titled "Lebanon will not be the next Gaza" has been launched by French civil society actors and signed by numerous public figures, urging President Emmanuel Macron to ensure the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire holds. Marie Yared of the Avaaz Foundation said the initiative responds to concerns that Israel repeatedly violated last year's truce.

stories.title: Iran: Prolonged conflict reshapes view of the regime, analyst says
stories.summary: Analyst Mehran Kamrave of the Arab Center for Research and Policy Studies identified three key levers Iran is using against the United States: sanctions, its nuclear programme, and control over the Strait of Hormuz. He noted that despite the ongoing conflict, the Iranian government is tightening domestic control and the prolonged war may actually be reducing public opposition to the regime.

stories.title: Trump, Iran cite progress in talks as uncertainty hangs over Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said the US is having 'very good conversations' with Iran but provided no further details, as uncertainty continues over the status of the Strait of Hormuz amid ongoing tensions.

stories.title: Over 10,000 police personnel deployed on security duty in Rawalpindi
stories.summary: Over 10,000 police personnel, including 400 elite commandos and 100 snipers, have been deployed in Rawalpindi ahead of the second round of US-Iran talks expected in Islamabad. Hotels and guest houses in the capital have been directed to close temporarily.

stories.title: ‘State-of-the-art’ models can struggle with basic enterprise tasks: AI unicorn executive
stories.summary: David Meyer, senior vice-president of product at US AI company Databricks, said that state-of-the-art AI models capable of solving complex Olympiad-level mathematics still struggle with routine enterprise tasks. He noted that the very traits making models advanced can cause problems in basic office work.

stories.title: Missiles strike Molniya drones manufacturing plant in Taganrog – media
stories.summary: Missiles struck the Atlant Aero enterprise in Taganrog, Russia, on the night of April 19. The facility is reportedly involved in manufacturing Molniya drones used by Russian forces.

stories.title: Iranian president insists on country's nuclear rights, ISNA reports
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian asserted that US President Donald Trump has no justification to deny Iran its nuclear rights. Pezeshkian's remarks, reported by ISNA, came as Washington and Tehran continue to disagree over nuclear issues.

stories.title: Zelensky condemns US extension of Russian sanctions waiver
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Zelensky condemned a U.S. decision to extend a sanctions waiver on Russia, which Washington justified as a measure to ease energy supply disruptions caused by the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Hezbollah is willing to cooperate with a ceasefire with Israel – for now
stories.summary: Hezbollah has indicated willingness to cooperate with a ceasefire with Israel for the time being. Approximately 2,300 Lebanese people have been killed in the latest conflict.

stories.title: SMOKERS’ CORNER: GEOPOLITICS OF THE PULPIT
stories.summary: An opinion piece examines the history of Western engagement in the Middle East and South Asia, focusing on how radical Islamist movements were used as strategic assets against secular or leftist rivals, including the CIA's involvement in the 1953 coup against Iran's Prime Minister Mosaddegh.

stories.title: Arson attempt hits London synagogue; Iran-linked group claims attack on Jewish-tied building
stories.summary: An arson attempt targeted a London synagogue, while an Iran-linked group claimed responsibility for an attack on a Jewish-affiliated building in the UK. No injuries were reported in either incident. UK Chief Rabbi Mirvis described a 'sustained campaign of violence and intimidation against the Jewish community.'

stories.title: Bulgaria votes as pro-Russian former president leads in the polls
stories.summary: Bulgarians voted in their eighth parliamentary election in five years on Sunday, with pro-Russian former president Rumen Radev leading in polls on promises to fight corruption and deliver political stability. Radev, a Eurosceptic former fighter pilot who opposes military support for Ukraine, stepped down from the presidency in January to contest the election.

stories.title: Corruption fuels mistrust in Bulgaria’s eighth election in 5 years
stories.summary: Bulgaria held its eighth parliamentary election in five years on Sunday, with former president Rumen Radev's political grouping favored to win on an anti-corruption platform. Radev, who advocates renewing ties with Russia and opposes military aid to Ukraine, entered the race after mass protests toppled the previous government in December.

stories.title: ADF neutralizes 203 out of 236 Russian drones launched overnight
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces neutralized 203 of 236 Russian drones launched in attacks beginning on the evening of April 18.

stories.title: Three women held in Sialkot for beggary in KSA
stories.summary: Pakistan's Federal Investigation Agency arrested four people, including three women, at Sialkot airport upon their return from Saudi Arabia via Oman. The group admitted to engaging in organized beggary in Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: Police investigate attempted arson attack at north-west London synagogue
stories.summary: Police are investigating an attempted arson attack at Kenton United Synagogue in Harrow, north-west London, on Saturday night. The incident caused minor smoke damage to an internal room but no injuries, according to the Community Security Trust. It is the latest in a spate of similar attacks on Jewish sites in the capital.

stories.title: Trump threatens Iran infrastructure, US team to head to Pakistan
stories.summary: President Trump announced a US delegation will travel to Pakistan on Monday for negotiations with Iran and again threatened strikes on Iranian infrastructure if no deal is reached. The ceasefire deadline is approaching on Wednesday.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz remains closed as US-Iran deal still 'far off'
stories.summary: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf stated that a deal with the United States remains far off as the Strait of Hormuz continues to be closed to shipping traffic.

stories.title: Mass shooting in Kyiv leaves 6 dead before police kill gunman
stories.summary: A mass shooting in a busy central district of Kyiv left six people dead before police killed the gunman. The incident was described as unprecedented in wartime Kyiv.

stories.title: Sindh High Court sees no clause in Sindh laws for blocking CNIC in civil cases
stories.summary: The Sindh High Court ruled that no provision exists in Sindh's general or special laws for blocking a person's computerized national identity card in civil litigation. The court noted that the Civil Procedure Code became a provincial subject after the 18th Constitutional Amendment.

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 51 of the US-Iran conflict?
stories.summary: On day 51 of the US-Iran conflict, Tehran announced it would keep the Strait of Hormuz closed until Washington lifts its blockade of Iranian ports.

stories.title: War update: 153 combat clashes on front line over past day, Pokrovsk direction most active
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces recorded 153 combat engagements with Russian troops along the front line on April 18, with the Pokrovsk direction being the most active sector.

stories.title: How the Israeli military targets the people who save lives
stories.summary: Israeli military attacks have killed at least 57 medical workers in Lebanon since early March. The report describes the targeting pattern as consistent with tactics previously used in Gaza.

stories.title: Bulgaria votes as pro-Russian former president leads the polls
stories.summary: Bulgarians voted in their eighth parliamentary election in five years, with pro-Russian former President Rumen Radev leading the polls. Radev has promised to end the cycle of weak governments and combat widespread corruption.

stories.title: 'New era': Humanoid robot outruns humans in Beijing half-marathon, beats world record
stories.summary: A humanoid robot won a robot half-marathon in Beijing on Sunday, completing the course in 50 minutes and 26 seconds—faster than the human world record. The event showcased China's advances in robotics technology.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz blocked as gaps remain on Iran peace talks
stories.summary: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz came to a standstill on Sunday after Iran reasserted control over the strategic waterway critical to global energy supply. The blockage occurred days before a fragile ceasefire between Iran and the United States was set to expire.

stories.title: A new Pakistan
stories.summary: An analysis discusses Pakistan's diplomatic efforts to mediate between Iran and the United States, noting the conflict has shifted the global strategic landscape and created a new geopolitical role for Islamabad that may require a review of its existing strategic doctrine.

stories.title: Michigan gas station clerk saves teen from alleged kidnapper after she whispers ‘help’
stories.summary: A gas station clerk in Hamtramck, Michigan, named Abdulrahman Abohatem helped rescue a 16-year-old girl who had been kidnapped at gunpoint on her way to school. The teenager entered his store and whispered "help," prompting Abohatem to intervene and place himself between the girl and her alleged abductor before police arrived.

stories.title: Iran keen on deal to end war but has higher ‘pain tolerance’: think tank chief
stories.summary: A Middle East-focused think tank leader familiar with ongoing negotiations said the economic toll of war is pushing Iran to seek a resolution beyond its fragile two-week truce with the United States. However, Iranian leaders believe their country's capacity to endure hardship exceeds that of the Americans, making them unlikely to concede first.

stories.title: Middle East: Hezbollah blamed after French peacekeeper killed in Lebanon
stories.summary: A French peacekeeper serving with the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) was killed and three others wounded in an ambush in southern Lebanon. French President Emmanuel Macron blamed Hezbollah for the attack, though the group denied responsibility.

stories.title: 'They are stealing the election': How Armenia became the next Russia-EU battlefield
stories.summary: Armenia is preparing for parliamentary elections in June, with both the EU and Russia closely monitoring the vote. Public support for EU membership is at record levels, suggesting a potential shift away from Moscow, but observers warn of foreign interference from both sides that could undermine the democratic process.

stories.title: What is UNIFIL? the UN mission in southern Lebanon explained
stories.summary: The United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) has operated in southern Lebanon since 1978, monitoring the border with Israel. Expanded after the 2006 Israel-Hezbollah war, the mission currently deploys over 7,500 peacekeepers to monitor the ceasefire and support the Lebanese army, though it lacks a mandate for military intervention.

stories.title: Enemy launches nearly 20 shelling attacks on three districts in Dnipro region since evening
stories.summary: Russian forces attacked three districts in Ukraine's Dnipro region nearly 20 times since evening, using drones and artillery.

stories.title: Spain’s Sánchez leads progressive push as far-right gathers in Milan
stories.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez hosted left-wing leaders at rallies in Barcelona on Saturday promoting democracy and progressive unity. A vocal critic of Donald Trump and the US-Israeli war in Iran, Sánchez called for peace while a rival gathering of far-right leaders convened simultaneously in Milan.

stories.title: War reparations
stories.summary: Iran included a demand for war reparations from the US and Israel in its 10-point ceasefire plan, citing damage from the February 28 attacks. The issue was reportedly discussed during recent negotiations in Islamabad, with international law experts suggesting the US may be liable for civilian infrastructure damage.

stories.title: Parliamentary speaker says Iran ‘victorious’ in war with US
stories.summary: Iran's parliamentary speaker declared Iran 'victorious' in its war with the United States as a two-week ceasefire approaches its April 22 expiration date, with no confirmation yet of renewal.

stories.title: Hong Kong police use drones for first time to tackle illicit street gambling
stories.summary: Hong Kong police deployed drones for the first time to combat illegal street gambling in Chung On Estate, arresting eight suspects aged 53 to 76 over two weeks. The joint operation, codenamed JusticePeak, was conducted by Sha Tin and Ma On Shan police divisions, seizing cash and gambling equipment.

stories.title: Iran, US still ‘far’ from breakthrough amid Strait of Hormuz impasse
stories.summary: Iranian parliament speaker Ghalibaf stated that Tehran remains 'fully prepared' for a resumption of US hostilities at any moment. He indicated that the two sides are still far from a breakthrough amid the ongoing Strait of Hormuz impasse.

stories.title: Watch: Runners v robots at China half marathon
stories.summary: Robots competed alongside human runners in a half marathon in Beijing, China, on Sunday. The winning robot finished ahead of all human competitors in the race.

stories.title: Wife of ‘facilitator’ held in Nokundi FC headquarters suicide blast case
stories.summary: Pakistani security forces in Quetta arrested the wife of an alleged facilitator of a female suicide bomber who attacked the Frontier Corps headquarters in Nokundi. Officials said the facilitator had taken a woman and her children to Afghanistan for suicide bombing training.

stories.title: Togo wants to act as 'bridge' between Sahel and international community
stories.summary: Togo presented a new geopolitical and security strategy for the Sahel region during a high-level meeting held in Lomé on Saturday. The West African nation aims to position itself as a diplomatic bridge between Sahel states and the international community.

stories.title: AI is advancing. Now it’s up to humans to redefine their worth
stories.summary: An analysis discusses how generative AI powered by large language models represents a breakthrough enabling humans to communicate with computers through natural language. The piece highlights the rise of "vibe coding" and AI agents that allow non-programmers to develop software, raising questions about the future of human roles.

stories.title: Why Iran’s ‘mosquito fleet’ remains a potent threat in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard maintains a flotilla of small boats known as a 'mosquito fleet' that remains a significant naval threat in the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Russian military loses 1,070 soldiers and five MLRS in war against Ukraine
stories.summary: Russia's total estimated combat losses in Ukraine from February 24, 2022, to April 19, 2026, reached approximately 1,318,220 personnel, with 1,070 soldiers and five multiple-launch rocket systems lost in the past 24 hours.

stories.title: Bennett, Eisenkot and Lapid said holding contacts on forming joint party
stories.summary: Former Israeli leaders Naftali Bennett, Gadi Eisenkot, and Yair Lapid are reportedly in discussions to form a joint political party called 'New Israel.' The proposed movement would hold primaries across 15 regions to determine its leadership ahead of upcoming elections.

stories.title: WATCH: West Bank settlers set home, car ablaze in Palestinian village, spray threatening graffiti
stories.summary: Approximately 20 Israeli settlers attacked the Palestinian village of Turmus Ayya in the West Bank, setting a home and car ablaze and spray-painting threatening graffiti including "Revenge" and "Hello from Khirbat Abu Falah."

stories.title: Returning to a fire-ravaged home in Wang Fuk Court: what to prepare
stories.summary: Around 1,900 families from Hong Kong's Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po are returning in batches starting April 20 to collect belongings from fire-ravaged homes. Nearly five months after a deadly blaze engulfed seven of eight buildings, about 6,000 residents have booked return slots while 47 households opted out.

stories.title: North Korea fires missiles ahead of possible US, South Korea talks
stories.summary: North Korea launched ballistic missiles ahead of potential talks between the United States and South Korea. Former South Korean presidential security adviser Kim Ki-jung suggested the launches may be intended to demonstrate self-defense capabilities distinct from Iran's situation.

stories.title: Lionel Messi scores twice as Inter Miami defeat Rapids in MLS
stories.summary: Lionel Messi scored twice, including the match-winning goal, as Inter Miami defeated the Colorado Rapids in an MLS match played before over 75,000 fans in Denver.

stories.title: China hosts humanoid robots in Beijing half marathon
stories.summary: During a half-marathon event in Beijing, China tested humanoid robots alongside human runners. The race demonstrated advances in robotic endurance, balance, and AI-driven behavior. Engineers involved view the milestone as a step toward broader real-world applications for humanoid robotics.

stories.title: More Britons opt to holiday in UK this summer amid uncertainty over flights
stories.summary: UK holiday park companies report a surge in domestic summer bookings as Britons worry about flight cancellations linked to the Iran war. Warnings of possible jet fuel shortages across Europe are driving more travelers to choose staycations over international trips this summer.

stories.title: More jobs for the elderly: Shanghai eyes senior labour force amid China demographic crisis
stories.summary: Shanghai is exploring ways to employ more elderly workers as China grapples with a demographic crisis and shrinking workforce. Despite the city's need for labor, older jobseekers like a 58-year-old former mechanic from Jiangsu province face barriers including high agency fees and physically demanding conditions.

stories.title: Stop managing NATO. Start rebalancing it.
stories.summary: A policy analysis argues that NATO should shift from day-to-day management to fundamental structural rebalancing. The piece proposes three specific reforms to strengthen the alliance for its next strategic era.

stories.title: A boat with no crew just shot down a Shahed. Ukraine says it’s a world first
stories.summary: Ukraine's 412th Nemesis Brigade reported that an unmanned surface vessel launched an interceptor drone that shot down a Russian Shahed kamikaze drone, which Ukraine described as the world's first such engagement and a new layer of maritime air defense.

stories.title: Attacks on US academics: A microcosm of a larger threat to democracy
stories.summary: A new DW documentary examines parallels between the erosion of democratic norms in the United States under Trump and in Turkey, as told through the perspective of Turkish press freedom advocate Can Dündar. The film highlights recent attacks on US academics as part of broader threats to democracy.

stories.title: Russian forces strike Zaporizhzhia region 756 times in 24 hours, one injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck the Zaporizhzhia region of Ukraine 756 times across 44 settlements in a 24-hour period, injuring one person. The attacks targeted areas throughout the region.

stories.title: Economy can weather Iran war risks: SBP chief
stories.summary: State Bank of Pakistan Governor Jameel Ahmad said Pakistan's macroeconomic indicators improved faster than expected due to prudent monetary and fiscal policies. He acknowledged that the Middle East conflict has introduced new risks but expressed confidence the economy can withstand them.

stories.title: Video: Trump says Iran cannot 'blackmail' US over strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump declared that Iran cannot 'blackmail' the United States over the Strait of Hormuz. Trump said Washington was engaged in talks with Tehran but would not be pressured, taking a 'tough stand' against what he called leverage attempts involving the waterway.

stories.title: Lebanon reopens key routes as repairs continue in south
stories.summary: The Lebanese Armed Forces announced the full reopening of the Khardali-Nabatieh road and partial reopening of the Burj Rahal-Tyre bridge in southern Lebanon. Repair work continues on other transport links damaged during recent Israeli military operations.

stories.title: France blames Hezbollah for soldier’s death in Lebanon
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron blamed Hezbollah for an attack in Lebanon that killed one French UN peacekeeper and wounded three others. Hezbollah denied responsibility. Macron urged Lebanese authorities to arrest the perpetrators and guarantee UNIFIL security.

stories.title: WSJ: Aides kept Trump out of Iran war room fearing 'impatience wouldn’t help'
stories.summary: According to The Wall Street Journal, US aides kept President Trump out of the room during real-time updates on military operations involving Iran, believing his impatience would be counterproductive. Trump reportedly reacted angrily after learning an American jet had been shot down with two airmen missing.

stories.title: Four day pride festival to be held at Dead Sea, largest in history of Middle East
stories.summary: A four-day pride festival billed as the largest in Middle East history is planned at the Dead Sea. Producer Aaron Cohen described the "Pride Land" event as the biggest undertaking of its kind in the region.

stories.title: On 1st day, Shin Bet chief changed background pic on all agency PCs to Temple Mount – report
stories.summary: Newly appointed Shin Bet chief David Zini reportedly changed the desktop background on all agency computers to an image of the Temple Mount on his first day. After internal backlash over what sources called a 'messianic' signal, the image was reverted to the agency logo and the change was described as accidental.

stories.title: UAV crash in Chernihiv damages homes and school, casualties reported
stories.summary: A UAV crash in the Ukrainian city of Chernihiv damaged two private homes and an educational institution, with casualties reported from the incident.

stories.title: Sikh pilgrims return home today via Wagah
stories.summary: Approximately 2,238 Sikh pilgrims from India are returning home via the Wagah Border after a week-long Baisakhi visit to Pakistan. The Punjab government hosted cultural events, including a ceremony at Hazuri Bagh in Lahore.

stories.title: Pakistan eyes $1.2bn inflow next month
stories.summary: The IMF Executive Board is expected to consider approval of a staff-level agreement next month that could release approximately $1.2 billion to Pakistan under the Extended Fund Facility and Resilience and Sustainability Facility. Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb held meetings with IMF and World Bank officials in Washington.

stories.title: Korangi Harbour gets Rs120m floating jetty
stories.summary: Pakistan's Maritime Affairs Minister announced that construction has begun on a Rs120 million eco-friendly floating jetty at Korangi Fisheries Harbour Authority in Karachi. The project aims to improve offloading facilities for export-quality fish and support small-scale fisherfolk.

stories.title: Climate moot rescheduled
stories.summary: DawnMedia postponed its Breathe Pakistan International Climate Change Conference, originally scheduled for April 22–23 in Islamabad, due to regional conflict and ongoing peace promotion efforts. The event has been rescheduled for May 6–7 at the Jinnah Convention Center.

stories.title: Thousands rally against Israeli government in Tel Aviv
stories.summary: Thousands of demonstrators gathered in Tel Aviv on Saturday night to protest against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government. Protesters demanded an investigation into the events of October 7 and criticized the government's impact on Israeli society and foreign relations.

stories.title: Carmakers scramble to plug £3bn shortfall for UK loan scandal payouts
stories.summary: Major carmakers including Ford, BMW, Stellantis, and Volkswagen face a £3 billion shortfall to cover payouts under the UK Financial Conduct Authority's £9.1 billion motor finance redress scheme launching this summer. Company filings suggest manufacturers' lending arms significantly underestimated the final compensation costs.

stories.title: MoD has lost track of veterans on recall list, says defence adviser
stories.summary: A key UK government defence adviser, George Robertson, revealed that the Ministry of Defence has lost track of military veterans on its recall list. Approximately 95,000 former soldiers and officers form Britain's strategic reserve, but officials have reportedly failed to maintain up-to-date contact records.

stories.title: Meet the Filipino vloggers finding financial freedom and defying stereotypes abroad
stories.summary: Filipino vlogger Lea Albritton, who moved from Leyte to Georgia in the US in 2019, has built an online following of 250,000 through videos about Filipino food, migration advice, and daily life. She balances content creation with running a recreational vehicle repair shop with her American husband.

stories.title: Chernihiv under massive drone attack, explosions reported in city
stories.summary: Chernihiv, Ukraine, came under a large-scale drone attack, with explosions heard across the city and multiple drone crashes reported in urban areas.

stories.title: Iran parliament speaker touts ‘progress’ in US talks, but Strait of Hormuz still shut
stories.summary: Iranian parliament speaker Ghalibaf reported some 'progress' in talks with the United States but said a 'big distance' remains and the sides are far from final discussions. The Strait of Hormuz remains closed. Separately, Trump praised Israel as a 'great ally.'

stories.title: IRGC says Hormuz 'fully closed' until US lifts blockade on Iranian ports
stories.summary: The IRGC navy announced it has fully closed the Strait of Hormuz, including a previously designated safe-passage corridor, until the US lifts its blockade on Iranian ports and ships. The declaration reverses earlier guidance that allowed coordinated vessel transit upon payment of fees.

stories.title: North Korea launches ballistic missiles toward sea
stories.summary: South Korea reported that North Korea launched multiple ballistic missiles toward the North's eastern waters, directed toward the sea.

stories.title: Bulgarians vote in high-stakes election
stories.summary: Bulgarian voters went to the polls for the eighth time in five years amid a protracted political crisis. A new left-leaning, pro-Russian party led by former President Rumen Radev is considered the frontrunner.

stories.title: North Korea fires short-range ballistic missiles in latest weapons tests
stories.summary: South Korea's military reported on Sunday that North Korea launched multiple short-range ballistic missiles, continuing a series of weapons tests that violate UN sanctions. The launches are the latest in an accelerating pattern of North Korean missile activity.

stories.title: LA port chief says fuel costs surge amid Iran conflict
stories.summary: Los Angeles port executive director Gene Seroka told CNN that the Iran conflict has doubled ship fuel costs, raising freight rates and consumer prices. He noted the six-week disruption has caused congestion at major Asian ports as Middle East-bound cargo stalls or is rerouted.

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Iran says ‘fundamental’ issues’ still to be resolved with US amid strait of Hormuz impasse
stories.summary: Iran's top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated on Saturday that talks with the United States had made some progress but significant gaps remain over nuclear issues and the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran closed the Strait of Hormuz again, demanding that Washington lift its naval blockade on Iranian ports before reopening the waterway.

stories.title: Sgt. First Class (res.) Lidor Porat killed in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: The IDF announced that Sgt. First Class (res.) Lidor Porat was killed during an incident in southern Lebanon. One other soldier was severely wounded, four were moderately wounded, and four sustained light injuries.

stories.title: Quirky China: doctor removes worm from woman’s brain, under-fire gamer dyes her skin black
stories.summary: Surgeons in Guangdong province, southern China, removed an 8-centimeter-long parasitic worm from a 61-year-old woman's brain after she experienced multiple unexplained health problems. Doctors believe the parasite may have originated from an incident in her youth.

stories.title: Talking to Lebanon: Peace, or a temporary respite from Hezbollah? - editorial
stories.summary: An editorial examined whether Israel's talks with Lebanon would lead to lasting peace or merely a temporary pause in hostilities with Hezbollah, arguing Israel should prioritize the safety of its northern residents.

stories.title: Israel carries out demolitions in south Lebanon, preparing for 'detonation options'
stories.summary: Israeli forces conducted demolitions in the southern Lebanese town of Bint Jbeil, approximately five kilometers from the border, according to Lebanese state media. The Israeli military separately reported eliminating a militant cell operating near its troops in southern Lebanon.

stories.title: Cash shortages grip Yemen despite currency stabilisation
stories.summary: Yemenis are experiencing severe cash shortages as exchange firms restrict currency conversion amid a continuing liquidity crisis, despite recent efforts at currency stabilisation.

stories.title: Iran closes Hormuz Strait again, as Trump warns against ‘blackmail’
stories.summary: Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz again amid escalating tensions, prompting US President Donald Trump to warn Tehran against "blackmail." Trump insisted that a US naval blockade of Iranian ports would continue until a deal was reached.

stories.title: Two US soldiers wounded in bear attack during training exercise in Alaska
stories.summary: Two US soldiers from the 11th Airborne Division were wounded in a bear attack during a land navigation training exercise near Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson in Alaska, according to the Anchorage Daily News.

stories.title: Lebanese Maronite party leader Geagea denounces Hezbollah as cause of violence, displacement
stories.summary: Lebanese Forces leader Samir Geagea denounced Hezbollah as a cause of violence and displacement in Lebanon. Meanwhile, Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem outlined five conditions his group requires for a ceasefire with Israel.

stories.title: Houthi official says Bab al-Mandeb may be closed
stories.summary: A senior Houthi official, deputy foreign minister Hussein al-Ezzi, warned that Yemen's Houthis could close the Bab al-Mandeb Strait if US President Donald Trump continues what he described as obstructing peace efforts.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces strike Russian TOS-1A Solntsepyok system in Zaporizhzhia region
stories.summary: Ukrainian defense forces struck a Russian TOS-1A Solntsepyok heavy flamethrower system in temporarily occupied parts of the Zaporizhzhia region of Ukraine.

stories.title: Australia's most-decorated soldier vows to fight war crime charges
stories.summary: Ben Roberts-Smith, Australia's most decorated living soldier, vowed to fight five war crime murder charges filed against him. It was his first public statement since being charged last week.

stories.title: Middle East war live: Iran reports 'progress' in US talks but final deal still far off
stories.summary: Iran's parliamentary speaker said Saturday that negotiations with the United States had advanced but remained far from a final agreement. Tehran announced the Strait of Hormuz would stay closed until Washington lifts its naval blockade on Iranian ports. The talks are focused on ending hostilities and resolving disputes over the strategic waterway.

stories.title: Israel’s UN ambassador questions France, China, Pakistan envoys on Hormuz
stories.summary: Israeli UN Ambassador Danny Danon said he asked diplomats from France, China, and Pakistan during a UN General Assembly session whether they had paid Iran for safe ship passage through the Strait of Hormuz. He said none of the ambassadors responded to the question.

stories.title: Iran fully closes Strait of Hormuz over U.S. blockade
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy fully closed the Strait of Hormuz in response to a US blockade, warning all vessels in the Persian Gulf and the Sea of Oman not to move from anchorage. Tehran stated that approaching the strait would be considered cooperation with the enemy.

stories.title: Tehran says new US proposals under review after Pakistan army commander's visit
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme National Security Council said US-Iran talks held in Islamabad, mediated by Pakistan, lasted 21 hours but ended without concrete results after Washington raised what Tehran called new and excessive demands. The council said talks may resume when US demands align with conditions on the ground.

stories.title: Ben Roberts-Smith denies war crimes allegations – As it happened
stories.summary: Former Australian soldier Ben Roberts-Smith denied war crimes allegations. Separately, Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles affirmed the US-Australia alliance's durability despite President Trump's criticism of Australia for not assisting in the war in Iran, noting no specific US request for assistance had been made.

stories.title: How a bear costume cost these luxury car insurance scamsters their freedom
stories.summary: Three people in California were sentenced for insurance fraud after staging fake bear attacks on luxury cars, including a Rolls-Royce and two Mercedes, using a person in a bear costume. They submitted fraudulent claims totaling nearly $142,000 in the scheme dubbed 'Operation Bear Claw.'

stories.title: Budanov: Russia's destruction of culture, memory, identity is another form of genocide
stories.summary: Ukrainian intelligence chief Kyrylo Budanov stated that Russia's systematic destruction of Ukrainian culture, memory, and identity constitutes another form of genocide and reflects Moscow's broader policy of intolerance toward Ukrainians.

stories.title: Iran says fighting could restart 'any moment', Israel on high alert
stories.summary: Iran's parliament speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said Tehran does not trust the United States and warned that fighting could resume at any moment. Israeli military and political sources told Israeli radio that the army has been placed on high alert over a possible collapse of the ceasefire.

stories.title: Iran reports 3,468 dead in war with US, Israel: Official
stories.summary: Iran's Martyrs and Veterans Foundation officially reported 3,468 people killed in the country's war with the United States and Israel.

stories.title: Iran-US talks deepened understanding but mistrust remains, parliament speaker Ghalibaf says
stories.summary: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said talks with the US deepened understanding but mistrust persists. He identified the Strait of Hormuz and nuclear issues as the main points of disagreement during negotiations.

stories.title: Iran plans gradual reopening of airspace, Tasnim reports
stories.summary: Iran announced a four-phase plan to gradually reopen its airspace, beginning with transit flights and progressing to domestic and international departures. The phased plan will eventually restore operations at Mehrabad Airport, Imam Khomeini International Airport, and other western airports, according to Tasnim News Agency.

stories.title: UAE minister labels Hormuz closure ‘economic terrorism’
stories.summary: A UAE minister called for the complete and unconditional reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, condemning its closure as economic terrorism. Saeed Bin Mubarak Al Hajeri said any resolution to the Iran conflict must address Tehran's nuclear capabilities, ballistic missiles, and regional threats.

stories.title: ‘No mood for work’: veteran ship mechanic’s future clouded by Aberdeen marina project
stories.summary: David Chan, a veteran ship machinery maintenance master in his seventies, faces an uncertain future as Hong Kong's Aberdeen Po Chong Wan temporary industrial area is affected by a planned marina development project. Chan has worked in the trade since the 1960s.

stories.title: BINI made history at Coachella. Can the Philippines build on it?
stories.summary: Filipino pop group BINI became the first P-pop act and the first Southeast Asian girl group to perform at the Coachella music festival in California, drawing enthusiastic crowds of fans waving Philippine flags at the Mojave Tent.

stories.title: China steps up aid to Africa but huge funding gap left by Trump’s cuts remains
stories.summary: During Vice-President Han Zheng's visit to Nairobi, China signed drought relief grants and delivered food aid to Somalia, Togo, Zimbabwe, and Zambia. Despite increased Chinese assistance, a significant funding gap remains in Africa following US aid cuts under President Trump.

stories.title: Video: Hezbollah official rejects Lebanon-Israel talks as 'submission'
stories.summary: Senior Hezbollah official Mahmud Qamati rejected planned direct talks between Lebanon and Israel, describing them as submission to Israeli desires. His comments highlight divisions within Lebanon, where the government pursues negotiations under international pressure while Hezbollah insists on operating independently.

stories.title: Kamala Harris says Trump put US troops at risk at Netanyahu’s urging
stories.summary: Former US Vice President Kamala Harris said President Donald Trump was pulled into a war at Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's urging, speaking at a Democratic Party fundraiser in Detroit. Netanyahu has previously rejected the claim, saying no one can tell Trump what to do.

stories.title: Hormuz closure deepens fuel crisis in South Asia
stories.summary: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz has worsened a fuel crisis in Bangladesh, which imports most of its energy. Long queues have formed at petrol stations, universities have shut, and authorities have cut working hours to conserve energy.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces strike two Msta-S self-propelled guns, two howitzers in Russia
stories.summary: Soldiers of Ukraine's 72nd Mechanized Brigade destroyed two Russian 2S19 Msta-S self-propelled artillery systems and two towed D-30 howitzers on Russian territory.

stories.title: Trump, Iran cite progress in talks amid uncertainty over Strait
stories.summary: Iran and the United States both cited progress in negotiations but remain divided on key issues, with the status of the Strait of Hormuz at the center of the dispute.

stories.title: Kamala Harris accuses Netanyahu of pulling Trump into Iran war
