stories.summary: Former Vice President Kamala Harris accused Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu of pulling President Trump into the Iran conflict during a speech at an event in Michigan. She also called the Trump administration the most corrupt in US history.

stories.title: Turkiye seeks to extend Iran gas deal, minister says
stories.summary: Turkish Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar said Ankara wants to extend a natural gas supply contract with Iran that is set to expire soon, but negotiations have not started due to the ongoing war. He said Turkey faces no immediate supply risks despite the conflict.

stories.title: Israeli settlers vandalise property, torch vehicle in West Bank village
stories.summary: Israeli settlers vandalized property, sprayed graffiti reading "Revenge," and set a vehicle on fire in the Palestinian village of Turmus Ayya near Ramallah in the West Bank. Settlers also attempted to establish an outpost in Area B near Khirbet Abu Falah.

stories.title: Trump calls Israel ‘great ally’ that ‘knows how to win’
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump praised Israel as a great ally on Truth Social, saying it "fights hard and knows how to WIN." The remarks came a day after Trump said Israel was prohibited from bombing Lebanon.

stories.title: US says over 12 warships enforcing blockade of Iranian ports
stories.summary: US Central Command said more than 12 warships and over 10,000 personnel are enforcing a blockade of Iran's ports. Officials reported that 23 Iranian-linked ships have been turned back through the Strait of Hormuz as part of the maritime interdiction operation.

stories.title: Israeli army carries out demolitions in south Lebanon town
stories.summary: Israeli forces carried out demolitions in the southern Lebanese town of Bint Jbeil as part of operations targeting border areas following the ceasefire with Hezbollah.

stories.title: Hezbollah leader rejects one-sided truce, signals response
stories.summary: Hezbollah Secretary-General Naim Qassem said any ceasefire with Israel must be mutual and warned that Hezbollah would respond to violations. He rejected what he characterized as a one-sided truce.

stories.title: ATESH agent cuts power to Russian supply railway hub in Luhansk
stories.summary: The partisan movement ATESH claimed responsibility for disabling a railway supply hub in Russian-occupied Luhansk, Ukraine, by cutting its power supply. The hub was reportedly used for Russian military logistics.

stories.title: France blames Hezbollah for French peacekeeper death in Lebanon
stories.summary: France demanded accountability after a French UNIFIL peacekeeper was killed in Lebanon, blaming Hezbollah for the incident. UNIFIL warned that the killing may constitute a war crime.

stories.title: North Korea fires suspected ballistic missiles, Japan says
stories.summary: North Korea fired suspected ballistic missiles, according to Japan. The launch marks North Korea's seventh ballistic missile test this year and its fourth in April alone.

stories.title: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson calls out EU on international law violation claims
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei responded to EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas's statement that the Strait of Hormuz must remain open under international law. Baghaei challenged the legal interpretation, pushing back against claims that Iran was violating international norms regarding transit through the waterway.

stories.title: Taiwan warned of widening ‘resilience gap’ in civil defences
stories.summary: Experts at a tabletop exercise held at National Chengchi University in Taipei warned that Taiwan faces a widening 'resilience gap' in civil defenses. They said Taiwan must overhaul its civil defense and energy strategy to withstand a potential blockade, calling current preparedness insufficient.

stories.title: Iran to prioritise ships paying 'costs of security' in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: A senior Iranian official told CNN that Iran will prioritize vessels that pay security fees for passage through the Strait of Hormuz. Ships that do not pay will have their transit postponed under reimposed restrictions on the waterway.

stories.title: Two water delivery contractors killed by Israeli forces in Gaza
stories.summary: UNICEF condemned the killing of two water delivery contractors by Israeli forces in the Gaza Strip. Israel said its troops opened fire after identifying a perceived threat.

stories.title: Iran reports 3,468 dead in war with US, Israel: official
stories.summary: Iran's Foundation of Martyrs and Veterans Affairs reported 3,468 deaths resulting from the war with the United States and Israel, as a fragile ceasefire remains in effect.

stories.title: School system to fully reopen across Israel starting Sunday, Education Ministry confirms
stories.summary: Israel's Education Ministry confirmed that the school system will fully reopen nationwide starting Sunday, including in northern communities. The decision follows updated security guidelines issued amid ceasefires with Lebanon and Iran.

stories.title: Iran's Quds Force chief Qaani visits Iraq: senior official
stories.summary: Iran's Quds Force commander Esmail Qaani visited Baghdad to hold talks on the Middle East war, with discussions focused on stabilizing security and easing political divisions in Iraq.

stories.title: Ghalibaf says others cannot pass Hormuz if Iran blocked, control rests with Tehran
stories.summary: Iran's parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said the Strait of Hormuz is under Iran's control and warned that if Iran is blocked from using it, others will not be allowed to pass either. He added that Iranian armed forces remain fully prepared for a possible resumption of hostilities.

stories.title: Russian Shahed drones equipped with SIM cards whose roaming blocked in Ukraine – 'Flash'
stories.summary: Russian Shahed-type drones deployed over Ukraine have been found equipped with SIM cards from the Russian mobile operator Tele2. Ukrainian sources report that roaming for these SIM cards has been blocked within Ukraine to disrupt drone communications.

stories.title: Arab, Muslim states condemn Israel's decision to send envoy to Somaliland
stories.summary: Several Arab and Muslim states condemned Israel's decision to send a diplomatic envoy to Somaliland. In response, the Republic of Somaliland accused the condemning nations of hypocrisy.

stories.title: Former President Radev's coalition leads in Bulgarian elections, exit polls show
stories.summary: Exit polls from Bulgaria's Sunday general election indicate that former president Rumen Radev's coalition leads with approximately 38 percent of the vote. The election followed unrest that unseated Boyko Borissov's government, leaving his pro-European GERB party behind in the results.

stories.title: AI is not eating up China’s software market but turbocharging it: HSBC analyst
stories.summary: An HSBC analyst said China's AI model companies are unlikely to displace the domestic software market because they lack deep industry expertise. Instead, a collaborative approach between AI firms and legacy software companies is the most likely outcome for serving enterprise needs.

stories.title: China martial arts prodigy, 5, often practises to point of tears is ready for May tournament
stories.summary: A five-year-old girl named Huang Zijun from Maoming, Guangdong province, China, has gained online attention for her skilled performances of Hung Kuen, a traditional southern Chinese martial art. She is preparing for a tournament in May.

stories.title: Europe’s far right rails at migration ‘tsunami’ after defeat of Hungary’s Orban
stories.summary: Supporters of the Patriots For Europe party, the third-largest bloc in the European Parliament, gathered at a rally in Milan. European far-right figures used the event to denounce migration, framing it as a "tsunami," following the electoral defeat of Hungary's Viktor Orbán.

stories.title: Iran says ‘major differences’ remain with US in talks
stories.summary: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that "major differences" persist between Iran and the United States despite some points of agreement in ongoing negotiations. He said Iran accepted a temporary ceasefire to allow the US to meet its demands and noted that Washington had begun communicating through intermediaries.

stories.title: Anti-Israel group files formal complaint against released IDF soldier in Sri Lanka
stories.summary: The Hind Rajab Foundation filed a formal complaint in Sri Lanka against a released US-Israeli IDF soldier, alleging he participated in war crimes while serving as a combat engineer in Gaza. The group said Sri Lanka has a duty to investigate and prosecute if necessary.

stories.title: Bahrain condemns Lebanon attack that killed French UN peacekeeper
stories.summary: Bahrain's Foreign Ministry condemned an attack in Lebanon that killed a French soldier serving with the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) and wounded three others. Bahrain described the incident as a "flagrant violation" of international law and expressed support for UNIFIL's peacekeeping mission and efforts to bring those responsible to justice.

stories.title: Kremlin creates illusion of international recognition of temporarily occupied territories through 'international' agreements – CCD
stories.summary: The head of Russia's occupation administration in Kherson, Volodymyr Saldo, signed a memorandum with North Korea's ambassador to Russia covering the supply of grain from temporarily occupied Ukrainian territories and "humanitarian contacts." Ukraine's Center for Countering Disinformation said the agreement aims to create an illusion of international recognition of the occupied regions.

stories.title: North Korea launches ballistic missiles towards sea off its east coast
stories.summary: North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles from the Sinpo area toward the sea off its east coast, marking the seventh such missile test this year.

stories.title: IDF reservist killed, nine others wounded by explosive in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: An IDF reservist, Sgt. First Class Lidor Porat, was killed and nine other soldiers were wounded by an explosive device in southern Lebanon during the ongoing ceasefire period.

stories.title: Sudan: Sudan - Three Quarters of Women Feel Unsafe As War Rages On
stories.summary: A senior UNFPA official reported that three-quarters of women in war-torn Sudan feel unsafe. Women and girls consistently report danger and risks of gender-based violence whether fleeing conflict or arriving at displacement camps.

stories.title: Africa: IGAD Envoy to Sudan - 'Quintet to Convene Meeting for Those Absent From Berlin Conf'
stories.summary: The IGAD envoy to Sudan announced that a 'quintet' group comprising the African Union, IGAD, the UN, the EU, and the League of Arab States plans to convene meetings next month for Sudanese parties absent from the Third International Conference on Sudan held in Berlin.

stories.title: South Sudan: 'Slaughtered Like Goats' - Despair and Abandonment in South Sudan
stories.summary: Senior UN officials told the Security Council that South Sudan faces political turmoil, rising violence, hunger, and disease. Budget cuts are limiting the UN peacekeeping mission's ability to protect civilians in the country.

stories.title: Libya: Joint Statement on Libya Unified Budget Agreement
stories.summary: The United States, Egypt, France, Germany, Italy, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, the UAE, and the United Kingdom issued a joint statement regarding an agreement on a unified budget for Libya.

stories.title: Congo-Kinshasa: Joint Statement on Progress Between DR Congo and AFC/M23 on the Ceasefire Meetings in Switzerland
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Alliance Fleuve Congo/M23 movement held ceasefire meetings from April 13 to 17 in Montreux, Switzerland. Qatar, the United States, Togo, the African Union Commission, and Switzerland participated in discussions on implementing the Doha peace framework.

stories.title: Over a thousand entertainment leaders sign letter supporting Israel’s Eurovision participation
stories.summary: Over 1,000 entertainment industry leaders signed a letter supporting Israel's participation in the Eurovision Song Contest. The signatories rejected boycott efforts, emphasizing music's role as a unifying force.

stories.title: At least 6 killed after gunman opens fire in Ukrainian capital
stories.summary: A gunman opened fire on a street in a southern residential district of Kyiv on Saturday, killing at least six people and injuring fourteen others. The attacker also took hostages inside a supermarket before being killed during an arrest attempt, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky.

stories.title: Singapore ranks No 1 for cyber defences but boardrooms are the weak link
stories.summary: Singapore ranked first overall for cyber defenses in the Asia-Pacific according to a study by Economist Impact and Telstra International. However, Singaporean executives ranked 10th out of 11 markets for leadership engagement on cybersecurity issues.

stories.title: China begins building US$1 billion hydropower station in Cambodia amid energy crisis
stories.summary: Construction has begun on a $1 billion Chinese-invested pumped-storage hydropower station in Cambodia's Koh Kong province. The Upper Tatay project aims to boost renewable energy capacity as the Iran war restricts developing countries' access to traditional fuel supplies.

stories.title: India ‘calls in’ Iranian envoy, conveys ‘deep concern’ after two oil tankers prevented from crossing Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs called in Iran's ambassador to convey deep concern after two oil tankers were prevented from transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The MEA described the diplomatic step as the envoy being "called in" rather than formally summoned.

stories.title: Iran war live: Tehran says no date set for US talks, Hormuz Strait closed
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps declared the Strait of Hormuz closed and stated it will remain shut until the United States ends its blockade of Iranian ports. Tehran also said no date has been set for further talks with Washington.

stories.title: 12 countries, including Pakistan, condemn Israel’s move to appoint envoy to Somaliland
stories.summary: Foreign ministers from twelve countries—including Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Somalia, Türkiye, and Indonesia—issued a joint statement condemning Israel's appointment of Michael Lotem as its first ambassador to Somaliland, Somalia's breakaway region.

stories.title: Ukraine says it hit three Russian warships in Crimea with drones
stories.summary: Ukraine claimed its drones struck three Russian warships in Crimea, including the landing ships Yamal and Azov. A third warship of unidentified type was also reportedly hit in the attack.

stories.title: 'I thought I might die': A Palestinian mother's account of Israeli detention
stories.summary: Palestinian mother Saeda al-Shrafi recounted her detention at an Israeli military checkpoint during mass displacement from northern Gaza in late 2023. She was held at Damon prison and was among hundreds of civilians stopped while moving south under Israeli military orders.

stories.title: Israeli army says soldier killed in southern Lebanon before ceasefire
stories.summary: The Israeli military confirmed that a soldier died from injuries sustained during fighting in southern Lebanon before the ceasefire took effect. The soldier was wounded on Friday in an incident that also injured three other troops. The army did not disclose further details about the circumstances.

stories.title: Thousands protest in Germany urging faster green shift, amid Iran war
stories.summary: Approximately 80,000 people protested across Germany demanding an accelerated transition to green energy. Demonstrators also expressed concerns about the ongoing Iran war and its broader geopolitical implications.

stories.title: War update: 135 clashes on front lines, Ukrainian forces repel 23 Russian attacks on Pokrovsk axis
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces engaged in 135 combat clashes with Russian forces on Saturday, with the heaviest fighting occurring along the Pokrovsk axis. Ukrainian troops repelled 23 Russian attacks on that front, inflicting over 90 casualties on Russian forces.

stories.title: Iran rejects EU call to keep Hormuz open
stories.summary: Iran rejected European Union calls to keep the Strait of Hormuz open, asserting its right to respond to military threats. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei responded on X to EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas, arguing that international law does not prohibit Iran from taking measures to prevent the strait from being used for military aggression against it.

stories.title: 'Die, Jews, Die!': NYC man sentenced to prison for antisemitic, anti-white assaults
stories.summary: A 42-year-old man named Skiboky Stora was sentenced to prison in New York City after being convicted of antisemitic and anti-white hate crime assaults. His convictions included two counts of hate crime assault in the third degree and hate crime stalking in the third degree.

stories.title: 'The weapons were loud, but there was always music': Sudanese band play on through the war
stories.summary: Sudanese band Aswat Almadina recalled being in the recording studio when the country's civil war erupted three years ago. Despite the ongoing conflict, the popular group has continued performing and making music.

stories.title: Gunman opens fire in Ukraine capital, killing at least 5
stories.summary: A gunman opened fire in Kyiv, killing at least five people before taking hostages at a supermarket. Police ultimately shot and killed the attacker during the standoff.

stories.title: SBU classifies Kyiv mass shooting as terrorist attack
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service (SBU) classified a mass shooting and hostage-taking incident in Kyiv's Holosiivskyi District as a terrorist attack. A pre-trial investigation is underway into the incident.

stories.title: Chernobyl's last wedding: The couple who married as a nuclear disaster unfolded
stories.summary: Serhiy and Iryna married in Pripyat 40 years ago, unaware that the Chernobyl nuclear reactor had exploded less than three miles from their wedding location.

stories.title: Eight India-bound ships return after attempting to cross Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Eight India-bound ships carrying energy cargo turned back after attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz. The Indian government coordinated with Iranian agencies and the Indian Navy to arrange repatriation of 22 earmarked vessels.

stories.title: Iran internet blackout now in its 50th day: NetBlocks
stories.summary: Iran's nationwide internet blackout has reached its 50th consecutive day, according to monitoring group NetBlocks. The shutdown had already become the longest on record as of April 5.

stories.title: US says Iran retains 40 percent of its attack drone arsenal
stories.summary: US military officials estimate that Iran retains approximately 40 percent of its attack drone arsenal despite recent strikes. The assessment, reported by The New York Times, indicates Tehran still holds significant unmanned aerial combat capabilities amid the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Two water delivery contractors killed by Israeli forces in Gaza, UN says
stories.summary: The United Nations reported that Israeli forces killed two water delivery contractors in northern Gaza after they approached the ceasefire line. The Israeli military said troops opened fire on what it described as "armed terrorists." Two other people were killed in separate incidents after crossing the Yellow Line.

stories.title: Ukraine urges US to reinstate sanctions on Russian oil – Stefanishyna
stories.summary: Ukrainian Deputy Prime Minister Olha Stefanishyna called on the United States to reinstate sanctions restricting trade in Russian oil, aiming to increase economic pressure on Moscow.

stories.title: Trump vs Pope | Two Americans, two paths
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV, the 70-year-old leader of 1.4 billion Catholics, publicly criticized U.S. President Donald Trump over the American-Israeli military campaign against Iran. The pontiff called for collective responsibility for peace, describing the world as being ravaged by tyrants.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz traffic falls to single digits as security fears keep ships stuck
stories.summary: Maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has dropped to single-digit vessel transits amid ongoing security concerns. Despite a ceasefire reducing the risk of direct escalation, experts say maritime security fears—not infrastructure gaps—are keeping ships from moving.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian in Gaza, wound others across territories
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed a young Palestinian man named Youssef Hassan northwest of Rafah in southern Gaza. He was taken to Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, where he was pronounced dead. Separately, a child was wounded by Israeli fire in the Mawasi area of Rafah, and 25-year-old Ahmed Hani Obeid died from earlier injuries.

stories.title: Israel military says suspected militant killed in West Bank
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced it killed a suspected militant who had entered the settlement of Negohot in the occupied West Bank. The military described the individual as a "terrorist" who infiltrated the community.

stories.title: Turkiye says Israel using security as a pretext to acquire 'more land'
stories.summary: Turkey accused Israel of using security concerns as a pretext to acquire more territory. The two countries have been exchanging daily diplomatic criticisms over conflicts including Israel's war in Gaza and tensions linked to Iran.

stories.title: Zelensky: Multiple versions under investigation in Kyiv shooting
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said investigators are examining multiple theories regarding the April 18 shooting in Kyiv that killed six people and injured 14. Authorities are working to establish all details about the gunman.

stories.title: Lebanon President, PM discuss readiness for Israel talks
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Prime Minister Nawaf Salam discussed their country's readiness for potential negotiations with Israel. Iran-backed Hezbollah and its supporters remain strongly opposed to any such talks.

stories.title: Israel army says established 'Yellow Line' in Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced it established a "Yellow Line" in Lebanon and conducted operations against what it described as threats in several areas. The military stated it was authorized to act against identified threats in the region.

stories.title: UK's Kensington Gardens reopens after police find no hazardous material near London Israeli embassy
stories.summary: London's Kensington Gardens reopened after police found no hazardous material near the Israeli embassy. Counter-terrorism police confirmed the embassy was not attacked and said they continue to work closely with embassy security.

stories.title: New Delhi summons Iranian envoy after Indian-flagged tankers shot at near Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: India summoned Iranian Ambassador Mohammad Fathali after two Indian-flagged vessels were fired upon near the Strait of Hormuz. India's foreign secretary conveyed New Delhi's "deep concern" over the shooting incident during the meeting.

stories.title: From grief to hope: Can Israel live together amid division? - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece reflects on internal divisions in Israeli society, asking whether the country can bridge divides as it moves between periods of grief and celebration. The author emphasizes unity and mutual respect amid ongoing disagreement.

stories.title: UN condemns attack that killed French UNIFIL peacekeeper in Lebanon
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned an attack in southern Lebanon that killed a French peacekeeper serving with UNIFIL and wounded three other soldiers. An initial UNIFIL assessment indicated the troops came under fire from non-state actors. Guterres called for restraint and accountability.

stories.title: SBP says govt has paid $2bn to UAE
stories.summary: Pakistan's State Bank of Pakistan confirmed the government has repaid $2 billion to the United Arab Emirates, part of a $3.5 billion debt stemming from 2019 balance-of-payments support. An additional $500 million had already been paid, with the remainder due by April 23. The large outflow threatens Pakistan's foreign exchange reserves.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces thwart Russian breakthrough attempt near Chasiv Yar
stories.summary: Ukraine's defense forces repelled a large-scale Russian attempt to break through near Chasiv Yar in the Donetsk region. The engagement thwarted a significant Russian offensive push in the area.

stories.title: Settlers reportedly beat Palestinian woman, raid several West Bank towns
stories.summary: Israeli settlers reportedly beat a Palestinian woman in the West Bank, and she was evacuated for medical treatment. Her sons were reportedly detained by the IDF. The town of Turmus Ayya, home to a large population of Palestinian Americans, was raided twice in one day with no arrests reported.

stories.title: The fog of Israel’s forever war: IDF's Lebanon strategy stuck in endless containment - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that the IDF's Lebanon strategy remains stuck in a cycle of endless containment. The author contends that the October 7 attack shattered the assumption that Iranian-backed proxies could be managed indefinitely along Israel's borders.

stories.title: Iran reasserts control of Hormuz Strait as Trump warns against ‘blackmail’
stories.summary: Iran's top negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf reasserted Tehran's control over the Strait of Hormuz, calling the US naval blockade of Iranian ports "a clumsy and ignorant decision." The statement came as US President Donald Trump warned Iran against using the strategic waterway as leverage.

stories.title: Russia Urges HIV Testing for One-Third of Population as Cases Rise
stories.summary: Russia is urging HIV testing for one-third of its population as infection rates continue to rise. The country faces one of the highest HIV prevalence rates in Europe despite record screening levels.

stories.title: Command Sgt.-Maj. (Res.) Barak Kalfon killed in southern Lebanon, IDF announces
stories.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces announced that Command Sgt.-Maj. (Res.) Barak Kalfon, 48, of the 226th Brigade from Adi, was killed during combat in southern Lebanon on Friday.

stories.title: ‘We won’t let them forget’: Tel Aviv protest demands Oct. 7 inquiry ahead of Memorial Day
stories.summary: Protesters gathered in Tel Aviv ahead of Memorial Day to demand an official inquiry into the October 7 attack. Ofri Bibas, a relative of victims, vowed that Prime Minister Netanyahu would not evade accountability. Bereaved families accused the government of wanting them to move on.

stories.title: Mexico's Sheinbaum denies 'diplomatic crisis' with Spain after conquest row
stories.summary: Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum denied a diplomatic crisis with Spain over the legacy of Spanish colonization. Sheinbaum stated there were never tensions between the two countries on the issue, which had been a recurring point of contention.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz: Open, closed, open, closed - What's actually happening?
stories.summary: Iran reopened the Strait of Hormuz on Friday for commercial vessels but then closed it again, accusing the United States of "piracy." Tehran warned that any ship approaching the strait would be targeted until the US blockade ends, deepening confusion over the waterway's status.

stories.title: Four injured in Russian attacks in Sumy region
stories.summary: Four civilians were injured in Russian attacks on the Sumy region on April 18, according to regional governor Oleh Hryhorov.

stories.title: Iran ‘reviewing new proposals’ put forward by U.S.;  Trump says cannot ‘blackmail’ with Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme National Security Council said it is reviewing new US proposals delivered by Pakistani army chief Asim Munir during a recent visit to Tehran. President Trump warned Iran it cannot use the Strait of Hormuz as blackmail leverage in negotiations.

stories.title: Iran says nearly 3,500 killed in war with US and Israel
stories.summary: Iran's Martyrs and Veterans Foundation reported that 3,468 people were killed during the country's recent war with the United States and Israel, which began on 28 February. The foundation's head, Ahmad Mousavi, confirmed the figure as cited by Iran's ISNA news agency.

stories.title: Thirteen US troops killed, nearly four hundred wounded in Iran war, CENTCOM says
stories.summary: US Central Command reported that 13 American troops have been killed and nearly 400 wounded in the war with Iran. CENTCOM spokesperson Tim Hawkins said 354 of those wounded have returned to duty, while US-Iran talks in Pakistan have not produced a long-term agreement.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz closed again, Iran says, as ships attacked
stories.summary: Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz again and attacked ships in the waterway. Tehran blamed a US blockade for its actions, claiming the blockade violated a ceasefire agreement reached between the two countries.

stories.title: Venezuela’s Machado says in close talks with US over her return
stories.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado said she is in close communication with the United States regarding her return to Venezuela. She expressed trust in the phased process Washington is pursuing in the country.

stories.title: Mob torches water tanker after it runs over, kills motorcyclist in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar
stories.summary: In Karachi's Gulistan-i-Jauhar neighborhood, an angry mob set a water tanker ablaze after its driver ran over and killed a 40-year-old motorcyclist in Block-18. The driver fled the scene, and police are investigating the incident.

stories.title: Manchester United beat Chelsea as Cunha strike boosts Champions League hope
stories.summary: Manchester United defeated Chelsea 1-0 in the Premier League, strengthening their hold on third place. The result leaves Chelsea needing other results to go their way in the Champions League qualification race.

stories.title: Iran military orders Indian ship to abort Strait of Hormuz passage
stories.summary: Iran's military ordered an Indian commercial ship to abort its passage through the Strait of Hormuz. Video footage captured the moment Iranian forces issued the directive to the vessel.

stories.title: Israel says established a ‘yellow line’ in Lebanon, as it has in Gaza
stories.summary: Israel announced it has established a 'yellow line' in Lebanon, marking the first time it has used such a designation there. The measure mirrors a similar boundary Israel previously imposed in Gaza.

stories.title: No date set for next round of Iran-US talks: Iran deputy foreign minister
stories.summary: Iran's deputy foreign minister confirmed that no date has been set for the next round of Iran-U.S. talks. Both sides remain focused on finalizing a framework of understanding before scheduling further negotiations.

stories.title: Venezuela's Machado says Spanish PM's leftist summit reason for not meeting him
stories.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado said she declined a meeting with Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez during her visit to Spain because he was hosting a summit of progressive leaders in Barcelona.

stories.title: Five injured in Russian attacks across Dnipropetrovsk region
stories.summary: Five civilians were injured by Russian strikes across the Dnipropetrovsk region on Saturday, according to regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha.

stories.title: French soldier killed in attack on UN mission in southern Lebanon, officials say
stories.summary: A French soldier serving with the UN peacekeeping mission UNIFIL was killed in an attack in southern Lebanon. UNIFIL described the incident as a deliberate attack, and an investigation has been launched.

stories.title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1515: Ukraine knocks out 880,000 barrels of Russian oil in day, while Washington eases sanctions for fourth time
stories.summary: On day 1,515 of the Russo-Ukrainian war, Ukraine struck Russian oil infrastructure, knocking out an estimated 880,000 barrels of oil production in a single day. Meanwhile, Washington eased sanctions on Russia for a fourth time, and Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha met with Moldovan President Maia Sandu.

stories.title: French UNIFIL soldier killed in Lebanon, Hezbollah responsible, says Macron
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron announced that a French UN peacekeeper was killed in an attack in southern Lebanon that also wounded three others. Macron said evidence pointed to Hezbollah being responsible, though the Iran-backed group denied involvement.

stories.title: Lebanon president, PM discuss readiness for Israel talks
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and the prime minister discussed readiness for potential negotiations with Israel. Aoun signaled a "new phase" in relations amid Hezbollah backlash and a fragile ceasefire following the deadly conflict.

stories.title: Israeli army says at least 14 soldiers killed in Lebanon war
stories.summary: The Israeli military confirmed that at least 14 of its soldiers have been killed since fighting began in Lebanon on March 2. More than 650 troops have also been wounded during the conflict.

stories.title: Israel projects strength abroad but struggles to protect its citizens at home - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece contends that while Israel projects military strength in conflicts abroad, it struggles with clarity and consistency in the West Bank, where civilians continue to face terrorism.

stories.title: Netanyahu shocked Trump 'prohibited' strikes on Lebanon, believes it inconsistent with ceasefire
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was reportedly surprised that President Trump publicly prohibited strikes on Lebanon, viewing the remarks as inconsistent with the US-backed ceasefire terms. Israeli officials sought clarification while clashes on the ground continued.

stories.title: Some tankers cross Strait of Hormuz before shots fired, ship-tracking data shows
stories.summary: Ship-tracking data showed some tankers managed to cross the Strait of Hormuz before shots were fired at vessels in the waterway. Iran had reimposed restrictions on passage through the strait on April 18.

stories.title: Ukraine cut Russia’s oil exports by 880,000 barrels in one day — that’s $100 million every 24 hours
stories.summary: Ukrainian strikes disrupted approximately 880,000 barrels of Russian oil exports in a single day, representing an estimated $100 million daily loss. Russia reportedly attempted to reroute oil shipments from the Sheskharis terminal to Tuapse in response.

stories.title: At Least 5 Killed After Gunman Opens Fire in Ukrainian Capital
stories.summary: At least five people were killed and 10 hospitalized after a gunman opened fire in a residential district of Kyiv, the Ukrainian capital.

stories.title: Israel army says established ‘Yellow Line’ in Lebanon, as in Gaza
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced it has established a so-called Yellow Line in Lebanon, similar to a boundary it created in Gaza. The army said it had already struck suspected militants who approached its troops along the line.

stories.title: Death toll in Kyiv shooting rises to six – mayor
stories.summary: The death toll from a mass shooting in Kyiv's Holosiivskyi district rose to six, according to Mayor Vitali Klitschko. The incident took place in a residential area of the Ukrainian capital.

stories.title: United plane makes emergency landing in Pittsburgh over ‘possible security issue’
stories.summary: A United Airlines flight from Chicago to New York made an emergency landing at Pittsburgh International Airport after crew reported a possible security issue. Passengers evacuated via emergency slides, and FBI agents, bomb technicians, and a K-9 unit responded to the scene.

stories.title: Israel probes soldiers over suspected links to Iran
stories.summary: Israel's Shin Bet internal security agency and police are investigating a suspected espionage network involving Israeli military personnel. Investigators believe some soldiers may have leaked sensitive information about military infrastructure to Iranian-linked actors.

stories.title: Bushra Bibi moves IHC seeking to suspend sentence in £190m corruption case on medical grounds
stories.summary: Bushra Bibi, wife of former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan, petitioned the Islamabad High Court to suspend her seven-year sentence in a £190 million corruption case on medical grounds. The case involves allegations of undue favors to property tycoon Malik Riaz regarding laundered money from the United Kingdom.

stories.title: IDF reservist killed by Hezbollah explosive in Lebanon amid truce, 3 troops hurt
stories.summary: IDF reservist Barak Kalfon, 48, was killed by a Hezbollah explosive device in southern Lebanon despite the ongoing truce. Three other Israeli troops were wounded. An initial IDF investigation found the bomb was not remotely detonated.

stories.title: Investigators examine whether Ukraine terrorist attack was directed by Russia
stories.summary: Ukrainian investigators are examining whether a terrorist attack in Kyiv was directed by Russia. A 58-year-old Ukrainian citizen born in Moscow killed six people by shooting passersby before barricading himself in a supermarket and taking hostages. Police killed the gunman after a 40-minute standoff in the Holosiivskyi district.

stories.title: Russian drone strikes train in Sumy region, driver injured
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a train in Ukraine's Sumy region, injuring the driver. The attack is part of ongoing Russian drone operations targeting Ukrainian infrastructure.

stories.title: UK, Netherlands, and Belgium just handed Ukraine core of future Black Sea demining fleet
stories.summary: The United Kingdom, the Netherlands, and Belgium provided Ukraine with vessels forming the core of a future Black Sea demining fleet. Ukrainian crews have already contributed to NATO's operational manual on demining in the Black Sea.

stories.title: Iran warns ships near Hormuz will be treated as targets
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned that any vessel approaching the Strait of Hormuz would be treated as hostile. The naval arm of the Guards stated that no ship should leave anchorage in the Persian Gulf or Sea of Oman, threatening to target any vessel that approaches the strait.

stories.title: Venezuela’s Machado says ‘no regrets’ about giving her Nobel Prize to Trump
stories.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado stated she has no regrets about symbolically giving her Nobel Peace Prize to US President Donald Trump. Speaking at a news conference in Madrid, she praised Trump for risking action on behalf of Venezuela's freedom.

stories.title: Iran's navy tells ships Strait of Hormuz shut again, two vessels report gunfire
stories.summary: Merchant vessels attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday received radio warnings from Iran's navy that passage was prohibited. Two ships reported being struck by gunfire, according to shipping sources in Athens.

stories.title: Will Keir Starmer resign?
stories.summary: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer faced questions over whether he would resign after it emerged that Peter Mandelson had failed a security clearance. Starmer stated he was unaware of the clearance failure.

stories.title: What is inside Ukraine’s new defense AI hub that will predict Russian moves?
stories.summary: Ukraine is building a new defense AI hub designed to analyze battlefield data and predict Russian military movements. The initiative aims to leverage artificial intelligence for strategic advantage in the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Iran says US backed down after Strait of Hormuz minesweeper threat
stories.summary: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf declared that the Strait of Hormuz is under Tehran's control and warned the United States against escalation. He said Iranian forces viewed US mine-clearing efforts in the waterway as a breach of the ceasefire.

stories.title: US planning to seize Iran-linked ships in coming days, WSJ says - report
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that the US is planning to seize Iran-linked ships in the coming days. The potential military action follows Iran's tightening grip on the Strait of Hormuz, including attacks on several vessels on Saturday.

stories.title: Iran says no date set for next round of negotiations with US
stories.summary: Iran's deputy foreign minister stated in Antalya, Turkey, that no date has been set for further negotiations with the United States. He said a framework of understanding must first be agreed upon before talks can resume.

stories.title: Pentagon kills Patriot’s next-gen interceptor worth only $8 million in funding
stories.summary: The Pentagon canceled funding for the Patriot system's next-generation interceptor, which had received only $8 million in funding. The decision raises questions about the future of US missile defense development.

stories.title: After BBC exposé, ex-SAPM on health voices alarm at uptick in HIV cases in Pakistan
stories.summary: Former Pakistani health adviser Dr. Zafar Mirza raised alarm over rising HIV cases in Pakistan following a BBC investigation uncovering infections in Taunsa. He cited reuse of contaminated syringes and inadequate blood screening as major contributors to the disease's spread.

stories.title: Kensington Gardens reopen after police deem suspicious items non-hazardous
stories.summary: London's Kensington Gardens reopened after police determined that suspicious items found near the Israeli embassy, including two jars of powdered substance, were non-hazardous. Counter-terrorism officers had investigated after a video was shared online claiming a group targeted the embassy with drones carrying dangerous substances.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV downplays feud with Trump: ‘Not in my interest’ to debate him
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV addressed his public disagreements with US President Donald Trump, stating it is not in his interest to engage in a debate. The pope insisted his criticism was not directed solely at Trump and dismissed media framing as inaccurate.

stories.title: US envoy argues Israeli policy on Syria and Turkey strategically counter-productive
stories.summary: US special envoy Tom Barrack, also ambassador to Turkey, argued that Israeli policy toward Syria and Turkey is strategically counter-productive. Barrack said Ankara plays a constructive role regarding Gaza and praised Syrian restraint in response to repeated IDF incursions.

stories.title: Mazzucato on the Iran war’s economic shock: Who pays the price?
stories.summary: Economist Mariana Mazzucato discussed the economic fallout of the war involving Iran in an interview with Redi Tlhabi, focusing on who bears the financial burden of the conflict.

stories.title: Ukraine orders 25,000 ground robots — more than double last year’s total
stories.summary: Ukraine has ordered 25,000 ground robots, more than doubling last year's total. The country's military robotics industry has grown rapidly since 2022.

stories.title: Iran reimposes control over Strait of Hormuz as ships report gunfire
stories.summary: Several oil and gas tankers briefly crossed the Strait of Hormuz during a temporary reopening, but Iran re-closed the route and two vessels were reportedly attacked. Iran reversed its ceasefire pledge to reopen the strait in protest of an ongoing US counter-blockade.

stories.title: Defense Forces strike Russian Solntsepyok MRLS in Zaporizhzhia
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces struck a Russian TOS-1A Solntsepyok heavy flamethrower multiple rocket launcher system in the temporarily occupied territory of Zaporizhzhia region.

stories.title: British counter-terrorism police investigating London arson attack
stories.summary: British counter-terrorism police launched an investigation into an arson attack that occurred Friday night in a London area with a significant Jewish community.

stories.title: Israel establishes ‘Yellow Line’ in Lebanon, strikes targets despite ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel announced the establishment of a "Yellow Line" occupation boundary in southern Lebanon, similar to one used in Gaza, marking areas where Israeli troops are operating. The Israeli military claims it retains the right to strike targets it deems threats despite the truce.

stories.title: Mexico arrests suspected Hungarian drug trafficker amid crime crackdown
stories.summary: Mexican authorities arrested Janos Balla, a 48-year-old Hungarian national suspected of drug trafficking, in the state of Quintana Roo. The arrest is part of President Claudia Sheinbaum's broader crackdown on cartel-related crime.

stories.title: Israel military says suspected militant killed in West Bank
stories.summary: The Israeli military reported that a suspected militant was killed in the West Bank. The Ramallah-based Palestinian health ministry identified the victim as 25-year-old Muhammad Ahmad Suwaiti.

stories.title: Military intelligence conducts series of raids, clears Russian positions in Zaporizhzhia region
stories.summary: Fighters from Ukraine's military intelligence (HUR) conducted a series of raids in the Zaporizhzhia direction, destroying and clearing Russian military positions in the temporarily occupied territory.

stories.title: Amid Israel's 'forever wars', Palestinians must not abandon the one-state solution
stories.summary: Since the October 2025 ceasefire between Hamas and Israel—reportedly violated more than 2,000 times—and the US-Israel war on Iran launched February 28, global attention has shifted away from the Palestinian cause. Israel launched a major wave of strikes coinciding with the US-Iran truce announced April 8.

stories.title: US Treasury goes after Iranian-backed militias in Iraq
stories.summary: The US Treasury Department targeted Iranian-backed militias operating in Iraq with new measures. The State Department's Rewards for Justice program also announced a $10 million reward for information on Ahmad al-Hamidawi, leader of the militia Kataib Hezbollah.

stories.title: From Erez to Jabaliya: A look inside of the IDF's new Gaza security zone
stories.summary: The IDF has established a new security zone in Gaza stretching from the Erez crossing to Jabaliya. The zone already features concrete fortifications, military positions, tunnel detection systems, cameras, and infrastructure for reserve soldiers.

stories.title: No date set for next round of Iran-U.S. talks: Iran Deputy Foreign Minister
stories.summary: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh stated that no date has been scheduled for the next round of Iran-U.S. negotiations. He said both sides are focused on finalizing a framework of understanding before proceeding further.

stories.title: Sudanese refugees trapped between borders and bureaucracy in Morocco
stories.summary: A growing number of Sudanese refugees fleeing the ongoing war in Sudan are arriving in Morocco but face significant obstacles related to border restrictions and bureaucratic hurdles that leave them stranded.

stories.title: Iran's 'valiant navy' ready to inflict 'new bitter defeats' on its enemies: Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei
stories.summary: Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei declared that Iran's navy stands ready to inflict defeats on its adversaries. The statement coincided with Iran reimposing restrictions on the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Two US army soldiers injured by brown bear during training exercise in Alaska
stories.summary: Two U.S. Army soldiers were injured by a brown bear during a land navigation training exercise in Arctic Valley, part of Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson's training area in Anchorage, Alaska. The military described the encounter on Thursday as a defensive attack by the bear.

stories.title: Starmer would have blocked Mandelson role over vetting failure, says Lammy
stories.summary: UK Deputy Prime Minister David Lammy stated that Prime Minister Keir Starmer would have blocked Peter Mandelson's appointment as ambassador to Washington had he known Mandelson failed security vetting. Lammy called it "inexplicable" that former top civil servant Oliver Robbins kept Downing Street uninformed about the vetting outcome.

stories.title: Two Indian ships reverse course in Hormuz strait, says vessel tracker
stories.summary: Two Indian ships reversed course in the Strait of Hormuz after Iran reimposed transit restrictions on the waterway. Iran said the closure was in response to a U.S. blockade on Iranian shipping and ports.

stories.title: War update: 54 combat engagements since morning, heaviest fighting continues in Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors
stories.summary: Russian forces launched 54 attacks on Ukrainian defense positions since the morning, with the heaviest fighting concentrated in the Pokrovsk and Kostiantynivka sectors. High activity was also reported in the Huliaipole sector.

stories.title: US strikes on alleged 'drug boats' spark legal controversy
stories.summary: The US military carried out additional strikes on vessels alleged to be carrying drugs. Critics argue the attacks are largely ineffective and primarily aimed at bolstering President Trump's domestic political standing, raising legal questions about the operations.

stories.title: US strikes on drug boats spark legal controversy
stories.summary: The United States has conducted additional strikes on suspected drug trafficking boats. Critics argue the attacks are largely ineffective and are primarily aimed at bolstering President Trump's domestic political standing.

stories.title: Canadian man Kenneth Law to plead guilty in suicide kit case to avoid murder trial
stories.summary: Kenneth Law, a 60-year-old Canadian man accused of helping 14 people in Ontario kill themselves by selling a legal but deadly substance online, will plead guilty to lesser charges of counselling or aiding suicide. Under a deal with prosecutors, first-degree murder charges will be withdrawn.

stories.title: Venezuela’s Machado says has ‘no regrets’ about gifting Nobel Peace Prize to Trump
stories.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado said she had no regrets about symbolically giving her Nobel Peace Prize to US President Trump. She praised Trump for risking action on Venezuela's behalf, referencing the US operation to seize Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro.

stories.title: Shooting in Kyiv leaves several killed, child among injured — mayor
stories.summary: A mass shooting in Kyiv left several people dead and a child among the injured, according to Mayor Vitali Klitschko. The incident occurred in a residential district of the Ukrainian capital.

stories.title: At least six killed in Kyiv as gunman opens fire and takes hostages
stories.summary: A gunman opened fire and took hostages inside a supermarket in Kyiv, killing at least six people. The attacker was shot and killed by police after a standoff.

stories.title: Unicef halts Gaza operations after Israeli attack kills drivers
stories.summary: UNICEF suspended operations in northern Gaza after Israeli forces killed two contracted truck drivers at the Mansoura water filling point in Gaza City, which supplies clean water to hundreds of thousands of residents via the Mekorot pipeline. Two other people were injured in the strike.

stories.title: Trump: Iran ‘got a little cute’ by blocking Hormuz again, but talks going ‘really well’
stories.summary: President Trump said Iran "got a little cute" by blocking the Strait of Hormuz again but claimed negotiations are going well. Iran's security council said it would hold the strait until the war fully ends, while Egypt and Pakistan are reportedly working toward a final US-Iran agreement.

stories.title: Gaza: Shortages of flour, fuel raise alarm over looming famine
stories.summary: Aid restrictions have worsened conditions in Gaza, with shortages of flour and fuel raising alarm about a looming famine. Local markets are running dry as humanitarian access remains severely limited.

stories.title: Ukraine police shoot dead gunman who killed six in Kyiv, took hostages
stories.summary: Ukrainian police in Kyiv shot and killed a gunman who had killed six people and taken hostages. Authorities identified the attacker as a 58-year-old man from Moscow, though no motive has been established.

stories.title: Lebanon condemns attack on Unifil forces, vows accountability
stories.summary: Lebanon's Foreign Ministry condemned an attack targeting the French contingent of UNIFIL in southern Lebanon. Officials described the assault as unacceptable and pledged to pursue those responsible while reaffirming commitments to protect international peacekeeping forces.

stories.title: Choosing not to be a peace-broker
stories.summary: An analysis discussed how India has chosen 'strategic silence' regarding the US-Israel war against Iran, declining to act as a peace-broker despite its size and political clout. Pakistan, Egypt, and Turkey have played active roles in de-escalation efforts.

stories.title: London Mayor Sadiq Khan urged to intervene in Nakba march ban
stories.summary: Pro-Palestine groups urged London Mayor Sadiq Khan to intervene after Metropolitan Police blocked a planned Nakba commemoration march route while approving a far-right rally in central London.

stories.title: Ukraine cannot rely solely on US aid – Pentagon
stories.summary: Pentagon policy official Elbridge Colby stated that future military support for Ukraine cannot depend solely on the US Department of Defense, increasing pressure on European allies to assume a larger share of the burden.

stories.title: ‘Test tube orgy’: Israeli scientists use yeast to assess humans’ mating preferences
stories.summary: Researchers at Israel's Weizmann Institute used yeast organisms to study human mating preferences. They found that yeast offspring from preferred partners were fitter than those from random pairings, suggesting humans choose mates likely to produce healthier offspring.

stories.title: Iran attacks ships, asserting control of Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched strikes on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, asserting control over the strategic waterway. The action came as US President Trump refused to lift a blockade on Iranian ports.

stories.title: UNIFIL: Why are UN peacekeepers in Lebanon?
stories.summary: A French UN peacekeeper was killed in Lebanon, highlighting growing risks for the UNIFIL peacekeeping mission. The UN force has operated in southern Lebanon for nearly 50 years and faces increasing scrutiny over its mandate and effectiveness.

stories.title: Iran closes Hormuz Strait again over US blockade, ships reverse course
stories.summary: Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz again after briefly reopening it, citing the continuation of the U.S. blockade. The repeated reversals raised doubts about the proximity of a peace deal to end the conflict.

stories.title: Israel uses Gaza tactics in Lebanon, establishes ‘Yellow Line'
stories.summary: The Israeli military has established a so-called "Yellow Line" in Lebanon and continued demolishing infrastructure within it. The army warned it would target anyone approaching the zone, employing tactics similar to those used in Gaza.

stories.title: Karachi policeman dies after being hit by alleged smugglers’ vehicle during checking
stories.summary: A policeman in Karachi was killed after being struck by a vehicle driven by alleged smugglers in Gulshan-i-Maymar. Constable Abdul Manan, 36, was hit when suspects refused to stop for a routine check and accelerated into him.

stories.title: Russia launches missile strike on central Kharkiv
stories.summary: Russian forces carried out a missile strike on central Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city, continuing a pattern of attacks on urban areas.

stories.title: NATO加盟国の大使ら日本訪問 「異例」の規模で日米連携を視察
stories.summary: Ambassadors from NATO member states visited Japan in an unusually large delegation to observe U.S.-Japan security cooperation. The visit came amid U.S. President Trump's expressions of dissatisfaction with NATO.

stories.title: Iran’s IRGC seems to be fighting Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi
stories.summary: Iran's IRGC appears to be publicly clashing with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. The IRGC-linked Tasnim news agency posted on X criticizing Araghchi's remarks about reopening the Strait of Hormuz as a "bad and incomplete tweet" that created "incorrect ambiguity."

stories.title: Flight cancellations in Europe possible as early as next month due to jet fuel shortages — IATA chief
stories.summary: IATA chief Willie Walsh warned that flight cancellations across Europe could begin as early as next month due to jet fuel shortages linked to the Middle East conflict. He urged European countries to develop coordinated contingency plans.

stories.title: UK’s Cooper urges full resumption of shipping through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper, speaking in Antalya, urged Iran to allow full resumption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. She noted operations had not returned to normal despite the ceasefire in the Iran war.

stories.title: 'Kinetic elimination does not work': US envoy breaks with Netanyahu doctrine in Antalya
stories.summary: US envoy Thomas Barrack, speaking in Antalya, Turkey, stated that "kinetic elimination does not work," breaking with Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu's doctrine. Barrack argued that regional conflicts cannot be solved by destroying enemies one by one through military force.

stories.title: Gaza genocide death toll reaches 72,549
stories.summary: Medical officials in Gaza report that 72,549 Palestinians have been killed and 172,274 wounded since October 7, 2023. Hospitals recorded eight deaths in the past 24 hours. Officials say 773 people have been killed since a ceasefire was signed in October of last year.

stories.title: Iranian gunboats fire on tanker in Strait of Hormuz, British military says
stories.summary: The UK Maritime Trade Operations center reported that Iranian gunboats fired on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz. The tanker and its crew were reported safe following the incident.

stories.title: Australia, Japan sign contracts to start $7 billion warship deal
stories.summary: Australia and Japan signed contracts for a warship deal valued at approximately $7 billion. The agreement supports Japan's shift away from postwar pacifism and aims to strengthen security ties beyond the U.S. alliance to counter China.

stories.title: Enemy drones strike Kharkiv: Market, industrial zone were hit
stories.summary: Hostile combat drones struck Kharkiv, Ukraine, hitting a market and an industrial zone. Impacts were recorded in an industrial area of the city.

stories.title: Trump announces he will have updates on Iran ‘by the end of today'
stories.summary: President Trump announced he would provide updates on the Iran situation by the end of the day. He previously warned he might end the ceasefire with Iran unless a long-term deal is reached by Wednesday.

stories.title: Foreign ministers of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Egypt discuss ‘evolving regional dynamics’
stories.summary: The foreign ministers of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Egypt met on the sidelines of the Antalya Diplomacy Forum to discuss evolving regional dynamics. The meeting included Deputy PM Ishaq Dar, Prince Faisal bin Farhan, Hakan Fidan, and Badr Abdelatty.

stories.title: US imposes sanctions aimed at Colombian fighters in Sudan
stories.summary: The United States imposed sanctions targeting Colombian fighters operating in Sudan and urged both the Sudanese government army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces to accept a three-month humanitarian truce.

stories.title: Foreign Ministers of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Egypt hold third consultative meeting in Antalya
stories.summary: The foreign ministers of Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Egypt held their third consultative meeting on the sidelines of the Antalya Diplomacy Forum. They expressed shared commitment to deepening coordination and expanding collaboration across key mutual interests.

stories.title: India protests after ships attacked in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: India summoned Iran's ambassador Mohammad Fathali after two Indian-flagged oil tankers came under fire while crossing the Strait of Hormuz. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri conveyed New Delhi's "deep concern" over the incident during urgent talks.

stories.title: Russian forces strike fire station in Sumy region again
stories.summary: Russian forces conducted another drone strike on a fire station in the Shostka district of Ukraine's Sumy region on April 18.

stories.title: Has Hezbollah crossed a red line in attack on French UNIFIL soldiers? - analysis
stories.summary: Multiple UN peacekeepers have been killed in recent fighting in southern Lebanon, including two Indonesian peacekeepers killed on March 30 by a roadside explosion. The attack on French UNIFIL soldiers raised questions about Hezbollah crossing a red line.

stories.title: Ukraine just took out mass shooter in Kyiv supermarket who killed six people
stories.summary: Ukrainian security forces neutralized a gunman who opened fire in a supermarket in Kyiv's Holosiivskyi district, killing multiple people. The shooter reportedly lived in Ryazan, Russia.

stories.title: Iran closes Hormuz Strait again over US blockade with ships mid-transit
stories.summary: Iran's military declared the Strait of Hormuz closed again on Saturday, hours after reopening it, with more than a dozen commercial ships mid-transit. The reversal cast doubt on U.S. President Trump's earlier optimism that a peace deal to end the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran was near.

stories.title: Two drivers killed in motorway crash in Perth and Kinross
stories.summary: Two male drivers were killed in a head-on collision on the M90 motorway near Kinross in Perth and Kinross, Scotland, on Friday night. Police Scotland reported that one car appeared to have been traveling in the wrong direction on the carriageway.

stories.title: Iran reimposes restrictions on Strait of Hormuz, accusing U.S. of violating deal to reopen it
stories.summary: Iran reimposed restrictions on the Strait of Hormuz, warning it would continue blocking transit as long as the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports remained in effect. The move reversed an earlier decision to allow non-military vessels through during a ceasefire.

stories.title: Kyiv gunman kills 6 and takes hostages before being shot dead by Ukraine police
stories.summary: A gunman killed at least six people on the streets of Kyiv before taking hostages in a supermarket. Ukrainian special tactical police units stormed the store after negotiations failed, and the attacker was killed while resisting arrest.

stories.title: London police probe arson attack on building tied to Jewish organization
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police are investigating an arson attack on a building linked to a Jewish organization. The incident follows a string of antisemitic arson attacks in north London, including fires at a synagogue and a Jewish ambulance service, with possible links to Iran-backed actors.

stories.title: Harsh Israel critic Analilia Mejía wins US House seat in New Jersey special election
stories.summary: Analilia Mejía, a Bernie Sanders ally who has accused Israel of genocide, won a special election for New Jersey's 11th congressional district. AIPAC had indirectly boosted Mejía during the primary by opposing more moderate candidate Tom Malinowski. She will hold the seat until January.

stories.title: The Palestinian woman on the cover of L'Espresso: Settlers were ready to kill us
stories.summary: Meead Abu al-Rub, a 35-year-old Palestinian woman from the occupied West Bank, recounted being harassed by Israeli settlers during the olive harvest season last October. A photo of the incident appeared on the cover of Italian magazine L'Espresso, drawing international attention.

stories.title: Italian group slammed for showing Israeli film at Lebanon event
stories.summary: An Italian cultural group faced criticism from activists for screening the Israeli film "Waltz with Bashir" at an event in Lebanon. Critics called the screening a "Zionist" erasure of the experiences of those who lived through Israel's 1982 invasion of Lebanon.

stories.title: US and Cuba hold talks in Havana for first time in 10 years — media
stories.summary: US State Department representatives held talks with Cuban officials in Havana for the first time in ten years, urging democratic and economic reforms and warning about consequences of ignoring Washington's guidance.

stories.title: Turkey says Israel using security as a pretext to acquire ‘more land’
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan accused Israel of using security concerns as a pretext to acquire more territory. Tensions between Turkey and Israel have escalated steadily since the Gaza war.

stories.title: French soldier killed in attack on UN mission in south Lebanon
stories.summary: A French soldier was killed in an attack on a UN peacekeeping mission in southern Lebanon. French President Emmanuel Macron condemned the "unacceptable attack" in calls with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Prime Minister Nawaf Salam.

stories.title: Syrian govt supporters, opponents clash in Damascus
stories.summary: Dozens of people protested in Damascus over rising living costs, leading to clashes between supporters and opponents of the Syrian government. Organizers vowed to continue pressing their demands despite the tensions.

stories.title: Colombia's Petro warns of Latin American 'rebellion' if US doesn't rethink policy
stories.summary: Colombian President Gustavo Petro warned in an interview with Spain's El País that continued U.S. pressure on dissenting Latin American leaders could spark a regional "rebellion" against Washington's influence.

stories.title: Pope Leo plays down rift with Trump, doubles down on peace
stories.summary: While traveling to Angola for a three-day visit, Pope Leo XIV sought to ease tensions with US President Donald Trump, stating he had no desire to engage in a public debate. The two leaders had clashed after the pope criticized the war in Iran.

stories.title: French film star Nathalie Baye dead at 77, says family
stories.summary: French actress Nathalie Baye has died at age 77. She starred in approximately 80 films and won France's César Award for best actress four times, including three consecutive years from 1981 to 1983.

stories.title: ‘No regrets’: Venezuela’s Machado defends giving Nobel medal to Trump
stories.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado stated she has no regrets about giving her Nobel Peace Prize medal to US President Donald Trump following the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro.

stories.title: Strategic success in the Iran war: What Israel and the US achieved together - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece assessed the US-Israel war against Iran as a strategic success, citing the dismantling of Iran's nuclear capabilities and ballistic missile programs as significant achievements for regional security.

stories.title: Three people sentenced to jail for bear-suit insurance scam in California
stories.summary: Three individuals in Los Angeles were sentenced to jail for an insurance fraud scheme in which they staged bear attacks on high-end vehicles using a person in a bear costume. The California Department of Insurance investigated after video evidence unconvincingly depicted the fake attacks.

stories.title: Colombia fights female genital mutilation
stories.summary: In Colombia's Risaralda region, female genital mutilation continues in some Indigenous Embera communities despite severe health risks. Congress is debating its first bill to ban the practice, with Indigenous women leading calls for its eradication.

stories.title: Trump says US won't let Iran 'blackmail us'
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump, speaking from the Oval Office, said "very good conversations" were ongoing with Iran but warned the US would not let Tehran "blackmail" Washington by threatening to close the Strait of Hormuz. He indicated more information would come by end of day.

stories.title: Two more Reform local election candidates accused of offensive posts
stories.summary: Two additional Reform UK local election candidates were accused of making offensive or potentially racist social media posts. Labour called on party leader Nigel Farage to dismiss them, saying Reform's vetting process was inadequate. Separately, Rupert Lowe's Restore Britain party reportedly accepted a donation from someone who publicly called for "another Hitler."

stories.title: Ukrainians to be able to observe peak of the Lyrid meteor shower on April 22
stories.summary: On the night of April 22, people in Ukraine will be able to observe the peak of the Lyrid meteor shower.

stories.title: Will US-Iran talks resume in Pakistan soon?
stories.summary: Conflicting timelines have emerged regarding US-Iran negotiations. Iran stated no date has been set for resumed talks, contradicting reports suggesting imminent negotiations in Islamabad, Pakistan, where Pakistan has been mediating between the two sides.

stories.title: Hezbollah denies involvement in deadly attack on UN peacekeepers
stories.summary: Hezbollah denied involvement in a deadly attack on UNIFIL peacekeepers in the Ghandouriyeh-Bint Jbeil area of southern Lebanon, after France accused the group of being behind the incident. The organization called for caution pending a Lebanese army investigation.

stories.title: Pakistan Army chief Munir concludes three-day Iran visit
stories.summary: Pakistan Army Chief Syed Asim Munir concluded a three-day visit to Iran, having arrived in Tehran on April 15. He was the first foreign military leader to visit Iran since a two-week ceasefire was agreed between Iran and the U.S. on April 8.

stories.title: Turkey says Iran gas pipeline contract nearing expiry
stories.summary: Turkey announced that its natural gas pipeline contract with Iran is nearing expiry in July. The agreement provides for delivery of 9.6 billion cubic metres of gas annually, though actual flows have frequently fallen short of that target.

stories.title: US extends license for Serbian oil company NIS
stories.summary: The United States extended a temporary operating license for Serbia's oil company NIS, which is under sanctions, until mid-June.

stories.title: Ukraine strikes Baltic Sea port, Volga river industrial sites
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck industrial sites along the Volga River and a Baltic Sea port near St. Petersburg that exports petroleum products. Russian regional governors reported the overnight attacks on April 18.

stories.title: Iran says reviewing 'new proposals' from US
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme National Security Council said it was reviewing new proposals from the United States, delivered through Pakistan's army commander who visited Tehran as a mediator. Iran warned its negotiators would not compromise in any dealings with Washington.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian man in West Bank
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed a Palestinian man near Hebron in the occupied West Bank during military raids across several towns. Other Palestinians were detained during the operations.

stories.title: “Lords of war.” Brazil’s president condemns UN Security Council
stories.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva criticized the five permanent members of the UN Security Council, labeling them "Lords of War" in a public condemnation of the body's structure and conduct.

stories.title: Replay : Donald Trump holds briefing amid Hormuz tension
stories.summary: President Donald Trump held a White House briefing on Saturday as Iran announced it was re-closing the Strait of Hormuz while the US maintained its blockade of Iranian ports. The dueling measures have heightened tensions in the critical shipping corridor.

stories.title: Iran partially reopens its airspace for flights
stories.summary: Iran partially reopened its airspace on Saturday, allowing international flights to cross the eastern part of the country.

stories.title: French soldier killed by Hezbollah in southern Lebanon, Macron says
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron stated on social media that a French soldier was killed in southern Lebanon, saying evidence pointed to Hezbollah's responsibility for the attack.

stories.title: Vessels report being hit by gunfire as Iran says Strait of Hormuz shut again
stories.summary: Merchant vessels attempting to transit the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday received radio warnings from Iran's navy that passage was not permitted. Multiple vessels reported being struck by gunfire as Iran declared the strait closed again.

stories.title: At least five dead in Kyiv shooting, suspected gunman killed
stories.summary: At least five people were killed and ten hospitalized in a shooting in a residential neighborhood of Kyiv on Saturday. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the deaths, and the suspected gunman was shot dead during an arrest attempt by police.

stories.title: French soldier serving with UNIFIL killed in Lebanon attack
stories.summary: A French soldier serving with the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) was killed in an attack in southern Lebanon. The incident occurred just days after Israel and Lebanon announced a 10-day ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: As fentanyl crisis evolves, experts say US is still ‘behind the eight ball’
stories.summary: Experts say the US fentanyl crisis continues to evolve, with the Trump administration's militarized enforcement approach and cuts to public health programs potentially undermining progress in addressing the epidemic.

stories.title: China could take control of Iran's enriched uranium
stories.summary: Beijing is reportedly offering to take control of Iran's stockpile of highly enriched uranium. The move could potentially bring the United States and Iran closer to reaching a broader deal.

stories.title: UNIFIL sheds light on southern Lebanon attack that killed French soldier
stories.summary: A French soldier serving with the UN peacekeeping force UNIFIL was killed and three others wounded during a road-clearing operation in southern Lebanon. UNIFIL and French officials said the attack was likely carried out by Iran-backed Hezbollah.

stories.title: No signs of regime collapse as Iran weathers weeks of war
stories.summary: Despite weeks of US and Israeli military strikes, analysts say Iran's leadership shows no signs of regime collapse and remains firmly entrenched. Iranians are watching ceasefire talks while economic pressure, repression, and war damage deepen internal tensions.

stories.title: Trump and Tehran’s series of mismanaged posts stall progress towards peace
stories.summary: A series of premature and mismanaged media announcements by both President Donald Trump and Tehran led to the collapse of progress toward a US-Iran peace settlement. Iran subsequently reinstated a full blockade on commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and refused to export its stockpile of highly enriched uranium.

stories.title: Macron, UNIFIL blame Hezbollah after French peacekeeper killed in Lebanon
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron and UNIFIL directly accused Hezbollah of ambushing and killing a French peacekeeper in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah denied involvement, while Lebanese President Joseph Aoun vowed to prosecute those responsible.

stories.title: IDF confirms strikes on Hezbollah operatives in Lebanon, in first since ceasefire
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces confirmed conducting strikes against Hezbollah operatives in Lebanon, the first since a ceasefire agreement was reached. The IDF said the strikes were carried out in self-defense under the terms of the deal. A Hezbollah official said the group was "not concerned" by Israel-Lebanon talks.

stories.title: Trump announces reforms to accelerate access to psychedelic drug treatments
stories.summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order directing the FDA to expedite review of psychedelic drugs including ibogaine for potential medical use. US military veteran groups have advocated for ibogaine as a treatment for post-traumatic stress disorder.

stories.title: Pakistan military chief, PM head home after Iran war diplomacy
stories.summary: Pakistan's Prime Minister and military chief completed a three-country diplomatic tour to Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Turkey focused on advancing the peace process related to the Iran conflict.

stories.title: The rupture: how Europe fell out of love with America
stories.summary: Transatlantic relations between Europe and the United States have deteriorated significantly since the brief renewal of cooperation under former President Joe Biden. The G7, once a forum for unified Western policy including sanctions against Russia, has seen its cohesion fracture under shifting US foreign policy priorities.

stories.title: Russian drone hits meat processing plant in Kharkiv region, three injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck a meat processing plant in Bohodukhiv, Kharkiv region, using a Molniya-type drone. Three female employees suffered acute stress reactions from the attack.

stories.title: Russia ready to help with removal of enriched uranium from Iran
stories.summary: Rosatom head Alexei Likhachev said Russia is ready to assist with the removal of enriched uranium from Iran. Trump claimed Washington would work with Tehran to transfer the material to the US, but Iran firmly denied any such agreement.

stories.title: French peacekeeper killed in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: A French United Nations peacekeeper was killed in southern Lebanon. French President Emmanuel Macron attributed the attack to Hezbollah, while the Iran-backed group denied any involvement in the incident.

stories.title: French film star Nathalie Baye dies aged 77, media report
stories.summary: French film actress Nathalie Baye died at the age of 77. President Emmanuel Macron paid tribute, saying France had "loved, dreamed and grown up" with the celebrated star of French cinema.

stories.title: Israel using security as a pretext to acquire ‘more land’: Turkiye’s FM Fidan
stories.summary: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan accused Israel of using security as a pretext to acquire more territory, speaking at the Antalya Diplomacy Forum. Fidan said the Netanyahu government has created an international "illusion" of acting in self-defense.

stories.title: How feud with Trump helped Pope Leo find his voice
