stories.summary: Pope Leo, leader of 1.4 billion Catholics, has adopted a more combative public stance following a feud with US President Donald Trump. The conflict with Trump is reported to have helped the pope sharpen his voice on key issues.

stories.title: Trump signs order to speed review of psychedelics, including controversial drug ibogaine
stories.summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order directing faster federal review of psychedelic drugs, including ibogaine, which is currently banned under the most restrictive federal drug category. The move follows advocacy from combat veterans and conservative lawmakers who support ibogaine as a potential PTSD treatment despite serious safety risks.

stories.title: Russia hits port, power facility in Ukraine overnight
stories.summary: Russian overnight attacks damaged port infrastructure in Ukraine's southern Odesa region and caused power blackouts affecting 380,000 consumers in the country's north.

stories.title: SBU strikes three Russian warships in occupied Crimea
stories.summary: Ukraine's SBU Alpha special operations unit struck three Russian military vessels in temporarily occupied Crimea. The attacks targeted warships stationed in the peninsula's waters.

stories.title: General Staff confirms strikes on four Russian oil industry facilities
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Forces struck four Russian oil industry facilities overnight on April 18, with fires reported at the targeted sites. Ukraine's General Staff confirmed the operations against the key energy infrastructure.

stories.title: UN peacekeeper killed and three wounded in south Lebanon shooting
stories.summary: A United Nations peacekeeper was killed and three others wounded when a UNIFIL patrol came under small-arms fire while clearing explosives near the southern Lebanese village of Ghandouriyeh. Initial assessments indicated the fire came from non-state actors, allegedly Hezbollah.

stories.title: 'I thought I might die': A Palestinian mother's account of Israeli detention
stories.summary: Palestinian mother Saeda al-Shrafi described weeks of interrogation, torture, and imprisonment after being detained by Israeli forces while fleeing northern Gaza. Her account was published as Palestinian Prisoners' Day was marked.

stories.title: IDF strikes Hezbollah terrorists in southern Lebanon who approached troops, yellow line
stories.summary: The IDF struck what it described as Hezbollah operatives in south Lebanon who approached Israeli troops and the demarcation yellow line. Israel said the strikes complied with the ceasefire agreement, while Hezbollah politicians called them a violation.

stories.title: UNICEF ‘outraged’ after Israeli forces kill water truck drivers in Gaza
stories.summary: UNICEF expressed outrage after Israeli forces killed water truck drivers at a distribution site in Gaza. The agency called on Israeli authorities to investigate the incident and ensure full accountability.

stories.title: Hormuz tensions highlight pressure tactics in US-Iran negotiations
stories.summary: Analyst H.A. Hellyer of the Royal United Services Institute characterized renewed US-Iran tensions over the Strait of Hormuz as mutual pressure tactics during ongoing negotiations. Talks are expected to continue in Islamabad, but both sides are leveraging positions—including the US blockade of Iranian ports—making a quick breakthrough unlikely.

stories.title: Turkey’s economy hit as Syrians return home
stories.summary: More than half a million of Turkey's 3.6 million Syrian refugees have returned to Syria since the war there ended last year. Their departure is weakening Turkey's economy, particularly in sectors dependent on low-cost labor; in Gaziantep, half of garment workshops closed due to worker shortages.

stories.title: PIA begins pre-Haj operations, to transport over 55,000 pilgrims
stories.summary: Pakistan International Airlines announced that its pre-Hajj operation will begin on April 19, transporting over 55,000 pilgrims to Saudi Arabia via 191 flights from cities across Pakistan.

stories.title: French soldier killed in attack on UN mission in southern Lebanon, officials say
stories.summary: A French soldier was killed and three others wounded in an attack during a road-clearing operation in southern Lebanon, with UNIFIL and French officials attributing it likely to Iran-backed Hezbollah. French President Emmanuel Macron condemned the "unacceptable attack" in calls with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun and Prime Minister Nawaf Salam.

stories.title: Israeli fire kills two Gaza water truck drivers
stories.summary: Israeli fire killed two water truck drivers in Gaza. UNICEF suspended activities at the affected site and called on Israeli authorities to investigate the incident.

stories.title: Russia losing $100M daily from Ukrainian strikes on oil infrastructure
stories.summary: The Ukrainian Unmanned Systems Forces reported that Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil infrastructure are costing Russia approximately $100 million per day in losses.

stories.title: Iranians fear sharpening pressure after war and crackdown
stories.summary: Post-war Iran faces economic devastation, rising government repression, and widespread uncertainty among its population despite a period of fragile calm following the cessation of hostilities.

stories.title: Hong Kong watchdog monitoring potential merger of city’s top 2 supermarket chains
stories.summary: Hong Kong's Competition Commission said it is closely monitoring a potential merger between the city's two largest supermarket chains, operated by Jardine Matheson and CK Hutchison. The watchdog's scrutiny comes amid declining grocery sales in the territory since 2020.

stories.title: This Independence Day, Israel must embrace uncertainty - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece reflects on Israel's Independence Day amid a prolonged war, arguing that the emotional landscape of the country has shifted and that Israel must learn to embrace uncertainty.

stories.title: Trump threatens to bomb Iran amid Strait of Hormuz tension
stories.summary: President Trump threatened to bomb Iran as tensions continued over the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has tied access to the waterway to the lifting of the US blockade, and the status of the ceasefire remained uncertain.

stories.title: US renews Russian oil waiver after pressure from countries dealing with Iran war price shocks
stories.summary: The Trump administration renewed a waiver allowing countries to purchase sanctioned Russian oil loaded on vessels through May 16, replacing an expired 30-day waiver. The move aims to control global energy prices amid the Iran war, though lawmakers criticized it as being lenient on Moscow.

stories.title: Closed? Open? Closed? Why is Iran changing course on the Strait of Hormuz?
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reopened the Strait of Hormuz briefly before shutting it again, a move Chinese analysts described as a leverage tactic ahead of possible negotiations with the United States. A two-week U.S.-Iran ceasefire was set to expire on Wednesday.

stories.title: Independence Day: 78+1 reasons I love Israel - opinion
stories.summary: Barbara Sofer published her 22nd annual list of reasons she loves living in Israel, timed for Israel's Independence Day celebrations marking 78 plus one years of statehood.

stories.title: Iran reimposes Hormuz Strait control, accuses US of breaching terms - report
stories.summary: Iran reportedly reimposed restrictions on the Strait of Hormuz, accusing the United States of breaching agreed-upon terms and failing to guarantee safe passage for ships traveling to and from Iranian ports.

stories.title: Gulf tensions escalate as Iran tightens control of Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Tensions between the United States and Iran are escalating over control of key shipping routes in the Persian Gulf, particularly the Strait of Hormuz, as both governments harden their negotiating positions.

stories.title: Ukraine not engaged in intergovernmental efforts with Germany to return men — Uliutin
stories.summary: Ukraine's Minister of Social Policy Denys Uliutin stated that Ukraine is not engaged in any intergovernmental efforts with Germany to facilitate the return of Ukrainian men to the country.

stories.title: Lesson for China? Iran’s low-cost 358 missile takes out million-dollar US assets
stories.summary: China's state media examined Iran's 358 loitering munition, a low-cost missile weighing about 50 kilograms, which has reportedly been used to shoot down expensive U.S.-made drones including the MQ-9 Reaper during the U.S.-Israel conflict with Iran.

stories.title: Pope Leo brings Africa tour to Angola as Trump feud drags on
stories.summary: Pope Leo continued his Africa tour with a visit to Angola, during which he spoke out against "tyrants" and those who use religion to justify war. The visit comes amid an ongoing public dispute between the pontiff and U.S. President Donald Trump.

stories.title: US forces turn 23 vessels back to Iran since blockade began, says military
stories.summary: The US military said that 23 ships had been turned back toward Iran since the United States imposed a blockade on Iranian ports and coastal areas earlier in the week.

stories.title: Iran closes strait of Hormuz again ‘until US lifts blockade’
stories.summary: Iran reimposed restrictions on the Strait of Hormuz after the U.S. refused to lift its blockade of Iranian ports. A UK maritime agency reported that IRGC vessels fired on a tanker attempting to pass through the strait on Saturday.

stories.title: Macron: French soldier killed in Lebanon
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron announced that a French soldier serving with UNIFIL in southern Lebanon was killed, with evidence suggesting Hezbollah was responsible. Three other French soldiers were wounded and evacuated.

stories.title: Ukraine's defense minister outlines key priorities for A1 Defense AI Center
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov outlined priority focus areas for the newly established A1 Defense AI Center, aimed at integrating artificial intelligence into Ukraine's defense capabilities.

stories.title: Russia-Appointed Official in Occupied Kherson Holds Talks with North Korean Envoy
stories.summary: A Russian-appointed official in occupied Kherson held talks with a North Korean envoy. The two sides discussed potential collaboration in agriculture, humanitarian initiatives, culture, sports, and education.

stories.title: Millions listen to Ethiopian star's song taking swipe at government
stories.summary: Ethiopian musician Teddy Afro released a new song lamenting a lack of national unity that has drawn millions of listeners. The track is widely interpreted as critical of the Ethiopian government.

stories.title: Hindi Rajab Foundation files complaint against Israeli-American tourist in Sri Lanka
stories.summary: The Belgium-based Hindi Rajab Foundation filed a legal complaint in Sri Lanka against an Israeli-American tourist. The organization described it as the first such complaint filed against a US citizen outside the United States.

stories.title: Magnitude 5 earthquake strikes off mountainous Nagano in Japan, says NHK
stories.summary: A magnitude 5 earthquake struck near Omachi in the mountainous Nagano prefecture of central Japan at approximately 1:20 p.m. local time, according to Japanese public broadcaster NHK.

stories.title: Trump claims on Iranian concessions trigger questions, rejections in Tehran
stories.summary: Following claims by Donald Trump regarding Iranian concessions, Tehran rejected the assertions. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced that the Strait of Hormuz would once again be restricted.

stories.title: Hormuz conflict continues as Iran closes strait over US blockade
stories.summary: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz briefly reached its highest level since early March on Saturday, but Iran subsequently announced it was closing the waterway once again amid the ongoing dispute with the United States.

stories.title: ‘We can’t wait’: Venice already seeking floods plan B five years after barriers’ launch
stories.summary: Venice is exploring alternatives to its Mose flood defense system five years after the barriers became operational. Rising sea levels and ecological damage from heavy use of the barriers are prompting city authorities to consider additional protective measures.

stories.title: Trump’s antipathy for Pope may have roots in childhood Protestant church
stories.summary: Donald Trump's public criticism of Pope Leo may be linked to his upbringing at Manhattan's Marble Collegiate Church, which was led by pastor Norman Vincent Peale, known for anti-Catholic views and opposition to the presidency of John F. Kennedy.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz discusses global, regional issues during tri-nation tour
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif completed a tri-nation diplomatic tour to Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Turkey. Discussions focused on strengthening bilateral relations, Pakistan's role in regional peace, and the evolving global situation.

stories.title: Iran’s supreme leader warns of ‘new bitter defeats’ for US and Israel
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned that Iran's navy was prepared to inflict 'new bitter defeats' on the United States and Israel.

stories.title: Russia hits port, power facility in Ukraine overnight
stories.summary: Russian forces struck port infrastructure in Ukraine and targeted an energy facility in the Chernihiv region overnight. The Chernihiv regional power distribution operator reported the attack on Telegram.

stories.title: Trump says he has 'good news' on Iran, no clarity on peace deal
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said on April 18 there had been "pretty good news" regarding Iran, signaling optimism about peace talks to end the ongoing war. However, he warned that a ceasefire might not be extended without a deal by Wednesday. No specific details of any agreement were provided.

stories.title: Unknown assailants storm Yavoriv recruitment center, attack security personnel
stories.summary: Three unidentified individuals stormed the Yavoriv district territorial recruitment and social support center in Ukraine's Lviv region and attempted to assault security personnel stationed there.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz : Iran to block transit until US lifts its blockade
stories.summary: Iran briefly reopened the Strait of Hormuz before closing it again after approximately 20 hours, citing U.S. non-compliance with ceasefire terms. Negotiations between the two sides continue in Islamabad amid rising tensions.

stories.title: UK’s counterterror police probe another London arson attack
stories.summary: UK counterterrorism police are investigating an arson attack on a shop in Hendon, a northwest London area with a large Jewish population. No injuries were reported. The incident follows a separate arson attack on a synagogue in nearby Finchley, where two people were arrested.

stories.title: Iran’s deputy FM says no date for more US talks until ‘framework’ agreed
stories.summary: Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister stated that further talks with the United States cannot proceed until both sides agree on a shared negotiating framework. No date for additional discussions has been set.

stories.title: Myanmar release of Suu Kyi top ally spurs small democracy hope
stories.summary: Myanmar's military government released a top ally of detained leader Aung San Suu Kyi, sparking cautious hope for democratic progress. However, residents and Suu Kyi herself expressed skepticism, noting the detention was unjust to begin with.

stories.title: Iran signals re-closure of Hormuz as it rejects uranium transfer abroad
stories.summary: Iran denied US claims that it had agreed to transfer enriched uranium abroad and threatened to re-close the Strait of Hormuz unless Washington lifts its naval blockade. A handful of vessels had begun transiting the waterway on Saturday before the renewed threat.

stories.title: Middle East : Fragile US-Iran talks hinge on nuclear and Hormuz disputes
stories.summary: U.S.-Iran negotiations remain tense with limited progress, as disputes over enriched uranium and the Strait of Hormuz persist. President Trump warned the conflict could resume without a deal, while mediators suggested compromises on nuclear restrictions may still be achievable.

stories.title: Sarfaraz named Pakistan’s Test coach for Bangladesh series in May
stories.summary: Former Pakistan captain Sarfaraz Ahmed has been appointed head coach for Pakistan's two-match Test series against Bangladesh in May. The matches, part of the ICC World Test Championship, will be played in Dhaka and Sylhet.

stories.title: Statement from supreme leader says Iran's navy 'stands ready' to defeat US
stories.summary: A statement attributed to Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei, shared via his Telegram channel, warned that Iran's navy stands ready to defeat US forces amid the ongoing Strait of Hormuz standoff. Khamenei has not been seen publicly since before the start of the war.

stories.title: Sudan’s war leaves thousands of children alone and displaced
stories.summary: Sudan's civil war between the army and the Rapid Support Forces is entering its fourth year, creating what the UN calls the world's largest humanitarian crisis. Thousands of children in Darfur and other regions have been displaced and separated from their families.

stories.title: Entertainment figures add names to letter rejecting calls to kick Israel out of Eurovision
stories.summary: Entertainment figures including Amy Schumer, Mila Kunis, and Erin Foster signed a letter opposing calls to expel Israel from the Eurovision Song Contest, calling such a move an 'inversion of justice.'

stories.title: ‘Whatever life throws at us, we don’t walk alone’: how a London synagogue attack birthed an act of solidarity
stories.summary: Finchley Reform Synagogue in London held a large Shabbat gathering days after an attempted firebombing attack on the building. Hundreds of congregation members attended in a show of solidarity against rising antisemitism.

stories.title: US again eases sanctions on Russian oil shipments
stories.summary: The United States issued a new license permitting the supply and sale of Russian-origin crude oil and petroleum products loaded onto vessels as of April 17, further easing sanctions on Russian oil shipments.

stories.title: Aurangzeb holds ‘productive’ meeting with US Treasury officials, discusses avenues for energy, mineral cooperation
stories.summary: Pakistani Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb met with U.S. Treasury officials on the sidelines of the World Bank and IMF Spring Meetings 2026 in Washington, D.C. Both sides discussed cooperation opportunities in the mineral and energy sectors.

stories.title: Fourth suspect in London arson attack on Jewish ambulances remanded in custody
stories.summary: Judex Atshatshi, 18, of Dagenham, east London, appeared at Westminster magistrates court and was remanded in custody as the fourth suspect charged in connection with the arson attack on four Jewish community ambulances in northwest London.

stories.title: In Phoenix, Trump eyes lower petrol prices and frets about the midterms
stories.summary: During an appearance in Phoenix, President Trump sought to present an optimistic outlook on the nearly two-month-long war in Iran. He also focused on lowering petrol prices and expressed concern about the impact of the conflict on upcoming midterm elections.

stories.title: Lebanon ceasefire: Families return south to ruins and hope
stories.summary: Displaced Lebanese families began returning to south Lebanon after a fragile 10-day ceasefire was announced. Returnees found widespread devastation following Israel's military operations in the region.

stories.title: ‘Collateral damage’: Exiled Lebanese tells 'Post' refugees back Israel’s fight against Hezbollah
stories.summary: Exiled Lebanese individuals told the Jerusalem Post that many Lebanese refugees support Israel's military campaign against Hezbollah. They expressed concern that the Iranian-backed group would reassert control if Israel withdrew prematurely.

stories.title: CDF Munir concludes 3-day Iran visit, discusses sustainable regional peace: ISPR
stories.summary: Pakistan's Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi concluded a three-day official visit to Iran. Discussions focused on regional security, diplomatic engagements, and de-escalation measures amid the evolving situation in the Middle East.

stories.title: Iran tells ships on radio that Strait of Hormuz 'is shut again'
stories.summary: Iran's navy broadcast radio messages to merchant vessels on Saturday declaring the Strait of Hormuz closed again and prohibiting all ship passage, according to shipping sources cited by Reuters.

stories.title: UK agency says IRGC-linked gunboats fired on tanker near Oman
stories.summary: The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency reported that two gunboats linked to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fired on a tanker approximately 20 nautical miles northeast of Oman. The vessel and crew were reported safe despite the attack occurring without prior radio warning.

stories.title: Israeli attacks in Lebanon kill one despite 'truce'
stories.summary: Israel launched new attacks in Lebanon that killed one person despite a truce agreement reached on April 16. The strikes were characterized as violations of the ceasefire arrangement between the two sides.

stories.title: Iran signals re-closure of Hormuz as it rejects uranium transfer abroad
stories.summary: Iran denied US claims about uranium transfer agreements and signaled the re-closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Ships approaching the waterway on Saturday turned back after Iran's navy declared it shut again.

stories.title: Iran closes Strait of Hormuz again over US blockade of its ports
stories.summary: Iran announced the closure of the Strait of Hormuz in response to a US blockade of its ports. Reports indicated that Iranian gunboats opened fire on a tanker in the waterway.

stories.title: Ukrainian Defense Ministry to contract 25,000 ground robotic systems in H1 2026 – Fedorov
stories.summary: Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov announced plans for the Defense Ministry to contract 25,000 ground robotic systems during the first half of 2026.

stories.title: Small nations, strong ties: Fiji’s ambassador talks faith, friendship, and Israel - interview
stories.summary: Fiji's Ambassador Jesoni Vitusagavulu discussed both strategic and spiritual reasons behind Fiji's support for Israel in an interview. He highlighted the small Pacific nation's faith-based and diplomatic ties with Israel.

stories.title: China trade deal has Canadians looking forward to cheaper electric vehicles
stories.summary: Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers including BYD, Geely, Nio, and Xpeng are preparing to enter the Canadian market following a trade deal between Ottawa and Beijing. Canadian consumers hope the entry of Chinese brands will drive down EV prices overall.

stories.title: Hong Kong Sevens at ‘pinnacle’ on 50th anniversary, pioneering coach Peter Duncan says
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Sevens rugby tournament is celebrating its 50th anniversary. Peter Duncan, who coached the Hong Kong team at the inaugural 1976 event and recently stepped down as president of Hong Kong China Rugby, described the tournament as having reached its pinnacle.

stories.title: Displaced Lebanese return as Israeli shelling violates ceasefire in south
stories.summary: Al Jazeera correspondents reported that displaced Lebanese residents were returning to southern Lebanon despite Israeli shelling that violated the ceasefire. Israeli bulldozers were also continuing home demolitions in the area.

stories.title: Turkiye woos investors amid Iran war fallout in Gulf economies
stories.summary: Turkish officials are promoting Istanbul as an alternative regional financial hub, seeking to attract investors affected by the economic fallout of the Iran war on Gulf economies.

stories.title: Trump says he has ‘good news’ on Iran, offers no clarity on peace deal
stories.summary: President Trump said he had received "good news" regarding Iran but offered no specifics on a peace deal. Hours earlier, Iran had temporarily reopened the Strait of Hormuz following a separate U.S.-brokered ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon.

stories.title: BBC reports from Lebanese border town as residents try to return home
stories.summary: BBC Arabic correspondent Carine Torbey reported from the southern Lebanese border town of Khiam as the Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire entered its second day and residents attempted to return to their homes.

stories.title: Iran war energy shock drives nuclear power plans in hard-hit Asia, Africa
stories.summary: The energy disruptions caused by the Iran war are accelerating nuclear power expansion plans across Africa and Asia. Nations with existing nuclear plants are increasing output as they scramble to secure short-term energy supplies.

stories.title: Sudan war enters fourth year as the humanitarian crisis deepens
stories.summary: Sudan's conflict between the Sudanese army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces has entered its fourth year after fighting erupted in April 2023. The war has displaced millions and created what the United Nations describes as the world's largest humanitarian crisis.

stories.title: Turkey says Israel using security excuse to acquire 'more land'
stories.summary: Turkey accused Israel of using security as a pretext to acquire additional land. The two countries have clashed repeatedly over Israel's war in Gaza and differing positions on Syria's future.

stories.title: Energy, transport, logistics: Svyrydenko presents Ukraine's investment 'wish list' in Washington
stories.summary: Ukrainian Prime Minister Yuliia Svyrydenko met with International Finance Corporation Managing Director Makhtar Diop in Washington to present Ukraine's investment priorities in the energy, transport, and logistics sectors.

stories.title: Settlers set fire to Palestinian buildings, cars in West Bank; no injuries or arrests
stories.summary: Settler attacks were reported near Nablus and in Masafer Yatta in the occupied West Bank, where assailants set fire to Palestinian buildings and cars. One attacker appeared to be guarded by an armed individual wearing IDF gear. The Israeli military said it is investigating the incidents.

stories.title: US blockade of Iran needs to end before the Strait of Hormuz is fully reope
stories.summary: Analyst Michael Shoebridge assessed that the United States may need to end its blockade of Iran before the Strait of Hormuz can be fully reopened to international shipping.

stories.title: Lebanese lives torn apart as Israel ceasefire loomed
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike struck the city of Nabatiyeh in southern Lebanon just hours before a ceasefire took effect at midnight Thursday. The attack flattened a five-story building, killing at least four people including the brother and nephew of survivor Khodr Sahmarani.

stories.title: Peruvian prosecutors raid election records warehouse
stories.summary: Peruvian prosecutors conducted a raid on an election records warehouse following complaints against officials and allegations of missing voter materials. Details on the specific officials involved or the scope of the missing materials were not immediately disclosed.

stories.title: The Iran war has revealed Trump’s pressure point: the economy
stories.summary: Seven weeks of the U.S.-Iran war have highlighted the economy as a key vulnerability for President Trump. Despite Iran's announcement that it would reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the conflict has exposed limits to Trump's tolerance for domestic economic disruption caused by the Middle East crisis.

stories.title: Four injured in Russian shelling across Kherson region over past day
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled more than 40 settlements across Kherson Oblast over a 24-hour period using various weapons, injuring four people and damaging local infrastructure.

stories.title: Hong Kong’s Mirror star Keung To urges public to learn from his driving mistakes
stories.summary: Hong Kong Cantopop singer Keung To of the boy band Mirror was fined HK$2,200 for careless driving, running a red light, and failing to display a probationary sign. The 26-year-old urged the public to learn from his driving mistakes.

stories.title: Iran threatens to again close Strait of Hormuz, if U.S. blockade continues
stories.summary: Iran, however, pushed back on Trump’s claim that Tehran had agreed to hand over its enriched uranium, saying its stockpile of enriched uranium was not going anywhere

stories.title: One dead after car hits pedestrians in Melbourne, police say
stories.summary: One person died after a car mounted a kerb and struck pedestrians in Melbourne, Australia. Police arrested a man at the scene in connection with the incident.

stories.title: Egypt minister: Hopes for Iran-US peace deal 'in the coming days'
stories.summary: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said at the Antalya Diplomacy Forum in Turkey that Egypt and Pakistan are working intensively as mediators to reach a final US-Iran agreement. He expressed hope that a deal could be reached within days.

stories.title: Rutte dismisses speculation about US leaving NATO
stories.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte dismissed speculation about the United States leaving NATO, while acknowledging President Donald Trump's frustrations with the alliance. Rutte also called on European nations to strengthen their defense industries.

stories.title: Iran reimposes Strait of Hormuz restrictions, accuses US of violating deal to reopen waterway
stories.summary: Iran reimposed restrictions on the Strait of Hormuz, accusing the US of violating terms of a deal to reopen the waterway. President Trump rejected the idea that Iran could charge tolls on the passage. A convoy of tankers transited the strait in the first major ship movement since the war began.

stories.title: Wang Fuk Court residents prepare for emotional return to site of deadly fire
stories.summary: Residents of Hong Kong's Wang Fuk Court are preparing for an emotional return to the site of a deadly fire last November that destroyed seven of the estate's eight buildings. Survivors must climb stairs to reach their units as lift systems were destroyed.

stories.title: Hungary’s incoming PM seeks Polish help to renew EU relations
stories.summary: Hungarian election winner Péter Magyar is seeking closer ties with Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk to help restore Hungary's relations with the European Union. Both center-right, pro-European leaders face the challenge of rebuilding rule-of-law standards and state institutions after prolonged periods of democratic backsliding in their respective countries.

stories.title: Earth gets brighter every year but progression is volatile, study finds
stories.summary: NASA-funded researchers at the University of Connecticut found that Earth's artificial light increased by a net 16% between 2014 and 2022, based on analysis of over 1.1 million satellite images. The study noted that the location and intensity of brightening have become increasingly volatile due to COVID-19, light pollution regulations, and economic fluctuations.

stories.title: How China’s military could learn vital lessons from war in Iran
stories.summary: An analyst suggested China could gain a strategic advantage from the war in Iran by reshaping Middle East trade and studying U.S. military operations. Peking University's Zhu Zhaoyi also urged Beijing to take a more active role in peace negotiations.

stories.title: Iran closes Hormuz again after less than 24 hours as two ships report being fired upon
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reimposed strict control over the Strait of Hormuz less than 24 hours after reopening the critical waterway. At least two vessels reported being fired upon while attempting to transit the strait, which carries roughly one-fifth of global oil and LNG shipments. It remains unclear whether the gunfire caused damage.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Trump says Iran ceasefire may end if no deal reached
stories.summary: "Maybe I ​won't ‌extend it, but the blockade is ‌going to ​remain," U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters ⁠on Air Force One on ‌his way back to Washington from Phoenix, Arizona

stories.title: More than 38,000 women, girls killed in Gaza war by end of 2025
stories.summary: A UN Women report stated that more than 38,000 women and girls were killed in the Gaza war by the end of 2025. Survivors face ongoing threats including starvation, repeated displacement, and severely restricted access to essential services.

stories.title: Hormuz: Spin in the Strait
stories.summary: The article examines the ongoing standoff in the Strait of Hormuz, contrasting actual military and naval tactics with propaganda narratives surrounding the blockade between the United States and Iran.

stories.title: A light unto the enemies: Three dangerous lessons from the Holocaust - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece draws lessons from Holocaust remembrance, arguing that memory must serve as a means toward action rather than an end in itself. The author discusses educational programs and delegations to Poland.

stories.title: Ambulance crew in south Lebanon describes Israel’s ‘triple-tap’ attack
stories.summary: Ambulance workers in south Lebanon described Israeli "triple-tap" strikes—repeated attacks on the same location—that killed four paramedics and wounded six others during operations in the area.

stories.title: “Today I was lucky that it wasn’t me”: Ukrainian journalists on living through Russian terror strikes
stories.summary: Ukrainian journalists described the psychological toll of living through ongoing Russian terror strikes, highlighting the constant threat of death from aerial attacks on civilian areas in Ukraine.

stories.title: Five tankers seen loading oil on Iran's Kharg Island, as US blockades Strait of Hormuz - report
stories.summary: Satellite imagery showed five tankers loading oil at Iran's Kharg Island while the US maintained its naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. An additional five tankers carrying approximately 9 million barrels of oil were earlier spotted in the Gulf of Oman but have since disappeared from tracking.

stories.title: The US has once again partially eased sanctions on Russian oil for one month
stories.summary: The US Treasury issued General License 134B, partially easing sanctions on Russian oil for cargoes already at sea until May 16. The one-month extension drew sharp criticism from Senate Democrats.

stories.title: Trump says US blockade of Iranian ports will ‘remain’ if no deal reached
stories.summary: President Donald Trump said on Saturday that he planned to maintain a US blockade of Iranian ports if a peace deal with Tehran is not reached, adding that he may not extend the ceasefire after its exp

stories.title: The Gaza Strip grapples with a major garbage, health crisis
stories.summary: Displaced families in Deir al-Balah and across the Gaza Strip are living near growing rubbish piles as destroyed infrastructure forces reliance on unsafe temporary dump sites. Poor sanitation and pest infestations are raising serious health concerns, compounded by limited humanitarian aid reaching the territory.

stories.title: As oil prices plunge below $91 after weeks, a new Hormuz crisis emerges
stories.summary: Brent crude oil prices fell over 9 percent, dropping below $91 per barrel, after Iran briefly signaled it would reopen the Strait of Hormuz before shutting it again in response to the ongoing US naval blockade.

stories.title: Middle East : What to expect from the truce between Lebanon and Israel ?
stories.summary: The United States and Israel announced a ceasefire agreement reached in Washington between Lebanon and Israel following historic direct talks between the two countries. Analysts described the truce as fragile, with Lebanese journalist Dany Moudallal discussing the stakes of the agreement with France 24.

stories.title: Counter-terror police investigate arson attack in London
stories.summary: Counter-terrorism officers at London's Metropolitan Police are investigating an arson attack on a business in Hendon, north-west London, that occurred on Friday. Few additional details have been released as the investigation remains in its early stages.

stories.title: Trump says US blockade will ‘remain’ if no deal is reached as Iran threatens to close Hormuz anew
stories.summary: President Trump stated that the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports will remain in place if no deal is reached. In response, Tehran threatened to close the Strait of Hormuz again, signaling renewed risk to a critical global oil shipping route despite ongoing ceasefire progress.

stories.title: Amid Israel's 'forever wars', Palestinians must not abandon the one-state solution
stories.summary: Writer Awad Abdelfattah argues that the US-Israel war on Iran threatens to bury Palestinian self-determination and contends that a one-state framework remains the only viable path for Palestinians amid ongoing conflicts.

stories.title: Egypt working with Pakistan on lasting US-Iran peace plan, minister says
stories.summary: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty announced that Egypt is collaborating with Pakistan on a framework for lasting US-Iran peace. He said Egypt, Turkey, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia are coordinating a broader regional effort to prevent escalation and stabilize energy markets and supply chains.

stories.title: Oil refinery on fire in Syzran, Russia – CCD
stories.summary: An oil refinery caught fire in the Russian city of Syzran. The cause of the blaze was not immediately specified in initial reports.

stories.title: Trump says U.S. blockade of Iranian ports will ‘remain’ if no deal reached
stories.summary: Mr. Trump told reporters there were "not going to be tolls" imposed by Iran on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, something that the Islamic republic put forward during previous peace deal pl

stories.title: An imminent deal or ‘lies’? Fog of claims and counterclaims shrouds US-Iran war
stories.summary: Negotiations between the United States and Iran over a comprehensive peace deal remain clouded by competing claims and counterclaims from both sides. Despite some ceasefire progress, prospects for an all-out peace agreement are described as very slim.

stories.title: Japan, Australia finalise contracts to deliver first 3 of planned frigates
stories.summary: Japan and Australia finalized contracts to jointly deliver the first three of 11 planned frigates based on the upgraded Japanese Mogami-class design. Defense ministers Shinjiro Koizumi and Richard Marles announced the deal in Melbourne as both nations deepen defense cooperation.

stories.title: Death penalty law proves the EU must treat Israel as an apartheid state
stories.summary: European Parliament member Pernando Barrena argued that Israel's adoption of a death penalty law targeting Palestinians strengthens the case that the EU should treat Israel as an apartheid state and sever ties with it.

stories.title: Hegseth compares media to the Pharisees, an ancient Jewish sect derided by Christians
stories.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth drew controversy by comparing the media to the Pharisees, an ancient Jewish sect often criticized in Christian tradition. Jewish groups said the comparison carried antisemitic connotations, while some Christians and conservatives defended the remark.

stories.title: Displaced by Iran war: out of Lebanon, into Syrian crisis
stories.summary: More than 227,000 people have fled conflict in Lebanon to Syria, where they face housing shortages, economic hardship, and a lack of state services. Despite a new ceasefire in Lebanon, many displaced people say they intend to remain in Syria.

stories.title: Ethiopia journalist abduction sparks press freedom fears
stories.summary: The managing editor of Ethiopia's Addis Standard was kidnapped by masked men inside the newsroom on Wednesday and remains missing. The abduction has heightened press freedom concerns as Ethiopia intensifies a crackdown on independent media ahead of June elections, including revoking accreditation for international outlets.

stories.title: Iranians fear fresh government crackdown after war: ‘There’s fire under the ashes’
stories.summary: Iranians expressed fears of a renewed government crackdown following the war, despite the regime appearing entrenched after surviving weeks of conflict. Economic difficulties that previously fueled mass unrest and a violent crackdown are expected to worsen.

stories.title: Could the PLA use minelaying drones in a first island chain blockade over Taiwan?
stories.summary: A Chinese military magazine suggested the PLA could use AJX002 minelaying drones for offensive operations targeting Japan's Ryukyu archipelago and Philippine waters as part of a first island chain blockade during a potential Taiwan conflict.

stories.title: As Meloni’s hold over Italy weakens, a progressive challenger gathers momentum in Genoa
stories.summary: Silvia Salis, the leftwing mayor of Genoa and former Olympian, is emerging as a progressive challenger as Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's grip on Italian politics weakens. A failed referendum on judicial reform triggered government resignations, while Meloni's relationship with Donald Trump has deteriorated over her criticism of his attacks on Pope Leo.

stories.title: ‘It’s kind of a tough situation’: US Catholics torn in feud between president and the pope
stories.summary: U.S. Catholics are divided over the public feud between President Donald Trump and Pope Leo XIV. In communities across the country, including Bible study groups in Decatur, Georgia, faith and politics are colliding as Trump's attacks on the pope polarize the diverse Catholic community.

stories.title: China limbless mum sews with mouth, uses limb stumps for daily tasks, raises 3 kids alone
stories.summary: An 81-year-old Chinese woman named Wang Yushi from Baiyin, Gansu province, was born without limbs and raised three children on her own. She learned to sew with her mouth and use her elbows for daily tasks.

stories.title: Russian shelling of Kharkiv region over past day leaves seven injured
stories.summary: Russian forces shelled the city of Kharkiv and 25 surrounding settlements over the past day, injuring seven civilians in the Kharkiv region of northeastern Ukraine.

stories.title: Iran closes Hormuz Strait again over US blockade with ships mid-transit
stories.summary: Iran's military declared the Strait of Hormuz closed again on Saturday, hours after reopening it, while more than a dozen commercial ships were mid-transit through the vital waterway. The reversal cast doubt on President Trump's assertion that a peace deal was close.

stories.title: Iran closes Strait of Hormuz again, IRGC fires on two vessels
stories.summary: Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz again as IRGC forces fired on two vessels. President Trump said it was uncertain whether he would extend a ceasefire set to expire on Wednesday, warning he might resume bombing.

stories.title: Iran closes Strait of Hormuz again citing continued US blockade
stories.summary: Iran re-closed the Strait of Hormuz, citing the continued US naval blockade. President Trump warned he might not extend a ceasefire set to expire on Wednesday and suggested he could resume bombing operations against Iran.

stories.title: Iran command says Hormuz closed again over US blockade
stories.summary: Iran's central military command announced it would resume strict control of the Strait of Hormuz, reversing its earlier decision to unblock the waterway. The command accused Washington of breaking a promise by continuing its naval blockade of ships traveling to and from Iranian ports.

stories.title: G-7 steps up efforts to break China’s grip on critical minerals
stories.summary: G-7 members are intensifying efforts to reduce dependence on China for critical minerals. The group is pursuing strategies to diversify supply chains for these strategically important resources.

stories.title: G-7 steps up efforts to break China’s grip on critical minerals
stories.summary: G-7 member nations are intensifying efforts to reduce dependence on China's dominance in critical mineral supply chains. The group is pursuing strategies to diversify sourcing of minerals essential for technology and green energy production.

stories.title: Iranians fear increased repression despite ceasefire, economic collapse
stories.summary: Iranians face growing fears of government repression despite a fragile ceasefire with the United States. The country's economy has deteriorated sharply, and citizens worry about increased state control in the post-conflict period.

stories.title: U.S. Extends Sanctions Waiver on Purchases of Russian Oil
stories.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department extended a sanctions waiver allowing purchases of Russian oil, reversing Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's statement two days earlier that Washington would not renew the license.

stories.title: Indian among second group of migrants deported from U.S. and taken in by Costa Rica
stories.summary: Costa Rica is one of a growing number of countries across Africa and the Americas that have signed contentious, often secretive agreements with the U.S. to accept deportees from other countries

stories.title: Trump’s gambit
stories.summary: FOR a man not known to be particularly religious, US President Donald Trump spent a lot of time on matters of faith last weekend, prompted, perhaps, by statements made by Pope Leo. The supreme head of

stories.title: Russia reports drone attacks: Oil depot, refinery on fire
stories.summary: A drone attack overnight into Saturday ignited a fire at an oil depot in Tikhoretsk, Krasnodar Krai, Russia. A separate fire was also reported at a refinery following the strikes.

stories.title: 27 drones down, one port on fire: Leningrad Oblast governor reports overnight attack by Ukrainian drones
stories.summary: The governor of Russia's Leningrad Oblast reported that 27 Ukrainian drones were intercepted overnight on April 18, while fires broke out at fuel depots and near Vysotsk port. Additional drone incidents were reported in Sevastopol and Samara.

stories.title: The burden of taxes
stories.summary: THE unwarranted and illegal war imposed on Iran represents an extraordinary exogenous shock for developing countries. Pakistan is particularly vulnerable on this front. It has an outsized import depen

stories.title: How US-Israeli war on Iran has eclipsed the crisis in Sudan
stories.summary: Writer Osama Abuzaid argues that the US-Israeli war on Iran has diverted global attention from Sudan's ongoing crisis. The article warns that Sudan's warring parties may exploit the shift in focus to intensify their conflict economy.

stories.title: Pakistan PM, army chief wrap up key trips in push for more US-Iran talks
stories.summary: Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir concluded a visit to Tehran while Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif returned from Turkey, with both trips aimed at facilitating another round of US-Iran negotiations.

stories.title: Trump frames Iran war as all but over in optimistic social media flurry
stories.summary: President Trump posted a series of optimistic social media messages framing the Iran war as nearly concluded. Iran's top negotiator pushed back, accusing the U.S. president of making seven false claims within just one hour of posting.

stories.title: ADF neutralizes 190 of 219 drones used by Russia to attack Ukraine overnight
stories.summary: Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 190 of 219 drones launched by Russian forces starting the evening of April 17. The operation demonstrated continued large-scale Russian drone assaults against Ukrainian territory.

stories.title: US Catholics unsettled by Trump’s feud with Pope Leo
stories.summary: The ongoing public dispute between President Trump and Pope Leo is unsettling American Catholics, a significant voting bloc. Political analysts suggest the feud could create vulnerabilities for Republican candidates in upcoming midterm elections.

stories.title: DR Congo accepts first set of deportees from the US
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo accepted its first group of deportees from the United States. The Congolese government stated that those expelled are only in the country on a temporary basis.

stories.title: Power outages
stories.summary: AS summer approaches, households and industries across the country are again facing prolonged power outages as night-time electricity demand, driven by cooling needs, far exceeds the available supply.

stories.title: Iran reimposes shipping restrictions on Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz again, with its armed forces resuming strict control over the strategic waterway. The reversal came one day after Tehran allowed non-military vessels to transit during a ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon.

stories.title: Mandelson scandal is biggest crisis for diplomatic service in decades, says ex-Foreign Office chief
stories.summary: Former Foreign Office permanent under-secretary Simon McDonald called the Peter Mandelson security vetting scandal the biggest crisis for Britain's diplomatic service in decades. McDonald defended civil servant Oliver Robbins, saying he was "thrown under a bus" by Prime Minister Keir Starmer when Robbins was dismissed from his role on Thursday.

stories.title: Ukraine’s FM meets Moldova’s president in Turkey, briefs her on the front line
stories.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha met Moldovan President Maia Sandu at the Antalya Diplomacy Forum in Turkey. He briefed her on frontline developments and Russian strikes, and they coordinated on the May 14–15 Council of Europe session in Chișinău regarding the Special Tribunal.

stories.title: US renews Russian oil waiver after pressure from countries dealing with Iran war price shocks
stories.summary: The United States renewed a waiver allowing purchases of Russian oil following pressure from countries affected by energy price spikes caused by the Iran war. The decision is aimed at controlling global energy prices that have risen sharply during the conflict.

stories.title: Central bank bosses enlist for war game to gauge threat of Lehman-style bust
stories.summary: Senior officials from the U.S. Federal Reserve, European Central Bank, and Bank of England are participating in a war-game exercise in Washington to test how they would handle the collapse of a globally significant bank. The drill reflects growing concerns about risks to global financial stability.

stories.title: Russian forces attack port, industrial infrastructure in Odesa region, leaving one injured
stories.summary: Russian forces struck port and industrial infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region overnight using strike drones. Administrative buildings, warehouses, buses, and storage tanks sustained damage, and one person was injured.

stories.title: Iran declares the Strait of Hormuz 'completely open' amid fragile ceasefire
stories.summary: Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz fully open to commercial shipping during the Lebanon ceasefire, causing a sharp drop in oil prices. President Trump welcomed the move but maintained a U.S. naval blockade, while France and the UK are leading plans for a neutral mission to secure the waterway.

stories.title: Southern Lebanon residents return home to devastation after ceasefire
stories.summary: Displaced Lebanese families are returning to heavily damaged towns like Nabatieh in southern Lebanon following the ceasefire with Israel. Residents found homes, businesses, and essential services devastated, and are relying on humanitarian aid for basic needs as they begin rebuilding.

stories.title: "We are just displaced and we have to go back" : Lebanese return to southern villages
stories.summary: Thousands of internally displaced Lebanese are returning to southern villages despite warnings from authorities about the fragility of the ceasefire with Israel. Many residents do not consider themselves refugees, viewing themselves as displaced citizens of a country where conflict has persisted for years.

stories.title: Jesus memes, threats and a war in Iran: A portrait of Trump under pressure
stories.summary: President Trump has grown increasingly frustrated that the war in Iran has lasted longer than he initially anticipated. The prolonged conflict, combined with economic pressures and cultural controversies, has put the president under mounting pressure.

stories.title: Trump is urged to act on Iranian site feared impervious to airstrikes
stories.summary: Experts are urging President Trump to address a deeply buried underground facility in Iran that may be impervious to America's most powerful bunker-busting bombs. The site's depth raises questions about U.S. military options for neutralizing Iran's nuclear infrastructure.

stories.title: War update: 151 combat clashes on front line over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces reported 151 combat engagements with Russian troops along the front line on April 17. The clashes occurred at multiple points across the contact line.

stories.title: IDF court-martials female troops who showed up for discharge in tank tops, short skirt
stories.summary: The IDF court-martialed three female soldiers who arrived for their discharge ceremony wearing tank tops and a short skirt, docking their pay. The incident follows controversy over medics being jailed for barbecuing on a base during Shabbat.

stories.title: Palestinian armed with knife breaches West Bank settlement, is shot dead — IDF
stories.summary: The IDF reported that a Palestinian man armed with a knife breached a West Bank settlement by climbing over the entrance gate. A local security guard shot and killed the assailant after he reportedly rushed at the guard with the knife.

stories.title: Nadav Lapid’s ‘Yes!’: Israeli director’s wartime film raises eyebrows and ire
stories.summary: Israeli director Nadav Lapid's wartime film "Yes!" has generated controversy and is now screening in select US theaters. The film has drawn both attention and criticism for its subject matter during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: Campaign launched to remove illegal guards’ cabins from outside houses in Islamabad
stories.summary: ISLAMABAD: Unprecedented security measures in the capital are gradually being strengthened ahead of peace talks between Iran and the United States, including the removal of security cabins outside hou

stories.title: Why Japan’s bond moves could see shift in East Asia’s financing model
stories.summary: Shifts in Japan's bond market could prompt changes to East Asia's longstanding financing model, which has relied heavily on bank loans rather than market-determined capital flows to fund business investment since the postwar period.

stories.title: UNICEF says Israeli fire kills two Gaza water truck drivers
stories.summary: UNICEF reported that Israeli fire killed two water truck drivers in Gaza, with two others injured in the attack. The agency confirmed the casualties involved personnel delivering water supplies in the territory.

stories.title: Trump cites 'some pretty good news' on Iran, says ceasefire may end if no deal reached by Wednesday
stories.summary: President Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One that he had received "pretty good news" regarding Iran and that matters in the Middle East appeared to be progressing well. He indicated the ceasefire could end if no deal is reached by Wednesday.

stories.title: Iran has learned that the Strait of Hormuz is its strongest deterrent
stories.summary: Donald Heflin, a senior fellow at Tufts University, argued that Iran's ability to control the Strait of Hormuz has proven to be its most effective deterrent, reducing its need for nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Hormuz domino effect: How the Middle East crisis affects food, flights and global supply chains
stories.summary: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz during the Middle East conflict has disrupted global supplies of jet fuel, fertilizers, industrial CO2, and naphtha beyond its well-known impact on oil prices. Despite a provisional reopening during a 10-day ceasefire, supply chain disruptions could lead to shortages of food and other essential products worldwide.

stories.title: U.S. extends waiver allowing countries to buy Russian oil
stories.summary: The waivers could complicate the West’s efforts ​to deprive Russia of revenue for its war in Ukraine and put Washington ⁠at odds with its allies

stories.title: Russians attack energy facility in Chernihiv region, 380,000 consumers left without power
stories.summary: A Russian attack on an energy facility in Ukraine's Chernihiv region on April 18 left approximately 380,000 consumers without electricity. The strike targeted energy infrastructure in the northern Ukrainian region.

stories.title: Most-wanted trafficker held in FIA crackdown
stories.summary:
ISLAMABAD: The Federal Investi­gation Agency (FIA) has arrested a most-wanted criminal and several other suspects as its crackdown on human smugglers and traffickers continues across the country.

stories.title: IOM says 13,000 crossed into Pakistan from Iran during war
stories.summary: • Taftan-Mirjaveh and Gabd-Kumb-Rimdan border crossings see a daily average of 296 people• 170,153 individuals enter Afghanistan from Iran during the same period• People’s return to Iran increases aft

stories.title: Ukraine works with Interpol to find thousands of cultural artefacts looted by Russians
stories.summary: Ukraine is collaborating with Interpol to recover thousands of cultural artifacts looted by Russian forces during the occupation of territories including Kherson. The Kherson Art Museum lost much of its 14,000-piece collection, which the director discovered missing upon returning after the city's liberation in late 2022.

stories.title: Hong Kong charity breeding Labrador with golden retriever to boost guide dog supply
stories.summary: Hong Kong Seeing Eye Dog Services is crossbreeding a Labrador with a golden retriever for the first time to increase its guide dog supply. Only 10% of applicants for guide dogs are currently matched immediately, and demand continues to outpace the number of available canines.

stories.title: Police intensify combing operation against terrorists after Chilas attack; 15 held
stories.summary:

stories.title: Venezuela’s Machado to hold Madrid rally as opposition frozen out after Maduro capture
stories.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado, a Nobel Peace Prize laureate now in exile, announced a rally in Madrid's Puerta del Sol to revive her push for political change. She has been sidelined after the abduction of President Nicolás Maduro and the Trump administration's backing of Delcy Rodríguez.

stories.title: Peace out: is Takaichi putting Japan’s pacifist constitution on the chopping block?
stories.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is pursuing the first-ever revision of Japan's post-World War II pacifist constitution. Her Liberal Democratic Party secured a two-thirds majority in the National Diet's lower house after February's election, clearing the threshold needed to pass constitutional amendments without support from other parties.

stories.title: Russian blogger’s fierce critique of Kremlin goes viral: ‘People are afraid of you’
stories.summary: Russian celebrity blogger Victoria Bonya posted a viral video criticizing Kremlin authorities, warning President Vladimir Putin that mounting domestic problems risk spiraling out of control. Her remarks came as Putin's approval ratings recorded their sixth consecutive weekly decline, creating a public relations challenge for the Kremlin.

stories.title: Russia loses 1,080 troops, 82 artillery systems in war against Ukraine over past day
stories.summary: Ukraine's military reported that Russia lost 1,080 troops and 82 artillery systems in a single day of fighting. Total Russian combat losses since February 24, 2022, have reached approximately 1,317,150 personnel, according to Ukrainian figures.

stories.title: US cloud dominance risks European security: report
stories.summary: PARIS: More than three-quarters of European countries use American cloud computing services for vital national security functions, a report published Friday found, warning that the dependency could ma

stories.title: Pakistan escorted Iran negotiators home amid Israel concerns
stories.summary: • Sources say Islamabad deployed some two dozen jets for mission• Airborne Warning and Control System also used for aerial surveillance• Similar protection ‘may be offered to Iranian officials in next

stories.title: Middle East crisis live: Iran warns it will close strait of Hormuz if US blockade continues
stories.summary: Iran has warned it will close the Strait of Hormuz if the US blockade continues, stating that passage through the waterway will require Iranian authorization. Iran accused US President Donald Trump of multiple falsehoods. Separately, Pakistani leaders concluded a Middle East diplomatic tour visiting Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Turkey.

stories.title: Putin believes now is best moment to 'destabilize' EU and NATO to reduce support for Ukraine – CCD
stories.summary: Russia is preparing to intensify information and hybrid attacks against the EU and NATO, as Vladimir Putin has been convinced that now is the right moment to "destabilize" them in order to reduce thei

stories.title: Pakistan seeks early approval of next IMF tranche
stories.summary: WASHINGTON: Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb said on Friday that while he has discussed with International Monetary Fund (IMF) officials the impact of the Iran conflict on Pakistan’s economy, “our

stories.title: US issues sanctions waiver on Russian oil sales again
stories.summary: The Trump administration issued a one-month sanctions waiver on Friday allowing the sale of Russian oil and petroleum products already loaded at sea, despite Treasury Secretary indications two days earlier that the measure would not be renewed. The decision comes amid efforts to ease global energy prices affected by the Iran war and Strait of Hormuz disruptions.

stories.title: FCC upholds ban on book imports from certain countries
stories.summary: • Rules govt can limit trade with India, Israel on security, foreign policy grounds• Declares ‘right to read’ fundamental to life under Constitution; warns curbs on knowledge risk intellectual, societ

stories.title: Tehran sees large turnout at pro-government women’s rally
stories.summary: Thousands of women and girls attended the "Sacrificed Girls" rally in central Tehran on Friday, according to Iranian state media. The pro-government demonstration paid tribute to women killed in U.S.-Israeli strikes during the war on Iran and expressed support for the country's leadership.

stories.title: Diesel price cut by Rs32 a litre, petrol unchanged
stories.summary: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday announced a reduction of Rs32.12 per litre in diesel prices while keeping petrol rates unchanged for the week ending April 24, passing on the impact

stories.title: Russian troops starve due to inability to deliver supplies to positions – intelligence
stories.summary: Intelligence officers intercepted a conversation between servicemen of the Russian Armed Forces who complained about the lack of food and water at their positions, indicating serious logistical diffic

stories.title: UK police charge fourth suspect over attack on Jewish community ambulances
stories.summary: UK police charged a fourth suspect in connection with an attack on Jewish community ambulances. A pro-Iranian group allegedly behind the attack also claimed responsibility for attempted arson at a synagogue in Finchley and at the Iran International offices in Wembley, London.

stories.title: Fire breaks out at oil terminal in southern Russia's Krasnodar region, officials say
stories.summary: A fire broke out at an oil terminal in Russia's southern Krasnodar region early on Saturday, April 19, prompting a large-scale firefighting operation. Regional emergency authorities confirmed the incident but did not immediately report casualties or the cause of the blaze.

stories.title: Hormuz ‘fully open’ but US keeps Iran blockade intact
stories.summary: • Trump expects deal to be finalised ‘in a day or two’• Calls PM, army chief ‘fantastic people’• Asserts Lebanon conflict separate from Hormuz deal; Iran insists Hormuz opening linked to Lebanon cease

stories.title: Trump says will bring Iran uranium ‘back home to the USA’
stories.summary: President Trump declared he would bring Iran's enriched uranium "back home to the USA." Tehran had previously stated that Iran's stockpile of enriched uranium would remain in the country, highlighting a significant gap between the two sides' positions.

stories.title: US extends waiver for sanctioned Russian oil purchase as global prices fall
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of the Treasury issued a new waiver permitting the delivery and sale of sanctioned Russian crude oil and petroleum products. The license covers shipments loaded from April 17 through May 16, following the expiration of a previous waiver on April 11, as the administration seeks to ease energy prices during the Iran conflict.

stories.title: IDF kills terrorist armed with knife after Negohot infiltration alert
stories.summary: The Israeli military said soldiers killed a knife-armed individual after an infiltration alert at the Negohot settlement in the occupied West Bank. The IDF dispatched troops to conduct additional scans of the area, reporting no other casualties.

stories.title: Iranians fear ‘pressure will 100% increase’ after US, Israeli strikes stop
stories.summary: Iranians are struggling to resume normal life after weeks of US and Israeli airstrikes and a January crackdown on protesters. Damage from the bombing and internet disruptions continue to affect daily routines. Talks are expected on extending a truce, and shops, restaurants, and government offices have remained open during a fragile calm.

stories.title: In Bangkok, Malaysia’s first Mr Bear winner finds spotlight queer life rarely gets at home
stories.summary: Gavin Chow, a 34-year-old Malaysian activist, was crowned Mr Bear International 2026 during Thailand's Songkran festival in Bangkok — the first Malaysian to win the title. The pageant is part of Thailand's growing queer festival circuit. In Malaysia, same-sex intimacy remains criminalized under federal law, and LGBTQ gatherings have faced police raids.

stories.title: Young Bulgarians hold out for change in eighth election in five years
stories.summary: Bulgaria is holding its eighth general election in five years, with voters split largely along generational lines. A pro-Russian former president leads in polls. Young Bulgarians, including 23-year-old parliamentary candidate Anna Bodakova, are pushing for change after mass protests over economic policies and corruption led to the prime minister's resignation.

stories.title: Russian drone hits house in Bohodukhiv, leaving two injured
stories.summary: On the night of April 18, Russian forces struck a residential building in the city of Bohodukhiv in the Kharkiv region with a drone.

stories.title: Israeli police destroy children’s footballs at Al-Aqsa mosque
stories.summary: Israeli police confiscated and destroyed footballs that children were playing with near Al-Aqsa mosque in Jerusalem. No further details on injuries or arrests were provided.

stories.title: South Sudan tensions escalate as opposition retakes key stronghold
stories.summary: The UN Security Council received a briefing Friday on worsening humanitarian conditions in South Sudan, days after opposition forces retook the strategic town of Akobo from government troops. The recapture has escalated tensions between the government and opposition.

stories.title: For first time in decades, PA bringing municipal vote to city in Gaza
stories.summary: The Palestinian Authority is preparing to hold municipal elections in Deir al-Balah in Gaza later this month, marking the first such vote in the city in over two decades. Hamas had blocked voting for 20 years, and it remains unclear whether the group will honor the results.

stories.title: US says it will pursue Iran-linked ships in Indo-Pacific region
stories.summary: US Central Command announced that American forces will pursue Iran-linked vessels beyond the Middle East, including in the Indo-Pacific region. Joint Chiefs Chairman General Dan Caine said the effort includes maritime interdiction actions targeting ships that departed before the blockade began.

stories.title: National Guard destroys Smerch MLRS, enemy equipment in Luhansk region
stories.summary: In early April, a unit of the National Guard, Lasar's Group, carried out a special operation in the Luhansk region, destroying a BM-30 Smerch multiple launch rocket system and other Russian military e

stories.title: British tourists hurl antisemitic abuse at Israeli couple in Vietnam: ‘Rats running away’
stories.summary: Two British tourists in Vietnam directed antisemitic abuse at an Israeli couple at a restaurant, accusing them of genocide and invoking white supremacist tropes about mass Jewish expulsions. One of the tourists reportedly shouted "Viva Iran" before both sang "Boom, boom Tel Aviv."

stories.title: Tragedy averted as 125 ferried to safety from Mangla Dam
stories.summary: MUZAFFARABAD: As many as 125 people, including women and children, were safely rescued from Mangla Dam on Thursday night after a sudden thunderstorm disrupted their return journey from Ramkot Fort, an

stories.title: Israeli forces kill person in Negohot settlement, army says
stories.summary: The Israeli military said its forces killed a person carrying a knife at the Negohot settlement in the occupied West Bank. The army said alarms were triggered after reports of an infiltration, and no other casualties were reported.

stories.title: Drones attack oil depot in Sevastopol
stories.summary: Drones struck an oil depot in the area of Kozacha Bay in temporarily occupied Crimea.

stories.title: Trump says US will ‘start dropping bombs again’ if no Iran deal is reached
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump warned that the United States would resume bombing Iran if no deal is reached between the two countries. The statement signals continued pressure on Tehran amid ongoing negotiations.

stories.title: Iran war: What is happening on day 50 of the US-Iran conflict?
stories.summary: On day 50 of the U.S.-Iran conflict, Iran announced it would reopen the Strait of Hormuz with conditions. Tehran threatened to close the waterway again if the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports continues.

stories.title: Trump says Iran ceasefire may end if no deal by Wednesday
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump said he may not extend a temporary ceasefire with Iran if negotiations fail to produce an agreement by Wednesday. Speaking aboard Air Force One, Trump warned that the US could resume bombing and maintain its blockade of Iranian ports if talks collapse.

stories.title: Dollar slips below Rs279 after 3 years
stories.summary:
KARACHI: After three years, the US dollar slipped below Rs279 on Friday in the inter-bank market, reflecting a sign of exchange rate stability.

According to data issued by the Exchange Companies Asso

stories.title: Hong Kong wants to become a global gold vault. Does the Iran war create an opening?
stories.summary: Hong Kong is seeking to position itself as a global gold storage hub, capitalizing on market volatility driven by the US-Israeli war on Iran. The conflict has intensified demand for safe-haven assets and diversified bullion storage. Hong Kong aims to leverage its unique status to become Asia's leading bullion center.

stories.title: Chinese robo-diving suit could help users consume almost 40% less oxygen
stories.summary: Chinese scientists have developed a robotic exoskeleton diving suit that reduced oxygen consumption by nearly 40 percent in tests. The flexible suit synchronizes with the diver's movements to boost underwater agility. Potential applications include seabed surveys, pipeline inspections, salvage operations, and military missions.

stories.title: China eatery sparks outrage for ‘beating wife’ sales slogan hinting domestic violence approval
stories.summary: A noodle restaurant in Xining, Qinghai province, China, drew widespread criticism for displaying a banner reading "beaten wife, kneaded dough." The slogan references an old saying from the Guanzhong plain region that likens beating a wife to kneading dough. The shop was condemned across mainland Chinese social media for appearing to condone domestic violence.

stories.title: Green MP: Labour caricatures working-class people over greyhound racing
stories.summary: UK Green Party MP Hannah Spencer accused Labour of "offensively caricaturing" working-class people by claiming they oppose a greyhound racing ban in England. Scotland and Wales announced bans on the sport last month, but Labour has indicated no plans to follow suit in England, citing the sport's traditional association with working-class culture.

stories.title: Winners and judges out of pocket as £20,000 writing awards appear to have closed
stories.summary: The Plaza Prizes, a writing competition established in 2022 that promised a £20,000 prize fund across 10 awards in 2025, appears to have shut down. Some judges, including a Booker Prize-winning novelist, report they were not paid. Several winners have also raised concerns about AI-related accusations.

stories.title: Palestinian rights orgs. push Australian Ministry of Defense to release arms export documents
stories.summary: Palestinian rights organizations are pressing Australia's Ministry of Defense to release arms export documents. The Australian Centre for International Justice noted this is their second attempt, after an earlier effort was discontinued shortly after its launch in November 2023.

stories.title: Canada stands in ‘full solidarity’ with Gulf partners, PM says
stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney declared Canada's "full solidarity" with Gulf partners and welcomed the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire and Iran's reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. His statement followed consultations with French President Emmanuel Macron and UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer.

stories.title: Curry, Warriors knocked out of NBA play-in tournament by Suns
stories.summary: The Phoenix Suns eliminated the Golden State Warriors from the 2026 NBA play-in tournament. Stephen Curry scored just 17 points in the loss, ending the defending champions' season.

stories.title: YouTube bans pro-Iran 'Explosive Media' AI animation channel
stories.summary: YouTube banned "Explosive Media," a pro-Iran channel that used AI-generated animations. The channel had previously been suspended on March 27, and its Instagram account was also removed, according to US media reports.

stories.title: Budanov says Russia worried about its contingent in Transnistria
stories.summary: The Russian authorities are concerned about the condition of their military contingent in Transnistria and want to strengthen it in some way.

stories.title: Hundreds of bone fragments found in Mexico City ahead of World Cup
stories.summary: Hundreds of bone fragments have been discovered in Mexico City during preparations for the upcoming World Cup. More than 480,000 people have been killed and 130,000 remain missing in Mexico's drug war since 2006.

stories.title: Iran says its enriched uranium ‘not going to be transferred anywhere’
stories.summary: Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei stated that Iran's enriched uranium stockpile would not be transferred anywhere, contradicting a claim by US President Donald Trump. Trump had previously asserted that Iran agreed to hand over nuclear material.

stories.title: Magnitude 5 quakes hit Japan’s Nagano prefecture
stories.summary: Two earthquakes measuring magnitude 5.0 and 5.1 struck Nagano Prefecture in central Japan on Saturday, with the first hitting the city of Omachi. The Japan Meteorological Agency warned of similar-scale aftershocks over the coming week but issued no tsunami warnings.

stories.title: Erdogan urges dialogue as Turkey convenes regional talks
stories.summary: Turkey hosted the Antalya Diplomacy Forum, bringing together regional leaders amid intensifying Middle East peace efforts. President Recep Tayyip Erdogan urged constructive dialogue and called for using the ceasefire as a window of opportunity for lasting peace.

stories.title: First cruise ship transits Strait of Hormuz since war began
stories.summary: The Malta-flagged cruise liner Celestyal Discovery became the first passenger vessel to transit the Strait of Hormuz since the war began, according to MarineTraffic. The ship had been docked in Dubai for nearly 47 days and was sailing without passengers toward Muscat, Oman.

stories.title: Middle East live: Iran threatens to close Strait of Hormuz again if US blockade continues
stories.summary: Iran threatened on Saturday to close the Strait of Hormuz again if the United States maintains its blockade of Iranian ports. The threat raises fresh doubts over recent diplomatic progress, including a ceasefire in Lebanon. The situation is being closely monitored amid broader Middle East tensions.

stories.title: What people in power think the impact of the Iran war will be
stories.summary: BBC economics editor Faisal Islam interviewed global leaders about the economic consequences of the ongoing Iran conflict, gathering perspectives on how the war is affecting the world economy.

stories.title: Six great reads: Iran’s social media memes, an abandoned department store and a 1,200-year-old record of cherry blossoms
stories.summary: The article compiles six recommended reads from the past week, covering topics including social media memes from Iran, an abandoned department store, and a 1,200-year-old Japanese record of cherry blossom blooming dates.

stories.title: ‘It’s a powder keg’: Romania leads EU measles cases as vaccination rates collapse
stories.summary: Romania leads the European Union in measles cases as vaccination rates have sharply declined. In the Transylvanian town of Săcele, a 2024 measles epidemic killed one unvaccinated toddler, with only seven general practitioners serving over 30,000 residents. Systemic bottlenecks and parental vaccine hesitancy have doctors warning of another serious outbreak.

stories.title: Two weeks that pushed Trump to the edge. Is his presidency unravelling?
stories.summary: President Trump faces mounting pressure after two turbulent weeks marked by the prolonged Iran war, rising inflation, and a public dispute with Christian leaders. Some longtime Trump supporters have expressed buyer's remorse. Barred from seeking another term, Trump is seen as politically unconstrained.

stories.title: Tale of two truces: Lebanon 'steps up' alongside Israel as Tehran and Washington edge toward a deal
