stories.title: Russian Stocks Slip After Iran Says Strait of Hormuz ‘Completely Open’ for Duration of Ceasefire
stories.summary: Russian energy stocks fell after Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz fully open for the duration of the ceasefire. Rosneft shares dropped over 4%, while Gazprom Neft fell nearly 3%, and Lukoil and Tatneft each declined more than 2%.

stories.title: Green Party strategist reveals plan for local elections and slams 'sectarian' claims
stories.summary: The UK Green Party launched its campaign for local elections scheduled for May 7. Elections coordinator Faaiz Hasan outlined the party's strategy and rejected what he called 'sectarian' accusations against the party.

stories.title: Zelensky: Conflict in Iran poses risks to Ukraine’s weapons supply
stories.summary: President Zelensky warned that the conflict in Iran poses risks to the supply of weapons to Ukraine. He noted that European partners are prepared to help find alternative solutions to address potential disruptions.

stories.title: Pope urges Cameroon to reject violence at mass that draws 120,000 people
stories.summary: Pope Leo urged Cameroonians to reject violence and show generosity during a mass attended by approximately 120,000 people in the port city of Douala. The event was the largest gathering of his four-nation Africa tour, held at Japoma Stadium under heavy security.

stories.title: Ukraine’s private-sector air defense groups downed their first jet Shahed — Russia’s drone that flies at 300+ km/h
stories.summary: A private-sector air defense group in Kharkiv Oblast shot down a jet-powered Shahed drone, which flies at speeds exceeding 300 km/h, marking the first such interception by a civilian enterprise. The network has expanded from 13 to 19 enterprises since March, integrated into Ukraine's Air Force command.

stories.title: UK: Footage used in Palestine Action trial contains 'perceived gaps', court hears
stories.summary: In a UK trial involving Palestine Action activists who raided an Elbit Systems factory in Bristol, a police officer testified that CCTV footage contained 'perceived gaps.' The officer described the company's surveillance system as 'not fit for purpose.'

stories.title: 9 firms win orbital AMTI deals, Space Force says
stories.summary: The U.S. Space Force announced that nine firms have been awarded contracts for orbital Air and Missile Tracking Integration (AMTI) capabilities. The Space Force did not disclose when the contracts were awarded or the individual dollar values.

stories.title: Nigeria: Offa Bank Robbery - Saraki Denies Fresh Charges, Alleges Political Plot
stories.summary: Former Nigerian Senate President Bukola Saraki has denied involvement in the 2018 Offa bank robbery after fresh criminal charges were filed by the Kwara State Government. Saraki described the charges as politically motivated and an abuse of judicial process.

stories.title: Questions raised over whether £3.8m government grant awarded to Wrexham AFC was lawful
stories.summary: Questions have been raised about whether a £3.8 million UK government grant to Wrexham AFC, co-owned by Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney, was lawfully awarded. The club received the stadium redevelopment grant without a contract or completed state aid assessment and has received £18 million in total taxpayer funding.

stories.title: Fallen idol: French singer Patrick Bruel accused of rape, sexual assault
stories.summary: French singer and actor Patrick Bruel, a longtime household name in France, faces charges of sexual assault and rape. Multiple accusations have emerged against the former teen heartthrob, while some members of his fanbase have publicly defended him.

stories.title: Iran opens Strait of Hormuz for remaining period of ceasefire, Iran’s Foreign Minister announces
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi announced the opening of the Strait of Hormuz to all vessels for the remaining duration of the ceasefire. The move follows the Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire in Lebanon.

stories.title: Report: Russia’s aviation regulator asks Transport Ministry to ban power bank use on flights
stories.summary: Russia's Federal Air Transport Agency has asked the Transport Ministry to ban the use of power banks on aircraft. The request followed an incident on a Ural Airlines flight in which a power bank caught fire mid-flight.

stories.title: Netanyahu: Long ‘road to peace’ begins, as Trump says Israel ‘PROHIBITED’ from bombing Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu spoke of a long 'road to peace' as a 10-day ceasefire with Lebanon largely held. President Trump declared Israel 'prohibited' from bombing Lebanon, though Lebanese media reported an Israeli strike on a motorcycle.

stories.title: Canada T20 World Cup game under ICC scrutiny after corruption claim
stories.summary: The International Cricket Council is investigating Cricket Canada over match corruption allegations, including Canada's eight-wicket loss to New Zealand at the T20 World Cup in Chennai. The probe followed allegations highlighted in a Canadian Broadcasting Corporation documentary.

stories.title: Army exploring refueling requirement for Cheyenne II MV-75: Official
stories.summary: The U.S. Army is exploring how to develop an aerial refueling capability for the MV-75 Cheyenne II tiltrotor. Maj. Gen. Clair Gill, PAE of Maneuver Air, said the Army needs to solve its own logistical resupply challenges in the air since it currently lacks organic refueling assets.

stories.title: Supreme court sides with oil and gas firms in Louisiana coastal damage fight
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled 8-0 in favor of oil and gas companies, including Chevron, in lawsuits over coastal land damage in Louisiana. The procedural decision grants the companies a new hearing in federal court after a state jury had ordered Chevron to pay over $740 million for coastal cleanup.

stories.title: EU to restore Syria relations, strengthen trade and security ties, document shows
stories.summary: The European Union plans to relaunch formal political contacts with Syria and pursue closer economic and security ties, according to a document seen by Reuters. The move marks a significant policy shift after years of frozen relations between Brussels and Damascus.

stories.title: LHC upholds govt’s policy abolishing free electricity units for power sector employees
stories.summary: The Lahore High Court upheld the Pakistani federal government's policy to monetize free electricity units previously provided to officers of the Water and Power Development Authority and power distribution companies. Justice Malik Javid Iqbal Wains ruled the benefit was a non-statutory perk that could be lawfully altered.

stories.title: 'Totally unfair' that EU countries making money on energy crunch: Former EU commissioner Breton
stories.summary: Former EU Internal Market Commissioner Thierry Breton criticized EU countries profiting from the energy crisis as "totally unfair." Breton, who helped drive the Digital Services Act and Digital Markets Act, was among five figures subjected to U.S. travel bans, which he likened to McCarthyism.

stories.title: US Congress passes 10-day extension of surveillance law amid Republican infighting
stories.summary: Both chambers of the U.S. Congress passed a 10-day extension of Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act after Republican infighting blocked a longer renewal. President Trump had urged Republican holdouts to support House Speaker Mike Johnson's plan for an unchanged extension of the warrantless surveillance law.

stories.title: Ukraine’s Navy to have five mine countermeasure vessels by June
stories.summary: Ukraine's Navy is set to have five mine countermeasure vessels in service by June 2026. The Netherlands is training the crew of the minehunter Zr. Ms. Makkum, which will be renamed Henichesk and transferred to Ukraine in June.

stories.title: Ceasefires and Communications
stories.summary: An analysis covers recent developments including President Trump's abrupt shift from threatening Iran to announcing a two-week ceasefire, followed by Pakistan-mediated negotiations. The piece examines the rapid diplomatic twists in the U.S.-Iran conflict.

stories.title: Myanmar's Suu Kyi sentence reduced under mass amnesty: source
stories.summary: Myanmar's ousted leader Aung San Suu Kyi, currently serving a 27-year prison sentence, had her term reduced under a mass amnesty that freed over 4,000 prisoners.

stories.title: Report: Russia’s Interior Ministry cuts off banks’ access to passport database without explanation
stories.summary: All Russian banks have lost access to the Interior Ministry's passport verification database through the SMEV interagency system since April 15. No official explanation has been provided for the disruption, according to Forbes Russia.

stories.title: Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire: civilians return to ruined towns in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: A ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah has paused fighting in southern Lebanon. Civilians are returning to heavily damaged towns, though uncertainty remains over the durability of the truce.

stories.title: Kosovo approves troop contribution for Gaza force
stories.summary: Kosovo's parliament approved by a unanimous 89-0 vote a government decision to contribute troops to the International Stabilization Force in Gaza.

stories.title: The history of America’s long-term efforts to plan for a war with China [BOOK EXCERPT]
stories.summary: Author Rowan Allport's new book, "War Plan Taiwan," examines the history of long-term U.S. military planning for a potential conflict with China over the defense of Taiwan. The excerpt details decades of American strategic preparations for such a contingency.

stories.title: Russia still tackling a blaze at Tuapse port
stories.summary: Firefighters in Russia continued battling a blaze at the Black Sea port of Tuapse on Friday, more than 24 hours after the facility was struck by Ukrainian drone attacks. Local authorities reported the efforts were ongoing.

stories.title: Macron demands assurances after Iran opens Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron welcomed Iran's reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the Lebanon ceasefire. Macron called for assurances to ensure continued freedom of navigation through the vital waterway.

stories.title: Macron, Meloni, Starmer and Merz welcome Hormuz Strait reopening
stories.summary: French President Macron and British Prime Minister Starmer hosted a video conference with European leaders including Italy's Meloni and Germany's Merz to discuss deploying a multinational force to the Strait of Hormuz after the war in Iran ends. Macron welcomed Iran's reopening of the strait to commercial shipping but called for its unconditional reopening.

stories.title: Strait of Hormuz open for all ships following Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire, Trump confirms
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi announced that the Strait of Hormuz is open for all ships following the Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire. He said vessels must follow a coordinated route announced by Iran.

stories.title: Bushra Bibi shifted back to prison following eye surgery: Adiala jail authorities
stories.summary: Bushra Bibi, wife of imprisoned former Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan, was returned to Adiala jail in Rawalpindi after undergoing eye surgery. She is serving sentences in two corruption cases totaling multiple years.

stories.title: 1.2 million people uprooted by war
stories.summary: More than 1.2 million civilians in Lebanon have been displaced since war erupted in the Middle East in late February. Among those uprooted are thousands of young mothers and pregnant women, many of whom have been forced to give birth in makeshift camps or other inadequate facilities.

stories.title: India launches world's largest census
stories.summary: India has launched the first phase of what is expected to be the largest census ever conducted, covering an estimated 1.4 billion people. More than three million officials are participating in updating data from the last census in 2011. The results could lead to significant changes in welfare programs and electoral boundaries.

stories.title: 021kid: Bringing Iran's revolution to the London drill scene
stories.summary: An Iranian-born artist known as 021kid is channeling Iran's revolutionary movement through London's drill music scene. Operating from the UK, the musician draws on Tehran's underground culture to raise international awareness.

stories.title: French film director Christophe Ruggia gets five-year sentence on appeal for abusing child actor
stories.summary: French film director Christophe Ruggia received a five-year prison sentence on appeal on Friday for repeatedly sexually assaulting actor Adèle Haenel when she was a child in the early 2000s.

stories.title: Over 50% of Russian aerial targets neutralized by EW systems – Ground Forces
stories.summary: Ukrainian Ground Forces reported that electronic warfare systems are neutralizing more than 50% of Russian aerial targets. EW capabilities have become a key component of Ukraine's overall air defense strategy.

stories.title: Lebanese trickle home as ceasefire with Israel mostly holds
stories.summary: A ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon was largely holding as some displaced residents began returning home. The conflict killed more than 2,100 people in Lebanon and displaced approximately 1.2 million.

stories.title: Three charged after attempted arson at Iran International office in London
stories.summary: Three individuals were charged in connection with an attempted arson attack at the Iran International media office in London. They are scheduled to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on April 17.

stories.title: Lebanese overcome destroyed bridges and roads to return home
stories.summary: Lebanese civilians worked to reopen roads and bridges destroyed by Israeli strikes in order to return to their homes in southern Lebanon. The efforts came as a fragile 10-day ceasefire took hold amid continued security risks.

stories.title: Ukraine depends on Western air defense. Zelenskyy says that has to change – and partners are on board
stories.summary: President Zelensky, speaking after meetings in Lviv, outlined plans to boost domestic production of air defense missiles and systems to reduce Ukraine's dependence on Western-supplied equipment. He said international partners support the shift toward self-sufficiency as part of long-term security guarantees.

stories.title: Protesters worldwide mark Palestinian Prisoners' Day, call for repeal of execution law
stories.summary: Demonstrators around the world marked Palestinian Prisoners' Day, calling for the release of more than 9,000 Palestinian detainees held by Israel and demanding the repeal of a new Israeli law that permits the execution of Palestinian prisoners.

stories.title: Renewed calls for EU sanctions on Israel amid global outrage
stories.summary: Israel's deteriorating diplomatic relations with Germany and Italy have strengthened calls for EU trade sanctions against Israel. A decision could come during the EU foreign ministers' meeting scheduled for the following week.

stories.title: Italy's Meloni breaks with Trump over war in Iran, pope
stories.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has broken with U.S. President Donald Trump over the war in Iran and related diplomatic disputes. The disagreement may push Meloni to align more closely with Europe's center-right political bloc.

stories.title: Record number of Rohingya refugees died at sea last year, UNHCR says
stories.summary: UNHCR reported that a record number of Rohingya refugees died at sea last year while attempting dangerous crossings in South and Southeast Asia. The agency described the waters as an 'unmarked graveyard' for thousands of desperate Rohingya.

stories.title: Russia’s state pollster records 6 straight weeks of declining approval for Putin
stories.summary: Russia's state-owned polling agency VTsIOM recorded a sixth consecutive weekly decline in President Putin's approval rating.

stories.title: Iran to require IRGC permission for vessels passing through Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran announced that all vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz will be required to obtain permission from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. An Iranian official stated commercial vessels would be granted passage while naval vessels would be denied.

stories.title: Southern Lebanon’s only functioning hospital damaged by Israeli strikes
stories.summary: Al Jazeera reported that Tibnin Hospital, described as the only functioning hospital in southern Lebanon, sustained damage from Israeli strikes. Correspondent Obaida Hitto reported from the scene on conditions at the facility.

stories.title: Ukraine’s long-range strikes prompt new Russian threat against Europe
stories.summary: Ukraine launched unprecedented numbers of long-range drones that penetrated Russian airspace, targeting oil infrastructure. Russia responded with new threats directed at European countries in connection with the strikes.

stories.title: Private air defense unit downs jet-powered drone for first time
stories.summary: A private air defense unit operating in Ukraine's Kharkiv region shot down a jet-powered drone for the first time. The drone was traveling at speeds exceeding 400 km/h.

stories.title: Donald Trump claims to have ended a 10th war – but will the Lebanon ceasefire hold?
stories.summary: A ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon took effect after Donald Trump announced it on social media. Lasting peace depends on resolving a border dispute dating to 2000 and addressing Hezbollah's arsenal, with the situation on the ground remaining unstable.

stories.title: Leningrad Region Asks Veterans to Join New Air Defense Units After Drones Smash Oil Export Terminals
stories.summary: Authorities in Russia's Leningrad Region have called on military veterans to join newly formed air defense units. The appeal follows an increase in Ukrainian drone attacks on critical oil and export infrastructure in the region since mid-March.

stories.title: Macron urges permanent reopening of Hormuz Strait
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron and British Prime Minister Keir Starmer hosted a video conference with European allies to discuss deploying a multinational force to the Strait of Hormuz after the war in Iran ends. Macron welcomed Iran's announcement that the strait would reopen to commercial shipping during the ceasefire but called for its unconditional permanent reopening.

stories.title: Europe welcomes Hormuz Strait reopening
stories.summary: French President Macron and British Prime Minister Starmer hosted a video conference with European allies to discuss deploying a multinational force to the Strait of Hormuz after the Iran war ends. Macron welcomed Iran's announcement to reopen the waterway during the ceasefire but called for its unconditional reopening.

stories.title: Trump and Hegseth American nutter-o-cracy gets Iran sanity check
stories.summary: Writer Alex Foley argues that the US war on Iran exposed disarray and ideological extremism in American leadership rather than calculated strategy. The article contends the conflict has eroded US global credibility.

stories.title: Trump and Hesgeth American nutter-o-cracy gets Iran sanity check
stories.summary: An analysis argues that the US war on Iran revealed internal disarray and ideological extremism within the Trump administration rather than a calculated military strategy, eroding American global credibility.

stories.title: ‘Cruelly hot’: Japan devises new term for heatwave days
stories.summary: Japan has introduced a new weather classification term for extreme heat days following its hottest summer on record in 2024, as rising global temperatures due to climate change drive more frequent heatwaves.

stories.title: REPLAY:  EU leaders deliver joint statement on Strait of Hormuz opening
stories.summary: French President Macron and British Prime Minister Starmer hosted a video conference with European allies on the possible deployment of a multinational force to the Strait of Hormuz. Macron welcomed Iran's announcement to reopen the waterway for commercial shipping during the ceasefire but called for its unconditional reopening.

stories.title: Mohsin Naqvi, FIA chief direct timely complaint redressal, transparent investigations during Karachi visit
stories.summary: Pakistani Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and FIA Director General Dr. Usman Anwar visited the FIA Karachi Zone, directing officials to ensure timely complaint redressal and transparent investigations.

stories.title: How two ceasefires and opening of Hormuz could boost Iran talks
stories.summary: Diplomatic efforts involving ceasefires in Lebanon and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz are under way, but questions remain about whether the progress is sufficient to prevent a resumption of hostilities between the US, Israel, and Iran.

stories.title: Ukraine receives 90% of funds backed by revenues from Russia’s frozen assets – Finance Ministry
stories.summary: Ukraine's Finance Ministry reported the country has received approximately $45 billion, representing 90% of expected funding backed by revenues from frozen Russian assets.

stories.title: Israel's campaign of terror in Lebanon takes another psychopathic turn
stories.summary: Israel has continued bombing Lebanese civilian areas despite the ceasefire, with strikes reported in locations including Qana in southern Lebanon. First responders recovered bodies from destroyed buildings following an Israeli strike on 12 April 2026.

stories.title: Turkey’s Erdogan urges Iran, US to use ceasefire to push for lasting peace
stories.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan urged the United States and Iran to use their ceasefire to pursue lasting peace, speaking at the fifth Antalya Diplomacy Forum. He warned against Israeli provocations and emphasized that diplomacy remains the shortest path to peace.

stories.title: London police investigating incident near Israeli embassy
stories.summary: London's Metropolitan Police are investigating an incident near the Israeli embassy in Kensington Palace Gardens on 17 April 2026. The investigation follows the discovery of debris at the site and an online video claiming a drone attack on the embassy.

stories.title: Iran reopens Strait of Hormuz to commercial ships during ceasefire
stories.summary: Iran reopened the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping during a ceasefire. U.S. President Donald Trump acknowledged the move but stated that the naval blockade on Iran would remain until a peace deal is signed.

stories.title: US naval blockade of Iran to persist despite opening of Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: President Trump announced on Truth Social that the Strait of Hormuz is open for commercial passage but that the US naval blockade on Iran will remain in effect until a deal with Iran is fully completed. Trump indicated negotiations are largely settled and the process should conclude quickly.

stories.title: China steps out of the shadows in Iran war
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping broke a six-week silence on the war in Iran, pledging a "constructive" role in ending the conflict. Beijing faces a balancing act between its long-term partnership with Iran and its broader strategic interests in the Middle East.

stories.title: US delays weapons to NATO’s eastern flank – Iran war drains stockpiles Europe was counting on
stories.summary: The United States has informed NATO countries on its eastern flank that planned weapons deliveries will be delayed. The conflict with Iran has drained U.S. stockpiles that European allies and Ukraine's air defense supply chain were relying on.

stories.title: Deportees arrive in Kinshasa from U.S. under Trump agreement
stories.summary: Approximately 15 deportees arrived in Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo, from the United States on Friday. The deportations were carried out under an agreement between the Congolese government and the Trump administration.

stories.title: Northrop Grumman’s Talon IQ testbed hot-swaps AI brains mid-flight
stories.summary: Northrop Grumman demonstrated its Talon IQ testbed aircraft's ability to swap between different companies' AI software systems during flight. Senior director Dan Salluce described how different behavioral algorithms could take control of the platform while it was airborne.

stories.title: Protesters worldwide mark Palestinian Prisoners' Day, call for repeal of execution law
stories.summary: Demonstrations took place worldwide to mark Palestinian Prisoners' Day, with protesters calling for the repeal of a recently passed Israeli law permitting execution of Palestinian detainees. Events were held in multiple countries, including in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron.

stories.title: IDF on high alert amid fragile, temporary ceasefires in Iran and Lebanon
stories.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces remain on high alert amid fragile, temporary ceasefires on both the Iran and Lebanon fronts. Israeli officials assess that Iran will quickly attempt to rebuild its military capabilities despite an estimated $100 billion in damages from the bombing campaign.

stories.title: Ukraine hopes to begin Gripen pilot training this year – Zelensky
stories.summary: President Zelensky said Ukraine hopes to begin training pilots on Swedish-made Gripen fighter jets this year. He is set to discuss the timeline with Sweden's King Carl XVI Gustaf during the monarch's visit.

stories.title: Iran: Internet blackout highlights real toll of censorship
stories.summary: The Iranian government imposed an internet blackout affecting millions of citizens, restricting their access to global communications and disrupting businesses. The shutdown underscores state control over digital infrastructure in Iran.

stories.title: Aner Shapira, hero of October 7, is heard in duet with Yehudit Ravitz
stories.summary: Israeli singer Yehudit Ravitz has recorded a duet with the late Aner Shapira, who was killed during the October 7 attack. The song, titled "Come on, Let's Get Out of Here," is based on a rap originally composed by Shapira.

stories.title: EU to restore Syria relations, increase trade and security ties
stories.summary: The European Union is preparing to restore diplomatic relations with Syria and increase trade and security ties. Plans include integrating Syria into regional infrastructure projects such as the India–Middle East–Europe Economic Corridor.

stories.title: Controversy as Lebanese banker Sehnaoui is praised for supporting Israel
stories.summary: US envoy Morgan Ortagus publicly praised Lebanese banker Antoun Sehnaoui, calling him a committed Zionist. The remarks drew controversy given that Israel had been conducting military operations against Lebanon at the time.

stories.title: Can Pakistan secure Iran-US nuclear compromise, as Trump says deal ‘close’?
stories.summary: Pakistan's civilian and military leaders have been shuttling between key capitals to help broker an Iran-US nuclear compromise. President Trump stated a deal is close and suggested he may travel to Islamabad to sign an agreement.

stories.title: Gunmen kidnap students heading to exams in Nigeria's Benue state
stories.summary: Gunmen abducted secondary school students traveling to university entrance exams and other travelers in Benue state, central Nigeria. Governor of the region confirmed the incident, marking the first reported student kidnapping in Nigeria this year.

stories.title: 'Wake-up call for Europeans to step up: There’s been a lack of investment' in defence
stories.summary: A defense expert examined the emerging European-led initiative to secure the Strait of Hormuz in a post-war context, describing it as a strategic shift. European actors are attempting to shape peace and stability conditions independently of a U.S.-led framework, reflecting broader questions about defense investment and transatlantic relations.

stories.title: ‘Maman is finally free!’: French widow, 86, flies home after ICE detention ordeal
stories.summary: Marie-Thérèse Ross-Mahé, an 86-year-old French widow, was released from U.S. immigration detention and returned to France after being arrested at her Alabama home for overstaying her visa. She had moved to the United States decades ago to marry a U.S. Army captain she met in the 1950s.

stories.title: Russian drones hit Ukraine's Danube port, officials say
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack overnight damaged port infrastructure at Izmail, Ukraine's largest Danube river port. One drone also strayed into Romanian territory. Both Ukrainian and Romanian authorities confirmed the incident on Friday.

stories.title: Necropolitics and the manufacture of indifference in Iran and beyond
stories.summary: A commentary examines how modern geopolitics normalizes civilian casualties as "collateral damage," drawing connections between conflicts in Iran, the Levant, and broader global power dynamics.

stories.title: Man found guilty of rape that led to Andrew Malkinson’s wrongful imprisonment
stories.summary: Paul Quinn was found guilty in a UK court of a 2003 rape in Salford for which Andrew Malkinson had been wrongfully imprisoned for 17 years. Quinn's conviction came after fresh forensic analysis identified traces of his DNA on the victim, resolving one of Britain's most notorious miscarriages of justice.

stories.title: US envoy Barrack plays down idea Turkey could be 'next Iran' for Israel
stories.summary: US envoy Tom Barrack, speaking at the Antalya Diplomacy Forum, downplayed the prospect of conflict between Turkey and Israel, characterizing rising tensions as rhetoric. He urged regional cooperation between the two countries on security and energy matters.

stories.title: Iran says Strait of Hormuz reopened after Lebanon ceasefire
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared the Strait of Hormuz completely open for all commercial vessels for the duration of the Lebanon ceasefire. The announcement was made in coordination with Iran's Ports and Maritime Organisation.

stories.title: Israeli opposition angry over Lebanon truce, label it 'betrayal'
stories.summary: Israeli opposition members criticized Prime Minister Netanyahu for agreeing to a truce in Lebanon, calling it a betrayal. Meanwhile, Iran's parliament speaker praised the ceasefire agreement.

stories.title: Boaz Bismuth, it’s time to redesign Israel’s overall public diplomacy structure - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion article argues that Israel needs structural reform of its public diplomacy apparatus, not just increased funding. It contends that without integrating domestic considerations alongside international priorities, Israel's messaging will remain fragmented.

stories.title: Ukrainian forces destroy Russian air defense system in occupied Mariupol
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces destroyed a Russian air defense system in the occupied city of Mariupol. The strike targeted Russian military assets in the temporarily occupied Donetsk region port city.

stories.title: Hours after ceasefire, a lifeline to south Lebanon reopens
stories.summary: The damaged Qasmiyeh Bridge in south Lebanon was partially reopened on Friday as a ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah took effect, allowing tens of thousands of displaced residents to begin returning home.

stories.title: Israel can talk to Lebanon - so why not the Palestinians? - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece questions why Israel can negotiate with Lebanon but has no comparable diplomatic engagement with the Palestinians. It asks about the Israeli government's long-term policy vision for the West Bank.

stories.title: Press association denounces Israel’s use of altered image to depict slain journalist
stories.summary: A Lebanese press association condemned Israel's use of a digitally altered image to justify the killing of Lebanese journalist Ali Shoeib in an Israeli strike on March 28. The Israeli army later admitted that the published image depicting Shoeib in a Hezbollah uniform had been photoshopped.

stories.title: Iran war: What does Tehran expect from fresh talks with US?
stories.summary: Experts are anticipating a second round of negotiations between Iran and the United States. While a diplomatic breakthrough is considered possible, analysts caution that significant obstacles remain and an agreement is far from guaranteed.

stories.title: The rape case that became one of Britain’s greatest miscarriages of justice
stories.summary: Paul Quinn's conviction, 23 years after a 2003 rape in Salford, exposed how an innocent man, Andrew Malkinson, was wrongly jailed for 17 years. The case is regarded as one of Britain's most significant miscarriages of justice, with failures affecting both the victim and the wrongly convicted man.

stories.title: Three charged after attempted arson at Iran International office
stories.summary: Three British individuals—two men and a teenager—have been charged with arson with intent to endanger life after allegedly throwing an ignited container toward the Iran International media office in London.

stories.title: Ceasefire with Israel brings respite to Lebanon, but obstacles to peace remain
stories.summary: A ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon has halted weeks of fighting, bringing relief to Lebanese civilians. However, significant obstacles remain to achieving a lasting peace agreement.

stories.title: Chinese LED chipmaker’s purchase of Dutch firm collapses after US opposition
stories.summary: China's Sanan Optoelectronics and its Malaysian partner abandoned their $239 million bid for Dutch technology company Lumileds Holding after the U.S. Committee on Foreign Investment (CFIUS) raised objections. The collapse marks another setback for Chinese technology investment overseas.

stories.title: Czech Foreign Ministry Summons Russian Ambassador Over Russian Military Threats
stories.summary: The Czech Foreign Ministry summoned Russia's ambassador over military threats made by senior Russian official Dmitry Medvedev. Medvedev had stated that production facilities in the Czech Republic were potential targets for Russian armed forces.

stories.title: Marines starting early work on sixth-gen fighter jet concepts
stories.summary: A senior U.S. Marine Corps general indicated that the service is beginning early conceptual work on a sixth-generation fighter jet. The general suggested the future Marine aircraft would likely resemble the U.S. Navy's F/A-XX next-generation fighter program, though development remains in its earliest stages.

stories.title: Russia’s Black Sea Fleet once fired missiles from the Mediterranean. Now it can barely leave Novorossiysk.
stories.summary: Analysts say years of Ukrainian drone and missile strikes have severely degraded Russia's Black Sea Fleet, reducing it largely to a land-support role. The fleet, once capable of launching missiles from the Mediterranean, is now largely confined to the port of Novorossiysk.

stories.title: King of Sweden visits Ukraine, meets Zelensky in Lviv
stories.summary: King Carl XVI Gustaf of Sweden visited Ukraine and met with President Zelensky in the western city of Lviv. The visit included discussions on military cooperation and support for Ukraine.

stories.title: How the MV-75 Cheyenne II is pushing the service to re-think its aviation lineup
stories.summary: The U.S. Army is evaluating the MV-75 Cheyenne II tiltrotor aircraft, a development that could reshape the service's aviation fleet. Potential changes include extending the range of Apache helicopters, assigning new missions to the Black Hawk, and exploring drone-based aerial refueling capabilities.

stories.title: Russia sank the Henichesk in 2022. In June, a ship bearing its name will join Ukraine’s Navy — but cannot sail home yet
stories.summary: A replacement vessel named Henichesk, after a ship Russia sank in 2022, is training in the Netherlands and will join Ukraine's Navy under the Ukrainian flag in June. The ship will remain in a British port until the war ends and Black Sea access reopens.

stories.title: ‘We’ve lost a lot’: Lebanese residents return to bombed-out homes in south Beirut
stories.summary: Residents of Beirut's southern suburbs began returning to their homes on Friday after a 10-day truce between Israel and Lebanon took effect. Many found their neighborhoods devastated by Israel's sustained bombing campaign, with little left of their former homes.

stories.title: Birmingham is awash with local election candidates – but will result be a ‘coalition of chaos’?
stories.summary: Birmingham faces a highly fragmented field of candidates from Labour, Conservatives, Greens, Reform, and independents in upcoming local council elections. Observers fear the crowded contest could produce an ungovernable council, with no single party able to secure a working majority.

stories.title: Russian strike halts Chernihiv CHP plant, leaving city without hot water
stories.summary: A Russian strike on the night of April 17 forced the shutdown of the Chernihiv combined heat and power plant, leaving the northern Ukrainian city without hot water. The attack targeted critical civilian energy infrastructure.

stories.title: No ceasefire for Iran’s Kurdish opposition parties in exile
stories.summary: Iran has intensified drone attacks on Iranian Kurdish opposition parties based in Iraq's Kurdistan region since the ceasefire announcement on 8 April. On 14 April, an Iranian drone strike in Sulaimaniyah killed Ghazal Moulan, a 19-year-old fighter with the Komala Toilers of Kurdistan.

stories.title: Lebanese President Aoun calls for negotiations following ceasefire
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun described the ceasefire with Israel as an opportunity to advance negotiations, urging that it not be squandered. He stated the Lebanese army would play a central role in overseeing the Israeli military's withdrawal from Lebanese territory.

stories.title: China turns Taiwan’s own voices against it in information war
stories.summary: China is conducting an information warfare campaign against Taiwan, using Taiwanese voices and social media to undermine public confidence. The operations coincided with large-scale Chinese military drills involving warships and fighter jets around Taiwan in December.

stories.title: Iran: Israel was forced into Lebanon ceasefire
stories.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated in a televised address that Israel was forced into declaring a ceasefire in Lebanon. He thanked Pakistan for its diplomatic role and reiterated that Iran has never sought nuclear weapons.

stories.title: Iran, US say Strait of Hormuz is fully open to commercial vessels
stories.summary: Iran and the United States both announced that the Strait of Hormuz was fully open to commercial vessels after nearly seven weeks of blockade that sent global energy prices soaring. President Trump acknowledged the development on social media.

stories.title: Iran war energy shock drives Asia and Africa nuclear power plans
stories.summary: The energy disruptions caused by the Iran conflict have accelerated nuclear power expansion plans in Africa and Asia. Nations with existing nuclear plants are increasing output to address short-term energy supply shortages.

stories.title: Where is US-Kuwaiti journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin?
stories.summary: International alarm is growing over the detention of U.S.-Kuwaiti journalist Ahmed Shihab-Eldin in Kuwait after he shared publicly available content related to the Iran war. Press freedom and human rights groups say his arrest reflects tightening censorship in Kuwait and the broader Gulf region.

stories.title: Sweden rights groups blast ‘honest living’ criteria for migrants
stories.summary: Sweden's government faces criticism from rights groups and legal experts over a proposed requirement that migrants demonstrate "honest living" to obtain or renew residency permits. If approved by parliament, the measure would take effect on July 13.

stories.title: UK police search near Israel’s London Embassy after threat of drone attack with ‘dangerous substances’
stories.summary: UK police in protective gear searched the area around Israel's London embassy in Kensington Palace Gardens after a group posted a video claiming a drone attack with dangerous substances. Police found no evidence of a strike and said there was no danger to the public; all embassy staff were reported safe.

stories.title: Israeli attacks killed over 38,000 women, girls in Gaza since October 2023, UN says
stories.summary: A UN Women report found that Israeli attacks in the Gaza Strip killed more than 38,000 women and girls between October 2023 and the end of 2025, comprising over half of the estimated 71,000 total deaths recorded by Palestinian health authorities.

stories.title: Ukraine returns another group of children from Russian-occupied Kherson region
stories.summary: Ukraine successfully returned another group of children from Russian-occupied areas of the Kherson region to Ukrainian-controlled territory. The effort is part of ongoing repatriation operations for minors displaced during the Russian occupation.

stories.title: UN Sudan chief says country ‘abandoned’ after three years of war
stories.summary: The UN's top humanitarian official in Sudan, Denise Brown, said the country has been "abandoned" after three years of war. She urged the international community not to forget about the ongoing crisis in Sudan.

stories.title: Italy should rethink nuclear power, IEA chief says
stories.summary: International Energy Agency chief recommended that Italy reconsider nuclear power as an energy option. Italy currently has no operating nuclear reactors and relies heavily on energy imports, including nuclear-generated electricity from neighboring France.

stories.title: Middle Israel: Orbán’s defeat, Hungary's political shift, and lessons for Israel - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece draws parallels between Hungary's recent political shift away from Viktor Orbán's authoritarianism and potential lessons for Israel. The analysis asks whether Israel can learn from Hungary's democratic transition to address its own political challenges.

stories.title: ‘Waiting without answers’: Gaza mother’s fear for her three imprisoned sons
stories.summary: On Palestinian Prisoners' Day, Inaam al-Dahdouh, a mother in Gaza, continues to seek information about her three sons detained by Israel two years ago. Their status and whereabouts remain unknown.

stories.title: Iran foreign minister says Strait of Hormuz ‘completely open’
stories.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi announced that the Strait of Hormuz is completely open for all commercial vessels during the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire period, in coordination with Iran's Ports and Maritime Organisation.

stories.title: In turnaround, Energy Ministry calls to relocate, not close, Haifa’s Iran-targeted Bazan oil refinery
stories.summary: Israel's Energy Ministry reversed its earlier position and now calls for relocating rather than closing the Bazan oil refinery in Haifa, which had been targeted by Iran. Officials cited 30 months of war as evidence of the need for domestic petroleum production rather than reliance on imports.

stories.title: How did the ceasefire in Lebanon happen, and what's next?
stories.summary: A series of political developments in the hours before the Lebanon ceasefire announcement paved the way for the agreement. The report examines the diplomatic maneuvering that led to the sudden halt in hostilities.

stories.title: MP accused of ties to Russian security services and Crimea property deal moved to house arrest after sanctions blocked bail payment
stories.summary: Ukrainian MP Shufrych, accused of ties to Russian security services, was moved to house arrest after sanctions blocked his bail payment. Prosecutors allege he paid a Russian National Guard unit to guard property he owns in Crimea, constituting financing of an occupying force.

stories.title: The Palestinian woman on the cover of L'Espresso: Settlers were ready to kill us
stories.summary: Meead Abu al-Rub, a Palestinian woman from the occupied West Bank who appeared on the cover of Italian magazine L'Espresso, described an encounter with armed Israeli settlers in October 2025. She told Middle East Eye that the settlers were prepared to kill them.

stories.title: Iran war energy shock threatens Southeast Asia’s supply chains. A win for China?
stories.summary: Some Western buyers at the Canton Fair in Guangzhou, China, are shifting orders back from Southeast Asia to Chinese suppliers amid energy-market volatility linked to the conflict in Iran. Exhibitors reported increased inquiries for home appliances and new energy products.

stories.title: Romanian broad ruling coalition parties must continue despite tensions, president says
stories.summary: Romanian President Nicusor Dan stated that the broad ruling coalition of four pro-EU parties must continue governing despite internal tensions. The coalition's largest party is expected to call for the prime minister's resignation on Monday.

stories.title: China says its military activities around Taiwan are 'reasonable, justified'
stories.summary: China defended its military activities around Taiwan as "reasonable" and "justified." The statement comes amid ongoing tensions over Beijing's territorial claims in the Taiwan Strait.

stories.title: Iran has opened Strait of Hormuz but will the US ease its economic squeeze?
stories.summary: The U.S. continued economic pressure on Iran even as Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared the Strait of Hormuz fully open to commercial shipping. Chinese observers warned the U.S. economic squeeze strategy could backfire on its own economy.

stories.title: Iran War: Energy shock drives Africa, Asia to nuclear power
stories.summary: The ongoing war involving Iran and resulting global energy disruptions are pushing countries in Africa and Asia to accelerate nuclear power development. The energy shock has prompted governments to seek alternatives to volatile fossil fuel markets.

stories.title: Ukrainian Air Assault Forces' training center helps recruits overcome fear of weapons
stories.summary: The 199th Training Center of the Ukrainian Air Assault Forces runs a program helping new recruits overcome their fear of weapons. Instructors frame weapons training in terms of protecting life to ease recruits' psychological adjustment.

stories.title: Trump says Iran war should end ‘soon’, both sides may meet at weekend
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump indicated the war with Iran should end soon and suggested both sides may meet over the weekend. Trump said the U.S. may extend its ceasefire with Iran but noted it might not be necessary as Tehran reportedly wants a deal.

stories.title: The three clocks of the Iran war
stories.summary: An analysis outlines three competing timelines shaping the Iran conflict: the Trump administration racing against US midterm elections, Iran pursuing a strategy of endurance, and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu seeking prolonged military engagement.

stories.title: World Cup 2026: Saudi Arabia sack coach Herve Renard
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia dismissed head coach Hervé Renard despite the team having already qualified for the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The French coach had previously won the Africa Cup of Nations with both Zambia and Ivory Coast.

stories.title: US to delay weapons deliveries to some European countries due to Iran war, sources say
stories.summary: The United States has informed some European allies that select weapons deliveries may face delays as the ongoing Iran war continues to draw on American weapons stockpiles. The delays affect planned shipments to multiple European countries.

stories.title: NATO revamps air surveillance approach for the ‘cost-war’ of low-flying drones, missiles
stories.summary: NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Transformation, Adm. Pierre Vandier, announced that the alliance is overhauling its air surveillance strategy to better counter low-flying drones and missiles. Vandier cited lessons learned from the Ukraine war and the Iran conflict as key drivers behind the shift toward a more cost-effective detection approach.

stories.title: With DEI out of favor, some push to honor Jewish philanthropist behind 5,000 Black schools
stories.summary: Lawmakers, archivists, and activists in the United States are pushing to honor Julius Rosenwald, a Jewish philanthropist and Sears executive who partnered with Booker T. Washington to fund approximately 5,000 schools for Black students across the Jim Crow South between 1917 and 1932.

stories.title: How the Lebanon ceasefire is viewed in Israel
stories.summary: Al Jazeera reported on reactions in Israel to the ceasefire with Lebanon, with correspondent Tony Cheng describing how Israeli civilians and media are responding to the halt in hostilities.

stories.title: EU to restore Syria relations, strengthen trade and security ties, document shows
stories.summary: The European Union is moving to restore diplomatic relations with Syria and strengthen trade and security ties, according to a leaked document. Syria, under interim President Ahmed al-Sharaa, is seeking broader international integration after most Western sanctions were lifted late last year.

stories.title: My Word: The ‘I-P Test’ of hypocrisy - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that international actors apply double standards when assessing the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. It cites Pakistan's and Spain's positions on Israel as examples of what the author characterizes as hypocrisy in global diplomacy.

stories.title: Global warming causes Colombian glacier to disappear
stories.summary: Colombia's last glacier has completely disappeared, with its surface area shrinking from five square kilometers in the 19th century to zero today due to global warming.

stories.title: Israelis upset by Iran ceasefire, pessimistic about war’s outcome, poll shows
stories.summary: A poll conducted shortly after the Iran ceasefire found that most Israelis expressed despair, anger, or confusion about the truce. Respondents were largely pessimistic about the war's outcome and skeptical of claims that Iran had been significantly weakened by the bombing campaign.

stories.title: Painkiller Pipeline: 300 Million Tapentadol Pills Sent from India to West Africa
stories.summary: A Bellingcat investigation, conducted in collaboration with Indian outlet Newslaundry, found that Indian pharmaceutical companies exported over 320 million tapentadol pills to West Africa over the past three years. The synthetic opioid has not been approved by regulators in the receiving West African countries.

stories.title: Gloomy weather can’t take shine off Hong Kong Sevens for visiting rugby fans
stories.summary: The Hong Kong Sevens rugby tournament kicked off its 50th anniversary edition at the 50,000-seat Kai Tak Stadium despite gloomy weather and an amber rainstorm warning. Organizers appeared to have resolved food shortage issues that affected the previous year's event.

stories.title: Communities in Dagestan Remain Isolated After Floods
stories.summary: Floods triggered by two waves of heavy rainfall in late March and early April in Dagestan, Russia, killed at least seven people and displaced more than 6,200. Several communities remain isolated.

stories.title: NATO will not collapse and US will defend its allies, Estonian minister says
stories.summary: Estonia's defence minister stated that NATO will not collapse and that the United States will continue to defend its allies, while warning that Europe is not yet capable of confronting Moscow independently.

stories.title: Amnesty condemns Burkina Faso junta’s sweeping ban of NGOs
stories.summary: Amnesty International has condemned Burkina Faso's ruling military junta for imposing a sweeping ban on non-governmental organisations. The junta, which seized power in a 2022 coup, has intensified its crackdown on NGOs operating in the country.

stories.title: Iran negotiators were escorted home from talks by Pakistani air force, fearing Israeli hit
stories.summary: Iranian negotiators returning from peace talks were escorted home by the Pakistani air force due to concerns that Israel might attempt to assassinate them. A regional diplomat said Pakistan insisted on providing the escort after a potential threat was raised during discussions.

stories.title: Levin says judge selection panel to meet, but no Supreme Court picks until his nominees okayed
stories.summary: Israeli Justice Minister Yariv Levin announced that a judge selection panel would convene but refused to approve Supreme Court appointments until his preferred nominees are accepted. He stated only district-level judges would be selected and announced reforms to family, traffic, and juvenile courts.

stories.title: Israeli military will “continue to hold” areas captured in Southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz announced that the military will continue to hold all areas captured in southern Lebanon. He reiterated Israel's commitment to disarming Hezbollah and stated that operations, including demolition of border village structures, are ongoing.

stories.title: Chinese trucks could go 100% electric, halving road transport oil use: industry
stories.summary: Industry estimates suggest China's heavy-duty truck fleet could eventually become nearly 100 percent electric, potentially halving the country's road transport oil consumption. Sany Truck chairman Liang Linhe discussed the projection at a forum on intelligent electric vehicle development in Beijing.

stories.title: Lebanon becomes key to Iran-US peace talks amid fears of Israel’s ‘hegemony’
stories.summary: A 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon, arranged by Pakistan with Saudi assistance, became a key condition for advancing Iran-U.S. peace talks. Analysts say the Lebanon truce was instrumental in clearing the path for a potentially conclusive second round of negotiations in Islamabad.

stories.title: Pro-Iran hackers appear to increase critical infrastructure cyberattacks
stories.summary: Pro-Iran hacking groups appear to be escalating cyberattacks against critical infrastructure. One group claimed responsibility for breaching the Los Angeles Metro system. The U.S. federal government has issued warnings about vulnerabilities in critical infrastructure networks.

stories.title: Ukrainian Special Forces strike Russia's Rubikon drone base near Mariupol
stories.summary: Ukraine's Special Operations Forces released footage of an overnight strike on April 17 targeting a logistics base of Russia's Rubikon drone technology center in occupied Manhush, Donetsk region, near Mariupol.

stories.title: Starmer, Macron push forward efforts to reopen Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: French President Macron and UK Prime Minister Starmer chaired a meeting of allies on Friday to consider sending a multinational force to secure the Strait of Hormuz. The initiative aims to ensure security and free-flowing trade through the waterway once the current Iran conflict ends.

stories.title: Britain, France chair meeting on Hormuz
stories.summary: French President Macron and British Prime Minister Starmer hosted a video conference with European allies at the Élysée Palace to discuss deploying a multinational force to the Strait of Hormuz. The proposed force would ensure safe passage through the critical waterway after the war in Iran concludes.

stories.title: The most dangerous drone unit Russia has just lost its logistics base near Mariupol — Ukraine found it and burned it
stories.summary: Ukraine's Special Operations Forces destroyed the logistics base of Rubikon, an elite Russian drone unit, near occupied Mariupol. Rubikon operates nearly every type of Russian attack and reconnaissance drone except Shahed models.

stories.title: Italy: 25 hostages freed as Naples bank gang vanishes underground
stories.summary: Three masked robbers held 25 people hostage during a bank heist in Naples, Italy, on Thursday, April 16, 2026. The perpetrators escaped through a tunnel connected to the city's sewer network and remain at large.

stories.title: Pakistan starts preparing for next round of U.S.-Iran talks: officials
stories.summary: Pakistan has begun preparations to host the next round of direct U.S.-Iran talks. The previous round, held in Pakistan on April 12, 2026, ended without an agreement.

stories.title: Myanmar to free more than 4,000 prisoners in amnesty
stories.summary: Myanmar's military government announced it will free more than 4,000 prisoners in an amnesty. Such releases are customary in Myanmar, typically occurring around Independence Day in January and the country's New Year celebrations in April.

stories.title: As commodities reshape geopolitics, currency pecking order gets a reset
stories.summary: The Middle East conflict is disrupting global energy markets and boosting commodity currencies such as the Norwegian crown and Australian dollar, both up over 7% against the U.S. dollar this year.

stories.title: Foreign Ministers from Turkey, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt to meet at Antalya forum
stories.summary: Foreign ministers from Turkey, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt convened at the Antalya Diplomatic Forum for a third round of multilateral talks. The meeting aimed to preserve the existing ceasefire, work toward a permanent resolution, and plan for post-war regional arrangements.

stories.title: Nigeria: How Jonathan, Wife Chased Me Out of PDP - Amaechi
stories.summary: Former Nigerian Minister of Transportation Rotimi Amaechi claimed that then-President Goodluck Jonathan and his wife Patience Jonathan forced him out of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

stories.title: Namibia: Loubser's Drama Club Opens Global Doors
stories.summary: Windhoek-based acting coach Michelle Loubser has been expanding Namibia's performing arts scene through a drama club she founded in 2020, creating international opportunities for local talent.

stories.title: Nigeria: Tinubu Signs 2026 Appropriation Bill, 2025 Budget Extension
stories.summary: Nigerian President Bola Tinubu signed the 2026 Appropriation Bill, authorizing aggregate expenditure of ₦68.32 trillion. He also signed legislation extending the 2025 budget implementation period from March 31 to June 30, 2026.

stories.title: Living under threat of landslides: The Italian villages at risk of disappearing
stories.summary: Italy faces significant risks from hydrogeological disasters including landslides, sinkholes, and floods due to its mountainous terrain and fragile geology. Over 500,000 buildings and nearly 38,000 churches, monuments, and heritage sites are situated in landslide-prone areas.

stories.title: Liberia: World Bank, Liberia Assess Economic Stability Under Oil Pressure
stories.summary: Liberian Finance Minister Augustine Kpehe Ngafuan and a delegation met with senior World Bank officials, including Ousmane Diagana, to discuss economic stability. The talks focused on mounting oil price pressures linked to the ongoing Middle East crisis.

stories.title: Liberia: Grand Kru Community Reclaims Identity With Name Change
stories.summary: The Nimeah Community in Grand Kru County, Liberia, officially renamed Andrewville and Wilsonville as Nimeah Plantation and Nimeah Beach. Residents described the decision as a historic restoration of cultural identity and local heritage.

stories.title: Liberia: Linsu, MOE Commence 2026 Nat'l Students Symposium
stories.summary: The Liberia National Students' Union and the Ministry of Education launched the 2026 National Students' Symposium on April 16 at the Ellen Johnson Sirleaf Ministerial Complex outside Monrovia.

stories.title: Kremlin denies Putin’s isolation from Russia’s woes amid blogger’s criticism
stories.summary: The Kremlin denied that President Vladimir Putin was insulated from bad news after Russian celebrity blogger Viktoria Bonya accused top officials of not honestly briefing the president about the country's problems. Her widely watched video listed five issues she claimed were being concealed from Putin.

stories.title: Ethiopia: Liberia, Ethiopia Ink Major Ai Agreements
stories.summary: Liberia and Ethiopia signed bilateral agreements on artificial intelligence, science, technology, and education during President Joseph Nyuma Boakai's two-day state visit to Addis Ababa. The accords mark a significant step in cooperation between the two African nations.

stories.title: Nigeria: Blord Granted Bail - Sowore
stories.summary: Nigerian social media figure Blord was granted bail after being remanded in custody since April 1. He had been detained with a court date set for April 27, according to reports.

stories.title: Nigeria: Hospital Malnutrition Worsening Due to Delayed Care - Experts
stories.summary: Health experts in Nigeria warned that hospital malnutrition is worsening due to delayed patient care. They called for an urgent overhaul of clinical nutrition protocols, including a 'golden hour' approach to nutritional screening upon admission.

stories.title: Nigeria: Nigerian Government Graduates 744 Ex-Insurgents Under Deradicalisation Programme
stories.summary: Nigeria graduated 744 former insurgents under a government deradicalization program. Chief of Defence Staff Olufemi Oluyede said the initiative combines military pressure with rehabilitation to curb extremism and stabilize affected communities.

stories.title: Macron and Starmer host allies for summit on Hormuz maritime security
stories.summary: French President Macron and UK Prime Minister Starmer hosted an allied summit focused on maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz. The United States did not participate in the France- and UK-led discussions on a post-war maritime force.

stories.title: Nigeria: Australian Firm Gets Six Lithium Mining Licences in Nigeria
stories.summary: An Australian firm acquired six lithium mining licences in Nigeria, comprising four exploration permits and two small-scale mining licences. The licences were previously held by Continental Lithium Limited.

stories.title: Ukraine MPs vote themselves untracked monthly cash inside an IMF-mandated tax bill
stories.summary: Ukraine's parliament voted to grant MPs an untracked monthly cash allowance of $4,555 with no reporting requirements or liability. The provision was included in a tax bill mandated by the International Monetary Fund and signed into law on April 15.

stories.title: Nigeria: Don't Increase Airfare or Suspend Operations, Nigerian Govt Begs Airlines
stories.summary: The Nigerian government urged airlines not to raise airfares or suspend operations amid surging fuel costs. The Airline Operators of Nigeria reported that aviation fuel prices had risen to about N3,300 per litre from N900 in February.

stories.title: Cyprus: Global politics felt at Candidates chess tournaments
stories.summary: The FIDE Candidates chess tournaments were held in Cyprus, drawing top international players. Geopolitical tensions related to Russia and the Middle East conflict cast a shadow over the competition.

stories.title: Nigeria: 2027 - Atiku Can Contest but Should Consider His Age - Amaechi
stories.summary: Former Nigerian Transportation Minister Rotimi Amaechi said ex-Vice President Atiku Abubakar is legally qualified to run for president in 2027. However, Amaechi urged Atiku to consider his age and capacity before contesting.

stories.title: Palestinians hand over suspect in 1982 attack on Jewish restaurant in Paris
stories.summary: Palestinian authorities handed over Hicham Harb, a suspect in the 1982 attack on a Jewish restaurant on Rue des Rosiers in Paris. Harb is accused of directing the assault and acting as one of the gunmen who fired on diners.

stories.title: UK’s Starmer faces calls to resign as Mandelson row reignites
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer faced renewed calls to resign after it emerged that former U.S. Ambassador Peter Mandelson had failed security vetting but was still allowed to take up the post before being fired over ties to Jeffrey Epstein.

stories.title: Trump says US focused on Iran despite ongoing Ukraine peace efforts
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump stated that while progress is being made on Ukraine peace efforts, the United States is currently prioritizing the resolution of its situation with Iran.

stories.title: Can Hungary wean itself off Russian energy, as its new leader has promised?
stories.summary: Hungary's new political leader has pledged to reduce the country's dependence on Russian energy imports, marking a departure from former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán's policies. The feasibility of this transition remains uncertain.

stories.title: Aurangzeb lauds Beijing’s support for Pakistan’s IMF programme during meeting with Chinese counterpart
stories.summary: Pakistani Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb thanked China for supporting Pakistan's IMF engagements during a meeting with his Chinese counterpart on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank Spring Meetings in Washington, D.C.

stories.title: Arrest of Philippine ex-lawmaker Zaldy Co ‘missing puzzle piece’ in flood-control probe
stories.summary: Fugitive former Philippine congressman Zaldy Co was arrested, reviving a stalled corruption investigation into a multibillion-peso kickback scheme tied to flood control projects. Co has accused President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. of personally benefiting from the scheme.

stories.title: Vietnam and China are now perfectly aligned
stories.summary: A secretly issued August 2024 Vietnamese military document reportedly rejects participation in any U.S.-led China containment strategy in the Asia-Pacific. The plan, dubbed the "Second US Invasion Plan," frames American promotion of democracy as a tool for regional hegemony and outlines preparations against a possible U.S.-led military intervention.

stories.title: Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan to visit Sri Lanka on April 19 and 20
stories.summary: Indian Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan is scheduled to visit Sri Lanka on April 19–20. During the trip, he is expected to meet opposition politicians, including representatives of Tamil political parties from the north, east, and hill country regions of the island.

stories.title: Myanmar frees more than 4,500 prisoners in traditional new year amnesty
stories.summary: Myanmar's military government released more than 4,500 prisoners in a traditional new year amnesty. The release comes one week after military chief Min Aung Hlaing was sworn in as president following an election widely criticized as neither free nor fair.

stories.title: The Iran war has exposed the limits of neutrality
stories.summary: The conflict involving Iran has exposed the limits of strategic neutrality for many nations, with Gulf energy disruptions and divisions among allied countries making ambiguity increasingly difficult to maintain.

stories.title: Russia preparing new spring-summer offensive in southeastern Ukraine – intelligence
stories.summary: Intelligence reports indicate Russia is preparing a new ground offensive in southeastern Ukraine for the spring-summer period, with the goal of capturing the entire Donbas region by September.

stories.title: Prosecutors in a Minnesota county charge ICE agent with assault
stories.summary: Prosecutors in a Minnesota county charged ICE agent Gregory Donnell Morgan, 35, with assault. Morgan allegedly pointed a gun at two people in another vehicle along a highway in the Twin Cities area.

stories.title: Iran rejects temporary ceasefire, calls for end to war
stories.summary: Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Saeed Khatibzadeh stated at the Antalya Diplomacy Forum that Iran rejects any temporary ceasefire and demands a comprehensive end to hostilities from Lebanon to the Red Sea. He affirmed Iran's commitment to keeping the Strait of Hormuz open.

stories.title: Hong Kong eyes HK$220 million private investment for national innovation centre
stories.summary: Hong Kong authorities plan to seek roughly HK$220 million in private-sector investment to help fund a HK$440 million national manufacturing innovation centre in Yuen Long. Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po announced the project in his February budget as the first such centre outside mainland China.

stories.title: Palestinian Authority extradites suspect in 1982 Paris attack
stories.summary: The Palestinian Authority extradited Hicham Harb, now 72, to face charges in connection with the August 9, 1982, attack in Paris. He is one of four suspects sought over the incident.

stories.title: Trump declares Hormuz strait open, raising hopes for peace deal
stories.summary: President Donald Trump declared the Strait of Hormuz open for commercial shipping, raising hopes for a broader peace deal. However, he stated that the US naval blockade specifically targeting Iran's ports would remain in place until a peace agreement is finalized.

stories.title: Smoother waters? China and Vietnam vow to ‘better’ navigate South China Sea disputes
stories.summary: During Vietnamese leader To Lam's four-day visit to China, Beijing and Hanoi issued a joint communique pledging to strengthen demarcation talks over disputed waters in the South China Sea. The two countries' ruling communist parties also adopted a new five-year action plan to bolster each other's domestic leadership.

stories.title: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire opens a window - but Hezbollah still holds the door
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon reached a ceasefire agreement, with both sides reportedly acknowledging that Hezbollah's armed presence is a central issue. Analysts note that whether Lebanon can take meaningful action to address Hezbollah's influence remains an open question.

stories.title: Press groups push Israeli court to expedite Gaza media access
stories.summary: Press organizations, including the Committee to Protect Journalists, have filed an emergency motion with Israel's highest court seeking to compel access for international media into Gaza.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: Macron says Lebanon-Israel ceasefire 'may already be undermined'
stories.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron warned that the Lebanon-Israel ceasefire, which took effect on April 16, 2026, may already be undermined. The ceasefire had been agreed upon for a 10-day period between Israel and Lebanon.

stories.title: Trump extended the ban on Russian ships docking in US ports — keeping a Biden-era measure alive through spring 2027
stories.summary: President Trump extended a Biden-era ban on Russian ships docking at U.S. ports, keeping the measure in effect through spring 2027. The White House cited Russia's policies as a continuing disturbance to U.S. international relations.

stories.title: NATO will not collapse and US will defend its allies, Estonian minister says
stories.summary: Estonia's defense minister stated that NATO will not collapse and that the United States will continue to defend its allies. The remarks came after President Trump threatened to withdraw the U.S. from the alliance over European members' refusal to send ships to unblock the Strait of Hormuz near Iran.

stories.title: Why did Michelin snub St Paul in its guide to the best restaurants in the Great Lakes region?
stories.summary: Michelin excluded Saint Paul, Minnesota, from its new Great Lakes restaurant guide despite including nearby Minneapolis. Critics raised concerns that smaller and immigrant-run restaurants in the state capital and beyond risk being overlooked under the city-funded arrangement.

stories.title: Cathay Pacific, HK Express passenger counts rise despite impact of Mideast war
stories.summary: Cathay Pacific Airways and its budget carrier HK Express reported higher passenger numbers in March compared to the previous year, despite disruptions from the U.S.-Israel war against Iran. Cathay Group announced plans to restore all flights after June, following earlier cuts of 2% for Cathay Pacific and 6% for HK Express between mid-May and late June.

stories.title: Syria’s Sharaa: Israel has acted with ‘brutality,’ but talks not at dead end
stories.summary: Syrian leader Ahmed al-Sharaa stated that Israel has acted with brutality but that negotiations are not at a dead end. Talks are currently focused on restoring the UN buffer zone in the Golan Heights, with Damascus also announcing that all former US military bases in Syria are now under state control.

stories.title: Ukrainian Defense Forces strike Russian 'Podlyot' and 'Nebo-M' radar systems, command posts, and storage base for Russian boats
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Forces struck Russian "Podlyot" and "Nebo-M" radar stations, command posts, and a boat storage facility in occupied Ukrainian territories and inside the Russian Federation.

stories.title: Shabbat candle lighting times for Israel and US
stories.summary: Shabbat candle lighting times were published for communities across Israel and the United States.

stories.title: Can the US and Iran conclude a lasting deal to end the war?
stories.summary: Ongoing negotiations between the United States and Iran face significant hurdles in reaching a lasting deal to permanently resolve their conflict.

stories.title: China complains of ‘harassment’ from New Zealand aerial patrols close to coastline
stories.summary: China lodged a formal protest with New Zealand over a P-8A anti-submarine patrol aircraft conducting reconnaissance near the Yellow Sea and East China Sea. Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun accused the flights of undermining China's security interests and endangering commercial aviation in the area.

stories.title: South Koreans breathe sighs of relief as escaped wolf is returned to zoo safely
stories.summary: A two-year-old male wolf named Neukgu was safely recaptured in South Korea after escaping from the O-World zoo in Daejeon on April 8. The nine-day search gripped the nation and made the animal a celebrity, while animal rights activists had expressed concerns about the wolf's welfare during the pursuit.

stories.title: 'All changed with the genocide': Palestinian women and girls face brutal abuse in Israeli jails
stories.summary: Since the onset of the Gaza war in October 2023, over 700 Palestinian women and girls have been arrested and held in Israeli prisons. Detainees reportedly face harsh conditions including starvation, isolation, and humiliation, according to accounts compiled by journalist Victoria Brittain.

stories.title: UN reforms can’t wait any longer, Kazakhstan’s Tokayev says amid fragile Iran truce
stories.summary: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, speaking at the Antalya Diplomacy Forum in Turkey, urged accelerated United Nations reforms, citing the war in Iran as evidence of the world body's inadequacy. He argued that multilateral diplomacy must be strengthened to restore global peace and security.

stories.title: Tens of thousands return to south Lebanon after ceasefire, defying Israeli warnings
stories.summary: Tens of thousands of displaced Lebanese civilians began returning to southern Lebanon after a 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon took effect at midnight. Israel warned residents not to return to areas south of the Litani River, saying its forces remain positioned there to monitor Hezbollah activity.

stories.title: Nigeria: No Ban On Hijab During Utme, JAMB Insists
stories.summary: Nigeria's Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) reaffirmed that candidates are not banned from wearing the hijab during the Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME).

stories.title: Nigeria: Ijaw Leaders Endorse Tinubu, Oborevwori
stories.summary: Prominent Ijaw leaders, including Presidential Amnesty Programme administrator Dennis Otuaro, endorsed President Bola Tinubu and Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori as their preferred candidates for the 2027 elections in Nigeria. The endorsement was announced in Warri.

stories.title: Svyrydenko after visit to US: Bessent supports Ukraine, progress made in IMF negotiations
stories.summary: Ukrainian Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko reported strong support from Washington following meetings in the United States, noting progress in negotiations with the IMF and backing from U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent.

stories.title: Could the Lebanon ceasefire lead to US-Iran talks breakthrough?
stories.summary: Al Jazeera's Tohid Asadi discussed the possibility that the ceasefire in Lebanon could create momentum for a broader diplomatic breakthrough in US-Iran peace negotiations.

stories.title: Turkey hosts latest diplomatic push on Middle East war
stories.summary: Foreign ministers of Turkey, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt are set to meet on the sidelines of a diplomatic forum in Turkey, with the Middle East war expected to be the dominant topic of discussion.

stories.title: Israeli scientists successfully germinate rare Swamp Orchid in conservation breakthrough
stories.summary: Israeli scientists achieved a conservation breakthrough by successfully germinating the rare Swamp Orchid. The newly grown plants are being cultivated in pots before being transplanted back into their natural habitat.

stories.title: Lebanese celebrate return to homes as 10-day ceasefire begins
stories.summary: A 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon has taken effect, prompting celebrations as Lebanese civilians began returning to their homes in areas affected by the conflict.

stories.title: Israeli strikes on desalination plant in Gaza kill two
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes hit a desalination plant in Gaza, killing at least two people. The destruction of the facility has worsened already severe humanitarian conditions in the enclave, where waste is accumulating in streets and residential areas.

stories.title: South Africa: Sassa Condemns 'Selling' Queue Positions At Its Offices
stories.summary: South Africa's Social Security Agency (SASSA) condemned the illegal practice of selling queue positions at its local offices, calling it exploitative of vulnerable beneficiaries seeking social grants.

stories.title: No rockets but no relief: Nahariya residents see no end to war despite Lebanon ceasefire
stories.summary: Residents of Nahariya in northern Israel expressed frustration and a sense of betrayal following the Lebanon ceasefire, despite the end of six weeks of Hezbollah rocket attacks. Many felt bewildered by the government's sudden decision to halt fighting without a clear resolution.

stories.title: South Africa: MEC Gaoage Molapisi Delivers Houses and Hosts District Imbizo for Military Veterans
stories.summary: [SAnews.gov.za] North West MEC for Cooperative Governance, Human Settlements and Traditional Affairs (COGTA), Gaoage Oageng Molapisi, will today hand over seven houses to military veterans in Jouberto

stories.title: Ukrainian Drone Strike Kills 1 in Belgorod Region
stories.summary: A Ukrainian drone strike in Russia's Belgorod region killed one person who was reportedly riding a motorcycle near the border with northeastern Ukraine.

stories.title: Pakistan-based LeT's co-founder injured in attack in Lahore
stories.summary: Two unidentified gunmen on a motorcycle attacked a car on Peco Road in Lahore, injuring Hamza, who is associated with Lashkar-e-Taiba co-founder Ghazi. Ghazi was unhurt in the shooting, which occurred near a TV channel's office. Police are investigating the incident.
