stories.summary: Pope Leo XVI, speaking during a visit to Cameroon, denounced a world ruled by tyrants and called for a decisive change of course away from conflict and exploitation of resources.

stories.title: 'They are champions at lying': Ex-defense official warns against US-Iran nuclear deal
stories.summary: A former Israeli defense official has cautioned against pursuing a nuclear deal with Iran, citing concerns over Tehran's credibility. The debate centers on Iran's stockpile of approximately 450 kilograms of enriched uranium accumulated since 2018, according to the official.

stories.title: Kyiv hit by deadly missile attack amid shortage of interceptors
stories.summary: A deadly missile attack struck Kyiv as Ukraine faces a critical shortage of ballistic missile interceptors. The lack of air defence capabilities left the capital exposed to the Russian strike.

stories.title: Russia trying to seize border villages in Sumy region for 10 days – military spokesperson
stories.summary: Russian forces have been attempting to seize border villages in Ukraine's northeastern Sumy region for 10 consecutive days, according to a Ukrainian military spokesperson. Residents of the targeted settlements had already been evacuated before the offensive began.

stories.title: Can Japan’s US$10b energy shield oust China’s influence in Southeast Asia?
stories.summary: Japan pledged US$10 billion in energy support to Southeast Asian nations, a move analysts describe as a strategic effort to counter China's regional influence amid disruptions to global oil markets caused by the Iran war. However, some observers questioned its impact given Southeast Asian countries' tendency toward strategic hedging.

stories.title: 170 soldiers added to list of Israel’s fallen since last Memorial Day
stories.summary: Israel added 170 soldiers to its official list of fallen since the last Memorial Day, along with 54 veterans who died from service-related injuries. The total number of fallen since 1860 now stands at 25,644, and wartime guidelines may require pre-recorded memorial ceremonies.

stories.title: Germany-Israel divide deepens after Merz criticism
stories.summary: Relations between Germany and Israel have deteriorated further after Israeli Finance Minister sharply criticized German Chancellor Merz's stance on Israel's settlement policy, highlighting a growing diplomatic estrangement.

stories.title: Germany, Israel see growing divide after criticism of Merz
stories.summary: Israeli Finance Minister sharply criticized German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's views on Israel's settlement policy, highlighting a growing rift in German-Israeli relations.

stories.title: Pope Leo blasts the 'tyrants' ravaging Earth with war and exploitation on Cameroon visit
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV condemned "a handful of tyrants" ravaging the world with war during a visit to Cameroon's separatist western region, where a years-long conflict has killed thousands. He called for global military spending to be redirected toward healthcare and education.

stories.title: Trade tensions make rest of world less keen to invest in US and China, survey finds
stories.summary: A survey by Allianz Trade found that U.S.-China trade tensions have reduced global companies' willingness to invest in either country, with the U.S. nearly twice as unpopular. Investment intention toward China dropped from 53 percent to 24 percent of respondents year-on-year.

stories.title: Why the US must prioritize Hezbollah in the Iran deal - opinion
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that the United States should prioritize addressing Hezbollah's role as part of any nuclear negotiations with Iran. The piece frames the talks as a broader regional security test affecting both Israel and Lebanon.

stories.title: Beirut said to balk as Trump pushes for 1st-ever call between leaders of Lebanon and Israel
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun reportedly told US Secretary of State Marco Rubio that he would not speak with Israeli PM Netanyahu, insisting on a ceasefire before any direct talks. Cross-border fighting between Israel and Lebanon continued in full force.

stories.title: Israeli forces kill Palestinian teenager, seize body
stories.summary: Israeli forces shot and killed Palestinian teenager Muhammad Rayyan northwest of Jerusalem, according to local authorities. The military also seized the teenager's body following the incident.

stories.title: In Cameroon, Pope Leo assails ‘tyrants ravaging’ world amid Trump row
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV delivered forceful remarks in Cameroon criticizing world leaders who spend billions on wars, calling them "tyrants ravaging" the world. His comments came after U.S. President Donald Trump attacked him on social media. The Pope also addressed the nearly decade-long conflict in Cameroon's anglophone regions.

stories.title: EU working on jet fuel plan as Iran crisis threatens air travel
stories.summary: The European Union is developing contingency plans for jet fuel supply as the Iran crisis threatens to disrupt air travel. Airlines have warned of potential shortages ahead of the summer travel season due to war-related supply chain disruptions.

stories.title: School shooting in Zakarpattia: Police search for parents of ninth-grade student
stories.summary: A ninth-grade student opened fire at a school in Ukraine's western Zakarpattia region, injuring another student. Police are searching for the shooter's parents, and the student is currently refusing to communicate with psychologists.

stories.title: India plans more seats for women in parliament, links it to ‘delimitation’
stories.summary: India's ruling BJP has linked implementation of a law reserving 33 percent of parliamentary seats for women to the completion of a delimitation exercise that would redraw constituency boundaries.

stories.title: Iran war: What has the war done to the cost of humanitarian aid?
stories.summary: The war on Iran has driven up the cost of humanitarian aid globally, with supply disruptions and soaring prices threatening vulnerable populations. Aid agencies describe the situation as a race against time, including in Afghanistan where the UN World Food Programme distributes emergency supplies.

stories.title: Pakistan continues to insist Lebanon part of current MidEast ceasefire deal even as US, Israel deny
stories.summary: Pakistan has continued to assert that Lebanon is included in the current Middle East ceasefire agreement, a claim denied by both the United States and Israel. US Vice President JD Vance stated publicly that no such promise regarding Lebanon was ever made during negotiations.

stories.title: US military says strike on vessel in Eastern Pacific kills three
stories.summary: The U.S. military said it struck a vessel in the Eastern Pacific on Wednesday, killing three people. The strike is part of the Trump administration's ongoing maritime operations, which have drawn condemnation from human rights advocates.

stories.title: Middle East crisis tests African economies [Business Africa]
stories.summary: The IMF now expects African economic growth to slow to 4.3% this year as the war in the Middle East poses new threats to the continent's economies. Analysts note that regional planners now have better tools to absorb economic shocks compared to past crises.

stories.title: Government approves 5-year, billion-shekel plan to develop Golan, give it its 1st city
stories.summary: The Israeli government approved a five-year, billion-shekel development plan for the Golan Heights, including upgrading Katzrin to city status. PM Netanyahu touted the initiative as a "massive development surge" aimed at attracting thousands of new families.

stories.title: China’s PBOC raises leverage ratios for foreign lenders to support outbound investment
stories.summary: China's central bank and foreign exchange regulator raised the overseas-loan leverage ratio for foreign banks and their joint ventures in China from 0.5 to 1.5. Analysts say the move will support Chinese companies' outbound investment while helping stabilize the yuan.

stories.title: Why India is rankled by Pakistan playing mediator in US-Iran war
stories.summary: Pakistan's facilitation of backchannel talks between the United States and Iran in Islamabad has drawn criticism from India. Analysts say the episode highlights shifting dynamics in West Asian geopolitics, with Pakistan positioning itself as a mediator despite its own financial and political instability.

stories.title: Why the Iran war did not go according to US plans
stories.summary: A US military campaign against Iran reportedly deviated from Washington's plans after officials misread Tehran's capabilities and overestimated American leverage, resulting in a costly 40-day war of attrition.

stories.title: Owner of luxury Hong Kong home fined HK$110,000 over illegal structures, pool
stories.summary: A Hong Kong court fined Sunset Boulevard Company HK$110,000 for constructing illegal structures and a swimming pool at House No. 76, Redhill Peninsula, in Tai Tam. The prosecution followed a government crackdown prompted by a record-breaking rainstorm and an investigation by the South China Morning Post.

stories.title: Ukraine receives GBP 752M from UK funded by frozen Russian assets
stories.summary: Ukraine received a final tranche of 752 million British pounds, approximately one billion U.S. dollars, from the United Kingdom. The funds come under the G7 Extraordinary Revenue Acceleration initiative, financed by frozen Russian assets, to bolster Ukraine's defense capabilities.

stories.title: Israeli strike destroys last working bridge over Lebanon’s Litani River
stories.summary: An Israeli airstrike destroyed the last operational bridge over the Litani River in southern Lebanon, severing a critical transport link to the region.

stories.title: Italian foreign minister in China to talk trade, Iran
stories.summary: Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani visited China to strengthen trade ties, support Italian businesses, and urge Beijing to help advance peace efforts related to the conflicts in Iran and Ukraine.

stories.title: Ben-Gurion Airport employee fired for photographing US military planes - report
stories.summary: A temporary employee at Ben-Gurion Airport in Israel was terminated after photographing US military aircraft and sharing the images via WhatsApp. The incident reportedly nearly caused a serious diplomatic and security issue between the US military and the Israel Defense Forces.

stories.title: US, Hamas reportedly hold direct talks, as Board of Peace disarmament plan stalls
stories.summary: Senior Trump administration official Lightstone reportedly held direct talks with Hamas official Hayya. Negotiations over the second phase of a ceasefire have stalled as Hamas resists disarmament requirements, arguing Israel is violating the first phase of the truce.

stories.title: “Together, We Remember” - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: Masa Israel Journey is hosting an International Yom HaZikaron ceremony expected to be watched by hundreds of thousands of Jews from approximately 60 countries. The event is titled "Together, We Remember."

stories.title: Why do Lebanese leaders keep courting Israel?
stories.summary: Lebanese and Israeli officials held direct talks in Washington for the first time in roughly 30 years. Protesters gathered in Beirut's Martyrs' Square to oppose the negotiations and any normalization with Israel.

stories.title: Only Peace Can Make a New World Order
stories.summary: An opinion piece argues that current global conflicts are dismantling the existing international order but are failing to produce a viable replacement. No specific new developments or actors beyond the general thesis were detailed.

stories.title: Ukraine holds Hryshyne’s center and northern Pokrovsk outskirts as Russia builds up for its next push, military says
stories.summary: Ukrainian forces maintained control of Hryshyne's center and the northern outskirts of Pokrovsk in Donetsk region. Russian forces failed to consolidate positions in Hryshyne, while Ukraine continued targeting and destroying Russian military assets in southern Pokrovsk to disrupt a buildup.

stories.title: Can historic Israel-Lebanon talks lead to ceasefire?
stories.summary: Israeli and Lebanese leaders are set for historic direct talks for the first time in 34 years, aimed at easing tensions and potentially reaching a ceasefire amid ongoing cross-border conflict.

stories.title: Food prices in Ukraine may rise by around 10% – Haidu
stories.summary: Rising fuel prices in Ukraine may drive food costs up by approximately 10% in the second half of the year, according to official Haidu. The trend reflects broader inflationary pressures on the country's economy during the ongoing conflict.

stories.title: More than 100 writers quit French publisher in protest against rightwing owner Vincent Bolloré
stories.summary: More than 100 writers, including novelist Virginie Despentes and philosopher Bernard-Henri Lévy, quit the historic French publishing house Grasset in protest against owner Vincent Bolloré. The conservative billionaire's media empire has been accused of promoting far-right ideas.

stories.title: China’s Qingzhou robotic craft tests space debris capture and clean-up
stories.summary: China's prototype Qingzhou robotic cargo spacecraft successfully tested capture and towing operations on non-cooperative space targets in orbit, according to state broadcaster CCTV. The experiments aim to develop orbital vehicles capable of clearing space debris and derelict satellites.

stories.title: Done and dusted? Trump’s portrayal of the war in Iran collides with reality
stories.summary: Analysts say the U.S.-Iran war has strengthened the military and hardline factions within Iran, contradicting President Trump's portrayal of the conflict's progress. The gap between the administration's narrative and conditions on the ground continues to widen.

stories.title: Netherlands to honor Zelensky and people of Ukraine with Four Freedoms Award
stories.summary: The international Four Freedoms Award ceremony is scheduled for April 16 in Middelburg, the Netherlands. This year's laureates are President Volodymyr Zelensky and the people of Ukraine.

stories.title: Rwanda ties Mozambique troop deployment to EU funding
stories.summary: Rwanda has linked the future deployment of its troops to fight terrorism in Mozambique's northern Cabo Delgado province to EU funding. Kigali's demand for compensation presents a strategic dilemma for European policymakers.

stories.title: US-sanctioned supertankers enter Gulf despite blockade
stories.summary: A U.S.-sanctioned Iranian supertanker entered the Persian Gulf despite the American naval blockade. The vessel's passage came a day after another sanctioned very large crude carrier, the Alicia, also crossed through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: US announces new sanctions against Iran oil sector
stories.summary: The United States announced new sanctions targeting Iran's oil sector, including shipping networks and firms accused of sanctions evasion, as Tehran has moved to close the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: White House Says It Will Not Renew Russian Oil Sanctions Waiver
stories.summary: The White House announced it will not renew a waiver on Russian oil sanctions. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent defended the temporary waiver, arguing it had prevented a larger price spike that could have actually increased Russia's energy revenues.

stories.title: Gaza's health system and patients pushed to the brink by Israel
stories.summary: Gaza's healthcare system is nearing collapse due to Israeli restrictions on medical supply deliveries and patient movement, pushing hospitals and patients to the brink.

stories.title: Fuel supply fears after blaze tears through crucial Australian refinery
stories.summary: A series of explosions caused by a gas leak ignited a major fire at the Viva oil refinery in Victoria state, Australia, producing flames up to 60 metres high. The refinery, one of only two operating in Australia, supplies about 10 percent of the country's fuel. Authorities warned of potential fuel supply disruptions.

stories.title: Ten-day ceasefire between Lebanon and Israel goes into effect
stories.summary: A 10-day ceasefire between Israel and Lebanon took effect Thursday evening to enable negotiations toward a permanent security agreement, according to Washington. The truce aims to create space for longer-term diplomatic talks.

stories.title: Trump announces Lebanon-Israel ceasefire, invites leaders to US
stories.summary: Israel and Lebanon agreed to implement a 10-day ceasefire beginning Thursday evening, as announced by US President Donald Trump. Washington said the truce is intended to facilitate negotiations toward a permanent security agreement, and Trump invited both nations' leaders to the US.

stories.title: Rubio to join call with Aoun, Netanyahu amid Israeli attacks
stories.summary: Lebanon confirmed that a phone call between Lebanese President Aoun and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu will take place Thursday, with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio joining the conversation amid ongoing Israeli attacks.

stories.title: Drone attack sparks fire at oil depot in occupied Crimea
stories.summary: A drone attack overnight on April 16 set fire to an oil depot in the settlement of Oktiabrske in Russian-occupied Crimea. A separate fire was also reported near the TES Oil and Gas Storage facility in the Bakhchysarai district.

stories.title: Ceasefire in Lebanon ‘as important’ as in Iran, Ghalibaf says
stories.summary: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that Tehran considers a ceasefire in Lebanon as important as one in the Iran conflict. He said Iran is working to compel the US and Israel to agree to permanent ceasefires across all conflict zones.

stories.title: Europe running low on jet fuel, stoking fears of flight cancellations
stories.summary: International Energy Agency executive director Fatih Birol warned that Europe has approximately six weeks of jet fuel reserves remaining, raising the possibility of flight cancellations. The shortage stems from disrupted oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz due to the Iran war, which Birol called the largest energy crisis ever faced.

stories.title: Israeli soldiers suspected of raping Palestinian detainee allowed to return to service
stories.summary: Israeli reservists suspected of raping and torturing a Palestinian detainee at the Sde Teiman detention facility have been allowed to return to military service after approval by the army chief.

stories.title: EU pumps over $1 billion into defense R&D, centered around  Ukraine war lessons
stories.summary: The European Union has allocated over $1 billion to defense research and development, with funded projects reflecting lessons learned from the war in Ukraine. Priority areas include loitering munitions and affordable mass drone production, signaling a shift toward 21st-century warfare capabilities.

stories.title: Iran mulls toll free Hormuz transit, warns over US blockade
stories.summary: Iran is reportedly considering offering toll-free transit through the Strait of Hormuz while simultaneously escalating threats against the US naval blockade of the waterway.

stories.title: Pedro Pascal v Pedro Piscal: actor in legal battle with Chilean spirit brand
stories.summary: Actor Pedro Pascal has filed a legal challenge against Chilean pisco merchant David Herrera, who registered the brand name "Pedro Piscal" with Chilean regulators in 2023. The case follows a pattern of Chilean brands resembling Hollywood celebrities' names.

stories.title: Malaysia and Australia strike energy supply pledge to bypass Iran war disruptions
stories.summary: Malaysia and Australia pledged to maintain oil and gas trade between them to mitigate disruptions caused by Iran's restriction of access to the Strait of Hormuz. The disruption followed US-Israeli strikes against Iran beginning February 28, prompting Asian nations to deepen regional energy cooperation.

stories.title: US says 3 killed in fifth drug boat strike in a week
stories.summary: The U.S. military conducted its fifth strike on an alleged drug-trafficking boat in the Eastern Pacific in one week, killing three people. The latest attack brings the total death toll from these strikes to at least 177.

stories.title: Sudan civil war: Civilians caught in the deadly crossfire of a ruthless army-RSF power struggle
stories.summary: Analyst Dallia Abdelmoniem warned that Sudan's civil war between the army and the Rapid Support Forces has become a systematic war on civilians. She described the conflict as a humanitarian catastrophe where survival has become a matter of chance for the population caught in the crossfire.

stories.title: After heavy Russian attack, Zelensky urges partners to speed up Patriot missile deliveries
stories.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky instructed Ukraine's Air Force commander to contact international partners who had previously committed to supplying missiles for Patriot and other air-defense systems, urging faster deliveries following a heavy Russian attack.

stories.title: At least 72,345 Palestinians dead in Gaza genocide: health ministry
stories.summary: Gaza's health ministry reported that at least 72,345 Palestinians have been killed and 172,250 wounded since Israel's military campaign began in October 2023. An additional 766 Palestinians have been killed since a ceasefire took effect in October 2025.

stories.title: Chinese drone exposes Indonesia’s ‘insufficient’ undersea capabilities
stories.summary: An Indonesian fisherman discovered a Chinese unmanned underwater vehicle marked "CSIC" in the Lombok Strait, a key waterway near Australia. Analysts said the find highlights Indonesia's insufficient undersea defense capabilities, though Jakarta is expected to address the matter through quiet diplomacy.

stories.title: Iran war brings US close to net crude exporter for first time since World War II
stories.summary: The Iran war has pushed the United States close to becoming a net crude oil exporter for the first time since World War II. Analysts and traders say the U.S. is rapidly approaching its export capacity as global supply disruptions reshape energy markets.

stories.title: Hong Kong police arrest 5 over shoplifting syndicate targeting Muji stores
stories.summary: Hong Kong police arrested five people suspected of running a shoplifting syndicate that targeted multiple outlets of Japanese retailer Muji. The suspects allegedly stole over 445 items of clothing worth approximately HK$113,000 across several stores in the Yau Tsim district.

stories.title: Could Lebanon's negotiations with Israel trigger new civil war?
stories.summary: As Lebanon marks 51 years since the start of its civil war, ongoing negotiations with Israel are stirring deep domestic divisions and raising fears that internal tensions could escalate toward renewed conflict.

stories.title: Daily Briefing Apr. 16 – Did Trump trigger direct talks for Israel’s and Lebanon’s leaders?
stories.summary: Times of Israel bureau chief Jacob Magid analyzed reported direct talks between Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors in Washington, the status of US-Iran negotiations, and a related US Senate vote.

stories.title: Police, prosecution trade blame over protest-related court losses
stories.summary: A public dispute erupted between Israel Police and the State Attorney's Office over the handling of protest-related court cases. Police accused the prosecution of failing to support officers, while prosecutors pushed back on the criticism.

stories.title: Hopes for Middle East peace grow as Israel discusses Lebanon ceasefire
stories.summary: Hopes for peace in the Middle East are growing as Israel engages in discussions over a potential ceasefire with Lebanon. Ending the fighting in Lebanon had been a key obstacle in earlier peace negotiations.

stories.title: Iran supreme leader’s adviser threatens to sink US ships in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: An adviser to Iran's supreme leader threatened to sink U.S. ships in the Strait of Hormuz. He also said a U.S. ground invasion would be welcomed, as Iran could take thousands of hostages.

stories.title: Israeli army says soldiers accused of abusing Palestinian to return to duty
stories.summary: The Israeli military announced that some reservist soldiers accused of abusing a Palestinian detainee have returned to combat duty. The development was reported by Israeli Army Radio.

stories.title: Slovenia’s new parliament speaker claims he’s not pro-Russian, plans Moscow visit, promises referendum on NATO exit
stories.summary: Slovenia's newly elected parliament speaker, Stevanović, has denied being pro-Russian while announcing plans to visit Moscow and proposing a referendum on NATO membership. He supports lifting EU sanctions against Russia, positioning himself as a potential ally of Slovakia's Prime Minister Fico.

stories.title: Australian court strikes down post-Bondi massacre protest law as unconstitutional
stories.summary: An Australian court struck down a New South Wales protest law enacted after the Bondi massacre as unconstitutional. A pro-Palestinian plaintiff argued the legislation was designed to suppress democratic protest rights.

stories.title: Wanted activist arrested in South Africa over support for Benin coup plot
stories.summary: Kemi Seba, a Beninese pan-African activist known for opposing French influence in Africa and supporting West African military leaders, was arrested in South Africa. He is wanted by Benin's government in connection with an alleged coup plot.

stories.title: Ceasefire is a 'natural entry point' for direct Israel-Lebanon talks, says president
stories.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun described a ceasefire with Israel as a natural entry point for direct negotiations, calling for an end to Israeli military operations targeting civilians and destroying Lebanese villages.

stories.title: TSMC targets over 30% revenue surge in 2026, ramps up capex amid booming AI demand
stories.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) projected revenue growth of more than 30 percent in 2026, driven by surging global demand for artificial intelligence chips. During its first-quarter earnings call, management downplayed the impact of memory price hikes and Middle East tensions on operations.

stories.title: UN warns tensions between DR Congo, Rwanda, and Burundi remain acute
stories.summary: The United Nations warned that tensions among the Democratic Republic of Congo, Rwanda, and Burundi remain acute. The UN stated that humanitarian and security conditions in the Great Lakes region have deteriorated to a worrisome level despite ongoing diplomatic efforts.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz concludes visit to Saudi Arabia, to head to Doha: PMO
stories.summary: Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif concluded his official visit to Saudi Arabia and departed for Doha, Qatar. He is scheduled to hold a bilateral meeting with Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani.

stories.title: Turkish police detain 162 people over online praise for school shootings
stories.summary: Turkish police detained 162 people for allegedly praising school shootings online. The arrests followed two separate school shooting incidents in Turkey — one on Tuesday injuring at least 16 people and another on Wednesday killing nine.

stories.title: ‘A dollar or two increase is devastating’: US readers on toll of rising gas prices
stories.summary: US readers described to the Guardian how rising gas prices stemming from the seven-week US-Israeli war on Iran have forced difficult trade-offs involving essential medicines, groceries, and housing costs. The price hikes come amid a fragile ceasefire in place since earlier in April.

stories.title: Utah passes new law to combat overcharges at dollar stores after Guardian investigation
stories.summary: Utah passed a new law doubling penalties for retailers that repeatedly charge more at checkout than listed shelf prices. The legislation, effective May 6, was introduced in direct response to a Guardian investigation into pricing practices at Dollar General and Family Dollar stores.

stories.title: Xinjiang’s Repression of Uyghurs Has Evolved, Not Ended
stories.summary: A rare insider testimony reveals that China's repression of Uyghurs in Xinjiang has evolved rather than ended. The account describes how Chinese authorities have adapted their methods to conceal ongoing state violence in the region.

stories.title: China says Tokyo embassy intrusion, bomb threat are among ‘grave violations’ in Japan
stories.summary: The Chinese embassy in Tokyo reported a series of security threats over the past month, including an intrusion and a bomb threat. Acting embassy head Shi Yong said a threatening letter was received on March 5 from a group claiming to include former Japanese police and military members.

stories.title: Sudan’s ‘abandoned crisis’ enters fourth year as calls for peace grow louder
stories.summary: Sudan's civil conflict has entered its fourth year, with calls for peace intensifying. Only 63% of health facilities remain operational according to the WHO, as cholera and other disease outbreaks spread amid attacks on healthcare workers and infrastructure.

stories.title: 2 Killed in Drone Attack on Krasnodar Region as Ukraine and Russia Trade Deadly Barrages
stories.summary: Two people were killed in a drone attack on Russia's Krasnodar Region as Ukraine and Russia exchanged deadly strikes. Unconfirmed reports suggest the Tuapse Oil Refinery was targeted and set ablaze in the Ukrainian attack.

stories.title: 3 abducted polio workers recovered in Bannu after joint efforts of police, jirga
stories.summary: Three polio workers abducted by militants in Bannu, Pakistan, were safely recovered through joint efforts by local police and tribal jirga elders.

stories.title: Haiti: High fuel, food prices pile new pressure on families
stories.summary: Haiti's government announced a 37% increase in diesel prices and a 29% increase in gasoline prices on April 2. The fuel price hikes have driven up the cost of essential food products, adding pressure on Haitian families.

stories.title: Last bridge to southern Lebanon destroyed in Israeli strike
stories.summary: An Israeli strike destroyed the last bridge connecting southern Lebanon to the rest of the country. A senior Lebanese security official said the bridge was shattered beyond repair.

stories.title: Church warden jailed for life for murder of lecturer has conviction quashed
stories.summary: The Court of Appeal in England quashed the murder conviction of Benjamin Field, a former church warden jailed for life in 2019 for killing university lecturer Peter Farquhar, 69, in Maids Moreton, Buckinghamshire. A retrial has been ordered in the case.

stories.title: Liberia: Tweah's U.S.$6.2m Trial Deepens
stories.summary: Retired Major General Daniel Ziankahn testified in Liberia's Criminal Court "C" that he had no knowledge of the Financial Intelligence Agency being integrated into the national security architecture during his tenure. The testimony came in the ongoing US$6.2 million corruption trial of former government officials.

stories.title: WATCH: Israel Navy missile boat intercepts Hezbollah drone launched towards Israel
stories.summary: An Israel Navy missile boat intercepted a Hezbollah drone launched toward Israel. The IDF also conducted strikes against targets in southern Lebanon and seized a large underground weapons cache.

stories.title: Ukraine needs EUR 5B to fund resilience plans, Deputy PM Kuleba
stories.summary: Ukrainian Deputy Prime Minister Kuleba stated that €5 billion is needed to finance the country's resilience plans. Efforts are underway to identify funding sources for the initiative.

stories.title: France readies AI-powered combat data-management similar to US ‘Maven’
stories.summary: France is developing an AI-powered combat data-management system comparable to the U.S. military's Project Maven. A senior French general stated the system could be ready within months, with exercises planned for September 2027, though specific technical details were not disclosed.

stories.title: ‘Sent to be killed’: How Russia forces migrants to fight in Ukraine
stories.summary: Central Asian migrants coerced into fighting for Russia on the front lines in Ukraine face a life expectancy of roughly four months, according to reporting on Moscow's use of forced migrant conscription.

stories.title: IDF seeks to arm itself with FPV assault drones as Hamas, Hezbollah conflicts evolve
stories.summary: The Israel Defense Forces issued a new tender for first-person-view assault drones as its conflicts with Hamas and Hezbollah evolve. Bidders include Ondas Holdings, Xtend, and Robotican.

stories.title: Netanyahu will speak with Lebanese president Aoun, Israeli minister says
stories.summary: Israeli Minister Gila Gamliel confirmed that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu would speak with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun on Thursday. US President Donald Trump had announced the historic first direct conversation between Israeli and Lebanese leaders.

stories.title: China condemns US Hormuz blockade as oil flows Disrupted
stories.summary: China condemned the US blockade of the Strait of Hormuz as dangerous and irresponsible, noting that in 2025 China imported 5.4 million barrels of crude oil daily through the waterway. President Trump claimed he was working with Beijing and that China welcomed efforts to reopen the strait.

stories.title: Pakistan receives $2bn from Saudi Arabia: State Bank
stories.summary: Pakistan's State Bank confirmed receipt of $2 billion from Saudi Arabia on April 15, 2026. The transfer came during Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's visit to Saudi Arabia, where Riyadh also pledged an additional $3 billion in deposits and extended an existing $5 billion facility for three more years.

stories.title: Europe live: Russia ‘does not deserve’ lifting of sanctions, Zelenskyy says, after deadly overnight strikes in Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia does not deserve the lifting of sanctions after deadly overnight strikes targeted Kyiv, Odesa, and Dnipro with nearly 700 drones and 19 ballistic missiles. The European Commission agreed that easing sanctions on Moscow would not help maintain pressure to end the war.

stories.title: U.S. rules out renewal of exemption from sanctions on Russian, Iranian oil
stories.summary: On March 5, the United States issued a 30-day sanctions waiver allowing India to purchase Russian oil despite sanctions related to the Ukraine war. The U.S. has since ruled out renewing exemptions from sanctions on Russian and Iranian oil.

stories.title: French MPs to debate antisemitism law that critics say will stifle criticism
stories.summary: French lawmakers are set to debate a bill defining antisemitism, proposed after a surge in anti-Jewish incidents. Critics, including rights groups, academics, and left-wing politicians, argue the legislation could be used to censor legitimate criticism of Israel and suppress Palestinian rights activism.

stories.title: Brazil’s Lula blasts Trump’s fear-based rule, calls for ‘great maturity’
stories.summary: Brazilian President Lula da Silva criticized U.S. President Donald Trump in an interview with El Pais, condemning Trump's April 7 threat against Iranian civilization and arguing that world leaders should seek respect rather than rule through fear.

stories.title: Pakistani army chief visits Tehran in hopes for renewed talks between US and Iran
stories.summary: Pakistan's army chief visited Tehran on Thursday to meet Iranian officials and push for an extension of the ceasefire that paused nearly seven weeks of war between Israel, the US, and Iran. The conflict has killed thousands and disrupted global oil markets.

stories.title: Forced to drop out: Yemen’s children trade school for survival
stories.summary: Yemen's ongoing armed conflict has forced millions of children out of school, as families prioritize day-to-day survival over education.

stories.title: Cameroon: Pope Leo Brings Message of Unity to Cameroon's Divided Anglophone Regions
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV traveled to Bamenda in western Cameroon to deliver a message of peace amid the ongoing Anglophone separatist conflict, which humanitarian organizations have described as one of the world's most neglected crises.

stories.title: Ukraine: At least 16 killed in overnight Russian strikes
stories.summary: Russian drone and missile strikes killed at least 16 people across Ukraine overnight, hitting residential buildings in Kyiv, Dnipro, and Odesa. The Ukrainian air force reported Russia launched 659 drones and 44 missiles, of which 636 drones and 31 missiles were intercepted.

stories.title: Sudan power crisis: Studying using candles, counting gas station trips
stories.summary: Sudan's protracted electricity crisis is being compounded by surging fuel prices and broader economic turmoil, affecting students who resort to studying by candlelight and residents who must make repeated trips to gas stations.

stories.title: Iran halts petrochemical exports until further notice
stories.summary: Iran suspended all petrochemical exports to prioritize domestic supply after Israeli strikes damaged several petrochemical hubs. The National Petrochemical Company instructed firms to halt exports until further notice.

stories.title: China warns travellers to avoid Seattle airport after academics denied entry to US
stories.summary: China's foreign ministry advised citizens to avoid Seattle-Tacoma International Airport after approximately 20 Chinese academics with valid visas were denied entry to the United States. The ministry said the scholars faced unreasonable interrogation while traveling to a conference.

stories.title: Drone attack sparks fire at Tuapse oil refinery in Russia
stories.summary: A fire broke out at an oil refinery in the city of Tuapse in Russia's Krasnodar Krai following a drone attack.

stories.title: New regulator powers could stifle advocacy, UK’s largest civil society bodies warn
stories.summary: Several of the UK's largest civil society organizations wrote to Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy urging the government to consult the sector before granting new powers to the Charity Commission. They warned that proposed social cohesion measures could suppress legitimate advocacy and restrict civic space.

stories.title: Iran-Israel war LIVE: U.S.-sanctioned supertankers enter Gulf despite blockade
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced a naval blockade on Iran on April 12, 2026, after peace talks between the U.S. and Iran in Islamabad failed to produce an agreement. Despite the blockade, U.S.-sanctioned supertankers have entered the Persian Gulf.

stories.title: Russian forces kill 13 across Kyiv, Odesa, and Dnipro in overnight missile and drone attack
stories.summary: Russian forces launched a massive overnight missile and drone attack on Ukraine on April 16, killing 13 people across Kyiv, Odesa, and Dnipro. The strikes were part of a broader wave of aerial assaults targeting multiple Ukrainian cities.

stories.title: Ukraine: Russian strikes hit Kyiv’s Podilsky district
stories.summary: Russian strikes hit Kyiv's Podilsky district, injuring dozens of people and damaging residential buildings. The attack was part of a broader wave of deadly Russian aerial assaults across Ukraine.

stories.title: US has turned back 13 ships in blockade of Iran, Joint Chiefs chairman says
stories.summary: Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff reported that the U.S. has turned back 13 ships as part of its naval blockade of Iran. Defense Secretary Hegseth disputed Tehran's claims of having closed the Strait of Hormuz, though the presence of lingering mines remains a concern.

stories.title: Is Iran’s economy buckling under war pressure or holding up?
stories.summary: Iran's sanctions-hit economy has suffered further damage from the war, though continued oil revenues have provided a degree of financial cushion against the worst effects.

stories.title: 2 children killed in Ukrainian drone strike on Russia
stories.summary: Two children, aged 5 and 14, were killed in a Ukrainian drone strike on Tuapse in Russia's Krasnodar Region, according to Governor Veniamin Kondratyev. Two adults were also injured in the attack.

stories.title: Odesa hit by waves of Russian attacks: Eight killed, 16 wounded
stories.summary: A nighttime Russian attack on the Ukrainian city of Odesa killed eight people and wounded 16 others.

stories.title: Iran's internet shutdown continues into its 48th day
stories.summary: Iran's internet shutdown has entered its 48th day, making it the longest continuous internet outage in recorded history according to monitor NetBlocks. The blackout has caused an estimated $1.8 billion in economic losses.

stories.title: Madonna announces new album, a sequel two decades later, 'Confessions on a Dance Floor: Part II'
stories.summary: Madonna announced a new album titled "Confessions on a Dance Floor: Part II," set for release on July 3 via Warner Records. The album is a sequel to her 2005 original, coming 21 years later.

stories.title: Hampshire College was ‘a magical place’ for a progressive education. It couldn’t survive this era
stories.summary: Hampshire College, a progressive liberal arts institution in Massachusetts that enrolled its first class in 1970, is closing after 56 years. The school fell victim to declining enrollment amid a decades-long crisis affecting liberal arts colleges across the United States.

stories.title: China fast-tracks hydrogen strategy to ‘scale-up’ phase in high-stakes energy transition
stories.summary: China's National Energy Administration pledged to accelerate the country's hydrogen industry development, calling it a strategic lever for national energy resilience. The announcement came amid global energy security concerns driven by the escalating Middle East conflict.

stories.title: China single mum works at building sites, lifting bags of cement for 16 years to support child
stories.summary: Wei Guiyun, a 40-year-old single mother from Hunan province, China, has gained widespread attention online after sharing her story of working on construction sites carrying cement bags for 16 years to fund her daughter's education.

stories.title: Trump says Lebanese and Israeli leaders to speak
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump announced that Lebanese and Israeli leaders would speak for the first time in decades on Thursday. Pakistan said peace in Lebanon was essential for the US-Iran talks it is mediating, as the Lebanon conflict had escalated after Iran-backed Hezbollah opened fire in support of Tehran on March 2.

stories.title: Lebanon expresses cautious optimism on US president's claim of direct talks with Israel
stories.summary: Lebanon expressed cautious optimism after US President Trump claimed Israeli and Lebanese leaders would hold direct talks on Thursday. No confirmation had been issued from either Jerusalem or Beirut at the time of reporting.

stories.title: 'Confusion' as Trump says Israel, Lebanon leaders to hold talks
stories.summary: US President Trump said Israeli and Lebanese leaders would speak Thursday in a historic first, though neither side initially confirmed. Lebanon was drawn into the broader Middle East war on March 2 when Iran-backed Hezbollah attacked Israel, prompting an Israeli offensive.

stories.title: Russian massive strikes kill at least 16 across Ukraine
stories.summary: A massive Russian barrage of 659 drones and 44 missiles killed at least 16 people across Ukrainian cities, with peace talks stalled more than four years into the war. Ukraine's air defense forces intercepted 636 drones and 31 missiles during the attack.

stories.title: Proposed antisemitism law in France stir free speech debate
stories.summary: French lawmakers are set to debate the "Yadan law," which would classify implicit expressions of hatred toward the state of Israel as antisemitic under terrorism laws. Critics warn the bill would suppress legitimate criticism of Israel and could paradoxically fuel further antisemitism in France.

stories.title: Teenager kills nine, wounds 13 in Turkey school shooting
stories.summary: A 14-year-old armed with five guns opened fire at a school in Turkey's southern Kahramanmaras province on Wednesday, killing nine people and wounding 13. It was Turkey's second school shooting in as many days, a rare occurrence in the country.

stories.title: DRC and M23 rebels eye peace monitoring agreement in Switzerland
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo and M23 rebels are engaged in peace-monitoring negotiations in Switzerland, even as fighting has spread into the South Kivu highlands, displacing and endangering civilians.

stories.title: ‘Iran has to come’ to the US for the World Cup, FIFA’s Infantino says
stories.summary: FIFA president Gianni Infantino stated that Iran must be allowed to participate in the US-hosted World Cup, emphasizing that Iranian players want to compete in the tournament.

stories.title: Why are fuel price protests sweeping the Republic of Ireland?
stories.summary: Fuel price protests have swept the Republic of Ireland, with truck convoys blocking roads and critical infrastructure. Organizers have indicated the demonstrations may extend north of the border.

stories.title: Russia warns drone companies in Europe could be 'potential targets'
stories.summary: Russia warned that drone companies operating in Europe could become potential targets. The statement came amid ongoing tensions over military technology transfers related to the Ukraine conflict.

stories.title: Anti-France influencer Kemi Seba arrested in South Africa for inciting rebellion in Benin
stories.summary: Pan-African activist Kemi Seba, who was born in France to Beninese parents and stripped of his French nationality two years ago, was arrested in South Africa for inciting rebellion by supporting a foiled coup in Benin. Seba, who has over 1.5 million social media followers, has been accused of amplifying Russian propaganda across Africa.

stories.title: Iran, US remain far apart on nuclear issue amid push for talks
stories.summary: The US and Iran remain far apart on the nuclear issue as Pakistan works to arrange new negotiations before a regional ceasefire expires on 22 April. The US is deploying thousands of additional troops to the Middle East.

stories.title: Wave of Russian drone and missile attacks kill at least 16 in Ukraine
stories.summary: A wave of Russian drone and missile attacks struck multiple locations across Ukraine, killing at least 16 people. Separately, Ukrainian officials reported that a Ukrainian drone attack killed two children in Russia.

stories.title: Syrian Kurds register for citizenship after decades marginalised
stories.summary: Syrian Kurds, marginalized for decades and denied citizenship, are now registering for Syrian nationality under a new decree that restores their legal rights and recognition.

stories.title: Indian man charged with sexual assault of passenger on Singapore-Perth Scoot flight
stories.summary: A 52-year-old Indian national was charged in Australia with sexually assaulting a female passenger on a Scoot flight from Singapore to Perth. The woman sought help from airline staff and was moved to another seat during the flight.

stories.title: YouTube suspends pro-Iran channel posting Lego-style clips mocking Trump
stories.summary: YouTube suspended Explosive Media, a pro-Tehran creator group widely suspected of ties to the Iranian government, for posting Lego-style animated clips mocking U.S. President Trump. The channel had gained notoriety during the U.S.-Iran war.

stories.title: Israeli ambassador said to meet discreetly with French far right’s Marine Le Pen
stories.summary: Israel's ambassador to France reportedly held discreet meetings with far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen, who has criticized President Macron's stance on Israel. Le Pen also reportedly met with Lebanon's envoy.

stories.title: “Just stop oil”: Ukraine’s drones return to Tuapse — the Rosneft site where the refinery and the Black Sea export pier are one asset
stories.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Rosneft-owned facility in Tuapse, Russia, which combines a refinery and a Black Sea oil export pier. Satellite imagery confirmed fires at the pier, tank farm, and power plant, continuing Ukraine's campaign to reduce Russian oil export revenues.

stories.title: Are we going back to war? The shocking truth behind the fragile ceasefire
stories.summary: Israel has resumed daily routines following a turbulent period, but residents remain on edge amid ongoing tensions with Iran and Hezbollah. Peace talks remain uncertain, and the possibility of renewed flare-ups persists.

stories.title: Pakistan: Second round of US-Iranian talks to take place soon
stories.summary: Pakistan announced that the United States and Iran are willing to hold a second round of talks soon, though no date has been set. Pakistan's foreign ministry also stressed that Lebanon remains part of a two-week regional ceasefire.

stories.title: Nigerian airlines plan shutdown over soaring fuel costs
stories.summary: Nigerian airlines announced plans for a shutdown in response to soaring aviation fuel costs. The rising prices threaten to disrupt air travel across the country.

stories.title: Live on Sunday: Declaration of Independence at the Kotel - Sponsored Content
stories.summary: A gathering is planned at the egalitarian section of the Western Wall in Jerusalem, where Jews from Israel and abroad will read the Declaration of Independence to affirm shared values.

stories.title: US jails men over IT worker ploy funding North Korea weapons
stories.summary: U.S. authorities jailed individuals involved in a scheme that used fake IT worker identities to funnel money to North Korea's weapons programs. More than 100 U.S. companies were targeted through so-called "laptop farms" operations.

stories.title: Photos of Nazis left at Haifa health ministry office on Holocaust Remembrance Day
stories.summary: Photos of Nazis were left at a Health Ministry office in Haifa on Holocaust Remembrance Day. The ministry said the incident was addressed promptly and did not disrupt services, but no suspects have been identified.

stories.title: Authorities seize over NIS 5m., weapons, ammunition in Rahat, order closure of Tel Aviv brothel
stories.summary: Israel Police seized over NIS 5 million in cash along with illegal weapons and ammunition during an operation in the southern city of Rahat. Separately, authorities ordered the closure of a brothel in Tel Aviv as part of broader law enforcement efforts.

stories.title: Somalia: Somaliland Rejects Somalian Government Claims Over Sovereign Diplomacy
stories.summary: Somaliland's Ministry of Foreign Affairs issued a statement rejecting what it called misleading claims by the Somali government regarding Somaliland's sovereign diplomatic relations, including its engagement with Israel.

stories.title: Capital Development Authority razes nearly 200 Noorpur Shahan houses during massive operation in Islamabad
stories.summary: Islamabad's Capital Development Authority demolished nearly 200 houses in Noorpur Shahan during an anti-encroachment operation under heavy police deployment. Police registered cases against 350 individuals under the Anti-Terrorism Act following a violent clash the previous day.

stories.title: Forced displacements to soar by 4.2 million by 2027, aid group warns
stories.summary: An aid organization warned that forced displacements globally could increase by 4.2 million people by 2027. This projected rise comes on top of the 117.3 million people already displaced worldwide.

stories.title: Europe lacks China strategy, needs new US approach, Biscop says
stories.summary: Belgian political scientist Sven Biscop, director at the Egmont Royal Institute for International Relations, argued that Europe lacks a coherent China strategy and needs to develop a new approach to its relationship with the United States.

stories.title: Paper oil
stories.summary: An analysis examines why global oil prices have not spiked dramatically despite the prolonged closure of the Strait of Hormuz and severe supply disruptions. Countries have been releasing strategic petroleum reserves, yet the price behavior remains puzzling to market observers.

stories.title: War on Iran: How the West is shaping a dystopian era
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has spoken openly about revitalizing colonialism, according to analysis, as allied states acknowledge the erosion of the rules-based international order amid the Western-led war on Iran.

stories.title: We failed to check if workers smoked at Wang Fuk Court, firms tell fire hearing
stories.summary: Two renovation subcontractors told an independent committee investigating Hong Kong's deadly Wang Fuk Court fire that they had not regulated workers' smoking behavior before the blaze. The firms also admitted to replacing fireproof windows with movable wooden boards at evacuation passages.

stories.title: How Jewish heritage projects in Morocco are being used to push pro-Israel politics
stories.summary: Organizations linked to Israel are reportedly using Jewish heritage preservation projects in Morocco to promote pro-Israel sentiment and counter pro-Palestinian sympathies among Moroccan youth.

stories.title: U.S.-sanctioned supertankers enter Gulf despite blockade
stories.summary: On April 15, 2026, an Iranian supertanker under U.S. sanctions crossed the Strait of Hormuz toward Iran's Imam Khomeini port, defying the U.S. naval blockade, according to Iran's Fars News Agency.

stories.title: US jury rules Live Nation is illegal monopoly
stories.summary: A federal jury in New York ruled that Live Nation, the parent company of Ticketmaster, operates as an illegal monopoly in an antitrust lawsuit. Separately, the IMF issued warnings about rising public debt amid a global energy crisis, while China's economy beat expectations despite the Iran war.

stories.title: Nigerian army buries soldiers killed in militant attacks
stories.summary: The Nigerian army held a burial ceremony on Wednesday for officers and soldiers killed in recent Islamist militant attacks in the northeast of the country.

stories.title: Car ploughs into e-bike riders and pedestrians in China
stories.summary: A driver in China rammed a vehicle into e-bike riders and pedestrians, with videos capturing the moment of the incident.

stories.title: Irked by JI banners on civic woes, Karachi mayor warns printing presses of shutdown
stories.summary: Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab threatened to shut down printing presses producing banners for the opposition Jamaat-i-Islami party that highlight civic issues. He also formed a KMC vigilance squad on e-bikes to curb vandalism in the city.

stories.title: Bye-bye, US? Why China’s trade with Africa benefits from Trump’s policy volatility
stories.summary: China's exports to Africa surged 32.1 percent year on year in the first quarter of 2026, reaching $60.66 billion and making Africa China's fastest-growing export market. The growth was driven by shipments of machinery, vehicles, solar technology, and batteries amid shifting trade patterns away from the U.S.

stories.title: Lebanon talks
stories.summary: U.S.-brokered talks between Lebanon and Israel were held in Washington, marking the first major direct meeting between delegations of both countries since the early 1990s. Lebanon sought an immediate ceasefire, while Israel focused on the disarming of Hezbollah.

stories.title: Russian missiles hit Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities, three dead
stories.summary: Russian forces struck Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities early on April 16, killing three people including a 12-year-old child and injuring more than 20. The missile attacks caused significant damage to buildings across multiple cities.

stories.title: Enemy drone strikes high-rise in Kyiv’s Podil district
stories.summary: A Russian drone struck a high-rise building in Kyiv's Podil district during a morning attack on the Ukrainian capital.

stories.title: Israeli air attack destroys buildings around south Lebanon hospital
stories.summary: Israeli air strikes near a hospital in southern Lebanon destroyed surrounding buildings and several emergency vehicles.

stories.title: Mark Mobius, ‘Indiana Jones of emerging markets’, dies at 89
stories.summary: Mark Mobius, widely known as the "Indiana Jones of emerging markets," died at age 89. He was credited as a pioneer in emerging markets investing and remained active in the field throughout his career.

stories.title: US Senate Republicans back Trump military sales to Israel
stories.summary: The U.S. Senate Republicans blocked two resolutions that would have stopped military sales of bombs and bulldozers to Israel. The vote backed President Trump's continued arms transfers to Israel.

stories.title: Pakistan ramps up shuttle diplomacy with PM in Saudi Arabia, CDF in Tehran
stories.summary: Pakistan is conducting shuttle diplomacy with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif visiting Saudi Arabia and the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff traveling to Tehran. The efforts coincide with U.S. expressions of optimism about a second round of Iran peace talks in Islamabad.

stories.title: Ten-day ceasefire between Lebanon and Israel comes into effect
stories.summary: A 10-day ceasefire between Lebanon and Israel came into effect shortly after Israel and Hezbollah exchanged cross-border fire in the final hours before the truce.

stories.title: Trump says Israel, Lebanon agree to 10-day ceasefire
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump announced that Israel and Lebanon have agreed to a 10-day ceasefire, set to begin at 5 PM EST. Trump said the agreement came after he spoke with the leaders of both countries.

stories.title: US optimistic about Iran deal, says Israel and Lebanon will talk
stories.summary: The US expressed optimism about reaching a deal with Iran as Pakistan-mediated talks approach. President Trump announced that Israeli and Lebanese leaders would speak soon, while Tehran issued warnings about Red Sea trade.

stories.title: ウクライナ防空支援 NATO各国強化 英は無人機12万機以上供与へ
stories.summary: NATO member states held a meeting on bolstering Ukraine's air defense capabilities amid Russia's ongoing military invasion. The United Kingdom announced its largest contribution to date, pledging over 120,000 drones to Ukraine.

stories.title: Netanyahu to speak to Lebanon's Aoun, Israeli minister claims
stories.summary: Israeli Science and Technology Minister Gila Gamliel claimed Prime Minister Netanyahu would speak with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun, citing US and Israeli involvement in efforts to disarm Hezbollah in Lebanon.

stories.title: TIME names Netanyahu among 2026 Most Influential, calls his post-Oct. 7 comeback bigger than Trump
stories.summary: TIME magazine named Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu among its 2026 Most Influential list. Editor-at-large Ian Bremmer wrote that Netanyahu engineered a political comeback after Hamas's October 7 massacre that may have surpassed Donald Trump's own resurgence.

stories.title: Emergency boilers sat in storage all winter. Now Ukraine is rethinking the whole approach.
stories.summary: Emergency boilers procured for Ukraine's energy needs reportedly sat unused in storage through the winter. Ukrainian authorities are now reassessing their energy infrastructure strategy ahead of October, when the next heating season begins and renewed Russian attacks are anticipated.

stories.title: Russian army loses 1,100 troops in single day of war against Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine's military reported that Russian forces lost approximately 1,100 troops in a single 24-hour period. Total estimated Russian combat losses since the February 2022 invasion through April 16, 2026, have reached approximately 1,315,070 personnel.

stories.title: Beninese pan-African activist Kemi Seba arrested in South Africa
stories.summary: Beninese pan-African activist Kemi Seba was arrested in South Africa on charges related to inciting rebellion, sought by Benin's government in Cotonou. He has been remanded in custody as extradition proceedings begin.

stories.title: For 5th time, Netanyahu included on Time’s annual list of 100 most influential people
stories.summary: Time magazine included Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on its annual list of 100 most influential people for the fifth time, noting both the October 7 security failure and his subsequent political comeback.

stories.title: Nighttime Russian attack on Odesa kills seven, wounds 11
stories.summary: A nighttime Russian attack on the Ukrainian city of Odesa killed seven people and wounded 11 others.

stories.title: Anti-war, anti-ICE demonstrations held across US on Tax Day
stories.summary: Demonstrations took place across the United States on Tax Day, 15 April, with protesters opposing the use of tax dollars for foreign wars and domestic immigration enforcement crackdowns by ICE.

stories.title: Bullish narrative around India’s economy at odds with struggling rupee
stories.summary: The Indian rupee gained around 1.5 percent since March 27, making it Asia's best-performing currency in that period. However, the recovery masks economic vulnerabilities worsened by the energy shock from the Iran conflict, as India imports 90 percent of its oil.

stories.title: US teens reject charges over ISIS-linked bomb plot in New York
stories.summary: Two teenagers from Pennsylvania rejected charges related to an ISIS-linked bomb plot in New York. Prosecutors alleged the pair discussed plans to kill up to 60 people in the attack.

stories.title: Satellite images reveal scale of Israeli demolitions as Lebanese villages destroyed
stories.summary: BBC Verify analysis of satellite imagery found that more than 1,400 buildings in Lebanese villages have been destroyed since 2 March as a result of Israeli demolitions.

stories.title: Man bitten by his own dog month ago dies from rabies in Karachi
stories.summary: A 34-year-old construction worker in Karachi's Malir area died from rabies after being bitten by his own dog a month earlier. He is the eighth reported rabies case in Pakistan's Sindh province.

stories.title: Ukraine: Deadly Russian strikes on Kyiv, Odesa and Dnipro leave 12 dead
stories.summary: Russian strikes on Kyiv, Odesa, and Dnipro killed at least 12 people, including a child, in mid-April. The attacks occurred as fighting continued and ceasefire efforts remained unsuccessful.

stories.title: Trump risks showdown with Xi before summit over Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: The U.S. naval blockade of Iran's ports is testing the fragile détente between Washington and Beijing ahead of a potential Trump-Xi summit. The Strait of Hormuz confrontation risks a showdown between the world's two largest economies.

stories.title: Tax relief on menstrual products proposed in Balochistan
stories.summary: Balochistan Education Minister Raheela Durrani chaired a consultative meeting in Quetta on proposed tax relief for menstrual hygiene products. The session, organized with UNICEF Pakistan, aimed to develop a joint assembly resolution on menstrual health and hygiene tax reforms.

stories.title: Egypt and Saudi Arabia are building alternatives to Hormuz
stories.summary: Egypt and Saudi Arabia are developing new logistics corridors as alternatives to the Strait of Hormuz. Maritime transport experts say the routes reduce transit time and costs for goods arriving in the Gulf.

stories.title: FIFA head says Iran will ‘for sure’ participate in soccer World Cup in US
stories.summary: FIFA president Gianni Infantino declared that Iran will participate in the US-hosted soccer World Cup, stating Iran must attend to represent its people, despite earlier suggestions by Trump that Iranian players might face safety concerns.

stories.title: Settlers try to steal Palestinian-owned sheep in Hebron Hills as West Bank violence soars
stories.summary: Israeli settlers attempted to steal Palestinian-owned sheep in the Hebron Hills in the occupied West Bank. A rights group reported 378 settler attacks during the first 40 days of the Iran war, with two Palestinians reportedly wounded near Bethlehem.

stories.title: 11 nations urge support for states facing Middle East war fallout
stories.summary: Eleven nations have urged the IMF and World Bank to provide coordinated emergency support for countries affected by the Middle East conflict. Meanwhile, Iran has threatened to disrupt Red Sea maritime routes if its ports remain under siege, and the U.S. blockade has turned back several vessels.

stories.title: Israel continues to pummel Lebanon
stories.summary: Israeli forces continued air strikes and artillery shelling in southern Lebanon, ordering residents south of the Zahrani River to move north. Sirens sounded in northern Israel after rocket fire was detected from Lebanon.

stories.title: Fire at key Australian refinery deepens fuel risks amid Iran war shortages
stories.summary: A major fire at a key refinery in Australia has disrupted fuel production, heightening concerns about fuel shortages already exacerbated by supply constraints linked to the Iran war.

stories.title: Europe prepares plan to replace US command in NATO if Trump decides to leave - WSJ
stories.summary: European officials are developing a contingency plan to replace US command structures within NATO should President Trump decide to withdraw, according to the Wall Street Journal. The plan aims to preserve nuclear deterrence and military cohesion against Russia rather than rival NATO.

stories.title: Death toll from Russian attack on Kyiv rises to four, 45 injured
stories.summary: The death toll from a Russian overnight attack on Kyiv has risen to four, with 45 people reported injured.

stories.title: Anthropic’s Nuclear Bomb
stories.summary: Anthropic launched its newest AI model, Claude Mythos Preview, on April 7. Analysis suggests the model could theoretically exploit previously unknown software vulnerabilities autonomously, raising concerns about the erosion of barriers between nation-state-level cyber capabilities and broader access.

stories.title: Anthropic’s Nuclear Bomb
stories.summary: Anthropic launched its newest AI model, Claude Mythos Preview, on April 7. Analysis suggests the model could theoretically exploit previously unknown software vulnerabilities autonomously, raising concerns about the erosion of barriers between nation-state-level cyberattack capabilities and broader access.

stories.title: Why is France’s bill against ‘new forms of anti-Semitism’ sparking controversy?
stories.summary: French lawmakers are debating a bill that would define implicitly expressed hatred toward Israel as antisemitism, making it punishable under terrorism laws. Critics including rights groups and left-wing politicians warn the "Yadan law" could suppress legitimate criticism of Israel and Palestinian rights activism.

stories.title: Xi Jinping stresses ‘patience’ on Taiwan reunification in talks with opposition leader
stories.summary: Chinese Communist Party leader Xi Jinping met Taiwan's opposition Kuomintang leader Cheng Li-wun at Beijing's Great Hall of the People, the first such meeting between sitting leaders of both parties in nearly a decade. Xi emphasized patience regarding Taiwan reunification.

stories.title: Water on Mars? Scientists discover 'bathtub ring' which may reveal contours of ancient ocean
stories.summary: Scientists have identified a geological formation on Mars resembling a 'bathtub ring' that may outline the contours of an ancient ocean. The discovery supports evidence that Mars was warmer and wetter early in its history.

stories.title: Russian missiles and drones kill at least 16 across Ukraine in worst attack this year
stories.summary: Russia launched its deadliest attack of 2026 on Ukraine, striking Kyiv and other cities overnight with drones and missiles, killing at least 16 people including a 12-year-old child and wounding scores. Multiple fires broke out across the capital, causing widespread damage.

stories.title: Trump’s ‘triumphal arch’ draws backlash, even from an expert who proposed it
stories.summary: President Trump's proposal for a "triumphal arch" drew widespread backlash, including criticism from the expert who originally suggested the concept. Such arches have historically been built by ancient civilizations to commemorate military or civic achievements.

stories.title: PTI secretary general offers his resignation, again
stories.summary: PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja publicly reiterated his intention to resign from the position, saying he had repeatedly asked party founder Imran Khan to relieve him of the role.

stories.title: Muslims the target? Fury as millions lose voting rights in India’s Bengal
stories.summary: Millions of voters in India's West Bengal state face potential disenfranchisement ahead of elections due to a controversial voter list revision that critics say disproportionately excludes Muslims.

stories.title: Attacks on security men escorting polio teams slammed
stories.summary: Pakistan's Polio Eradication Initiative condemned three attacks on security personnel escorting polio vaccination teams in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan. A police constable was killed in Nasirabad while on duty with a polio team. So far, 27 million of a targeted 45 million children have been vaccinated.

stories.title: Lebanon 'not aware' of upcoming contact with Israel, source tells AFP
stories.summary: A Lebanese official source told AFP that Beirut was not aware of any planned contact with Israel through official channels, despite US President Trump claiming on Truth Social that Israeli-Lebanese talks would occur Thursday.

stories.title: How Russia killed 16 Ukrainian civilians overnight — even as Ukraine intercepted 95% of its missiles and drones (updated)
stories.summary: Russia launched approximately 703 aerial weapons — including missiles and Shahed-type drones — at Ukrainian cities in two waves, striking Kyiv, Odesa, and central Ukraine. Despite Ukraine intercepting about 95% of incoming threats, at least 16 civilians were killed, including a child in Kyiv and eight people in one Odesa building.

stories.title: Trump’s son to accompany him on visit to China
stories.summary: Eric Trump and his wife Lara will accompany U.S. President Donald Trump on his May 14–15 visit to China. A Trump Organisation spokeswoman said Eric will attend in a personal capacity and has no business ventures or plans in China.

stories.title: As Ohio again tries to block Hebrew Union College’s restructuring, a new rabbinical school emerges
stories.summary: Ohio Attorney General Dave Yost has taken legal action to block the restructuring and closure of Hebrew Union College's Cincinnati campus, citing donor intent and the institution's historical significance. Meanwhile, a new rabbinical school is emerging as an alternative.

stories.title: 21,400 civilians remain in active combat zone in Donetsk region
stories.summary: Approximately 21,400 civilians remain in active combat zones within Ukraine's Donetsk region.

stories.title: A Fragile Ceasefire with Iran and the Price of Ending the War
stories.summary: The United States and Iran are set to resume talks via Pakistani mediation after the first round in Islamabad failed to produce an agreement, with significant gaps remaining. Meanwhile, President Trump imposed a blockade on Iranian ports, and Israel continued its assault on Lebanon's border town of Bint Jbeil while engaging in direct talks with Lebanon in Washington.

stories.title: Rethinking Security Cooperation in the Age of Commercial Tech
stories.summary: Commercial technologies are increasingly enabling the U.S. military and allied forces to operate with greater efficiency and lethality. President Trump has mandated the Department of Defense to prioritize commercial solutions, and Congress has reinforced this approach to help outmatch adversaries including China and Russia.

stories.title: Rethinking Security Cooperation in the Age of Commercial Tech
stories.summary: Commercial technologies are increasingly enabling the US military and allied forces to operate with greater efficiency and lethality. President Trump has directed the Department of Defense to prioritize commercial solutions, and Congress has reinforced these efforts to address challenges in the defense industrial base's ability to match adversaries like China and Russia.

stories.title: Amid Lebanon truce talks, Israel kills 3 paramedics
stories.summary: Israel struck paramedic teams in the town of Mayfadoun in southern Lebanon's Nabatiyeh district, killing three paramedics amid ongoing ceasefire negotiations. The Lebanese health ministry reported three consecutive strikes on the medical personnel.

stories.title: Prolonged Iran war to have serious consequences, warns Aurangzeb
stories.summary: Pakistani Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb warned that a prolonged conflict in the Middle East would have serious financial consequences for Pakistan and the global economy. Speaking to CNBC from Washington, he noted Pakistan's diplomatic efforts to facilitate engagement between the U.S. and Iran.

stories.title: World Bank chief economist warns of hunger risk from war in Iran
stories.summary: World Bank Chief Economist Indermit Gill warned that the war in Iran poses a significant hunger risk globally. He cautioned that global inflation could rise from approximately 3 percent to as much as 4.7 percent this year.

stories.title: Pakistani delegation, led by Army chief Munir, reaches Iran for peace talks
stories.summary: A Pakistani delegation led by Army Chief Munir arrived in Tehran for peace talks aimed at mediating the conflict. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi welcomed the delegation upon arrival, according to Iranian media reports.

stories.title: This video of ‘Iran capturing US pilot’ was filmed in Pakistan
stories.summary: A viral video falsely claiming to show Iran capturing a downed U.S. F-35 pilot was actually filmed in Pakistan. The South China Morning Post's fact-checking team investigated the claim circulating on social media amid the US-Israel war on Iran.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV visits Cameroon as Biya faces unrest and separatist war
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Yaoundé, Cameroon, on Wednesday and urged the country's leaders to address corruption. The visit comes as President Biya's government faces domestic unrest and an ongoing separatist conflict.

stories.title: The End of Managed Escalation in the Gulf
stories.summary: The US-Israeli war against Iran has undermined the decades-old deterrence model that governed Gulf security, exposing the limits of managed escalation strategies. The conflict has disrupted a framework built on covert strikes, proxy warfare, and US security guarantees, while Iran had relied on missiles, regional partners, and nuclear latency.

stories.title: Japan remains most trusted power in Southeast Asia despite military build-up: survey
stories.summary: A survey by the Singapore-based ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute found that Japan remains the most trusted external power among Southeast Asian countries. Analysts noted that Tokyo should maintain transparency about its military build-up and constitutional reform efforts to reassure regional partners that its actions support collective security.

stories.title: Five miners killed in Duki coalfield accidents
stories.summary: Five coal miners were killed in two separate mine accidents in the Bolan and Duki coalfield areas of Balochistan, Pakistan. Methane gas accumulation trapped miners underground in one incident, while another miner was injured.

stories.title: Operationalizing Economic Statecraft: A New Imperative for the Pentagon
stories.summary: The Potomac Institute for Policy Studies and War on the Rocks published the sixth installment in an 11-part series exploring how the U.S. Department of Defense should integrate economic statecraft into its strategy and national security practice. The article argues that supply-chain vulnerabilities could determine the outcome of a future major conflict before kinetic operations begin.

stories.title: Chinese investors cheer Tesla’s AI chip progress, pushing up shares of local suppliers
stories.summary: Chinese suppliers of Tesla components, including Ningbo Tuopu Group and Zhejiang Sanhua Intelligent Controls, saw share prices rise by up to 4.6 percent on Thursday after Tesla announced its AI5 inference chip was 45 days ahead of schedule. Tesla's own Nasdaq-listed stock had jumped nearly 7.7 percent the previous day.

stories.title: New home prices in China’s biggest cities record first rise in 10 months
stories.summary: New home prices in China's four first-tier cities rose 0.2 percent in March, the first increase in ten months, according to National Bureau of Statistics data. Shanghai and Guangzhou each gained 0.3 percent, Shenzhen rose 0.2 percent, and Beijing held flat. Analysts cautioned it is too early to declare the property market stable.

stories.title: China trims US Treasury holdings amid rising debt supply as global ownership hits record
stories.summary: China reduced its holdings of US Treasury securities to $693.3 billion in February, down from $694.4 billion in January, according to US Treasury Department data. The decrease continued a broader long-term trend of Beijing diversifying its foreign exchange reserves, even as total overseas holdings of US sovereign debt reached a record high.

stories.title: Drone attack on Kharkiv injures two, damages gas pipeline
stories.summary: Russian drones struck multiple districts in Kharkiv, Ukraine. Strikes in the Industrial and Nemyshlyanskyi districts damaged residential buildings, severed a gas pipeline, and injured two people.

stories.title: From auction block to loving home: China netizens remember celebrity dog’s heartwarming journey
stories.summary: Deng Deng, a Shiba Inu famous for being China's first dog sold at judicial auction for 160,000 yuan, died on April 7 at age 13. His owner, identified as Shu, announced the death on social media. The dog had spent five years in his adoptive home and was widely remembered by Chinese internet users.

stories.title: Why many Kashmiris are donating gold, breaking piggy banks for Iran
stories.summary: Kashmiris have been donating gold and breaking open savings in solidarity with Iran amid the ongoing war, drawing on centuries-old historical and cultural ties between Kashmir and Iran.

stories.title: Nigeria: Flood Warnings As Govt Issues Urgent Alert To 33 States
stories.summary: The Nigerian Federal Government released its 2026 Annual Flood Outlook, predicting widespread flooding and prompting state governments across 33 states to intensify preventive measures.

stories.title: Australia: Refinery fire raises fuel supply concerns amid Iran war
stories.summary: A fire broke out at Viva Energy's Geelong refinery in Australia, which supplies approximately 10% of the nation's fuel. The incident has raised fuel supply concerns as the ongoing Iran war keeps global oil prices elevated.

stories.title: Nigeria: Atiku Signals Last Presidential Run, Asserts Northern Political Dominance
